He let out a soft little yawn, blinked his big green eyes at the warm sun, and decided that chasing butterflies was the most fun thing a little gray cat could ever do on a sunny afternoon.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text:
Once upon a time, there was a fluffy little cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had soft white paws, big green eyes, and a tail that liked to twitch when he was happy. Every morning, when the sun started to wake up and peek through the bedroom window, Whiskers would wake up too. Yawn! Big stretch! Out went his front paws, and out went his back legs. He was ready for a brand new day.

Today, the sun made a bright, golden puddle right on the soft living room rug. Whiskers loved the golden puddle. It was warm, cozy, and the best place in the whole house for a cat nap. Purr, purr, purr went Whiskers as he curled himself up into a tiny furry circle right in the middle of the sunshine. He closed his sleepy eyes and dreamed about chasing crunchy autumn leaves and catching big bouncy balls of colorful yarn.

Suddenly, a little blue butterfly fluttered right past his nose. Flutter, flutter, went the butterfly's wings. Whiskers opened one green eye. Then he opened the other green eye. His tail gave a little wiggle. One, two, three, pounce! Whiskers jumped up, but the butterfly was too fast and flew right out the open window. Whiskers giggled in his kitty way and licked his paw. That was fun!

Just then, his favorite human, a little girl named Lily, walked into the room carrying a shiny bowl. 'Time for breakfast, Whiskers!' she cheered. Whiskers trotted over as fast as his little legs could carry him, going meow, meow, meow. He ate every single bite of his yummy fish dinner. With a full tummy and a happy heart, Whiskers trotted back to his sunny spot on the rug. The sun was still warm, and it was time for another snooze. Good night, sweet sunshine. Good night, little Whiskers.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
Barnaby was a roly-poly orange tabby cat who lived in a cozy red farmhouse. Barnaby had stripes like a tiger and a tummy that was as soft as a marshmallow. More than anything in the whole wide world, Barnaby loved to play games. His absolute favorite toy was a big, bright, shiny red ball that bounced up and down with a happy boing-boing sound.

Every afternoon, Barnaby would wait by the screen door for the farmer to roll the ball across the wooden porch. When the ball rolled, Barnaby dashed after it. Pat-pat-pat went his little kitty feet! He chased it across the porch, past the old rocking chair, and right up to the big brown boots by the door. Barnaby batted the ball with his left paw. Then he batted it with his right paw. Boing! The ball bounced high into the air, and Barnaby jumped up to catch it, looking just like a furry little acrobat.

Sometimes, the ball would roll under the big green sofa in the living room. Oh no! Barnaby would peek underneath the cushions with his big round eyes. It was dark down there, but Barnaby was a brave kitty. He reached his long, soft paw far, far underneath. He felt something round and smooth. Got it! With a mighty tug, he pulled the big red ball back out into the light. He gave a triumphant little meow and did a happy spin on his furry back.

When the afternoon sun began to turn pink and purple, Barnaby started to feel very sleepy. All that running and bouncing is hard work for a little cat! He rolled the red ball into his special basket in the corner. Then, Barnaby curled up right next to his favorite toy, tucked his nose under his tail, and closed his eyes. The farm grew quiet, and Barnaby purred himself fast asleep, dreaming of bouncing high up into the clouds.

stories.title: Mittens Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Mittens was a clever black-and-white cat with paws that looked like she was wearing tiny white boots. She lived in a cheerful house filled with buzzing bees in the garden and tall green grass. Mittens was very curious, and today she wanted to explore the backyard to see who she could meet.

First, she tiptoed softly across the green lawn. Tip-toe, tip-toe, went her paws. She stopped by the big oak tree and looked up. Who was that? It was a fluffy grey squirrel chattering away in the branches. 'Chitter-chatter!' said the squirrel. 'Meow!' said Mittens. They played a fun game of peek-a-boo around the thick tree trunk. Mittens hid behind the leaves, and the squirrel peeked down from above. They both laughed in their own special animal ways.

Next, Mittens walked over to the wooden fence where a row of bright yellow sunflowers grew tall and proud. A friendly brown puppy was digging a little hole in the dirt nearby. Thump, thump, went the puppy's tail. Mittens was not scared at all. She walked right up and booped her wet pink nose against the puppy's cold black nose. Boop! The puppy gave a happy bark and rolled over onto his back. Mittens gently patted his soft tummy with her velvet paw.

By the time the afternoon winds began to cool, Mittens had made two wonderful new friends in the sunny yard. She trotted back to the porch where a warm bowl of fresh milk was waiting just for her. She drank every drop, cleaned her whiskers until they sparkled, and curled up on the welcome mat. It was a wonderful day for a friendly little cat, and as she drifted off to sleep, she knew tomorrow would bring even more fun adventures in the bright green garden.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy little house, lived a little orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had soft fur, two pointy ears, and a long, swishy tail. Every morning, when the sun started to wake up, a bright golden patch of light would shine right through the living room window. Whiskers loved the golden light. It was his favorite thing in the whole wide world. 

One sunny morning, Whiskers stretched his front paws way up high. Big stretch! Then, he yawned a giant kitty yawn. *Yaaawn!* He scampered across the soft rug to find his special sunbeam. But oh no! The sunbeam was not on the floor today. It had moved up, all the way up to the big yellow armchair! 

'Meow?' said Whiskers. How would he get up there? Whiskers looked at the chair. He looked at his little paws. He gave a little wiggle of his furry bottom, and *hop!* He jumped right onto the cushion. But he missed the sunbeam! He landed on a fluffy green pillow instead. 

Whiskers did not give up. He scooted to the left. He scooted to the right. And then, he found it! The warm, cozy sunbeam was wrapping all around him like a giant, invisible hug. Whiskers closed his green eyes and purred. *Purr, purr, purr, purr.* It felt so warm and nice on his tummy. 

Soon, a little yellow butterfly fluttered past the window. *Flutter, flutter, go!* Whiskers opened one sleepy eye. He gave a gentle swipe with his paw, but he was just too cozy to chase it. He tucked his paws underneath his fluffy chest and curled up into a tight, furry circle. The sunbeam kept him warm, the house was quiet and safe, and Whiskers drifted off to sweet kitty dreamland. Goodnight, sweet sunbeam. Goodnight, little cat.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
Meet Barnaby! Barnaby is a fluffy black-and-white cat with white paws that look like he is wearing tiny little socks. Barnaby loves to play games. His most favorite toy in the whole house is a shiny, bouncy, bright red ball. It is as round as a button and as red as a strawberry. 

Every afternoon, Barnaby likes to hunt for his ball. Today, the red ball was hiding. Where could it be? Barnaby walked into the kitchen on tiptoe. *Tap, tap, tap* went his little paws on the shiny floor. He peeked under the table. No red ball there. Only Mommy’s big brown boots! 

Then, Barnaby trotted down the hallway. He looked inside the laundry basket. He pushed his soft black nose right into a pile of warm towels. *Sniff, sniff.* No red ball there either! Just a sleepy-looking stuffed teddy bear. 

Barnaby let out a little sigh. *Meow.* Where was his favorite toy? Just then, he heard a funny sound from the living room. *Roll, tap, bounce!* Barnaby’s ears perked straight up. He spun around in a little circle. There it was! The bright red ball was peeking out from underneath the sofa! 

Barnaby got down very, very low. He wiggled his furry bottom once. He wiggled it twice. One, two, three, and *pounce!* Barnaby jumped right on top of the red ball with all four paws! He hugged it tight so it could not roll away again. 

Then, Barnaby batted the ball with his paw. *Boing!* The ball rolled across the floor, and Barnaby chased after it, running as fast as his little legs could carry him. What a fun game! Barnaby and his red ball played happily together until the stars came out to shine in the evening sky.

stories.title: Mittens Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Mittens was a gentle gray cat with a pink nose and soft, velvet paws. Mittens lived in a pretty cottage with a big green garden full of flowers. Mittens loved to explore the garden every single day. She liked smelling the yellow daisies and watching the buzzing bumblebees fly from petal to petal. 

One breezy afternoon, while Mittens was sniffing a red rose, she heard a tiny sound. *Squeak, squeak, squeak.* Mittens stopped. She froze completely still. She did not even twitch her whiskers. She turned her head and looked down near the garden fence. 

Sitting on the green grass was a very small, brown mouse with big round ears and a long, thin tail. His name was Pip. Pip looked up at Mittens, and his little nose trembled. *Squeak!* Pip was scared of the cat! 

Mittens wanted to show Pip that she was a very friendly cat. She did not want to chase him. Instead, Mittens sat down politely on the grass. She wrapped her tail neatly around her front paws. Then, she blinked her big yellow eyes very slowly. That is how cats say hello and smile! 

Pip stopped shaking. He took one little step closer. *Sniff, sniff.* He smelled Mittens' soft fur. Mittens leaned forward and gave a tiny, gentle *meow*. It sounded like a friendly whisper. 

Pip realized this cat was not mean at all. In fact, she was very nice! Pip did a little happy hop. Mittens reached out and touched Pip's tiny paw with her own soft white paw. It was the start of a wonderful friendship. From that day on, Mittens and Pip played hide-and-seek in the garden every single afternoon. They chased falling leaves and shared sunny spots in the grass, the best of friends forever.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy little house, lived a fluffy orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had two big green eyes, four soft paws, and a long tail that liked to twitch when he was happy. Every morning, the golden sun would wake up before anyone else. It would stretch its long, warm arms right through the big living room window and paint a bright, square patch on the soft brown carpet. 

Whiskers loved that patch of carpet more than anything in the whole wide world. When he saw it, he would do a little happy dance on his tiptoes. Trot, trot, trot, went his soft paws. Then, down he would plop, right in the middle of the golden warmth. He would roll over onto his back, stretch his legs up high into the air, and let out a soft, happy sigh. Purr, purr, purr went his little motor inside.

Soon, a little yellow butterfly fluttered past the window. It danced up and down, up and down. Whiskers blinked his green eyes. He wanted to catch the butterfly, but the sunbeam was just too warm and cozy. His eyelids felt very, very heavy. He gave a big yawn, showing his tiny pink tongue and little white teeth. 

'Meow,' whispered Whiskers softly. He curled his tail around his nose and closed his eyes. The sunbeam wrapped around him like a giant, warm hug. He dreamed of chasing balls of yarn that smelled like catnip. The house was quiet and peaceful. Whiskers slept and slept, all curled up in his favorite golden spot, dreaming sweet kitty dreams until the afternoon came along to tickle his whiskers once again.

stories.title: The Playful Ball of Blue Yarn
stories.text:
Down in the basement, where the boxes stacked high, lived a little black cat named Shadow. Shadow had fur as dark as night, except for one tiny white spot right on his chest that looked like a falling star. Today, Shadow was on a very important mission. Grandma had left her knitting basket wide open on the floor, and rolling right near the edge was a big, bright ball of blue yarn.

Shadow crouched down low. He wiggled his bottom once. He wiggled his bottom twice. His tail swished back and forth on the cool concrete floor. Pounce! Shadow leaped forward through the air, his paws outstretched. He landed right on top of the blue yarn!

The yarn did not just sit there. Oh no! It was very sneaky. It gave a little wobble and began to roll away. Roll, roll, roll went the blue ball, heading across the room. Shadow chased after it in a flurry of black fur. He batted it with his left paw. Tap! Then he batted it with his right paw. Tap, tap! 

The yarn rolled under the rocking chair. Shadow squeezed his squishy tummy under the chair to follow. Boop! He bumped his nose on the wooden rung. 'Mew!' he complained, shaking his head. But then the yarn popped out the other side. Shadow zoomed out after it.

He chased the yarn in circles, getting faster and faster until he was dizzy. Finally, he gave the yarn one last gentle hug with both front paws. They both tumbled to a stop near Grandma's slippers. Shadow purred loudly, licking his paw and washing his face. He had caught the runaway blue yarn, and it was time for a well-earned rest right beside his favorite basket.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Night Out
stories.text:
Barnaby was a chubby gray tabby cat who wore a shiny red collar with a little brass bell that went jingle, jangle, jingle whenever he walked. Barnaby loved his home inside the warm yellow cottage, but when the moon came up and painted the sky in dark blue velvet, Barnaby liked to go on little neighborhood adventures.

Tonight, the moon was big and round like a silver coin. Barnaby pushed open the back door, which was left slightly ajar. Squeak went the door. Step, step, step went Barnaby's paws onto the cool green grass. Jingle, jangle, went his collar. He walked softly over to the garden fence.

Sitting on top of the wooden fence was his very best friend, a fluffy white cat named Luna. 'Meow-hello!' purred Luna, swishing her tail. Barnaby hopped up onto the fence right beside her. Together, they looked up at the sparkling stars that twinkled like tiny diamonds in the night sky. They watched a tiny firefly glow on and off, on and off, floating past their noses.

Then, they heard a rustle in the bushes. Crunch, crunch, crunch. Was it a monster? No! It was a tiny hedgehog looking for a midnight snack. Barnaby and Luna watched with wide, curious eyes. The hedgehog gave a friendly little snort and waddled away into the dark.

Barnaby yawned a big kitty yawn. The night air was getting chilly, and his tummy was starting to rumble for his midnight kibble. He bumped heads with Luna to say goodbye. Trot, trot, trot, ran Barnaby all the way back home. He slipped through the door, curled up at the foot of the big bed, and fell fast asleep after his exciting night under the stars.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Sunny Spot
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy little house, lived a fluffy orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had the softest fur, the pinkest nose, and a tail that went swish, swish, swish. Every morning, the warm yellow sun would peek through the big living room window and paint a bright, beautiful square right on the wooden floor. Whiskers loved this sunny spot more than anything in the whole wide world. It was his special magic spot. When the sun came out, Whiskers would stretch his front paws way out. Big stretch! Then he would stretch his back legs. He would let out a tiny kitty yawn, showing his little white teeth. Meow! Time to find the sunbeams. Whiskers trotted across the room on his soft little paws. Pat, pat, pat went his feet. He stepped right into the warm yellow square. Ah, it felt just like a warm hug from mama! Whiskers curled himself up into a tight, cozy ball, just like a fuzzy orange cinnamon roll. He closed his sleepy green eyes and began to purr. Purr, purr, purr went Whiskers. It sounded like a happy little engine running inside his tummy. A friendly little brown mouse named Pip peeked out from behind the sofa. Pip saw Whiskers sleeping in the sun and wanted to say hello. Pip took one tiny step, then another. Squeak! Whiskers opened one sleepy eye. Did he chase the mouse? Oh, no! Whiskers was much too cozy and happy in his warm sunbeam. He just blinked slowly at Pip and gave a sleepy little purr. Pip smiled and scurried away to find a piece of cheese. The sun moved slowly across the floor, and Whiskers moved right along with it, following his favorite light. By afternoon, the big sun began to hide behind the fluffy white clouds. The warm square on the floor started to fade away. Oh no! Where did the sun go? Whiskers opened both eyes and stood up. He shook his fluffy tail. Time for a new adventure! He saw a red ball of yarn rolling across the rug. Whiskers ran after it, batting it with his paw. Tap, tap, tap! He had so much fun playing. But when evening came and the moon shone bright in the dark sky, Whiskers knew just where to go. He curled up on the soft bed next to his favorite human, purring a sweet goodnight song until he fell fast asleep.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Barnaby was a sleek black cat with shiny green eyes and white paws that looked like he was wearing tiny little socks. Barnaby lived in a wonderful house filled with fun toys, but his absolute favorite thing in the whole world was a bouncing, shiny red ball. The ball was as bright as a ripe strawberry and had a fun little jingle bell hiding right inside it. Every afternoon, Barnaby would wait patiently by the toy basket until it was time to play. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby's human friend threw the red ball across the living room rug. Zoom went the ball! Barnaby’s eyes went wide. He dropped down low to the floor, wiggled his fluffy bottom, and got ready to pounce. One, two, three, go! Barnaby dashed across the room like a tiny black lightning bolt. Pat, pat, pat went his little feet. He leaped into the air with a big hop and caught the red ball right between his front paws. Jingle, jingle, went the bell inside. Barnaby purred loudly, feeling very proud of his great catch. He rolled over onto his back, holding the ball up in the air with all four paws. But oh dear! The ball gave a sudden little wiggle and rolled away. It rolled past the big green armchair. It rolled under the wooden rocking chair. Barnaby scrambled up quickly and gave chase. Where did it go? He peeked his head under the rocking chair. He saw a fuzzy tail, but it wasn't the ball—it was just his own tail swishing back and forth! He giggled a little kitty giggle inside. Then he heard a funny sound from the kitchen. Tap, tap, roll! The red ball was rolling across the shiny kitchen tiles. Barnaby raced into the kitchen as fast as he could go. He slid a little bit on the smooth floor, making a funny skittering sound. Whee! That was fun! He reached out one soft paw and tapped the ball gently. Tap! The ball bounced against the pantry door and rolled right back to him. Barnaby scooped it up and held it tight. He was the happiest kitty in the whole neighborhood. After playing such a wonderful game, Barnaby felt his eyelids growing very heavy. He curled up in his favorite cozy basket, tucked his white paws under his chin, and hugged his shiny red ball all the way to dreamland.

stories.title: Mittens and the Butterfly
stories.text: Once upon a time, there was a sweet little kitten named Mittens. Mittens had soft grey fur and a little white patch right on her chest that looked just like a fluffy cloud. Mittens lived in a pretty house with a big green garden full of colorful flowers. Red flowers, yellow flowers, and purple flowers grew all around, smelling very sweet in the warm breeze. One bright morning, Mittens stepped out onto the back porch to explore the garden. The grass felt cool and tickly against her tiny paws. She took a deep breath. Sniff, sniff! She smelled sweet roses and damp earth. Suddenly, a little flutter caught her eye. Flutter, flutter, go! It was a beautiful butterfly with wings as bright as sunshine, dancing through the air. The butterfly was yellow with black spots, and it flew gracefully from one flower to another. Mittens sat down in the soft green grass and tilted her head. Her long whiskers twitched with excitement. She had never seen anything so magical before! The butterfly landed gently on a pink daisy right in front of her. Mittens leaned forward slowly, moving inch by inch. She wiggled her bottom and got ready to catch her new winged friend. Boing! Mittens leaped up into the air, reaching out with her little grey paws. But the butterfly was much too quick! With a gentle flutter, it zoomed up into the blue sky. Missed it! Mittens landed softly back in the grass with a light plop. She didn't feel sad at all. Instead, she let out a little chirp and trotted after the fluttering insect. The butterfly flew around the big apple tree, and Mittens ran around the trunk. Round and round they went, playing a joyful game of tag in the sunshine. The butterfly danced over the garden pond, making ripples in the water. Mittens stopped at the edge of the pond and watched her own reflection in the shiny water. Hello there, kitty! She tapped the water with one paw, making a splash. Splash, splash! The cool water felt nice on her toes. The butterfly landed safely on a high branch where Mittens couldn't reach, resting its tired wings. Mittens sat down beneath the tree, looking up with a happy smile. She had the most wonderful time playing in the garden. When the warm sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Mittens stretched her legs and walked back to the porch. She curled up in her cozy basket, closed her eyes, and dreamed of flying yellow butterflies until the stars came out.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text: Once upon a time, there was a fluffy little cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had soft gray fur, two pointy ears, and a long tail that liked to swish, swish, swish. Every morning, when the sun peeked through the big bedroom window, something magical happened. A bright, warm golden patch of light landed right on the soft green rug. Whiskers loved the sunbeam. He stretched out his front paws. Big stretch! Then he stretched out his back paws. Long stretch! Whiskers padded softly across the room, his little paws going patter-pat, patter-pat. He hopped right into the middle of the warm sunbeam and curled up into a cozy little furry ball. 'Purr, purr, purr,' sang Whiskers. It was the best place in the whole wide house. Soon, a little yellow butterfly fluttered past the window. Flutter, flutter, flutter went its wings. Whiskers opened one green eye. He gave his little pink nose a tiny wiggle. Then, he raised one paw and gave a gentle tap to the air. Tap, tap! But the butterfly flew high up into the blue sky. Whiskers did not mind at all. He just curled right back up in his wonderful warm sunbeam. He closed his eyes and dreamed of sweet kitty treats and milk in a red bowl. The sunbeam felt like a giant, warm hug from the sky. Whiskers yawned a big, wide kitty yawn. Ahhh-meow! He was so safe, so happy, and so very sleepy. The warm light wrapped all around him like a cozy blanket. Soon, little Whiskers was fast asleep, dreaming his sweet cat dreams in the golden light.

stories.title: The Playful Ball of Yarn
stories.text: Little cat Pip loved to play. Pip had bright blue eyes and tiny white paws that looked like he was wearing little white socks. One sunny afternoon, Pip saw something round and bright sitting on the living room floor. It was a big ball of red yarn! It looked just like a giant cherry. Pip walked over slowly, stepping tiptoe, tiptoe, tiptoe. He tilted his furry head to the left. Then he tilted his furry head to the right. He gave the red yarn a tiny poke with his nose. Boop! Suddenly, the red yarn rolled away. Whee! Pip’s eyes went wide with excitement. He chased after it as fast as his little legs could carry him. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went his feet! The red yarn rolled under the big brown sofa. Pip dove right after it. Swoosh! He peeked out from underneath the sofa with a piece of red yarn stuck right to his nose. 'Meow!' laughed Pip, shaking his head. The yarn unrolled all across the floor, making a long, squiggly red road. Pip walked right along the red road, balancing like a tiny circus cat. One step, two steps, three steps! Then, he pounced! Pounce, pounce, went little Pip, landing right on top of the soft red ball. He gave it a gentle hug with his front paws and gave it a soft lick. The red yarn was his very best friend in the whole world. Pip purred a happy little song, curled his tail around his tummy, and rested right there on the soft yarn, ready for his next big game.

stories.title: The Sleepy Kitty's Bedtime Star
stories.text: When the sky turned dark and painted itself in shades of purple and deep blue, little cat Luna knew it was almost bedtime. Luna was a pretty black cat with a shiny coat and whiskers that twinkled like stars. She sat on the front porch steps and looked up at the big night sky. The moon was a bright yellow banana shining down on the quiet sleeping neighborhood. A tiny star blinked way up high. Twinkle, twinkle, little star! Luna let out a soft, sleepy yawn. She rubbed her face with her soft paw. Wash, wash, wash went her paw over her little ears. It was time for kitty sleep. Luna walked back inside the warm house. She padded softly down the hallway, her tail held high in the air like a question mark. She walked past the sleeping toys and past the quiet kitchen. Finally, she reached her favorite spot in the whole house: a basket filled with the softest, fluffiest yellow blankets. Luna hopped up into the basket. Hop! She turned around once. She turned around twice. Then she curled up tight, tucking her cold nose right under her warm tail. The house was quiet. The moon was bright. Outside, the night wind blew softly through the trees, whispering a gentle lullaby. Rustle, rustle, go the leaves. Luna closed her big green eyes and listened to the peaceful sounds of the night. She felt safe, cozy, and loved. With one final soft purr, little Luna drifted off to sleep, ready to wake up and play again when the morning sun came back to say hello.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy little house, lived a fluffy orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had two big green eyes, four soft white paws, and a long tail that liked to twitch when he was happy. Every morning, the bright yellow sun would peek through the big living room window. The sun made a lovely, warm square right on the soft blue rug. Whiskers loved the sun square more than anything else in the whole wide world. 

One sunny morning, Whiskers woke up and stretched. Big stretch! He reached his front paws way out, and then he stretched his back legs. Yawn! Whiskers opened his mouth wide. Meow! It was time to find the sun. He trotted quietly across the wooden floor. Tippy-toe, tippy-toe, go the little cat paws. When he reached the living room, he saw it. The golden sun square was waiting just for him. 

Whiskers curled up into a perfect fuzzy ball right in the middle of the warm light. Ahhh, it felt so good. It felt like a warm hug from Mama Cat. He closed his eyes and purred. Purr, purr, purr, purr. His tummy went up and down, up and down. A little butterfly fluttered past the window outside, but Whiskers was too sleepy to chase it. The sunbeam was his favorite place to be. 

Soon, a little girl named Lily walked into the room. She saw sleepy Whiskers resting in the light. 'Good morning, my sweet kitty,' Lily whispered softly. She knelt down and gave Whiskers a gentle stroke on his soft head. Whiskers purred even louder. He opened one green eye to look at his favorite girl. Lily sat right down on the rug next to him, and Whiskers stretched out his warm furry body to share the lovely sunbeam with his best friend. They sat together in the golden light, feeling happy, cozy, and loved all morning long.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Ball
stories.text:
Barnaby was a sleek black cat with a shiny coat and a tiny white spot right under his chin. Barnaby was very curious. He loved to explore every single corner of the big house where he lived. One afternoon, while looking under the big green sofa, Barnaby found something wonderful. It was a little red ball! The ball was round, bouncy, and bright red like a juicy apple. Barnaby poked it with his paw. Boing! The ball rolled across the floor.

Barnaby's eyes went wide. Oh boy! A new game! He chased after the red ball as fast as his four paws could carry him. Tap, tap, tap went his paws on the floor. The ball rolled past the kitchen table. Barnaby zoomed right after it. The ball rolled under the yellow rocking chair. Barnaby ducked his head low and wriggled his fuzzy bottom. One, two, three, pounce! He jumped right on top of the ball, but it squirted out from under his paws and kept on rolling.

Oh no you don't! thought Barnaby. He leaped over a pile of soft pillows. He slid across the smooth hallway rug. The red ball bounced down the short hallway and stopped right near his food bowl. Barnaby dashed forward and trapped the ball between his front paws. He gave it a gentle tap with his nose. He was the champion ball catcher!

Just then, his owner, Tommy, walked into the room and laughed out loud. 'Did you find your toy, Barnaby?' Tommy asked. Tommy picked up the red ball and tossed it gently across the room. Barnaby scrambled after it with a happy meow. Playing with his red ball was the best way to spend the afternoon, and Barnaby was the happiest kitty in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Mittens Finds a Butterfly
stories.text:
Mittens was a playful calico cat with patches of orange, black, and white on her soft fur. She wore a little blue collar with a tiny silver bell that went jingle, jingle, jingle whenever she walked. Mittens spent her afternoons exploring the big green garden behind her house. The grass tickled her tummy, and the flowers smelled sweet like honey. 

Today, Mittens was sitting under a big green fern, washing her left paw. Lick, lick, lick went her pink tongue. Suddenly, a flash of bright yellow caught her eye. It was a beautiful butterfly with wings that fluttered up and down, up and down. The butterfly danced through the air like a piece of flying sunshine. Mittens stopped washing her paw immediately. Her ears perked straight up, and her green eyes grew as big as saucers.

Flutter, flutter, went the butterfly. Tippy-toe, tippy-toe, went Mittens. She crept through the green grass, trying to be as quiet as a mouse. Jingle went her bell! Oh no! The butterfly heard the little bell and fluttered up higher into the sky. Mittens froze. She sat very still and waited for the butterfly to come back down. 

Slowly, the yellow butterfly drifted down and landed right on top of a red daisy flower. Mittens wiggled her bottom one, two, three times. She got ready to pounce. But right before she jumped, the butterfly opened its wings wide, winked at Mittens, and flew up, up, up over the wooden garden fence.

'Meow!' called out Mittens in surprise. She trotted over to the fence and looked up into the big blue sky. The butterfly was gone, flying away to its home. Mittens didn't mind at all. Chasing the flying sunshine had been so much fun. With a happy purr, she turned around and trotted back to the porch for a nice, long cat nap in the cool shade.

stories.title: Oliver's Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little orange cat named Oliver woke up with a big stretch. Yawn! He opened his green eyes and saw something very exciting on the living room rug. It was a bright red ball! The ball was round and shiny. It looked like a tiny cherry, but it was much better because it could roll. Oliver wiggled his bottom. One wiggle, two wiggles, three wiggles! Zoom! He pounced on the red ball. The ball rolled across the floor, and Oliver chased after it with his soft little paws. Pat-pat-pat went his feet. The ball rolled under the big green sofa. Oliver stopped and blinked. Where did the ball go? He peeked underneath the sofa. It was dark down there, but Oliver saw two shiny spots. Those were not the ball; those were his own whiskers brushing against the dust bunnies! Oliver reached out his paw. He stretched it as far as it could go. Tap! He touched the red ball. He pulled it back out into the bright sunshine. The ball rolled again, bouncing right over Oliver's fluffy tail. Oliver giggled, making a happy little purr sound deep in his throat. Purr, purr, purr. He chased the ball into the kitchen, right past Mama Cat's bowl. Mama Cat smiled and gave Oliver a gentle lick on his head. Oliver was so happy. He curled up right next to his red ball and gave himself a nice face wash. Lick, lick, wash, wash. His little paws cleaned behind his ears. Then, feeling very tired after all that hard playing, Oliver closed his eyes. He dreamed of red balls bouncing in the sky like sweet strawberries. Goodnight, little Oliver. Sleep tight with your favorite toy.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Box
stories.text: Barnaby was a black and white cat with white paws that looked like little socks. One afternoon, a delivery truck brought a big brown cardboard box to the front door. The box was tall and wide. It was bigger than Barnaby! When Papa opened the box and took out the new toaster, the box was completely empty. Barnaby looked at the empty box. His eyes went big and round like two saucers. A big cardboard box was the best thing in the whole wide world! Barnaby walked over to the box. He sniffed it with his pink nose. Sniff, sniff. It smelled like paper and adventure. Barnaby lifted his front paws and hopped right inside. Plop! He was sitting right in the middle of the box. But Barnaby wanted to see what was happening outside. He stood up on his hind legs and popped his head over the edge of the cardboard wall. Peek-a-boo! I see you! Barnaby called out to his friend the puppy, who was sleeping on the rug. The puppy opened one sleepy eye and wagged his tail. Barnaby ducked down again, hiding completely inside his secret castle. He curled up into a tight little furry ball. It was so cozy inside the box. It felt safe, warm, and quiet. Barnaby closed his eyes for a quick catnap. When he woke up, he decided the box needed a decoration. He reached out and scratched the side with his claws. Scratch, scratch, scratch. That made a fun sound! Then Barnaby jumped out of the box with a big springy leap. Boing! He ran around the room in a happy circle before diving right back in. The box was his favorite spaceship, his favorite castle, and his favorite bed all at the same time. Barnaby curled up inside and purred himself to sleep, dreaming of flying to the moon in his wonderful brown box.

stories.title: Mittens Finds the Sunbeam
stories.text: Mittens was a fluffy grey cat with the softest fur you ever did feel. On this particular morning, the weather outside was chilly and grey. The wind whispered through the trees, making the branches dance. Brr! Inside the house, however, something magical was happening. The clouds parted outside the big living room window, and a bright, golden beam of sunshine stretched all the way across the wooden floor. It looked like a warm yellow river made of light. Mittens saw the sunbeam and her whiskers twitched with joy. She trotted over on her little pink-toed feet. Step, step, step. She walked right into the middle of the golden light. Oh, it felt so warm! It was like getting a big, cozy hug from the sky. Mittens sat down in the very center of the sunbeam and closed her eyes. She tilted her head up to soak up the cozy heat. Her fur seemed to sparkle like silver glitter in the light. But after a little while, the sunbeam started to move. The big clock on the wall ticked softly, and the sunbeam slowly slid across the floor, moving toward the sofa. Mittens opened one eye. Hey! Where is my warm spot going? She asked herself. She stood up and chased the moving light. As the sunbeam shifted, Mittens shifted with it, staying right in the golden middle. She rolled over onto her back, kicking her paws gently in the air. Look at me, I am catching the sunshine! she seemed to say. Finally, the sunbeam came to a rest right on top of a soft blue pillow. Mittens climbed up onto the pillow, curled into a perfect fuzzy doughnut, and sighed a happy sigh. The sun was warm, the pillow was soft, and Mittens was the happiest cat in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy little house, lived a fluffy orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had two big green eyes, four soft paws, and a long tail that liked to twitch when he was happy. Every morning, the big golden sun would wake up and peek through the living room window. The sun would paint a bright, warm yellow rectangle right on the soft green rug. Whiskers loved this yellow rectangle more than anything in the whole wide world. It was his special sunbeam. 

One sunny Tuesday morning, Whiskers woke up and stretched. Big stretch! He stretched his front paws way out, then he stretched his back legs, and finally, he gave a big kitty yawn. 'Meow!' said Whiskers. He trotted into the living room and saw his favorite sunbeam waiting for him. But wait! The sunbeam was moving! The big clock on the wall tick-tocked, and the sunbeam slowly crept across the floor, moving toward the big armchair. 

'Oh no,' thought Whiskers. 'My warm bed is running away!' Quick as a wink, Whiskers scampered across the room. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went his little paws. He jumped right into the middle of the warm light and curled up into a tight, furry ball. He closed his eyes and purred. *Purr, purr, purr, purr.* It sounded like a tiny motor hummed inside his chest. The sunbeam felt just like a warm hug from a giant blanket. 

Soon, Lily, the little girl who lived in the house, walked into the room. She saw Whiskers sleeping in his sunbeam and giggled. 'Good morning, sleepyhead,' whispered Lily softly so she wouldn't scare him. She knelt down and gave Whiskers a gentle stroke on his soft back. Whiskers opened one green eye, purred even louder, and bumped his wet nose against Lily's hand. Then, he stretched out his legs and rolled onto his back, showing his soft white tummy. Lily laughed and rubbed his tummy gently. The sunbeam wrapped all around them both, making everything feel warm, safe, and happy. Whiskers closed his eyes again and dreamed of chasing bouncy red yarn balls through fields of golden flowers, right inside his wonderful, cozy sunbeam.

stories.title: Barnaby's Bouncy Red Ball
stories.text:
Barnaby was a sleek black cat with shiny fur that looked like night-time silk. Barnaby lived in a cheerful yellow farmhouse with a red roof, where there were lots of interesting things to explore. Barnaby was a very curious cat. He had twitchy ears that could hear the tiniest squeak and bright yellow eyes that missed nothing. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby was sitting on the wooden porch, watching the fluffy white clouds float across the big blue sky. Suddenly, something caught his eye rolling across the green grass. *Boing, roll, bounce!* 

It was a ball. Not just any ball, but a bright, shiny, bouncy red ball! It belonged to Tommy, the farmer's little boy, but it had bounced right out of his toy wagon. Barnaby crouched down low to the ground. His bottom wiggle-woggled. One, two, three, wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! *Pounce!* Barnaby jumped forward, but the red ball rolled away. *Wheee!* It rolled past the big wooden tractor wheel. Barnaby dashed after it. *Pitter-patter, zoom!* He batted the ball with his soft paw. *Tap-tap!* 

The red ball rolled across the yard, right toward the garden patch where the orange pumpkins grew. Barnaby chased it, his tail held high in the air like a question mark. The ball bounced off a big green watering can and zipped toward the porch steps. Barnaby ran as fast as his little legs could carry him. He leaped into the air, reaching out with both paws, and trapped the bouncy red ball right between his front feet. *Gotcha!* 

Just then, Tommy came running around the corner of the house. 'Hey! There is my ball!' Tommy shouted happily. Barnaby looked up at Tommy, gave the ball one last gentle tap with his paw, and purred. Tommy picked up the red ball and tossed it gently a few inches away. Barnaby tapped it right back to him. They played catch together all afternoon in the warm sunshine. When the sun began to sink behind the hills, turning the sky pink and orange, Barnaby curled up right next to Tommy's muddy boots. He was tired, happy, and ready for a long, sweet nap after such a fun day of chasing his very favorite bouncy red ball.

stories.title: Mittens Finds a Fuzzy Friend
stories.text:
Mittens was a tiny grey kitten with four white paws that looked like she was wearing brand-new snow boots. Mittens lived in a cozy apartment filled with soft pillows and interesting corners. Because Mittens was small, everything in the big world looked huge and exciting to her. She loved to explore behind the sofa, peek inside paper grocery bags, and bat at dangling shoelaces. But today, Mittens was on a very important mission. She was looking for a new toy to play with all by herself. 

She trotted down the carpeted hallway, her little bell jingling softly on her red collar. *Tingle-ling, tingle-ling.* She peeked into the kitchen, but there were only shiny pots and pans. She looked under the big dining room table, but there was only a dropped crumb of toast. Finally, Mittens wandered into the sunny playroom. Right in the middle of the soft blue rug sat a basket full of colorful yarn. And right on top of the blue yarn sat something small and fluffy. It was round, brown, and had two floppy felt ears. It was a little stuffed bunny toy! 

Mittens stopped. She blinked her big blue kitten eyes. She tilted her head to the left, then to the right. *Meow?* she asked the bunny. The bunny did not move. It just sat there with a painted smile. Mittens decided to investigate. She crept closer, stepping very softly on her tiptoes. *Step, step, step.* She reached out one little paw and gently patted the bunny's soft brown ear. *Boop!* The bunny tipped over onto its side. 

'Gasp!' thought Mittens. She jumped back in surprise, puffing out her fluffy tail to look twice as big. But when the bunny didn't jump back, Mittens realized it was friendly. She walked back over and gave the bunny a gentle nudge with her wet nose. Then, she curled her body right around the stuffed toy, wrapping her front paws securely around it. It was the softest, cuddliest toy in the whole room. Just then, her human mommy walked in and smiled warmly. 'Looks like you found a new friend, Mittens,' she said. Mittens purred happily, resting her chin right on top of the fuzzy brown ear, ready for a cozy afternoon cuddle with her very best little friend.

stories.title: Whiskers and the Warm Sunbeam
stories.text: Once upon a time, there was a fluffy little orange cat named Whiskers. Whiskers had soft fur, two pointy ears, and a very long tail that liked to swish, swish, swish! Every morning, when the sun popped up in the sky, Whiskers would wake up and stretch. Big stretch! Front paws out, back legs back, and a big kitty yawn. Good morning, Whiskers! Today was a very special day because a golden sunbeam was shining right through the big living room window. Whiskers loved the sunbeam more than anything in the whole wide world. It was warm, cozy, and felt just like a giant hug from the sun. Whiskers trotted across the soft rug with quiet little paws. Tip-toe, tip-toe, tip-toe. He reached the bright patch of light and curled up into a tiny, perfect ball. Purr, purr, purr went Whiskers. His tummy rumbled with pure happiness. Soon, his friend Leo the puppy came bounding into the room. Woof, woof! barked Leo. Leo wanted to play fetch with a squeaky red ball. But Whiskers was too cozy in his warm sunbeam. He just blinked his big green eyes and flicked the tip of his tail. Not right now, Leo, Whiskers seemed to say. It is naptime! Leo understood. He sat right down next to the sunbeam and chewed on his toy, keeping his furry friend company. The sunbeam slowly moved across the floor, and Whiskers slowly scooted right along with it. Inch by inch, he stayed inside the golden warmth. Outside, the birds sang sweet little songs, and the green leaves danced in the gentle breeze. But inside, it was the coziest place on Earth. Whiskers closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of fish-shaped biscuits and floating clouds. When he finally woke up, the sun was hiding behind a big fluffy cloud, but Whiskers still felt warm all over. He gave one final stretch, rubbed his nose against Leo's soft ear, and got up to find a yummy snack. What a wonderful, sunny day for a sleepy little cat.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball of Yarn
stories.text: Barnaby was a playful black-and-white kitty with shiny green eyes and white paws that looked like he was wearing tiny white boots. Barnaby loved to chase things. He chased shadows on the wall, he chased fluttering yellow butterflies in the garden, and most of all, he loved chasing toys. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby's human friend, Mia, left a big basket of knitting supplies right on the living room floor. Sitting right on top was the most amazing thing Barnaby had ever seen. It was a giant ball of bright red yarn! It was round, fuzzy, and looked just like a delicious cherry. Barnaby's eyes went wide. He lowered his furry tummy close to the floor and wiggled his bottom. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Pounce! Barnaby leaped right onto the big red ball. Boing! The ball of yarn didn't just sit there. Oh, no! It began to roll. Whee! yelled Mia with a laugh as the yarn rolled across the wooden floor. Barnaby chased after it as fast as his four little legs could carry him. Tap, tap, tap went his paws. He batted the yarn with his left paw. Tap! Then he batted it with his right paw. Tap! The red yarn rolled under the big green sofa. Barnaby peeked underneath. He could see two glowing eyes staring back at him in the shadows. He reached his paw as far as it could go, stretching, stretching, stretching. Got it! He hooked the yarn with his claws and pulled it back out into the bright room. But oh, no! The yarn had unraveled a little bit, leaving a long red trail behind it. Now there was red yarn wrapped around the table legs, wrapped around the chair legs, and wrapped in a big silly loop right around Barnaby's own tail. Barnaby spun around in circles trying to catch his tail. Round and round he went, getting himself all tangled up like a little fuzzy present. Mia came over and giggled. She gently helped untangle her silly kitty, wrapping the red yarn back up into a neat ball. Barnaby purred a loud, happy song and gave Mia's hand a soft lick with his sandpaper tongue. Then, he curled up right on top of the yarn basket for a well-deserved rest.

stories.title: Mittens Finds a New Friend
stories.text: Mittens was a gentle gray tabby cat with soft stripes and pink paw pads. Mittens lived in a cozy yellow house with a big garden full of red roses, tall green grass, and buzzing bumblebees. Mittens was a very curious cat. Every afternoon, she liked to go on an adventure to see what was happening outside. Today, Mittens stepped off the porch and walked softly onto the lawn. Softly, softly, step, step, step. She sniffed a lovely yellow flower. Sniff, sniff. Ah, what a sweet smell! Then, she heard a funny little sound coming from near the old wooden fence. Rustle, rustle, rustle. Mittens froze. She perked her ears straight up. What could that be? She crept closer, keeping her belly low to the grass. Peeking behind a big green leaf, Mittens saw something wonderful. It was a tiny brown frog! The little frog had shiny round eyes and sat very still, looking right back at Mittens. Ribbit, said the little frog. Meow, whispered Mittens softly so she would not scare her new tiny friend. The frog gave a little hop. Boing! Mittens batted playfully at the air where the frog had just been. Boing went the frog again, hopping right onto a flat gray stepping stone. Mittens giggled inside her furry tummy. She loved games of tag! She trotted after the frog, making sure to be very gentle with her soft paws. The frog hopped through the garden patch, past the watering can, and right up to the little birdbath. Splash! A tiny drop of water landed right on Mittens' pink nose. Brrr! Mittens gave her nose a quick little swipe with her paw, making her whiskers twitch. The little frog sat on the edge of the birdbath and smiled its big froggy smile. Mittens sat down in the soft grass right beside it. They stayed there together for a long time, watching the clouds float by in the big blue sky. When the sun began to sink low and turn the sky pink and orange, the little frog gave one final hop back into the cool green bushes. Goodbye, little frog, Mittens purred. She turned around and trotted happily back to her cozy yellow house, ready for a warm bowl of milk and a sweet kitty dream.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
You have fur of golden brown,
Best little kitty in the town.
When you are so happy, purr,
Rubbing your soft, cozy fur.
Chasing bugs across the floor,
Then you sit beside the door.
Up you stretch to reach the ball,
Playing games both big and small.
Curling up to take a rest,
Sleeping in your fuzzy nest.
Night is coming, stars are bright,
Kitty sleeps until the light.
Dreaming of a fish to eat,
Little kitty, soft and sweet.

rhymes.title: Five Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
See the kitty wake and play,
Starting off a brand new day.
Pointy ears and whiskers white,
Running in the morning light.
Pouncing on a ball of yarn,
Walking by the wooden barn.
Drinking milk out of a bowl,
Happy little kitty soul.
Climbing up a fuzzy tree,
Looking down at you and me.
Softly meowing in the sun,
Now the day has just begun.
Jumping down upon the mat,
What a lovely, friendly cat.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Cuddling in your little bed.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you see?
A little brown bird in the green leafy tree.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you do?
Chasing the bugs in the morning dew.
Soft little paws on the carpet so red,
Creeping around till you go to your bed.
Tail going swish and a flick and a sway,
Having so much fun the whole live-long day.
Climbing up high on a cushion so deep,
Closing your eyes and falling asleep.
Dreaming of mice that can wiggle and run,
Basking all day in the bright golden sun.
Wake up now, kitty, and give me a purr,
Rubbing your face on my jacket of fur.
Best little kitty, so gentle and sweet,
Curl up right now at the end of my feet.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Chasing bugs upon the floor,
Waiting by the kitchen door.

Wear a coat of fuzzy grey,
Ready for a game to play.
Jump up high into the air,
Curl up on the rocking chair.

Purr a happy little tune,
Underneath the yellow moon.
Rub your nose against my hand,
Best pet in the sleepy land.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Curled up in your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Five white whiskers on my face,
Running all around the place.
Soft paws stepping on the rug,
Looking for a gentle hug.

Pouncing on a ball of string,
Happy as a little king.
Drinking milk out of a bowl,
Taking on a playful role.

Climbing up the scratching tree,
Looking down to bark at me.
Wait, cats don't bark, they softly meow,
Saying hello to you right now.

Time to stretch and yawn so wide,
Curl up right here by my side.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
Chasing little mice away.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Golden sunshine on the floor,
Cat is napping by the door.
Wake up, kitty, time to play,
On this happy, sunny day.

Tap your paws and twitch your tail,
Watch the little garden snail.
Spin around and chase your toy,
Filling up the room with joy.

Climb up high upon the chair,
Rest your fluffy body there.
Close your eyes and softly purr,
Rubbing your soft winter fur.

Night is coming, stars are bright,
Kitty sleeps until the light.
Dreaming of a bowl of cream,
Sleeping in a happy dream.

rhymes.title: Little Cat Paws
rhymes.text:
Little cat, little cat, walking on the floor,
Soft little paws stepping by the door.
Stretching out your legs, yawning in the sun,
Time to chase a ball, time to have some fun.
Pointy little ears listening to a sound,
Jumping very high up above the ground.
Curling in a ball on a cozy chair,
Softest little kitty sleeping over there.
Rubbing on my hand, purring loud and sweet,
You are the cutest kitty that I could ever meet.
Chasing down a string, running left and right,
Sleeping all the day and playing all the night.
Little fuzzy tail twitching in your sleep,
Into dreamland now, nice and soft and deep.
Wake up, little kitty, time to play anew,
I am so very glad that I have got you.

rhymes.title: Three Little Kittens
rhymes.text:
Three little kittens lost their mittens,
And they began to cry.
Oh, mother dear, we sadly fear,
Our mittens we have lost.
What! Lost your mittens, you naughty kittens!
Then you shall have no pie.
Mew, mew, mew, mew,
No pie, no pie, no pie.
The three little kittens found their mittens,
And they began to smile.
Oh, mother dear, see here, see here,
Our mittens we have found.
Put on your mittens, you silly kittens,
And you may have some pie.
Purr, purr, purr, purr,
Oh, let us eat the pie!

rhymes.title: Sleepy Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Sleepy kitty cat lying on the rug,
Sleeping all snug like a little bug.
Sunlight makes a spot warm upon the floor,
Kitty will not move until a little more.
Soft fur is gray, eyes are closed up tight,
Resting all day till the coming night.
Dreams of chasing mice running in the grass,
Watching pretty birds as they fly and pass.
Now a little twitch of a fuzzy paw,
Cutest little kitty that you ever saw.
Breathe in and out, slow and steady now,
Resting on the rug, taking gentle bow.
Nighttime will come with the shining moon,
Kitty will wake up very, very soon.
Until then sleep through the afternoon bright,
Holding onto dreams in the fading light.

rhymes.title: Little Paws
rhymes.text:
Little cat with fur so gray,
Likes to sleep and likes to play.
Soft white paws upon the floor,
Walking softly through the door.

Curly tail goes swish and sway,
Chasing little bugs away.
Curled up in a cozy bed,
Resting now his sleepy head.

Purring softly, loud and deep,
Soon the kitten goes to sleep.
Dreaming of a shining ball,
Playing games both big and small.

Morning comes with yellow light,
Kitty wakes up bright and white.
Time to stretch and time to run,
Playing all day in the sun.

rhymes.title: Kitty Cat, Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you see?
A little brown bird in the apple tree.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you know?
The soft white winter brings falling snow.

Kitty cat, kitty cat, where is your toy?
Under the rug with a squeaky joy.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what is that sound?
A ball of yarn rolling on the ground.

Kitty cat, kitty cat, time for a nap?
Right in the warmth of my favorite lap.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you dream?
Swimming in rivers of sweet cream.

Kitty cat, kitty cat, waking up now?
Stretching your back and saying meow.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, you are so sweet,
From pointy ears to furry feet.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Kitten
rhymes.text:
Soft brown fur and whiskers long,
Singing out a purring song.
Jumping up upon the chair,
Looking at the world out there.

Catching beams of yellow light,
Playing until starry night.
Drinking milk from tiny bowl,
Happy kitty, bless his soul.

Curled into a fuzzy ball,
By the warm and sunny wall.
Closing eyes so cute and deep,
Time to cuddle, time to sleep.

Dreaming of a happy mouse,
Running all around the house.
When the morning sun appears,
Kitty wakes and twitch his ears.

rhymes.title: Little Cat, Little Cat
rhymes.text:
Little cat, little cat, sitting on the floor,
Waiting by the kitchen for a tasty treat or more.
With your soft white fur and your whiskers so neat,
You walk around the house with your tiny pink feet.
When the day is over and the stars shine bright,
You curl into a ball for a sleepy, quiet night.
Purring soft and loud as you drift away,
Dreaming of the games that you played today.
Softly purr, softly sleep, dreaming in the dark,
Chasing little mice through a golden park.
Now the morning sun wakes the sleepy town,
Little cat gets up and looks all around.
Stretching out your legs, big and wide and tall,
You are the happiest little cat of all.
Time to play again in the morning light,
Little furry friend, everything is right.

rhymes.title: Pounce and Play
rhymes.text:
Paws upon the carpet, running very fast,
Catching at a feather that is floating past.
Green eyes shining bright in the afternoon,
Singing to the birds and the yellow moon.
Jump up on the chair, look around the room,
Swishing round your tail like a little broom.
Find a ball of yarn, red and soft and round,
Rolling it along all across the ground.
Then you take a rest in a cozy space,
Sleeping all the day in your favorite place.
Wake up with a stretch, wiggle up your nose,
From your furry ears down to tiny toes.
Little ball of joy, furry and so sweet,
You are just the best from your head to feet.
Now it time to eat from your silver bowl,
You have captured all of our happy soul.

rhymes.title: Purr, Purr, Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Purr, purr, kitty cat, sleeping in the sun,
Playing with your toys when the day is done.
Soft and fluffy tail, long and gray and grand,
Best little pet in the happy land.
Walk across the floor with a quiet tread,
Climbing up to rest on a cozy bed.
Rub against my hand, let me pet your head,
Listening to every single word I said.
You are so cute and you are so sweet,
Running on your quick little furry feet.
Watch the little bugs flying in the air,
Leaping very high without any care.
Now the night is here, stars begin to glow,
You are my best friend, this I want you know.
Close your sleepy eyes, rest your weary head,
Sleeping safely now in your little bed.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
You have fur of golden brown,
Best pet in the sleepy town.

Now you curl up on the rug,
Sleeping like a little bug.
With your tail tucked by your nose,
From your whiskers to your toes.

When you wake up from your sleep,
Do not make a single peep.
Chase a ball across the floor,
Then come walking through the door.

Purring softly, loud and clear,
Glad that you are sitting here.

rhymes.title: Five Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Five white whiskers on my face,
Sitting in my favorite place.
Soft black paws and shiny eyes,
Catching butterflies and flies.

Climbing up the tall green tree,
Looking down at you and me.
Jumping softly to the ground,
Without making any sound.

Drinking milk from little bowl,
Happy heart and happy soul.
Chasing shadows on the wall,
Having lots of fun with all.

Now it is time to go to bed,
Resting my tired kitty head.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Golden sunshine on the floor,
Kitty sleeping by the door.
Stretching out a sleepy paw,
Best little cat you ever saw.

Feather toy upon a string,
Kitty jumps and starts to sing.
Meow, meow, hear the sound,
Leaping high above the ground.

Running fast and hiding low,
Where is little kitty? Oh!
There you are behind the chair,
With your fluffy tail right there.

Climb up high into my lap,
Time to take a cozy nap.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Show me how you swish your tail,
Drinking milk out of a pail.

Now you curl up on the rug,
Looking for a cozy hug.
Close your sleepy golden eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

Purring softly, deep and low,
Moving very, very slow.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
Chasing little mice away.

Good-night, kitty, time to rest,
Sleeping is what you do best.
Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with peace and kitty love.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Kitty cat is round and white,
Sleeping in the morning light.
Stretching out your little paws,
Claw-ing softly with your claws.

Jump up high and catch the string,
Play with almost anything!
Bat the ball across the floor,
Run right to the open door.

Now you are a tired pet,
Not a single worry yet.
Curl into a furry ball,
By the bedroom nursery wall.

Breathe in softly, in and out,
What is kitty dreaming about?
Butterflies of yellow gold,
Safe inside the happy fold.

rhymes.title: Three Little Kittens
rhymes.text:
Three little kittens lost their mittens,
And began to cry, oh me, oh my!
Mother cat said, 'Oh, you silly kittens,
Then you shall have no warm fish pie!'

Three little kittens found their mittens,
And they began to purr, oh yes, oh yes!
Mother cat said, 'Oh, my clever kittens,
Eat your fish pie and do not mess!'

Three little kittens washed their mittens,
Hung them up to dry in the breeze.
Mother cat smiled at her sweet kittens,
Giving them a cuddle and a squeeze.

Now they are sleeping safe and warm,
Far away from any storm.
Little kittens snug and tight,
Sleeping softly through the night.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty cat so sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Soft and fluffy, gray and white,
Sleeping softly through the night.

When you wake you like to play,
Chasing little bugs all day.
With a wiggle of your tail,
You can chase a tiny snail.

Now it is time for a nap,
Curled upon my cozy lap.
Purring softly, loud and deep,
While you fall so fast asleep.

Dreaming of a bowl of milk,
Soft as any piece of silk.
Sleep until the day is done,
Little cat beneath the sun.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
See the kitty stretch and yawn,
Greet the lovely golden dawn.
Walking softly on the floor,
Looking out the open door.

Jumping up to catch a string,
Playing with a little thing.
Running fast across the rug,
Giving me a furry hug.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy kitty bed.
Close your eyes and take a rest,
Kitty, you are quite the best.

Purr and purr and purr all day,
While the shadows float away.
Sweet little cat of mine so dear,
I am so glad that you are here.

rhymes.title: Whisker Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Whiskers long and whiskers white,
Kitty shining in the light.
Softly padding on the ground, making not a single sound.

Jump up high upon the chair,
Looking at the toys down there.
Bat a ball of wool around,
Watch it roll upon the ground.

Drink your milk from out your bowl,
Keeping your sweet kitty soul.
Rub against my knee and purr,
Soft and gentle ball of fur.

Climb into a sunny space,
Smile upon your happy face.
Now the day is almost through,
Sleepy kitty, I love you.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
You have whiskers on your nose,
And pink pads beneath your toes.

When the sun begins to rise,
You awake and blink your eyes.
Stretching high up in the air,
Looking for a cozy chair.

Chasing shadows on the floor,
Trotting softly to the door.
Purring loudly on my knee,
Happy as a cat can be.

Now it is time for a nap,
Curled up safely in my lap.
Sleep until the stars shine bright,
Little kitty cat, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Sun
rhymes.text:
See the kitty in the sun,
Having lots of fuzzy fun.
Jumping high to catch a ball,
Playing near the garden wall.

Softly stepping on the grass,
Watching butterflies that pass.
Wearing boots of shiny white,
Running in the morning light.

Now he stops to wash his face,
Sitting in his favorite place.
Swishing round his furry tail,
Drinking from a little pail.

Time to rest his sleepy head,
Curled upon his cozy bed.
Close your eyes and softly purr,
Sleeping with your gentle fur.

rhymes.title: Three Little Kittens
rhymes.text:
Three little kittens play all day,
Chasing toys and finding play.
One is black and one is white,
One is orange and very bright.

They scamper fast across the floor,
Running right up to the door.
Batting at a ball of string,
Happy for each little thing.

When they catch a tickly mouse,
They run all around the house.
Then they stop to take a rest,
Cuddling is what they do best.

Wrapped up in a blanket warm,
Safe away from wind and storm.
Purring softly in a heap,
Till the morning light doth peep.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Paws
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Up the stairs and down the hall,
Chasing after bouncy ball.

Purring softly on the bed,
Resting your sleepy head.
Curly tail and whiskers long,
Singing out a happy song.

Drinking milk from saucer blue,
Kitty, I am fond of you.
Curled up in a furry ring,
You are my favorite little thing.

Now the sun is going down,
Quiet shadows wrap the town.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

rhymes.title: Three Little Cats
rhymes.text:
One little cat with fur so white,
Plays with a ribbon day and night.
Two little cats with stripes of brown,
Run around and tumble down.

Three little cats in coats of gray,
Sleep beneath the sun all day.
Soft and warm upon the floor,
Waiting by the kitchen door.

Tickle a chin and pat a head,
Time to tuck them into bed.
Purring songs so soft and low,
Watch the sleepy kittens grow.

Dreams of fish and mice so small,
Happy little cats all. 
Now the moon is shining bright,
Sleep tight, kitties, sleep tonight.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Cat
rhymes.text:
See the sleepy little cat,
Sleeping on the welcome mat.
Stretching out his paws up high,
Reaching for the morning sky.

Yawning with a pinkish tongue,
Every kitty song is sung.
Now he curls into a ball,
By the sunny garden wall.

Butterflies go flying by,
Dancing in the summer sky.
Kitty watches with one eye,
Then he gives a gentle sigh.

Softly dreaming in the beam,
Floating down a happy stream.
Rest your paws until the morn,
Sweetest kitty ever born.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Paws
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Soft gray fur and whiskers long,
Singing out your happy song.

Jumping up to catch a toy,
Bringing mommy so much joy.
Chasing bugs across the floor,
Wanting to go through the door.

Curling up to take a nap,
Right upon my gentle lap.
Purring softly, deep and low,
Moving very, very slow.

Dreaming of a sunny day,
Chasing birds that fly away.
Goodnight, kitty, rest your head,
Sleeping safely in your bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
See the kitty in the sun,
Having lots of furry fun.
Stretching out his little legs,
Begging for some scrambled eggs.

Batting at a ball of string,
Watching little robins sing.
Climbing up the maple tree,
Looking down at you and me.

Meowing softly for a treat,
With four little muddy feet.
Rubbing gently on my shoe,
Saying that I love you too.

Curled into a furry ball,
Sleeping by the garden wall.
Stars are shining bright above,
Kitty filled with so much love.

rhymes.title: Pounce, Little Cat
rhymes.text:
Pounce, little kitty, touch the floor,
Running toward the kitchen door.
Sharp little claws that go tap-tap,
Ready for a cozy nap.

Tail waving high in the air,
Leaping over every chair.
Chasing shadows on the wall,
Having fun both big and small.

Soft little nose so pink and neat,
Walking down the quiet street.
Drinking milk from out a bowl,
Stealing every loving soul.

Time to rest your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Purring loud and purring deep,
Now the kitty goes to sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
You have fur of golden brown,
Best little kitty in the town.

When you play with balls of yarn,
You run quickly past the barn.
Then you chase a buzzing bee,
Running right up to the tree.

When the afternoon is bright,
You take a nap in golden light.
Curled up in a furry ball,
Sleeping near the garden wall.

When the stars begin to glow,
And the sleepy winds do blow,
You purr a song so soft and deep,
Closing your eyes to go to sleep.

rhymes.title: Paws and Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Soft white paws upon the floor,
Walking softly through the door.
Twitching whiskers, shiny eyes,
Looking at the sunny skies.

Catch a feather in the air,
Jump upon the rocking chair.
Make a funny little sound,
Leaping high above the ground.

Drink your milk from shiny bowl,
Play with toys that softly roll.
Rub against my cozy knee,
Happy as a cat can be.

Now the playtime days are done,
Underneath the setting sun.
Curl up tight upon the bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Pussycat
rhymes.text:
Here is a sleepy pussycat,
Resting on a fuzzy mat.
With a tail that goes swish-swish,
Waiting for a tasty fish.

Climbing up the window sill,
Sitting very safe and still.
Watching birds fly in the blue,
Wondering what they can do.

Stretching out your legs so wide,
Finding cozy spots to hide.
Purring happy songs of glee,
Sitting on my gentle knee.

Night is coming, shadows fall,
Moonlight shining on the wall.
Dreaming sweet dreams till the dawn,
Little kitty, sleep right on.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Soft gray fur and whiskers long,
Singing out your happy song.

When you see a fuzzy ball,
You will chase it down the hall.
Running fast and jumping high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Curled up in a cozy bed,
Resting your little kitty head.

Purr, purr, purr all through the night,
Till the morning brings the light.

rhymes.title: Paws and Claws
rhymes.text:
Paws of white and nose of pink,
What is little cat to think?
Maybe fish upon a plate,
Or a mouse outside the gate.

Climbing up the carpet tree,
Looking very proud and free.
Swishing tail from left to right,
Playing in the morning light.

Softly stepping on the floor,
Pawing at the wooden door.
Wanting out to see the day,
Ready for a game to play.

Happy cat so full of fun,
Resting in the golden sun.

rhymes.title: The Midnight Prowl
rhymes.text:
Black cat walking in the dark,
Passing by the quiet park.
Green eyes shining bright and clear,
Nothing does a kitty fear.

Jumping up upon the chair,
Making cute and funny air.
Rubbing softly on my knee,
Purring happy as can be.

Drinking milk from little bowl,
Stealing straight into my soul.
Curled up in a furry ring,
Like a precious little king.

Time to sleep and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: The Little Kitty
rhymes.text:
See the little fluffy cat,
Sleeping on the welcome mat.
When she wakes she likes to play,
Chasing little bugs away.

Soft paws walking on the floor,
Waiting by the kitchen door.
Purring loud for all to hear,
Bringing cozy snuggles near.

Climbing up the scratching post,
She is what I love the most.
Curling in a fuzzy ball,
Happiest cat of them all.

Now the sleepy cat says goodnight,
Moon is shining big and bright.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little kitty, you're the best.

rhymes.title: Five Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Whiskers twitching in the sun,
Kitty wants to have some fun.
Jumping up to catch a string,
Happy kitty starts to sing.

Pouncing softly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Running fast across the rug,
Needing just a gentle hug.

Soft white tummy, ears so small,
Walking down the hallway hall.
Chasing feathers in the air,
Leaping over every chair.

Now the playtime game is done,
Kitty had a lot of fun.
Time to curl up in a bed,
Resting fuzzy little head.

rhymes.title: Paws and Purrs
rhymes.text:
Little kitten, sweet and small,
Playing with a bouncy ball.
Green eyes shining bright and clear,
Glad that you are living here.

Rubbing softly on my knee,
As happy as a cat can be.
Drinking milk from little bowl,
You have won my whole heart's goal.

Climbing up the sofa high,
Watching birds fly in the sky.
Curling up to take a nap,
Sleeping safely in my lap.

Dreaming of a mouse or toy,
Filled with peace and kitty joy.
When you wake we'll play some more,
Happiest kitty on the floor.

rhymes.title: Little Paws
rhymes.text:
Little cat with whiskers white,
Walking softly through the night.
Soft paws make a patter sound,
Hopping gently on the ground.

Time to play a little game,
Calling softly by your name.
Chase the ball across the floor,
Then come resting by the door.

Curled up like a fuzzy ball,
Sleeping by the garden wall.
Dreaming of a saucer treat,
Curling up your little feet.

Now the morning sun is bright,
Kitty wakes with pure delight.
Time to stretch and time to run,
Playing underneath the sun.

rhymes.title: Soft and Sweet
rhymes.text:
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you see?
A little brown bird in the green leafy tree.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you do?
Purring a song that is happy for you.

Soft little ears and a pink little nose,
Warming the tips of your velvety toes.
Jumping up high to catch at the string,
Happy to play and to dance and to sing.

Drinking your milk from a shiny blue bowl,
Guarding your toys with a gentle sweet soul.
Climbing up high on the sofa to rest,
Knowing your home is the place you love best.

Closing your eyes as the evening draws near,
Feeling so cozy and safe, little dear.
Dreaming of mice that are made out of yarn,
Sleeping so soundly away from the barn.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Air
rhymes.text:
Fluffy tail and shiny eyes,
Jumping up to reach the skies.
Batting at a ribbon red,
Ready now to jump in bed.

Soft purrs rumble in your chest,
Sleeping is what you do best.
Curled up in a sunny spot,
Happy with the warmth you've got.

Wake up now and stretch so wide,
Hide away and look for hide.
Pouncing on a fuzzy mouse,
Running all around the house.

Time to wash your furry face,
Sitting in your favorite place.
Good-bye kitty, time for sleep,
Counting stars that shine so deep.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Kitty
rhymes.text:
Little kitty on the rug,
Sleeping tight and feeling snug.
Curled up in a furry ball,
Not a single worry at all.

Soft white paws and whiskers long,
Humming out a sleepy song.
Purring loud and purring low,
Watching golden sunbeams glow.

Now the kitty starts to yawn,
Waiting for the early dawn.
Closing up two big green eyes,
Dreaming of the butterfly skies.

Time to rest your tired head,
In your warm and cozy bed.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little kitty, sleep tight, tight.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Paws
rhymes.text:
Pitter patter on the floor,
Kitty runs to reach the door.
Bouncing here and bouncing there,
Leaping high up in the air.

Chasing after balls of string,
Happy as a bird can sing.
Soft fur brushing on my knee,
Playing games with little me.

Stretching out both arms and legs,
Begging for some kitty treats.
Climbing up the scratching post,
Loving tummy rubs the most.

Now the playtime fun is done,
Kitty had a lot of sun.
Time to curl up on my lap,
Taking such a nice long nap.

rhymes.title: Three Little Kittens
rhymes.text:
Three little kittens playing in the sun,
Having lots and lots of fun.
One chases butterflies of blue,
One says meow to me and you.

Third little kitty gives a leap,
Now she is so fast asleep.
Soft little tails that wiggle round,
Making not a single sound.

Paws so soft and ears so small,
Cutest kitties of them all.
Climbing up the sofa chair,
Looking at us sitting there.

Now the stars are in the sky,
Little moon is floating high.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Kitty sleep is the very best.

rhymes.title: Little Kitty Paws
rhymes.text:
Little kitty, soft and sweet,
Walking on your tiny feet.
Chasing bugs across the floor,
Then you nap beside the door.

Pointy ears and whiskers long,
Singing out your purring song.
Curled up in a furry ball,
You are fuzzy, best of all.

Soft gray fur and shining eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.
Stretching out your legs so wide,
Where do you plan now to hide?

Time for bed and time to rest,
Sleeping is what you do best.
Goodnight kitty, sleep till dawn,
When you wake, you'll start to yawn.

rhymes.title: The Playful Cat
rhymes.text:
See the kitty jump and play,
Chasing shadows all the day.
Bouncing high upon the rug,
Giving me a cozy hug.

Swishing tail from side to side,
Running fast and far and wide.
Pouncing on a ball of yarn,
Running quickly to the barn.

Climbing up the maple tree,
Looking down to summon me.
Softly meowing in the breeze,
Hiding underneath the leaves.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the quiet town.
Rest your paws and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Kitty Cat, Kitty Cat
rhymes.text:
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you see?
A little brown bird in the old green tree.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you hear?
A buzzing green fly that is flying quite near.

Kitty cat, kitty cat, where do you go?
Walking in gardens where flowers all grow.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, what do you do?
Chasing bright butterflies out in the blue.

Kitty cat, kitty cat, time for a nap,
Curling right up in a warm cozy lap.
Kitty cat, kitty cat, breathing so deep,
Drifting away in a wonderful sleep.

Soft little purrs as you dream of your toys,
Far away now from the loud little noise.
Dream of the sunshine and dream of your milk,
Wrapped in a blanket of softest pink silk.

stories.title: Bunny's Big Red Carrot
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy green meadow, lived a little white rabbit named Pip. Pip had two long, floppy ears and a twitchy pink nose. Every morning, Pip would hop out of his warm burrow and wiggle his nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff. What did he smell? Breakfast! Today, Pip wanted something very special for breakfast. He wanted the biggest, crunchiest, reddest carrot in the whole garden. Pip hopped, hop, hop, hop, all the way to the vegetable patch. There it was! Jutting out of the dark brown dirt was the greenest top of a carrot. Pip grabbed the green leaves with his tiny paws. He pulled back with all his might. He pulled with his left paw. He pulled with his right paw. He planted his fluffy feet firmly on the ground and tugged. One, two, three, PULL! Pop! The carrot came right out of the ground, and Pip tumbled backward onto his soft, fuzzy bottom. Oh, what a wonderful carrot it was! It was as big as Pip himself. Pip dusted off his furry tummy and smiled a big bunny smile. He rolled the giant carrot all the way home to his burrow. When he got inside, he washed his paws and sat down at his tiny wooden table. Crunch, crunch, crunch went Pip as he took big bites of the sweet, juicy carrot. It tasted even better than he had imagined. Eating healthy vegetables gave Pip so much energy. He felt strong and happy. When his tummy was full and round, Pip gave a big, sleepy yawn. He curled up in his soft bed of clover leaves and closed his eyes. Dreaming of more adventures, Pip the rabbit fell fast asleep. Good night, little carrot-eater. Good night, Pip.

stories.title: Pip's Hoppy Day
