He closed his brown eyes and let out a soft, contented sigh. 'Goodnight, world,' whispered Barnaby. The stars twinkled in the dark night sky, keeping watch over the sleepy little bunny as he drifted off into a sweet and peaceful dreamland.

stories.title: Bunny's Big Red Carrot
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy green meadow, lived a little fluffy rabbit named Barnaby. Barnaby had very long ears, a twitchy little pink nose, and a fluffy cotton-tail that wiggled whenever he was happy. Today, Barnaby was very, very happy because it was morning time, and morning time meant breakfast! Barnaby hopped out of his warm burrow and bounced right into his vegetable garden. Hop, hop, hop! Jump, jump, jump! He looked left. He looked right. And what do you think he saw? Right in the middle of the garden patch sat the biggest, roundest, brightest red carrot in the whole wide world! It was even bigger than Barnaby's paws. Barnaby squeaked with joy. He rubbed his tummy. He wiggled his nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff! It smelled so sweet and yummy. Barnaby knew just what to do. He reached out his fuzzy paws and grabbed the leafy green top of the carrot. He pulled with all his might. He pulled to the left. He pulled to the right. He planted his little back feet deep into the dirt and tugged again. Oh, oh, oh! The big red carrot did not move at all. It was stuck tight in the ground. Barnaby did not give up. He took a deep breath. He puffed out his furry chest. He sang a little bunny song. Then, he gave one giant, super-duper pull! Pop! The big red carrot came loose, and Barnaby tumbled backward into a soft patch of clover. Whoops-a-daisy! Barnaby giggled and sat right up. He held his giant prize high in the air. He decided to share his wonderful red carrot with all his forest friends. First, he shared a crunchy bite with Bella Bird. Then, he shared a sweet nibble with Sammy Squirrel. And finally, Barnaby ate the very best part all by himself. His tummy was full, his heart was happy, and he was ready for a nice long nap in the sun. The end.

stories.title: Hop, Hop, Little Bunny
stories.text: Down by the big blue pond, where the tall green grass swayed in the gentle breeze, lived a sweet little rabbit named Pip. Pip had soft white fur that felt just like a marshmallow and two big ears that listened to all the sounds of the forest. Every single morning, Pip loved to play his favorite game. Can you guess what it was? It was the Happy Hop Game! Pip would stretch his front paws way up high, bend his knees way down low, and shout, 'Hop, hop, hop!' Off he would go, bounding over tiny pebbles, leaping across small puddles of rain, and dancing through fields of yellow dandelions. As Pip hopped along the sunny path, he met his friend Oliver Owl sitting in an oak tree. 'Good morning, Pip!' hooted Oliver Owl. 'Where are you hopping to today?' Pip stopped, wiggled his pink nose, and smiled. 'I am hopping to find my favorite bouncing rock!' he replied cheerfully. 'Would you like to come and play?' Oliver Owl shook his head with a sleepy smile. 'No thank you, little Pip, I am too sleepy today, but I will watch you play from up here.' So Pip continued on his joyful journey. Hop, hop, hop went his little feet. He reached the big gray bouncing rock just near the edge of the woods. Pip climbed right up on top and looked out at the wide world. He saw buzzing bees, fluttering butterflies, and sparkling water. Pip felt so grateful for his strong little legs. He decided to do ten extra-special jumps just for fun. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! With a final huge leap, Pip landed softly in a bed of moss. He curled up into a little furry ball, closed his sleepy eyes, and dreamed about tomorrow's big adventure. The end.

stories.title: The Sleepy Bunny's Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking behind the hills, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink, purple, and gold. High up in her cozy burrow, a little brown rabbit named Clover was getting ready for bed. Clover had been running and jumping all day long, and now her little paws felt very, very tired. Her mama rabbit fluffed up her bed of soft green moss and dry autumn leaves. 'Time to wind down, my sweet little bunny,' said Mama Rabbit softly. Clover yawned a big, wide yawn. Ahhh-choo! No, that wasn't a sneeze, just a sleepy little sigh. Clover snuggled deep into her warm bed. But wait! Where was her favorite bedtime toy? It was her fuzzy blue blankie! Clover sat right back up and looked around. She sniffed the air. She twitched her little pink nose. Ah, there it was, tucked right underneath a big wooden root. Clover crawled over, grabbed her fuzzy blue blankie in her teeth, and dragged it back to her cozy spot. She wrapped it tightly around her shoulders just like a warm hug. Mama Rabbit sat beside her and gently stroked her long brown ears. 'Let's count the stars together, Clover,' whispered Mama. They looked out the round doorway of the burrow at the darkening night sky. One bright star winked. Two bright stars winked. Three bright stars winked. Clover's eyelids felt as heavy as stones. She gave her mama a warm, sleepy cuddle. Her tummy was full of fresh clover leaves, her blanket was soft, and the night was peaceful and quiet. Clover closed her eyes tight and drifted off into a sweet, wonderful sleep, dreaming of green meadows and bouncing high into the starry clouds. Goodnight, little bunny. Goodnight, sweet dreams.

stories.title: Bunny's Big Red Carrot
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy little burrow under a big green hill, lived a very fluffy little bunny named Barnaby. Barnaby had two long, floppy ears that wiggled whenever he was happy. Today, Barnaby was extra happy because the sun was shining, and it was a wonderful day for a garden adventure! Barnaby hopped out of his warm bed, gave a little stretch, and twitch-twitched his pink nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff! What could that delicious smell be? It smelled sweet, and earthy, and oh-so-yummy! Barnaby followed his twitchy nose all the way to the edge of the vegetable patch. There, peeking out from the rich brown dirt, was the biggest, reddest carrot he had ever seen in his whole life! It was a giant carrot with bright green leafy hair. Barnaby clapped his little paws together with glee. Oh boy! This was going to be a grand feast! But there was a tiny problem. The big red carrot was stuck fast in the ground. Barnaby grabbed the green leafy top with his teeth and pulled. He pulled with all his might! He pulled so hard his little back paws left the ground, but the carrot did not budge even a tiny bit. Oh no! Barnaby sat down and patted his tummy, thinking hard. How could he get the carrot out? Just then, his good friend Bella the butterfly fluttered by. "Need some help, Barnaby?" she asked cheerfully. Barnaby nodded his head up and down very fast. Together, they made a fantastic team. Bella cheered, "One, two, three, tug!" Barnaby pulled back with everything he had. POP! The big red carrot came right out of the dirt, and Barnaby tumbled backward with a funny little roll. Wheeee! They did it! Barnaby sat up, brushed the dirt off his furry nose, and giggled. He invited Bella to share a delicious bite of the crunchy carrot. It was the sweetest, most wonderful carrot ever, and Barnaby knew that sharing with a friend made everything twice as fun. As the afternoon sun began to dip low in the sky, Barnaby gave a sleepy yawn, rubbed his eyes, and hopped happily back to his cozy burrow, dreaming of his next big garden adventure.

stories.title: Hop, Skip, and Jump
stories.text: Down by the edge of the whispering blue river, where the soft green grass tickled little bellies, lived a little white bunny named Pip. Pip had the fluffiest tail that looked just like a puff of cotton candy. Pip loved to move! Sitting still was simply not much fun when there was a whole wide world to explore. Every morning, Pip would wake up, wiggle his whiskers, and announce to the morning dew, "Today is a hop, skip, and jump kind of day!" First came the hop. Pip would bend his knees, coil up like a spring, and BOING! Up into the air he would go, landing softly with a little thud on the padded moss. One hop, two hops, three hops high, touching the bright blue morning sky! Next came the skip. Pip would skip around the big oak tree, left paw, right paw, dancing a happy little rabbit jig while the tiny ladybugs watched from the clover leaves. But his very favorite thing of all was the big jump. Right across the bubbling brook sat a smooth, shiny stepping stone. Pip lined up his toes, took a deep breath, and leaped across the water with a joyful squeak! SPLASH? No, no splashes today! Pip landed safely on the other side, right in a patch of golden buttercups. He gave a little happy wiggle of his cotton-tail and looked around. Who should be hiding behind a fern but Sammy the snail? Sammy poked out his slow little head and smiled. "Good morning, Pip! You are jumping so high today!" Pip did a happy little spin. "Want to jump with me, Sammy?" Sammy giggled slowly, "I am much too slow for jumping, Pip, but I can cheer for you!" So Pip hopped and skipped and jumped all afternoon long, practicing his grandest leaps while Sammy cheered him on. When the stars began to twinkle like diamonds in the evening velvet, Pip was wonderfully tired. He curled up in his soft bed of clover, his tummy full of fresh grass, knowing that tomorrow would bring a whole new set of hops, skips, and jumps.

stories.title: The Sleepy Little Bunny
stories.text: The sun was sinking slowly behind the rolling green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of peach, lavender, and pink. It was almost bedtime in the meadow, and all the little animals were getting ready for sleep. Inside a cozy burrow tucked beneath the roots of an old willow tree, little bunny Clover was getting ready for bed too. But Clover was not sleepy at all! Her eyes were wide open, and her ears were perked up high. "Not tired yet, Mama," Clover whispered, giving her nose a little twitch. Mama Bunny smiled gently and wrapped a soft, warm knitted blanket around Clover's shoulders. "Let us look out the door, little one, and say goodnight to the world," Mama whispered softly. Together, they peeked out of their burrow. First, they saw the yellow moon rising high and bright in the sky, looking like a glowing slice of melon. "Goodnight, moon," whispered Clover, giving a gentle wave of her paw. Next, they saw a little brown owl blinking its big round eyes from a high branch. "Goodnight, owl," whispered Clover. They watched a tiny firefly dance past their door, glowing with a warm, friendly light. "Goodnight, firefly," Clover murmured, her voice sounding a little bit softer and a little bit slower. A gentle evening breeze rustled the clover leaves outside, singing a sleepy lullaby through the grass. Shhh, shhh, whispered the wind. Clover let out a very big, very long yawn. Oh, her eyelids felt so heavy, like they had little weights attached to them. The big wide world was growing quiet and still. Mama Bunny pulled Clover close, rocking her softly from side to side. "Time to dream sweet dreams, my little bunny," Mama cooed. Clover rested her fluffy head on Mama's warm shoulder, closed her eyes tight, and let out a happy sigh. She was safe, she was warm, and she was dearly loved. The stars watched over her as she drifted off to sleep, dreaming of green meadows, sweet carrots, and floating on clouds of fluffy white cotton.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, soft and white,
Hops around with all his might.
Twitch your nose and shake your ears,
Chasing off all sleepy fears.

Jump up high into the air,
Bounce around without a care.
Land upon your fuzzy feet,
Having such a joyful treat.

Nibble on a carrot green,
Bestest bunny ever seen.
Now it is time to go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Wait for lovely, brand new day.
Dream of fields of clover sweet,
Rest your tired, hopping feet.

rhymes.title: Five Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little rabbit starts to play,
Hops around the meadow all the day.
Two little rabbits join the fun,
Basking in the golden sun.

Three little rabbits skip and bound,
Happy footsteps on the ground.
Four little rabbits twitch a nose,
Tickling all their little toes.

Five little rabbits find a tree,
Sitting down so safe and free.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Burrow is the very best.

Softly now they close their eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Sweet little bunnies fast asleep,
While the silver moonbeams creep.

rhymes.title: Fluffy Tail
rhymes.text:
Bunny has a fluffy tail,
Looking just like snowy sail.
Wiggles left and wiggles right,
Dancing in the morning light.

Hops across the garden green,
Pronounced the cutest ever seen.
Finds a clover on the floor,
Wants to find a whole lot more.

Ears go floppy, up and down,
Happiest rabbit in the town.
Runs away to play a game,
Calling out a merry name.

Now the sun is going low,
Time for little bunny's show.
Snuggle in the bed so deep,
Sleepy bunny falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Nose
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, twitch your nose,
Jump up high upon your toes.
Hop around the garden green,
Best little hopper I have seen.
Long soft ears of fuzzy white,
Playing in the morning light.
Find a carrot, big and sweet,
Such a yummy rabbit treat.
Nibble, nibble, go the teeth,
Sitting on the grass beneath.
Now you curl up on the floor,
Ready for a nap and more.
Close your sleepy eyes so deep,
Little bunny falls asleep.
Sweetest dreams until the dawn,
While the stars are shining on.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Bunny
rhymes.text:
Hop, little bunny, hop, hop, hop,
When I say go, you must not stop.
Jump to the left, jump to the right,
Fur is so fluffy, eyes are so bright.
Wiggle your tail, say hello,
Where are you going, where will you go?
Under the bush and over the stone,
Making the meadow feel like a home.
Smell the flowers, sweet and red,
Time to jump back to your bed.
Stretch your paws and give a yawn,
Greeting the cheerful, happy dawn.
Now you rest your furry head,
Tucked so cozy in your bed.
Sleep well, bunny, through the night,
Till the morning sun shines bright.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little bunny looking for a friend,
Hopping down the path that has no end.
Two little ears bouncing in the breeze,
Hiding underneath the apple trees.
Three fuzzy tails shaking all around,
Happy little paws upon the ground.
Four sunny daisies growing in a row,
Where the softest summer breezes blow.
Five little carrots pulling from the dirt,
Not a single bunny getting hurt.
Six happy jumps up into the sky,
Watching little birds go flying by.
Seven sweet nibbles of a clover leaf,
Bringing happy joy and sweet relief.
Eight cozy yawns when the day is done,
Sleeping through the setting of the sun.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Nose
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, twitch your nose,
Wiggle all your tiny toes.
Hop across the garden green,
Best little rabbit ever seen.

Find a carrot, big and sweet,
Such a yummy, crunchy treat.
Munch it slowly, one, two, three,
Happy as a bunny can be.

Jump up high into the air,
Bounce around without a care.
Soft fur and a cotton tail,
Never, ever feeling frail.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to snuggle in your bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bunnies
rhymes.text:
Five little bunnies hopping on the floor,
One jumped away and then there were four.
Four little bunnies happy and so free,
One climbed up to sit beneath a tree.

Three little bunnies playing in the sun,
Running and jumping, having so much fun.
Two little bunnies twitching up their ears,
Chasing away all their little fears.

One little bunny left all alone,
Decided it was time to trot back home.
Hopping along the path so bright and gay,
Ending a wonderful and busy day.

Now the stars are shining in the sky,
Little bunny resting close and high.
Dreaming of the morning light so new,
Sleeping tight until the day is through.

rhymes.title: Bunny's Big Long Ears
rhymes.text:
Bunny has two ears so long,
Listening to a robin's song.
Soft and floppy, pink and sweet,
From his head down to his feet.

Running fast across the lane,
Happy that it does not rain.
Jumping over sticks and stones,
Far away from sleepy zones.

Stopping by a patch of clover,
Looking all the wide world over.
Finding flowers bright and red,
Nodding down his sleepy head.

Time to cuddle in the hay,
Resting after joyful play.
Whisper soft and whisper low,
Sleep well, bunny, time to go.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Ears
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
With a twitchy little nose,
Down from head unto his toes.
Fluffy tail so soft and white,
Hopping in the morning light.
Looking for a leafy treat,
Using two big furry feet.
Crunching on a carrot red,
Hopping back into his bed.
Long soft ears that flop around,
Making not a single sound.
Snuggle close and go to sleep,
While the stars begin to peep.
Dreaming of the meadow green,
Best little bunny ever seen.

rhymes.title: Five Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little bunny looking for some fun,
Bouncing in the golden sun.
Two little bunnies jump across the floor,
Knocking softly on the door.
Three little bunnies wiggle up their ears,
Chasing all away their fears.
Four little bunnies munch upon some hay,
Playing games throughout the day.
Five little bunnies curl up in a nest,
Time to take a little rest.
Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
Now the bunny falls asleep.
Dreaming of a carrot patch,
Waiting for the sun to catch.
Goodnight bunny, time for bed,
Rest your little fuzzy head.

rhymes.title: The Bunny Hop Dance
rhymes.text:
Tap your feet upon the ground,
Spinning slowly all around.
Jump up high and touch the air,
Like a bunny sitting there.
Wiggle, wiggle goes your nose,
From your head down to your toes.
Flap your arms just like big ears,
Cheering loud with happy cheers.
Now we crouch down very low,
Ready, steady, here we go!
Hop, hop, hop across the floor,
Let us do it onceing more.
Sit right down and hug your knees,
Resting quietly, if you please.
Now the little dance is done,
Wasn't that so much fun?

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Foo Foo
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Wiggles nose and wiggles toes,
That is where the bunny goes.

Soft white fur and fluffy tail,
Hopping down the garden trail.
Finds a carrot in the dirt,
Wearing his new yellow shirt.

Jumping over sticks and stones,
Looking for some crunchy cones.
Now the sun begins to fade,
Resting in the leafy shade.

Time to sleep and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Bunny rabbit, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little bunny wakes from bed,
Puts a flower on his head.
Two little bunnies start to play,
Chasing butterflies away.

Three little bunnies sniff the air,
Smelling clovers everywhere.
Four little bunnies jump and run,
Basking in the golden sun.

Five little bunnies wiggle ears,
Listen closely for new cheers.
Six little bunnies find a hill,
Sitting very, very still.

Seven little bunnies hop so fast,
Making sure they have a blast.
Eight little bunnies start to chew,
Eating yummy lettuce too.

Nine little bunnies yawn and sigh,
Watching clouds go floating by.
Ten little bunnies fall asleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.

rhymes.title: The Fuzzy Cottontail
rhymes.text:
See the bunny soft and sweet,
Hopping on his furry feet.
Ears are long and pink and wide,
With a little puff inside.

Jumping fast and jumping slow,
Where he goes, we do not know.
Stopping by a garden wall,
Answering the robin's call.

Digging in the rich brown mold,
Finding treasures bright and old.
Nibbling on a clover leaf,
Free from worry, free from grief.

Now the evening breeze is chill,
Silence falls upon the hill.
Curled up in his little bed,
Resting now his sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Foo Foo
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hopping fast,
Saw a shiny flower past.
Up he jumped into the air,
Looking at a fuzzy bear.

Twitchy nose and fluffy tail,
Sitting by a wooden pail.
Nibbling on a carrot sweet,
Such a happy little treat.

Now the sun is going down,
Quiet shadows wrap the town.
Ears go floppy, eyes grow deep,
Time for bunny fast asleep.

Stars are shining bright above,
Wrapped in warmth and cozy love.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your comfy little bed.

rhymes.title: Hop Little Rabbit
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop, go round and round,
Little paws upon the ground.
Jump, jump, jump into the sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.

Wiggle ears both left and right,
In the warm and golden light.
Find a clover green and sweet,
Wonderful for bunny feet.

Run along the garden path,
Time to take a bubbly bath.
Dry your fur so soft and white,
Everything is feeling right.

Now the moon is glowing clear,
Whispering a tune to hear.
Sleepy bunny, time to rest,
In your safe and happy nest.

rhymes.title: The Fuzzy White Bunny
rhymes.text:
See the bunny white and neat,
Dancing on his little feet.
Scrambling through the garden green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.

Sniffing at a yellow rose,
Tickling his pinkish nose.
Digging in the rich brown dirt,
Not a single paw is hurt.

Time to bounce and time to play,
Happy through the sunny day.
Chasing butterflies that fly,
Reaching up so very high.

Now the evening breeze is cool,
Sitting by the quiet pool.
Dreaming till the morning sun,
Bringing days of brand new fun.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, hop, hop, hop,
Jump across and never stop.
Wiggle ears up in the air,
Show them everywhere, so fair.

Little bunny, twitch your nose,
Smell the flower as it grows.
Find a carrot, sweet and red,
Time to munch before your bed.

Little bunny, thump your feet,
Life is happy, life is sweet.
Curl up in your cozy nest,
Little bunny, time to rest.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Wait for sunrise and new play.

rhymes.title: Five Fuzzy Friends
rhymes.text:
One white bunny sitting in the sun,
Wiggling his nose, having lots of fun.
Two floppy ears standing very tall,
Listening to the robin's morning call.

Three furry paws jumping up so high,
Reaching for a cloud in the blue sky.
Four bouncy hops all around the tree,
Happy as can be, wild and free.

Five little carrots hidden in the ground,
Bunny looks around, safe and safe and sound.
Gives a happy wiggle and a joyful cheer,
Glad to have his fuzzy friends so near.

Now the stars are shining in the night,
Hugging mommy bunny till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Hop to the Moon
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, bunny dear,
Springtime is at last here.
Jump high off the green grass,
Watch the fluffy clouds pass.

Little tail is round and white,
Running through the soft moonlight.
Find a clover on the ground,
Make a happy little sound.

Twitch your whiskers left and right,
Hide away out of sight.
Soon the stars will start to glow,
Rest your little head below.

Dreaming of a carrot patch,
Sweetest dreams you'll ever catch.
Sleepy bunny, time to doze,
Resting up your pinkish nose.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Foo Foo
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Wiggles nose and wiggles toes,
Where he goes, nobody knows.

Ears are long and soft and white,
Hopping in the morning light.
Nibble, nibble on the grass,
Watch the fluffy rabbit pass.

Soft and sweet and full of fun,
Basking in the golden sun.
Now he takes a little leap,
Soon the bunny falls asleep.

Dreaming of a carrot treat,
With his tiny fuzzy feet.
Night is here, the stars awake,
Sleeping for the morning's sake.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bunnies
rhymes.text:
One little bunny looking for a friend,
Hopping down the pathway to the bend.
Two little bunnies twitching up their nose,
Finding pretty flowers where the clover grows.

Three little bunnies jumping in the sun,
Having lots of laughter and so much fun.
Four little bunnies hiding in the hay,
Playing games together all through the day.

Five little bunnies snuggling up so tight,
Saying to each other, sleep well and goodnight.
Now the moon is shining up above the trees,
Whispering a lullaby inside the breeze.

Close your sleepy eyes and rest your furry head,
Tucked into your cozy little rabbit bed.
Dreaming happy dreams until the morning light,
Little bunny babies, sleep so well tonight.

rhymes.title: Hop Little Rabbit
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop goes the bunny fast,
Running through the meadow at the last.
Big brown eyes and fluffy little tail,
Running down the winding grassy trail.

Crunch, crunch, crunch goes the yummy snack,
Carrots in a row inside his pack.
Long gray ears that listen to the sound,
Of the gentle raindrops falling to the ground.

Soft and warm upon the forest floor,
Hop around and then you hop some more.
Now the sun is sinking in the west,
Time for little bunnies to take a rest.

Curl up in the burrow out of sight,
Sleeping safely through the starry night.
Morning comes and brings another day,
Time for little bunnies to hop and play.

rhymes.title: Little White Bunny
rhymes.text:
Little white bunny hops all around,
Jump, jump, jumping up from the ground.
Long floppy ears and a twitchy pink nose,
Dancing along with his wiggle-wag toes.
He finds a green leaf and takes a big bite,
Chewing it slowly in afternoon light.
Then he curls up in his cozy warm bed,
Resting his tired and sleepy small head.
Stars twinkle brightly high up in the sky,
Watching the bunny as dreams flutter by.
Morning will come with the sun shining deep,
While the little rabbit is fast-asleep.
Wake up, dear bunny, the meadow is green,
The prettiest place that you ever have seen.
Hop to the left and then hop to the right,
Playing and laughing until the dark night.

rhymes.title: Five Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little rabbit looking for a snack,
Found a bright carrot behind a old stack.
Two little rabbits playing in the sun,
Hopping together and having great fun.
Three little rabbits sniffing at a rose,
Tickling their whiskers and each little nose.
Four little rabbits running down the lane,
Happy that there is no wind or no rain.
Five little rabbits jumping in the grass,
Watching the fluffy white clouds softly pass.
Now they are tired and ready to rest,
Snuggling close in a warm bunny nest.
Close your sweet eyes as the shadows fall low,
Dreaming of fields where the sweet flowers grow.
Goodnight, sweet rabbits, until the new day,
When you will wake up and bounce all away.

rhymes.title: The Cotton Tail
rhymes.text:
Fluffy the bunny has a tail of white,
Dancing around in the soft morning light.
He wiggle-wiggles his nose at a bee,
Then takes a leap by the big apple tree.
He loves to nibble on clover so sweet,
Using his paws as a knife and a fork-plate-seat.
Over the log and right under the gate,
Hurry up, bunny, or you will be late!
Your friends are waiting to play in the park,
Running and jumping before it gets dark.
Now the sun sets in a beautiful red,
Time for the bunny to go into bed.
Pull up the blankets and tuck in your toes,
Resting your little and twitchy pink nose.
Sleep through the night till the morning is here,
Bringing new joy to the meadow, my dear.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, soft and white,
Hopping in the morning light.
Twitch your nose and shake your tail,
Running down the grassy trail.

Jump up high into the air,
Bounce around without a care.
Find a carrot, sweet and red,
Time to munch and time to fed.

Now the sun is going down,
Leaving shadows on the town.
Fold your ears and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

Dream of clover, green and sweet,
Rest your tired furry feet.
Sleep until the morning sun,
Ready for another run.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bunnies
rhymes.text:
One little bunny bouncing on the floor,
Two little bunnies running out the door.
Three little bunnies chewing on a leaf,
Four little bunnies hiding underneath.

Five little bunnies hopping in the sun,
Look at them go, having so much fun!
Big ears wiggle, fluffy tails do shake,
Eating all the yummy garden cake.

Now they stop and listen to the breeze,
Whispering a secret through the trees.
Time to cuddle in a cozy nest,
Every little bunny needs some rest.

Snuggle close and shut your sleepy eyes,
While the moon is shining in the skies.
Goodnight bunnies, sleeping all the night,
Till the morning brings a sunny light.

rhymes.title: Bunny's Garden Patch
rhymes.text:
In the garden green and wide,
Little rabbit likes to hide.
Behind the cabbage, big and round,
Making not a single sound.

Sniff the air and wiggle nose,
Hopping on his tippy toes.
Digging holes in yummy dirt,
Wearing not a single shirt.

Finds a parsley, fresh and green,
Freshest rabbit ever seen.
Chomp and chew and take a bite,
Eating till the morning light.

Now his tummy is so full,
Tired of the garden pull.
Hops away to go to bed,
Resting down his sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Foo Foo
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Wiggling nose and furry toes,
Where he goes, nobody knows.

Ears so long and soft and white,
Hopping through the starry night.
Finding clover on the ground,
Making not a single sound.

Now he stops to take a look,
Reading in his picture book.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
Tucked inside his cozy bed.

Goodnight, bunny, sleep till morn,
Where the golden light is born.
Dream of carrots sweet and red,
Resting softly in your bed.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Hops
rhymes.text:
One little rabbit wants to play,
Hopping down the garden way.
Two little ears go flop, flop, flop,
Never wanting they should stop.

Three little whiskers twitch so neat,
Four fuzzy pads upon his feet.
Five little carrots bright and sweet,
Make a yummy rabbit treat.

Six little jumps across the stone,
In the meadow all alone.
Seven soft paws of fluffy gray,
Dancing through the sunny day.

Eight happy bounds up in the air,
Jumping high without a care.
Nine little dreams of sleep so deep,
Ten little bunnies fall asleep.

rhymes.title: The Bunny Dance
rhymes.text:
See the bunny hop, hop, hop,
Watch him go and never stop.
Flop his ears from side to side,
Running fast and running wide.

Twitch his nose and blink his eyes,
Looking for a sweet surprise.
Green grass tickles little feet,
Making every moment sweet.

Now he hides behind a tree,
Playing games for you and me.
Peek-a-boo, I see you there,
Sitting in your grassy chair.

Time to give a little wave,
Little bunny bold and brave.
Curl up tight and close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Little bunny drops down low,
Watching lovely flowers grow.
Twitch your nose and shake your tail,
Hopping down the grassy trail.
Find a carrot, sweet and bright,
Nibble, nibble through the night.
Soft fur and two floppy ears,
Chasing all away our fears.
Jump around and skip and play,
Running through the sunny day.
Now it's time to go to bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
Dreams of carrots, rich and deep.

rhymes.title: Hop, Bunny, Hop
rhymes.text:
See the bunny jump and spring,
Hear the little robins sing.
Hopping fast and hopping slow,
Where do little rabbits go?
Underneath the garden gate,
Never stopping, never late.
Eating lettuce, green and sweet,
Such a yummy, tasty treat.
Fluffy tail and twitching nose,
Softly walking on his toes.
Jump up high upon the grass,
Watch the sunny hours pass.
Time to rest your tired feet,
Find a cozy, safe retreat.
Curl up tight upon the floor,
Bunny sleeping, snorin' more.

rhymes.title: The Cotton Tail
rhymes.text:
Bunny has a coat of white,
Dancing in the morning light.
Bouncing over every stone,
In the meadow all alone.
Long green ears that wiggle round,
Listening to every sound.
Thump your foot upon the ground,
See how fast you can go round.
Little paws that softly tread,
Hopping to a clover bed.
Smelling flowers in the breeze,
Underneath the shady trees.
Play all day until it's night,
Stars are shining big and bright.
Hug your pillow, close your eyes,
Till the morning sun shall rise.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, soft and white,
Hops around with all his might.
Wiggles nose and wiggles toes,
Where he goes, nobody knows.
Long floppy ears up in the air,
Jumping here and jumping there.
Finds a carrot, orange and sweet,
Takes a little yummy eat.
Chews it slowly, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Eating up his healthy lunch.
Now he's tired, time to rest,
Burrow is the very best.
Curls up in his cozy bed,
Sleepy paws and sleepy head.
Close your eyes and say goodnight,
Little bunny, soft and white.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bunnies
rhymes.text:
Five little bunnies sitting in the sun,
Ready for a day of jumping and of fun.
First little bunny jumps up high,
Reaching for the big blue sky.
Second little bunny wiggles his nose,
Tickling his fuzzy little toes.
Third little bunny digs a hole in the ground,
Looking for a treasure that can be found.
Fourth little bunny gives a happy squeak,
Playing hide-and-seek for a full week.
Fifth little bunny yawns a sleepy yawn,
Waiting for the coming of the dawn.
Now the sun is setting in the west,
All the little bunnies need a little rest.
Snuggle in the blankets nice and tight,
Saying to each other, sleep well, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Bunny's Garden
rhymes.text:
In the garden green and bright,
Lives a bunny small and light.
He loves to hop upon the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.
He finds a flower growing red,
Right beside his clover bed.
Sniffs it gently, what a smell!
He loves his garden home so well.
Now he does a little dance,
Given half a happy chance.
Flapping ears and twitching tail,
Never wanting to look pale.
Soon the stars begin to glow,
Shining softly down below.
Bunny curls up on the floor,
Sleeps until the morning roar.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, soft and white,
Hopping through the morning light.
Twitch your nose and shake your tail,
Running down the grassy trail.

Jump up high into the air,
Bounce around without a care.
Find a carrot, big and red,
Then you munch it in your bed.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Tucked inside your cozy bed.

Dream of fields of clover green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.
Good-night bunny, sleep till morn,
Rest until another dawn.

rhymes.title: Five Little Hoppers
rhymes.text:
One little bunny looking for a treat,
Hopping on his furry little feet.
Two little bunnies playing in the sun,
Having lots and lots of joyful fun.

Three little bunnies nibbling on the grass,
Watching all the puffy clouds go past.
Four little bunnies hiding in a tree,
Playing games of happy hide-and-see.

Five little bunnies ready for a nap,
Curling up in cozy velvet wrap.
Snuggle close and shut your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the sparkling starry skies.

Morning comes with sunshine very bright,
Chasing all the shadows of the night.
Bunnies wake and stretch their paws anew,
Ready for a day of fun for you.

rhymes.title: Floppy Ears
rhymes.text:
Floppy ears and furry toes,
Little pink and twitchy nose.
Hopping fast and hopping slow,
Where do little bunnies go?

Over rocks and under trees,
Dancing in the gentle breeze.
Finding flowers pink and blue,
Drinking drops of morning dew.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Softly twinkling down below.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Burrow is the very best.

Sleepy bunny goes to sleep,
While the moon shines bright and deep.
Dreaming dreams of fields of clover,
Till the nighttime hours are over.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny, soft and white,
Hops around with all his might.
Twitchy nose and fluffy tail,
Hops along the grassy trail.

Sees a flower, pink and red,
Nods his sleepy little head.
Jumps up high into the air,
Leaves a footprint over there.

Finds a carrot, big and sweet,
Takes a little yummy treat.
Chews it slowly, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Eating up his healthy lunch.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Little bunny says goodnight,
Sleeping till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Rabbit
rhymes.text:
Hop, little rabbit, hop, hop, hop,
When you reach the garden, stop.
Wiggle your ears so soft and tall,
Play a game with one and all.

Run through the clover, green and sweet,
Using your quick and furry feet.
Hide in the bushes out of sight,
Underneath the golden light.

Jump over puddles on the ground,
Looking all around, around.
Find a friend to share the day,
Dance and giggle as you play.

Time to rest your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the evening skies.
Cuddle up and close them tight,
Sleep until the morning light.

rhymes.title: The Fluffy Bunny Tale
rhymes.text:
See the bunny in the grass,
Watch him gently hop and pass.
Long white ears that wiggle round,
Making not a single sound.

Paws are soft and eyes are bright,
Fur is cozy, clean, and white.
He loves to jump and he loves to play,
In the meadow every day.

Sniffing flowers on the ground,
Looking for a friend around.
Found a squirrel in a tree,
Happy as a bunny can be.

Stars are shining up above,
Sending dreams and lots of love.
Curl up now upon the floor,
Sleep until we wake once more.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Hop
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Wiggles nose and wiggles toes,
Where he goes, nobody knows.

Fluffy tail goes wag, wag, wag,
Carrying a tiny bag.
Eating carrots, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Having a delicious lunch.

Long brown ears that flop and bend,
Every forest beast's best friend.
Jumping over logs and trees,
Dancing in the gentle breeze.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best little rabbit yet.
Curls up in his cozy bed,
Sleeping softly, nodding head.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bunnies
rhymes.text:
One little bunny plays in the sun,
Having so much joyous fun.
Two little bunnies jump so high,
Right up to the butterfly.

Three little bunnies sniff a rose,
Right upon each twitchy nose.
Four little bunnies run and hide,
Safe and cozy deep inside.

Five little bunnies fall asleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.
Dreaming of a meadow green,
Best adventure ever seen.

Wake up, bunnies, greet the day,
Time to hop and time to play.
Jump around and shout out loud,
Make your furry mama proud.

rhymes.title: The Bunny's Garden
rhymes.text:
In the garden green and bright,
Bunny plays till morning light.
Digging holes in yummy dirt,
Wearing not a single shirt.

Finding lettuce crisp and sweet,
Such a lovely morning treat.
Chewing slowly, munch, munch, munch,
Having quite a tasty lunch.

Birdies sing a happy song,
While the bunny hops along.
Leaping over garden walls,
Catching acorns as they falls.

Now the afternoon is here,
Time to rest, my furry dear.
Close your eyes and take a rest,
Sleeping in your fuzzy nest.

rhymes.title: Little Bunny Foo Foo
rhymes.text:
Little bunny hops so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Wiggle nose and twitch your ears,
Chasing all the sleepy fears.

Hopping fast and hopping slow,
Watch the fluffy rabbit go.
Jump across the garden bed,
With a little furry head.

Nibble on a clover sweet,
Using tiny furry feet.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.

Time to rest your tired head,
In your cozy little bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Whiskers
rhymes.text:
Bunny wakes up in the morn,
Glad that little day was born.
Stretches out his paws so wide,
Looking for a place to hide.

Runs across the grassy green,
Quickest bunny ever seen.
Finds a carrot in the dirt,
Hope that he does not get hurt!

Crunch and munch and chew it all,
Catch a beetle big and small.
Play a game of hide and seek,
Make a happy little squeak.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Cuddle close and dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Bunny
rhymes.text:
Soft white fur and eyes so pink,
Rabbit stops to have a drink.
From the stream so cool and clear,
Knowing safety is right here.

Jump up high and tumble down,
Best jumper in all the town.
Wiggle tail of cotton white,
Shining softly in the light.

Friends are waiting in the tree,
Happy as a bird can be.
Share a berry, sweet and red,
Time to rest a sleepy head.

Mama bunny sings a song,
All the meadow sings along.
Snuggle in the burrow deep,
Now the bunny falls asleep.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Pip loved the morning. He stretched his tiny wings and said, 'Quack, quack, good morning, world!' Pip lived near a big, beautiful farm with his mama and his duckling brothers and sisters. Today, Mama Duck had a special surprise. 'Come along, little ones,' she quacked softly. 'Let us go find the big puddle by the old red barn.' Pip loved puddles. He waddled as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him. Waddle, waddle, waddle went Pip. He skipped over a shiny green leaf and hopped past a sleepy brown cow. 'Moo,' said the cow. 'Quack,' said Pip happily. When they reached the big puddle, Pip's eyes grew wide. It was not just any puddle. It was a giant, mud-filled wonderland! The rain from the night before had made the ground wonderfully squishy. Pip's brothers and sisters jumped right in. Splash, splash, splish! Mud flew everywhere, landing on their fluffy yellow feathers. Pip wanted to join the fun, but he stopped at the edge. The mud looked very thick. 'Is it too muddy?' Pip wondered. Mama Duck smiled warmly. 'Go on, little Pip. Try it!' Pip took a tiny step with his right foot. Squish! Then his left foot. Squish-squash! Pip giggled. It felt tickly and warm between his toes. He flapped his wings and shouted, 'Whee!' Pip ducked his head down and scooped up some mud with his bill. He made a funny little mud hat on his head. All the other ducklings laughed and clapped their wings. They danced in a circle, splashing mud high into the air. Splash, splash, splish, splash! They wiggled their tail feathers and sang their happy duck songs. By the time the sun was high in the sky, Pip was covered in mud from his bill to his tail. He did not look like a yellow duck anymore; he looked like a little chocolate duck! 'Time to clean up,' quacked Mama Duck gently. She led the little ducklings over to the sparkling blue pond. One by one, they hopped into the cool, refreshing water. Swish, swish went their feathers as they washed away the brown mud. Pip shook himself off, sending sparkling droplets of water flying in the sunlight. He was clean, he was fluffy, and he was very, very happy. As they waddled back home for a nap, Pip whispered to himself, 'Being a duck is the best adventure in the whole wide world.'

stories.title: Oliver's Lost Quack
stories.text: Deep in the whispering reeds of Willow Pond lived a little green-headed duck named Oliver. Oliver was usually a very loud and proud duck. Every morning, he would sing his loudest song to wake up the frogs. 'QUACK! QUACK! QUACK!' he would shout across the water. But today, something very strange happened. Oliver woke up, opened his beak wide, and pushed air out. But no sound came out. Not a single peep! Oliver tried again. He puffed out his chest, opened his bill as big as a giant circle, and squeezed. Still, nothing happened. Just a tiny, squeaky puff of air. 'Oh dear,' thought Oliver, his eyes growing wide with worry. 'Where is my quack? Did it fly away?' Oliver decided to go on a grand search to find his missing quack. He waddled quickly along the muddy bank, looking behind every smooth grey stone and under every tall green fern. First, he met Sammy the squirrel, who was busy burying an acorn. 'Hello, Sammy!' Oliver tried to say, but only a silent puff came out. Sammy tilted his head. 'Did you say something, Oliver? You look very quiet today.' Oliver shook his head sadly and pointed to his beak. Sammy patted Oliver's shoulder kindly. 'I hope you find it!' Next, Oliver paddled out onto the calm, glassy water of the pond. He floated past Benny the blue dragonfly, who was hovering lazily in the warm air. 'Bzzzt,' said Benny. Oliver opened his beak and tried his hardest to answer. He squeezed his eyes shut and pushed. A tiny, raspy squeak slipped out. 'Squeak!' Benny buzzed around Oliver in a little circle. 'That is a very funny quack,' giggled the dragonfly. Oliver sighed and let his chin drop down to his chest. Just then, Mama Duck swam up beside him. She had a warm, knowing smile on her face. 'What is the matter, my little Oliver?' she asked gently. Oliver pointed to his beak and made a sad little face. 'Ah,' said Mama Duck knowingly. 'You have been talking too much and playing too hard in the cold wind yesterday. Your voice is just resting!' Mama Duck reached down and plucked a sweet, juicy water plant from the bottom of the pond. 'Here, eat this green leaf, and then drink some cool water.' Oliver nibbled the green leaf. It tasted fresh and crisp. Then he took a long, refreshing gulp of water. He opened his beak to try one more time. He took a deep breath, puffed out his feathers, and let out a mighty, joyful 'QUACK!' It echoed all the way across Willow Pond. Sammy the squirrel cheered, and Benny the dragonfly did a loop-de-loop. Oliver smiled a big duck smile. His quack was back, right where it belonged.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy wooden coop beside a babbling brook, lived a little white duck named Barnaby. Barnaby was a very stylish duck who loved bright, cheerful colors. More than anything in the whole world, Barnaby wanted a pair of shiny red boots. Every single day, he would waddle down to the village shoe shop and look at the tiny red boots displayed proudly in the window. They were bright red, shiny as an apple, and had little black laces. 'Oh, how I wish those boots were mine,' Barnaby would quack softly, pressing his beak against the cool glass. One sunny Tuesday morning, Barnaby woke up and found a big cardboard box waiting for him right outside his door. It was tied with a bright yellow ribbon. Barnaby's heart did a happy little flip-flop. He used his beak to untie the ribbon and pulled off the lid. Inside, resting on a bed of soft white tissue paper, was a brand-new pair of shiny red boots! They were just his size. Barnaby could hardly contain his excitement. He hopped up and down, flapping his wings. With a little wiggle and a firm push, he slipped his webbed feet right into the boots. They fit like a dream! They were snug, warm, and wonderfully red. Barnaby could not wait to show all his farmyard friends his fabulous new fashion. He stepped out of his coop and began to waddle down the path. Clump, clump, clump went his red boots on the hard dirt path. Barnaby puffed out his chest proudly. He waddled past the sleeping barn cat, who opened one green eye and purred, 'My, what fancy shoes, Barnaby.' Barnaby smiled and gave a happy 'Quack!' But then, Barnaby came to a tricky spot on the path. The big rainstorm from yesterday had left a giant, gooey patch of thick mud right in the middle of the way. Barnaby stopped. He looked at his shiny red boots. If he walked through the mud, they might get dirty! But Barnaby also loved mud. What was a duck to do? 'Well,' thought Barnaby, 'boots are made for walking, and mud is made for squishing!' Without another second of hesitation, Barnaby marched right into the thick, brown mud. Clump-squish, clump-squish went his red boots. It felt wonderfully squishy around his ankles. Barnaby laughed out loud and stomped his feet, sending brown mud splattering in all directions. His boots were covered in mud now, but they were still just as red underneath. When he reached the pond, he jumped right in. Swish! The cool water washed the mud away instantly, leaving his boots shining just as bright as new. Barnaby swam in circles, kicking his red-booted feet high above the water. He was the happiest duck in the whole farmyard.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Splash
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, down by the bright blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had two big orange feet, a soft fluffy yellow coat, and a very loud, happy voice. Quack, quack, quack! Pip loved mornings because mornings meant it was time to play.

Today, Pip had a very important mission. He wanted to make the biggest, splashiest splash in the whole wide pond. His mother, big Mother Duck, waddled beside him, keeping a watchful eye. Waddle, waddle, waddle went their little webbed feet on the green grass. 

'Can I make a big splash today, Mama?' asked Pip, flapping his tiny wings.

'Of course you can, my little duckling,' said Mother Duck with a gentle smile. 'Just follow me to the water's edge.'

When they reached the edge of the pond, the water sparkled like diamonds in the sun. Little frogs sat on green lily pads, singing, 'Ribbit, ribbit!' Dragonflies zoomed past with shiny blue wings. Pip looked at the water, and the water looked right back at him.

Pip took a deep breath. He puffed out his yellow chest. One, two, three, go! Pip ran as fast as his webbed feet could carry him. Patter, patter, patter went his feet on the mud. He leaped into the air and tucked in his wings.

SPLASH!

Water flew up into the sky like tiny raindrops. It landed on the lily pads. It landed on Mother Duck's back. It even landed on a little frog who blinked in surprise. Pip popped right back up to the surface, shaking his head. Water droplets flew everywhere.

'Did you see that, Mama?' shouted Pip, doing a happy little dance in the water. 'I made a giant splash!'

'That was the best splash I have ever seen,' said Mother Duck, wrapping her wing around him. 

Pip felt so proud. He paddled around the pond all day long, practicing his swimming and saying hello to all his fish friends. When the sun began to set and painted the sky in pink and orange, Pip and his mother waddled back to their cozy nest. Pip snuggled up close, closed his eyes, and dreamed of tomorrow's big adventures. Goodnight, Pip!

stories.title: Where Is My Feather?
stories.text:
The wind was blowing a soft, gentle breeze through the tall green reeds by the pond. Whoosh, went the wind. Little Ducky was waking up from a lovely nap. He stretched his left wing, and then he stretched his right wing. But wait. Something felt just a little bit different today.

Ducky looked down at his soft yellow tummy. He looked at his fuzzy tail. Then he looked at the ground. Oh no! His favorite blue feather was gone!

Ducky loved his blue feather. It was bright and shiny, and he wore it right on top of his head like a little crown. 'Quack!' cried Ducky. 'Where is my special feather?'

Ducky decided to go on a grand adventure to find it. He waddled down the muddy path and met his friend, Barnaby the Brown Bunny.

'Hello, Barnaby,' said Ducky. 'Have you seen my blue feather? The wind blew it away.'

Barnaby wiggled his long pink nose. 'No, Ducky, I haven't seen your feather. But I did see something blue hiding behind that big pumpkin over there!'

Ducky thanked the bunny and waddled over to the pumpkin as fast as his webbed feet could go. Waddle, waddle, waddle! He peeked behind the pumpkin. Was it his feather? No! It was just a round, blue bouncy ball left behind by the farmer's children.

Ducky felt a little bit sad, but he didn't give up. He kept on searching. He waddled past the tall green grass and met Sammy the Squirrel.

'Hello, Sammy,' said Ducky. 'Have you seen my blue feather?'

Sammy chattered his teeth. 'Check up in the old oak tree, little duck!'

Ducky looked up. High up in the branches, caught gently on a green leaf, was a flash of bright blue. It fluttered in the breeze. It was his feather!

'Oh, thank goodness!' cheered Ducky. But how would he get it down? He couldn't climb trees like a squirrel. Just then, a friendly breeze blew through the branches. Whoosh! The wind gently carried the feather down, floating softly through the air like a parachute. 

Ducky opened his beak and caught the feather right out of the air. He popped it back on top of his head. He was so happy he did a little spin.

'Thank you, wind!' quacked Ducky. He waddled back home, feeling like a king with his favorite feather shining in the sun.

stories.title: Ducky's Muddy Boots
stories.text:
It had been raining all night long. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the raindrops against the big barn window. But when morning came, the rain stopped, and the sun burst through the clouds with a warm, golden smile. 

Little Ducky woke up with a giant yawn. 'Quack-a-doodle-doo!' he shouted happily. Wait, ducks don't say doodle-doo, do they? Ducky giggled at his own silly joke. Today was going to be a wonderful day because the rain meant only one thing: puddles!

Ducky loved puddles more than anything in the whole world. He hopped out of his nest and put on his shiny red rain boots. Squeak, squeak went the boots as he waddled out the door. They were just the right size for his webbed feet.

He waddled down the path until he found the biggest, muddiest puddle in the farmyard. It was huge! It was brown, bubbly, and looked like a giant bowl of chocolate pudding.

'Time for a muddy adventure!' cheered Ducky.

He walked right up to the edge of the puddle and looked down. He could see his own reflection staring back at him. He raised a foot and got ready to jump.

One, two, three, JUMP!

SPLORCH!

Mud went flying everywhere. It landed on the fence. It landed on a daisy flower. It even landed on Ducky's beak with a funny little plop. Ducky laughed out loud. He splashed his left foot. Splash, splash! Then he splashed his right foot. Splash, splash!

Soon, his farm friends came running over to see what all the noise was about. Penny the Pig trotted over, oinking with joy. 

'Can I play too, Ducky?' asked Penny.

'Come on in!' cried Ducky. 'The mud is wonderful!'

Punny the Pig jumped right into the puddle with a giant OINK and made an even bigger splash. Then Cow came over, and Sheep came over. Soon, all the farm animals were laughing and splashing together in the big brown puddle. The farm was full of happy noises—quacks, oinks, moos, and Baas.

When it was time to go home for lunch, Ducky was covered in mud from his head to his toes. He didn't look like a yellow duck anymore; he looked like a chocolate duck! 

Mother Duck smiled warmly when she saw him. 'Time for a warm bath, my little muddy duck,' she said. Ducky washed off his red boots and snuggled into his clean nest, already dreaming of the next rainy day.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy green park, there lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had soft, fluffy feathers, two bright orange feet, and a very loud, happy quack. Every morning, Pip would wake up and stretch his little wings. Stretch, stretch, flap, flap! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, which meant there were puddles everywhere.

Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went his little orange feet on the soft grass. He stopped by his favorite big oak tree and looked down. Right in the middle of the path was a giant, shimmering, mud puddle. It was brown, squishy, and looked like the most fun in the whole wide world.

"Quack, quack!" said Pip with a big smile. He took one step closer. Then, he dipped his webbed foot right into the mud. Squish, squash, squish! The mud went between his toes. It felt tickly and warm. Pip giggled, or as ducks do, he gave a happy little chatter.

Without waiting another second, Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle. Splash! Mud flew up into the air and landed on his head, making a little brown mud-hat. Pip flapped his wings and splashed water and mud everywhere. He spun around in circles, making deep circles in the mud.

Soon, his duck friend, Penny, waddled over. Penny had feathers as white as snow. She looked at Pip and tilted her head. "Quack?" she asked, which meant, "What are you doing?"

"Come on in!" called Pip. "The mud is wonderful!"

Panny jumped in with a big splash! Splash, splash, go the ducks! They played together for a long, long time, making funny mud pictures with their feet. They pretended they were brave explorers in a chocolate swamp.

When the sun came out from behind the clouds, it was time to get clean. Pip and Penny waddled over to the shiny blue pond. They dove right in and washed all the brown mud away. Swoosh, go the feathers! Soon, Pip was yellow and fluffy again.

He shook his tail feathers and dried off in the warm sunshine. What a wonderful day for a little duck.

stories.title: The Lost Feather
stories.text:
Little duckling Ducky loved to go for walks around the farm. He had the softest yellow down, a cute little bill, and a heart full of curiosity. Today, Ducky was walking near the big red barn when he noticed something blowing in the gentle breeze. It was a pretty, fluffy feather, dancing up and down in the air.

Ducky chased after it. Trot, trot, waddle, waddle! The feather floated this way, and Ducky waddled that way. Finally, the feather drifted down and landed softly right on top of a hay bale. Ducky stretched his neck up high, but he was just a little too short to reach it.

"Oh dear," thought Ducky. "How can I get my feather back?" Just then, Cow moseyed on by, chewing on a piece of sweet green grass. "Moo," said Cow kindly. "What is the matter, little duck?"

"I found a lovely feather, but it is too high up on the hay bale," Ducky explained, giving a sad little quack.

Cow smiled her gentle cow smile. "Let me help you," she said. Cow gently blew a soft puff of air from her big nose. Puff! The gentle breeze carried the feather off the hay bale and straight down to the ground right in front of Ducky.

"Thank you, Cow!" cheered Ducky happily. He picked up the feather with his beak, but then he had a very nice idea. He looked at Cow, who looked a little hot under the warm sun. Ducky waddled over and tucked the soft feather behind Cow's big, floppy ear.

Cow blinked in surprise and then smiled a big cow smile. "Moo-rvelous!" she said, making Ducky giggle.

Next, Ducky waddled over to the duck pond to show his mother. He waddled fast on his little orange feet. Waddle, waddle, waddle! When he reached the water, his mother was swimming in circles with her webbed feet. "Quack, hello my sweet little duckling," she said.

Ducky hopped into the cool water and paddled over to her side. He told her all about his adventure with the feather and the kind cow. His mother nuzzled him with her soft bill. Ducky felt so safe, so happy, and so very loved as they swam together into the sunset.

stories.title: Paddy's Big Blue Pond
stories.text:
Paddy was a very energetic little duck who lived by a big, sparkling blue pond. Every morning, Paddy woke up before the sun. He would shake his tail feathers, stretch his wings, and say, "Quack, quack, good morning, world!" Paddy loved the water more than anything else. To Paddy, the pond was a magical playground filled with shiny fish, green lily pads, and friendly frogs.

Today, Paddy had a very important mission. He wanted to swim all the way across the big blue pond to visit his very best friend, a little green frog named Barnaby, who lived on the other side near the tall reeds.

Paddy hopped into the water. Splash! He started to paddle with his strong webbed feet. Paddle, paddle, paddle go his feet under the water, while his little yellow body glided smoothly on top like a tiny boat. The water felt cool and refreshing against his warm feathers.

As Paddy swam, a little fish popped its head up from the water. "Blub, blub!" said the fish. Paddy smiled and gave a friendly quack. He swam around a big green lily pad that floated gently on the ripples. He even played hide-and-seek with a dragonfly that zoomed past his head, buzzing happily in the warm air. Zoom, zoom, went the dragonfly!

Paddy kept his eyes on the tall reeds across the pond. He could see them swaying in the breeze. "Almost there!" Paddy quacked to himself, paddling a little bit faster. His orange feet kicked quickly under the water. Kick, kick, kick!

At last, Paddy reached the muddy shore. He waddled out of the water, shaking the sparkling drops from his feathers. "Ribbit, ribbit!" sang Barnaby the frog, jumping up onto a smooth rock to greet him.

"Hello, Barnaby!" said Paddy. The two friends played games all morning long. They played tag among the reeds and listened to the birds sing sweet songs high up in the trees. Paddy was so glad he made the journey across the big blue pond because adventures with friends are always the best kind of adventures.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had soft, fluffy feathers that felt just like a warm cotton ball, and two bright orange feet. Every single day, Pip loved to go on grand adventures in the tall green grass. Today, Pip had a very important mission. He wanted to make the biggest, splashiest splash in the whole wide world! Pip waddled along the muddy path, going waddle, waddle, waddle, quack, quack, quack. He passed by a busy brown bunny who was munching on clover. 'Hello, bunny!' said Pip. The bunny wriggled his nose and gave a little hop. Pip kept on going because the pond was calling his name. Soon, the bright blue water came into view. It sparkled in the warm morning sun like a million tiny diamonds. Pip hurried his waddle. He reached the soft, muddy edge of the pond and looked down at the water. He could see his own little reflection looking right back up at him. 'Time for a big splash!' whispered Pip to himself. He stretched out his tiny yellow wings. He took a deep breath, puffed out his chest, and ran as fast as his little orange feet could carry him. Ready, set, go! Pip leaped right off the grassy bank and into the air. For one magical second, he was flying. Then, down, down, down he went. SPLASH! Water flew up into the air like a sparkling fountain. Droplets landed on the lily pads and on the nose of a friendly green frog. 'Ribbit!' said the frog, clapping his webbed feet. Pip bobbed right back up to the top like a little yellow cork. He shook his feathers and water went flying everywhere. 'Quack, quack, hooray!' shouted Pip, kicking his legs and creating little ripples in the water. He paddled in circles, feeling happy and proud. He had made the best splash in the whole wide world. Swimming around and around, Pip smiled from ear to ear. Bath time in the big pond was simply the most fun thing a little yellow duck could ever do. As the warm sun climbed higher in the sky, Pip floated peacefully, ready for his next exciting outdoor adventure.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck Finds a Friend
stories.text: Down by the edge of the whispering reeds, where the cattails grew tall and green, lived a sweet little duck named Daffodil. Daffodil had feathers the color of buttercups and a gentle, happy quack. Daffodil loved to explore, but today she felt a little bit lonely. She wanted a special friend to play games with in the warm sunshine. Daffodil waddled down to the water's edge, leaving tiny webbed footprints in the soft mud. 'Quack, quack,' she called out softly, wondering who might hear her. A dragonfly with shiny blue wings zipped past her head. 'Bzzzt!' went the dragonfly, flying up into the bright blue sky much too fast for a little duck to catch. Daffodil sighed a soft little sigh and hopped into the cool water. She paddled past a big, sleepy turtle resting on a warm log. 'Good morning, Mr. Turtle,' said Daffodil politely. The turtle blinked his slow, heavy eyes and nodded his green head, but he did not want to play tag. Daffodil kept paddling, her webbed feet kicking happily beneath the water. Suddenly, she heard a funny sound coming from behind a large patch of floating lily pads. It went, 'Squeak, squeak, splash!' Daffodil tilted her head to the left, then to the right. She paddled closer, her curious tail feathers wagging just a little bit. There, hiding behind a big green leaf, was a tiny baby duckling with fluffy brown and yellow feathers. The little duckling looked a little bit lost and a whole lot shy. 'Hello there,' said Daffodil in her nicest, friendliest voice. 'My name is Daffodil. Would you like to swim with me?' The little duckling perked right up and smiled a big duck smile. 'My name is Barnaby,' he cheeped happily. Barnaby jumped into the water with a joyful little hop, right beside Daffodil. Together, they swam in big circles, chased each other through the tall green reeds, and splashed water at the dancing dragonflies. Daffodil wasn't lonely anymore. She had found the best friend in the whole wide world, and they spent the rest of the sunny afternoon playing happily together in the sparkling blue pond.

stories.title: Oliver's Shiny Feather
stories.text: Oliver was a very busy little duck who lived on a farm with a big red barn. Oliver had a coat of feathers that were mostly white, except for one very special feather right on top of his head that shimmered bright green in the sunlight. Whenever Oliver walked around the farmyard, he felt extra proud of his shiny green feather. Today, Oliver had places to go and friends to see. He waddled out of his cozy nest in the straw and stretched his wings. 'Quack!' he greeted the morning sun. First, Oliver waddled over to the big wooden fence where the friendly brown cow was chewing on sweet green grass. 'Moo,' said the cow, looking down kindly. Oliver puffed out his chest so the cow could get a very good look at his shimmering green feather. The cow blinked her big brown eyes approvingly. Next, Oliver waddled past the old red tractor, going waddle, waddle, waddle all the way. He stopped by the chicken coop where the fluffy yellow chicks were pecking at the dirt. 'Peep, peep!' cried the little chicks, running in circles around Oliver's webbed feet. Oliver felt very important leading his tiny fan club across the dusty farmyard. But then, a sudden gust of wind came swooping across the open field. Whoosh! The wind blew past Oliver's head. Oh no! Oliver felt a strange tickle right on top of his head. He reached up with his beak, but he was too late. His shiny green feather had caught the breeze and was floating up into the air! 'Quack!' cried Oliver in surprise. The feather floated up, up, up past the roof of the red barn. Oliver started to waddle as fast as his orange feet could go, chasing his favorite feather across the grass. Up and down the feather danced on the wind, playing a fun game of tag with the little duck. Finally, the wind stopped blowing, and the feather drifted gently downward. It landed softly right on top of a low wooden bucket of water. Oliver rushed over and looked down. He let out a huge sigh of relief. He scooped his special feather up with his beak and placed it safely back on his head. Oliver was so happy that he did a little happy dance right there in the farmyard, quacking merrily all the way back to his cozy nest.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Splash
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had two bright orange feet, a soft fluffy coat of feathers, and a very loud, happy voice. Quack, quack, quack! Pip loved mornings because mornings meant it was time for water play.

Pip waddled out of his cozy nest in the tall green reeds. He shook his tail feathers and stretched his tiny wings. Today, Pip had a very big goal. He wanted to make the biggest splash in the whole wide pond. His animal friends were all watching. Bella the brown bunny sat on the grassy bank, and Sammy the fluffy squirrel perched on a low tree branch.

Pip took a deep breath. He started walking toward the water. Tap, tap, tap went his little webbed feet on the mud. The water looked cool and inviting. Little ripples danced across the surface. Pip reached the very edge of the water. He lifted one webbed foot high into the air. Then, he lifted the other one. 

'Ready, set, go!' whispered Sammy the squirrel from his tree.

Pip closed his eyes tight and jumped straight up. Splash! Water flew everywhere. It sparkled like tiny diamonds in the bright morning sun. Drops landed on Bella bunny's long ears, and a few even reached Sammy's bushy tail. 

'Hooray!' cheered Bella, twitching her nose with delight. 'That was the biggest splash ever, Pip!'

Pip floated happily on the gentle waves. He kicked his orange feet and bobbed up and down. Water rolled right off his waterproof feathers because ducks have coats that keep them nice and dry. Pip opened his beak and sang out loud. Quack, quack, hooray! Swimming in the pond was the most fun thing in the whole world. Pip paddled in circles, making little whirlpools in the water. Bella and Sammy clapped their paws. Pip felt so proud and happy. As the warm sun climbed higher in the sky, Pip curled up on a soft patch of grass for a nice, long nap, dreaming of even bigger splashes for tomorrow.

stories.title: Oliver's Lost Feather
stories.text:
Deep in the green, leafy park, lived a very friendly duck named Oliver. Oliver had feathers as green as fresh spring grass on his head and a chest as brown as chocolate. He loved to waddle around the park paths and say hello to everyone he met. Quack, hello! Quack, good day!

One breezy afternoon, a strong gust of wind swept through the park. Whoosh! The wind blew past the old oak tree and tickled Oliver's back. Oliver shook his feathers and kept walking. But when he looked down at the grass, he noticed something strange. One of his special, shiny blue wing feathers had fallen out! 

'Oh no,' whispered Oliver. 'My favorite blue feather is gone.'

Oliver knew he had to find it. He waddled quickly down the winding path. 'Quack! Have you seen my blue feather?' he asked a busy little ant crawling near a rock. The ant shook its tiny head and kept on walking. Oliver didn't give up. He kept looking.

He waddled past the big red slide and under the wooden bridge. Splash went his feet in a little puddle. Suddenly, a bright flash of blue caught his eye near the patch of yellow daisies. Oliver hurried over as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him.

There it was! Resting gently on top of a daisy was his beautiful blue feather. The wind must have blown it right onto the flower.

'Found you!' quacked Oliver happily. He gently picked up the feather with his beak. But how would he put it back? Just then, his kind friend Clara the duck waddled by. Clara used her soft wing to tuck the blue feather safely back into Oliver's wing.

'Thank you, Clara,' said Oliver, feeling warm and cozy inside. Oliver flapped his wings and waddled back to the pond with a big smile. He was so glad his feather was back where it belonged. The rest of the afternoon was filled with happy quacks and fun games in the water with all of his wonderful park friends.

stories.title: Daisy Duck's Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
Daisy was a sweet white duck with a bright orange bill and the curliest tail feather in the barnyard. Daisy lived near a big red barn where all kinds of animals lived. There were fuzzy sheep, gentle cows, and playful piglets. Daisy loved her home, but most of all, she loved rainy days.

When dark gray clouds rolled across the sky and raindrops started to fall tap, tap, tap on the roof, Daisy knew it was time for an adventure. Pitter-patter went the rain, turning the dirt path into a squishy, muddy wonderland. 

Daisy stepped out of her cozy wooden coop. Squish, squash, squish went the mud beneath her webbed feet. It felt tickly and warm between her toes. Daisy let out a happy quack. She loved the mud!

Waddling along the path, Daisy met Barnaby the pig. Barnaby was rolling happily in a big muddy puddle. 'Oink, oink! Hello, Daisy!' said Barnaby. 'Isn't the mud wonderful today?'

'Quack, yes! It is the best,' replied Daisy. She decided to join the fun. Daisy walked right into the center of the softest, muddiest puddle she could find. She dipped her bill down and scooped up a little bit of mud, then tossed it up in the air with a joyful shake of her head.

Splish, splash, squish! Daisy danced around in circles. Her white feathers got brown spots all over them, but she didn't mind at all. She looked like a polka-dot duck, and she thought it was just marvelous. 

Soon, the rain stopped, and a big, beautiful rainbow stretched across the sky. Red, orange, yellow, green, and blue painted the air. Daisy looked up at the rainbow and quack-cheesed a giant smile. 

Time to clean up! Daisy waddled over to the sparkling farm pond. She dove right into the cool, clear water. Swish, swash, went the water around her feathers. In just a few seconds, all the mud washed away, leaving her feathers sparkling white once more. Daisy climbed out onto the grassy bank, feeling fresh and happy. She shook her wings dry in the warm sunshine and happily waddled back home, ready for her next big barnyard adventure.

stories.title: Daffy Duck's Big Muddy Splash
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down by the shimmering blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Daffy. Daffy had two bright orange feet, soft fluffy feathers, and a beak that always went quack, quack, quack! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long. The grass was wet, the leaves were shiny, and there were big, wonderful puddles everywhere. Daffy waddled out of his cozy nest. Waddle, waddle, waddle went his feet. He shook his tail feathers and blinked his round eyes. 'Quack!' said Daffy. It was time for an adventure! First, Daffy waddled over to the big green hill. He saw his friend Bella the bunny hopping by. 'Hello, Bella!' quacked Daffy. 'Hop, hop, hop!' went Bella. Daffy waddled a little faster. He wanted to find the biggest puddle in the whole wide world. Round and round the big oak tree he went, past the patch of sweet red strawberries, until he stopped right at the edge of the path. Oh, look! There it was. A gigantic, muddy, bubbly puddle! It shimmered in the morning sun. Daffy tilted his head. He looked to the left. He looked to the right. Then, he took a big breath. 'Ready, set, go!' he whispered to himself. With a joyful flap of his little wings, Daffy jumped right into the middle of the mud. Splash! Mud went up. Mud went down. Mud went all around! 'Splat, splat, splish!' laughed Daffy. He kicked his orange feet and made big brown bubbles. He scooped up a little mud on his beak and painted a funny dot on his nose. A friendly little frog on a lily pad croaked, 'Ribbit! That looks like so much fun!' Daffy nodded and flapped his wings again. Splash, splash, splash! Soon, Daffy was covered in mud from his head to his tail. He did a happy little duck dance. He waddled in a circle, singing his favorite quack-quack song. When he was all tired out from splashing, Daffy waddled back to the clean blue pond. He jumped right into the cool water. Swish, swash, wash! The clean water washed all the brown mud away. Daffy floated on his back like a little yellow boat, looking up at the puffy white clouds. He smiled a big duck smile. Playing in the mud was the best thing in the whole wide world. With a happy sigh, Daffy closed his eyes for a little nap, dreaming of tomorrow's big adventures.

stories.title: Daffy Duck Finds a Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Good morning, little ducklings! Today we are visiting the whispering river where the reeds sway gently in the breeze. Meet our friend, Pip the duck. Pip was a curious little duck who loved to explore. Every morning, after eating a breakfast of crunchy green lily seeds, Pip would go on a treasure hunt along the muddy riverbank. Today, the sun was shining brightly, turning the river into a ribbon of sparkling gold. Pip waddled along the water's edge, his webbed feet making soft squishing sounds in the damp earth. Squish, squash, squish! Pip looked down. He looked up. He poked his yellow beak into the tall green grass. What could he find today? A wiggly worm? A shiny green beetle? Suddenly, something caught his eye near the roots of a weeping willow tree. It glittered in a tiny patch of sunlight. Pip tilted his head. He took one step closer. Then another step closer. He stretched out his neck and looked down. Right there, half-buried in the dark soil, was a smooth, round pebble. It wasn't just any pebble; it was bright blue, sparkling like a tiny piece of sky fallen right onto the ground! Pip gasped, or as much as a duck could gasp. 'Quack!' he whispered excitedly. He gently nudged the pebble with his beak. It rolled a little bit. Tap, tap, tap. Pip picked up the blue pebble in his beak. It felt cool and smooth. He wanted to show his best friend, Barnaby the beaver, who lived in a cozy lodge nearby. Pip waddled as fast as his little orange feet could carry him. He waddled past the big mossy log, past the patch of yellow daisies, and straight up to Barnaby's front door. 'Quack, quack!' called Pip, waving his head. Barnaby popped his furry head out of the water. 'Well, hello there, Pip! What do you have?' Pip opened his beak and dropped the sparkling blue pebble right into Barnaby's paws. Barnaby's eyes went wide. 'My goodness, Pip! That is the most wonderful treasure I have ever seen!' Pip did a happy little wiggle. He felt so proud. Barnaby carefully placed the sparkling blue pebble right on top of a flat rock for all the river animals to admire. From that day on, whenever the sun hit the pebble, it sparkled just for them. Pip smiled happily, knowing that sharing his special treasure made the whole day bright.

stories.title: Daffy Duck's Sleepy Time Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was beginning to sink low behind the green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink, orange, and purple. Down at the quiet pond, the day was coming to an end. The dragonflies had stopped zooming, the little frogs had stopped leaping, and the tall reeds whispered a soft goodnight song in the evening breeze. It was time for bed, and our little friend Ducky was getting very, very sleepy. Ducky was a sweet little duck with feathers as soft as dandelion fluff. He gave a big, wide yawn, opening his yellow beak wide. Ahh-choo—no, ahh-yawn! He blinked his heavy eyelids. His webbed feet felt as heavy as stones. 'Time to find a cozy sleeping spot,' Ducky softly quacked to himself. He waddled slowly across the soft green grass, making his way toward the edge of the safe, calm pond. Waddle, waddle, rest. Waddle, waddle, rest. Along the way, Ducky said goodnight to his animal friends. He whispered 'Goodnight' to the ladybug resting on a clover leaf. He whispered 'Goodnight' to the mother sheep sleeping on the distant hillside. Finally, Ducky reached his favorite nest tucked safely beneath the big fern fronds. The nest was made of soft moss, warm feathers, and dried sweet grass. It was the coziest place in the whole wide world. Ducky gently stepped into the middle of his nest and turned around three times. Spin, spin, spin, and down he sat. He tucked his warm yellow bill right under his soft wing to keep it cozy. He fluffed up his feathers so he looked like a little round ball of yellow sunshine. The water of the pond lapped gently against the shore. Lap, splash. Lap, splash. It sounded like a sweet lullaby. The stars began to twinkle in the dark velvet sky like tiny silver buttons. Ducky closed his eyes tightly. He listened to the night bugs hum their gentle tune. He felt safe, he felt warm, and he felt so very loved. With a final soft sigh, Ducky drifted off to dreamland, floating on a cloud of sweet sleepy thoughts. Goodnight, little Ducky. Sleep tight until the morning sun wakes you up for a brand new day of fun.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Muddy Adventure
