stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Pip had bright orange webbed feet that went squish, squatch, squish on the green grass. Quack, quack! sang Pip. It was a wonderful day for an adventure. Pip waddled down the gentle grassy hill toward the sparkling blue pond. Along the way, he met his friend Bella the butterfly. Hello, Bella! quacked Pip. Bella fluttered her pretty blue wings and danced in the warm air. Pip kept walking, wiggling his fluffy tail feathers from side to side. Suddenly, Pip stopped. Right in the middle of the path was a big, juicy puddle of mud! Oh boy! thought Pip. Ducks love mud. Pip stepped one orange foot right into the thick, brown goo. Squish! Then he stepped his other foot in. Squatch! Pip giggled, flapping his little yellow wings. He bent down and scooped up some mud with his bill. Yummy mud, thought Pip, though he didn't eat it, he just liked the squishy feeling. Then, Pip plopped his whole round tummy right down into the puddle. Slurp! Brown mud bubbled up all around him. Pip kicked his webbed feet, making happy splashing noises. Splash, splash, splash! He looked down at his tummy and laughed. He was covered in mud from his beak to his tail. Just then, Mama Duck came waddling over. Quack, quack, time for a bath, little one! she said gently. Pip stood up, shaking off the extra mud drops. He waddled behind his mama all the way back to the sparkling blue pond. Pip jumped right into the cool, clean water. Splash! He shook his feathers and washed the mud away. The water sparkled in the sunshine, and Pip floated happily on the ripples. Floating on the water felt just as good as playing in the mud. Pip tucked his head under his wing and smiled. What a busy and wonderful day for a little yellow duck!

stories.title: Ducky's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Deep in the green meadow lived a curious little duck named Barnaby. Barnaby loved shiny things, but most of all, he loved shoes. Every morning, Barnaby would watch the farmer walk by in his big, bright red boots. Stomp, stomp, stomp went the boots! Barnaby wanted boots, too. One breezy afternoon, Barnaby found a surprise by the big red barn. Sitting right on the wooden porch were a pair of tiny, shiny red boots! Barnaby let out a happy quack. He waddled over as fast as his webbed feet could carry him. First, Barnaby tried to put his left foot into the left boot. Oof! he grunted. His wide webbed foot was a little too big. Barnaby pushed harder. Squish! His foot popped right inside. Then, he squeezed his right foot into the other boot. Squish! Barnaby looked down. He was wearing boots! He tried to take a step. Clump! went his left foot. Clump! went his right foot. Barnaby wobbled to the left. He wobbled to the right. Oh dear, boots were much heavier than webbed feet! Barnaby tried to waddle down the path to show his friend Sammy the sheep. Clump, clump, thump! Sammy looked up and blinked his big brown eyes. Baa, nice boots, Barnaby! said Sammy. Barnaby smiled proudly and tried to flap his wings. But wait! Barnaby wanted to go swimming in the duck pond. He waddled down to the water's edge and looked at the cool blue waves. He lifted his foot to jump in. Splash! But wait—boots are heavy! Barnaby started to sink just a tiny bit. Oh my, thought Barnaby, ducks don't need boots to swim. With a wiggle and a tug, Barnaby pulled his left foot out of the red boot, and then his right foot. Pop! Pop! The boots floated on the water like little red boats. Barnaby paddled happily beside them, splashing the water with his bare webbed feet. Quack, quack! Sometimes, being a barefoot duck is the best way to be after all.

stories.title: The Lost Feather
stories.text: The sun was beginning to set, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. Little Oliver duck was getting ready for bed in his cozy nest made of soft reeds. But wait! Something felt missing. Oliver reached back with his yellow bill to smooth his fluffy feathers. Oh no! His favorite fuzzy feather was gone. It was a soft, downy feather that kept him extra warm at night. Oliver let out a sad little quack. Where could it be? He stood up and decided to retrace his steps before bedtime. First, he waddled over to the tall green cattails where he had played hide-and-seek earlier that afternoon. Hello, Mr. Frog, have you seen my special feather? asked Oliver. The green frog blinked his big round eyes and croaked, Ribbit, no feather here, little duck! Oliver did not give up. He waddled along the soft mud bank toward the big sleeping willow tree. The gentle wind whispered through the long green leaves. Swoosh, swoosh went the branches. Oliver looked under the tree roots. Nothing there! Then, he checked near the big smooth rock where he liked to sunbathe. The rock was warm, but the feather was not there. Oliver felt a little tired. His heavy eyelids started to droop. He gave one last little look behind a patch of bright yellow daisies. And guess what he saw? There was his fluffy feather, gently tickling a little bee! The bee buzzed softly, Bzzz, is this yours, little duck? Oliver nodded and scooped up his feather with his bill. Thank you, little bee, he quacked happily. With his precious feather safely tucked against his chest, Oliver waddled back to his cozy nest in the reeds. He curled up into a soft, warm ball. Oliver closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, holding his special feather close. Good night, little duck.

stories.title: Daffy's Big Yellow Boots
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a little yellow duckling named Daffy. Daffy had the softest feathers, the orange-est beak, and two big, shiny, brand-new red boots! Oh, how Daffy loved his boots. They squeaked when he walked. Squeak, squeak, squeak! They clomped when he ran. Clomp, clomp, clomp! Daffy wanted to show his special boots to all his animal friends.

First, Daffy waddled over to the tall green reeds where Penny the frog was sitting. 'Ribbit, ribbit!' said Penny. 'Look at your bright red boots, Daffy!' Daffy did a little happy dance, shaking his tail feathers. 'Quack, quack!' he cheered. Next, Daffy waddled up the grassy hill to say hello to Barnaby the fluffy brown bunny. Barnaby twitch-twitched his long ears. 'Thump, thump!' went his feet. 'Those boots look very bouncy, Daffy!' 

Soon, big fluffy grey clouds rolled across the sky. Plip, plop, plip, plop! Big raindrops started to fall. 'Oh no!' thought Daffy. 'Time to go swimming!' But wait. Daffy tried to jump into the pond, but his heavy red boots pulled him down. Splash! He felt very clumsy in the water. Ducks do not need boots to swim; ducks need webbed feet!

Wise old Mama Duck gently helped Daffy take off the boots. 'Silly duckling,' she cooed softly. 'Your wonderful webbed feet are made for swimming.' Daffy kicked his bare feet. Whee! He zipped through the water like a tiny yellow speedboat. He did loops and dives, splashing cool water drops everywhere. Daffy realized that swimming with his natural webbed feet was much better than wearing heavy boots. When the rain stopped and the warm sun came back out, Daffy left his boots on the grassy bank for dress-up time, ready for his next big toddler adventure.

stories.title: Pip's Missing Quack
stories.text:
Morning had broken at Whispering Willow Pond, and all the little ducklings were lining up for morning breakfast. Mama Duck lined them up in a neat row: one, two, three, four! 'Quack, quack, quack!' sang Mama Duck. The first duckling replied, 'Quack!' The second duckling replied, 'Quack!' The third duckling replied, 'Quack!' But when it was little Pip's turn at the very end of the line, nothing came out. Pip opened his beak wide: 'Achoo!' Oh dear. Pip had a case of the morning hiccups and his quack was completely gone!

Pip was very worried. How could a little duckling be a proper duck without his quack? He decided to go on a quest to find it. He waddled over to Bessie the black and white cow grazing in the meadow. 'Moo,' said Bessie kindly. 'Did you lose your quack, little one?' Pip shook his head. That was not his sound! Next, Pip waddled into the farmyard to find Barnaby the bouncy bunny. 'Squeak,' whispered Barnaby. But that was not it either.

Pip sat down near the big red barn and let out a tiny, sad sigh. Suddenly, a big tickly feather floated down right in front of his face. It tickled his nose. It tickled his beak. Pip scrunched up his face, closed his eyes tight, and took a giant breath. 'ACHOO!' he sneezed a mighty sneeze. And right after the sneeze, floating out into the fresh morning air came a loud, happy sound: 'QUACK!' 

Pip jumped high into the air with joy. His quack was back! He did a happy little waddle all the way back to the pond, where Mama Duck and his brothers and sisters were waiting. They all opened their beaks together and sang out a chorus of joyful quacks. Pip splashed into the cool blue water, happier than ever, knowing his special duck voice was safe and sound.

stories.title: Ducky's Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
It was a wonderful, messy Wednesday afternoon after a long morning rain shower. Oliver the little green-headed mallard duck loved rainy days. Why? Because rainy days meant puddles! And big puddles meant glorious, squishy, squashy mud. Oliver packed his bucket and his little yellow shovel, ready to explore the big farmyard behind the old wooden fence.

As Oliver waddled down the muddy path, he met his best friend, a little pink piglet named Oink. Oink was rolling around in a gooey mud puddle. 'Oink, oink! Come on in, Oliver, the mud is lovely!' Oliver looked down at his clean yellow feathers. He looked down at the dark, thick mud. Without another second of hesitation, Oliver jumped right in! SPLAT! Mud flew up to his left eye. SPLASH! Mud covered his right wing. 'Quack-quack-whee!' shouted Oliver with pure toddler glee.

Oliver and Oink spent the afternoon making mud pies. They patted the cool mud into Oliver's little yellow bucket, turned it upside down, and lifted it up. Ta-da! A perfect mud castle. They even decorated the top with a shiny green leaf and a smooth pebble. Oliver wiggled his toes deep into the mud. It squished between his webbed feet like warm chocolate pudding. They laughed and played until the sun began to sink low behind the big green hills.

Soon, Oliver heard a familiar voice calling across the grass. 'Time to wash up for dinner, little duckling!' called Papa Duck. Oliver looked at his muddy reflection in a puddle and giggled. He was as dirty as a little duck could possibly be! Together with Oink, Oliver waddled over to the clear, sparkling pond. He dove right under the water, shaking his feathers clean. Swish, swash, swirl! The mud washed away, leaving Oliver sparkling clean and ready for a cozy bedtime story.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy green park, there lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had soft, fluffy feathers, bright orange webbed feet, and a very loud, happy quack. Every morning, Pip would wake up and say, 'Quack, quack, good morning, sun!' One bright and sunny day, Pip went exploring by the big blue pond. The grass tickled his tummy as he waddled along. Waddle, waddle, waddle went Pip. Suddenly, Pip stopped. Right in the middle of the path was a giant, squishy, brown puddle! It looked so fun. Pip tilted his head and blinked his round black eyes. 'Can I splash?' he wondered. Pip took a little step closer. He dipped one orange webbed foot right into the mud. Squish! Squat! It felt cold, gooey, and tickly. Pip giggled. He loved the feeling of mud between his toes. Without waiting another second, Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle with a giant splash! Splash, splash, splash went water everywhere. Droplets flew up into the air like sparkling diamonds. Pip flapped his little yellow wings and shook his tail feathers. 'Quack-quack-hooray!' he cheered loudly. But oh dear, as Pip played, he got mud all over his yellow feathers. He looked like a chocolate duck instead of a yellow one! Just then, his mother, Mama Duck, came swimming by. 'Quack, hello there, little one,' she said with a gentle smile. 'Time to wash off that silly mud.' Pip waddled behind his mother back to the big blue pond. Slide! Pip hopped into the cool, refreshing water. He kicked his feet and splashed around. Swish, swash, swish went the water, cleaning every single speck of mud right off his feathers. Pip was clean and fluffy once more. He cuddled close to his mama, feeling happy, warm, and ready for his next big adventure in the park.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck Loses Her Quack
stories.text: Deep in the whispering reeds of Willow Creek lived a sweet little duck named Daffodil. Daffodil had a neat white collar of feathers and a lovely voice. Every afternoon, Daffodil would gather all her woodland friends for a singing concert by the water. The frogs would croak, the crickets would chirp, and Daffodil would sing her favorite song: 'Quack, quack, quack, look at my back!' The animals loved her cheerful music. But one chilly morning, Daffodil woke up with a tickle in her throat. She sat up in her nest of soft moss and tried to say good morning to the morning breeze. She opened her beak wide and pushed hard. 'Q-u-a-c-k...' she whispered, but nothing came out! Her voice was completely gone. Daffodil patted her throat with her wing. Oh no! Where was her quack? She felt very worried. How could she sing with her friends without her quack? Slowly, she waddled down to the water's edge where the turtles and frogs were waiting. 'Good morning, Daffodil!' chorused the frogs. Daffodil opened her beak and tried her very best. Squeak! A tiny, funny little squeak popped out instead of a big, proud quack. The little green frog blinked in surprise, and then he started to chuckle. Daffodil giggled too. It was a very silly sound! Soon, all her friends were making silly squeaks and whispers right along with her. They didn't need a loud quack to make music together. They tapped their feet on the muddy bank and made funny clicking noises with their beaks. Daffodil realized that even without her usual voice, she could still have fun and make beautiful music with the people she loved. And the very next morning, after drinking a big cup of warm pond water and resting her head, Daffodil opened her beak and shouted a huge, happy 'QUACK!' that echoed all across Willow Creek.

stories.title: Barnaby's Shiny Red Boots
stories.text: Barnaby was a very stylish little duck who lived on a cheerful farm with lots of noisy animal friends. Barnaby loved to look down at his feet. But every single day, his feet looked the exact same: bright orange and bare. Barnaby wanted something special. One sunny afternoon, while the farmer was busy working in the red barn, Barnaby waddled over to the front porch. There, sitting right by the screen door, was a tiny box. Barnaby peeked inside with his curious round eyes. Inside the box were two tiny, shiny, bright red rain boots! They had little yellow buckles and looked just the right size for a duck. Barnaby gasped with joy. 'Quack!' he whispered. He carefully stepped his left webbed foot into the left boot. Then he stepped his right webbed foot into the right boot. They fit like a glove! Barnaby stood up tall and proud. Tap, tap, tap went his new boots on the wooden porch. He had never heard such a wonderful sound before. He waddled down the steps and headed toward the farmyard to show everyone. First, he walked past the big brown cow. 'Moo,' said the cow. 'Look at those fancy shoes!' Barnaby beamed and shook his tail feathers. Next, he trotted past the fluffy white sheep. 'Baa,' said the sheep. 'Very handsome, Barnaby!' Barnaby felt like the most important duck in the whole wide world. But then, Barnaby saw the muddy pigpen. A big patch of wet mud sat right in front of him. Barnaby loved mud, but would his new boots get dirty? He hesitated for just a moment. Then he remembered that boots were made for splashing. With a happy squeal, Barnaby leaped right into the thickest, squishiest mud on the farm. Splash! The mud squished up the sides of his bright red boots. Barnaby laughed and clapped his wings together. His boots were red, his feet were happy, and it was the best day ever on the farm.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had soft fluffy feathers, two bright orange webbed feet, and a very loud, happy voice. Quack, quack, quack! Pip loved mornings because mornings meant it was time to play. Today, Pip woke up feeling extra brave. He stretched his little wings, shook his tail feathers, and waddled out of his cozy nest. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went his feet on the green grass. Pip was on a very important mission. He wanted to make the biggest, splashiest splash in the whole wide pond! As Pip walked down to the water, he met his friend Bella the butterfly. Hello, Pip! Where are you going? asked Bella. I am going to make a big splash! said Pip proudly. Bella fluttered her pretty wings. Good luck, Pip! At the edge of the water, Pip stopped. The water looked cool and refreshing. Little ripples danced in the breeze. Other ducks were already swimming around, gliding smoothly like little boats. Pip took a deep breath. He knew his feet were made for swimming, but today he wanted to try something extra special. He closed his eyes, counted to three in his duckling brain, and ran as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him. Splish, splash, splosh! Pip leaped right into the middle of the pond. Water flew high up into the air like sparkling diamonds. Drops landed on the lily pads. Drops landed on the tall green reeds. Splash, splash, splash! Pip came up to the surface with water dripping from his beak. He shook his head and laughed. Did you see me? I made a big splash! All the other ducks quapped and cheered. Bella the butterfly clapped her wings from a nearby flower. Pip felt so happy and proud. He paddled around in circles, kicking his feet and making little waves. Swimming in the pond was the best thing in the world. As the sun climbed higher in the sky, Pip felt a little bit tired from all his exciting jumping. He floated gently on the water, letting the tiny waves rock him back and forth like a cradle. Being a little duck was wonderful, and Pip could not wait to see what adventures tomorrow would bring.

stories.title: The Lost Feather
stories.text: Down by the edge of the whispering reeds, a little duck named Ducky Doodle was getting ready for a morning walk. Ducky Doodle had the shiniest green head and the softest gray feathers in the entire neighborhood. He loved to explore the tall grass, look for juicy green bugs, and chat with his animal friends. But today, something strange had happened. Ducky Doodle felt a little tickle on his back. He reached around with his beak to scratch it, but when he looked down, oh no! One of his favorite fluffy feathers was missing! It was a soft, downy feather that kept him extra warm on chilly nights. Ducky Doodle let out a worried little quack. Oh dear, where could my feather be? he wondered. He decided to retrace his steps and find his lost treasure. First, he waddled over to the muddy puddle where he had played yesterday. Squish, squach, squish went his webbed feet. He looked behind a big round stone. He looked under a pile of damp autumn leaves. But the feather was not there. Next, Ducky Doodle hopped up the little green hill to see his friend Sammy the squirrel. Hello, Sammy! Have you seen my fluffy feather? asked Ducky Doodle. Sammy stopped nibbling on an acorn and shook his fluffy head. No, Ducky Doodle, I haven't seen it, but let me help you look! Together, the duck and the squirrel searched everywhere. They looked behind the tree trunk. They looked in the patch of wild clover. Suddenly, a gentle breeze blew through the meadow. Whoosh! A soft white object fluttered down from the branches above. It danced in the air like a tiny parachute and landed right on top of Ducky Doodle's head. Ducky Doodle reached up with his wing and felt the soft texture. My feather! he cheered happily. It had been stuck in the low-hanging branches of the apple tree all along. Sammy the squirrel chattered with joy. Yay! You found it! Ducky Doodle tucked the feather safely back among his other feathers and gave a happy quack. He thanked his good friend Sammy and waddled all the way home, feeling warm, cozy, and very lucky indeed.

stories.title: Oliver's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Oliver was a curious little duck who lived near a wonderful, muddy farm. Oliver had bright orange feet that were always ready for an adventure and a yellow bill that loved to explore. Unlike some ducks who liked to stay clean and neat in the clear blue water, Oliver had a secret love for the biggest, squishiest mud puddles he could find. One rainy afternoon, after a heavy downpour, the farmyard was covered in magnificent puddles of brown, gooey mud. Oliver poked his head out of his cozy little duck house and sniffed the air. Mmm, he thought, it smells like adventure! He stepped outside and shook his tail feathers. Squish! went his left foot into the soft earth. Squosh! went his right foot. Oliver smiled from beak to tail. He waddled across the yard, leaving a trail of funny webbed footprints behind him. Right in the middle of the path was the biggest puddle of all. It bubbled slightly when the wind blew. Oliver walked right up to the edge and peeked in. He could see his own reflection staring back at him. Hello there, reflection duck! said Oliver with a friendly quack. Without another second of hesitation, Oliver jumped right into the center of the mud puddle. Splash! Mud flew everywhere. It dotted his yellow tummy. It speckled his little wings. It even left a tiny brown dot right on the tip of his bill. Oliver thought it was the most fun thing in the entire world. He flapped his wings and kicked his feet, making mud pies all around him. Soon, his friend Barnaby the pig trotted over. Oink, oink! Can I join you, Oliver? asked Barnaby. Of course! said Oliver. The two friends splashed and played in the mud until they were completely covered from head to toe, or rather, from beak to hoof. But wait! How would Oliver get clean before bedtime? His mother duck would be surprised! Luckily, there was a sparkling clean stream just a few steps away. Oliver and Barnaby waded into the clear water. Swish, swish, went their bodies as they washed away all the brown mud. The water turned a little bit brown, but Oliver was sparkling clean again. He shook off the water droplets, fluffed his soft feathers, and waddled back home, ready for a cozy, peaceful sleep after his wonderfully muddy day.

stories.title: Pip's Big Yellow Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a little yellow duck named Pip. Pip had soft, fluffy feathers and feet that went web, web, web when he walked in the mud. Today was a very special day because Pip received a brand new pair of shiny red boots in the mail! They were bright, they were bold, and they squeaked with every single step. Squeak, squawk, squeak went the boots as Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. He could not wait to show all of his farmyard friends his wonderful new footwear. First, Pip waddled over to the muddy puddle where Barnaby the pig was rolling around. Hello, Barnaby! Look at my brand new boots! said Pip proudly, lifting up his webbed foot. Barnaby grunted happily and splashed a tiny bit of mud right onto the toe. Oh no! cried Pip, but then he giggled because mud is actually quite fun. Next, Pip waddled down the grassy hill to find Tessa the cow. Moo, what lovely red shoes, said Tessa, chewing on some sweet green clover. Pip felt so proud that he did a little spinning dance. Squeak, squeak, squeak went the boots in the green grass. But then, dark gray clouds rolled across the sky, and big, fat raindrops began to fall. Plip, plop, plip went the rain. Pip did not want to get his new boots ruined, so he quickly waddled back toward the big red barn for shelter. Along the way, he met Sammy the snail, who was crawling very slowly on a broad green leaf. Hello, Sammy! Do you want to ride on my boot? asked kind little Pip. Sammy smiled and crawled right onto the shiny red surface. Pip walked very carefully so his tiny friend would not fall off. Finally, they reached the safety of the barn just as the rain stopped pouring. The sun came back out, warming the wet earth with its golden rays. Pip looked down at his boots and realized they were muddy, wet, and utterly perfect. He had shared a wonderful adventure with his friends and kept a little snail dry. Pip took off his boots, patted his tummy, and decided that being a helpful duck in squeaky boots was the best job in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck's Morning Bath
stories.text: Every single morning when the sun peeked over the green hills, Daffodil Duck woke up with a big stretch and a loud quack! Quack, quack, good morning, world! she sang to the tall oak trees. Daffodil was a very neat duck with feathers as white as puffy clouds and a beak as bright as a ripe lemon. But today, Daffodil had a tiny problem. Her feathers were ruffled, her head tuft was sticking straight up in the air like a funny little fountain, and she felt quite messy indeed. It was time for her morning bath in the glistening blue pond. Daffodil waddled down the winding dirt path, her tail feathers shaking with excitement. Waddle, waddle, waddle went her feet. When she reached the water's edge, she dipped just one webbed toe into the cool, refreshing ripples. Brrr! she giggled, pulling her foot right back up. But the water felt too good to resist for long. With a brave little leap, Daffodil launched herself right into the middle of the pond. Splash! Water droplets flew everywhere like glittering diamonds in the sunshine. Daffodil bobbed up and down like a little white boat on the waves. She tucked her head under the water and swished it around, washing away the sleepies. Then she flapped her strong wings, creating a magnificent spray of bubbles and foam. A tiny green frog sitting on a lily pad croaked a cheerful song, cheering her on. Daffodil cleaned her beak with her wing, smoothed down her chest feathers until they shone, and gave her tail a happy wiggle. Now she was the cleanest, prettiest duck in the whole pond. She swam in a circle, practicing her fancy floating tricks. Being a duck was simply wonderful, especially when bath time was this much fun. With a happy sigh, Daffodil paddled off to find some crunchy lily stems for breakfast, ready for whatever playful adventures the afternoon might bring.

stories.title: The Great Pond Search
stories.text: Little Quacker was a very curious duckling with bright orange feet and an insatiable appetite for discovery. One bright afternoon, Quacker lost his favorite shiny blue marble right near the edge of the rushing stream. Oh dear, oh dear! Where could it be? he quacked, peering into the tall green reeds. Determined to find his precious toy, Quacker set off on a grand search across the meadow. First, he waddled past a patch of sweet-smelling yellow daisies. He peeked underneath their bright petals, but there was no marble to be found—only a sleepy bumblebee buzzing a soft lullaby. Hello, bee! Have you seen my blue marble? asked Quacker politely. The bee shook its fuzzy head and flew away to the next flower. Next, Quacker waddled toward the old wooden bridge where Oliver the owl sat blinking in the shade. Hoo-hoo, little duck, what are you looking for today? asked wise old Oliver in a low, gentle voice. I lost my shiny blue marble, and I cannot find it anywhere, explained Quacker with a little sigh. Oliver tilted his head and pointed a feathery wing toward the water. Look where the minnows play, where the water is clear and bright. Quacker thanked the owl and hurried back to the stream. He lowered his beak right down to the shallow water and peered beneath a smooth, mossy stone. And guess what he saw? There it was! The shiny blue marble was resting right in the middle of the sparkling pebbles, looking just like a fallen piece of the sky. Quacker scooped it up gently with his beak and did a happy little victory dance right on the muddy bank. He had searched high and low, solved a mystery, and found his favorite treasure. With the marble safely tucked under his wing, Quacker waddled happily back home to his nest, smiling all the way.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of a bright green park, lived a very little duck named Pip. Pip had soft yellow feathers that looked like fluffy buttercups and webbed orange feet that went squish-squash, squish-squash in the damp grass. Pip loved mornings because mornings meant it was time to visit the big blue pond. Today, Pip was feeling extra brave. 'Quack, quack!' he said to his mother. 'I am ready for a big splash!' Mother Duck smiled and wagged her tail feathers. 'Lead the way, my little duckling,' she gently quacked. Pip waddled as fast as his little legs could carry him. He passed the tall green reeds where the buzzing dragonflies danced. He passed a friendly brown frog who said, 'Ribbit, ribbit, good morning, Pip!' Pip waved a wing and kept on walking. Soon, the sparkling blue water came into view. The pond looked like a giant mirror reflecting the fluffy white clouds in the sky. Other little ducklings were already swimming in circles, making happy peep-peep sounds. Pip hurried right to the very edge of the water. He looked down and saw his own reflection staring back at him. He dipped one orange webbed foot into the cool water. Brrr! It felt so refreshing. But Pip did not just want to dip his foot. He wanted to swim! He took a deep breath, flapped his tiny wings, and waddled right off the muddy bank. Whoosh! Pip went sliding right into the water. Splash! Water droplets flew everywhere like sparkling diamonds in the sunlight. Pip popped right back up to the surface, bobbing up and down like a little yellow cork. 'Look at me!' cheered Pip. 'I am swimming all by myself!' He kicked his webbed feet and paddled in a circle. He chased a friendly little floating leaf and played hide-and-seek behind a green lily pad. Swimming was the most fun thing in the entire world. When the sun began to get warm and high in the sky, Pip climbed back onto the grassy bank. He shook his feathers until they were dry and fluffed up just like a pillow. He snuggled close to his mother for a nice afternoon nap, dreaming of all the splashing adventures waiting for him tomorrow.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck Finds a Friend
stories.text: Down by the winding river, where the sweet-smelling wildflowers grew, lived a gentle duck named Daffodil. Daffodil had feathers as white as snow and a bright orange beak that was always curved into a happy smile. Daffodil was a very friendly duck, but today she felt a little bit lonely. All of her duck family members were busy taking a nap in the warm afternoon sun. 'Quack,' whispered Daffodil softly. 'Who wants to play a game with me today?' She decided to take a little stroll along the riverbank to see who she could find. She waddled past a patch of purple clover and tiptoed around a smooth gray rock. Suddenly, she heard a funny sound coming from inside a hollow log. It sounded like rustling leaves and quiet giggles. 'Hello? Is anyone in there?' asked Daffodil, tilting her head to the side. Out popped a small, furry head with twitching whiskers and two big round eyes. It was Barnaby, a fluffy little bunny with long floppy ears. Barnaby looked a bit surprised, but when he saw Daffodil's kind face, his nose stopped twitching and he smiled. 'Hello,' said the bunny softly. 'I am hiding from the bouncing grasshoppers.' Daffodil let out a friendly little quack. 'You do not need to hide anymore! Do you want to play a game with me?' Barnaby hopped right out of the log, his fluffy cotton-tail bobbing up and down. 'I would love to play! What game should we play?' Daffodil thought for a moment. 'Let us play follow the leader!' she chirped. Daffodil waddled down the grassy slope, and Barnaby hopped right behind her, boing, boing, boing! Then it was Barnaby's turn to lead. He hopped in zigzag patterns through the yellow daisies, and Daffodil waddled quickly behind him, trying her very best to keep up. They played and played until they were both wonderfully tired. They sat down together under the shade of a big leafy willow tree. Daffodil shared a crunchy green leaf, and Barnaby shared a sweet dandelion treat. They were very different animals, but they knew right away that they would be best friends forever.

stories.title: The Muddy Footprint Mystery
stories.text: It was a wonderful, rainy afternoon on the farm, and puddles were everywhere. Puddles are a duck's absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world! Barnaby the duck loved to march right through the middle of them. Squish, squash, squelch went his orange webbed feet as he walked near the red barn. Suddenly, Barnaby stopped in his tracks. Right there in the soft mud near the garden gate was a very strange mark. It looked like a footprint, but it was much bigger than a duck's foot, and it had funny little round toes. 'Quack?' wondered Barnaby aloud. 'What kind of creature made this big muddy print?' He decided to become a detective duck and follow the trail of muddy footprints to solve the mystery. He put on an imaginary detective hat and lowered his head to the ground. The first footprint led past the wooden fence where the black-and-white cows lived. Barnaby looked up and asked, 'Moo, cow, did you make this big muddy track?' The cow lazily chewed some grass and shook her head. 'Moo-no, little duck, that wasn't me.' Barnaby kept on following the trail. The muddy footprints went past the fluffy sheep who were munching on clover. 'Baa, sheep, was it you?' asked Barnaby. The sheep shook their woolly heads and said, 'Baa-no, not us!' The trail kept going and going until it led right to the big green vegetable patch. Barnaby tiptoed very quietly. He peeked behind a large pumpkin, and guess what he saw? There sat little Pip, his cousin, covered in mud from head to toe, holding a giant shiny watering can! Pip giggled and shook his tail feathers, spraying muddy water everywhere. 'Surprise!' quapped Pip happily. 'I made the funny footprints because I was doing a rain dance!' Barnaby laughed a big belly laugh. The mystery of the muddy footprints was finally solved. Without another second to waste, Barnaby jumped right into the biggest puddle he could find and splashed mud right along with his cousin. They had the most wonderful, messy, muddy time until the rain clouds finally went away and the golden sun came out to dry them off.

stories.title: Pip the Duck's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Pip loved sunny mornings. He loved the bright blue sky. But most of all, Pip loved puddles. Today, after a big rainstorm, the biggest puddle in the whole wide yard was waiting just for him. Pip flapped his tiny wings. Quack, quack, he cheered! He waddled as fast as his webbed feet could carry him right over to the sparkling water. Splash! Pip jumped right into the middle. Mud squished between his toes. It felt wonderfully squishy and warm. Pip kicked his legs. Water droplets flew up into the air like little diamonds. He dipped his yellow bill under the surface and blew bubbles. Blub, blub, blub! A little green frog hopped by on a lily pad. Ribbit, said the frog. Can I play too? Yes, yes! quack Pip. Come splash with me! The frog leaped into the puddle with a little splash. They splashed and giggled together, making giant waves. Soon, Mama Duck came waddling over. She looked at Pip, who was now covered in mud from his head to his tail feathers. My goodness, Pip, you are a very muddy duckling, Mama said with a gentle smile. But Pip just smiled back and shook his feathers, sending water flying everywhere. Quack, I am having so much fun, Mama! Time to wash off, little one, Mama Duck gently nudged Pip toward the clean blue pond. They swam in circles, cleaning the mud away. Pip floated on his back and watched a fluffy white cloud float by. It was the best day ever.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck Finds a Friend
stories.text: Down by the edge of the whispering reeds lived a cheerful little duck named Daffodil. Daffodil had feathers as soft as dandelion fluff and a bright orange beak that was always smiling. Every morning, Daffodil went on a walk to find something new. Today, she heard a strange sound coming from beneath a big green leaf. Rustle, rustle, squeak. Daffodil stopped and tilted her head. She blinked her round black eyes. She took one step closer. Quack? she whispered softly, not wanting to scare whoever was hiding. The leaf trembled, and a tiny gray mouse peeked out. The mouse was shivering and looked very sad. Hello, little mouse, said Daffodil in her kindest voice. Why are you hiding? The mouse sniffled and rubbed his nose with a tiny paw. I lost my favorite acorn, and now I am all alone, he squeaked. Daffodil wanted to help her new little friend. Do not worry, she said cheerfully. Two sets of eyes are better than one. Let us look together! Daffodil and the mouse searched all around the riverbank. They looked under smooth grey stones. They looked behind the tall green grass. Finally, Daffodil stretched her neck and peeked inside a hollow log. Aha! There it was, shining in the dark. Daffodil scooped the acorn up with her beak and gently placed it right in front of the mouse. The mouse did a happy little dance. Yay! You found it! Thank you so much, Daffodil Duck! Daffodil quack-smiled and wrapped her wing around her new friend. From that day on, the duck and the mouse did everything together. They shared snacks, played hide and seek in the flowers, and watched the golden sunsets over the water. Daffodil learned that helping a friend made her heart feel as warm as summer sunshine.

stories.title: The Great Feather Tickle
stories.text: The sun was beginning to set, painting the evening sky in shades of pink and purple. It was almost bedtime down by the lily pond. Little Barnaby Duck was tucked into his nest of soft reeds, but he was not sleepy at all. His eyes were wide open like two shiny buttons. Barnaby rolled to the left. He rolled to the right. He let out a loud, bouncy quack. Mama Duck patted him gently with her wing. Time to rest, little duckling, she whispered softly. Close your eyes and dream of sweet things. But Barnaby giggled. He did not want to sleep yet. He had a silly plan. He waddled quietly over to his brother, who was already snoring softly. Snore, quack, snore. Barnaby plucked one of his own soft, fluffy down feathers. He held it tightly in his bill. Then, very carefully, he tickled his brother's nose. Tickle, tickle, tickle! The brother duck sneezed a big, funny sneeze. Achoo! Then he opened his eyes and giggled. Who did that? Barnaby laughed and hid behind a broad green leaf. But his orange webbed feet were sticking out, giving him away. Oh, I see you, Barnaby! said his brother, and he reached out to tickle Barnaby right back under his wing. Soon, all the little ducklings were giggling and tickling each other in a pile of soft feathers. Giggles bubbled up like water in a spring. Mama Duck laughed too. Well, I suppose a little play is good before bed, she said warmly. She gathered all her little ducklings into a cozy circle and wrapped them in her warm wings. They listened to the gentle lullaby of the wind blowing through the reeds. Barnaby closed his eyes, feeling safe and loved. He drifted off to sleep with a happy smile on his little bill.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Pip loved sunny mornings. He loved the soft green grass beneath his webbed feet. Quack, quack! went Pip as he stretched his little wings. Today, Pip was on a mission. He wanted to find the biggest, squishiest puddle in the whole wide farmyard. Mommy Duck smiled and said, 'Be careful, Pip! Keep your feathers clean!' But Pip had other plans. He waddled past the big red barn. He waddled past the sleepy old tractor. Then, he heard a funny sound. Slurp, squelch, splash! What could that be? Pip hurried as fast as his little legs could carry him. Round the corner of the vegetable patch, right by the wooden fence, there it was. The most magnificent puddle in the world! It was big. It was brown. It was wonderfully muddy. Pip stopped right at the edge. He poked his beak into the brown water. It was cool. It was wet. It was perfect. Pip did not want to stay clean today. He wanted to play! With a happy little wiggle of his tail feathers, Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle. Splash! Mud flew up into the air. Mud landed on his yellow tummy. Mud even landed on top of his head. 'Quack-quack-wheee!' shouted Pip with joy. He kicked his feet and made giant bubbles in the mud. He flapped his wings and made brown waves. Oh, what a messy duck! Just then, Mommy Duck came walking over. She looked at muddy Pip and gasped. Pip held his breath. Would Mommy be mad? Mommy Duck tilted her head, looked at the happy little duckling, and smiled. Then, Mommy Duck jumped right into the puddle too! Splash! Mud flew everywhere. Mommy and Pip splashed together until they were the muddiest ducks on the farm. When playtime was over, they waddled down to the sparkling blue pond. They dove beneath the cool water and washed all the mud away. Pip shook his feathers until they were fluffy and dry. 'That was the best day ever,' thought Pip, snuggling close to his mommy for a well-deserved afternoon nap.

stories.title: The Lost Feather
stories.text: Little Ducky was getting ready for bed. The sun was sinking low behind the hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink and orange. The farm was growing quiet. Cows were sleeping in the pasture, and sheep were dozing in the meadow. Little Ducky fluffed his soft downy feathers. But wait! Something felt strange. Little Ducky reached out a wing and patted his back. Oh no! One of his softest, fluffiest feathers was missing! It was his favorite feather, the one that kept him extra warm when the night wind blew. 'Quack,' whimpered Little Ducky softly. He looked under his nest. The feather was not there. He looked behind the large green fern. The feather was not there either. Little Ducky decided he must go on a search. He could not sleep without his special feather! He waddled quietly down the path. First, he met Barnaby the brown bunny. 'Hello, Barnaby,' whispered Little Ducky. 'Have you seen my fluffy feather?' Barnaby twitched his long nose and wiggled his cotton tail. 'No, Little Ducky, I haven't seen it, but let me help you look!' Together, they hopped and waddled past the sleeping chickens. Next, they met Bella the fluffy sheep. 'Baa,' said Bella softly. 'Have you seen the little yellow feather?' Bella shook her curly white head. 'I haven't, but I will help you look too!' Now there was a little duck and a bunny and a sheep searching through the twilight. They looked near the wooden trough. They looked by the garden gate. Suddenly, a gentle breeze blew through the trees. Whoosh! A soft, yellow object floated down from the branches of the old apple tree. It drifted gracefully through the air like a tiny parachute. Little Ducky watched it closely. Down, down, down it came, right onto the top of Little Ducky's head! Little Ducky reached up with his beak and touched it. It was warm. It was soft. It was his very own missing feather! 'Quack, hooray!' cheered Little Ducky happily. Barnaby clapped his paws, and Bella gave a happy little baa. Little Ducky tucked the feather safely back into his wing. He thanked his good friends for their help. Then, with a happy heart and a very sleepy yawn, Little Ducky waddled back to his cozy nest, closed his eyes, and drifted off to dreamland.

stories.title: Puddle Dancing
stories.text: Drip, drop, drip, drop! Rain was falling on the farm. Big, fat raindrops fell from the grey clouds and tapped gently on the roof of the barn. Tap, tap, tap! Some animals do not like the rain. The fluffy cats run inside to stay dry. The horses stand under the big oak tree to keep their coats from getting soaked. But for Daisy the duck, rain was the most exciting thing in the entire world! Daisy woke up, stretched her wings, and let out a happy quack. Rain meant puddles! And puddles meant dancing! Daisy hopped out of her cozy coop and stepped right out into the wet yard. The ground was spongy and soft. Everywhere she looked, there were shiny puddles reflecting the grey sky. Daisy lifted her right webbed foot. Tap! Then she lifted her left webbed foot. Tap! She was doing a special rain dance. Tap-tap-tap, splash-splash-splash! She spun around in a circle, her yellow feathers glowing bright against the gloomy day. 'Quack-quack, dance with me!' she called out to the farmyard. Soon, a little brown frog hopped over from the pond. The frog sat on the edge of a puddle and croaked a beat. Ribbit, croak, ribbit, croak! Daisy used the frog's music to make her dance even sillier. She waddled forward. She waddled backward. She shook her tail feathers from side to side. She dipped her bill into the cool puddle water and flicked sparkling drops of water into the air. They glittered like tiny diamonds in the grey light. More animals started to watch from their dry spots. A little calf mooed in delight. A baby chick chirped a cheerful tune. Daisy was so happy making everyone smile on a rainy day. She splashed through one puddle, then two puddles, then three puddles! Water flew everywhere, making big ripples in the calm rain pools. By the time the clouds started to part and the golden sun peeked back out, Daisy was wonderfully wet and wonderfully tired. A rainbow stretched across the sky in brilliant colors of red, yellow, green, and blue. Daisy looked up at the rainbow, gave one last happy quack, and waddled back home, ready for a long winter's nap after her big day of puddle dancing.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Pip waddled out of his cozy nest. Pip loved sunny mornings. He loved the bright blue sky. But most of all, Pip loved puddles. Big puddles, small puddles, round puddles, and squishy puddles! Today, the farmyard had the biggest, squishiest puddle of all right by the old red barn.

'Quack, quack!' cheered Pip, flapping his tiny wings. He hurried as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him. He reached the edge of the great puddle and peeked inside. He saw his own little round face looking back at him. 'Hello, water friend!' Pip quacked happily.

Without a single second of hesitation, Pip jumped right in. Splish, splash, splosh! Brown muddy water flew up into the air. It landed on his yellow feathers. It landed on his little orange beak. Pip laughed and kicked his feet, making bubbles rise to the surface. 'Whee!' he shouted. He paddled in circles, feeling like the happiest duck in the whole wide world.

Soon, his friend Barnaby the bunny came hopping down the path. 'Hello, Pip!' said Barnaby, twitching his nose. 'You look very muddy today.' Pip shook his tail feathers, sending mud drops flying everywhere. 'Quack! Mud is the best!' invited Pip. 'Come and join the fun, Barnaby!' But Barnaby shook his head. Bunnies do not like getting their soft fur muddy. Instead, Barnaby picked up a little wooden stick and tossed it gently into the puddle. 'Fetch the stick, brave captain Pip!' whispered Barnaby.

Pip swam after the floating stick, pushing it along with his beak. He felt like a grand pirate ship sailing across a chocolate sea. When he reached the other side, he pushed the stick ashore. Barnaby clapped his paws. 'Horray for Captain Pip!' 

By now, the sun was getting high in the sky. Pip was tired, and his tummy began to rumble. Time for lunch! Pip climbed out of the wonderful mud puddle, leaving a trail of funny little muddy footprints behind him. 'Quack, quack, thank you, puddle!' said Pip. He waddled over to his mother to eat some crunchy green lettuce, already dreaming of the next big puddle he would find tomorrow.

stories.title: The Lost Feather
stories.text:
Little duckling Daisy loved playing hide-and-seek in the tall, green reeds by the riverbank. The river was her playground. Today, she was playing with her best friend, Oliver the frog. 'One, two, three, four, five! Ready or not, here I come!' quacked Daisy, covering her eyes with her webbed wing.

Oliver leaped high into the air and hid beneath a giant lily pad. Daisy waddled through the tall grass, peeking behind buttercups and looking under smooth river stones. 'Where are you, Oliver?' she asked, giggling. Suddenly, a gentle breeze blew through the meadow. Whoosh! The wind tickled Daisy's back. Something felt a little bit different. Daisy reached back with her beak and felt a tickle. Oh no! One of her very favorite fluffy grey feathers had come loose and floated away on the wind!

'My feather! My special feather!' cried Daisy, chasing after it. The feather drifted gracefully through the air like a tiny parachute. It floated over a patch of red clover. It floated past a busy bumblebee. Daisy ran as fast as her little legs could go, flapping her wings to help her run faster. 'Wait, feather, wait!' she called out.

The wind carried the feather right toward the edge of the river. Oh no! If it fell into the water and floated away, it would be gone forever. Daisy stretched out her neck. She stretched out her beak as far as it could possibly reach. Just as the feather touched the tip of the water, *snip!* Daisy caught it safely in her beak!

She pulled the feather back and held it tightly. Oliver popped his head out from under the lily pad and croaked, 'Ribbit! Good catch, Daisy!' Daisy smiled proudly, tucking the soft feather safely back beneath her wing. 'Found you, Oliver!' she giggled, forgetting all about hide-and-seek as they both splashed happily into the cool blue river together.

stories.title: Quacky's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text:
The sun was slowly sinking behind the green hills, painting the sky in shades of pink, purple, and gold. High up in the oak tree, little birds were tucking their heads under their wings. Down by the quiet pond, it was time for little duckling Quacky to get ready for sleep.

Quacky was still wide awake. He stood on the soft mossy bank, flapping his wings. 'I am not sleepy, Mama Duck!' he quacked, shaking his head. Mama Duck smiled warmly. She gently nuzzled Quacky with her soft bill. 'Even little ducks need to rest their wings, my sweet duckling,' she whispered softly.

Let us go for one last gentle ride before bed, suggested Mama Duck. Quacky hopped onto the water, and Mama Duck glided out in front. Quacky paddled right behind her. The water was as smooth as a sheet of glass. It mirrored the twinkling stars that were just beginning to pop out in the darkening sky. *Splash, swish, splash, swish* went their webbed feet, making gentle ripples in the pond.

A sleepy-eyed dragonfly buzzed softly overhead, saying goodnight. A little brown frog sat on a log and sang a low, rumbling song. *Ribbit, ribbit, time for sleep.* Quacky let out a tiny yawn. His eyelids felt heavy, like they had little rocks attached to them. The day had been so long and so full of fun adventures, and now his little muscles felt tired.

Mama Duck swam over to a cozy nest made of soft reeds and warm feathers hidden safely beneath the weeping willow tree. 'Here we are, Quacky,' she murmured. Quacky waddled into the nest and curled up tightly against his mother's warm, fluffy feathers. He closed his eyes and listened to the gentle lapping of the water against the shore.

'Goodnight, stars,' whispered Quacky sleepily. 'Goodnight, moon.' Mama Duck sang a quiet, soothing duck lullaby, and within moments, little Quacky was fast asleep, dreaming of tomorrow's sunny swims.

stories.title: Daffy Duck's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Daffy woke up with a very big stretch. Quack, quack, quack! Today was a special day because it had rained all night long, and that meant one wonderful thing: puddles. Daffy waddled out of his cozy nest and flapped his soft wings. He looked down at his webbed orange feet. They wiggled with excitement. Outside, the grass was bright green and sparkling with shiny raindrops. Daffy waddled down the grassy hill, going waddle, waddle, waddle, splash! He stopped right at the edge of the biggest, muddiest puddle in the whole backyard. It was brown, squishy, and looked like the most fun place on the entire farm. Daffy dipped one webbed foot right into the mud. Squish! It felt cool and squiggly between his toes. He giggled and stepped all the way in. Splash, splash, go the little duck feet! He flapped his wings and sent shiny brown droplets flying into the air. Oh, how he loved the mud. Suddenly, his friend Barnaby the bunny hopped over, twitching his nose. Hello, Daffy! said Barnaby. Can I play in the puddle too? Of course you can, quacked Daffy. Puddles are for sharing. Barnaby dipped a furry paw into the water, but quickly pulled it back with a sneeze. Brrr, it is too squishy for me! chuckled the bunny. That is okay, smiled Daffy. You can watch me do a silly duck dance. Daffy spun around in a circle, flapping his wings and singing his favorite quacking song. Quack, quack, quack, splash, splash, splash! Barnaby clapped his paws and giggled. By lunchtime, Daffy was covered in mud from his bill to his tail feathers. His mother duck called out, Time to wash up, little one! Daffy waddled over to the sparkling pond. He dove right in, doing a happy belly flop. Swish, swish went the water, washing all the mud away until he was bright yellow again. Daffy shook his feathers dry, ready for his afternoon nap in the warm sunshine, dreaming of even more puddles for tomorrow.

stories.title: The Little Duck Who Lost His Quack
stories.text: Down by the blue, winding river lived a fluffy little duckling named Pip. Pip was a very happy duckling who loved to talk to everyone he met. He would say hello to the buzzing bees, good morning to the leaping frogs, and chat with the tall green reeds. But one bright Tuesday morning, something very strange happened. Pip woke up, opened his bill wide, and tried to say his morning greeting. He pushed hard, but no sound came out at all. He tried again. Quack! But instead of a loud, cheerful quack, all that came out was a tiny, squeaky whisper. Squeak! Pip gasped and put his wings over his beak. Oh no, he whispered in his little squeaky voice. I have lost my big duck quack! Pip was very worried. How could he talk to his friends without his proper quack? He waddled quickly over to his wise old grandmother, who was floating peacefully near the lily pads. Good morning, Grandma, whispered Pip, sounding like a tiny mouse. His grandmother looked at him with kind, twinkling eyes. What is the matter, my little feather ball? she asked softly. I lost my quack, Pip cried. I only have a squeak now. Grandmother duck smiled warmly and patted his head with her wing. Do not worry, little one. Sometimes when we use our voices too much, they just need a little rest. Let us drink some cool river water together. Pip dipped his bill into the sparkling water and took a long, refreshing sip. Then, he sat quietly on a smooth stone, listening to the gentle breeze rustling through the trees and the water lapping against the shore. He closed his eyes and breathed in the fresh air. After a little while, he felt much better. He opened his bill, took a deep breath, and tried once more. QUACK! It was the loudest, most wonderful quack he had ever made. The frogs jumped in surprise, and the bees buzzed happily. Pip danced a little jig on his rock, so glad to have his big voice back, and promised to take good care of it forever.

stories.title: Pip's Big Swimming Adventure
stories.text: The sun was peeking over the rolling green hills, painting the sky in shades of pink and orange. It was a brand new day at the duck pond, and today was the biggest day of little duckling Oliver's life. Today, he was going to swim in the deep end of the pond for the very first time. Up until now, Oliver had only splashed in the shallow puddles by the muddy bank. He was a little bit nervous. His heart went thump, thump, thump inside his fluffy chest. What if the water was too deep? What if his webbed feet forgot how to paddle? His mother duck gently nudged him forward with her soft bill. You are ready, my sweet Oliver, she encouraged him. Just trust your wings and your wonderful webbed feet. Oliver took a deep breath and took one tiny waddle forward. Waddle, waddle, slide! He went right down the grassy slope and slipped into the cool, blue water. At first, he gasped and fluttered his wings, feeling a little flutter of fear. But then, something amazing happened. He did not sink at all. His fluffy feathers kept him floating right on top of the water like a little yellow boat. Oliver looked down and saw his bright orange feet kicking beneath the surface. Kick, kick, go the little feet! Splash, splash, go the happy wings! Oh, this is wonderful! Oliver quacked with pure joy. He paddled past a friendly green frog sitting on a lily pad. Ribbit, good job, little duck! croaked the frog. Oliver swam in big circles, feeling braver and braver with every stroke. He chased a little floating leaf and played hide and seek with his brothers and sisters beneath the weeping willow tree. By the time the sun began to set, painting the evening sky purple, Oliver was the happiest duck in the whole wide world. He swam right back to the cozy nest, snuggled up close to his mother, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of endless blue water and bright sunny adventures.

stories.title: Daffodil Duck's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, a little yellow duck named Daffodil woke up with a big stretch. Quack, quack, good morning world! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, which meant one thing: giant puddles everywhere. Daffodil waddled out of her cozy nest and flapped her soft wings. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went her webbed feet on the green grass. She marched right over to the biggest, squishiest mud puddle in the whole farmyard. It was glorious. Daffodil stopped at the edge and looked down. She could see her own cute little face staring back at her from the shiny brown water. Should she jump in? Of course she should! With a happy little squeak, Daffodil leaped right into the middle. Splash! Mud went up, mud went down, and mud landed right on top of her head. It was warm and squishy between her toes. Daffodil loved the mud. She kicked her feet and made big bubbly waves. Splash, splash, splash! Soon, her duckling friends came running over to see what all the fuss was about. Pip and Squeak stopped at the edge and tilted their heads. They looked at the muddy water, and then they looked at Daffodil. Come on in, the mud is lovely, Daffodil quack-quacked, shaking her tail feathers. Pip jumped in with a big splat. Squeak followed right behind him with a joyful peep. Now there were three happy ducks splashing together in the giant puddle. They pretended they were brave explorers sailing across a chocolate ocean. They paddled in circles and blew bubbles under the water. When they finally hopped out, they shook themselves dry, sending sparkling droplets flying everywhere. Daffodil looked down at her muddy feathers and giggled. What a wonderful, messy, magnificent day to be a little yellow duck.

stories.title: The Great Pond Race
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the blue pond, and the tall green reeds were dancing in the gentle breeze. Little Quacker, a fluffy duckling with bright orange feet, stood at the starting line with his best friends. Today was the day of the Great Pond Race all the way to the big weeping willow tree. Are you ready? asked Mama Duck, standing on the big flat rock. Quacker puffed out his little yellow chest and nodded very seriously. Ready, set, quack! cried Mama Duck. Zoom! Off they went across the water. Quacker paddled as fast as his little webbed feet could go. Kick, kick, kick! Little ripples spread out behind him in shiny V-shapes. But oh no, a big green lily pad was right in his path. Quacker gently bumped his beak against it. Boing! He giggled and bounced right off, changing direction just a little bit. A friendly blue dragonfly zipped past his ear, buzzing a cheerful song to cheer him on. Quacker flapped his wings to help him glide faster over the sparkling water. He was catching up to his friend Barnaby, who was paddling with all his might. Just a little bit further now, thought Quacker. He could see the long hanging branches of the weeping willow tree dipping right down into the cool water. With one final big push, Quacker glided past the finish line. Hooray! shouted Mama Duck from the shore. Quacker spun around in a happy circle, spraying water drops everywhere. All the ducklings crowded around, cheering and splashing together. Even though it was a race, everyone crossed the finish line together, making it the best race in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Ducky's Lost Feather
stories.text: Barnaby Duck was getting ready for bed when he noticed something very strange. He reached back to smooth his fluffy tail feathers, but wait a minute. One of his favorite blue feathers was missing! Oh no, whispered Barnaby, looking very sad. It was his lucky feather, the one that kept him extra warm at night. He decided he must go on a quick nighttime search before the stars came out. Barnaby waddled softly across the dark green grass, keeping his eyes wide open. He looked under the big wooden wheelbarrow. Is my feather under here? he asked a sleeping ladybug. The ladybug just snored a little tiny snore. Barnaby kept walking, his webbed feet making a soft rustling sound in the clover. Next, he checked behind the bright red watering can. He peeked inside a big empty flower pot. Nothing there! Barnaby let out a little sigh that sounded like a soft breeze. Just then, a bright beam of moonlight shone down on the garden path. Right there, resting gently on top of a soft tuft of dandelion fluff, was a flash of bright blue. My feather! Barnaby squeaked with pure joy. A playful night breeze must have carried it away while he was playing earlier. Barnaby waddled over as fast as he could and scooped up his lost feather in his beak. He tucked it safely back into his tail feathers, wiggling his bottom happily to make sure it was snug and secure. Feeling warm and safe once again, Barnaby waddled back to his cozy nest under the big oak tree. He closed his sleepy eyes, tucked his head under his wing, and dreamed sweet dreams about flying high up into the starry night sky.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings swimming in a row,
Looking for a place where the green weeds grow.
The first little duckling said, 'Let us dive deep!'
The second little duckling said, 'Time for a sleep.'
The third little duckling found a shiny round stone,
And carried it away to call it his own.
The fourth little duckling chased a yellow bee,
And flapped his little wings right up in a tree.
The fifth little duckling said, 'Quack, quack, hello!'
To all the happy fishes swimming down below.
Mama Duck arrived and called out with delight,
'Come along, my babies, the sun is shining bright!'
They waddled all together back to their cozy nest,
Of all the little ducklings, these five are the best.
They tucked in their heads and closed their sleepy eyes,
Dreaming of the pond under starry skies.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duckling walking by the pool,
Water in the middle looks so bright and cool.
He sees a patch of mud that is soft and brown,
And tumbles right into it upside down.
Splash goes the water, splat goes the mud,
Right on the feathers of our little bud.
He wiggles his tail and he shakes his head,
Jumping on the ground where the flowers red.
Mama Duck comes running with a happy smile,
Watching little duckling play there for a while.
'Time to wash your feathers in the sunny lake,
Before we eat our breakfast and our morning cake.'
Into the blue water, the duckling takes a leap,
Washing off the mud while the fishes peep.
Now he is so clean and fluffy as can be,
The happiest little duckling for you to see.

rhymes.title: Quack, Quack, Quack
rhymes.text:
Hear the little duck say quack, quack, quack,
Walking with a wiggle on the dusty track.
He has yellow feathers and a little bill,
Marching down the valley to the grassy hill.
He meets a furry bunny hopping on the grass,
And dips his little head as the rabbit pass.
Then he finds a puddle full of shining rain,
And splashes in the water with a loud refrain.
Up go his webbed feet high in the air,
Showing off his swimming with a jaunty flair.
Sun begins to set in the glowing west,
Time for little duckling to go to his nest.
He curls up tightly with his brothers all around,
Making not a whisper and not a single sound.
Sleep, little duckling, till the morning light,
Dreaming of the water through the quiet night.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went swimming one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little ducks went swimming one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little ducks went swimming one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only two little ducks came back.

Two little ducks went swimming one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came swimming back!

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duckling
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duckling walking on the grass,
Watching all the busy bugs and beetles pass.
Flapping little wings so soft and bright,
Ready for a sunny morning full of light.

Waddling to the water by the big green tree,
Hoping that a tiny fish will swim with me.
Jumping in the puddle with a happy splash,
Swimming to the lily pads in a sudden dash.

Quacking out a happy song into the air,
Showing off my shiny feathers everywhere.
Playing with my mother all the afternoon,
Singing to the rising yellow sleepy moon.

Now the stars are blinking in the quiet sky,
Saying to the sleepy little ducks goodbye.
Crowning up my cozy nest with feathers deep,
Tucking in my little head to fall asleep.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Puddle Song
rhymes.text:
Hear the little duckling shout,
When the sun is coming out.
Put upon your shiny boots,
Walking by the tree and roots.

Find a puddle big and round,
Stomping loudly on the ground.
Jump right in and make a splash,
Running in a happy dash.

Water flying in the air,
Droplets landing everywhere.
Laughing till your tummy hurts,
Splashing on your little shirts.

Now the happy day is done,
Time to rest away the sun.
Dry your feathers, go to bed,
Sleepy duck with sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duck so bright,
Swimming in the morning light.
Padding fast and padding slow,
Where do little ducklings go?

Splashing water on his toes,
Water droplets on his nose.
Quacking loud to say hello,
Watch the happy duckling go.

Flapping wings of yellow down,
Swimming all around the town.
Happy ducks do love to play,
Swimming through the sunny day.

Now the sun is going down,
Little duck sleeps safe and sound.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings in a row,
Waddling where they want to go.
Mother duck says, "Quack, quack, quack,"
And guides them down the muddy track.

One jumps into the shiny pond,
Of swimming, he is very fond.
Two more jump in with a splash,
Making water spray and dash.

Four and five are swimming too,
In the water clear and blue.
Happy ducks all swimming round,
Making such a happy sound.

Time to dry and time to rest,
Sleeping in the cozy nest.

rhymes.title: Quacky Duck
rhymes.text:
Quacky duck has orange feet,
Waddling down the garden street.
Looking for a bug to eat,
Walking on his webbed feet sweet.

See him swim across the lake,
Watch the little ripples make.
Happy quacks into the air,
He is dancing without care.

Feathers soft and yellow too,
Swimming in the water blue.
Now he flaps his wings so high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Time to find his mother dear,
Evening time is drawing near.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only four little ducks came back.
Four little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only three little ducks came back.
Three little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only two little ducks came back.
Two little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came back.

rhymes.title: The Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
See the little yellow duck,
Waddling through the soft green muck.
With his bright and orange feet,
He is looking for a treat.
Down beside the shiny pond,
Of the water he is fond.
With a happy little quack,
He swims away and then comes back.
He flaps his wings up in the air,
Splash goes water everywhere!
Then he preens his feathers bright,
Underneath the morning light.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy duckling bed.
Dreaming of the water blue,
Little duck, I love you too.

rhymes.title: Ducky Paddle Day
rhymes.text:
Little duck is swimming fast,
Making bubbles as he passed.
Floating on the water deep,
While the tiny fishes sleep.
Green lily pads float all around,
Not a single scary sound.
Sunlight warms his yellow back,
Hear him happy sing his quack.
Up and down his webbed feet go,
Swimming fast and swimming slow.
Chasing bugs of shiny blue,
Wondering what they want to do.
Now the sun begins to set,
Little duck is warm and wet.
Time to waddle home to rest,
For a duck, the pond is best.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
But only two little ducks came back.

Two little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
And all the little ducks came swimming back.

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duck on the lake,
Swimming in circles for goodness sake.
Flapping his wings so soft and bright,
Greeting the morning with morning light.

He has a beak that is orange and round,
Making a happy and cheerful sound.
Quack goes the duck as he floats all day,
Chasing the little blue bugs away.

He dives his head in the water deep,
Then on the grass he goes to sleep.
Dreaming of rivers and weeds so green,
The happiest duck you've ever seen.

When he wakes up he will splash and play,
Happily swimming the hours away.
So give a wave to the duck so neat,
With funny webbed and waddling feet.

rhymes.title: Waddle Waddle Little Duck
rhymes.text:
Waddle waddle little duck on the floor,
Walking right up to the wooden door.
Quacking a song for the children to hear,
Bringing big smiles and a springtime cheer.

Down to the pond where the ripples glow,
Swimming so fast and then very slow.
Kicking his feet with a splash and a bound,
Happy to play in the water around.

Feathers so white and a bill so bright,
Dancing around in the sunny light.
Bowing his head with a friendly quack,
Carrying dreams on his fluffy back.

Now it is time for his nap on the grass,
Watching the beautiful butterflies pass.
Resting his eyes till the morning sun,
Ready again for another great run.

rhymes.title: Five Little Yellow Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little yellow ducks went out to play,
Down by the pond on a sunny day.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little yellow ducks went out to play,
Chasing the bugs in the meadow so gay.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little yellow ducks went out to play,
Swimming around in the bright blue bay.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack!'
And all five little ducks came swimming back.

rhymes.title: Little Duck Waddle
rhymes.text:
See the little duck go waddle, waddle, walk,
Opening his beak to squawk and talk.
He finds a puddle in the soft green grass,
And watches all the little beetles pass.

He dips his bill into the water so cool,
Splishing and splashing in the little pool.
He shakes his feathers till they shine and gleam,
Floating along like a happy dream.

When the bright sun goes down in the west,
The sleepy little duck goes to his nest.
He tucks his head beneath his soft brown wing,
And dreams of wonderful and happy things.

rhymes.title: Puddle Jump
rhymes.text:
Ducky, ducky, in the rain,
Tap at my windowpane.
Jump into the mud so brown,
Splash the water all around.

Orange feet go patter-pat,
What do you think of that?
Flap your wings and sing a song,
While the rain keeps falling long.

Now the sun is shining bright,
Making everything look white.
Ducky swims away to play,
Ending such a happy day.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And only four little ducks came back.
Four little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And only three little ducks came back.
Three little ducks went out to look,
Down by the sparkly running brook.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And only two little ducks came back.
Two little ducks went swimming deep,
While baby lamb went fast asleep.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And only one little duck came back.

rhymes.title: The Yellow Duckling
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duck so bright,
Wakes up with the morning light.
Splish and splash inside the pool,
Water nice and clear and cool.
Waddling fast upon the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.
Flapping wings of yellow gold,
Brave and gentle, never bold.
Chasing bugs and dragonflies,
Underneath the sunny skies.
Quack and quack and quack all day,
Come and join us in our play.
Feathers soft and fluffy too,
Swimming in the ocean blue.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the cozy town.

rhymes.title: Ducky's Pond Party
rhymes.text:
Hear the little duckling sing,
Flapping every fuzzy wing.
Jumping in the mud so sweet,
With his orange webbed feet.
Swimming round the lily pad,
Making Mama duck so glad.
Catching fishies one by one,
Having lots of summer fun.
Bubbles floating in the air,
Happy ducks are everywhere.
Blowing kisses to the breeze,
Dancing with the willow trees.
Stars are shining in the night,
Moon is glowing soft and white.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy little bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother Duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother Duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother Duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only two little ducks came back.

Two little ducks went out to play,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother Duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came swimming back.

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duckling swims in the blue,
Splishing and splashing all the day through.
Waddling on the grass with feet so wide,
Staying right close by his mother's side.

Beak is bright orange, feathers so soft,
Watching the fluffy white clouds way aloft.
Opening his little beak wide to say quack,
Then stretching his wings and patting his back.

Jumping in puddles of cool summer rain,
Hopping right out and jumping again.
Chasing a butterfly into the green trees,
Feeling the tickle of soft gentle breeze.

Now the bright sun is beginning to steep,
Time for our little duckling to sleep.
Closing his eyes in his warm cozy nest,
Little yellow duckling is taking a rest.

rhymes.title: Pond Time Fun
rhymes.text:
Down by the pond where the tall rushes grow,
Little green ducklings are putting on a show.
Flapping their wings in the bright morning sun,
Splashing the water and having great fun.

Swimming in circles and diving down low,
Watching the small silver fishes swim slow.
Catching a bug on the tip of a leaf,
Chewing it up with a happy belief.

Mother Duck watches them splash in the bay,
Teaching her ducklings the safe swimming way.
'Paddle your feet!' she will happily quack,
Carrying sleepy ones right on her back.

Stars start to twinkle up high in the sky,
Singing a sweet little soft lullaby.
Dreaming of swimming all through the deep night,
Until the morning brings golden warm light.

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duckling sweet,
Dancing on your webbed feet.
Waddling softly on the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.
Swimming in the water blue,
Saying cheerful quacks to you.
Flapping feathers in the sun,
Having lots of springtime fun.
Now the day is almost done,
Sleeping till the morning sun.
Goodnight, duckling, go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.
Dreaming of the pond so wide,
Floating safely by my side.
Soft and cozy in your nest,
Little duck, it is time to rest.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack,'
And only four little ducks came back.
Four little ducks went swimming around,
Making a happy splashing sound.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack,'
And only three little ducks came back.
Three little ducks hopped out to play,
Chasing a dragonfly away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack,'
And only two little ducks came back.
Two little ducks skipped down the lane,
Happy to see the gentle rain.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came back.

rhymes.title: Pond Time Play
rhymes.text:
Little duck by the pond so clear,
Tell me why you are smiling here.
Water ripples round your chest,
Floating is your favorite test.
Dip your yellow beak right down,
Never worry, never frown.
Catch a bug that buzzes by,
Look up at the dragonfly.
Shake your tail and make a splash,
Swim across in just a dash.
Other ducks are joining in,
Let the water games begin.
Quacking loudly all around,
Making such a happy sound.
Now you waddle back to rest,
Little duck, you are the best.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
