Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only four little ducks came back.
Four little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only three little ducks came back.
Three little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only two little ducks came back.
Two little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
And all the five little ducks came back.

rhymes.title: The Yellow Duckling
rhymes.text:
See the little yellow duck,
Waddling through the soft green muck.
He has got two orange feet,
Walking down the sunny street.
When he wants to take a swim,
Water looks so cool to him.
Splish and splash and dive and pop,
Little duck will never stop.
Flapping wings of fuzzy down,
He is swimming all around.
Quack says he and quack says she,
Happy as a duck can be.
Now the sun is going down,
Leaving all the sleepy town.
Time to rest his little head,
In his cozy duckling bed.

rhymes.title: Pond Time Play
rhymes.text:
Little duck beside the stream,
Swimming in a sunny dream.
Catch a bug and chase a fly,
While the clouds go floating by.
Webbed feet paddle fast and slow,
Watch the little ripples go.
Feathers soft and waterproof,
Better than a shiny roof.
Friends are calling from the shore,
Wanting to play games some more.
Dive below and pop right up,
Drinking from a buttercup.
Evening stars begin to peep,
Time for little ducks to sleep.
Close your eyes and do not cry,
Morning time is drawing nigh.

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duck so sweet,
Walking on your webbed feet.
Swimming in the water blue,
Quacking loud and happy too.

Now you dive beneath the spray,
Having so much fun today.
Flapping wings of snowy white,
Underneath the morning light.

Catch a bug and munch a seed,
Eating every single weed.
Now you rest upon the stone,
In a cozy world your own.

Sun is setting in the sky,
Little duck begins to cry?
No, you smile and softly sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings swimming in a row,
Where are they going? Does anybody know?
Following their mother to the lily pad,
Making her so proud and very very glad.

One little duckling dives beneath the wave,
Showing all the others that he is very brave.
Two little ducklings splash around and play,
Chasing little minnows all the livelong day.

Three little ducklings quack a merry tune,
Looking up above them at the silver moon.
Four little ducklings waddle on the shore,
Wanting just a little bit of swimming more.

Five little ducklings tumble into bed,
Pulling cozy blankets right above their head.
Mother duck is smiling as she tucks them tight,
Whispering a gentle and a sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: Pond Time Fun
rhymes.text:
Pond is shining bright and clear,
Glad that summer days are here.
Little duck begins to swim,
Following a dragon's whim.

Splash and paddle, swish and dive,
Glad to be so much alive.
Feathers soft and beak so bright,
Running in the golden light.

Meet a frog upon a log,
Swimming past a happy dog.
Quack a greeting, loud and clear,
To the friends who gather near.

Now the water starts to ripple,
As we share a little tipple.
Time to rest our weary head,
Climbing to our cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only four little ducks came back.
Four little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only three little ducks came back.
Three little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only two little ducks came back.
Two little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came swimming back.

rhymes.title: Waddle Waddle Duck
rhymes.text:
See the little yellow duck,
Waddling through the gentle muck.
Flapping wings so soft and light,
Feathers shining clean and bright.
Walking down to find a stream,
Where the water sparkles gleam.
Jumping in with happy cries,
Looking at the sunny skies.
Bouncing up and floating down,
Wearing nature's golden crown.
Paddling in a happy ring,
Oh, it is a joyful thing.
Kicking feet go splash, splash, splash,
Making such a happy dash.
Now the sun begins to set,
Time to dry each little wet.

rhymes.title: Quacky Quack Duck
rhymes.text:
Little duck has a yellow bill,
Waddling down the grassy hill.
Looking for a bug to eat,
Moving fast his webbed feet.
Quack, quack, quack is what he says,
Swimming in the pond for days.
Chasing after dragonflies,
Underneath the friendly skies.
Soft feathers of sunny gold,
Cutest story ever told.
Time to rest his little head,
In his cozy little bed.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.
Dreaming of the water blue,
Little duck, I love you too.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings swimming in a line,
The water is cool and the weather is fine.
One little duck says, "Look what I can do!"
He splashes his feet and he calls out, "Quack, too!"

Four little ducklings dive down deep,
While a sleepy brown frog is taking a sleep.
They look for bright pebbles of yellow and red,
Then swim right back up to their cozy bed.

Three little ducklings waddle on the shore,
They look for some worms and they look for some more.
They flap their small wings and they jump in the air,
And dance in a circle without any care.

Two little ducklings float on the blue,
Singing a happy and cheerful duck song for you.
They paddle around till the stars start to glow,
And the soft evening winds begin to blow.

One little duckling is ready for rest,
Snuggled up close in a warm little nest.
Momma Duck sings as the shadows fall deep,
And all the sweet ducklings go fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Splash, Splash, Little Duck
rhymes.text:
Yellow feathers, soft and bright,
Waddling in the morning light.
Splashing water in the air,
Happiness is everywhere.

Webbed feet walking on the ground,
Making such a funny sound.
Squish and squash in mud so sweet,
Tickling every little feet.

Catching bugs upon the breeze,
Hiding underneath the trees.
Stretching out a little bill,
Drinking from the running rill.

Now the sun is going down,
Painting all the sky a brown.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy feather bed.

rhymes.title: Quacky Duck Goes to Play
rhymes.text:
Quacky Duck is wearing shoes,
Walking with a happy snooze.
Wait, ducks do not wear shoes at all,
They just love to play and ball.

Down the river they will slide,
With a tiny fish to guide.
Up and down the gentle wave,
Little ducks are bold and brave.

Eating bits of sunny bread,
With a leaf upon their head.
Dancing till the day is done,
Basking in the golden sun.

When the moon begins to peep,
All the ducks are fast asleep.
Dreaming of a pond so blue,
Saying quiet dreams to you.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings swimming in a row,
Looking for a place where the fresh weeds grow.
Mother duck calls out, 'Quack, quack, come here!'
All the little ducklings paddle without fear.

Down to the river where the water is blue,
Splishing and splashing, what can they do?
One little duck dives under the spray,
Finding a shiny green pebble to play.

Two little ducks kick their webbed feet high,
Watching a fluffy white cloud in the sky.
Three little ducks flap their wings so wide,
Sliding on the mud like a slippery slide.

Four little ducks sing a happy song,
Five little ducklings all sing along.
Sun begins to set in the evening glow,
Time for little ducks to sleep in a row.

rhymes.title: Yellow Feather
rhymes.text:
Yellow little duckling sitting by the stream,
Looking at the water like a happy dream.
Soft little feathers all bright and clean,
Prettiest duck that you've ever seen.

Waddling on the grass with a funny waddle walk,
Stopping by the flowers just to hear them talk.
Opening his yellow beak to say a little quack,
Shaking water droplets right off his back.

Swimming in the circle round the lily pad,
Playing with his mommy makes him very glad.
Diving for a minnow, swimming fast and deep,
Now the little duckling wants to go to sleep.

Closing up his eyes as the stars awake,
Floating like a feather on the sleepy lake.
Goodnight, little duck, resting in your nest,
Time for little ducklings to take a little rest.

rhymes.title: Quack, Quack, Quack
rhymes.text:
Quack, quack, quack goes the little yellow duck,
Looking for a worm in the clover and the muck.
Waddling through the garden, searching all around,
Finding juicy beetles right upon the ground.

Up goes his tail and down goes his head,
Time for breakfast, little duck is being fed.
Then he hears a splash from the pond nearby,
Spreading out his wings ready now to fly.

Not quite flying yet, but a hop and a bound,
Landing in the water with a splash and a sound.
Paddling with his feet, making ripples wide,
Happy as can be with his mommy by his side.

Chasing little dragonflies buzzing in the air,
Little yellow duckling without a single care.
When the day is over and the sky is red,
Little duck goes waddling right back to his bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little ducks went out to play,
Chasing the bugs along the way.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little ducks splashed in the pool,
Keeping their webbed feet nice and cool.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
But only two little ducks came back.

Two little ducks waddled around,
Pecking the seeds upon the ground.
Mother duck said, 'Quack, quack, quack, quack,'
And all five little ducks came back!

rhymes.title: Little Yellow Duck
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duck by the stream,
Swimming along in a sunny dream.
Flapping your wings so soft and bright,
Greeting the morning with golden light.

Looking for bugs in the grassy green,
The happiest duckby you've ever seen.
Quacking a song to the morning breeze,
Swaying along with the willow trees.

Jumping right into the water so blue,
Splashing around and making a coo.
Chasing a frog as he hops away,
Ready to play for the rest of the day.

Now comes the evening, the stars appear,
Time for bed when the moon is near.
Tuck in your head and close your eyes,
Underneathneath the beautiful skies.

rhymes.title: Waddle Waddle Quack
rhymes.text:
Waddle, waddle, goes the duck,
Walking down the muddy muck.
Feathers soft and yellow bright,
Sparkling in the morning light.

Open up your orange bill,
Walking slowly up the hill.
See you find a lovely treat,
Something yummy, nice to eat.

Splash into the river deep,
While the little fishes sleep.
Kick your feet from side to side,
Taking such a happy ride.

Now the sun is going down,
Leaving shadows on the town.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy feather bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducks
rhymes.text:
Five little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only four little ducks came back.

Four little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only three little ducks came back.

Three little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only two little ducks came back.

Two little ducks went out one day,
Over the hills and far away.
Mother duck said, Quack, quack, quack, quack,
But only one little duck came back.

rhymes.title: Yellow Duckling
rhymes.text:
Little yellow duckling swims around,
Making not a single sound.
Padding through the water blue,
Saying happy quacks to you.

Soft and fluffy is his coat,
Floating like a little boat.
Chasing bugs and lily pads,
Making all the fishes glad.

When the sun begins to set,
He is never cold or wet.
Waddling back to cozy nest,
Time to take a little rest.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars begin to peep.

rhymes.title: Splish Splash Pond
rhymes.text:
Down beside the glassy pond,
In the reeds he loves so fond,
Little duck begins to play,
Splashing water all the day.

Flapping wings of yellow gold,
Brave and daring, bright and bold.
Dipping down his little bill,
Drinking from the running rill.

Froggy jumps up in the air,
Duckling gives a happy stare.
Round and round they go and race,
Smiling every happy face.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying every duck goodnight.

rhymes.title: Five Little Ducklings
rhymes.text:
Five little ducklings swimming in a row,
Looking for a place where the soft green grasses grow.
First little duckling flaps his little wing,
Happy that the morning birds are starting up to sing.
Second little duckling dives beneath the blue,
Finding shiny pebbles polished bright and new.
Third little duckling stops to catch a fly,
Watching fluffy clouds go sailing through the sky.
Fourth little duckling gives a happy quack,
Carrying a raindrop balanced on his back.
Fifth little duckling waddles to the shore,
Ready to begin to play and explore.
Mama Duck is watching from the willow tree,
Calling out her babies with a melody.
All the little ducklings tumble in the sun,
Splashing in the water till the day is done.
Now it is the evening, time to go to rest,
Snug and warm together in their cozy nest.

rhymes.title: Waddle Waddle Little Duck
rhymes.text:
Waddle, waddle, little duck, walking on the ground,
Looking for a juicy worm that can be found.
Soft yellow feathers and a beak so bright,
Dancing in the golden sun all the morning light.
Down to the river where the waters flow,
Watch the happy duckling paddle to and fro.
Kicking webbed feet underneath the blue,
Saying hello to a passing frog or two.
Splash go the ripples as he takes a dive,
Glad to be a little duck feeling so alive.
Fluttering his little wings up into the air,
Showing all his duckling friends that he does not care.
Circling around in a happy little game,
Every single day with him is never quite the same.
Now the sun is sinking low behind the hill,
Water in the quiet pond is growing very still.
Time for little duck to tuck his sleepy head,
Dreaming happy dreams inside his cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Quacky Duck Goes Splash
rhymes.text:
Quacky is a little duck dressed in yellow down,
Happiest little creature in the animal town.
He has two orange feet that make a funny sound,
Walking through the meadow as he looks around.
Here is a puddle filled with shiny rain,
Quacky wants to jump inside and play again.
One, two, three and splash goes his little chest,
Splashing muddy water is what he loves the best.
Other little ducklings come running to the fun,
Playing all together underneath the golden sun.
Chasing little dragonflies buzzing in the breeze,
Hiding underneath the shadows of the leafy trees.
Now the mud is washed away in the flowing stream,
Quacky starts to look around in a sleepy dream.
Mama Duck is calling from the cozy nest,
Time for tired little ducks to take a little rest.
Snuggled up together till the morning light,
Sleeping very peacefully through the quiet night.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down on the big green farm, lived a very happy cow named Bessie. Bessie had soft brown spots, big brown eyes, and a shiny black nose. She loved the farm, but most of all, she loved the big muddy puddle right by the old wooden barn. Today was a special day because the sun was warm and the mud looked wonderfully squishy. Bessie trotted over to the puddle. 'Moo-moo!' she said happily. She dipped one front hoof right into the dark, thick mud. Squish, squash, squelch! It felt so cool and tickly between her toes. Bessie giggled, shaking her tail from side to side. Next, she dipped her other hoof in. Squish, squash, squelch! Little brown mud splatters flew up into the air. They landed on the grass and on her tummy. 'Oh, this is so much fun!' thought Bessie. She wanted to dance. So, she lifted her left foot, then her right foot, stomping and splashing in the mud. Splash, splash, splish! The little yellow duck waddled over to the puddle. He looked at Bessie and tilted his head. 'Quack, quack!' said the duck, which meant, 'Can I play too?' Bessie smiled her biggest cow smile. 'Moo-moo, come on in!' she called out. The duck jumped right into the mud with a happy splash. They splashed together until they were both covered in mud from head to toe. Soon, Farmer John walked by with a bucket of water. He saw Bessie and the duck playing in the big muddy mess. Farmer John chuckled. 'Well, hello there, muddy friends! Time to wash off those dirty boots.' With a gentle spray of cool water from the hose, Bessie was clean once more. Her white coat gleamed in the sunshine, and her spots shone bright. Bessie gave Farmer John a big friendly lick on his hand. She had the best mud day ever, and she could not wait for tomorrow to play all over again.

stories.title: Daisy's Midnight Snack
stories.text: The moon was shining high and bright over the sleeping farm. All the animals had tucked themselves into bed. The little piglets were snoring softly in their pen. The fluffy sheep were cuddled up together in the meadow. And the little brown cow named Daisy was wide awake. Daisy had a tiny tummy rumble. 'Moo-oo,' she whispered very quietly so she wouldn't wake her friends. She looked up at the big silver moon. She looked over at the big rolling hill covered in clover. Oh, how Daisy loved clover! It was her absolute favorite snack in the whole wide world. Daisy began to tiptoe across the soft green grass. Tip-toe, tip-toe, went her big hooves. She tried to be as quiet as a little mouse, even though she was a big cow. She giggled softly to herself as she walked. When she reached the top of the hill, she saw a patch of clover sparkling in the moonlight. It looked like green treasure! Daisy sat down gently on the grass. She leaned her head down close to the ground. Sniff, sniff. Ah, it smelled so sweet and fresh. Daisy opened her mouth and took a big, happy bite of the yummy clover. Munch, munch, munch! It tasted like sunshine and sweet morning dew. She ate a little bit more. Munch, munch, crunch! Her tummy felt nice and warm and full now. Daisy let out a long, peaceful sigh. The night breeze gently blew through her soft ears. She blinked her sleepy eyes. The moon began to dip lower in the sky, and the stars twinkled goodnight. Daisy curled up right there on the clover hill. She closed her eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming sweet dreams of green grass and starry night skies. Sleep tight, sweet little Daisy.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Balloon
stories.text: Barnaby was a young calf who lived with his mother in the big pasture. Today was the farm festival, and the air was filled with music and laughter. Farmer Sue was handing out bright, colorful balloons to all the animals. Barnaby watched with wide, excited eyes as a shiny red balloon floated gently in the air on a long white string. 'Moo?' asked Barnaby, pointing his nose right at the red balloon. Farmer Sue smiled and tied the string securely around Barnaby's soft tail. 'Here you go, Barnaby!' she said. The red balloon bobbed up and down behind him. Every time Barnaby wagged his tail, the balloon danced in the air. Up and down, left and right, float, float, float! Barnaby thought this was the most magical thing he had ever seen. He wanted to show his best friend, the fluffy white lamb. Barnaby turned around in a circle to look at his balloon. 'Moo-moo!' he called out happily. The lamb bounced up and down, clapping her tiny hooves together. 'Baa, baa, look at you go!' she bleated. Barnaby started to trot across the green grass, and the red balloon floated right behind him like a loyal little friend. He ran past the yellow hay bales. He trotted past the red barn. The balloon bounced happily against the breeze. Suddenly, a little gust of wind came blowing through the pasture. Whoosh! The wind caught the balloon and lifted it higher into the sky. Barnaby stopped and looked up. The string slipped gently off his tail. The red balloon floated up, up, up towards the fluffy white clouds. Barnaby watched it go, feeling a little bit sad. But then, he remembered all the fun he had playing tag with his floating red friend. He smiled and gave a happy little moo. The balloon drifted away over the hills, leaving Barnaby with a heart full of joy and a wonderful memory of his special festival day.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly cow named Bessie woke up with a big stretch. Moo! It was time to explore the farmyard and find her very best animal friends. Bessie had four strong legs and big brown spots, but today she had a brand-new adventure in mind. She trotted over to the big red barn where the shiny tractors lived. The farmer had just finished watering the garden, and there was a giant, squishy puddle right in the middle of the path. Bessie stopped and looked down. The mud was dark, wet, and looked like a whole lot of fun. Do cows like mud? Bessie smiled and dipped one hoof right into the middle. Squish, squash, squelch! The mud made a funny noise that made Bessie giggle. She put her second hoof in, then her third, and then her fourth. Soon, Bessie was standing right in the middle of the happy, muddy puddle. She swished her tail from side to side and shook her big head. Just then, her friend Barnaby the pig came running over. Oint, oink! squealed Barnaby. Can I join you, Bessie? Of course you can! mooed Bessie warmly. Barnaby jumped right into the puddle, sending brown water splashing up into the air. Splash! They played together for a long, wonderful time, making silly shapes in the mud with their feet. A little yellow duck waddled past and quayed happily at the muddy pair. By the time the sun was high in the sky, Bessie and Barnaby were the muddiest animals on the whole farm. But oh, how happy they were! The farmer walked over with a big hose of cool, refreshing water. Time for a bath, my silly friends! laughed the farmer. Bessie let out a gentle moo of thanks as the cool water washed her clean. She was ready for a nice long nap in the soft green grass, dreaming of her next big muddy adventure.

stories.title: The Starry Night Moo
stories.text: The sun was sinking low behind the rolling hills, painting the sky in bright shades of pink, orange, and purple. Down on Clover Meadow Farm, the little yellow ducklings were tucked under their mother's wings, and the sleepy sheep were resting their woolly heads. But Clarabelle the cow was wide awake. Clarabelle loved the evening time more than anything else in the whole wide world. She stood near the wooden fence, looking up at the sky as the very first twinkling star appeared like a tiny diamond. Hello, little star, whispered Clarabelle softly. She took a deep breath of the cool night air, smelling the sweet clover and fresh hay. Clarabelle had a very special job on the farm. Every night, right before all the little toddlers in the nearby houses went fast asleep, she liked to sing a special lullaby to the moon. She cleared her throat, took another big breath, and let out a long, musical moo. Moo-oooo-ooo! Her voice echoed gently across the peaceful fields, sounding like a warm, cozy blanket wrapping around the farm. High up in the sky, the bright yellow moon seemed to smile down at her. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves in the big oak tree, whispering back to the friendly cow. Clarabelle looked around her pasture. The fireflies were starting to dance in the dark, blinking their little lights on and off like floating fairy lanterns. One, two, three fireflies landed right on Clarabelle's soft nose, making her cross her eyes and giggle. It tickled so much! She stayed very still so she wouldn't wake her tiny glowing friends. The night grew quieter and quieter until the only sounds were the crickets singing their nightly tune and Clarabelle's happy breathing. With a contented sigh, the sweet cow laid her heavy head down on the soft, cool grass. She closed her big brown eyes and drifted off to dreamland, knowing that the stars were watching over her until the bright morning sun returned to wake the farm once again.

stories.title: Daisy's Magic Bell
stories.text: Daisy was a very special cow who lived in a bright green pasture right next to a bubbling brook. What made Daisy so special? She wore a shiny golden bell around her neck that went ding-dong, ding-dong wherever she walked! Every morning when the sun peeked over the mountains, Daisy would shake her head on purpose just to hear the happy sound. Ding-dong! Good morning, world! she would moo cheerfully. Today, Daisy had a very important mission. The farmer had lost his favorite red gardening hat, and nobody could find it anywhere. Daisy decided she would use her magic bell and her keen cow eyes to search the entire farm. She started her journey by the old wooden trough where the horses drank their water. She shook her neck: ding-dong, ding-dong! She peeked behind the big haystacks, but the hat was not there. Next, she trotted over to the apple orchard, where the sweet red apples hung low on the branches. A little brown bunny hopped out from the tall grass and looked up at the big cow in surprise. Hello, bunny! mooed Daisy gently. Have you seen a red hat today? The bunny wiggled his nose and pointed toward the vegetable garden with one long ear. Daisy smiled and thanked her furry friend, hurrying over to the garden as fast as her four hooves could carry her. Ding-dong, ding-dong went her bell, ringing out like a joyful song. When she arrived at the pumpkin patch, what do you think she saw? Resting right on top of a big orange pumpkin was the farmer's lost red hat! A playful little goat was trying to wear it like a crown. Daisy gave a gentle nudge with her soft nose, took the hat back, and carried it proudly in her mouth all the way to the farmhouse porch. The farmer was so happy that he gave Daisy a sweet, crunchy carrot as a reward. Daisy chewed happily, her golden bell ringing out one last joyful note as she headed back to her sunny meadow.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly brown and white cow named Bessie woke up with a big stretch. Moo! said Bessie to the bright yellow sun. Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, leaving big, squishy, wonderful puddles all over the pasture. Bessie loved puddles more than anything in the whole wide world. She trotted along the path, her big black hooves going clip-clop, clip-clop, over the rolling hills. The grass tickled her tummy, and the gentle wind whispered through her floppy ears. Soon, she saw the biggest puddle of all right near the old wooden fence. Oh, how her heart fluttered with excitement! Without waiting another second, Bessie stepped right into the middle of the puddle. Spliche, splash, squelch! went the mud between her toes. Mud squirted up her left leg. Mud squirted up her right leg. Bessie giggled a cow giggle, which sounded like a low, happy rumble in her chest. She stomped her left foot. Splash! She stomped her right foot. Squelch! Soon, little brown speckles were dotted all over her white spots. She looked down at her feet and thought she looked simply magnificent. Just then, her good friend Barnaby the fluffy white sheep came bouncing over. Baa, baa, Bessie! What are you doing? asked Barnaby. Bessie tossed her head playfully and gave a happy moo. I am making mud boots! she seemed to say. Barnaby tilted his head, watching the brown water bubble up. Can I have mud boots too? he asked. Bessie nodded her big head, stepping aside to share the wonderful, squishy fun. Together, the cow and the sheep splashed and stomped until they were the muddiest animals on the entire farm. The farmer walked by with a bucket of apples, saw the messy pair, and chuckled out loud. Well, look at you two funny creatures! he laughed, giving them each a sweet, crunchy apple treat. Bessie chewed her apple slowly, feeling warm, happy, and delightfully messy. When the sun began to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange, Bessie walked slowly back to the cozy barn. She curled up in the soft straw, closing her heavy eyes. As she drifted off to sleep, she dreamed of shiny green grass, warm sunshine, and millions of squishy, wonderful mud puddles waiting just for her.

stories.title: The Moon Jump
stories.text: High up in the midnight sky, the silver moon shone bright and round like a giant glowing pancake. Down on the quiet farm, all the animals were fast asleep. Snoring sheep, resting roosters, and dreaming dogs filled the night with peaceful sounds. But one little calf named Daisy was wide awake. Daisy had big brown eyes and a spot on her forehead that looked just like a tiny star. She looked up at the sparkling stars twinkling like tiny diamonds in the dark velvet sky. Tonight, Daisy felt extra brave and extra bouncy. She trotted softly over to the low stone wall at the edge of the pasture. The grass was cool and wet with morning dew, tickling her little hooves. Daisy whispered to herself, I think tonight is the night. I am going to jump right over the moon! She backed up two big steps. One, two, three! Then she ran forward as fast as her little legs could carry her. With a mighty heave, she sprang up into the air. Wheee! cried Daisy as she flew up, up, up into the cool night breeze. She soared higher than the fence. She soared higher than the tall oak tree where the sleepy owls lived. The wind rushed past her ears, making her feel like a bird with big, invisible wings. For a tiny second, her nose came so close to the glowing moon that she thought she could lick it like a giant cone of vanilla ice cream. The moon seemed to smile down at her with a gentle, silvery glow. But soon, gravity gently pulled her back down toward the soft green grass. Down, down, down she floated, landing with a very soft, very clumsy thud right back in her favorite clover patch. Plop! Daisy giggled, shaking her head until her little bell went jingle-jangle. She had not quite reached the moon, but she had flown higher than any cow in the history of the farm. Panting happily, she looked up one last time and gave the moon a quiet little goodnight moo. Then, feeling tired and wonderfully adventurous, Daisy curled her legs beneath her soft white tummy. She closed her eyes and drifted off to sweet, starry dreams, knowing that tomorrow night, she might just try again.

stories.title: Bessie's Magic Bell
stories.text: Deep in the greenest pasture of Sunny Brook Farm lived a cheerful cow named Buttercup. Buttercup wore a shiny brass bell around her neck on a bright red ribbon. Every time she walked, the bell made a delightful sound. Clink, clank, jingle, jang! It was the happiest music on the farm. Buttercup loved her bell more than anything because it helped her friends find her when they played hide and seek among the tall cornstalks. One sunny afternoon, Buttercup woke up from her nap and noticed something terribly wrong. Her bell was completely quiet. She shook her head left and right. Nothing! Not a single clink or jank. Oh, no! whispered Buttercup in her softest moo. Where has my merry music gone? Without wasting a single moment, she set off across the clover fields to solve the mystery. First, she waddled over to the duck pond where three yellow ducklings were paddling in the cool water. Quack, quack, Buttercup! Have you seen my missing music? she asked. The ducklings shook their fluffy yellow heads. We did not see your music, they chirped, but we found a shiny pebble in the mud! Buttercup thanked them kindly and kept on walking. Next, she trotted past the red barn where Henry the horse was munching on sweet hay. Neigh, Buttercup! Are you looking for something shiny? asked Henry, pointing his long nose toward the old wooden water trough. Buttercup peered over the edge of the wooden trough. Down at the very bottom, hiding under a floating green lily pad, was her shiny brass bell! It had slipped off her ribbon while she was drinking water earlier that morning. Buttercup was so relieved that she let out a loud, joyous moo that echoed across the hills. She gently scooped her nose into the water, nudged the bell with her soft pink snout, and lifted it up. With a little help from the farmer, the bell was safely tied back onto her red ribbon. Buttercup shook her head once, twice, three times. Clink, clank, jingle, jang! The merry music was back, louder and sweeter than ever. Buttercup danced a little happy jig in the grass, so glad her favorite song had returned to the farm.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a sweet brown cow named Bessie woke up with a big stretch. Moo-oo-oo! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, leaving big, squishy puddles everywhere. Bessie loved squishy puddles. She trotted out of the barn on her four strong hooves, clip-clop, clip-clop, looking for adventure. The little yellow duck waddled past and quacked a happy hello, shaking water off his bright orange feathers. Bessie blinked her big brown eyes and saw the biggest, muddiest puddle in the whole pasture. It was right under the big oak tree. She walked right up to the edge and looked down. She could see her friendly face smiling back at her in the shiny water. Without waiting another second, Bessie stepped right in with a loud squelch! Squish, squash, squish! Mud squirted up between her toes, and it felt so warm and tickly. Bessie giggled, making a gentle sound deep in her throat. She stomped her left foot. Squelch! Then she stomped her right foot. Squish! A little frog hopped out of the mud and landed on a lily pad, ribbiting in surprise. Bessie leaned her head down and blew bubbles in the puddle. Blub, blub, blub! Muddy water splashed onto her nose, making a funny brown spot right on the tip. A little brown bird flew down to watch the fun, singing a cheerful morning song. Soon, the farmer came walking down the lane with a bright red bucket, calling out for his favorite cow. Oh, Bessie! Are you making mud pies again? he asked with a warm chuckle. Bessie tossed her head playfully and gave a happy moo. She stepped out of the puddle, leaving a trail of lovely mud prints in the green grass. The farmer gently brushed off her back and gave her a crisp, sweet apple as a morning treat. Bessie chewed happily, munch, crunch, munch, thinking that being a muddy cow was the best job in the entire wide world.

stories.title: The Starry Night Dance
stories.text: Deep in the quiet countryside, when the sun went down and the moon came up, all the animals on the farm went fast asleep. All the animals, that is, except for a little spotted cow named Dotty. Dotty had big, round spots that looked just like fluffy clouds on her white coat. Tonight, the moon was glowing like a giant silver coin in the dark velvet sky, and millions of tiny stars twinkled like glitter. Dotty felt a tickle in her hooves. A magical music seemed to float on the gentle night breeze. It sounded like whispering leaves and crickets singing a lullaby. Dotty blinked her sleepy eyes and stood up on her four sturdy legs. Stretch, yawn, moo! She decided it was the perfect night for a dance. She trotted softly over to the meadow where the grass was cool and soft. First, she practiced her tippy-toe steps. Tap, tap, tap went her hooves on the ground. Then, she tried a big, sweeping spin, swishing her long tail through the air. A wise old owl sitting on a tree branch opened one round eye and hooted softly in approval. Dotty looked up at the glowing moon and smiled. She remembered an old nursery rhyme about a cow jumping over the moon, and she giggled to herself. Could she do it? She bent her knees down low, took a deep breath, and sprang up into the air with all her might! Wheeee! She didn't jump over the moon, but she leaped higher than the fence post, feeling as light as a floating balloon. As she landed gently back on the clover, a shooting star streaked across the dark sky, leaving a trail of sparkling light. Dotty clapped her hooves together in delight. She did a little wiggle and a final bow to her audience of sleeping sheep and resting chickens. Finally, the midnight air grew a little chilly, and a big yawn slipped out of Dotty's mouth. She walked back to her warm, cozy barn, snuggled down into the soft, sweet-smelling hay, and closed her eyes. With visions of dancing stars and silver moons swirling in her sleepy head, Dotty drifted off into the sweetest dream of all.

stories.title: Bessie's Morning Breakfast
stories.text: Good morning, little reader! Today we are going to visit the farm to see what our friend Barnaby the cow is doing. Barnaby is a big, friendly cow with patches of black and white just like a giant puzzle. The sun is just peeking over the top of the red barn, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink and orange. Barnaby wakes up very early every single day because he has a very important job to do. His job is to eat lots and lots of yummy green grass so he can grow big and strong. Barnaby stretches his long neck and says, Good morning, world! Moo-oo! He ambles slowly across the meadow, where the morning dew makes the grass sparkle like diamonds. Every step he takes makes a soft swish-swish sound in the tall clover. Barnaby looks down and sees his breakfast waiting for him. There is sweet green grass, crunchy yellow buttercups, and tall, swaying stalks of clover. He opens his wide mouth and takes a big, happy bite. Munch, crunch, chew! Barnaby loves the taste of fresh morning plants. He chews to the left, and then he chews to the right, moving his jaw round and round in a very silly way. A little ladybug lands right on his black nose, tickling him gently. Barnaby crosses his eyes to look at the tiny red bug and gives a soft little sneeze. Achoo! The ladybug flies away up into the blue sky. Barnaby goes right back to his breakfast, happily munching away until his tummy is full and round like a basketball. A cool breeze blows through the meadow, rustling his floppy ears. Barnaby lets out a long, contented sigh and rests his heavy head on a patch of soft moss. He closes his eyes for a little morning nap, listening to the buzzing bees and the singing birds, knowing that tomorrow morning, he will wake up and do it all over again.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of a big green pasture, lived a friendly brown-and-white cow named Bessie. Bessie loved the warm sun. She loved the sweet green grass. But most of all, Bessie loved when it rained, because rain made big, squishy puddles of mud! One Tuesday, after a nice morning shower, Bessie trotted over to her favorite spot near the big oak tree. 'Squish, squash, squish,' went the ground under her heavy hooves. Bessie looked down at her feet and had a very silly idea. 'Moo!' she said with a happy wiggle. 'Today, I am going to have muddy boots!' Bessie stepped her front right hoof right into the middle of the deepest, wettest puddle. 'Splash!' Mud flew up into the air. It landed on a blade of grass. It landed on a yellow butterfly, who fluttered away with a giggle. 'Squish, squash, splat!' Bessie stepped her front left hoof in. Then her back right hoof. Then her back left hoof. Soon, Bessie was standing in mud all the way up to her ankles. She felt wonderfully gooey and cool. Just then, her little friend Pip the bird flew down from the oak tree. Pip tilted his head and chirped, 'Bessie, your boots are so big and brown!' Bessie shook her head and mooed a happy song. She danced a little muddy dance. Boom, boom, went her feet. Squish, squish, went the mud. A little frog hopped out of the bushes and said, 'Ribbit! Can I wear muddy boots too?' 'Moo-sive yes!' thought Bessie. They played together all morning long, splashing and stomping until the sun came out and dried the mud. When it was time for afternoon nap, Bessie walked back to the barn. Farmer John smiled and said, 'Well, Bessie, you certainly had a fun day!' Bessie gave a sleepy, happy moo, curled up in the fresh straw, and dreamed about squishy, squashy mud puddles.

stories.title: The Moon That Wanted Milk
stories.text: High up in the midnight sky lived a bright, shiny yellow moon. Every night, the moon watched over the sleeping world. It watched the sleeping cats. It watched the sleeping dogs. And every night, the moon watched a little black-and-white cow named Clara sleeping in her cozy meadow. One night, the moon felt a funny little rumble in its tummy. 'Rumble, rumble, growl,' went the sky. The moon was hungry! It looked down at the dark green grass and saw Clara chewing her midnight cud. The moon leaned down a little bit closer and whispered, 'Hello, little cow. I am so hungry up here in the dark.' Clara blinked her big brown eyes. She was very surprised to hear the moon talking to her. 'Moo?' asked Clara softly. 'Do you want a snack?' The moon said, 'Oh yes, I would love a snack. But I am too high up to reach the grass.' Clara thought for a moment. She wanted to help her shiny friend. So, Clara walked over to the highest hill in the meadow. She stood on her tiptoes. She stretched her neck up as high as she could. Then, Clara took a deep breath and gave a very special, magical moon-moo. 'Mooo-ooo-ooo!' Right out of her mouth floated a warm, sweet, glowing cup of starry milk! The milk floated up, up, up into the sky like a little white balloon, right toward the hungry moon. The moon caught the cup with a gentle moonbeam. 'Clink!' went the imaginary cup. 'Slurp, slurp, gulp,' went the happy moon. The milk was warm and sweet and tasted just like sleeping flowers and gentle night breezes. The moon licked its bright lips and smiled a big, glowing crescent smile. 'Thank you, sweet Clara,' whispered the moon. 'That was the best midnight snack in the whole wide universe.' Clara smiled, curled her tail around her legs, and went right back to sleep, knowing she had fed her glowing friend in the sky.

stories.title: Barnyard Ballet
stories.text: The sun was setting behind the red barn, painting the sky pink and orange. All the animals were getting ready for sleep, but Daisy the cow was wide awake. Daisy did not want to sleep. Daisy wanted to dance! Daisy was a very big cow, but she had very light feet. At least, she thought she did. She trotted over to the big wooden fence and looked at her shadow on the ground. 'Time for the grand barnyard ballet,' whispered Daisy to herself. She lifted her right front hoof and pointed it just like a tiny ballerina. Then, she raised both of her big floppy ears like graceful wings. 'One, two, three, moo!' counted Daisy softly. She spun around in a circle. 'Thump, thump, thump,' went her hooves on the soft grass. She leaped into the air. Well, she didn't leap very high, but she made a very nice floating motion with her heavy body. A little brown bunny popped out from the clover patch and watched in amazement. The bunny wiggled his nose and clapped his tiny paws together. 'Hooray for Daisy!' squeaked the bunny. Daisy curtsied. She dipped her head low and swished her long tail back and forth. Next, she tried a grand jeté. She galloped forward and kicked her back leg high. 'Whoops-a-daisy!' she giggled as she almost lost her balance. She wobbled to the left. She wobbled to the right. But she didn't fall down. Instead, she turned it into a funny wiggle dance. She shook her spots from her nose to her tail. She shook her left ear, then her right ear. The bunny started to hop along with her, hopping up and down in the grass. Soon, other animals woke up to watch. The ducks quacked a rhythm. The pigs did a little spin. Daisy felt like the star of the whole world. By the time the moon came up, Daisy was tired out from all her dancing. She gave a big yawn, bowed to her animal friends, and trotted back to the barn. She closed her eyes and dreamed of toe shoes made of grass and stages made of stars.

stories.title: Bessie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly cow named Bessie woke up with a very big yawn. Moooo! Today was a special day because Farmer Joe brought home a brand new pair of shiny red rain boots. Bessie looked down at her four big hooves. She wagged her little tail and thought, Oh boy! Boots would be so much fun to wear! But wait, cows do not wear boots. How would they ever fit? Bessie stepped outside into the muddy barnyard. Squish, squall, squish went the sticky brown mud between her toes. Oh no, her hooves were getting all messy! Bessie trotted over to the big wooden fence where the shiny red boots were sitting in a neat little row. She picked up the first boot in her mouth and tried to put it on her front left hoof. Boop! The boot was way too small. Bessie giggled. She tried a bigger boot on her back hoof. Slip, slide, plop! The boot fell right off into a puddle. Oh dear, making shoes fit a cow is tricky business! Just then, her good friend Barnaby the pig trotted by. Oink, oink! What are you doing, Bessie? Barnaby asked. I want to wear these pretty red boots, Bessie replied, shaking her head. But my hooves are much too big! Barnaby smiled and had a wonderful idea. Why don't you wear them on your ears? he squealed. Bessie laughed and gently placed a boot over each big cow ear. They looked like funny red earmuffs! Then, Barnaby put the other two boots on his little front trotters. We are the boot fashion stars of the farm! Bessie mooed happily. All the other animals gathered around to clap and cheer. The ducks quacked, the sheep baaed, and the chickens clucked. Bessie danced a little muddy jig, shaking her head so the red boots wobbled back and forth. Even though her boots did not go on her feet, they made the best funny hats in the whole wide world. When the sun started to go down, Bessie took off her boots and gave them a nice clean wash with the garden hose. She curled up in the soft hay inside the warm barn, feeling very happy and very sleepy. She closed her big brown eyes and dreamed of red boots and muddy puddles. Goodnight, Bessie. Goodnight, red boots. Moooo, goodnight!

stories.title: Clover Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The sun was slowly going down behind the rolling green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink, orange, and purple. Down in the meadow, a little brown-and-white calf named Clover was munching on sweet clover grass. Munch, crunch, munch. Clover loved the nighttime, but tonight her eyelids felt heavy like big, cozy blankets. Yawn! Clover stretched her front legs way out in front of her and shook her little tail. Time to get ready for bed! But wait, where was her blankie? Clover looked over by the big oak tree, but her blankie was not there. She looked by the wooden water trough, but it was not there either. Oh no! How could Clover go to sleep without her favorite fuzzy green blanket? She decided to ask her animal friends for help. First, she walked over to the fence where Barnaby the horse was standing. Neigh! Have you seen my blankie, Barnaby? Clover asked softly. Barnaby shook his long mane and neighed, No, Clover, I have not seen it. But look up at the sky! The first bright star is shining just for you. Clover looked up, but she still felt a little sleepy and sad. Next, she waddled over to the duck pond. Quack, quack! Mrs. Duck, have you seen my fuzzy green blankie? Clover asked. Mrs. Duck flapped her wings and said, Quack, no! But listen to the crickets singing their sweet lullaby. Chirp, chirp, chirp! Clover listened closely, but she still missed her blanket. Finally, she walked over to her gentle mother, who was waiting by the big red barn. Mama Cow looked down with kind, warm eyes and smiled a big cow smile. Oh, my sweet little Clover, Mama Cow mooed softly. Your blankie is right here on your back! Clover looked down, and sure enough, the patch of green grass she had been resting on earlier had stuck to her fur, looking just like a little green blanket. Clover giggled and rubbed her cheek against her mother's soft neck. Mama Cow wrapped her warm body around Clover, creating the coziest bed in the whole wide world. The crickets sang their gentle song, the stars twinkled like tiny diamonds, and the cool night breeze whispered through the trees. Clover closed her eyes tight. She felt safe, she felt warm, and she felt so very loved. Goodnight, little stars. Goodnight, green meadow. Goodnight, sweet Clover. Moo, moo, sweet dreams.

stories.title: Barnyard Band
stories.text: Good morning, little sunshine! Today is a very loud and very happy day on the farm. Daisy the cow woke up with a big stretch and a happy Mooo! But today, her moo sounded a little bit different. It sounded like music! Daisy decided that today she was going to start the very first barnyard band. She trotted over to the big metal milk pails sitting by the barn door. Clang, clang, bang! Daisy tapped the pails gently with her hoof. Oh, what a wonderful drum beat! Tap, tap, go the hooves, clang, clang, go the pails. Soon, her friends came running to see what all the noise was about. Penny the pig came trotting up with a funny little oink. Oink, oink! Can I play in your band, Daisy? Penny asked, doing a happy little spin. Of course you can, Penny! Daisy mooed with joy. What instrument would you like to play? Penny looked around and found a hollow log on the ground. She tapped it with her little hooves. Thump, thump, thump! That is your bass drum, Penny! Daisy cheered. Next came Sammy the sheep, bounding through the tall green grass. Baa, baa! I want to join the music too! Sammy shouted. Sammy found two smooth wooden spoons and clicked them together. Click, clack, click, clack! Perfect, laughed Daisy. You are our rhythm master. Finally, Bella the duck waddled over, flapping her wings. Quack, quack, quack! I have a wonderful singing voice! Bella announced proudly. Yes, you do, Bella! Let us make the biggest, happiest song in the whole world together. Daisy started with her clanging milk pails, Penny added her deep thumping log, Sammy clicked his wooden spoons, and Bella sang the sweetest quack-quack song you ever did hear. Even the farmer stopped his tractor to listen to the wonderful music. All the animals danced in a big circle, laughing and playing until the sun reached the very top of the sky. When they were all tired out from dancing, they sat down in the soft green grass and shared a big bundle of sweet hay. Making music with friends was the most fun thing a cow could ever do. Daisy gave one last happy moo, and the whole barnyard cheered. Hooray for the band!

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down on the green, green farm, lived a happy little cow named Bessie. Bessie had soft black and white spots and two wiggly ears. She loved to swish her long tail and munch on crunchy green grass. Today, the sun was shining brightly, and the birds were singing a sweet morning song. Bessie walked over to the big red barn to see her farmyard friends. 'Moo, moo!' she called out happily to the little yellow ducklings splashing in the pond. The ducklings quacked back, 'Quack, quack, Bessie! Come play with us!' But Bessie had her mind set on something else. She wanted to explore the big pasture behind the hill. As Bessie trotted along, her big hooves went clippity-clop on the dirt path. The path led right past a big, squishy mud puddle. Bessie stopped. She looked down at the dark, shiny mud. Yesterday's rain had made it extra gooey and wet. Bessie tilted her head. She loved the feel of cool mud between her toes. With a joyful snort, Bessie stepped right into the middle of the puddle. 'Squish, squash, squop!' went the mud. Bessie giggled, shaking her head. She lifted one hoof, then the other, making funny little suction noises. 'Moo-hoo!' she laughed. Just then, Farmer John walked by carrying a bucket of fresh water. He looked at Bessie and chuckled. 'Well, well, Bessie! You look like a very muddy cow today!' Bessie gave a happy flick of her tail and splashed a tiny bit of mud on a daisy. The friendly little frog sitting on a lily pad croaked in approval. Bessie stayed in the puddle for a long, wonderful time until the sun started to get very warm. When she finally stepped out, she was covered in polka dots of mud from head to toe. She walked over to the horse trough for a nice, long drink of cool water. Slurp, slurp, slurp! Then she trotted back to her soft straw bed in the barn, feeling cozy, tired, and very happy. As she closed her big brown eyes for a nap, she dreamed of squishy mud puddles and sweet green grass. Goodnight, Bessie.

stories.title: Daisy's Midnight Snack
stories.text: The moon was high and glowing like a giant silver coin in the dark night sky. All across the farm, the animals were fast asleep. The little pink pigs were snoring in their pen. The fluffy white sheep were cuddled up on the hillside. But in the big red barn, a curious brown cow named Daisy was wide awake. Daisy had big, round eyes and a little pink nose that twitched in the dark. Her tummy let out a funny rumble. 'Rumbly-rumble-rum,' went her tummy. Daisy realized she was hungry. She wanted a midnight snack! She tiptoed out of her cozy straw stall, making sure not to wake the sleepy old barn cat. Tippy-toe, tippy-toe went her hooves. Daisy walked softly across the wooden barn floor. She peeked out the big open barn door. Outside, the night air was cool and smelled sweet like clover and pine trees. The grass was covered in sparkling morning dew that looked like tiny diamonds. Daisy stepped out into the cool night air. She looked up at the twinkling stars and gave a quiet little 'Moo.' The stars seemed to twinkle right back at her. Daisy waddled over to the patch of sweetest clover right by the old wooden fence. The crickets were playing a gentle nighttime lullaby. Rub-a-dub-dub went the crickets' wings. Daisy bent her soft neck down and took a bite of the sweet, dewy grass. Munch, munch, munch. It tasted so delicious in the quiet moonlight! She ate a little bit of clover, then a little bit of dandelion greens. Her tummy felt warm and full. The gentle night breeze blew softly through her ears, making her feel sleepy and cozy. Daisy let out a soft yawn. 'Yaaaawn,' she sighed. It was time to go back to sleep. She walked slowly back into the warm barn, found her soft spot in the hay, and curled up tight. The moon watched over her as she drifted off into sweet dreams. Goodnight, stars. Goodnight, Daisy.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Balloon
stories.text: It was a wonderful day at the farm, and Barnaby the little calf was having a birthday. Barnaby was very playful and loved to chase butterflies through the meadows. Today, his best friend, a little brown puppy named Pip, trotted over with a special surprise in his mouth. Pip was carrying a shiny, bright red balloon tied to a long piece of yellow string. The balloon bobbed up and down in the breeze, looking like a floating cherry. 'Moo-moo!' said Barnaby with great excitement, his eyes widening. Pip dropped the string right into Barnaby's soft pink mouth. Barnaby held the string carefully so he wouldn't pop the balloon with his horns. He walked slowly around the farmyard, showing off his wonderful new toy to everyone. First, he showed the mother hen and her fluffy yellow chicks. The chicks chirped in amazement and fluttered their tiny wings. Next, Barnaby showed the lazy old farm cat, who just blinked sleepily and purred. Barnaby trotted over to the big apple tree, his tail swishing back and forth with joy. Suddenly, a playful gust of wind swept across the pasture. It blew the bright red balloon high up into the air! 'Oh no!' thought Barnaby. The balloon pulled hard on the string, lifting Barnaby's head up high. Barnaby didn't want to let go. He trotted faster, his little hooves going tip-tap, tip-tap on the grass. He leaped into the air in a funny little calf jump. Boing! The balloon floated higher, and Barnaby floated up just a tiny bit too, feeling as light as a feather. Pip barked happily and chased after them both. They ran all around the big green field, laughing in their own special way. Finally, the wind calmed down, and the balloon floated gently back down to earth. Barnaby caught the string with his nose and gave a happy snort. He and Pip sat down together in the soft grass, watching the shiny red balloon dance in the gentle breeze. It was the best birthday ever.

stories.title: Bessie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly cow named Bessie woke up with a very big yawn. Moooo! Today was a special day because the farmer left a big red box right outside her cozy barn door. Bessie blinked her big brown eyes and ambled over to the box, her little bell going clink-clank-clink with every single step. She poked her soft nose inside and gave a happy snort. Inside the shiny box were two bright red boots! They were big and round, just right for cow hooves. Bessie decided right then and there that she simply had to try them on. With a wiggle and a waggle, she slipped her left hoof into the first boot. Then she squeezed her right hoof into the second boot. Oh boy, oh boy! Bessie was wearing boots! She lifted her left hoof and stomped it down. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Mud went flying everywhere, splish, splash, splosh! The other farm animals came running over to see what all the fuss was about. Penny the Pig squealed with delight, and Barnaby the Horse neighed a loud hello. They had never seen a cow in boots before! Bessie felt so proud and tall. She decided to take a little walk around the muddy pasture to show off her fantastic new footwear. She trotted past the hay bales and strolled by the duck pond. The little yellow ducks quacked in surprise and flapped their wings. Bessie smiled her biggest cow smile and gave a cheerful moo. But wait! Walking in heavy boots made Bessie feel very, very hungry. Her tummy began to rumble. Grumble, grumble, went her tummy. It was time for breakfast! She walked over to the sweet clover patch and munched on the green grass. Crunch, crunch, crunch. Eating grass was her absolute favorite thing to do in the whole wide world. After she ate her fill, the warm sun began to shine right on her back, making her feel so cozy and sleepy. Bessie gave a long, gentle yawn and kicked off her big red boots. Her hooves felt so light and free again. She curled up in the soft hay and drifted off to a happy cow dream. What a wonderful day on the farm!

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Moo
stories.text: Deep in the green, green pasture lived a little calf named Barnaby. Barnaby had big floppy ears, a pink wet nose, and the softest white spots on his furry back. Every morning, the sun would peek over the hill, and all the cows would say hello. They would say, Mooo! Mooo! Mooo! But one bright morning, Barnaby woke up and tried to say his morning greeting. He opened his mouth wide and pushed out all his breath. But guess what came out? Nothing! Not a single sound! Barnaby was so surprised that he touched his throat with his hoof. Oh no! Where was his moo? He felt a little bit worried and a little bit sad. How could a little cow be a cow without a proper moo? He decided to go on an adventure across the farm to find his missing sound. First, he trotted over to the muddy pigpen where his friend Oinkers was rolling in the cool mud. Oinkers looked up and said, Oink, oink! Barnaby shook his head and tried to moo, but only a tiny squeak came out. Oinkers blinked and shrugged his curly tail. Next, Barnaby waddled down to the duck pond. The mother duck paddled by with her ducklings and said, Quack, quack! Barnaby tried again, puffing out his cheeks as hard as he could. But still, no moo! The little yellow ducklings peeped in wonder. Barnaby felt like giving up. He sat down by the big oak tree and let out a little sigh. Just then, a tiny brown mouse popped out from the tall grass. The mouse squeaked, Squeak, squeak! And do you know what happened next? When Barnaby heard the mouse, he laughed a big, bouncy toddler laugh! And as he laughed, something tickled his throat. Up, up, up the sound bubbled, right from his tummy and out of his mouth. Moooooo! It was the loudest, happiest moo in the whole wide farm! Barnaby jumped up and danced a little jig. He had found his moo, and it was better than ever. He mooed to the sky, he mooed to the trees, and he mooed a happy goodnight to the setting sun.

stories.title: The Moon That Wanted to Be a Cow
stories.text: High up in the midnight sky, far above the sleepy green farm, lived a bright, round, glowing yellow moon. The moon looked down every single night and watched all the animals doing their bedtime routines. The sheep counted their wool, the owls blinked their golden eyes, and the cows curled up in the soft clover. But the moon had a secret wish. More than anything in the universe, the moon wanted to be a cow! The moon thought cows were just the most magical creatures on earth. They got to walk on the soft green grass, they got to munch on sweet clover, and best of all, they got to jump clear over the moon! The moon giggled a silvery giggle, lighting up the clouds. One quiet Tuesday night, the moon decided to try being a cow right up there in the sky. First, the moon practiced making a cow sound. It whispered softly into the starry night, Mooo... mooo... moo. It sounded just right! Next, the moon tried to chew some imaginary grass, nibbling on a fluffy little white cloud like it was a tasty snack. Yum, yum, yum, thought the moon. But there was one big problem. The moon didn't have any legs to stomp or a tail to swish away the buzzing flies. How could it be a real farm cow without hooves? Down below in the pasture, a wise old cow named Clementine looked up at the glowing sky. Clementine had big kind eyes and wore a shiny brass bell. She saw the moon looking so lonely and wishing so hard. Clementine knew just what to do. She tilted her head back, took a deep breath, and gave the longest, sweetest moo you ever heard. She mooed right up to the stars! Then, Clementine did something amazing. She bent her knees, pushed off the ground, and leaped up, up, up into the air. Wheee! She jumped right over the glowing yellow moon! The moon gasped in delight and clapped its starry hands together. The moon realized it didn't need to be a cow on the ground, because it had a wonderful cow friend right down on the farm who shared the magic of midnight with it every single night. The moon smiled down warmly, wrapping the farm in a blanket of silver light, and whispered one final goodnight moo as the whole world drifted off to sleep.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly cow named Bessie woke up with a big stretch and a happy 'Moo!' The sun was shining warmly, and the yellow buttercups were dancing in the gentle breeze. Bessie loved her morning walks across the dew-kissed grass. Today, she trotted over to her favorite spot near the sparkling blue pond. 'Moo-moo-marching along,' she sang to herself, her four hooves going thump, thump, thump on the soft ground. Near the pond, a funny thing had happened. The recent rain had turned a patch of earth into a big, squishy, mud puddle. It was gooey. It was gloopy. It looked like chocolate pudding! Bessie looked down at her clean, shiny black-and-white hooves. Then, she looked at the squishy mud. Toddlers love mud, and cows do too! Bessie dipped one hoof right into the middle of the puddle. Squish! Squoosh! Bubbles popped up with a happy little sound. 'Plip, plop, squish,' said the mud. Bessie giggled a cow giggle—which sounded a lot like a gentle rumble in her tummy. She stepped her second hoof in, then her third, and her fourth. Now all four of her feet were standing right in the squishy, gooey mud. A little frog hopped by, saying 'Ribbit!' as if to say hello to the muddy cow. Bessie wiggled her toes inside the mud and shook her tail. Splash! A tiny bit of mud flew up and landed right on the tip of her pink nose. Bessie crossed her eyes and tried to look at the mud on her nose. 'Moo!' she laughed. Just then, Farmer John walked by carrying a shiny silver bucket. He saw Bessie standing in the puddle and smiled a big, wide smile. 'Well, hello there, muddy Bessie!' he said kindly. Bessie gave a happy toss of her head. She didn't mind being messy at all, because messy days are the most fun days of all. Farmer John gently washed her hooves with clean, cool water from the hose, and Bessie danced a little happy dance. She trotted back to her green pasture, feeling fresh, clean, and ready for a wonderful nap under the big apple tree.

stories.title: The Moon Jump
stories.text: High up in the midnight sky, the silver moon shone like a giant glowing banana. Down on the farm, all the animals were fast asleep, snoring softly in their cozy beds. But one little calf named Barnaby was wide awake. Barnaby had big brown eyes, floppy ears, and big dreams. He looked up at the twinkling stars and whispered, 'I wonder what it feels like to touch the sky.' Barnaby stood up on his wobbly little legs and gave a soft, sleepy stretch. 'Moo,' he whispered so he wouldn't wake his mama. He trotted over to a little hill where the grass was sweet and short. The wind whispered through the trees, singing a gentle lullaby. Barnaby remembered an old nursery rhyme about a cow that jumped over the moon. He puffed out his furry chest and decided tonight was the very best night to try it. He bent his knees down low. One, two, three—hop! Barnaby leaped up into the cool night air. He went higher than a blade of grass. He went higher than a fence post. He even went higher than the barn roof! For one magical second, Barnaby felt like he was flying. The wind tickled his tummy and ruffled his soft white fur. He reached out a hoof toward the shiny moon. He didn't quite touch the moon—it was still much too far away—but he flew higher than any cow had ever flown before. Whee! It was the most exciting thing that had ever happened to him. Then, gravity gave him a gentle hug and pulled him softly back down. Down, down, down he floated, landing right back in a patch of clover with a soft, bouncy thud. Boing! Barnaby blinked his big eyes and smiled a wide cow smile. He looked up at the moon and gave a happy little moo. 'That was amazing,' he giggled. Yawning a huge, jaw-stretching yawn, Barnaby curled up right where he landed. He tucked his nose under his warm front leg and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of rockets, stars, and soaring high above the sleeping farm.

stories.title: Daisy's Daisy Chain
stories.text: Out in the rolling green meadows where the buttercups bloom, lived a gentle cow named Daisy. Daisy was very special because she loved flowers more than anything else in the whole wide world. Every afternoon when the sun was high and warm, Daisy would go on a flower-finding adventure. Today, she was looking for bright yellow daisies and pretty pink clover. 'Moo-moo-search, search, search,' she hummed softly as she walked through the tall grass. Her big black tail swished back and forth, keeping away the buzzing bumblebees. Suddenly, Daisy spotted a patch of the prettiest flowers she had ever seen. They were growing right near the old wooden fence. Daisy walked over, bent her long neck down, and gently nibbled the stems. Snip! She picked a lovely white daisy with her soft pink lips. Then she picked another, and another, until she had a whole bunch of colorful blossoms resting safely on the grass. Daisy had a clever plan. She wanted to make a special crown to wear on her head, just like a meadow queen. With the help of some friendly bluebirds who tied the stems together with their little beaks, Daisy created a gorgeous flower chain. She carefully lifted her head and let the bluebirds place the crown right between her two pointy horns. It looked magnificent! The flowers smelled sweet like honey and sunshine. Daisy felt so proud that she let out a loud, joyful 'Moo!' that echoed across the valley. All her farmyard friends turned to look. The little brown puppy barked in approval, and the fluffy white sheep gave a happy baa. Daisy trotted over to the horse trough to see her reflection in the clear water. She blinked at the pretty cow looking back at her, wearing a crown of flowers. She felt like the fanciest cow in the whole countryside. She spent the rest of the sunny afternoon parading proudly around the pasture, showing off her wonderful meadow crown to everyone she met, feeling happy, loved, and beautifully adorned.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the big green farm, a friendly cow named Bessie woke up with a big stretch. Moo-oo-oo! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, leaving big, squishy, wonderful puddles everywhere. Bessie loved puddles. She loved how the water tickled her hooves and how the mud squished between her toes. 'Moo!' said Bessie to her best friend, a little fluffy duck named Ducky. Ducky quacked a happy reply and waddled right into the biggest puddle of all. Bessie trotted over, her black and white spots shaking with excitement. She wanted to join the fun. But wait! Cows do not wear shoes, but Bessie had four brand-new, bright yellow rain boots given to her by the farmer. They were shiny and yellow like lemons. Bessie carefully stepped into her first boot. Squish! Then the second boot. Squish! Then the third boot and the fourth boot. Now Bessie had four bright yellow boots on her four big feet. She clip-clopped toward the mud puddle. The other animals gathered around to watch. The pig grunted, the sheep baaed, and the horse neighed softly. Bessie took a deep breath and jumped right in. Splash! Mud went up, mud went down, mud went all around. A big brown blob landed right on Bessie's nose. Bessie licked her nose with her long pink tongue. 'Yum! Well, maybe not yum, but fun!' she giggled. She splashed again. Splash, splash, splash! Ducky flapped his wings and swam in circles, happy to have a cow joining his puddle party. Bessie stamped her left foot, then her right foot, making a funny marching rhythm. Thump, thump, squish, squish! The farmer walked by and laughed out loud, holding a big red towel. 'Well, Bessie,' smiled the farmer, 'it looks like you are the muddiest cow in the whole wide world.' Bessie mooed proudly, shaking her tail. She didn't mind being muddy at all. After a long time of splashing and playing, the sun came out fully and dried the grass. Bessie took off her yellow boots one by one, gave them a good rinse in the water trough, and trotted back to the barn for a well-deserved nap. As she closed her big brown eyes, she dreamed of rain and muddy boots.

stories.title: The Starry Midnight Moo
stories.text: Deep in the valley, when the sun went down and the moon came up, all the farm animals got ready for bed. The chickens tucked their heads under their wings. The horses leaned against the wooden fence. But little calf Barnaby was wide awake. His tummy felt a little empty, and his eyes were wide open like two big shiny buttons. 'Moo?' whispered Barnaby to his mother, Clarabelle. Clarabelle opened one warm, loving eye and nuzzled her baby. 'It is time for sleep, little one,' she hummed softly. But Barnaby shook his head. He looked up at the velvet night sky. The stars were twinkling like tiny diamonds, and the big yellow moon looked just like a giant wedge of delicious cheese. 'I want to reach the stars, Mama,' said Barnaby. Clarabelle smiled a gentle cow smile. 'You don't need to reach the stars, Barnaby. The stars are special friends who watch over us while we sleep.' Barnaby blinked. He watched a shooting star zip across the dark sky. Whoosh! 'Can cows fly?' asked Barnaby, remembering the nursery rhyme he had heard the farmer sing earlier that day. Clarabelle chuckled, a low, rumbling sound that felt like a warm blanket. 'Some magical cows can, in stories. But real cows have strong hooves made for walking on the sweet green grass.' Barnaby stood up on his wobbly legs and stretched. He took a few steps away from his mother and looked at his shadow cast by the moonlight. He tried to tiptoe as high as he could. He stretched his neck up toward the sky and let out a soft, tiny, musical moo. Moo-ooo! The wind blew gently, rustling the leaves in the apple tree. A firefly danced right in front of Barnaby's nose, blinking its yellow light on and off. Barnaby giggled and tried to touch the bug with his wet nose, but the firefly fluttered up higher. 'Goodnight, little star,' whispered Barnaby to the firefly. Suddenly, a big yawn popped out of Barnaby's mouth. His legs felt heavy, and his eyelids felt like they were made of lead. The moon seemed to glow a little brighter, wrapping the whole meadow in a cozy silver light. Clarabelle pulled her baby close, wrapping her warm body around him to keep him safe and snug. Barnaby rested his heavy head on the soft hay. He closed his eyes and listened to the peaceful nighttime sounds of the farm. Crickets chirped a lullaby, the night breeze hummed through the trees, and his mother breathed a slow, steady rhythm. Barnaby smiled in his sleep, dreaming of dancing with the moon and jumping over the stars.

stories.title: The Great Clover Hunt
stories.text: Morning had broken, and the grass sparkled with morning dew. Daisy the cow woke up with a rumble in her tummy. Her tummy made a funny sound. Grrr-moo! It was breakfast time, but not just any breakfast. Today, Daisy wanted something extra special. She wanted a lucky four-leaf clover. Daisy knew that four-leaf clovers were hard to find, but she was a very determined cow. She flicked her tail, swished away a sleepy fly, and set off on a grand adventure across the meadow. First, she checked near the old wooden fence where the yellow buttercups grew. She bent her long neck down and sniffed. Sniff, sniff, sniff. She found a bumblebee collecting pollen. 'Bzzzt!' said the bee. 'Excuse me,' said Daisy politely. 'Have you seen a four-leaf clover?' The bee shook his fuzzy head and flew away to a red flower. Daisy kept walking. Clpp-clop, clpp-clop went her hooves on the soft earth. Next, she checked by the big gray rock where the little brown bunnies liked to play. She peeked behind the rock. There sat three fluffy bunnies twitching their noses. 'Hello, bunnies,' mooed Daisy softly. 'Are there any lucky clovers hiding here?' The bunnies hopped around, wiggling their cotton tails, but they didn't see any four-leaf clovers. Just regular three-leaf clovers, which were tasty too, but not quite what Daisy was looking for. Daisy let out a little sigh. Her shoulders slumped. Finding a four-leaf clover was harder than she thought. Just then, a little yellow butterfly landed right on Daisy's black and white ear. It fluttered its wings and flew a few feet away, landing right in the middle of a patch of green grass under the shade of the apple tree. 'Are you trying to show me something?' asked Daisy with a hopeful smile. She trotted over to the apple tree and looked down at the bright green patch. She pushed aside a blade of grass with her nose. And there, shining brightly in a ray of sunlight, was a perfect, beautiful, four-leaf clover. Daisy gasped with joy. 'I found it!' she shouted happily. She gently plucked the clover with her lips and chewed it slowly. It tasted extra sweet and crunchy. Daisy did a little happy dance, shaking her head and kicking her back legs. The bunnies hopped, the bee buzzed, and the butterfly danced in the air. It was the best breakfast a lucky cow could ever ask for.

stories.title: Bessie's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of a big green pasture, lived a friendly brown cow named Bessie. Bessie loved the warm sunshine, the sweet-smelling clover, and her very best friends in the whole wide world. Her best friends were a bouncy little lamb named Woolly and a cheerful yellow duck named Ducky. Every single day, the three friends would play games together until the sun went down. One morning, after a big rainstorm, Bessie woke up and looked outside. The grass was wet, the leaves were shiny, and there were big, squishy puddles everywhere! Bessie loved puddles. She gave a happy 'Moo!' and trotted over to the biggest puddle in the field. 'Look at this!' said Bessie. She stepped right in with her big hooves. Squelch, squish, squelch! Mud bubbled up around her toes. 'That looks like fun!' quacked Ducky, splashing in the shallow water. Woolly the lamb bounced on his little legs, eager to join the game. 'Me too, me too!' cried Woolly. He jumped forward, but oh dear, Woolly slipped! He landed right on his fuzzy little tummy in the soft, brown mud. Oh no! Woolly was covered in mud from his nose to his fluffy tail. He looked like a chocolate sheep! Bessie and Ducky giggled. 'Are you okay, Woolly?' asked Bessie gently. Woolly shook himself, sending little mud drops flying everywhere. 'I am okay! And I am very muddy!' he laughed. Then, Bessie had a wonderful idea. If Woolly was a chocolate sheep, she could be a polka-dot cow! Bessie stomped her feet, making more mud splash up her legs. Ducky flapped his wings and sprayed water droplets all around them. They played and played, making silly mud pies and laughing until their tummies hurt. Soon, the warm sun came out from behind a fluffy cloud and dried up the puddles. It was time to go home to the big red barn. Farmer John was waiting with a bucket of fresh water and a big smile. 'Well, well, look at my little explorers!' said Farmer John. He gently washed the mud away with a nice, warm sponge. Bessie felt clean, cozy, and very sleepy. She snuggled down in the soft hay beside Woolly and Ducky, dreaming of the next big adventure in the mud.

stories.title: The Moon That Ran Away
stories.text: It was bedtime on the farm, and the moon was shining bright like a giant silver coin in the dark blue sky. Inside the cozy barn, a little spotted calf named Barnaby was trying very hard to go to sleep. But Barnaby was too excited. He blinked his big brown eyes and looked out the open barn door. High up in the sky, he saw the shiny white moon hanging right over the hill. 'Moo,' whispered Barnaby to his mama. 'Look at the moon. It looks just like a giant silver balloon.' Mama Cow smiled and nudged him with her warm nose. 'It sure does, little one. Now close your eyes and dream sweet dreams.' Barnaby closed his eyes for a moment, but then he heard a funny sound outside. Whoosh! The wind blew through the tall grass. Barnaby opened his eyes again and looked out. Oh no! The moon was gone! The sky where the moon had been was completely dark. Barnaby gasped. 'Mama, wake up! The moon ran away!' Mama Cow opened one sleepy eye. 'Did it now?' she murmured. 'Yes! It rolled right down the hill and hid!' whispered Barnaby. Being a very brave little calf, Barnaby decided he must go find the missing moon. He tiptoed out of the barn on his little hooves. Tap, tap, tap went his feet on the quiet dirt path. He walked past the sleeping chickens. He walked past the big tractor. Finally, he reached the top of the big green hill.
