The red ball rolled away through the green grass. Barnaby let out a happy little whinny. "Neigh!" he said, which meant, "This is so much fun!" He trotted after the rolling ball, his hooves making a happy sound on the dirt path. The ball bumped into a little yellow daisy and bounced back toward Barnaby. This time, Barnaby used his nose to give it a bigger push. Whee! The ball bounced across the field. A fluffy white sheep looked up from her munching and blinked. A little pink piglet giggled and wiggled his curly tail. Barnaby felt so joyful that he did a little happy dance, kicking up his back heels and shaking his fluffy mane. The sun was warm, the grass was sweet, and Barnaby had his very own bouncing ball to play with. But soon, Barnaby felt a little rumble in his tummy. Playing games was wonderful, but lunchtime was even better! Barnaby trotted over to the wooden fence where the farmer had left a big, fresh pile of crunchy carrots and sweet green apples. Barnaby munched happily, crunch, crunch, crunch. He rubbed his soft nose against the wooden post, feeling safe and loved. As the afternoon breeze blew gently through the trees, Barnaby took a little rest in the shady grass, dreaming of red balls and sunny green fields.

stories.title: Bella's Muddy Hooves
stories.text: Bella was a sparkly white pony who lived in a cozy red barn at the edge of a rolling green hill. Bella loved many things: she loved sweet yellow corn, she loved fluffy white clouds, and most of all, she loved when the rain stopped and the sun came out to play. One morning, after a big rainstorm during the night, Bella woke up and peeked her head out of her stall. Squish, squat, squish went her hooves as she stepped outside into the yard. Oh, dear! The rain had made a giant, wonderful, gooey puddle right by the barn door. Bella stopped and looked down at the dark, shiny mud. Most horses might have tried to step around it, but Bella had a very playful spark in her heart. She lifted one front hoof and dipped it right into the middle of the puddle. Plop! Mud squished up between her toes in the funniest way. Bella giggled in horse language, shaking her head. She stomped her other front foot down. Splash! Mud droplets flew up into the air like tiny brown fireflies. A little brown bird sitting on the fence chirped a loud tweet of surprise. Bella decided this was the best game in the whole wide world. She trotted in a little circle, making her hooves go squish-splash, squish-splash, until her white legs were covered in cozy brown mud socks. She looked down at herself and gave a happy snort. She looked completely silly! Just then, Farmer Jill walked out of the barn carrying a big bucket of water and a large, soft brush. Farmer Jill saw the muddy pony and smiled a big, warm smile. "Well, hello there, little mud monster!" Farmer Jill laughed. Bella tilted her head and gave a soft, friendly whinny. Farmer Jill used the warm water and the soft brush to wash away all the silly mud, singing a gentle song while she worked. Bella stood very still, enjoying the warm water tickling her back. Once she was sparkly white again, Farmer Jill gave her a crunchy apple reward. Bella chewed happily, knowing that mud puddles were fun, but being a clean pony with a full tummy was the best ending of all.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was beginning to sink low behind the big green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink, purple, and sleepy orange. High up in the pasture, a little brown horse named Starry was getting ready for bed. Starry had a white star right on his forehead that twinkled just like the ones in the night sky. But before Starry could go to sleep, he needed to say goodnight to all his favorite things on the farm. First, Starry trotted softly over to the old oak tree. "Goodnight, tall tree," Starry whispered with a soft blow of air from his nose. The tree leaves rustled a gentle whisper back, shhh, shhh. Next, Starry walked over to the wooden fence where his friend the little brown bunny lived. "Goodnight, bunny," Starry said. The bunny wiggled his long ears and gave a little hop into his cozy burrow. Starry made his way down the winding dirt path toward his warm, straw-filled barn. The air was getting cooler, and the crickets were beginning to sing their evening song. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. Starry stepped inside his cozy stall, where the sweet smell of dried hay filled the air. He yawned a big, wide horse yawn, showing his teeth. He lowered his head slowly, letting his heavy eyelids close for a moment. He curled his legs underneath his warm body and lay down in the deep, golden straw. It was so soft and comfortable. Outside, the very first real star of the evening blinked in the darkening blue sky, shining right down through the barn window onto Starry's special white forehead star. Starry closed his eyes tight and listened to the quiet sounds of the farm settling down for the night. He felt safe, he felt warm, and he felt deeply loved. With one final, contented sigh, the little horse drifted off into a deep, sweet sleep, dreaming of green grass, sunny skies, and tomorrow's brand new adventures.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat, a swishy tail, and four strong hooves that went clippity-clop, clippity-clop on the soft grass. Barnaby loved to run and jump, but most of all, Barnaby loved his toys. Today, Barnaby had a brand new toy. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! Barnaby trotted over to the red ball. He gave it a gentle nudge with his soft velvet nose. Boop! The red ball rolled a little bit forward. Barnaby giggled. He tossed his head and gave the ball a little kick with his front hoof. Whee! The ball bounced across the green grass, rolling past the fluffy sheep and the sleepy cow. Barnaby chased after it, going trot-trot-trot as fast as his little legs could carry him. He caught up to the ball just before it rolled into the muddy puddle. 'Not today, puddle!' neighed Barnaby happily. He nudged the ball back toward his favorite shady apple tree. A little red apple fell from the tree with a plop, right next to the red ball. Barnaby looked at the apple, and then he looked at the ball. He decided to share his game with his bird friends. Two little yellow birds landed on top of the red ball and chirped a happy song. Barnaby danced around them in a big circle, stamping his hooves softly. Clop-clop-clop, goes the happy horse! The sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange. Barnaby was getting very sleepy now. He gave the red ball one last gentle nuzzle and whispered, 'Goodnight, red ball.' He curled up in the warm straw of his cozy barn, closed his big brown eyes, and dreamed of bouncing red balls and sweet green grass. The end.

stories.title: Bella's Morning Trot
stories.text: Good morning, little horse! Her name is Bella, and she has a sparkly white star right on her forehead. When the golden sun wakes up, Bella wakes up too. She stretches her long legs and shakes her fluffy tail. Shake, shake, shake! Bella steps out of her warm wooden stable and sniffs the fresh morning air. Sniff, sniff, ahh, it smells like sweet clover and morning dew. Time for a morning walk! Bella starts to move. First, she walks slowly. Clop, clop, clop goes her hooves on the dirt path. She sees a little brown bunny hopping in the bushes. 'Good morning, bunny!' thinks Bella, twitching her soft ears. Then, Bella hears the birds singing in the tall trees. Tweet-tweet! She decides to speed up a little bit. Now she is doing a bouncy trot. Trot-trot-trot, trot-trot-trot! Her mane bounces up and down in the wind. It feels so good to run! Bella runs across the meadow, jumping over a tiny yellow dandelion flower. She stops by the sparkly blue stream to take a big, slurping drink of cool water. Slurp, slurp, ahh, that is so refreshing. After her drink, Bella sees her best friend, a little speckled pony named Pip. Pip comes running over, and they touch noses. Boop! They are so happy to see each other. They prance together in the sunshine, kicking up their heels. Playtime is the best time of the day. But soon, the morning turns into afternoon, and Bella's tummy starts to rumble. It is time for a yummy lunch of green grass. Bella munches and crunches until she is full and happy. What a wonderful day for a little white-starred horse.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Pip was a tiny pony with fuzzy brown ears and a fluffy white mane. Pip lived on a friendly farm with ducks, pigs, and sheep. Yesterday, it rained and rained and rained. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the raindrops on the big red barn roof. Today, the rain had stopped, and the sun was shining brightly in the blue sky. But the rain left something behind. Big, squishy, brown puddles! Pip loved puddles. He trotted over to the biggest puddle in the middle of the yard. Squish, squash, squish went his little hooves in the wet mud. Pip giggled and shook his head. He looked down and saw his reflection in the water. Hello, reflection Pip! Pip lifted one front hoof and splashed the water. Splash! Water droplets flew everywhere, sparkling in the sunshine. A little pink pig waddled over, oinking happily. 'Oink, oink, can I play too?' asked the pig. 'Neigh, neigh!' said Pip, which meant yes! Pip and the pig splashed in the mud together, making bubbles and laughing. Pip's brown legs were now covered in funny brown mud boots. He looked just like a mud monster! Then, Farmer John came out with a big bucket of water and a soft brush. 'Well, look at you two muddy animals,' laughed Farmer John. 'Time for a bath!' Pip stood very still while Farmer John washed away the tickly mud with warm water. Scrub, scrub, scrub went the brush. Pip's coat became shiny and clean again. Pip gave a happy shake and neighed a big 'Thank you!' to the farmer. He did a happy little dance, clippity-clop, ready for his next fun adventure on the sunny farm.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green farm, there lived a little brown horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a soft white star on his forehead and four little hooves that went clippety-clop all day long. Barnaby loved to run in the big pasture, munch on crunchy green grass, and swish his long tail at the buzzy bees. One bright morning, Farmer Fred left a big, shiny red ball right in the middle of the yard. Barnaby stopped munching. He blinked his big brown eyes. What could that bouncy thing be? Barnaby took one step closer. Sniff, sniff, went his velvety nose. The ball smelled like shiny new rubber and fun. Barnaby decided to say hello. He gave the big red ball a gentle nudge with his nose. Boing! The ball rolled across the grass. Barnaby giggled in horse language, which sounded like a soft, happy snort. He trotted after it. Trot, trot, trot, went his hooves. The ball stopped near the wooden fence. Barnaby tried to nudge it again, but this time it rolled a little faster. He thought it was the best game ever invented. Then, a little yellow butterfly landed right on top of the red ball. Barnaby stayed very, very still so he wouldn't scare his tiny new friend. The butterfly fluttered its wings, up and down, up and down, before flying away into the blue sky. Barnaby gave the ball one more happy little push. It rolled all the way back to the barn door, right where Farmer Fred was standing with a bucket of sweet oats. Farmer Fred smiled and patted Barnaby's warm neck. Good boy, Barnaby, said the farmer. Did you have fun playing with your new toy? Barnaby gave a soft neigh and munched his yummy oats. It had been the most exciting day on the farm. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Barnaby gave a big yawn. He curled up in the soft, golden hay inside his cozy stall, closed his big sleepy eyes, and dreamed sweet dreams about chasing bouncy red balls all the way to the moon and back.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Meadow
stories.text: High up on a rolling green hill lived a gentle white pony named Starry. Starry was very special because she loved the nighttime. While all the other farm animals went to sleep when the sun went down, Starry liked to look up at the sparkly stars twinkling in the dark sky. One evening, the little moon was a bright silver crescent, smiling down at the quiet earth. Starry stretched her front legs and shook her long, silky mane. Time for a midnight stroll, she whispered softly to herself. She walked very quietly across the grass so she wouldn't wake up the sleeping sheep. Softly, softly went her tiny hooves. Squish, squatch, went the cool grass beneath her feet. Starry looked up and saw a little firefly buzzing near a big oak tree. Hello, little light, said Starry. The firefly blinked its tiny yellow light, as if saying hello back. Starry trotted over to the bubbling brook to take a cool drink of water. Slurp, slurp, went Starry. The water was as clear as glass, showing the bright stars reflecting right back up at her. She felt so happy and peaceful. Suddenly, a soft breeze whispered through the leaves of the trees. Whoosh. It sounded like a lullaby singing to the whole world. Starry felt her eyelids growing heavier and heavier. Her adventures for the night were coming to an end. She walked over to her favorite patch of soft, clover-filled grass right beneath the giant oak tree. She gently laid her sleepy body down, folding her legs neatly beneath her. She rested her head on a pillow of soft green moss. The crickets began to sing a gentle bedtime song. Chirp, chirp, chirp. Starry closed her eyes and let out a long, cozy sigh. The stars watched over her from the velvet sky, twinkling their brightest light to keep her safe all through the night. Starry drifted off into a deep, happy sleep, waiting for the sunrise of a brand new day.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Pip was a tiny pony with a shiny black coat and a very curious nose. Pip lived in a cozy corral next to a big red barn. Today, the sky was filled with big gray clouds, and after a loud rumble of thunder, rain began to fall. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter, went the raindrops on the barn roof. Pip loved the rain. It made everything look fresh and green. But best of all, the rain made puddles. Big, squishy, muddy puddles. As soon as the rain stopped and the sun peeked out again, Farmer Meg opened the wooden gate. Pip dashed right out into the yard. Trot, trot, splash! Pip's hoof landed right in the biggest puddle he could find. Mud flew up into the air and landed with a splat on the grass. Pip giggled and stamped his front foot again. Squish, squash, squish! His hoof made funny sucking sounds in the thick, brown mud. Pip thought it was the most wonderful game in the whole wide world. He trotted over to the old wooden fence and shook his wet mane, sending sparkly water droplets flying everywhere. A little brown duck waddled over, tilting its head in surprise. Quack, quack! said the duck, as if asking to join in on the fun. Pip tossed his head and gave a happy little whinny. Come on in, the mud is lovely! he seemed to say. Soon, Pip was covered in friendly brown mud from his nose all the way down to his hooves. He looked like a chocolate-covered pony. Just then, Farmer Meg walked over with a big sponge and a warm bucket of water. Oh, Pip, she laughed, shaking her head with a smile. Look at you! You are one muddy little horse. Pip stood very still while Farmer Meg washed away the squishy mud, giving him gentle scratches behind his ears. Pip closed his eyes in pure bliss. Even though the mud was gone, Pip knew he would always remember his wonderfully messy puddle adventure.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the farm, a friendly little horse named Barnaby trotted out of his cozy stable. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat that sparkled in the morning light, a fluffy white mane, and the softest black nose. Today, Barnaby felt extra happy. He kicked up his back hooves and gave a loud, cheerful neigh! 'Neigh-neigh!' he called out to his friends, the fuzzy yellow ducklings by the pond. Barnaby loved playing outside, but today he was looking for something very special. He wanted to find a new game to play in the big green meadow. As Barnaby trotted near the old oak tree, he spotted a wonderful surprise sitting right in the tall grass. It was a big, bright, shiny red ball! Barnaby had never seen a ball this big before. He walked closer and gave it a tiny gentle poke with his soft nose. Boing! The big red ball rolled a little bit to the left. Barnaby’s big brown eyes grew wide with excitement. He gave a happy little prance. This was going to be the best game ever! He pushed the ball with his nose, and it rolled all the way across the soft green grass. 'Whee!' thought Barnaby, even though horses don't usually say whee out loud. Soon, Pip the little brown bunny hopped over to see what all the fun was about. 'Can I play too, Barnaby?' Pip seemed to wiggle his nose and say. Barnaby nodded his head up and down. Of course his furry friend could play! Barnaby gently nudged the big red ball toward Pip, and Pip used his tiny paws to push it right back. They played catch for a long, long time under the warm sunshine. The little ducklings waddled over and queped happily, cheering for Barnaby and Pip. The ball bounced this way and that way, making everyone giggle and smile. When the afternoon sun started to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby knew it was almost time for dinner. He felt wonderfully tired from all the fun running and playing. Barnaby nudged the big red ball safely back into the corner of the cozy barn so it would be ready for tomorrow. He munched on a sweet, crunchy carrot and let out a long, sleepy yawn. Barnaby curled up in the fresh straw, closing his eyes with a happy heart, dreaming of all the games he would play with his round red friend tomorrow. Goodnight, Barnaby.

stories.title: Bella's Muddy Hooves
stories.text: Deep in the green pasture lived a sweet little pony named Bella. Bella had spots like creamy snowflakes on her back and a tail that swoished like a feather duster. Bella loved many things in the world: sweet green grass, crunchy red apples, and warm summer breezes. But above all things, Bella loved jumping in puddles! Yesterday, it had rained a big, splashing rain all afternoon. The big gray clouds cried giant teardrops, filling the farmyard with wonderful, squishy, mud puddles. When the sun woke up this morning, the sky was bright blue again, and the ground was nice and squishy. Bella woke up, stretched her front legs, and trotted right over to the biggest, muddiest puddle near the old red barn. 'Squish, squash, squish,' went the mud between her toes. Bella looked down at her feet and giggled. Her neat, clean hooves were now covered in thick, chocolatey mud! She lifted up her front left hoof and gave a happy little stomp. Splash! Mud flew up into the air in tiny brown dots. That was so much fun! Bella decided to do it again. She stomped her front right hoof. Splash! More mud flew everywhere, landing softly on the green grass. Then Bella did a little happy dance, tapping her toes in the puddles. Squish, squish, splash, splash! Farmer John walked out of the barn carrying a bucket of fresh water, and he stopped when he saw Bella. Bella tilted her head and blinked her big brown eyes, wondering if the farmer would be mad about the mess. But Farmer John just chuckled a deep, rumbling laugh. He loved happy little ponies. 'Well, look at you, Bella!' Farmer John said with a smile. Bella gave a soft, happy snort, as if to say, 'I am a muddy monster!' She trotted around the yard, leaving a trail of funny muddy footprints behind her. Soon, her pony friend Clover came over to see what was happening. Clover looked at the big puddle, then looked at Bella’s muddy legs. Clover decided to join in the fun, too! Soon, both little ponies were splashing and trotting through the soft, warm mud, having the greatest adventure on the farm. When they were all tired out from splashing, the sun dried the mud just a little bit, keeping them warm. Finally, Farmer John brought out a big hose with nice, cool water. He gently washed away all the mud, making Bella’s coat shiny and clean once more. Bella nuzzled Farmer John’s hand to say thank you. Even though the mud was gone, Bella knew there would always be another rainy day, and she could hardly wait for her next muddy adventure.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Lullaby
stories.text: The moon was high and glowing like a bright silver coin in the deep blue night sky. All across the farm, the animals were getting ready for bed. The little chicks tucked their heads under their soft wings, the cows curled up in the soft hay, and the sleepy barn owls whispered quiet hoots in the dark. But in the middle of the meadow, a little white horse named Starry was still wide awake. Starry had a coat as white as fresh winter snow and a mane that looked like twinkling stars. Starry looked up at the night sky and blinked his big, sleepy eyes. He was tired, oh so tired, but he just wasn't quite ready to go to sleep yet. The wind blew softly through the tall grass, making a gentle rustling sound, like a whispered song. 'Hush, little horse,' whispered the wind. Starry let out a soft sigh and took a slow, quiet walk across the meadow. The grass felt cool and tickly against his little hooves. A tiny firefly buzzed by, glowing with a warm yellow light, dancing around Starry’s nose. Starry followed the firefly with his eyes as it danced up toward the sleepy clouds. The night was so peaceful and quiet. Starry walked over to his favorite sleeping spot under the big weeping willow tree. The long leaves of the tree hung down like green curtains, making a cozy, private room just for him. Starry gently lay down on the soft, thick bed of green grass. He curled his legs up close to his tummy and rested his heavy head on the ground. The crickets in the grass began to sing their evening lullaby. Chirp, chirp, go to sleep. Chirp, chirp, rest your head. Starry closed his eyes slowly. He thought about the sunshine he would see tomorrow, the green grass he would eat, and the fun games he would play with his friends when the morning light returned. But for now, it was time to rest. The stars blinked down at him like friendly little nightlights, watching over him in the dark. Starry breathed in deep, and breathed out slow. His tummy rose and fell in a steady, gentle rhythm. The farm grew quieter and quieter until there was nothing to hear except the gentle rustle of the night breeze. Starry drifted off into a deep, sweet sleep, dreaming of flying across the sky on wings of starlight. Goodnight, Starry. Sleep tight until the morning sun.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the farm, a little brown horse named Barnaby woke up with a very big yawn. Yaaawn! Barnaby loved jumping in puddles after the rain, but his hooves always got a little bit muddy and cold. Today, Farmer Fred had a wonderful surprise waiting right outside the big red barn. What could it be? Barnaby trotted out with a happy click-clack, click-clack of his shoes. There, sitting in the soft green grass, were four shiny red boots! They were bright, they were bouncy, and they were just the right size for a little pony. Barnaby blinked his big brown eyes in surprise. He gently stepped his left front hoof into the first boot. Squish! Then his right front hoof. Squish! Next came the back left hoof, and finally, the back right hoof. Now Barnaby was wearing four bright red boots from top to bottom! He felt so proud. He wanted to show all his farmyard friends his brand new look. First, he trotted over to see Penelope the pig. Penelope squealed with delight, 'Oink, oink! Those boots are simply marvelous, Barnaby!' Barnaby tossed his mane and pranced proudly toward the duck pond. Quack, quack! went the ducks, flapping their wings in approval. 'Waddle-dee-doo, what a dashing pony!' they cheered. Barnaby felt like dancing. He did a little twist and a little twirl. He stomped one foot, then two feet, making a funny squishy sound in the mud. Squish, squash, squish! But wait, wearing boots made running a tiny bit tricky. When Barnaby tried to gallop fast across the meadow, he slipped just a little bit. Whoops-a-daisy! He realized that while boots were super fun for splashing, his own bare hooves were much better for running fast like the wind. With a soft neigh of thanks, Barnaby slipped the boots off and placed them neatly by the fence. Then, he kicked up his heels and ran, free as a bird, through the warm summer grass. It was the best day ever, and Barnaby learned that sometimes the best outfit is the one you were born with. As the sun began to set behind the rolling hills, Barnaby trotted back to his cozy stall, curled up in the soft straw, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of red boots and sunny days.

stories.title: The Little Starry Pony
stories.text: High up in the dreamy sky, right next to the sleepy silver moon, lived a magical little horse named Starry. Starry was not like other horses because he had a coat that twinkled just like the night sky, dotted with glowing yellow stars. Every evening when the sun went down and the world grew quiet, Starry would slide down a rainbow slide right into the children's meadow. His job was very important. He helped all the little animals of the forest find their way home to bed. One quiet night, Starry heard a tiny, sad sound coming from behind a big pumpkin patch. Sniff, sniff, boo-hoo. Starry trotted over on quiet, velvety hooves. There sat Oliver the little owl, blinking his big round eyes. 'Oh, Starry!' hooted Oliver softly. 'I flew too far away from my tree house, and now it is too dark to see the path!' Starry smiled a warm, gentle smile. He lowered his shiny head so Oliver could climb right up onto his back. 'Hold on tight, little owl,' whispered Starry in a voice as soft as a breeze. With a gentle kick of his glittering legs, Starry lifted off the ground and began to float just a few inches above the tall grass. His glowing star-coat lit up the dark path like a magical nightlight. The little trees whispered hello, and the sleeping flowers smiled as they passed. They flew past the sleepy brook that went babbling by in the dark. They floated right over the sleeping sheep who were dreaming of fluffy clouds. Soon, they reached the big oak tree where Oliver lived with his family. Oliver hopped out of Starry's mane and landed safely on his branch. 'Thank you, Starry! You are my hero!' hooted Oliver happily, closing his eyes for a cozy sleep. Starry neighed a quiet goodnight and floated back up into the starry sky. He curled up next to the crescent moon, feeling warm and happy inside. He knew that helping a friend is the greatest magic of all. With one last twinkle of his glowing coat, Starry drifted off to sleep, waiting for the next wonderful adventure under the midnight sky.

stories.title: Clover's Carrot Crunch
stories.text: Deep in the green and leafy valley lived a cheerful white pony named Clover. Clover had a silky white mane that bounced when he walked, and a pink nose that loved to sniff the morning air. Now, Clover had one absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world, and that thing was crunchy, orange carrots! Every single morning, Farmer Meg would bring Clover a big wooden bucket filled with fresh vegetables from her garden. Clover knew the exact time the bucket would arrive. He would stand by the wooden fence, tapping his front hoof impatiently. Tap, tap, tap! Goes the little white pony. At last, the gate would open, and Farmer Meg would walk in carrying the heavy wooden bucket. 'Good morning, my sweet Clover!' she would say with a bright smile. Clover would dip his soft velvet muzzle right into the bucket. He would search through the green tops until he found the biggest, crunchiest orange carrot of the lot. He would pick it up with his soft lips and give it a loud, happy crunch! Cronch, cronch, cronch! Orange carrot bits would fly everywhere, but Clover did not mind at all. He thought carrot juice was the most delicious drink a pony could ever wish for. One morning, however, something very funny happened. Farmer Meg brought the bucket just like always, but when Clover looked inside, there were no carrots at all! Instead, the bucket was filled with round, bumpy purple turnips. Clover blinked. He sniffed once. He sniffed twice. He nudged the turnips with his pink nose. A turnip is definitely not a carrot! Just then, Farmer Meg giggled. 'Oh, silly me! I left your carrots in the vegetable basket by the porch!' she said, running back to fetch them. While she was gone, Clover decided to give one little purple turnip a tiny nibble. Nibble, nibble. Yuck! It tasted too spicy and sharp. Clover shook his head so hard his ears flopped. No turnips for this pony! Just then, Farmer Meg returned with a shiny bunch of fresh carrots. Clover let out a loud, joyful neigh. He munched and crunched his favorite treat until his tummy was completely full and happy. With a contented sigh, Clover lay down in the warm sunshine and took a long, peaceful afternoon nap, dreaming of orange fields as far as the eye could see.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green farm, there lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a coat the color of sweet honey and a mane as soft as a cloud. Every morning, the farm gate would open, and Barnaby would trot out into the big pasture to say hello to his animal friends. The sheep would say, 'Baa!' and Barnaby would give a happy, gentle 'Neigh!' Today was a very special day because Barnaby saw something bright and shiny sitting near the old wooden fence. It was a big red ball! Barnaby had never seen a big red ball before. He walked slowly over to it, his hooves going click-clack on the soft grass. He lowered his velvety nose and gave the ball a tiny little nudge. Boop! The ball rolled a little bit to the left. Barnaby’s big brown eyes widened with delight. He gave the ball a slightly bigger nudge with his nose. Wheee! The ball rolled all the way across the clover patch. Barnaby trotted after it, his tail swishing happily in the warm breeze. He gently tapped the ball with his front hoof. Tap! The ball bounced and rolled toward the sleepy brown cow resting under the shade of the big oak tree. The cow blinked her big brown eyes and mooed softly as the ball rolled right past her nose. Barnaby trotted up, stopped right beside the ball, and let out a happy snort. He looked at the cow as if to say, 'Look at my fun game!' A little yellow butterfly fluttered down and landed right on top of the red ball, as if it wanted to join the game too. Barnaby stayed very still so he wouldn't scare the tiny butterfly away. He loved his new toy more than anything in the whole wide world. When the golden sun began to dip low in the sky, painting the clouds in shades of pink and orange, Farmer John came walking down the path. 'Time for bed, Barnaby,' called the kind farmer. Barnaby gave one last gentle nudge to his ball, making it roll into the cozy barn. Then, he trotted inside, curled up in his soft, clean straw bed, and dreamed all night long about chasing his big red ball across the green, green grass.

stories.title: Bella's Muddy Hooves
stories.text: Down by the sparkling blue stream lived Bella, a playful young pony with a coat as white as fresh winter snow. Bella loved nothing more than running fast across the meadows, feeling the cool wind rush through her long white mane. One afternoon, after a gentle morning rain shower, the farmyard was very wet. Puddles of squishy, gooey mud were everywhere. Bella trotted out of her warm stable and looked down at the ground. Squish, squash, went her front hoof right into a big puddle. Bella tilted her head and giggled a little horse giggle. She lifted her hoof and watched the dark mud drip down. Splash! She stomped her other hoof into the puddle, sending shiny water droplets flying up into the air like tiny diamonds. That looked like so much fun! Bella decided to do a little puddle dance. Left hoof squish, right hoof splash! She danced all around the farmyard, making funny brown patterns on her usually spotless white legs. Soon, her best friend, a fluffy black-and-white sheep named Pip, trotted over to see what all the noise was about. Pip took one look at Bella’s very muddy legs and let out a funny little sneeze. 'Baa-aah!' Pip seemed to say, 'You look so silly!' Bella tossed her head and neighed cheerfully. She did one more big stomp into the biggest puddle of all, splashing a tiny bit of water near Pip’s clean white wool. Pip jumped backward with a start, then shook his fluffy head and playfully bumped his head against Bella’s shoulder. They chased each other around the big apple tree, their hooves making funny squishy sounds in the wet earth. By the time the sun came out to dry the puddles, Bella was the muddiest pony on the entire farm. She had mud on her knees, mud on her ankles, and even a little smudge right on the tip of her pink nose. Just then, Farmer Sarah walked over with a big hose filled with cool, refreshing water. 'Well, well, looks like someone had a grand adventure today,' the farmer laughed. Bella stood very still and closed her eyes happily as the cool water washed away all the squishy mud. She felt clean, fresh, and ready for a nice long nap in the warm afternoon sun.

stories.title: Starry's Midnight Trot
stories.text: High up on a green hill, where the grass was sweet and the sky touched the clouds, lived a magical little horse named Starry. Starry was named because he had a shiny white star right in the middle of his forehead, and when the night sky came out, he looked just like a fallen star himself. During the day, Starry liked to gallop with the other horses, playing tag and eating clover. But his absolute favorite time of day was nighttime, when the moon shone like a giant silver coin. One peaceful night, when all the other animals on the farm were fast asleep, Starry opened his eyes. He flicked his fuzzy ears and listened to the crickets singing their sleepy song. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. Starry stood up on his four strong legs and stretched out his neck. He wanted to go on a special midnight adventure. He trotted quietly out of his stable, making sure his hooves went tip-toe, tip-toe across the wooden floor so he wouldn't wake anyone up. Outside, the grass was cool and covered in sparkling morning dew that looked like tiny stars on the ground. Starry tossed his head and began to trot across the meadow. The wind whispered gentle secrets in his ears, and the friendly owl sitting high up in the pine tree hooted a quiet hello. 'Hoo-hoo, good evening, Starry,' the owl whispered. Starry neighed softly back and kept on going until he reached the edge of the glassy blue pond. He leaned his head down to take a cool drink of water. When he looked at the water’s surface, he saw his own reflection staring back at him, glowing softly under the moonlight. The little white star on his forehead sparkled brightly in the water. Starry smiled his horse smile and did a little happy spin right by the water's edge. He felt so free, so happy, and so loved. After dancing beneath the silver moon for a little while longer, Starry let out a soft yawn. His eyelids felt heavy and sleepy. He turned around and trotted gently back to his warm barn, curling up in the deep, sweet-smelling hay. He closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, ready to dream about the bright and wonderful world waiting for him tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, down on the cozy green farm, lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat, a soft black mane, and four strong hooves that went clippity-clop, clippity-clop on the dirt path. Barnaby loved to eat crunchy green apples and sweet, yellow carrots. But more than anything else, Barnaby loved to play! One bright Tuesday, Farmer Fred brought something very exciting into the big pasture. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! It was as big as a watermelon and bouncy like a kangaroo. Barnaby trotted over with a happy whinny. "Neigh!" he said, which meant, "Oh boy, what a wonderful surprise!" Barnaby gently nudged the big red ball with his velvety nose. Boing! The ball rolled across the green grass. Barnaby trotted after it, going clippity-clop, clippity-clop! He tapped the ball with his left front hoof. Whee! The ball bounced high into the air and landed near the wooden fence. A little brown bunny hopped out to watch the fun. Barnaby giggled in horse language. He gave the ball another gentle push. This time, it rolled right toward the muddy puddle! Oh no! Barnaby stopped just in time. Horses do not like getting their clean hooves too muddy. So, Barnaby used his nose to steer the ball away from the puddle and back onto the soft green grass. His friend, a fluffy white sheep, came over to watch. "Baa!" said the sheep, cheering for Barnaby. Barnaby felt so proud. He trotted in a big circle around the ball, kicking up his heels with joy. The sun was getting warm, and Barnaby had played a whole lot. He walked over to the wooden fence where Farmer Fred was waiting with a yummy, crunchy carrot. Barnaby chewed his carrot happily, resting his nose against the big red ball. It had been the best day ever in the pasture. Barnaby gave one last soft, sleepy neigh, ready for a nice long nap in the warm afternoon sun.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Meadow
stories.text: High up on a rolling green hill, where the wildflowers danced in the breeze, lived a gentle white horse named Starry. Starry had a tail as white as fluffy clouds and a tiny patch on her forehead that looked just like a twinkling star. Every single morning, when the golden sun peeked over the top of the hill, Starry would wake up, stretch her long legs, and give a happy little yawn. "Good morning, meadow!" Starry would say to the buzzing bees and the singing birds. Starry spent her days walking softly through the tall green grass. She loved to listen to the whisper of the wind in the trees and the happy gurgle of the little brook nearby. Sometimes, Starry would stop by the brook to take a cool, refreshing drink of water. Slurp, slurp, went Starry. Then she would splash her hoof just a little bit, making sparkly water droplets fly into the air. But as the afternoon turned into evening, the sky changed colors. First, it turned pretty pink, then soft purple, and finally deep, sleepy blue. The little birds tucked their heads under their wings, and the bees went back to their buzzing hives. Starry knew it was almost time for bed. She walked slowly to her favorite spot under the big, leafy apple tree. The grass there was as soft as a giant green blanket. Starry gave a gentle sigh. She folded her front legs and lowered her heavy body down to the ground. Up, down, settled Starry, making herself as cozy as could be. She closed her big brown eyes and listened to the crickets singing their quiet lullaby. Chirp, chirp, went the crickets. The moon smiled down from the velvet sky, shining its gentle light right on Starry's sleepy white back. Starry dreamed sweet dreams of running through fields of golden stars, safe and warm in her cozy meadow. Good night, Starry.

stories.title: Pip the Pony's Splashy Day
stories.text: Meet Pip! Pip was not a big horse. In fact, Pip was a tiny pony with short little legs and a very fluffy mane that bounced every single time he moved. Pip lived in a sunny pasture right next to a bubbling, giggling brook. Pip loved his home because there were always so many fun things to explore. One warm summer afternoon, the sun was shining extra bright, and Pip felt very, very hot. "Phew!" puffed Pip. "It is a warm day today!" He needed a way to cool down his furry little body. Pip trotted over to the edge of the brook. Splash, splash, went the water over the smooth round stones. Pip poked his soft nose into the water. It felt so cool and refreshing! He stepped his tiny right hoof into the water. Then his left hoof. Then all four hooves! Pip was standing right in the middle of the shallow stream. A little green frog hopped onto a lily pad nearby and croaked, "Ribbit!" Pip giggled and shook his head. He lowered his mouth and took a long, cool sip of the sweet water. Gulp, gulp, went Pip. Then, something wonderful happened. Pip decided to splash! He lifted his right front hoof and brought it down hard in the water. Splash! A huge shower of glittering water droplets flew up into the air and landed right on his back. Pip shook his fluffy mane, sending water flying everywhere. He felt so happy and cool. A friendly yellow duck swam by and quacked happily, joining in on the water game. Pip splashed again, making little waves that tickled his ankles. He danced a silly little pony dance right there in the brook, clippity-splash, clippity-splash! When he was finally nice and cool, Pip stepped back onto the grassy bank. He rolled from side to side in the warm, dry dirt, just like ponies love to do, shaking off the water like a big, happy puppy. Pip stood up, shook his fluffy coat until he was all puffy again, and trotted off to find a yummy green clover snack, smiling all the way.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny green farm, there lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a coat the color of sweet honey and a mane as soft as a cloud. Every morning, Barnaby would trot out of his cozy wooden stable and say good morning to the world with a happy, gentle 'Neigh!' 

One bright Tuesday, Barnaby trotted into the big meadow to find something very special waiting in the grass. It was a big, shiny, red bouncy ball! Barnaby had never seen a big red ball before. He blinked his big brown eyes and stepped a little closer. Tap, tap, tap went his little hooves on the soft dirt.

'Whinny!' said Barnaby, which meant, 'What are you?'

The ball did not answer. It just sat there, looking very red and very round. Barnaby decided to investigate. He gently nudged the ball with his soft velvet nose. Boop! 

The ball rolled away a little bit. 'Wheee!' thought Barnaby. So he nudged it again. Nudge, nudge, roll! The ball rolled across the clover and stopped near the old oak tree. Barnaby trotted after it, his tail swishing happily in the warm breeze.

Soon, Barnaby’s best friend, a fluffy white duck named Ducky, waddled over. 'Quack, quack!' said Ducky. 'Can I play too?' 

Barnaby nodded his head up and down. Together, the horse and the duck played the best game ever. Barnaby used his nose to roll the ball to Ducky, and Ducky flapped his wings and pushed it right back to Barnaby’s hooves. They played until the sun started to go down, painting the sky in pink and purple colors.

When the stars came out to twinkle, Barnaby felt very sleepy. He nuzzled the big red ball one last time and whispered, 'Goodnight, ball.' Then, he trotted back to his warm stable for a good night's rest, dreaming of bouncing red balls under the golden sun. The end.

stories.title: Bella's Muddy Hooves
stories.text:
Bella was a sparkly white pony who loved to gallop across the grassy hills. She had four strong hooves that went clop, clop, clop wherever she went. Bella loved the sunshine, she loved crunchy green apples, but more than anything else in the whole wide world, Bella loved puddles.

It had rained all night long, leaving big, squishy, wonderful puddles all over the farmyard. When Bella woke up and peeked out of her stable door, she saw them gleaming in the morning light. 'Snort!' went Bella with excitement. Today was going to be a muddy day!

She trotted out into the yard. Clop, clop, squish! Her front left hoof landed right in the middle of a big, juicy puddle. Brown water splashed up in tiny droplets, sparkling like diamonds in the air. Bella giggled—or as much as a horse can giggle, which sounds like a soft, happy snort.

She marched to the next puddle. Squish, squash, squelch! Now her hooves were covered in thick, warm mud. She lifted her right leg high and stomped down. Splash! Mud went on her ankles. She stomped her other leg. Splash! Mud went on her knees. Bella thought she looked like a magnificent mud monster.

Just then, Farmer Farmer walked by carrying a bucket of carrots. He stopped and laughed when he saw Bella’s muddy legs. 'Well, hello there, Bella! You look like you're having a very messy adventure!' 

Bella walked over to the farmer and gave him a gentle nudge on his sleeve, leaving a tiny muddy nose print on his jacket. The farmer smiled and fed her a sweet, crunchy carrot. 'Time to wash those hooves off soon, little pony,' the farmer said kindly.

Bella munched her carrot happily. She splashed in one last puddle, just for good luck, before letting the gentle rain shower wash her clean again. What a fun day to be a horse!

stories.title: Starry's Lullaby Trot
stories.text:
The moon was high and glowing like a silver silver-dollar in the midnight sky. All the animals on the farm were fast asleep. The cows were sleeping in the pasture, the sheep were snoozing in the fold, and little Starry the pony was wide awake in her stable.

Starry was a gentle horse with a coat as dark as night and a little white star on her forehead, which is how she got her name. Starry didn't feel like sleeping yet. She wanted to look at the beautiful night sky.

Quietly, so she wouldn't wake anyone up, Starry stepped out of her stable door. Tippy-toe, tippy-toe went her quiet little hooves on the cool grass. The night air felt fresh and smelled like sweet hay and blooming flowers.

She looked up at the twinkling stars. They looked like tiny diamonds scattered across a giant velvet blanket. Starry wanted to dance with the stars. So, she began to trot softly across the meadow. 

Click-clack, click-clack went her hooves in a gentle rhythm, like a quiet song. She trotted in a big circle. Then she trotted in a zigzag. She tossed her long, dark mane and pranced lightly, pretending she was a flying horse soaring through the galaxy.

A little firefly fluttered by, glowing with a soft yellow light. 'Hello, little star of the grass,' Starry seemed to say as she gently blew a puff of warm air toward the bug. The firefly danced around her ears, guiding her path.

After a little while, Starry began to feel a lovely, cozy yawn coming on. Yaaaawn went Starry, opening her mouth wide. Her legs felt heavy and tired in the best possible way. The night breeze sang a soft lullaby through the leaves of the willow tree.

Starry walked slowly back to her warm bed of straw. She curled up comfortably, closed her big brown eyes, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of dancing with the stars until the morning sun woke up the world.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green farm, there lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a coat the color of sweet honey and a mane as soft as a cloud. Every morning, the farm gate would open wide, and Barnaby would trot out into the big pasture to say hello to the world. Trot, trot, trot went his little hooves on the soft grass. One bright morning, Barnaby saw something very strange and very exciting sitting right in the middle of his favorite clover patch. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! Barnaby stopped. He blinked his big brown eyes. He flicked his fuzzy ears. He had never seen a red ball before. Barnaby walked slowly over to the ball. Sniff, sniff, went his soft pink nose. The ball did not smell like grass. It did not smell like carrots. It smelled like sunny days and fun! Barnaby wanted to play. How do horses play with a big red ball? He gave it a gentle tap with his nose. Boop! The red ball rolled away, giggling in Barnaby's imagination. Whee! Barnaby trotted after it. Trot, trot, trot! He nudged it again. Boop! The ball bounced over a little puddle and rolled near the old oak tree. Barnaby giggled, making a soft snorting sound that meant he was very happy. Just then, his friends came over to see what all the fun was about. Daisy the cow ambled over, chewing her cud. Cluck, cluck, came Mrs. Hen, running as fast as her little legs could carry her. 'Look what I found!' Barnaby seemed to say with a happy toss of his head. The red ball rolled back and forth between Barnaby's hooves. Barnaby was so careful. He did not want to pop his new toy. He just wanted to push it with his nose and chase it through the daisies. The sun climbed higher into the bright blue sky, warming Barnaby's back. He played with the big red ball all morning long, feeling like the luckiest horse in the whole wide world. When the afternoon shadows grew long, Barnaby gave the ball one last gentle nudge right up against the barn wall so it would be safe for tomorrow. Then, he trotted happily over to the water trough for a long, cool drink. What a wonderful day it had been on the farm with his very own red ball.

stories.title: Barnaby's Muddy Hooves
stories.text: Splish, splash, squish, squash! It had rained all night long on the cozy farm, and now the big pasture was full of wonderful, squishy mud puddles. Barnaby the little honey-colored horse woke up, stretched his long legs, and let out a happy little neigh. Yawn! Good morning, sun! Barnaby loved sunny days, but today was special. Today was a puddle day! He trotted out of his warm barn and stopped right at the edge of the grass. His eyes grew wide with delight. Right in front of him was a big, shiny puddle of muddy water. It looked just like a chocolate mirror! Barnaby walked right up to the edge. He lowered his soft nose and blew a bubble in the water. Blub, blub, blub! Then, Barnaby lifted one front hoof. He stamped it down into the puddle. Splash! Mud flew up into the air in tiny brown droplets. Barnaby giggled. That was fun! He stamped his other front hoof. Splash, splash! Now his front hooves were covered in thick, dark mud shoes. Barnaby felt like he was wearing magic boots. He decided to take a little walk. Squish, squish, went his hooves in the wet mud. It made a funny squishing sound that made Barnaby shake his head and flick his tail with joy. 'Neigh!' he called out to his friend the duck, who was swimming happily in a bigger puddle nearby. The duck quacked back, as if to say, 'Welcome to the club, Barnaby!' Barnaby pranced around the pasture, making little mud prints everywhere he went. One, two, three, four, muddy hoofprints on the green, green grass. He spun around in a little circle, leaving a lovely circle of swirls. But soon, Barnaby's tummy began to rumble. Time for breakfast! Barnaby trotted back toward the barn, leaving a trail of happy, muddy footsteps behind him. His farmer friend smiled and shook his head, coming out with a big bucket of sweet oats and a warm sponge. 'Well, Barnaby,' the farmer chuckled, 'looks like you had a very busy morning.' Barnaby munched happily on his oats while the farmer gently washed his hooves clean with warm water. Splash went the clean water, washing away the mud. Barnaby was clean again, but he smiled, already dreaming of the next rainy day and the squishy, splashy mud puddles waiting just for him.

stories.title: Barnaby's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was beginning to sink low behind the green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink, orange, and sleepy purple. The farm was growing very quiet. The cows were lying down in the clover, the chickens were tucked safely inside the coop, and the little birds had stopped their singing. It was time for Barnaby the little honey-colored horse to go to sleep. But Barnaby was not quite tired yet. He felt wide awake! He wanted to run just one more time across the soft meadow. Trot, trot, trot went his gentle hooves as he made his way toward the big wooden barn. The evening breeze blew softly, rustling the leaves on the old oak tree and whispering, 'Hush, little horse, the day is done.' Barnaby walked inside the warm, cozy barn. The air smelled sweet like fresh hay and dried clover. His stall was lined with deep, fluffy straw that looked just like a giant golden bed made especially for him. Barnaby walked into his stall and turned around in a circle once, twice, three times, making his bed just right. Then, with a soft sigh, Barnaby lowered his front legs and gently laid his big body down into the soft straw. Thump went his tummy as he rested. He let out a long, sleepy breath. Whishhh. Barnaby closed his big brown eyes. His long eyelashes brushed against his furry cheeks. Outside, the first little star twinkled in the dark blue sky, blinking down at the peaceful farm. A little cricket began to chirp a quiet bedtime song. Chirp, chirp, chirp, went the cricket. Barnaby listened to the music of the night. He felt so safe, so warm, and so loved in his cozy barn. His ears twitched one last time, and then they relaxed completely. Barnaby was fast asleep, dreaming of green pastures, red balls, and sunny morning gallops. Good night, Barnaby. Sleep tight until the morning sun wakes you up for a brand new day of fun.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, in a green, green meadow, lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat, a fluffy white mane, and four strong hooves that went clip-clop, clip-clop on the soft grass. Barnaby loved to run and jump, but most of all, Barnaby loved his toys.

One bright Tuesday, Barnaby trotted over to the big wooden fence. Sitting right in the middle of the buttercups was a surprise. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! Barnaby blinked his big brown eyes. He leaned down and gave the ball a gentle nudge with his soft, velvety nose. 

Boing! The red ball rolled away.

"Whinny!" laughed Barnaby. He trotted after it. Clip-clop, clip-clop, clip-clop! 

Barnaby decided to play a game. He tapped the ball with his left front hoof. Tap! The ball bounced over a patch of daisies. Barnaby trotted around the daisy patch and met the ball on the other side. Then, he gave the ball a tiny, gentle push with his nose. Wheee! The ball rolled all the way down the gentle green hill.

Barnaby galloped down the hill, his tail swishing happily in the breeze. When he reached the bottom, there was his red ball, waiting for him by the cool blue brook. 

Just then, his animal friends came out to watch. Pip the little yellow duck waddled over and quacked loudly. Bella the fluffy bunny hopped up and twitched her nose. 

"Look at me!" Barnaby seemed to say as he gave the ball one more happy nudge. 

Pip and Bella cheered. Barnaby felt like the luckiest horse in the whole wide world. Playing with his red ball was the most fun a little horse could ever have. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby gave his ball one last friendly nuzzle. He trotted back to his cozy barn for dinner, dreaming of all the fun games he would play with his red ball tomorrow. Goodnight, Barnaby!

stories.title: Barnaby's Muddy Hooves
stories.text:
It had rained all night long in the big green pasture. When the morning sun finally woke up, the ground was squishy, wet, and wonderfully muddy. Barnaby the little brown horse poked his head out of his barn door and sniffed the fresh air. 

"Snort!" said Barnaby. He loved muddy days!

Barnaby stepped outside. Squish, squatch, squish went the mud beneath his four hooves. He looked down at his feet. They were covered in dark, gooey mud. Barnaby thought it looked like fun boots. He trotted across the yard, making funny sucking sounds with every step he took. Squish-squash! Squish-squash!

He wanted to show his best friend, a little brown puppy named Pip. Pip came running over, barking happily. Pip sniffed the mud on Barnaby's hoof and sneezed. Achoo!

Barnaby giggled in horse language. He lifted his right front hoof and made a little muddy footprint on the grass. Then he lifted his left front hoof and made another. Squish! Pip chased the moving hooves, barking and wagging his tail. 

Soon, Barnaby wanted to trot faster. He started to run across the big field. Clop-clop-splat! A little bit of mud flew up into the air and landed right on Barnaby's nose. Barnaby crossed his eyes and tried to look at the mud spot on his nose. Pip laughed, wagging his tail even harder.

But wait! Mama horse was walking over. She had clean water in a shiny metal bucket. Mama horse smiled warmly at her playful little boy.

"Time to wash those muddy hooves, Barnaby," Mama seemed to say.

Barnaby stood very still while Mama gently splashed cool water over his feet. Splash, splash, rinse, rinse! The dark mud washed away, leaving his hooves clean and shiny once again. 

Barnaby shook his fluffy mane and gave Mama a big, sweet horse kiss on her cheek. Even though the mud was gone, Barnaby knew he had the best muddy-hoof adventure ever. He curled up in the warm straw for a nice, cozy nap, ready for whatever tomorrow might bring.

stories.title: Barnaby's Apple Tree
stories.text:
Deep in the sunny meadow stood the biggest, oldest apple tree in the world. Its branches were heavy with round, red, juicy apples that smelled sweet like sugar. Barnaby the little horse loved this tree more than anything else.

Every morning, Barnaby would trot over to the apple tree. Clip-clop, clip-clop! He would stand underneath the low-hanging branches and look up with big, hopeful eyes. Today, the apples looked extra delicious. But they were hanging just a little bit too high for Barnaby to reach with his nose.

"Can I have an apple?" Barnaby whispered, stretching his neck up as far as it could go. He stretched and stretched, but his nose only brushed a single green leaf.

Suddenly, a little blue bird named Pip flew down from the sky. Pip landed right on the very top branch of the apple tree. Pip chirped a happy song and hopped up and down.

Shake, shake, shake went the branch!

Thump! Down fell a big, bright red apple right onto the soft green grass. 

Barnaby’s eyes went wide with joy. He bent down and gently rolled the apple with his nose. Crunch, crunch, crunch went the apple as Barnaby took a big, happy bite. Sweet apple juice burst in his mouth. It was the yummiest, most delicious apple he had ever tasted in his whole life.

Barnaby chewed happily and looked up at the friendly blue bird in the tree. He gave a soft, grateful whinny to say thank you. Pip chirped back a happy reply.

Then, another apple fell down. Thump! And another one! Thump! Barnaby nudged the apples around, sharing them with his little bird friend on the grass.

When all the apples were eaten, Barnaby rubbed his happy tummy against the warm trunk of the tree. He was full, he was happy, and he was loved. With a contented sigh, Barnaby closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep under the shade of his favorite apple tree, dreaming of sweet red apples all afternoon long.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green meadow, lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat, a soft black mane, and a very waggy tail. Every morning, the sun would tickle Barnaby's nose, and he would say, "Neigh! Time to play!" One sunny Tuesday, Barnaby trotted over to the big wooden fence. Sitting right in the middle of the soft green grass was a giant, shiny, bouncy red ball. Barnaby had never seen a red ball this big before! He blinked his big brown eyes. "Whose ball can this be?" he wondered. He gave the ball a gentle nudge with his velvety nose. Boing! The ball rolled a little bit. Barnaby giggled. Then, he gave it a little tap with his front hoof. Whee! The ball rolled faster. Barnaby trotted after it, his little hooves going clip-clop, clip-clop on the ground. "Catch me if you can!" Barnaby whinnied. A little yellow butterfly fluttered by, landing right on the ball. Barnaby stopped so he wouldn't scare his tiny bug friend. The butterfly tickled the ball, then flew away up into the blue sky. Barnaby decided to try a different trick. He nudged the ball up a tiny grassy hill. Up, up, up went the ball. But oops! Barnaby nudged it just a little too hard. Down, down, down rolled the red ball! It rolled past the old brown barn. It rolled past the big leafy apple tree. Finally, it gently bumped into a wooden water trough and stopped. Barnaby trotted down the hill as fast as his little legs could carry him. "Gotcha!" he said happily. Just then, Farmer Fred walked over with a crunchy green apple. "Good boy, Barnaby," said Farmer Fred, giving him a gentle pat. Barnaby munched his apple, happy as could be. He had the best red ball in the whole wide world, and tomorrow, they would play all over again.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Meadow
stories.text: The sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors. It was almost bedtime down in the cozy meadow. A little white horse named Starry let out a big, wide yawn. Yaaawn! Starry had a star-shaped patch right on her forehead that sparkled just a tiny bit in the evening light. "Time to get ready for sleep," whispered Mama Horse, nuzzling Starry's soft neck. But Starry was not sleepy at all. Her hooves felt bouncy. "Can we play one more game of hide-and-seek, Mama?" asked Starry. Mama Horse smiled. "Just a short one, little star." Starry closed her big brown eyes and counted to three. One, two, three! When she opened her eyes, Mama Horse was hiding behind the big, leafy apple tree. Starry trotted over, going tip-toe, tip-toe on the soft grass so she wouldn't make too much noise. "Found you!" whinnied Starry with a happy wiggle. Now it was Starry's turn to hide. She trotted quickly behind a big pile of golden hay. She tucked her ears back and tried to stay as quiet as a little mouse. Mama Horse pretended to look everywhere. "Where is Starry? Is she behind the flowers? No! Is she near the fence? No!" Mama Horse walked closer to the hay bale. "Aha! I see a wiggly tail!" Starry giggled and jumped out. Playing hide-and-seek was so much fun, but now, the bouncy feeling in Starry's legs was turning into a heavy, sleepy feeling. The crickets began to sing a soft, soothing song. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. The wind blew softly through the green grass, whispering hush-hush. Starry walked over to her favorite patch of clover right beside her mama. She lay down softly, curling her legs beneath her warm, fuzzy body. Mama Horse stood right beside her, keeping watch like a gentle giant. Starry closed her eyes and let out one more tiny yawn. The stars twinkled high above in the deep blue sky, shining down on the sleepy little horse. Good night, Starry. Sweet dreams.

stories.title: Buttons Goes for a Gallop
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to meet a very special pony named Buttons. Buttons was small, round, and had patches of white and brown all over his soft furry body. He looked just like a fluffy stuffed animal that had come to life! Buttons lived on a cheerful farm with lots of other animals. There were fluffy white sheep that went baa, pink pigs that went oink, and a noisy rooster that shouted cock-a-doodle-doo. Every morning, Buttons liked to go on a big adventure around the farmyard. Today, Buttons decided he wanted to gallop. Do you know how horses gallop? Let's show our hands and stomp our feet! Clip-clop, clip-clop, go the little hooves! Buttons trotted past the sheep pen. The little lambs bleated happily as Buttons trotted by. "Good morning, fuzzy lambs!" neighed Buttons in his highest, friendliest voice. Then, Buttons trotted past the muddy puddle where the pigs liked to splash. Oink, oink! went the little piglets. Buttons stopped just at the edge of the puddle. He did not want muddy hooves today! Instead, he trotted over to the garden where the crunchy orange carrots grew. Farmer Ben was watering the plants with a big green watering can. Splash went the water! Buttons loved the cool water splashes on a warm sunny day. He shook his soft mane and let out a happy snort. "Brrr-ach!" went Buttons, making a silly bubbling sound with his lips. Farmer Ben laughed and handed Buttons a sweet, crisp carrot. Buttons chewed it up with a loud cronch, cronch, cronch! Eating carrots was his absolute favorite thing to do. After his snack, Buttons felt full of energy again. He did a happy little spin, kicking up his back hooves just a tiny bit. Whee! The farm was such a wonderful place for a little pony. With a final wave of his fluffy tail, Buttons trotted off to find a sunny spot for a nice, cozy afternoon nap.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green farm, there lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a coat the color of sweet honey and a mane as soft as a dandelion puff. Every morning, Barnaby would trot out of his cozy wooden stable and say good morning to the world with a happy, gentle 'Neigh!' One bright Tuesday, Farmer Brown left a big, shiny red ball right in the middle of the paddock. Barnaby stopped and blinked his big brown eyes. What could this strange red circle be? He took one tiptoe step closer. Then another. He gently nudged the ball with his velvety soft nose. Boop! The ball rolled a little bit. That was fun! Barnaby gave the ball a gentle little tap with his front hoof. Whee! The ball bounced across the green grass, spinning and glowing in the warm sunshine. Barnaby trotted after it, his little hooves going clip-clop, clip-clop on the earth. He trotted faster. Clip-clop, clip-clop, zoom! Barnaby loved to run. His long tail swished back and forth like a happy flag in the breeze. He nudged the red ball again, watching it roll near the old oak tree. The friendly farm ducks quaddled in approval from their little pond, flapping their wings as if they were cheering him on. Barnaby felt so happy and free. Playing with the big red ball was the best game ever invented. Soon, his tummy began to rumble. It was time for a yummy snack of crunchy green grass and sweet, crisp carrots. Barnaby gave the red ball one last gentle nuzzle, whispering a soft goodbye for now. He trotted back to Farmer Brown, feeling very proud and full of joyful energy. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Barnaby curled up in his soft straw bed. He closed his sleepy eyes and dreamed of red balls bouncing across the sky, happily galloping through his sweet horse dreams until the morning light.

stories.title: Bella's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Deep in the rolling green hills, there lived a playful little pony named Bella. Bella was white as snow, with spots on her back that looked just like fluffy little clouds. Bella loved to explore every single corner of the farm. One rainy afternoon, the sky turned gray and big, fat raindrops started to fall. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the rain on the barn roof. When the storm finally stopped, the sun came peeking back out, warming the earth and making everything smell fresh and clean. But the rain had left something very special behind in the pasture: a big, squishy puddle of mud! Bella trotted right over to the edge of the puddle and looked down. She could see her own reflection staring right back at her. Splish, splash! Bella dipped one tiny hoof right into the middle of the mud. It felt squishy, cool, and tickly between her toes. She giggled a little horse giggle and splashed her other hoof. Oh, how wonderful it felt! Soon, Bella was dancing a happy mud dance. Splash, splash, swish, go the hooves! Mud splashed up her legs and made funny little freckles on her nose. A little brown bird landed on a nearby fence post and chirped a merry song, watching Bella having so much fun. Bella shook her fluffy tail, sending tiny droplets of water sparkling into the air like little diamonds. Of course, playing in the mud meant getting very dirty indeed! Mama horse walked over, her big warm eyes filled with love. She nuzzled Bella gently on the neck. 'Time for a nice bath, my little mud-pie,' Mama seemed to say. Together, they walked down to the sparkling blue brook. The cool water washed all the mud away, leaving Bella clean and shiny once again. Bella gave a happy shake and galloped back across the meadow, ready for her next grand and wonderful adventure under the big blue sky.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking behind the hills, painting the clouds in shades of lavender and gold. It was almost bedtime on the farm, and all the animals were getting very tired. In the cozy stable, a little foal named Starry was blinking his heavy eyelids. Starry had a shining white star right in the middle of his forehead, which is how he got his lovely name. Mama horse nuzzled him gently, whispering soft horse-hums to help him relax. 'Time to rest your little hooves, Starry,' Mama seemed to say as she wrapped her warm neck around him. Starry gave a soft yawn. He was a very good little horse today, but running and jumping all over the meadow had made him quite sleepy. He walked over to his bed of golden straw, which smelled sweet like summer hay. He lay down very carefully, folding his long legs underneath his soft tummy. Outside the stable door, the crickets began to sing their quiet evening song. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the tiny musicians in the grass. A bright yellow moon climbed slowly up into the velvet night sky, surrounded by twinkling little stars that looked just like the one on Starry's head. Starry closed his big brown eyes and listened to the gentle night breeze whispering through the open window. He thought about the green grass he would eat tomorrow and the fun races he would run with his friends. But for now, it was time to sleep. Mama horse stood right beside him, keeping him safe and warm all through the night. Starry breathed in and out, slow and deep. He was safe, he was loved, and he was the happiest little horse in the whole wide world. With a final little sigh, Starry drifted off into dreamland, sleeping soundly until the bright morning sun would wake him up to play all over again.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning on the farm, a little brown horse named Barnaby trotted happily into the big green pasture. Barnaby had a soft, shiny mane and four strong hooves that went clip-clop, clip-clop on the soft dirt path. Today was a very special day because Barnaby saw something bright and round sitting near the wooden fence. It was a big, shiny red ball! Barnaby had never seen a red ball before. He blinked his big brown eyes and walked closer. He gave the ball a gentle nudge with his velvety nose. Boop! The ball rolled away a little bit. Barnaby let out a happy little whinny. Neigh! He trotted after it. He gently pushed the ball with his nose again. Whee! The ball rolled through the tall green grass. A little yellow butterfly fluttered around the ball, dancing in the warm sunshine. Barnaby thought the butterfly was playing too. He lifted one front hoof and tapped the ground. Tap, tap, tap. He shook his bushy tail and tossed his head. The red ball rolled down a tiny grassy hill, stopping right next to a patch of sweet, crunchy carrots. Barnaby trotted down the hill, his hooves making a happy sound in the dirt. When he reached the bottom, he decided it was time for a tasty snack. He munched on a green carrot top. Munch, munch, munch. But he kept the red ball right between his front hooves so it wouldn't roll away. A friendly farmer walked by and smiled. Good morning, Barnaby, the farmer said, rubbing the little horse right between his soft ears. Barnaby closed his eyes and leaned into the warm hand, feeling so loved and happy. The sun shone bright in the blue sky, the grass smelled sweet, and Barnaby had his very favorite new toy. When the afternoon shadows grew long, Barnaby gave the red ball one last gentle nudge. He trotted back to the big red barn for dinner, dreaming of all the fun games he would play with his shiny red ball tomorrow.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Meadow
stories.text: The sun was beginning to set behind the rolling hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink, purple, and gold. High above, the very first twinkling star of the evening popped out to say hello. Down in the meadow, a gentle white horse named Starry opened her big, sleepy eyes. Starry had a silver mane that shimmered like moonlight and a tail as soft as a cloud. The day had been full of running and jumping, but now the farm was getting very quiet. A brown cow lay down in the grass to rest. A little black sheep curled up for a nap. Starry let out a long, soft yawn. Yaaaaawn. She stretched her front legs out wide and shook her head, making her soft ears wiggle. It was time to find a cozy spot to sleep. Starry walked slowly across the meadow, her hooves making a soft thud-thud sound on the damp grass. She looked for a place that was warm and sheltered from the evening breeze. Near the edge of the woods, she found a patch of clover that was extra soft and thick. She lowered her front knees down gently, then her back legs, until she was lying down completely. Starry tucked her nose under her chest and closed her eyes. A gentle night breeze whispered through the leaves of the big oak tree above her. Swish, swish, went the leaves, singing a quiet lullaby. Far away, an owl hooted softly. Hoo, hoo. Starry felt safe, warm, and wonderfully cozy. She breathed in the sweet smell of the night air and breathed out a long, relaxed sigh. Her eyelids felt heavy, like they were made of stone. The stars twinkled brighter and brighter, watching over the sleeping farm. Starry dreamed of flying through fluffy clouds made of cotton candy and running across fields of silver stars. She was the happiest little horse in the whole wide world, resting peacefully until the bright morning sun would come to wake her up again.

stories.title: Barnaby's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Splish, splash, splosh! It had rained all night long, and now the farmyard was covered in big, squishy puddles of mud. Pip, a little brown pony with a fluffy white star on his forehead, stood at the open gate of his stable. Pip loved sunny days, but today looked like the most fun day ever. He stepped outside, and his little hoof went right into a puddle. Squish! Pip giggled, shaking his head. That tickled! He lifted his hoof and saw shiny brown mud dripping down. Pip decided to go on a grand adventure to find the biggest, squishiest puddle on the whole farm. He trotted past the duck pond, where three yellow ducklings were paddling in the water. Quack, quack! they called out, splashing water with their tiny webbed feet. Pip trotted past the red tractor and past the tall hay bales. Everywhere he looked, there were puddles shining like mirrors in the morning light. Suddenly, Pip spotted the king of all puddles right in the middle of the courtyard. It was wide, deep, and wonderfully muddy. Pip trotted right up to it. He dipped his nose down and blew bubbles in the water. Blub, blub, blub! Then, he splashed his front right hoof. Splash! Then his front left hoof. Splash, splash! Mud flew up into the air and landed on his shiny coat. Pip didn't mind at all. He rolled his head around and let out a happy little snort. A friendly brown puppy ran over, barking with joy, and jumped into the puddle too. Woof, woof! They played together all morning, splashing and running until the sun came out from behind the clouds and warmed their backs. Soon, it was time for a nice warm bath from the farmer, but Pip smiled, knowing that mud puddles were truly the best invention in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green pasture, lived a friendly little horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a shiny brown coat that sparkled in the warm morning sun, a fluffy black tail, and four strong hooves that went clip-clop, clip-clop all day long. Barnaby loved to run, jump, and play games with his farm animal friends. One sunny morning, Farmer Fred rolled a big, bright red ball right into the middle of the pasture. Barnaby stopped munching on his sweet clover and blinked his big brown eyes. 'What is that?' he neighed softly. He trotted closer, going clip-clop, clip-clop, and gently nudged the ball with his soft velvet nose. Boing! The big red ball rolled away. Barnaby gave a happy little whinny and trotted after it. He gently pushed the ball with his nose again, sending it bouncing across the green grass. Duck waddled over, quacking with delight, and Piggy oinked happily from the mud puddle. Barnaby used his nose to roll the ball right to his friends. Duck flapped her wings, and Piggy squealed with joy. Then, Barnaby gently nudged the ball back toward himself. They played together for a very long time, laughing and playing in the sunshine. When the sun began to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange, Barnaby felt very sleepy. He gave the red ball one last gentle nudge into the barn corner. Then, he walked over to his cozy stall filled with soft, yellow straw. Barnaby yawned a big horse yawn, closed his eyes, and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of his big red ball.

stories.title: Starry's Sleepy Meadow
stories.text: High up on a rolling green hill lived a little white horse named Starry. Starry got her name because she had a white spot right on her forehead that looked just like a twinkling star. Every morning, Starry would wake up and say hello to the golden sun. She loved to gallop through the tall grass, feeling the cool breeze tickle her soft white mane. But today, Starry felt a little bit tired. Her legs felt heavy, and her eyelids felt droopy. 'Time for a quiet day,' she whispered to herself. Starry walked slowly, going clip-clop, clip-clop, down to the shade of a big, leafy apple tree. A friendly little bird chirped a sweet song from the branches above. Starry lay down gently on the soft, green grass. She curled up just a little bit and rested her heavy head on the ground. A fuzzy yellow butterfly fluttered gently past her nose, landing on a daisy nearby. Starry blinked her big, sleepy eyes and watched the butterfly dance in the air. The wind whispered softly through the apple tree leaves, making a soothing rustling sound. Rustle, rustle, rustle. It sounded just like a lullaby. Starry closed her eyes tightly and let out a long, gentle sigh. She felt safe, warm, and wonderfully cozy under the big tree. All her farm friends were quiet so Starry could rest. The sheep stopped baaing, and the cows stopped mooing. Starry slept deeply through the warm afternoon, dreaming sweet dreams of clover fields and flying with butterflies. When she finally woke up, the stars were twinkling in the night sky, just like the one on her head.

stories.title: Buttons the Pony's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Meet Buttons! Buttons was a tiny pony with short, stubby legs and a very curious nature. Buttons lived on a cheerful farm with lots of other animals. Today had been a very rainy day, which meant one wonderful thing: puddles! Big, squishy, mud puddles were everywhere. Buttons loved mud puddles more than anything in the whole wide world. He trotted out of his dry stable, going clip-clop, clip-clop, right into the big farmyard. He stopped by a lovely, deep puddle of brown mud. 'Ooh,' thought Buttons, 'that looks like fun!' He stepped his front right hoof right into the middle of the puddle. Sluuurch! The mud squished up between his toes in the most satisfying way.
