Buttons giggled in horse language and stepped his other hoof in. Soon, all four of his little hooves were standing right in the squishy mud. He swished his tail back and forth, splashing little drops of mud everywhere. A little brown puppy scampered over, barking playfully at the splashing hooves. Buttons lowered his head and blew bubbles in the puddle with his soft nose. Blub, blub, blub! The puppy yipped with excitement and chased the splashing water. Buttons was having the greatest time ever. He felt so happy and free. But soon, his tummy began to rumble. It was time for dinner! Buttons stepped carefully out of the puddle, leaving little muddy hoofprints all the way back to the stable. Farmer John smiled when he saw the muddy little pony. He gave Buttons a gentle brush and a bucket of sweet oats. Buttons munched happily, dreaming of the next rainy day.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a bright green pasture, lived a little brown horse named Barnaby. Barnaby had a soft, shiny coat, a fluffy white tail, and four strong hooves that went clicket-clack, clicket-clack on the dirt path. Barnaby loved to run, jump, and play in the warm sunshine.

One sunny morning, Barnaby trotted over to the big wooden fence. Sitting right there in the soft green grass was something brand new. It was round, it was shiny, and it was as red as a ripe, juicy strawberry. It was a big bouncy ball!

Barnaby blinked his big brown eyes. He leaned down and gave the ball a gentle nudge with his velvety nose. Boop! The red ball rolled away a little bit. Barnaby let out a happy little neigh. "Nee-ghhh!" he said.

Curious, Barnaby took one step forward. Then, he lifted his right front hoof and tapped the ball. Tap! The ball bounced and rolled across the meadow, flashing bright in the sunlight. Barnaby chased after it. Clicket-clack, clicket-clack went his hooves on the ground. He was as fast as the wind!

The red ball bounced over a little yellow daisy. Barnaby jumped right over the daisy, too. Whee! He trotted around the ball, trying to guide it back to his cozy barn. But the ball was bouncy and silly. It zig-zagged to the left, and Barnaby zig-zagged, too. It zig-zagged to the right, and Barnaby bounded after it.

Soon, Barnaby’s friends came to see what all the fun was about. There was Daisy the cow and Penny the fluffy sheep. "Moo!" said Daisy. "Baa!" said Penny. They watched as Barnaby gently pushed the red ball with his nose. He wasn't playing alone anymore. It was a game for everyone.

As the afternoon sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby started to feel very sleepy. He gave the red ball one last gentle nudge right up to the barn door. He tucked the ball safely inside where it would wait for tomorrow's adventures.

Barnaby walked over to his favorite patch of sweet hay. He let out a big, cozy yawn. He folded his long legs and laid down under the starry sky. He closed his eyes, dreaming of red balls, sunny meadows, and happy gallops. Good night, Barnaby.

stories.title: Clover's Muddy Hooves
stories.text:
Good morning, little readers! Today we are going to visit Clover the pony. Clover was a very special pony. She was the color of toasted honey, and she had a white star right on the middle of her forehead. Clover lived on a friendly farm with lots of tall trees and sweet-smelling clover flowers.

Now, Clover loved a lot of things. She loved crunchy orange carrots. She loved sweet green apples. But most of all, Clover loved to splash! And today was the best day for splashing because it had rained all night long.

When Clover woke up, she stepped out of her warm stall and peeked outside. Squish! Her front hoof went right into a puddle. Oh, boy! A big, wonderful, squishy puddle of mud. The mud was dark and shiny, and it looked like chocolate pudding. Clover loved chocolate-pudding mud!

Clover trotted over to the biggest puddle in the whole pasture. She dipped her left front hoof in. Squish, squash, squish! She made a funny bubbling sound. Then she dipped her right front hoof in. Bubble, bubble, pop! Clover giggled in her own horsie way.

Suddenly, Clover wanted to do a happy dance. She lifted her left leg and stamped. Splash! Mud flew up into the air in tiny brown droplets. She stamped her right leg. Splash, splash! Mud decorated her shiny legs like little boots.

"Neigh-neigh!" called Clover to her bird friends up in the oak tree. The little bluebirds chirped a happy song. They thought Clover looked very silly and fun.

Clover bent her head down. She wanted to see her reflection in the puddle water. But as she leaned close, she tickled her own nose with a blade of grass. Ah-choo! Clover sneezed, and the water rippled in circles, making her reflection wiggle and wobble.

Just then, the farmer walked over with a big hose of cool, sparkly water. "Time to wash those muddy hooves, Clover!" the farmer said with a smile. 

Clover didn't mind at all. The cool water felt amazing on her tired legs. Swish, swash, went the clean water, washing the mud away. Clover stood very still, enjoying the nice tickly shower.

Once she was all clean and sparkly again, Clover shook her mane. Shake, shake, shake! Water flew everywhere. Then she trotted back to her dry hay, ready for a nice long nap after her very muddy, very fun morning.

stories.title: Starry's Bedtime Trot
stories.text:
The sun was hiding behind the rolling green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of purple and pink. High up in the evening sky, the very first little star of the night blinked on. It twinkled like a tiny diamond.

In the meadow below, a little white horse named Starry looked up and blinked back. Starry had a coat as white as fluffy cotton balls and a mane that felt like silk. It was almost time for bed, but Starry had one important job to do first.

It was time to say good night to all the farm animals! Starry began to trot across the soft grass. Clicket-clack, clicket-clack went his gentle hooves, making a quiet, soothing sound in the quiet evening air.

First, Starry trotted over to the big red barn. He poked his soft nose over the half-door. There sat Barnaby the bunny, twitching his long nose. "Time for sleep, little bunny," Starry whispered softly. The bunny yawned and curled up tight. "Good night, Starry," he softly squeaked.

Next, Starry walked down the path toward the duck pond. The water was as smooth as glass. Three little yellow ducklings were tucked snugly under their mother's warm feathers. Starry dipped his head in a polite little bow. "Quack-night, little ducks," Starry murmured. The ducklings tucked their heads under their wings and drifted off to sleep.

Starry continued his gentle evening trot. He passed the sleeping sheep and the resting cows. Every animal smiled in their sleep as they heard Starry's comforting footsteps.

Finally, Starry made his way back to his very own cozy stall. The moon was now shining bright and round, acting like a giant nightlight in the dark blue sky. A pile of fresh, sweet-smelling hay waited for him in the corner.

Starry stepped inside and let out a long, peaceful sigh. He folded his front legs and laid his heavy head down on the soft straw. The night breeze whispered through the open window, singing a sweet lullaby.

Starry closed his big brown eyes. He felt warm, safe, and deeply loved. The little star in the sky kept watch over him as he drifted off into wonderful, magical dreams. Good night, Starry. Sweet dreams.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Tree
rhymes.text:
Little horse runs fast and free,
Galloping across the lea.
Trot and canter, jump and play,
Happily through all the day.

Ears twitching up so high,
Watching clouds go floating by.
Soft brown mane and shiny coat,
Floating like a little boat.

Now it is time to take a rest,
Curled up in a cozy nest.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
Dreams of meadows wide and deep.

Goodnight, pony, safe and sound,
Resting softly on the ground.

rhymes.title: Hooves Go Tap
rhymes.text:
Hooves go tap upon the floor,
Trotting right up to the door.
Swish your tail and blink your eyes,
Look at all the butterflies!

Eat the clover, green and sweet,
Such a tasty, yummy treat.
Nicker softly, loud and clear,
Let your pony friends draw near.

Run around the dusty ring,
Hear the happy birdies sing.
Jump a little wooden bar,
You can reach the shining star.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping safely in the town.

rhymes.title: Pony, Pony, Little Star
rhymes.text:
Pony, pony, little star,
Running near and running far.
Kick your heels up in the air,
Showing off your shiny hair.

Farmer brings a bunch of hay,
For a busy, happy day.
Munching happily until,
Shadows stretch across the hill.

Mother horse is standing nigh,
Humming out a lullaby.
Snuggle close and do not weep,
Time for little horses to sleep.

Morning light will soon awake,
Down beside the shiny lake.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Tree
rhymes.text:
Little pony, big and brown,
Gallop up and gallop down.
Trot along the grassy lane,
Wind is blowing through your mane.

Kick your hooves up in the air,
Running without any care.
Find an apple on the ground,
Sweetest snack that can be found.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day you will not forget.
Lie down softly in the hay,
Rest until the coming day.

Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.
Dream of fields so green and wide,
With your mama by your side.

rhymes.title: Clickety Clack
rhymes.text:
Clickety clack, clickety clack,
Riding on the pony's back.
Up and down the wooden floor,
Trotting right up to the door.

Swish your tail from left to right,
Coat of shining snowy white.
Nicker softly, shake your head,
Time to head on to your bed.

Carrot crunching in the stall,
You are loved the most of all.
Soft brown eyes so big and sweet,
Happy little pony feet.

Now the barn is dark and still,
Moonlight shining on the hill.
Sleepy pony time to rest,
In your cozy little nest.

rhymes.title: Horsie on the Farm
rhymes.text:
Horsie, horsie, full of grace,
Running in a happy race.
Jump the puddle, skip the stone,
In the meadow all alone.

Shake your ears and give a neigh,
Eating yummy bales of hay.
Roll around upon the ground,
Bestest friend that can be found.

Birds are singing in the tree,
Singing happy songs for free.
Dust is dancing in the light,
Everything is warm and bright.

Now the shadows start to grow,
Walking very, very slow.
Time to dream beneath the moon,
Morning sun will coming soon.

rhymes.title: Gallop Little Pony
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, little horse,
Trot around the farm of course.
Kick your heels up in the air,
Running through the meadow fair.

Mane is flowing in the breeze,
Running past the leafy trees.
Stop to munch the clover sweet,
Such a tasty little treat.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little horse to go.
Walk into the barn so deep,
Ready now for quiet sleep.

Close your big brown sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Little horse, sleep tight tonight.

rhymes.title: Clippety Clop
rhymes.text:
Clippety clop goes the pony's feet,
Walking down the country street.
Swishing his tail from side to side,
Ready for a happy ride.

Brown and shiny is his coat,
Sounding like a happy boat.
Floating through the tall green grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.

He lets out a happy neigh,
Chewing on some yellow hay.
Nudging with his velvet nose,
Right down to his tiny toes.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Tired little horse, go slow.
Snuggling in the straw so deep,
Time to cuddle up and sleep.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
See the pony standing tall,
Living in the wooden stall.
With a golden, shiny mane,
Dancing in the gentle rain.

Stomping hoofs upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Pancing through the open gate,
Never wanting to be late.

Chasing butterflies of blue,
With his shiny coat anew.
Happy horse all through the day,
Jumping up and far away.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving us a lovely light.
Rest your head upon the floor,
Sleeping till the morning roar.

rhymes.title: The Little Brown Horse
rhymes.text:
See the little brown horse go run,
Jumping high into the sun.
He has a tail so long and sweet,
With happy hooves upon his feet.

Clop, clop, clop goes the pony now,
Saying hello to the friendly cow.
He loves to gallop across the land,
Eating apples from your hand.

His ears are soft just like a bear,
With shiny ribbons in his hair.
He trots around the big green tree,
As happy as a horse can be.

The sun goes down, the day is done,
He had so much playing in the fun.
Now he sleeps in his cozy bed,
With sleepy eyes and a sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Moon
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, little steed,
Running fast at a bouncy speed.
Over the grass and through the hay,
We are playing all the day.

Touch your nose and shake your mane,
Dancing in the summer rain.
Kick your hooves up in the air,
Showing how much you love to care.

A shiny star is in the sky,
Watching little horses fly.
Trot along the silver floor,
Till we reach the stable door.

Wrap me in a blanket bright,
Sleep until the morning light.
Dreaming of the fields of green,
The happiest pony ever seen.

rhymes.title: Neigh, Little Pony
rhymes.text:
Neigh, little pony, soft and white,
Shining brightly in the light.
You have a star upon your head,
Time to wake up from your bed.

Prance around the paddock wall,
Playing games both big and small.
Stomp your hooves upon the ground,
Make a happy cloppy sound.

Eat your carrots, crunch them sweet,
Such a tasty morning treat.
Now you run across the floor,
Right up to the wooden door.

Rest your head upon my knee,
Take a gentle nap with me.
Goodnight, pony, sleep so deep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Trotting To The Farm
rhymes.text:
See the little pony run,
Basking in the golden sun.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Watch the happy pony go.
Swishing tail from side to side,
Ready for a fun-filled ride.
Kicking up his heels in glee,
As happy as a horse can be.
Munching on the clover sweet,
Such a yummy, tasty treat.
Blinking with his big brown eyes,
Underneath the big blue skies.
Rubbing noses with his friends,
Where the dusty pathway ends.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little horse to sleep.

rhymes.title: Clip Clop Goes The Horse
rhymes.text:
Clip and clop and clip and clop,
See the pony start to hop.
Down the lane and past the tree,
Running wild and running free.
Wearing shoes of shiny steel,
Happy from his nose to heel.
Soft white star upon his head,
Walking to his cozy bed.
Farmer pats his velvet mane,
Waiting for the morning rain.
Snorting softly in the hay,
After such a busy day.
Dreaming of a grassy hill,
While the barn is dark and still.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Tucked into your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Little Dapple Grey
rhymes.text:
Little horse with dapple grey,
Running out to park and play.
Jumping fences, big and high,
Reaching for the open sky.
Ears are twitching, listening near,
Nothing does the pony fear.
Neighing softly to the breeze,
Rustling through the leafy trees.
Gallop fast and gallop slow,
That's the way the horses go.
Rolling in the meadow grass,
Watching pretty birdies pass.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Time to rest your sleepy feet,
Have a dream so soft and sweet.

rhymes.title: Trotting Little Pony
rhymes.text:
Little pony, big and brown,
Trotting up and trotting down.
Swish your tail and shake your mane,
Running in the summer rain.

Soft black nose and shiny eyes,
Looking at the sunny skies.
Prancing through the grass so green,
Cutest horse you've ever seen.

Stop and munch a yummy treat,
Stamping with your little feet.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy straw-filled bed.

Close your eyes and dream all night,
Till the morning golden light.
Sleepy pony, safe and sound,
Sleeping softly on the ground.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Stars
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, run and play,
Running through the hay today.
Jump the creek and leap so high,
Reaching for the evening sky.

White star shining on your face,
Moving with such magic grace.
Kick your heels up in the air,
Showing off your beauty there.

Friendly neighs for all to hear,
Bringing lots of joy and cheer.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping on the quiet ground.

Dreams of carrots sweet and bright,
Keep you warm the whole dark night.
Gallop softly in your sleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.

rhymes.title: The Golden Horseshoe
rhymes.text:
Golden horseshoe on your toe,
Tell me where you want to go.
Down the lane or through the gate,
Come along, do not be late!

Eat the clover, sweet and red,
Time to rest your sleepy head.
Pat your back and stroke your mane,
Till the morning comes again.

Little hooves go tap, tap, tap,
Taking now a little nap.
Wind is singing in the trees,
Carried on a gentle breeze.

Stars are blinking from above,
Sending you so much warm love.
Rest your legs and drift away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Trotting Pony
rhymes.text:
Little pony, big and brown,
Trotting up and trotting down.
Swish your tail and shake your mane,
Running in the summer rain.

Soft black nose and shiny eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.
Prance along the grassy lane,
Happy pony on the plain.

Kick your heels up in the air,
Tossing back your pretty hair.
Time to rest your weary feet,
Time to eat a little wheat.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Time to sleep so soft and slow.
Close your eyes and dream all night,
Sleeping in the morning light.

rhymes.title: Clickity Clack
rhymes.text:
Clickity clack, upon the floor,
Trotting right up to my door.
Hello horse, so big and grand,
Let me pat your gentle hand.

Eat your apple, crunch and chew,
I am making friends with you.
Wear a ribbon, red and bright,
Gallop fast into the night.

Jump the fence and skip the hay,
We are going out to play.
Round and round the paddock floor,
Trotting past the wooden door.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the sleepy town.
Rest your head upon the hay,
We will play another day.

rhymes.title: Gallop Away
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, through the trees,
Feeling like a flying breeze.
White star shining on your head,
Time to skip the clover bed.

Neigh hello and neigh goodbye,
Reaching for the deep blue sky.
Run so fast and jump so high,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.

Find a puddle in the lane,
Splash the water in the rain.
 Shake your coat and feel so free,
 Standing by the willow tree.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving us a silver light.
Time to dream of fields of green,
Nicest horse I've ever seen.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Tree
rhymes.text:
Little horse runs fast and free,
Galloping across the lea.
Tossing up his shiny mane,
Running through the summer rain.
Click-clack go his little hooves,
Through the grass and leafy grooves.
He loves to jump and he loves to play,
Eating sweet and clover hay.
When the afternoon is bright,
He is such a happy sight.
Now he stops to rest his head,
In his cozy wooden shed.
Swish goes his long hairy tail,
As he leans against the rail.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Sleepy horse with sleepy head.

rhymes.title: The Pony's Big Red Apple
rhymes.text:
Pony stands beside the gate,
Waiting for his yummy plate.
Farmer brings a shiny treat,
Something crunchy, fresh, and sweet.
It is round and bright and red,
Right beside the pony's shed.
Pony takes it with his nose,
Smelling sweet from head to toes.
Crunch and munch goes pony's bite,
Eating in the morning light.
Now the apple all is gone,
Pony stretches on the lawn.
Blinking with his big brown eyes,
Underneath the sunny skies.
Happy horse is full and glad,
Best little pony that we ever had.

rhymes.title: Trotting to the Barn
rhymes.text:
Sun is setting in the sky,
Birds are softly flying by.
Pony trots along the track,
With a farmer on his back.
Softly neighing to the sheep,
While the little lambs fall sleep.
Stars are peeking from above,
Sending lots of peace and love.
Down the dusty farmyard way,
Ending up a busy day.
Into the stable warm and deep,
Where the horses go to sleep.
Blanket on his sleepy back,
Resting on the wooden rack.
Close your eyes and dream all night,
Till the morning brings the light.

rhymes.title: Gallop Little Horse
rhymes.text:
Little horse runs through the grass,
Watch him go so fast, so fast!
Kicking up his little feet,
Trotting down the country street.
Black mane flowing in the breeze,
Running underneath the trees.
Stomping hooves go clip-clop-cland,
In this happy meadow land.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.
Morning sun will soon appear,
Bringing joy and daytime cheer.
Wake up, pony, time to play,
Have a happy, sunny day!

rhymes.title: Horsie on the Farm
rhymes.text:
Horsie stands beside the gate,
Waiting for his food on plate.
Crunchy carrots, sweet and green,
Freshest horse you've ever seen.
Velvet nose and big brown eyes,
Looking at the butterﬂies.
Give a pat upon his mane,
Out here in the sunny lane.
He will give a happy neigh,
Eating lots of yummy hay.
Running round the big corral,
He is such a friendly pal.
Now the sun is going down,
Lighting up the sleepy town.
Say good night and softly creep,
Horsie is now fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Clppity-Clop Goes the Pony
rhymes.text:
Clippity-clop goes the pony's feet,
Walking down the grassy street.
Waving tail of shiny white,
Running in the morning light.
Stop and nibble clover sweet,
Such a special horse's treat.
Jumping over logs of wood,
Doing everything he should.
Now he's taking time to rest,
With his mother, he is blest.
Snuggling close against her side,
Safe from any windy ride.
Dreaming of the golden hay,
And another sunny day.
Wake up, pony, time to run,
Playing underneath the sun.

rhymes.title: Little Pony, Jump So High
rhymes.text:
Little pony in the clover,
Gallop under, gallop over.
Kick your heels up in the air,
Running without any care.

Shake your mane of shiny brown,
Never ever wear a frown.
Trot along the garden wall,
Catch a bouncing red soft ball.

Time to stop and time to rest,
Sleeping in your cozy nest.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
Counting little fluffy sheep.

Morning sun begins to glow,
Time for little horse to go.
Stamp your hoof and give a neigh,
Have a happy, sunny day.

rhymes.title: Clop, Clop, Little Horse
rhymes.text:
Clop, clop, goes the horse today,
Munching on the sweet green hay.
Running through the morning dew,
Looking bright and feeling new.

Soft brown nose and gentle eyes,
Reaching up to touch the skies.
Wag your tail and leap around,
Dancing on the grassy ground.

Farmer brings an apple sweet,
What a yummy, tasty treat!
Crunch and munch and chew it down,
Bestest pony in the town.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little horse to sleep.
Rest your head upon the floor,
Till the sun shines back once more.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
See the pony run and play,
Out inside the golden hay.
With a coat of shiny gold,
Bravest pony, young or old.

Pancing softly in the breeze,
Running underneath the trees.
Jumping over sticks and stone,
Making happiness his own.

Neigh and snort with pure delight,
Shining softly in the light.
Give a friendly little bow,
Eating clover yummy now.

Now the day is done and through,
Time to dream of skies so blue.
Sleepy pony goes to rest,
In his warm and cozy nest.

rhymes.title: Little Dapple
rhymes.text:
Little horse with shiny eyes,
Galloping beneath the skies.
Running fast across the green,
Happiest you've ever been.

Trot along and shake your mane,
Dancing in the summer rain.
Kicking up your little heels,
See how very glad it feels.

Softly neighing to the sun,
Now your playing has begun.
Stop and munch the clover sweet,
Such a tasty daytime treat.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for ponies goes to sleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy golden bed.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Moon
rhymes.text:
Pony, pony, big and brown,
Galloping around the town.
Running fast and running free,
Come and play a game with me.

Stomp your hoof and give a neigh,
We will race the clouds today.
Over fences, high and wide,
What a joyful pony ride!

Wind is blowing in your mane,
Racing down the country lane.
Now you stop to take a rest,
In the meadow you love best.

Moon is shining up above,
Sending dreams of peace and love.
Little pony, safe and sound,
Sleeping softly on the ground.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden mane and coat of gold,
Bravest horse of young or old.
Trotting down the dusty track,
With a smile upon your back.

Jump the brook and clear the wall,
Having fun both big and small.
Sniffing flowers on the way,
Happy on a sunny day.

Shadows stretch across the grass,
Watching sleepy moments pass.
Barn door opens wide and wide,
Time to step away inside.

Eat your hay and chew your oats,
Floating like the little boats.
Time to dream the night away,
Until comes another day.

rhymes.title: The Little Brown Pony
rhymes.text:
See the little pony run,
Basking in the golden sun.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Watch the happy pony go.

Waving mane of silky white,
Running in the morning light.
Kicking up his tiny hoof,
Far away from any roof.

Softly neighing to his friends,
Where the grassy meadow ends.
Eating clover sweet and green,
Best little horse you've ever seen.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little horse to go.
Close your eyes and time to sleep,
Counting fluffy little sheep.

rhymes.title: Gallop, Gallop, Little Horse
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, down the lane,
Flying tail and flying mane.
Jumping over sticks and stones,
Happy horse with cheerful tones.

Stop and munch the yellow hay,
Having such a fun-filled day.
Nudging with a velvet nose,
Where the purple violet grows.

Prancing near the wooden fence,
Making every toddler sense
How much fun a horse can be,
Running wild and running free.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little horse is going to sleep.
Rest your head upon the hay,
Wake up for another day.

rhymes.title: Clip-Clop Goes the Horse
rhymes.text:
Clip-clop, clip-clop goes the beat,
Moving fast his sturdy feet.
Brown and shiny coat so bright,
Running in the morning light.

Shake your tail and shake your head,
Time to leave your cozy bed.
Run across the morning dew,
Horse is saying hello to you.

Jump a puddle, splash the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Trotting past the apple tree,
As happy as a horse can be.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Whispering a soft goodnight.
Snuggle in the straw so deep,
Little horse is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Pony Trotting By
rhymes.text:
Little pony trotting by,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
With a swish of shiny tail,
Down the grassy winding trail.

Clpp-clop, clippity-clop,
Little horse will never stop.
Running through the morning dew,
Looking bright and happy too.

Stop and eat a clover snack,
With a pat upon your back.
Soft brown ears and velvet nose,
Warming up from head to toes.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little pony you're the best.

rhymes.title: Gallop Fast and Gallop Slow
rhymes.text:
Gallop fast and gallop slow,
Watch the little pony go.
Stomp your feet upon the floor,
Trotting right up to the door.

Mane is blowing in the breeze,
Running underneath the trees.
Happy neighs and joyful sounds,
Jumping up and making bounds.

Find an apple on the ground,
Best treat that can ever be found.
Munch it up and chew it tight,
Everything is feeling right.

Time to lie down in the hay,
After such a busy day.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little horse is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Horsie on the Farm
rhymes.text:
Horsie on the farm so sweet,
Dancing with your little feet.
Wearing shoes of shiny steel,
Oh, what joy you always feel.

Rub your nose against my hand,
Nicest pony in the land.
White and brown and fluffy too,
All the toddlers play with you.

Run around the paddock ring,
Hear the happy birdies sing.
Kick your heels up in the air,
Jumping without any care.

Stars are shining bright and clear,
Bedtime is so very near.
Whisper soft a lullaby,
Little horsie, wave goodbye.

rhymes.title: Little Horse Trot
rhymes.text:
Little horse, little horse, running fast,
Galloping past the trees at last.
Soft brown ears and a shiny mane,
Running out in the sunny lane.

Clip-clop, clip-clop, on the ground,
Making a happy trotting sound.
Up the hill and down the dale,
Wagging a happy, swishy tail.

Now it is time to stop and rest,
Back in the stable you love best.
Eat some clover, sweet and green,
The happiest pony ever seen.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.
Dream of fields so wide and grand,
In your lovely little land.

rhymes.title: Pony Shoes Go Tap
rhymes.text:
Hear the pony walking by,
Underneath the big blue sky.
Shiny hooves of silver gray,
Prancing through the day.

Tap and tap and tap they go,
Walking fast and walking slow.
Stop to eat a juicy pear,
Breathing in the fresh spring air.

Shake your tail and give a neigh,
Time to chase the clouds away.
Jump across the garden wall,
Having fun, big and small.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Pony goes to gentle sleep.
Rest your head upon the hay,
Wake again to laugh and play.

rhymes.title: Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden mane and coat of brown,
Finest pony in the town.
Trot along the grassy track,
With a baby on your back.

Soft black nose and friendly eyes,
Watching all the butterflies.
Prancing through the morning dew,
Saying cheerful words to you.

Spin around and give a cheer,
Glad the summertime is here.
Jump a little, hop a bound,
Happy hooves upon the ground.

Evening comes with quiet grace,
Bringing slumber to this place.
Dreaming of the morning sun,
When the happy race is won.

rhymes.title: Little Horse Goes Clip-Clop
rhymes.text:
Little horse with shiny eyes,
Trotting underneath the skies.
Swishing tail of golden brown,
Walking all around the town.

Clip and clop and clickety-clack,
With a rider on his back.
Running through the grassy green,
Finest horse you've ever seen.

Stopping by the apple tree,
Looking very proud and free.
Munching on a crunchy snack,
Happy horse and that is that.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little horse, you are the best.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Stars
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, run and play,
Running through the sunny day.
Big brown hooves upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Mane is blowing in the breeze,
Racing past the leafy trees.
Jumping over logs and stone,
In a world so all his own.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Moving just a little slow.
Time to tuck your sleepy head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

Dreaming of the morning light,
Sleeping through the quiet night.
Softly breathing, safe and deep,
Little horse is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Pony Playtime
rhymes.text:
Soft white pony in the sun,
Time to have a lot of fun.
Nudging at the wooden gate,
Never wanting to be late.

Tossing up his little head,
Ready for the day ahead.
Prancing through the flowers bright,
Looking oh so pure and white.

Found a puddle on the floor,
Splash and dab and splash some more.
Happy squeals and muddy feet,
Life upon the farm is sweet.

Evening comes with purple skies,
Rubbing now his sleepy eyes.
Curled up in the cozy hay,
Waiting for another day.

rhymes.title: Little Horse, Little Horse
rhymes.text:
Little horse, little horse, running fast,
Look at you go past, past, past!
Little horse, little horse, shiny mane,
Galloping out in the sunny rain.

Little horse, little horse, on the hill,
Standing so proud and very still.
Little horse, little horse, eating grass,
Watching the fluffy white clouds pass.

Little horse, little horse, big brown eyes,
Looking up at the clear blue skies.
Little horse, little horse, twitch your ear,
Tell me you love to be right here.

Little horse, little horse, time to rest,
Sleeping at home is what you love best.
Little horse, little horse, close your eyes,
Dreaming beneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Clip-Clop Go the Hooves
rhymes.text:
Clip-clop, clip-clop, down the lane,
Wind is blowing through my mane.
Clip-clop, clip-clop, touch the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Trotting, trotting, fast and slow,
That is how the ponies go.
Prancing, prancing, up the street,
Moving all four fuzzy feet.

Jump a little over there,
Kicking up our heels with care.
Running through the open gate,
Playing with our pony mate.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Clip-clop time is done for today,
Tomorrow we will come and play.

rhymes.title: Dapple Gray
rhymes.text:
I have a pony named Dapple Gray,
He likes to eat sweet oats all day.
He has a tail of silky hair,
And gallops lightly through the air.

He wears a shiny leather shoe,
And walks upon the morning dew.
He gives a friendly little neigh,
Whenever I come by to play.

We race across the meadow green,
The happiest friends you've ever seen.
He stops to munch a clover sweet,
And gently stamps his little feet.

Now day is done and stars awake,
Sleeping beside the quiet lake.
Goodnight, my pony, sleep so deep,
While angels watch you as you sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Pony Hooves
rhymes.text:
Little pony, big and bright,
Running in the morning light.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Everywhere you want to go.

Swish your tail so fluffy white,
Underneath the sunny light.
Prance along the grassy green,
Prettiest horse I've ever seen.

Kick your heels up in the air,
Jumping here and jumping there.
Now it's time to rest your head,
In your cozy, straw-filled bed.

Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
While the little fireflies sleep.
Dream of apples sweet and red,
Resting softly in your bed.

rhymes.title: Gallop to the Tree
rhymes.text:
Gallop, gallop, little horse,
Running on the muddy course.
Jump over the yellow hay,
Having fun and time to play.

Shake your mane from side to side,
What a wonderful, fun ride!
Neigh so happy, loud and clear,
Glad that spring is finally here.

Find a carrot, crunch and munch,
Eating up your yummy lunch.
Drink some water from the brook,
Sitting by the shady nook.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the sleepy town.
Rest your legs and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden mane and shiny coat,
Floating like a little boat.
Walking down the river side,
Ready for a sleepy ride.

Pat his nose so soft and sweet,
Stamping with his little feet.
Clicket-clack upon the stone,
Never feeling all alone.

Birds are singing in the tree,
Singing happy songs for me.
Horse is happy, horse is glad,
Best little friend I ever had.

Night is coming, shadows fall,
Quiet now upon them all.
Whisper soft and whisper low,
Time for little horse to go.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a happy little piglet named Pip. Pip had two floppy pink ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. Today was a very special day because the sun was shining warmly, and the big sky was as blue as a robin's egg. Pip woke up early, stretched his little legs, and gave a happy squeak. Oink, oink! Good morning, world! Pip waddled out of his cozy barn and looked all around. Oh, what is that over there? It was a giant, magnificent puddle of squishy, squelchy mud. Pip's eyes lit up with pure joy. There is nothing in the whole wide world that Pip loved more than mud. He trotted over as fast as his little trotters could carry him. He stopped right at the edge of the puddle and dipped one small hoof into the brown, gooey water. Squish! It felt cool and tickly. Then, he dipped his other hoof in. Squish, squash! Pip let out another joyful squeak and stepped right into the middle of the puddle. He sat down with a big plop! Mud splashed up on his left ear. Mud splashed up on his right ear. Mud covered his tummy and his back until he was wearing a coat made entirely of mud. Pip giggled and rolled from side to side. He made big mud angels in the wet earth. Suddenly, he heard a friendly voice call out, 'Hello there, Pip! Having fun?' Pip looked up and saw his good friend Bella the cow peeking over the wooden fence. 'Oink, oink! Yes, Bella! It is so squishy!' said Pip. Bella smiled and chewed her green grass. Soon, other farm animals came by to see what all the fun was about. Penny the duck waddled over and quacked happily, dipping her bill into the water. Even though ducks love water, Pip insisted that mud was the absolute best. Pip splashed and played until the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange. His tummy began to rumble a happy little rumble. Time for supper! Pip stepped out of the muddy puddle, leaving a trail of happy little footprints behind him. He trotted over to the water trough and washed his hooves until they were clean and pink again. As he munched on his crunchy yellow corn back in the warm barn, Pip smiled a sleepy smile. It had been the best, muddiest day ever. He curled his tail into a tight little spring, closed his heavy eyes, and drifted off to dream sweet dreams of squishy, squelchy mud.

stories.title: Penny's Picnic Surprise
stories.text: High up on a sunny hill, where the daisies danced in the gentle breeze, lived a cheerful little pig named Penny. Penny wore a pretty red ribbon tied right between her floppy ears. Today was a very exciting day because Penny was going on a grand adventure: a springtime picnic all by herself! Penny went into the rustic wooden farmhouse kitchen to pack her picnic basket. She opened the pantry and carefully selected her absolute favorite treats. First, she added three shiny red apples that smelled sweet and crisp. Next, she packed a bunch of bright green celery sticks, and right on top, she placed a jar of yummy strawberry jam. Penny closed the basket lid with a satisfying click. She picked up the handle in her snout and set off down the winding dirt path. The path was lined with yellow buttercups and tall green grass that tickled her tummy as she waddled along. The birds were singing a merry tune in the leafy treetops, cheering her on. After walking for a little while, Penny found the most wonderful spot under the shade of a big, leafy apple tree. A soft carpet of green clover covered the ground, looking just like a fluffy green bed. Penny carefully set her basket down and spread out a bright yellow checkered blanket. She sat right in the middle and opened her basket. She took out a shiny red apple and took a loud, crunchy bite. Crunch, crunch, crunch! It was so delicious. Just as she was about to open the jar of strawberry jam, she heard a soft rustling sound in the bushes nearby. Rustle, rustle, rustle. Penny gasped and her little snout twitched. Out popped a fuzzy gray bunny with long, twitchy ears and a tiny cotton ball tail. The bunny sniffed the air and looked right at Penny with big, round eyes. Penny giggled and said, 'Hello, little bunny! Would you like to share my picnic?' The bunny did a little hop of happiness, which meant yes! Penny shared a crunchy celery stick with her new furry friend, and they munched together side by side. The warm breeze rustled the apple leaves above them, singing a lullaby of peace and friendship. When they finished eating, Penny packed up her basket and gave the bunny a friendly wave goodbye. She walked back home up the sunny hill with a full tummy and a very happy heart, ready to tell her mother all about her wonderful picnic surprise.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Boots
stories.text: Barnaby was a very particular little pig. He lived on a bustling, noisy farm where animals ran, flew, and trotted everywhere. But Barnaby had one special thing that made him the proudest pig on the whole farm: a brand new pair of shiny, bright red rain boots. They were delivered in a cardboard box tied with a yellow string, and when Barnaby first put them on his trotters, he felt like he could conquer the world. They fit him just right, not too tight and not too loose. The only problem was that the sun had been shining for a whole week, and there was not a single drop of rain in sight. Barnaby desperately wanted to show off his red boots, but the ground was completely dry and dusty. Every morning, Barnaby would wake up, slip on his red boots, and trot out to the middle of the farmyard. He would stomp his left foot—stomp, stomp! Then he would stomp his right foot—stomp, stomp! He hoped the loud noise would wake up the clouds and make it rain. The other farm animals watched him with amusement. Sammy the rooster crowed a morning greeting, and Dolly the sheep bleated softly, but Barnaby just kept on stomping. 'Come on, rain!' Barnaby squeaked hopefully. But the sky stayed bright blue and cloudless. Barnaby sighed and sat down by the big red barn, looking sadly down at his shiny boots. They looked so pretty, but boots were meant for puddles! Just then, the wind began to blow a little cooler. A flock of fluffy white clouds slowly drifted across the horizon, growing bigger and grayer by the minute. Suddenly, a gentle breeze swept through, and the sky turned a deep, dramatic gray. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter! The first cool raindrops began to fall from the sky, landing softly on Barnaby's snout. Barnaby squealed with absolute delight. He jumped straight up into the air. The rain fell faster and heavier, turning the farmyard dust into wonderful, splashing puddles. Barnaby ran as fast as his little legs could carry him, splashing through every single puddle in sight. Splash, splash, splish, splash! Water flew everywhere, but Barnaby didn't care at all. His red boots shone brightly in the rain as he danced in circles, laughing and oinking with sheer happiness. He had finally gotten his rainy day, and his red boots were the stars of the show.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text: Once upon a very sunny morning, a little pink pig named Pip woke up with a big wiggle of his curly tail. Oink, oink! Good morning, world! Pip lived on a cozy farm with his best animal friends, but today, Pip had only one very important mission. He wanted to find the biggest, squishiest, mud puddle on the entire farm. Pip trotted out of his warm straw bed and stepped right into the bright farmyard. The sun was shining, and the yellow buttercups were nodding hello. First, Pip trotted past the big red barn. He saw Cow chewing on some green grass. Moo, moo, said Cow. Good morning, Pip! Pip waved his little trotter and said, Oink, moo! But Pip did not stop, because he was on a mud hunt. Next, Pip waddled past the tall windmill. He saw Hen scratching in the dirt with her fluffy yellow chicks. Cluck, cluck, said Hen. Have you seen any bugs today, Pip? Pip shook his pink snout and said, Oink, cluck! He was still looking for mud. Pip walked a little further down the bumpy dirt path. Suddenly, his twitchy pink nose caught a wonderful, earthy smell. Sniff, sniff, sniff. Oh boy! Pip knew that smell anywhere. It was wet, wonderful mud! Pip hurried as fast as his little short legs could carry him. He zoomed past the pumpkin patch and came to a sudden stop right at the edge of the biggest, darkest, most magnificent puddle on the whole farm. It was a masterpiece of mud! Pip let out a squeal of pure joy. Squeak! Without wasting a single second, Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle with a giant SPLASH! Mud flew up into the air like brown fireworks. It landed on his nose, his ears, and even his curly tail. Pip rolled over to the left. Squish, squash, squish! Then Pip rolled over to the right. Slosh, mud, slosh! He kicked his little legs and made bubbly mud pies. Being muddy was the absolute best feeling in the whole wide world. Soon, Duck waddled over and quacked happily at the sight. Quack, quack! Can I join you, Pip? Of course! said Pip with a happy oink. Duck hopped in, and they splashed together until the sun started to go down behind the big green hills. Pip was wonderfully dirty, wonderfully happy, and very, very ready for a cozy bedtime sleep.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Boots
stories.text: Barnaby was a sweet little pig who loved to dress up in funny clothes. One rainy Tuesday morning, Farmer Brown left a small cardboard box right outside Barnaby pen. Barnaby trotted over, curious as could be. Oink? What is this? he wondered. He pushed the flap open with his pink snout and peered inside. To his absolute delight, sitting right at the top of the box was a pair of bright, shiny, cherry-red rain boots. They had little yellow buckles and looked just the right size for a little pig. Barnaby squealed with excitement. He knew right away that he simply had to try them on. Now, putting boots on four hooves is not an easy task for a pig, but Barnaby was very determined. He squished his left front hoof into the first boot. Then he squished his right front hoof into the second boot. But wait! Barnaby still had two back hooves left. He wobbled and wiggled until he managed to slide his back hooves into the other two boots. There he stood, wearing four shiny red boots on his four little trotters. Barnaby took a step forward. Clump, clump, thump! Went his hooves against the wooden floor of his pen. It sounded like a marching band. Barnaby thought that was the funniest sound in the whole wide world. He trotted out into the farmyard to show all his friends his fabulous new fashion statement. Horse looked over the wooden fence and neighed in surprise. Well, look at you, Barnaby! Those boots are remarkably red! Sheep stopped chewing clover and bleated, Baa! Very stylish for a rainy day! Barnaby felt like the fanciest pig in the countryside. He decided to go for a nice walk through the damp grass. Clump, clump, thump went the boots with every single step. He walked past the apple tree and past the duck pond, feeling very proud indeed. But then, Barnaby saw the biggest puddle on the path. Without thinking, he marched right into the middle of it. Splash! Water went everywhere. But because he was wearing his wonderful red boots, his hooves stayed completely dry and cozy. Barnaby giggled and stomped his feet. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Rainy days were truly the best when you had red boots to wear.

stories.title: Penny's Picnic Surprise
stories.text: It was a wonderful afternoon, and Penny the piglet had a very important job to do. Today was the farm animals' monthly picnic, and Penny was in charge of packing the basket. Penny put on her favorite polka-dot apron and tied a yellow ribbon around her curly tail. Oink! Time to get cooking! she cheered. First, Penny went to the garden patch to pick some bright red strawberries. She popped one into her mouth. Yum! Sweet and juicy. She filled a wooden basket with the lovely berries. Next, Penny trotted over to the apple tree. Thump! A big, round, green apple fell right out of the branches and landed softly on the grass. Penny picked it up with her snout and placed it gently on top of the strawberries. Finally, Penny went to the barn to ask Cow for a bottle of fresh, creamy milk. Cow mooed happily and handed over the bottle with a friendly nod. Penny placed everything carefully into her big picnic basket. It was heavy, but Penny was a strong little pig. She carried the basket all the way to the top of the sunny grassy hill where all her friends were waiting. Duck was there, and so was Sheep and Horse. They all cheered when they saw Penny arrive. Hello, everyone! Penny called out cheerfully. I brought lots of delicious treats for our big picnic! She opened up the basket and pulled out the strawberries, the big green apple, and the creamy milk. Everyone's eyes grew wide with happiness. They sat down on the soft green grass and began to eat together. The strawberries were sweet, the apple was crunchy, and the milk was cool and refreshing. They shared stories and giggled as the afternoon breeze blew gently through their ears. When all the food was gone, Penny looked around at her wonderful friends with a full tummy and a very happy heart. Picnic days were simply magical, especially when shared with the best friends in the whole world. As the golden sun began to dip below the horizon, they all trotted back down the hill together, humming a happy little farm tune.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a very sunny morning, a little pink pig named Pip woke up with a giant wiggle in his curly tail. Today was a special day because outside his cozy barn, big, fluffy puddles were waiting after a lovely rain shower. Pip hopped right out of his warm straw bed and trotted over to the front porch. There they were! A brand new pair of shiny, bright red rain boots. Pip squealed with absolute joy. Oink, oink! He quickly slipped his little trotters into the boots. Clop, clop, went his feet as he walked down the steps. Pip could not wait to find the biggest, splashiest puddle in the whole farmyard. He waddled past the sleeping brown cow, past the tall green cornstalks, and right up to the sparkling water near the old red tractor. Pip took a deep breath, raised his front trotter high into the air, and stomped down as hard as he could. Splash! Water flew up into the warm air like tiny shining diamonds. Oh, it was so much fun! Splash, splash, splash went the red boots. Pip giggled and snorted. He splashed so hard that a little frog popped its head out of the water to say hello. Ribbit! Pip smiled a big piggy smile and waved his trotter. Soon, the muddy water was swirling all around his boots. Pip wiggled his toes inside and felt the squishy mud between his heels. He danced a silly piggy dance, spinning around in circles. But then, Pip felt his tummy make a funny rumbling sound. Grumble, grumble! All that splashing had made him very hungry for his morning slop and crunchy green apples. Pip looked down at his shiny red boots, now covered in friendly brown mud. He trotted happily back to the barn, dreaming of apples and more puddles tomorrow. What a wonderful day to be a little pig!

stories.title: Barnaby Bear and the Lost Toy
stories.text: Deep inside the cozy animal playpen, a little pig named Barnaby had a very important mission. Barnaby was holding his most favorite toy in the whole wide world, a squeaky yellow duck named Ducky. Ducky was soft, bright yellow, and made the happiest squeak whenever Barnaby gave him a gentle squeeze. Squeak! Squeak! Barnaby and Ducky did everything together. They ate crunchy carrots together, took muddy naps together, and sang lullabies under the twinkling stars. But today, while Barnaby was running around playing tag with the fluffy white lambs, something terrible happened. Ducky was gone! Barnaby stopped right in his tracks. Oh no! Where could Ducky be? Barnaby searched everywhere. He looked under the green cabbage leaves. He looked behind the wooden water trough. He even peeked inside the empty hay bales. No Ducky! Barnaby let out a sad little snort. A big tear rolled down his pink cheek. Just then, his good friend Penny the duck waddled over, flapping her wings. Quack, quack! Are you looking for this, Barnaby? Penny asked kindly. She pointed her orange beak right toward the big pile of soft, warm hay in the corner. Barnaby trotted over as fast as his little legs could carry him. He pushed aside the golden hay with his snout. And there was Ducky, safe and sound, taking a little nap! Barnaby gasped with relief. He scooped up Ducky in his trotters and gave him a huge squeeze. Squeak! Ducky squeaked happily. Barnaby did a happy little dance, shaking his curly tail from side to side. He thanked Penny with a warm piggy hug. From that day on, Barnaby tied a bright blue ribbon around Ducky so he would never, ever get lost again. They spent the rest of the afternoon playing happily in the warm sun.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Sleepytime Snort
stories.text: The sun was slowly going down behind the green hills, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink, orange, and purple. Down on the farm, all the animals were getting very tired. The fluffy sheep were closing their eyes, and the little yellow chicks were tucked safely under their mother's wings. But little Penny Pig was still wide awake! Penny had far too much energy to go to sleep. She wanted to play hide and seek with the moon. Penny trotted over to the big wooden fence and looked up at the twinkling stars. She gave a little playful oink. Mama Pig walked over, smiling softly, and wrapped a cozy patchwork blanket around Penny's shoulders. Time for bed, my sweet little piglet, Mama whispered gently. Penny shook her head. But I am not tired, Mama! She giggled, doing a little hop. Mama Pig smiled knowingly. She knew just what to do to help Penny feel sleepy. First, they went for a slow walk around the barnyard to say goodnight to everything. Goodnight, brown cow. Goodnight, old red tractor. Goodnight, buzzing bumblebees. Penny whispered her goodnights softly, feeling her eyelids growing just a tiny bit heavy. Next, they sat down on the soft, sweet-smelling straw. Mama Pig began to hum a soothing lullaby, a gentle tune about rolling in the clover and dreaming of sweet strawberries. Penny rested her head on a fluffy hay pillow. She closed her eyes and listened to the peaceful sounds of the farm at night. A gentle breeze whispered through the open barn door. Yawn! Penny let out a big, wide yawn. Her little trotters felt heavy as feathers. With one last soft snort, Penny drifted off into a deep, magical sleep, dreaming of rainbows and sunny puddles. Goodnight, sweet Penny Pig. Sleep tight until the morning sun.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a little pig named Pip. Pip was a very happy pig with a curly-wurly tail, a pink button nose, and four little trotters. Pip loved many things, but most of all, Pip loved mud! Every single morning, Pip would wake up and say, 'Oint! Oint! Time for mud!' One sunny morning, the sun was shining down, and the farm was buzzing with life. The cows were mooing, the hens were clucking, and Pip was looking for the biggest, squishiest puddle on the whole farm. He trotted past the big red barn, saying hello to the fuzzy yellow chicks. 'Peep peep!' went the chicks. 'Oink oink!' replied Pip, and he kept on walking with a happy wiggle of his bottom. Soon, Pip found it. It was the most magnificent puddle he had ever seen. It was brown, it was thick, and it looked wonderfully wet. Pip let out a squeal of pure joy. He walked right up to the edge of the puddle and dipped one tiny trotter in. 'Splash!' went the water. It felt cool and nice. Then, he dipped his other trotter in. 'Splash, splash!' Then, with a joyful giggle, Pip plopped his whole tummy right into the middle of the mud. 'Splat!' The mud went everywhere. It splashed up on his left ear, and it splashed up on his right ear. It covered his little pink snout, making a funny brown mud-patch right on the end. Pip rolled over onto his back and wiggled his four legs in the air. 'This is the best day ever!' he thought. He made happy piggy sounds, blowing bubbles in the thick brown sludge. 'Oink! Oink! Oink!' Soon, his animal friends came over to see what all the fun was about. Barnaby the brown horse poked his head over the wooden fence and neighed softly. Bessie the cow blinked her big brown eyes and said, 'Moo, you look very messy, Pip!' But Pip just smiled his biggest piggy smile. Being messy was part of the fun of being a little pig. After a long time of playing, splashing, and making mud pies, the warm sun began to dry the mud on Pip's back. It felt tickly and tight. Pip gave a big yawn. Playing in the mud is hard work! He climbed out of the puddle, leaving little muddy footprints all the way back to his cozy straw bed. He curled up tight, wiggled his curly tail, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of even bigger puddles for tomorrow.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Penny Pig loved shiny red things. She loved red apples, red strawberries, and most of all, she loved red balloons. Today was a very special day because Farmer Fred had given Penny a big, shiny, round red balloon on a long string. Penny held the string tightly in her little trotter. 'Wheee!' cheered Penny, dancing around the barnyard. The balloon bobbed up and down in the air, dancing right along with her. It floated over the hay bales and bounced gently against the blue sky. Penny felt like the luckiest pig in the whole wide world. She walked over to show her friend, Sammy the sheep. 'Look, Sammy! My red balloon!' she said proudly. Sammy bleated happily, 'Baa! That is a very nice balloon, Penny!' Penny held the string so carefully. But then, oh no! A playful gust of wind came blowing through the farm. It swooped down from the apple trees and gave a big WHOOSH! The wind tickled Penny's ear, and before she could tighten her grip, the string slipped right out of her trotter. 'Oh, no! Come back!' cried Penny. The bright red balloon shot up into the air, higher and higher, past the roof of the big red barn, past the tall green trees, and up toward the fluffy white clouds. Penny watched it go with big, sad eyes. A little tear rolled down her cheek. Her wonderful red balloon was flying away. Just then, Wise Old Owl swooped down from a branch. 'Hoot hoot, do not cry, little Penny. Look up high!' Penny blinked away her tear and looked up. The red balloon had gotten stuck in the branches of the big oak tree. It was safe, just floating gently against the leaves. Penny did not have wings, but she knew just what to do. She asked her tall friend, Barnaby the horse, to help her. Barnaby trotted over, stretched his long neck up to the branches, and gently plucked the string with his soft lips. He handed the string right back to Penny. Penny gasped with delight and grabbed the string with both trotters, holding on extra tight this time. 'Thank you, Barnaby!' she squealed. She gave the balloon a gentle pat, and danced all the way home, keeping her precious red balloon safe and sound.

stories.title: Percy's Picnic Surprise
stories.text: Percy was a very hungry little pig. His tummy let out a loud rumble. 'Rumbly-rumble-rum!' went Percy's tummy. It was lunchtime on the sunny farm, and Percy decided it was time to have a grand picnic all by himself. He found a lovely green spot right under the shade of a big apple tree. Percy brought along his favorite red-and-white checkered basket. Inside the basket, Farmer Fred had packed some wonderful treats just for Percy. Percy sat down on the soft grass, tucked a napkin under his chin, and opened the basket with a joyful squeal. 'Oink! Let us see what we have today!' First, out came a shiny green apple, round and crisp. Percy took a big, noisy crunch. 'CRUNCH, crunch, crunch!' The apple was sweet and juicy, and the very best kind of apple a pig could ever eat. Next, Percy reached deep into the bottom of the basket and pulled out three delicious carrot sticks. They were bright orange and very crunchy. Percy munched them up one by one, making happy little munching sounds. 'Munch, munch, munch!' But wait, what was that hiding at the very bottom of the basket? Percy peered inside and saw a shiny, yellow bowl filled with something round and sweet. It was a bowl of warm strawberry porridge! Percy loved strawberry porridge more than anything else in the whole wide world. It smelled like sweet strawberries and cozy milk. He picked up his wooden spoon and took a big spoonful. 'Yum, yum, yummy in my tummy!' he sang out loud. The porridge was warm and sweet, and it filled his tummy right up to the top. Just as Percy finished his last bite of porridge, a little breeze blew through the apple tree branches. 'Thump!' Something dropped right down from the tree and landed softly beside his basket. Percy blinked and looked down. It was a big, ripe, red apple, even bigger than the first one! Percy giggled and rubbed his happy, full tummy. 'Thank you, tree!' he oinked happily. He packed his empty basket, gave a sleepy yawn, and stretched out on the soft green grass for a lovely afternoon nap, dreaming of sweet strawberries and crunchy green apples.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text:
Once upon a very sunny morning, a little pink pig named Pip woke up with a big stretch and a happy little oink. Oink, oink! Pip lived on a cozy green farm with his animal friends, but Pip had one absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world. Do you know what it was? Mud! Pip loved squishy, squashy, cool, brown mud.

Pip trotted happily out of his warm straw bed and wiggled his curly tail. He bumped his snout against the gate. Click, clack, squeak! The gate swung open wide. Pip did a happy little dance, shaking his little pink ears. He set off down the grassy path to find the biggest, squishiest mud puddle on the entire farm.

Along the way, Pip met his good friend Barnaby the brown horse. Barnaby neighed a friendly hello. "Good morning, Pip! Where are you running off to so fast?" Pip gave a cheerful squeal and said, "Oink, oink! I am going to find the best mud puddle for a grand morning splash!" Barnaby shook his long mane and smiled. "Have fun, little Pip!" 

Pip kept on trotting, his little hooves going tip-tap, tip-tap on the dirt. Soon, he smelled something wonderful. Sniff, sniff, sniff went Pip's cute pink snout. Ah, it was rich, damp earth! Pip rounded the big red barn and there, right in the middle of the yard, was the most magnificent puddle of mud he had ever seen. It was wide, it was dark, and it was wonderfully deep.

Pip could not wait another second. He ran right up to the edge and jumped in with a gigantic SPLAT! Mud flew up into the air and landed gently on his ears. Pip giggled and rolled from side to side. He kicked his little legs in the air and made funny splish-splash noises. Squelch, squelch, squelch went the mud beneath his tummy. He made funny mud boots on his hooves and painted little brown polka dots on his snout.

Just then, Farmer Meg walked by carrying a bucket of fresh apples. She saw Pip covered from head to toe in brown mud and laughed a warm, booming laugh. "Well hello there, muddy Pip! You look like you are having the best time ever." Pip gave a happy little grunt and bobbed his muddy head. 

After a long time of splashing and playing, Pip's tummy began to rumble. Grumbly-rumble went Pip's tummy. It was time for lunch! Pip climbed out of the puddle, leaving a trail of happy little mud footprints all the way back to his pen. He munched on sweet, crunchy apples and drank cool water. Pip curled up in the clean straw for a lovely afternoon nap, dreaming of all the wonderful muddy adventures he would have again tomorrow.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Red Balloon
stories.text:
Penny was a very sweet little pig who loved shiny, bright things. Today was a very special day because Farmer Joe gave Penny a big, beautiful red balloon. It was round like a tomato and danced happily in the gentle afternoon breeze. Penny held the white string tightly in her hoof and skipped around the farmyard, feeling like the happiest pig in the world.

Penny showed her bright red balloon to all her animal friends. First, she trotted over to Bessie the cow. Bessie mooed softly and blinked her long eyelashes. "My, what a lovely red balloon, Penny!" Next, Penny showed Claude the rooster. Claude puffed out his feathers and crowed, "Cock-a-doodle-doo, that balloon is as red as my comb!" Penny beamed with pride and did a little happy twirl, holding her balloon up high.

Suddenly, a strong gust of wind came swooping across the farm. Whoosh! The wind blew through the apple trees and rustled the green leaves. Oh no! The wind was just too strong for Penny's little hoof. Before she could grab the string tightly, the red balloon slipped right out of her grasp. "Oink!" cried Penny in surprise.

Up, up, up into the bright blue sky went the red balloon. It danced past the fluffy white clouds and sailed higher than the tallest red barn. Penny watched sadly as her precious balloon got smaller and smaller. Two big tears welled up in her big brown eyes. She felt like sitting right down in the grass and crying.

Just then, her clever friend Ollie the owl swooped down from a wooden branch. "Do not cry, little Penny!" hooted Ollie kindly. "I can help you find your balloon. Just follow me!" Ollie fluttered his wings and flew slowly toward the edge of the farm, keeping his big round eyes fixed on the sky.

Penny forgot all about her tears. She scampered as fast as her little hooves could carry her, following Ollie through the pumpkin patch and past the tall green cornstalks. She looked up and searched the sky with all her might. 

Suddenly, Ollie pointed a wing toward a large, leafy apple tree. "Look there, Penny!" he called out. Penny trotted right up to the tree and gasped with joy. There, caught gently in the low-hanging branches, was her bright red balloon! It was safe and sound, not popped at all.

Penny stood on her tiptoes, stretched her little front legs as far as they could go, and grabbed the white string securely. She hugged the balloon tightly against her pink tummy. "Thank you so much, Ollie!" she oinked happily. Penny walked all the way home with her red balloon safely tied to her wrist, smiling from ear to ear.

stories.title: Percy Pig's Sweet Strawberry Surprise
stories.text:
Once upon a warm summer morning, a little pig named Percy woke up feeling extra hungry. Percy was a plump little pig with a curly tail and a very big appetite. He rubbed his tummy and decided it was time to find a delicious morning treat. He decided to visit the sunny patch behind the garden where the sweetest red strawberries grew.

Percy trotted out of his cozy pen, his little hooves going patter-patter on the soft dirt. The sun was shining brightly in the sky, and little yellow butterflies fluttered through the warm air. Percy sniffed the sweet breeze. He could smell something fruity and wonderful. He hurried his steps, eager to reach the strawberry patch before anyone else did.

When Percy arrived at the garden, his jaw dropped in amazement. The strawberry patch was full of big, bright red strawberries hiding under green leaves. They looked juicy and ready to eat. Percy let out a joyful squeal and dove right in. He plucked a big, ripe strawberry with his teeth and chewed it happily. Mmm! It was sweet and juicy, bursting with delicious flavor.

Percy ate one strawberry, then two strawberries, then three! His pink snout became stained a lovely shade of pink. He thought he was the luckiest pig in the whole wide world. But just as he reached for a particularly large strawberry hiding under a leaf, he heard a tiny voice whisper, "Hello there! Can I have a strawberry too?"

Percy blinked in surprise and looked down near his front hoof. Sitting in the grass was a tiny green frog with big blinking eyes. It was Barnaby the frog. Barnaby looked very small next to big Percy, but he had a very friendly smile on his green face.

Percy was a very kind little pig who loved to share his treats. He smiled back at the frog and gave a friendly oink. Percy used his hoof to gently push the biggest, juiciest strawberry right toward his tiny green friend. Barnaby's eyes lit up with joy. The little frog hopped onto the strawberry and took a happy little bite.

Percy and his new friend spent the rest of the morning eating strawberries together side by side. Percy ate the big ones, and Barnaby ate the small ones, and they both had sticky pink faces. When their tummies were completely full, Percy patted his round belly and gave a contented sigh. He waddled back home to his pen with a happy heart, already looking forward to his next sweet farm adventure.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, there lived a little pink piglet named Pip. Pip had two floppy ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. More than anything else in the whole wide world, Pip loved mud. He loved squishy mud, squelchy mud, cool mud, and warm mud. Every single morning, Pip would wake up and say, 'Oint! Oint! Time for a mud adventure!' Today, the sun was shining bright and yellow in the sky. The birds were singing sweet little songs in the trees. Pip trotted out of his cozy barn, his little hooves going clippity-clop, clippity-clop on the soft green grass. He sniffed the air. He smelled flowers, he smelled fresh hay, and best of all, he smelled wet earth. He followed his little pink snout over the hill, past the big red tractor, and right down to the edge of the farmyard. There it was! The biggest, most glorious puddle of mud Pip had ever seen. It was shining and shimmering in the sunlight. Pip let out a happy squeal. 'Wheeeee!' he shouted, running as fast as his short little legs could carry him. SPLASH! Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle. Mud flew up into the air like brown fireworks. It splashed on his left ear. It splashed on his right ear. It even landed right on the tip of his wiggly snout. Pip giggled and blew bubbles in the mud. 'Bloop, bloop, bloop,' went the bubbles. Soon, Pip was covered in mud from his head all the way down to his little curly tail. He looked like a big walking chocolate drop. Then, along came his best friend, Barnaby the duck. Barnaby waddled over, flapping his yellow wings. 'Quack, quack, Pip! Can I play in the mud too?' asked Barnaby. Pip smiled a big piggy smile. 'Oink, yes! Come on in!' Barnaby jumped into the puddle with a loud SPLISH-SPLASH! Together, Pip and Barnaby splashed and danced and sang silly songs all morning long. They made mud pies and mud boats. When the sun began to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange, Mama Pig called out, 'Time for bed, little piglet!' Pip waddled out of the puddle, shaking off the extra water. He was tired, he was happy, and he was wonderfully muddy. He gave Barnaby a big hug goodnight and trotted back to the barn. As Pip curled up in his soft straw bed, he closed his eyes and smiled. He could still feel the warm, squishy mud between his toes. Goodnight, Pip.

stories.title: Penny's Shiny Red Apple
stories.text: Deep in the green and leafy orchard, a happy little pig named Penny was taking a sunny afternoon stroll. Penny wore a tiny blue bow behind her left ear, which bobbed up and down every time she took a step. Her hooves went pit-pat, pit-pat on the soft earth. Today was a very special day because all the delicious fruit on the trees was ripe and ready to pick. Penny loved fruit, but her absolute favorite food in the whole wide world was crunchy, sweet red apples. She walked past the tall pear trees and the buzzing beehives until she stopped right in front of the biggest apple tree in the whole orchard. It was the Grand-Daddy Apple Tree, loaded with bright red fruit that glowed like little rubies in the sunlight. Penny tilted her head back and looked way, way up. High up on the lowest branch hung one exceptionally large, shiny red apple. It looked so juicy and sweet that Penny’s mouth began to water immediately. 'Oink-oink,' whispered Penny, 'I must have that apple.' But there was a tiny problem. The apple was hanging just a little bit too high for a short little pig. Penny stood up on her back hooves and stretched her front legs as high as they could possibly go. She reached and she stretched, but her nose only brushed the bottom of a green leaf. She tried jumping. 'Boing!' went Penny. But she still missed the apple by a mile. Penny didn't give up. She remembered what her papa always said: 'If at first you don't succeed, try a different way, little pig!' So Penny decided to use her big, strong snout to give the tree trunk a gentle nudge. She put her nose right against the rough bark and pushed. One, two, three, push! The tree trunk wobbled just a tiny bit. The leaves rustled, whispering a soft shhh-shhh sound. Then, with a happy little wobble, the giant red apple let go of its branch. Thump! It landed right on the soft grass in front of Penny’s hooves. Penny squealed with pure joy. She picked up the shiny apple in her teeth and carried it over to a shady spot beneath a big oak tree. She took a big, crunchy bite. 'CRUNCH!' went the apple. Sweet, delicious apple juice filled her mouth. It was the most wonderful apple Penny had ever tasted in her entire life. She chewed happily, her tail giving a little happy wag. When she finished every last bite, she licked her snout, curled up in the cool grass, and took a lovely afternoon nap with a full tummy and a very happy heart.

stories.title: Porky's Playful Balloon
stories.text: Once upon a sunny Tuesday, a cheerful little pig named Porky received a wonderful surprise at the village fair. It was a big, bright, shiny yellow balloon tied to a long piece of sparkly green string. The balloon was so round and happy that it looked just like a second sun floating right beside Porky. Porky held onto the green string very tightly with his trotter. He walked carefully down the carnival lane, making sure his balloon didn't bump into anything sharp. 'Look at my balloon!' Porky squealed happily to everyone he passed. The little lambs bleated in delight, and the fuzzy brown bunnies hopped along beside him to get a better look at the floating wonder. The wind began to blow gently, whispering through the trees. 'Whoosh, whoosh,' went the wind. Suddenly, a stronger gust of wind came dancing down the lane. It caught the big yellow balloon and pulled it upward. 'Oh, no!' gasped Porky, his eyes growing wide. The balloon wanted to fly up into the blue sky to play with the white fluffy clouds. The string slipped just a little bit through Porky's hoof. He squeezed his eyes shut and held on with all his might. He didn't want to let go of his special balloon. But wait! Porky was very light, and the balloon was very full of floating air. Slowly, ever so slowly, Porky’s little hooves lifted right off the ground. He was floating! Porky opened his eyes and looked down. The grass was getting smaller. The fence posts looked like tiny wooden blocks. Porky wasn't scared at all; instead, he giggled a high, piggy giggle. 'Wheeeee! I am flying like a bird!' he shouted. He sailed over the duck pond, waving hello to the swimming ducks who quashed in surprise. He sailed past the church steeple and nodded to a sleepy brown owl taking a nap on a branch. The wind carried him gently in a big, joyful circle all around the farmyard. All the farm animals stopped what they were doing and looked up, cheering for the flying pig. Finally, the wind grew tired and gently lowered Porky right back down into a soft pile of fragrant hay. Landing with a gentle 'thud,' Porky let go of the string and watched the balloon dance up into the sky to say hello to the sun. Porky brushed the hay off his snout and smiled a huge, proud smile. It was the most exciting adventure a little pig could ever dream of having.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text: Once upon a very sunny morning, a little pink pig named Pip woke up with a big stretch and a happy squeak. Oink, oink! Pip loved mornings because mornings meant adventure. Pip trotted out of his cozy straw barn and looked all around the farmyard. The sun was warm, the sky was bright blue, and a gentle breeze rustled the green leaves on the tall oak trees. But Pip was not looking at the sky. Pip was looking at the ground. Right in the middle of the path was a big, round, squishy puddle of mud! It was leftover from the rainstorm the night before, and it looked like the most wonderful place in the whole wide world. Pip let out a joyful squeal and did a little happy dance with his tiny trotters. He trotted over to the edge of the puddle and dipped one small hoof right into the brown, gooey water. Squish! It felt cool and tickly. Pip smiled a wide piggie smile. Without another second of waiting, Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle with a loud SPLASH! Mud flew up into the air and landed on his pink snout. Pip giggled and shook his curly little tail. He sat down in the mud and rubbed his tummy, making big mud angels just like children make snow angels. 'This is the best day ever!' thought Pip. Soon, his best friend Barnaby the bunny came hopping down the path. Barnaby stopped and looked at Pip, his long ears twitching with surprise. 'Hello, Pip! Why are you so muddy?' asked Barnaby, tilting his head. Pip smiled proudly and said, 'Because mud is the most fun thing to play in! Want to join me?' Barnaby looked at his own clean white paws, then looked at the big, messy puddle. He shook his head. 'No thank you, Pip. I like to stay dry. But I will watch you play!' Barnaby cheered from the dry grass. Pip splashed and played all morning long. He blew bubbles in the mud and pretended he was a giant ship sailing on a chocolate sea. By lunchtime, Pip was covered in mud from his snout to the tip of his curly tail. When Farmer John called out, 'Time for lunch, little pig!' Pip scampered out of the puddle, leaving a trail of happy little muddy footprints behind him. He munched on sweet apples and crunchy carrots, feeling warm, tired, and wonderfully happy. As the sun began to set, Pip curled up in his clean straw bed. He closed his heavy eyes and dreamed of even bigger, squishier mud puddles for tomorrow.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Red Balloon
stories.text: Penny was a very cheerful little pig who loved shiny, bright things. Today, Farmer Meg had given Penny a wonderful surprise: a big, round, bright red balloon! The balloon bobbed up and down in the air, tied securely to Penny’s tiny pink hoof with a long piece of yellow string. Penny felt like she was the luckiest pig on the whole farm. She trotted around the farmyard, showing her special balloon to all her animal friends. 'Look what I have!' Penny oinked happily to Bessie the cow. Bessie mooed and blinked her big brown eyes. Penny oinked to Doodle the rooster, who fluffed his feathers and crowed a cheerful good morning. Penny was having the best time marching through the grass, watching her red balloon dance in the gentle breeze. But then, something unexpected happened. A sudden gust of wind blew across the farmyard, whoosh! The wind caught the big red balloon and pulled it right out of Penny's grasp. 'Oh no!' cried Penny, watching as the balloon floated higher and higher into the bright blue sky. It drifted past the roof of the red barn, past the tall oak tree, and up toward the fluffy white clouds. Penny's lower lip quivered, and a little tear came to her eye. She did not want to lose her favorite red balloon. Just then, her clever friend Oliver the owl swooped down from a branch. 'Do not worry, Penny!' hooted Oliver wisely. 'I have very good eyes. Let us follow it!' Penny wiped her tear and started to trot as fast as her little legs could carry her, keeping her eyes fixed on the floating red dot in the sky. Oliver flew ahead, guiding her through the apple orchard and past the duck pond. The balloon began to float lower and lower as it lost some of its air. Finally, it gently landed right in the middle of a leafy green patch of clover near the vegetable garden. Penny hurried over as fast as she could and scooped up her balloon. It was a little bit soft now, but it was still bright red and still very special. Penny hugged the balloon tightly and gave Oliver a grateful oink. 'Thank you, Oliver!' she cheered. Penny walked all the way back to her barn, holding the string tighter than ever before, knowing that adventures are always better when you have good friends to help you out.

stories.title: Percy's Picnic Surprise
stories.text: It was a gorgeous Saturday afternoon, and Percy the pig had a very important job to do.
