Today, Percy was hosting a grand picnic for all his best farmyard friends down by the bubbling brook. Percy had been preparing all morning long. He had packed his favorite red-and-white checkered basket with delicious treats that every pig and animal would love. Inside the basket, there were crisp red apples, sweet yellow bananas, crunchy green celery sticks, and three jars of the most scrumptious strawberry jam you ever did see. Percy put on his favorite blue straw hat to keep the warm sun out of his eyes, grabbed the handle of the basket in his mouth, and began his cheerful journey across the green meadow. Step by step, Percy trotted along the winding dirt path, humming a happy little tune. Oink, oink, tra-la-la! As he walked, the delicious smell of the food made his tummy rumble hungrily. 'I hope my friends are as hungry as I am,' Percy thought to himself with a wide smile. Soon, he reached the shady spot under the giant willow tree by the water. He carefully set his basket down on the soft green grass and laid out a large, clean picnic blanket. One by one, his friends began to arrive. Bella the duck waddled over with a quack, bringing fresh watercress from the stream. Sammy the sheep bounded in with a joyful baa, carrying a bunch of sweet clover. And little timid Timmy the mouse scurried up with a single, perfect blackberry. 'Welcome, everyone!' Percy oinked hospitably, gesturing to the lovely spread. They all sat down in a circle and began to share the wonderful food. They laughed and chatted as the cool water rushed gently over the smooth stones in the brook. Just as they were finishing their meal, a gentle breeze blew through the willow branches, causing a shower of soft green leaves to flutter down onto the blanket. 'What a lovely surprise!' squealed Bella, dancing a little web-footed jig. Percy looked around at his wonderful friends, his full tummy, and the peaceful, sunny surroundings. He realized that the best part of a picnic isn't just the yummy food, but sharing it with the people you care about most. As the afternoon sun began to dip low in the sky, painting the clouds in shades of pink and gold, Percy and his friends packed up the basket together. They said their warm goodbyes and promised to have another wonderful picnic very soon. Percy trotted back home to his barn, feeling warm, happy, and ready for a very cozy night's sleep.

stories.title: Pip's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a very happy little pig named Pip. Pip had two floppy pink ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. More than anything in the whole wide world, Pip loved mud. He loved squishy mud, squelchy mud, cool mud, and warm mud. Every single morning, Pip would wake up and say, 'Oink, oink! Time for a mud bath!' One sunny Tuesday, Pip trotted out of his cozy barn to find his favorite mud puddle. But oh no! The sun was very hot, and the puddle had dried up. It was just dusty, crusty dirt. Pip let out a sad little sigh. 'Oink,' he whimpered. Without his mud, how could he slide? How could he splash? Just then, his good friend Duck waddled by. 'Quack, quack, Pip! Why the long snout?' asked Duck. 'My puddle is gone!' said Pip. Duck smiled a big ducky smile. 'Follow me!' Duck led Pip all the way to the big shiny water pump by the garden gate. Pip pushed the handle down with his heavy trotter. Squeak, squeak, pump, pump! Splash! Cool, clear water gushed out onto the dry dirt. Pip stomped his feet. Thud, thud, thud! He wiggled his bottom. Shake, shake, shake! Slowly, the dry dirt turned into thick, wonderful, squishy mud. Pip giggled a happy piggy giggle. He dropped right down onto his tummy and went wheeeee! He slid from one side to the other. He made big mud bubbles with his snout. Pop, pop, pop! Duck flapped his wings and cheered. 'Hooray for Pip!' Soon, Piggy's other farm friends came over. Cow came to watch, and Sheep came to say hello. They all laughed as Pip splashed water droplets high into the air. Pip was the luckiest, muddiest pig on the whole farm. When the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Mama Pig called out, 'Time for bed, little pig!' Pip stepped out of his wonderful puddle, sparkling clean from the evening dew. He gave Duck a big muddy hug—well, almost!—and trotted back to his warm straw bed. As Pip closed his eyes to dream of tomorrow's games, he curled his little tail and gave one last happy, sleepy 'Oink.' Goodnight, Pip.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Bright Red Boots
stories.text: Deep in the rolling green hills of Apple Tree Farm, there lived a little piglet named Penny. Penny was full of curiosity and loved to explore. One rainy morning, Farmer John left a special package right outside Penny's pen. Penny trotted over, her little hooves click-clacking on the wooden floor. She gave the brown box a gentle nudge with her pink snout. Sniff, sniff, sniff! Inside the box were the most wonderful things Penny had ever seen. They were a pair of shiny, bright red rain boots! They were just the right size for her four little trotters. Penny slipped her left foot in. Squish! She slipped her right foot in. Squelch! Oh, how she loved them. They were as red as a ripe strawberry and squeaked with every single step. Squeak, squeak, went the left boot. Squeak, squeak, went the right boot. Penny could not wait to show her friends. She trotted out into the farmyard just as the rain began to fall plip, plop, plip, plop. First, she met Barnaby the Horse. Barnaby whinnied softly. 'My, what lovely red boots you have, Penny!' Penny danced a little jig. Squeak, squeak! Next, she saw Woolly Sheep munching on clover. Woolly blinked his big brown eyes and smiled. 'Those boots look ready for a puddle walk!' he bleated. Penny nodded her snout eagerly. She walked over to the biggest, splashingest puddle by the old oak tree. Penny looked down at her bright red boots. Then, she jumped right into the middle of the water! Splash! Muddy water flew everywhere, sparkling in the grey light. Penny laughed a bubbly pig laugh. 'Oink-oink-wheeeee!' She splashed again. Splash, splash, splash! Her red boots kept her toes warm and dry. She stomped through the shallow streams and danced around the big stones. Every animal on the farm came to watch Penny's rainy day parade. Even the little brown birds in the tree chirped a happy tune. When the rain finally stopped and the golden sun peeked out from behind the clouds, Penny's boots were covered in happy mud splatters. She trotted back home, tired and wonderfully happy. She kicked off her boots by the barn door, curled up in her soft hay, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of red boots and endless puddles.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Apple Tree
stories.text: Barnaby was a very cheerful pig with a round belly and a bright yellow hat. He lived near the edge of a great big orchard where the sweetest apples in the world grew. Every autumn, the apple trees became heavy with fruit that was crisp, red, and delicious. Barnaby's absolute favorite thing in the whole world was apple crunch day. On this special morning, Barnaby woke up bright and early. He stretched his legs, gave his curly tail a happy twitch, and grabbed his trusty wooden basket. 'Today is the day!' he squeaked excitedly. He trotted down the dirt path until he reached the biggest apple tree in the orchard. The branches reached high up into the blue sky, dotted with bright red globes. But there was a little problem. The best apples were hanging on the very highest branches, far out of Barnaby's reach. He stood on his tiptoes and stretched his neck as high as it could go. He reached with his left trotter, then his right trotter. He even jumped up into the air. Boing! But he could not quite reach the lowest high apple. Barnaby scratched his head and said, 'Hmm, what is a hungry pig to do?' Just then, Sammy Squirrel scampered down the trunk of the tree, holding a tiny acorn. 'Need some help, Barnaby?' chattered Sammy. 'Oh, yes please!' said the pig. Sammy scampered back up the bark as fast as lightning. He scurried out onto the highest branch and began to wiggle it gently. Shake, shake, shake! Suddenly, the tree began to rain red apples. Thump, thump, thump! They bounced softly on the green grass all around Barnaby. The little pig's eyes went wide with joy. He scooped up a big, shiny apple and took a giant bite. Crunch! Sweet, juicy apple flavor filled his mouth. 'Yummy in my tummy!' oinked Barnaby. He filled his basket to the very brim with apples of all shapes and sizes. Then, he shared them with Sammy Squirrel, Cow, and all his other barnyard friends. They sat together under the leafy green shade, munching and crunching away. When the sun began to dip low, painting the sky with streaks of purple and gold, Barnaby patted his full tummy. He rolled back to his cozy pen, happy, tired, and ready for sweet dreams of crunchy apples.

stories.title: Pip's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a very happy little pig named Pip. Pip had two floppy pink ears, a curly little tail that went boing, and a shiny wet snout. Pip loved one thing more than anything else in the whole wide world. Do you know what it was? Mud! Pip loved squishy, squashy, warm, brown mud.

One sunny morning, Pip woke up and stretched his legs. Oink, oink! he said. He trotted out of his cozy straw barn and looked around. The sun was shining, the birds were singing, and it was time for fun. Pip scampered over to his favorite spot by the big old oak tree. But oh no! The mud puddle was completely empty. It was dry, cracked, and dusty. There was not one single drop of sloppy mud to be found.

Pip wrinkled his pink snout and gave a sad little sigh. Oink... he whispered. How could he have his morning wiggle without a proper puddle? Just then, his good friend Barnaby the duck waddled by. Quack, quack, Pip! Barnaby said, flapping his wings. Why look so glum? Pip pointed his hoof at the dry dirt. No mud, he grunted. Barnaby smiled and said, Follow me! Pip followed Barnaby all the way to the big red water pump near the vegetable garden. Barnaby grabbed the handle with his beak and pushed down with all his might. Squeak, squeak, went the pump. Splash! A cool stream of water gushed out onto the dry earth.

Pip jumped up and down with glee. He ran right into the flowing water and began to dig his hooves into the dirt. Dig, dig, dig! Splash, splash, splash! Soon, the dry ground turned into the most wonderful, thick, gooey mud puddle ever. Pip did a happy little spin and belly-flopped right into the middle of it. Splat! Mud flew up into the air and landed right on his nose. Pip giggled and rolled from side to side. He kicked his little legs in the air and blew big muddy bubbles. Blub, blub, oink! Barnaby splashed in the water next to him, quacking happily. Pip was the luckiest pig on the farm. By the time the sun began to set, Pip was covered in mud from his snout to his curly tail. He trotted back to the barn, tired, clean on the inside, and wonderfully dirty on the outside, ready for sweet dreams of mud.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Balloon
stories.text:
Deep in the rolling green hills of Daisy Farm lived a cheerful little pig named Penny. Penny wore a bright yellow polka-dot ribbon right between her floppy ears. Today was a very special day because it was Penny’s third birthday. To celebrate, Farmer John gave her a big, shiny, red balloon that danced in the breeze on a long white string.

Penny loved her balloon more than muddy puddles and apple slices combined. She held the string tightly in her trotter and skipped down the farm path. Oink, oink, hooray! she sang to herself. She showed her balloon to Clover the cow, who gave a friendly moo. She showed it to Woolly the sheep, who gave a happy baa. Penny felt like the happiest birthday pig in the whole wide world.

Suddenly, a mischievous gust of wind swept across the farm. Wooosh! The wind tugged playfully at the string. Penny held on with all her might, but her trotter was a little bit slippery from eating a sticky strawberry. Oh no! she gasped. The string slipped right out of her grasp. Up, up, and away went the bright red balloon. It floated high into the bright blue sky, past the wooden fence, past the red barn roof, and higher still toward the fluffy white clouds.

Penny squeezed her eyes shut and let out a loud, heartbroken oink. Her special birthday balloon was gone! But Penny was a brave little pig. She opened her eyes and started to trot as fast as her little legs could carry her, chasing the shadow of the balloon on the ground. Wait for me! she called out. She ran past the haystacks and through the pumpkin patch. Just when Penny thought she would never catch it, the wind gently changed direction. The red balloon drifted lower and lower, floating right toward the branches of the apple tree.

Plop! The string tangled softly in the green leaves, right within reach. Penny leaped up and grabbed the string with her teeth. She pulled it down and gave a joyful squeal. She had her balloon back! Penny hugged the red sphere safely against her chest and trotted home, knowing it was the best birthday ever.

stories.title: Percy's Picnic Surprise
stories.text:
Percy was a plump little pig with a very big tummy and an even bigger appetite. It was a lovely afternoon, and Percy decided it was the perfect time for a picnic in the orchard. He packed his red-and-white checkered basket with all his favorite treats: three shiny green apples, two crunchy carrots, and a giant wedge of yellow cheese.

Perey trotted happily through the tall grass, his little hooves making a soft patter sound. Squish, squash, step, step. He found a lovely spot beneath the shade of an apple tree and spread out his picnic blanket. Oink, oink, time to eat! Percy said, rubbing his tummy with excitement. He opened the basket and took out a crunchy carrot. He took one big bite. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Delicious.

Just as Percy reached for a green apple, he heard a rustling sound in the bushes nearby. Rustle, rustle, squeak. Percy stopped chewing and perked up his ears. Out popped a little brown bunny with a twitchy nose. The bunny looked at the carrots, and then looked at Percy with big, sad eyes. Sniff, sniff went the bunny. Percy had a kind heart. Even though he was very hungry, he knew it is always nice to share with a friend.

Hello, little bunny, Percy grunted kindly. Would you like to share my picnic? The bunny did a happy little hop and wiggled his fluffy tail. Percy pushed one of the crunchy carrots and a green apple toward the bunny. They sat side by side on the grass, munching happily together. Crunch, crunch, crunch went Percy. Nibble, nibble, nibble went the bunny. When they finished all the food, Percy’s tummy was full and warm.

The bunny did a little backflip to say thank you, which made Percy giggle until his curly tail wagged. They played hide-and-seek behind the apple trees until the sun began to turn golden orange. Percy packed up his empty basket and strolled back to his barn, feeling warm inside. Sharing his picnic made him happier than eating alone ever could, and he couldn't wait for his next adventure with his new furry friend.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, there lived a little pink pig named Pip. Pip had two floppy ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. More than anything else in the whole wide world, Pip loved mud. Big mud, small mud, thick mud, and thin mud! Every single morning, Pip would wake up and trot out of his warm barn. 'Oink, oink!' he would squeal with absolute joy. Today was a extra special day because it had rained all night long. The farmyard was full of glorious puddles. Pip could smell the sweet, wet earth from far away. He trotted as fast as his little trotters could carry him. 'Squish, squash, squish, squash,' went his feet on the wet path. He stopped right at the edge of the biggest, brownest puddle on the entire farm. It looked like a chocolate swimming pool just for him! Pip did not wait even one second. He jumped right into the middle with a giant splash! Mud flew up into the air and landed on his nose. 'Splish, splash, oink, oink!' laughed Pip. He wiggled his bottom and rolled over onto his back. He made mud angels with his little hooves. A little yellow duck waddled by and quacked, 'Hello, Pip! You are very muddy!' Pip smiled and snorted, 'Mud is the best thing to wear!' Soon, Farmer brown came walking down the lane with a bucket of yummy food. He saw Pip covered from head to toe in thick, brown mud. Farmer Brown chuckled and scratched Pip right behind his floppy ears. 'Well, look at you, my happy little piggy,' the farmer said with a warm smile. Pip grunted happily and rubbed his muddy cheek against Farmer Brown's boot. After a long time of playing and splashing, the sun came out to dry the farm. Pip felt sleepy and warm. He waddled back to his cozy straw bed in the barn, curled up tight like a little furry cinnamon roll, and dreamed of even more puddles for tomorrow. Goodnight, Pip!

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Red Balloon
stories.text: Penny was a very cheerful little pig who loved bright, shiny things. Today, her mommy gave her a big, beautiful red balloon. It was round like an apple and floated right up in the air. Penny held the string very tightly in her hoof. 'Whee!' she squealed, skipping down the sunny farm path. She showed her balloon to her friend, Barnaby the bull. 'Look at my red balloon!' she said proudly. Barnaby nodded and munched on some green grass. Penny skipped past the old red tractor and past the big hay bale. The sun was warm, and a gentle breeze was blowing through the trees. Suddenly, a big puff of wind came zooming by. 'Whoosh!' went the wind. It pulled the string right out of Penny's hoof! 'Oh no!' cried Penny. The red balloon went higher and higher into the blue sky. It looked like a tiny floating strawberry way up in the clouds. Penny did not want to lose her lovely balloon. She decided to chase it. She trotted across the green meadow, shouting, 'Come back, red balloon!' The balloon floated over the apple tree. Penny stopped and jumped up as high as she could, but her hooves stayed on the ground. She was too short to reach it. Just then, Sammy the squirrel scampered down the trunk of the apple tree. 'Do you need help, Penny?' asked Sammy with a chatter. 'Yes, please!' said the little pig. Sammy was very quick and very clever. He climbed up to the very top branch of the tree. He reached out his little furry paw and grabbed the floating red string just in time! Sammy safely climbed back down and handed the string right back to Penny. Penny hugged her balloon tight. 'Thank you so much, Sammy!' she cheered. She tied the string securely around her wrist this time so it would never fly away again. With a happy heart, Penny skipped all the way home, holding her precious red balloon very close.

stories.title: Percy's Picnic Party
stories.text: Percy the pig loved to eat. He loved crunchy carrots, sweet red apples, and juicy green watermelons. Today, Percy decided to have a big picnic party in the sunny meadow for all his farmyard friends. He packed a large wicker basket with lots of yummy treats. He put in three crunchy carrots, four shiny red apples, and a big round watermelon. Then, Percy put on his favorite blue polka-dot hat and grabbed his basket. 'Time for a picnic!' he snorted happily. He walked down the grassy path until he found a lovely spot under a big, shady oak tree. He spread out a bright red-and-white checkered blanket on the soft green grass. He placed the carrots, apples, and watermelon neatly on the blanket. Soon, his friends began to arrive for the party. Bella the cow came walking over, swishing her tail. Next came Daisy the duck, waddling with a happy 'Quack, quack!' Finally, mischievous little monkey named Max swung down from the oak tree branches. 'Hello, Percy! What a wonderful picnic!' they all said together. Percy smiled a big piggy smile and told everyone to sit down. 'Help yourselves!' he said generously. Bella the cow munched happily on a crunchy carrot. Daisy the duck pecked gently at a sweet red apple slice. Max the monkey clapped his hands and ate a big piece of juicy watermelon. Percy sat right in the middle of his friends, munching on a tasty treat of his own. The sun shone warmly through the leaves of the tree, making little dancing shadows on the picnic blanket. They giggled, shared stories, and ate until their tummies were wonderfully full. When the picnic was finished, they all lay down on the soft grass and looked up at the fluffy white clouds floating in the blue sky. 'Thank you for the best picnic ever, Percy,' whispered his friends. Percy closed his eyes, feeling so loved and happy. It was a truly wonderful day on the farm.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, there lived a little pink pig named Pip. Pip had two floppy ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. Pip loved many things, but his most favorite thing in the whole wide world was mud. Oh, how Pip loved mud! Every single morning, when the sun popped up and said hello, Pip would stretch his little legs, wiggle his snout, and trot outside to find the biggest, squishiest puddle he could possibly see. One sunny Tuesday, Farmer Brown turned on the garden hose to water his giant orange pumpkins. *Sssssssshhhhhh!* went the hose, splashing water all over the soft dirt. Slowly, the dry dirt turned into a dark, gooey, wonderful mud puddle. Pip’s eyes went wide with joy. "Oink, oink!" squealed Pip, and he dashed across the green grass as fast as his little trotters could carry him. *Splash! Splat! Slosh!* Pip jumped right into the middle of the puddle. He rolled to the left, he rolled to the right, and he covered his tummy in thick, cool mud. He made mud boots for his feet and a mud hat for his head. It felt so good! Soon, his friend Barnaby the duck waddled by. "Quack, quack, Pip! That looks like fun," said Barnaby. "Do you want to play a game?" Pip nodded happily. They played hide-and-seek behind the big red barn. Pip tried to hide, but his bright pink tail kept wiggling behind a bale of hay. Barnaby laughed and shouted, "I see you, Pip!" Then, they played tag, running and slipping in the grass until their little legs were tired. When the sun started to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange, Farmer Brown called out, "Time for bed, little pig!" Pip walked back to his warm straw pen. He was dirty, tired, and very, very happy. He closed his eyes, curled his little tail, and dreamed sweet, muddy dreams all through the starry night.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Red Boot
stories.text: Penny was a cheerful little pig who lived on a cozy green farm. Penny loved fashion, and her absolute favorite item of clothing was a shiny pair of bright red rubber boots. Whenever she wore them, she felt like she could leap over the moon! One rainy afternoon, Penny decided to go for a walk to splash in the puddles with her red boots on. *Squeak, squelch, squeak, squelch* went her boots as she walked down the muddy path by the apple orchard. Suddenly, Penny felt something funny. Her right foot felt very light, while her left foot felt very heavy. She stopped and looked down. Oh, no! Her right red boot was completely gone! Penny gasped and looked all around. She looked behind a large green cabbage, she looked under a wheelbarrow, and she even looked up in the apple tree, though pigs certainly do not climb trees. "Oink! Where could my boot be?" wondered Penny. Just then, her friend Sammy the squirrel scampered down the trunk of a big oak tree. Sammy was holding something very strange on his head. It was shiny, bright red, and looked remarkably like a tiny hat. "Hello, Penny!" chirped Sammy. "Is this your funny red acorn basket? I found it by the puddle and thought it made a wonderful hat!" Penny giggled so hard her curly tail bounced up and down. "Oh, Sammy," smiled Penny, "that is not a hat. That is my missing red boot! I need it to keep my trotter dry." Sammy gently took the boot off his head and handed it back to the little pig. Penny slipped her foot right back inside. It was snug and dry. "Thank you, Sammy!" she said cheerfully. Penny danced all the way home, splashing happily in every single puddle, so glad to have her favorite red boots safely back on her feet.

stories.title: Percy's Picnic Surprise
stories.text: Percy was a round, friendly pig with a tummy that loved to rumble. Today was a very special day because Percy was going to have a wonderful picnic under the big shade tree. He packed his red and white checkered basket with the best treats he could find. Inside the basket, there was a sweet, juicy red apple, a crunchy yellow carrot, and a giant jar of sticky, yummy strawberry jam. Percy trotted happily across the meadow, humming a cheerful little pig tune. "Oink-la-la, oink-la-la!" sang Percy. When he reached the shade tree, he spread out his favorite picnic blanket on the soft green grass. He placed his apple in the middle, his carrot on the side, and the jar of strawberry jam right next to him. Just as Percy sat down and licked his lips, a sudden gust of wind blew through the leaves. *Whoosh!* The wind swept across the grass and blew Percy’s checkered blanket up into the air. Oh, dear! The apple rolled away, hiding behind a bush. The crunchy carrot bounced down a little hill. Worst of all, the jar of strawberry jam tipped over, and a little red glob landed right on Percy's nose! Percy crossed his eyes and looked at his nose. He sniffed. It smelled sweet and delicious. From behind the tree, his friends Bella the bunny and Mimi the mouse peeked out and giggled softly. "Surprise, Percy!" they cheered, running over to help him catch the rolling apple and retrieve the bouncing carrot. Percy laughed a big, hearty pig laugh. He wiped the jam off his nose with a leaf and shared his yummy treats with his dear friends. They ate the apple, munched the carrot, and licked the sweet jam until all their tummies were full and happy. It turned out to be the best picnic ever.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text: Once upon a very sunny morning, a little pink pig named Pip woke up with a big wiggle of his curly tail. Oink, oink! Pip loved mornings. Today, the sun was shining bright, and the farmyard was full of wonderful sounds. Cows were mooing, chickens were clucking, and the wind was blowing the green grass this way and that. Pip jumped right out of his cozy straw bed and trotted out into the warm sunshine. He had a very important mission today. He wanted to find the biggest, squishiest, mud puddle on the whole farm! Pip waddled past the big red barn. He said hello to Daisy the cow, who chewed her grass and gave him a gentle moo. Pip didn't stop because he was on a mud hunt! He waddled past the old wooden tractor. He peeked under the white fence. Where, oh where, was the mud? Suddenly, Pip smelled something wonderful. It was damp, earthy, and smelled like pure fun. Sniff, sniff, went Pip's cute little pink snout. He followed the yummy smell around the corner of the garden patch. And there it was! The king of all puddles. It was wide, deep, and beautifully brown. Pip let out a squeal of pure joy. Oink! Hooray! Without waiting even one tiny second, Pip leaped right into the middle of the puddle. Splash! Mud went up, mud went down, and mud went all around. Pip giggled and sat right down in the cool, squishy dirt. He kicked his little trotters in the air, making wonderful splashing sounds. Splish, splash, splosh! He rubbed the mud behind his floppy ears. He painted his tummy with thick, brown mud paint. A little bird landed on a nearby branch and chirped a happy tune, watching Pip have the time of his life. Pip felt so cool and happy. Playing in the mud was the absolute best thing in the whole wide world. After a long time of splashing and playing, Pip's tummy started to rumble. It was time for lunch! Pip climbed out of his glorious puddle, shaking the extra drops from his curly tail. He left a trail of happy muddy footprints all the way back to his pen, dreaming of his next big muddy adventure.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Apple Treat
stories.text: Deep in the orchard, behind the big red barn, lived a friendly little pig named Barnaby. Barnaby was round and pink, and he had two big floppy ears that drooped over his eyes whenever he bent down to sniff the ground. Today, Barnaby had a very special goal. He wanted to find a sweet, crunchy red apple for his afternoon snack. The apple tree stood right in the middle of the grassy yard, its branches heavy with shiny red fruit. Barnaby trotted over to the tree, his little hooves going tap-tap-tap on the soft dirt. He looked up, and up, and up. The apples were hanging high on the branches, far above his head. Oh dear, thought Barnaby. How will I reach them? He tried to stretch his neck as far as it could go. He stood up tall on his back legs. He reached out with his snout. But the apples were still too high! Just then, his friend Bella the bunny hopped by. Hello, Barnaby! she said, twitching her white nose. What are you doing? I want an apple, but they are too high up, Barnaby grunted softly. Bella smiled her big bunny smile. Let me help you! Bella ran over to the tree trunk and gave it a gentle, happy push. Shake, rattle, roll! Suddenly, a big, bright red apple let go of its branch and tumbled down through the leaves. Thump! It landed right on the soft grass right in front of Barnaby's nose. Barnaby gasped with delight. Oink! Thank you so much, Bella! Barnaby nudged the shiny apple with his snout. It rolled a little bit, and then he took a big, happy crunch. *Crunch, munch, crunch!* The apple was sweet, juicy, and wonderfully crisp. Barnaby chewed happily, sharing the very first bite with his kind bunny friend. Eating apples under the warm farm sun was simply wonderful. Barnaby wagged his little curly tail, so happy to have such a sweet treat and such a wonderful friend to share the afternoon with.

stories.title: Penny's Polka Dot Boots
stories.text: Penny was a very cheerful little piglet who lived on a farm with a bright yellow farmhouse. Penny loved fashion, and she loved colors. But more than anything else, Penny loved puddles. Whenever it rained, the farmyard filled up with wonderful pools of water. But Penny had a problem. Her little hooves would get cold when she splashed too long! One rainy morning, the farmer walked over to Penny's pen and smiled. He carried a tiny little box tied with a bright blue ribbon. For you, Penny, the farmer said gently. Penny untied the ribbon with her snout and opened the box. Inside were four tiny, shiny yellow boots with bright blue polka dots! Penny squealed with absolute delight. Oink-oink-hooray! She slipped her little front hooves into the boots, and then her back hooves, too. They fit her perfectly! The yellow boots bounced as she walked, making her feel like the fanciest pig in the whole county. Outside, the rain was still falling with a soft, pitter-patter sound. Perfect weather for a walk! Penny trotted out of her cozy straw house and stepped right into the biggest puddle she could find. Splash, splash, splash went her polka dot boots! The water flew up in tiny, sparkling diamonds. Penny danced a little piglet jig in the mud. Tap-tap-go your little polka dot feet, she sang to herself. The ducks in the pond swam over to watch her wonderful boots. Quack, quack! they seemed to say. They thought Penny looked very stylish indeed. Penny splashed through the puddles for a long, happy time. Her hooves stayed warm, and her boots stayed bright and shiny. When the rain finally stopped and the sun peeked out from behind a fluffy white cloud, Penny trotted back to her pen. She took off her boots and gave them a little wipe. What a wonderful day it had been. Penny curled up in the warm straw for a nap, dreaming of tomorrow's puddle adventures in her favorite polka dot boots.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, there lived a little pink piglet named Pip. Pip had two floppy ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. More than anything else in the whole wide world, Pip loved mud. He loved squishy mud, squelchy mud, and big brown puddles of glorious mud. One sunny morning, Pip trotted out of his cozy barnyard home to find the ultimate mud puddle. 'Oink, oink!' cheered Pip, doing a happy little dance with his tiny trotters. He wiggled his pink nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff. Ah, he smelled something wonderful! Following his nose, Pip trotted past the big red tractor, past the buzzing beehive, and right over to the vegetable patch. There, near the juicy tomato plants, sat the biggest, wettest, most magnificent puddle on the whole farm. It was glistening in the warm sunshine. Pip could hardly contain his excitement. He squealed with pure joy and zoomed straight toward it. Splash! Right into the middle he went. Mud flew up to the left. Mud flew up to the right. A big brown blob landed right on top of Pip’s head like a funny little hat. Pip giggled and blew bubbles in the mud. 'Bloop, bloop, bloop,' went the bubbles. Soon, a curious little duck waddled over. 'Quack, quack!' said the duck, tilting his head. 'Can I play too?' Pip smiled his biggest piglet smile and splashed his foot. 'Oink! Come on in, the mud is lovely!' The duck jumped in, and they splashed together until they were covered from head to toe in thick, gooey mud. Just then, Farmer Farmer called out, 'Time for lunch, little pig!' Pip knew it was time to go, but he promised to come back tomorrow. With a happy sigh, our little muddy pig trotted back to the barn, dreaming of his next big adventure in the wonderful world of mud.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Apple
stories.text: Barnaby was a very polite and cheerful little pig who lived in a green pasture filled with sweet clover and apple trees. Barnaby loved apples more than anything. Red apples, green apples, big apples, small apples—he loved them all. One breezy autumn afternoon, Farmer Meg gave Barnaby a shiny, red, crisp apple as a special treat. 'Thank you, oink, oink!' grunted Barnaby happily. He held the apple very carefully in his trotter and started walking toward his favorite resting spot under the big oak tree. But oh no! Barnaby was so excited that he forgot to watch where he was going. He tripped over a bumpy tree root. 'Whoops-a-daisy!' cried Barnaby. The big red apple slipped right out of his trotter. It rolled, and it rolled, and it rolled away! It rolled past a sleeping sheep. It rolled under a wooden fence. And finally, it plopped right into a patch of tall, green grass. Barnaby blinked his big brown eyes. Where did his yummy apple go? He began to search everywhere. He looked behind a bale of hay. No apple there. He looked inside an empty bucket. No apple there either. Just as Barnaby started to feel a little bit sad, he heard a rustling sound in the tall grass. 'Rustle, rustle, munch, munch.' Barnaby tiptoed closer and parted the tall blades of grass with his snout. Guess what he saw? There was his shiny red apple, and sitting right next to it was his best friend, Bella the bunny. Bella looked up with her nose twitching and said, 'Hello, Barnaby! I found this rolling around. Would you like to share it with me?' Barnaby’s face lit up with a huge smile. 'Oink! Yes, please!' They sat down together in the soft grass and shared the crunchy, sweet apple. Sharing made the apple taste even better than before, and Barnaby learned that losing something isn't so bad when you have a wonderful friend to share the adventure with.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Polka-Dot Boots
stories.text: Penny was a stylish little pig who loved bright colors and fun clothes. Today was a very special day because Farmer Joe gave Penny a brand new pair of shiny yellow rain boots with bright red polka dots all over them. They were the most beautiful boots Penny had ever seen in her entire life. 'Oink, oink, look at me!' squealed Penny, prancing around the farmyard. Click-clack, click-clack went her new boots on the wooden pathway. She showed them to the brown cow, who mooed in approval. She showed them to the fluffy sheep, who bleated a happy hello. Penny felt like the fanciest pig in the whole wide world. But soon, dark gray clouds rolled across the sky. Boom! Went the thunder. Splish, splash! Down came the rain. The farmyard quickly filled with little puddles of water. Other animals ran to hide in the dry barns and cozy stables. But not Penny! Penny smiled a big piggy smile. This was her chance! She didn't need to hide because she had her brand new polka-dot boots. Penny marched right out into the gentle rain. 'Stomp, stomp, stomp!' went her boots in the puddles. Water splashed up, but her feet stayed wonderfully dry and warm inside the yellow boots. She danced in a circle, singing a happy little pig song. 'I am Penny, brave and bold, in my boots of red and gold!' A little yellow bird flew down and sang along with her. Penny splashed and twirled until the rain stopped and a bright, colorful rainbow stretched across the sky. Penny’s boots were muddy, but she had the most fun afternoon ever. She trotted back home, tired and happy, ready to show off her boots again tomorrow.

stories.title: Pip's Big Mud Puddle
stories.text: Once upon a time, there was a little pink pig named Pip. Pip had two floppy ears, a curly-wurly tail, and four little hooves that went click, clack, click on the green grass. Today was a very special day because it had just finished raining. The sun was shining bright, making the grass sparkle like diamonds. Pip loved sunny days after the rain. Do you know why? Because rain means one very important thing for a little pig. Mud! Pip let out a happy little squeal. Oink, oink! He trotted across the yard as fast as his little legs could carry him. He stopped right at the edge of the biggest, squishiest, mud puddle in the whole wide world. The mud was dark, brown, and looked so very inviting. Pip dipped one tiny hoof right into the middle. Squish, squatch, squash! It felt cool and tickly between his toes. Pip giggled and stepped in with his other hoof. Then, with a big plop, he sat right down in the middle of the gooey, wonderful mud. He wiggled his bottom left and right. He splashed his front hooves up and down, sending brown droplets flying into the air. Splash, splash, splish! A little frog hopped by and said ribbit, but Pip was having too much fun to mind. He rolled all the way over onto his back, coating his tummy in thick, warm mud. Now Pip was a mud pie pig from his snout to his tail. Soon, Mama Pig came walking over. She looked at muddy Pip and smiled her big, warm piggie smile. She didn't scold him at all. Instead, Mama Pig stepped right into the puddle beside him and sat down with a giant squish. They were both as muddy as could be. Pip leaned his head against his mama and let out a long, contented sigh. It was the best mud puddle day ever, and Pip was the happiest little pig in the whole farmyard. As the warm afternoon sun began to dry the mud into a cozy coat, Pip closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of even bigger puddles tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Boots
stories.text: Barnaby was a bright-eyed little pig who lived in a cozy red barn with his family. Barnaby had a shiny pink snout and a tail that curled into a perfect little cinnamon roll. One morning, the farmer brought a special package into the barnyard. Inside the package was something wonderful. It was a pair of shiny, bright red rain boots, just the right size for a little pig! Barnaby squealed with delight. Oink, oink, hooray! He immediately wanted to put them on. Getting the boots onto his hooves was quite a funny job. He had to wiggle his left hoof and push. Pop! The first red boot was on. Then he had to wiggle his right hoof and push hard. Pop! The second red boot was on. Barnaby stood up proudly. He looked down at his feet. They were as red as ripe strawberries and gleamed in the morning light. He took a step, and the boots made a loud, funny noise on the wooden barn floor. Squeak, stomp, squeak, stomp! Barnaby marched out into the farmyard to show all his animal friends his fantastic new footwear. First, he met Henrietta the hen. Henrietta blinked her round eyes and clucked, Cluck, cluck! Those are very bright boots, Barnaby! Next, he saw Barnaby's best friend, a fluffy white sheep named Woolly. Woolly baa-ed happily and trotted over to take a closer look. They danced a little silly dance together, going stomp, stomp, squeak on the hay. Just then, a few gentle raindrops began to fall from the fluffy gray clouds above. Perfect! Barnaby didn't need to worry about getting his hooves wet today. He happily stomped through every little puddle he could find, watching the water splash against his shiny red rubber boots. Squeak, splash, squeak, splash! He felt like the grandest pig in the entire kingdom. When it was time to go back inside for a delicious supper of apples and corn, Barnaby carefully wiped his boots clean. He placed them right by the door so they would be ready for his next big adventure tomorrow.

stories.title: Penny's Picnic Basket
stories.text: Little Penny pig loved sunny afternoons above all else. Today, she decided to have a special picnic all by herself under the big, shady apple tree near the garden. Penny put on her favorite yellow straw hat and grabbed a checkered red-and-white picnic basket. What delicious treats should she pack? First, she opened the pantry and found three crisp, juicy red apples that smelled sweet and delicious. She placed them carefully at the bottom of the basket. Next, she found a tall jar of golden, sticky honey and a lovely bunch of green grapes that looked like tiny glass beads. Everything fit inside the basket just like a puzzle. With her basket tucked safely in her trotter, Penny skipped down the grassy path. Tra-la-la, went her happy piggie heart. When she reached the apple tree, she spread her soft blue blanket out on the green grass. She sat down, tucked her legs neatly underneath her, and opened the basket lid. The sweet smell of apples and honey filled the warm breeze. Penny picked up a red apple and took a big, crunchy bite. Crunch, crunch, munch! It was so juicy that a tiny drop of juice landed right on her pink snout. She wiped it away with a quick swipe of her hoof. Then she plucked a sweet green grape and popped it into her mouth. Yum, yum, yum! While she was eating, a little yellow butterfly fluttered down and landed right on the edge of her picnic basket. Penny stayed very still so she wouldn't frighten her tiny visitor. The butterfly opened and closed its delicate wings, as if saying hello to the little pig. Penny smiled and shared a tiny slice of apple, leaving it on the grass nearby for her winged friend. After she finished every single bite, Penny laid back on her soft blanket and looked up through the green leaves of the tree at the fluffy white clouds floating lazily by in the blue sky. Some clouds looked like sheep, and one even looked like a giant flying pig. Penny felt so cozy and full that she let out a gentle yawn. With a warm breeze tickling her ears, she closed her eyes for a wonderful little afternoon nap.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a little pink pig named Pip. Pip loved many things. He loved crunchy green apples, he loved running in the warm sunshine, and most of all, he loved mud! Every single morning, Pip would wake up, stretch his little legs, and say, 'Oink, oink! Today is a wonderful day for a mud splash!' One sunny Tuesday, Pip trotted down the grassy hill to find the biggest, squishiest puddle on the whole farm. His friends, Bella the bunny and Barnaby the duck, were playing nearby. 'Hello, Pip!' chirped Bella. 'Where are you going?' 'I am going to find the best mud!' squealed Pip, his little curly tail wagging back and forth. He skipped happily until he found it. It was a giant, glorious, brown puddle left over from the rain the night before. Pip ran as fast as his little trotters could carry him. Splash, crash, squish, squelch! He jumped right into the middle. Mud went up, mud went down, mud got all over his pink snout. 'Oink-oink-wheee!' laughed Pip, clapping his hooves together. The mud felt cool and tickly on his tummy. Soon, Bella and Barnaby came over to watch. 'Can we play too?' asked Barnaby. 'Of course!' said Pip. Bella tried a little hop, and Barnaby did a happy paddle. Soon, all three friends were making funny mud footprints. Squish, squelch, squish, squelch. Pip showed them how to slide on their bellies like happy little seals. They laughed and played until the sun began to hide behind the big oak tree. 'Time for dinner, little piggies!' called the farmer from across the field. Pip wiggled out of the puddle, shaking off the extra drops. He looked down at himself. He was covered in brown mud from his nose to his toes. He looked just like a chocolate cupcake! Pip trotted back to his warm straw bed, feeling happy, tired, and very clean on the inside. As he closed his eyes to sleep, he dreamed of tomorrow's big, squishy mud puddle. Good night, Pip!

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Barnaby was a very happy little pig who lived in a cozy red barn with a white wooden fence. Today was a very special day because it was Barnaby’s third birthday! To celebrate, Farmer Brown gave him a big, shiny, bright red balloon. It danced up and down in the air, tied to Barnaby’s trotter with a long yellow string. Barnaby thought it was the most wonderful thing in the whole wide world. 'Look at my balloon!' oinked Barnaby to his best friend, Penny the pony. 'It is as red as a strawberry!' Barnaby decided to take his balloon for a walk around the farmyard. He trotted past the hay bales and waved hello to the fluffy yellow chicks. The balloon floated right behind him, bobbing gently in the breeze. Up and down, round and round it went. Barnaby giggled and did a little happy dance. But oh dear! A sudden gust of wind came swooshing through the trees. Whoosh! The wind blew past Barnaby's ears. Before he could grab the string tightly, the balloon slipped right out of his trotter. 'Oink! Oh no!' cried Barnaby. The red balloon drifted up into the sky. It floated past the barn roof, higher than the chimney, higher even than the sleepy old owl in the oak tree. Barnaby watched it go with big, sad eyes. He thought his birthday was ruined. Just then, his wise old mother walked over and gently patted his head. 'Do not worry, little one,' she whispered softly. 'Let us look around the farm together.' Barnaby sniffed and wiped a little tear from his cheek. He walked with his mother toward the apple orchard. And what do you think they found? Stuck in the low branches of an apple tree was a brand new, shiny blue balloon, left behind by the village children! Barnaby’s eyes grew big and bright. He reached up and gently grabbed the string. 'Look, Mama! A blue balloon!' he cheered. It was even more fun than the red one. Barnaby spent the rest of his birthday playing happily under the trees, holding his new blue balloon high in the sky.

stories.title: Penny's Picnic Basket
stories.text: Deep in the sunny meadow, a little polka-dot pig named Penny was getting ready for a grand picnic. Penny loved delicious snacks. She packed her red-and-white checkered basket with three crunchy carrots, two sweet strawberries, and one enormous watermelon slice. 'This is going to be the best picnic ever!' squeaked Penny, her curly tail bouncing with excitement. She picked up her basket handle in her mouth and trotted down the winding path toward the big picnic blanket under the shady apple tree. Along the way, she met Sammy the squirrel. 'Good morning, Penny! What is in your basket?' asked Sammy, twitching his bushy nose. 'Yummy treats for my picnic!' replied Penny proudly. 'Would you like to walk with me?' Sammy squeaked a happy yes, and the two friends skipped down the path together. Soon, they met a fuzzy caterpillar inching along a leaf. 'Hello, Penny!' said the caterpillar. 'Can I come to the picnic too?' 'Of course!' said Penny with a big smile. When they finally reached the shady tree, Penny carefully spread out her soft blanket. She opened the basket and laid out all the food. Sammy nibbled on a carrot, the caterpillar munched on a sweet strawberry leaf, and Penny took a giant, juicy bite of the big watermelon slice. Juice went drip-drop on her pink chin, making her giggle. Just then, a gentle breeze blew a shower of pink apple blossoms down onto the blanket like confetti. It was so magical and pretty. They ate and laughed until their tummies were wonderfully full and happy. When the sun began to turn the sky into a soft pink and orange color, Penny packed up her empty basket. She hugged her friends tightly and whispered, 'Thank you for making my picnic so much fun.' Trotting back home under the twinkling stars, Penny felt like the luckiest little pig in the whole world. She curled up in her cozy bed and fell fast asleep, dreaming of strawberries and sweet sunshine.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Day
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a happy little piglet named Pip. Pip had two floppy pink ears, a curly-wurly tail, and a very wiggly snout. Today was a very special day because it had just finished raining, and that meant one thing: mud puddles! Pip loved mud more than anything in the whole wide world. He trotted out of his cozy barn, making a happy little sound that went, 'Oink, oink, oink!' His tiny hooves went clip-clop, clip-clop on the soft grass as he searched everywhere for the biggest, squishiest puddle he could find. Soon, Pip stopped right at the edge of a giant puddle of thick, brown mud. It looked just like chocolate pudding! Pip smiled from ear to ear. He dipped one front hoof into the cool, wet mud. It squished between his toes. 'Ooh, squishy!' giggled Pip. Then, he dipped his other hoof in. Splash! He stepped all the way into the middle of the puddle. Pip sat right down in the squishy mud and gave a joyful squeal. He rolled to the left. Roll, roll, roll! He rolled to the right. Roll, roll, roll! Soon, Pip was covered in mud from his snout all the way to the tip of his curly tail. He looked like a funny, muddy monster, but he was the happiest pig in the world. Just then, his friends came by. Bella the bunny hopped over and twitched her nose. 'Can I play too, Pip?' she asked. Pip nodded and splashed a little drop of mud. Bella jumped in, and they made funny mud pies together. They patted the mud and pretended to bake cakes for all the farm animals. The sun came out and warmed their backs, making the day even better. When it was time for dinner, Mama Pig called out, 'Time to wash up, little piglet!' Pip gave one last happy wiggle in the mud before hopping out. He trotted back to the barn, feeling cozy and tired from his big adventure. After a quick splash in the water trough, Pip snuggled into his soft straw bed. He closed his eyes and dreamed all about sweet, squishy mud puddles.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Red Balloon
stories.text: Penny was a cheerful little pig with a bright yellow bow tied right between her ears. Today was the village farm fair, and Penny was holding the most wonderful thing in the whole world: a big, shiny, red balloon. The balloon bobbed up and down in the air, pulling gently on the string held tightly in Penny's trotter. 'Hold on tight, little balloon,' Penny whispered with a happy smile. She walked past the tall cornstalks and the buzzing beehives, proudly showing off her balloon to everyone she met. The sheep baaed, the cows mooed, and the ducks quacked in pure delight. But oh no! A sudden gust of wind came blowing through the farm. Whoosh! The wind blew so hard that it tickled Penny's nose. Penny sneezed, 'Achoo!' And just like that, the string slipped right out of her trotter. 'Oh, no! My balloon!' cried Penny. The red balloon floated up into the bright blue sky. It went past the wooden fence, past the green apple tree, and higher than the old red barn. Penny looked up with big, sad eyes. She really, really wanted her balloon back. Just then, Sammy the squirrel scampered down the apple tree. 'Don't worry, Penny! I can help!' chattered Sammy. Sammy was very fast and very good at climbing. He scrambled up the tall oak tree as fast as his little legs could carry him. He reached out his paw, but the balloon was still just a little too high. Then, Benny the bird flew up, carrying the balloon string gently in his beak. With a soft flap of his wings, Benny brought the floating red balloon right back down to the ground. Penny clapped her trotters together and jumped up and down. 'Yay! Thank you so much, my good friends!' she cheered. She tied the string securely around her wrist this time so it would never float away again. Penny, Sammy, and Benny walked together to the fair, sharing sweet strawberry lemonade and celebrating their wonderful, happy day.

stories.title: Porky Pig's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was sinking slowly behind the rolling green hills, painting the evening sky in lovely shades of pink, orange, and soft purple. Down on the quiet farm, it was almost time for sleep. Little Porky Pig was getting very sleepy, indeed. Porky wore his favorite blue pajamas with little white stars printed all over them. He gave a big yawn that went, 'Yawn-o-saurus!' and rubbed his tired eyes with his trotter. But before he could go to sleep in his cozy straw bed, Porky needed to say goodnight to all of his farmyard friends. First, Porky waddled over to the horse stable. 'Goodnight, horsey,' whispered Porky in a soft, gentle voice. The big brown horse neighed softly and lowered its head. Next, Porky trotted quietly past the duck pond. 'Goodnight, little ducks,' he said. The ducks paddled in circles and quacked a sleepy 'Quack, quack,' before tucking their heads under their wings. Porky kept walking slowly, his slippers going scuff, scuff, scuff on the path. He stopped by the sheep pen. 'Goodnight, fluffy sheep,' he murmured. The little lambs bleated softly and snuggled close to their mothers to stay warm in the evening breeze. The sky grew darker, and the first bright stars began to twinkle like tiny diamonds high above the farm. The moon came up, round and glowing like a big silver coin. Porky felt a warm, cozy feeling deep inside his tummy. He turned around and waddled back to his own warm barn. Mama Pig was waiting there with a big, loving hug. She tucked him into his soft bed and pulled the patchwork quilt right up to his chin. 'Sleep tight, my sweet little piglet,' Mama Pig whispered softly, kissing his forehead. Porky closed his eyes, listening to the gentle night sounds of the farm. He took a deep breath in and a slow breath out. With a happy little sigh, Porky drifted off to dreamland, smiling as the stars watched over him all through the night.

stories.title: Pip the Pig's Big Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green field, there lived a little pig named Pip. Pip was a very happy pig with a curly, wiggly tail and a pink, round snout. Every single morning, Pip would wake up with the sunrise, give a big stretch, and say, oink, oink, good morning, world! Today was a very special day because it had rained all night long, which meant one thing: the biggest, squishiest, most wonderful puddle in the whole wide farmyard was waiting just for Pip. Pip trotted out of his cozy barn, his little hooves going tap, tap, tap on the dirt path. He stopped at the edge of the yard and looked ahead. Oh, joy! There it was. A big, brown, bubbly puddle sparkling in the morning sun. Pip could not wait another second. He gave his curly tail an extra wiggle and ran as fast as his little legs could carry him. Splish, splash, squash! Right into the middle of the puddle went Pip. Mud went flying up, up, up into the air, landing gently on his ears. Pip giggled and rolled from side to side. He kicked his legs and made bubbly, squishy noises with his tummy. Oink, oink, shouted Pip, this is the best mud ever! Soon, his barnyard friends came over to see what all the fuss was about. Barnaby the duck waddled up and quacked, hello, Pip! Can I join the fun? Of course, you can, said Pip with a big, muddy smile. So Barnaby splashed his webbed feet, sending water droplets everywhere. Then, Clover the cow walked over, let out a friendly moo, and swished her tail. Even though Clover was too big for the puddle, she loved watching Pip and Barnaby play. They played tag in the mud. Pip would run, and Barnaby would try to catch him, but the mud was so slippery that everyone slid around in silly circles. They laughed until their tummies hurt. After a long time of splashing and playing, the warm sun began to dry the mud on Pip's back, making funny patterns like spots on a cow. Pip was tired, but he was the happiest little pig in the world. He trotted back to the barn to snuggle in the fresh, clean straw for a nice morning nap, dreaming all about his next big, beautiful, muddy adventure.

stories.title: Penny Pig's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Penny Pig loved balloons more than anything else on the farm. Today was Penny's birthday, and the farmer had given her a shiny, bright red balloon tied to a long, yellow string. Penny held the string tightly in her trotter and walked all around the farm to show everyone her wonderful present. First, she visited the sheep. Baa, baa, happy birthday, Penny! said the fuzzy sheep. Look at my red balloon, squealed Penny happily, making the balloon dance up and down in the air. Next, she trotted over to the horse pasture. Neigh, neigh, said the tall brown horse, that is a very pretty balloon, Penny. Penny felt so proud and special. She trotted near the big apple tree, the wind began to blow gently, whispering through the leaves. Whoosh! A sudden gust of wind caught the red balloon. Oh, no! cried Penny. The balloon pulled hard on the string. Penny held on with all her might, but the wind was too strong, and the string slipped right out of her trotter. Up, up, up went the red balloon, floating higher and higher into the blue sky. Penny watched it go, her little snout trembling. She thought she might cry. But then, wise old owl sitting in the tree hooted softly. Do not be sad, little pig, look up! Penny blinked her big brown eyes and looked up. The red balloon was high in the sky, looking like a tiny floating berry, and right beside it was a fluffy white cloud shaped just like a pig! Penny smiled. That is so silly, she giggled. Even though her balloon had floated away into the sky, she still had her birthday, her warm farm, and all of her good friends. She gave a happy little oink and ran off to play games in the soft green grass, waving one last goodbye to her flying red friend.

stories.title: Porky Pig's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was starting to sink low behind the big green hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink, orange, and purple. Down on the farm, the daytime noises were getting quieter and quieter. The chickens had climbed up into the hen house to roost, the horses were resting in their stalls, and little Porky Pig was getting ready for bed. Porky was a sweet little pig with floppy ears and a soft, round tummy. Today had been a very busy day of playing hide and seek in the hay bales and chasing butterflies through the clover patch. Now, Porky felt heavy and sleepy. His little eyelids were drooping, closing down like tiny window shutters. Oink, yawned Porky, rubbing his eyes with a tiny hoof. His mama gave him a warm, gentle nuzzle with her snout. Time for sleep, my sweet little piglet, she whispered softly. Porky wiggled into a cozy pile of fresh, sweet-smelling straw inside the barn. He turned this way, and he turned that way, until he found the most comfortable spot in the whole world. Outside, the crickets began to sing their quiet nighttime song. Creak, chirrup, creak, chirrup. It sounded like a sweet lullaby just for Porky. A bright silver moon peeked through the wooden slats of the barn window, shining a gentle, friendly light right onto Porky's bed. Porky closed his eyes tight. He thought about the bright red apples he would eat for breakfast tomorrow, and the fun games he would play with his friends. With a final, gentle sigh, Porky snuggled deeper into the straw. His tummy rose and fell in a slow, steady rhythm. The farm grew completely still and peaceful under the blanket of stars. Sleep tight, little Porky Pig, whispered the night wind, resting safe and sound until the morning sun would come up to wake him for a brand new day of happy adventures.

rhymes.title: Little Piggy
rhymes.text:
Little pig goes oink, oink, oink,
Jumping high and jumping down.
Little pig wears shiny boots,
Walking all around the town.

He has got a curly tail,
Wiggly snout and pinkest ears.
When he plays outside to run,
He is full of happy cheers.

Mud is squishy, mud is fun,
Splashing in the deep blue pool.
Resting underneath the tree,
When the afternoon is cool.

Now the sun is going down,
Time to sleep and close your eyes.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: Five Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Five little trotters in the hay,
Looking for a game to play.
Found a puddle on the ground,
Made a happy, splashing sound.

Oink goes mama, oink goes babe,
Running through the grassy glade.
Eating apples sweet and red,
Time to rest in cozy bed.

Morning comes with yellow light,
Stars are fading out of sight.
Little pig wakes up to run,
Playing underneath the sun.

Chasing butterflies so free,
Laughing by the willow tree.
Happy piglet, safe and sound,
Happiest piglet all around.

rhymes.title: Pink Piggy Wiggle
rhymes.text:
See the pink pig wiggle and shake,
Eating yummy bits of cake.
Running down the winding lane,
Waiting for the gentle rain.

Ears are floppy, nose is wet,
He is such a lovely pet.
Jumping up and jumping down,
Happiest fellow in the town.

Finds a clover patch so green,
Prettiest sight you've ever seen.
Munches on a crunchy snack,
Carries clover on his back.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little pig is going to sleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your warm and cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Little Oinker
rhymes.text:
Little oinker in the pen,
Wiggles snout and wiggles then,
Jumps right in the muddy floor,
Squeals and asks for splashing more.

Ears flop down and tail goes round,
Makes a happy grunting sound.
Splish and splash and slippery slide,
Sitting by his mother's side.

Now the sun begins to set,
Little pig is clean and wet.
Put on pajamas soft and white,
Time to say a sleepy goodnight.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Dreaming of another day.

rhymes.title: Three Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Three little pigs in a row,
Watch them happily go, go, go!
One wears a hat of blue,
One wears a shiny red shoe.

They dance around the apple tree,
As happy as a pig can be.
They stomp their feet upon the ground,
And make a funny trotting sound.

When the moon is bright and high,
Shining softly in the sky,
They cuddle up in cozy hay,
To rest until the coming day.

Goodnight hats and goodnight shoes,
No time now for waking snooze.

rhymes.title: Pink Piggy Wiggle
rhymes.text:
Pink piggy wiggle your tail so sweet,
Dance around on your little feet.
Jump in the puddle of shiny blue,
Laughing and shouting a happy oink too.

Find a clover green and bright,
Nibble it down with all your might.
Chase a butterfly flying high,
Watching it flutter up in the sky.

When the stars begin to peep,
Little piggy falls asleep.
Snoring softly in the bed,
With a pillow beneath his head.

Dreaming of mud and sunny skies,
Resting now his sleepy eyes.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Piggy
rhymes.text:
Little pink piggy, round and sweet,
Walking down the muddy street.
With a curly tail behind,
Leaving happy tracks to find.

Trotting through the clover green,
Prettiest pig you've ever seen.
Up and down the wooden pen,
Playing hide and seek again.

Sniffing at a yellow flower,
Happy every single hour.
Jumping in a giant puddle,
Giving mom a gentle cuddle.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy straw-filled bed.

rhymes.title: Oink Oink Goes the Pig
rhymes.text:
Oink, oink, oink goes the little pig,
Dancing a jig that is so big.
Stomping feet upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Running fast across the grass,
Watching all the duckies pass.
Shaking ears of softest pink,
Tasting water from the sink.

Eating carrots sweet and red,
Rolling in the garden bed.
Wiggling noses left and right,
 Shining like a starry light.

Time to sleep and dream a dream,
Floating down a sleepy stream.
Hugs and kisses till the morn,
Happy piglet newly born.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Little Pig
rhymes.text:
Splish and splash in muddy gray,
Piggy loves to play all day.
Coated thick from head to toe,
Watch the happy piglet go.

Laughing as the water flies,
Rubbing sleepy little eyes.
Friends are coming down the lane,
Dancing in the summer rain.

Sunshine peeking through the blue,
Showing every shade of hue.
Piggy jumps with all his might,
Feeling oh so full of light.

Now the playtime comes to close,
Washing mud from little toes.
Wrapped up tight in blankets warm,
Safe inside the sleepy farm.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
Little pink pig with a curly tail,
Walking down the dusty trail.
Stopping by the muddy ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Oink, oink, oink goes the little pig,
Jumping in a puddle big.
Splashing water left and right,
Having fun until the night.

Trotting to the cozy barn,
Safe away from any harm.
Eating clover, sweet and green,
Nicer pig you've never seen.

Now it is time to go to sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.

rhymes.title: Three Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Three little trotters step in the mud,
Thump, thump, thump with a little thud.
Pink little snout and floppy ears,
Waving goodbye to all of his fears.

Eating corn from a wooden bowl,
Happy and warm inside his soul.
Wiggle the tail from side to side,
Taking a bumpy tractor ride.

Rolling around in the hay so sweet,
Falling right down on two pink feet.
Snoring softly, deep and low,
Watch the sleepy piggy grow.

Good night, pig, sleep tight tonight,
Wake up with the morning light.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Day
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Little piggy walking by.
Finding water in the street,
Cooling off his tired feet.

Plopping down into the wet,
Bestest game he hasn't met.
Brown all over, head to toe,
Watch the happy piggy go.

Mommy pig calls out his name,
Time to finish up the game.
Off the mud and into bed,
Resting up his sleepy head.

Dreaming of the morning sun,
When the new day has begun.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Piggy
rhymes.text:
Little pink piggy with a curly tail,
Walking down the sunny farmyard trail.
Finding a puddle of squishy mud,
Dropping right down with a happy thud.

Splish and a splash and a rolly-poll,
Having so much fun down in the hole.
Wiggling his ears and shaking his snout,
Nowhere else he would rather be about.

Covered in brown from his head to his toes,
Mud right up to his little pink nose.
Giving a squeal and a happy little grunt,
Searching around for a juicy fruit hunt.

Trotting back home when the day is done,
Dreaming of mud and tomorrow's bright sun.
Climbing right into his warm little bed,
Resting his tired and sleepy pink head.

rhymes.title: Three Little Piggies
rhymes.text:
Three little piggies jump up and down,
Running around in the big farm town.
First little piggy has a yellow hat,
Sitting on the grass with a little rat.

Second little piggy eats a shiny pear,
Throwing green leaves up in the air.
Third little piggy dances on his toes,
Wiggling around his little pink nose.

Sun is shining bright in the clear blue sky,
Watching the fluffy white clouds float by.
Clapping our hands and singing a song,
Every little toddler can sing along.

Time for a nap in the warm afternoon,
Sleeping very softly beneath the moon.
Dreaming of games and playing outside,
Ready for tomorrow's wonderful ride.

rhymes.title: Percy the Pig
rhymes.text:
Percy the pig loves to eat a sweet treat,
Apples and carrots are yummy to eat.
Munching and crunching with a happy sound,
Dropping bright pieces all over the ground.

Chasing a butterfly flying so high,
Watching it flutter up into the sky.
Waving a hoof at a passing green frog,
Sitting so still on an old wooden log.

Running so fast on his four little feet,
Making the farmyard look extra neat.
Stopping to rest by a big shady tree,
As happy as a little pig can be.

Now the bright stars are beginning to glow,
Telling the sleepy farm it is time to go.
Closing his eyes in the cozy red barn,
Safe from the wind and the cold winter yarn.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Piggy
rhymes.text:
Little pink piggy, short and sweet,
Running around on four small feet.
Wiggly snout and a curly tail,
Drinking milk from a shiny pail.
In the meadow, bright and green,
Happiest pig you've ever seen.
Jumping up and down with glee,
Happy as a pig can be.
Muddy puddles on the ground,
Splashing water all around.
Oink and oink and oink he goes,
Right up to his little nose.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little pigs to go.
Curl up tight and go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

rhymes.title: Three Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Three little trotters in the hay,
Dancing gaily through the day.
One little pig says, 'Oink, oink, oink!'
Thinking what a pig would think.
Two little pigs go running fast,
Hoping that the day will last.
Three little pigs jump in the pool,
Where the water nice and cool.
Splash and splish and squish and squelch,
Eating apples by the belch.
Now they dry their muddy fur,
Not a single pig can stir.
Snoring softly in the bed,
Dreams are dancing in each head.
Goodnight pigs, sleep safe and sound,
Best little piggies all around.

rhymes.title: The Pig on the Hill
rhymes.text:
On a hill so green and high,
Watches clouds go floating by.
Pernilla Pig wears a yellow hat,
Looking very proud of that.
She finds a clover on the ground,
Looking all around the town.
Happy squeals of pure delight,
Shining in the morning light.
Trotting down the muddy lane,
Singing in the gentle rain.
Finding bugs and eating seeds,
Meeting all her piggy needs.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Bidding everyone goodnight.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the coming of the day.

rhymes.title: Little Pig in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Little pig with rosy snout,
Playing all the day about.
Trotting on your little feet,
Looking for a tasty treat.

Running through the clover green,
Happiest pig you've ever seen.
Wagging your sweet curly tail,
Walking by the wooden pail.

Sun is shining warm and bright,
Turning everything to light.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Crawling in your cozy bed.

Oink, oink, hear the piggie say,
Dreaming of another day.
Stars are shining in the sky,
Little pig, now close your eye.

rhymes.title: Mud Puddle Fun
rhymes.text:
See the little piggy run,
Having such a lot of fun.
Jumping in the mud so brown,
Bestest piggy in the town.

Splash and splatter all around,
Happy hooves upon the ground.
Little ears begin to flap,
Ready for a little nap.

Splish and splashing in the pool,
Water feels so nice and cool.
Now it is time to get clean,
Freshest pig you've ever seen.

Washing up with water bright,
Sleeping through the starry night.
Sweet little pig, snug and warm,
Safe inside the cozy barn.

rhymes.title: Three Little Pigs Play
rhymes.text:
Three little pigs go out to play,
Happy on a sunny day.
Dancing in the meadow wide,
With a smile on every side.

First little pig finds an apple sweet,
Crunchy and a yummy treat.
Second little pig sings a song,
All the animals sing along.

Third little pig takes a leap,
Counting sheep before they sleep.
Now the sun is going down,
Lighting up the sleepy town.

Time to cuddle in the hay,
Dreaming of the next bright day.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your warm and cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Little Piggy Goes to Sleep
rhymes.text:
Little pig, little pig, in the hay,
You have had a busy day.
Now the sun is going down,
Quiet is the sleepy town.

Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy little bed.
Dream of mud and puddles deep,
Little pig is fast asleep.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Lullaby and lullaby.
Floppy ears and snout so pink,
Time to rest, now do not blink.

Morning comes with golden light,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Curly tail is still and deep,
Little pig is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Piggy Dance
rhymes.text:
Stomp your trotters on the ground,
Spin around and make a sound.
Oink and giggle, clap your hands,
Happiest pig in all the lands.

Jump into the mud so sweet,
Feel it squish beneath your feet.
Wiggle now your curly tail,
Sailing like a happy whale.

Splash the water in the air,
Mud is flying everywhere.
Wash it off when day is done,
That was such a lot of fun.

Now we rest our piggy head,
Crawling back into our bed.
Smiling softly in the night,
Sleeping till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Five Little Pink Trotters
rhymes.text:
Five little pink trotters dancing in the sun,
Jumping up and down, oh they want some fun.
One little trotter jumps into a pool,
Splashing all around where the water's cool.

Two little trotters find an apple red,
Rolling it along softly to the shed.
Three little trotters give a happy oink,
Touching little noses with a little boink.

Four little trotters scamper in the grass,
Watching all the fuzzy little ducklings pass.
Five little trotters curl their little tails,
Sailing off to dreamland on fairy tales.

Now the playtime's over and the stars are bright,
Sleeping little piglet says a sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Piggy's Muddy Day
rhymes.text:
Little pig in mud so deep,
Time to wake up from your sleep.
Oink and squeak and shout hooray,
We will play outside today.

Splash your feet and stomp around,
Make a noise upon the ground.
Brown and messy, what a sight,
Happy pig until the night.

Roll over on your left side,
Open up your mouth so wide.
Blow a bubble in the goo,
Piggy, I am splashing too.

Now the sun is going down,
Best small piggie in the town.
Wash the mud from off your head,
Time to go right into bed.

rhymes.title: Three Little Piggies
rhymes.text:
Three little piggies in a row,
Watch them hop and watch them go.
First one wears a yellow hat,
Second one is round and fat.

Third one has a curly tail,
Carrying a shiny pail.
Running through the clover sweet,
Dancing with their little feet.

Now they stop to eat a snack,
Carrots in a canvas sack.
Crunchy munchy in the sun,
Having lots of piggy fun.

When the stars begin to peep,
All three piggies fall asleep.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
While the moon is far away.

rhymes.title: The Curly Tail Song
rhymes.text:
See the little pinkish pig,
Dancing jiggy-wiggy jig.
With a nose that likes to root,
Wearing mud upon his boot.

Wiggle waggle goes his snout,
Looking all around about.
Curly tail goes round and round,
Falling softly on the ground.

Oink aloud and jump up high,
Touching all the open sky.
Happy farmyard, beep and bop,
Little piggie will not stop.

Now he curls up in his hay,
Ending up a busy day.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy piggy bed.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
Little pink pig with a curly tail,
Walking around with a shiny red pail.
He loves to play in the warm, bright sun,
And running away is so much fun.
He sees a puddle big and wide,
And jumps right in with a happy slide.
Splish and splash and mud on his nose,
Tickling all of his little pink toes.
Oink goes the piglet, happy and gay,
Chasing the butterflies all through the day.
He rolls in the dirt and grunts with glee,
As happy as can be under the tree.
Now the sun is setting down so low,
It is time for the little pig to go.
He trots to his barn and closes his eyes,
Dreaming of mud up to the skies.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Piggy Hooves
rhymes.text:
Ten little piggy hooves dancing on the floor,
Waddling through the open barnyard door.
One little piggy finds an apple red,
Two little piggies jump into their bed.
Three little piggies play hide and seek,
Four little piggies give a little squeak.
Five little piggies munching on some hay,
Having so much fun the live-long day.
Six little piggies splash in the brook,
Seven little piggies look in a book.
Eight little piggies wear a funny hat,
Nine little piggies cuddle with the cat.
Ten little piggies tired and all through,
Saying goodnight to the skies so blue.
They snuggle real close in the cozy straw,
The sweetest little piggies you ever saw.

rhymes.title: Porky's Morning Song
rhymes.text:
Morning has come and the rooster crows,
Awake is the pig with the wiggly nose.
He hops out of bed and stretches his legs,
And runs to the coop for some chicken eggs.
The farmer is smiling and waving hello,
Ready for wherever the pig wants to go.
They walk down the path to the grassy green hill,
Where the wind blows softly and everything is still.
Porky the piglet sings out a song,
And all of his friends love to sing along.
They dance in a circle and clap their hands,
The happiest animals in all the lands.
Now it is time for a yummy snack,
A nice juicy carrot and a pat on the back.
The little pink pig lets out a loud cheer,
Glad to be living on the farm this year.

rhymes.title: The Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
See the little pink pig go round,
Trotting softly on the ground.
With a curly tail so neat,
And four little muddy feet.

He loves to play out in the sun,
Running fast and having fun.
He gives a happy little squeal,
Eating up his yummy meal.

When the stars shine bright and deep,
Little pig goes fast asleep.
In his cozy bed of hay,
Resting till the coming day.

Goodnight, pig, sleep tight and deep,
While the moon begins to peep.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Sleeping softly through the night.

rhymes.title: Muddy Puddles
rhymes.text:
Puddy pig loves mud to see,
Jumping with unbridled glee.
Splish and splash and slosh about,
Wiggling his pink little snout.

Water splashes in the air,
Droplets land upon his hair.
He is covered head to toe,
Watch the happy piggie go!

Duckies swim and watch him play,
In the middle of the day.
Laughing as he rolls around,
Making such a silly sound.

Time to wash the mud away,
Wait until another day.
Now he is so clean and bright,
Ready for a sleepy night.

rhymes.title: Three Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Three little trotters walk the lane,
Dancing softly in the rain.
Pink and happy, full of joy,
Every little girl and boy.

Piggy wears a hat of blue,
Saying cheerful oinks to you.
Jumping up and jumping down,
Happiest pig in all the town.

Soon the clouds begin to part,
Sunshine warms a happy heart.
Butterflies fly all around,
Touching lightly on the ground.

Time to rest his weary head,
Trot on home to cozy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sigh,
Little piggie, lullaby.

rhymes.title: Little Piggy Wiggle
rhymes.text:
Little piggy in the pen,
Wiggles out and back again.
Turns around and flaps his ears,
Chasing all his little fears.
Finds a puddle deep and wide,
Jumps right in with happy pride.
Splashes water all around,
Slips and slides upon the ground.
Oinks a happy morning tune,
Underneath the golden moon.
Washes off his muddy feet,
Finds a yummy apple treat.
Chews his food and goes to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Dreaming of another day,
When he comes back out to play.
