rhymes.title: Five Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Five little trotters in the mud,
Playing with a little bud.
First one goes *oink oink oink*,
Looking for a magic link.
Second one goes rolling round,
Happy on the farmyard ground.
Third one wears a hat of blue,
Saying hello friend to you.
Fourth one eats a golden pear,
Sitting in the rocking chair.
Fifth one takes a sleepy nap,
Resting in a cozy lap.
Now the day is done and bright,
Saying to the sun goodnight.
Little piggies fast asleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Pink Piggy Song
rhymes.text:
Pink little piggy with a tail,
Swimming in a wooden pail.
No, that's silly, pigs don't swim,
They go jumping on a whim!
Trotting down the country lane,
Singing in the summer rain.
Finding carrots sweet and red,
Rolling in a straw-filled bed.
Big round tummy, shiny snout,
Walking all the farmyard out.
Saying hello to the sheep,
Counting numbers while they sleep.
Curly tail goes wiggle wag,
Carrying a happy bag.
Now the little pig is done,
Hiding from the setting sun.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
Little pink pig has a curly tail,
He loves to play in a wooden pail.
He has a snout that is pink and sweet,
And tiny shoes on his little feet.

He walks around in the soft green grass,
And smiles at ducks as they gently pass.
He loves to run and he loves to leap,
Then curls right up in the hay to sleep.

The sun goes down in the sky so bright,
The little pig sleeps till morning light.
Oink, oink, oink goes the happy sound,
The sweetest piggie in all the town.

Wake up now for a brand new day,
Time to jump and time to play.
The little pig is full of glee,
As happy as a pig can be.

rhymes.title: Five Little Piglets
rhymes.text:
Five little piglets in the mud,
Playing together with a thud.
One little piggy finds a toy,
Jumping around with so much joy.

Two little piglets splash and play,
Chasing the butterflies away.
Three little piglets start to sing,
Hearing the farmyard church bells ring.

Four little piglets munch on hay,
Hungry and happy all the day.
Five little piglets go to sleep,
While furry mice begin to creep.

Now the barnyard is quiet and still,
Resting down by the little hill.
Dreaming of mud and apples sweet,
A lovely place for a piggie's feet.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Puddle Song
rhymes.text:
Splish, splash, splosh goes the little pig,
Dancing a dance that is small and big.
He loves the mud from his head to toe,
Wherever the muddy puddles go.

He wiggles his ears and he wiggles his nose,
Right down to his little pink piggie toes.
He finds a puddle that's deep and wide,
And jumps right into the muddy side.

Bubbles go pop in the water brown,
The happiest piggie in all the town.
The farmer smiles as he walks along,
And listens to the little pig's song.

Oink, oink, oink is the song he sings,
Happier than a bird with wings.
Time to go home as the day grows late,
Waiting right by the garden gate.

rhymes.title: Little Piggy Goes to Sleep
rhymes.text:
Little pig wakes up and yawns,
Right beside the dewy lawns.
He has spots of dusty pink,
And he takes a morning drink.

Then he runs to find some mud,
Splashing safely with a thud.
Round and round he likes to play,
All throughout the sunny day.

Now the sun begins to set,
Piggy is not finished yet.
Time to wash his muddy face,
Moving to a cozy place.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little piggy starts to sigh.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Three Little Piggies
rhymes.text:
Three little piggies jump up and down,
Running around the big green town.
One wears a hat of yellow bright,
Making sure the morning's right.

Two have boots of shiny red,
Ready for a walk instead.
Three carries a basket small,
Walking softly by the wall.

They love to giggle, they love to sing,
Enjoying every single thing.
Eating apples sweet and red,
Before they go back to bed.

Now the moon is glowing high,
Whispering a lullaby.
Three little piggies dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Oink, Oink, Little Pig
rhymes.text:
Oink, oink, says the little pig,
Dancing a dance that is jolly and big.
Wiggling his tail so curly and neat,
Prancing around on his four little feet.

He finds a puddle of water and blue,
Jumping right in with a happyahoo!
Splashing the water all over the ground,
Making a funny and wonderful sound.

His mama comes over to see him play,
Smiling and nodding her head today.
She gives him a hug and a pat on the head,
Ready to tuck him right into his bed.

The farm is quiet, the night is near,
Whispering secrets for piggies to hear.
Sleep, little pig, till the morning light,
Dreaming of mud till the very next night.

rhymes.title: The Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
See the little pink pig hop,
Jumping right up to the top.
Wiggle tail and oink out loud,
Making all the farmyard proud.

Running through the soft green grass,
Watching butterflies float past.
Stomping in the yellow clay,
Having so much fun today.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little piggie, you are best.

Dreaming of a muddy pool,
Where the water nice and cool.
Good night, piggie, go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Five little trotters in a row,
Where is the little pig to go?
Over the bridge and past the tree,
Looking for a friend to see.

Snout goes sniff and ears go flop,
Little piggie will not stop.
Finding apples sweet and red,
Time to munch until he's fed.

Now his tummy is quite round,
Sitting down upon the ground.
Blinking eyes so sleepy-slow,
Ready now for bed, you know.

Blanket warm and pillow tight,
Sleep until the morning light.
Sweetest dreams to you, my dear,
Glad that you are sleeping here.

rhymes.title: Mud Pie Song
rhymes.text:
Make a mud pie nice and sweet,
For the little pig to eat.
Stir it round and stir it deep,
While the baby ducks are asleep.

Piggie dances in the sun,
Having lots of muddy fun.
Splash and squish and squelch around,
Falling down upon the ground.

Time to wash the dirt away,
End of such a happy day.
Warm bath water, soapy clean,
Best little pig you've ever seen.

Wrapped up in a towel so bright,
Giving mummy hugs so tight.
Now it's time to softly say,
We will do it all next day.

rhymes.title: Little Pink Pig
rhymes.text:
Little pink pig with a curly tail,
Walking around with a shiny blue pail.
Looking for mud in the soft green grass,
Watching the fluffy white clouds as they pass.

He stops at a puddle and looks all around,
Then drops all fours right down to the ground.
He splashes and kicks with a happy squeal,
Eating up apples as his evening meal.

The sun goes down and the stars shine bright,
He tucks in his snout and says sleep tight.
With a warm little snore and a gentle sigh,
He dreams of the mud under the sky.

Goodnight, little piglet, rest your head,
Snuggled so cozy in your straw bed.
Tomorrow is waiting for fun and play,
So sleep until morning and greet the new day.

rhymes.title: Three Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Three little pigs in the morning light,
Waking right up as the sun grows bright.
They put on their boots and they skip and play,
Chasing the butterflies all through the day.

They jump in the hay and they run so fast,
Hoping this wonderful game will last.
One little piglet finds a red ball,
Throwing it over the garden wall.

Another little piglet eats yummy corn,
Chewing it happily since early morn.
The third little piglet sings a sweet tune,
Howling a song to the morning moon.

Now lunchtime is here and they eat their greens,
Filling their bellies with yummy beans.
They curl up together to rest and sleep,
While farmyard secrets are quiet and deep.

rhymes.title: Muddy Puddle Fun
rhymes.text:
Oink goes the piglet, happy and gay,
Ready to start a brand new day.
Trotting along with a wiggle and hop,
Never once planning to ever stop.

He finds a big puddle of squishy mud,
And jumps right in with a giant thud.
Water goes splashing up in the air,
Landing on piggies everywhere.

A duck comes swimming to see the sight,
Quacking along with pure delight.
They dance in the mud till the afternoon,
Singing a happy little farmyard tune.

When evening falls and the sky is red,
The sleepy pig waddles back to bed.
He dreams of the mud and the sunny skies,
Closing his tired and heavy eyes.

rhymes.title: Little Pig, Little Pig
rhymes.text:
Little pig, little pig, in the mud,
Stomping around with a happy thud.
Curly tail and a pink-pink snout,
Happy little pig with a happy shout.

Splash and dash in the bubbly pool,
Water is splashing, nice and cool.
Happy piglet, big and round,
Jumping up and down on the ground.

Time to wash and time to sleep,
Counting stars instead of sheep.
Rest your head in the cozy hay,
Dreaming of another sunny day.

Good night, pig, sleep tight now,
Wake up with the horse and cow.

rhymes.title: Five Little Trotters
rhymes.text:
Five little pigs in the morning light,
Running around till the sun is bright.
One finds an apple, red and sweet,
Two find clover for a tasty treat.

Three little pigs go rolling around,
Four little piglets tumble to ground.
Five little piggies squeal with glee,
Running fast across the grass so free.

Sun goes down in the evening sky,
Birds in the branches singing bye-bye.
Little pigs yawn and close their eyes,
Underneath the moon so big and wise.

Snuggled in bed with a happy sigh,
Little piggies resting by and by.

rhymes.title: Pink Piggy Wiggle
rhymes.text:
Pink piggy wiggle, nose so sweet,
Dancing around on four small feet.
Wag your tail and give a cheer,
Glad you are my farm friend dear.

Jump in the hay and hide away,
Playing games throughout the day.
Now it is time to stop and rest,
Sleeping in your barn is best.

Soft little snort and gentle sigh,
While the clouds go floating by.
Stars are shining in the night,
Moon is glowing soft and bright.

Close your eyes and sleep until dawn,
When the happy new day is drawn.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had a coat of fluffy, white wool that bounced when he hopped. Boing, boing, hop, hop, hop! The sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors. All the other farm animals were getting ready for bed. The cows went moo, the horses went neigh, and the little birds tucked their heads under their wings. But Sammy was not tired at all. He wanted to play! Sammy trotted over to his best friend, Barnaby the butterfly. 'Let us play hide and seek!' said Sammy. Barnaby fluttered his pretty blue wings and hid behind a big green leaf. Sammy closed his eyes and counted, one, two, three! Then he looked under the flowers and behind the rocks. 'Peek-a-boo! I see you!' giggled Sammy. They played for a little while longer, but soon, Sammy began to yawn. Big, sleepy sheep yawns. *Yaaaaawn*. The wind blew softly through the grass, making a gentle shushing sound. *Hush-a-bye, little sheep*. Sammy’s fluffy legs felt very heavy. He walked back to his cozy barn where his mama was waiting for him. Mama sheep gave Sammy a warm, comforting nuzzle on his fuzzy head. 'Time for bed, my little lamb,' she whispered softly. Sammy snuggled deep down into the sweet-smelling hay. It was so warm and cozy. He closed his brown eyes and listened to the crickets singing their quiet nighttime song. Sammy thought about the bright green grass, the happy butterflies, and the fun games they had played together. A tiny smile spread across his sweet little face. He took a nice, deep breath in, and let it all the way out. Soon, Sammy was fast asleep, dreaming sweet dreams of fluffy white clouds in a starry blue sky. Goodnight, Sammy. Sleep tight.

stories.title: Pip's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Pip was a very curious little sheep. While the rest of the flock stayed munching on the safe, green grass of the meadow, Pip liked to explore. One sunny morning, after a big rainstorm, Pip spotted something very interesting. It was a giant puddle right in the middle of the path! The puddle was shiny, brown, and splashy. Pip trotted over on his little black hooves, *tap-tap-tap*. He looked down at the water and saw his own fluffy reflection looking back up at him. 'Baa!' said Pip in a friendly voice. The reflection said *baa* right back! Pip thought that was just wonderful. He lifted up one front hoof and dipped it right into the water. *Splash!* Cool water splashed all around. It felt so fun! Pip got braver. He stepped all the way into the middle of the big, brown puddle. *Squish, squash, squish!* Mud squished between his tiny toes. Pip laughed a happy sheep laugh. He shook his head, and a little drop of mud flew right onto his nose. Oh, silly Pip! But then, Pip looked down at his beautiful, white, fluffy wool. Oh no! His coat was not white anymore. It was covered in brown mud from his head all the way to his little tail! Just then, Mama sheep came walking down the path. 'Baa-baa!' she called out with a giggle. Mama knew just what to do. She led Pip down to the sparkling blue brook where the water ran clear and fast. Pip stepped into the shallow water, and Mama helped wash away all the silly mud. Scrub, scrub, rinse, rinse! The cool water washed the brown away, and Pip was white and fluffy once more. Pip learned that mud puddles are very fun for splashing, but being clean and fluffy is even better.

stories.title: Woolly's Big Yellow Sweater
stories.text: The autumn winds were beginning to blow across the farm, and the air felt chilly. Brrr! Woolly the sheep shivered as a cold breeze tickled his nose. 'Baa,' shivered Woolly. His friends, the ducks and the pigs, had feathers and thick mud to keep them warm, but Woolly needed a little extra help. Farmer John looked at Woolly and smiled. 'Don't you worry, my fluffy friend,' said the farmer. 'I have a wonderful surprise for you!' Farmer John brought out a bright, cheerful, yellow sweater. It was the color of a warm summer sun and as soft as a cloud. Woolly put his head right through the neck hole, and his front legs popped through the sleeves. Ta-da! Woolly looked down at himself. He looked just like a big, walking lemon, and it made him giggle. The yellow sweater fit him absolutely perfectly. It hugged his tummy and kept the chilly wind completely away. Woolly felt so cozy and warm that he started to dance a little happy jig. *Hop to the left, hop to the right, wiggle your tail with all your might!* All the other farm animals gathered around to look at Woolly’s fantastic new outfit. The cow mooed in approval, and the horse neighed happily. Woolly felt so proud and special in his bright yellow sweater. He trotted all around the farmyard, showing off his sunny style to everyone he met. Even the little birds chirped a happy tune as Woolly walked by. When evening came, and the stars twinkled in the dark sky, Woolly curled up in the warm straw. He didn't feel a single bit cold. He just felt snug, happy, and loved in his wonderful yellow sweater. Goodnight, Woolly.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the fluffiest, whitest fleece in the whole wide world. It felt just like a big marshmallow! Every morning, the sun would wake up with a bright yellow smile, and Sammy would wake up too. 'Baa, baa!' Sammy would say to the morning breeze. Today was a very special day because Sammy was going to learn how to play hide-and-seek with his fluffy friends. First, Sammy found a big green bush. He tucked his head right behind the leaves. 'Are you ready?' called his friend Bella the butterfly. Sammy giggled a little baa-laugh. Bella flew all around the bush, looking high and low. 'Peek-a-boo, Sammy! I see your fluffy tail!' she cheered. Sammy jumped out with a happy skip. Next, it was time to practice hopping over little puddles left by the morning rain. Splash, splash went Sammy's tiny hooves. He tried his very best to jump high like a bunny rabbit, but instead, he did a silly tumble right onto a patch of soft clover. Oh, how Sammy laughed! By the time the afternoon sun started to yawn and turn into a sleepy orange color, Sammy's tummy began to rumble. Time for some yummy, green grass dinner! Munch, munch, chew, chew, went Sammy. He ate until he was as round as a little ball. The sky turned from blue to a sparkly purple night. The bright moon came out to watch over the sleepy meadow. Sammy felt very tired. He walked slowly back to his cozy barn. His mother was waiting there with a warm, gentle nuzzle. Sammy curled up on a bed of sweet-smelling hay. He closed his heavy eyes and listened to the crickets sing a quiet lullaby. Goodnight, little Sammy Sheep. Sleep tight and dream of fluffy clouds.

stories.title: Buttons and the Big Woolly Coat
stories.text: Deep in a sun-warmed pasture lived a little sheep named Buttons. Buttons was not like the other sheep. While everyone else had neat, tidy wool, Buttons had curls that went every which way. Some curled left, some curled right, and one tuft right on top of his head pointed straight up at the sky like a funny antenna. One sunny morning, the farmer walked into the field carrying a pair of shiny silver shears. Snip, snap, went the shears in the air. It was shearing day! The other sheep lined up to get their heavy winter coats brushed and trimmed. Buttons watched with big, wide eyes. He felt very nervous. Was it going to tickle? Was it going to cold? When it was his turn, the kind farmer gave him a gentle pat on the nose. 'Don't worry, little Buttons,' the farmer whispered softly. Snip, snip, snip went the shiny blades. Out fell a few bits of dried grass, a stuck daisy, and a tiny twig that Buttons had collected during his morning adventures. As the wool came off, Buttons felt lighter and lighter. Suddenly, he could bounce higher than ever before! Boing, boing, went Buttons all around the paddock. He felt like a brand new sheep made of marshmallow air. He looked at the big pile of fluffy wool sitting on the grass. It looked just like a giant white cloud that had fallen right out of the sky. Buttons ran over and gave the big pile of wool a cozy, happy headbutt. The other sheep gathered around, and they all did a happy little sheep dance together in the warm afternoon sun. Buttons learned that getting a haircut wasn't scary at all; it was just a wonderful way to feel breezy and free. When evening finally arrived, Buttons trotted back to the barn, feeling cool, clean, and ready for the sweetest dreams.

stories.title: Pip the Little Lost Lamb
stories.text: Pip was a tiny lamb with the softest black ears and a nose that always twitched when he smelled something sweet. Today, the meadow flowers were blooming in bright reds, yellows, and blues. Pip was so busy chasing a friendly bumblebee that he trotted right past the old oak tree and down the winding path. He looked around, and his woolly friends were nowhere in sight! Oh dear, thought Pip, my fleece is all a-flutter. Where did everyone go? Pip let out a tiny, worried 'Baa!' A moment later, wise old Barnaby Owl opened his big round eyes from a high branch. 'Who-who are you looking for, little one?' asked the owl softly. 'I am looking for my flock,' Pip replied, blinking his big dark eyes. 'Just follow the sound of the bubbling brook and look for the big wooden fence,' hooted Barnaby. Pip thanked the kind owl with a polite nod and scampered down the path. Splash, splash, went his hooves through the shallow water. He listened very carefully. Soon, carried on the gentle afternoon breeze, he heard a familiar chorus of cheerful 'Baa-baas'. Pip's heart did a happy leap inside his fuzzy chest. He trotted around the bend and there was his mother, standing right by the gate, waiting with a warm, welcoming smile. Pip raced as fast as his little legs could carry him and snuggled right into his mother’s soft side. 'I found my way back!' Pip cheered happily. The sun began to dip below the horizon, painting the sky in pink and gold. Pip curled up in the safe, cozy meadow, happy to be home with his family, knowing he would never wander too far away again.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a fluffy green hill, there lived a little lamb named Sammy Sheep. Sammy had the softest, whitest wool in the whole wide world. It felt just like a big marshmallow! Every morning, Sammy would wake up with the golden sun. He would stretch his front legs, wiggle his little tail, and say, 'Baa, baa, good morning, world!' Sammy loved to play hide-and-seek with his best friend, a little yellow butterfly. They would run through the bright yellow buttercups, giggling and playing all day long. Sammy would skip over tiny stones and hop across the little bubbling brook. But when the afternoon sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and purple, Sammy would start to yawn. Big, round yawns! 'Yaaaawn,' went Sammy. His little eyelids felt very heavy, just like two sleepy pillows. The wise old owl in the big oak tree would hoo gently, telling all the farm animals that bedtime was near. Sammy knew just what to do. He trotted over to his cozy spot in the meadow, right next to his mama. Mama Sheep nuzzled Sammy’s soft neck with her warm nose, giving him a big, sweet sheep hug. Sammy closed his eyes tightly and snuggled deep into the soft grass. He listened to the gentle evening breeze whispering through the leaves. The little yellow butterfly fluttered away to its own leafy bed. Sammy took a deep breath in and a slow breath out. He thought about all the fun things they would do tomorrow—running in the grass, chasing butterflies, and eating sweet clover. But for right now, it was time for sweet dreams. Sammy curled up into a little white ball of fluff and drifted off to sleep. Goodnight, Sammy Sheep. Sleep tight under the twinkling stars.

stories.title: Buttons the Lost Bell
stories.text: Baa, baa, went Buttons the little brown sheep as she trotted down the dusty farm path. Buttons was a very special sheep because she wore a shiny silver bell around her neck. Every time she hopped, skip-jumped, or ran, the bell would go 'Ting-a-ling-a-ling!' It was a happy sound that made all the other farm animals smile. One sunny morning, Buttons was jumping over a patch of red clover when her silver bell made a funny sound. Clink! Oh no! The little bell fell right off her red ribbon and rolled away into the tall, tickly green grass. Buttons stopped and looked down at her neck. The bell was gone! 'Baa?' she cried out softly. She wanted her shiny bell back. Just then, Barnaby the big brown dog trotted over. 'Woof woof! Can I help you, little friend?' asked Barnaby with a wag of his tail. Buttons nodded her head up and down. Together, the two friends started to look. They looked under the big wooden fence. They looked behind the red barn door. They looked inside a hollow log where a friendly squirrel lived. But the bell was nowhere to be seen. Suddenly, Barnaby’s big black nose gave a twitch. 'Sniff, sniff, sniff!' He trotted over to a patch of bright yellow sunflowers and began to dig gently with his paw. What do you think he found? Right there in the dirt, gleaming in the morning sun, was the shiny silver bell! Buttons let out a happy little 'Baa-baa-hoo!' She danced in a circle while Barnaby picked up the bell and gently placed it back on her red ribbon. 'Ting-a-ling-a-ling!' sang the bell once again. Buttons gave Barnaby a gentle nudge with her warm nose to say thank you. They walked back to the farm together, making sweet music all the way.

stories.title: Pip's Puddle Splash
stories.text: Pitter-patter went the big raindrops on the roof of the old red barn. It was a rainy Tuesday morning, and little Pip the sheep was standing by the window of the big barn. Pip had fluffy white fleece that looked like a puffy cloud. He watched the water drops slide down the glass. 'Plip, plop, splash!' went the puddles outside in the farmyard. Pip loved rainy days because rainy days meant big, muddy puddles. He did not mind getting his paws wet at all. When the rain finally stopped and the sun peeked out from behind a gray cloud, making a big sparkly rainbow, Pip knew it was time for fun. He put on his imaginary yellow rain boots and trotted right out the barn doors. Splish! Splash! Pip jumped right into the biggest, muddiest puddle he could find. Water splashed high up into the air, glittering in the sunlight like diamonds. 'Baa, ha, ha!' laughed Pip, shaking his head so his floppy ears wiggled back and forth. His friend Penny the pig came running over, squealing with pure joy. 'Oink, oink! Can I jump too?' asked Penny. 'Baa, yes!' said Pip, making room for Penny in the puddle. Together, the two happy animals splashed and stomped, making the biggest mud pies in the whole wide world. They made mud splatters on their noses and mud drips on their tails. By the time Mama Sheep called them in for dinner, both Pip and Penny were covered in mud from head to toe. They didn't care one single bit because they had the best adventure ever. After a warm bath and a good brush, Pip’s wool was whiter than snow, and he curled up for a cozy night, dreaming of more splashy puddles.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had a coat of wool as fluffy as a marshmallow and as white as snow. The sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors. It was almost time for bed, but Sammy was not tired at all! 'Baa-baa!' said Sammy. 'I want to play!' Sammy hopped over a tiny yellow daisy. He trotted past a busy little beetle. He even tried to play tag with his own shadow. But the shadow was very quiet and wouldn't run back. Sammy trotted over to his mama. 'Mama, I am not ready for sleep!' Mama Sheep smiled a gentle, warm smile. 'Let us take a quiet walk, my little sweetpea,' she whispered. Together, Sammy and his mama walked slowly across the meadow. They saw the big yellow moon peeking up from behind the tall hills. It looked like a big, smiling night-light in the sky. Sammy looked up and let out a tiny yawn. 'Yawn!' went Sammy. His little legs suddenly felt very heavy, like they were made of sleepy stones. A gentle evening breeze blew through the grass, singing a soft shushing song. 'Ssshh, ssshh,' whispered the wind. Sammy blinked his big brown eyes once. He blinked them twice. The world around him felt so safe and cozy. Mama Sheep wrapped her warm, woolly side right next to Sammy. She hummed a sweet, low lullaby that sounded like a happy river. Sammy closed his eyes tight. He thought about green grass, bright yellow daisies, and fluffy clouds. With one last happy little wiggle, Sammy drifted off into the land of sweet dreams. Goodnight, Sammy Sheep. Sleep tight until the morning sun wakes you up to play again.

stories.title: Sammy's Woolly Jumper
stories.text: The morning sun was shining bright and warm over the farm. Little sheep Sammy woke up and stretched his legs. 'Baa-baa!' he said. But today, Sammy felt a little bit chilly. The morning breeze was blowing a cool wind across the meadow. 'Brrr!' shivered Sammy. His wool felt a little too short to keep him warm. Just then, Farmer Jill walked into the meadow carrying a big, bright basket. Inside the basket were three colorful things. There was a red jumper, a blue jumper, and a yellow jumper with little duck pictures on it! Farmer Jill smiled and said, 'Good morning, Sammy! Do you want a cozy jumper today?' Sammy did a little happy hop. 'Baa! Yes, please!' Farmer Jill gently helped Sammy put on the bright yellow jumper. It had sleeves for his front legs and a big opening for his fluffy head. Sammy looked down at his new clothes. It was so bright and sunny! He trotted over to the muddy puddle to see his reflection. 'Ooh, look at me!' he seemed to say. His friend Pip the pig trotted over. 'Oink! That jumper looks very handsome on you, Sammy!' Pip squealed. Sammy felt so proud and warm inside. He didn't feel chilly at all anymore. He ran and jumped through the tall green grass, his yellow jumper stretching and bouncing with every leap. The other sheep came over to say hello and admired the bright yellow color. Sammy felt like the luckiest sheep in the whole wide world. When the afternoon sun finally came out to warm up the farm, Farmer Jill helped Sammy take off the jumper and folded it neatly in her basket. Sammy gave Farmer Jill a happy little nudge with his nose to say thank you. It was a wonderful day to be a sheep in a bright yellow jumper.

stories.title: Sammy Learns to Count
stories.text: Little lamb Sammy loved to explore the farm every single day. Today, Sammy had a very important job. Wise old Owl told him that there were wonderful things to count all around the farmyard. Sammy stood by the big red barn and blinked his big eyes. 'Let us find out what we can count!' said Sammy. First, he looked down at the soft green grass. Pop, pop, pop! Out came tiny, friendly frogs. Sammy counted them slowly. 'One green frog, two green frogs, three green frogs!' The little frogs jumped away with a happy ribbit. Sammy giggled and clapped his hooves. Next, Sammy walked over to the wooden fence where the ducks lived. Quack, quack, went the fluffy yellow ducklings. Sammy waddled behind them and counted out loud. 'One little duckling, two little ducklings, three little ducklings, four little ducklings!' The mama duck gave a happy quack to say hello. Sammy smiled a big sheepish smile. He was getting so good at counting things! Finally, Sammy trotted over to the big apple tree near the garden. Thump! A big red apple fell right onto the grass. Then another one fell down. Sammy counted the red apples on the grass. 'One, two, three, four, five!' Five round, juicy red apples. Just then, Farmer John walked by with a big basket. 'Well, hello there, Sammy! Are you counting our farm friends?' Sammy let out a loud, happy 'Baa!' to say yes. Farmer John patted Sammy on his fluffy head and gave him a crunchy carrot as a special treat for doing such a wonderful job. Sammy chewed his yummy carrot and looked all around the farm. Counting was so much fun when you had wonderful friends to count with.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a fluffy green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the softest white wool in the whole wide world. Every morning, Sammy loved to wake up with the golden sun. 'Baa, baa!' he would say to his mommy. 'Good morning, sweet world!' Sammy would run and jump in the meadow. He liked to chase fluttering yellow butterflies and play hide-and-seek behind tall green bushes. Sometimes, he would wiggle his little black nose at friendly buzzing bees. But today was a very special day because Sammy was growing up big and strong. Mommy Sheep said, 'Sammy, it is time to eat some sweet green clover to keep your tummy happy.' Munch, munch, crunch went Sammy. He ate until he was completely full. Then, he drank some cool, clear water from the bubbling brook. Splash went his little hooves! Sammy felt so happy and full of energy. He danced around in a circle. But soon, the warm afternoon sun began to make his heavy eyelids blink. Blink, blink, went Sammy's eyes. The sky started to turn shades of pink and orange. The birds flew back to their cozy nests high up in the trees. Mommy Sheep smiled a warm, gentle smile and nuzzled Sammy's fuzzy head. 'Time to rest your tired little legs, my darling,' she whispered softly. Sammy gave a big, sleepy yawn. Ahhh-wooo. He trotted over to his favorite patch of soft clover. He curled his legs up underneath his round, fluffy body. The wind whispered a lullaby through the leaves. Swish, swish, went the trees. Sammy closed his eyes tightly. He thought about all the fun things he did today, like jumping high and chasing butterflies. He felt completely safe and loved right beside his mommy. Slowly, Sammy drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep, dreaming of fluffy clouds in a bright blue sky.

stories.title: Woolly's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Woolly was a very curious little sheep who lived on a cheerful farm with lots of animal friends. One rainy morning, Woolly woke up and looked out his barn window. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the raindrops on the roof. The farmyard was full of big, squishy puddles! Woolly loved puddles more than anything in the world. He trotted over to the corner of the barn and found something amazing. A pair of bright red boots! They were shiny, brand new, and just the right size for his little black hooves. Woolly slipped his front hooves right into the boots. Clop, clop, clop went the boots on the wooden floor. He felt like the most stylish sheep on the whole farm. He eagerly opened the barn door and stepped outside into the cool, fresh air. 'Baa!' cheered Woolly with pure excitement. There was a giant muddy puddle right in front of him. Without wasting a single second, Woolly hopped right into the middle of it. Splash! Mud and water went flying everywhere. A little brown duck quacked in surprise and waddled away. Woolly giggled and jumped again. Splash, splash, splish! His shiny red boots made the best squishy sounds. Soon, his friends came over to watch. Penny Pig trotted up and oinked happily. Sammy Chicken fluttered his feathers and chirped. They all thought Woolly looked so silly and wonderful in his big red boots. Woolly splashed until he was completely wet and his tummy was rumbling for lunch. He trotted back to the warm barn, taking off his boots with a gentle nudge. He munched on some delicious hay while watching the rain slow down. It had been the most fun rainy day ever, and Woolly couldn't wait to wear his boots again tomorrow.

stories.title: The Little Lost Bell
stories.text: Barnaby was a jolly little sheep who wore a shiny golden bell around his neck. Ting-a-ling, ting-a-ling went his bell whenever he skipped through the tall green meadow. Barnaby loved the sweet sound of his bell. It made him feel very important. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby was playing tag with his best friend, a fluffy white duck named Ducky. They ran through the tall grass, playing and laughing. Barnaby jumped over a little log. Wheee! But as he landed on the other side, something felt very light. He shook his head. Oh no! His precious golden bell was gone! Barnaby stopped and looked all around. The grass was very tall and green. 'Baa, baa,' he cried softly, feeling a little bit sad. Ducky waddled over and flapped his wings. 'Quack! Don't worry, Barnaby. We will find it together!' So the two friends began to search. They looked under big brown rocks. They peeked behind friendly yellow sunflowers. They even asked a wise old brown cow if she had seen a shiny bell. The cow mooed and shook her head gently. Just when Barnaby thought they would never find it, a little flutter caught his eye. Right under a patch of purple clover, something was catching the bright sunlight. Sparkle, sparkle! Barnaby trotted over quickly and nudged the clover out of the way. There it was! His wonderful golden bell was resting safely on a green leaf. Barnaby was so happy that he did a happy little dance. He picked up the bell and tied it securely around his neck again. Ting-a-ling, ting-a-ling! It sounded better than ever. Barnaby hugged his good friend Ducky, thankful for such a wonderful day of adventure on the farm.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text:
Once upon a little green hill, there lived a very fluffy little sheep named Sammy. Sammy had wool as soft as a marshmallow and hooves that went clickety-clack on the rocks. The sun was beginning to go down, and the sky turned a pretty shade of orange and pink. Yawn! Sammy let out a big sheep yawn. Baaaa! It was almost time for bed, but Sammy was not quite ready. He wanted to play one last game of hide-and-seek with his best friend, Pip the bunny. 

"Ready or not, here I come!" bleated Sammy gently. He closed his eyes and counted to three. One, two, three! Sammy opened his eyes and looked around the meadow. Where could Pip be? Sammy walked past the big oak tree. He walked past the sparkling blue brook. He looked behind a large patch of bright yellow daisies. No Pip! Then, Sammy heard a little giggle coming from behind a fuzzy bush. Rustle, rustle, rustle. Out popped Pip with a wiggle of his long ears! "You found me, Sammy!" cheered Pip happily. Sammy did a happy little hop. Playing hide-and-seek was so much fun, but now Sammy's eyelids felt very, very heavy. The night breeze whispered a gentle lullaby through the leaves. 

Sammy walked over to his cozy sleeping spot right next to his mama. Mama sheep gave Sammy a warm, comforting nuzzle on his fuzzy head. "Time for sleep, my sweet little lamb," whispered Mama softly. Sammy curled up into a soft, cozy ball in the sweet-smelling grass. He closed his eyes tight and thought about the bright yellow daisies and his fun game with Pip. The moon smiled down from the starry sky, shining a silver light over the peaceful meadow. Sammy took a deep, slow breath in, and let a slow breath out. Snug and warm in his thick woolly coat, Sammy drifted off into a deep, sweet sleep. Good night, Sammy Sheep. Sweet dreams until the morning sun wakes up the meadow again.

stories.title: Baa Baa's Big Blue Balloon
stories.text:
Bright and early one sunny morning, a little lamb named Baa Baa trotted out into the farmyard. Today was a very special day because the friendly farmer handed Baa Baa a shiny, bright blue balloon! It bounced and danced in the gentle morning breeze, tied tightly to Baa Baa's little hoof with a yellow ribbon. Baa Baa gasped with pure delight. "Baa!" he cheered, spinning around in a happy circle. The balloon bobbed up and down, looking just like a piece of the summer sky floating right here on the farm. 

Baa Baa wanted to show his wonderful balloon to all of his farmyard friends. First, he waddled over to Henny the hen who was pecking at the dirt. "Look, Henny! Look at my big blue balloon!" said Baa Baa. Henny clucked in surprise and fluffed her feathers. Next, Baa Baa bounced over to Barnaby the big brown horse, who was munching on some crunchy green hay. Barnaby gave a friendly neigh and gently bumped the balloon with his soft velvet nose. Boop! The balloon bounced away with a funny squeak, making Baa Baa giggle and chase after it on his little hooves. 

Around the red barn they went, past the muddy pigpen and over the little wooden bridge. The balloon floated higher and higher, pulling gently on the ribbon. Oh no! A tiny gust of wind lifted the balloon up, up, up towards the branches of the apple tree. Baa Baa reached up as high as his short little legs would let him, but he could not quite reach. Just then, a helpful little squirrel scampered down the trunk and caught the yellow ribbon. The squirrel handed the ribbon safely back to the happy little lamb. Baa Baa gave a grateful little bleat and hugged his balloon tight. What an exciting adventure for a little sheep on a sunny farm day!

stories.title: Woolly's Muddy Adventure
stories.text:
Woolly was a very clean sheep. His fleece was as white as freshly fallen winter snow, and he liked to keep it that way. Every morning, Woolly would graze on the green grass and sniff the sweet-smelling flowers, making sure not to get a single speck of dirt on his coat. But today, after a big morning rainstorm, something exciting and messy happened in the meadow. A giant, squishy, wonderfully muddy puddle had formed right in the middle of the path. All the other little farm animals were splashing and jumping right through it, having the most magnificent time imaginable. 

Duck was splashing with his webbed feet, going splash, splash, splash! Piggy was rolling around, going oink, oink, oink in the warm brown mud. Woolly stood at the edge of the puddle and watched. His little black nose twitched. He looked down at his clean white wool, and then he looked back at the slippery, squishy mud. "Baa?" wondered Woolly quietly. He took one little step closer. Then he took another little step. Suddenly, a playful breeze blew a leaf right into the middle of the puddle. Without even thinking, Woolly hopped right in! 

Squish, squash, squelch! went the mud between his little black hooves. It felt wonderfully warm and tickly. Woolly let out a joyful baa and gave a happy little shake. Splash went his front hoof, and splat went his back hoof! Before he knew it, Woolly was covered in brown mud from his head all the way to his fluffy tail. He looked like a chocolate sheep instead of a white one! He laughed and played with his friends all afternoon long, having the muddiest, best day of his entire life. When the sun finally began to set, Mama sheep brought over a warm bucket of bubbly water and gave Woolly a nice, soapy bath. Woolly was clean again, but he smiled as he remembered his wonderful, muddy adventure.

stories.title: Sammy the Sleepy Sheep
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green hill, there lived a little fluffy sheep named Sammy. Sammy had the softest white wool in the whole wide pasture. Every morning, the sun would peek over the mountains and say, 'Baa-good morning, Sammy!' And Sammy would jump up, wiggle his fuzzy tail, and trot over to his best friend, Barnaby the butterfly. Today was a very special day because Sammy wanted to learn how to bounce high like the little white clouds in the sky. Sammy bent his four little woolly legs. He squeezed his eyes tight. He said, 'One, two, three, BOUNCE!' But Sammy did not bounce into the sky. Oh no! Sammy went 'flop' right into a big, squishy patch of yellow daisies. Barnaby the butterfly giggled, fluttered his colorful wings, and landed right on Sammy's black nose. 'Tickle, tickle, buzz, buzz!' laughed Barnaby. Sammy sneezed a happy sheep sneeze—'Achoo!'—and the daisies tickled his tummy. Just then, Mama Sheep came walking over. She had a warm, cozy smile and wool that was just as soft as Sammy's. 'Time for a snack, my sweet little lamb,' said Mama Sheep. She led Sammy down to the cool, clear stream where they drank sweet, sparkling water. After their yummy drink, Sammy felt his heavy eyelids start to droop. Running and bouncing all morning makes a little sheep very, very tired. Mama Sheep nuzzled Sammy close, wrapping him in a warm woolly hug. Sammy let out a long, sleepy yawn. 'Baa-night, Mama,' whispered Sammy softly. He curled up in the soft green grass, closed his eyes, and dreamed about bouncing on fluffy white clouds all the way to sleepyland. Goodnight, Sammy.

stories.title: Pip's Missing Wool
stories.text: Pip was a tiny, curious sheep with curly wool and big, brown, wondering eyes. Pip loved to explore the farmyard every single morning after breakfast. One bright Tuesday, Pip woke up, shook his fluffy coat, and noticed something very strange. 'Baa? Where is my left side?' Pip wondered aloud. A little piece of his fluffy white wool was missing! Pip looked down by the wooden fence, and there it was—a tiny tuft of soft white wool caught on a pointy twig. 'Oh no!' said Pip. 'My wool is running away!' Pip decided to follow the trail of fluffy white tufts to find his missing wool. He trotted past the red barn where the big brown horse was eating sweet hay. 'Neigh, little Pip, have you seen my breakfast?' asked the horse. 'No,' said Pip, 'I am looking for my runaway wool!' Pip kept trotting until he reached the muddy pigpen. The pink piggy rolled in the mud and oinked, 'Oink, oink, look at my mud boots!' Pip giggled and kept following the white tufts all the way to the big oak tree. Guess what Pip found under the tree? It was a family of tiny baby birds! They were sitting in a cozy nest made completely of Pip's soft, fluffy wool. The mother bird chirped happily and said, 'Tweet, tweet, thank you, kind sheep, to keep our babies warm while they sleep.' Pip smiled his biggest sheep smile. He didn't need that little bit of wool anymore because helping tiny birds was much more important. Pip trotted back to his mama, feeling warm and happy inside, ready for a cozy afternoon nap in the golden sunshine.

stories.title: Bo Peep's Bright Blue Bow
stories.text: High up on the rolling green hills, where the sky was bright blue and the wind blew gently, lived a cheerful little sheep named Clover. Clover had the curliest coat of wool you ever did see, and today she had a very important mission. She found a shiny, bright blue bow in the grass, and she wanted to wear it on her head for the grand farm parade! Clover trotted over to her friend, Bella the cow. 'Moo, Clover, that blue bow looks lovely on your fluffy head!' said Bella. Clover did a happy little spin, showing off her wonderful bow to all the farm animals. But oh dear! A sudden gust of wind came swooshing through the trees. *Whoosh!* The wind blew hard, and *pop*, the bright blue bow flew right off Clover's head! It danced up into the air, fluttering like a little blue bird. 'Baa! Come back, bow!' cried Clover, and she began to trot as fast as her little hooves could carry her. The bow blew over the wooden bridge. It blew past the duck pond where the yellow ducklings were swimming in a row. *Splash, quack, quack!* Finally, the silly wind got tired and gently dropped the bright blue bow right onto a low, friendly apple tree branch. Clover stopped right underneath the tree. She stood on her tiptoes, stretched her neck up high, and gave a gentle nibble. *Snip!* She caught the bow in her mouth and safely placed it back on her fluffy head. Clover let out a happy baa of triumph. She trotted proudly all the way back home, her blue bow shining in the sun, ready to tell all her sheep friends about her big, windy adventure.

stories.title: Sammy the Sleepy Sheep
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green hill, there lived a little white sheep named Sammy. Sammy had the softest, fluffiest wool in the whole flock. It felt just like a big, warm cloud! Every morning, the shepherd would ring a shiny silver bell, and all the sheep would wake up ready to play. Baa, baa, went the big sheep. Baa, baa, went the little lambs. They would run and jump and skip across the meadow. But not Sammy! Sammy was very, very sleepy. While his friends played tag in the clover, Sammy let out a big yawn. Yaaawn! He blinked his heavy, sleepy eyes and looked around for a cozy place to nap. First, he tried to sleep under a big green tree, but the little ants tickled his hooves. Tickle, tickle, go away ants! Then, he tried to nap by the babbling brook, but the splashing water was too loud. Splish, splash, gurgle, gurgle! Sammy walked a little further until he found a soft patch of yellow dandelions. This looks just right, thought Sammy. He curled his fluffy white body into a tiny ball and closed his eyes. The warm sunshine wrapped around him like a golden blanket. A gentle breeze whispered lullabies through the grass. Soon, Sammy was fast asleep, snoring softly. Snore, snore, went little Sammy. While he slept, he dreamed of jumping over the moon, floating on cotton candy clouds, and eating fields of sweet, green grass. The other sheep tiptoed past him so they would not wake him up. When the sun began to set and paint the sky in pink and purple, Sammy finally opened his eyes. He stretched his front legs way out and gave another big yawn. He felt rested, happy, and full of energy! The shepherd blew his whistle, and Sammy bounded back to his flock, ready for bedtime stories under the starry night sky. Goodnight, Sammy. Sweet dreams, little sheep.

stories.title: Buttons the Woolly Jumper
stories.text: High up on the rolling green hills lived a happy little sheep named Buttons. Buttons was very special because she was not just fluffy—she was extra, extra curly! Her wool bounced up and down every single time she took a little hop. Boing, boing, went Buttons' woolly coat. One sunny morning, Buttons woke up with a big smile because it was Shearing Day! The friendly farmer came walking up the path with a shiny pair of buzzing clippers. Bzzzz, went the clippers. Do not worry, little ones, said the farmer with a kind laugh. A haircut just helps you stay cool and light for the summer! All the other sheep lined up patiently, feeling a little nervous. But Buttons was brave and excited. When it was her turn, she sat very still. Snippity-snip, clackity-clack, off came her heavy wool in one big, fluffy fleece that looked just like a giant white pillow. Buttons stood up and gasped. Oh! Without her heavy coat, she felt as light as a feather! She could run faster than the wind, spin in circles, and leap high into the air. Wheee! shouted Buttons as she zoomed down the hill. But wait, what happened to all that wonderful wool? The farmer gathered up the fleece, washed it sparkling clean in the farm basin, and took it to the cozy farmhouse. There, the farmer's wife used her spinning wheel to spin the wool into long, bright red yarn. Whirr, whirr, went the spinning wheel. Then, using two wooden knitting needles, she knitted the yarn into a brand new, wonderfully warm, bright red jumper. The next day, the farmer brought the jumper outside and slipped it right over Buttons' head. It had shiny yellow buttons down the front, just like her name! Buttons looked down at her new outfit and did a happy little dance. Her woolly jumper kept her cozy on chilly nights, and she was the most stylish sheep on the whole farm.

stories.title: Pip Finds a Friend
stories.text: Down by the old wooden red barn, there lived a tiny baby lamb named Pip. Pip was the smallest sheep in the flock, and he had floppy ears that bounced when he walked. Flop, flop, went his little ears. Pip loved to explore the farmyard, but today, he felt just a little bit lonely. The big sheep were busy eating clover, and the mother sheep were resting in the shade. I want a friend to play with, whispered Pip with a little baa. So, he set off on a grand adventure across the farmyard to find a playmate. First, he trotted over to the muddy pigpen. There he saw a pink piggy splashing in the cool, brown mud. Oink, oink! said the piggy. Do you want to jump in the mud with me, Pip? Pip looked down at his clean, snowy-white wool. Oh no, he thought. If I jump in the mud, my fleece will turn brown! So, Pip shook his head and said, No thank you, piggy, I like my wool clean. Next, Pip hopped over to the big red tractor. Perched right on top was a fluffy yellow duckling. Quack, quack! said the duckling. Do you want to go for a swim in the deep blue pond with me, Pip? Pip looked at the deep water and shivered. Oh no, he thought. Sheep do not know how to swim, we float like corks! So, Pip shook his head and said, No thank you, duckling, I am not a swimmer. Feeling sad, Pip sat down by the garden gate and let out a tiny, soft sigh. Just then, he felt a tickle on his nose. A-achoo! sneezed Pip. Right in front of him was another little lamb about his exact same size. This lamb had brown spots on her ears and a very wiggly tail. Hello! said the new lamb. My name is Penny. Do you want to play hide-and-seek behind the hay bales with me? Pip's ears perched straight up, and his tail wagged with joy. Yes, please! said Pip. For the rest of the sunny afternoon, Pip and Penny played the best game of hide-and-seek ever. They giggled, skipped, and chased butterflies together until the sun went down. Pip was not lonely anymore because he had found his very best friend in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a fluffy time, there was a little lamb named Sammy Sheep. Sammy had the softest, woolliest coat in the whole green meadow. His wool was as white as a fluffy marshmallow and as warm as a big hug from Mama Sheep. The sun was beginning to go down, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. The stars were starting to peek out like little silver nightlights. It was almost time for bed, but Sammy did not want to sleep just yet. He wanted to play! Sammy bounced across the soft grass. Boing, boing, boing went his little hooves. He tried to play hide-and-seek with his friend, Barnaby the Butterfly. Barnaby fluttered his bright yellow wings and landed right on Sammy’s black nose. 'Baa-aah!' giggled Sammy, making his nose wiggle. Barnaby flew up to the big oak tree, and Sammy trotted right behind him. But as Sammy looked up at the tree, he let out a very big, loud yawn. *Yaaawn!* His little eyes felt as heavy as two big stones. Mama Sheep walked over to him, her bell going *tinkle, tinkle, tonk* in the gentle evening breeze. She nuzzled Sammy’s soft neck and said, 'Time for bed, my little cloud.' Sammy knew Mama was right. He walked over to his favorite cozy spot in the tall clover. He curled up into a tight, furry ball, tucking his little hooves underneath his fluffy tummy. The cool night air blew softly, but Sammy was as warm as toast inside his thick wool coat. Mama Sheep sang a sweet, quiet lullaby, and the crickets joined in with a gentle *chirp, chirp*. Sammy closed his eyes tightly. He thought about bouncing with butterflies and playing in the green meadow. Slowly, his breathing grew deep and steady. *In and out. In and out.* Sammy Sheep drifted off to sleep, dreaming of fluffy white clouds and sweet green clover. Good night, Sammy Sheep.

stories.title: Sammy's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the green farm, and the grass sparkled with morning dew. Sammy Sheep woke up with a happy skip. *Baa!* Today was a wonderful day for a walk. Sammy trotted over to the big wooden fence where his animal friends lived. First, he saw Ducky splashing in a big puddle. *Quack, quack!* Ducky was having so much fun making big yellow splashes in the water. Sammy tilted his head. He had never made a splash before. He walked a little closer to the puddle. The ground felt squishy and wet under his small black hooves. *Squish, squish, squish!* It felt tickly and fun. Sammy took one more step. *Plop!* His front hoof went right into the mud. Oh, it was so delightfully messy! Sammy decided to tap his foot. *Stomp, stomp, stomp!* Mud flew up into the air and landed right on his white wool. Now Sammy Sheep had a big brown spot on his side. He looked down and giggled, making a funny little noise. 'Baa-aah!' Just then, Farmer Farmer walked by with a bucket of crisp, red apples. He stopped and looked at Sammy. 'Well, look at you, little muddy sheep!' laughed the farmer. Sammy shook his head happily. But muddy wool can get very heavy and itchy. Mama Sheep trotted over with a warm smile. 'Time for a wash, my muddy little lamb,' she said gently. Mama led Sammy down to the sparkling blue brook. The water was cool and refreshing on his warm skin. *Splash, swish, bubble!* Mama helped him wash away all the silly brown mud. Sammy kicked his legs and played in the shallow water, watching the mud wash away downstream. Soon, Sammy was as clean and white as a fresh pile of snow again. He shook his fluffy coat, sending tiny crystal droplets flying everywhere like diamonds in the sun. Sammy learned that muddy puddles are wonderfully fun to visit, but being a clean, fluffy sheep feels pretty great too. He trotted back to the green meadow, ready for his next big farm adventure.

stories.title: The Big Woolly Sweater
stories.text: Winter was coming to the farm, and the wind was starting to blow. *Whoosh, whoosh!* went the chilly wind through the bare trees. Sammy Sheep shivered a little bit. He fluffed out his thick woolly coat to keep himself warm. 'Baa-aah,' he said softly, blowing a little puff of white air into the cold morning sky. His friend, Pip the farm mouse, scurried past wearing a tiny red scarf around his neck. 'Brrr, Sammy! It is getting so cold!' squeaked Pip. Sammy looked down at his own fluffy coat. He had so much wool! It was the thickest, softest wool on the whole farm. Suddenly, Sammy had a very kind idea. If he had so much warm wool, maybe he could share some with his friends who didn't have cozy winter coats. Sammy trotted happily over to Farmer Ben. Farmer Ben was sitting on the wooden porch drinking warm apple cider. Sammy gave the farmer's boot a gentle nudge with his wet black nose and said, 'Baa!' Farmer Ben smiled down at the little sheep. 'Ah, Sammy. Are you ready for your winter haircut?' he asked kindly. Sammy nodded his head up and down. Farmer Ben brought out his gentle, buzzing clippers. *Bzzzz, bzzzz!* went the clippers, but they didn't hurt at all. They just tickled Sammy's skin. Soft, fluffy piles of white wool began to fall all around him, like warm summer snowflakes. Soon, Sammy was feeling nice and light. Farmer Ben took the big bags of fluffy wool inside his warm yellow farmhouse. He spun the wool into soft yarn and knitted wonderful winter clothes for everyone on the farm. A few days later, Pip the mouse came out wearing a brand new, super-soft white sweater made from Sammy's very own wool. Little yellow ducky had a tiny woolly vest, and even Farmer Ben wore a cozy wool hat. Sammy felt so happy and warm inside, even without his heavy coat. Sharing his warm wool made his heart feel as cozy as could be, all winter long.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little fluffy sheep named Sammy. Sammy had wool as white as a fluffy cloud and hooves that went click-clack on the stones. The sun was beginning to set, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink and orange. It was almost time for bed, but Sammy was not sleepy at all! 'Baa-baa,' cried Sammy, bouncing up and down. 'I want to play!' First, Sammy trotted over to his friend Benny the Bunny. 'Do you want to hop with me?' asked Sammy. Benny shook his long ears. 'No, Sammy, it is time to sleep. Look at the stars.' Sammy looked up, but he still wanted to play. Next, Sammy scampered over to Penny the Pig. 'Do you want to splash in the mud with me?' asked Sammy. Penny grunted and yawned. 'No, Sammy, my eyes are heavy. It is time to rest.' Sammy trotted back to his cozy barn. The wise old owl hooted softly from the rafters. 'Hoot hoot, little sheep, counting stars is a good way to sleep.' Sammy curled up on his bed of sweet-smelling hay. He closed his eyes and began to count. One little star, two little stars, three little white clouds in the sky. Sammy felt his soft wool getting heavier and heavier. His little legs stopped dancing. His ears drooped down. He let out a long, cozy yawn. 'Baa,' whispered Sammy, drifting off to dreamland. Goodnight, Sammy Sheep. Sweet dreams until the morning sun wakes you up to play again.

stories.title: Sammy's Woolly Sweater
stories.text: It was a chilly autumn morning on the farm, and a cold breeze was blowing through the grass. Whoosh! Sammy the little sheep shivered. He hugged himself with his tiny hooves. 'Baa-baa,' shivered Sammy. 'I am so cold!' The other sheep were all cozy in their thick coats, but Sammy had just gotten a haircut, and his wool was still growing back. Farmer Jill saw Sammy shivering and smiled warmly. 'Do not worry, little Sammy,' she said gently. 'I have just the thing for you.' Farmer Jill went inside her red farmhouse and came back out with a wonderful surprise. It was a bright red sweater with yellow duckies on it! She helped Sammy put his head through the hole and his front legs through the sleeves. Pop! Sammy looked down at his new outfit. It was warm, soft, and so colorful. Sammy felt a big smile spread across his face. He trotted over to the duck pond to show off his new look to his friends. 'Quack quack!' said the ducks, flapping their wings in approval. 'Baa-baa!' bleated Sammy happily, doing a little spin. The red sweater kept him as snug as a bug all morning long. He ran and jumped through the crunchy yellow leaves without feeling a single shiver. When lunchtime came, Sammy ate his green grass with extra joy. He loved his fuzzy red sweater so much that he did not even want to take it off for naptime. As the sun warmed up the afternoon, Sammy curled up in the hay, wearing his favorite sweater, feeling loved, warm, and very happy.

stories.title: Sammy and the Lost Bell
stories.text: Ting-a-ling-ling! Went the little silver bell around Sammy Sheep's neck as he trotted through the meadow. Sammy loved his shiny bell. It made a happy sound every time he jumped or skipped. But today, something terrible happened. Sammy was running through the tall buttercups when he felt a sudden lightness. Oh no! The shiny bell had slipped right off his red ribbon! Sammy stopped and looked all around the grass. 'Baa-baa!' he cried in distress. 'Where is my bell?' He searched under the big green leaves. He looked behind the wooden fence. But the bell was nowhere to be seen. Just then, his friendly duck friend, Ducky Daddles, waddled by. 'Quack! What is the matter, Sammy?' asked the duck. 'I lost my shiny bell,' Sammy explained sadly. 'Let us look together!' said Ducky Daddles. They searched high and low. Ducky Daddles peeked in the pond, and Sammy looked in the hay. Suddenly, a little chirping sound came from a bush. Tweet-tweet! A tiny bluebird was hopping around a sparkly object. 'Look,' whispered Ducky Daddles. Sammy crept closer on his soft hooves. There, nestled right in the middle of a yellow dandelion patch, was his shiny silver bell! The little bluebird thought it looked like a lovely toy. Sammy gently nudged the bell with his soft nose. 'Baa-thank you, little bird,' he said kindly. The bird flew up to the sky with a happy chirp. Sammy tied the bell back onto his ribbon with the help of Farmer Jill. Ting-a-ling-ling! It rang out louder and sweeter than before. Sammy jumped for joy, so happy to have his favorite bell back where it belonged.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green hill, there lived a little fluffy sheep named Sammy. Sammy had the softest, curliest white wool in the whole wide world. Every morning, Sammy woke up with the bright yellow sun. He would stretch his front legs, wiggle his tiny tail, and say, 'Baa, baa, good morning, daisy flowers!' Sammy loved to spend his days playing tag with his best friend, a little brown bunny named Pip. They would hop and skip all over the meadow, chasing butterflies and chewing on sweet, crunchy green grass. But when the afternoon sun began to dip behind the big green mountains, Sammy started to feel very, very sleepy. His heavy eyelids would blink slowly, and he would let out a long, cozy yawn. 'Yaaawn!' said Sammy. His mama, Mother Sheep, would walk over and give him a warm, gentle nuzzle. 'Time to get ready for bed, my sweet little lamb,' she would whisper softly. Sammy trotted over to his favorite patch of soft, clover-filled grass right next to a big oak tree. He curled his legs underneath his warm, fluffy body and made himself into a tight little ball of wool. The friendly breeze whispered a quiet lullaby through the leaves of the tree. Sammy closed his big brown eyes and listened to the gentle sounds of the meadow settling down for the night. Crickets began to chirp their sleepy song, and fireflies flickered their glowing lights like tiny yellow stars in the grass. Sammy thought about all the fun things he and Pip had done that day. He remembered the yellow butterfly that landed on his nose and the delicious clover he had eaten for lunch. A happy little smile spread across Sammy's sleepy face. He took a deep, deep breath of the fresh evening air, feeling safe and loved. Mother Sheep lay down right beside him, keeping him warm and protected under the starry night sky. Sammy let out one last tiny yawn, snuggled even closer to his mama, and drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep, dreaming of fluffy white clouds and sweet green grass until the morning sun would rise again.

stories.title: Sammy's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: It was a wonderful, rainy morning on the farm, and little Sammy Sheep was feeling very curious. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the gentle raindrops as they fell from the big gray clouds high up in the sky. Sammy loved the rain because it made all the flowers grow big and tall. But today, the rain had created something even more exciting right in the middle of the green meadow. It had made a big, squishy, brown puddle of mud! Sammy trotted over to the edge of the puddle and looked down. He could see his own reflection staring right back up at him. 'Baa!' said Sammy with a little wiggle of his nose. He thought the mud looked like chocolate pudding. Now, Sammy's mama had always told him to keep his white wool clean, but the puddle looked like the most fun place in the whole wide world. Sammy dipped one small, black hoof right into the edge of the mud. *Squish!* It felt so warm and tickly between his toes. Sammy giggled and dipped his other hoof in. *Squelch!* Before he knew what he was doing, Sammy took a little hop right into the middle of the puddle. Splash went the brown mud in every single direction! A tiny drop of mud landed right on his nose, and Sammy shook his fluffy head, making his wool wobble all around. He had never felt anything so silly and fun in his whole life. He splashed with his left foot, and then he splashed with his right foot, making little muddy bubbles pop in the air. But just a few minutes later, Sammy heard a familiar voice calling out across the grass. 'Baa-baa-baa!' called Mother Sheep, walking over with a gentle smile. Sammy looked down at his once-white wool, which was now covered in brown spots. He looked a little worried that he might be in trouble. Instead, Mother Sheep chuckled softly and nuzzled his muddy head. 'Well, little one, you certainly know how to have an adventure,' she said lovingly. Together, they walked over to a fresh, clean stream of water where Sammy could wash all the mud away. Sammy splashed happily in the clean water, feeling refreshed, clean, and so very happy after his wonderfully muddy day.

stories.title: The Great Wooly Sweater
stories.text: The autumn winds were starting to blow across the green hills, and little Sammy Sheep noticed that the air was getting a little bit chilly. *Brrr!* shivered Sammy, rubbing his little hooves together. His thick, curly wool coat was getting very long and very heavy, and he knew exactly what that meant. It was almost time for the big annual shearing day on the farm! The farmer, a kind man named Farmer John, walked out into the meadow carrying a pair of shiny, clicking shears. 'Hello there, little Sammy,' Farmer John said with a warm, friendly smile. Sammy wasn't scared at all because he knew Farmer John was gentle and nice. Sammy stood very still while Farmer John worked his magic. *Snip, snip, snip* went the shears. With every gentle snip, a big, fluffy blanket of white wool fell away from Sammy's body. It felt like taking off a heavy winter coat on a hot day! Sammy felt so light and bouncy that he immediately did a happy little jump in the air. When Farmer John was all done, Sammy looked down and saw a huge, mountain-sized pile of his very own soft white wool sitting right on the green grass. He let out a curious 'Baa?' wondering what would happen to all that wonderful wool. A few days later, Sammy found out. Farmer John's wife, a kind woman with a bright red sweater, took the wool and spun it into long, strong threads of yarn. Then, she used knitting needles to turn the yarn into the warmest, softest, coziest little red sweater you have ever seen. When the winter snow finally started to fall outside, Farmer John brought the little red sweater out to the meadow and slipped it gently over Sammy's head. It fit him like a warm hug from his favorite person. Sammy walked around the snowy farm showing off his stylish new outfit to all his animal friends. The little brown bunny, Pip, hopped up and touched the soft red yarn with his nose. 'Baa-baa-hoo!' cheered Sammy, feeling wonderfully warm and snug all winter long, wearing his very own wooly sweater.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text:
Once upon a fluffy green hill, there lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the softest, curliest white wool in the whole wide world. It felt just like a big marshmallow! Every morning, the sun would wake up with a bright yellow yawn, and Sammy would jump out of bed to start his day. Today was a very special day because Sammy was going to learn how to play hide and seek with his farm friends. 

First, Sammy went to find Bella the brown cow. 'Moo, moo!' said Bella. 'I am hiding behind the big red barn!' Sammy giggled and trotted as fast as his little hooves could carry him. He peeked behind the barn doors, but Bella was too big. Then, he looked up, and there was Bella's tail swishing in the wind. 'Found you!' baaed Sammy happily. 

Next, it was Sammy's turn to hide. He squeezed his eyes shut so tight he thought they might pop. One, two, three, four, five! He crouched down low in the patch of yellow daisies. The daisies tickled his nose. Ah-choo! Sammy sneezed a big sheep sneeze. 'Baa-choo!' 

'I hear a sneeze!' called out Penny the pink pig. Penny trotted over and gently nudged Sammy with her snout. 'Found you in the flowers, Sammy!' They all laughed and clapped their hooves and trotted around the meadow in a happy circle. 

As the afternoon sun began to dip down low, painting the sky in lovely shades of orange and purple, Sammy started to feel a little bit sleepy. His little black hooves felt heavy, and his eyelids felt droopy. He walked back to his cozy pen where his mama was waiting with a warm, comforting hug. Sammy snuggled close into his mama's soft wool. She hummed a sweet, gentle lullaby that sounded just like the whispering wind. Sammy let out a long, happy sigh. He closed his eyes and drifted off to dreamland, ready for more fun adventures when the sun woke up again tomorrow. Goodnight, Sammy.

stories.title: Buttons the Woolly Jumper
stories.text:
High up on the windy hilltop lived a bouncy little lamb named Buttons. Buttons was no ordinary lamb. While all the other sheep had plain white fleece, Buttons had fleece that changed color whenever he felt a big emotion! When he was excited, his wool sparkled like tiny stars. When he was curious, his wool turned a bright, sunny yellow. 

One sunny morning, Buttons woke up feeling very curious indeed. He trotted over to the farmer's clothesline where a bunch of colorful laundry was dancing in the breeze. 'Baa! Look at all those pretty colors,' Buttons whispered to himself. He scampered closer to investigate. There were red shirts, blue socks, and green trousers flapping up and down. 

Suddenly, a strong gust of wind blew a bright blue sock right off the clothesline. It fluttered through the air like a little bird and landed right on top of Buttons' head! Buttons giggled. He looked into a shiny puddle of rainwater to see his reflection. With the blue sock on his head, his yellow curious wool peeked out from underneath, making him look like a funny, woolly sunflower. 

Just then, his friend Pip the duck waddled by. 'Quack, quack! Nice hat, Buttons!' said Pip, flapping his wings in delight. Buttons felt so happy that his wool started to sparkle with bright pink polka dots. He spun around in a circle, doing a silly little lamb dance. Pip joined in, waddling and quacking to the rhythm of the wind. 

They danced all morning until their tummy rumbles told them it was time for lunch. Buttons trotted over to the patch of sweet clover and munched on the green grass until he was full. As the afternoon shadows grew long, Buttons sat down on the soft grass, feeling warm, happy, and delightfully sleepy. His wool turned back to a cozy, comforting white. He curled up into a little ball, closed his eyes, and dreamed of dancing socks and sunny skies. What a wonderful day it had been for the colorful little lamb.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Balloon
stories.text:
Down by the sparkling blue stream, there lived a curious little sheep named Barnaby. Barnaby loved to collect shiny things. He had shiny pebbles, shiny leaves, and even a shiny silver wrapper that the farmer had dropped. But more than anything, Barnaby dreamed of touching the sky. He wanted to know what the fluffy white clouds tasted like. Were they made of cotton candy? Were they cool like morning dew? 

One bright afternoon, the village children came to visit the farm for a birthday party. They brought colorful party balloons. There were red ones, green ones, and a big, shiny yellow balloon that bobbed up and down on a long, sparkly string. Barnaby's eyes grew as big as saucers. He trotted over as quietly as a mouse, his little hooves going tip-tap, tip-tap on the grass. 

When a friendly little boy named Leo got distracted by a butterfly, the string of the yellow balloon slipped gently from his hand. Up, up, up went the balloon toward the sky! Barnaby knew he had to act fast. With a joyful 'Baa!', he leaped into the air and gently caught the sparkly string with his teeth. 

He didn't float away to the clouds, but holding the string made him feel like he was flying. The yellow balloon bobbed right above his head like a little sun. Leo turned around and saw Barnaby holding the string. 'Look! Barnaby has the balloon!' Leo cheered, clapping his hands. 

The other children ran over, laughing and playing games around the happy sheep. Barnaby trotted proudly across the meadow, holding the balloon tight so it wouldn't float away. When the party finally ended, Leo tied the balloon securely to the wooden fence post so Barnaby could look at it all afternoon. Barnaby nuzzled the fence post lovingly, feeling like the luckiest sheep in the entire world. As the sun began to set, painting the fluffy clouds pink and gold, Barnaby smiled. He didn't need to taste the clouds after all, because having such wonderful friends was sweeter than any cotton candy in the sky.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a sunny green hill, there lived a little fluffy sheep named Sammy. Sammy had the softest, whitest fleece in the whole wide meadow. Every morning, Sammy woke up with the bright yellow sun. He would stretch his front legs, wiggle his little tail, and say, 'Baa, baa, good morning, world!' Sammy loved to spend his mornings playing games with his best friends. His very favorite game was hide-and-seek. Sammy would close his eyes tightly and count to three. One, two, three! Then, he would trot around looking for his friends behind the big green bushes. Sometimes, he found Bella the butterfly resting on a flower. Sometimes, he found Pip the little bunny hiding in the tall grass. Sammy always gave a happy little jump when he found them. But when the afternoon sun started to sink low in the sky, Sammy would begin to feel a little bit sleepy. His little hooves felt heavy, and his eyelids felt droopy. It was almost time for naptime. Sammy's mommy would walk over to him and give him a warm, gentle nuzzle. 'Time to rest your woolly head, my sweet little lamb,' Mommy Sheep would whisper softly. Sammy would lie down on the soft green grass, which felt just like a cozy green mattress. He would close his big brown eyes and listen to the gentle breeze whispering through the trees. As he drifted off to sleep, he dreamed of fluffy white clouds that looked just like him, floating softly across the blue sky. Goodnight, Sammy Sheep. Sleep tight and sweet dreams in the meadow.

stories.title: Sammy's Woolly Jumper
stories.text: It was a breezy autumn morning on the farm, and the wind was blowing very hard. Whoosh, went the wind! Little Sammy Sheep stood by the wooden fence and shivered. Brrr! It was getting quite chilly outside, and Sammy did not have a coat. Just then, Farmer John walked into the paddock carrying a big basket of colorful yarn. 'Good morning, Sammy,' said Farmer John with a kind smile. 'The weather is turning cold, so it is time to make you a brand new, warm woolly jumper!' Sammy let out a happy little 'Baa!' because he loved the idea of a cozy new outfit. Farmer John gently brushed Sammy's thick, curly fleece. Then, using special sheep shears, he gently trimmed away the extra wool. Snip, snip, snip went the shiny scissors. It did not hurt at all; in fact, it felt like a nice, tickly massage! Sammy felt so light and bouncy without all that heavy wool. Farmer John took the fluffy white wool to his workshop. He spun the wool into soft yarn and dyed it bright, cheerful colors like sunny yellow, sky blue, and apple red. Then, he knitted it all together into a wonderful, snuggly jumper just for Sammy. When Farmer John came back out to the field, he slipped the bright red jumper right over Sammy's head. Sammy looked down at his tummy and smiled from ear to ear. The jumper fit him like a glove and kept him wonderfully warm against the chilly wind. Sammy trotted over to his friends to show off his new clothes. 'Look at me!' he seemed to say with a happy bounce. From that day on, Sammy was the coziest, warmest, and most stylish little sheep in the whole farmyard.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Finds a Lost Bell
stories.text: One bright and sunny afternoon, Sammy Sheep was munching on some sweet clover by the edge of the babbling brook. Suddenly, he heard a funny little sound coming from the tall yellow flowers. Tinkly-tonk, tinkly-tonk went the noise. Sammy stopped chewing and tilted his head. He took a few quiet steps closer, stepping softly on his little hooves. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter. Right there in the middle of the buttercups, something was shining in the sunlight. Sammy lowered his velvety nose and sniffed. It was a shiny silver bell attached to a bright red ribbon! But the bell looked very sad because it was lost and did not have anyone to wear it. 'Baa?' said Sammy softly, asking if the bell was okay. The little bell gave a soft jingle, as if saying hello. Sammy knew just what to do. He gently picked up the red ribbon with his teeth and trotted over to his friend, Barnaby the big brown horse. 'Excuse me, Barnaby, do you know who this bell belongs to?' Sammy seemed to ask. Barnaby neighed gently and shook his head. Then Sammy asked Penelope the playful pig. Penelope snorted and shook her curly tail. Nobody knew whose bell it was! Just then, little Lily the lamb came running over, looking very worried. She was searching everywhere for her favorite shiny necklace. When Lily saw Sammy holding the bell, her face lit up with joy. 'My bell!' she cried happily. Sammy gently placed the shiny bell back around Lily's neck. Tinkly-tonk, it rang out happily. Lily gave Sammy a big, grateful nudge. Sammy smiled a big sheepish smile, feeling so happy that he had helped his little friend find her treasured bell on the sunny farm.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a fluffy green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the softest, woolliest coat in the whole wide pasture. Every morning, the warm sun would wake Sammy up with a gentle nudge. "Baa, baa!" said Sammy, stretching his little legs. He loved to bounce up and down in the soft clover. Boing, boing, boing went Sammy! He would chase fluttering yellow butterflies and say hello to the buzzy bees. The butterflies danced in the air, and the bees went buzz, buzz, buzz. Sammy thought it was the best day ever. But soon, the big yellow sun started to go down behind the tall mountains. The sky turned into a pretty pink and purple blanket. Sammy let out a big yawn. Yaaawn! His little eyelids felt very heavy. The other sheep were already snuggling together in the cozy grass. Sammy trotted over to his mother, who gave him a warm nuzzle. "Time for bed, my little lamb," whispered Mama Sheep. Sammy closed his eyes and dreamed of sweet green grass and fluffy white clouds. Good night, Sammy Sheep.
