Sleep tight until the morning sun wakes you up for another happy day of bouncing in the meadow.

stories.title: Pip's First Jump
stories.text: Pip was a tiny sheep with big, bouncy legs. Today was a very special day because Pip was going to learn how to jump over the little brook! Pip walked to the edge of the water and looked down. Splash, splash went the little stream over the shiny pebbles. A friendly little frog popped up and said, "Ribbit! You can do it, little sheep!" Pip took one step back. Then, Pip took two steps back. He shook his fluffy tail and got ready. Ready, set, go! Pip leaped high into the air. He felt like he was flying like a bird in the bright blue sky. But oh dear! Pip did not quite make it across. Splash! Right into the cool, shallow water went Pip. The frog giggled, "Ribbit, ribbit! That was a fun splash!" Pip shook the water off his wool. Shake, shake, shake went Pip, making sparkly water drops fly everywhere. He did not give up. Pip tried again with a mighty bounce. Boing! Up, up, up he went. And WHOOSH! Pip landed safely on the other side of the brook. "Yay!" cheered all the farm animals. Pip felt so proud and happy. He danced a happy little sheep dance in the green grass to celebrate his very first successful jump.

stories.title: The Woolly Jumper
stories.text: It was a chilly autumn morning on the farm, and a little lamb named Barnaby was shivering. Brrr! The wind was blowing the red and yellow leaves all around. "Baa, I am so cold," shivered Barnaby. The kind farmer walked by with a big pair of shiny shears. Snip, snip, go the shears, and off came Barnaby's extra woolly coat. The farmer took the soft wool inside the warm farmhouse. He spun the wool into thick, cozy red yarn. Spin, spin, spin went the spinning wheel. Then, the farmer knitted the red yarn into a brand new, wonderful woolly jumper. When the farmer came back outside, he held up the little red jumper. "This is for you, Barnaby," said the farmer with a warm smile. Barnaby put his head right through the neck hole. The jumper fit him just right! It was warm, soft, and bright red like a juicy apple. Barnaby trotted over to the sheep pond to look at his reflection. He looked wonderful! Barnaby felt as warm as toast. He could jump and play in the chilly wind without feeling cold at all. "Thank you!" baaed Barnaby happily, doing a joyful little spin to show his friends his brand new, lovely red woolly jumper.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes Splash
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in a big green meadow, lived a little fluffy sheep named Sammy. Sammy had wool as white as a marshmallow and as soft as a cloud. Every morning, Sammy would wake up and say, "Baa! Good morning, sun! Good morning, grass!" Sammy loved to eat green grass. Nibble, nibble, munch, munch went his little mouth. But today was not just any ordinary day. Today was very, very hot. The sun was shining bright in the blue sky. Whew! It was warm. Sammy felt hot under his thick, woolly coat. He fanned his little ears. He stomped his little hooves. "Baa! I am too warm!" said Sammy. Just then, his best friend, Pip the duck, came waddling by. Quack, quack! Pip was heading down to the cool, shimmering pond. "Hello, Sammy! Are you coming for a swim?" asked Pip. Sammy looked at the sparkling water. He had never been swimming before. His fleece was so heavy! Would he float? Sammy took one step forward. Then another. Squish, squash went his hooves in the muddy bank. The water touched his little black toes. Ooh, it felt so cool and nice! Sammy smiled a big sheep smile. "Baa! Here I come!" With a joyful hop, Sammy bounced right into the shallow edge of the pond. Splash! Water went everywhere. Pip flapped his wings and quacked with delight. Sammy bobbed up and down in the water. His heavy wool soaked up the cool liquid, but Sammy did not sink at all. He floated like a fluffy white boat! "Baa-ha-ha! This is so much fun!" laughed Sammy. He splashed the water with his hooves. Splish, splash, splosh! The water droplets sparkled in the sunshine like little diamonds. Sammy felt so refreshed and happy. He wasn't hot anymore. After a long time playing in the water, Sammy waded back out onto the warm grass. Shake, shake, shake went Sammy. Water flew everywhere, making a mini rain shower! Then, a warm breeze blew across the meadow, drying his fluffy fleece until it was even puffier than before. Sammy felt light as a feather. "Thank you, pond! Thank you, Pip!" he said happily. From that day on, whenever the sun shone too bright, Sammy Sheep knew exactly where to go for a cool and wonderful splash.

stories.title: Woolly’s Lost Bell
stories.text: Deep in the rolling green hills lived a sweet little lamb named Woolly. Woolly wore a shiny silver bell around his neck. Ting-a-ling, ting-a-ling! Every time Woolly hopped, skipped, or jumped, his bell made the happiest music in the whole wide world. It helped the shepherd find Woolly when the sun began to set. One bright afternoon, Woolly was playing hide-and-seek with his bouncy lamb friends. "Ready or not, here I come!" bleated Woolly. He scampered through a patch of tall yellow daisies. He ducked under a big leafy fern. He leaped over a little brown log. Wheee! Woolly was having a wonderful time. But then, something felt different. His neck felt very light. And the happy music had stopped. Ting-a-ling? Where was the sound? Woolly stopped hopping. He stretched his neck down. Oh no! His shiny silver bell was gone! Woolly looked to the left. Just daisies. He looked to the right. Just clover. "Baa!" cried Woolly softly, feeling a little bit worried. How would he make his happy music now? How would the shepherd find him? Just then, Sammy the squirrel poked his head out from a hollow tree. "Did you lose something shiny, little lamb?" chattered Sammy, pointing a furry paw toward the big brown log. Woolly’s eyes lit up. He trotted over to the log as fast as his little legs could carry him. Peeking out from the grass right beside the log was a flash of silver. Ting-a-ling! The bell had caught on a twig and popped right off his collar. Woolly gently nuzzled the bell with his soft pink nose. He picked it up in his mouth and carried it back to the shepherd, who smiled and gently tied it securely back onto Woolly's neck. "Thank you, kind squirrel!" thought Woolly. With a happy skip, Woolly bounded back into the meadow. Ting-a-ling, ting-a-ling went the bell, singing its sweet song once more. Woolly was the happiest lamb in the meadow, and he promised to be extra careful when playing hide-and-seek near the log again.

stories.title: The Sleepy Little Starry Sheep
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking behind the hills, painting the sky in soft shades of pink, purple, and orange. The day was done, and the evening stars were beginning to twinkle like tiny diamonds in the velvet night. In the cozy barn, all the animals were getting ready for bed. The cows curled up in the hay. The horses rested their heavy heads. And little Barnaby Sheep was yawning a very big yawn. Yaaaaawn! Barnaby had wool that felt like a cozy pillow. His eyes were heavy, and his legs felt as tired as tired could be. But Barnaby could not sleep just yet. He had a very important bedtime routine. First, Barnaby needed a bedtime hug from his mother. Mama Sheep wrapped her warm, woolly body around Barnaby and nuzzled his little ears. "Time for rest, my sweet little lamb," she whispered softly. Barnaby felt safe and warm. Next, Barnaby liked to count his favorite things before he closed his eyes. He looked up at the barn roof where little dust motes danced in the moonlight. One star, two stars, three little fireflies glowing in the dark. Barnaby blinked slowly. His eyelids felt like heavy window shutters closing down for the night. But wait! Something was missing. Barnaby's favorite stuffed toy, a little plush bunny named Floppy, was not in his bed. Barnaby sat up. He looked under his soft hay bedding. Nothing there! He looked behind the wooden water bucket. Nothing there! Then, Barnaby heard a tiny squeak. Floppy the bunny was tucked safely into the corner of the manger, resting his own floppy ears. Barnaby let out a sigh of relief. He trotted over, gently picked up Floppy in his mouth, and carried the toy back to his cozy spot in the hay. Barnaby snuggled down very deep. He hugged Floppy tight against his fluffy chest. The night breeze whispered a gentle lullaby through the open barn window. Whoosh, whoosh went the wind. The moon shone a soft, silvery light right onto Barnaby's nose. Barnaby closed his eyes tight. He thought of green grass, sunny meadows, and splashing in the cool pond. His breathing grew slow and steady. In and out. In and out. Barnaby was finally fast asleep, dreaming sweet, fluffy sheep dreams until the morning sun would come up to wake him again.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text:
Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the fluffiest, whitest fleece in the whole wide world. It felt just like a big marshmallow! Every morning, Sammy loved to skip and hop. He would bounce, boing, boing, boing, all across the meadow. He would say hello to the yellow buttercups and the buzzing bumblebees. 'Baa, baa, good morning, little bee!' Sammy would happily call out.

As the afternoon sun began to warm the grass, Sammy started to feel very, very tired. His little pink eyelids grew heavy. Yawn! Sammy let out a big toddler yawn. It was time for a nap. But Sammy could not just sleep anywhere. He needed his special sleepy spot under the big apple tree. He trotted over, patter-patter-patter, and circled around three times. Then, Sammy curled up into a tight, cozy little ball.

Just as Sammy closed his eyes, a gentle breeze whispered through the leaves. Whoosh. The breeze carried the sweet scent of clover. Sammy snuggled deeper into his own soft wool. It was the warmest blanket in the world! His mother, gentle Mother Sheep, walked over and gave his head a soft, loving nudge. 'Time for sweet dreams, my little lamb,' she whispered softly.

Sammy closed his eyes tight. He listened to the other farm animals singing a sleepy lullaby. The cows mooed softly, and the birds chirped their final tweets. Sammy took a deep, slow breath in, and let it out. He dreamed of clouds made of cotton candy and rivers of cool, sparkling water. With a happy twitch of his little black nose, Sammy drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep. Goodnight, Sammy Sheep. Sleep tight until the morning sun wakes you up for more bouncing and playing on the green hill.

stories.title: Woolly Winnie's Rainbow Sweater
stories.text:
Far away in a sunny pasture lived Winnie the Sheep. Winnie was a very special sheep because she did not have plain white wool. Oh no! Winnie had wool that changed colors whenever she was extra happy. On Monday, Winnie woke up and felt as bright as the morning sky. Suddenly, her fluffy wool turned a beautiful, brilliant shade of sky blue! All her farm friends gasped in wonder.

'Look at Winnie!' clucked Henrietta the Hen. 'She is as blue as a robin's egg!' Winnie spun around, feeling so proud. But Winnie's favorite color was not just blue. On Tuesday, she felt as warm as a ripe red strawberry, and her wool turned bright red. On Wednesday, she felt as sunny as a daisy, and her fleece turned a glorious, glowing yellow. The farm looked like a walking rainbow whenever Winnie walked by.

One afternoon, little ducklings waddled up to Winnie with sad little quacks. 'We are so cold,' they shivered. Winnie knew just what to do. She gave a little shake, and guess what happened? Tiny, soft tufts of colorful wool floated off her back like floating dandelion seeds. Winnie caught the tufts and gently tucked them around the shivering little ducklings to keep them warm and cozy.

The ducklings smiled and snuggled into the colorful wool. 'Thank you, Winnie!' they cheeped happily. Winnie felt so much love in her heart that her whole body started to glow. This time, her wool did not just turn one color. It sparkled with pink, purple, green, and gold all at the same time! Winnie pranced around the pasture, laughing a joyful sheep laugh. She was the happiest, most colorful little sheep in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Buttons the Baker Sheep
stories.text:
Baa, baa, baker sheep! Buttons loved to bake yummy treats in his little wooden kitchen by the windmill. Every single morning, before the rooster even crowed, Buttons put on his tall baker's hat. It wobbled this way and that way as he walked. Wobble, wobble, wobble! Buttons tied a crisp white apron around his fluffy waist and got straight to work.

First, Buttons needed flour. He scooped it up with a wooden spoon. Scoop, pour, scoop, pour! Next came sweet, sticky honey from the beehive next door. Drip, drop, drip, drop went the golden honey into the mixing bowl. Buttons rolled up his fuzzy sleeves and stirred the batter with a big wooden paddle. Stir to the left, stir to the right, mix it up with all your might! The kitchen smelled like warm cinnamon and sweet vanilla.

Now it was time to make the dough into fun shapes. Buttons pinched and patted the dough. He made little star cookies, round little muffins, and even a cookie shaped like a little sleeping lamb. Pop, pop, pop went the sweet treats into the hot, cozy oven. While the treats baked, Buttons did a happy little baker dance. Tap your hoof, shake your wool, keep the kitchen nice and full!

Ding! The oven timer chimed. Buttons opened the oven door, and a big cloud of delicious steam puffed out. The treats were golden brown and ready to eat. Buttons invited all his animal friends over for a tasty snack party. They munched and crunched, and licked their sticky fingers. 'You are the best baker ever, Buttons!' they cheered. Buttons beamed with joy, his baker's hat wobbling proudly on his head.

stories.title: Sammy Sheep Goes to Sleep
stories.text: Once upon a time, on a soft green hill, lived a little lamb named Sammy. Sammy had the fluffiest, whitest fleece in the whole wide world. It felt just like a big marshmallow! Every morning, the sun would peek over the mountains and say, 'Baa-baa, time to wake up, Sammy!' Sammy would stretch his little legs, wiggle his tail, and go hopping through the tall green grass. He loved to play hide-and-seek with his best friend, a little brown bunny named Barnaby. 'Ready or not, here I come!' Sammy would bleat, hiding behind a big round boulder. Barnaby would wiggle his nose and find Sammy right away, because Sammy's fluffy white wool was so bright. After playing all morning, Sammy’s tummy would rumble. Time for breakfast! Sammy munched on the sweetest, greenest clover he could find. Crunch, crunch, munch. It was so delicious. Then, he drank cool, sparkly water from the little stream that ran right through the meadow. Splash, splash, went his little hooves. But by the time the afternoon sun started to yawn and turn orange, Sammy’s eyes began to feel very, very heavy. He blinked once. He blinked twice. Yawn! Sammy was tired. He trotted back to his cozy barn where his mama was waiting. Mama Sheep gave him a big, warm cuddle, wrapping her soft wool around him. 'Time for bed, my sweet little lamb,' she whispered softly. Sammy lay down on the fresh, fragrant hay. He closed his brown eyes and listened to the gentle wind whispering outside the barn door. One little sheep, two little sheep, jumping over the moon. Sammy drifted off into the most wonderful, cozy dreams, smiling all night long until the bright morning sun came back to say hello again.

stories.title: Daisy's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Daisy was a very happy little sheep who lived on a busy, noisy farm. She had sparkly black eyes and a coat of wool that bounced every time she walked. Bounce, bounce, bounce! Daisy loved her home, but more than anything, she loved to explore. One sunny Tuesday, after a big morning rainstorm, Daisy trotted out of her pen to see what was new. She sniffed the fresh, wet air. Sniff, sniff! Suddenly, she saw something amazing near the big red tractor. It was a puddle! A big, shiny, brown puddle of mud. Now, sheep are usually very careful to keep their wool clean and white, but Daisy looked at the mud and thought it looked like the most fun thing in the whole world. She took one step closer. Squish! went the mud between her little black hooves. It felt squishy, cool, and tickly. Daisy let out a happy little 'Baa!' and stepped right into the middle of it. She splashed her foot. Splash! Mud flew up into the air and landed right on her nose. 'Achoo!' sneezed Daisy, making a funny face. She tried to do a little dance in the mud, wiggling her bottom and shaking her head. Soon, her sparkling white fleece had brown spots all over it. She looked like a giant chocolate-chip cookie! Just then, the farmer walked by with a bucket of fresh water and a big brush. He laughed out well when he saw muddy Daisy. 'Well, well, look at you!' said the farmer. 'Time for a bath, little explorer.' Daisy didn't mind at all. The warm water felt so nice, and the big brush scratched her back right where it itched. Soon, she was clean, white, and fluffy once more. As the sun dried her wool, Daisy smiled, already dreaming of her next big adventure on the farm.

stories.title: Woolly's Big Yellow Hat
stories.text: Woolly was a gentle sheep who wore a very special secret. Underneath his curly white wool, he had the biggest imagination on the farm. Today, Woolly woke up with a grand plan. He wanted to find a hat. Not just any hat, but a hat that was bright, sunny, and made him feel like a king. Woolly trotted out of the pasture and began his search. First, he walked past the chicken coop. 'Cluck, cluck,' said Henrietta the hen. 'Are you looking for something, Woolly?' Woolly nodded. 'I am looking for a hat!' Henrietta offered him an empty yellow bucket. Woolly carefully balanced the bucket on top of his head. He looked down at the duck pond to see his reflection. Plop! The bucket slid right off his head and into the water. 'Oh dear,' giggled Woolly. Next, he walked over to the apple tree. A bright red apple fell right onto his head, resting snugly in his curly wool. Woolly giggled and shook his head, but the apple rolled away into the grass. Just then, a friendly butterfly with bright yellow wings fluttered down. It landed softly right between Woolly's ears and stayed there, gently flapping its wings. Woolly looked in the pond again. With the yellow butterfly sitting proudly on his head, he looked like he was wearing a gorgeous crown made of sunshine. 'Baa! This is the best hat ever!' cheered Woolly. He pranced proudly back to his sheep friends, showing off his lovely yellow butterfly hat to everyone on the farm. The other sheep bleated in delight, and Woolly stood tall, feeling like the happiest, most stylish sheep in the whole wide world.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Tell me why you stand so still.
Do you see a butterfly,
Dancing in the sunny sky?

Little lamb, please jump and play,
Make it such a happy day.
Hop along and touch the ground,
Spin yourself all round and round.

Little lamb, your wool is white,
Shining softly in the light.
Soft as pillows on a bed,
Rest your tired, sleepy head.

Little lamb, now day is done,
Say goodnight to golden sun.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the coming of the day.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Jump
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little sheep,
Time to jump and time to leap.
Over fences, high and low,
Watch the fluffy woolly go.

Run across the meadow green,
 Happiest lamb you've ever seen.
Find a clover on the ground,
Chew it up without a sound.

Shake your tail and stamp your feet,
Life on the farm is oh so sweet.
Give a friendly little baa,
Calling out to mama sheep.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little lambs to sleep.
Dream of fields so soft and wide,
Sleeping safely by her side.

rhymes.title: Woolly Wonders
rhymes.text:
Soft and woolly, white and round,
Walking gently on the ground.
Nibbling grass so fresh and green,
Cutest lamb you've ever seen.

When the winter winds blow cold,
Keeping cozy, brave and bold.
With a coat of fleece so grand,
Warmest sheep in all the land.

Jump into the muddy pool,
Water splashy, clean and cool.
Shake the water from your head,
Time to trot on home to bed.

Moon is shining bright and clear,
Whispering for all to hear.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little fluffy sheep, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Sheep, Wake Up
rhymes.text:
Little sheep upon the hill,
Morning sun begins to shine.
Wake up now and eat your fill,
Drink the water cool and fine.

Prance around the grassy space,
Jump up high into the air.
Find a happy smiling face,
Show your woolly coat with care.

Chase the butterflies so bright,
Make a funny little sound.
Run until the golden light,
Starts to sink into the ground.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time to rest your little head.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
In your cozy wooden bed.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa White Sheep
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little fluffy sheep,
Tell me what you like to do.
Do you like to take a leap,
In the morning sky of blue?

Yes, I like to skip and play,
Nibble on the clover green.
Running through the fields all day,
Happiest you've ever seen.

Then when night begins to fall,
And the moon is shining bright.
I will answer nature's call,
Sleeping softly through the night.

Dreaming of a sunny day,
When the morning comes anew.
I will wake and shout hooray,
Just like little children do.

rhymes.title: The Softest Wool
rhymes.text:
See the little woolly lamb,
Soft as any feather bed.
Happier than any clam,
Nodding off his sleepy head.

White as snow and warm and sweet,
Walking on four tiny toes.
Dancing with his little feet,
Wiggling his pink button nose.

Eating grass out in the sun,
Having such a joyful time.
Now our little story's done,
Finished with this happy rhyme.

Time to cuddle up real tight,
Stars are glowing in the sky.
Say a gentle, sweet goodnight,
Let the sleepy hours go by.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little sheep upon the hill,
Grazing softly, calm and still.
With a coat of white and wool,
Eating clover till it's full.

Hopping up and skipping down,
Best wee lamb in all the town.
When the sun begins to set,
Not a single thing to fret.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Tucked inside your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and count to ten,
Wake up happy back again.

Baa, baa, says the little sheep,
Now it's time to fall asleep.
Dreaming of the morning dew,
Goodnight, little lamb, to you.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Bell
rhymes.text:
Silver bell upon the neck,
Check it twice and double check.
When the sheep begins to run,
Playing out beneath the sun.

Ting-a-ling the bell will ring,
Making every birdie sing.
Jumping over sticks and stones,
Far away from houses, homes.

Stop to eat the yellow hay,
Having fun the livelong day.
Give a nudge and give a baa,
Running right to mamma dear.

Now the stars are shining bright,
Bidding all the farm goodnight.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little lamb so soft and white.

rhymes.title: Fluffy Fleece
rhymes.text:
Puffy cloud upon the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.
Fluffy fleece from horn to toe,
Watch the little lambkin go.

Trot along the meadow green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.
Bouncing high into the air,
Jumping here and jumping there.

Finding friends of brown and gray,
Ready for a game of play.
Running through the gentle breeze,
Underneath the leafy trees.

Time to wash the mud away,
End of such a happy day.
Snuggle close and rest your head,
In your warm and cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little woolly sheep of white,
Dancing in the morning light.
Hoppity hop across the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.
Eating clover sweet and green,
Prettiest sheep you've ever seen.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
When you wake up to go play.
Baa baa says the little sheep,
Falling in a lovely sleep.
Stars are shining up above,
Wrapped in warmth and cozy love.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Snug inside your grassy bed.

rhymes.title: The Little Lost Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little lamb is running fast,
Looking for his friends at last.
Over hills and valleys wide,
Nowhere left for him to hide.
Where is mama? Where is she?
Underneath the apple tree.
Baa baa calls the baby sheep,
Starting now to start and weep.
Mama hears his gentle cry,
Looking up into the sky.
Running quickly to her child,
With a tender smile so mild.
Nose to nose they touch and say,
Glad we found each other today.
Now they walk back home so slow,
Happy sheep in morning glow.

rhymes.title: Counting Sheep
rhymes.text:
One little sheep jumps the gate,
Two little sheep think it's great.
Three little sheep go for a run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Four little sheep eat some hay,
Having such a joyful day.
Five little sheep start to sing,
Greeting what the day will bring.
Six little sheep shake their wool,
Keeping meadow pastures full.
Seven little sheep skip and bound,
Hopping all around the ground.
Eight little sheep take a rest,
Cuddling up is what they love best.
Nine little sheep softly sigh,
Ten little sheep say goodbye.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little woolly sheep of white,
Dancing in the morning light.
Bouncing high upon the grass,
Watching friendly birdies pass.

Soft and fluffy is your coat,
With a little shiny note.
Running through the clover sweet,
Skipping with your little feet.

Now the sun begins to fall,
Shadows stretch against the wall.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

Close your eyes and gently sleep,
Little, happy, gentle sheep.
Dream of fields of green and blue,
All the world is loving you.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Jump
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little sheep today,
Come outside and let us play.
Jump up high into the air,
Throw away your every care.

Trotting down the muddy lane,
Singing in the gentle rain.
Splashing in a puddle wide,
With your furry friends beside.

Now the rain is gone away,
What a bright and sunny day.
Nibble on the yellow corn,
Ever since the early morn.

Evening stars begin to peep,
Time to cuddle up and sleep.
Rest your hooves and close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: The Golden Bell
rhymes.text:
Golden bell upon your neck,
Ting-a-ling a tiny speck.
Running up the grassy hill,
Stopping just a moment still.

Looking for a flower sweet,
Prancing on your tiny feet.
Butterflies fly all around,
Touching lightly on the ground.

Listen to the evening breeze,
Whispering among the trees.
Mommy sheep is standing near,
Whispering words of love, my dear.

Snuggle close and drift away,
After such a busy day.
Dream of stars so bright and deep,
Sleep, my little lovely sheep.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Tell me why you're standing still.
Do you want to run and play,
In the meadow all the day?

Hopping here and jumping there,
Fuzzy wool up in the air.
Little lamb with eyes so bright,
You are such a lovely sight.

Time to rest your little head,
In your cozy grassy bed.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little, fluffy, sleepy sheep.

Stars are shining in the sky,
While the wind blows softly by.
Dream of clovers sweet and green,
Best little sheep ever seen.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa's Wool
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little sheep,
Do you have wool in a heap?
Yes, sir, yes, sir, fluffy and white,
Keeps me cozy through the night.

One bag for the farmer man,
Doing all the chores he can.
One bag for the little boy,
Filling up his heart with joy.

One bag for the baby low,
Watching all the daisies grow.
Soft and warm from top to toe,
Everywhere the sheep will go.

Jump around and give a cheer,
Springtime is at last here.
Happy sheep with fleece so bright,
Dancing in the morning light.

rhymes.title: Five Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Five little sheep bouncing on the grass,
Watching all the fluffy white clouds pass.
One jumped high and shouted out wee,
Look at what I can do and see!

Four little sheep munching on clover,
Till one silly lamb rolled right over.
Three little sheep skipping in a line,
Feeling happy and feeling fine.

Two little sheep taking a little nap,
Resting their heads on Mother's lap.
One little sheep waking up to play,
Ready for a brand new sunny day.

Now the stars are coming out so bright,
Saying to the little sheep, sleep tight.
Moon is smiling from up above,
Sending down a sleepy hug.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Sheep
rhymes.text:
See the little woolly sheep,
Standing on the hill so steep.
Eating grass of green and bright,
Running in the morning light.

Soft and fluffy is his coat,
With a bell upon his throat.
When he jumps, he says, 'Baa, baa!'
Running straight to find his ma.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
Little, quiet, sleepy sheep.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Clouds are floating very high.
Dreaming in the meadow deep,
Goodnight to the little sheep.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little lamb today,
Tell me what you like to play.
Do you jump up in the air?
Do you bounce without a care?

Soft white wool from head to toe,
Watch the happy creature go.
Prancing through the flowers red,
Time to rest your sleepy head.

Farmer brings a bucket sweet,
Giving you a yummy treat.
Drinking water from the brook,
Sitting in a cozy nook.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Hug your mama through the night.
Rest your little fleece so deep,
Sleepy, happy, little sheep.

rhymes.title: Jump Over the Moon
rhymes.text:
Little sheep, please dance and play,
Chase the butterflies away.
Stamp your little hoofs in glee,
Dance beneath the apple tree.

Jump up high into the air,
Spin around and show your hair.
Wool is warm and wool is grand,
Bestest sheep in all the land.

Now the stars begin to glow,
To the cozy barn we go.
Lie down on the hay so sweet,
Rest your tired little feet.

Shadows dance upon the wall,
Nighttime covers farm and all.
Close your eyes and do not peep,
Sweetest dreams, my little sheep.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Jump So High
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Can you please stand very still?
Now go running through the grass,
Watch the happy springtime pass.

Fluffy woolly coat of white,
Shining softly in the light.
Baa, baa, says the little sheep,
Time to wake from morning sleep.

Jump up high into the air,
Spin around and show your hair.
Prance along the meadow floor,
Now let us do it all once more.

When the stars begin to glow,
To your cozy bed you go.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Sleeping in your woolly nest.

rhymes.title: Five Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Five little sheep in a row,
Eating clover sweet and low.
One little sheep runs away,
Looking for a game to play.

Two little sheep skip and hop,
Jumping right up to the top.
Three little sheep chew their hay,
Happy on a sunny day.

Four little sheep say hello,
Watching all the daisies grow.
Five little sheep curl up tight,
Sleeping through the quiet night.

Baa, baa, goes the gentle sound,
As they rest upon the ground.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Little sheep, sleep tight tonight.

rhymes.title: Woolly Wiggles
rhymes.text:
Soft and fluffy, big and round,
Little hooves upon the ground.
Shake your wool and wiggle toes,
Touch your little button nose.

Run around the grassy tree,
Happy as a lamb can be.
Bleat a happy little song,
As you gaily bounce along.

Farmer brings a bucket sweet,
Giving every sheep a treat.
 Munching clover, fresh and green,
Freshest sheep you've ever seen.

Sun is setting in the sky,
Little birds begin to fly.
Say goodnight and softly peep,
Sleepy little fluffy sheep.

rhymes.title: Little White Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little white sheep in the meadow so green,
You are the fluffiest lamb I have seen.
You bounce on your toes and you jump all around,
Making sweet music without any sound.

You nibble the clover so tasty and sweet,
With tiny black hooves on your wonderful feet.
The sun is now setting, the day is all done,
We played all day long in the bright golden sun.

Now curl up in bed like a little round ball,
As shadows grow long on the old garden wall.
The stars in the sky give a soft, gentle light,
So close your sweet eyes and sleep through the night.

Tomorrow we'll wake up and play in the dew,
My dear little sheep, I am so fond of you.
The moon watches over your cozy wool bed,
While sweet sleepy dreams dance inside your small head.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little lamb, running in the hay,
Tell me what you like to do all through the day.
I like to run fast and I like to play leap,
Until I get sleepy and ready to sleep.

Do you like the mud that is squishy and brown?
I stomp in the puddles all over the town!
Do you like the grass that is yummy and sweet?
I munch on the clover with two little feet.

Your coat is as white as a cloud in the sky,
I watch all the fluffy white clouds floating by.
Your nose is as black as a shiny new shoe,
And I love to cuddle and play games with you.

The farm is now quiet, the chickens are still,
The big sleepy moon is awake on the hill.
So lie on the grass in the soft clover bed,
And rest your tired little wool underneath your head.

rhymes.title: The Woolly Jumper
rhymes.text:
Sammy the sheep has a very thick coat,
Warm as a scarf and a woolly blue boat.
When winter winds blow and the weather gets cold,
He shares all his wool with the young and the old.

Farmer comes out with his clippers that buzz,
Snip goes the wool just like magic it was!
A big pile of fluff on the green garden ground,
As Sammy goes dancing and spinning around.

The yarn is made soft by the fire so bright,
To keep all the animals cozy at night.
A sweater for mouse and a scarf for the bird,
The kindest little sheep that you ever heard.

Now Sammy is light as a feather in spring,
And listens closely to sweet robins sing.
His coat will soon grow back as white as can be,
As happy and free as a lamb on the lea.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little woolly sheep so white,
Jumping in the morning light.
Running through the grassy green,
Happiest sheep you've ever seen.

Baa, baa, says the sheep,
Time to wake up from your sleep.
Trotting to the little brook,
Where the happy fishes look.

Soft wool like a cotton cloud,
Making noises loud and proud.
Nibbling clover on the hill,
Now the little sheep is still.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy tractor bed.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
Sweet dreams, little fluffy sheep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Lambs
rhymes.text:
Five little lambs playing in the hay,
Hopping and a-jumping all the day.
One ran off to find a red ball,
Now there are four lambs having a ball.

Four little lambs looking at a bee,
Buzzing all around the apple tree.
One skipped away to smell a rose,
Now there are three lambs on their toes.

Three little lambs splashing in the mud,
Having so much fun with a silly thud.
One trotted off to take a little nap,
Now there are two lambs in Farmer's lap.

Two little lambs looking at the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go floating by.
One ran away to chase a yellow duck,
Now just one little lamb is out of luck.

One little lamb standing all alone,
Time to take this little baby home.
Into the barn where the straw is deep,
Now all five little lambs are fast asleep.

rhymes.title: The Happy Little Farm
rhymes.text:
The sun is shining bright and warm,
Down upon the happy farm.
Sammy Sheep begins to play,
Jumping high and far away.

He has a coat of woolly hair,
Softest wool you can compare.
He runs around the wooden pen,
Saying hello to every hen.

Cluck, cluck, says the chicken red,
Time to find your cozy bed.
No, not yet, says Sammy Sheep,
I am not quite ready for sleep.

I want to run and skip around,
Making such a happy sound.
Baa, baa, baa, he sings with glee,
Happiest sheep for you to see.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time to cuddle and to sleep.
Goodnight sheep and goodnight farm,
Safe and warm away from harm.

rhymes.title: Little Wooly Sheep
rhymes.text:
Little sheep upon the hill,
Standing very soft and still.
With a coat of white and gray,
Ready for a happy day.

Baa, baa, says the sheep,
While the little lamb falls asleep.
Jumping high up in the air,
Without a single tiny care.

Munching on the clover green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.
Running fast across the grass,
Watching all the birdies pass.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Three Little Lambs
rhymes.text:
Three little lambs went out to play,
Down in the meadow far away.
They hopped around and skipped so high,
Underneath the big blue sky.

One little lamb found a yellow flower,
Standing there for half an hour.
Two little lambs began to race,
Running at a speedy pace.

Three little lambs went splash, splash, splash,
Through the water in a dash.
Getting muddy on their feet,
Looking oh so very sweet.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Time to rest and act so slow.
Cuddle close and sleep till morn,
Happy lambs where they were born.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Bright
rhymes.text:
Baa, baa, little sheep so bright,
Wearing wool of snowy white.
Tell me what you like to do,
When the sky is clear and blue.

I like running on the farm,
Safe and cozy from all harm.
Eating apples sweet and red,
Waiting for my cozy bed.

Can you do a little dance,
If you get a happy chance?
Stomp your hooves and shake your wool,
Keep your tummy nice and full.

Now the moon is shining down,
On the sleeping country town.
Say goodnight and close your eyes,
Till the morning sun doth rise.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little woolly lamb so white,
Prancing in the morning light.
Jumping high and running fast,
Having so much fun at last.

Soft as pillows on the bed,
With a fluffy little head.
Baa, baa, says the happy sheep,
Ready now to go to sleep.

Trotting through the meadow green,
Cutest lamb you've ever seen.
Nibbling clover on the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little lambs to sleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Snuggled in your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Five little sheep upon a hill,
Dancing round and never still.
One ran off to find a friend,
Playing games until the end.

Four little sheep now eat some grass,
Watching pretty birdies pass.
Two more jumped a little log,
Barking softly at a dog.

Three little sheep go for a swim,
Splish and splash right at the brim.
Two more bounce upon the hay,
Having such a joyful day.

Now there is just one sheep left here,
Saying to the moon, hello my dear.
Time to curl up on the floor,
Sleeping till we wake up more.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa's Big Red Boots
rhymes.text:
Baa baa sheep put on his shoes,
Walking far to cure the blues.
Red boots marching in the mud,
Stomping right into a flood.

Splish and splash and giggle too,
Happy little sheep are you.
Now the boots are muddy brown,
Walking all around the town.

Time to wash them in the stream,
Making everything so clean.
Dry your wool and shake your head,
Time to tiptoe back to bed.

Mama gives a gentle hug,
Tucked into a cozy rug.
Dreaming of the muddy floor,
Till the morning opens door.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Tell me why you stand so still.
Do you want to run and play,
In the meadow all the day?

White as snow is every fleece,
Bringing all the farm great peace.
Baa, baa, says the happy sheep,
While the baby falls asleep.

Hopping high and jumping low,
Watch the little creature go.
Nibbling grass so fresh and green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.

Now the sun begins to set,
Do not worry, do not fret.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Three Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Three little sheep in a row,
Where are you trying to go?
Over the bridge we will leap,
While the big farm cows are asleep.

Bells on their necks go ring-a-ling,
Listen to the song they sing.
Trot, trot, trot along the way,
Having such a joyful day.

Soft and woolly, big and round,
Dancing lightly on the ground.
Spinning fast and turning slow,
Watch the fluffy woolly show.

Now the stars are shining bright,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Cuddling close in the barn so deep,
Little sheep are fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Sammy's Soft Fleece
rhymes.text:
Sammy sheep has wool so white,
Shining softly in the light.
Pat his back and feel it glow,
Softest wool you'll ever know.

Prancing through the clover patch,
No one is a better match.
Happy jump and happy bound,
With his hooves upon the ground.

Calling out a friendly baa,
Running near and running far.
Chasing butterflies of blue,
Playing games the whole day through.

Shadows lengthen on the grass,
Watching sleepy moments pass.
Time to rest your woolly feet,
Dreaming dreams so soft and sweet.

rhymes.title: Little Woolly Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little woolly lamb so white,
Running in the morning light.
Bouncing on the grassy hill,
Then a moment standing still.

Chewing clover, sweet and green,
Prettiest sheep you've ever seen.
Tumping tails and happy baas,
Jumping over garden flaws.

Now the sun is going down,
Lights are twinkling in the town.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Snuggled in your cozy bed.

Dreaming of the stars above,
Wrapped in hugs and gentle love.
Close your eyes and slumber deep,
Little happy sleepy sheep.

rhymes.title: Five Soft Sheep
rhymes.text:
Five soft sheep upon the farm,
Keeping safe from wind and harm.
One jumps high into the air,
Kicking legs without a care.

Two little lambs go munch, munch, munch,
Eating green grass for their lunch.
Three fuzzy friends say baa, baa, baa,
Calling out to Mama Sheep near, far.

Four fluffy backs so neat and round,
Trotting softly on the ground.
Five sleepy sheep now fall asleep,
Counting stars instead of sheep.

Goodnight meadow, big and wide,
With the fluffy flock inside.
Sleep until the morning ray,
Brings another happy day.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Baa baa little sheep today,
Show me how you love to play.
Do you hop and do you run,
Playing underneath the sun?

Yes, I run and yes, I jump,
Over every grassy bump.
Then I stop to rest my feet,
Chewing something nice and sweet.

Wool is fluffy, wool is white,
Shining softly in the light.
Like a cloud up in the blue,
Little sheep, I think of you.

Now the day is almost done,
Say goodbye to golden sun.
Time to dream and time to sleep,
Goodnight little woolly sheep.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Little Lamb
rhymes.text:
Little lamb with wool so white,
Running through the grass so bright.
Jumping high and jumping low,
Watch the happy creature go.

Soft and fluffy like a cloud,
Bleating softly, not too loud.
Eating clover in the sun,
Having so much playful fun.

Trotting down the winding lane,
Dancing in the gentle rain.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping safely in the town.

Little lamb, close both your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dreaming of a meadow green,
Sweetest sleep you've ever seen.

rhymes.title: Five Little Sheep
rhymes.text:
Five little sheep upon a hill,
Eating grass and standing still.
One little sheep begins to run,
Jumping gaily in the sun.

Four little sheep go baa, baa, baa,
Calling out to Mama Sheep afar.
Two little sheep decide to play,
Kicking up their heels all day.

Three little sheep jump over a log,
Barking softly goes the dog.
Four little sheep are feeling great,
Near the wooden garden gate.

Now five little sheep are fast asleep,
Counting dreams they love to keep.
Wrapped in woolly coats so warm,
Safe from any windy storm.

rhymes.title: The Woolly Jumper
rhymes.text:
Sheep has wool of fluffy gray,
Wearing sweaters every day.
When the weather turns up cold,
Keeping little bodies bold.

Snip goes shear and off it goes,
Making yarn for baby's clothes.
Knit a scarf and knit a hat,
Sitting on the kitty mat.

Little lamb says baa to you,
Wearing something soft and blue.
Hop along and skip around,
Hooves go tapping on the ground.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Tucked inside a cozy bed.
Stars are shining up above,
Filled with tenderness and love.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Now the evening wind is still.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
Do not make a single peep.

Stars are shining bright and high,
Floating in the velvet sky.
Moonlight glows upon your fleece,
Bringing quiet dreams and peace.

Rest your little tired feet,
Dream of clover fresh and sweet.
Snuggle down and do not cry,
While the stars go sailing by.

Morning light will soon appear,
Bringing joy and daytime cheer.
Now it is the time for rest,
Sleeping is what you do best.

rhymes.title: Bouncy Woolly Jumper
rhymes.text:
Hopping through the meadow green,
Cutest sheep you've ever seen!
Jumping high up in the air,
Woolly bouncing everywhere.

With a baa and with a bleat,
Dancing with her little feet.
Spinning round and looking bright,
Fleece as soft as morning light.

Chasing butterflies that fly,
Underneath the sunny sky.
Stopping for a yummy treat,
Clover green and crisp and sweet.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that she has played yet.
Time to rest her weary head,
Curled up in her cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Fluffy Sheep
rhymes.text:
One white sheep jumps over the gate,
Two white sheep are staying up late.
Three white sheep go munching hay,
Four white sheep run out to play.

Five white sheep say baa, baa, baa,
Running to their mamma sheep's spa.
Shaking wool so soft and grand,
Happiest sheep in all the land.

Sun is shining warm and deep,
Waking up from gentle sleep.
Prancing through the flowers red,
Time to jump right out of bed.

Clapping hands for sheep so sweet,
Marching with our toddler feet.
Now our happy song is done,
Playing with the sheep was fun.

rhymes.title: Little Lamb, Jump!
rhymes.text:
Little lamb upon the hill,
Can you please stay very still?
No, I want to hop and play,
Running in the sun all day.

Soft white wool and fuzzy toes,
Funny twitching little nose.
Baa, baa, says the happy sheep,
Ready now to go to sleep.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little clouds go floating by.
Moon is smiling bright and high,
Time to wave a sweet goodbye.

Dream of clover sweet and green,
Best little sheep ever seen.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Safe inside your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Baa Baa's Wool
rhymes.text:
Woolly sheep has coat so white,
Shining softly in the light.
Eating grass upon the lawn,
From the morning until dawn.

Springtime breeze begins to blow,
Making flowers start to grow.
Little lamb runs all around,
Prancing lightly on the ground.

Happy sounds of baa, baa, baa,
Calling out to mama sheep.
Safe and warm in morning dew,
She is coming right to you.

Now the sun is going down,
Quiet shadows fill the town.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Sleeping in the meadow's nest.

rhymes.title: Five Little Lambs
rhymes.text:
One little lamb goes hop, hop, hop,
Two little lambs will never stop.
Three little lambs say baa, baa, baa,
Running fast to find their ma.

Four little lambs skip in the hay,
Having fun throughout the day.
Five little lambs are sleepy now,
Resting underneath the bough.

Nighttime comes with quiet breeze,
Whispering through the leafy trees.
Soft wool blankets keep them warm,
Far away from wind and storm.

Dreaming dreams of fields so green,
Sweetest sights that can be seen.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little lambs, sleep tight, sleep tight.

stories.title: Timmy Turtle's Tiny Shell
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, down by the sparkling blue pond, lived a very little turtle named Timmy. Timmy had a bright green shell that was as shiny as a polished apple. He loved to splash his webbed feet in the warm, muddy puddles. But today, Timmy had a big problem. His shell felt just a little bit too heavy, and he wanted to play tag with his friends, the darting dragonflies. Timmy tucked his head inside his cozy shell and thought. 'How can I run as fast as the frogs?' he wondered. Just then, his wise old grandmother, Nana Turtle, poked her gentle head out of the reeds. 'Slow and steady wins the race, my sweet Timmy,' she whispered with a warm smile. 'You do not need to rush to have the most fun.' Timmy blinked his big round eyes. He decided to test her advice. Instead of running, he played hide-and-seek. He pulled his legs inside his shell and waited. Count to three, one, two, three! His friend Sammy the dragonfly fluttered right past him without seeing a thing. Timmy popped his head back out and giggled a happy little turtle giggle. 'Boo!' he shouted, surprising Sammy. They both laughed and played together all afternoon. Timmy realized that his special shell wasn't just for carrying around; it was the best hiding spot in the whole wide world. When the golden sun began to dip low behind the tall green trees, Timmy felt a sleepy yawn coming on. He tucked his tiny paws safely inside, closed his eyes, and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of flying dragonflies and warm, muddy puddles. Being a little turtle was truly the best adventure a tiny creature could ever ask for, especially when you have a cozy home right on your back.

stories.title: Toby Turtle's Red Boots
stories.text: Deep in the whispering green woods, there lived a curious turtle named Toby. Toby had a shell that looked like a delicious chocolate chip cookie, and he loved to explore every single inch of the mossy forest floor. One bright morning, Toby found something shiny tucked beneath a big fern. It was a pair of bright red boots! They were tiny, just the right size for a little turtle's front feet. Toby was so excited. He wiggled his toes and slipped the boots right on. 'Tap, tap, tap,' went his feet against the crunchy autumn leaves. He felt like the fanciest turtle in the entire forest. He waddled over to show his good friend, Bella the bunny. 'Look at my new shoes, Bella!' squeaked Toby proudly. Bella hopped up and down with delight. 'Oh, Toby! They are the most wonderful boots I have ever seen!' she cheered. Toby felt so proud that he decided to go on a grand parade all the way to the big berry bush. But oh dear, the boots were a little bit slippery on the damp grass. Toby wobbled to the left, and he wobbled to the right. Oopsie-daisy! He tumbled right over onto his back, wiggling his red boots in the air like two little strawberries. Bella giggled and gently pushed him back onto his feet. Toby looked down at the bright red boots. They were very pretty, but walking was much trickier with them on. Toby decided to take the boots off and carry them on his back instead. Now he could crawl fast and free, just like he always did. He shared a yummy red berry with Bella, and they watched the clouds float by in the bright blue sky. Toby learned that sometimes the best things in life are the ones you were already born with, like four strong feet and a very happy heart.

stories.title: Tessa Turtle Finds a Friend
stories.text: Tessa Turtle loved the morning dew. Every day, before the sun was even fully awake, she would crawl out from under her favorite log and stretch her neck. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Today was a very special day because Tessa was going to the great lily pad party at the center of the pond. She wanted to dance, but she was feeling just a little bit shy. Tessa walked very slowly down the muddy path. Along the way, she met Pip, a little yellow duckling who was flapping his fluffy wings. 'Quack, quack! Hello, little turtle!' cheeped Pip happily. 'Are you going to the party too?' Tessa nodded shyly and tucked her head in just a tiny bit. 'I am going, but I do not know how to dance,' she whispered softly. Pip smiled a big duck smile. 'Dancing is easy! You just wiggle your tail and shake your flippers like this!' Pip waddled in a silly circle, making Tessa laugh out loud. Her shyness melted away like morning mist. Tessa joined in, shaking her little tail and tapping her webbed feet on the soft mud. Together, Tessa and Pip waddled all the way to the big green lily pad. All the frogs were croaking a merry song, and the fish were blowing sparkly bubbles in the water. Tessa felt so brave with her new friend by her side. She spun around in a slow, happy turtle dance. She didn't need to be fast because she was having the most wonderful time in the whole wide world. When the party finally ended, Tessa and Pip promised to play together every single day. Tessa crawled back to her cozy log under the moonlight, feeling warm, happy, and full of joy. She snuggled deep inside her shell, knowing that making a new friend was the greatest adventure of all.

stories.title: Toby Turtle Takes a Walk
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, little Toby Turtle woke up and poked his green nose out of his cozy shell. Good morning, world! he whispered. Today was a very special day because Toby wanted to visit his very best friend, Penny the Duck, down by the sparkling blue pond. Toby stretched his four little legs, one, two, three, four, and began to walk. Slow and steady, that was Toby's motto. He took a tiny step forward. Crunch went a dry brown leaf beneath his toes. A bright yellow butterfly fluttered right past his nose, dancing in the warm morning breeze. Hello, butterfly! Toby called out happily. The butterfly did a little twirl and flew up toward the fluffy white clouds. Toby smiled and kept on moving. He crawled over a small, mossy rock, bump-a-bump went his shell. He crept under a big green fern that tickled his shell like a soft tickly blanket. Every now and then, Toby stopped to rest because walking all the way to the pond is big work for a little turtle. He blinked his big, round eyes and watched a busy red ladybug crawl up a blade of grass. You are very fast, little ladybug, Toby thought. But Toby was not in a hurry at all. He loved feeling the warm sunshine on his back and listening to the birds sing sweet little songs in the tall trees. After a long, lovely time, Toby could hear a happy quacking sound. Quack, quack, quack! It was Penny! Toby peeked through the tall green reeds and saw the shiny blue water sparkling in the light. Penny paddled over to the muddy bank with a big splash. Good morning, Toby! Penny sang out. I am so glad you came to play. Toby beamed with joy and wiggled his little tail. It took me a long time, Penny, but slow and steady wins the day, said Toby. They spent the rest of the afternoon sharing crunchy green lily pads, playing hide-and-seek behind the cattails, and splashing their toes in the water. When the sun began to turn a pretty shade of orange, Toby gave Penny a warm hug. It was time to head home for bedtime. Toby walked back along the exact same path, feeling cozy, tired, and very happy. He crawled inside his safe shell, closed his sleepy eyes, and dreamed sweet dreams about his wonderful day at the pond.

stories.title: Toby's Shell is Safe
stories.text: Deep in the green, leafy garden, a little turtle named Toby lived under a big patch of sweet strawberries. Toby loved his home. Most of all, Toby loved his shell. His shell was hard and strong, painted with pretty patterns of brown and yellow, just like a tiny house that he could carry wherever he went. Every morning, Toby would peek his head out to see what adventures awaited him in the big garden. Today, the garden was full of exciting new sights and sounds. A big, fluffy bumblebee buzzed by, making a loud zzz-zzz sound as it landed on a bright pink flower to drink sweet nectar. Toby watched the bee with wide, curious eyes. Then, he decided it was time to explore the big patch of green grass near the vegetable patch. He crawled along the dirt path, feeling the cool earth beneath his tummy. Suddenly, a big grey cloud rolled across the sky, and a loud rumble went through the air. Rumbl-rumble-rumble went the sky! Oh my, whispered Toby. A few big raindrops started to plop down on the ground. Plop, plop, plop! Then came a gentle pitter-patter of rain, getting faster and louder by the second. The garden was getting wet, and Toby was getting wet too! But Toby did not worry at all. He knew just what to do when the weather turned wild. He pulled his head all the way inside his cozy shell. He pulled his four little feet inside, and tucked his tail in tight. Pop! He was completely hidden away in his very own safe fortress. Inside his shell, it was dark, warm, and wonderfully quiet. He could hear the raindrops tap-tap-tapping on his hard roof like a little drum circle playing just for him. Tap-tap-tap, tap-tap-tap! Toby felt so safe and cozy inside his little mobile home. He curled up tight and took a nice little rest while the rain washed the garden clean. After a little while, the tapping sound stopped. The air smelled fresh and sweet, full of the scent of wet soil and blooming flowers. Toby slowly poked his green head back out into the world. He blinked his eyes against the bright light. Look at that! High up in the sky was a huge, beautiful rainbow with red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple stripes. Toby let out a happy sigh. The rain was gone, the garden was sparkling with shiny water drops, and his shell had kept him safe and dry. Toby stretched his legs and crawled out to chase a shiny snail.

stories.title: Toby Finds a Red Berry
stories.text: The morning sun was shining brightly through the tall blades of green grass in the meadow. Toby Turtle was wide awake and feeling very hungry. My tummy is rumbling, Toby said with a little giggle, rubbing his green belly with a tiny paw. It was time to go on a food-finding mission! Toby started walking through the thick green jungle of grass stems. He looked to the left, and he looked to the right. He saw a little brown worm wiggling in the dirt. Hello, worm! said Toby. The worm waved hello and wriggled away under a pebble. Toby kept on moving, his hard shell bumping gently against the wild clover leaves. Then, way up ahead, something caught his eye. It was bright, and it was shiny, and it was the prettiest shade of red Toby had ever seen. It was a big, juicy garden berry hiding right under a leafy green canopy! Oh boy, whispered Toby, his eyes growing as big as saucers. That looks so yummy! But there was a tiny problem. The berry was sitting up on a little mound of dirt, and Toby was very short. How was he going to reach his delicious breakfast? Toby did not give up. He walked right up to the mound and stretched his neck as high as it could possibly go. He stretched and stretched, but his nose was still a little bit too far away. Boop! He missed it by just an inch. Toby tried again. He stood up tall on his back feet, balancing carefully on his shell, and gave one giant reach with his mouth open wide. Snap! He caught the sweet red berry right in his mouth. Oh, it was so sweet and juicy! A burst of yummy berry flavor filled his mouth, making him kick his little back legs with pure delight. Mmm, mmm, best breakfast ever! Toby chewed happily, savoring every single bite until it was all gone. With a full tummy and a very happy heart, Toby wiped his mouth with his paw and looked around for his next big adventure in the wonderful, sunny meadow.

stories.title: Toby Turtle's Slow Walk
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, little Toby Turtle woke up in his cozy shell. Good morning, sleepy head! whispered the warm yellow sun. Toby peeked his green head out and blinked. Today was a very special day. It was the big Garden Race! Toby wanted to race to the juicy red strawberry at the other side of the path. Are you ready, Toby? asked Sammy the snail. I am ready, said Toby in his quiet, happy voice. Slow and steady wins the race. Toby tucked his toes and started to move. Crunch, crunch, went the tiny pebbles under his feet. Step by slow step, Toby walked through the clover. A big, bouncy bunny hopped right past him. Whee! shouted the bunny. Zoom! went a busy little bee. But Toby did not rush. He looked at a shiny blue drop of morning dew. He smiled at a friendly brown beetle. Being a turtle meant he could see all the wonderful little things in the big world. As the afternoon sun began to glow like a warm orange, Toby saw the bright red strawberry. He reached out a gentle green foot and touched the sweet fruit. Hooray! cheered all the bugs in the grass. Toby won the race because he took his time and enjoyed every single step of the journey. Toby ate a sweet bite of strawberry and felt very happy. Then, he tucked his head and his little feet back into his cozy shell for a nice, long nap under the stars.

stories.title: Tina Turtle Finds a Friend
stories.text: Deep in the cool, clear blue pond, Tina Turtle swam through the green lily pads. Splash, splash, went her little webbed flippers. Tina loved to swim, but today she felt a little bit lonely. She wanted a special friend to play hide and seek with. Who wants to play? called Tina in a bubbly voice. A big orange fish swam by and blew bubbles, but the fish was too fast. A yellow duck quacked hello, but the duck flew up into the sky. Tina crawled up onto a warm, flat rock to rest her shell. The sun felt so nice and cozy on her back. Suddenly, she heard a soft splash in the water. Hello there! whispered a small, spotted frog who was sitting on a green leaf. Are you having a good day? asked the friendly frog. I am, said Tina, but I am looking for a friend to play with. I love playing hide and seek! said the frog. I am very good at hiding in the green reeds. Would you like to play with me? Oh, I would love that! cheered Tina. The little frog hopped into the tall grass, and Tina counted to three. One, two, three! Ready or not, here I come! Tina looked under the lily pads. She looked behind the smooth brown rocks. Then, she saw two big, blinking frog eyes peeking out from the green moss. I see you! laughed Tina. The happy frog jumped up and down. They played all afternoon, splashing and swimming and hiding in the sunshine. Tina was not lonely anymore because she had made a wonderful new friend.

stories.title: Tommy Turtle's Cozy Shell
stories.text: Tommy Turtle loved his shiny, domed shell more than anything in the whole wide world. It was green and brown, with lovely patterns that looked like little puzzle pieces. It was his very own mobile home! Come on, Tommy, let's go explore the big garden! called his mother. Tommy popped his head out of his shell. Good morning, Mama! he chirped. Tommy crawled over the soft green moss, carrying his heavy shell on his back. It was strong and hard, like a little castle. Suddenly, big, gray clouds rolled across the sky. Boom! went the loud thunder. Splish, splash! Big raindrops began to fall from the sky. Oh, no! cried Tommy, feeling a little bit scared of the loud weather. Quick, Tommy, use your shell! called his mama. Tommy knew just what to do. He pulled his head all the way inside. He pulled his four little feet inside, too. He pulled his short tail right in. Inside his shell, it was dark, quiet, and wonderfully cozy. He could hear the raindrops pattering on the roof of his house, tap, tap, tap, like tiny fingers playing a drum. But inside, Tommy was as dry as toast. He curled up in a ball and closed his eyes for a little rest. After a few minutes, the rain stopped. The sun came back out, shining brightly and warming the air. Tommy popped his head back out. The world smelled fresh and sweet. The grass was sparkling with water drops. Tommy smiled a big, happy smile. His shell was the best house in the world because it kept him safe wherever he went.

stories.title: Toby Turtle Takes a Walk
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, little Toby Turtle woke up in his cozy shell. "Good morning, world!" he blinked, stretching his tiny green legs. Toby loved his big green shell. It felt like a warm backpack that he could carry everywhere he went. Today, Toby wanted to visit his very best friend, Lily Ladybug, who lived near the big red strawberry patch. Toby poked his head out and whispered, "Time for a little walk!" He took one slow step forward. Then, he took another slow step. S-l-o-w and steady. That was Toby's special way. Along the path, he met Sammy Snail. "Hello, Sammy!" chirped Toby. Sammy smiled and slimed along at an even slower pace. Toby kept moving, one tiny foot at a time. The grass tickled his belly, and the warm sun kissed his nose. After what felt like a long, wonderful adventure, Toby finally reached the strawberry patch. "Hi Toby!" cheered Lily Ladybug, waving her tiny antennae. They spent the whole afternoon sharing sweet red berries and playing hide-and-seek behind the green leaves. Toby hid by pulling his head and legs right inside his magic shell. When the sun began to set, painting the sky pink and orange, Toby felt happy and sleepy. He gave Lily a gentle wave goodbye and started his slow, happy walk back home. Climbing into his soft bed of moss, Toby curled up tight. He pulled his shell close and whispered, "It is so nice to be a turtle." With a big yawn, Toby closed his eyes and drifted off to dreamland, ready for another slow and wonderful day tomorrow.

stories.title: Timmy's Splashy Day
stories.text: Timmy was a little river turtle with a shiny, bumpy shell that looked just like a green stepping stone. Timmy loved the water, but more than anything, Timmy loved bubbles. Every morning, he would swim to the edge of the blue river where the bubbly foam danced on the ripples. Today, the sun was shining brightly, making the water sparkle like millions of tiny diamonds. Timmy wiggled his flippers. Splash, splash, splash! He kicked his feet and made little ripples that tickled the tummy of a passing yellow duckling. "Quack quack!" said the duckling. "Hello, Timmy!" Timmy bobbed his head up and down to say hello back. He wanted to swim all the way to the big lily pad in the middle of the river, but swimming fast was hard work. So, Timmy took a nice deep breath and floated on his back, just like a little green boat. The gentle river current carried him softly along. Up and down, up and down went Timmy on the tiny waves. Suddenly, a big, bubbly splash popped right on his nose! "Pop!" went the bubble. Timmy giggled and tried to catch another one with his nose, but it floated away into the bright blue sky. He swam around the green lily pad once, twice, three times, playing tag with his own shadow in the clear, cool water. By afternoon, Timmy's little tummy began to rumble. He found a yummy, crunchy green leaf floating by and munched it right up. With a happy sigh, Timmy crawled onto a warm, flat rock to dry his shell in the golden sunshine. He closed his eyes, listened to the gentle water sing its sleepy song, and took a long, cozy nap right there in the warm afternoon breeze.

stories.title: Tessa's Magic Shell
stories.text: Tessa was a curious little sea turtle with flippers that looked like butterfly wings. She lived in a magical blue ocean where the coral was pink and purple, and the fish wore coats of yellow and red. Tessa loved to swim through the soft, wavy sea grass, but her favorite thing in the whole wide world was her shiny shell. Her shell had swirling patterns that looked like little ocean waves. Whenever Tessa felt scared or tired, she knew exactly what to do. She would tuck her head, her flippers, and her tail safely inside her shell, and it would transform into a cozy little submarine! Inside, it was quiet and peaceful, like a secret clubhouse just for her. One sunny morning, Tessa decided to explore the great big coral reef. She swam past a friendly blue whale who gave a giant, happy spritz of water into the air. "Whoosh!" went the whale. Tessa giggled and swam through a ring of bubbly sea foam. Then, a little shadow darted past. It was Penny Pufferfish, looking a little bit lost. "Hello, Penny! Can I help you?" asked Tessa kindly. Penny nodded her round, spiky head. "I cannot find my way back to the yellow coral castle." Tessa smiled warmly. "Follow me! My shell will guide the way." With her shiny shell glowing in the sunlight that peeked through the blue water, Tessa led the little pufferfish safely home. Penny cheered and blew a flurry of happy bubbles. Tessa felt so proud and happy inside. She swam back to her favorite resting spot on a warm, sandy floor, tucked her flippers in, and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of all the wonderful ocean adventures she would have tomorrow.

stories.title: Timmy's Tiny Green Shoes
stories.text: Once upon a sunny time, near a big blue pond, lived a little turtle named Timmy. Timmy had a shiny, emerald-green shell that he polished every morning with a soft oak leaf. But Timmy had a big problem. Today was the Grand Garden Race, and all the forest animals were getting ready. Little Bunny was stretching her long legs. Speedy Squirrel was doing jumping jacks. And Timmy? Timmy was standing very still. "Oh dear," whispered Timmy, looking down at his slow, wiggly feet. "I cannot run fast like Bunny. I cannot jump high like Squirrel. How will I ever win the golden lettuce leaf?" Just then, wise old Grandmother Owl swooped down from her branch. She tilted her head and blinked her big yellow eyes. "Do not worry, little Timmy," hooted Grandmother Owl softly. "You have something very special. You just need to find it." Timmy thought about her words. He looked at his shell. He looked at the bumpy, rocky path of the race. Suddenly, an idea popped into his tiny turtle head! He didn't need to run fast. He didn't need to jump. Timmy lined up at the starting line right next to Speedy Squirrel and Little Bunny. "Ready, set, GO!" chirped the bluebird judge. Bunny zoomed off in a giant leap, but she tripped over a root and said, "Ouch!" Squirrel dashed up a tree to show off, but he dropped his acorns and had to chase them. But Timmy? Timmy just tucked in his head and rolled. Wheee! Because his shell was so round and smooth, Timmy rolled right over the bumpy rocks, past the tangled roots, and straight down the grassy hill. He rolled past Bunny. He rolled past Squirrel. With a gentle bump, Timmy rolled right across the finish line and bumped into the golden lettuce leaf! All the animals cheered and clapped. Timmy popped his head out with a huge smile. He learned that being slow wasn't a bad thing at all. Sometimes, going your own special way is the best way to win.

stories.title: Toby Turtle's Sleepy Shell
stories.text: The sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. Down by the muddy riverbank, Toby Turtle was getting very, very sleepy. Yawn! Toby stretched his front legs. Yawn! Toby stretched his back legs. But Toby had a bedtime routine, and he could not go to sleep until he said goodnight to his favorite things. First, Toby crawled very slowly over to the big weeping willow tree. "Goodnight, tall tree," whispered Toby. The willow leaves whispered back in the evening breeze, *swish, swish, swish*. Next, Toby paddled his little webbed feet into the cool, gentle water. "Goodnight, sparkly river," he bubbled. A little frog hopped by and croaked, *ribbit, ribbit*, which is frog language for goodnight. Then, Toby crawled onto his favorite warm flat rock. The rock had been baking in the sun all day, and it felt like a cozy heating pad for his belly. Toby climbed up and got as comfortable as he possibly could. But wait! Something was missing. Toby looked around. He needed his pajamas! But turtles don't wear cloth pajamas. Toby’s pajamas were his very own hard, cozy shell. Slowly, Toby pulled his head inside. *Swoosh.* He pulled his four green feet inside. *Swoosh.* And finally, he tucked in his little stubby tail. Inside his shell, it was dark, quiet, and wonderfully safe, like a little secret bedroom built just for him. Toby closed his eyes. Outside, the crickets began to sing their night-time lullaby. *Crick, crick, chirp, chirp.* Toby smiled in the dark and drifted off to dreamland, safe and sound inside his little green house. Goodnight, Toby Turtle. Sleep tight until the morning sun.

stories.title: Tessa's Traveling Tea Party
stories.text: It was a bright Saturday morning, and Tessa Turtle had a very important job to do. She was going to host a tea party in the clover patch! Tessa put on a tiny daisy flower behind her ear to look extra fancy. Then, she packed her favorite acorn-cup teapot and three tiny pebble teacups onto a large, flat lily pad. "Now, who should I invite?" wondered Tessa, looking around the garden with her bright, curious eyes. Just then, Sammy Snail slinked by, carrying his house on his back. "Hello, Sammy!" called Tessa. "Would you like to come to my tea party?" Sammy smiled his slow, wiggly smile and said, "I would love to, Tessa!" Next, Tessa waddled over to the juicy strawberry patch, where Fuzzy Caterpillar was munching on a leaf. "Hello, Fuzzy!" called Tessa. "Would you like some daisy-petal tea?" Fuzzy clapped his many little hands and said, "Oh yes, please!" All three friends gathered around the clover patch table. Tessa poured the pretend tea from her acorn teapot into the pebble cups. *Glug, glug, glug.* Sammy took a tiny sip and sighed happily. Fuzzy nibbled on a sweet strawberry leaf and did a happy wiggle. They didn't need to rush anywhere. They didn't need to fly or jump. They just sat together in the warm sunshine, sipping tea and sharing sweet stories about the garden bugs. When the afternoon turned into evening, the friends hugged goodbye. Tessa packed up her acorn teapot and waddled slowly back to her log. Her tummy was full of happiness, and her heart was warm. Being a turtle meant you didn't have to be in a hurry. You could take your time, make wonderful friends, and enjoy all the little sweetnesses that the garden had to offer every single day.

stories.title: Toby Turtle Takes a Walk
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a big green garden, lived a little turtle named Toby. Toby had a shiny, bumpy shell that was green like crisp lettuce and brown like yummy chocolate. Toby was very, very small, and he moved very, very slowly. Slow, slow, slow went Toby Turtle.

One sunny morning, Toby woke up and stretched his little legs. He blinked his sleepy eyes and whispered, 'Today is a wonderful day for a walk!' Toby poked his head out of his cozy shell. *Pop!* Out came his head. *Wiggle, wiggle!* Out came his four short legs.

Toby wanted to visit his very best friend, Lily Ladybug, who lived by the big red strawberry. Toby started to walk. He took one tiny step. One. Then he took another tiny step. Two. A friendly butterfly fluttered by and called, 'Good morning, Toby!' Toby smiled and waved a tiny foot. 'Good morning, butterfly!' he said softly.

As Toby crept along the garden path, he saw a bright yellow flower. He stopped to sniff it. *Sniff, sniff.* Ah, it smelled so sweet! Then he saw a smooth brown pebble. Toby crawled right over the pebble. *Bump, bump,* went his tummy. Hee-hee, that tickled!

After a long, long time—which was only a few minutes for Toby—he finally reached the big red strawberry. Guess who was waiting there? Lily Ladybug! 'Hello, Toby!' cheered Lily. 'I have a fresh strawberry leaf for us to share.' Toby's eyes sparkled with joy. He munched on the tasty leaf with Lily. Eating together was so much fun.

When the sun began to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange, Toby knew it was time for bed. He crawled back to his favorite spot under a big green leaf. Toby tucked in his little feet. He tucked in his little tail. Last of all, he tucked in his sleepy head. *Click, snug!* Safe inside his warm shell, Toby closed his eyes and dreamed sweet, slow dreams. Goodnight, Toby Turtle.

stories.title: Timmy Turtle's Splashy Day
stories.text:
Down by the edge of a cool, blue pond lived a cheerful little turtle named Timmy. Timmy loved the water more than anything else in the wide world. Every single morning, Timmy would wake up, wiggle his toes, and slide right into the sparkling pond with a happy *splish-splash!* 

Today, the sun was shining bright and warm, making the water feel just right. Timmy swam past a group of wiggly tadpoles. 'Hello, tadpoles!' bubbles Timmy. The tadpoles zoomed by and bubbled back, 'Hi, Timmy!' Timmy paddled his little webbed feet. *Kick, kick, glide.* Swimming was such a joyful game.

Soon, Timmy saw his friend Sammy the Smiling Frog sitting on a big green lily pad. Sammy was practicing his jumping. *Ribbit!* jumped Sammy into the air, landing with a loud *plop!* right back on the pad. 'Can you jump like me, Timmy?' asked Sammy playfully. 

Timmy looked at his heavy green shell. Turtles do not jump like frogs. But Timmy had a better idea! 'Watch this!' said Timmy. He swam underneath the big lily pad and gently pushed it up with his nose. *Whee!* shouted Sammy as his lily pad bobbed up and down like a little boat. 'That is even better than jumping!' giggled Sammy the Frog.

They played water games all morning long. Timmy splashed water with his tail. *Splash, splash, splash!* Sammy caught shiny water droplets on his green nose. They laughed and played until their tummies began to rumble with tiny turtle hunger.

Timmy climbed out of the cool pond and onto a warm, flat rock. The sun felt so cozy on his wet shell. He ate some crunchy green pond moss for lunch. Mmm, delicious! Feeling full and happy, Timmy rested his chin on his front paws. The gentle breeze whispered through the tall grass, singing him a sleepy lullaby. Timmy closed his eyes, thankful for another wonderful, splashy day in his lovely blue pond. Sweet dreams, Timmy Turtle.

stories.title: Tess Turtle Finds a Hat
stories.text:
Deep in the whispering woods, a little girl turtle named Tess woke up with a big yawn. 'Good morning, world!' she chirped. Tess loved to explore, but today was very, very sunny. The golden sunbeams shone right down on her head. 'Ooh, it is warm today,' said Tess. 'I need something to keep the sun away. I need a hat!'

Off went Tess on a fun-filled hat hunt. She crawled slowly through the clover. *Swish, swish* went the green leaves against her shell. Suddenly, Tess spotted something red on the ground. It was a shiny red apple! Tess rolled the apple over and tried to balance it on her head. *Oops!* Roll, roll, roll went the apple right off her head and onto the grass. Tess giggled. 'Silky apple, you are too round to be a hat!'

Tess kept on walking, step by slow step. Next, she found a fluffy yellow dandelion puff. 'Ooh, this looks soft!' she whispered. Tess carefully placed the dandelion on her head. It looked like a golden crown. But then, a playful breeze blew by. *Whoosh!* Puff went the dandelion, and all the yellow seeds floated up into the sky like tiny parachutes. Tess clapped her little hands. 'Bye-bye, dandelion hat!'

Just then, a friendly bluebird flew down from a tall oak tree carrying a wide, woven green leaf. The bluebird chirped a merry song and dropped the leaf right in front of Tess. 'Chirp, chirp! Try this, little turtle!' 

Tess picked up the lovely green leaf with her mouth and placed it right on top of her head. It was wide, cool, and shady. It fit her head like magic! Tess looked at her reflection in a puddle of clear rain water. 'Oh, it is the most beautiful hat in the whole wide world!' she cheered.

Tess wore her new leaf hat all the way home. The sun did not bother her at all anymore. When she got back to her cozy log, she curled up inside her shell, keeping her leaf hat safe for tomorrow's adventures. Goodnight, Tess.

stories.title: Toby Turtle Takes a Walk
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a big green garden, lived a little turtle named Toby. Toby had a shiny, bumpy shell that was green like crisp lettuce leaves. Toby loved his shell. It was his cozy home, his jacket when it was chilly, and his slide when he wanted to play. Every morning, Toby would peek his head out. Poke, poke went his nose. 'Good morning, sun!' whispered Toby.
