Ready to play in the water with you.

Walking on mud and splashing in play,
Eating green lettuce all through the day.
Basking right up on a cozy brown log,
Winking hello to a big green frog.

Slow is his walk as he goes on his way,
Smiling and happy throughout the whole day.
Into the water he slips with a splash,
Swimming away in a very small dash.

Now he is resting down deep in the pond,
Of his warm shell he is oh so fond.

rhymes.title: The Turtle's Tune
rhymes.text:
The little green turtle goes step by slow step,
With plenty of patience and plenty of pep.
He carries his house right up on his back,
And packs all his things in a tiny brown sack.

The sun is so warm on his shiny round shell,
He loves his green pond and he loves it so well.
A dragonfly flies and dances on high,
While our little turtle just watches it fly.

He munches a leaf that is crunchy and green,
The happiest turtle that ever was seen.
He blinks his dark eyes and he takes a short rest,
Because resting right here is what he loves best.

The stars are now coming to shine in the sky,
So let us sing turtle a sweet lullaby.

rhymes.title: Little Green Turtle
rhymes.text:
Little green turtle, crawling so slow,
Where are you going, where will you go?
Walking along on the soft, green ground,
Looking for snacks that can easily be found.

You have a shell that is shiny and brown,
The coziest little house in the town.
When you are tired and ready for sleep,
Into your shell you quietly creep.

Pull in your head and tuck in your toes,
Nobody bothers you, goodness knows.
Dreaming of rivers and lily pads bright,
Sleeping right through the quiet, dark night.

Morning comes early with sunshine and dew,
Little green turtle, I'm waking up too!
Time to go swimming and splash in the lake,
What a fun journey we both get to make.

rhymes.title: Toby Turtle's Shell
rhymes.text:
Toby the turtle has a shell so green,
The finest house that you've ever seen.
He carries it with him wherever he goes,
Right down to the water and streams that flow.

When it starts raining and starts to pour,
Toby is safe and he needs nothing more.
He tucks in his head and his little feet too,
Waiting right there till the storm is through.

When the sun shines and the sky is bright,
Toby comes out in the morning light.
He walks very slowly across the soft sand,
The happiest creature in all of the land.

He munches on lettuce and drinks from the brook,
Looking around with a sweet, gentle look.
Little green turtle, so happy and free,
You are a wonderful friend to me.

rhymes.title: Five Little Turtles
rhymes.text:
Five little turtles sitting on a stone,
One went for a swim all alone.
Water was cool and the water was deep,
Little green turtle began to leap.

Four little turtles sitting on a log,
Watching the jump of a funny green frog.
One slid right down with a soft, gentle splash,
Swimming away in a magical dash.

Three little turtles resting in the sun,
Having such a wonderful, playful run.
One went to look for a strawberry sweet,
Finding a yummy and delicious treat.

Two little turtles left on the shore,
Wishing and hoping to play some more.
One crawled away to his cozy shell home,
Leaving the last one to quietly roam.

One little turtle is all by himself,
Looking just like a toy on a shelf.
He closes his eyes and he takes a deep rest,
Knowing his turtle life is the best.

rhymes.title: Little Green Shell
rhymes.text:
Little turtle on the ground,
Walking slowly all around.
He has got a shell so green,
Cutest pet you've ever seen.

Pokes his head out of his shell,
Looking round the grassy dell.
Sees a bug upon a tree,
Wiggles toes with so much glee.

Now the sun begins to set,
He is not quite ready yet.
Crawls into his cozy bed,
Rests his sleepy little head.

Goodnight turtle, sleep till morn,
Fresh and happy you'll be born.
Dreams of swimming in the blue,
Little turtle, I love you.

rhymes.title: Puddle Splash
rhymes.text:
Tiny turtle takes a walk,
Stopping by to hear frogs talk.
Ribbit, ribbit goes the frog,
Sitting on a slippery log.

Turtle waddles in the rain,
Water drops upon the pane.
He wears boots of shiny red,
Nodding gently with his head.

Splish and splash inside the mud,
Watch the opening flower bud.
Turtle smiles a happy smile,
Resting for a little while.

Now the rain is gone away,
Rainbow colors out to play.
Turtle climbs into his shell,
Sleeping in his woodland dell.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Slow and steady wins the race,
Turtle has a happy pace.
Never rushing, always bright,
Walking in the morning light.

Munching on a leafy treat,
Using hands and tiny feet.
Blinking with his big round eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.

Butterfly goes flying high,
Way up in the sunny sky.
Turtle waves a little hand,
Bestest turtle in the land.

Stars are shining in the deep,
Turtle whispers time to sleep.
Into bed he safely creeps,
While the quiet forest sleeps.

rhymes.title: Little Turtle Shell
rhymes.text:
Little turtle in the pond,
Swimming all the day beyond.
He has got a cozy shell,
Where he likes to hide so well.

Poke your head out in the sun,
Now the day has just begun.
Little green feet walking slow,
Watch the happy turtle go.

Climb upon a woody log,
Wave hello to Mr. Frog.
Splash your toes in water blue,
Little turtle, I love you.

Time to sleep inside your bed,
Tuck in both your feet and head.
Dream of bugs and flowers sweet,
Rest your little turtle feet.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Walking slowly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Carrying a house so wide,
Where a turtle likes to hide.

Sunlight warms his sleepy back,
Following a muddy track.
Leaves are green and sky is blue,
Turtle wants to play with you.

Reach a little webbed hand out,
Look around and look about.
Find a clover on the floor,
Eat a leaf and then eat more.

Now the evening star is bright,
Turtle says a quiet goodnight.
Pull your head in nice and deep,
Time for little friends to sleep.

rhymes.title: Green and Bumpy
rhymes.text:
Green and bumpy is his shell,
Living in the garden well.
Crawling through the clover patch,
Looking for a snack to catch.

Blink your little sleepy eyes,
Underneath the sunny skies.
Slide into the water cool,
Swimming in the garden pool.

Float upon the water high,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.
Paddle with your tiny feet,
Life is happy, life is sweet.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best green turtle I have met.
Close your eyes and slumber deep,
Time for little ones to sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Turtle's Green Shell
rhymes.text:
Little turtle on the floor,
Walking slowly to the door.
He has got a shell so green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.

Poke your head out in the sun,
Now our playtime has begun.
Stretch your neck and blink your eyes,
Look at all the butterflies.

Little feet go tap, tap, tap,
Time to take a little nap.
In your house so safe and tight,
Sleep until the morning light.

Goodnight turtle, rest your head,
In your cozy turtle bed.
Dream of leaves and flowers sweet,
Rest your little turtle feet.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Turtle walks along the street,
Moving slow his little feet.
Carrying his house of brown,
Walking all around the town.

Stop to munch a clover leaf,
Chewing slowly, what a treat.
Now he smiles a happy grin,
Pulling all his arms right in.

Push them out and crawl away,
Splashing in the pond today.
Bubbles pop up in the air,
Turtle friends are everywhere.

Sun is setting in the sky,
Wave your little hand goodbye.
Crawl into your shell to rest,
Turtle home is always best.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Puddle
rhymes.text:
Rain is falling from the sky,
Clouds are floating way up high.
Turtle wears his boots today,
Ready for some rainy play.

Squish and squash and squish and squelch,
Eating up a yummy kelp.
Jumping in the mud so deep,
While the little fish fall sleep.

Turtle laughs and claps his hands,
Building castles in the sands.
Now the sun begins to glow,
Watch the pretty rainbow show.

Time to dry the muddy feet,
Find a cozy place to sleep.
Turtle had a happy day,
Now it's time to rest and play.

rhymes.title: The Little Green Turtle
rhymes.text:
There is a little turtle,
Who lives down by the lake.
He has a happy smile,
And eats a strawberry cake.

He swims around the water,
And plays hide and seek.
He hides inside his shell,
For more than just a week.

He has four little feet,
That paddle to and fro.
He walks along the mud,
Because he likes it slow.

Goodnight, little turtle,
Rest your sleepy head.
Tomorrow is another day,
Go sleep in your shell bed.

rhymes.title: Turtle Time
rhymes.text:
Turtle, turtle, in the sun,
Tell me, are you having fun?
You have a shell of green and brown,
The sweetest turtle in the town.

You walk along the garden floor,
And knock upon the wooden door.
You munch a leaf of yummy green,
The happiest shell I've ever seen.

When the rain begins to fall,
You do not worry, not at all.
You tuck your head and toes inside,
And take a cozy, sleepy ride.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for turtles fast asleep.
Close your bright and shiny eyes,
Dreaming of the morning skies.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Slow and steady wins the race,
Turtle walks at his own pace.
He carries his house upon his back,
Along the muddy woodland track.

He sees a bug upon a tree,
And waves his little flipper free.
He loves to swim in waters blue,
With little fish and frogs to do.

He takes a nap upon a stone,
Inside his heavy, bumpy home.
Then wakes up when the day is bright,
To crawl into the golden light.

Oh, little turtle, small and sweet,
With tiny, precious walking feet,
We love to watch you as you go,
Walking softly, nice and slow.

rhymes.title: Little Green Shell
rhymes.text:
Little turtle in the pond,
Swimming where the weeds grow blond.
Pop your head out, say hello,
Where are you so slow to go?

Green shell shiny in the sun,
Walking slowly is so fun.
Four small feet upon the ground,
Making not a single sound.

Climb up on a bumpy log,
Wave goodbye to Mr. Frog.
Tuck your head in nice and tight,
Sleep until the morning light.

Wake up when the sky is blue,
Little turtle, I love you.
Snap a leaf and take a bite,
Have a happy day and night.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Toby Turtle takes a walk,
Never likes to rush or talk.
One slow foot steps on the floor,
Creeping softly by the door.

He has spots of brown and green,
Cutest pet you've ever seen.
Carries house right on his back,
Packed up in a little pack.

When he feels a sudden breeze,
Crawls beneath the leafy trees.
Pulls his nose in out of sight,
Hiding till the morning light.

Then he pops his face right out,
Looking all around about.
Slow and steady wins the race,
With a smile upon his face.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Mud
rhymes.text:
Tiny turtle by the stream,
Swimming in a sunny dream.
Water ripples, cold and clear,
Glad that summer days are here.

Finds a little patch of mud,
Stomps a foot with quite a thud.
Splash goes water in the air,
Droplets landing everywhere.

Wiggles tail and blinks an eye,
Watches dragonflies fly by.
Crawls upon a cozy stone,
Happy in his shell alone.

Yawns a little turtle yawn,
Waiting for another dawn.
Closes eyes to rest his head,
In his cozy turtle bed.

rhymes.title: Little Green Turtle
rhymes.text:
Little turtle in the grass,
Watch him slowly, slowly pass.
He has got a shell so green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.

He has four feet on the ground,
Walking slowly all around.
When he wants to go to sleep,
Into shell he takes a peep.

Head goes in and feet go too,
Now he is hidden from view.
Wait a minute, count to four,
Head is popping out once more!

Little turtle, time to play,
Have a happy, sunny day.
Munching on a clover leaf,
Turtle life is far from brief.

rhymes.title: The Muddy Pond
rhymes.text:
Down beside the muddy pond,
Turtle swims and is so fond.
Water splashes on his nose,
Tickling his tiny toes.

He can paddle, he can float,
Like a tiny green-roof boat.
Swimming past a lily pad,
Turtle never feels quite sad.

Dragonfly flies overhead,
Turtle goes to his safe bed.
Climbs upon a sunny log,
Waves hello to green bullfrog.

Sun is shining very bright,
Turtle shell reflects the light.
Time to rest his little head,
In his cozy riverbed.

rhymes.title: Slow and Steady
rhymes.text:
Slow and steady wins the race,
Turtle has a gentle pace.
Never rushing, calm and sweet,
Walking on his little feet.

Carries house upon his back,
Never loses any track.
Underneath the big oak tree,
Happiest a pet can be.

Eating berries, sweet and red,
Then he goes to take a bed.
Safe and sound inside his shell,
Everything is going well.

Goodnight turtle, sleep so deep,
Stars are watching while you sleep.
Dreaming of the water blue,
Turtle, we adore you too.

rhymes.title: Little Green Turtle
rhymes.text:
Little green turtle in the sun,
Swimming in the pond for fun.
He has a shell that is so strong,
As he swims the whole day long.
He pops his head out of his shell,
To say hello and wish you well.
He has four feet that paddle slow,
Wherever he decides to go.
A little splash right in the lake,
Watch the gentle ripples make.
He munches on a yummy leaf,
And shakes his head in soft relief.
Now it is time to go to sleep,
Buried in the mud so deep.
Sleep, little turtle, through the night,
Until the morning brings its light.

rhymes.title: The Slowpoke Race
rhymes.text:
See the turtle on the floor,
Waddling slowly to the door.
He does not ever want to run,
He likes to bask out in the sun.
He carries his house upon his back,
Along a winding garden track.
A butterfly goes flying by,
Way up high into the sky.
The turtle stops to watch it pass,
Sitting softly on the grass.
He tucks his head in for a nap,
And hears a gentle water tap.
He wakes up with a happy grin,
And lets his little feet begin.
Slow and steady wins the day,
As he happily goes his way.

rhymes.title: Turtle's Cozy Shell
rhymes.text:
Turtle, turtle, in the pond,
Of the water you are fond.
You swim around so calm and cool,
In the middle of the pool.
When the rain begins to fall,
You are safe and dry and small.
Tuck your head inside your coat,
While the lily pads all float.
When the storm is gone and past,
You can stretch your legs out fast.
Crawl upon a wooden log,
Wave hello to Mr. Frog.
The sun is warm, the sky is blue,
Little turtle, I love you.
Time to rest your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the painted skies.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Splash
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big, floppy ears that went flap, flap, flap, and a long, grey trunk that went swoosh! Today was a very hot day, and the sun was shining bright in the sky. Phew, it was warm! Ellie walked with her mummy through the tall grass, stomping her big feet. Boom, boom, boom! 'Mummy, I am so hot,' said Ellie, giving a little squeak. 'Don't worry, my little one,' said Mummy Elephant with a gentle smile. 'Let us go find the sparkling river.' 

Soon, they reached the cool, blue water. Other jungle animals were already there splashing about. Monkey was hanging from a vine, and Hippo was already soaking his big tummy. Ellie ran right to the edge of the water. She dipped her toes in. Brrr! It felt so nice and cool. 'Now watch this, Ellie,' said her mummy. Mummy Elephant dipped her long trunk right into the river. She sucked up water, up, up, up went the water inside her trunk! Then, WHOSH! She sprayed a giant, wonderful fountain of water all over her back. Splash! 

Ellie giggled a happy baby elephant giggle. Tee-hee-hee! She wanted to try too. Ellie walked a little closer to the water. She put the very tip of her trunk down into the river. She tried to suck up water. Slurp, slurp! Oh, goodness, she tickled her own nose! Ellie sneezed a big elephant sneeze. Achoo! All the little fishies swam away fast. Mummy laughed and nudged Ellie gently with her warm side. 'Try again, sweet Ellie. Take your time.' 

Ellie tried once more. She sucked up the water. This time, she got it! Her trunk felt heavy and full. She pointed her trunk up high into the air, toward the fluffy white clouds. Ready, set, go! Ellie blew hard. Pfffft! A wonderful spray of water burst out of her trunk, sparkling in the sunshine. It rained down on her head, her ears, and her toes. 'Yay! I did it! I am a splashing elephant!' shouted Ellie, clapping her big ears together. She splashed and stomped and played in the river all afternoon long. When the sun began to sink low and turn the sky pink and orange, Ellie felt cozy, clean, and very sleepy. She snuggled up right next to her mummy for a warm nap, dreaming of cool water and big, happy splashes.

stories.title: Ellie's Lost Balloon
stories.text:
Up, up, up went the bright red balloon! It danced in the gentle morning breeze, bobbing over the green jungle trees. It belonged to Ellie, a sweet little baby elephant with big, velvety ears. Ellie loved her red balloon more than anything in the whole wide world. She held tight to the yellow string with the very tip of her long, grey trunk. As Ellie walked along the jungle path, she met her good friend, Sammy Monkey. 'Hello, Ellie!' chattered Sammy, doing a little flip. Ellie waved back, but as she raised her trunk to say hello, oh no! Her fingers slipped. Or rather, her trunk slipped! The yellow string went loose. 

Whoosh! The bright red balloon shot up into the sky, higher and higher, past the tall banana leaves, past the chattering monkeys, and up toward the fluffy white clouds. 'Oh, no!' cried Ellie, her big brown eyes filling with worry tears. 'My balloon is flying away!' Sammy Monkey swung up into the branches. 'Don't worry, Ellie! I will help you catch it!' Sammy climbed up, up, up, as fast as a monkey can go, reaching for the floating red toy. But the balloon went higher still, carried by a friendly puff of wind. Ellie stomped her feet. Boom, boom, boom! She felt sad. She wanted her bouncing, floating red friend back. 

Just then, tall giraffe came stepping over the bushes. Her name was Gina. 'Why are you looking down, little Ellie?' asked Gina kindly, bending her long, spotted neck down low. 'My red balloon flew up into the sky,' sniffled Ellie. Gina smiled a warm, gentle smile. 'Well, let me take a look from up here.' Gina stretched her long neck all the way up toward the sky. Way up high! She blinked her big eyelashes. 'Ah, I see it! It is stuck right near that cloud.' Gina reached out her long, gentle nose and tapped the balloon. Pop? No, not pop! She gently nudged it down, down, down toward the treetops. 

Sammy Monkey was waiting! He grabbed the yellow string just in time. 'Got it!' cheered Sammy, swinging down to the grass. He handed the string right back to Ellie. Ellie wrapped the string tightly around her trunk, holding on with all her might. She let out a joyful trumpet sound. Toot-toot-hooray! 'Thank you, my wonderful friends,' beamed Ellie. She hugged Sammy and Gina with her trunk. Holding her precious red balloon safely, Ellie skipped happily all the way home, learning to always hold on tight to her favorite things.

stories.title: Ellie Learns to Share
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny afternoon, baby elephant Ellie found a big pile of shiny, bright green jungle leaves. Oh, they looked so yummy and crisp! Ellie loved crunchy leaves. She picked up a huge bunch with her long grey trunk and popped them into her mouth. Munch, munch, crunch! They tasted sweet and delicious. 'Yum, yum, yum,' whispered Ellie to herself, her tummy rumbling with happiness. Just then, her little friend Timmy Turtle waddled slowly down the path. Timmy looked very tired, and his little green shell was dusty from the long walk. 

Timmy stopped right in front of Ellie and gave a tiny wave. 'Hello, Ellie,' said Timmy in his soft, slow voice. 'It is a very warm day, and I am so hungry.' Ellie looked at her big pile of shiny green leaves. She looked at Timmy Turtle. At first, Ellie pulled the pile closer to her tummy. She tucked her chin down. These were HER leaves. She found them all by herself! 'Mine,' thought Ellie, feeling a little sting of selfishness in her heart. She took another big bite. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Timmy Turtle sighed softly and looked down at the dusty ground, turning to waddle away. 

Ellie paused. She watched Timmy's slow little feet step away in the dirt. Timmy looked so small and so sad. Ellie remembered how her mummy always said, 'Sharing makes our hearts grow twice as big, Ellie.' Ellie stopped chewing. She opened her mouth and swallowed her bite. Then, she used her long trunk to gently scoop up half of the bright, crisp green leaves. She slid them across the grass right in front of Timmy Turtle. 'Here you go, Timmy,' said Ellie with a big, happy smile. 'You can have some of my yummy leaves.' 

Timmy Turtle's eyes grew as wide as saucers. A huge smile spread across his little green face. 'Oh! Thank you so much, Ellie!' said Timmy. He happily munched on the crunchy leaves. Munch, munch, munch! Ellie felt a warm, fuzzy feeling bloom right inside her chest. Sharing felt even better than eating all by herself! They sat together in the warm jungle sunshine, eating their leaves and chatting happily. When they were all done, Ellie and Timmy played hide-and-seek behind the big fern plants until the stars came out to twinkle in the night sky.

stories.title: Ella's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, there lived a little elephant named Ella. Ella had two floppy ears, one very long trunk, and four very big, gray feet. Ella loved the jungle, but she loved puddles even more. Every single morning, Ella would wake up and wiggle her toes. Splash, splash, go the little puddles! Squish, squish, go the big mud puddles! One sunny morning, the jungle animals were having a grand parade. Monkey was swinging from the tall trees. Zebra was marching with his shiny black and white stripes. Giraffe was stretching her long, spotted neck way up high. Ella wanted to join the parade, but she had a big problem. Her big gray feet were cold! Oh no! Ella looked down at her toes and let out a little trumpet sound. Toot-toot! Just then, her kind friend Turtle came crawling by. Turtle was carrying a big package wrapped in shiny yellow leaves. What could it be inside? Ella used her long trunk to gently unwrap the leaves. Inside were four bright red boots! They were gigantic boots, just the right size for a little elephant. Ella was so excited that she did a happy little dance. Boom, boom, went her feet! She slipped her big gray left foot into the first red boot. Then she slipped her big gray right foot into the second red boot. She put boots on all four of her feet! They looked so funny and bright. Ella marched right over to the parade line. March, march, left, right, left! Monkey pointed and giggled. Zebra smiled a big, toothy grin. Giraffe clapped her hooves together. Ella’s new boots made a happy squishy sound with every single step. The parade started moving down the winding jungle path. Ella marched proudly at the very front. Suddenly, dark gray clouds rolled across the sky. Plip, plop, plip, plop. Raindrops began to fall on the leaves. The other animals started to look for a dry place to hide. But not Ella! Ella smiled a big elephant smile. The rain fell down, but Ella’s feet stayed warm and dry inside her wonderful red boots. She found a giant mud puddle right in the middle of the path. With a giant leap, Ella jumped right into the middle of it. Splash! Mud went flying everywhere. Monkey cheered. Zebra danced. Everyone laughed and splashed in the rain together. Ella knew that having big feet was great, but having big feet with red boots was simply the best thing in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: High up on the sunny hill, a little baby elephant named Barnaby was having the best day ever. Today was his third birthday! To celebrate, his mama gave him a shiny, bright blue balloon. The balloon was round and smooth, and it floated gently at the end of a long white string. Barnaby held the string tightly in his trunk. He loved his blue balloon so much that he gave it a little hug. Barnaby and his mama decided to take a walk through the whispering tall grass. Swish, swish, went the grass against Barnaby’s legs. Barnaby held his balloon up high so everyone could see it. First, they passed wise old Owl sitting on a branch. 'Happy birthday, Barnaby!' hooted Owl. Barnaby waved his trunk and said, 'Look at my balloon!' Next, they passed playful little Bunny hopping in the clover. 'Happy birthday!' squeaked Bunny. Barnaby smiled from ear to ear. But then, a sudden puff of wind came blowing through the trees. Whoosh! The wind was stronger than Barnaby expected. It tugged at the string in his trunk. Oh no! Barnaby’s grip slipped. Let go! The shiny blue balloon popped right out of his trunk and drifted up into the sky. Up, up, up it went, past the green leaves, past the singing birds, floating higher and higher toward the fluffy white clouds. Barnaby let out a sad little cry. A tear rolled down his dusty cheek. He watched his wonderful birthday balloon getting smaller and smaller. His mama wrapped her warm, comforting trunk around his shoulder. 'Don't worry, my sweet little one,' she whispered softly. 'Let's look for something new.' Barnaby sniffled and wiped his eye with his big floppy ear. Just as they turned around to walk home, Barnaby heard a funny sound in the bushes. Rustle, rustle, snap! Out popped a little gray squirrel carrying something round and blue. It was not a balloon at all. It was a giant, round blueberry! The squirrel looked at Barnaby and giggled. 'Is this yours?' asked the squirrel kindly. Barnaby’s eyes went wide. It wasn't his balloon, but it was round, blue, and looked very delicious. Barnaby’s tummy gave a happy little rumble. He took the giant blueberry in his trunk and thanked the friendly squirrel. Barnaby realized that losing a balloon wasn't the end of the world, especially when you find a tasty treat and have a loving mama by your side. They walked home together, sharing the sweet blue berry, smiling all the way.

stories.title: Pip's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was beginning to set behind the rolling green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. Down in the cozy valley, a little baby elephant named Pip was getting ready for bed. Pip had the softest gray skin, the cutest button eyes, and a tiny trunk that loved to wiggle. But tonight, Pip was not sleepy at all. He rolled over on his back and kicked his little legs in the air. His mama smiled lovingly and tucked him in with a soft, starry blanket. 'Time to rest your eyes, my little one,' whispered Mama Elephant gently. Pip shook his big head. He wanted to play! He wanted to stomp his feet and trumpet to the moon. Mama Elephant knew just what to do. She began to sing a slow, soothing bedtime song. It was a gentle humming sound that echoed through the warm evening air. Mmm-mmm, went the lullaby. Pip stopped kicking his legs and started to listen. The music felt like a warm hug. Mama reached out with her long, flexible trunk and gently stroked Pip’s forehead. It felt so relaxing. Pip closed his heavy eyes for just a moment. He listened to the crickets chirping their quiet evening song in the grass. He listened to the gentle wind rustling the leaves of the big acacia tree. Slowly, Pip began to feel very, very heavy. His right ear flopped down onto the soft grass. Then his left ear flopped down too. His tiny tail stopped twitching. Pip let out a long, sleepy yawn. Ahhh-wooo. Mama continued her sweet humming, rocking gently from side to side. Pip dreamed of a magical land made of floating clouds and sweet green leaves. He imagined flying high above the treetops on the back of a friendly butterfly. His breathing became slow and steady. In and out. In and out. The stars came out one by one, twinkling like tiny diamonds in the deep blue sky, watching over the sleeping valley. Mama Elephant leaned down and gave her little baby one final, tender kiss on his forehead. Pip was finally fast asleep, resting peacefully until the bright morning sun would wake him up to play all over again.

stories.title: Ella's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ella. Ella had big, floppy ears that went flop, flop, flop, and a long, squiggly trunk that went wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Ella loved the jungle, but today, the sun was shining extra hot. Phew! It was so, so warm. Ella needed to cool down. 'Mamma, I am hot!' said Ella, making a little trumpet sound. 'Let us go find the water hole,' said her kind mamma. So, off they marched. Stomp, stomp, stomp went their big feet on the soft dirt. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Along the way, Ella saw her friend Monty the monkey. 'Hello, Monty!' called Ella. Monty was swinging in the trees. 'Whee!' cried Monty, tossing a bright yellow banana peel. Ella used her long trunk to catch the banana peel and tickled Monty's tummy. Tee-hee-hee! They giggled and kept on walking. Soon, Ella heard a happy sound. Splish, splash, splash! It was the sparkling blue water hole. Other baby animals were already there, splashing and playing in the cool mud. Ella could not wait. She ran as fast as her little legs could carry her. Thump, thump, thump! When she reached the water, she did not just jump in. No, no! Ella used her magical trunk like a hose. She dipped the tip of her trunk deep into the cool, refreshing water. Sloop, sloop, sloop! She sucked up a big, big belly full of water. Then, she pointed her trunk straight up in the air. Ready, set, go! WHOOSH! Ella sprayed a gigantic, sparkly fountain of water all over herself. Water droplets danced in the bright sunshine like diamonds. 'Yay!' cheered all the animals. Ella felt so cool and happy. Next, Ella found the squishiest, muddiest puddle of all. She plopped right down on her tummy. Squish, squelch, squish! The mud felt tickly and cold against her warm skin. She rolled to the left, and she rolled to the right, covering herself from head to toe in thick, brown mud. Mud is the best sunscreen for a happy little elephant. Mamma smiled and joined in, spraying a gentle shower right on top of Ella's head. They splashed and played until the sun began to hide behind the tall green trees. Ella was nice and cool, wonderfully tired, and as happy as could be. 'Time for bed, my little water baby,' whispered Mamma. Ella gave one last happy trumpet, snuggled close to her mamma's warm side, and drifted off to sweet jungle dreams.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Barnaby was a sweet little blue elephant who loved colorful things. Today was a very special day because Barnaby went to the big jungle carnival with his daddy. The carnival was full of loud, happy sounds and wonderful smells. There was popcorn popping and music playing. But Barnaby's most favorite thing in the whole wide world was the balloon man. The balloon man had balloons of every color you could ever dream of. Red ones, green ones, yellow ones, and purple ones. Barnaby pointed his little trunk and chose the biggest, shiniest, brightest red balloon. It danced on a long string, bobbing up and down in the breeze. 'Hold on tight, Barnaby,' said Daddy. Barnaby held the string firmly in his trunk. He felt so proud. He marched through the carnival, showing off his wonderful red balloon. He walked past the spinning merry-go-round and waved at the dancing zebras. But then, oh no! A playful little breeze came swooshing through the trees. Whoosh! The wind tugged at the string. Barnaby was looking at a spinning pinwheel, and before he knew it, his trunk opened just a tiny bit. Slipped! The red balloon popped right out of his grasp. 'Oh no, my balloon!' cried Barnaby. Up, up, up went the red balloon into the bright blue sky. It floated past the tall coconut trees. It floated higher than the monkeys could swing. Barnaby watched with big, sad eyes as his beautiful red balloon grew smaller and smaller, turning into a tiny dot. A big, round tear rolled down Barnaby's cheek. Daddy knelt down and gave Barnaby a giant, cozy elephant hug. 'Do not worry, my little Barnaby,' Daddy whispered softly. 'Sometimes things float away, but we can make new happy memories.' Just then, a friendly little parrot flew down from a branch. In the parrot's beak was something wonderful. It was a bright yellow pinwheel that spun in the wind with a happy click-clack sound. The parrot dropped the pinwheel right at Barnaby's feet. Barnaby picked it up with his trunk and gave it a gentle puff. Whoosh! The yellow pinwheel spun round and round, creating a blur of sunny color. Barnaby gasped and clapped his big ears together. 'Look, Daddy! It spins!' Barnaby giggled, chasing the colorful blurs on the ground. He realized that while the balloon was gone, the carnival was still full of fun. Barnaby held Daddy's hand, spinning his new toy, and smiled the biggest smile ever. It turned out to be the best day after all.

stories.title: Barnaby's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was sinking low behind the hills, painting the sky in shades of soft pink and sleepy orange. It was bedtime in the quiet jungle. Little baby elephant Barnaby was getting very sleepy. His heavy eyelids felt like they were made of stone. Blink, blink, blink went his big brown eyes. But Barnaby had one little problem. He could not find his favorite snuggly blanket. It was a soft, green blankie that smelled like sweet clover. 'Where is my blankie?' whispered Barnaby, making a tiny, worried squeak. He looked behind the big fern leaves. It was not there. He looked under the fallen log. It was not there either. Just then, his wise old grandpa walked over. Grandpa elephant had very big ears and a very gentle smile. 'Are you looking for your cozy blankie, little one?' asked Grandpa in a deep, rumbling voice that sounded like a lullaby. Barnaby nodded his head up and down. 'Let us look together,' Grandpa said kindly. They went on a quiet search through the twilight jungle. The crickets were starting to sing their evening song. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. The fireflies turned on their tiny glowing lights, floating like fairy stars in the dark air. Blink, blink went the fireflies. Barnaby and Grandpa walked softly, making hardly any sound at all. Tip-toe, tip-toe went their big feet. They checked near the sleepy watering hole where the frogs were saying goodnight. Ribbit, ribbit went the frogs. Still, no green blankie. Barnaby began to yawn. A big, wide, sleepy yawn that stretched his trunk wide open. Yawn! Grandpa smiled and gently nudged a cozy bush with his trunk. 'Look right there, sleepyhead,' said Grandpa. Resting softly on top of the sweet-smelling clover was the green blankie, folded just right. Barnaby let out a happy little gasp. He scooped up his blankie with his trunk and hugged it tight against his chest. It was so soft and warm. Grandpa led Barnaby to their favorite sleeping spot under the giant baobab tree. Mamma elephant was waiting there, ready with a bedtime story. Barnaby snuggled down into the soft grass. He wrapped his green blankie around his shoulders and held tight to Grandpa's big, warm foot. Mamma whispered a gentle bedtime story about stars and clouds. Barnaby's eyes closed tight. His breathing became slow and deep. He was safe, he was cozy, and he was deeply loved. Goodnight, little Barnaby elephant. Sweet dreams until the morning sun.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the big green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears, a long gray trunk, and four very big feet. One sunny morning, Ellie woke up and found a surprise waiting right outside her tent. They were a pair of bright, shiny, red rain boots! Ellie’s eyes went wide. She had never worn boots before. She wiggled her toes and decided to try them on. Slip, slop, slide! Her left foot went in. Slip, slop, slide! Her right foot went in. Ellie stood up tall and looked down at her feet. 'Stomp, stomp, stomp!' went the red boots. They made a loud, happy noise on the dirt path. Ellie was so excited that she started to march all around the jungle. She marched past the tall banana trees. She marched past the sleeping monkeys. 'Look at my red boots!' trumpeted Ellie with a happy toot-toot from her trunk. Soon, Ellie came to a big, squishy mud puddle. Most of the animals tried to stay away from the deep mud, but not Ellie today. She walked right up to the edge of the puddle and looked down at her shiny red boots. 'Can boots go splash?' she wondered aloud. Ellie lifted her big right foot way up high in the air and brought it down hard into the middle of the puddle. Splash! Mud flew up into the air. A little frog popped out of the water and croaked in surprise. Ellie giggled and lifted her other foot. Splash, squish, pop! She stomped and danced in the mud until her red boots were completely covered in brown slop. They were not shiny anymore, but they were definitely having fun. Just then, her mother walked over and smiled warmly. 'It looks like your boots love the mud, Ellie,' Mama Elephant said gently. Ellie nodded and gave her mother a big mud-splattered hug. By the time the sun began to set, Ellie was very tired. She washed her boots in the clean river water, placed them neatly by her bed, and curled up for a cozy sleep, dreaming of all the splashing she would do tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Barnaby was a sweet little elephant who loved parties more than anything else in the whole wide world. Today was a very special day because it was his third birthday. All of his jungle friends came over to celebrate with him. There were monkeys, zebras, and colorful parrots singing songs. The best part of the party was the balloons. Mama Elephant had given Barnaby a big, shiny, yellow balloon on a long string. Barnaby held the string tightly in his trunk. He walked around showing everyone his wonderful balloon. It bobbed up and down in the air, looking just like a bright little sun. Barnaby felt so happy that he spun around in a circle. But oh dear! As he spun around, his trunk slipped just a little bit. Whoosh! The yellow balloon slipped right out of his grasp. It floated up into the air, higher and higher, past the green leaves of the tallest tree. Barnaby let out a sad little trumpet sound. 'Oh no, my balloon!' he cried softly. He thought his birthday was ruined. But Barnaby’s friends were very kind. Wise old Monkey swung up into the branches to see if he could catch it. The balloon was still too high, floating near a fluffy white cloud. Then, Barnaby had a clever idea. He remembered that elephants are exceptionally good at something very special. Barnaby took a deep, deep breath. He filled his long trunk with air until his cheeks puffed out. Then, he pointed his trunk straight up at the sky and blew out the biggest puff of wind he could manage. Whoosh! A strong, friendly gust of wind shot up into the air. The wind gently pushed the yellow balloon back down toward the ground. Barnaby reached out with his trunk just in time. Grab! He caught the string safely in the tip of his trunk and pulled it down. All of his friends cheered loudly and clapped their paws. Barnaby smiled from ear to ear. He held the string even tighter this time, feeling like the luckiest elephant in the whole jungle on his very special birthday.

stories.title: The Great Peanut Hunt
stories.text: Deep in the sunny savannah, a little elephant named Oliver woke up with a very rumbling tummy. 'Rumble, rumble, go my tummy,' Oliver sang to himself. It was time for breakfast, and Oliver had a very specific craving. He did not want leaves. He did not want grass. Today, Oliver wanted crunchy, yummy peanuts! Oliver set off on a grand adventure across the yellow grass to find them. He walked along the dusty path, swinging his long trunk back and forth. Sniff, sniff, sniff went Oliver’s trunk. He smelled the sweet flowers. He smelled the warm earth. But he did not smell any peanuts yet. Suddenly, a little yellow butterfly fluttered past his nose. Oliver followed the butterfly behind a big green bush. And what do you think he found hiding right behind the bush? A large wooden basket filled to the very brim with crunchy peanuts! Oliver’s eyes lit up like bright little lanterns. He let out a loud, joyful trumpet sound that echoed across the plains. 'Hooray!' he cheered. But there was a tiny problem. The basket had a heavy lid on top of it, and Oliver’s trunk was just a little too short to lift it up properly while standing on the ground. Oliver scratched his head with his big gray ear. How was he going to get the lid off? Just then, his friend Sammy the squirrel scampered over. 'Need some help, big guy?' Sammy asked cheerfully. Oliver nodded happily. Sammy scurried up the side of the basket and pushed the wooden lid off with all his might. Clatter! The lid fell to the ground, revealing all the wonderful peanuts inside. Oliver reached in with his trunk and picked up three crunchy peanuts at once. He popped them into his mouth and chewed happily. They were the most delicious peanuts he had ever tasted in his entire life. Oliver shared half of the basket with Sammy as a thank-you gift, and the two friends munched away happily until Oliver’s tummy was completely full and happy.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, there lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved splashing in the mud with her big gray feet. But today was a very special day. The sun was shining, and the sky was as blue as a robin's egg. Ellie found a box under the big banana tree. She opened it up with her trunk, and inside were the most wonderful things in the whole wide world: a pair of shiny, bright red rain boots! Ellie gasped with joy. She picked up the first boot and giggled. 'Oh, how lovely!' she whispered to her friend, the little brown monkey. Ellie tried to put the boot on her front left foot. Squish, squash! It was a tight squeeze, but POP! It went right on. Then she put the second red boot on her front right foot. Thump, thump! She looked down at her feet and danced a happy little jungle jig. 'Look at me!' she trumpeted. 'Toot, toot!' Next, Ellie decided to show her mama. She walked through the tall green grass, making a funny squeaking sound. 'Squeak, squak, squeak,' went the boots. Mama Elephant turned around and smiled a big, warm elephant smile. 'My, oh my, Ellie! Those red boots look simply splendid on you!' Ellie felt so proud. She wanted to test them out in the biggest puddle she could find. She trotted over to the muddy path where the rain had left a giant, bubbly puddle. 'Ready, set, go!' cheered the monkey. Ellie ran as fast as her four legs could carry her and jumped right into the middle of the water. SPLASH! Mud flew up to the leaves. Water droplets sparkled in the air like diamonds. Ellie laughed and clapped her ears together. 'Splash, splash, splash!' she sang. Her new red boots kept her toes dry and happy. Even though her boots were now covered in messy brown mud, Ellie thought they looked even better than before. When it was time to go home for dinner, Ellie skipped all the way back, leaving little red bootprints behind her. She ate her crunchy leaves, drank cool water from the river, and curled up to sleep. As she closed her big brown eyes, she kept her shiny red boots right beside her pillow, dreaming of even bigger splashes for tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Balloon Adventure
stories.text: High up in the floating clouds, a gentle breeze swept across the treetops. Barnaby was a baby elephant with ears as big as cabbage leaves and a trunk that could wiggle like a lively little snake. Barnaby loved birthdays, even if it wasn't his birthday today. Why? Because birthdays meant balloons! Today, the friendly giraffe had given Barnaby a shiny, yellow balloon on a long white string. Barnaby held the string tightly in the very tip of his trunk. The balloon bobbed up and down in the air, going up, up, up, and then down, down, down. 'Hello, little balloon!' Barnaby said in his softest, sweetest voice. He decided to take his balloon for a walk around the watering hole. First, Barnaby walked past the sleepy hippopotamus. The hippo opened one big eye, yawned a giant yawn, and said, 'My, what a bright yellow sun you have on a string, Barnaby!' Barnaby giggled. 'It is not the sun, Mr. Hippo. It is my very own balloon!' The balloon danced in the breeze, pulling gently on Barnaby's trunk. It felt ticklish and fun. Next, Barnaby met three little pink flamingos standing on one leg. The flamingos fluttered their wings and chirped, 'Can we fly with your balloon, Barnaby?' Barnaby shook his head playfully. 'No, but you can hop along beside us!' So, the elephant and the flamingos went on a happy parade. They marched past the tall bamboo stalks and around the big mossy rock. Suddenly, a sudden gust of wind blew through the trees. WHOOSH! The wind pulled the string. 'Oh, no!' thought Barnaby. The balloon started to float higher into the sky, past the green leaves, toward the fluffy white clouds. Barnaby did not want his yellow friend to fly away forever. Quick as a wink, he stretched his long trunk as high as it could possibly go. He stood up on his tiptoes. He stretched and stretched. SNAP! His trunk wrapped gently around the soft rubber of the balloon. He pulled it safely back down to the ground. Barnaby let out a big sigh of relief. He hugged the balloon against his soft gray cheek. 'I have you now,' he whispered happily. He tied the string securely around his sturdy little wrist so it would never float away again. From that day on, Barnaby and his yellow balloon went everywhere together, sharing smiles and sunny adventures all across the wonderful jungle.

stories.title: Ollie's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking behind the purple mountains, painting the sky in soft shades of pink and orange. It was time for little animals to wind down, and Ollie the elephant was getting very sleepy. Ollie lived in a cozy nest of soft green ferns with his kind and gentle parents. Tonight, Ollie did not want to sleep. His eyes were wide open like big brown buttons, and his ears kept flapping back and forth. 'Time for bed, little peanut,' whispered Papa Elephant, gently stroking Ollie's back with his warm trunk. Ollie shook his big head. 'Not tired yet, Papa! I want to count the fireflies!' So, Papa Elephant smiled and said, 'Alright, let us count the fireflies together.' They sat quietly under the darkening sky. One tiny firefly blinked its yellow light near a fern leaf. 'One,' whispered Ollie softly. Another firefly fluttered past his trunk, glowing like a little star. 'Two,' Ollie murmured, his voice getting a tiny bit quieter. A third firefly danced in circles above his head. 'Three,' yawned Ollie, and this time, his eyelids felt as heavy as big gray stones. The jungle grew very quiet. The crickets began to sing a gentle bedtime song: 'Chirp, chirp, go to sleep.' A soft night breeze rustled the leaves, making a soothing sound like whispering water. Mama Elephant wrapped her warm trunk around Ollie's tummy in a comforting hug. 'You are safe, my little one,' she sang softly. Ollie let out a long, sleepy sigh. All the day's fun—running, splashing, and playing—was now resting in his happy memories. He curled his legs underneath his big round body and rested his heavy head on a pillow of soft moss. His trunk made a funny little snoring sound: 'Whuff, snort, whuff.' Papa and Mama Elephant watched over their little boy with so much love in their hearts. The stars came out one by one, shining brightly to watch over the sleeping jungle. Ollie dreamed of flying on a cloud of cotton candy, surrounded by glowing fireflies and gentle music, sleeping soundly until the bright morning sun would wake him up to play all over again.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved splashing in puddles with her big, happy feet. One sunny morning, Ellie found a surprise sitting right by her favorite muddy hole. It was a pair of shiny, bright red boots! They were big, bold, and very red. Ellie clapped her trunk with joy. She wanted to wear them right away. She carefully lifted her giant left foot and nudged it toward the first boot. Squish! Her toes went right inside. Then, she lifted her giant right foot and pushed it into the second boot. Stamp! Now Ellie had fabulous red boots on her feet. She took a big step forward. Thump, thump, went the boots. Ellie thought they sounded magnificent. She wiggled her toes inside the warm leather. It felt so cozy. She walked over to the mud puddle and looked down at her reflection in the water. She looked very dashing indeed! But wait. Ellie wanted to test her new boots out properly. She lifted her left foot high into the air and brought it crashing down right into the squishy, gooey mud. Splash! Mud flew everywhere, landing on the leaves, the grass, and even on her own trunk. Ellie giggled a deep, rumbling elephant giggle. But oh no! As she tried to lift her foot back up, it felt very heavy. The thick mud was holding onto her boots like a giant, sticky hug. Squish, squatch, squish went the boots as she tried to pull. Oh, dear! She was stuck. Just then, her good friend Mono the monkey swung down from a tall vine. 'Do you need help, Ellie?' asked Mono with a cheeky grin. Ellie nodded her trunk. Together, Mono pulled on her left ear, and Ellie gave a mighty tug with her strong legs. Pop! Out came her first foot, and then the second. Ellie wobbled and giggled, deciding that while red boots were fun, bare feet were much better for splashing in the mud. She picked up her boots, thanked her monkey friend, and continued her happy day in the jungle.

stories.title: Barnaby's Magic Peanut
stories.text: Deep in the whispering jungle lived a sweet baby elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby had soft gray skin, floppy ears that flapped in the breeze, and a wonderful long trunk that could do all sorts of clever things. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby was walking along the jungle path when he spotted something very unusual resting on a smooth green leaf. It was a golden peanut! It sparkled and shone in the warm sunlight like a tiny treasure. Barnaby blinked his big brown eyes in amazement. He walked slowly over to the leaf and gently touched the golden peanut with the very tip of his sensitive trunk. As soon as he touched it, the peanut let out a soft, magical giggle. 'Hello, Barnaby!' whispered the peanut. Barnaby was so surprised that he let out a little trumpet sound from his trunk. 'Pruuu-t!' he called out. He had never met a talking peanut before. The golden peanut rolled around in a circle and said, 'I am a magic wish peanut! If you give me a gentle tickle, I will grant you one fun adventure.' Barnaby loved adventures more than anything else in the whole wide world. He carefully scooped up the golden peanut with his trunk and gave it the softest, tickliest little nudge. Suddenly, *poof*! A cloud of sparkly blue and purple smoke swirled all around him. When the smoke cleared away, Barnaby was no longer in the jungle. He was standing on a giant fluffy white cloud high up in the sky! Below him, birds flew by and sang cheerful morning songs. Barnaby looked down at his feet and realized he could bounce on the cloud like a giant trampoline. Boing, boing, went Barnaby, jumping up and down with pure delight. He flapped his big ears and pretended he was flying alongside the fluffy white cumulus clouds. He played for what felt like hours, giggling and trumpeting happily into the open air. But soon, his tummy began to rumble. He missed his home in the green jungle and his favorite leafy snacks. Barnaby gently whispered to the golden peanut, 'I want to go home, please.' *Poof*! In another cloud of sparkly smoke, Barnaby was right back on the jungle path. The golden peanut turned back into a regular snack, which Barnaby happily munched. It was the best day ever.

stories.title: The Little Star That Got Lost
stories.text: Nighttime had finally arrived in the great savanna, painting the sky a deep, velvety indigo. All the animals were tucked into their cozy beds, fast asleep. Little Pip, a baby elephant with big, curious eyes, was wide awake. He loved looking up at the twinkling stars that dotted the night sky like glowing diamonds. Tonight, however, something strange was happening. One little star had wandered away from its friends and fallen all the way down. It landed with a soft *plop* right in the tall grass near Pip's sleeping spot. Pip blinked sleepily and tiptoed over on his soft, padded feet. There, glowing softly in the grass, was a tiny star. It looked very scared and was shivering in the cool night breeze. Its bright yellow light was flickering weakly, almost like a tiny candle about to go out. 'Hello little star,' whispered Pip in his softest, gentlest voice so as not to wake the other animals. The star blinked back at him sadly. 'I fell down,' whispered the star, its voice sounding like chiming glass bells. 'I cannot reach my home up in the sky anymore.' Pip's kind heart felt very sorry for the little star. He knew just what he had to do. He lowered his long, strong trunk all the way down to the ground. The little star rolled carefully onto the tip of Pip's trunk, feeling the warm, comforting touch of the baby elephant. 'Hold on tight!' Pip whispered with a reassuring smile. Pip bent his knees and crouched low to the ground. Then, with all his might, he sprang upward and launched himself gently into the air, lifting his trunk as high as he possibly could toward the heavens. He stretched and stretched until his trunk touched the lowest edge of the great night sky. With a happy little cheer, the star hopped off his trunk and zipped right back up to its cozy spot beside the moon. It sparkled brightly, shining down a warm thank-you beam directly onto Pip's forehead. Pip smiled warmly, walked back to his cozy patch of grass, and drifted off to sleep under a sky full of twinkling friends.

stories.title: Ella's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, there lived a little baby elephant named Ella. Ella had big, floppy ears that went flap, flap, flap, and a long, wonderful trunk that went wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. Today was a very hot day. The sun was shining bright, and all the animals were looking for a way to stay cool. The monkeys were resting in the shady trees, and the zebras were swishing their tails. Ella felt so warm. She decided it was time to find the watering hole for a big, fun splash! Ella walked down the muddy path. Slurp, slurp went her little feet in the wet mud. She swung her trunk from side to side, singing a happy elephant song. When she arrived at the sparkling blue river, she saw her friends already playing in the water. Hippo was blowing bubbles, and duck was paddling in circles. Ella was so excited! She ran right up to the water's edge. But wait, how do elephants drink and splash? With their trunks, of course! Ella dipped the very tip of her long trunk into the cool, clear water. She sucked in a big breath. Gulp, gulp, gulp went the water up her trunk. Her trunk grew big and round, just like a water balloon. Then, Ella pointed her trunk right up into the bright blue sky. Whoosh! She blew out the water with a joyful trumpet sound. Splash went the water all around, like a cool summer rain. Hippo cheered, and duck quacked with delight. Ella giggled and did it again. She filled her trunk and gave herself a tickly shower right on her back. It felt so wonderful and refreshing. Then, she rolled around in the soft mud at the edge of the river, making funny squishy noises. Mud is the best sunscreen for a happy little elephant. As the afternoon breeze began to blow, Ella felt clean, cool, and very sleepy. She snuggled up next to her mama in the tall, green grass, ready for a sweet nap after such a fun day of splashing.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the sunny savanna, a gentle little elephant named Barnaby received a very special surprise. It was a bright red balloon, round and shiny, tied to a long string. Barnaby loved his new balloon more than anything in the whole wide world. He held the string tightly in the very tip of his trunk and marched proudly through the tall grass. Thump, thump, thump went his big round feet. Barnaby wanted to show his balloon to all his animal friends. First, he trotted over to giraffe, who was munching on green leaves high up in a tree. 'Hello, giraffe!' trumpeted Barnaby softly. Giraffe smiled down and blinked her long eyelashes at the shiny red balloon. Next, Barnaby waddled over to zebra, who was resting near a big rock. Zebra neighed a happy hello and gently booped the balloon with his black and white nose. Barnaby felt so proud and happy. But oh no! A sudden gust of wind came swooping across the savanna. Wooosh went the wind, blowing past Barnaby's big ears. The wind tugged at the string, and before Barnaby could say a single word, slip went the string right out of his trunk. Up, up, up went the bright red balloon into the sky. It floated past the fluffy white clouds, getting smaller and smaller every second. Barnaby gasped and blinked his big brown eyes. He felt a little sad and let out a tiny, quiet squeak. He watched his balloon drift higher and higher until it looked like a tiny dot in the blue sky. Just then, a friendly little yellow bird landed softly on Barnaby's shoulder. The bird chirped a sweet, comforting melody, as if to say, 'Do not worry, little friend.' Barnaby smiled and realized he didn't need a balloon to have a wonderful day. He still had his strong legs to stomp with, his wonderful trunk to wiggle, and his lovely friends all around him. Barnaby wrapped his trunk around bird in a gentle hug and happily trumpeted a cheerful tune as he walked back home for dinner.

stories.title: The Great Peanut Hunt
stories.text: Good morning, little readers! Today, we are going on a grand adventure with Oliver the elephant. Oliver had the softest gray skin, the biggest twinkling eyes, and a tummy that was rumbling loudly. Rumbly, tumbly went Oliver's tummy. It was time for breakfast! But Oliver could not find his favorite morning treat anywhere. Where were the yummy, crunchy peanuts? Oliver decided to search the whole jungle to find them. He started by looking behind a big, leafy bush. He pushed the green leaves aside with his strong trunk, but there were no peanuts there—only a sleepy little green frog who said, 'Ribbit, ribbit, go away!' Oliver waved politely and kept on walking. Thump, thump, thump went his happy feet. Next, Oliver checked inside a hollow log. He peeked his trunk inside, but he only found a family of fuzzy caterpillars tickling each other and giggling. Oliver giggled too, because tickles are the best. Then, Oliver stopped and closed his eyes. Sniff, sniff, sniff went his sensitive trunk. What did he smell? He smelled something earthy, nutty, and oh-so-delicious! Oliver followed the wonderful smell down a winding path of wildflowers. Yellow flowers, purple flowers, and pink flowers danced in the gentle morning breeze. Right at the end of the path sat a large, woven basket left behind by friendly jungle travelers. Oliver peeked inside the basket with his trunk. Surprise! It was filled to the very top with crunchy, tasty peanuts. Oliver let out a loud, joyful trumpet blast that echoed through the trees. Toot-toot! He carefully picked up a peanut with the tip of his trunk, popped it into his mouth, and crunched down happily. Crunch, crunch, crunch. It was the most delicious breakfast in the whole wide world. Oliver shared his treats with his frog and caterpillar friends, and they all had a wonderful morning together in the sunny jungle.

stories.title: Ella's Big Bubble Bath
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the big sunny jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ella. Ella had big floppy ears, four chubby little feet, and a long, wiggly trunk. Today was a very hot day, and Ella felt sticky from head to toe. 'Mummy,' trumpeted Ella, 'I am too hot!' Mummy elephant smiled her big, warm smile and said, 'Let us go down to the sparkly blue river for a big, splashing bubble bath, my sweet little one.' Ella did a happy little dance, shaking her tiny tail from side to side. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went her heavy feet as she trotted down the grassy path, swish-swishing her trunk all the way to the water's edge. When they reached the river, Ella could not wait another single second. She waded right into the cool, refreshing water up to her tummy. Bubbles floated everywhere, pink and green and shiny gold, catching the bright afternoon sunlight. Ella dipped her long trunk all the way down into the water, sucked up a big, cool gulp, and sprayed it right up into the air. Whoosh! Water went high, high, high into the blue sky, sparkling like millions of tiny diamonds before tumbling back down in a wonderful shower. 'Whee!' giggled Ella, clapping her big ears together with a loud slap. Next came the best part of all. Mummy scooped up a thick, fluffy pile of bubbly river foam and gently placed it right on top of Ella's head like a fancy crown. Ella looked at her reflection in the shiny water and laughed out loud. 'Look, Mummy, I am a bubble king!' Mummy chuckled softly and rubbed Ella’s back with a soft sponge. They splashed and giggled together for a long, wonderful time, washing away all the dust and heat of the day. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds with lovely shades of pink and orange, Ella felt nice and clean, and oh-so-sleepy. She stepped out of the river and shook herself dry with a big, floppy wobble. Cuddling close to her warm mummy, Ella yawned a giant elephant yawn. 'Goodnight, river bubbles,' whispered Ella softly, closing her heavy eyes as Mummy sang a gentle lullaby, rocking her softly under the twinkling stars until sweet dreams came to find her.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the green, whispering woods lived a cheerful little elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby loved bright colors more than anything else in the whole wide world. Today was a very special day because it was his third birthday party, and his best friend, a cheeky little monkey named Milo, had given him the most wonderful present ever: a big, shiny, bright red balloon. The balloon bobbed up and down in the gentle breeze, dancing happily against the blue sky as Barnaby held tightly to the white string with the very tip of his trunk. 'Thank you, Milo!' trumpeted Barnaby, feeling as proud as could be. He marched through the tall grass, holding his balloon high so all the forest animals could see his marvelous treasure. A little yellow butterfly fluttered by, landing softly on Barnaby’s knee. Barnaby giggled and stopped to look. But oh dear! In all the excitement, Barnaby loosened his grip just a tiny, tiny bit. Zoom! The bright red balloon gave a little wiggle and slipped right out of his trunk. 'Wait! Come back!' cried Barnaby, watching the shiny balloon float up, up, up into the air toward the leafy branches of a big oak tree. Barnaby’s lower lip quivered, and a big tear welled up in his kind, dark eye. He was just about to cry when his wise old friend, Sammy the Squirrel, scampered down the trunk. 'Do not worry, Barnaby,' chattered Sammy cheerfully. 'We can help you get it back!' Sammy climbed swiftly up the tree, leaping from branch to branch like a furry little acrobat. The forest animals gathered around to help. Timmy the turtle pushed a wooden box under the tree, and Ellie the bird fluttered her wings to make a gentle breeze blow the balloon back down. With one final stretch, Sammy gently nudged the string with his paw, and flutter-flutter-flutter, the red balloon drifted slowly down right into Barnaby’s waiting trunk. Barnaby’s face lit up with a huge, beaming smile. He wrapped his trunk safely around the string, giving it a gentle squeeze. 'Yay!' cheered all the animals together. Barnaby shared some yummy birthday banana cake with every single one of his wonderful friends, holding his precious red balloon tighter than ever all afternoon long.

stories.title: Oliver's Big Footsteps
stories.text: In a cozy corner of the great grassy savanna lived a little baby elephant named Oliver. Oliver had enormous feet, much too big for his little body, and they always made a funny sound wherever he went. Stomp, stomp, stomp went his left foot. Thud, thud, thud went his right foot. Oliver loved to follow his papa around all day long, learning how to be a big, strong elephant. 'Papa,' Oliver asked one sunny morning, looking down at his giant toes, 'why are my feet so terribly big and clumsy?' Papa stopped walking, turned around, and smiled down at his little boy. 'Come with me, Oliver,' Papa rumbled in a deep, gentle voice, 'and I will show you why.' Papa led the way across the dusty path, stepping over rocks and through patches of sticky mud. Oliver followed closely behind, stomping his big feet with all his might. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Suddenly, they reached a wide, muddy puddle that stretched all the way across the trail. It looked deep, dark, and terribly gooey. 'Oh no,' squeaked Oliver, stopping right in his tracks. 'How will we ever get across this sticky mess without sinking all the way to our bellies?' Papa smiled knowingly and stepped right into the middle of the thick mud. Squish, squelch, squash! Papa’s massive feet pressed deep into the earth, creating a wide, flat, sturdy stepping stone right in the middle of the gooey mess. 'Your turn, little one,' encouraged Papa. Oliver took a deep breath, lifted his heavy leg, and placed his giant foot right inside the imprint Papa had made. His big foot fit perfectly, keeping him high and dry above the sticky mud. Squelch went the mud around his toes, but Oliver did not sink at all. 'I did it!' cheered Oliver, clapping his floppy ears together with delight. He took another big step, and another, stomping happily across the puddle using Papa's big footprints as a safe little road. When they finally reached the dry grass on the other side, Oliver looked back at the muddy puddle and then down at his enormous feet with a brand-new feeling of pride. They were not clumsy at all; they were wonderful! 'Thank you, Papa,' whispered Oliver, giving his father a warm, dusty hug with his trunk. From that day on, Oliver walked a little taller, proudly making his happy, heavy footsteps all across the savanna.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Splash
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears that went flap, flap, flap, and a long, curly trunk that went swoosh, swoosh, swoosh. It was a very hot and sunny day. The sun was shining bright yellow in the sky. Whew, it was hot! Ellie walked with her mommy to the big mud puddle. 'Splash, splash, go!' said Mommy Elephant. Ellie looked at the cool, brown mud and giggled. She dipped her little toes right into the mud. Squish, squach, squish went the mud between her toes. That tickled so much! Ellie laughed out loud. Then, Ellie decided to use her trunk like a magical hose. She dipped her long trunk down into the water and sucked up a big, big gulp. Slurp, slurp, slurp! Her trunk got round and chubby. Now it was time for the best part. Ellie pointed her trunk high up into the air and blew. Whoosh! A giant spray of water shot out like a sparkly fountain. The cool water showered down on her back. Splash, splash, splish! Ellie spun around in circles, flapping her big ears with joy. 'I am a happy elephant!' she trumpeted. More animals came over to join the fun. Little monkey swung down from a branch and splashed his feet. A fluffy white duck quacked loudly and paddled in the puddle. Ellie shared her water spray with everyone. The sun felt warm, but the water felt cool and refreshing. They played and splashed until the afternoon sky turned a pretty shade of pink and orange. Ellie was all clean, and she was very, very tired. Mommy Elephant gave her a warm, cozy hug with her trunk. 'Time for bed, my little Ellie,' Mommy whispered softly. Ellie closed her big brown eyes and yawned a big elephant yawn. She snuggled down into the soft green grass, dreaming of more splashy adventures. Goodnight, Ellie. Sleep tight and sweet dreams in the jungle.

stories.title: Ellie's Lost Balloon
stories.text: One sunny morning, Ellie the elephant went for a nice walk in the park. She held a string tied to a big, beautiful red balloon. The balloon bobbed up and down in the air. Pop, bob, bob went the red balloon! Ellie loved her balloon very much. She walked past the tall green trees and waved hello to the chirpy little birds. Suddenly, a big puff of wind came blowing through the park. Whoosh! The wind was very strong. It blew Ellie's hand right open. Oh no! The red balloon slipped out of her trunk. Up, up, up into the sky flew the red balloon. It went higher and higher, past the green leaves, and up toward the fluffy white clouds. Ellie looked up with wide eyes. A little tear popped into her eye. 'My balloon,' she whispered sadly. She wanted her balloon back. Just then, her clever friend Monkey swung down from a branch. 'Do not worry, Ellie! I can help you!' said Monkey cheerfully. Monkey was fast and knew how to climb. He scrambled up the tallest tree in the park. He reached out his long arms, but the balloon was still too high. Then, friendly Bird flew up into the sky. Flutter, flutter went Bird's wings. Bird gently tapped the balloon with her beak. Pop? No, she did not pop it! She just nudged it sideways. The gentle breeze blew the balloon right back down toward the ground. Ellie reached out her long, curly trunk. She stretched as high as she possibly could. Reach, reach, reach! Wrap went her trunk around the floating string. She caught it just in time! Ellie pulled the string down and hugged her red balloon tight against her chest. She jumped up and down with happiness. 'Thank you, my good friends!' Ellie trumpeted with a big smile. Monkey and Bird cheered for joy. Ellie held the string extra tight for the rest of her wonderful walk in the sunny park.

stories.title: Ellie's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was sinking low behind the tall green hills, painting the sky with purple and gold. It was almost bedtime in the cozy jungle. Ellie the baby elephant was getting very sleepy. Her big ears felt heavy, and her little eyelids felt droopy. Blink, blink, blink went her eyes. Mommy Elephant knew just what to do to help her baby fall fast asleep. Mommy gathered all the forest animals to sing a quiet bedtime lullaby. First came the little brown squirrel. He brought a soft bed of green moss and laid it gently on the ground. Next came the fluffy white rabbit. He brought a blanket made of dandelion fluff that was as soft as a cloud. Ellie walked slowly over to her comfy bed. She curled her big body into a nice, snug ball. Mommy Elephant stood right beside her, keeping watch like a gentle giant. Then, the sleepy forest animals began to hum a sweet, quiet song. Hm-m-m, hm-m-m went the little birds softly in the branches. The crickets started to chirp a tiny nighttime tune. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets in the grass. Ellie closed her eyes tightly and listened to the peaceful sounds all around her. Mommy Elephant wrapped her long, warm trunk gently around Ellie's tummy, giving her the biggest and coziest hug in the whole wide world. Ellie felt so safe and so very loved. Her breathing slowed down nice and steady. In and out, in and out. The stars began to twinkle high up in the dark blue night sky like tiny diamonds. One by one, the jungle animals whispered their quiet goodnights. 'Goodnight, little squirrel. Goodnight, little rabbit. Goodnight, Mommy,' Ellie thought in her sleepy head. A tiny smile crept onto her face. Ellie drifted off into a deep, wonderful sleep, dreaming of sunny days and splashing puddles. Sleep well, sweet little elephant.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie had two big floppy ears, a long gray trunk, and four very happy feet. Today was a very special day because it was raining! Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the rain drops on the broad banana leaves. Ellie loved the rain more than anything in the whole wide world. She loved the cool drops on her back and the wonderful squishy mud under her toes. But today, Ellie had something new. Her mommy gave her a pair of bright red rain boots! They were shiny, red, and smelled like strawberries. Ellie was so excited that she did a little happy dance, swinging her trunk from side to side. 'Time to go outside, Ellie!' called her mommy with a big smile. Ellie stepped into her first boot. Left foot, squeeze, pop! Then her second boot. Right foot, squeeze, pop! They fit her chunky feet just right. Ellie waddled outside, making a funny wobbly walk because her feet felt so heavy and big. Squish, squash, squish, squash went the mud. Ellie stomped right into a big, round puddle. Splash! Water flew up into the air like sparkling diamonds. She giggled a silly elephant giggle. 'Brrrr-ump!' went her trunk, spraying a little fountain of water into the sky. Ellie walked all around the jungle looking for her animal friends to show off her fantastic red boots. First, she saw Sammy the monkey hanging upside down from a grapevine. 'Look at my boots, Sammy!' cheered Ellie. Sammy clapped his hands and chattered, 'Ooh-ooh-aah-aah! So shiny and red!' Next, she waddled past Tessie the tiger, who was resting under a shady bush. Tessie blinked her golden eyes and purred, 'What wonderful boots for a rainy day, Ellie!' Ellie felt so proud and happy. She stomped through three more puddles, making the biggest splashes she could possibly make. Splash, splash, splish! By the time the golden sun started to peek out from behind the gray clouds, Ellie was wonderfully muddy from her trunk down to her bright red boots. Her mommy brought out a big fluffy green towel and gave her a warm, cozy rub-down. Ellie kicked off her boots, ready for a nice long nap, dreaming of all the fun puddles she would jump in tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the sunny savannah, where the tall golden grass whispers in the warm breeze, lived a gentle baby elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby had the softest gray skin, the cutest tiny tail, and a trunk that could pick up the tiniest little flowers. Today was Barnaby's third birthday, and his best friend, Pip the yellow bird, had given him a magnificent surprise. It was a big, shiny, bright blue balloon! The balloon was so round and happy, bobbing up and down in the air like a floating blueberry. Barnaby loved his blue balloon instantly. He wrapped the little string gently around his trunk so it wouldn't float away, and he went for a lovely stroll across the grassy plain. 'Look at my balloon!' Barnaby trumpeted softly to a passing giraffe. 'Toot-toot!' The giraffe smiled down from way up high and nodded. Barnaby walked past the sparkling watering hole where the baby hippos were playing. He felt so light and happy, he wanted to skip. But oh no! A sudden gust of wind came swooping through the acacia trees. Whoosh! The wind tickled Barnaby's ears and tugged playfully at the string. Before Barnaby could say boo, the string slipped right out from under his trunk. 'Oh, no!' cried Barnaby, blinking his big brown eyes as the blue balloon zipped up into the sky. Up, up, up it went, past the tall trees, floating higher and higher toward fluffy white clouds. Barnaby felt a little tear roll down his cheek. He really loved that balloon. Just then, Pip the bird fluttered down right onto Barnaby's head. 'Don't worry, Barnaby! I can fly high and help you find it!' chirped Pip bravely. Pip flapped his wings as fast as he could, zooming up into the blue sky. Barnaby watched anxiously, crossing his toes and holding his trunk still. After a few moments, Pip came flying back down, tweeting a happy song. 'Your balloon is stuck in the branches of the big baobab tree!' announced Pip. Barnaby hurried over to the giant tree as fast as his little legs could carry him. The balloon was just out of reach, bobbing gently in the leaves. Barnaby knew just what to do. He stretched his long, flexible trunk all the way up, up, up. He reached past the rough bark and the green leaves. Gently, oh so gently, his trunk tickled the string. Got it! Barnaby pulled the string back down and hugged his balloon tight. He was the happiest elephant in the whole world again.

stories.title: Ollie's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking below the horizon, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink, purple, and sleepy orange. High up in the branches of the sleeping trees, little birds tucked their heads under their wings. It was time for bed in the jungle. In a cozy patch of tall ferns, a little baby elephant named Ollie was wide awake. Ollie had a round tummy, floppy ears that felt like velvet, and big sleepy eyes. But Ollie's eyes were too busy looking at the fireflies dancing in the twilight. 'Time for sleep, little Ollie,' whispered his mama, gently stroking his back with her warm trunk. Ollie yawned a huge, jaw-stretching yawn. 'Yaaaawn! But Mama, I am not sleepy yet,' mumbled Ollie, blinking slowly. Mama elephant smiled a tender, loving smile. She knew just how to help her little boy fall asleep. 'Let's take a slow walk to the sleepy river and listen to the night song,' she suggested softly. Ollie nodded and leaned close to his mama's big, comforting side. They walked slowly through the cool grass, pat-pat, pat-pat, making hardly a sound. The jungle was quiet and peaceful now. The crickets were starting their evening music. Chirp-chirp, chirp-chirp went the crickets in the bushes. A little frog by the water went croak, croak, in a low, gentle voice. Ollie and his mama reached the edge of the glassy river. The water reflected the first bright evening star twinkling like a diamond in the velvet sky. Mama elephant wrapped her strong, gentle trunk around Ollie in a warm, loving hug. She began to hum a deep, rumbling lullaby. It was a special mama elephant song, full of love and safety. Ollie felt the rumble deep inside his own tummy. It felt like a warm, cozy blanket wrapping all around him. The stars blinked down kindly. The river sang its soft, bubbling song. Ollie's heavy eyelids started to flutter. First down, then up, then down again. He leaned his heavy head against a soft mossy rock and let out a long, peaceful sigh. 'Goodnight, fireflies,' whispered Ollie in a tiny sleepy voice. Within moments, the little elephant was fast asleep, dreaming sweet dreams of flying among the sparkling stars, safe and warm in the heart of the jungle.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears, a long grey trunk, and four very big feet. One sunny morning, Ellie woke up and found a big box outside her tent. She walked over with a heavy thump, thump, thump. She opened the box with her long trunk. Inside were four shiny, bright red rain boots! Ellie was so excited. She stomped her left foot. Squeak! She stomped her right foot. Squeak! They fit just right.
