Ellie wanted to show all her friends her new boots. She started to walk down the muddy jungle path. Splish, splash, splish, splash went her red boots in the puddles. A little monkey swinging from a tree vine called out, 'Hello, Ellie! I love your shiny red boots!' Ellie flapped her big ears and smiled a big elephant smile. Next, she saw her friend Tessa the tiger. Tessa was resting near a bush. Tessa blinked her yellow eyes and purred, 'My oh my, Ellie! Those red boots look wonderful on you!' Ellie felt so proud and happy. She kept walking, making happy little trumpeting sounds. 'Pa-roooo!' Soon, she reached the big muddy river where all the jungle animals liked to play. The hippos were floating, and the ducks were swimming. Ellie waded right into the mud. Her red boots stayed bright and clean because they were magic boots. She danced a little silly elephant dance. Left foot, right foot, spin around! All the animals clapped their hands and paws. Ellie realized that sharing a happy moment with friends was the best part of wearing special boots. When the sun began to go down, painting the sky pink and orange, Ellie knew it was time to go home. She walked back along the trail, giving a friendly wave to every bird and bug. When she reached her tent, she carefully took off her boots and put them neatly by the door. She curled up on her soft leaf bed, thinking about her wonderful adventures. Ellie closed her big brown eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of more red boot fun tomorrow. Good night, Ellie.

stories.title: Barnaby's Balloons
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods lived a cheerful baby elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby loved colors more than anything in the world. Today was Barnaby's special birthday, and his mommy had a wonderful surprise waiting for him. She led him to the edge of the meadow, and there, tied to a sturdy tree branch, was a bunch of bright, beautiful balloons. There was a red balloon, a blue balloon, a yellow balloon, a green balloon, and a shiny purple balloon. Barnaby let out a joyful trumpet sound, 'Toot-toot!' He reached out his long, gentle trunk and gently touched the green balloon. It bounced away with a soft boing. Barnaby giggled. He loved how they danced in the gentle breeze. All his animal friends gathered around to sing a happy birthday song. Sammy the squirrel chattered happily, and Fiona the fox wagged her bushy tail. Barnaby wanted to share the fun with everyone. He carefully untied the red balloon and handed it to Sammy. Sammy held the string tightly and did a happy little hop. Then Barnaby untied the blue balloon and gave it to Fiona. Fiona grinned from ear to ear. Next, Barnaby kept the yellow, green, and purple balloons for himself. They walked together through the sunny meadow, watching the balloons float high up in the blue sky. A little puff of wind came along, and Barnaby's balloons bobbed up and down like happy little birds. Barnaby felt so lucky to have such kind friends and such wonderful colorful balloons. They played games of tag and hide-and-seek all afternoon until the sun started to sink low behind the green hills. The balloons bobbed gently in the evening air, glowing in the golden light. Barnaby gave his friends big hugs with his trunk. It was the best birthday a little elephant could ever wish for. As the stars began to twinkle like tiny diamonds in the night sky, Barnaby held his last balloon close, smiled a sleepy smile, and walked slowly home to bed, dreaming of floating high up in the clouds.

stories.title: Oliver's Big Bubble
stories.text: Oliver was a very curious little elephant who lived near a sparkling blue lake. Oliver loved water. He loved splashing, he loved swimming, and most of all, he loved blowing bubbles. One afternoon, Oliver found a special bottle of bubble soap sitting on a flat rock by the water. The label had a picture of a giant rainbow bubble on it. Oliver picked up the bubble wand with his long grey trunk. He dipped the wand deep into the soapy water, pulled it out carefully, and took a very deep breath. Then, he blew through the wand with all his might. Whoosh! A tiny bubble came out, then a medium bubble, and then, right before his eyes, a giant, shimmering bubble started to grow. It was bigger than a watermelon! It was bigger than a pumpkin! The giant bubble floated right up into the air, shining with all the colors of the rainbow. Reds, blues, yellows, and greens danced on the shiny surface. Oliver clapped his big ears in pure delight. 'Look at that!' he whispered to a little frog sitting on a lily pad. The frog croaked in amazement. The giant bubble drifted slowly over the lake, bobbing up and down in the soft breeze. Oliver followed it step by step, making sure it didn't pop on a sharp tree branch. A butterfly landed softly on top of the bubble for just a second, making the colors swirl even brighter. Oliver laughed a deep, rumbly elephant laugh. Suddenly, the breeze picked up, and the bubble floated higher and higher, all the way up to the fluffy white clouds. Pop! It turned into a million tiny soapy droplets that sparkled like little diamonds in the sun. Oliver smiled from ear to ear. That was the most magnificent bubble he had ever seen in his whole life. He picked up his bottle, walked back to his favorite muddy spot, and decided it was time to take a nice, relaxing mud bath to finish his wonderful day.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Mud Bath
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big, floppy ears that went flap, flap, flap, and a long, squiggly trunk that went toot, toot, toot! It was a very, very hot day in the jungle. The sun was shining high in the blue sky. Whew, it was warm! Ellie wanted to play, but she felt too hot. Her mama said, 'Let us go find a cool treat, little one!' Ellie flapped her big ears and trotted along with a thump, thump, thump. They walked past the tall green trees and the colorful flowers until they reached the edge of the sparkling river. Near the river was a big, wonderful patch of squishy, squelchy, brown mud! Ellie squealed with joy. 'Mmm-mmm, mud!' she trumpeted. She trotted right up to the mud puddle and dipped her long trunk inside. She sucked up the cool water and mud, and then—SPLOOSH! She sprayed it all over her back! It felt so cool and tickly. Ellie giggled and rolled around in the mud. Squish, squash, squish, went the mud between her toes. She covered her tummy, her legs, and even the tip of her little tail in the dark, cool mud. A cheeky little monkey up in the tree giggled and threw a mango skin down. Ellie caught it with her trunk and tossed it back with a happy toot! Being covered in mud made Ellie feel so refreshed and cool. Soon, all her elephant friends came running over to join the fun. They splashed and stomped and played together in the big, beautiful mud bath. When the sun began to go down, it was time to get clean. They jumped into the river and washed it all away with a big splash. Ellie dried off in the warm breeze and curled up next to her mama for a cozy nap. She dreamed sweet dreams of squishy, squelchy mud and warm jungle breezes. Goodnight, Ellie.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Barnaby was a sweet little elephant with a big heart and an even bigger blue balloon. Oh, how Barnaby loved his shiny blue balloon! It was round, it was bright, and it bobbed up and down in the air like a happy little bird. Barnaby held the string tightly in his trunk as he walked through the tall grass. He wanted to show his balloon to all his animal friends in the forest. First, he showed it to Sammy the Squirrel. Sammy chattered and clapped his paws. Then, he showed it to Bella the Bunny, who wiggle-waggled her pink nose in delight. Barnaby felt so proud of his lovely blue balloon. But oh dear, oh no! A sudden gust of wind came WHOOSH through the trees. It blew so hard that it tickled Barnaby's trunk. Barnaby let out a little sneeze—'Achoo!'—and before he knew it, the string slipped right out of his trunk! Up, up, up went the blue balloon, floating higher and higher into the sky. 'Oh, no! Come back, balloon!' cried Barnaby. He stretched his trunk up as high as it could go, but the balloon was already too high. Barnaby started to pout. A big, salty tear rolled down his cheek. He felt very sad. Just then, his wise old friend Oliver the Owl swooped down from a branch. 'Do not worry, little Barnaby,' hooted Oliver kindly. 'Look up! Your balloon is stuck on that friendly apple tree!' Barnaby wiped his eyes and looked up. Sure enough, the blue balloon was gently resting against a big green leaf. But how would he reach it? Barnaby had an idea! He took a deep breath, puffed out his chest, and stretched his long, flexible trunk all the way up, up, up. He stretched it past the leaves, past the little bird's nest, and gently wrapped the tip of his trunk right around the balloon string! 'Horray!' cheered Barnaby, pulling the balloon safely down. He hugged the round, shiny toy against his chest and smiled the biggest smile ever. He held the string extra tight this time and skipped all the way home.

stories.title: The Great Jungle Parade
stories.text: The jungle was buzzing with excitement today because it was time for the Annual Jungle Music Parade! All the animals were getting ready to march, and leading the parade was none other than Benji the energetic baby elephant. Benji loved music more than anything else in the whole wide world. Whenever he heard a beat, his big feet just had to stomp, and his trunk just had to sway. 'It is time to start the band!' shouted Benji happily. He picked up his favorite instrument, a shiny silver trumpet, and blew a loud, brassy note—TOOT, TOOT, TOOT! That was the signal for everyone to fall in line. Soon, Timmy the Tiger joined in, shaking a pair of yellow maracas that went chack-chack-chack. Then came Penny the Parrot, strumming a tiny guitar that went strum-strum-strum. And last but not least, Sammy the Sloth crawled along slowly, beating a little red drum that went boom, boom, boom! Benji puffed out his chest and started to march down the winding dirt path. Left, right, left, right went his big grey feet. Thump, thump, thump went the ground beneath them. All the jungle animals came out of their houses to watch the wonderful parade. The little monkeys clapped their hands, and the colorful birds sang along in sweet harmony. Benji marched past the tall bamboo stalks and under the giant fern leaves, waving his trunk cheerfully at every single spectator. When they reached the clearing by the sparkling waterfall, it was time for the grand finale! Benji raised his long trunk high into the air and blew the longest, happiest note of all. The maracas shook, the guitar strummed, and the drum boomed a mighty beat. Everyone cheered and danced in a big circle until the sun went down. Benji beamed with joy. Leading the parade was the best job in the whole world, and he could not wait until the next time the music would play in his beloved jungle home.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the great big jungle, there lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears, a long grey trunk, and four very big feet. One sunny morning, Ellie found a surprise package sitting right under her favorite banana tree. She walked over with a heavy thump-thump-thump. Inside the shiny box was a pair of bright red boots! They were huge and shiny and smelled like strawberries. Ellie was so excited. She wanted to wear them right away. She sat down in the soft grass and tried to put a boot on her front left foot. Push, wiggle, squish! It fit like a glove. Then she put a boot on her front right foot. Stomp, stretch, squeeze! Now she had two red boots. But wait, Ellie had four feet! She still needed boots for her back feet. Oh no, there were only two boots in the box. Ellie let out a little sad trumpet sound. "Pa-woooo." Just then, her clever monkey friend, Coco, swung down from the branches above. Coco giggled and clapped his hands. "Don't worry, Ellie! Two boots are plenty for a goofy dance!" Coco shouted. Ellie thought about this and smiled a big elephant smile. Who needed four boots when you could hop on two? Ellie stood up and lifted her front left foot. Tap! Then she lifted her front right foot. Tap! She stomped through the muddy puddles, making squishy sounds that made both of them laugh out loud. Splash, splash, went the red boots! The water flew up in sparkly drops, catching the warm sunshine. Other jungle animals came out to watch the fun. Zebra trotted over and clapped his hooves. Parrot flew in circles, chirping a happy tune. Ellie felt like the luckiest elephant in the whole wide world. Wearing her two bright red boots, she danced in the mud all morning long. When the sun began to go down, her tummy started to rumble for dinner. Ellie hugged her friend Coco and waved goodbye to the crowd. She stomped back home to her cozy sleeping spot, leaving little red boot prints all along the path. It had been the most wonderful day ever.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the green, leafy jungle, a little baby elephant named Barnaby was having a magnificent day. Today was his third birthday, and his mommy had given him the best present in the whole wide world. It was a big, round, shiny balloon that was as yellow as a fresh lemon. Barnaby loved his balloon so much that he tied the string tightly around his little trunk. Whenever he walked, the balloon bobbed up and down in the air, following him wherever he went. Bounce, bounce, went the yellow balloon against the blue sky. Barnaby marched through the tall grass, feeling very proud and happy. But suddenly, a cheeky little breeze came swooshing through the trees. Whoosh! The wind blew softly, tickling Barnaby's trunk. Barnaby gave a little sneeze. "Achoo!" When he sneezed, his trunk popped wide open, and the string slipped right out of his grip. Oh no! The yellow balloon zipped up into the sky. Zoom! It went higher than the bushes. It went higher than the tall palm trees. Barnaby gasped and reached up with his trunk, but the balloon was much too far away now. Tears filled Barnaby's big brown eyes. He let out a tiny, sad trumpet noise. "Pa-eep." He thought his balloon was gone forever. Just then, a friendly giraffe named Gina peered down from the clouds. Gina had a very long neck. She stretched her neck up, up, up, way past the green leaves. With her gentle nose, Gina caught the runaway balloon just in time. She carefully brought it back down to the ground and handed the string back to Barnaby. Barnaby gasped with joy. He wrapped his trunk around the string again, holding it extra, extra tight this time. He gave Gina a big, wet elephant kiss on her knee to say thank you. Gina smiled and nudged him gently with her nose. Barnaby hugged his yellow balloon and skipped all the way home to his birthday party. He had learned a very important lesson today about holding on tight to the things you love.

stories.title: Pip's Tiny Splash
stories.text: Pip was a very small elephant with very big dreams. While all the grown-up elephants in his family had enormous ears and long, powerful trunks, Pip was just knee-high to a blade of grass. Sometimes, Pip felt a little bit left out when the big elephants played in the deep watering hole. They could splash water all the way up to the treetops, making gigantic waterfalls that cooled the whole jungle. Pip could only squirt a tiny dribble of water, barely enough to wash his own toes. One hot afternoon, the sun was shining down with all its might. The mud was baking dry, and everyone was looking for a way to stay cool. The big elephants lined up at the edge of the big pond, ready for a grand swimming session. Pip wanted to join the fun, so he trotted along behind them, stepping in their giant footprints. When they reached the water, the big elephants jumped in with a massive cannonball splash! Splash-boom! Waves crashed against the muddy banks, sending frogs leaping into the air. Pip stood at the edge, looking down at the deep water. He felt a little bit nervous. The water looked awfully big, and he was awfully small. But Pip took a deep breath. He marched right up to the water's edge, filled his little trunk with as much water as it could hold, and blew with all his might. Poot! A tiny, perfect little fountain of water shot out of his trunk. It sparkled like tiny diamonds in the sunshine and landed right on his own head. Pip giggled and shook his floppy ears. The big elephants stopped splashing and looked over at little Pip. They smiled warmly and cheered for him. Then, his mommy gently scooped him up with her trunk and lifted him onto her wide, safe back. Together, they splashed around in the shallow water, making the happiest sounds in the jungle. Pip realized that being small wasn't so bad after all, especially when you have a big family to share the fun with.

stories.title: Ella's Big Mud Bath
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ella. Ella had big floppy ears, four chubby legs, and a very long, wiggly trunk. Most of all, Ella loved the warm, sunny mornings in the jungle. One bright morning, the sun felt extra hot. 'Oof,' said Ella, flapping her big ears. 'It is too hot today!' Her mommy smiled and said, 'Let us go find a nice, cool mud puddle, little one!' Ella did a happy little dance. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went her big feet as she skipped along the jungle path. Soon, they found the biggest, squishiest, muddiest puddle in the whole wide world. It was bubbling with fun! Ella walked right up to the edge. She dipped one big foot into the brown, gooey mud. 'Squish!' said the mud. Ella giggled. Then, she dipped her second foot. 'Squelch!' said the mud. Ella laughed out loud. Without waiting another second, Ella sat right down in the middle of the puddle. Splash! Mud flew everywhere, landing on the leaves and making funny dots on her tummy. But Ella was not done yet. She used her long, wiggly trunk like a magical hose. She dipped the tip into the cool mud, sucked it all the way up, and blew it right up into the air. 'Pbbbt!' went her trunk. A big shower of cool, wet mud landed right on top of her own head. It felt so squishy and wonderful. 'I am a mud monster!' Ella cheered, splashing her feet and making big waves in the puddle. Her mommy stood nearby, spraying her own back with water and smiling lovingly at her playful baby. Other jungle animals stopped by to watch. A little monkey chattered, and a colorful parrot squawked in delight. Ella felt so happy, cool, and clean in her own special way. After a long time playing, the warm sun began to dry the mud on Ella's back, turning it into a cool, hard shell that kept her safe from the buzzing bugs. 'Time to wash off and get ready for a nice nap,' said Mommy. Together, they walked over to the sparkling river. Splash went Ella into the clear, blue water. She washed away the mud and drank a long, refreshing gulp. With a full tummy and a sleepy yawn, Ella snuggled up right next to her mommy in the soft grass. She closed her heavy eyes and dreamed of squishy, wonderful mud.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods lived a sweet little elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby loved bright colors more than anything else in the world. Today was a very special day because it was Barnaby's birthday, and his best friend, a little brown monkey, gave him a gigantic, shiny red balloon. The balloon was round like a tomato and bounced happily in the breeze on the end of a long string. Barnaby held the string tightly in his trunk. 'Thank you so much!' trumpeted Barnaby, doing a happy little spin. He walked through the forest, feeling very proud of his wonderful birthday present. The red balloon bobbed up and down in the air, saying hello to the buzzing bees and the fluttering butterflies. But oh no! A sudden gust of wind came swooping through the trees. Whoosh! The wind was stronger than Barnaby expected. It pulled the string right out of his trunk. 'Oh no!' cried Barnaby, blinking his big brown eyes in surprise. Up, up, up went the shiny red balloon, floating higher and higher into the bright blue sky. It drifted past the tall green treetops, looking smaller and smaller every second. Barnaby wanted his balloon back. He stomped his foot and let out a little trumpet sound. Luckily, his clever friends were watching. Sammy the squirrel scampered up the tallest oak tree as fast as his furry legs could carry him. 'Hold on, Barnaby, I will try to grab it!' chattered Sammy. But the balloon was just a little bit too high, floating way out of Sammy's reach. Next, Bella the bird flapped her strong wings and flew straight up into the sky. She zoomed past the clouds and gently tapped the string with her beak. 'Got it!' chirped Bella. She guided the floating red balloon all the way back down to the ground, placing the string right back into Barnaby's waiting trunk. Barnaby was so overjoyed that he wrapped his trunk around Bella in a gentle hug. He held the string extra-tight this time, making sure it would never float away again. Surrounded by all his wonderful jungle friends, Barnaby shared his birthday treats, and the red balloon danced happily in the breeze above them all.

stories.title: Oliver's Big Bedtime Yawn
stories.text: The stars were just beginning to twinkle in the purple evening sky, and all the animals in the great grassy savanna were getting ready for sleep. All, that is, except for little Oliver the elephant. Oliver had big round ears, tiny little toenails, and a mountain of energy left inside him. 'I am not sleepy at all!' said Oliver, running in a big circle around the acacia tree. His mommy gently shook her head and smiled. 'Even little elephants need to rest their big feet and dream sweet dreams,' she whispered. Oliver stopped running and let out a huge, loud yawn. 'Yaaaaawn!' It was so big that a little bird sleeping in the branches woke up and blinked. 'See?' said Mommy. 'Your body is telling you it is time for bed.' Oliver did not want to miss out on any fun, but his eyelids felt heavier than heavy stones. 'Will you help me get ready for sleep?' asked Oliver softly. 'Of course,' said Mommy. First, Oliver needed to brush his big white teeth. He used his long trunk to hold a giant toothbrush, scrubbing back and forth. Scrub, scrub, scrub went the brush inside his mouth. Next, it was time for a cozy bedtime story. Mommy sat down under the glowing moon and told Oliver a wonderful tale about a magical forest where the leaves tasted like sweet strawberries. Oliver listened closely, resting his heavy head against his mommy's warm, soft leg. The crickets began to sing a gentle lullaby in the grass, rubbing their little legs together. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. The gentle breeze rustled the tall grass, making a soft shushing sound. Oliver closed his eyes and took a deep, slow breath. He imagined floating on a fluffy white cloud, high above the savanna. His big ears flopped down onto the ground, and his long trunk curled up neatly like a sleeping snake. Mommy wrapped her trunk around Oliver in a loving, safe embrace, keeping him warm through the night. With one last tiny sigh, Oliver drifted off to sleep, ready for all the wonderful adventures that would wait for him when the bright sun came up again.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the big, warm jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears, a long grey trunk, and four very big, very clumsy feet. Every morning, Ellie loved to splash in the mud with her friends. Splash, splash, squish, squash! Mud went up, mud went down, mud went all around. But one sunny morning, the sun was shining extra bright, and the ground was a little bit chilly. Ellie's mama had a special surprise waiting by the big green banana tree. She said, 'Good morning, my sweet Ellie! Look what I found just for you.' Ellie blinked her big brown eyes and walked over with a heavy thump-thump-thump. There on the soft grass stood a pair of bright red boots. They were shiny, they were new, and they were the most wonderful color Ellie had ever seen. Ellie picked up one boot with her long trunk. She sniffed it. It smelled like shiny new rubber. 'Can I try them on, Mama?' asked Ellie happily. 'Of course,' smiled her mama. Ellie stepped her first big left foot into the left boot. Squeak! Then she stepped her right foot into the right boot. Squeak, squak! They fit her wiggly toes just right. Ellie felt so tall and so proud. She decided to go for a walk to show all her jungle friends her brand-new boots. She walked past the tall bamboo stalks. Thump, squeak! Thump, squeak! The little monkeys swinging in the trees stopped to point and clap. 'Look at Ellie's red boots!' chattered cheeky monkey. Next, Ellie walked down to the sparkling blue river where Sammy the snake was resting on a warm rock. 'Hello, Sammy! Do you like my new boots?' asked Ellie, lifting her foot high in the air. Sammy hissed softly and nodded his head. 'They are very shiny, Ellie!' She kept walking until she found her best friend, a little zebra named Zuzu. Zuzu trotted over with a happy neigh. 'Your boots make a funny squeak when you walk, Ellie!' giggled Zuzu. Ellie laughed a big belly laugh. She loved the funny sound her boots made. Suddenly, the sky turned a little bit gray. Uh-oh! Big raindrops began to fall from the clouds. Plip, plop, plip, plop. The other animals scurried away to find dry shelter under the broad banana leaves. But Ellie just stood right where she was. She looked down at her feet. Her toes were warm and dry inside the bright red boots. The rain could not get her toes wet at all! Ellie started to dance a happy little elephant dance. She stomped her left foot. She stomped her right foot. She twirled around in a clumsy circle. 'Hooray for my red boots!' she trumpeted loudly into the cloudy sky. When the rain stopped and the warm sun came back out, Ellie walked all the way home to her mama. She gave her mama a big, tight hug with her trunk. 'Thank you for my boots, Mama. They made my rainy day so much fun!' Her mama nuzzled Ellie's cheek and whispered, 'You are very welcome, my little dancing elephant.' Ellie curled up in the soft grass and fell fast asleep, dreaming of shiny red boots and puddles to jump in tomorrow.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the green, green forest lived a little baby elephant named Barnaby. Barnaby had tiny white tusks, a wiggly trunk, and a heart full of curiosity. Today was a very special day because it was Barnaby's third birthday! All of his jungle friends came to celebrate with him. There was Leo the lion, Bella the bunny, and Penny the parrot. They brought yummy fruit salad, sweet melon slices, and lots of hugs. But the best part of the whole party was the balloons. There were yellow balloons, green balloons, purple balloons, and one giant, shiny, red balloon that floated high up into the air on a long white string. Barnaby stared at the big red balloon with wide, sparkly eyes. It was round like a big tomato and danced happily in the gentle breeze. 'Would you like to hold the string, Barnaby?' asked his mama gently. Barnaby nodded his head up and down. 'Yes, please!' he said. Mama placed the soft white string right into the tip of Barnaby's long trunk. Barnaby curled his trunk around the string, holding it safely and securely. Oh, how happy he felt! The balloon bobbed up and down in the air, pulling gently on his trunk as if it wanted to play a game of tag. Barnaby started to walk around the party clearing. The red balloon followed right behind him, floating like a faithful little cloud. 'Look at me!' trumpeted Barnaby to his friends. Leo the lion roared a happy birthday cheer. Bella the bunny did a happy hop. Penny the parrot squawked a merry tune. Barnaby felt like he was the king of the whole wide world. But then, a sudden puff of wind blew through the trees. Whoosh! The wind was stronger than Barnaby expected. It caught the big red balloon and lifted it higher into the sunny sky. 'Whoa!' gasped Barnaby as the string slipped just a tiny bit. The balloon tugged upward, wanting to fly up to the fluffy white clouds. Barnaby didn't want his special birthday balloon to float away forever. Quickly, he used his long trunk to reach up high. He wrapped his trunk firmly around the string, pulling it down closer to his face. He gave it a gentle, loving squeeze. Phew! That was a close one. Barnaby decided that holding the string with just his trunk was a bit too tricky when the wind decided to play. Instead, he carefully looped the string around his ear, right where it was nice and secure. That worked even better! Now the red balloon bobbed right next to his big floppy ear, whispering secrets to him as the wind blew. Barnaby smiled from ear to ear. He spent the rest of the afternoon walking through the forest with his shiny red friend, dancing and playing games with all of his wonderful friends. When the sun began to set and painted the sky in pink and orange, the party came to an end. Barnaby walked home hand-in-trunk with his mama, still wearing his balloon safely by his ear. As they climbed into bed, Barnaby whispered, 'Thank you for the best birthday ever, balloon.' And with a happy sigh, the little elephant closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, holding sweet dreams in his trunk.

stories.title: The Little Lost Star
stories.text: Once upon a starry, starry night, little Ellie the baby elephant woke up from her cozy nap. The moon was a bright silver banana hanging in the dark, velvety sky, and the stars twinkled like tiny diamonds. Ellie stretched her front legs and yawned a big elephant yawn. 'Yawn-hoo!' she whispered to herself. Then, something caught her eye down by the edge of the quiet river. It was a tiny, shimmering light, bobbing up and down in the tall green reeds. Blink, blink, sparkle, sparkle. Ellie blinked her sleepy eyes. What could that be? She tipped her head to the left, then to the right. Being a brave little elephant, she decided to go take a closer look. She crept very softly through the grass. Thump, tip-toe, thump, tip-toe. Even though she was a baby elephant, she tried her very best to be as quiet as a little mouse. When she reached the riverbank, she peeked through the tall blades of grass. Right there, sitting on a big lily pad, was a tiny glowing star! It looked just like the stars up in the sky, but it was shaking and shivering. 'Oh dear, oh dear,' whimpered a tiny, sweet voice. 'I think I fell right out of the sky, and now I am all alone in the dark!' Ellie's kind heart melted. She knew she had to help. She gently reached out her long grey trunk, stretching it out like a soft velvet slide all the way to the lily pad. 'Hello little star,' Ellie whispered softly so she wouldn't frighten it. 'Do not be afraid. I am Ellie. Are you lost?' The little star sniffled, its light flickering a soft, warm yellow. 'Yes, Ellie. I slipped off the Milky Way while I was dancing, and now I cannot reach my home up high.' Ellie thought for a moment. How could a little elephant help a star get back to the sky? Then, she had a brilliant idea. She knew that elephants are very strong, and their trunks can reach high places. 'Climb onto my trunk, little star,' encouraged Ellie. 'I will give you a lift.' The tiny star hesitated for a second, then hopped gently onto the very tip of Ellie's trunk. It felt as warm as a sunbeam and tickled Ellie's skin, making her want to giggle. 'Hold on tight!' said Ellie. She closed her eyes, planted her four big feet firmly on the soft ground, and stretched her long neck up toward the heavens. She lifted her trunk higher and higher, reaching up toward the glittering night sky. She stretched as tall as the tallest palm tree in the jungle. The little star looked up and saw its starry friends twinkling encouragement from above. With a joyful cheer, the little star gave a big hop right off Ellie's trunk and zoomed straight back up into the dark sky, swirling and twirling all the way to its cozy place in a constellation. 'Yay! You made it!' trumpeted Ellie happily in a quiet, joyful whisper. The little star twinkled brightly down at Ellie, flashing a grateful thank-you message in Morse code of light. Ellie smiled, feeling so proud and happy inside. She turned around and trotted softly back to her sleeping mama, curling up warmly by her side. As Ellie closed her eyes to finish her sleep, she knew that even the smallest little elephant could do big, wonderful things when they have a kind heart and a helping trunk.

stories.title: Ella's Big Bubble Bath
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the big green jungle, lived a little baby elephant named Ella. Ella had big floppy ears, four chubby little feet, and a long, wonderful trunk. But today, Ella was not feeling happy. She had been playing in the gooey mud all morning long, and now she was covered from head to toe in thick, sticky brown dirt. Her momma smiled and said, 'Oh, Ella! It is time for a big bubbly bath!' Ella loved bubbles! Momma elephant scooped up lots of sparkly river water in her own long trunk. Then, she sprayed a cool, refreshing shower right over little Ella. Whee! Water went splash, splash, splash! Ella giggled and flapped her big ears. Next came the green jungle soap. Momma scrubbed Ella's left leg, and then her right leg, and then her big round tummy. Scrub, scrub, scrub! Little bubbles started to pop all around them. Pop, pop, pop! Ella wanted to make bubbles too. She dipped her trunk into the soapy water, took a big deep breath, and blew. Whoosh! Out came a giant, shiny soap bubble that floated high up into the air. It was bigger than a watermelon! Ella chased the giant bubble around the riverbank, stomping her feet. Boom, boom, boom! But she was too slow, and the bubble popped right on her nose with a tiny tickle. That made Ella laugh out loud. 'Hee-hee-hee!' she trumpeted. Finally, Momma rinsed all the soap away with one more big spray of clean river water. Ella shook herself just like a wet puppy. Shake, shake, shake! Water drops flew everywhere like tiny diamonds in the sunshine. Now, Ella was clean, sweet-smelling, and ready for a nice long afternoon nap in the soft grass. She curled up next to her momma, closed her sleepy eyes, and dreamed all about big, wonderful bubbles floating in the sky.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Balloon
stories.text: High up on the sunny hill, a little yellow elephant named Barnaby was having the best day ever. Today was his third birthday, and his very best friend, a cheeky little monkey named Milo, had given him a present. It was a big, shiny, bright red balloon! The balloon bobbed up and down in the warm breeze, dancing happily against the blue sky. Barnaby held the string tightly in his trunk. He walked down the winding jungle path, feeling so proud of his wonderful toy. 'Look at my red balloon!' he trumpeted softly to the passing butterflies. But oh no! Just as Barnaby walked beneath a tall, leafy banana tree, a gust of wind came blowing through. Whoosh! The wind tugged gently at the bright red string. Barnaby squeezed his trunk, but the string slipped right through. Oh dear! The red balloon floated up, up, up into the sky, higher than the monkey, higher than the tree, and higher than the birds. Barnaby let out a sad little cry. 'Boo-hoo,' sniffed the little yellow elephant, wiping a tear with his floppy ear. Seeing his friend looking so sad, clever Milo swung down from the branches. 'Do not worry, Barnaby!' chattered Milo. 'Let us look for something even better!' Just then, floating down from the bushes, came a whole bunch of golden, sweet bananas. Milo caught them skillfully and shared them with Barnaby. Soon, they were both munching happily on the delicious treats, crunching and chewing. Barnaby realized that even though his red balloon was gone flying in the clouds, sharing sweet bananas with his best friend was much more fun anyway. He gave Milo a big, tight hug with his long trunk, and they played games in the sunshine until the sun began to sink low in the evening sky.

stories.title: Oliver's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was finally beginning to go down behind the tall green mountains, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and purple. It was time for little Oliver the elephant to go to sleep. But Oliver was wide awake! He stomped his little feet on the soft moss. Thump, thump, thump! He swung his trunk back and forth. Swish, swish, swish! He was having far too much fun to even think about closing his eyes. His wise old grandma walked over and patted his back gently with her trunk. 'Time to rest your little head, my sweet boy,' she whispered softly. Grandma began to sing a slow, sweet jungle song. The crickets in the tall grass joined in with a gentle chirp, chirp, chirp. The hoot owls high in the branches added a sleepy hoo, hoo, hoo. Oliver listened to the lovely music. He walked over to his favorite sleeping spot beneath the great banyan tree. The grass was as soft as a feather pillow, and the evening breeze felt cool and nice against his skin. Oliver yawned a huge, wide yawn. 'Yaaaawn!' he went, showing all his tiny baby teeth. He stretched out his legs and laid his heavy head down on the ground. One by one, Oliver thought about all the fun things he had done today. He remembered splashing in the cool mud puddle with his friends. He remembered chasing the yellow butterflies through the tall ferns. And he remembered munching on the sweet green leaves for his afternoon snack. Those were such happy memories. Slowly, Oliver's heavy eyelids began to droop. He closed his left eye, and then he closed his right eye. His breathing became deep and slow. In and out. In and out. The little elephant was finally fast asleep, dreaming sweet dreams of flying balloons and bubbly rivers, resting peacefully until the bright morning sun would wake him up to play all over again.

stories.title: Ellie's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the bright green jungle, there lived a little elephant named Ellie. Ellie had big floppy ears, a long gray trunk, and four very big feet. Today, it was a rainy day. Plip, plop, plip, plop went the raindrops on the big broad leaves. Ellie looked down at her big feet. She wanted to play outside in the wet, squishy mud! But her mom said, 'If you go outside, you must wear your boots, Ellie!' Ellie ran to her closet and opened the big red door. There they were. The biggest, brightest, reddest boots in the whole wide jungle. Ellie giggled with delight. She picked up the first boot with her long trunk. Whoosh! She tried to put it on her left front foot. But wait, her foot was just too big! Ellie pushed and she shoved. She wiggled and she wobbled. Oh dear, the boot would not go on. Ellie felt a little sad. She sat down on a soft green cushion and let out a little puff of air through her trunk. Pfffft! Her mom walked into the room with a warm smile. 'Let me help you, my sweet little elephant,' said her mom. Mom gently took the boot and showed Ellie how to point her toes. One, two, three, slide! Pop! The first red boot was on! Ellie clapped her big gray hands together. Yay! Then came the second boot. Mom helped Ellie slide that one on too. Now Ellie had two bright red boots on her feet. They shined like shiny apples. Ellie stomped her feet on the floor. Thump, thump, thump! It made a happy sound. 'Time for the mud puddles!' cheered Ellie. She waddled outside as fast as her big legs could carry her. Squish, squash, squish, squash went her boots in the muddy puddles. Water splashed up, up, up into the air! Ellie laughed a big, booming toddler laugh. She trumpeted with joy, 'Toot, toot, mud is so much fun!' Her mom watched from the porch and smiled. Ellie splashed and played all morning long, wearing her favorite big red boots, until the sun came out to dry the jungle floor.

stories.title: Ellie Finds a Lost Star
stories.text: The sun was going down behind the tall mountain. The sky turned from blue to sleepy purple, and then to dark, cozy black. Little Ellie the elephant was getting ready for bed. She wore her favorite star-printed pajamas and brushed her big white teeth. 'Time for sleep, little one,' whispered her daddy, tucking her into her big leaf bed. But Ellie did not want to sleep just yet. She poked her head out of the tent and looked up at the big, beautiful night sky. Twinkle, twinkle, little stars, shining bright like diamonds. Ellie pointed her long trunk up high. Point, point, point! But wait. Something was not quite right. Down in the soft grass, right near a big sleeping toadstool, something was glowing. It was small, and yellow, and twinkling softly. Blink, blink, blink. Ellie gasped. She hopped right out of her cozy bed and tiptoed across the grass on her quiet tippy-toes. Tap, tap, tap went her feet. She leaned way down and looked closely. Oh goodness! It was a tiny little star! Somehow, it had slipped right out of the sky and tumbled all the way down to the jungle floor. The little star looked very scared and very cold. It shivered and shook. 'Oh, hello little star,' whispered Ellie in her softest, sweetest voice. 'Did you fall down from your cozy home?' The star blinked twice, as if to say yes. Ellie knew just what to do. She used her long, gentle trunk like a soft spoon. She scooped up the tiny star very, very carefully. The star felt warm and tickly against the tip of her trunk. 'Hold on tight,' said Ellie. She walked over to the tallest tree in the jungle, right beneath the great big moon. She stretched her neck up as high as she could reach. Up, up, up went her trunk. The tiny star reached out its little points and grabbed hold of the velvet night sky. Zip! It popped right back into its special place among the constellations. The star sparkled extra bright, sending a warm yellow wink down to Ellie. Ellie smiled a big happy smile. She whispered, 'Goodnight, little star.' Then she scurried back to her leaf bed, closed her sleepy eyes, and dreamed sweet, starry dreams until the morning sun woke her up.

stories.title: The Great Peanut Hunt
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! Today was a very special day in the jungle. It was the annual Jungle Snack Day! And guess what Ellie’s favorite snack in the whole wide world was? Crunchy, yummy peanuts! Ellie woke up with a big stretch. Stretch her trunk up high, stretch her legs out wide. Yaaaawn! She ran into the kitchen where her mommy was cooking. 'Is it time?' asked Ellie with excitement dancing in her big brown eyes. 'Yes, Ellie,' said her mommy. 'Today we are going on a peanut hunt!' Mommy handed Ellie a small yellow basket with a red ribbon tied around the handle. 'I want to find a hundred peanuts!' cheered Ellie. She dashed out the front door and began her big adventure. First, she looked behind the big banana tree. She lifted the green leaves with her trunk. Peek-a-boo! Was there a peanut? No, just a sleepy little green frog saying 'Ribbit!' Ellie giggled and kept on walking. Next, she checked near the rushing river. Swish, swash went the cool blue water. She looked under a smooth gray stone. Was there a peanut hiding there? Nope! Just a wiggly pink worm doing a little dance. Ellie smiled and waved. 'Keep looking, Ellie!' she whispered to herself. She marched over to the tall grass patch. It was tickly and green. She smelled something nutty. Sniff, sniff, sniff! Ellie used her strong trunk to blow away the top layer of dirt. And right there, nestled in the soft earth, was a big, round, bumpy peanut! Ellie’s eyes went wide. 'Aha! Found you!' she cried. She picked it up gently and placed it right inside her yellow basket. Clink! Went the peanut against the bottom. Then she found another one, and another one, until her basket was completely full to the top. Ellie skipped all the way home to share her yummy treasure with her mommy and daddy. They munched and crunched together, licking their lips and giggling. It was the best peanut hunt ever!

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and grey,
Stomps his feet and likes to play.
Swings his trunk up in the air,
Showing off his floppy pair.

Big round tummy, fuzzy head,
Time to march right out of bed.
Stomp, stomp, stomp across the floor,
Looking for a leafy door.

Ears go flapping left and right,
Basking in the morning light.
Splashing water, cool and sweet,
Happy sounds from head to feet.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy jungle bed.

rhymes.title: The Friendly Trunk
rhymes.text:
See the elephant in the tree,
Looking down at you and me.
Long grey nose is called a trunk,
Drinking water with a slurp.

Reach it high and reach it low,
Watch the sparkling water go.
Spraying drops of magic blue,
Right on me and right on you.

Flapping ears go flap, flap, flap,
Ready for a little nap.
Walking slowly down the lane,
Dancing softly in the rain.

Baby elephant, safe and sound,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Hold my hand and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Water in the river deep,
While the little fishes sleep.
Elephant is coming by,
Looking at the sunny sky.

Sucks up water in her nose,
Right from trunk down to her toes.
Whosh it goes up in the air,
Splashing droplets everywhere.

Mummy smiles and joins the fun,
Basking in the golden sun.
Happy noises, loud and clear,
Cheering for the jungle year.

Time to dry and time to rest,
With a mummy is the best.
Snuggle close and softly sigh,
Stars are shining in the sky.

rhymes.title: Little Gray Elephant
rhymes.text:
Little gray elephant walking around,
Stomping his big feet on the ground.
Swishing his trunk up in the air,
Blinking his eyes and looking there.

He loves to play in the mud so deep,
Then he curls up and goes to sleep.
Dreaming of peanuts sweet and tall,
Having great fun both big and small.

Flapping his ears like paper wings,
Listening to what the jungle sings.
Walking along the river stream,
Lost in a happy little dream.

Goodnight, elephant, time for rest,
Snuggled up close is what is best.
Stars are shining bright and high,
Singing a sweet and quiet lullaby.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Puddle
rhymes.text:
Big gray nose is very long,
Singing a happy little song.
Splash, splash, splash in the mud,
Look at the happy little bud.

Water is cool upon his skin,
Watch the happy fish begin to spin.
Ears go flapping back and forth,
Going south and going north.

Trot along with heavy feet,
Finding something nice to eat.
A juicy leaf upon a tree,
Shared with a buzzing little bee.

Sun is sinking in the west,
Time for little ones to rest.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Until the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: The Friendly Giant
rhymes.text:
Gray and gentle, big and tall,
Never mean and never small.
He has a trunk that likes to spray,
Water on a sunny day.

Friends come running when he calls,
Playing near the garden walls.
Monkey swings from tree to tree,
Happy as a bird can be.

Elephant gives a friendly toot,
Eating up a yellow fruit.
Mama smiles and holds his hand,
Walking through the lovely land.

Now the moon is glowing bright,
Bidding all the world goodnight.
Sleep until the morning dew,
Little elephant, we love you.

rhymes.title: The Little Elephant
rhymes.text:
See the little elephant grey,
Marching through the trees today.
Swishing with his trunk so long,
Singing out a happy song.

Stomp, stomp, stomp his big feet go,
Walking very fast or slow.
Flapping ears that flap and fly,
Reaching up to touch the sky.

Water splashing in the pool,
Keeping little bodies cool.
Squirting drops of shiny spray,
Having fun and games all day.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little ones to go.
Curled up safely in the night,
Sleeping till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Big Gray Dumbo
rhymes.text:
Big gray elephant, big and tall,
Playing with a shiny ball.
Rolling it along the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Long gray trunk to smell a rose,
Blowing bubbles through his nose.
Big round tummy, big gray toes,
Off to where the jungle grows.

Eating leaves up in a tree,
As happy as a child can be.
Swish your tail and flap your ears,
Chasing all the sleepy tears.

Twinkle stars begin to peep,
Time to cuddle up and sleep.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
When you wake to dance and play.

rhymes.title: Trunk Up High
rhymes.text:
Trunk up high and trunk down low,
Watch the friendly elephant go.
Big round feet go thump, thump, thump,
Over every little bump.

Eating peanuts, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Having such a tasty lunch.
Swishing water with a swish,
Making every happy wish.

Little baby, do not cry,
Watch the birds go flying by.
Mamma hugs you nice and tight,
Keeping you so safe all night.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Wait for tomorrow and a brand new day.
Dreaming of the jungle green,
Best little elephant ever seen.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching down the path today.
Stomp your foot and count to three,
Happy as a bird set free.

Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a lovely jungle ride.
Flップ flap go your ears so wide,
Where do little beetles hide?

Find a puddle in the sun,
Splashing water is so fun.
Spray it high up in the air,
Cooling breezes everywhere.

Now it is time to take a rest,
Curled up safely in your nest.
Close your sleepy eyes so deep,
Little elephant, fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Ten Grey Toes
rhymes.text:
Ten grey toes upon the ground,
Walking round and merry round.
Elephant is big and tall,
Never stumbling, never fall.

Long gray trunk to smell a rose,
Tickling gently on your nose.
Big round tummy, soft and sweet,
Walking on your heavy feet.

Wave your tail and say hello,
Watch the gentle river flow.
Eat a leaf and chew it slow,
Now it is time to gently go.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little bird is flying by.
Sleepy elephant in the night,
Sleeping till the morning light.

rhymes.title: The Peanut Song
rhymes.text:
Elephant, elephant, what do you see?
Crunchy green peanuts under the tree.
Pick them all up with your trunk so long,
Singing a happy little elephant song.

Walk through the grass with a heavy tread,
Wear a green leaf upon your head.
Find your mama and give a shout,
That is what elephants are about.

Splash in the water, cool and blue,
I am a happy elephant, how about you?
Shake your tail and dance around,
Making a happy rumbling sound.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Dreaming of peanuts sweet and tall,
Goodnight, elephant, best of all.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching down the path today.
Stomp your feet upon the ground,
Make a happy, booming sound.

Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a lovely jungle ride.
Flap your ears just like a fan,
Catch me if you really can!

Splish and splash inside the pool,
Water makes you nice and cool.
Now it is time to take a rest,
Sleeping in your cozy nest.

Close your eyes and do not peep,
Little elephant falls asleep.
Dreaming of the trees so tall,
Goodnight, baby, that is all.

rhymes.title: Five Gray Feet
rhymes.text:
Five gray feet upon the floor,
Walking through the jungle door.
Trunk goes up and trunk goes down,
Happiest elephant in the town.

Eating leaves from high up high,
Reaching all the way to the sky.
Crunch and munch a tasty treat,
Best food a young one could eat.

See him smile and see him play,
Running and jumping all the day.
Now the sun begins to set,
Best day he will not forget.

Snuggle close and cuddle tight,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with peace and sleepy love.

rhymes.title: Peanut the Little Gray Pal
rhymes.text:
Peanut the elephant loves to play,
Jumping and running throughout the day.
He has a tail and a wiggly nose,
Wiggling right down to his toes.

Friends come running from the trees,
Dancing softly in the breeze.
Monkeys chatter, birds will sing,
Joy is such a lovely thing.

Now the shadows start to grow,
Moving very, very slow.
Time to curl up on the ground,
Without making any sound.

Big gray blanket, sky so blue,
Sending sleepy hugs to you.
Rest your head and gently sigh,
Little elephant, lullaby.

rhymes.title: The Happy Elephant
rhymes.text:
See the elephant walking by,
Stamping feet beneath the sky.
Swishing tail and big round toes,
Looking for a friend he knows.

Now he lifts his trunk so high,
Reaching upward to the sky.
Making sounds like trumpet blare,
Splashing water in the air.

Flapping ears that shake and swing,
Hear the happy baby sing.
Walking through the jungle trees,
Feeling every gentle breeze.

Time for bed and time for rest,
Snuggling close is what is best.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little elephant falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Five Big Steps
rhymes.text:
Big gray elephant takes a walk,
Never needing words to talk.
Swinging trunk from left to right,
Underneath the morning light.

Stopping by a muddy pool,
Water nice and clean and cool.
Tipping water on his head,
Ready now to find his bed.

Walking past the tall green trees,
Buzzing goes the honey bees.
Blinking eyes and yawning wide,
Mama elephant stays beside.

Curling up upon the ground,
Not another single sound.
Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with gentle peace and love.

rhymes.title: Trunk So Long
rhymes.text:
Elephant, elephant, strong and grand,
Walking softly on the land.
Ears like fans of breezy blue,
Coming out to play with you.

Reaching for a tasty leaf,
Chewing slowly, what a treat.
Drinking water from the stream,
Like a happy daytime dream.

Stomping feet go thump and thud,
Playing nicely in the mud.
Now it is time to turn around,
Sitting softly on the ground.

Waving trunk and saying bye,
As the sleepy birds fly by.
Curling up to dream all night,
Morning sun is shining bright.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching down the path today.
Stomp your feet upon the ground,
Make a happy, rumbling sound.
Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a lovely jungle ride.
Flap your ears just like a fan,
Catching breezes if you can.
Find some water, cool and clear,
Splash your friends who gather near.
Spray the water in the air,
Droplets falling everywhere.
Now you're clean and feeling bright,
Ready for a starry night.
Curle your trunk and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Trunk Up High
rhymes.text:
See the elephant in the zoo,
Waving trunk to me and you.
Reaching up so very high,
Touching all the passing sky.
Walking slowly, round and round,
With a heavy, happy sound.
Gray and gentle, big and tall,
Never clumsy, never small.
Eating peanuts, crunch, crunch, crunch,
 Munching on a tasty lunch.
Blinking with a friendly eye,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.
Now it's time to take a rest,
Lying in a cozy nest.
Goodnight, elephant, sleep so deep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: The Friendly Giant
rhymes.text:
Oh, the elephant is a friend so dear,
Bringing smiles and spreading cheer.
With two ears like giant sails,
Walking by the monkey trails.
He can trumpet loud and clear,
Making all the jungle cheer.
With his trunk, he drinks the spring,
Happy as a bird can sing.
Muddy toes and wrinkly skin,
Let the quiet game begin.
Rocking gently left and right,
Hiding safely from the night.
Softly humming lullabies,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Time to dream of jungle trees,
Swaying in the evening breeze.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Grey
rhymes.text:
Little elephant grey and tall,
You are not so very small.
With your trunk you like to play,
Splashing water every day.

Big round ears go flap, flap, flap,
Time to take a little nap.
Four stout legs and tiny tail,
Walking down the dusty trail.

Peanuts are a yummy treat,
Tasty things for you to eat.
Marching through the jungle green,
Best old friend I've ever seen.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in your jungle town.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Little baby, you are best.

rhymes.title: Stomping Through The Grass
rhymes.text:
Hear the heavy footsteps sound,
Stomping softly on the ground.
See the gray beast walking by,
Reaching up to touch the sky.

Swish your trunk from side to side,
Take a gentle, bumpy ride.
Smile and giggle, laugh and play,
We are happy here today.

Big feet make a funny thud,
Walking through the sticky mud.
Blow a bubble in the air,
Happy creatures everywhere.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little baby falls asleep.
Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Dancing in the evening breeze.

rhymes.title: Five Grey Elephants
rhymes.text:
One grey elephant in the sun,
Having lots of noisy fun.
Two grey elephants stomp around,
Making thunder on the ground.

Three grey elephants swing their trunk,
Sitting on a tree's old stump.
Four grey elephants swim and play,
Cooling off throughout the day.

Five grey elephants trumpet loud,
Standing proud inside a crowd.
Big floppy ears so soft and wide,
With their mummies by their side.

Now the playtime comes to close,
Wiggling every little toes.
Time for bed and quiet rest,
Sleeping is the very best.

rhymes.title: The Little Grey Elephant
rhymes.text:
See the little elephant grey,
Stomping through the grass to play.
Stomp, stomp, stomp across the floor,
Then he wants to play some more.

He has ears so big and wide,
Like a blanket by his side.
Flap, flap, flap they go all day,
Chasing pesky flies away.

He has a trunk so long and neat,
Reaching down to touch his feet.
Swoosh, swoosh, water in the air,
Splashing coolness everywhere.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Rest your heavy sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Trunk So Long
rhymes.text:
Elephant, elephant, tall and grand,
Walking on the golden sand.
Swinging trunk from side to side,
Taking baby for a ride.

Big round tummy, feet like logs,
Walking past the happy frogs.
Eating leaves up in the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.

Hear him trumpet loud and clear,
Calling all his jungle dear.
Friends are coming down the trail,
Holding onto every tail.

Now the playtime fun is through,
Saying bye-bye to the zoo.
Crawling under blankets deep,
Elephant is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Mud
rhymes.text:
Little elephant wants a bath,
Walking down the muddy path.
Brown and sticky, oh what fun,
Playing underneath the sun.

Squish and squach between his toes,
Mud is getting on his nose.
Splish and splash and shake his tail,
Happy as a shiny whale.

Mommy sprays him with her trunk,
Cleaning every little chunk.
Water sparkles in the light,
Making everything so bright.

Now he is all clean and dry,
Watching stars up in the sky.
Curled up tight and feeling sweet,
Dreaming of his favorite treat.

rhymes.title: The Little Grey Elephant
rhymes.text:
See the little grey elephant walking around,
Stomping his big round feet on the ground.
He has two ears like a big floppy fan,
Splashing in water the best that he can.

He has a long nose that we call a trunk,
Swinging it up when he plays with a skunk.
He loves to eat peanuts and munch on sweet hay,
Happy and smiling throughout the whole day.

When evening comes and the sun goes to sleep,
Little grey elephant doesn't make a peep.
He curls up his trunk and he closes his eyes,
Dreaming of stars shining bright in the skies.

Goodnight to his toes and goodnight to his head,
Time for an elephant snug in his bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Peanuts
rhymes.text:
Five little peanuts sitting in a row,
Waiting for an elephant to say hello.
Along came an elephant walking so slow,
With a big trunk swinging to and fro.

He sniffed at the first one and ate it right up,
Chomping it down like a hungry pup.
He sniffed at the second with a happy sound,
Crunching it up till no pieces were found.

He sniffed at the third one and gave a loud toot,
Biting it down with a crunch and a boot.
He sniffed at the fourth one and gobbled it fast,
Leaving the very last peanut at last.

He ate up the fifth one and rubbed his round tum,
Happy as can be and beating a drum.

rhymes.title: Trunk Up High
rhymes.text:
Trunk up high and trunk down low,
Watch the baby elephant put on a show.
Stomping in circles around the big tree,
Happy as happy as can ever be.

Flapping his ears like a bird in the sky,
Watching the beautiful butterflies fly.
He makes a big trumpet, toot-toot and hooray,
Inviting his jungle friends out here to play.

They dance in the mud and they splash in the pool,
Keeping their big heavy bodies quite cool.
Now the sun's setting, the day is all done,
Time to stop playing and finish the fun.

Walking back home to a warm mama's side,
Resting all night on a soft grassy tide.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and grey,
Walking through the woods today.
Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a happy jungle ride.

Big round ears that flap and fly,
Reaching up into the sky.
Stomp your feet upon the floor,
Hear the happy baby roar.

Find a puddle in the street,
Splash the water with your feet.
Now it is time to take a rest,
Sleeping in your cozy nest.

Close your eyes and count to ten,
Wake up and play games again.
Dreaming of the trees so tall,
Little elephant loved by all.

rhymes.title: Peanut Time
rhymes.text:
Elephant, elephant, strong and tall,
Playing with a yellow ball.
Hungry tummy, time to eat,
Peanuts are a yummy treat.

Use your trunk to pick them up,
Drink some water from a cup.
Munch them up and chew them right,
Shining in the morning light.

Now your tummy is so round,
Sit right down upon the ground.
Blink your eyes and give a wink,
Stop a second just to think.

Time to cuddle with your mom,
In the jungle safe and calm.
Whisper soft and whisper low,
Watch the sleepy jungle grow.

rhymes.title: The Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Splish and splash in mud so brown,
Best young elephant in the town.
Suck up water, spray it high,
Reaching all the way to the sky.

Wash your back and wash your toes,
Tickle now your little nose.
Shake your tail and shake your head,
Time to dry and time for bed.

Stars are shining bright and clear,
Luna moon is drawing near.
Soft pajamas, warm and sweet,
Resting all your heavy feet.

Hug your blanket, hug your toy,
Every little girl and boy.
Sweetest dreams until the dawn,
Little elephant, rest on.

rhymes.title: Big Gray Elephant
rhymes.text:
Big gray elephant, big and tall,
You are the biggest one of all.
You have ears that flap and sway,
And a trunk to help you play.

Stomp your feet upon the ground,
Make a loud and happy sound.
Squirting water in the sun,
Having so much summer fun.

Swing your trunk from left to right,
Underneath the starry night.
Eating leaves up in the trees,
Swaying softly in the breeze.

Time for bed, close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.
Snuggle close and sleep up tight,
Elephant, elephant, sleep tonight.

rhymes.title: The Little Trunk
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, so sweet,
Walking on your giant feet.
Swishing your long tail around,
Making such a happy sound.

Take your trunk and take a sip,
Take a little water dip.
Splash it high up in the air,
Sprinkling droplets everywhere.

Find your mommy, give a hug,
Snuggle like a little bug.
Walk along the jungle track,
Riding safely on her back.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy jungle bed.
Close your eyes and softly sigh,
Little elephant, lullaby.

rhymes.title: Peanut the Elephant
rhymes.text:
Peanut is a happy friend,
Loving fun that has no end.
Gray and cute from head to toe,
Watch the little baby go.

Makes a trumpet sound so loud,
Making all the jungle proud.
Trotting through the muddy clay,
Having such a joyful day.

Waves his ears just like a fan,
Catching peanuts in a can.
Smiles for everyone he meets,
Eating yummy jungle treats.

Stars are shining in the deep,
Elephant is going to sleep.
Dreaming of the morning sun,
When the day is new and done.

rhymes.title: The Little Grey Elephant
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and grey,
Marching through the grass today.
Swishing trunk from side to side,
Taking bugs for a little ride.

Flapping ears go flap, flap, flap,
Time to take a sleepy nap.
Big round feet go stomp, stomp, stomp,
Walking to the muddy swamp.

Splish and splash in water deep,
While the little birdies sleep.
Spray the water in the air,
Droplets falling everywhere.

Now the sun begins to set,
Elephant is nice and wet.
Time to cuddle with his mom,
Sleeping safe and feeling calm.

rhymes.title: Stompy the Elephant
rhymes.text:
Stompy elephant, walking slow,
Watch him wag his tail just so.
He has got a trunk so long,
Singing out a happy song.

Eating leaves up in the trees,
Swaying softly in the breeze.
Crunching peanuts, oh so sweet,
With his big and dusty feet.

Can you stomp just like him now?
Marching with a loud bow-wow?
No, elephants go pa-woo-woo!
Making happy sounds for you.

Now the day is almost done,
Say goodbye to golden sun.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.

rhymes.title: Five Big Grey Feet
rhymes.text:
One, two, three, four, five grey toes,
Look at that long water hose!
Elephant drinks water down,
Walking all around the town.

Big fat tummy, round and sweet,
Happy from his head to feet.
Swinging trunk up to the sky,
Watching butterflies fly by.

Gray skin feels so warm and nice,
Eating blocks of cooling ice.
Friends are coming out to play,
On this sunny jungle day.

Time to rest his heavy head,
Crawling to his leafy bed.
Dreaming of a rainy day,
When he gets to splash and play.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching through the trees all day.
Stomp your foot and tap your toe,
See how fast and far you go.

Big floppy ears go flap, flap, flap,
Time to take a little nap.
Long gray trunk goes swoosh and spray,
Splashing water all the way.

Walk around the jungle tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a happy jungle ride.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Peanuts
rhymes.text:
Five little peanuts in a row,
Watch the baby elephant go.
He picks one up with his trunk so long,
Singing out a happy song.

Crunch and munch and chew them all,
Big and heavy, short and tall.
Four little peanuts left to eat,
Oh, what such a yummy treat.

Three little peanuts on the ground,
Looking all around the mound.
Two little peanuts sweet and brown,
Rolling softly rolling down.

One little peanut left to see,
Shared with monkey in the tree.
Belly full and happy now,
Bowing down a sleepy bow.

rhymes.title: Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Time to wash the dust away,
At the end of a happy day.
Walk into the river blue,
Just like big elephants do.

Fill your trunk with water cool,
Standing by the muddy pool.
Spray it high into the air,
Splashing droplets everywhere.

Wash your tummy, wash your toes,
Wash the tip of your gray nose.
Rub your back against the stone,
 Happiest beast that is known.

Now the sun is shining bright,
Stars come out to say goodnight.
Cuddle close and sleep till morn,
Sweetest baby ever born.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Grey
rhymes.text:
Little elephant big and grey,
Likes to stomp and likes to play.
Stomping feet upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Long grey trunk to sniff and smell,
Swishing water very well.
Splishing splash in mud so deep,
Before it is time for sleep.

Big floppy ears flap to and fro,
Wiggling fast and wiggling slow.
Little tail goes swish and snap,
Ready for a cozy nap.

Good night trunk and good night feet,
Dream of peanuts fresh and sweet.
Stars are shining in the sky,
Little elephant, wave goodbye.

rhymes.title: Peanut Time
rhymes.text:
Elephant, elephant, look at you,
Wearing stockings made of blue.
Walking down the jungle trail,
Wiggling your little tail.

Time to eat a crunchy snack,
Sitting on your mama's back.
Peanuts yummy, peanuts round,
Dropping softly to the ground.

Use your trunk to pick them up,
Drinking water from a cup.
Munching happily away,
Having such a joyful day.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the jungle town.
Elephant, elephant, rest your head,
Time to crawl into your bed.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Mud
rhymes.text:
Up and down the river bend,
Elephant finds a little friend.
Splashing water in the air,
Droplets landing everywhere.

Muddy toes and muddy knees,
Tickling all the forest trees.
Laughing out a happy sound,
Rolling all around the ground.

Wash the mud off in the stream,
Watching stars begin to gleam.
Snuggling close in cozy night,
Holding mama very tight.

Morning comes with golden sun,
Ready for another run.
Elephant is brave and true,
We are very fond of you.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
See the elephant in the zoo,
Swinging trunk to say hello to you.
Big round ears that flap and play,
Stomping feet to start the day.
Walking slowly down the track,
With a baby on his back.
Gray and round from head to toe,
Watch the gentle giant go.
Munching leaves up in the tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Splashing water with a shout,
Water flying all about.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
Crawling to his grassy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Stomp, Stomp, Little Gray
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching down the path today.
Swish your trunk up in the air,
Show your lovely floppy pair.
Jump into the mud so deep,
Where the happy frogs can leap.
Wash it off with river spray,
Laughing through the sunny day.
Find a friend to share a hug,
Snuggling up against a bug.
Time to eat a sweet green leaf,
Chewing slowly, to our belief.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Dreaming dreams of jungle trees,
Swaying in the evening breeze.

rhymes.title: The Friendly Giant
rhymes.text:
Hear the trumpet loud and clear,
An elephant is drawing near.
Heavy feet go thump, thump, thump,
Over every little bump.
Big grey tummy, round and wide,
With a little bird inside.
Swishing tail from side to side,
Ready for a jungle ride.
Reaching for a yummy snack,
Hopping on a turtle's back.
Blowing bubbles in the pool,
Keeping nice and fresh and cool.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying everybody goodnight.
Snoring softly, deep and low,
Off to dreamland he will go.

rhymes.title: Little Elephant Stomp
rhymes.text:
Little elephant, big and gray,
Marching down the path today.
Swing your trunk from side to side,
Take a happy jungle ride.

Big round ears that flap and blow,
Watch the little river flow.
Stomp your feet upon the floor,
Then let out a happy roar!

Grab a leaf of green and tall,
Catch a big red bouncy ball.
Time to play and time to run,
Elephant life is full of fun.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Peanuts
rhymes.text:
Five little peanuts in a shell,
Elephant Ellie knows them well.
She cracks them open one by one,
Eating peanuts is so much fun.

Crunch and munch and chew so sweet,
Peanuts are her favorite treat.
Now there are four left to share,
Floating softly in the air.

Three little peanuts in the dirt,
Not a single one is hurt.
Two little peanuts on the ground,
Looking all around the town.

One little peanut left to eat,
Making Ellie's tummy neat.
All the peanuts now are gone,
Time to stretch and yawn, yawn, yawn.

rhymes.title: Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Water splashing in the tub,
Time to give Ellie a scrub.
Use the soap and wash her toes,
Right down to her little nose.

Fill her trunk with water bright,
Spray it up into the light.
Splish and splash upon the floor,
Ellie always asks for more.

Scrub her back and wash her ears,
Wash away the soapy tears.
Wrap her in a towel so grand,
Softest towel in the land.

Now she is so clean and bright,
Ready for a cozy night.
Snuggle close and softly creep,
Little elephant goes to sleep.

stories.title: Leo's Golden Mane
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright and sunny jungle, lived a little lion named Leo. Leo was very happy, but he had one big question every single morning. He would look at his fluffy head in a puddle of water and ask, 'When will I get a big, beautiful golden mane like my papa?' Papa lion would always smile, give Leo a gentle nose bump, and say, 'Grow, little Leo, grow!' Every day, Leo tried his very best to grow his mane. He ate crunchy green leaves and sweet, juicy berries. He drank cool water from the sparkling river. He even stood in the warm sunshine and stretched up as high as his tiny paws could reach. 'Grow, mane, grow!' Leo would whisper to the wind. One morning, Leo woke up and yawned a big toddler yawn. 'Roar!' he practiced. He hopped out of his cozy grass bed and ran straight to the puddle to check his hair. To his big surprise, there was a tiny puff of golden fluff right around his head! It was not as big as Papa's yet, but it was sparkly, soft, and completely his own. Leo jumped up and down with pure joy. 'Look at me! Look at me!' he cheered, running through the jungle to show all his friends. Monkey clapped his hands, and Elephant trumpeted a happy tune. Leo learned that great things take a little bit of time, a lot of healthy snacks, and big daily doses of patience. From that day on, Leo wore his tiny golden puff with extra pride. He loved running fast, playing hide and seek in the tall grass, and watching his fluffy mane get just a tiny bit bigger every single week. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Leo curled up next to Papa. He touched his growing mane and smiled a sleepy smile. 'Good night, little mane,' he whispered. Papa wrapped a warm, protective paw around his little boy, and they both drifted off to sleep, dreaming sweet jungle dreams under the twinkling stars.

stories.title: Leo Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The sun was starting to hide behind the big green trees, and the jungle was getting very quiet. It was bedtime for little Leo the lion, but Leo did not want to go to sleep. He wanted to play! 'Just one more jump!' shouted Leo, leaping over a little yellow flower. Mama lion sat on a soft patch of moss and shook her head gently. 'It is time to rest your paws, my sweet little cub,' she said with a warm, comforting purr. Leo shook his head and scampered behind a large green fern. He was playing hide and seek with the moon. Mama stood up and walked over, scooping Leo into a big, cozy hug. She carried him back to their soft bed made of green leaves and sweet-smelling grass. 'Let us count the quiet things in the jungle,' Mama whispered softly into Leo's fuzzy ear. Leo blinked his big brown eyes and listened. 'One,' whispered Mama, 'the little blue bird is tucked under her wing.' Leo nodded. 'Two,' whispered Mama, 'the bouncy green frog is sitting still on his lily pad.' Leo yawned a giant lion yawn that made his jaw go wide. 'Three,' whispered Mama, 'the bright yellow stars are twinkling good night in the sky.' By the time Mama reached three, Leo's heavy eyelids were drooping down. His fast little paws were finally still. He snuggled deep into the soft grass bed and rested his head on Mama's warm furry paw. The jungle breeze blew softly through the trees, singing a gentle lullaby. Leo let out one last tiny, sleepy sigh. His adventures were over for today, but he knew the bright sun would bring a whole new set of fun games tomorrow. Mama licked the top of Leo's head softly. 'Sweet dreams, my brave little lion,' she cooed. Leo was fast asleep, dreaming of golden butterflies and warm sunny days.

stories.title: Leo's Lost Toy
stories.text: Leo the lion cub had a very special toy. It was a little wooden monkey that his papa had carved just for him. Leo loved his monkey more than anything in the whole wide world. He took it everywhere he went. He took it to the river, he took it to the berry bushes, and he even took it to naptime. But one sunny afternoon, something terrible happened. Leo reached down to hold his monkey, and it was gone! 'Oh no!' cried Leo, his lower lip trembling. 'My little monkey is lost!' Papa lion stopped chewing his grass and looked over at the sad little cub. 'Do not worry, Leo,' Papa said kindly. 'We will look together.' Off they went on a big jungle adventure to find the missing toy. First, they looked behind a big bumpy rock. No monkey there, just a friendly green lizard doing push-ups. Next, they looked under a big pile of dry brown leaves. No monkey there, just a family of wiggly red worms. Leo began to feel like he would never see his favorite toy again. He let out a little sniffle. Just then, a little chatter came from up above in the branches. It was cheeky little monkey! He was swinging through the trees, holding Leo's wooden toy in his tiny hand. 'Give it back, please!' called Leo politely. The cheeky monkey giggled and gently dropped the wooden toy right into Leo's open paws. 'Yay!' cheered Leo, jumping up and down with happiness. He hugged his wooden toy tight and thanked his tree-climbing friend. Papa lion smiled warmly and nuzzled Leo's cheek. Leo learned that when you lose something important, it helps to keep looking and never give up hope. With his favorite toy safe in his paws, Leo skipped all the way home, ready for his next big toddler adventure.

stories.title: Leo's Lost Golden Crown
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, little Leo the lion woke up with a big stretch. He gave a tiny yawn. Roar! Oh, wait. Today was a very special day. It was Leo's birthday, and he had a shiny golden crown to wear. But when Leo reached up to his fluffy mane, the crown was gone! Oh no! Where could it be? Leo looked under his cozy yellow pillow. No crown. He looked inside his big toy box filled with wooden blocks and bouncy balls. No crown there either! Leo started to feel a little sad. A birthday lion needs his crown! Just then, his best friend Mia the monkey swung down from a leafy tree. Do not worry, Leo, said Mia with a cheerful chatter. Let us look together! They searched behind the tall green grass. They peeked behind the big brown rocks. Flutter, flutter, went a blue butterfly. Chirp, chirp, went a yellow bird. Suddenly, Leo saw something shiny sparkling near the sparkling blue river. Look, Mia! Shouted Leo. He scampered over on his quick paws. There sat his golden crown, floating gently on a big green lily pad like a little boat! But how did it get there? A cheeky little frog hopped away, croaking a happy tune. He must have borrowed it for a boat ride! Leo reached out his paw and scooped up his crown. It was a little wet, but it was just as shiny as before. Leo shook the water drops away. Then, he placed the crown right on top of his fluffy head. Hooray! Cheered Mia, clapping her hands. Leo gave a happy, proud roar that sounded all the way across the sunny jungle. Roar! He was ready for his birthday party. All his animal friends gathered around to sing a joyful song. They shared sweet berries and played silly games. Leo smiled his biggest lion smile. Even though his crown went on a little water adventure, it was the best birthday ever. Leo patted his head to make sure the crown stayed put. It was safe and sound, right where it belonged.

stories.title: Leo Learns to Share
stories.text: Deep in the green and leafy jungle, a little lion named Leo had a brand new red ball. It was round, it was bouncy, and it was his absolute favorite toy in the whole wide world. Bounce, bounce, went the red ball as Leo played with it all by himself. Soon, his friend Sammy the bunny came hopping along. Hello, Leo! Said Sammy with a twitch of his nose.
