Leo trotted over to the muddy puddle to see his friends. There was Pip, the tiny brown mouse, and Zara, the bouncy baby zebra. 'Good morning, Leo!' squeaked Pip. 'Would you like to play hide and seek?' Leo loved hide and seek! He closed his eyes tight and began to count in a loud, proud lion voice. 'One, two, three, four, five!' While Leo was counting, Pip hid behind a big round rock, and Zara hid behind a tall green palm tree. Leo opened his golden eyes and swished his long tail. 'Ready or not, here I come!' he roared softly, so he wouldn't scare his friends. Leo tiptoed on his soft, padded paws. He looked behind a bush. No Pip. He looked under a pile of sweet-smelling yellow flowers. No Zara. Then, Leo heard a tiny giggle coming from behind the round rock. 'I hear you!' shouted Leo playfully. He bounded over and gave a happy little play-growl. 'Rawr! Found you, Pip!' Pip squeaked with delight and scampered onto Leo's fuzzy head. Next, they found Zara hiding by the tree, shaking her black and white stripes with joy. The three friends played together all morning long under the warm sun. They ran through the grass, rolled in the soft dirt, and chased each other until their little legs felt wonderfully tired. When the sun started to sink low in the sky, turning the clouds pink and orange, Leo felt a heavy sleepiness creep into his eyes. He gave one more giant yawn. 'Yaaaaawn!' said Leo. His mommy lion walked over and wrapped her big, warm tail around him like a cozy blanket. Leo snuggled close against her soft fur. He closed his eyes, dreaming of golden sunbeams, friendly butterflies, and games of hide and seek with his best friends. 'Goodnight, sweet Leo,' whispered Mommy. And little Leo slept safe and sound until the morning sun woke him up again for another wonderful day.

stories.title: Leo's Golden Crown
stories.text: Deep in the green jungle, where the tall trees tickled the clouds, lived Leo the lion cub. Leo was very special because he was learning how to be a brave king of the jungle just like his daddy. But today, Leo was not feeling very brave at all. He had lost his favorite yellow leaf crown, and without it, he was sure he wasn't a real king. 'Oh dear,' sighed Leo, letting out a soft, sad sigh that blew a dandelion puff across the path. Just then, his good friend Maya the little monkey swung down from a vine, hanging upside down right in front of his nose. 'Why so sad, little lion friend?' asked Maya, blinking her big brown eyes. 'I lost my special king crown, and now I don't feel brave,' mumbled Leo, looking down at his paws. Maya scratched her furry head and chattered happily. 'Don't worry, Leo! A true king doesn't need a leaf crown. A true king has courage right inside his heart!' Leo blinked. He put one paw on his fuzzy chest. 'Right here?' he asked. 'Right there!' cheered Maya. To help Leo feel brave, Maya invited him on a special royal quest to find the shiniest treasure in the jungle. Off they went! They tip-toed past the busy ant hill, marching one by one. They tiptoed around the sleeping crocodile, making sure not to make a single sound. 'Shh,' whispered Leo, pressing a paw to his mouth. Finally, they reached the sparkling blue waterfall at the edge of the jungle. Sunlight danced on the water, making it glitter like gold. 'Look!' shouted Maya, pointing to the very edge of the water. There, resting on a flat green lily pad, was a smooth, shiny yellow pebble that looked just like a crown jewel! Leo’s eyes widened with excitement. He reached out a careful paw and scooped up the shiny pebble. It felt cool and smooth in his soft paw. 'I found the jungle treasure!' cheered Leo, holding the pebble high up into the air. He felt a warm, bubbly feeling of courage spread all the way from his tummy to the tip of his fluffy tail. He didn't need a leaf crown after all. He had his kind friend, his clever paws, and a brave, happy heart. With a joyful leap, Leo put the shiny pebble safely behind his ear and ran back home to show his mommy and daddy. 'You really are our brave little king,' purred his daddy, nuzzling Leo's soft golden head. Leo smiled a big, toothy lion smile, ready for whatever wonderful adventures tomorrow would bring.

stories.title: Leo's Morning Roar
stories.text: The morning sun was just waking up, painting the sky with lovely shades of pink, purple, and gold. In a cozy den beneath a big shady tree, little lion cub Leo opened one sleepy eye. Then, he opened his other sleepy eye. He gave his furry tummy a little scratch and wiggled his toes. Today was a very important day because Leo was going to practice his big lion roar! He stood up tall on his four stubby legs, shook his fluffy golden mane, and took a huge, deep breath of the fresh morning air. 'Are you ready?' asked a little red bird sitting on a branch above him. Leo nodded bravely. He opened his mouth as wide as it could possibly go. He pulled back his lips and puffed out his chest. Then, he let it rip! But instead of a scary, mighty sound, all that came out was a tiny, squeaky little noise. 'Squeak!' Leo stopped and looked down at his paws, feeling a little bit silly. The red bird tilted her head and giggled. 'That sounded more like a happy mouse than a big brave lion!' Leo giggled too. He knew that practicing takes time, just like learning how to jump or how to chase his bouncy ball. He decided to try again. He took an even bigger breath, filling his tummy up with air until he looked like a fuzzy yellow balloon. He stomped one little foot on the soft grass for extra power. 'ROAR!' went Leo. Well, it was more of a medium-sized roar, but it was much better than before! A few yellow butterflies fluttered up into the air in surprise, dancing around his head. Leo clapped his paws together in delight. 'Did you hear that?' he asked the red bird. 'I am getting louder!' Just then, a deep, rumbling voice echoed across the sunny field. It was Daddy Lion, letting out a magnificent, window-rattling roar that shook the dew drops right off the leaves. 'BOOM! ROAR!' went Daddy. Leo looked up at his giant daddy with wide, starry eyes. Someday, he would have a roar just as loud and strong as that. But for now, his little medium roar was just right for a little lion. Leo opened his mouth once more and gave a happy little practice roar to the morning sky. Then, with a joyful bounce, he scampered off to find his breakfast, ready to explore the big, beautiful world waiting just outside his door.

stories.title: Leo's Golden Mane
stories.text: Once upon a sunny time, in the big green grass of the jungle, lived a little lion cub named Leo. Leo had big paws, a wet black nose, and the softest, fluffiest golden fur you ever did see. Every single morning, Leo would wake up, stretch his front legs way out, and give a big, happy yawn. Roar! Well, it sounded more like a tiny squeak, but Leo thought it was very fierce. Today was a very special day because Leo was going on a big adventure to find his morning sunshine. He trotted along the dirt path, patter-pat, patter-pat, using his little paws. Along the way, he met his friend Sammy the Squirrel. Hello, Sammy! said Leo. Good morning, little lion, chattered Sammy, dropping a crunchy acorn. Leo sniffed the acorn and gave a happy little wag of his tail. Then, he kept on walking until he reached the sparkly blue river. Splish, splash went the cool water against the smooth stones. Leo leaned down to take a little drink, lap, lap, lap, with his pink tongue. Looking down into the water, Leo saw a fluffy yellow cloud reflecting back at him. He patted the water with his paw, creating lots of happy ripples. Oh look, giggled Leo, I caught the sunshine in the water! A gentle breeze blew through the tall green trees, making the leaves dance a happy green dance. Leo felt so warm and cozy. He sat right down on the soft green moss and curled his tail neatly around his toes. Being a little lion cub was the best job in the whole wide world. The sun climbed higher and higher in the bright blue sky, wrapping the jungle in a warm, golden hug. Leo let out one more sleepy little yawn. It was time for a nice, long nap in the shade of the big banana tree. He closed his eyes, listening to the buzzing of the friendly bumblebees and the soft whispering wind. Goodnight, jungle, whispered Leo as he drifted off to dreamland, knowing tomorrow would bring a whole new day of fun and games.

stories.title: Leo Learns to Roar
stories.text: Deep in the warm and cozy grasslands, a little lion named Leo was practicing his very best roars. His mama told him that big lions have big voices that can shake the tallest trees. Leo wanted to be just like his mama, strong and brave and loud. He puffed out his little furry chest and opened his mouth as wide as it could possibly go. He pushed out all the air from his tummy and shouted with all his might. Squeak! went Leo. That did not sound like a big lion at all. It sounded more like a tiny mouse saying hello. Leo sat down in the yellow grass and looked very confused. He patted his tummy and tried again. Squeak-squeak! went his little voice. His friend Ellie the Elephant walked by, swinging her long grey trunk from side to side. Hello there, little Leo, trumpeted Ellie gently. Why are you making such funny little noises? I am trying to make a big lion roar, pouted Leo, but it only sounds like a tiny mouse. Ellie smiled warmly with her kind brown eyes. Every big sound starts with a little practice, she said kindly. Why don't you try taking a deep breath of the sweet flower air, and then let it out together? Leo thought that sounded like a wonderful idea. He took a big, deep sniff of the bright red flowers growing near the path. Sniff, sniff, ahhh. Then, he opened his mouth and roared his very best roar. Roar-roar! It was still a little bit squeaky, but it was louder than before. Ellie clapped her big ears together with joy. Hooray for Leo! she trumpeted happily. Leo giggled and felt very proud of his growing voice. He practiced a few more times, marching proudly down the path with his head held high. Even the butterflies danced around him in celebration. Leo knew that with a little time and a lot of practice, his big lion roar would fill the whole jungle with happiness and cheer.

stories.title: Leo's Sleepy Starry Night
stories.text: The golden sun was beginning to sink low behind the distant purple hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. Little Leo the lion cub was getting very, very sleepy. His little eyelids felt as heavy as big stones, and his paws just wanted to rest. Mama Lion walked over and nudged him gently with her warm nose. Time to find our cozy sleeping spot, little one, she purred softly. Leo gave a big, jaw-stretching yawn and rubbed his eyes with his paw. Okay, Mama, he whispered, leaning against her soft furry side. They walked together through the darkening grass, patter-pat, patter-pat, looking for the best bed under the sky. Fireflies began to blink on and off in the shadows, glowing like tiny yellow stars floating in the air. Look, Mama, twinkling bugs! pointed Leo with his little paw. The fireflies danced in a circle, lighting the way to a soft bed of velvety green moss. Leo curled up tight into a warm, furry little ball. Mama Lion wrapped her long tail around him to keep him safe and cozy. Above them, the night sky turned a deep, velvety blue, dotted with a million sparkling diamonds. The moon looked down with a gentle, glowing smile. Leo closed his eyes and listened to the soothing lullaby of the nighttime crickets chirping outside. Chirp, chirp, went the crickets, singing a sweet song of rest. Leo felt so safe, so warm, and so deeply loved. He let out one final, tiny sigh of pure contentment as he drifted off to sleep. Goodnight, bright stars. Goodnight, glowing moon. Goodnight, little Leo, whispered the wind through the trees. The jungle rested quietly in the dark, cradling the sleeping cub in peace until the morning light would wake him up to play all over again.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Roar
rhymes.text:
Little lion, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Time to play and time to run,
Basking in the golden sun.

Open up your mouth so wide,
Show the teeth you keep inside.
Let out now a mighty sound,
Shake the happy jungle ground.

Roar a little, loud and clear,
Let the forest creatures hear.
You are brave and you are bold,
With a mane of shining gold.

Now the playtime day is done,
Down has gone the yellow sun..
Time to sleep and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Paws
rhymes.text:
One little paw makes a happy bound,
Two little paws pat the jungle ground.
Three little paws jump up in the air,
Four little paws chase a teddy bear.

Five little paws give a giant stretch,
Catching every little thing they fetch.
Little lion cub, so full of grace,
Running all around this happy place.

See him leap and see him prance,
Doing happy little jungle dance.
Stopping now to take a little rest,
Cuddling with the one he loves the best.

Mama lion holds him close and tight,
Kissing him and wishing him good night.
Sleep until the morning light appears,
Banish all your little toddler fears.

rhymes.title: Golden King
rhymes.text:
Golden lion, furry friend,
Playing games that never end.
Chasing butterflies of blue,
Tell me, lion, what do you do?

I can climb a little tree,
Look how very strong I be.
I can swim across the stream,
While the little fishes gleam.

Now I want a little snack,
Sitting on my furry back.
Eating berries sweet and red,
Getting ready for my bed.

Yawning wide and closing eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Dreaming of the jungle tall,
Sleeping softly through it all.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Roar
rhymes.text:
Little lion, soft and sweet,
Stomping with your furry feet.
Walking through the golden grass,
Watch the happy jungle pass.

Time to give a little roar,
Not too loud, just one and four.
Roar, roar, hear the sound,
Jumping high up off the ground.

Now it is time to take a rest,
Sleeping is what you do best.
Curled up tight beneath the tree,
As happy as a cub can be.

Close your eyes and softly sigh,
While the stars shine in the sky.
Dreaming of the sunny day,
When you wake to run and play.

rhymes.title: The Brave Little King
rhymes.text:
Golden mane upon your head,
Time to jump right out of bed.
Stretch your arms up to the sky,
Wave a friendly butterfly.

You are brave and you are bold,
With a heart of shiny gold.
Walking down the jungle trail,
Wagging your long furry tail.

Roar a happy morning song,
All your friends will sing along.h
Monkey swings up in the tree,
Happy as a cub can be.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little cubs to go.
Snuggle in your cozy bed,
Sleepy lion, rest your head.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Grass
rhymes.text:
Soft brown paws upon the ground,
Looking all around, around.
What is hiding in the tree?
Come and look along with me.

Butterfly goes flying by,
Dancing in the open sky.
Little lion wants to play,
Chasing troubles far away.

Jump up high and catch the air,
Spinning in a circle there.
Tired paws begin to creep,
Lion falls right fast asleep.

Moon is shining bright and clear,
Morning sun will soon appear.
Sweet little dreams for you tonight,
Sleeping till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Roar
rhymes.text:
Little lion in the sun,
Time to play and time for fun.
Shake your mane and stamp your feet,
Find a friend you love to meet.

Open up your mouth so wide,
Keep your happy heart inside.
Let out just a little squeak,
That is what the babies speak.

Prancing through the tall green grass,
Watch the yellow butterflies pass.
Jump up high and touch the sky,
Wave a happy wave goodbye.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in our jungle town.
Curl up tight and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden lion, furry tail,
Sailing on a grassy sail.
Paws so soft and whiskers bright,
Shining in the morning light.

Walking by the river stream,
Floating in a happy dream.
See the water splash and play,
Happy lion all the day.

Roar a little, purr a lot,
Resting in a shady spot.
Mama hugs you close and tight,
Kissing you a sweet goodnight.

Stars are twinkling up above,
Filled with family time and love.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: King of the Jungle
rhymes.text:
Little lion, strong and brave,
Walking from your cozy cave.
Clap your paws and count to three,
Climb up on a wooden tree.

Monkey swings up in the air,
Lion watches from his chair.
Zebra runs across the floor,
Lion gives a friendly roar.

Playing games of hide and seek,
Playing all through every week.
Jumping high and running fast,
Having so much fun at last.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little lion falls asleep.
Rest your head and quiet sigh,
While the moon goes sailing by.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Wake Up Now
rhymes.text:
Little lion, wake up now,
Stretch your paws and show me how.
Sun is shining in the sky,
Little birds are flying high.
Golden mane is soft and bright,
Ready for the morning light.
Walk across the grassy floor,
Time to give a happy roar.
Little cub, you look so sweet,
Running on your tiny feet.
Chase a butterfly today,
Come along and time to play.
Mana lion is close behind,
Gentle, loving, warm, and kind.
Snuggle down when day is done,
You're our little golden sun.

rhymes.title: Five Little Lions
rhymes.text:
Five little lions jumping in the grass,
Watching all the fuzzy bunnies pass.
One little lion said let us run,
Playing underneath the golden sun.
Two little lions pounce upon a tree,
Swishing tails so happy and so free.
Three little lions let out a roar,
Playing games upon the jungle floor.
Four little lions drink the river sweet,
Cooling down their furry little feet.
Five little lions curl up in a heap,
Closing up their eyes and going to sleep.
Dreaming of the stars up in the night,
Sleeping soundly till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Roar Goes the Lion
rhymes.text:
Roar goes the lion, big and tall,
Playing with a shiny yellow ball.
Paws are soft and steps are light,
Fur is golden, warm, and bright.
Sitting on a cozy jungle rock,
Listening to the ticking of a clock.
Time for dinner, time for rest,
Being with your family is best.
Mommy hugs you safe and tight,
Kissing you a fond goodnight.
Close your eyes and count to three,
Dreaming by the jungle tree.
Stars are twinkling in the blue,
Little lion, we all love you.
Sleep until the morning ray,
Ready for another happy day.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Wake Up
rhymes.text:
Little lion, wake up now,
Shake your mane and say meow.
Stretch your paws up to the sky,
Watch the fluffy cloud go by.

Time to run and time to play,
In the grass so green today.
Prance around and stomp your feet,
Life is happy, life is sweet.

Swish your tail from left to right,
Underneath the morning light.
Find a friend to chase and run,
Having so much happy fun.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little cubs to go.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
See the lion in the sun,
Ready for some jumping fun.
Golden fur and whiskers bright,
Running in the morning light.

Little cub with paws so small,
Walking near the garden wall.
Let us hear your happy sound,
Jumping softly on the ground.

Roar a little, mighty roar,
Not too loud, just like before.
Time to wiggle, time to shake,
Just for goodness, goodness sake.

Now the day is almost done,
Say goodbye to golden sun.
Time for bed and cozy rest,
Sleeping is what lions do best.

rhymes.title: The Golden King
rhymes.text:
Little king with golden hair,
Sitting in your cozy chair.
Though your chair is made of grass,
Watch the butterflies fly past.

Tap your toes and count to four,
Let out such a tiny roar.
Friends are coming down the lane,
Dancing in the gentle rain.

Elephants and zebras too,
Want to come and play with you.
Splashing in the water spray,
Laughing through the sunny day.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Crawling to your cozy bed.
Dreaming of the jungle green,
Sweetest sleep you've ever seen.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
Little lion in the sun,
Running, jumping, having fun.
Soft and furry, big and bold,
With a mane of yellow gold.

See him leap up in the air,
With a fuzzy, friendly stare.
Now he gives a little bound,
Landing softly on the ground.

Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.
Close your eyes and count to three,
As happy as a cub can be.

Dreaming in the golden light,
Sleeping softly through the night.
Morning comes with sunny skies,
Lion opens up his eyes.

rhymes.title: The Brave Little Cub
rhymes.text:
Hear the little lion roar,
Louder than he did before.
Walking through the jungle grass,
Watching butterflies float past.

Stomping with his tiny feet,
Looking for a tasty treat.
Mama lion stays close by,
Watching as the clouds go by.

Swishing tails and happy smiles,
Walking many happy miles.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little cubs to go.

Snuggling in the den so deep,
Lion falls fast down to sleep.
Rest your paws and quiet head,
Safe inside your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden mane upon his head,
Jumping on his grassy bed.
Roaring softly, just for play,
Happy through the sunny day.

Chasing bugs of yellow hue,
Underneath the sky so blue.
Now he stops to take a rest,
Snuggling up is what is best.

Wrap around him, gentle breeze,
Whispering among the trees.
Close your eyes and breathe in slow,
Now the sleepy stars will glow.

Little lion, safe and sound,
Bestest friend that can be found.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Lion cub, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: The Little Lion King
rhymes.text:
Little lion in the sun,
Running fast and having fun.
Golden fur and whiskers bright,
Playing until the morning light.

He lets out a little squeak,
Playing hide and gentle seek.
Stomping with his fuzzy feet,
Walking down the jungle street.

Climbing up a little mound,
Looking all around the ground.
Chasing butterflies so high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground. 
Rest your head and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion, Roar
rhymes.text:
Paws so soft and tail so long,
Singing out a happy song.
Little lion, bold and brave,
Living in a shady cave.

Time to practice how to roar,
Louder than the waves on shore.
Open up your mouth so wide,
Feel the courage deep inside.

Roar aloud for all to hear,
Bringing all your jungle dear.
Monkeys chatter, birds will sing,
Hello to the jungle king!

Now the roaring day is done,
Time to rest away the sun.
Snuggled tight in Mama's arm,
Safe and cozy, safe from harm.

rhymes.title: Leo's Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Little lion wants a mane,
Waiting out the golden rain.
Looking in the shiny pool,
Water nice and clear and cool.

Is it big and is it grand?
Bestest mane in all the land?
Not quite yet, you are too small,
Growing big and very tall.

Flutter, flutter, oh what's that?
On top of your little hat?
A yellow butterfly so sweet,
Landing right upon your feet.

Now you have a furry crown,
Walking all around the town.
Happy lion, full of glee,
Happy as a bird can be.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Little lion in the sun,
Running, jumping, having fun.
Soft paws touching on the ground,
Looking all around, around.

Time to chase a butterfly,
Flitting softly in the sky.
Little lion stops to play,
Smiling all the livelong day.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the grassy town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your warm and cozy bed.

Goodnight, lion, time to rest,
With your mama, you are blest.
Dream of magic, dream of sheep,
Now it's time to fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Hear the little lion roar,
Louder than he did before.
Showing off his tiny teeth,
With a happy heart beneath.

Stomping feet go thump, thump, thump,
Over every grassy bump.
Swishing tail from left to right,
Everything is shining bright.

Time to find a shady tree,
Sitting happy as can be.
Drinking water cool and clear,
Knowing that his friends are near.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Rocking gently to and fro.
Little lion nods his head,
Climbing into cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden fur and fuzzy toes,
Sunshine glowing on his nose.
Little lion wants to play,
All throughout the happy day.

Leaping high into the air,
Playing games without a care.
Chasing bugs of yellow hue,
Underneath the sky so blue.

When the afternoon is done,
Saying goodbye to the sun.
Snuggled close in furry paws,
Safe beneath the jungle laws.

Moonlight shines upon his face,
In this warm and quiet place.
Dreaming sweet and dreaming deep,
Little lion falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
Little lion walks around,
Stomping softly on the ground.
Golden fur and whiskers sweet,
Happy paws upon his feet.

See him leap and see him run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Now he gives a tiny roar,
Then he rests upon the floor.

Closes up his sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Dreaming of a jungle tree,
As happy as a cub can be.

Time to rest his furry head,
Snug inside his cozy bed.
Good night, lion, sleep until
Morning wakes the sleepy hill.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Little lion, strong and bold,
With a coat of yellow gold.
Time to wake and time to play,
Greeting all the brand new day.

Can you give a little roar?
Stomping softly on the floor?
Shake your tail and blink your eyes,
Look up at the morning skies.

Jump up high and leap around,
Making happy jumping sound.
Chasing butterflies in glee,
Running to the jungle tree.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Lion sleeping in his nest.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
Golden lion in the grass,
Watching butterflies that pass.
He has spots upon his face,
Running in a happy race.

Big brown eyes and furry ears,
Chasing all his little fears.
Wants a mane so big and tall,
Biggest lion of them all.

Papa lion comes along,
Singing out a happy song.
Lifts the baby in the air,
Showing love beyond compare.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Lullaby is floating by.
Little lion goes to sleep,
While the moon begins to peep.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
See the little lion run,
Playing underneath the sun.
He has golden fur so bright,
Running till the fading light.

Softly steps upon the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Then he lets out little cries,
Blinking with his sleepy eyes.

Time to rest his fuzzy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.
Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Swaying in the gentle breeze.

Goodnight, lion, time to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.
Close your eyes and slumber deep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Little lion, big and bold,
Made of sunshine and of gold.
Can you give a mighty roar,
Like you've never done before?

Open up your mouth so wide,
Show the courage deep inside.
Let a little rumble out,
Twirling softly round about.

Not a roar that scares the sheep,
Just a sound before you sleep.
Purring softly on the floor,
Now you do not roar no more.

Snuggle close and hug me tight,
Sleep until the morning light.
Dreaming happy dreams all day,
While the butterflies all play.

rhymes.title: King of the Grass
rhymes.text:
Golden king upon the grass,
Watch the fluffy bunnies pass.
He has whiskers on his face,
Running in a happy race.

Wags his tail from side to side,
Walking with a bouncy stride.
Leaping over little stones,
Far away from kingly thrones.

Now he stops to take a rest,
Cuddling is what he likes best.
In the middle of his pack,
Sleeping on his fuzzy back.

Sun is sinking in the west,
Lion resting with the rest.
Stars are shining up above,
Filled with family and with love.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Roar!
rhymes.text:
Little lion, furry mane,
Playing in the sunny lane.
Open up your mouth so wide,
Show the happy cub inside.

Stomp your paws upon the floor,
Let me hear your little roar!
Not too loud and not too deep,
Time to wake or go to sleep.

Now you curl up on the grass,
Watch the fluffy bunnies pass.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy lion bed.

Tomorrow is another day,
Full of sunshine, full of play.
Goodnight, lion, sleep so tight,
Sleeping softly through the night.

rhymes.title: The Golden Mane
rhymes.text:
See the lion walking by,
Underneath the big blue sky.
Golden fur and whiskers bright,
Running in the morning light.

He has spots upon his toes,
And a tickle on his nose.
Jumping over sticks and stones,
King of all the happy zones.

When he runs, he likes to race,
With a smile upon his face.
Chasing butterflies around,
Spinning circles on the ground.

Now the sun begins to set,
Lion is a sleepy pet.
Yawns a big and sleepy yawn,
Waiting for the happy dawn.

rhymes.title: Five Little Cubs
rhymes.text:
Five little lion cubs playing in the sun,
First little lion says, oh this is fun!
Second little lion wiggles his cute tail,
Third little lion chases after a snail.

Fourth little lion gives a mighty squeak,
Fifth little lion loves to play hide and seek.
Running through the grass so green,
Best little lions ever seen.

Soon the afternoon is through,
Mommy lion calls for you.
Time to wash your furry face,
Snuggled in a cozy place.

Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your warm and sleepy bed.
Dreaming of the golden sun,
Now the sleepy night has won.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
Little lion walks around,
Softly stepping on the ground.
Golden fur and happy face,
Running in a sunny place.

Wiggle ears and twitch your nose,
From your head down to your toes.
Time to play and time to run,
Having lots of jungle fun.

See him jump and see him spring,
Happy like a little king.
Now he stops to take a rest,
Curled up in his cozy nest.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Little lion, sleep tight, tight.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion, Roar
rhymes.text:
Little lion wakes up bright,
Stretching in the morning light.
Yawning wide with fuzzy jaws,
Scratching with his tiny paws.

Time to find a leafy tree,
Where the happy monkeys be.
Give a friendly little sound,
Jumping softly on the ground.

Shake your mane from side to side,
Running with a joyful stride.
Happy lion, brave and sweet,
Dancing with your furry feet.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the grassy town.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Tucked into your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: The Golden King
rhymes.text:
In the grass so green and tall,
Lived a lion, cute and small.
With a mane of golden hair,
Happiest cub everywhere.

Stomping feet and swishing tail,
Walking down the dusty trail.
Saying hello to his friends,
Where the sunny pathway ends.

Chasing butterflies in flight,
Running till the afternoon light.
Making every creature smile,
Resting for a little while.

Stars are peeking from above,
Filled with sleepy peace and love.
Close your eyes and softly purr,
Snuggling in your golden fur.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
Little lion walking slow,
Where do you want to go?
Across the grass so green and bright,
Running in the golden light.

Little lion, give a roar,
Louder than you did before!
Not too loud to make us scare,
Just a happy little bear.

Little lion, shake your mane,
Dancing in the summer rain.
Jump up high and touch the sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.

Now it is time to take a rest,
Sleeping is what you do best.
Curl up tight upon the floor,
Little lion, no more roar.

rhymes.title: Golden King
rhymes.text:
See the lion in the sun,
Having lots of outdoor fun.
With a furry golden coat,
And a happy little note.

He has got a fluffy tail,
Walking down the grassy trail.
Looking for a friend to play,
All throughout the sunny day.

Monkey swings up in the tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Elephant says look at me,
Splashing by the water sea.

Now the sun is going down,
Little lion wears his crown.
Time to sleep and close his eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Roar, Lion, Roar
rhymes.text:
Roar, lion, roar today,
While we come outside to play.
Stomp your paws upon the ground,
Make a happy little sound.

Chase the butterflies around,
Where the yellow flowers are found.
Leap across the tiny stone,
In the jungle all your own.

Mommy lion calls your name,
Time to finish up the game.
Snuggle close and drink your milk,
Soft as any piece of silk.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Wait until another day.
Sweetest dreams to you, my dear,
Glad that you are resting here.

rhymes.title: Little Lion Paws
rhymes.text:
Little lion walking round,
Softly steps upon the ground.
Golden mane so soft and bright,
Running in the morning light.

See him leap and see him run,
Playing underneath the sun.
He lets out a happy squeak,
Playing hide and seek all week.

When the stars begin to glow,
To his cozy bed he'll go.
Crouching down to take a rest,
Lion naps are quite the best.

Close your eyes and drift away,
Dreaming of another day.
Soft and sweet the breezes blow,
Sleep, my little lion, go.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Hear the little lion roar,
Louder than he did before!
Stretching out his fuzzy toes,
Wiggling his pink button nose.

Jumping over sticks and stones,
Far away from furry homes.
Catching butterflies in flight,
Dancing in the golden light.

Time to stop and time to eat,
Finding something good and sweet.
Drinking water from the brook,
Looking in every cozy nook.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Whispering in the evening breeze.

rhymes.title: The Golden King
rhymes.text:
Golden fur and whiskered face,
Walking with a royal grace.
Little lion is so sweet,
Running on his nimble feet.

Waving hello to a bird,
Listening to every word.
Bouncing up and bouncing down,
Wearing leafy greenest crown.

Happy smiles upon his face,
In this sunny, lovely place.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Snuggling is the very best.

Moonlight shines upon his head,
Tucked into a grassy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
Dreams of jungle joys to keep.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Wake Up
rhymes.text:
Little lion in the sun,
Time to wake up and have some fun.
Stretch your paws up to the sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.

Fuzzy ears and golden hair,
Running here and running there.
Make a happy little sound,
Hopping softly on the ground.

Now it is time to find a tree,
Climb up high and look at me.
Give a friendly little roar,
Then you can go play some more.

Sun is sinking in the west,
Time for little cats to rest.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.

rhymes.title: The Brave Little Cub
rhymes.text:
See the lion walking by,
Underneath the big blue sky.
With a golden furry coat,
And a happy little note.

Walking through the yellow grass,
Watch the funny monkeys pass.
Give a friendly little wave,
Little lion is so brave.

Chasing butterflies of blue,
Wondering what he can do.
Pouncing on a fallen leaf,
Bringing happiness and grief.

Time to cuddle with his mom,
Feeling cozy, safe, and calm.
Drifting off to dreamland deep,
Little lion falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion
rhymes.text:
Roar, little lion, roar so loud,
Make your mama very proud.
Show your teeth, but only play,
We will have a happy day.

Jump around and stomp your feet,
Jungle life is very sweet.
Run across the meadow green,
Best little cub ever seen.

Find a friend to chase and play,
Laugh and frolic all the day.
Drink some water from the stream,
Like a happy waking dream.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving us its gentle light.
Tuck your tail and curl up tight,
Say to everyone good night.

rhymes.title: The Little Lion Cub
rhymes.text:
See the little lion run,
Playing underneath the sun.
He has golden fur so bright,
Running till the evening light.

Now he lets out such a yawn,
Stretching softly on the lawn.
Time to rest his fuzzy head,
Climbing into cozy bed.

Mommy lion hugs him tight,
Kisses him and says goodnight.
Dreams of jungle fun are near,
Sleeping safely, do not fear.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little clouds go floating by.
Sleep until the morning ray,
Ready for another day.

rhymes.title: Leo's Loud Roar
rhymes.text:
Little lion takes a stand,
In the grassy, sunny land.
He wants to be fierce and bold,
Braver than the knights of old.

He opens up his mouth so wide,
Feeling proud and full of pride.
He lets out a little sound,
Jumping softly off the ground.

Squeak goes Leo with a grin,
Let the funny game begin!
Birds are laughing in the tree,
Happy as can ever be.

Try again, my little friend,
Happy moments without end.
Now a bigger roar comes out,
Making everyone shout!

rhymes.title: Paws in the Grass
rhymes.text:
Paws of velvet, soft and light,
Running in the morning bright.
Tails are swishing left and right,
Lion cubs are such a sight.

Chasing bugs of yellow gold,
Stories of the jungle told.
Climbing up a little mound,
Looking all around the ground.

Butterflies begin to play,
Dancing on this happy day.
Hide and seek is so much fun,
Playing underneath the sun.

Tired paws begin to creep,
Falling softly into sleep.
Dreaming of a sunny stream,
Sleeping like a little dream.

rhymes.title: Little Lion, Big Mane
rhymes.text:
Little lion walking by,
Looking at the sunny sky.
Golden fur and whiskers too,
Happy little friend to you.

Stretching out his paws so wide,
Walking with a happy stride.
Making friends along the way,
Ready for a fun-filled day.

See him jump and see him run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Now it is time for a nap,
Sleeping in a cozy lap.

Dreaming of the trees so tall,
Little lion, best of all.
Time to close your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Lion, Roar
rhymes.text:
Hear the little lion say,
I am going out to play!
Prancing through the grass so green,
Cutest cub you've ever seen.

He opens up his mouth so wide,
With his mama by his side.
Trying out a giant roar,
Louder than he did before.

Squeak goes he and then he tries,
Looking up with happy eyes.
Butterflies begin to dance,
Giving him another chance.

Now he lets out one more sound,
Jumping happily around.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: The Golden King
rhymes.text:
Lion king upon the rock,
Waiting for the morning clock.
Golden mane and shiny eyes,
Watching all the butterflies.

He lets out a happy sound,
Trotting all across the ground.
Splashing in the river blue,
Just like happy duckies do.

Sniffing flowers sweet and red,
Time to find a cozy bed.
Moon is shining bright and high,
Singing lullabies nearby.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Little lion, rest your head,
In your soft and mossy bed.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a very happy little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long curly tail, and a tummy that was always ready for yummy snacks. One sunny morning, Milo woke up and stretched his arms way, way up to the sky. Ooh-ooh! Ah-ah! he squeaked. It was time for breakfast! Milo scampered down his favorite tall tree, hopping from branch to branch. Swish, swoosh, went the leaves as he zoomed past. Suddenly, something bright yellow caught his eye resting right on a large green leaf. It was a banana! But this was not just any ordinary banana. It was the biggest, shiniest banana Milo had ever seen. As Milo reached out his little paw to touch it, the banana let out a little giggle. Tee-hee! Milo pulled his hand back in surprise. Did my snack just laugh? he wondered. He crept closer and gently tapped the banana again. It giggled louder and started to hop up and down! Boing, boing, boing! The magic banana hopped right off the leaf and bounced onto the soft moss. Milo clapped his hands with joy. A bouncing banana! This was going to be the best day ever. Milo chased the banana through the tall ferns. Ready, set, go! He ran as fast as his little legs could carry him. The banana rolled under a log. Milo ducked down low and crawled under. Quack, quack! went a little duck, surprised to see a monkey saying hello. Milo giggled and kept on chasing. The banana bounced over a sleepy turtle. Slow and steady, smiled the turtle as Milo zipped right on by. Up, up, up a small grassy hill rolled the magical yellow fruit. Milo scampered up right behind it. When they reached the very top, the banana stopped bouncing. It gave one final little spin and sat still in the warm grass. Milo sat down next to his new friend. He was a little bit tired, but his heart was full of happy bubbles. Can I eat you now? Milo asked politely. The banana gave a sweet little nod. So, Milo peeled back the bright yellow skin and took a big, delicious bite. Yum, yum, yum! It was the sweetest, tastiest banana in the whole wide world. Milo rubbed his full tummy and curled his long tail around a friendly tree branch. What a wonderful adventure. With a big yawn, little Milo closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of more magical snacks to come.

stories.title: Coco's Jungle Drums
stories.text: Deep in the whispering jungle, where the flowers bloomed in bright pinks and yellows, lived a playful monkey named Coco. Coco loved making music. Every single day, he would look for fun new sounds to share with all his animal friends. Today, Coco was on a very special mission. He wanted to find the best drumming beat in the whole forest! Ooh-ooh-ah-ah! shouted Coco as he swung through the trees, searching high and low. First, Coco stopped by a big hollow log resting near the sparkling river. He picked up two small, smooth sticks in his paws. Let us try this! he whispered to himself. Tap, tap, tap went the sticks against the old log. Boom, boom, boom! responded the log with a deep, happy sound. Coco danced a little jig on top of the log, shaking his fuzzy hips from side to side. But wait, Coco thought, can we make it louder? Suddenly, a fluffy parrot flew down from the canopy. Squawk! Let me help! The parrot started to clap its wings together. Flap, flap, flap! That sounded pretty good, but Coco knew the jungle had even more sounds to offer. He hopped off the log and scampered over to a bush filled with bright red berries. Shh, shh, shh, went the rustling leaves as Coco brushed past them. Then, he found a patch of hard, hollow bamboo stalks standing tall in the sunlight. Coco tapped the bamboo with his fingers. Clack, clack, clack! It sounded like little wooden castanets. A tiny green frog hopped onto a nearby rock and joined in the fun. Ribbit, ribbit! croaked the frog, keeping a steady rhythm. Now Coco had logs, leaves, bamboo, and a croaking frog choir! He climbed up to the highest branch so everyone could hear him. It was time for the grand jungle concert. Coco raised his paws high into the air. Ready, set, play! he cheered. Boom, boom went the log! Clack, clack went the bamboo! Flap, flap went the parrot's wings! Ribbit, ribbit went the happy little frog! All the animals in the jungle gathered around to listen and dance. Little monkeys twirled around the trees. Elephants stomped their feet to the beat. Giraffes swayed their long necks back and forth. The whole jungle was alive with music and laughter. Coco sat in the middle of it all with a giant smile stretched across his furry face. Making music with friends was the greatest thing in the world. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in shades of purple and orange, the music slowly grew softer. The animals let out happy sighs and curled up for the night. Coco whispered a quiet goodnight to his drums, hugged his fluffy tail, and drifted off to sleep to the gentle hum of the jungle.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Barnaby was a sweet little monkey with fuzzy brown ears and tiny toes that loved to wiggle. One sunny afternoon, while playing near the edge of the jungle, Barnaby found something amazing. Sitting right in the tall green grass was a big, bright red rubber ball! It was round like the sun and shiny like a polished apple. Wow! gasped Barnaby, his eyes growing as big as saucers. He walked up to the ball and gave it a gentle poke with his finger. Boing! The ball bounced away just a tiny bit. Barnaby giggled. He gave it a bigger nudge with his nose. Whee! The ball rolled across the clearing, stopping right near a sleepy butterfly. The butterfly fluttered its wings and flew up into the air as if inviting Barnaby to play. Barnaby clapped his paws together. He chased after the big red ball, running as fast as his little legs could go. Pat-pat-pat went his feet on the soft dirt. The ball rolled toward a shallow puddle of water left behind by yesterday's rain. Oh no! thought Barnaby. Balls don't like getting wet! But before he could grab it, the ball hit a small bump in the ground and bounced right over the puddle. Splash! Just a tiny drop of water flew into the air, making a cool little mist that sparkled in the sunlight. Barnaby laughed out loud. He leaped right over the puddle, soaring through the air like a tiny flying monkey. Land safely on the other side! Ta-da! He scooped up the big red ball in his arms and squeezed it tight. It was so light and bouncy. Barnaby decided to share his new treasure with his best friend, a playful little zebra named Zuzu, who lived nearby. Come play catch, Zuzu! called out Barnaby. Zuzu trotted over with black and white stripes gleaming in the sun. Ready? asked Barnaby. He threw the big red ball toward Zuzu. Zuzu gently bumped the ball back with her nose. Boing! The ball flew back to Barnaby. Catch! They spent the whole afternoon tossing the big red ball back and forth, laughing and playing until their legs felt tired. When the sky turned a pretty pink and orange, Barnaby gave the ball one final hug. It had been such a fun day full of bouncing and running. Holding his favorite red ball, Barnaby walked slowly back to his cozy tree home, ready for sweet dreams and tomorrow's brand new adventures.

stories.title: Milo's Morning Banana
stories.text: Once upon a bright and sunny morning, high up in the leafy green jungle, lived a very happy little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a long curly tail, and big sparkly eyes that loved to look for fun adventures. When Milo woke up, he stretched his arms up high. Big stretch! He scratched his fuzzy tummy. Scratch, scratch, scratch! Then, Milo sniffed the warm morning air. What was that delicious smell? It was his absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world: a bright yellow banana! Milo jumped right out of his cozy bed made of soft green leaves. Hop, hop, hop! He scampered down the thick brown trunk of his tall tree house. He used his strong hands and his wiggly, waggly tail to balance. Whee! Running along the jungle floor, Milo giggled as a little blue butterfly fluttered past his nose. Hello, butterfly! But Milo's tummy let out a loud rumble. Grumble, grumble, rumble! It was time for breakfast. He looked up, and there it was, hanging from the very top branch. A big, curved, yellow banana, smiling right back at him. Milo climbed up, hand over hand, foot over foot. Climb, climb, climb! He reached out his little furry paw. Got it! But wait, how do you open a banana? Milo remembered what his mama taught him. You pinch the top, and peel it down! One strip, two strips, three yellow strips. Ahh, perfect. Milo took a big, crunchy bite. Yum, yum, yum! It was sweet and soft and so delicious. He ate every single bite until his tummy was nice and full. Then, Milo wiped his mouth with his fuzzy hand, gave a happy little sigh, and curled up for a sunny morning nap. Good morning, Milo!

stories.title: Milo Plays Hide and Seek
stories.text: The sun was shining warmly down on the green jungle, and little Milo the monkey was ready to play a game. Today's game was his very favorite: hide and seek! Milo covered his big brown eyes with both of his paws. No peeking! He started to count in a squeaky, happy voice. One, two, three, four, five! Ready or not, here I come! Milo uncovered his eyes and looked around. Where would his jungle friends be hiding? He looked behind a big green leaf. Nobody there! He looked under a colorful flower. Just a sleepy little ladybug! Then, Milo heard a funny sound coming from the tall banana trees. Giggles! Tee-hee-hee! Milo tiptoed over on his soft little feet. Tap, tap, tap, went his toes. He peeked behind the thick green trunk, and guess who he saw? It was his best friend, Pip the parrot, trying to hide his bright red feathers with a tiny green leaf! I found you, Pip! shouted Milo, clapping his hands together with joy. Now it was Pip's turn to count, and Milo needed to find a really, really good hiding spot. Where could he go? Milo looked up. Ahh, perfect! He scrambled up the tall tree vines. Climb, climb, climb! He curled himself up into a little furry ball right behind a big bunch of bright yellow bananas. He stayed as quiet as a mouse. Shh! Pip flew around, looking high and low. Where is Milo? Pip wondered. Then, Pip looked up at the banana bunch and saw a long, curly tail hanging down and wiggling back and forth. Wag, wag, wag! I see your tail, Milo! Pip chirped happily. They both laughed and giggled together. Playing hide and seek in the sunny jungle was the most fun in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Milo's Big Swing
stories.text: It was a wonderful afternoon in the jungle, and a gentle breeze was blowing through the tall trees. Little Milo the monkey was sitting on a sturdy branch, kicking his legs back and forth. Swish, swash, swish! He looked up at the long, strong vines hanging all around him. Today, Milo decided, was going to be the day of the big swing! He reached out with his fuzzy paws and grabbed hold of a thick, leafy green vine. He gave it a little tug to make sure it was strong. Pull, pull, pull! It was super strong. Milo took a deep breath, lifted his feet right up off the safe branch, and pushed off into the warm open air. Wheeeee! Milo flew through the bright blue sky like a little brown bird. The warm wind tickled his furry face and made his big ears flap back. He soared past colorful flowers, buzzing bees, and fluffy white clouds. Look at me, mama! Milo called out happily as he zoomed by. Down, down, down he swung, and then up, up, up he went again on the other side. On the swing back, Milo stretched his arms out wide, pretending he was a super-monkey flying across the whole jungle. When the vine finally slowed down, Milo landed safely on a soft patch of moss with a gentle thud. Hop! His heart was beating fast, thumping against his chest. Thump, thump, thump! That was so much fun! Milo giggled and clapped his little hands together. He looked at the big vine, waiting for him to grab it again. Without wasting a single second, Milo ran back, grabbed the green vine tight, and shouted, Let's do it again! And away he flew into the sunny sky.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a long curly tail, and the biggest, brightest smile you ever did see. Milo loved to do two things more than anything else in the whole wide world: swing from branch to branch and eat sweet, yellow bananas. Every single morning, the sun would peek through the tall trees, saying good morning to the jungle. Milo would stretch his arms up high, yawn a big monkey yawn, and blink his sleepy eyes. 'Time for breakfast!' Milo would chatter happily. One sunny morning, Milo swung down to his favorite banana tree. But oh no! The tree was completely empty. Not a single banana was in sight. Milo scratched his furry head. Where did all the bananas go? Just then, he heard a funny sound coming from behind a large green leaf. Giggles! Hee-hee-hee! Milo crept closer on his soft little paws. He peeked behind the leaf and guess who he saw? It was his best friend, Pip the parrot! Pip was holding a bright, sparkly golden banana that shimmered in the morning light. 'Look, Milo!' squawked Pip. 'I found a magic banana!' Milo’s eyes went round as saucers. A magic banana? He had never seen anything so special. Pip handed the banana to Milo. As soon as Milo touched it, the banana started to giggle and wiggle right in his hands! 'Tee-hee!' giggled the banana. Milo laughed out loud. He had the best idea. Instead of eating the magic banana, Milo decided it would be much more fun to play with it. Milo and Pip played catch with the wiggle-banana. Up, up, up into the air went the banana! Down, down, down it tumbled into Milo’s furry paws. They played tag around the thick tree trunks, zooming fast like little superheroes. They spun in circles until they were so dizzy they both tumbled onto the soft, green moss with happy giggles. Suddenly, the magic banana stopped wiggling. It opened up its little banana peel and shared sweet, delicious slices with Milo and Pip. Yum, yum, yum! It was the most delicious breakfast Milo had ever tasted. As the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Milo curled up on his favorite branch. He wrapped his long, cozy tail around himself, closed his eyes, and dreamed sweet, happy dreams about his wonderful day with the magic banana.

stories.title: Coco's Big Red Balloon
stories.text: High up in the bouncy canopy of the bright green jungle lived a sweet little monkey named Coco. Coco had ears like big fluffy pancakes and fingers that loved to wiggle. Today was a very special day because it was Coco’s third birthday! All of his jungle animal friends gathered around to celebrate. Ellie the elephant trumpeted a loud, happy tune with her long trunk. Zazu the zebra stomped his hooves on the soft grass. And Leo the lion gave a gentle, friendly roar. 'Happy birthday, Coco!' they all cheered together. Then, Zazu stepped forward and handed Coco a wonderful surprise. It was a big, shiny, bright red balloon! The balloon bobbed up and down in the breeze, dancing just for Coco. Coco’s eyes sparkled with joy. He reached out and grabbed the white string tightly. 'Thank you!' chattered Coco happily. He loved his new balloon more than anything. Coco decided to take his red balloon on a grand adventure through the jungle. He walked down the winding dirt path, holding the string high in the air. The balloon floated right behind him like a loyal little friend. Suddenly, a playful breeze swooped down from the treetops. Whoosh! The wind caught the red balloon and lifted it higher into the air. 'Whee!' giggled Coco, as he leaped into the air to catch the string. He swung from a thick green vine, zooming through the air right beside his balloon. The balloon seemed to play a game of tag with him. Up it went over a tall fern bush, and down it swooped near a sparkling blue stream. Coco chased it with joyful leaps and bounds. But then, oh no! The wind blew a little too hard. The balloon floated higher and higher, way up toward the very top of the tallest coconut tree. Coco stopped and looked up. The balloon was getting farther away! Coco knew just what to do. Being a clever little monkey, he used his strong arms and legs to climb up the coconut tree, hand over hand, foot over foot. Up, up, up he went until he reached the very top branch. He stretched out his arm as far as it could possibly go. Tip-toe, stretch, reach! Success! Coco’s fingers closed safely around the white string. He gave it a gentle tug and pulled his precious red balloon back down. Coco hugged the big red balloon tight against his soft furry chest. He climbed back down the tree to his waiting friends. Together, they shared a big yummy birthday cake made of delicious sweet mangoes. Coco smiled a big, happy monkey smile, holding his favorite red balloon all through the evening until the twinkling stars came out to say goodnight.

stories.title: Barnaby's Busy Jungle Day
stories.text: Good morning, little jungle friends! Today we are going to follow a very busy little monkey named Barnaby. Barnaby had bright orange fur on his cheeks and a tail that could curl into the shape of a perfect letter 'O'. Barnaby woke up before the sun was even fully awake. He opened his big brown eyes, stretched his arms wide, and said, 'Today is going to be a wonderful day!' Barnaby lived in a tall, leafy mango tree right in the middle of the noisy, colorful jungle. First, Barnaby needed to brush his teeth. Of course, monkeys don't use a toothbrush. Instead, Barnaby chewed on a fresh, minty green leaf until his mouth felt nice and clean. Chomp, chomp, chomp! Next, it was time for morning exercises. Barnaby stood on one foot, just like a flamingo, and counted to three. One, two, three! Then he hopped up and down on the soft grass like a bouncy little bunny. Hop, hop, hop! After exercising, Barnaby’s tummy let out a loud rumble. Grrr-rumble! Time for breakfast. Barnaby scampered up his favorite tree to find something yummy to eat. He spotted three big, juicy red apples hanging from a branch. Barnaby reached out, picked the apples, and shared them with his neighbors, Sammy the squirrel and Bella the bluebird. Munch, munch, munch! Everyone was happy and full. With a full tummy, Barnaby decided to play hide-and-seek with his jungle friends. 'Ready or not, here I come!' called out Sammy the squirrel. Barnaby quickly scrambled behind a giant green fern leaf. He covered his eyes with his little paws so nobody could see him. Can you help Barnaby stay very, very quiet? Shh! Sammy looked behind a rock. He looked behind a tree trunk. But Barnaby was too clever! Finally, Sammy peeked behind the fern leaf and shouted, 'Found you, Barnaby!' Barnaby burst into a fit of happy monkey giggles. Tee-hee-hee! They played games all afternoon long, running through the warm sunshine and splashing in the cool puddles after a quick tropical rain shower. Splash, splash, splash! By the time the golden sun began to sink behind the distant mountains, Barnaby was very tired. His eyelids felt heavy, and his little paws felt sleepy. He climbed back up into his cozy nest of leaves in the tall mango tree. He curled up tight, closed his eyes, and listened to the gentle sounds of the jungle singing him a sweet lullaby. Goodnight, Barnaby. Goodnight, jungle.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long curly tail, and a very big tummy that loved to rumble. Every single morning, Milo would wake up with a huge yawn and a big stretch. Stretch up high to the sky, little Milo! Today was a very special day because Milo smelled something wonderful. Sniff, sniff, sniff went his little monkey nose. It smelled sweet, and yellow, and yummy. It smelled like a banana! Milo swung from branch to branch. Swish, swash, swoosh! He used his strong hands and his bouncy feet. He climbed up the tallest tree in the whole jungle. There, sitting right on top of a big green leaf, was the biggest, brightest banana Milo had ever seen. But wait! The banana was too high. How would Milo reach it? He thought and he thought. Then, Milo remembered his special monkey trick. He could jump! Milo bent his knees. One, two, three, jump! He leaped through the air and grabbed the banana with both hands. Hooray! Milo did a little happy dance. Cha-cha-cha, wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! He peeled the banana slowly. Peel, peel, peel. And then, he took a big bite. Munch, crunch, yummy! It was the sweetest banana in the whole wide world. Milo rubbed his happy tummy and smiled a big monkey smile. After such a busy morning, Milo felt very sleepy. He curled up in a cozy ball on a soft branch. He wrapped his long tail around himself like a warm blanket. Close your eyes, little Milo. Time for a little monkey nap. Good night, Milo. Sweet dreams in the jungle trees.

stories.title: Coco Counts Cocoanuts
stories.text: Hello, little friends! Today we are going on a fun counting adventure with Coco the monkey. Coco loved to play games, and his absolute favorite game was counting things he found in the sunny jungle. Are you ready to count with Coco? Let us go! First, Coco found one shiny red flower. Can you point to the flower? One! Coco clapped his hands. Yay! Then, Coco swung over to a big muddy puddle. Splash, splash, splash went his little monkey feet. Sitting right by the puddle were two buzzing bees. Let us count them together. One, two! Buzz, buzz, go the little bees. Coco giggled and covered his mouth. Tee-hee-hee! Next, Coco climbed up a friendly brown tree trunk. Looking up at the blue sky, he saw three fluffy white clouds floating softly by. Can you count the clouds with your fingers? One, two, three! They looked just like cotton candy up in the air. Coco kept climbing higher and higher until he reached the very top. Guess what he found waiting for him there? Cocoanuts! Let us count the round brown cocoanuts sitting in the nest. One, two, three, four! Four big cocoanuts ready for a game of catch. Coco picked up one cocoanut and rolled it gently. Roll, roll, roll! He clapped his hands because counting was so much fun. Four cocoanuts, three clouds, two bees, and one pretty flower. Coco felt like the smartest monkey in the whole jungle. He gave himself a big hug. Hug, hug, hug! Can you give yourself a big hug, just like Coco? Great job! Counting with Coco was the best fun ever. Now, the sun is beginning to set, painting the sky pink and orange. Coco waves goodbye to his animal friends. Wave, wave, wave, little monkey. Time to rest until our next counting adventure tomorrow.

stories.title: The Great Jungle Tickle
stories.text: It was a bright and sunny afternoon in the jungle, and Barnaby the monkey had a case of the giggles. Barnaby was a very playful monkey who loved to make his friends smile. Today, he had a funny idea. He wanted to play the biggest game of tickle tag ever! Barnaby leaped down from his favorite mango tree. Boing, boing, boing went the little monkey. He looked around to see who he could tickle first. There was Ellie the elephant, splashing water with her long gray trunk. Splish, splash, splosh! Barnaby tiptoed behind her very, very quietly. Tip-toe, tip-toe. He reached out his fuzzy little fingers and tickled Ellie right on her big gray tummy. Coochie-coo! Ellie let out a loud trumpet sound and shook with laughter. Ha-ha-ha, hoo-hoo-hoo! She thought it was so funny. Next, Barnaby saw Sammy the snake, resting on a smooth green leaf. Sizzle, hiss, went Sammy. Barnaby tickled Sammy right under his chin. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! Sammy giggled and rolled around in delight. Everyone in the jungle was laughing now. The colorful parrots in the trees began to chirp and giggle too. Squawk, squawk, giggle, giggle! Barnaby felt so happy seeing all his friends smiling. But soon, Barnaby felt a little tickle on his own fuzzy toes. Who could it be? It was a tiny green frog, jumping up and down. Ribbit, ribbit! The little frog tickled Barnaby right back. Tee-hee-hee! Barnaby laughed so hard he fell backward onto a soft patch of grass. Rollover, rollover, thump! All the jungle animals gathered around and cheered for Barnaby. They danced in a circle and clapped their hands. What a wonderful, joyful day it had been. Barnaby gave his friends warm monkey hugs. Hugs for Ellie, hugs for Sammy, and hugs for the little green frog. As the stars twinkled in the night sky, Barnaby closed his eyes with a happy grin, dreaming of more silly tickle games to play.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long curly tail, and a very big tummy that loved to rumble. Every morning, Milo would wake up and say, 'Ooh ooh, ah ah! Time to play!' One sunny morning, while swinging from branch to branch, Milo saw something very special. It was resting on a big green leaf. It was a bright yellow banana, but it was not just any ordinary banana. It was sparkly and shiny, glowing with a soft golden light. Milo blinked. He scratched his head. He gave a little giggle. 'Is this a magic banana?' he whispered to his friend, a little green parrot named Pip. Pip flapped his wings and squawked, 'Try it, Milo! Try it!' Milo reached out his furry hand and picked up the shiny banana. The moment his fingers touched the peel, *poof*! A shower of sparkly yellow stars danced all around them. Milo gasped with delight. He took a tiny little nibble. *Munch, munch, crunch!* Suddenly, Milo felt his toes begin to wiggle. Then, his arms began to stretch. Before he knew it, Milo was floating gently up into the air! He was flying like a bird over the treetops. 'Wheee!' shouted Milo, clapping his hands together. He flew past tall trees, colorful flowers, and friendly butterflies. He even waved hello to a sleepy sloth hanging upside down. The magic banana filled Milo with so much happy energy that he did a little loop-de-loop in the clouds. But soon, Milo's tummy gave another little rumble. Flying was fun, but he was getting hungry for a snack. He landed softly back on his favorite branch right next to Pip. 'That was the best ride ever,' Milo giggled, patting his tummy. He shared the rest of the sweet, delicious banana with his feathered friend. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Milo curled up in his cozy nest of leaves. He held his curly tail tight, closed his big brown eyes, and dreamed of flying high up in the starry sky. Good night, little Milo.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the jungle, where the tall bamboo stalks swayed in the warm breeze, lived a cheerful little monkey named Barnaby. Barnaby loved jumping, leaping, and exploring every single day. Today was a very special day because Barnaby found a surprise. Tied to a low-hanging vine was a shiny, bright red balloon. It bobbed up and down in the air, saying *squeak, squeak* as it danced. Barnaby had never seen a balloon before. He tilted his head to the left, then to the right. He poked it gently with one finger. *Boing!* The balloon bounced away just a little bit. Barnaby giggled. 'Hello, red friend,' he said in his softest monkey voice. He carefully untied the string and held it tightly in his little paw. He decided to take his new red balloon for a walk through the jungle. First, Barnaby skipped past the bubbling river. Splash, splash went his furry feet in the cool water! The red balloon floated happily right behind him, bobbing in the breeze. Next, Barnaby hopped over a big, sleepy log. *Hop!* The red balloon floated right over the log, too. Suddenly, a gust of wind came swooping through the trees. *Whoosh!* The wind pulled the balloon string, lifting Barnaby's feet right off the ground! 'Oh, my!' gasped Barnaby, holding on with both hands. The balloon carried him gently up into the air, higher and higher, until he was eye-to-eye with a friendly toucan sitting on a branch. 'Good morning!' squawked the toucan. 'Good morning!' replied Barnaby with a big smile. They soared together over the leafy canopy, watching the bright green jungle shrink below them. After a little while, the wind grew gentle again, and Barnaby floated softly back down to the mossy ground. He gave the balloon a big hug. It was the best adventure a little monkey could ever have. When evening came, Barnaby tied the balloon safely to his bed of leaves so it wouldn't float away while he slept. He curled up in a ball, dreaming of red balloons and flying high in the sky. Sweet dreams, Barnaby.

stories.title: Coco's Drumming Jungle Party
stories.text: Way down where the vines grow thick and the flowers bloom bright, there lived a joyful little monkey named Coco. Coco had the bounciest feet and the loudest laugh in the entire jungle. More than anything else in the world, Coco loved to make music. Every morning, he would look for things to bang on. He banged on hollow logs. *Thump, thump, thump!* He banged on large coconut shells. *Clack, clack, clack!* But today, Coco wanted to make a really big sound. He wanted to throw a jungle party for all his animal friends. First, Coco found two smooth wooden sticks on the forest floor. Then, he found an old, empty hollow tree stump that made a deep, booming sound when he hit it. *Bung, bung, bung!* Coco started to dance and play his drum rhythm. *Tap, tap, tap, thump, thump, thump!* Hearing the fun beat, his friends began to gather around. Bella the butterfly fluttered down and danced in circles. Sammy the snake wiggled his green body back and forth in the grass. Ellie the elephant came stomping over, trumpeting a happy tune with her long trunk. 'Time to dance!' cheered Coco, beating his drum even faster. All the animals joined in the fun. The monkeys swung from the vines, clapping their hands. The parrots sang loud, colorful songs high up in the branches. The whole jungle was alive with laughter, music, and happy footsteps. Coco's arms got a little bit tired from drumming, but his big smile just kept getting wider. He loved seeing all his friends so happy and full of joy. As the golden sun began to dip below the horizon, the music slowly grew softer and quieter. The animals yawned and stretched, tired from all the wonderful dancing. Coco gave his drum one last gentle tap. *Tap.* 'Good night, jungle friends,' whispered Coco softly. He climbed up into his favorite leafy bed, closed his eyes, and drifted off to sleep, still humming a happy little song in his heart.

stories.title: Milo's Morning Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy canopy of the great jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big, bouncy ears, a long, swirly tail, and a tummy that was rumbling loudly. Rumbly-rumble-rumble went Milo's tummy! It was time for breakfast. Milo swung from one thick, brown branch to another. Swing, swish, go! He used his strong tail to hang upside down. From his upside-down view, Milo spotted something bright yellow. It was a bunch of delicious, ripe bananas hanging from a tall tree! 'Yum, yum, yum!' chattered Milo with a happy giggle. But the bananas were just a little bit too far away. Milo needed to reach them. He stretched out his furry little arm. He stretched and stretched, but he could not touch them. Oh no! What should Milo do? He thought and thought. Then, Milo had a wonderful idea. He would use his bouncy legs to jump! Milo bent his knees. One, two, three, jump! He leaped through the warm jungle air and landed right on the banana branch. Boing! The branch wobbled up and down. Milo giggled even louder. He grabbed the biggest, yellowest banana of the bunch. Time to peel! Milo pulled down the yellow skin. Peely-peel-peel. Inside was soft, sweet fruit. He took a big bite. Mmm! It was so sweet and yummy. Milo ate every single bite until his tummy was completely full and happy. He rubbed his round tummy and smiled a big monkey smile. Then, feeling very sleepy and cozy from his big breakfast, Milo curled up into a soft, furry ball on a safe, leafy branch. He closed his brown eyes and drifted off to dreamland, safe in the warm jungle. Good night, little Milo, sleep tight until tomorrow's fun begins!

stories.title: Max Makes a Music Band
stories.text: Good morning, little readers! Meet Max. Max was a playful little monkey who loved to make happy sounds all day long. Max lived near a sparkling blue river where the jungle was full of fun things to tap, bang, and shake. Today, Max decided he wanted to start a big, noisy jungle band! He scampered down his favorite tree and looked around for instruments. First, Max found two hollow coconut shells on the ground. Tap-tap-tap! They made a wonderful clicking sound when he hit them together. 'Clickity-click, clickity-click!' sang Max happily. Next, Max found a wide, empty wooden box left behind by friendly explorers. He used his little paws to drum on the top. Boom-boom-boom! The wooden box made a deep, echoing sound that bounced through the trees. 'This is my drum!' cheered Max with a big grin. But a band needs more than drums and coconuts. Max looked up and saw a bush with shiny green leaves. He gently shook the branches. Shimmery-shake-shake! The leaves made a soft, rustling sound, just like a maraca. Now Max had a whole set of instruments. He decided to invite his jungle friends to play along. First came Ellie the Elephant. Ellie stomped her big feet to the beat. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Then came Sammy the Snake, slithering along and hissing a sweet melody. Ssss-ssss-sss! Finally, Polly the Parrot flew down and squawked a cheerful tune. Squawk, squawk, hello! Max played his coconuts. Ellie stomped her feet. Sammy hissed, and Polly squawked. Together, they made the happiest music in the whole wide jungle. They played and played until the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange. Max thanked his wonderful friends for the fun musical day. It was time to put the instruments away and rest. Max climbed back up to his cozy bed of leaves, humming a sweet little tune in his heart. What a wonderful day to be a musical monkey in the bright, beautiful jungle!

stories.title: Maya's Magic Tickle Tree
stories.text: Deep in the heart of the sunny jungle, there lived a very silly monkey named Maya. Maya loved to play games, and her absolute favorite game in the whole wide world was making her friends giggle. Today, Maya was on a special mission. She was looking for the famous Magic Tickle Tree! Legend said that this tree had soft, feathery leaves that loved to tickle anyone who walked by. Maya bounded through the green bushes, her tail swishing happily behind her. Hop, hop, go! She looked up, down, and all around. Where could the Magic Tickle Tree be hiding? Suddenly, Maya heard a funny sound. 'Hehehe! Hohoho!' Someone was laughing! Maya crept quietly behind a large green fern and peeked through. There stood the Magic Tickle Tree, with its sparkly pink leaves dancing in the gentle breeze. Whoosh, whoosh went the leaves. As Maya stepped closer, the wind blew a soft breeze right toward her. The feathery leaves brushed against Maya's furry tummy. Titch-titch-tickle! Maya let out a loud, bubbly giggle. 'Hee-hee-hee! That tickles!' she shouted. The tree tickled her nose. Achoo! Sneezed Maya, laughing even harder. Then, Maya had an idea. She wanted to share the tickly fun with all her jungle neighbors. She called out to her friends. First came Toby the Turtle. Toby walked up slowly. The pink leaves brushed his shell. Tickle, tickle! Toby pulled his head inside and chuckled, 'Hee-hee!' Next came Benny the Bear, who got tickled right on his fuzzy ears and laughed a big, rumbly laugh. All the animals gathered around the Magic Tickle Tree, dancing, jumping, and giggling together in the warm sunshine. The jungle echoed with happy animal sounds. When the afternoon turned into evening, the animals gave the magic tree a gentle pat and said thank you for the wonderful giggles. Maya curled up under the tree, still smiling from all the fun. She closed her eyes, dreaming of tickly pink leaves and happy jungle friends.

stories.title: Milo's Morning Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy canopy of the great jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a very long tail for swinging, and a tummy that was ready for breakfast. Good morning, jungle! said Milo with a big, happy chatter. Today was a very special day because today was the day of the Big Banana Hunt. Milo stretched his arms up high, reach, reach, reach, and scratched his fuzzy head. Where, oh where, is my yummy yellow banana? He looked under a giant green leaf. No banana. He looked behind a big brown tree trunk. No banana there either. Oh dear, whispered Milo, making a little pouty face with his soft lips. Just then, his clever monkey ears heard a funny sound. Squish, squish, squish. Milo scampered up a vine, hand over hand, super fast. Up, up, up he went until he was sitting on the very best branch of all. Guess what he saw hanging right in front of his nose? A big, curved, bright yellow banana, smiling right back at him! Milo clapped his hands together with joy. Yay! He cheered, doing a little happy dance on the branch. He reached out his fuzzy fingers, grabbed the banana, and peeled it back. Peeling bananas is so much fun, pull, pull, pull! Inside was sweet, soft fruit. Milo took a big bite. Yum, yum, yum! It tasted so delicious and sweet. He shared a little piece with his tiny beetle friend crawling on the bark. Thank you, sweet beetle, for helping me look, said Milo. With a full tummy and a happy heart, Milo curled his long tail around a sturdy branch, gave a big yawn, and rubbed his eyes. Being a little monkey is the best adventure in the whole wide world, he thought as he drifted off to sleep under the warm jungle sun.

stories.title: Coco Goes to the Moon
stories.text: Little Coco was a very curious monkey who loved to look up at the night sky. Every evening, before bedtime, Coco would sit on his favorite wooden fence and stare at the big, glowing silver moon. It looks just like a giant, round piece of glowing cheese! Coco giggled, patting his round tummy. One magical night, Coco decided it was time to visit his glowing friend. First, he needed a spaceship. He found a big red cardboard box left behind by some explorers. Coco hopped right inside the box. Zoom, zoom, zoom! He made rocket ship noises with his mouth. Next, he needed a special astronaut helmet. He put a shiny coconut shell right on top of his head. Perfect! Now Coco was ready for blastoff. Five, four, three, two, one, BLAST OFF! Coco shouted, jumping up into the air with all his might. He climbed up the tallest tree in the jungle, swinging from branch to branch like a shooting star blazing across the dark sky. Up, up, up he climbed until the leaves parted and he was looking right at the moon. Hello, Mr. Moon! whispered Coco softly. The moon seemed to smile down with a gentle, silvery light, wrapping the little monkey in a warm, cozy glow. Coco sat on a fluffy white cloud that felt just like a giant marshmallow. He bounced up and down, boing, boing, boing, laughing out loud. He picked a tiny star to keep in his pocket as a special souvenir. But soon, a big yawn crept into Coco's mouth. Oh, I am getting so sleepy, he whispered, rubbing his heavy eyelids. He climbed back down his leafy ladder, safe and sound, right into his cozy hammock made of soft woven vines. He hugged his star tight, closed his eyes, and dreamed sweet, starry dreams all night long.

stories.title: The Muddy Monkey Mishap
stories.text: The sun was shining bright, and the jungle air was as warm as a warm bath. Little Pip the monkey was hopping around looking for something fun to do. Splash, splash, went a sound nearby. Pip peeked through the ferns and saw a lovely, squishy puddle of mud right in the middle of the path. Ooh, squishy! Pip said, his eyes going wide with excitement. Monkeys love to play, and Pip loved things that were messy and fun. He walked right up to the edge of the puddle and dipped one furry toe inside. Brrr! No, it wasn't cold at all; it was wonderfully warm and gooey. Pip stepped all the way in with both feet. Squish, squash, squish, went the mud between his toes. It tickled so much that Pip let out a loud, happy giggle. Tee-hee! Then, Pip had a wonderfully silly idea. He scooped up a handful of thick, brown mud and patted it right on top of his head like a silly hat. Look at me! I am King Mud-Monkey! he cheered, striking a grand pose for the passing butterflies.
