He stomped his feet, making the mud fly up into the air in little brown droplets. Splash, splatter, plop! A little blob of mud landed right on his nose. Pip crossed his eyes to look at the funny brown spot on his nose and laughed even harder. But soon, Pip started to feel very heavy and sticky. His fur was no longer fluffy; it was completely covered in brown clay. Oh my, whispered Pip, feeling a little tired from all the stomping. Just then, a gentle tropical rain shower began to fall from the sky. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter went the cool raindrops, washing all the sticky mud right off Pip's fur. Pip danced in the refreshing rain, spinning around and around until he was sparkling clean again. What a wonderfully muddy adventure!

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big, fluffy ears, a long curly tail, and a tummy that loved to rumble. Every single morning, Milo would swing from branch to branch, looking for his very favorite treat: yummy, yellow bananas! One sunny Tuesday, Milo swung past a giant vine and spotted something extraordinary. It was a banana, but not just any banana. This banana was bright pink, and it was glowing with sparkling golden stars! 'Ooh-ooh-aah-aah!' chattered Milo in surprise. He reached out a furry paw and plucked the magical banana from the tree. As soon as he touched it, the banana began to giggle. 'Tee-hee-hee!' it laughed. Milo blinked his big brown eyes. 'Did you just giggle?' he asked. 'I sure did!' said the magic banana. 'If you take a bite of me, I will give you a very special ride!' Milo was a brave little monkey, so he took a tiny, nibbly bite. Yummy! It tasted like sweet strawberries and sunshine. Suddenly, *WHOOSH!* The magic banana grew as big as a boat. Milo hopped right on top, holding tightly to its stem. Up, up, up they went, flying high above the jungle canopy. They zoomed past colorful parrots, waved hello to sleepy sloths, and tickled a fluffy white cloud. 'Whee!' shouted Milo, clapping his hands together. They soared over rivers that sparkled like diamonds and trees that tickled the sky. After a wonderful adventure, the magic banana gently floated back down, landing right outside Milo's cozy treehouse. The banana shrunk back to its normal size with a soft *pop*. Milo gave the stem a grateful pat. 'Thank you for the best ride ever,' he whispered. His tummy felt happy, his heart felt full, and as the golden sun began to set behind the trees, Milo curled up in his leafy bed. He hugged his curly tail, closed his eyes, and dreamed of flying high among the stars. Good night, Milo.

stories.title: The Great Jungle Hide-and-Seek
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the tropical canopy, and it was time for the biggest game of the day. Jungle Hide-and-Seek! Little Maya, a bouncy baby monkey with bright, curious eyes, loved this game more than anything in the world. 'Ready or not, here I come!' trumpeted Barnaby the baby elephant, closing his big eyes and counting to ten with his trunk. Maya giggled, covering her mouth with her paws so she wouldn't make a sound. 'Where should I hide?' she whispered to herself. She looked up at the tall coconut trees. She looked down at the soft green ferns. Then, she saw the perfect spot. Maya scampered up a large mango tree and hid right behind a big, juicy green leaf. She tucked her long tail in, pulled her knees to her chest, and stayed as still as a statue. 'Ten!' called Barnaby. 'Coming to find you!' Maya held her breath. She heard heavy, happy footsteps stomping through the grass. *Stomp, stomp, stomp.* Then, she heard a gentle trunk sniffing the air. *Sniff, sniff, sniff.* Barnaby walked right under the mango tree. He looked left. He looked right. He scratched his head with his foot. 'Hmm, I wonder where little Maya could be?' he mumbled loudly. Maya couldn't help it. Her nose tickled. 'Achoo!' she sneezed. Barnaby spun around and gasped with delight. 'Aha! I hear you up there in the tree!' Maya popped her head out from behind the leaf and laughed. 'You found me, Barnaby!' Down she swung, landing safely on the soft grass right in front of her big-eared friend. 'Your turn to hide!' Maya cheered, covering her eyes and starting to count. 'One, two, three, four...' Barnaby waddled away as fast as his little legs could carry him, trying to hide behind a tiny bush that was way too small for an elephant. Maya peeked through her fingers and giggled so hard she fell backward onto a patch of soft moss. Playing with friends in the warm jungle sunshine was the most wonderful way to spend an afternoon. When the sky turned orange and pink, Maya gave Barnaby a big monkey hug, waved goodbye, and climbed up to her cozy branch for a peaceful, happy sleep.

stories.title: Milo's Musical Jungle Band
stories.text: The jungle was usually full of quiet rustles and gentle breezes, but today, Milo the monkey wanted to make some noise! Milo was sitting on a fallen log, tapping a hollow stick against a bumpy gourd. *Tap-tap, tap-tap, thump, thump!* It made a wonderful rhythmic sound. 'I want to start a band!' Milo chattered happily, doing a little dance on the log. Just then, Zazu the zebra trotted by, swishing her tail. 'Can I join your band, Milo?' she asked. 'Of course!' said Milo. 'You can play the shaker!' He handed Zazu a hollow seed pod filled with tiny pebbles. *Shake-shake, rattle-rattle!* It sounded just like rain falling on big green leaves. Next came Pip, a cheerful little parrot with feathers of red, blue, and yellow. 'Squawk! Can I join too?' chirped Pip. 'Yes, Pip! You can sing the high notes!' said Milo. Soon, more jungle friends heard the joyful racket and came running to join the fun. Ellie the elephant stomped a heavy, steady beat with her big feet. *Boom, boom, boom!* Sammy the squirrel strummed his tiny claws against a stretched vine like a guitar string. *Twang, twang, twang!* Together, they formed the very first Jungle Music Band. Milo stood in the center, acting as the enthusiastic conductor. He waved his curly tail up and down like a baton. 'One, two, three, play!' he cheered. The forest came alive with the most amazing symphony. The shaker rattled, the drum beat, the vine twang-twanged, and the parrot sang a sweet melody. Even the frogs in the nearby stream joined in with a loud, ribbiting chorus. All the animals in the jungle stopped what they were doing to listen. Some monkeys in the distance started clapping their paws, while little butterfly friends fluttered around in time with the music. Milo felt his heart dance with joy as he banged his gourd drum. Making music together with his best friends made him feel like the happiest monkey in the whole wide world. As the stars twinkled overhead, the band played one final, gentle lullaby. The music slowed down, getting softer and softer, until it was just a quiet hum. Everyone yawned, smiled, and curled up together under the moonlight, dreaming sweet, musical dreams.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long curly tail, and a very wiggly nose. More than anything in the whole wide world, Milo loved bananas. He loved them squishy, he loved them sweet, and he loved them yellow! One sunny morning, Milo woke up with a big stretch. 'Yawn!' he said, scratching his furry tummy. 'I am so hungry!' Milo scampered down his favorite tree, hop-hop-hop, and bounced onto the jungle path. Today felt like a special day. The birds were singing a happy tune, and the butterflies were dancing in the air. Milo looked up, and right there, hanging from the highest branch of the tallest tree, was the biggest banana he had ever seen. It was glowing with a bright golden light. 'Ooh-ooh-aah-aah!' shouted Milo with joy. But there was a little problem. The banana was way up high, and Milo was down low. How would he reach it? First, Milo tried to jump. He bent his knees, pushed off the soft ground, and leaped up, up, up! But he only touched a green leaf. 'Boing!' he landed back on his feet. Next, Milo tried to climb. He grabbed the rough bark with his fingers and toes, and scritch-scratch, scritch-scratch, he went up the trunk. But the branch was too thin, and it started to sway back and forth. 'Whoops-a-daisy!' cried Milo, sliding right back down. Milo sat on a mossy rock and put his little paws on his cheeks. He needed a clever plan. Just then, his bouncy monkey friends, Lila and Pip, swung by on a thick green vine. 'What's the matter, Milo?' asked Lila. 'I want that big golden banana, but I cannot reach it,' sighed Milo. Pip grinned a wide monkey grin. 'We can help! Let's work together as a team!' Lila and Pip grabbed Milo's long curly tail. Milo grabbed the vine. One, two, three, SWING! They flew through the warm jungle air like flying superheroes. Wheeee! Milo reached out his hand. Snap! He plucked the magical golden banana right off the branch. They landed safely in a soft pile of leaves. 'Hooray!' cheered all the monkeys. Milo shared his delicious, sweet banana with Lila and Pip. It was the best breakfast ever. From that day on, Milo knew that working together with friends makes every adventure much more fun.

stories.title: Max Makes Music
stories.text: Deep in the whispering jungle, where the flowers bloom in bright pinks and blues, lived a cheerful little monkey named Max. Max was full of energy from the tip of his ears to the bottom of his feet. He loved to jump, he loved to tumble, and most of all, he loved to make noise! One bright Tuesday morning, Max found a hollow wooden log on the forest floor. Tap, tap, tap! went his knuckles against the wood. 'Boom, boom, boom!' it echoed through the trees. Max giggled. He had just made a drum! Suddenly, a bright green parrot flew down and squawked a high-pitched song. 'Squawk, squawk, hello!' Max’s eyes lit up. 'Aha!' he whispered to himself. 'We can make a jungle band!' Max picked up two small sticks and tapped them together. Click-clack, click-clack! A fuzzy little koala bear heard the jolly rhythm and joined in by shaking a rattle made of dried seed pods. Shake-shake, shake-shake! A group of tiny tree frogs hopped onto a large lily pad and added their voices to the music. Ribbit-ribbit, ribbit-ribbit! Max started to drum faster on his hollow log. Boom-boom-boom! The parrot chirped, the koala shook, the frogs croaked, and Max banged his drum with all his might. The whole jungle was alive with wonderful music. Soon, all the animals of the forest came running to see what was happening. Elephants stomped their big feet to the beat. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Zebras clapped their hooves. Clap, clap, clap! Even the sleepy sloths blinked their big eyes and swayed slowly from side to side. Max stood up on his log and raised his drumsticks high in the air. 'Welcome to the great jungle concert!' he announced with a big smile. The animals danced and sang together under the warm golden sun. They danced until their legs were tired and their tummies giggled with joy. When the sun began to set, painting the sky in shades of purple and orange, the music slowly grew softer. Rock-a-bye, rock-a-bye, went the gentle rhythm. One by one, the animals yawned and curled up for a cozy sleep. Max curled up on his favorite branch, hugging his trusty wooden drum. He closed his eyes and whispered, 'What a wonderful day for making music.' And he drifted off to dream sweet, musical dreams.

stories.title: Barnaby's Busy Day
stories.text: Barnaby was a very busy little monkey with soft brown fur and a bright red vest. Barnaby lived in a cozy treehouse nestled in the branches of a giant mango tree. Every morning, Barnaby had a very important job: he had to check on all his jungle neighbors to make sure they were having a wonderful day. First, Barnaby swung out of his treehouse door on a sturdy green vine. Wheee! He landed right in front of Sammy the squirrel, who was counting his acorns. 'Good morning, Sammy!' chirped Barnaby, tipping an imaginary hat. 'Good morning, Barnaby!' chattered Sammy, tossing a shiny acorn into the air. Next, Barnaby skipped down the winding path until he reached the sparkling blue river. There he found Penny the pelican splashing water with her big webbed feet. Splash, splash, splash! 'Careful, Penny!' laughed Barnaby. 'The water is splashing everywhere!' Penny smiled and scooped up a refreshing beakful of water. Barnaby continued his morning walk, hopping over colorful flowers and waving to buzzing bumblebees. Buzz-buzz, buzz-buzz! Suddenly, Barnaby heard a soft sniffle coming from behind a large bush. He stopped and parted the big green leaves. There sat Toby the tiny tiger cub, looking very sad. 'What is the matter, Toby?' asked Barnaby gently, sitting down beside him. 'I lost my favorite red rubber ball,' whimpered Toby, wiping a tear from his furry cheek. Barnaby’s kind heart went out to his friend. 'Don't you worry, Toby. We will find it together!' Barnaby looked up into the trees. He looked under the large ferns. He even peeked behind a hollow log. Then, up in the branches of a low-hanging bush, he saw a flash of bright red. 'Aha! There it is!' cried Barnaby. He scrambled up the bush and gently retrieved the red rubber ball. He handed it to Toby with a warm, friendly grin. Toby’s face lit up with a huge smile. 'Yay! Thank you so much, Barnaby!' Toby barked happily, and they played a fun game of catch, tossing the ball back and forth. By the time the sun began to sink low in the sky, Barnaby was wonderfully tired. He gave Toby a big hug, said goodbye, and climbed back up to his cozy treehouse. He curled up in his soft leaf bed, closed his eyes, and smiled. Helping friends made for the best days of all.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a long curly tail, and the biggest, brightest smile you ever did see. Milo loved to do two things more than anything else in the whole wide world: swing from branch to branch and eat delicious, yellow bananas! Every single morning, the sun would peek through the tall trees, saying, 'Good morning, Milo!' And Milo would chatter happily, 'Ooh, ooh, aah, aah!' One sunny Tuesday, Milo woke up with a very rumbling tummy. Rumble, rumble, went his little tummy. 'Time for breakfast!' chattered Milo. He scampered up the tallest banana tree in the jungle. He climbed higher and higher, stepping carefully on the strong green vines. Up, up, up he went until he reached the very top. But guess what he found? Oh no! There were no yellow bananas left on the tree. Just one tiny, funny-looking green thing. It was shaped like a banana, but it sparkled with little silver stars! Milo blinked his big brown eyes. 'What is this?' he whispered. He gave the sparkly green thing a gentle tap with his tiny finger. Pop! Suddenly, the green banana turned bright pink and started to float in the air! 'Wheee!' giggled Milo. The magical banana danced in a circle, doing loop-de-loops above his head. Milo clapped his hands together and jumped up and down. He reached out his fuzzy paws and grabbed the floating fruit. With a soft *whoosh*, the pink banana turned back into a normal, yummy yellow banana, but it was as big as Milo himself! Milo's eyes grew wide with excitement. He peeled the banana and took a huge, crunchy bite. Yum, yum, yum! It tasted like sweet strawberries and honey. As he finished the very last bite, Milo felt a funny tickle in his toes. Suddenly, he floated two whole inches off the ground! He could fly! Milo zoomed through the jungle canopy, laughing and doing somersaults in the warm air. He flew past his monkey friends, waving hello. 'Look at me!' he cheered. When the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and purple, Milo landed gently back on his favorite cozy branch. He curled up his long tail, closed his heavy eyes, and dreamed of flying bananas and sweet jungle treats. Good night, magical Milo.

stories.title: Max Makes a New Friend
stories.text: Deep in the whispering bamboo forest lived a cheerful little monkey named Max. Max wore a bright red vest that his mama had sewn for him, and he loved to explore every corner of the jungle. Today, Max was on a very important mission. He wanted to find a new friend to play hide-and-seek with. 'Who wants to play?' Max called out, swinging on a flexible green vine. Swing, swish, swing went the vine! He swung past a sleepy green parrot. 'Squawk, not now, Max, I am taking a nap,' squawked the parrot, tucking his head under his wing. Max patted his fuzzy tummy and giggled. Next, he swung past a busy family of orange tree frogs. Ribbit, ribbit, went the frogs, jumping from leaf to leaf. 'We are too busy catching flies!' croaked a little frog. Max did not give up. He climbed down the trunk of a giant mango tree and looked under a big, velvety fern. And there, sitting all by himself, was a tiny purple creature with big floppy ears and a polka-dot tail. It was a baby bush baby! The little bush baby looked a little shy and hid his face behind his paws. Max smiled his warmest, friendliest monkey smile. He hopped closer, making a funny little face and wiggling his ears. 'Hello there! My name is Max. Do you want to play?' The little bush baby peeked through his fingers. He let out a soft, happy squeak and lowered his paws. 'My name is Pip,' he whispered softly. Max clapped his hands with joy. 'Let's play hide-and-seek, Pip!' Max covered his eyes with his furry paws and began to count loudly. 'One, two, three, four, five! Ready or not, here I come!' Pip scampered away as fast as his little legs could carry him, hiding behind a giant mushroom. Max opened his eyes and searched everywhere. He looked under a log, he looked up in the bushes, and then he heard a tiny giggle coming from behind the mushroom. 'Aha! I found you!' shouted Max. Pip jumped out, laughing and clapping his hands. They played hide-and-seek all afternoon, chasing each other through the tall grass and drinking sweet nectar from the flowers. When the stars twinkled in the night sky, Max and Pip hugged goodbye, promising to play again tomorrow. Max skipped all the way home to his treehouse, his heart full of happiness because he had made a wonderful new friend.

stories.title: The Great Jungle Drum Circle
stories.text: It was a bright, breezy morning in the tropical rainforest, and something very exciting was about to happen. Today was the day of the Great Jungle Drum Circle! Coco, a little monkey with bouncy curls and a love for rhythm, woke up extra early. Tap, tap, tap went Coco's fingers on a hollow log. 'Today is the day!' chattered Coco excitedly. He grabbed his favorite pair of wooden drumsticks that he had carved himself from fallen branches. He bounded through the trees, eager to join his animal friends in the clearing by the sparkling river. When Coco arrived, the clearing was already buzzing with life. Barnaby the bear was sitting on a large boulder, holding two big hollow gourds. Fiona the flamingo stood on one leg, gently tapping a pair of bamboo tubes with her beak. Even Leo the lion was there, ready to stomp his paws to the beat. 'Hello, Coco! Are you ready to make some music?' asked Barnaby with a booming, friendly laugh. 'Yes, yes, yes!' cheered Coco, doing a little backflip. The animals gathered in a big, happy circle under the shade of a giant banana tree. Coco took his place in the middle and raised his wooden drumsticks high up into the air. 'One, two, three, let's play!' shouted Coco. Bam, bam, bam went Barnaby's gourds. Clack, clack, clack went Fiona's bamboo tubes. Thump, thump, thump went Leo's heavy paws on the soft earth. And *tap-a-tap, zoom-zoom-zoom* went Coco's drumsticks on his hollow log! The music echoed through the green canopy, waking up the colorful butterflies and making the flowers dance in the gentle breeze. It was a wonderful, joyful song of the jungle. Little baby monkeys swung down from the vines to clap their tiny hands. Birds fluttered above, singing sweet, high-pitched melodies that blended with the drumbeats. Coco felt the rhythm deep inside his fuzzy toes. He danced in a circle, drumming faster and faster, making everyone laugh and cheer. The music grew louder and happier, filling the whole forest with warmth and friendship. When the song finally came to an end, all the animals cheered and hugged one another. Coco held his drumsticks high, feeling so proud and happy. Making music together with his friends was the absolute best thing in the whole wide world. They spent the rest of the day sharing sweet mangoes, telling funny stories, and dreaming up new rhythms for tomorrow's big show.

stories.title: Milo's Morning Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy canopy of the great big jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a very long tail that could wrap around branches like a cozy blanket, and big, bright eyes that loved to look for fun. When the golden sun peeked through the trees, saying good morning to the world, Milo opened his eyes and gave a big, wide yawn. Yawn! Time to wake up! Milo scratched his tummy and thought about his very favorite thing in the whole wide world: bananas! He leaped from branch to branch, going hop, skip, and jump. Whee! First, Milo swung by his best friend Ellie the elephant. 'Good morning, Ellie!' called Milo. Ellie gave a happy toot with her long trunk. 'Toot-toot, good morning, Milo!' Then, Milo scampered past Sammy the snake, who was coiled up on a rock, soaking in the warm sun. 'Sssss-sweet morning to you, little monkey!' hissed Sammy with a friendly smile. Milo giggled and kept on moving because his tummy was starting to rumble. Rumble, rumble, went his tummy. It was time for breakfast! Milo climbed up to the very top of the tallest banana tree. There hung a bunch of bright yellow, curved, delicious bananas. Milo reached out his little hand and gently plucked the biggest one. He peeled back the yellow skin—peel, peel, peel—and took a big, happy bite. Yum, yum, yum! It was sweet and soft and oh-so-yummy. Milo chewed happily and rubbed his belly. With a full tummy and a happy heart, Milo curled up on his favorite branch for a little rest, ready for whatever afternoon adventure would come next. Goodnight, morning sun, hello sweet little monkey dreams.

stories.title: Max Makes a Splash
stories.text: It was a hot, sunny afternoon in the jungle, and Max the little monkey was feeling very, very warm. Phew! The sun was shining brightly, and the air felt thick and heavy. Max wiped a fuzzy hand across his forehead and looked down at the sparkling, cool blue river winding right through the trees. 'Ahhh,' thought Max, 'that water looks so refreshing!' Max loved climbing trees, but today he wanted to try something brand new. He scampered down the trunk of his favorite mango tree, his little feet going patter-patter-patter on the soft dirt. When he reached the riverbank, he dipped one tiny toe into the water. Brrr! It was cool and crisp, but it felt so good! Max giggled with delight. He wanted to go in, but he was a little bit nervous. Just then, his friend Bella the hippopotamus poked her big pink nose right up out of the water. 'Splish, splash, hello Max!' she rumbled happily. 'Come on in, the water is lovely!' Max felt brave. He took two steps forward, grabbed a hanging vine with his strong little hands, and gave a joyful little leap. Wheeeeee! Max let go of the vine and flew through the air, right toward the river. Splash! Water went everywhere. Drip, drop, plip, plop! Max popped his head out of the water, shaking his wet fur so the droplets flew like tiny diamonds in the sun. 'Look at me, Bella! I am swimming!' cheered Max. He splashed his hands, making big waves, and kicked his feet. It was the most fun he had ever had. By the time the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Max climbed out of the river, feeling cool, clean, and happy. What a wonderful day for a little monkey adventure.

stories.title: Barnaby's Lost Hat
stories.text: Barnaby was a very smart monkey who wore a bright red hat every single day. The hat was special because it had a little yellow feather right on top, and it kept the sun out of his eyes while he played. One breezy afternoon, Barnaby was playing tag with his jungle friends. He ran fast—zoom! He jumped high—whee! But suddenly, a strong gust of wind came blowing through the trees. Whoosh! The wind blew right past Barnaby’s head and snatched his favorite red hat away. 'Oh no!' cried Barnaby. 'My hat!' The red hat fluttered up into the air, dancing like a red leaf in the wind. Barnaby chased after it as fast as his little legs could carry him. He ran past the tall bamboo stalks and under the big fern leaves. 'Stop, hat, stop!' he called out. The hat floated gently down and landed right on top of a very tall giraffe named Gina. Gina blinked her big brown eyes and looked up. 'Well, hello there, Barnaby,' she said softly. 'Are you looking for this?' Barnaby stopped and looked up at the tall giraffe. He giggled because Gina looked so funny with a tiny red monkey hat perched high on her long head. 'Yes, please, Gina! That is my favorite hat,' said Barnaby. Gina bent her long neck all the way down, down, down, until her head was right next to Barnaby’s. Barnaby reached up, took his red hat, and placed it right back on his head, tucking the yellow feather in tight. 'Thank you, Gina!' said Barnaby with a big hug. He gave a happy little dance and promised to hold onto his hat much tighter next time the wind decided to blow.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a very long tail that could wrap around branches like a hug, and the biggest, brightest eyes you ever did see. Today was a very special day because Milo woke up with a loud tummy rumble. Rumble, rumble, rumble went Milo’s tummy! He was so hungry. 'Time for breakfast!' chattered Milo to himself. He swung from branch to branch, leaping through the air with a whee! He looked under a large green leaf. No bananas there. He looked inside a hollow log. Only a sleepy little beetle. Oh dear. Where were the bananas? Just as Milo was about to pout, something shiny caught his eye. It was peeking out from behind a fluffy white cloud. It was a golden, glowing, extra-big banana! But wait, how could a monkey reach a banana in the sky? Milo thought really, really hard. He tapped his furry head. Tap, tap, tap. Then, he had a clever idea. Milo used his super-strong tail to hang upside down from the very highest branch. He stretched out his arms as far, far, far as they could go. He stretched his fingers. He wiggled his toes. He gave one giant stretch and yelled, 'Grab!' Pop! The golden banana came loose right into his fuzzy hand. Milo pulled himself back up to the branch and peeled the banana. It was the yummiest, sweetest banana in the whole wide world. It tasted like sunshine and honey. Milo rubbed his happy tummy and giggled. 'That was an adventure!' he whispered. With a happy wave to the sky, Milo curled up in his cozy nest for a little nap, dreaming of more golden bananas.

stories.title: Barnaby's Red Balloon
stories.text: Deep in the jungle, where the flowers grew big and bright, lived a little monkey named Barnaby. Barnaby loved to jump, and hop, and play all day long. One sunny morning, something wonderful floated right past his favorite tree. It was a round, shiny, bright red balloon! The balloon bobbed up and down in the warm breeze. Up and down, up and down, just like a dancing heart. 'Hello, red balloon!' chattered Barnaby with a big smile. He wanted to play with the balloon, so he began to chase it. First, Barnaby swung from a long green vine. Whee! He reached out his hand, but the balloon drifted just a little bit higher. Oh, no you don't! thought Barnaby. Next, he climbed up the trunk of a tall coconut tree. He scrambled up, up, up until his nose touched the leafy top. He reached out again, but the breeze blew the balloon away, over the sparkly blue river. Barnaby did not give up. He loved a good chase! He jumped across the stepping stones in the water. Splash, splash, went his little feet. He scrambled up the grassy hill on the other side. There sat the red balloon, resting gently on a patch of soft green grass. Barnaby tiptoed over very quietly. Tip-toe, tip-toe, tip-toe. He gave the string a gentle, gentle tug. The balloon bounced happily in his hand. Barnaby hugged his new red balloon tightly. It squeaked a happy squeak. He sat down on the grass and watched the clouds roll by, holding his shiny red treasure. It was the best day ever, and Barnaby’s heart felt as light and happy as his floating red balloon.

stories.title: Pip's Bedtime Yawn
stories.text: The sun was beginning to go down behind the big green jungle trees, painting the sky in pink and orange colors. It was almost bedtime, but little monkey Pip was not ready to sleep. Not yet! Pip had too much energy. He wanted to bounce. He wanted to spin. He wanted to do one hundred somersaults. 'Time to wind down, little monkey,' said Mama Monkey softly, wrapping her warm arms around him. But Pip giggled and shook his head. 'No sleep! Play!' he chattered, doing a little dance on the branch. Mama Monkey smiled. She knew just what to do. 'Let us play the quiet game,' she whispered. 'Can you stretch your arms up high like the tall trees?' Pip reached his arms up to touch the evening stars. Stretch, stretch, stretch. 'Good job,' said Mama. 'Now, can you curl up small like a fuzzy green caterpillar?' Pip rolled himself into a tight little ball on the branch. He tucked his nose right under his tail. 'Can you breathe in the sweet smell of the night flowers?' Pip took a deep, deep breath in through his nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff. And then, Pip let out a giant, noisy monkey yawn. Ahhhhh-choo—no, wait! Ahhhhh-wooooo! A big, sleepy monkey yawn. Suddenly, Pip’s eyelids felt very, very heavy. They felt like they had little rocks on them. His arms felt heavy, too. His legs felt tired from all the bouncing. The jungle grew quiet around them. Crickets began to sing a soft lullaby. Chirp, chirp, chirp went the crickets. Pip snuggled close to his mama’s soft fur. He closed his big brown eyes and whispered, 'Goodnight, stars. Goodnight, trees.' And before you could count to three, little monkey Pip was fast asleep, dreaming sweet jungle dreams.

stories.title: Milo's Morning Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy canopy of the great jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big, round brown eyes, soft brown fur, and a tail that curled just like a question mark. Every single morning, when the golden sun peeked through the trees and tickled his nose, Milo would wake up with a big stretch. Stretch, stretch, go his little arms! Yawn, yawn, goes his sleepy mouth! Today was a very special day because Milo's tummy was rumbling. It was time for breakfast. Milo knew exactly what he wanted. He wanted a big, bright yellow banana! Milo scampered up the tall trunk of the banana tree, going hop, skip, and jump. He used his strong hands and his wiggly feet to climb higher and higher. Up, up, up he went until he reached the very top. There, hanging in a bunch, was the biggest, yellowest banana in the whole wide jungle. It curved just like Milo's smile. Milo reached out his hand, gave the banana a gentle tug, and SNAP! It came right off. 'Hooray!' cheered Milo, doing a happy little dance on the branch. He peeled back the yellow skin, strip by strip, revealing the sweet, soft white fruit inside. He took a big bite. Yum, yum, yum! It was so sweet and delicious. Milo ate every single bite until his tummy was nice and full. Then, he rubbed his belly and let out a happy sigh. It was going to be a wonderful day of play in the jungle, and Milo was ready for all the fun adventures waiting just around the corner.

stories.title: Max Makes Music
stories.text: Deep in the heart of the noisy jungle, there lived a little monkey named Max. Max loved sounds. He loved the buzzing of the bees, the rustling of the leaves, and the chirping of the colorful birds. But most of all, Max loved making his own music! One sunny afternoon, Max found a hollow, empty log resting on the soft forest floor. He picked up two small, smooth sticks in his paws. 'Tap, tap, tap!' went the sticks against the log. It made a wonderful drum sound. Boom, boom, boom! Max grinned a wide, toothy grin and started to dance a silly little monkey jig, shaking his fuzzy hips from side to side. Soon, his good friend Pip the parrot flew down from a branch. Pip had a shiny tambourine in her claws. She shook it up and down. 'Jingle, jingle, rattle, shake!' sang the tambourine. Next came Ellie the baby elephant, stomping her feet on the ground. 'Thump, thump, thump!' went her big grey feet. What a funny band they made! Max tapped his log, Pip jingled her tambourine, and Ellie stomped her feet. Together, they made a cheerful jungle symphony. All the other animals gathered around to listen and clap their paws and wings. The monkeys swung from the vines, cheering for the band. Max felt so proud and happy. Making music with his friends was his absolute favorite thing in the whole world. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, the music slowly got softer and quieter. The tired little musicians gave one final bow. Max curled up on his favorite branch, ready to dream sweet, musical dreams all through the night.

stories.title: Coco's Lost Little Leaf
stories.text: Little Coco was a very curious monkey who loved to collect treasures from the jungle floor. Today, she found the most magnificent green leaf. It was wide, smooth, and shaped just like a heart. Coco decided this leaf was her very special friend, and she named it Greeny. She carried Greeny everywhere she went. She carried it while she swung from the vines, and she carried it while she nibbled on juicy berries. But suddenly, a big, silly gust of wind blew through the trees. Whoosh! The wind tickled Coco's nose, and *pop*, Greeny slipped right out of her paws! 'Oh no!' cried Coco, as the wind carried her precious leaf high up into the air. Greeny fluttered and danced in the breeze, floating higher and higher above the green treetops. Coco could not let her friend fly away forever! So, she began to chase after it. She swung quickly from branch to branch. Swish, swoosh, go her strong arms! 'Wait for me, Greeny!' she called out with a giggle. She climbed past a sleeping koala and waved hello to a chattering parrot. The wind carried Greeny toward a low-hanging fern, and gently, softly, the leaf drifted down, down, down, landing right on top of a giant toadstool. Coco scrambled down the trunk in a hurry. She crept up slowly, holding her breath, and reached out her tiny hand. *Got it!* She scooped up Greeny and gave the leaf a big hug. Coco was so relieved and happy to have her leafy friend back safely. She tucked Greeny securely behind her furry ear, ready for their next big adventure together in the wonderful, magical jungle.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text:
Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a very happy little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long tail that could curl just like a question mark, and a very tummy-rumbling appetite. Every single morning, the sun would peek through the canopy, shouting a warm 'Good morning!' and Milo would wake up with a big stretch. Today was a very special day because Milo was on a big quest to find the most delicious, yum-yum-yummy banana in the whole wide jungle.

First, Milo swung from a tall vine. Whoosh! He flew past a chatty green parrot. 'Hello, Milo!' squawked the parrot. 'Hello, Polly!' giggled Milo as he zoomed right on by. He climbed up the thick trunk of the grand coconut tree. He looked left. He looked right. He even looked upside down, hanging by his strong tail! But there were no bananas there, only bumpy coconuts that made a funny hollow sound when he tapped them with his tiny knuckles. Tap, tap, tap! Milo giggled and kept on going.

Next, Milo hopped down to the sparkling river. Splish, splash, splosh! He saw a little pink fish blowing bubbles. 'Bloop, bloop!' went the fish. Milo made funny fish faces back, puffing out his cheeks until he looked just like a fuzzy balloon. But still, no bananas were in sight. His tummy let out a loud, funny sound. Rumbly-rumble-rum! Milo rubbed his tummy and thought, 'Where, oh where, could my breakfast be hiding?'

Just then, a bright yellow butterfly fluttered right past his nose. It danced in the air, looping and twirling like a falling leaf. 'Follow me!' seemed to say the little butterfly. So Milo did. He climbed higher than he had ever climbed before, all the way to the very tippy-top of the tallest banana tree in the jungle. And guess what he found waiting right there? A bunch of bananas so big, bright, and golden that they looked just like little pieces of sunshine! Milo clapped his hands together with joy. He picked the biggest, happiest banana of them all, peeled it back with a loud 'SNAP!', and took a giant, yummy bite. Ahhh, it was the sweetest treat in the whole jungle! With a happy tummy and a sleepy yawn, Milo curled up in his leafy nest for a well-deserved nap.

stories.title: Max the Monkey's Big Red Ball
stories.text:
High up in the branches of a grand old mango tree lived Max. Max was a bouncy, playful little monkey who loved to play games more than anything else in the world. Today, Max had a brand-new toy. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! It was as red as a ripe strawberry and bounced higher than a jumping frog. Boing, boing, boing went the ball as Max tapped it with his little fuzzy paw. Max squealed with delight, his tail wagging back and forth like an excited puppy's.

Max wanted to share the fun with all of his jungle friends. He tucked the big red ball under his arm and scurried down the tree trunk. 'Who wants to play catch?' he called out happily. First, he saw Barnaby Bear, who was munching on some sweet clover. 'Look, Barnaby! Catch!' shouted Max, tossing the ball gently. Barnaby reached out his big, fluffy paws and caught it with a soft thud. 'Good catch!' cheered Max, clapping his hands. Barnaby rolled the ball right back to Max's feet. Roll, roll, roll!

Next, the ball bounced away and rolled toward Sammy Snake, who was resting in the warm sun. The ball tapped Sammy's tail gently. 'Boop!' laughed Max. Sammy smiled his best snake smile and gave the ball a gentle little nudge with his nose, sending it skittering across the soft grass. Max chased after it, running as fast as his little legs could carry him. Patters of tiny footprints left a trail in the dirt as he zoomed around a big green bush, giggling the whole time.

Suddenly, the big red ball bounced too far! It rolled right toward a muddy puddle. Oh no! Max gasped and hurried to catch it. With a splash, the ball landed right in the middle of the mud. Splat! Max stopped right at the edge of the puddle and looked down at his favorite toy. It had a little bit of mud on its shiny red side. Max picked it up, wiped it clean with a soft green leaf, and smiled. Playing with friends was the best fun ever, even when things got a little bit messy. With the clean ball safely in his paws, Max and his buddies played happily until the sun began to set, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors.

stories.title: Coco's Jungle Dance Party
stories.text:
Deep in the warm, leafy jungle, where the flowers bloomed in bright pinks and purples, lived a little monkey named Coco. Coco was known far and wide as the silliest dancer in the trees. While other monkeys liked to groom their fur or nap in the shade, Coco loved to move his feet! Whenever the wind blew through the leaves and made a rustling sound, Coco heard it as music. Shhh, shhh, went the wind, and Coco would start to wiggle his fingers and shake his fuzzy little hips.

One sunny afternoon, Coco decided it was time for a grand jungle dance party. He climbed up to the highest branch of the tallest tree and beat his chest like a little drum. Thump, thump, thump! 'It's time to dance!' he shouted down to the forest floor. Hearing the commotion, his friends began to gather around. Penny the parrot flew down first, landing gracefully on a branch. Then came Toby the tortoise, shuffling along very slowly, and Ellie the elephant, swinging her long trunk back and forth to the imaginary beat.

Coco yelled out his favorite dance moves for everyone to try together. 'First, we do the Monkey Hop!' he cried, bouncing up and down on one foot. Boing, boing, boing! All the animals tried their best to hop, even Toby the tortoise, who gave a tiny little lift of his shell. 'Next, we do the Wiggly Tail Shake!' Coco twirled around so fast his tail looked like a fuzzy brown propeller. The animals laughed out loud as they shook their tails, trunks, and wings in every single direction.

Finally, Coco shouted, 'Now, freeze like a statue!' Everyone stopped moving instantly. Penny froze with one wing in the air, Ellie froze with her trunk curled high, and Coco froze on one foot, looking wonderfully silly. They held still for three whole seconds before breaking into giggles and tumbling over in a heap of happy fur and feathers. The jungle had never heard such joyful laughter. Coco smiled a big, toothy monkey smile, knowing that dancing with friends made his heart feel as light as a floating feather. When the stars began to twinkle in the evening sky, the tired little dancers curled up together, dreaming of their next big jungle show.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text:
Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a very happy little monkey named Milo. Milo had soft brown fur, a long wiggly tail, and big, curious eyes that loved to look at everything. Every morning, the sun would peek through the tall trees, saying, 'Wake up, Milo!' And Milo would jump right out of his cozy leaf bed.

Today was a very special day because Milo found something wonderful. It was a bright yellow banana, but it was not just any ordinary banana. It was a magic banana! As soon as Milo touched it, the banana giggled. Tee-hee-hee! Milo giggled back. Ha-ha-ha!

'Let's play!' said the magic banana. Milo put the banana on his head like a silly hat. Then, he balanced it on his nose. Balance, balance, oh! It fell down into the soft green grass with a gentle plop.

Suddenly, the banana began to float. Up, up, up it went, right into the air. Milo leaped from branch to branch to catch it. Swing, swing, go! He grabbed the banana with his little furry hands and gave it a big hug.

'Thank you for the fun game,' Milo whispered. Since Milo was so kind and gentle, the magic banana did something extra special. It turned into a shower of sparkly golden stars that tickled Milo's toes. Milo laughed and clapped his hands together. Clap, clap, clap!

By now, the sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in pink and orange colors. Milo felt a big, sleepy yawn coming on. Yaaaawn! He climbed back up to his cozy leaf bed, curled up tight with his long tail wrapped around him, and closed his eyes. The jungle was quiet and peaceful. Goodnight, magic banana. Goodnight, little Milo. Sleep tight and sweet dreams in the warm jungle trees.

stories.title: Coco's Big Red Balloon
stories.text:
High up in the bouncy jungle canopy lived Coco the monkey. Coco loved to explore. Today, something bright and red was floating through the trees. It was a big, shiny red balloon! 

Coco swung down from a thick vine. Wheee! He reached out his little hand and gently grabbed the balloon string. Pop? No, it did not pop! It danced right in the breeze. Up and down, side to side, the red balloon swayed.

'Hello, red balloon,' said Coco with a big smile. He decided to take his new friend for a walk through the jungle. First, they visited Benny the brown bear. Benny waved his paw and said, 'Hello, Coco! Hello, red balloon!' The red balloon bobbed up and down like it was saying hello back.

Next, Coco and the balloon bounced over to the blue river. Splash, splash went the little fish in the water. Coco wanted to see if the balloon could swim. He held the string very carefully and dipped the balloon's bottom near the cool water. Tickle, tickle went the water splashes! Coco giggled and pulled the balloon back up into the warm air.

Soon, Coco's tummy started to rumble. Rumbly-tummy! It was time for a yummy snack. Coco found a bunch of sweet, yellow bananas hanging from a tree. He peeled one banana and took a big bite. Munch, munch, munch! He even shared a pretend bite with his red balloon friend.

As the afternoon breeze grew softer, Coco felt very cozy. He held the red balloon string tight in his furry hand, sat down on a soft patch of green moss, and watched the clouds drift by in the blue sky. It had been a wonderful day of adventure with his shiny red balloon. Coco closed his heavy eyes and drifted off to a happy nap in the gentle jungle breeze.

stories.title: Pip's Jungle Drum
stories.text:
Deep in the green, whispering jungle lived a little monkey named Pip. Pip had bright, sparkly eyes and feet that always wanted to tap, tap, tap. Pip loved making music all day long.

One sunny morning, Pip found a hollow, empty log lying on the ground. Tap, tap, tap went Pip's fingers on the log. Boom, boom, boom! It sounded just like a big drum! Pip grinned from ear to ear. He had found a jungle drum.

Soon, Pip started to play a fun rhythm. Tap-tap-tap, boom-boom-boom! Hearing the lovely music, all of Pip's jungle friends came running to see. Bella the bird flew down from the sky and tweeted a pretty song. Tweet, tweet, tweet! Sammy the snake slithered over and hummed a low, wiggly tune. Hmmm, hmmm, hmmm!

Pip played the drum faster. Tap, tap, tap! The animals danced around in a circle. The fuzzy little monkeys hopped up and down. Hop, hop, hop! The gentle elephants swayed their long trunks from side to side. Swish, swish, swish! Everyone was having so much fun making music together in the warm sunshine.

After a little while, the music slowed down. Slow, slow, slow. The animals were getting a little bit tired from all their dancing. Pip gave the drum one last gentle tap. Boomp! 

'That was wonderful,' said Bella the bird, flapping her wings happily. Pip gave his jungle drum a loving pat and smiled at all his good friends. It felt so nice to share music and laughter in the jungle. With the sun shining down through the leafy trees, Pip curled up on a soft branch, hugged his favorite log drum, and rested his happy little head. What a wonderful, musical day it had been for the little monkey and his friends.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy trees of the jungle, lived a little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, a long curly tail, and a very big tummy that loved to rumble. Every single morning, Milo would wake up, stretch his arms up high, and shout, 'Ooh-ooh-aah-aah! Time to play!' Milo had many animal friends in the jungle. There was Ellie the elephant, who loved to splash in the cool river, and Tessie the tiger, who loved to practice her loud ROAR. But Milo's absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world was bananas. Yellow bananas, sweet bananas, big bananas, and small bananas! One sunny morning, Milo swung from vine to vine, looking for his breakfast. He swung high, and he swung low. He did a little flip and a big hop. Suddenly, hanging from the very highest branch of the tallest tree, he saw something amazing. It was a giant, glowing yellow banana! It sparkled in the morning sun like a golden star. 'Ooh-ooh!' gasped Milo. 'That is the biggest banana I have ever seen!' But how would he reach it? It was too high for a normal jump. Milo scratched his furry head. He thought hard. Then, he had a wonderful idea! He called out to his friend Ellie. 'Ellie! Can you help me reach the magic banana?' Ellie smiled her big, friendly smile. She walked over to the tree and let Milo climb right up her long, gray trunk. Up, up, up went Milo, walking on Ellie's head. Still, he was a little bit too short! Then, Tessie the tiger trotted over. 'Hop on my back, little monkey!' she purred. Milo hopped from Ellie's head onto Tessie's soft back. Now he was much higher! Milo stretched out his long monkey arm. He stretched as far as he could go. Tip-toe, tip-toe, reach, reach, reach! SNAP! He plucked the giant banana right off the branch. Milo tumbled down, laughing and giggling, landing safely in a soft pile of green leaves with the giant banana safely in his paws. 'Thank you, my friends!' cheered Milo. Instead of eating the whole thing by himself, Milo peeled the giant banana and shared it with Ellie and Tessie. They all sat together in the warm jungle sunshine, munching happily and making silly monkey noises. It was the best breakfast ever. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Milo curled up in his cozy nest of leaves, wrapped his long tail around himself, and fell fast asleep, dreaming of sweet yellow bananas. The end.

stories.title: Milo Learns to Share
stories.text: Deep in the whispering jungle, where the flowers bloomed bright red and purple, lived a cheerful little monkey named Coco. Coco had fluffy brown fur, cheeks that puffed out when he chewed, and a collection of wonderful toys. He had a shiny red ball that bounced super high, a drum that went bang-bang-bang, and a little wooden car that zoomed across the dirt paths. Coco loved his toys more than anything. He loved them so much that he did not like to share them with anyone else. One sunny afternoon, Coco was sitting under a shady banana tree, playing with his shiny red ball. He was tossing it up and catching it, giggling to himself. Just then, along came Pip. Pip was a tiny baby monkey with big ears and big, sad eyes. Pip walked up to Coco, pointed at the ball, and made a quiet little squeak, asking to play. Coco immediately hugged the ball tightly to his furry chest. He frowned and shook his head. 'No, no, no!' said Coco. 'This is my ball! You cannot play with it.' Pip looked down at his tiny feet, turned around, and slowly hopped away, looking very sad indeed. Coco watched him go, but he didn't feel happy. He tried to bounce his shiny red ball, but it bounced right into a bush and got stuck. He tried to play his drum, but a stick broke. Suddenly, playing all by himself wasn't fun anymore. Coco felt a little flutter in his tummy. He realized that playing alone is quite lonely. He looked over at Pip, who was sitting by a puddle, trying to draw circles in the mud with a little twig. Coco took a deep breath. He knew what he had to do to fix things. He walked over to the bush, tugged hard, and pulled the shiny red ball free. Then, with a gentle smile, Coco skipped over to baby Pip. 'Do you want to roll the ball with me?' asked Coco softly. Pip's big ears perked up. His eyes opened wide, and a huge, bright smile spread across his little monkey face. 'Ooh-ooh!' he cheered happily. They sat down in the soft grass and rolled the ball back and forth, back and forth, laughing and squealing with delight. The ball rolled fast, and the ball rolled slow. Coco discovered something wonderful. Sharing his toys didn't make him have less fun; it made the fun twice as big! From that day on, Coco and Pip shared all their games, toys, and snacks. The jungle echoed with their happy laughter as they swung through the trees together, best friends forever. The end.

stories.title: Milo's Bedtime Jungle
stories.text: The sun was slowly sinking behind the tall green mountains, painting the evening sky in shades of purple and gold. The daytime animals were yawning, stretching, and getting ready for bed. High up in the branches of the great banyan tree, little monkey Barnaby was wide awake. Barnaby had bright, curious eyes and a tail that liked to wiggle when he was excited. 'I am not sleepy!' Barnaby told the twinkling stars. 'Not even a little bit!' His mother gave him a warm, gentle nuzzle. 'It is time to rest your paws, my little monkey,' she whispered softly. 'Let us take a quiet walk through the sleepy jungle before bed.' Barnaby grabbed his mother's warm, furry hand, and they began to walk softly through the branches. First, they tiptoed past the big river. There sat Ellie the elephant, curled up in the soft mud, fast asleep and softly snoring. *Purr-shoo, purr-shoo,* went Ellie. Barnaby giggled quietly. Next, they tiptoed past the tall bamboo stalks. There hung sleepy bats, dangling upside down with their tiny wings wrapped around them like cozy little blankets. They were dreaming sweet dreams of the night sky. Barnaby whispered, 'Good night, little bats.' Further down the path, they saw Tessie the tiger. Tessie was curled up into a big, orange-and-black furry ball, breathing slowly and deeply. *In and out, in and out.* The jungle was becoming quieter and quieter. The crickets began to sing a gentle bedtime song. *Chirp, chirp, chirp,* went the crickets, like a lullaby made just for the trees. Barnaby started to feel a heavy, sleepy feeling in his eyelids. He blinked once, he blinked twice, and then he gave a very big monkey yawn. *Yaaawn!* His mother scooped him up into her arms and carried him back to their cozy nest made of soft leaves and warm moss. She tucked him in snugly, wrapping his long tail around him like a warm blanket. She gently stroked his furry head and hummed a sweet, soothing tune. Barnaby looked up at the bright moon shining through the leaves. He felt so safe, so warm, and so very loved. His eyes drifted closed. He let out one last tiny yawn and fell fast asleep, dreaming of swinging through the green jungle stars. The end.

stories.title: Milo's Magic Banana
stories.text: Once upon a time, high up in the green, leafy jungle, lived a very happy little monkey named Milo. Milo had big brown eyes, soft brown fur, and a tail that could curl just like a question mark. Every morning, the sun would wake up, stretch its golden rays, and say good morning to the jungle. Milo would stretch too. Big stretch up high! Big stretch down low! Milo loved his jungle home because there were so many tall trees to climb and so many furry friends to play with. One sunny Tuesday, Milo was swinging through the branches when he spotted something very special sitting on a large green leaf. It was a bright yellow banana, but it was not just any ordinary banana. It was sparkling with tiny, twinkling silver stars! Milo blinked once. He blinked twice. Wow! A magic banana! Milo gently picked up the shiny banana and gave it a little sniff. It smelled like sweet honey and warm sunshine. Just as he touched the peel, the banana whispered, 'Milo, find a friend and share!' Milo knew exactly what to do. He swung through the vines as fast as he could, making happy chatter noises. 'Ee-ee-ah-ah!' he called out. Soon, he found his best friend, a little green parrot named Pip, who was resting on a branch. 'Hello, Pip!' chirped Milo, holding out the sparkling fruit. Pip fluttered his colorful wings and chirped happily. 'For me?' he asked. Milo nodded and peeled back the bright yellow skin. They both took a big bite. Suddenly, a shower of golden sparkles rained down on them! The sparkles tickled their tummies and made them giggle uncontrollably. 'Hee-hee-hee! Ho-ho-ho!' they laughed. The magic banana tasted like delicious strawberry ice cream. From that day on, Milo and Pip knew that the best magic in the whole wide jungle wasn't the sparkling fruit itself, but the joy of sharing a treat with a very good friend. Milo curled his tail, gave one last happy wave, and curled up for a cozy jungle nap.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Deep in the whispering bamboo forest, there lived a curious little monkey named Barnaby. Barnaby had fluffy ears that wiggled whenever he heard a funny sound. Today, Barnaby heard a very interesting sound. Boing! Boing! Boing! What could that be? Barnaby scampered down his favorite tree trunk, pattering his little feet against the soft moss. He peeked behind a large fern, and there it was. A big, round, shiny red ball! It was the brightest red Barnaby had ever seen. The ball rolled a little bit. Boing! Barnaby clapped his hands with glee. 'A play toy!' he chattered. Barnaby reached out and gave the ball a gentle tap with his paw. The ball rolled forward, and Barnaby chased after it, giggling all the way. He hopped over a tiny rock and slid under a low-hanging vine. The red ball bounced right toward his friend, Ellie the Elephant. Ellie had a big grey trunk and the kindest eyes in the forest. 'Hello, Barnaby!' trumpeted Ellie softly. 'Would you like to play catch?' Barnaby nodded eagerly. 'Ooh-ooh! Yes, please!' he replied in monkey talk. Ellie used her long trunk to scoop up the big red ball. She gave it a gentle puff of air, sending it floating gracefully through the warm jungle air. Whew! Right back to Barnaby. Barnaby caught the ball in his furry arms and tumbled down onto the soft grass, laughing a big, happy belly laugh. They played catch for a long, long time until the sun began to turn orange and purple in the evening sky. Barnaby hugged the big red ball tight and whispered, 'Good game, red ball.' Then, hand in hand with Ellie, he walked back to his tree, ready for sweet dreams and happy playtime adventures tomorrow.

stories.title: Coco's Counting Jungle
stories.text: Good morning, little ones! Meet Coco. Coco is a tiny monkey with a very bouncy tail and a big, bright smile. Today is a very special day because Coco is going on a counting adventure through the sunny jungle, and he wants you to come along! Are you ready? Let us count together! First, Coco swings through the trees until he stops on a branch. Let us look up. How many warm yellow suns are shining in the sky? Just one! Can you point to the sky and say one? Great job! Coco climbs a little higher and hears a buzzing sound. Buzz, buzz! He looks closely at a fuzzy flower. How many busy bumblebees are drinking sweet nectar? Let us count them. One, two! Two fuzzy bees flying round and round. Can you buzz like a bee? Bzzzz! Next, Coco scurries down to the sparkling blue river to wash his paws. Who is swimming in the water? Let us look. One, two, three! Three friendly little fish are splashing around, making tiny bubbles. Pop, pop, pop! Can you make fish lips? Very good! As Coco continues his walk, he looks up at a tall coconut tree. He scratches his head and wonders how many big brown coconuts are resting at the top. Let us count them out loud. One, two, three, four! Four round coconuts just waiting for a breeze. Wow, we are doing so well! Finally, Coco sits down in a cozy patch of green grass to rest his little feet. Who comes hopping over to say hello? One, two, three, four, five! Five cute little frogs sitting on a log. They all look at Coco and say, 'Ribbit!' Coco smiles and claps his hands. One sun, two bees, three fish, four coconuts, and five frogs. That is a wonderful number adventure! Coco gives a happy wave and says, 'Thank you for counting with me today! See you next time, little friends!'

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Swing
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Swing your tail for happy me.
Climb up high and touch the sky,
Wave to birds that flutter by.

Jump from branch to leafy vine,
Look the sun is shining fine.
Eat a snack that tastes so sweet,
Bananas are a yummy treat.

Scratch your head and make a sound,
Ooh and ahh and look around.
Tickle toes and wiggle ears,
Cheer away the sleepy tears.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for monkey go to sleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy jungle bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Play
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys jumping high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
One little monkey starts to squeak,
Playing games of hide and seek.

Two little monkeys dance around,
Stomping feet upon the ground.
Three little monkeys clap their hands,
Dancing through the jungle lands.

Four little monkeys spin and twirl,
Watching all the green leaves swirl.
Five little monkeys shout hooray,
We have had a happy day.

Now the jungle grows so still,
Moonlight shines upon the hill.
Cuddle close and hold on tight,
Sleep well, monkeys, through the night.

rhymes.title: Monkey Choo, Monkey Chew
rhymes.text:
Monkey, monkey, what do you do?
I find snacks that are yummy too.
Peel a yellow banana wide,
See the sweet white fruit inside.

Monkey, monkey, up so high,
Watching clouds float in the sky.
Swing your arms and shout out loud,
Make your monkey family proud.

Find a coconut on the floor,
Roll it right up to my door.
Tap it gently, hear the sound,
Rolling all across the ground.

Time to rest your furry feet,
Wrap your tail and go to sleep.
Dream of vines and sunny days,
In so many happy ways.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Brushing Teeth
rhymes.text:
Little monkey, bright and gay,
Brushes teeth to start the day.
Up and down and all around,
Making not a single sound.

Grab the brush with bristles blue,
Put on paste, just like a zoo.
Squeeze a little drop of white,
Make each tooth shine clean and bright.

Brush the top and brush the low,
Watch the foamy bubbles grow.
Spit it out into the sink,
Faster than a rapid blink.

Now your smile is shining wide,
With a happy roar inside.
Jump into the morning sun,
Brush your teeth, oh what fun!

rhymes.title: Monkey Time for Bed
rhymes.text:
Little monkey, time for sleep,
Count the furry little sheep.
Stars are shining in the sky,
Moon is glowing way up high.

Put away your toys and blocks,
Take off shoes and fuzzy socks.
Climb into your cozy bed,
Rest your tired little head.

Wrap yourself in blankets warm,
Safe and snug from any storm.
Close your big brown sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

Dream of jungle trees so green,
Best adventures ever seen.
Slumber softly through the night,
Till the morning golden light.

rhymes.title: Monkey and the Rain
rhymes.text:
Pitter-patter falls the rain,
On the jungle windowpane.
Little monkey looks outside,
Where can little monkeys hide?

Grab a yellow polka dot,
Wear a funny little hat.
Step outside into the breeze,
Splashing by the forest trees.

Splash in puddles on the ground,
Make a happy squishy sound.
Jumping high and jumping low,
Watch the muddy water go.

Rainbow shining in the blue,
Smiling at the world and you.
Monkey dances in the sun,
Rainy days are so much fun!

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Cheeks
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Swing your arms for you and me.
Catch a vine and leap so high,
Way up in the bright blue sky.
Jump up down upon the ground,
Make a happy monkey sound.
Ooh ooh aah aah hear him shout,
See what he is all about.
Climb a branch to find a treat,
Something yummy, nice and sweet.
Yellow banana in his hand,
Bestest monkey in the land.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little monks to go.
Curl your tail and close your eyes,
Sleep beneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Swing
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys playing in a tree,
Swinging through the branches, wild and free.
One little monkey lets go of the vine,
Lands on the grass and is doing just fine.
Four little monkeys laughing out loud,
Showing their tricks to the jungle crowd.
Two little monkeys race to the top,
Trying to see who will be the first to stop.
Three little monkeys munching on a pear,
Dropping sweet pieces down in the air.
Four little monkeys jumping up and down,
Best little jumpers all through the town.
Now all the monkeys are ready for bed,
Pillows of moss underneath every head.
Sleep little monkeys until the new light,
Whispering softly to you, sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: Monkey See, Monkey Do
rhymes.text:
Monkey see and monkey do,
Can you hop like bunnies do?
Scratch your tummy, tap your head,
Time to jump upon the bed.
Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Find a banana to be your treat.
Swing your arms from side to side,
Take a fun and bouncy ride.
Make a funny monkey face,
Run around the leafy place.
Spin in circles round and round,
Sit right down upon the ground.
Now be quiet, make no sound,
Peace and quiet all around.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to snuggle in your bed.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Swing
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Won't you come and play with me?
Swing your arms and count to three,
Happy as a monkey can be.

Jump up high into the air,
Throw a banana way up there.
Catch it with a happy stare,
Showing off your furry hair.

Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Monkey food is very sweet.
Tickle toes and find a seat,
This is quite a jungle treat.

Now the sun is going down,
Put away your monkey frown.
Sleepy time in jungle town,
Rest your head upon the ground.

rhymes.title: Cheeky Monkey Chat
rhymes.text:
Cheeky monkey, brown and small,
Can you climb the jungle wall?
Up and down and all around,
Never staying on the ground.

Pick a fruit and take a bite,
Chewing softly through the night.
Big round eyes so shiny bright,
Bathed in golden morning light.

Scratch your tummy, make a sound,
Spinning round and round and round.
Best banana ever found,
Dropping softly to the ground.

Waving bye to all your friends,
Where the leafy jungle ends.
Now the sleepy story bends,
And the happy playtime ends.

rhymes.title: Monkey See, Monkey Do
rhymes.text:
Monkey see and monkey do,
I can jump just high like you!
Touch your nose and wiggle toes,
Follow where the river flows.

Swing across the wooden vine,
Everything is looking fine.
Drink some water, cool and sweet,
Dancing with your fuzzy feet.

Make a funny monkey face,
Running in a little race.
Find a cozy hiding place,
Smile and use a gentle grace.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little birds are flying by.
Close your eyes and do not cry,
Monkey lullaby, goodbye.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Jump
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Won't you come and play with me?
Swing your tail from left to right,
Keep on smiling, big and bright.

Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Find a yummy fruit to eat.
Up above the jungle floor,
Let's go looking for some more.

Jump up high and touch the sky,
Wave to birds that flutter by.
Now it's time to rest your head,
Cuddle in your leafy bed.

Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars shine down so deep.
Dream of jungle games to play,
Until comes another day.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Swing
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys swinging in the breeze,
Laughing and playing high up in the trees.
One little monkey goes ooh-ooh and ah-ah,
Running along with his mama and papa.

Two little monkeys munching on a pear,
Tossing sweet pieces high up in the air.
Three little monkeys splashing in the lake,
Making big ripples for the ducks to make.

Four little monkeys dancing on the grass,
Watching the beautiful butterflies pass.
Five little monkeys curling up to rest,
Sleeping together in their cozy nest.

Now the bright moon is shining up above,
Filled with sweet dreams and a whole lot of love.
Whisper good night to the stars so bright,
Sleep tight, little monkeys, until morning light.

rhymes.title: Monkey See, Monkey Do
rhymes.text:
Monkey see and monkey do,
I can hop and so can you!
Touch your nose and touch your toes,
Wiggle fingers, wiggle nose.

Reach way up to catch a star,
Travel near and travel far.
Spin around and take a bow,
Sit right down and listen now.

Monkey laughs and monkey plays,
Happy through the sunny days.
Scratch your tummy, make a sound,
Roll together on the ground.

Now the day is almost done,
We are finished having fun.
Yawn a little, close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Swing
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Swinging wild and swinging free.
Up above the jungle floor,
Asking for a banana more.

Catch a vine with hands and feet,
Looking for a tasty treat.
Up and down and all around,
Never touching dusty ground.

Clap your paws and count to three,
Laughing loud and full of glee.
Now the sun begins to set,
Best day yet, you can bet.

Time to sleep and rest your head,
Curled up in your leafy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sigh,
Little monkey, lullaby.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Play
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys jumping high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
One fell down and bumped his head,
Mama put him right to bed.

Four little monkeys swinging low,
Watch the gentle breezes blow.
One climbed up a tall bamboo,
Playing games with me and you.

Three little monkeys eating pear,
Juicy drops are in the air.
One shared half with furry bear,
Showing love and showing care.

Two little monkeys peek and play,
Having fun throughout the day.
Now they sleep until the dawn,
Night-night, monkeys, sleep on.

rhymes.title: Monkey Business
rhymes.text:
Monkey, monkey, climb so high,
Reaching for the butterfly.
Orange peel and yellow skin,
Let the monkey game begin.

Tickle tummy, tickle toes,
Touch your little furry nose.
Scratch your head and make a face,
Running all around the place.

Beat the drum and shake the tree,
Dance a happy jig with me.
Jump up high and shout hooray,
For another sunny day.

Stars are shining bright and clear,
Bedtime is approaching near.
Snuggle close and drift away,
Dreaming of another day.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Swing
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Swinging wild and swinging free.
Reach up high and touch the sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.

Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Monkey snacks are yummy sweet.
Eat a banana, peel it down,
Best little monkey in the town.

Jump around from vine to vine,
Sun is warm and weather's fine.
Tickle toes and shake your head,
Time to bounce back to your bed.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.
Dream of jungle fun all night,
Until morning brings the light.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Jumping
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys jumping high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
One fell down and bumped his head,
Mama put him right to bed.

Four little monkeys swinging low,
Watch them tumble to and fro.
One fell down and bumped his nose,
Showing all his funny toes.

Three little monkeys acting grand,
Dancing on the golden sand.
One fell down and bumped his knee,
Crying underneath the tree.

Two little monkeys left to play,
Chasing all the clouds away.
One fell down and bumped his chin,
Time to let the sleep begin.

rhymes.title: Monkey See, Monkey Do
rhymes.text:
Monkey see and monkey do,
I can jump around like you.
Touch your nose and blink your eyes,
Look around with great surprise.

Scratch your head and beat your drum,
Suck a sticky sugar plum.
Make a funny monkey face,
Spin around in one big space.

Clap your hands with joyful sound,
Stomp your feet upon the ground.
Give a hug and squeeze so tight,
Everything is feeling right.

Now be quiet, make no noise,
Rest your little girls and boys.
Sleepy monkey, soft and deep,
Now it's time to fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Swing
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Swinging wild and swinging free.
Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Jungle life is oh so sweet.

Reach up high to touch the sky,
Watch the little bluebirds fly.
Grab a vine and take a leap,
While the lazy lions sleep.

Eat a yummy yellow snack,
Scratch your fuzzy little back.
Turn around and touch the ground,
Make a happy monkey sound.

Now the sun is going down,
Quiet shadows wrap the town.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to crawl into your bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Jumping
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys jumping high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
One fell down and bumped his head,
Mama put him right to bed.

Four little monkeys jumping low,
Moving fast and watching go.
One tripped up and hurt his knee,
Crying underneath the tree.

Three little monkeys jumping round,
Making such a funny sound.
One got dizzy, lost his place,
Landed with a silly face.

Two little monkeys left to play,
Jumping all throughout the day.
Now they stop and wave goodbye,
Watching stars light up the sky.

rhymes.title: Monkey Business
rhymes.text:
Monkey, monkey, looking round,
Can you touch the grassy ground?
Monkey, monkey, turn around,
Make a happy chatter sound.

Climb a tree both tall and green,
Best little climber ever seen.
Find a banana sweet and bright,
Peel it back and take a bite.

Tickle your tummy with your paw,
Show me your big, friendly jaw.
Wave your long tail in the air,
Jump without a single care.

Now the playtime fun is through,
Time to rest your fingers too.
Snuggle tight and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Jump
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Won't you jump and play with me?
Climb up high and swing around,
Never touch the grassy ground.

Catch a banana sweet and bright,
Eat it up with great delight.
Scratch your tummy, make a sound,
Jump right back upon the ground.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day you will not forget.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars begin to peep.

Dream of vines and jungle trees,
Dancing softly in the breeze.
Good-night, monkey, sleep till dawn,
When the new day sparkles on.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Monkeys
rhymes.text:
Ten little monkeys swinging on a vine,
One falls off and now there's nine.
Nine little monkeys playing peek-a-boo,
One runs away and leaves just two.

Wait a minute, let's count fast,
Counting monkeys is a blast!
One, two, three and four and five,
Glad to be so much alive.

Six and seven, jump so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Eight and nine, now spin around,
Ten go tumbling to the ground.

Now they giggle, now they cheer,
Best little monkeys all the year.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
Time to rest and end the day.

rhymes.title: Monkey Business
rhymes.text:
Monkey wears a furry hat,
Sitting on a fuzzy mat.
Eating peanuts one by one,
Having lots of silly fun.

Wiggle ears and twitch your nose,
Tickle all your little toes.
Make a funny monkey face,
Spin around and win the race.

Swing from branch to leafy tree,
As happy as a bird can be.
Point your finger at the sky,
Wave a happy wave goodbye.

Now the playtime comes to rest,
Sleeping in a cozy nest.
Stars are shining bright and deep,
Monkey is now fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Brrr
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in a tree,
Swinging wild and swinging free.
Climbing up and jumping down,
Best jumper in all the town.

Yellow banana sweet and bright,
Eating every single bite.
Curling up his fuzzy tail,
Sailing like a happy whale.

Now the sun begins to hide,
Monkey sleeps and feels inside.
Softly dreaming in the night,
Till the morning brings the light.

Ooh ooh aah aah hear him say,
Time to rest after the play.
Good night monkey sleep so deep,
Stars are watch for you to keep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Monkeys Swinging
rhymes.text:
Five little monkeys swinging high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
One little monkey shouts out loud,
Waving to the jungle crowd.

Four little monkeys play a game,
Calling out each other's name.
Jumping from a leafy vine,
Everything is looking fine.

Three little monkeys clap their hands,
Dancing to the jungle bands.
Two little monkeys start to run,
Having so much happy fun.

One little monkey left behind,
Best little friend you'll ever find.
Now they curl up in their bed,
Resting every sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Monkey Business
rhymes.text:
Monkey holds a shiny prize,
Wonder shining in his eyes.
Tickle tickle on his toes,
Where the little monkey goes.

Hop along and skip around,
Touching lightly on the ground.
Funny faces he can make,
Just for his mama's sake.

Big green leaves of jungle trees,
Dancing in the cooling breeze.
Reaching for a yummy treat,
Tasting something very sweet.

Time to cuddle time to rest,
Sleeping in a cozy nest.
Close your eyes and do not peep,
Monkey is now fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Jump
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Won't you come and play with me?
Jump up high and touch the sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.

Swing your arms and shake your tail,
Sailing on a wooden sail.
Climb a branch and count to four,
Now let's do a little more.

Clap your hands and beat your drum,
See the happy jungle come.
Eat a yummy banana snack,
Ride upon an elephant's back.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.

rhymes.title: Five Cheeky Monkeys
rhymes.text:
Five cheeky monkeys swinging low,
Where they go, they do not know.
One grabs a vine and gives a shout,
That is what they're all about.

Two little monkeys munch a pear,
Juicy drops are in the air.
Three little monkeys tap their toes,
Right upon their furry nose.

Four little monkeys make a sound,
Jumping softly on the ground.
Five little monkeys laugh and play,
Having fun throughout the day.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little monkeys fall asleep.
Dreaming of the jungle green,
Best adventures ever seen.

rhymes.title: Monkey See, Monkey Do
rhymes.text:
Monkey see and monkey do,
I can wiggle ears like you!
Stomp your feet and beat a drum,
Listen to the jungle hum.

Scratch your tummy, make a smile,
Rest and sit here for a while.
Reach up high to catch a star,
Wonder how it travels far.

Turn around and touch the floor,
Open up the wooden door.
Give a hug and wave goodbye,
As the little birds fly by.

Now the moon is bright and round,
Not a single busy sound.
Wrap your tail and snuggle tight,
Sleep until the morning light.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Jump
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Jumping high for all to see.
Swing your arms and count to three,
Happy as a monkey can be.

Climb up high and touch the sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.
Wave a friendly little bye,
As the birds begin to fly.

Makes you giggle, makes you grin,
Let the monkey game begin.
Clap your hands and spin around,
Stomp your feet upon the ground.

Now it is time to take a rest,
Snuggling is the very best.
Close your eyes and softly sigh,
Little monkey, lullaby.

rhymes.title: Banana Treat
rhymes.text:
Hungry monkey wants a snack,
Sitting on a leafy track.
Peel the yellow skin away,
Eating yummy food today.

Munch and crunch and bite it down,
Walking all around the town.
Tummy happy, feeling bright,
Eating until it is night.

Sweet and tasty, oh so good,
Just like every monkey should.
Rub your tummy, lick your lips,
Swaying your sweet little hips.

Now the snack is gone and done,
We have had so much fun.
Time to curl up in your bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.

rhymes.title: Jungle Swing
rhymes.text:
Swing, swing, through the vine,
Jungle weather is so fine.
Monkey plays from side to side,
Taking such a joyful ride.

Reach your hands up in the air,
Monkey has hair everywhere.
Laughing loud with all his friends,
Playing till the daytime ends.

Jump down low and leap up high,
Touching stars up in the sky.
Spinning round and round around,
Landing safely on the ground.

Stars are shining in the deep,
Monkey is now fast asleep.
Dreams of trees and jungle green,
Sweetest monkey ever seen.

rhymes.title: Little Monkey Brrr
rhymes.text:
Little monkey in the tree,
Won't you come and play with me?
Swing your arms and count to three,
Happy as a monkey can be.

Climb up high and touch the sky,
Watch the birds go flying by.
Eat a snack that's sweet and round,
Then jump down upon the ground.

Tickle toes and scratch your head,
Time to sleep in leafy bed.
Close your eyes and rest your feet,
Dreaming of a monkey treat.

Morning comes with golden sun,
Time to start a day of fun.
