It was truly a wonderful morning for a little bear who loved honey so much. The end!

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Rainy Day
stories.text:
Pitter-patter, pitter-patter! Raindrops were falling from the big grey clouds high up in the sky. Barnaby Bear looked out his little round window and pressed his wet black nose right against the cool glass. 'Oh no,' said Barnaby with a little frown. 'It is raining outside, and I cannot go out to play in the sunny meadow.' He wanted to chase butterflies and run through the green grass.

Barnaby sat on his cozy rug and thought about what to do on a rainy day. Suddenly, his furry ears perked right up. 'I know!' he exclaimed with a happy grin. 'I can build a giant castle right here inside my warm den!' Barnaby scurried around his room collecting all his favorite things. He grabbed three fluffy yellow pillows, two big blue blankets, and a stack of soft cushions from his armchair.

He dragged the first pillow over to the corner. Then, he draped the big blue blankets over the wooden chairs to make a secret roof. 'Heave-ho!' pushed Barnaby, crawling underneath his brand new blanket fort. It was dark and cozy inside, just like a cave for a little bear. Barnaby brought in his favorite fuzzy toy rabbit and sat him right in the middle of the soft cushions. 'Welcome to my castle, little rabbit!' whispered Barnaby.

Soon, Barnaby heard a friendly knock on his wooden front door. Knock, knock, knock! Barnaby peeked his furry head out from under the blue blanket and scurried over to open the door. Standing on the porch was his good friend, Little Badger. Little Badger was wearing a shiny yellow raincoat and shiny red boots. 'Can I come inside your warm house?' asked Little Badger, shaking the raindrops off his fur.

'Come right in!' said Barnaby happily. The two little friends crawled inside the cozy blanket fort together. They played with wooden blocks, stacked them up high, and watched them tumble down with a loud crash. 'Crash!' they laughed, clapping their paws together with glee. They listened to the gentle rain falling outside on the roof—tap, tap, tap—while they stayed warm and dry inside. When the rain finally stopped and a bright rainbow appeared in the sky, Barnaby and Little Badger went outside to splash in the puddles. It was the best rainy day ever!

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, deep in the green and leafy woods, lived a little brown bear named Barnaby. Barnaby had soft, fuzzy ears, a shiny black nose, and a very big tummy that loved sweet honey. Today, Barnaby woke up with a big yawn. 'Yawn-o-saurus!' he whispered to himself, stretching his furry arms way up high to touch the ceiling of his cozy cave.

'Today is a day for an adventure,' Barnaby said, putting on his favorite red boots. Tap, tap, tap went his boots as he stepped outside into the warm sunshine. The forest was full of wonderful sounds. The bluebirds were singing sweet songs in the tall oak trees, and the little stream was going 'gurgle, gurgle, splash' as it rushed over smooth, round stones.

Barnaby walked along the winding dirt path, looking for something fun to do. Soon, he heard a funny sound coming from behind a big green bush. 'Hee-hee-hee! Wheee!' It sounded like someone having a wonderful time. Barnaby tiptoed over, peeking around the leaves. There sat a little yellow duckling with bright orange flippers. The duckling was trying to jump over a tiny puddle, but every time he tried, he fell right into the water with a plop!

'Oh dear,' said Barnaby in his deepest, friendliest bear voice. 'Do you need some help?'

The little duckling blinked his round black eyes and quacked happily. 'Quack, quack! I want to jump across, but my legs are too short!'

Barnaby smiled a big, toothless bear smile. 'I have very long legs,' he said kindly. 'Hold onto my paw, and we can jump together.'

The little duckling grabbed Barnaby's big furry paw. One, two, three, jump! They sailed right over the puddle and landed safely on the other side. 'Hooray!' cheered the duckling, flapping his wings. 'My name is Ducky!'

'And my name is Barnaby Bear,' said Barnaby. From that moment on, Barnaby and Ducky were the best of friends. They spent the whole afternoon playing hide-and-seek behind the ferns, chasing floating autumn leaves, and sharing a delicious snack of crunchy berries. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby gave Ducky a gentle hug. 'Goodbye, my new friend,' Barnaby said. 'Let's play again tomorrow.' Barnaby walked back to his cozy cave with a very happy heart, ready for sweet dreams after such a wonderful day.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Honey Pot
stories.text:
Deep in the whispering woods, where the moss grew thick and soft, lived Barnaby Bear. Barnaby was a happy little bear with fur the color of toasted marshmallows. More than anything in the whole wide world, Barnaby loved sweet, sticky honey. He loved it on toast, he loved it in a bowl, and sometimes he just loved to lick it right off his furry paws.

One bright Tuesday morning, Barnaby woke up with a rumbling in his tummy. 'Rumble, rumble, growl,' went his tummy. 'It is time for breakfast,' thought Barnaby. He hopped right out of his bed, rubbed his sleepy eyes, and trotted over to his kitchen shelf. But oh, oh, oh! The shelf was completely empty! His big clay pot of honey was totally, absolutely gone.

'Where could my honey be?' wondered Barnaby, scratching his furry head. He looked under the table. No honey there. He looked inside his wooden toy chest. Just a squeaky duck and some shiny marbles. Suddenly, Barnaby saw a tiny trail of golden drops on the floorboards. Drip, drop, drip went the trail, leading right out the front door and into the sunny garden.

'A clue!' whispered Barnaby excitedly. He put on his thinking cap—which was just a silly green leaf perched between his ears—and followed the sticky yellow path. The trail led past the big red rosebush where the busy bees were buzzing. Bzzz, bzzz, went the bees. Then, the trail led around the old oak tree where the squirrels played tag.

Barnaby tiptoed quietly, following the golden drips. The trail stopped right in front of a hollow log. Barnaby bent down and peeked inside. Two big, bright eyes blinked back at him. Then, a little voice giggled, 'Peek-a-boo!'

Out popped Barnaby's little cousin, Pip. Pip had honey smeared all over his chin, from one furry ear to the other! 'I found your honey, Barnaby,' giggled Pip. 'I wanted to make you a surprise breakfast.'

Barnaby looked at the empty pot and then at his funny little cousin. Instead of being cross, Barnaby laughed a big, belly-laugh that shook the leaves on the trees. 'Well, little cousin,' smiled Barnaby, scooping up a tiny bit of leftover honey with his finger and dotting it right on Pip's nose. 'Next time, we can share the surprise!' They sat down together in the warm grass and giggled, licking their paws until they were clean.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Goes to Sleep
stories.text:
The sun was slowly sinking behind the purple mountains, painting the evening sky with strokes of pink and lavender. High up in the tall pine trees, the little birds tucked their heads beneath their wings and whispered goodnight. Down in the soft green meadow, the flowers closed their sleepy petals.

In his cozy cave, Barnaby Bear gave a giant, jaw-cracking yawn. 'Hooo-ahhh,' yawned Barnaby, rubbing his tired eyes with his knuckles. His furry arms felt heavy, and his big brown legs felt like they were made of sleepy-time lead. Playing all day with his forest friends had been wonderful, but now it was time to rest.

First, Barnaby needed to get ready for bed. He tiptoed to the bathroom and brushed his sharp little teeth. Brush, brush, brush went the toothbrush, making lots of bubbly foam. Then, Barnaby washed his paws in a bowl of warm water, splashing just a tiny bit on the floor. 'Oopsie daisy,' he giggled softly.

Next, Barnaby put on his favorite pajamas. They were bright blue with little yellow moons and twinkling silver stars all over them. He slipped his furry arms through the sleeves and pulled the soft cotton up to his chin. He looked just like a little sleepy astronaut ready to float into dreamland.

Barnaby walked over to his bed. His bed wasn't made of metal or wood; it was made of a huge, fluffy pile of dry autumn leaves and soft, sweet-smelling moss. Barnaby fluffed his pillow, which was stuffed with soft dandelion fluff. He climbed in and wiggled around until he found the most comfortable spot.

'Is everything cozy?' whispered Barnaby to his favorite stuffed toy, a little cloth bunny named Barnaby Jr. The bunny didn't answer, but his button eyes seemed to shine with love. Barnaby pulled his warm blanket right up to his chin. The cave was quiet and safe. Outside, the gentle night wind blew through the trees, singing a soft lullaby. *Hush-a-bye, little bear, sleep until the morning light.* Barnaby closed his eyes. His breathing slow and steady—in and out, in and out. Within a minute, Barnaby Bear was fast asleep, dreaming of honey pots and flying stars. Goodnight, Barnaby.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Once upon a time, deep in the green and leafy woods, lived a little brown bear named Barnaby. Barnaby had soft, fluffy fur, two round ears, and a very big tummy that loved sweet honey. Every morning, Barnaby would wake up, stretch his arms way up high, and say, "Good morning, sun!" Today was a very special day because Barnaby wanted to find a brand-new friend to play with.

First, Barnaby trotted down the grassy path. He saw a busy little squirrel jumping up and down in a tall oak tree. "Hello, squirrel!" called Barnaby in his deepest, friendliest bear voice. The squirrel chattered, dropped an acorn, and quickly zipped away to hide. Oh, thought Barnaby, maybe the squirrel is playing hide-and-seek. But Barnaby was too big to fit in the tiny tree hollow, so he kept on walking.

Next, Barnaby waddled over to the sparkling blue river. Splish, splash, splash! A little green frog was jumping on the lily pads. "Ribbit, ribbit!" sang the frog. Barnaby tried to jump like the frog. He bent his knees, went boing, and landed right in a muddy puddle! Squish, squatch, went the mud between his toes. Barnaby giggled. Splashing in mud was fun, but the frog hopped away to catch a fly, leaving Barnaby all by himself again.

Just as Barnaby began to feel a little bit lonely, he heard a soft rustling in the berry bushes. Rustle, rustle, munch, munch. Barnaby peeked behind the leaves and saw another little bear! This bear had patches on her knees and a bright yellow flower tucked right behind her furry ear. "Hello," said the little bear with a warm smile. "My name is Bella."

"I am Barnaby!" said Barnaby happily. "Do you want to play?" Bella nodded her head eagerly. Together, the two little bears shared a sweet red strawberry, chased each other around a big mossy rock, and rolled down the grassy hill until they were dizzy. When the golden sun began to sink behind the trees, Barnaby and Bella gave each other a big, warm bear hug. Barnaby smiled all the way home. He had found a wonderful friend, and his heart felt as full as his honey jar.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Honey Pot
stories.text:
Barnaby Bear woke up with a loud rumble in his tummy. Rumble, rumble, rumble! It was time for breakfast. Barnaby looked up on the high wooden shelf inside his cozy cave. There it was, sitting right in the middle: his favorite honey pot. It was round, made of shiny red clay, and filled to the very brim with golden, sticky honey.

Barnaby climbed down from his bed, rubbed his sleepy eyes, and walked over to the shelf. He stood on his tiptoes, stretched his furry arms as high as they could reach, and gently grabbed the honey pot. "Got you!" whispered Barnaby with a big grin. He carried the heavy pot over to his favorite wooden table and sat down in his little rocking chair.

Now, how to get the honey out? Barnaby used his paw. He dipped his big furry paw right into the pot. Slurp! He pulled his paw out, and it was covered in thick, sweet, golden honey. Barnaby licked his fingers one by one. "Yummy, yummy, in my tummy!" he cheered. The honey tasted like sunshine and sweet summer flowers.

Suddenly, a little buzzing sound flew past his ear. Bzzzzzz! Barnaby blinked. It was a fuzzy yellow bee! The bee flew around the honey pot, buzzing softly. "Bzz, bzz, that is our honey, Barnaby!" the bee seemed to say. Barnaby paused and looked at the little bee. He remembered how hard the bees worked all day long flying from flower to flower.
<div>
Barnaby smiled kindly at his tiny visitor. He took a little wooden spoon, scooped up a tiny drop of honey, and placed it gently on a green leaf for the bee. The bee buzzed happily, landed on the leaf, and began to eat. Barnaby finished the rest of his honey with a happy sigh. Sharing made the sweet treat taste even better. With a full tummy and a happy heart, Barnaby curled up for a cozy morning nap, dreaming of golden flowers and buzzing bees.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Gets Ready for Bed
stories.text:
The sun was starting to go down behind the tall green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink, orange, and purple. High up in his cozy cave, Barnaby Bear let out a very big yawn. Yaaaaawn! His furry eyelids felt heavy, and his little legs felt tired from a whole day of running and playing in the woods.

"Time to get ready for bed, Barnaby," he whispered to himself. First, Barnaby needed to wash up. He waddled over to his washbasin, splashed a little cool water on his furry face, and brushed his teeth until they sparkled like little white pearls. Scrub, scrub, scrub went his toothbrush.

Next, Barnaby opened his wooden chest of drawers to find his favorite pajamas. They were bright blue with little yellow stars printed all over them. Barnaby carefully put on his pajama top, stepped into his pajama bottoms, and zipped up the front. He looked down at himself and smiled. The stars on his pajamas looked just like the real stars starting to twinkle in the night sky.

Before climbing into his soft bed, Barnaby walked over to the cave entrance to say goodnight to the world outside. "Goodnight, tall trees," he called softly. "Goodnight, sparkling river. Goodnight, sweet little bees." The gentle evening breeze whispered back through the leaves, singing a quiet lullaby.

Barnaby crawled under his warm patchwork quilt and pulled it right up to his furry chin. He hugged his favorite stuffed bunny tightly. Mama Bear came over, gave him a gentle kiss on his forehead, and whispered, "Sleep tight, my little bear." Barnaby closed his eyes, listening to the quiet sounds of the night, and drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep, ready for wonderful dreams.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning in the big green woods, a little brown bear named Barnaby woke up with a big stretch. Yawn! Good morning, sun! Barnaby wore a bright red vest with shiny brass buttons. Today was a very special day because Barnaby wanted to find a brand new friend to play hide-and-seek with. He hopped out of his cozy bed made of soft moss and trotted down the winding path. Crunch, crunch, crunch went the autumn leaves under his little paws. First, Barnaby saw a busy squirrel darting up a tall oak tree. 'Hello, squirrel!' called Barnaby in his happiest voice. The squirrel chattered, flicked its bushy tail, and zipped away to hide a acorn. That was fun, but Barnaby wanted someone to play with. He kept walking until he reached the sparkly blue stream. Splish, splash! A little frog hopped onto a lily pad and croaked, 'Ribbit!' Barnaby waved his paw. 'Hello, froggy! Do you want to play hide-and-seek?' The frog blinked its big round eyes and jumped back into the cool water. Barnaby giggled. Then, he heard a sweet buzzing sound near a patch of yellow flowers. Bzzzz! It was Barry the bee. Barry was flying from flower to flower, collecting sweet nectar. Barnaby walked over very slowly and sat down in the soft grass. 'Hello, little bee,' whispered Barnaby. Barry landed right on Barnaby's black nose! Boop! Barnaby crossed his eyes to look at the bee, and they both giggled in their own special way. 'Would you like to be my friend?' asked Barnaby. Barry buzzed a happy little tune, which meant yes! They played the best game of hide-and-seek behind the big sunflowers. Barnaby hid his eyes with his paws, counting to three. One, two, three! Ready or not, here I come! He found Barry sitting on a petal, laughing softly. They played together until the golden sun began to sink low behind the hills. It was time for little bears to go home. Barnaby gave his new friend a gentle wave. 'Good night, Barry. Let us play again tomorrow!' Barnaby trotted back to his cozy moss bed, feeling so happy inside. He curled up tight, closed his sleepy eyes, and dreamed all about his wonderful day of finding a friend.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear and the Honey Pot
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods, little Barnaby Bear woke up with a very rumbly tummy. Grr-owl went his tummy! Barnaby rubbed his furry tummy and smiled because he knew exactly what he wanted for breakfast. Honey! Sweet, sticky, golden honey. Barnaby popped out of his den and sniffed the morning air. Sniff, sniff, sniff. Ah, he smelled something super sweet coming from the tall pine tree near the edge of the meadow. Barnaby waddled as fast as his short legs could carry him. Waddle, waddle, waddle! When he reached the tree, he looked up and gasped. Hanging right from a sturdy branch was a big brown pot with the word HONEY written on the side in big yellow letters. Oh boy! Barnaby reached up with his furry paws, but the pot was just a little bit too high. Oh no! He stood on his tiptoes and stretched his arms way up high, but his fingers only tickled the bottom of the pot. Barnaby thought hard. How could he reach his yummy treat? Just then, his good friend Sammy the squirrel scampered down the trunk carrying a basket of pinecones. 'Need some help, Barnaby?' asked Sammy with a cheeky grin. 'Yes, please!' said Barnaby. Sammy had a brilliant idea. 'Let us stack these soft cushions of moss right here under the tree.' Together, the bear and the squirrel gathered big fluffy piles of green moss and stacked them high. Barnaby stepped up onto the mossy pile. He stretched up again, reached his paw inside the pot, and pulled out a big, glorious glob of golden honey. Hooray! Barnaby tasted the honey on his paw. Mmm, yummy, sticky, sweet perfection! He shared a sweet drop with Sammy to say thank you for being such a helpful friend. They sat together under the pine tree, eating honey and laughing until their tummies were completely full. When the sun climbed high into the bright blue sky, Barnaby gave Sammy a big bear hug. It was the best honey adventure ever!

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Rainy Day Fun
stories.text: Pitter-patter, pitter-patter! Raindrops were falling from the fluffy grey clouds outside Barnaby Bear's cozy den. Oh, thought Barnaby, looking out his window with a little frown. It is raining today. I cannot go outside to chase butterflies or roll in the clover. Barnaby sat on his rocking chair and sighed. Siiiiigh. But wait! Mama Bear walked into the room carrying a large wooden box filled with wonderful things. 'A rainy day is not for being sad, my little cub,' said Mama Bear with a warm smile. 'It is a wonderful day for using our big imaginations!' Barnaby's eyes lit up with excitement. What was inside the magic box? First, Mama pulled out a pair of bright yellow rubber boots. Squish, squish! Next, she pulled out a shiny red umbrella and a box of colorful crayons. Barnaby knew just what to do. He put on his yellow boots and opened his red umbrella right inside the living room. Look at me, Mama! I am a sailing ship on a red sea! Then, Barnaby and Mama Bear sat down on the soft rug with large sheets of paper. Barnaby picked up a blue crayon and drew big splashing raindrops. Then he drew a smiling sun hiding behind the clouds, waiting to come out again. Next, they built a giant castle out of wooden blocks. Barnaby placed the very last block on top very carefully. Ta-da! It was the tallest castle in all the whole wide world. They pretended that Barnaby was a friendly giant bear guarding the castle gates. Roar! went Barnaby, but in a very gentle, silly voice so nobody would be scared. Soon, the pitter-patter sound on the window slowed down. Pitter... patter... stop. Barnaby ran to the window and pressed his furry nose against the glass. The grey clouds rolled away, and a giant, beautiful rainbow stretched across the sky. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple! Barnaby squealed with joy and dashed out the door with his yellow boots on. Splash went his paws in the big puddles! He jumped up and down, laughing as the water splashed all around. Rainy days were not boring at all. In fact, they were full of the most magical fun a little bear could ever imagine.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the big green woods, lived a little brown bear named Barnaby. Barnaby had soft, fuzzy ears, a very wet black nose, and a tummy that loved honey. Today, Barnaby woke up with a big stretch. Yawn! "Good morning, sun!" he whispered. Barnaby hopped out of his cozy bed made of dry leaves and soft moss. He stepped outside into the bright, warm air. "Today is a wonderful day for an adventure," said Barnaby to himself. He waddled down the winding dirt path, sniffing the flowers as he went. Sniff, sniff, sniff! He smelled sweet pink clover, bright yellow buttercups, and damp, earthy soil. As Barnaby walked, he heard a funny sound coming from behind a big berry bush. Giggles! Soft, bubbly giggles. Barnaby stopped and tilted his head. Tilt to the left, tilt to the right. "Hello? Is someone there?" asked Barnaby in his deepest, friendliest growl. The giggling stopped, and a small, furry face popped up from behind the bush. It was a little red fox with a white-tipped tail. Her name was Penny. Penny had big, bright eyes and a twitchy nose just like Barnaby. "Hello!" said Penny with a cheerful wave of her paw. "I am hiding from the buzzing bees." Barnaby smiled his biggest bear smile. He loved making new friends. "I am Barnaby. Do you want to play hide-and-seek with me?" Penny clapped her paws together happily. "Oh, yes! I love games! You count to three, and I will hide." Barnaby covered his eyes with his big paws. One, two, three! He counted slowly and carefully. Then he opened his eyes and looked all around. Where could Penny be? He looked behind a tall pine tree. No Penny. He looked inside a hollow log. No Penny. Then, Barnaby heard a soft rustling noise near the big rock. He tiptoed over very quietly. Tippy-toe, tippy-toe, goes the bear! He peeked behind the rock, and there sat Penny, trying very hard not to giggle out loud. "Found you!" shouted Barnaby gently. Penny jumped up, laughing. "You are so good at finding! Now it is your turn to hide." They played hide-and-seek all morning long under the warm golden sun. When their tummies started to rumble, Barnaby shared his sweet honey pots, and Penny shared her crunchy red apples. They sat side by side on the soft grass, munching happily together. Barnaby looked at his new best friend and felt a warm, fuzzy feeling inside his heart. Having a friend to play with made the big forest feel even more magical. As the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby gave Penny a big bear hug. "Good-bye, Penny. Let's play again tomorrow," said Barnaby. Penny smiled and flicked her tail. "I would love that, Barnaby." Barnaby waddled back down the path to his cozy leaf bed, yawning a big, happy yawn. He curled up tight, closed his eyes, and dreamed sweet dreams about his wonderful new friend.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Honey Pot
stories.text: The wind was blowing softly through the tall trees, making the leaves dance and swirl in the autumn air. Swish, swash, went the leaves. In his cozy little cave, Barnaby Bear woke up with a loud tummy rumble. Rumble, rumble, went his tummy! Barnaby sat up and rubbed his eyes. He felt very, very hungry. Today, his tummy was asking for only one thing: sweet, golden honey. Barnaby stood up on his four fuzzy paws and wobbled over to his cupboard. He opened the wooden door and looked inside. Oh, no! The cupboard was completely empty. Not a single drop of honey was left. Barnaby let out a sad little sigh. "Oh dear," he mumbled. "Where is my yummy honey?" Just then, a cheerful little bluebird landed right on Barnaby's windowsill. Chirp, chirp, went the bird. "Hello, Barnaby! Why the long face?" asked the friendly bluebird. Barnaby pointed to his empty cupboard. "I have no honey for my breakfast." The bluebird fluttered its bright blue wings. "Don't worry, my furry friend! I saw a big, busy beehive hanging from the old oak tree near the river. It is full of sweet, sticky honey!" Barnaby's ears perked right up. A beehive! He thanked the little bluebird with a happy nod and started on his journey to the river. Waddle, waddle, went Barnaby's feet along the forest floor. The air smelled crisp and cool. Soon, he reached the big oak tree. Barnaby looked up high into the branches. Way up high, hanging from a thick green branch, was a round, buzzing beehive. Bzzzzzz, went the bees as they flew all around it. Barnaby walked right up to the trunk of the tree and stretched his arms up as high as they could possibly go. Reach, reach, reach! But the beehive was still too far away. Barnaby stood up tall on his back legs. He stretched even higher, standing on his tiptoes. His paws brushed the bottom of the hive. Just a little bit more! Suddenly, a friendly little squirrel scampered down the trunk. "Need some help reaching that, Barnaby?" asked the squirrel. Barnaby nodded eagerly. "Yes, please!" The clever squirrel scampered up the tree, gave the beehive a gentle little nudge with its nose, and down tumbled a big, golden pot of honey right into Barnaby's waiting paws! Catch! Barnaby hugged the heavy honey pot tightly to his chest. It smelled so sweet and delicious. He used his paw to scoop up a big, golden dollop of honey and popped it right into his mouth. Mmm, yum! It was the sweetest honey he had ever tasted. Barnaby shared some with his kind squirrel friend and the little bluebird who had flown over to watch. Together, they ate their sweet treat under the rustling leaves, feeling very happy and full. Barnaby learned that asking for help makes hard tasks easy, and sharing makes good things taste even better.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Rainy Day
stories.text: Pitter-patter, pitter-patter, went the raindrops outside. Barnaby Bear pressed his wet black nose against his cave window and watched the water drops race down the glass. It was a very rainy day in the forest. All the animals were staying dry inside their homes. Barnaby let out a little sigh. He could not go outside to chase butterflies or play hide-and-seek with Penny Fox today. The puddles were simply too big, and the mud was much too squishy. "What can a little brown bear do on a rainy day?" Barnaby wondered aloud. He walked away from the window and looked around his cozy cave. First, he looked under his bed. Nothing there except his favorite squeaky frog toy. Then, he looked inside his toy box. Inside the box, sitting right on top, was a big box of colorful crayons and a stack of large white paper. Barnaby’s eyes lit up with joy. Drawing! That was one of his most favorite things to do in the whole wide world. Barnaby carried the crayons and paper over to his soft rug. He sat down criss-cross-applesauce, took the cap off a bright red crayon, and began to draw. He drew a big, round circle for the sun, even though the sun was hiding behind gray clouds today. Then, he took a blue crayon and drew a happy river curving across the page. Barnaby loved colors. He picked up a green crayon and drew tall trees with lots of leafy branches. While he was drawing, he heard a knock on his cave door. Knock, knock, knock! Barnaby jumped up and hurried to open it. Standing on his porch was Penny Fox, wearing a tiny yellow raincoat and shiny red galoshes. Splash! She stepped inside, shaking the raindrops from her fluffy tail. "Hello, Barnaby! It is too wet to play outside, so I came to visit you," said Penny with a bright smile. Barnaby was so happy he did a little spinning dance. "Look what I have! We can color pictures together!" Penny clapped her paws and sat right down on the rug next to Barnaby. She grabbed a yellow crayon and started drawing buzzing bees and sweet flowers all over Barnaby's paper. Barnaby used an orange crayon to draw himself and Penny playing together in the sunshine. They colored for a long, long time, talking and laughing as the rain fell softly outside the cave walls. When they were all finished, they held up their colorful pictures to show each other. Barnaby's cave did not feel gloomy or boring anymore. It felt warm, bright, and full of fun. Barnaby realized that rainy days were not bad at all, especially when you spent them with a wonderful friend. Soon, the pitter-patter of the rain slowed down, and a lovely rainbow stretched across the sky outside. Barnaby and Penny put on their boots and ran outside to splash happily in the big, shining puddles.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a time, deep in the green and leafy woods, there lived a little brown bear named Barnaby. Barnaby had soft, fluffy fur, round furry ears, and a tummy that loved to rumble. Every morning, Barnaby would wake up, stretch his arms up high, and say, "Good morning, sun! Good morning, trees!" One sunny day, Barnaby decided to go on a big adventure to find a new friend. He waddled down the winding path, stepping over crunchy brown leaves. Crunch, crunch, crunch went his big paws. As he walked, he saw a bright yellow butterfly fluttering near a patch of sweet strawberries. "Hello, butterfly!" whispered Barnaby gently so he would not scare it away. The butterfly danced in the air, landing softly on Barnaby’s black button nose. Barnaby crossed his eyes to look at the pretty yellow wings and let out a happy little giggle. "Tee-hee!" laughed the bear. But the butterfly flew away, zig-zagging up toward the tall oak trees. Barnaby followed the fluttery wings, waddling as fast as his short legs could carry him. Suddenly, he heard a funny sound behind a big green bush. *Squeak, squeak, rustle, rustle.* Barnaby stopped. He tilted his head to the left. Then he tilted his head to the right. "Who is there?" asked Barnaby in his deepest, friendliest bear voice. Out popped a tiny, twitchy-nosed rabbit with long floppy ears. The rabbit looked at Barnaby’s big furry body and shivered just a little bit. Barnaby wanted to show the rabbit that he was a kind bear, so he sat right down on the soft grass. He picked a sweet, red strawberry and rolled it gently across the grass toward the rabbit. The rabbit sniffed the strawberry with its twitchy pink nose. *Sniff, sniff, sniff.* Then, the little rabbit gave a little hop forward. Nibble, nibble, gobbled the rabbit. The rabbit did a happy little hop and bounced right up to Barnaby. It nudged Barnaby’s fuzzy paw with its soft nose. Barnaby smiled from ear to ear. "Would you like to play hide-and-seek with me?" asked the bear. The rabbit wiggled its ears as if to say yes. Barnaby closed his eyes and counted to three in a loud, playful whisper. "One, two, three! Ready or not, here I come!" Barnaby opened his eyes and looked behind a big fern. There was the little rabbit, trying to hide its long ears with its paws. Barnaby pretended he could not see his new friend anywhere. "Where could my little friend be?" wondered the bear loudly. The rabbit popped out and giggled a happy little squeak. They played games all afternoon under the warm golden sunshine. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Barnaby gave his new friend a warm, gentle bear hug. "It is time for bed," said Barnaby softly. The little rabbit hopped back to its cozy burrow, and Barnaby waddled back to his cozy den. As he curled up on his soft bed of moss, Barnaby smiled. He had the best day ever because he found a wonderful new friend in the woods.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Red Balloon
stories.text: It was a bright and beautiful morning in the forest, and Barnaby Bear woke up with a big yawn. *Yaaawn!* He rubbed his sleepy eyes with his paws. Today was a very special day because it was Barnaby’s birthday. His mother had a big surprise waiting for him outside their cozy cave. Barnaby waddled out into the sunshine, and his eyes grew as big as saucers. Tied right to the wooden fence was a shiny, floating, bright red balloon. It bobbed up and down in the gentle breeze, saying hello. "For me?" asked Barnaby with a huge smile. His mother nodded and smiled warmly. Barnaby reached out a soft paw and gently touched the smooth, shiny surface of the balloon. *Boop!* went the balloon as it bounced against his furry finger. Barnaby loved his red balloon instantly. He decided to take it on a grand walk through the magical woods to show all of his woodland neighbors his wonderful birthday toy. He held the long white string very tightly in his paw so it would not float away into the clouds. First, Barnaby waddled past the sparkling blue stream. *Splash, splash, splash* went his toes in the cool water. He looked down and saw his reflection in the water holding the floating red balloon, and he waved at himself. Next, he walked past Mrs. Owl, who was resting on a high tree branch. "Happy birthday, little bear!" hooted Mrs. Owl wisely. Barnaby waved his free paw high in the air and said, "Thank you, Mrs. Owl! Look at my balloon!" The balloon danced in the wind, as if it were dancing along to the happy sounds of the forest. Barnaby felt so proud holding his bright red treasure. But then, oh no! A sudden gust of wind blew through the trees. *Whoosh!* The wind tugged playfully at the string. Barnaby squeezed his paws together, holding on with all his might. The balloon pulled upward, trying to fly up into the sky to play with the fluffy white clouds. Barnaby giggled as his feet almost lifted off the ground. "Whoa! Slow down, balloon!" laughed the little bear. He realized that holding a balloon was like having a lively pet that wanted to dance in the sky. He decided to sit down on a soft patch of green grass to rest his little legs. He gently pulled the string down so the balloon rested right on his lap. He hugged the round, shiny sphere carefully, making sure it was safe. Just then, his mother walked through the trees carrying a delicious honey cake with one glowing yellow candle on top. "Time for birthday cake, Barnaby!" she sang. Barnaby’s tummy did a happy little flip-flop. He tied the balloon securely to a sturdy stick in the ground so it could watch the party. Barnaby ate every single crumb of his sweet honey cake, sharing a tiny piece with his red balloon friend too. It was the happiest birthday a little bear could ever wish for, filled with love, sunshine, and a wonderful floating red balloon.

stories.title: Barnaby's Honey Hunt
stories.text: The morning sun was shining brightly through the green canopy of the forest, warming the fur of a little brown bear named Barnaby. Barnaby sat up in his cozy nest of leaves and rubbed his tummy. *Rumbly-rumble* went his tummy. Today was a very important day. Barnaby had a deep, powerful craving for something sweet, golden, and sticky. He wanted honey! Barnaby hopped up on all fours and set off on a delicious mission known to all bears as the great honey hunt. He waddled down the winding path, sniffing the air with his black button nose. *Sniff, sniff, sniff.* He smelled pine needles. He smelled damp earth. He smelled fresh green grass. But no honey yet! Barnaby kept walking, determined to find the golden treasure. Suddenly, he heard a familiar buzzing sound high up in the air. *Bzzzzzz, bzzzzzz.* Barnaby stopped in his tracks and looked up toward the sky. Flying in a little circle were three fuzzy black-and-yellow bees. "Follow the bees!" whispered Barnaby excitedly to himself. He knew that where there were bees, a sweet beehive was never too far away. Barnaby tiptoed as quietly as a big bear could tiptoed. *Thud, thud, thud* went his soft paws on the mossy ground. He followed the buzzing insects past a patch of purple wildflowers and around a large gray boulder. There, hanging from the thick branch of a giant oak tree, was a big, round, dripping honeycomb. It gleamed golden in the sunlight, looking oh-so-delicious. Barnaby licked his lips. *Slurp!* He stretched his furry arms up as high as they could possibly reach. He stood up tall on his back paws and reached for the sweet prize. But the honeycomb was just a little bit too high. Barnaby stretched even higher, standing on his tiptoes. *Tip-toe, tip-toe!* Still, his fingertips only brushed the bottom of the hive. The friendly bees buzzed around his ears in a gentle circle, as if they were cheering him on. Barnaby let out a little puff of air. Then, he remembered something very important. Bears are great climbers! Barnaby wrapped his strong arms around the rough bark of the oak tree. He dug his claws gently into the wood and began to climb. *Hug and pull, hug and pull.* Up, up, up went the little brown bear until he was level with the dangling golden hive. Barnaby smiled proudly. He gently plucked a piece of the sweet, dripping honeycomb right off the branch. He carefully climbed back down the tree trunk and sat down on the soft grass to enjoy his hard-earned treat. He took a big bite of the sweet, sticky honey. It tasted like sunshine, flowers, and pure happiness. Barnaby licked his paws until they were completely clean, feeling full, happy, and ready for a nice long afternoon nap.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning in the big green woods, there lived a little bear named Barnaby. Barnaby had fluffy brown fur, two shiny black eyes, and a very big heart. Today was a special day because Barnaby woke up and felt extra happy. He stretched his arms up high, touched the sky, and gave a big, loud yawn. Good morning, sun! Good morning, trees! whispered Barnaby to the woods. Barnaby loved to explore. He put on his favorite red boots and hopped out of his cozy cave. As he walked down the dusty path, he heard a funny sound. Rustle, rustle, snap! What could that be? wondered Barnaby. He tiptoed very softly, trying not to make a sound. Behind a big green bush, he saw something small and wiggly. It was a little bunny with long floppy ears. The bunny looked a little bit lost. Hello, little bunny, said Barnaby in his gentlest voice. I am Barnaby Bear. The bunny blinked its pink eyes and gave a little hop. Hello, Barnaby! My name is Pip. Can you help me find my way to the carrot patch? Pip asked. Barnaby smiled from ear to ear. Of course I can! Following me is as easy as one, two, three. They walked together down the winding path. Along the way, they saw yellow butterflies dancing in the air. Barnaby pointed to them and giggled. Look at the fluttering wings, Pip! Pip clapped his paws together. So pretty! They walked a little further and found a big puddle of sparkling water. Splash, splash went Barnaby’s red boots. Splash, splash went Pip’s little feet. They laughed and played until they reached the big carrot patch. There were crunchy, orange carrots growing everywhere. Pip found his mommy and gave her a big hug. Thank you so much for your help, kind Barnaby, said Pip’s mommy. Barnaby felt warm and cozy inside. Helping a friend is the best thing in the whole wide world, he thought. He waved goodbye to Pip and skipped all the way back to his cave, ready for a nice long nap after such a wonderful day.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear's Honey Pot
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods, little Barnaby Bear had a very important mission today. His tummy was rumbling, and when Barnaby’s tummy rumbled, it meant only one thing. He needed honey! Sweet, sticky, golden honey. Barnaby grabbed his favorite yellow spoon and set off on an adventure. First, he looked under a big grey rock. No honey there, just a sleepy little worm saying hello. Next, he looked up into the tall oak tree. No honey there, just a squirrel playing hide and seek with an acorn. Oh, where is the honey hiding? wondered Barnaby, patting his round tummy. Suddenly, he smelled something wonderful. It smelled sweet like flowers and sunshine. Buzz, buzz, buzz went the air. Barnaby followed the sound and the sweet smell all the way to a flowery meadow. There, hanging from a sturdy branch, was a big beehive. And buzzing all around it were friendly little bees. Hello, busy bees! said Barnaby politely. May I please have a tiny taste of your delicious honey? The bees buzzed a happy tune and fluttered around. They knew Barnaby was a good friend to the forest. One kind little bee flew right down and landed on Barnaby’s nose. Tickle, tickle, went the bee’s tiny legs. Barnaby giggled so hard he almost fell over. The bees led him to a small wooden pot filled with the most golden, shiny honey you ever did see. Barnaby dipped his yellow spoon right into the pot. He pulled it out and took a big, happy lick. Yum, yum, yummy! It was the sweetest honey in the whole wide world. Barnaby shared a tiny drop on a leaf for his buzzing friends. Thank you, sweet bees, said Barnaby with a big smile. He rubbed his full, happy tummy and danced a silly little bear dance. With his heart full of joy and a sticky nose, Barnaby walked back home to his cozy den, dreaming of his next sweet adventure in the sunny woods.

stories.title: Barnaby Bear Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The sun was slowly going down behind the tall green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and purple. In his cozy little cave, Barnaby Bear gave a very big yawn. Yaaaaawn! His furry eyelids felt heavy, and the stars were beginning to twinkle in the night sky. It was almost time for bed. But before he went to sleep, Barnaby had a nightly routine. First, he had to tidy up his toys. He put his wooden blocks in the toy box and tucked his favorite stuffed rabbit right beside his pillow. Goodnight, little rabbit, whispered Barnaby. Next, it was time to put on his favorite blue pajamas with little white stars all over them. They fit him just right and kept him warm and snug. Then, Barnaby sat down in his rocking chair and listened to the night sounds outside. Hoo, hoo went the wise old owl in the tree. Shh, shh whispered the gentle wind through the leaves. Everyone in the forest was getting ready for sleep. Barnaby snuggled deep into his bed, pulling his soft patchwork quilt right up to his fuzzy chin. His mama came in and gave him a gentle kiss on his forehead. Sleep tight, my sweet little bear, Mama whispered softly. Barnaby closed his eyes and took a nice, deep breath. He thought about all the fun things he had done today. He had played with Pip the bunny, chased yellow butterflies, and tasted sweet golden honey. What a wonderful day it had been. He smiled in his sleep as the moon shone brightly through the cave window, casting a warm and gentle glow all around. Barnaby drifted off into dreamland, listening to the quiet lullaby of the forest, ready to wake up tomorrow and do it all over again. Goodnight, Barnaby Bear.

rhymes.title: Little Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
Little brown bear wakes up from bed,
He scratches his sleepy, furry head.
He stretches his arms up to the sky,
And watches a little bird fly by.

He walks in the grass so green and bright,
His shiny black nose is a lovely sight.
He looks for honey sweet and gold,
The finest treat in the forest old.

He finds a bee buzzing in the air,
And gives the fluffy insect a stare.
Then he waddles down by the flowing stream,
To wash his paws and softly dream.

The sun goes down behind the trees,
He feels the cool and gentle breeze.
He crawls inside his cozy den,
To sleep until the morning then.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bears
rhymes.text:
Five little bears went out to play,
Down in the woods on a sunny day.
The first little bear climbed a tree,
To find a golden buzzing bee.

The second little bear chased a ball,
And bumped his nose against the wall.
The third little bear ate berry pie,
With purple juice upon his eye.

The fourth little bear took a nap,
With his soft paws upon his lap.
The fifth little bear splashed in the brook,
And closed his favorite story book.

Now stars are shining in the sky,
The sleepy bears begin to sigh.
They curl up tight in beds of wool,
Because their happy day is full.

rhymes.title: Bear Hugs
rhymes.text:
Time for hugs before we sleep,
While shadows in the forest creep.
Big brown bear has arms so wide,
With cozy fur on every side.

He gives a squeeze so soft and sweet,
From furry ears to tiny feet.
He hugs his blanket, hugs his toy,
And fills his heart with gentle joy.

The moon is shining round and bright,
To watch him through the quiet night.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Safe inside your little bed.

Dream of honey, dream of streams,
Filled with happy toddler dreams.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little bear, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Bear's Pajamas
rhymes.text:
Little bear puts on his clothes,
Warm wool socks upon his toes.
Button up his fuzzy vest,
Time for little bears to rest.

Now he grabs his teddy toy,
Every happy girl and boy.
Climbs into his cozy bed,
Pillows soft beneath his head.
Mama bear turns out the light,
Kisses him and says goodnight.
Twinkle stars up in the sky,
Watch the sleepy bears go by.
Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
Little bear is fast asleep.
Softly dreaming through the night,
Till the morning brings the light.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
Brown bear walking through the trees,
Sniffing flowers in the breeze.
Finding berries sweet and red,
Nibbling them until he's fed.

Big round paws go pad, pad, pad,
Making every toddler glad.
See him wiggle, see him play,
Running through the grass all day.
Now he sits beside a stream,
Lost in such a happy dream.
Washing furry hands and face,
In this lovely woodland place.
When the sun begins to sink,
Bear takes just a little drink.
Waddles home to sleep until,
Morning wakes the sleepy hill.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Bear Claws
rhymes.text:
Ten little bear claws, round and sweet,
Walking down the forest street.
Two furry ears upon his head,
Jumping on his leafy bed.

Big brown nose goes sniff, sniff, sniff,
Catching every funny whiff.
Looking for a honey jar,
Traveling near and traveling far.
Climbing up a friendly tree,
Saying hello to a bee.
Now he rolls upon the floor,
Wanting to play even more.
Tickle, tickle on his tummy,
Honey treats are oh so yummy.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Sleeping in his cozy nest.

rhymes.title: Little Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
Little brown bear wakes up today,
Stretches his paws and wants to play.
He wiggles his nose and wags his tail,
And walks along the winding trail.

He finds a bee upon a tree,
Buzzing around so wild and free.
The honey is sweet and golden bright,
He eats it all up with pure delight.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Back to his cozy cave he must go.
He curls up tight upon the floor,
And sleeps until it is morning once more.

Good night, little bear, close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dream of honey and fields of green,
The happiest bear that ever was seen.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Rain
rhymes.text:
Pitter-patter falls the rain,
On the window and the pane.
Big brown bear puts on his hat,
Looking very fine and fat.

He steps outside to feel the breeze,
Swishing through the leafy trees.
He finds a puddle on the ground,
And stomps his feet with a happy sound.

Splish and splash and messy mud,
Watch the water start to flood.
He laughs aloud and dances round,
Jumping up and hitting the ground.

Now the rain is stopping fast,
Sunny skies are here at last.
Bear goes home to dry his toes,
With a sleepy wrinkle on his nose.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Bear Claws
rhymes.text:
One little bear claw digging in the dirt,
Two little bear paws wearing a brown shirt.
Three little honey pots sitting on a shelf,
Four little bear cubs helping themselves.

Five buzzing bees flying all around,
Six little acorns falling to the ground.
Seven soft berries sweet and red,
Eight sleepy yawns before going to bed.

Nine furry friends saying big hello,
Ten dancing steps where the rivers flow.
Round and round the forest green,
Best little bear you have ever seen.

Now the day is done and through,
Stars are twinkling in the blue.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little brown bear is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Bear's Red Boots
rhymes.text:
Little bear puts on his boots,
Stomping down among the roots.
One, two, left and right,
Making sure they fit him tight.

Puddle splash and puddle jump,
Over every little bump.
Mud is squishy, mud is wet,
Best adventure he has met!

Now the sun begins to fade,
Time to leave the forest glade.
Take off boots and wash his toes,
Time to rest his sleepy nose.

Mommy gives a hug so deep,
Little bear falls fast asleep.
Stars are shining in the skies,
Close your lovely little eyes.

rhymes.title: Honey Pot Day
rhymes.text:
Little bear wakes up and sings,
Listening to the buzzing wings.
Honey pot is on the shelf,
He wants some all by himself.

Tip-toe, tip-toe, up he goes,
Standing right upon his toes.
Reaching high to take a scoop,
Down he tumbles with a whoop!

Sticky paws and sticky chin,
Where does all the fun begin?
Licking fingers, sweet and sweet,
Such a yummy honey treat.

Time to wipe his furry face,
Crawl into his resting place.
Dreaming of the golden sun,
Now his sleepy day is done.

rhymes.title: Bear's Lullaby Moon
rhymes.text:
The moon is glowing up above,
Sending out a little love.
Little bear is in his bed,
With a pillow for his head.

Wind is whispering through the trees,
Dancing gently in the breeze.
Close your eyes and do not weep,
Time for little bears to sleep.

Teddy bear is by his side,
Safe and warm where shadows hide.
Breathing softly, in and out,
Free from any little doubt.

Nighttime whispers all around,
Making not a single sound.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little bear, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear, little bear, touch your nose.
Little bear, little bear, touch your toes.
Little bear, little bear, turn around.
Little bear, little bear, sit on the ground.

Little bear, little bear, wave hello.
Little bear, little bear, time to go.
Little bear, little bear, find some honey.
Little bear, little bear, make us funny.

Little bear, little bear, stomp your feet.
Little bear, little bear, take a seat.
Little bear, little bear, blink your eyes.
Little bear, little bear, jump up high.

Little bear, little bear, give a hug.
Little bear, little bear, find a bug.
Little bear, little bear, time to sleep.
Little bear, little bear, do not peep.

rhymes.title: Five Fuzzy Bears
rhymes.text:
One fuzzy bear climbing up a tree,
Looking for a bit of sweet honey.
Two fuzzy bears splashing in the stream,
Eating up a bowl of berry cream.

Three fuzzy bears dancing in the sun,
Having lots of very special fun.
Four fuzzy bears sleeping in a bed,
With a leafy pillow for each head.

Five fuzzy bears waking up to play,
Greeting the bright and happy day.
Bears go running, bears go slow,
Walking where the daisies grow.

Bears say hello and bears say bye,
Watching clouds go floating by.
Now the stars begin to glow,
Time for little bears to go.

rhymes.title: Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See?
rhymes.text:
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you see?
I see a bird sitting on a tree.
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you hear?
I hear a buzzing bee buzzing near.

Brown bear, brown bear, what do you smell?
I smell sweet flowers down in the dell.
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you taste?
Yummy red berries, oh what a waste!

Brown bear, brown bear, what do you touch?
Soft green grass I love so much.
Brown bear, brown bear, where is your bed?
Under the leaves with a pillow for my head.

Brown bear, brown bear, closing your eyes?
Dreaming of honey up in the skies.
Brown bear, brown bear, time for your rest.
Sleeping in the woods is the very best.

rhymes.title: Little Bear's Big Red Ball
rhymes.text:
Little bear has a big red ball,
He bounces it against the garden wall.
He throws it high into the air,
And catches it with gentle care.
He rolls it left, he rolls it right,
It shines so round and very bright.
He hugs his ball upon his knee,
As happy as a bear can be.
The sun is setting in the sky,
The little birds are flying by.
It is time to put the toys away,
And end a fun and busy day.
He climbs into his cozy bed,
And rests his sleepy, furry head.
He closes both his tired eyes,
Beneath the starry, twinkling skies.

rhymes.title: Five Sweet Honey Pots
rhymes.text:
Five sweet honey pots in a row,
Where do they come from? Do you know?
A little brown bear comes walking by,
With twinkling eyes and a happy sigh.
He dips his paw in pot number one,
And licks the honey in the sun.
He opens pot number two with care,
And finds sweet gold waiting there.
Pot number three is sticky and sweet,
A very tasty and yummy treat.
Pot number four is creamy and light,
Eaten all up before the night.
Pot number five is empty and clean,
The happiest bear you've ever seen.
He rubs his tummy and gives a yawn,
And falls asleep until the dawn.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Bear
rhymes.text:
The sleepy little bear wakes up from sleep,
He counts the fluffy clouds that leap.
He stretches out his furry paws,
And shows his little painted claws.
He waddles down the woodland lane,
To watch the falling summer rain.
He finds a cozy tree to share,
With every little woodland bear.
The wind begins to softly blow,
And makes the sleepy flowers grow.
He hugs his favorite teddy tight,
And whispers softly in the night.
The moon is shining round and high,
Like silver cookie in the sky.
The little bear begins to creep,
And gently drifts off into sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Bear's Red Hat
rhymes.text:
Little bear puts on his hat,
Sitting on the grassy mat.
Red and bright, oh look and see,
Hanging from the apple tree.

Now he takes a little walk,
Listening to the birdies talk.
Chirp and sing and fly away,
To the woods to go and play.

Little bear begins to run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Big brown paws go tap, tap, tap,
Ready for a cozy nap.

Yawning wide and feeling slow,
Where does little bear now go?
To his bed of leaves so deep,
Closing eyes and going to sleep.

rhymes.title: Honey Pot Bear
rhymes.text:
Fat little bear loves sweet honey,
Looking very bright and sunny.
Walking down the forest track,
With a basket on his back.

Smelling something yummy now,
Maybe from a spotted cow?
No, it is a buzzing bee,
Flying round the honey tree.

Climbing up the bark so high,
Reaching up into the sky.
Grab the pot and take a taste,
Nothing here is going to waste.

Tummy full and feeling sweet,
Time to wash his furry feet.
Curl up tight upon the floor,
Sleeping till the morning roar.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Bear Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Sleepy bear, close your eyes,
Watch the stars begin to rise.
Moon is glowing in the blue,
Shining softly down on you.

Blanket warm and pillow deep,
Time for little bears to sleep.
Dreaming of a sunny stream,
Floating in a happy dream.

Wind is blowing through the trees,
Whispering a gentle breeze.
Softly purrs the sleepy cub,
Snuggling his furry grub.

Night is quiet, calm and still,
Resting on the woody hill.
Morning sun will soon appear,
Sleep until the dawn is here.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear, little bear, touch your toes.
Little bear, little bear, touch your nose.
Little bear, little bear, turn around.
Little bear, little bear, sit on the ground.

Little bear, little bear, wave your hand.
Little bear, little bear, stomp in the sand.
Little bear, little bear, climb a tree.
Little bear, little bear, smile at me.

Little bear, little bear, find some honey.
Little bear, little bear, act so funny.
Little bear, little bear, run away fast.
Little bear, little bear, home at last.

Little bear, little bear, close your eyes.
Little bear, little bear, time for bed sighs.
Little bear, little bear, sleep till the dawn.
Little bear, little bear, night has gone on.

rhymes.title: The Fuzzy Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
See the fuzzy brown bear walking by,
Looking way up at the big blue sky.
He finds a bee buzzing in the air,
And dances around without a care.

He walks through the woods and stomps his feet,
Looking all over for something sweet.
He spots a huge pot of golden honey,
And gives a big grin that looks so funny.

He dips in his paw and takes a big taste,
Eating it up with never a waste.
His tummy is full and happy inside,
Filled with a warm and wonderful pride.

The shadows grow long as the sun goes low,
It is time for the fuzzy brown bear to go.
He walks to his cave to rest his sweet head,
And tucks himself into his cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Bear Claws
rhymes.text:
Ten little bear claws, fuzzy and brown,
Wiggling up and wiggling down.
Two furry ears that listen so well,
To stories the gentle wind has to tell.

A big round nose that sniffs out the breeze,
Walking right past the tall green trees.
A sweet little mouth that loves honey and jam,
Eating as happily as a little lamb.

Big furry arms that give a tight hug,
Wrapped up so safe like a tiny bug.
Sharp little claws that dig in the dirt,
Keeping the little bear safe from hurt.

Now the stars shine in the evening skies,
Closing up those sleepy brown eyes.
Dreaming of honey and skies so blue,
Little brown bear, I am sleeping too.

rhymes.title: The Little Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
See the little brown bear waking from his sleep,
Out of his cozy cave he begins to creep.
He waddles to the river where the water flows,
And dips his paws right in to tickle his toes.

He looks up at the sky so big and blue,
And sings a happy song for me and you.
He shakes his furry head and gives a roar,
Then runs across the grass to look for more.

He finds a yellow flower on the ground,
And sniffs it up and down without a sound.
Then night comes creeping with the pale moon light,
And hugs the little bear and says goodnight.

He crawls back to his bed so warm and deep,
And closes his brown eyes to go to sleep.
Dreaming of honey pots of gold so bright,
Sleep tight, little bear, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Five Little Bears
rhymes.text:
One little bear climbs a tall green tree,
Looking for a sweet and buzzing honey bee.
Two little bears jump up and down,
Running all around the sleepy forest town.

Three little bears splash in the river blue,
Making happy bubbles in the water too.
Four little bears dance upon the grass,
Watching all the pretty butterflies pass.

Five little bears curl up in a bed,
With a soft brown pillow underneath each head.
They yawn and stretch their furry paws up high,
As twinkling stars appear up in the sky.

The mother bear sings a gentle lullaby,
While fluffy clouds go sailing drifting by.
Now all the little bears are fast asleep,
While silence in the woods is deep.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
Hear the furry bear walking through the trees,
Sniffing all around to catch the gentle breeze.
He finds a berry bush with fruit so red,
And eats a yummy snack before his bed.

He rubs his round tummy with a happy paw,
And gives the biggest yawn you ever saw.
He pats his furry head and wiggles his nose,
Right down to the tips of his fuzzy toes.

The sun goes down behind the mountain high,
Painting golden colors in the evening sky.
It is time for the bear to rest his head,
And climb into his cozy little bed.

Pull the blankets up and close your eyes tight,
The moon is shining down with silver light.
Tomorrow is a brand new day to play,
So sleep until the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear, little bear, touch your nose.
Little bear, little bear, touch your toes.
Little bear, little bear, turn around.
Little bear, little bear, sit on the ground.
Little bear, little bear, clap your hands.
Little bear, little bear, stomp like lands.
Little bear, little bear, reach up high.
Little bear, little bear, wave bye-bye.
Little bear, little bear, find some honey.
Little bear, little bear, make a face funny.
Little bear, little bear, take a big nap.
Little bear, little bear, close your eye-flap.
Little bear, little bear, wake up and play.
Little bear, little bear, have a great day.
Little bear, little bear, let's go run.
Little bear, little bear, you are so fun.

rhymes.title: Ten Brown Bears
rhymes.text:
One brown bear climbing in a tree.
Two brown bears looking right at me.
Three brown bears jumping on the bed.
Four brown bears with a hat of red.
Five brown bears eating sweet plum.
Six brown bears rubbing a big tum.
Seven brown bears walking in the rain.
Eight brown bears riding on a train.
Nine brown bears dancing in the hall.
Ten brown bears catching a soft ball.
Bears go high and bears go low.
Bears go fast and bears go slow.
Now the bears are getting very sleepy.
Now the bears are crawling right up softly.
Time for bed, the stars are shining bright.
Say goodnight to all the bears, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Big Bear, Sleepy Bear
rhymes.text:
Big bear, sleepy bear, in his cozy cave.
Big bear, sleepy bear, so gentle and brave.
Winter time is coming with the chilly snow.
Big bear, sleepy bear, time to rest below.
Curled up tight in a ball of brown fur.
Not a single sound, not a single stir.
Dreaming of the honey in the summer breeze.
Dreaming of the climbing up the forest trees.
Snoring very softly through the dark night.
Holding his favorite blankie nice and tight.
Moonlight shining softly on his furry head.
Safe and sound inside his leafy little bed.
Sleep until the springtime brings the flowers out.
Sleep until the birdies flutter all about.
Rest your heavy eyes until the morning dew.
Big bear, sleepy bear, we all love you.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear, little bear, touch your toes,
Little bear, little bear, wipe your nose.
Little bear, little bear, turn around,
Little bear, little bear, sit on the ground.

Little bear, little bear, jump up high,
Little bear, little bear, wave goodbye.
Little bear, little bear, find your bed,
Little bear, little bear, rest your head.

Little bear, little bear, close your eyes,
Little bear, little bear, no more cries.
Little bear, little bear, dream all night,
Little bear, little bear, sleep so tight.

Morning comes with a golden ray,
Time to wake up and start the day.
Little bear, little bear, wake and see,
Happy as happy as can be.

rhymes.title: Teddy Bear, Teddy Bear
rhymes.text:
Teddy bear, teddy bear, stomp your feet,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, find a treat.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, pour the tea,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, drink with me.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, hug your toy,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, be full of joy.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, climb a tree,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, buzz like a bee.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, catch a ball,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, do not fall.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, brush your fur,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, hear it purr.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, time for sleep,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, count your sheep.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, in the dark,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, leave your mark.

rhymes.title: Brown Bear, Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you see?
I see a bird sitting in a tree.
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you know?
I know the river has water that flows.

Brown bear, brown bear, where is your pot?
Honey is sweet and I want a lot.
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you smell?
Flowers in spring that blossom so well.

Brown bear, brown bear, who is your friend?
Playing together until the day ends.
Brown bear, brown bear, what do you hear?
Whispering wind and songs ringing clear.

Brown bear, brown bear, time for a nap,
Resting your head in cozy red lap.
Brown bear, brown bear, sleeping so deep,
Safe in your cave while shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear, little bear, touch your toes,
Little bear, little bear, touch your nose.
Little bear, little bear, turn around,
Little bear, little bear, sit on the ground.

Little bear, little bear, clap your hands,
Little bear, little bear, stomp in the sands.
Little bear, little bear, jump so high,
Little bear, little bear, wave bye-bye.

Little bear, little bear, find your bed,
Little bear, little bear, rest your head.
Little bear, little bear, close your eyes,
Little bear, little bear, watch dreams rise.

Little bear, little bear, sleeping tight,
Little bear, little bear, sleep all night.
Morning comes with a golden sun,
Little bear wakes up ready for fun.

rhymes.title: Ten Sweet Honey Pots
rhymes.text:
One little honey pot sitting on a shelf,
Barnaby wants to eat it all by himself.
Two little honey pots golden and bright,
Eating them up makes everything right.

Three little honey pots sticky and sweet,
Making a yummy and wonderful treat.
Four little honey pots in a long row,
Watch how fast little Barnaby can go.

Five little honey pots sitting right there,
Shared with a friend who is kind and fair.
Six little honey pots, lick your paws clean,
Best tasting honey you've ever seen.

Seven little honey pots up on the wall,
Careful, dear bear, do not let them fall.
Eight little honey pots, yummy and round,
Nine little honey pots safe and sound.

Ten little honey pots gone in a flash,
Now it is time to go wash in a dash.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Bear Lullaby
rhymes.text:
The sun is going down to sleep,
The little stars begin to peep.
Big brown bear is in his bed,
With a pillow for his head.

Soft wind whispers through the tree,
Buzzing goes the sleepy bee.
Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
Time for little bears to sleep.

Moonlight shines upon the floor,
Shadows dance beside the door.
Dream of honey sweet and gold,
While the cozy blankets hold.

Nighty-night to furry paws,
Nighty-night to sleepy claws.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little bear, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Brown Bear
rhymes.text:
Little brown bear wakes up today,
Wants to go outside and play.
He puts on his fuzzy shoes,
And he looks around for clues.

He sees a bird up in a tree,
He shares a sweet and sticky bee.
He rolls around upon the grass,
And watches fluffy white clouds pass.

The sun begins to slowly dip,
He takes a tiny honey sip.
He yawns a very sleepy yawn,
And rests until the early dawn.

The stars are shining very bright,
So gentle bear says sleepy night.
He hugs his blanket oh so tight,
Until the morning golden light.

rhymes.title: Teddy Bear, Teddy Bear
rhymes.text:
Teddy bear, teddy bear, touch the ground,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, spin around.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, show your shoe,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, I love you.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, climb the stair,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, brush your hair.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, turn out the light,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, say goodnight.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, hug your toy,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, smiling boy.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, rest your head,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, go to bed.

Teddy bear, teddy bear, close your eyes,
Teddy bear, teddy bear, dream of skies.
Teddy bear, teddy bear, safe and sound,
While the quiet night goes round.

rhymes.title: The Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
A big furry bear walks through the wood,
Eating sweet berries just like he should.
He finds a yellow pot of honey,
And dances around all silly and funny.

A butterfly lands upon his nose,
Tickling softly from head to toes.
The bear gives a gentle, happy sneeze,
And waves hello to the buzzing bees.

He waddles along the river stream,
And thinks of a sweet and golden dream.
The water goes splash against his feet,
Making the afternoon complete.

He heads back home as day is done,
Now hiding away is the golden sun.
He curls in his cave so safe and deep,
And rocks himself to a lovely sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear wakes up today,
Wants to find a game to play.
Stretches arms up to the sky,
Waves a friendly bee goodbye.

Trots along the forest floor,
Looking for a honey store.
Finds a pot of golden sweet,
What a yummy, tasty treat!

Pats his tummy, full and round,
Sits upon the grassy ground.
Blinks his eyes and gives a sigh,
Watches butterflies go by.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little bear to go.
Curls up in his cozy bed,
Dreams inside his sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
Brown bear, brown bear, walking through the trees,
Sniffing sweet flowers in the morning breeze.
Soft furry paws go tap, tap, tap,
Looking all around for a cozy nap.

Climbs a little hill of green,
Happiest bear you've ever seen.
Waves his paw at passing birds,
Humming gently without words.

Finds a hollow log of wood,
Tastes some berries that are good.
Chews them up and licks his chin,
Let the afternoon begin!

Shadows stretch upon the ground,
Not a single frightful sound.
Big bear snores a sleepy tune,
Underneath the silver moon.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Paws
rhymes.text:
Ten little paws upon the floor,
Walking right up to the door.
Opening it wide and wide,
Looking at the world outside.

Sees a puddle on the ground,
Splashes water all around.
Splash and splish and splash and spritz,
Laughing until Mama fits.

Time to dry the furry coat,
Pretend to be a sailing boat.
Sailing on the living room rug,
Giving Mama a big bear hug.

Drink some milk from a yellow cup,
Now it's time to rest right up.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear with fuzzy toes,
Wiggles round his button nose.
Walks into the sunny wood,
Looking for some yummy food.

Sees a buzzing honey tree,
Climbs up high for all to see.
Stretches out his paw so wide,
Takes a little sweet inside.
Munces honey, sticky sweet,
What a lovely, tasty treat!
Then he waddles down below,
Moving very, very slow.
Finds a soft and leafy bed,
Rests his heavy, sleepy head.
Closes up his big brown eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
Brown bear, brown bear, walking by,
Looking at the open sky.
Sees a bird up in the tree,
Singing out a melody.

Little bear says hello there,
Dancing with a happy air.
Jumps across a little stone,
Glad he is not all alone.

Finds a berry bright and red,
Pops it right inside his head.
Chews it slowly, oh so good,
Deep inside the green, green wood.

Now the sun is going down,
Lighting up the sleepy town.
Time for bed, the shadows creep,
Little bear is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Bear's Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Time for sleep, my furry friend,
Day is coming to an end.
Moon is shining bright and high,
Stars are twinkling in the sky.

Wrap your blanket nice and tight,
Sleep until the morning light.
Softly breathe and close your eyes,
Underneath the gentle skies.

Dream of rivers running blue,
Dream of honey sweet for you.
Forest leaves are rustling low,
Making music soft and slow.

Rest your paws and quiet head,
Tucked inside your cozy bed.
Sleep until the break of day,
All your worries drift away.

rhymes.title: Little Bear, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Little bear with furry toes,
Touch your little button nose.
Little bear with fuzzy ears,
Smile at everything you see here.
Little bear, go stomp, stomp, stomp,
Walk across the grassy swamp.
Little bear, go jump, jump, jump,
Leap across the grassy clump.
Little bear, now spin around,
Sit right down upon the ground.
Little bear, give a hug,
Snuggle tight just like a bug.
Little bear, close your eyes,
Watch the sleepy stars arise.
Little bear, time to sleep,
Do not make a single peep.

rhymes.title: The Honey Pot
rhymes.text:
Brown bear walking through the trees,
Looking for some buzzing bees.
Finds a pot of honey sweet,
What a yummy, sticky treat!
Licks his paws and licks his chin,
Where does sticky honey begin?
In the forest green and wide,
Little bears are full of pride.
Eats a spoonful, one, two, three,
Happy as a bear can be.
Now his tummy feels so round,
Sitting heavy on the ground.
Yawns a big and sleepy yawn,
Waiting for the golden dawn.
Closes up his heavy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Sleep well, bear, until the morn,
Rest until a brand new dawn.

rhymes.title: Bear's Big Paws
rhymes.text:
Big brown bear wakes up today,
Wants to go outside and play.
Runs across the meadow green,
Happiest bear you've ever seen.
Chases leaves that start to blow,
Watching all the rivers flow.
Stomps his feet with heavy sound,
Pounds his paws upon the ground.
Catches butterflies in flight,
Dancing in the morning light.
Then he sits upon a stone,
Happy in the woods alone.
Sun is sinking in the sky,
Little birds begin to fly.
Time to snuggle in his den,
Till the morning comes again.
Goodnight, bear, sleep safe and sound,
While the stars go round and round.

rhymes.title: Little Bear's Red Hat
rhymes.text:
Little bear puts on his hat,
Sitting on the woven mat.
Red and bright for all to see,
Happy as a bear can be.

Down the path he likes to go,
Walking very, very slow.
He meets a squirrel in a tree,
Chasing bugs so wild and free.

Little bear begins to wave,
Stepping from his cozy cave.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little bear to go.

Climbing softly into bed,
Resting down his sleepy head.
Stars are shining in the sky,
Little bear says sweet goodbye.

rhymes.title: Ten Fuzzy Paws
rhymes.text:
Fuzzy bear has furry toes,
Wiggling right beneath his nose.
He can stomp and he can run,
Playing underneath the sun.

Catching raindrops in a pail,
Watching flutterflies take sail.
Then he finds a yellow cup,
Drinking all the water up.

Time to dance across the floor,
Knocking on the wooden door.
Friends are waiting in the street,
Marching with their little feet.

Spinning round and round again,
Happy in the summer rain.
Now the day is done and past,
Sleeping soundly now at last.

rhymes.title: Bear in the Woods
rhymes.text:
Little bear wakes up at dawn,
Walking out upon the lawn.
Eating berries sweet and red,
Nodding sleepy little head.

Climbing up a grassy hill,
Everything is calm and still.
He can hear a birdie sing,
Welcoming the joyful spring.

Down the river water flows,
Tickling little bear's toes.
Splashing water in the air,
Laughing is the playful bear.

Shadows grow across the ground,
Not another single sound.
Moonlight shines upon his bed,
Resting now his furry head.

stories.title: Toby Tiger Wakes Up
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the bright green jungle, lived a little tiger named Toby. Toby had soft orange fur, big brown stripes, and a tiny, pink nose that loved to wiggle. Yawn! Toby opened his big amber eyes. He stretched his front paws way, way out, and then he stretched his back legs until they were as long as noodles. Good morning, jungle! Toby rolled over on his fuzzy back and kicked his paws in the air. He was ready for a wonderful day of play. First, Toby wanted to practice his tiger walk. He crept very, very slowly through the tall green grass. Tip-toe, tip-toe, tip-toe. He made sure not to make a single sound. Suddenly, Toby popped up out of the grass and shouted, Roar! But it was not a scary roar. It was a happy, playful little roar that made the butterflies flutter away with giggles. Then, Toby saw his very best friend, a little monkey swinging from a vine. Hello, monkey! called Toby. Do you want to play hide and seek? The monkey clapped his hands and hid behind a big green leaf. Toby closed his eyes and counted to three. One, two, three! Ready or not, here I come! Toby peeked behind a banana tree. No monkey. He peeked under a big fern. No monkey. Then, Toby looked up. There was the monkey, giggling softly on a branch right above his head! I found you! purred Toby, doing a happy little spin. After playing hide and seek, Toby's tummy began to rumble. Grumble, rumble, went his tummy. It was time for breakfast! Toby trotted over to the cool river with his mommy. Mommy Tiger helped Toby wash his face and paws. Splash, splash, went the cool water. Then, they shared a yummy breakfast of sweet jungle berries. Toby ate every single berry until his tummy was nice and round. The warm sun began to shine down, making Toby feel very sleepy. He snuggled close to his mommy in a cozy bed of soft moss. Mommy Tiger wrapped her warm tail around him like a big fuzzy blanket. Toby closed his eyes, thinking about all the fun games they would play tomorrow. He drifted off to dreamland with a happy little smile on his face, ready for sweet tiger dreams.

stories.title: Toby Tiger Goes Splash
stories.text: It was a very hot afternoon in the jungle, and the sun was shining bright. Phew, it is hot today! said Toby Tiger, wiping a little drop of sweat from his forehead. His orange fur felt extra warm, and his stripes seemed to sizzle in the sunshine. Toby looked at his mommy and asked, Can we go find something cool? Mommy Tiger smiled and nodded her head. Let us go to the splashing river, Toby! Toby was so excited that he did a little hop, skip, and a jump. He loved the river! As they walked down the winding jungle path, Toby saw a brightly colored parrot flying overhead. Squawk, squawk! sang the parrot. Follow me to the water! Toby followed the parrot, moving his little paws as fast as they could go. Soon, they could hear the happy sound of water babbling over smooth stones. Splash, splash, bubble, bubble. Toby let out a joyful cheer when he saw the sparkling blue water glistening in the sunlight. He ran right down to the riverbank. But wait! Toby stopped and looked down at his paws. He had never jumped into the deep part of the river all by himself before. He felt just a little bit shy. Mommy Tiger walked up beside him and gave him a gentle nudge with her nose. You can do it, my brave little tiger, she whispered softly. Toby took a deep breath. He dipped one paw into the water. Ooh! It felt so cool and refreshing against his warm fur. That felt wonderful! Then, he dipped his other paw in. Splash, splash! Toby giggled. Next, he walked in a little deeper until the water tickled his tummy. Wow! This is the best day ever! cried Toby. He splashed the water with his paws, making big droplets fly up into the air like sparkling diamonds. A little frog hopped onto a lily pad nearby and croaked hello. Toby tried to catch the water drops, but they slipped right through his fuzzy fingers. He floated on his back, looking up at the fluffy white clouds shaped like animals in the sky. He saw a cloud that looked just like a tiger! After playing in the cool water for a long time, Toby felt relaxed and happy. Mommy Tiger helped him dry off in the warm breeze. Toby shook his fur until it was fluffy again. With a happy tummy and a cool body, Toby trotted home, looking forward to his next big water adventure.

stories.title: Toby Tiger Counts His Spots
stories.text: One quiet afternoon, Toby Tiger sat under a big shady tree with a basket of shiny red apples. Toby loved to count things. Today, he wanted to count something very special. He wanted to count his stripes! But how do you count your own stripes when they are all over your body? Toby looked down at his front paw. He saw one dark, wiggly stripe. One! he said proudly. But when he looked at his other paw, he saw two more stripes. Two and three! This was going to be trickier than he thought. Just then, his friend the wise old turtle crawled by.
