stories.text: Once upon a sunny jungle day, a little tiger named Timmy woke up with a big stretch. Rrroarr! went Timmy, but softly, because he was just a little cub. Today was a very special day. Timmy wanted to play hide-and-seek with his jungle friends. But first, he needed to practice his tiptoe walk. Timmy looked down at his big, stripey paws. He lifted one paw. Then he lifted the other. Tap, tap, tap went his soft toe beans on the warm dirt path. He saw Benny the butterfly fluttering by. Benny landed right on a bright yellow flower. Timmy wanted to say hello without scaring his tiny friend. So, he flattened his orange and black ears and crept forward very, very slowly. He sucked in his tummy and made his body as low to the ground as a fluffy caterpillar. One, two, three, four steps! Timmy stopped and giggled. He was doing it! He was the best tiptoe tiger in the whole wide world. Suddenly, a rustling sound came from behind a tall green bush. Swish, swish, went the leaves. Out popped Sammy the monkey. 'Found you, Timmy!' shouted Sammy, swinging from a twisty vine. Timmy laughed and gave a happy little pounce into a patch of soft green grass. He rolled onto his back and wiggled his four paws in the air. 'Good try, Sammy!' purred Timmy, sounding just like a giant happy kitty cat. Next, they played tag near the muddy riverbank. Timmy ran as fast as the wind, his stripes blurring in the golden sunshine. He splashed his paws in a cool puddle, sending sparkling water drops flying everywhere. Splash, splash, splash! It felt so tickly and wonderful. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and purple, Timmy's tummy started to rumble. Time for dinner! Timmy trotted all the way back to his cozy den, where his mama was waiting with a yummy meal. After he finished eating, Timmy snuggled close to his mama's warm, soft fur. She gave him a gentle lick right between his ears. Timmy closed his sleepy eyes, dreaming of more wonderful tiptoe adventures for tomorrow. Goodnight, little tiger.

stories.title: Timmy's Lost Stripe
stories.text: The morning sun was shining bright over the green trees when Timmy Tiger woke up and looked at his reflection in a shiny puddle. He blinked once. He blinked twice. Something looked very, very strange! Timmy gasped and sat straight up. One of his lovely black stripes was missing right from his left shoulder! Oh no! Where could it have gone? Timmy stood up on all four paws and began to search everywhere. 'Have you seen my stripe?' Timmy asked Coco the coconut tree, rustling his leafy top. Coco shook his coconuts, but no stripe fell down. Timmy walked over to the bubbly blue river. 'Have you seen my stripe?' he asked the friendly river turtles. They blinked their dark eyes and slowly paddled away, not holding any stripes at all. Timmy felt a little sad. He loved his stripes because they made him look like a fierce, wonderful tiger cub. Just then, he heard a happy giggle coming from behind a big fern bush. Out bounced Pip, the cheeky little monkey. Guess what Pip was wearing like a fancy scarf? Timmy's missing black stripe! It had brushed off on a sticky branch yesterday when Timmy was climbing and playing hide-and-seek. Pip wrapped the stripe around his furry neck and danced around in a silly circle. 'Look at me! I am a monkey-tiger!' cheered Pip. Timmy could not stay mad for even a single second. He burst out laughing. 'Hey, that belongs to my shoulder, you silly monkey!' said Timmy with a grin. Pip giggled and climbed up the tall trunk, dropping the stripe safely right back onto the grass. Timmy picked up the stripe in his mouth, walked over to a flat sunlit rock, and pressed it firmly against his fur. Magic! It stuck right back into place, looking just as neat as all the others. Timmy smiled a big tiger smile and did a happy little wiggle. From that day on, Timmy always checked his favorite trees before playing, making sure all his stripes stayed right where they belonged. He loved his special coat, and he loved playing with his wonderful jungle friends even more.

stories.title: Timmy Tiger Paints the Jungle
stories.text: One breezy afternoon, little Timmy Tiger found a large box of colorful paints resting near a hollow log. The paints had been left behind by some exploring artists who visited the jungle earlier that day. Timmy's eyes sparkled with excitement. He dipped his soft, furry paw right into a jar of bright blue paint. Oh, it felt cold and squishy between his toes! Timmy decided to make a special painting on a large, flat gray boulder. Press! Down went his paw. Lift! Up came his paw. A bright blue tiger paw print appeared on the rock. 'Look what I made!' whispered Timmy happily to himself. He decided he wanted to paint a whole rainbow jungle masterpiece. Next, he dipped his other paw into sunny yellow paint. Press! Down went the paw right next to the blue one. Splash went a tiny drop of yellow on his own nose, making him look very silly indeed. Timmy giggled and wiped his nose with the back of his wrist, leaving a funny streak of yellow paint across his forehead. Then came the red paint, and the green paint, and the sparkly purple paint. Timmy danced across the rock, stamping his feet to make a rhythm: thump, stamp, wiggle, stamp! Soon, the big gray boulder was covered in colorful, happy paw prints of every shade imaginable. Just then, all his jungle friends gathered around to see the big surprise. Benny the butterfly fluttered down and landed right on a purple paw print, matching the color with her own lovely wings. Sammy the monkey clapped his hands together and cheered loudly, doing a happy backflip in the air. Even wise old Mama Tiger walked over, smiling warmly at her creative little cub. She nuzzled Timmy's painted forehead lovingly. 'You are the most artistic little tiger in the jungle,' she purred softly. Timmy beamed with pride, his colorful paws resting proudly on the grass. When the sun went down, the colorful rock glowed softly in the twilight, and Timmy fell asleep dreaming of all the rainbow colors he would use tomorrow.

stories.title: Tilly Tiger's Tiptoe Day
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green jungle, lived a little tiger named Tilly. Tilly had soft orange fur, dark black stripes, and a very wiggly tail. Today was a very special day because Tilly wanted to play hide-and-seek with her jungle friends. 'Roar!' said Tilly, but not too loud. Just a happy little toddler roar! First, Tilly tiptoed over to the tall bamboo stalks. She scrunched up her nose and tried to hide behind a skinny stick. But her big, silly stripes peeked out! Giggling softly, Monkey swung down from a branch and called out, 'I see you, Tilly!' Tilly clapped her paws together with joy. Next, Tilly decided to try a different hiding spot. She walked quietly on her soft, padded paws toward the muddy riverbank. 'Splish, splash,' went her little feet in the warm mud. She crouched down low in the tall green grass, making herself as small as a mouse. Along came Ellie the Elephant, flapping her big ears. Ellie peeked through the grass with her kind eyes and trumpeted softly, 'Found you, little tiger!' Tilly popped right up and gave a happy wiggle. By now, the sun was beginning to set, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink and orange. Tilly's tummy began to rumble. It was time for dinner! She bounded happily back to her cozy den where her mama had a delicious bowl of warm jungle soup waiting for her. Tilly slurped every last drop and licked her whiskers clean. She snuggled down into her soft leafy bed, feeling safe and loved. Mama Tiger stroked Tilly's furry head and whispered, 'Time for sleep, my sweet little tiger.' Tilly yawned a big, wide toddler yawn, closed her sleepy eyes, and dreamed about all the fun adventures they would have tomorrow. Goodnight, Tilly Tiger. Sleep tight.

stories.title: Tommy Tiger's Lost Toy
stories.text: Deep in the leafy jungle, a little tiger named Tommy loved to play with his favorite toy. It was a bright red rubber ball that bounced high into the air. Every morning, Tommy would wake up, stretch his front paws, and go bouncing his ball through the trees. One sunny afternoon, Tommy gave the ball a big, enthusiastic tap. 'Boing!' went the red ball. It bounced over a log, rolled past a bush, and disappeared right into a thick patch of colorful flowers. Tommy blinked his big amber eyes. Oh no! Where did his favorite toy go? Tommy set off on a gentle search. He walked down the winding dirt path, using his sensitive nose to sniff the air. He smelled sweet mangoes and damp earth, but no rubber ball. He peeked behind a large green leaf. 'Are you hiding there, red ball?' he whispered. But it was only a sleepy green frog, who blinked and said, 'Ribbit!' Tommy smiled and gave a friendly wave. Then, Tommy checked under a fallen log where the fuzzy caterpillars lived. He gently lifted a big fern leaf with his paw. And guess what he found? Peekaboo! There was his bright red ball, nestled right in the middle of a patch of yellow daisies. Tommy was so happy he did a little happy dance on his tiptoes. He picked up the ball carefully in his mouth and trotted all the way back to his favorite sunny spot in the clearing. He rolled the ball back and forth with his paws, giggling with delight. Playing was so much fun, especially when you found things that were lost. As the afternoon shadows grew long and cool, Tommy cuddled up with his red ball right beside him. He rested his heavy head on his paws and let out a contented sigh. It had been a wonderful day of searching and playing. With a gentle yawn, Tommy drifted off to dreamland, holding his precious toy safe in his paws.

stories.title: Toby's Stripes of Friendship
stories.text: Little Toby was a very friendly tiger cub who lived near a sparkling blue waterfall. Toby had bright orange fur and lovely black stripes that went all the way from his ears down to the tip of his tail. Toby loved making new friends, but sometimes he was a little bit shy. Today, Toby decided he wanted to share his yummy coconut treats with the other jungle animals. He carefully placed three sweet treats into a woven basket made of vines. With his basket in his mouth, Toby set off down the trail. Soon, he met Bella the Butterfly fluttering her beautiful blue wings. Bella landed gently on a leaf right in front of Toby. Toby smiled his biggest, warmest tiger smile and offered her a sweet coconut treat. Bella fluttered her wings happily and said, 'Thank you so much, Toby!' That made Toby's heart feel warm and fuzzy inside. Encouraged, Toby walked a little further until he saw Sammy the Squirrel chattering away in a tree. Sammy scampered down the trunk in a big hurry, doing a little flip. Toby held out another coconut treat with his paw. Sammy's eyes went wide with delight as he nibbled the yummy snack. 'You are the nicest tiger in the jungle,' Sammy chattered cheerfully. Toby felt so proud and happy. He had one treat left in his basket. Just then, Penny the Parrot swooped down from the canopy with a colorful flutter of feathers. Toby happily shared his last treat with Penny, who sang a sweet, cheerful song to say thank you. By sharing his treats, Toby realized that making friends was the best thing in the whole wide world. With a happy heart, Toby skipped all the way home to his den, ready to tell his family about his wonderful day of sharing. He curled up in his cozy spot, closed his eyes, and smiled in his sleep, dreaming of all his wonderful jungle friends.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger walks around,
Making not a single sound.
Soft and orange is his fur,
Listen to the tiger purr.

Stripes of black from head to toe,
Watch the happy kitty go.
Jumping high and running fast,
Having lots of fun at last.

Now he stops to take a rest,
Crouching in his cozy nest.
Closing up his amber eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Sleeping softly in the breeze.
Goodnight, tiger, time to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Roar Goes the Tiger
rhymes.text:
Roar goes the tiger, loud and bright,
Playing in the morning light.
Chasing butterflies away,
Having such a happy day.

Wiggling his pink little nose,
Tickling his fuzzy toes.
Climbing up a grassy hill,
Now he stops and sits quite still.

Looking for a leafy tree,
Where a monkey swings so free.
Swishing is his furry tail,
Sailing like a shiny boat's sail.

Time to find a yummy snack,
Riding on his mommy's back.
Happy tiger, safe and sound,
Best old jumper can be found.

rhymes.title: Toby's Stripes
rhymes.text:
Count the stripes upon his back,
Orange mixed with lovely black.
Toby is a friendly cat,
Sitting on the forest mat.

Paws are gentle when they tread,
Sleeping in a flower bed.
Chasing leaves that flutter down,
Happiest in all the town.

Drink some water from the stream,
Wake up from a happy dream.
Shake your fur so soft and dry,
As a bird goes flying by.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that he hasn't met.
Time to cuddle close and tight,
Tiger hugs and sleep tight, night.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, walking by,
Looking at the butterfly.
Stripes of orange, bright and neat,
Walking on your furry feet.

Wiggle, waggle, tail goes round,
Touching softly on the ground.
Now you give a happy jump,
Overneath a little stump.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Crawling to your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.

Good night, tiger, time to rest,
In the jungle you love best.
Dream of games and happy play,
Until the coming of the day.

rhymes.title: Stomp Like a Tiger
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, big and tall,
Playing near the garden wall.
Stomp your feet upon the floor,
Give a little baby roar!

Run around the giant tree,
As happy as a bird can be.
Catch the ball and kick it high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Tiger hugs his blanket tight,
Saying to the world, good night.

Stars are shining in the deep,
While the tiger falls asleep.
Sweetest dreams to you, my friend,
Until the very morning end.

rhymes.title: The Orange Tiger
rhymes.text:
Orange tiger, in the sun,
Having lots of jungle fun.
Running fast across the green,
Best little tiger ever seen.

Jump into the river spray,
Splashing water all the day.
Shake your fur from left to right,
Underneath the golden light.

Time to curl up in a ball,
Hearing sleepy night birds call.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Until the dawning of the day.

Sleep well, tiger, cozy tight,
Resting through the quiet night.
Morning brings a brand new sun,
Ready for another run.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, furry friend,
Walking where the jungle ends.
Stripey coat of black and gold,
Bravest tiger, strong and bold.

Soft pink nose and whiskers long,
Singing out a happy song.
Pouncing softly on the ground,
Looking for what can be found.

Little paws go patter-pat,
Look at that, oh look at that!
Chasing leaves that float and fly,
Underneath the big blue sky.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Cuddled in your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little tiger, time to sleep.

rhymes.title: Tiger Time to Play
rhymes.text:
Tiger runs across the green,
Happiest you've ever seen.
Swishing tail from side to side,
Running fast and running wide.

Jumping over logs of wood,
Doing everything he should.
Roaring softly, roar, roar, roar,
Wanting to play even more.

Splashing in a muddy puddle,
Needing now a giant cuddle.
Washing paws and cleaning face,
Running back to resting place.

Eating yummy jungle treat,
Falling fast asleep so sweet.
Dreaming of the morning sun,
Waiting for another run.

rhymes.title: Count the Tiger Stripes
rhymes.text:
Count the stripes upon his back,
Orange fur and shiny black.
One and two and three and four,
Now he gives a little roar.

Five and six and seven, eight,
Tiger playing is so great.
Jumping up to catch a fly,
Reaching way up to the sky.

Nine and ten, now take a rest,
Sleeping is what tigers do best.
Curled up tight upon the floor,
We don't hear a single roar.

Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with sleepy peace and love.
Dreaming through the quiet night,
Till the early morning light.

rhymes.title: Little Striped Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange fur and stripes of black,
I will gently pat your back.

Time to run and time to play,
Chasing butterflies all day.
Leaping over leafy logs,
Saying hello to the frogs.

Softly stepping on the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Twitching your long furry tail,
Down beside the river trail.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the jungle town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little tiger, you're the best.

rhymes.title: Toby's Splashy Day
rhymes.text:
Toby tiger wants to play,
On a sunny summer day.
Walking to the river blue,
Looking for a thing to do.

Jump right in and make a splash,
Running in a joyful dash.
Water droplets in the air,
Flying everywhere up there.

Squishy mud upon your toes,
Water dripping from your nose.
Splish and splash and giggle too,
Jungle water feels like new.

Now the playtime comes to end,
Say goodbye to every friend.
Cuddled in a cozy bed,
Sleeping with a sleepy head.

rhymes.title: The Brave Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Little tiger stands so tall,
Not a giant, very small.
Practicing a mighty sound,
Standing firmly on the ground.

Open up your mouth so wide,
Feel the courage deep inside.
Take a breath and try again,
With your forest animal men.

A little roar that shakes the trees,
Swaying softly in the breeze.
Mama smiles and gives a hug,
Looking at a tiny bug.

Time to dream and time to sleep,
While the shadows start to creep.
Stars are shining up above,
Filled with family peace and love.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little tiger wakes up bright,
Stretches paws to morning light.
Orange fur is soft and sweet,
Walking on his furry feet.

Counting stripes from head to toe,
One, two, three, and off we go!
Four and five and six so fine,
Seven, eight, and number nine.

Ten black stripes upon his back,
Walking down the jungle track.
He can leap and he can bound,
Making not a single sound.

Now the sun begins to sleep,
Little tiger will not peep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to snuggle in your bed.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, big and bold,
Watch him shake his coat of gold.
Pointy ears and whiskers white,
Running in the golden light.

Time to give a happy shout,
See what tigers are about!
Open up your mouth so wide,
Feel the jungle joy inside.

Roar aloud and stomp your feet,
Walking down the woody street.
Catch a butterfly in play,
Have a happy tiger day.

Now the stars are shining bright,
Giving us a cozy light.
Curled up tight and sleeping deep,
Little tiger falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Paws in the Grass
rhymes.text:
Pitter-patter goes the paw,
Best little tiger you ever saw.
Creeping through the emerald green,
Softest creature ever seen.

Stopping by the river side,
Where the happy fishes hide.
Splash a little drop of blue,
Tiger wants to play with you!

Running fast and jumping high,
Reaching for the azure sky.
Chasing leaves that flutter down,
Best jumper in the town.

Time to rest your orange head,
Crawling to your cozy bed.
Mama tiger hugs you tight,
Sleep well, baby, through the night.

rhymes.title: Little Striped Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange coat and stripes of black,
Pat your little fuzzy back.

Jump up high into the air,
Show your playful tiger stare.
Chase a butterfly around,
Softly landing on the ground.

Purr a happy little song,
All day long you bounce along.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little cats to go.

Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Dream of jungle trees so green,
Sweetest tiger ever seen.

rhymes.title: Toby's Tail
rhymes.text:
See the tiger swish his tail,
Swishing like a windy sail.
Wiggle left and wiggle right,
Stripes are shining in the light.

Stomp your feet upon the floor,
Give a tiny little roar!
Roar so loud and roar so proud,
Making happy sounds out loud.

Time to run and time to play,
All throughout the sunny day.
Splash into the water blue,
Happy tiger, dancing too.

Now the playtime days are done,
Time to rest away the sun.
Cuddle close and sleep up tight,
Tiger, tiger, rest tonight.

rhymes.title: Five Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
One little tiger waking up,
Drinking milk from a tiny cup.
Two little tigers jump and play,
Chasing shadows all the day.

Three little tigers climb a tree,
Looking out for you and me.
Four little tigers splashing mud,
Stomping through a bubbly flood.

Five little tigers yawn and sigh,
Watching clouds go floating by.
Cuddling up in cozy bed,
Pillows soft beneath each head.

Snuggle close and shut your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Sleep until the morning light,
Tiger babies, sleep tight, tight.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange fur and stripes of black,
Pat your little fuzzy back.

Time to jump and time to play,
Chasing butterflies all day.
Little paws go tip-toe-toe,
See how fast a cub can go!

Roar a tiny little sound,
Jumping softly on the ground.
Now the sun is going down,
Best small tiger in the town.

Curl up tight and go to sleep,
While the stars shine bright and deep.
Dream of jungle trees so green,
Sweetest tiger ever seen.

rhymes.title: Tiger in the Grass
rhymes.text:
Tiger walking in the grass,
Watch the little kitty pass.
Stripes of orange, stripes of night,
Looking very proud and bright.

Can you give a little purr?
Rubbing on your golden fur.
Can you leap and can you bound,
Making not a single sound?

Stop and wiggle round and round,
Sitting down upon the ground.
Time to eat a yummy treat,
Something nice for you to eat.

Now the playtime days are done,
Resting underneath the sun.
Close your eyes and softly sigh,
Little tiger, lullaby.

rhymes.title: Five Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
One little tiger waking from a nap,
Stretching out his paws upon his little lap.
Two little stripes upon his shiny nose,
Wiggling around his tiny little toes.

Three little jumps into the water blue,
Splashing all around just like tigers do.
Four little friends are coming out to play,
Happy in the jungle on a sunny day.

Five little roars that echo in the trees,
Carried softly by the gentle morning breeze.
Now the little tiger starts to yawn and creep,
Curling up in bed to fall right fast asleep.

Goodnight to the jungle and the river wide,
Sleeping by his mama with a joyful pride.
Dreams of golden sunshine and a happy song,
Little baby tiger, sleeping all night long.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Stripes of orange, stripes of black,
Patches on your little back.

In the jungle, green and deep,
While the little monkeys sleep,
Little tiger starts to play,
Chasing butterflies all day.

Jump up high and give a roar,
Then you run across the floor.
Curl up in your cozy bed,
Rest your sleepy, furry head.

Time to dream and time to rest,
With your mama, feeling blest.
Close your eyes and sleep so tight,
Goodnight, tiger, sleep till light.

rhymes.title: Tiger's Stripes
rhymes.text:
Tiger, tiger, big and bold,
With a coat of yellow gold.
Tell me where your stripes all go,
Walking in the river flow.

One stripe here and one stripe there,
Running through the sunny air.
Bouncing up and bounding down,
Happiest cat in the town.

Catch a leaf that falls from trees,
Dancing in the gentle breeze.
Make a friend and give a smile,
Rest beside him for a while.

Now the sun is going down,
Putting on its sleepy gown.
Tiger hugs his mother tight,
Dreaming sweetly through the night.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Roar, little tiger, let me hear,
Sounds of joy that bring good cheer.
Paws so soft and tail so long,
Singing out a happy song.

Jump into the river splash,
Making such a water dash.
Shake your fur until it's dry,
Watching birdies fly on high.

Find a snack of berries sweet,
What a yummy, tasty treat!
Now it's time to run around,
Stomping softly on the ground.

Shadows stretch across the floor,
Tiger doesn't want to roar.
Yawning wide because of sleep,
Counting stars that twinkle deep.

rhymes.title: Little Stripe
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, furry and bright,
Running fast in the morning light.
Orange coat and black stripes too,
Looking all around at you.

Pounce and play upon the grass,
Watch the yellow butterflies pass.
Wiggle your tail and hide your face,
Running all around the place.

Now the sun is going down,
No more running through the town.
Curl up tight upon the floor,
Tiger sleep and snore some more.

rhymes.title: Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Soft little paws upon the ground,
Walking without a single sound.
Tiger cub with eyes so green,
The cutest kitty ever seen.

Jump so high into the air,
Looking for a friend right there.
Make a roar that sounds like squeak,
Playing hide and go-and-seek.

Drink the water from the stream,
Time to start a sleepy dream.
Tiger hugs and kisses too,
Little tiger, I love you.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Roar, little tiger, big and loud,
Making all the jungle proud.
Climb a tree and look around,
Happy with the happy sound.

Chase a leaf of green and red,
Time to bounce upon your bed.
Tickle toes and tickle nose,
Where the happy tiger goes.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little birds are flying high.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger walks around,
Softly stepping on the ground.
Orange fur and stripes of black,
Pat him gently on the back.
Little tiger likes to play,
Chasing butterflies all day.
Jumping high up in the air,
Without a single worry or care.
Now the sun is going down,
Quiet shadows wrap the town.
Tiger curls up on the floor,
Softly sleeping, time to snore.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Swaying in the gentle breeze.

rhymes.title: Tiger's Stripes
rhymes.text:
Stripes of black and coat of gold,
Watch the little tiger bold.
Walking through the jungle grass,
Letting all the monkeys pass.
Tiger makes a happy sound,
Rolling softly on the ground.
Pouncing on a feather toy,
What a clever little boy!
Now he wiggles furry toes,
Scratching at his little nose.
Yawning with a sleepy sigh,
Watching clouds go floating by.
Cuddling up in cozy bed,
Resting now his sleepy head.
Sleep, sweet tiger, through the night,
Till the morning brings its light.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger!
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, big and bright,
Running in the morning light.
Show your teeth and give a roar,
Stomping softly on the floor.
Prancing near the river side,
Where the happy fishes hide.
Splash your paws into the blue,
Little tiger, I see you!
Time to rest your orange head,
Crawling to your cozy bed.
Pull the blankets up so high,
Watch the moon up in the sky.
Stars are shining, bright and clear,
Sleepy tiger, do not fear.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little tiger wakes up bright,
Stretching paws into the light.
Orange fur so soft and sweet,
Walking on four fuzzy feet.

Black stripes running down his back,
Making such a lovely track.
Little tiger says hello,
Watch the happy kitty go.

Running through the jungle green,
Best little tiger ever seen.
Chasing butterflies so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little tiger, you are best.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger!
rhymes.text:
Can you roar just like a cat?
Stomp your feet and pat, pat, pat!
Little tiger wears a grin,
Let the jungle fun begin.

Jump up high and touch the floor,
Then let out a little roar!
Roar, roar, hear him say,
Time to jump and time to play.

Wiggle, wiggle goes his tail,
Sailing like a furry sail.
Now he stops to take a look,
Reading from his picture book.

Time for hugs and time for bed,
Pillow underneath his head.
Goodnight tiger, sleep up tight,
Dream sweet dreams the whole dark night.

rhymes.title: TIGER ON THE GO
rhymes.text:
Tiger walks upon the grass,
Watch the striped kitty pass.
Softly padding, one, two, three,
Hiding by the banyan tree.

Pouncing softly on a leaf,
Having fun beyond belief.
Now he runs across the lane,
Dancing in the summer rain.

Splish and splash upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Shake your fur to make it dry,
Wave a happy wave goodbye.

Tiger curls up in his bed,
Pillow underneath his head.
Stars are shining up above,
Filled with sleepy tiger love.

rhymes.title: Little Stripey Tiger
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange fur and stripes of black,
Carrying a gentle pack.

In the jungle, warm and bright,
Playing all the sunny light.
Jump and leap upon the grass,
Watch the happy monkeys pass.

Time to give a little roar,
Then you rest upon the floor.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars above you peep.

Dream of trees and leafy bowers,
Resting through the quiet hours.
Goodnight, tiger, sleep till morn,
Fresh and happy you are born.

rhymes.title: Toby's Paws
rhymes.text:
Toby tiger has big paws,
Sharp and shiny little claws.
Stamping on the forest floor,
Letting out a happy roar.

Running down the muddy track,
Stripey patterns on his back.
Chasing butterflies of blue,
Wondering what they will do.

Stopping by the river side,
Where the happy fishes hide.
Splash and sparkle in the sun,
Look at how they jump and run.

Tired now from all the play,
Ending such a lovely day.
Curls up in his cozy bed,
Sleeping softly, sleepyhead.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
One, two, three, four, stripes of black,
Sitting on a tiger's back.
Five and six, his paws so neat,
Tippy-tapping on his feet.

Seven, eight, his tail goes swish,
Looking for a swimming fish.
Nine and ten, he gives a bound,
Leaping high above the ground.

Now he curls up in the shade,
Where the leafy ferns are laid.
Yawning wide, a sleepy sound,
Softest tiger can be found.

Close your eyes and rest your head,
Tiger in your cozy bed.
Dreaming till the morning light,
Little tiger, sleep tight, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange fur and black stripes too,
I am so glad I found you!

Can you give a little roar?
Roar once, roar twice, and no more.
Now you curl up on the floor,
Sleeping softly by the door.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your warm and cozy bed.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the sun brings brand new day.

Good night, tiger, time to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Dream of jungle trees so green,
Sweetest tiger ever seen.

rhymes.title: Tiger Stripes Go Round
rhymes.text:
Tiger, tiger, running fast,
Hope the sunny day will last.
Jump up high and touch the sky,
Wave a friendly paw goodbye.

Stripey tail goes swish and sway,
All throughout the happy day.
Find a friend to run and play,
Chasing troubles far away.

Now the jungle gets quite still,
Moonlight shines upon the hill.
Crawl into your furry nest,
Time for little cats to rest.

Softly purr a sleepy tune,
Underneath the golden moon.
Sleep until the morning light,
Tiger, tiger, sleep tight, good night.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Bounce, bounce, tiger bold,
In the forest green and old.
Show your bright and shiny coat,
Floating like a little boat.

Tap your paws upon the ground,
Listen to the happy sound.
Spin around and try to see,
Who is hiding by the tree.

It's a monkey swinging down,
Wearing nature's leafy crown.
Give a giggle, give a cheer,
Glad to have a playmate near.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Tiger is too tired to leap.
Snuggle close and close your eyes,
Underneath the evening skies.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange fur and stripes of black,
With a fuzzy, wiggly back.

Time to jump and time to play,
Chasing butterflies all day.
Little nose that likes to sniff,
Running up the grassy cliff.

Now the sun is going down,
Leaving behind golden brown.
Time to curl up in your bed,
Rest your sleepy, heavy head.

Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Dreaming of the jungle trees,
Whispering in the gentle breeze.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Hear the tiger softly say,
'Let us go outside and play!'
Stretching arms up to the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.

Walking softly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Then you give a little pounce,
Up you go with every bounce!

Toby is a friendly cat,
Playing with a fuzzy rat.
Running fast across the floor,
Giving such a happy roar.

Now the day is nearly done,
Time to rest away the sun.
Snuggle deep into your nest,
Tiger cubs deserve a rest.

rhymes.title: Tiger Stripes and Spots
rhymes.text:
Count the stripes upon your back,
Orange mixed with shiny black.
One, two, three, and four and five,
Glad to be so much alive!

Jump into the muddy pool,
Water nice and fresh and cool.
Splash the water all around,
Happy tiger safe and sound.

Time to shake the water dry,
Underneath the big blue sky.
Eat a leaf and chew a twig,
Growing up so tall and big.

Time to snuggle in the dark,
Far away from jungle park.
Sleep until the morning light,
Tiger cub, sleep tight, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Orange coat and stripes so black,
Happy tiger, look and smack!
Jump up high into the air,
Show your cute and fuzzy hair.
Wag your tail from side to side,
In the jungle, take a ride.
Find a friend to play a game,
Every tiger has a name.
Chasing butterflies around,
Making such a happy sound.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy tiger bed.

rhymes.title: Roar, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
See the tiger in the sun,
Running fast and having fun.
Soft paws patting on the floor,
Let us hear a little roar!
Roar, roar, nice and low,
Watch the happy tiger go.
Climbing up a fuzzy tree,
Looking all around to see.
Butterfly upon a leaf,
Tiger jumps without a grief.
Catch it gently in your hand,
Bestest tiger in the land.
Now it is time for a nap,
Sleeping in a cozy lap.
Dreaming of the jungle breeze,
Resting underneath the trees.

rhymes.title: Stripes and Spots
rhymes.text:
Tiger has some lovely stripes,
Eating juicy forest tripes.
Well, he loves a berry snack,
Carried safely on his back.
Stomp your feet and give a cheer,
Glad that little cats are here.
Friendly smile and whiskers long,
Singing out a happy song.
Now we march across the floor,
Giving one big happy roar!
Then we sit and count to three,
Quiet as a sleepy bee.
Snuggle down upon the rug,
Waiting for a mama hug.
Twinkle stars are shining bright,
Sleep well, tiger, through the night.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger on the floor,
Trying out a tiny roar.
Soft and fluffy, orange and bright,
Running in the morning light.

Stripey tail goes swish and sway,
Ready for a fun-filled day.
Walking softly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.

Climbing up a little tree,
Happy as a cub can be.
Chasing bugs of green and blue,
Wondering what else to do.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little cats to go.
Curled up in a cozy bed,
Sleeping sleepy little head.

rhymes.title: Five Little Stripes
rhymes.text:
Five little stripes on a tiger so sweet,
Marching along on four little feet.
One went to sleep in a cozy sun spot,
Wishing for weather that's nice and hot.

Two went to play by the river so blue,
Splashing around like tigers do.
Three went to hide behind a big tree,
Quietly peeking for everyone to see.

Four went to chase a butterfly high,
Fluttering softly up in the sky.
Five stayed right on his furry cute back,
Ready to roll on a grassy track.

Now they are back on the tiger so grand,
Best little cub in the jungle land.

rhymes.title: Tiger's Naptime
rhymes.text:
Little tiger had some fun,
Running all beneath the sun.
Now his paws are feeling slow,
Where does little tiger go?

To his den of leaves and grass,
Watching fluffy dream clouds pass.
Closing up his amber eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

Mama purrs a lullaby,
While the gentle breezes sigh.
Snuggle close and rest your head,
In your warm and cozy bed.

Morning time will come around,
With a happy jumping sound.
Rest until the brand new day,
Tiger time to sleep and play.

rhymes.title: Little Tiger Paws
rhymes.text:
Little tiger on the ground,
Walking without any sound.
Soft and fuzzy orange fur,
Listen to the kitty purr.
Black stripes painted on his back,
Walking down the jungle track.
He can jump and he can play,
Chasing butterflies all day.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the jungle town.
Curl up tight and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dreaming of a sunny tree,
As happy as a cat can be.
Goodnight tiger, rest your head,
Time for sleeping in your bed.

rhymes.title: Tiger's Stripes
rhymes.text:
See the tiger walking by,
Looking up into the sky.
Orange coat and stripes of black,
Carrying a shiny pack.
Stamping with a gentle beat,
Using furry little feet.
Roaring softly to his friends,
Where the winding river bends.
Jumping over leafy logs,
Saying hello to the frogs.
Happy tiger, full of glee,
Climbing up a fuzzy tree.
Now the stars begin to glow,
Swinging to and fro, and fro.
Time to rest your sleepy paws,
Sleeping underneath the stars.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Tiger
rhymes.text:
Little tiger, time to rest,
Snuggled in your cozy nest.
Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
Now you drift away to sleep.
Orange stripes upon your head,
Tucked inside your leafy bed.
Dream of bouncing high and low,
Where the sweet bananas grow.
Mama tiger hugs you tight,
Kisses you a fond goodnight.
Stars are shining bright and clear,
Knowing that your friends are near.
Not a sound is in the trees,
Whispering a gentle breeze.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little tiger, sleep tight, tight.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text:
Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and get ready with Gerry the Giraffe. Gerry has a very long neck. Can you stretch your neck up high like Gerry? Stretch, stretch, stretch! Gerry lives on the sunny savanna, and today is a very special day. It is time for him to go to the jungle playground to meet all of his animal friends. But first, Gerry needs to put on his clothes. Now, getting dressed when you have four long legs and a super-duper long neck can be a little bit tricky. Let us help Gerry figure out what to wear! 

First up, Gerry needs his socks. Oh dear, oh dear! Where do the socks go? On his feet, of course! Gerry has four big feet. One, two, three, four! He bends way down low to wiggle his toes into his fuzzy yellow socks. Red socks, blue socks, polka dot socks! Toddlers, can you wiggle your toes just like Gerry? Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! 

Next, Gerry needs his shirt. Gerry pulls a bright red shirt over his head. Pop goes his head through the top! But wait, look at his long neck. His neck is still sticking way out of the shirt like a giant yellow pole. That is okay! Gerry thinks his new look is very silly and very fun. He giggles, 'Giggle, giggle, giggle!' 

Finally, Gerry needs his favorite red hat to keep the warm sun out of his big brown eyes. He lifts his long neck up as high as it can go, reaches up with his hoof, and places the hat right on top of his head. Ta-da! Gerry is fully dressed and ready to play. He brushes his teeth, gives his mom a big hug, and skips out the door. 'Goodbye, Mom!' he calls. Gerry is ready for an amazing day of fun with his friends in the sunny savanna. Are you ready to play too?

stories.title: Gerry Goes Shopping
stories.text:
Hello again, little friends! Today, Gerry the Giraffe is going on a big adventure to the animal supermarket. Gerry needs to buy some yummy snacks for his lunchbox. Can you march in place like Gerry walking to the store? March, march, march! Gerry loves going shopping because he gets to see all of his favorite neighbors along the way. 

When Gerry walks into the big supermarket, he looks all around. The store is full of delicious fruits and vegetables. Gerry grabs a shiny red shopping cart. Because Gerry is so very tall, he does not even have to bend down to push the cart. He pushes it with his nose, beep beep! 

First, Gerry stops in the fruit aisle. He wants to buy some yummy, yellow bananas. Gerry stretches his long neck up, up, up to the very top shelf. He gently picks a bunch of bananas with his soft purple tongue. One, two, three, four, five bananas go right into his cart. Mmm, bananas are so sweet and delicious! 

Next, Gerry needs some crunchy green leaves. Where are the green leaves? Oh, they are way up high on the hanging displays! Gerry stands on his tiptoes and reaches up with his long neck. He grabs a big bunch of leafy greens. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Gerry takes a tiny little taste test right there in the store. 'Yummy in my tummy!' he smiles. 

Finally, Gerry pushes his cart to the checkout line. The cashier is a friendly little monkey. The monkey looks up at Gerry and giggles. 'That will be five shiny shells, please, Gerry!' Gerry counts out his shells and puts his groceries into a big cloth bag. He waves goodbye to the monkey and skips all the way home, ready to eat his wonderful lunch. What a fun day at the store!

stories.title: Gerry Takes a Bath
stories.text:
Splish, splash, splish, splash! It is the end of a very busy day, and Gerry the Giraffe is covered in dusty savanna dirt from head to toe. Gerry has dirt on his knees, dirt on his tummy, and even a little speck of dirt right on the tip of his nose. Oh my goodness! It is definitely time for a warm, bubbly bath. Can you pretend to splash water like Gerry? Splash, splash, splash! 

Let us help Gerry get into the big, bubbly bathtub. The tub is filled with warm, cozy water and fluffy white bubbles that look like little clouds. Gerry steps into the tub with a big *plop!* Water splashes everywhere. Gerry laughs, 'Ha, ha, ha!' The bubbles tickle his tummy. 

Now it is time to wash up. First, we need some strawberry-scented soap. We scrub Gerry's long legs. Scrub, scrub, scrub! We scrub his spotted back. Scrub, scrub, scrub! Look at all those funny bubble hats on Gerry's head. He looks like a king wearing a crown made of fluffy white foam. Gerry uses the bubbles to give himself a funny mustache. He looks in the mirror and roars like a lion, 'Roar!' Then he giggles at his own silly reflection. 

Next, it is time to rinse the soap away. Gerry takes a big cup and pours warm water over his head. Rinse, rinse, rinse! All the dirt washes right down the drain, bye-bye dirt! Gerry is sparkling clean and smells like sweet strawberries. 

Finally, Gerry steps out of the tub and wraps himself up in a big, fluffy blue towel. He rubs his arms and legs until he is nice and dry. Gerry gives a big, happy yawn. He puts on his cozy star-printed pajamas and snuggles deep into his soft bed. His mom turns off the light and whispers, 'Good night, sweet giraffe.' Gerry closes his eyes and drifts off to sleep, dreaming of tall trees and sunny days. Sleep tight, Gerry!

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and get ready with Gerry the giraffe. Gerry lives in a big sunny grassland, and today is a very special day because he is going to his very first animal party with all his woodland friends. Ding-dong goes the alarm clock! Gerry stretches his long, long neck all the way up to the sky. Yawn! He blinks his big brown eyes and wiggles his fuzzy little ears. Time to get dressed, Gerry! First, Gerry needs to put on his shirt. Oh dear, his neck is so tall that he needs a special super-long shirt with lots and lots of buttons. Button one, click. Button two, click. Button three, click. Gerry counts them all the way up to ten! Now, Gerry looks down at his feet. He has four long, bouncy legs. He needs to put on his shiny yellow shoes. One shoe, two shoes, three shoes, four shoes! Tie the laces in a big floppy bow. But wait, Gerry looks in the mirror and giggles. He forgot something very important! He forgot his silly polka-dot hat. Gerry stretches his neck up, up, up, and plops the bright red hat right on top of his head. Perfect! Now Gerry is dressed and ready to go. He skips out the front door, shouting hello to the buzzing bumblebees and the fluttering butterflies. He walks down the winding path, swinging his long tail left and right. Soon, Gerry arrives at the party. All his animal friends cheer and clap their paws. 'Hooray for Gerry!' they shout. Gerry does a happy little dance, shaking his knees and wobbling his long neck from side to side. Eating yummy green leaves and playing games with his best friends makes Gerry feel like the luckiest giraffe in the whole wide world. As the sun begins to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Gerry gives everyone a big warm hug. What a wonderful, busy, happy day it has been. Time to walk home under the twinkling stars, wash those big feet, and snuggle deep into bed for sweet dreams.

stories.title: Gerry Goes to the Playground
stories.text: Splish, splash, sunshine! Today Gerry the giraffe is going to the neighborhood playground for a fun-filled afternoon of play. Gerry loves the playground because everything is so colorful and exciting. He takes giant steps over the green grass, marching left, right, left, right, until he reaches the big shiny gate. Hello, playground! The very first thing Gerry sees is the giant slide. It is tall, but Gerry is even taller! He bends his knees down low and climbs up the ladder, ruff, ruff, puff. When he gets to the top, he can see all the way across the park. He waves hello to a little brown squirrel sitting in an oak tree. Then, Gerry shouts 'Wheee!' and slides all the way down, whoosh! He lands safely in the soft woodchips with a happy thump. Next, Gerry spots the tall yellow swings. He wants to swing, but his long legs are a little too big for the toddler swing. So what does Gerry do? He uses his clever mind to help his friends instead. Little monkey wants to swing, but he cannot reach the chains. Gerry gently lifts the little monkey up and places him safely in the swing seat. Then, Gerry uses his long fingers to give the swing a gentle push. Back and forth, back and forth, higher and higher! Little monkey giggles with joy, shouting 'Faster, Gerry, faster!' Gerry smiles a big, warm giraffe smile. Sharing and helping friends makes his heart feel so warm and happy. After swinging for a long time, Gerry walks over to the sandbox. He digs his long hooves into the cool, soft sand and builds a giant castle with three towers and a moat. He decorates the top with shiny purple pebbles and bright green leaves. All the playground friends gather around to admire the magnificent castle. They clap their hands and cheer for Gerry. As the afternoon breeze blows gently through the trees, Gerry sits down on the grass for a healthy snack of crunchy orange carrots and sweet green leaves. Playing together is the absolute best way to spend a sunny day.

stories.title: Gerry's Counting Adventure
stories.text: Come along on a fun counting adventure with Gerry the giraffe! Today, Gerry is going on a special walk through the whispering woods to find tasty treats for a yummy afternoon picnic. Are you ready to count along with Gerry? Let us begin! First, Gerry takes a big stretchy step outside his cozy yellow cottage. Look up in the sky! Gerry sees one big, bright, golden sun shining down to warm his furry back. Can you point to the sun? Great job! Gerry takes two more steps and stops near a leafy green bush. He blinks his big brown eyes and counts two buzzing yellow bees flying in circles. Buzz, buzz, buzz! They fly right past his long spotted nose. Gerry giggles and keeps on walking. Soon, Gerry reaches the sparkling blue river. He looks down at the water and spots three slippery orange fish splashing and jumping in the waves. Splash, splash, splash! They wave their little fins hello. Gerry waves back with his hoof. Now, Gerry is getting very hungry. He stretches his super-long neck up, up, up into the leafy branches of the tall acacia tree. Let us count the yummy green leaves together! One, two, three, four. Gerry plucks four delicious leaves right off the branch and munches them up with a loud crunch, crunch, crunch. How yummy! Suddenly, Gerry hears a rustling sound in the bushes near his feet. Five tiny brown ladybugs with black spots crawl out to say hello. One, two, three, four, five! They crawl all the way up Gerry's long leg for a friendly visit. Gerry stays very still so he does not tickle them. He loves all his little woodland neighbors, big and small. With a full tummy and a happy heart, Gerry counts his steps all the way back home. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Gerry is safely back at his front door, ready for a cozy afternoon nap. Counting is so much fun when you share it with a gentle, long-necked friend like Gerry the giraffe.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tall, very sweet friend. Who is it? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry is waking up in his cozy bed, and guess what? The sun is shining bright and warm in the sky. Gerry stretches his long, long neck. Stretch, stretch, stretch! He stretches all the way up to the ceiling. 'Good morning, sun!' says Gerry. Now, it is time for Gerry to get dressed for a fun day of playing outside with his animal friends. But wait! Getting dressed when you are a giraffe is a very tricky job. First, Gerry needs to put on his cozy shirt. He picks up a bright yellow shirt with big blue dots. How does a giraffe put on a shirt? He has to lift his long arms way up high! Gerry raises his left arm up, up, up. Then he raises his right arm up, up, up. He slips the shirt over his head. Oh, oh! His head is so high up that he bumps the ceiling light! Tinkle, tinkle, goes the light. Gerry giggles. 'Oops!' he says. Next, Gerry needs to put on his pants. Now, pants are even trickier than shirts. Gerry has four long, long legs. One, two, three, four! He steps his first foot into the pants. Then his second foot. Then his third foot. And then his fourth foot! Gerry wobbles like a jelly on a plate. Wibble, wobble, wibble, wobble! Oh no, he is losing his balance! Gerry reaches out and holds onto his tall wooden wardrobe to steady himself. That is much better. He pulls his pants all the way up to his tummy. Zip, zip, goes the zipper! Look at Gerry now. He is wearing his bright yellow shirt and his nice blue pants. But wait, his feet are still bare. Gerry looks down at his hooves. 'Shoes, shoes, where are my shoes?' he asks. He finds his little red shoes under the bed. He bends his long neck all the way down, down, down to his feet. Stretch goes his neck! He ties the left shoe. Tie, loop, and pull! Then he ties the right shoe. Tie, loop, and pull! Gerry is finally all dressed and ready to go outside. He does a happy little dance, shaking his tall body from side to side. Shook-a, shook-a, shook-a! 'I am ready for the day!' cheers Gerry. He opens his front door and steps out into the warm, golden sunshine. What a wonderful morning for a tall, happy giraffe.

stories.title: Gerry's Tummy Rumble
stories.text: Rub-a-dub-dub, what is that loud sound coming from the trees? Rumbl-e-e, rumbl-e-e, rumble! Oh my goodness, it is Gerry the Giraffe’s tummy! Gerry’s tummy is making very big noises because Gerry is very, very hungry. When you are a tall giraffe, your tummy is very big, and it needs lots and lots of yummy food to keep you strong. Gerry looks up into the sky. He sees some fluffy white clouds, and way up at the very top of the tallest tree, he sees the most delicious green leaves in the whole wide world. 'Yum, yum, yum!' says Gerry. But there is a little problem. The leaves are high up in the sky, and Gerry is standing on the ground. How can he reach them? Gerry knows just what to do. He uses his super-duper giraffe superpowers! First, Gerry stands up as straight and tall as a flagpole. He stretches his neck up toward the clouds. Stretch, stretch, stretch! He opens his mouth wide. Ahhh! But the leaves are still just a little bit too far away. Gerry does not give up. He stands on his tippy-toes. One, two, three, stretch! He reaches up with his long, purple tongue. Swoosh! Out comes Gerry’s tongue. It is so long and stretchy. Gerry’s tongue wraps right around a bunch of juicy green leaves. Snap! He picks them right off the branch. Gerry pulls the leaves into his mouth and starts to chew. Munch, munch, munch! Crunch, crunch, crunch! The leaves taste sweet and fresh like morning rain. Gerry smiles a big, happy smile. But his tummy says rumble, rumble, rumble again. One leaf is not enough for a big giraffe! Gerry looks at another tree. This tree has sweet yellow flowers growing at the very top. Gerry stretches his neck to the left. Stretch! He grabs a flower. Munch, munch, munch! Then he stretches his neck to the right. Stretch! He grabs another flower. Munch, munch, munch! Gerry eats and eats until his tummy is round and full like a basketball. Pat, pat, pat goes Gerry on his happy tummy. The rumbling has stopped. 'Thank you, trees!' whispers Gerry. He gives the tallest tree a gentle, loving nuzzle with his soft nose. Now Gerry is full, happy, and ready to take a nice afternoon nap in the cool, green grass.

stories.title: Gerry Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The sun is starting to go down, down, down behind the green hills. The sky is turning pink and orange and purple. The little birds are flying back to their nests, singing, 'Chep, chep, chep! Time for bed!' It is time for Gerry the Giraffe to go to sleep, too. Gerry gives a big, long yawn. Yaaawn! He rubs his sleepy eyes with his hooves. Rub, rub, rub. Gerry is feeling very tired after running and playing all day long. But wait! How does a giant giraffe go to sleep? Do you think Gerry sleeps in a little toddler bed? No way! His long neck would hang right off the edge! Do you think Gerry sleeps standing up? Sometimes giraffes do that, but tonight Gerry wants to be extra cozy. He walks over to a soft patch of green grass under a big shady tree. First, Gerry has to bend his long, knobby legs. Bend the left knee, bend the right knee. Down, down, down goes Gerry. He sits right down on his tummy, folding his long legs neatly underneath him like a fluffy pillow. Now comes the trickiest part of all. What does Gerry do with his super-long neck? He cannot just let it flop on the ground! So Gerry curls his long neck all the way around, resting his heavy head gently upon his own back. There he is, curled up just like a big, sweet, yellow-and-brown cinnamon roll! Gerry closes his eyes. The soft evening breeze blows gently through the leaves above. Swish, swish, go the leaves. A little cricket sings a lullaby in the grass. Chirp, chirp, chirp. Gerry takes a nice, deep breath in. And a long breath out. He feels so safe and so cozy in his grassy bed. The moon comes up into the dark blue night sky, shining its bright silver light down on Gerry. The little stars twinkle and wink at him. Twinkle, twinkle, little stars. Gerry is fast asleep, dreaming sweet dreams of tall trees, green leaves, and sunny days. Good night, Gerry. Sleep tight, little giraffe. See you in the morning when the sun comes up again.

stories.title: Gerry Goes to the Park
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green land, lived a tall, gentle giraffe named Gerry. Gerry had bright yellow fur, big brown spots, and the longest, wiggliest neck in the whole wide world. Gerry loved sunny mornings because sunny mornings meant it was time to visit the toddler playground! With a tap and a tap and a tip-toe-tap, Gerry walked down the bumpy dirt path. His long legs made big, swooshy steps. When Gerry reached the playground, all his little animal friends shouted, 'Hooray! Gerry is here!' A tiny blue bird named Pip fluttered down and landed right on Gerry's long, purple nose. 'Good morning, Gerry!' chirped Pip. 'Can you help us find our lost red balloon?' Gerry blinked his big, sleepy eyes and smiled. 'Of course I can, little Pip!' Gerry said in a deep, rumbling, happy voice. Gerry stretched his long, stretchy neck up, up, up into the sky. He stretched past the fluffy white clouds, past the tall oak tree, and way up high. 'I see it!' Gerry called out. Tied to the very top branch of the big green tree was the bright red balloon, bouncing up and down in the wind. Gerry reached out his soft nose and gently plucked the string with his teeth. Down, down, down came Gerry's long neck, all the way back to the grass. He handed the red balloon right to Pip. 'Yay! Thank you, Gerry!' cheered all the little animals, jumping up and down with glee. Gerry felt so warm and happy inside. Playing with friends was the very best thing to do. Then, the afternoon sun began to sink low, painting the sky in pink and orange. It was time for dinner. Gerry bent down, using his long, dark tongue to munch on the sweet, crunchy green leaves from the low bushes. Yum, yum, yum! Gerry chewed his tasty leaves and let out a long, sleepy yawn. 'Goodnight, playground,' whispered Gerry. He curled his long legs underneath his big round tummy, closed his eyes, and drifted off to a sweet, dreamy sleep, knowing he was the tallest and happiest giraffe in the whole wide world. The end.

stories.title: Gerry's Magic Scarf
stories.text: The wind was blowing a soft, chilly breeze across the grassy plain. 'Brr!' shivered Gerry the giraffe, wrapping his long neck in a warm, cozy hug. But even with a hug, Gerry's neck felt just a little bit cold. 'Oh my,' said Gerry, looking down at his friends the fuzzy little bunnies. 'My neck is simply too long for ordinary clothes!' Just then, his clever monkey friend, Coco, swung down from a leafy branch. Coco was holding a big basket full of colorful yarn. 'Don't worry, Gerry!' chattered Coco. 'We are going to knit you the most magical scarf in the whole wide world!' All the jungle animals gathered around to help. The elephants used their big feet to hold the yarn balls still. The little mice used their tiny paws to weave the yarn together. And Coco knitted as fast as his furry fingers could go. Loop, loop, pull. Loop, loop, pull. They knitted red stripes, blue stripes, yellow stripes, and bright green stripes. It took a very long time, because Gerry's neck was super-duper long! Finally, Coco shouted, 'All done!' They wrapped the giant scarf around Gerry's neck. It went round and round and round, one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight times! Gerry looked down at himself in the mirror of the shiny blue pond. He looked like a walking rainbow! 'How do you feel, Gerry?' asked all the animals eagerly. Gerry blinked his big brown eyes and gave a happy wiggle. 'I feel so warm! I feel so snuggly! And I look simply fantastic!' cheered Gerry, dancing a silly little giraffe jig. His big hooves went stomp, stomp, stomp on the soft dirt. The colorful scarf bounced up and down with every single step. Gerry thanked all his wonderful friends with giant giraffe hugs. From that day on, whenever the chilly wind blew, Gerry the giraffe stayed warm and cozy with his wonderful, magical, rainbow scarf. The sun came out, shining bright and warm, and Gerry smiled a big, toothy giraffe smile. Every day was a happy day when you had great friends and a very warm neck. The end.

stories.title: Gerry's Starry Night
stories.text: The sun was hiding behind the hills, and the sky was turning a dark, sparkly blue. It was bedtime in the meadow, but Gerry the giraffe was wide awake. He looked up at the twinkling stars high above. 'Hello, little stars,' whispered Gerry softly. Gerry had a wonderful bedtime routine. Before he went to sleep, he loved to count the shiny lights in the sky. But tonight, the stars looked extra close, almost as if they were playing hide and seek with him. 'I wonder if I can touch a star tonight,' Gerry thought to himself. He stood up on his four long, sturdy legs and stretched his neck up toward the sky. He stretched and stretched, reaching as high as he possibly could. He stretched past the sleeping birds, past the tall mountain peak, and up into the cool night air. His nose came closer and closer to a sparkly golden star. The little star winked at Gerry and giggled. 'Hello there, tall friend!' twinkled the star. Gerry giggled right back. It was so much fun being tall enough to say goodnight to the stars! But soon, a big yawn popped right out of Gerry's mouth. *Yawn!* Gerry knew it was time for rest. He slowly brought his long neck back down to the soft, grassy ground. He curled his legs up and tucked his nose under his chest. The night breeze sang a gentle lullaby through the leaves of the trees. The fireflies danced around him like tiny floating lanterns, glowing yellow and green. Gerry closed his heavy brown eyes, feeling safe and cozy in the quiet dark. He dreamed of sliding down rainbow stars and jumping over the moon, with his long neck swaying gently in the night breeze. Sleep tight, sweet Gerry, whispered the wind. Sleep tight under the sparkling sky. The end.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tall, very sweet friend. Who is it? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry has a long, long neck. Can you stretch your neck up high like Gerry? Stretch, stretch, stretch! Gerry lives in the big, sunny grasslands where the sky is bright blue and the clouds look like fluffy cotton candy. Today is a special day because Gerry is going to a fun toddler party with all his animal friends. But first, Gerry needs to get dressed! Getting dressed is tricky when you are a tall giraffe. Let us help him! First, Gerry needs his bright yellow socks. Oh my goodness, his legs are so long! One sock goes on hoof number one. Stretch, reach, pull! That is it! Now sock number two. Stretch, reach, pull! Now Gerry has two happy yellow feet. Next, Gerry needs his favorite red shirt with shiny silver stars on it. Gerry lifts his long, long neck way up high into the air. He slips his head right through the neck hole. Pop! There is his smiling face! But wait, where do his arms go? Gerry has long front legs. He has to wiggle and giggle to get his sleeves on. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! Giggle, giggle, giggle! There goes sleeve number one, and there goes sleeve number two. Gerry looks down at his bright red shirt. It fits him just right! But wait, something is missing. What could it be? Oh, it is his chilly ears! Gerry’s ears get cold when the morning breeze blows through the trees. So Gerry picks up his fuzzy blue scarf. He wraps it around his long neck one time. Then two times. Then three times! Now Gerry is all cozy and warm. He looks in the mirror and gives a big, happy grin. He stomps his hooves on the ground. Tap, tap, tap! He is ready to go to the party. Gerry opens his front door and steps outside into the warm sunshine. He waves goodbye to his bird friends. 'Have a wonderful day, Gerry!' they tweet. Gerry walks down the path, ready for fun. Can you wave goodbye to Gerry just like his bird friends? Wave, wave, wave! What a busy, happy morning for our tall friend.

stories.title: Gerry Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The sun is going down in the big, beautiful grasslands. The sky is turning pink and orange and purple, just like a bowl of yummy fruit sherbet. The day is over, and little toddlers are getting ready for bed. Guess who else is getting ready for bed? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry had a very busy day running, jumping, and playing with the monkeys. Now, Gerry is feeling so, so sleepy. Can you give a big, sleepy yawn like Gerry? Ready? Open wide and yawn! Ahhh! Gerry walks over to his favorite sleeping spot under the big acacia tree. The stars are starting to twinkle in the night sky like little diamonds. But wait! How does a tall giraffe go to sleep? Does he lie down flat on the ground? Let us see! Gerry bends his long, long legs. Bend, bend, bend! He tucks his knees right underneath his tummy. Then, he lowers his long neck all the way down to the soft, green grass. He rests his heavy head right next to a bunch of sweet-smelling yellow flowers. Sniff, sniff, ahhh. That smells so nice! But wait, Gerry is still missing something very important before he can close his eyes. He needs his favorite bedtime story! A little brown owl flies down from the tree branches and sits on a leaf. 'Would you like a story, Gerry?' asks the owl. Gerry nods his sleepy head up and down. The owl tells a quiet, gentle story about the moon and the stars and the sleepy clouds. Gerry listens with his big, brown eyes. His eyelids feel heavier and heavier. Heavy, heavy, heavy. The crickets start to sing a soft bedtime song outside. Chirp, chirp, chirp, goes the cricket. The gentle night breeze whispers through the leaves. Swish, swish, swish. Gerry closes his eyes tight. He takes a deep breath in, and lets a deep breath out. Puff! Gerry is fast asleep, dreaming sweet dreams of crunchy green leaves and sunny days. Can you close your eyes and pretend to sleep like Gerry? Good night, sweet giraffe. Sleep tight until the morning sun comes up again.

stories.title: Gerry's Lunchtime Munch
stories.text: Tummy rumble, tummy tumble! It is lunchtime in the sunny grasslands, and Gerry the Giraffe has a very big appetite. Can you rub your tummy and say yum, yum, yum? Yum, yum, yum! Gerry’s tummy is rumbling because he played tag all morning with the bouncy little zebras. Now it is time to eat, eat, eat! But where is Gerry’s food? Gerry does not eat pizza or cookies like little toddlers do. Gerry loves to eat fresh, green leaves from the very top of the tall trees! Let us look up. Way, way, up! Can you reach your hands up high to the sky? Stretch your fingers as high as they can go! That is how Gerry reaches his yummy lunch. Gerry walks over to the biggest, greenest tree in the whole wide world. He stands right next to the trunk. He looks up through his long eyelashes. There are so many delicious green leaves waiting just for him. Gerry opens his wide mouth. He sticks out his long, purple tongue! Can you stick out your tongue like Gerry? Boop! Gerry’s tongue is super long and super strong. It wraps around a bunch of crisp, green leaves. Pull, munch, crunch! Gerry pulls the leaves right off the branch. He chews them up with a loud, happy sound. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Oh, those leaves taste so sweet and juicy. Gerry looks for more. Here is a crunchy leaf, and there is a crunchy leaf. He eats ten green leaves. Let us count them together! One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Gerry’s tummy is finally full and happy. He pats his round tummy with his hoof. Pat, pat, pat! He gives a big, polite giraffe burp. Excuse me, Gerry! Now it is time for a little rest in the cool shade of the tree. What a yummy, crunchy, wonderful lunchtime it was for our very tall and very hungry friend, Gerry.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tall, very sweet friend. Who could it be? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry is waking up in his cozy yellow bed. Stretch, stretch, stretch goes Gerry! He stretches his long, long neck all the way up to the ceiling. Yawn! Time to get dressed for a brand-new day of fun adventures. Gerry sits on his fuzzy blue rug and looks inside his big wooden toy box to find his clothes. First, Gerry needs to put on his shirt. He finds a bright red shirt with shiny silver stars on it. Gerry holds the shirt in his hooves. Oh my goodness, his neck is so long! How will the shirt go all the way down? Gerry giggles. He scrunches his neck down low, like a bouncy spring, and pops his head right through the neck hole. Pop! Yay! The red shirt fits him just right. Next, Gerry needs to put on his favorite pants. They are bright green pants with big yellow polka dots. Gerry steps his left foot in. One! Then he steps his right foot in. Two! He pulls the pants all the way up to his tummy. But wait! Gerry looks down and lets out a loud gasp. Oh no! His tall, spotted tail is still trapped inside the pants! Do you see it wiggle, wiggle, wiggle? Gerry laughs a big, happy giraffe laugh. He gently reaches back, lifts the back of his pants, and pops his fluffy tail out into the fresh morning air. Phew! All better! Now, Gerry just needs one more very important thing. Shoes! Gerry has four feet, which means he needs four little yellow shoes. He bends down slowly, one knee at a time. He slips a shoe on his front left foot. Slip! Then his front right foot. Slip! Then his back left foot. Slip! And finally, his back right foot. Slip! Gerry stomps his feet on the floor. Stomp, stomp, stomp! He looks in the mirror and smiles from ear to ear. He looks so handsome in his red star shirt, green polka dot pants, and four yellow shoes. Gerry is ready to step outside, wave hello to the warm yellow sun, and play with all of his wonderful toddler friends today. Can you give Gerry a big wave? Hello, Gerry!

stories.title: Gerry's Breakfast Munch
stories.text: Tummies are rumbling! Do you hear that loud noise? Grrr-rumble, grrr-rumble! That is Gerry the Giraffe’s tummy, and it is telling him that it is time for breakfast. Gerry lives in a big, beautiful green park filled with tall trees and pretty flowers. He loves to eat yummy food in the morning to give him lots of energy for running and jumping. Gerry takes a big, bouncy walk over to the tallest tree in the whole park. It is an acacia tree, and it has lots of green leaves right at the very top. Gerry looks up. Way, way, up into the blue sky. The yummy leaves are so high up that other animals cannot reach them. But Gerry is a giraffe, and giraffes are famous for having super-duper long necks! Gerry takes a deep breath. He reaches his long neck straight up toward the fluffy clouds. Stretch, stretch, stretch! He opens his mouth wide. Chompy-chomp-chomp! Gerry munches on the sweet, crunchy green leaves. They taste so fresh and yummy, just like crunchy lettuce mixed with sweet honey. But wait! Gerry feels a little tickle on his nose. Achoo! Gerry sneezes a big giraffe sneeze. Ah-choo! That tickle came from a silly little ladybug sitting right on a green leaf. The ladybug waves its tiny black legs at Gerry, and Gerry giggles. Hello, little ladybug! Gerry is very polite, so he wants to share his breakfast. He gently nudges a low leaf closer to the ladybug so they can eat together. Munch, munch, munch go Gerry’s teeth. Nibble, nibble, nibble goes the tiny ladybug. After eating a whole bunch of green leaves, Gerry’s tummy feels nice and full. But wait, he is a little bit thirsty now. Gerry walks over to the cool, sparkling blue river nearby. He bends his long legs way down low, like a giant yellow spider, so his mouth can reach the water. Slurp, slurp, slurp! He drinks a big, refreshing gulp of water. Ah, delicious! Gerry wipes his mouth with the back of his hoof, stands back up tall, and lets out a happy sigh. His breakfast tummy is happy, he shared with his tiny bug friend, and now he is ready to play hide-and-seek with the butterflies!

stories.title: Gerry Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The golden sun is starting to go down behind the green hills. The sky is turning pink and purple and soft orange. That means it is time for the day to end and bedtime to begin. Where is Gerry the Giraffe? Let us look around. Ah, there he is! Gerry is walking very softly back to his cozy nest of soft green grass under the big, twinkling stars. Oh, look how slow Gerry is moving. Can you walk like a sleepy giraffe? Slow, and steady, and heavy. Tap, tap, tap go his hooves on the soft earth. Gerry lets out a long, sleepy yawn. Yaaaawn! He rubs his big brown eyes with his hooves. He is feeling very, very tired after playing all day long. But wait, how does a giraffe go to sleep? Do you think they sleep standing up, or do they lie down? Let us watch Gerry and see! First, Gerry bends his front knees very slowly. Bend, bend, bend. Then he gently rests his tummy down on the soft green grass. But what about his very long neck? A long neck is tricky! Gerry curves his super-long neck all the way around, resting his sweet head right on his own back, like a fluffy yellow scarf. There, now he is nice and comfy and warm. The little night birds are singing a sweet bedtime lullaby in the branches above. Tweet, tweet, go the birds. The gentle night breeze is whispering through the green leaves. Shhh, shhh, goes the wind. Gerry closes his big brown eyes and listens to the quiet night sounds. He thinks about all the fun things he did today: wearing his red star shirt, eating crunchy green leaves from the tall tree, and playing with the little ladybug. He smiles a sweet sleepy smile in the dark. The bright moon shines down on him like a big silver nightlight. Gerry takes a slow, deep breath in, and lets a slow breath out. In, and out. In, and out. Gerry is fast asleep, dreaming sweet, happy dreams about tomorrow's new adventures. Goodnight, Gerry. Goodnight, little stars. Goodnight, toddlers, time for sweet dreams too!

stories.title: Gerry Goes to the Park
stories.text:
Once upon a time, there was a little yellow giraffe named Gerry. Gerry had four long legs, a very long neck, and big brown spots that looked just like chocolate chip cookies. Gerry loved to go to the big green park with his mommy. Today was a very special day because Gerry was going to try the big yellow slide all by himself. 

Gerry trotted through the grass, clip-clop, clip-clop, making happy footprints in the dirt. When he reached the playground, he looked up at the tall slide. It looked so high up in the blue sky! 'Can I do it, Mommy?' asked Gerry, blinking his long eyelashes. 'Of course you can, little one,' smiled his mommy, nuzzling his soft cheek. 

Gerry started to climb the steps. One, two, three, four long steps! Because his legs were so long, he had to fold them up just like a pocketknife to fit on the slide. His bottom wiggled, and his long neck stretched out in front of him. He felt a little bit nervous, but mostly he felt very excited. 

'Whee!' shouted Gerry as he zoomed down the slide. He went swoosh all the way to the bottom, landing softly in the woodchips. His tail swished back and forth, and he giggled a loud, rumbling giggle. 'Again! Again!' cheered Gerry. He hopped right back up and went down the slide five more times. By the time the sun began to set, painting the sky pink and orange, Gerry was wonderfully tired. He gave his mommy a big, warm hug, resting his long neck over her shoulder. They walked slowly back home under the twinkling stars, dreaming of more playground adventures tomorrow.

stories.title: Gerry's Breakfast Feast
stories.text:
Good morning, sunshine! Gerry the giraffe woke up with a big yawn. He stretched his front legs out wide and blinked his big brown eyes. His tummy made a loud rumbling sound. Rumble, rumble, went Gerry's tummy. It was time for breakfast, and Gerry was as hungry as a little bear. 

Gerry lived in a sunny place full of green trees and tall bushes. But Gerry did not eat cereal in a bowl like little boys and girls. Gerry loved to eat fresh, green leaves right off the very tops of the trees. He walked over to his favorite acacia tree. It was so tall that a little bunny could walk underneath it and not even touch the lowest branch. But for Gerry, reaching the top was a fun game. 

Gerry stretched his super-duper long neck up, up, up towards the clouds. He poked out his dark purple tongue. Giraffes have special tongues that can wrap right around prickly branches without getting hurt. Reach, grab, and pull! Gerry munched on a crunchy green leaf. Then he grabbed a sweet yellow flower. Munch, crunch, munch. 

'Yummy in my tummy!' mumbled Gerry with his mouth full of leaves. A little yellow butterfly fluttered by his nose, tickling his whiskers. Gerry sneezed, 'Achoo!' and the butterfly flew away to say hello to a daisy. Gerry finished every single leaf on the top branch until his tummy was nice and round. He felt happy, full, and ready to play hide and seek with his jungle friends. What a wonderful way to start a brand new day.

stories.title: The Tall Starry Night
stories.text:
The sun was hiding behind the big green hills, and the sky turned a deep, sleepy purple. Little Gerry the giraffe was getting very sleepy, too. He gave a huge yawn that made his jaw go wide. It was time for bed, but Gerry had one very favorite bedtime ritual. He loved to look at the night sky before closing his eyes. 

Gerry walked over to a quiet clearing where the moon shone like a giant silver coin. Because Gerry had such a long neck and stood so very tall, his head was closer to the sky than almost anyone else in the whole wide world. He looked up at the twinkling stars that blinked down at him like tiny golden nightlights. 

'Good evening, little star,' whispered Gerry softly so he wouldn't wake the sleeping birds. He stood very still on his four sturdy legs. A cool night breeze gently brushed against his soft yellow fur. He felt safe and warm, wrapped in the quiet shadows of the evening. His mommy stepped close beside him, resting her neck gently against his. It was their special nighttime hug, called a neck-cuddle. 

Gerry closed his heavy eyelids. One eye closed, then the other. He let out a long, peaceful sigh. He dreamed about floating on a fluffy white cloud, high above the trees, playing tag with the moonbeams. As the night grew quiet, Gerry slept soundly, knowing that tomorrow would bring another wonderful day of reaching high and playing in the sunshine.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tallest friend get dressed. Can you guess who it is? Yes, it is Gerry the gentle giraffe! Gerry lives in a big yellow house right by the tall green trees. The sun is shining brightly, and the birds are singing sweet morning songs. 'Time to get up, Gerry!' whispers the soft morning breeze. Gerry slowly stretches his long, long legs. First, he stretches one leg high up into the blue sky. Then he stretches his other leg. Oof! Being tall is a big job. Now, Gerry needs to put on his funny spotted shirt. His shirt has big brown spots and little yellow spots, just like his furry coat. He wiggles his head through the top hole. Pop! His little brown horns pop right out. Next, Gerry needs to brush his teeth. He needs a super-duper extra long toothbrush and a big blob of minty toothpaste. He brushes his top teeth, and then he brushes his bottom teeth. Scrub, scrub, scrub! Gerry has a very long neck, so brushing takes a little bit longer than it does for you or me. But Gerry does a super job. After brushing, it is time for breakfast. Gerry looks up at the very top of the acacia tree. That is where the yummiest green leaves live. He stretches his long purple tongue. Slurp! He grabs a delicious, crunchy leaf right off the branch. Crunch, crunch, crunch. It tastes so sweet and fresh! Gerry drinks a big glass of cool water to wash his breakfast down. Gulp, gulp, gulp. Now Gerry's tummy is happy and full.
