He is dressed in his favorite shirt, his teeth are sparkling clean, and he is ready for a wonderful day of play with all his woodland friends. Can you wave goodbye to Gerry as he sets off on his morning walk? Wave bye-bye, Gerry! Have a wonderful and joyful day!

stories.title: Gerry Goes to the Park
stories.text: Are you ready for an adventure, little friends? Gerry the giraffe is going to the neighborhood playground today, and he is so excited! He skips and hops all the way down the golden path. Thump, thump, thump goes his big hooves. When Gerry arrives at the park, he sees his friends playing on the swings and the slides. Bunny is hopping high in the air, and Bear is sliding down the red slide. 'Hello, Gerry!' they shout happily. Gerry wants to play too. He walks over to the shiny yellow slide. But oh dear! Gerry is much too tall for the slide. His head is up in the clouds, and his feet are on the ground. How can Gerry slide down? He puts his thinking cap on. Then he has a brilliant idea! Gerry sits down gently on the soft green grass and stretches his long neck all the way up the slide's ladder. 'Wee!' squeaks Bunny, climbing onto Gerry's long nose. Gerry lowers his head slowly, and Bunny slides right down Gerry's smooth, fuzzy nose like a tiny furry rocket. Whee! Bunny giggles and claps his paws together with joy. Next, Bear wants a turn. Bear climbs up onto Gerry's forehead and slides down his long, golden neck. 'Wheee!' shouts Bear with a big happy smile. All the animals take turns sliding down Gerry's wonderful giraffe slide. It is the best slide in the whole wide world because it is made of a kind and helpful friend. After playing on the slide, the sun begins to get a little bit sleepy. The sky turns pink and orange and soft purple. It is time for everyone to head back home. Gerry gives all his friends a warm, gentle hug with his long neck. They whisper soft goodnights to one another. Gerry walks slowly back to his cozy yellow house under the twinkling stars. He climbs into his big bed, closes his sleepy brown eyes, and dreams of all the fun slide rides they will share again tomorrow.

stories.title: Gerry's Starry Night Lullaby
stories.text: The sun is sinking low behind the hills, and the bright moon is starting to peek out from the fluffy clouds. It is time to wind down and get ready for sleep. Gerry the giraffe is getting very sleepy, too. He lets out a big, gentle yawn. Ahhh-woooo! His long eyelashes flutter softly. Gerry walks slowly back to his cozy bedroom. The room is quiet and peaceful, filled with the soft glow of a little nightlight shaped like a friendly star. Gerry takes off his spotted shirt and folds it neatly on a tiny wooden chair. He climbs into his extra-large bed, which has soft blue blankets and fluffy white pillows. But wait! Gerry's long neck is still poking way up high. How does a tall giraffe get comfortable to sleep? Gerry curls his long, bendy neck around in a big, cozy circle, just like a soft furry donut on his pillow. There, that is much better! Now his head is resting safely and comfortably right beside his fuzzy paws. Outside his bedroom window, the crickets are singing a quiet bedtime song. Chirp, chirp, chirp. The gentle night breeze whispers through the leaves of the big tree outside. Gerry closes his heavy eyes. He thinks about all the fun things he did today: stretching his legs, eating yummy green leaves, and playing slide games at the park with his lovely animal friends. His heart feels warm and happy. The moon shines down a bright, silvery beam to watch over him. Gerry takes a deep breath in, and lets a slow breath out. In and out. In and out. The world is quiet and still. Sleep tight, dear Gerry. Rest your tall head and sweet long neck. Tomorrow brings a brand new day full of magical adventures and happy smiles. Sweet dreams, little giraffe. Goodnight to the moon, goodnight to the stars, and goodnight to you, my wonderful little toddler friend.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help a very tall friend get ready for his busy day. Are you ready? Wonderful! Once upon a sunny morning, high up in the green treetops, lived a sweet little giraffe named Gerry. Gerry had bright yellow fur, lovely brown spots, and a neck so long it could touch the fluffy white clouds. 'Yawn!' went Gerry, stretching his long, long legs. It was time to get dressed for preschool in the savanna jungle! Gerry looked into his big wooden closet. First, Gerry needed his favorite shirt. He grabbed a bright red shirt with shiny silver buttons. But wait! How does a tall giraffe put on a shirt? Slowly and carefully! Gerry bent his long neck way down low, like a graceful swan bending to drink from a cool blue stream. He wiggled his left arm through the sleeve. Pop! Then he wiggled his right arm through the other sleeve. Zip! He buttoned the buttons all the way up. One, two, three, four, five! 'Tada!' whispered Gerry with a big happy smile. Next, Gerry needed his trousers. He picked out a pair of stretchy blue pants with big yellow pockets. Putting on pants is always a funny adventure when you have four long legs. Gerry lifted his first leg up high into the air. One! Then his second leg. Two! Then his third leg. Three! And finally, his fourth leg. Four! He wiggled his bottom and pulled the pants all the way up. Oh boy, Gerry looked very handsome indeed. But wait, what is missing? Shoes! Oh goodness me, shoes are very important for running and jumping. Gerry had four little hooves. He found four bright green sneakers with sparkly pink laces. Bending down once more, Gerry slipped his little hooves into his shoes. One shoe, two shoes, three shoes, four shoes! He even tied the laces into neat little bows, all by himself. Finally, Gerry grabbed his yellow backpack filled with crunchy green leaf snacks. He wrapped his long spotted neck in a cozy striped scarf because the morning breeze was chilly. Gerry stepped outside his front door and took a big, deep breath of the fresh morning air. He was ready to play, learn, and explore with all his jungle friends. 'Have a wonderful day, Gerry!' shouted the little yellow duck by the pond. Gerry waved his long spotted arm and happily skipped down the golden path. Getting dressed was so much fun today!

stories.title: Gerry Goes to Sleep
stories.text: The golden sun is sinking slowly behind the tall green hills, painting the evening sky in lovely shades of pink, purple, and orange. It is getting very late in the warm savanna, and little toddlers everywhere are getting sleepy. Up in the acacia tree, our tall friend Gerry the giraffe is feeling sleepy too. Gerry had a wonderful day running through the tall grass, playing hide and seek with the monkeys, and munching on crunchy green leaves. Now, his long legs feel a little bit tired, and his big brown eyes are blinking very slowly. Yawn! Gerry gives a giant sleepy yawn. But wait! How does a very tall giraffe get ready for bed? It is quite a funny routine! First, Gerry needs to brush his teeth. He has a giant toothbrush with soft blue bristles and minty toothpaste. He opens his mouth wide and brushes his top teeth, and then he brushes his bottom teeth. Scrub, scrub, scrub! Next, Gerry drinks a big warm cup of sweet honey milk. Slurp, slurp, slurp! It warms his tummy right up. Now it is time to put on his cozy pajamas. Gerry puts on fuzzy yellow pajamas with little sleeping moons and stars printed all over them. He wraps his long neck in a soft blanket just like a giant colorful scarf. But where does a giraffe sleep? Do giraffes sleep in a little wooden bed? Oh no! Giraffes are much too tall for tiny beds. Instead, Gerry finds a soft patch of green grass right under the twinkling stars. Because Gerry has long legs, he has to fold them up carefully, one by one. First, he kneels down on his front knees. Then, he tucks his back legs neatly underneath his big spotted tummy. Finally, he curls his long, graceful neck around in a big loop, resting his heavy head gently upon the cool, soft ground. It is like resting on a fluffy pillow made of clouds. The crickets are singing a sweet lullaby. Chirp, chirp, chirp! The gentle night breeze whispers through the green leaves. Gerry closes his heavy eyelids. He thinks about all his wonderful adventures today and smiles a sweet sleepy smile. The bright moon shines down on him like a friendly silver nightlight. Goodnight, little monkeys. Goodnight, little birds. Goodnight, sweet Gerry the giraffe. Sleep tight and have the most wonderful dreams under the sparkling night sky.

stories.title: Gerry's Tasty Snack
stories.text: Mmm, yummy in my tummy! Little toddlers, do you know what time it is? It is snack time in the sunny savanna, and Gerry the giraffe is having a very hungry afternoon. Gerry’s tummy is making a funny sound. Rumble, rumble, rumble! 'I want a yummy treat,' says Gerry, patting his spotted tummy with a gentle hoof. Gerry looks all around the bright green jungle. Down on the ground, there are tiny red strawberries. But Gerry is much too tall to reach the ground easily. If he bends down too far, he wobbles! Whoops-a-daisy! So, Gerry looks up, up, up into the sky. That is where the best treats live! The acacia trees have the greenest, crispiest leaves in the whole wide world. Gerry walks over to the biggest tree with his long, steady legs. Crunch, crunch, go his footsteps on the dry dirt. He opens his mouth and sticks out his tongue. But wait! Do you know what color a giraffe's tongue is? It is a funny shade of dark purple! And guess what else? Gerry's tongue is super long, just like a magic ribbon. He stretches his purple tongue way, way out. Reach, reach, reach! He wraps his long tongue around a bunch of juicy green leaves. Snap! He pulls them right off the branch. Gerry closes his mouth and begins to chew. Crunch, crunch, munch, munch! The leaves taste sweet and fresh, like morning rain and sunshine. Gerry takes another big bite. Munch, munch, munch! Then, a little yellow butterfly flutters by, carrying a tiny basket of sweet yellow bananas. 'Would you like a banana, Gerry?' asks the friendly butterfly. Gerry smiles his biggest smile. He lowers his head just a little bit and gently takes a soft yellow banana with his lips. Peel, peel, go the banana skin. Gerry eats the sweet banana in one big bite. Yummy, yummy, yummy! His tummy is full and happy now. Gerry rubs his tummy and lets out a happy little sigh. Snack time is truly the very best time of the entire day. Can you rub your tummy just like Gerry, little toddlers? Great job!

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tall, very sweet friend, Gerry the giraffe. Gerry lives out on the sunny African savanna, and the bright morning sun is peeking over the acacia trees. "Time to get up!" chirps a little yellow bird named Pip. Gerry stretches his long, long neck all the way up into the sky. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Gerry gives a big, happy giraffe yawn. Good morning, Gerry! Now, it is time for Gerry to get dressed for his very busy day of playing games with his animal friends. First, Gerry needs to put on his shirt. But oh dear! Gerry has a long neck, and his shirt has a little hole. How does Gerry put it on? He has to wiggle and squiggle! Gerry pokes his nose through the neck hole first. Then he wiggles his long neck down, down, down until the soft yellow shirt pops right onto his shoulders. Hooray! Next, Gerry needs to wear his special striped scarf because the morning breeze is a little bit chilly. Gerry takes the long, long, long blue and red scarf and wraps it around his neck once. Then he wraps it around twice. Then three times! Now his neck is extra warm and super cozy. But wait, what about his four long, spindly legs? Gerry looks down at his feet. He needs socks! Gerry has big feet, so he needs big socks. He reaches down with his mouth, gently grabs a bright green sock, and slides it onto his first front foot. Pull, pull, pull! Then he puts a sock on his second foot. Then his third foot. And finally, his fourth foot! Gerry stomps his feet on the soft grass. Stomp, stomp, stomp! His feet are nice and warm. Finally, Gerry puts on his shiny red hat right between his two little ossicones—which are just the cute little horns on top of a giraffe's head. Gerry looks at his reflection in a shiny, clear pool of water. He looks wonderful! He looks handsome, colorful, and ready for an adventure. Gerry gives a happy little dance, shaking his tail and his long legs. Can you dance like Gerry? Shake your arms, wiggle your legs, and jump up high just like a tall giraffe getting ready for a wonderful, fun-filled day!

stories.title: Gerry's Tall Tree Snack
stories.text: It is snack time on the savanna, and Gerry the giraffe has a very rumbly tummy. Grumbly, grumbly, rumble! Gerry is so hungry, and he is looking for his absolute favorite treat in the whole wide world: crunchy, green acacia leaves. But there is a little problem. The delicious green leaves are way up high at the very top of the tall tree. Oh no! How can Gerry reach them? Gerry walks over to the big tree and looks up. Way, way up! The little monkeys are sitting on the lower branches, munching on tiny fruits. They wave down at Gerry. "Hello, Gerry!" they chatter. Gerry smiles his big giraffe smile and waves back with his long tail. But Gerry does not want tiny fruits. He wants the juicy, fresh leaves way at the top where the fluffy white clouds float by. Gerry knows just what to do. First, he stands up as tall, tall, tall as he possibly can. He straightens his long back legs and his long front legs. He stretches his long neck all the way up toward the sky. Stretch, stretch, stretch! But the leaves are still just a little bit too high. Gerry needs to use his secret weapon: his super-duper tongue! Giraffes have long, dark, stretchy tongues that can wrap around branches like a soft purple ribbon. Gerry opens his mouth wide. Out comes his long, purple tongue! Slurp! He reaches it out past the lower branches, past the middle branches, all the way to the very tippy-top of the tree. He gently wraps his tongue around a bunch of sweet green leaves. Then, with a gentle tug, he pulls them right into his mouth. Munch, munch, crunch! Gerry chews his yummy snack with a big, happy smile. The leaves are so crunchy and sweet. He takes another reach with his tongue. Slurp, munch, crunch! The little monkeys clap their hands and cheer for Gerry. "Yay!" they squeak. Gerry shares a few little leaves with his bird friend Pip, too. Eating snacks together is so much fun. With a very full and happy tummy, Gerry gives a contented sigh and gets ready for his afternoon nap in the warm, golden sunshine.

stories.title: Gerry's Hide-and-Seek Game
stories.text: It is a bright and beautiful afternoon, and Gerry the giraffe is playing a game of hide-and-seek with all of his animal friends on the grassy plains. Zebra, Elephant, and Baboon are playing too. "One, two, three, four, five!" counts Zebra, closing his eyes tight with his hooves. "Ready or not, here I come!" Gerry looks around quickly. Where can a tall giraffe hide? Gerry has a very long neck, long legs, and a tall body covered in big, beautiful brown spots. He cannot hide behind a little bush because his head pokes right over the top! He cannot hide behind a small rock because his legs are way too long. Gerry giggles. He has an idea. He trots over to a tall group of leafy green trees that match his yellow and brown pattern. Gerry stands very, very still right in the middle of the tall trees. He closes his eyes and tries not to wiggle. Zebra opens his eyes and starts to look around. Zebra looks behind the big gray elephant. "Found you, Elephant!" laughs Zebra. Then Zebra looks behind a big round rock. "Found you, Baboon!" giggles Zebra. But Zebra cannot find Gerry anywhere. Zebra scratches his black-and-white head. "Hmm, where is Gerry?" he wonders out loud. Gerry tries not to laugh, but a little giggle escapes. "Hee-hee!" Little bird Pip flies up and sits right on the tip of Gerry's ear, pointing down with a wing. Zebra looks up, and up, and up. Way up in the sky, he sees Gerry's friendly face smiling down through the green leaves. "There you are, Gerry! I see your tall neck and your spots!" shouts Zebra, clapping his hooves together. Gerry steps out from the trees with a happy prance, shaking his long legs. "You found me!" beams Gerry. Playing hide-and-seek with friends is the best game ever. Gerry, Zebra, Elephant, and Baboon all play together until the sun begins to set, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors, ending a wonderful day of play.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help a very tall friend get ready for his busy day. His name is Gerry, and he is a sweet baby giraffe with bright orange spots. Gerry lives in a big, cozy house where everything is extra tall to fit his long, long neck. Stretch your necks up high just like Gerry! Stretch, stretch, stretch! Good job! Now, Gerry opens his sleepy eyes and gives a big, happy giraffe yawn. Yawn! Time to get dressed for playtime. Gerry walks over to his big wooden wardrobe and opens the door. Hmm, what should Gerry wear today? He sees a pile of colorful socks. Oh boy, socks! Gerry loves cozy socks. But wait, Gerry has four long legs. That means he needs four socks! One, two, three, four! Gerry bends his knees and carefully puts a blue sock on his first long leg. Then a red sock on his second leg. A green sock on his third leg. And a yellow sock on his fourth leg! Look down at your own feet, toddlers. Do you have socks on today? Tap your toes! Next, Gerry needs to wear his favorite yellow t-shirt. But Gerry's neck is so long that putting on a shirt can be a little tricky. He holds the shirt up high in his little hooves, scrunches down low to the floor, and swoosh! He pops his head right through the neck hole. Ta-da! The bright yellow t-shirt fits him just right, showing off all of his lovely brown spots. Finally, Gerry looks in the mirror and puts on a silly purple hat with a fluffy green pom-pom on top. It wobbles when he walks. Gerry does a happy little dance, shaking his legs and wiggling his tail. He is fully dressed, completely ready, and super excited to go outside into the warm sunshine to play hide-and-seek with his jungle friends. Are you wearing a fun outfit today too? Give a little twirl and smile, because you and Gerry look absolutely wonderful and ready for a fun-filled day of wonderful adventures!

stories.title: Gerry's Treetop Snack
stories.text: Hello again, little friends! Are you ready for another fun story about our tall pal Gerry the giraffe? Today, Gerry’s tummy is rumbling. Listen to it go: grumble, rumble, rumble! That means it is time for breakfast, and Gerry has a very special way of eating his morning meal. Unlike us, Gerry does not sit at a little table with a bowl of cereal. No way! Gerry likes to eat breakfast way up high in the bright green sky. He walks outside into the sunny meadow where the tall acacia trees grow. Put your hands high in the air like leafy branches and wave them in the breeze. Can you feel the wind? Gerry looks up at the very top of the biggest tree. That is where the most delicious, tender green leaves live. But wait! Gerry’s mouth is way down at the bottom of his long neck, and the leaves are way up at the top. How will he reach them? Gerry knows just what to do. He opens his mouth wide and sticks out his tongue. But this is no ordinary tongue—it is a super-duper long, purple tongue! It can stretch and stretch like a rubber band. Stretch your tongues out just for fun—bloop! Gerry reaches his long tongue up, up, up past the brown bark, past the little twigs, right up to the very best bunch of juicy green leaves. He wraps his clever tongue around the leaves, gives a gentle little tug, and pulls them right into his mouth. Munch, munch, munch! Gerry chews his breakfast happily, making big chomping noises. Crunch, crunch, crunch! How does it taste, Gerry? Delicious! He takes another big reach, grabbing a yellow flower this time. Nectar and leaves are a giraffe's favorite treat. Gerry swallows his food with a happy sigh and rubs his full tummy. Eating high up in the trees is so much fun. Let us all rub our tummies together and say, yum, yum, yum!

stories.title: Gerry Learns to Share
stories.text: Once upon a sunny afternoon, Gerry the giraffe was playing in the soft green grass with his favorite red bouncing ball. It was a bright red ball that rolled and bounced every time he gave it a gentle tap with his hoof. Boing, boing, bounce! Gerry loved his ball more than anything in the world. He tossed it up into the air and caught it with his nose. He rolled it back and forth between his long front legs. Just then, his little friend Penny the penguin waddled over. Well, not a penguin—let us say Pip the little red panda! Pip scampered over with a curious look on his furry face. Pip sat down in the grass and watched Gerry play with the red ball. Pip’s eyes were big and round, and he looked like he wanted to join in the fun. Gerry stopped bouncing the ball and looked at Pip. For a tiny second, Gerry hugged the ball tightly against his chest. He wasn't sure if he wanted to share his special toy. What if Pip took it away? What if it rolled into a muddy puddle? But then Gerry looked at Pip’s sad little pout and remembered how much more fun it is to play together. Sharing is a wonderful thing! Gerry smiled a big, warm giraffe smile. With a gentle push of his nose, Gerry rolled the bright red ball across the grass straight toward Pip. Ready, set, roll! Pip gasped with surprise and delight. His little paws shot out and stopped the ball. Pip giggled a high-pitched giggle and rolled the ball right back to Gerry. Boing! Gerry caught it easily with his hoof. They played together for a very long time, rolling the ball back and forth, laughing and playing in the sunshine. Gerry learned that sharing his favorite toy didn't mean losing it; it meant making a wonderful game even better with a good friend. They both gave a cheerful wave to each other as the sun began to set, happy and tired from a wonderful day of play.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to meet Gerry the giraffe. Gerry lives in a sunny place with big green trees and fluffy white clouds. The sun is shining brightly, and it is time for Gerry to wake up and get dressed for a fun day of play. Gerry stretches his long, long legs. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Then he stretches his long, long neck. Reach, reach, reach! Now, Gerry needs to put on his clothes. First, Gerry looks for his socks. Oh my goodness, a giraffe has very long legs, which means he needs super-duper long socks! Gerry bends way down low. He reaches for his left foot and pulls up a bright red sock. Up, up, up it goes, all the way up his long leg. Next, Gerry reaches for his right foot. He pulls up a bright blue sock. Up, up, up it goes! Now Gerry's feet are nice and cozy. What is next? A shirt! Gerry has a special yellow shirt with big brown spots, just like his own beautiful pattern. Gerry lifts his shirt high up into the air. He puts his long neck right through the middle hole. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! The shirt slides down his long neck and covers his tummy. But wait! Gerry looks in the mirror. He is missing something very important. Can you guess what it is? His hat! Gerry loves his funny green hat. He picks it up with his nose and tosses it gently into the air. Plop! The hat lands right on top of his head. Gerry looks so handsome. He stomps his big hooves on the ground. Stomp, stomp, stomp! He is ready to go outside and say hello to all his jungle friends. Gerry opens his front door and steps into the warm sunshine. What a wonderful day to be a well-dressed giraffe! Can you wiggle like Gerry? Can you reach up high like Gerry? Great job, little ones! You did it.

stories.title: Gerry's Tall Snack Time
stories.text: Mmm, tummy rumble! It is snack time for Gerry the giraffe. Gerry has been running and jumping all morning long, and now his tummy is telling him it is time to eat. But guess what? Gerry is so tall that he cannot eat grass on the ground like a little bunny or a tiny puppy. Gerry needs to look way, way up into the sky to find his yummy food. Gerry walks over to the biggest, greenest acacia tree in the whole wide jungle. He stops right underneath its leafy branches. Gerry tilts his head back and opens his big brown eyes. Look at all those delicious green leaves way up high! How is Gerry going to reach them? I know! With his super-duper long neck and his magical purple tongue. Gerry opens his mouth. Out comes his long, stretchy tongue. Slurp! He wraps his tongue right around a tasty green branch. Pull, pull, pull! Gerry gives a gentle tug, and snap! A bunch of crunchy leaves comes right off the tree. Gerry closes his mouth and chews. Munch, munch, munch. Oh, how delicious! The leaves are sweet and juicy. But Gerry is still a little bit hungry. He wants more! He looks to the left, and he looks to the right. Way up at the very top of the tree, there is one giant green leaf glowing in the sun. Gerry stretches his neck as high as it can possibly go. He stands on his tippy-toes. Tip-toe, tip-toe! He reaches up with his tongue. Just a little bit more... almost there... Got it! Gerry snatches the special leaf and brings it down into his mouth. Munch, munch, munch, swallow! Gerry rubs his happy tummy. He is full, he is happy, and he is ready for a nice afternoon nap under the cool shade of the big green tree. Goodnight, hungry tummy! Goodnight, tall giraffe!

stories.title: Gerry Plays Hide and Seek
stories.text: Tick-tock, tick-tock! It is time to play a game of hide and seek with Gerry the giraffe and his jungle friends. Gerry loves playing hide and seek, even though he is the tallest animal in the whole wide world. Can a tall giraffe hide very easily? Let us find out together! Little Monkey is the seeker today. Little Monkey covers his eyes with his furry paws and starts to count out loud. One, two, three, four, five! While Little Monkey is counting, Gerry has to find a really good hiding spot. But where can a giant giraffe hide? Gerry looks around quickly. He sees a big rock, but he is much too tall for it. He sees a tiny bush, but his legs are much too long for it. Oh no! Gerry begins to giggle. He thinks he is just too tall to hide anywhere. Then, Gerry looks up at the tall green trees with their big leafy branches. He has a brilliant idea! Gerry tiptoes over to a tall tree and stands very, very still. He stretches his neck up high right next to the tree trunk. He tucks in his ears and closes his eyes tight. If I don't move a muscle, nobody will ever find me, thinks Gerry. Little Monkey finishes counting. Ready or not, here I come, screeches Little Monkey! Little Monkey opens his eyes and starts swinging through the jungle. He looks behind the big rock. Nobody there! He looks behind the tiny bush. Nobody there! Little Monkey scratches his furry head. Where oh where could Gerry be? He looks up into the sky, and suddenly, he sees four long legs and a big spotted neck standing right beside the tree. But wait, Gerry's spots look just like the tree bark and the sunbeams! Peek-a-boo! shouts Little Monkey, pointing right at Gerry. Gerry bursts out laughing. You found me, Little Monkey! You are the best seeker in the whole wide jungle. Gerry and Little Monkey dance around the tree together, so happy and full of joy. What a wonderful game of hide and seek!

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and get ready for a big day of play with Gerry the Giraffe. Gerry is a very tall giraffe with a long, golden neck and lots of pretty brown spots. He lives in a sunny place where the acacia trees tickle the sky. When Gerry wakes up, the yellow sun is peeking over the hills. Gerry stretches his long legs. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Now it is time to get dressed, but being so tall makes getting dressed a very silly puzzle. First, Gerry needs to put on his shirt. He finds a bright red shirt with blue buttons. He loops his long neck down, down, down to reach the floor. He wiggles his front legs into the armholes. Oh, no! The sleeves are way too short for his long legs! Gerry giggles a big giraffe giggle. He tries again. This time, he uses his nose to guide the shirt all the way up his neck. Pop! His little ears pop right out of the top. Silly Gerry! Next, Gerry needs to wear his favorite yellow polka-dot socks to keep his hooves warm. But oh my goodness, look how far down his feet are! He has to bend all the way down, bending his knees like giant rubber bands, to reach his toes. One sock on his left foot. Squish! One sock on his right foot. Squish! Gerry wiggles his toes inside the socks. They feel so cozy and warm. Finally, Gerry needs his favorite shiny green hat. He stretches his neck up, up, up towards the tree branches where the hat is hanging. He uses his long, purple tongue to gently grab the brim. Plop! Right on top of his head it goes. Gerry looks in the mirror and smiles a big, toothy smile. He is ready for a super fun day of running and jumping with all of his jungle friends. Can you wiggle your toes like Gerry? Can you stretch your neck up high to the sky? Great job, little ones! Gerry is dressed and ready to play.

stories.title: Gerry's Big Splash
stories.text: It is a hot, sunny afternoon in the grassland, and Gerry the Giraffe is feeling very warm. Phew! The sun is shining brightly, and the grass is dry. Gerry fans his ears back and forth. Flap, flap, flap! He looks over at his friends, the little monkeys and the bouncing zebras. They are all looking for a way to cool down. 'I know!' says Gerry in his deep, rumbling voice. 'Let us go find the big watering hole!' Gerry takes a giant step. One long leg goes forward, and then the other. He can see everything from up high. He looks over the tall bushes and spots the shiny blue water sparkling in the distance. 'Follow me!' he calls out. Gerry walks with a bouncy step, swinging his long tail. Swish, swish, swish! When they reach the water, it looks so cool and refreshing. But wait! Gerry is so very tall. How is he going to get into the water? First, Gerry has to do the giraffe split. He spreads his long front legs far, far apart. He bends his knees very carefully. Down, down, down he goes, closer and closer to the water. His long neck stretches down to take a little sip. Slurp, slurp, slurp! The water is cool and sweet. Next, Gerry wants to get a little bit wetter. He scoops up water with his trunk-like tongue and splashes it over his back. Splish, splash, splash! Water droplets fly up into the air like little diamonds in the sun. The monkeys giggle and splash in the shallow edges. The zebras kick up water with their hooves. Gerry laughs a big, bubbly laugh. He lowers his tummy right down onto the soft, wet mud. Squish, squash! Gerry loves the mud. It feels so squishy and cool against his skin. He rolls a tiny bit to the left and a tiny bit to the right. Now Gerry is covered in cool mud from his toes to his tummy. He feels so refreshed and happy. When it is time to go, Gerry stands up tall, shaking off the water drops like a big furry sprinkler. Shake, shake, shake! What a wonderful, splashy day.

stories.title: Gerry's Starry Lullaby
stories.text: The golden sun is starting to go down behind the big green trees. The sky is turning pink and purple, and the first little star is blinking hello. It is time for sleep in the tall grass, and Gerry the Giraffe is feeling very sleepy, sleepy, sleepy. Gerry gives a big, wide yawn. Ahhh-choo! No, that is a sneeze! Ahhh-yawn! That is better. Gerry closes his big brown eyes for a moment, but then he remembers something very important. He has to say goodnight to all of his tall tree friends! Gerry walks very quietly now on his soft hooves. Tap, tap, tap go his feet on the dirt. He bends his long neck to whisper goodnight to the sleepy little birds in the branches. 'Goodnight, birdies,' he whispers softly. The birds tuck their heads under their wings and chirp a tiny 'goodnight, Gerry.' Then Gerry walks over to the big acacia tree where he loves to sleep. But wait! How does a giraffe lie down for a nap? Gerry bends his long back legs first. Down, down, down. Then he folds his front legs underneath his soft tummy. He lowers his long neck in a big, gentle loop, resting his heavy head right on the cozy grass. He looks up at the twinkly stars shining in the dark blue sky. Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how Gerry loves the way you are. The wind blows softly through the grass, making a shushing sound. Shhh, shhh, shhh. Gerry closes his big eyes again. He dreams of crunchy green leaves and sunny days with his friends. His tummy goes up and down, up and down as he breathes in and out. The jungle is quiet and peaceful. The moon smiles down at Gerry keeping watch over the sleeping animals. Goodnight, little birds. Goodnight, bright stars. Goodnight, sweet Gerry the Giraffe. Time to close your eyes, little toddler, and drift off to sweet dreams too. Sleep tight.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and play with Gerry the Giraffe. Gerry lives in a big sunny grassland where the grass is green and the sky is bright blue. Can you stretch your arms up high like a tall giraffe? Stretch, stretch, stretch! Gerry is waking up from his nice cozy nap, and guess what? It is time for him to get dressed for a brand new fun day. First, Gerry needs to put on his very favorite yellow shirt. But wait! Gerry has a super duper long neck. Oh boy, how does a giraffe put on a shirt? Let us help him! We pull the shirt way up, up, up, past his knees, past his tummy, past his spots, and all the way up his long neck. Pop! His little head pops right out the top. Good job, Gerry! Next, Gerry needs to put on his cozy socks. Giraffes have four long legs, which means they need lots and lots of socks. One sock for foot number one, tickle tickle. One sock for foot number two, wiggle wiggle. One sock for foot number three, stomp stomp. And one sock for foot number four, jump jump! Now Gerry has warm feet. But look outside, the sun is starting to shine very brightly. Gerry needs to protect his cute little eyes. He reaches up and puts on his big red sunglasses. Do you have sunglasses? Put on your imaginary sunglasses just like Gerry! Now Gerry looks in the mirror and gives a big happy grin. He sees his brown spots, his little fuzzy horns on top of his head, and his bright red sunglasses. He is ready to go outside and play with all of his animal friends. Do you want to go outside too? Let us stomp our feet together. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Have a wonderful day, Gerry!

stories.title: Gerry Goes to the Playground
stories.text: Look who is visiting the toddler playground today! It is Gerry the Giraffe, and he is so excited to play on the big yellow slide. Gerry takes big giant steps across the soft green grass. Stomp, go his big hooves. Stomp, stomp, stomp! All the little animal friends wave hello. Hello, Gerry! Gerry walks over to the swings. He wants to have a turn, but oh dear, his neck is so long that it gets tangled in the chains! giggle, giggle, giggle! His monkey friend helps him untangle. Thank you, little monkey. Next, Gerry walks right over to the big sandbox. He loves the warm sand between his toes. Can you wiggle your toes like Gerry in the sand? Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! Gerry uses his long neck to look over the top of the tall slide. He sees the slippery slide and smiles a big toothy smile. Time to climb the ladder! Gerry puts one long leg up, then another long leg, and another one, until he is sitting right at the very top of the slide. Wow, he is so high up in the sky! He can see the whole playground from up here. He sees the spinning merry-go-round, the red rubber balls, and his friends cheering for him. Are you ready to slide down, Gerry? Here we go! Wheeeeeee! Gerry slides all the way down the slide very fast. Zoom! He lands on the soft ground with a happy thud. That was so much fun! Gerry claps his hooves together and yells, Again, again! The other toddlers clap their hands too. Playing at the park with Gerry is the best part of the whole day. Time to give a big hug to our favorite tall friend. Hug, hug, hug!

stories.title: Gerry's bedtime star
stories.text: The sun is going down, down, down behind the green hills. The sky is turning a pretty color of purple and dark blue. It is time for little toddlers to wind down, and it is time for Gerry the Giraffe to get ready for sleep. Gerry is feeling a little bit sleepy. Can you make a sleepy face and yawn? Big yawn, oh ho ho! Gerry walks very slowly back to his cozy bed made of soft green leaves. Yawn goes Gerry again. But before he goes to sleep, Gerry loves to look up at the twinkling night sky. His neck is so tall that his head is almost touching the shiny stars! He looks up and whispers hello to the bright yellow moon. Good night, moon. The little stars twinkle back at him. Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder where you are. Gerry stretches his long neck one last time to give the tallest tree a gentle good-night kiss. Smooch! Then he curls up his long legs and tucks his head under his spotted shoulder. He closes his big brown eyes. The gentle night breeze whispers soft lullabies through the leaves. Shh, shh, shh, goes the wind. Gerry dreams sweet dreams about green grass, yellow slides, and playing all day long with his toddler friends. It is time for you to close your eyes too, little one. Snuggle deep under your warm blanket. Breathe in, and breathe out. Good night, Gerry. Good night, stars. Good night, sweet toddler. Sleep tight and have the most wonderful dreams until the morning sun wakes us all up again.

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text:
Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and get ready with Gerry the giraffe. Gerry is very tall, taller than the kitchen table, taller than the big green armchair, and almost as tall as the front door! Gerry opens his big brown eyes and gives a big, happy giraffe yawn. Yaaaaawn! Time to get dressed for a fun day of playing outside in the warm sunshine.

First, Gerry needs to put on his special toddler t-shirt. He finds a bright yellow shirt with big blue stars on the front. Gerry lifts his long, long neck way up high into the air. He holds the shirt in his mouth and gently pulls it down, down, down over his head. Pop! His little fuzzy ears pop right through the holes. 'Silly me,' giggles Gerry, 'that is a bit too high!' So he stretches his long neck back down to the floor and pulls the sleeves onto his front legs. One leg, two legs, three legs, four legs! All tucked in nicely.

Next, Gerry needs to put on his favorite polka-dot socks. Since Gerry has four long legs, he needs four long socks. He wiggles his left front hoof. Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle. He slides a red polka-dot sock all the way up his leg. Then he does the same for his right front hoof. Up goes the blue polka-dot sock! Now for the back legs. Gerry reaches his head around to tickle his back toes. He slips a green polka-dot sock on his left back hoof and an orange polka-dot sock on his right back hoof. Look at those wonderful socks! Gerry stamps his hooves on the carpet. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Happy little giraffe hooves.

Finally, Gerry looks in the mirror. He sees a tall, bright, wonderfully dressed giraffe staring right back at him. He has his yellow star shirt and his four colorful polka-dot socks. Gerry smiles a big, toothy giraffe smile. He is ready to go outside and stomp in the grass. He grabs his little green backpack and runs to the front door, ready for a brand new adventure. Goodbye, Gerry! Have a wonderful day!

stories.title: Gerry's Big Stretch
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in the middle of a bright green jungle, lived a very happy little giraffe named Gerry. Gerry loved to play hide-and-seek with all his jungle friends. Today, Gerry and his friends were playing right near the sparkling blue river where the tall bamboo grows thick and green. It was Gerry's turn to hide, so he closed his big brown eyes and began to count loudly. 'One, two, three, four, five!' he shouted with a big smile on his face.

While Gerry was counting, all his little animal friends scrambled around to find the best hiding spots. Sammy the squirrel scampered up a rough tree trunk and hid behind a cluster of giant leaves. Bella the bunny hopped as fast as her little legs could carry her and squeezed right underneath a big hollow log. Penny the parrot fluttered her colorful wings and nestled high up in the branches of an acacia tree. Everyone was completely quiet, holding their breath so Gerry would not find them too quickly. It was so much fun!

'Ready or not, here I come!' called out Gerry. He opened his big brown eyes and started looking around. He looked to the left, and he looked to the right. He saw green grass and colorful flowers, but no friends. Gerry knew he needed a really big stretch to see over the bushes. He pushed his long, spotted neck straight up toward the fluffy white clouds. He stretched and stretched until he felt like he was touching the very sky! From way up high, Gerry could see everything.

With his super-long neck and bird's-eye view, Gerry spotted Sammy's fuzzy tail twitching behind the leaves. He saw Bella's twitchy nose peeking out from under the log. And he saw Penny's bright feathers shining in the tree branches. Gerry let out a joyful giggle. He bent his long neck back down and trotted over to his friends. 'Found you all!' cheered Gerry. They all danced around in a circle, so happy to play together in the sunny jungle. What a wonderful game of hide-and-seek!

stories.title: Gerry's Yummy Snack
stories.text:
The sun is shining brightly in the golden afternoon, and Gerry the giraffe is feeling just a tiny bit hungry in his tummy. Rumble, rumble, goes Gerry's tummy! Gerry loves snack time more than anything else in the whole wide world. Today, he is craving the most delicious, crunchy green leaves from the very top of the tallest acacia tree in the meadow. But wait! Those yummy leaves are way up high, higher than a bird can fly, and much too high for a little toddler to reach without a little bit of help.

Gerry walks over to the big acacia tree and looks up with wide, sparkly eyes. He opens his mouth and licks his lips. Mmm, those leaves look so fresh and green! Gerry stretches his long neck upward, reaching and reaching. He is so close, but his nose just barely brushes the bottom branches. Gerry tries to tiptoe on his little hooves. Tip-toe, tip-toe, up on his tiptoes! Still, the yummy snack is just a little bit out of reach. He needs to do a big giraffe stretch to get the very best treats.

Taking a deep breath, Gerry stretches his neck as high as it can possibly go. He reaches all the way up into the clouds. And pop! His long, dark-blue tongue shoots out to grab a bunch of leaves. Slurp! He gently pulls the green leaves into his mouth. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Gerry chews his snack with a happy smile. The leaves taste sweet and juicy, just like a sunny day in the meadow. He eats a few more crunchy leaves until his tummy is completely full and happy.

With a full tummy, Gerry lets out a contented little sigh. He rubs his round tummy with his front hoof and gives a sleepy yawn. It was such a yummy snack time, but now it is time for a nice afternoon nap under the cool shade of the big tree. Gerry curls his long legs underneath him and closes his eyes, dreaming of more delicious green leaves and sunny days with all his wonderful jungle friends. Good night, Gerry!

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help our very tall, very sweet friend. Who is it? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry lives way up high where the fluffy white clouds float by. Gerry is opening his big sleepy eyes. Stretch, stretch, stretch goes his long, long neck! Gerry yawns a big giraffe yawn. Good morning, sun! Good morning, trees! Gerry looks down at his toes. Time to get dressed for a fun day of play! First, Gerry needs his shirt. But wait! Gerry’s neck is so, so long. How does a giraffe put on a shirt? Let us help him! We pull the bright yellow shirt way up, up, up, past his knees, past his tummy, and all the way up his long neck. Pop goes his little head! Yay! Now Gerry has his nice yellow shirt on. Next, Gerry needs his pants. Oh, silly Gerry! He has four long legs. That means he needs four pants legs! Let us count them together: one, two, three, four! We slip the blue pants onto his long, bouncy legs. Pull them up and wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! Gerry stomps his hooves. Stomp, stomp, stomp! He feels so cozy and ready to run. But wait, what is missing? Shoes! Gerry looks at his big hooves. He has four little shoes to put on. One shoe on this hoof, click! One shoe on that hoof, clack! One more shoe, and the last shoe. All done! Gerry looks in the mirror. He looks so handsome in his yellow shirt, blue pants, and shiny shoes. He gives a happy little dance, shaking his spots from left to right. Now Gerry’s tummy starts to rumble. Rumbly, tumbly, time for breakfast! He skips out the door into the sunny morning meadow, ready for a yummy green-leaf breakfast with all his jungle friends. Goodbye, Gerry! Have a wonderful day playing games in the tall grass!

stories.title: Gerry's High-Up Picnic
stories.text: Hello again, little friends! Today, Gerry the Giraffe is having a very special party. It is a sunny picnic day in the big green park! Gerry loves picnics because he loves yummy food. But Gerry is the tallest animal in the whole wide world. Where should he put the picnic blanket? Down on the soft green grass? No, no! If Gerry sits on the ground, his head is so far up in the sky that he cannot even see his friends! So, Gerry finds a giant, fluffy green cloud of leaves way up in the tallest tree. That is his picnic spot! Gerry gets his little red basket. What is inside? Let us peek! Oh, yummy treats! There are crunchy green leaves, sweet yellow bananas, and a big jug of fresh water. Gerry climbs up the tree, step by step, using his long legs. He spreads out his polka-dot picnic blanket on a sturdy branch. Just then, his friends come walking by. Monkey hops over. Elephant stomps up. Zebra trots to the tree. They look up and call out, 'Hello, Gerry!' Gerry smiles his biggest giraffe smile. 'Hello, friends!' he calls down. 'Come on up to my picnic!' But wait. Monkey can climb, but Elephant and Zebra cannot climb tall trees! Oh no! How will they eat together? Gerry thinks hard with his big brain. He has a wonderful idea! Gerry uses his super-duper long neck. He bends his neck all the way down, down, down, like a friendly slide. Monkey slides right down his neck, whee! Elephant and Zebra stand at the bottom, and Gerry shares his sweet bananas with his trunk and his hooves. They all munch and crunch together. They laugh and play games until the sun goes down. What a happy, high-up picnic day!

stories.title: Gerry's Bedtime Lullaby
stories.text: The sun is going down, down, down. The sky turns pink and purple and deep, dark blue. The little stars are waking up and blinking hello. Twinkle, twinkle, little stars! That means it is time for sleepy little toddlers to get ready for bed. And guess who else is sleepy? Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry has been running and jumping all day long. Now his long legs feel heavy. His spots want to rest. Gerry walks slowly back to his favorite sleeping spot under the big acacia tree. The moon is shining like a giant silver night-light in the sky. Gerry looks up at the moon and gives a tiny, sleepy yawn. Ah-choo—no, not a sneeze! A big, cozy yawn! Let us all yawn together like Gerry: oooh, stretch your mouth wide! Good. Now Gerry wants to get comfy. But how does a giraffe sleep when his neck is so long? Does he lie down flat? Let us see! Gerry bends his knees. He folds his long legs underneath his soft tummy. Then, he curves his long neck all the way around, resting his sweet head right on his back. There now, he looks just like a cozy little yellow cinnamon roll! The night breeze blows softly through the leaves. Swish, swish, swish go the branches. Little crickets are singing a quiet bedtime song. Chirp, chirp, chirp. Gerry closes his big brown eyes. He thinks about all the fun things he did today: wearing his yellow shirt, eating yummy leaves at his high-up picnic, and playing with his animal friends. His heart feels warm and happy. Gerry takes a deep breath in, and lets a slow breath out. The stars watch over him. The moon smiles down at him. Gerry is safe, Gerry is warm, and Gerry is fast asleep. Goodnight, stars. Goodnight, tree. Goodnight, sweet Gerry the Giraffe. Time for you to close your eyes, too, little toddler. Sweet dreams!

stories.title: Gerry Gets Dressed
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going to wake up and help a very tall friend get dressed. Can you guess who it is? It is Gerry the Giraffe! Gerry has a long yellow neck and lots of brown spots. But oh no! Gerry has a big problem today. He is going outside to play, and he needs to get dressed all by himself. Are you ready to help Gerry? Let's count his legs together: one, two, three, four long legs! First, Gerry needs to put on his shirt. He lifts his tiny hooves up, up, up into the air. Oh, goodness! His neck is so long that the shirt gets stuck halfway up! Can you help Gerry pull the shirt up? Let's all say pull together! Pull, pull, pull! Yay! The bright red shirt is on his tummy. Now, Gerry needs his socks. But wait. Gerry does not just have two feet. He has four feet! That means he needs four warm, fluffy blue socks. Let us put a blue sock on foot number one. Pop! Now a blue sock on foot number two. Pop! Now a blue sock on foot number three. Pop! And one more blue sock on foot number four. Pop! Gerry wiggle-wiggles his four toes. Do your toes wiggle like Gerry's toes? Can you wiggle your toes in the air just like a silly giraffe? Wonderful job! Next, Gerry needs his favorite yellow hat to keep the warm sun out of his big brown eyes. But his head is so high up in the blue sky that the hat blows away in the wind! Whew! Chasing hats is hard work. Gerry runs after it, stomping his hooves: thump, thump, thump! He catches the hat and places it right on top of his head. Look at Gerry now! He has his red shirt, his four blue socks, and his yellow hat. He looks so handsome and ready for a fun day in the tall trees. Gerry smiles a big giraffe smile and says thank you to his toddler friends. You helped him so much! Now Gerry is all dressed up and ready to stomp outside to eat some yummy, green leaves. Let us wave goodbye to Gerry. Bye-bye, Gerry! Have a wonderful day playing in the warm sunshine.

stories.title: Gerry's Tall Tree Snack
stories.text: Hello again, little friends! Are you hungry? Gerry the Giraffe is very, very hungry today. His tummy is making a funny rumbling sound. Can you make a tummy rumble sound like Gerry? Rumbling-rumbling-rumble! Gerry looks up at the sky. He wants to eat some delicious green leaves from the very tallest tree in the whole wide world. But wait! The tree is so tall that even Mommy and Daddy cannot reach the top. How will Gerry get his yummy snack? Let us figure it out together! Gerry stretches his long, spotted neck up, up, up. He stretches higher than a cloud! He stretches higher than a bird! Can you stretch your neck up high like a tall giraffe? Let us all stretch together! Reach, reach, reach your hands up to the sky! Gerry opens his mouth wide. He wants to munch, munch, munch on the crisp green leaves. But the leaves are just a tiny bit too high. Oh no! Gerry needs to jump. Ready, set, jump! Gerry hops up into the air. Boing! He opens his mouth again. Snap! Munch, munch, munch goes Gerry. How does a leaf taste? Is it sweet? Is it crunchy? Gerry thinks the green leaves are the most delicious treat in the whole jungle. He chews slowly, moving his jaw from side to side. Chew, chew, chew, swallow! Gerry shares some yummy leaves with a little brown monkey swinging in the branches. The monkey says thank you by doing a silly flip. Gerry giggles a deep, happy giraffe giggle. Eating snacks with friends is so much fun! Gerry's tummy is finally full and happy. He pats his tummy with a hoof and rubs it gently. Pat, pat, pat! Now it is time to take a little rest in the cool shade of the big green tree. Close your eyes, little toddlers, and take a big deep breath in, and let it out. Gerry is resting now, dreaming of all the yummy green snacks he will eat tomorrow. Goodnight, sweet little giraffe!

stories.title: Gerry's Hide and Seek
stories.text: Time to play a game! Do you like to play hide and seek? Gerry the Giraffe loves hide and seek more than anything in the world. Today, Gerry is going to hide, and you are going to find him. Are you ready? Cover your eyes with your little hands! No peeking! Let's count to three together: one, two, three! Ready or not, here we come! Now uncover your eyes and look around. Where is Gerry? Let us look behind the big green bush. Is Gerry behind the bush? No, that is just a fluffy white bunny hopping away. Hop, hop, hop! Let us look behind the yellow flowers. Is Gerry behind the flowers? No, that is just a buzzy little bee collecting honey. Buzz, buzz, buzz! Wait a minute. Look up at the sky! Way up high, above the green bush, above the yellow flowers, above the tall grass, what do we see? We see two brown ears and a long yellow neck poking out from the clouds! It is Gerry! Gerry tried to hide, but he is just too tall to fit behind anything. He pops his head out and laughs a loud, jolly laugh. Got you, Gerry! You are too tall to hide! Gerry giggles and dances a silly little dance. He shakes his left leg, he shakes his right leg, he shakes his long spotted tail, and he shakes his polka-dot head. Can you dance a silly giraffe dance with Gerry? Shake your arms, shake your legs, and wiggle all around! That was so much fun. Gerry loves playing games with his clever toddler friends. Finding Gerry was the best part of the whole day. Gerry gives everyone a gentle nuzzle with his soft nose. Boop! Now it is your turn to hide. Hide your face behind your hands, and Gerry will count to three. One, two, three, here comes Gerry to find you! What a wonderful day of playing games together in the warm, sunny meadow.

rhymes.title: Tall and Sweet
rhymes.text:
See the tall giraffe outside,
With his pretty spots so wide.
Reaching up into the trees,
Dancing softly in the breeze.

He has ears to hear me call,
He is growing big and tall.
Long neck stretching to the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.

Yellow coat of golden brown,
Happiest giraffe in town.
Chewing leaves of green and bright,
Eating snack-time day and night.

Now he wiggles all his toes,
Points his little fuzzy nose.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
Curling softly in his bed.

rhymes.title: Spots in the Sun
rhymes.text:
Gerry wears a coat of gold,
Bravest giraffe you can behold.
Running through the sunny grass,
Watching little beetles pass.

Four long legs that tap and beat,
Bouncing on his happy feet.
Reaching up to grab a leaf,
Chewing slowly, what a chief!

Birds fly up to say hello,
To the tallest friend we know.
Swishing tail from side to side,
Taking critters for a ride.

Evening stars begin to peep,
Time to cuddle up and sleep.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Munching Green Leaves
rhymes.text:
Little giraffe with spots so bright,
Eating green leaves every night.
Long brown tongue goes mmm, mmm, yum,
Beating like a happy drum.

Stretching high above the tree,
Looking down to wave at me.
Friendly smile upon his face,
Running in a gentle race.

Pat his back and say good cheer,
Glad to have our helper here.
Stomping feet upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Now the stars are shining deep,
Time for Gerry goes to sleep.
Softly sighing, sweet and low,
Off to dreamland he will go.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots of brown,
Walks all over jungle town.
Reaches high into the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.
Long neck stretches way up high,
While the little birds fly by.
Yellow spots upon his face,
Running at a bouncy pace.
Munches leaves upon a tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Bows his head to say good day,
Now it is time for us to play.
Stamps his feet upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Wiggles ears and wags his tail,
Greeting every friendly snail.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
Curling up in cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Stretch, Giraffe, Stretch
rhymes.text:
Stretch, giraffe, up to the sun,
Playing games is so much fun.
Look at you so tall and grand,
Walking on the golden sand.
Bend your knees and touch your toes,
Wiggle that soft velvet nose.
Stomp your hooves upon the floor,
Let us hear you shout out more.
Swing your tail from side to side,
Take a gentle piggy ride.
Find a leaf that's fresh and green,
Biggest neck that's ever seen.
Blink your big brown gentle eyes,
Underneath the morning skies.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time to go right off to sleep.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Yellow body, spots of brown,
Best giraffe in all the town.
Eating leaves that taste so sweet,
Standing on four sturdy feet.
Long neck reaching for the light,
Shining brightly in the night.
Soft fur feels so warm and nice,
Listen to the chirping mice.
Dance around the forest tree,
Happy, busy, wild and free.
Nod your head and smile a smile,
Resting for a little while.
Shadows growing big and long,
Singing out a bedtime song.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
See the tall giraffe today,
Standing in the grass to play.
Reaching for the sky so high,
Watching little birds fly by.

Long brown spots upon his skin,
Happy smile upon his chin.
Stretching up to grab a tree,
Looking very proud and free.

Eats a leaf that is so green,
Bestest giraffe ever seen.
Bends his neck down to the ground,
Walking all without a sound.

Now the sun is going low,
Time for little friends to go.
Say goodnight and wave goodbye,
Underneath the sleepy sky.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Giraffe has spots from head to toe,
Watch the happy fellow go.
Long yellow legs go tap, tap, tap,
Ready for a little nap.

Ears can wiggle, tail can swish,
Eating grass is all his wish.
Reaching up to touch the cloud,
Making toddler voices proud.

Soft brown nose and big brown eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.
Stretching high up in the air,
Standing right beside the bear.

Now he sits down on the floor,
Does not want to wander more.
Closes up his sleepy eyes,
Underneath the evening skies.

rhymes.title: Munching Leaves
rhymes.text:
Munch, munch, munch upon a tree,
Tall giraffe is happy, see?
Long tongue out to grab a bite,
Everything is feeling right.

Yellow body, golden sun,
Playing games is so much fun.
Stretching up to find some more,
Walking by the jungle door.

Little toddlers clap and shout,
Seeing what it's all about.
Giraffe dances all around,
Stomping softly on the ground.

Yawn goes he and close each eye,
Time to sing a lullaby.
Stars are shining bright and deep,
Tall giraffe is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so brown,
You are the tallest in our town.
You eat the leaves up in the tree,
And bend way down to smile at me.
Your long, long neck goes up so high,
Right up into the big blue sky.
You stomp your feet and give a cheer,
We are so glad that you are here.
With floppy ears and gentle eyes,
You look so sweet and very wise.
Let's run and play upon the grass,
And watch the happy zebras pass.
The sun is setting in the west,
Of all our friends, we like you best.
Now close your eyes and go to sleep,
While quiet little crickets peep.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Gerry has a spotted coat,
Longer than a furry goat.
Yellow fur and patches brown,
Walking all around the town.
Reach your neck up to the sun,
Running races is so fun.
Munching leaves of crispy green,
Best giraffe we've ever seen.
Blinking eyes so big and wide,
With a baby by your side.
Stomp your hooves upon the floor,
Do you want to play some more?
Nod your head and say hello,
Watch the little river flow.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for Gerry goes to sleep.

rhymes.title: Reach Up High
rhymes.text:
Stretching up to touch the sky,
See the tall giraffe go by.
Long and yellow, soft and sweet,
Walking on four hooves and feet.
Reaching for a leafy snack,
With a pretty patterned back.
Swishing tail to chase the flies,
Underneath the sunny skies.
Bending down to take a drink,
Standing by the river's brink.
Little birds upon your head,
Time to snuggle in your bed.
Close your eyes and rest your feet,
Have a dream that's nice and sweet.
Goodnight, Gerry, sleep till dawn,
Sleeping softly on the lawn.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so brown,
You are the tallest in the town.
You reach up high to touch the sky,
While little fluffy clouds float by.

You have a very long, sweet face,
And walk around with so much grace.
Your neck is long, your legs are tall,
You never ever seem to fall.

You munch on leaves that look so green,
The happiest beast that I have seen.
You nod your head and say hello,
Wherever you decide to go.

Now go to sleep in cozy bed,
With sleepy thoughts inside your head.
The stars are shining bright and deep,
Good night, giraffe, go go to sleep.

rhymes.title: Spotty Friend
rhymes.text:
Look at the spots upon your skin,
A happy smile is on your chin.
You run across the grassy plain,
And dance inside the gentle rain.

Your ears are cute and furry too,
I love to play each day with you.
You stomp your feet upon the floor,
And want to play a little more.

We jump and skip around the tree,
As happy as can ever be.
You bend your neck to say good day,
And then you turn and trot away.

The sun is warm, the sky is blue,
My favorite friend is sweet giraffe, it is true.
So give a wave and shout hooray,
For such a sunny, happy day.

rhymes.title: Giraffe Song
rhymes.text:
Up so high above the trees,
Dancing softly in the breeze.
You have two little horns of brown,
And you are the king of this small town.

You eat the leaves that taste so sweet,
With happy hooves upon your feet.
You run so fast across the land,
Upon the warm and golden sand.

The little birds fly all around,
And make a pretty tweeting sound.
You look at them and blink your eyes,
Beneath the sunny yellow skies.

Now close your eyes and rest your head,
Upon your cozy sleepy bed.
The day is done, the night is here,
Sleep tight, giraffe, my friend so dear.

rhymes.title: Tall and Yellow
rhymes.text:
Gerry is a tall giraffe,
He makes all the toddlers laugh.
He has spots of brown and gold,
Cutest friend you want to hold.
Reaching up into the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.
Long blue tongue to grab a tree,
Eating yummy leaves for tea.
Bending down to take a drink,
Faster than a blink, blink, blink.
Stomping feet upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the town.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Rest your sleepy, heavy head.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Look at Gerry walking by,
Reaching right up to the sky.
Yellow coat with spots so bright,
Shining in the morning light.
Long white horns upon his head,
Jumping right out of his bed.
Walking to the jungle tree,
Looking at a buzzing bee.
Munching leaves of crispy green,
Best giraffe you've ever seen.
Running fast across the plain,
Dancing in the falling rain.
Waving with a happy hoof,
Standing high above the roof.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for Gerry fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Stretch Your Neck
rhymes.text:
Stretch your neck up very high,
Wave hello to butterfly.
Gerry has a friendly smile,
Walking for a little while.
Eating breakfast in the sun,
Having lots of toddler fun.
Four big shoes upon his feet,
Looking darling and so neat.
Swishing with his fuzzy tail,
Sailing like a happy whale.
Drinking water from the stream,
Having such a pleasant dream.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving us a cozy light.
Couch is soft and bed is deep,
Gerry hugs his toys to sleep.

rhymes.title: Gerry's Spots
rhymes.text:
Little giraffe with spots so brown,
You are the tallest one in town.
Your neck is long, your legs are high,
Almost reaching up to the sky.

You love to munch on leafy trees,
And sway about in the gentle breeze.
With big brown eyes and furry ears,
You chase away all toddler fears.

You gallop fast across the plain,
In the sunshine and the rain.
Your yellow coat is bright and sweet,
From your head down to your feet.

Now the sun begins to set,
The nicest friend we've ever met.
Time to sleep and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Reach Up High
rhymes.text:
Reach up high into the air,
Gerry is a gentle bear... wait, a giraffe!
Stretch your neck and start to laugh.

Green leaves hanging on the tree,
Waiting there for you and me.
Your purple tongue comes out to play,
Nibbling breakfast every day.

Stomp your hooves upon the ground,
Spinning slowly all around.
Swing your tail from side to side,
Ready for a bumpy ride.

Toddlers clap and toddlers cheer,
Glad that Gerry is so near.
Now it's time to say goodnight,
Till the morning brings its light.

rhymes.title: The Giraffe Dance
rhymes.text:
Tip-toe, tip-toe, hear the sound,
Gerry's hooves touch the ground.
He can dance and he can prance,
In a happy jungle dance.

Bend your knees and shake your head,
Time to jump upon your bed.
Stretch your neck both left and right,
Basking in the morning light.

Friends are coming down the trail,
Monkey swinging by his tail.
Elephant and zebra too,
Visiting the sunny zoo.

Play together, laugh and run,
Basking in the golden sun.
Gerry smiles a giant smile,
Resting for a little while.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so bright,
Standing up against the light.
Reach your neck up to the sky,
Wave to clouds that wander by.

Munching leaves up on the tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Long brown legs go stomp, stomp, stomp,
Walking through the grassy swamp.

Twitch your ears and shake your mane,
Dancing in the gentle rain.
Now the sun begins to glow,
Time to rest and walking slow.

Curl your neck upon the floor,
Sleep until the morning roar.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Spotty Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Little spots of brown and gold,
Cutest story ever told.
Stretch your neck so very high,
Almost touching starry sky.

Chewing yummy green bouquet,
Having such a fun-filled day.
Running fast across the plain,
Dancing in the summer rain.

Nod your head and blink your eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.
Soft and gentle is your heart,
Playing such a lovely part.

Now the evening breeze blows cool,
Resting by the quiet pool.
Time for bed and quiet sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Reach Up High
rhymes.text:
Reach up high and touch the sun,
Being tall is so much fun.
Gerry is a friendly friend,
Loving you until the end.

Ears wiggle back and forth so neat,
Stomping with your hooves of feet.
Eating leaves that taste so sweet,
Walking down the yellow street.

Moon is shining up above,
Sending hugs and sleepy love.
Close your eyes and snuggle tight,
Sleeping through the quiet night.

Dream of games and sunny skies,
Opening your sleepy eyes.
Morning comes with cheerful light,
Everything is feeling right.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots of brown,
Looking up and looking down.
Walking through the golden grass,
Watch the gentle giant pass.

Long, long neck reaches the sky,
Wave hello as he walks by.
Eating leaves up in the tree,
Happy as a giraffe can be.

Four long legs and hooves so neat,
Stomping softly with his feet.
Swishing tail from side to side,
Taking toddlers for a ride.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping safely on the ground.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Rest your sleepy, spotted head.

rhymes.title: Leaves to Eat
rhymes.text:
Gerry has a purple tongue,
Old and wise or very young.
Reaching for the branches high,
Touching all the clouds nearby.

Munching leaves of crispy green,
Best giraffe you've ever seen.
Swallowing a yummy treat,
Making tummy full and sweet.

Birds are singing in the air,
Blowing kisses everywhere.
Gerry dances on his toes,
Touching with his velvet nose.

Now the snack time comes to pass,
Sitting down upon the grass.
Time to dream and time to rest,
Giraffe sleep is truly best.

rhymes.title: Yellow Spots
rhymes.text:
Yellow spots upon his coat,
Velvet scarf around his throat.
Gerry wears a happy smile,
Walking for a little while.

Bending down to drink some water,
Just like any jungle daughter.
Splish and splash upon the floor,
Gerry always asks for more.

Running fast and feeling free,
Underneath the acacia tree.
Little toddlers jump and play,
Dancing all the hours away.

Twinkle stars begin to gleam,
Filling up with golden dream.
Say goodnight to tall giraffe,
Ending with a happy laugh.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so brown,
Looking at the grassy ground.
Stretch your neck up to the sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.

Munching leaves up in the tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Long brown legs and gentle eyes,
Standing underneath the skies.

Wiggle ears and shake your tail,
Walking down the sunny trail.
Now it is time to say good night,
Sleeping in the pale moonlight.

Dream of leaves so green and sweet,
Resting all your four long feet.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Giraffe friend, you are the best.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Gerry is a funny sight,
Spotted brown and yellow bright.
Reaching for the leaves above,
Sending everybody love.

Tongue is purple, long and sweet,
Pulling down a tasty treat.
Munching loudly, crunching slow,
Watch the tall giraffe now go.

Stomping softly on the grass,
Watching all the zebras pass.
Swishing tail to keep away,
Bugs that want to softly play.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the quiet town.
Rest your neck upon the ground,
While the stars are shining round.

rhymes.title: Stretch Up High
rhymes.text:
Stand up tall upon the plain,
Dancing in the gentle rain.
Giraffe friend is very high,
Touching all the clouds so by.

Look around and see your friends,
Where the yellow pathway ends.
Elephant and zebra too,
Want to come and play with you.

Run around and skip and jump,
Over every little bump.
Your long legs are fun to swing,
Happy giraffe, dance and sing.

Now the day is almost done,
Say goodbye to golden sun.
Time for bed and cozy sleep,
While the tiny crickets beep.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
See the tall giraffe so grand,
Walking through the grassy land.
He has spots of brown and gold,
Cutest neck you've ever hold.

He can reach the trees so high,
Almost touching all the sky.

Running in the morning light.
Blinking with his pretty eyes,

Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.
Dreaming of the trees above,
Filled with happiness and love.

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots
rhymes.text:
Gerry has a spotted coat,

Orange patches, big and bright,

Wiggle ears and wag a tail,
Walking down the dusty trail.
Stretching up to grab a leaf,
Chewing slowly, what a chief!

Baby toddlers, look around,
Can you stomp upon the ground?
Reach your hands up to the sun,
Let us play and have some fun.

Now it is time to say goodbye,
Wave your hands up to the sky.
Sleepy giraffe goes to rest,
Knowing that he is the best.

rhymes.title: Reach Up High
rhymes.text:
Little giraffe, look at me,
Standing by the acacia tree.
Neck is long and face is sweet,
Tappy-tap your little feet.

Reach your hands up to the top,
Never ever want to stop.
Plucking leaves of green and red,

Gerry smiles a happy smile,
Resting for a little while.
Drinking water from the stream,
Living in a happy dream.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Rocking gently to and fro.

Counting little jumping sheep.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so brown,
Looking up and looking down.
Walking through the jungle trees,
Sniffing up the morning breeze.
Long yellow neck so grand,
Tallest creature in the land.
Stretching up to reach the sky,
Watching birds go flying by.
Chewing leaves that taste so sweet,
Happy from his head to feet.
Stomping hooves upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Now it is time to say hello,
To our friendly friend below.
Wave goodbye and count to three,
Happy giraffe beneath the tree.

rhymes.title: Spotty Dotty

Spotty dotty, brown and tall,
Does not fit inside a wall.
Longer than a garden hose,
With a wiggle on his nose.
Walking slow and walking tall,
Greeting every beast and small.
Bending down to drink a stream,
Looking happy as a dream.
Eats the leaves from way up high,
Right beneath the sunny sky.
Twitching ears and blinking eyes,

Now he runs to play a game,

Sing a song for all to see.

rhymes.title: Reach Up High
rhymes.text:
Reach up high into the air,
See the giraffe standing there.
Yellow coat of spotted gold,
Cutest story ever told.
Long blue tongue to grab a treat,
Yummy leaves so crisp and sweet.
Stomping feet go tap, tap, tap,

Wake up now and stretch out wide,
With our spotted friend beside.
Jump up high and shout hooray,
For a happy toddler day.
Smile and giggle, clap your hands,
Best giraffe in all the lands.

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
See the tall giraffe go by,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
With his spots of brown and gold,
He is a wondrous sight to hold.

He has legs so very long,
Walking to a happy song.
Nibbling leaves from up above,
Filled with kindness and with love.

Wiggling ears and blinking eyes,
Underneath the sunny skies.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for tall giraffe to sleep.
Fold his legs and rest his head,

From his head down to his feet.

Counting spots is such a fun,

One and two and three and four,

Like a falling drop of rain,

Glad that Gerry friend is here.

Now the happy day is done,
Evening shadows hide the sun.

Whispering a sweet goodnight.

Stomp your hooves upon the floor,

Reach for clouds of fluffy white,
In the lovely morning light.
Laugh and giggle with delight,

Now it is time to rest your toes,
From your head down to your nose.

Soft yellow fur and brown, too,

rhymes.title: Tall and Small
rhymes.text:

Making little toddlers laugh.

Reaching up to touch the sky,

Resting down his sleepy head.

Gerry giraffe is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Spotty the Giraffe

rhymes.title: Reach For The Sky

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:

Long, long neck and gentle face,

rhymes.title: Spots and Dots

rhymes.title: Tall Giraffe
rhymes.text:
Tall giraffe with spots so brown,

rhymes.text:

stories.title: Zeke the Zebra Loses His Stripes
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the big, bright grassland, woke up a little zebra named Zeke. Zeke loved his stripes. They were bold. They were black. They were white. They zigged and they zagged all over his fuzzy little body. Zeke stretched his legs, gave a happy little whinny, and trotted over to the watering hole to see his best friend, Tess the tortoise. But when Zeke looked down into the sparkly, clear water, he gasped a tiny gasp. Oh no! Something was wrong. Very, very wrong! Zeke blinked his big brown eyes and looked closer. His reflection was staring back at him, but it did not look right at all. His stripes were missing! Where did they go? Zeke felt his tummy go all fluttery. He looked down at his front leg. It was just plain white. He looked at his back leg. It was just plain white. He looked at his tummy. It was as plain and white as a puffy cloud. 'Tess!' cried Zeke, running over to his turtle friend as fast as his little hooves could carry him. 'Tess, look at me! My stripes are gone! I am just a plain white horse now! How will the other animals know I am a zebra?' Tess poked her wrinkly green head out of her shell and blinked slowly. 'Oh, dear me,' said Tess in her slow, sleepy voice. 'Where do you think they went, Zeke?' Zeke thought very hard. He thought about everything he had done since the sun woke up. 'Well,' said Zeke, 'I galloped through the tall, tickly grass. Then I rolled in the muddy puddle near the big acacia tree. And then I ran through the patch of sticky black mud!' Tess smiled a gentle smile. 'Aha!' said Tess. 'I bet your stripes are not gone at all. I bet they are just hiding underneath all that mud and grass!' Zeke gasped. He trotted back to the sparkling watering hole. He dipped his hoof into the cool water and splashed a little bit onto his leg. Then he rubbed gently with his soft nose. Swish, swish, swish! Suddenly, a dark line appeared! Zeke splashed more water. Swish, swish, swish! Another line appeared, and another, and another! The bold black and white stripes started popping out, one by one, shining brightly in the warm morning sun. Zeke giggled and did a happy little tap-dance with his hooves. 'They are back!' cheered Zeke. 'My wonderful stripes are back!' Tess clapped her flippers happily. Zeke learned a very important lesson that day: sometimes, your favorite things just need a little bath to shine again. With a happy heart and his stripes glowing in the light, Zeke trotted off to play hide-and-seek in the tall, tall grass, knowing his black and white coat would keep him safe and happy all day long.

stories.title: Zuri's Magical Pajamas
stories.text: The sun was sliding down behind the big green hills, painting the sky in sleepy pinks and purples. It was almost bedtime in the grassy plains, and little Zuri the zebra was getting ready for sleep. But Zuri did not want to sleep. Zuri wanted to jump! She wanted to run! She wanted to do cartwheels across the meadow! 'Come on, Zuri,' said Mama Zebra softly, tucking her head under her chin. 'It is time for night-night. Put on your sleepytime magic.' Zuri blinked her sleepy eyes. 'What is sleepytime magic, Mama?' Mama Zebra smiled warmly and pointed her nose toward a special bundle of clothes resting on a smooth flat rock. 'Those are your brand new bedtime pajamas,' whispered Mama. 'They are not just any pajamas. They are magical star-stripes.' Zuri trotted over to the rock and looked down. Resting there were the coziest, softest pajamas she had ever seen. They were made of dark blue flannel, covered from top to bottom in bright, glowing yellow stars. Zuri carefully stepped into the legs. One, two, three, four! She wriggled her fuzzy body until the soft fabric hugged her tight. Then, something amazing happened. As soon as the pajamas touched her skin, Zuri let out a giant, echoing yawn. Yaaaaawn! Her eyelids felt heavy, like they were made of big, soft pillows. 'Ohhh,' whispered Zuri, her voice sounding sleepy and small. 'The magic is working, Mama.' Mama Zebra nuzzled Zuri’s cheek with her warm nose. 'It is time to count your blessings, my little star-zebra,' Mama hummed gently. Zuri lay down in the sweet-smelling grass and curled into a cozy ball. She looked up at the big dark sky, where real stars were blinking down at her. Her pajamas matched the sky! They twinkled with yellow light every time she took a soft, slow breath. In, out. In, out.
