"Your stripes might be awake, Zack, but do you know what they like to do when the sun goes down? They like to go to sleep, one by one." Zack blinked his big brown eyes. "They do?" "Yes," said Mama Zebra. "Let us tuck them in for the night." Zack curled up on the soft, cool grass beside his mother. He looked down at his front leg. "Okay, Mama. Let's tuck them in." Mama Zebra gently touched his nose. "First, the top stripe on your forehead goes to sleep. Goodnight, top stripe." Zack closed his eyes for a second. "Then, the stripe on your left ear gets very heavy and drops down. Goodnight, ear stripe." Zack let his long ear flop down happily. "Next, the big stripe across your tummy wraps around you like a cozy blanket. Goodnight, tummy stripe." Zack took a deep breath, feeling his tummy rise and fall. "And finally, all the stripes on your long legs curl up tight. Goodnight, leg stripes." Zack felt his legs relax completely against the earth. The sky grew darker, and the first bright stars began to blink into the night sky like tiny nightlights. The crickets started to sing a sweet, quiet lullaby in the grass. Zack felt completely safe, warm, and loved, nestled right beside his mama. His stripes were all resting quietly, and before he knew it, Zack closed his eyes and drifted off into a sweet, peaceful sleep, dreaming of his next big adventure in the morning sun.

stories.title: Zeke the Zebra's Lost Stripe
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, in the middle of the big green grass, lived a little zebra named Zeke. Zeke had black stripes and white stripes, just like all his zebra friends. But one morning, when Zeke woke up and looked down at his tummy, he gasped. Oh, no! One of his black stripes was missing! Zeke blinked his big brown eyes. He rubbed his tummy with a furry hoof. Where could his stripe have gone? Did it fall off while he was sleeping? Did it run away to play hide-and-seek? Zeke decided he needed to go on a big adventure to find his lost stripe. First, he trotted over to his best friend, Tess the tall giraffe. 'Tess, Tess!' called Zeke, shaking his little mane. 'Have you seen my missing stripe? I think it rolled away!' Tess blinked her long eyelashes and looked up at the fluffy white clouds. She stretched her very long neck and looked all around the acacia trees. 'No, Zeke,' said Tess with a gentle smile. 'I do not see your stripe up here in the leaves. But keep looking! Maybe it went for a swim.' Zeke gave a little nod and trotted down to the cool blue watering hole. There he met Pip the playful Hippo, who was blowing big bubbly bubbles in the water. 'Hello, Pip!' said Zeke. 'Have you seen my black stripe? It went missing this morning!' Pip splashed a happy little wave with his stubby tail. 'Glub glub, no stripe down here in the mud, Zeke! Just lots of sticky green lily pads!' Zeke giggled. He did not want a lily pad for a stripe. He wanted his very own stripe back. He kept walking, his little hooves going clip-clop, clip-clop on the warm dirt path. He felt a little bit tired. He sat down under a shady tree to rest his legs. He gave a big yawn. Yawn, yawn, big sleepy yawn! Then, Zeke felt something tickle his tummy. He looked down and tickled his tummy with his nose. And guess what he saw? There was his black stripe! It wasn't lost at all. It had just scrunched up into a funny little zigzag because Zeke had curled up into such a tight ball while he was sleeping. Zeke let out a happy giggle. He stretched out his legs, and his stripe popped right back into place, straight and neat. Zeke jumped up and did a happy little zebra dance. Clip-clop, stomp-stomp, swish-swish went his tail! He ran back to tell Tess and Pip the good news. He was whole again, from his fuzzy ears to his little black tail, and he was the happiest zebra in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Zoe's Muddy Boots
stories.text: Little Zoe the zebra loved splashing in puddles. Whenever it rained in the grassy savanna, big gray clouds would rumble, and big round raindrops would go plip, plip, plop on the ground. Zoe would wiggle her ears with excitement. Today, the biggest puddle in the whole park was right by the big baobab tree. Zoe trotted over, her black and white stripes shining in the damp sunshine. She stopped right at the edge of the water. She looked down at her hooves. She didn't have rubber boots like the human children she sometimes saw on the edge of the park. She had bare, happy hooves! Zoe lifted her right front hoof high into the air. Ready, set, go! She stomped it down into the puddle with a giant SPLASH! Muddy water flew up, up, up into the air like sparkling brown fireworks. 'Whee!' giggled Zoe, shaking her head so her little black mane bounced. She stomped her left front hoof. SPLASH! Then her back right hoof. SPLASH! Then her back left hoof. SPLASH, SPLASH, SPLASH! Soon, Zoe was covered in tiny brown mud freckles from the tip of her black nose all the way down to her stripy tummy. A little yellow butterfly fluttered down and landed right on Zoe's nose. The butterfly opened and closed its wings softly. 'Hello, little butterfly,' whispered Zoe, crossing her eyes to look at her new tiny friend. The butterfly tickled her nose so much that Zoe let out a big, happy sneeze! Achoo! The butterfly fluttered away up into the blue sky. Just then, Zoe's mama trotted over. Mama Zebra had big, kind eyes and lots of lovely stripes. Mama looked at Zoe, who was now a muddy brown-and-white zebra instead of a black-and-white zebra. Mama chuckled a warm, rumbly zebra chuckle. 'Well, look at my little mud pie!' Mama said gently. Zoe giggled and nuzzled her soft nose against her mama's neck. 'I had so much fun, Mama! I made a hundred splashes!' Mama smiled and licked a little speck of mud off Zoe's cheek. 'It is wonderful to splash, my sweet Zoe. But now it is time for a nice warm rain shower to rinse off.' Just then, a gentle warm breeze blew, and a little sprinkle of rain fell from a passing cloud, washing Zoe's legs clean and shiny once more. Zoe skipped home, her heart full of joy and ready for the next puddle day.

stories.title: Zack's Stripey Pajamas
stories.text: The sun was sinking low behind the grassy hills, painting the sky in bright pink, orange, and purple swirls. It was almost bedtime in the meadow, and little Zack the zebra was getting very, very sleepy. He rubbed his big sleepy eyes with a hoof and let out a long, soft yawn. Yaaawn! Mama Zebra walked over with a gentle smile. 'Time to get ready for sleep, my little Zack,' she whispered. Zack loved bedtime, but tonight was a very special night. Tonight was the night Zack got to wear his brand-new pajamas! Mama pulled out a pair of cozy, soft pajamas from a basket. And guess what pattern they were? They were covered in bright yellow stars and little sleepy moons! Zack slipped his front legs into the armholes, and Mama buttoned them all the way up his tummy. Zack looked down at himself. He already had black stripes and white stripes, and now he had yellow star stripes, too! He looked like a magical nighttime sky walking around on four little hooves. 'Look, Mama!' whispered Zack proudly. 'I am a star zebra!' Mama gave him a warm nuzzle. 'You are the brightest star in my sky,' she said softly. Next, it was time for teeth brushing. Zack chomped on a green twig toothbrush, scrub-a-dub-dubbing his little white teeth until they sparkled in the twilight. Then, Mama tucked him into his cozy bed made of soft green moss and sweet-smelling hay. Zack pulled up his starry blanket right up to his chin. It was so snug and warm. 'Tell me a bedtime story, Mama,' begged Zack, blinking sleepily. Mama sat down beside him and began to hum a sweet, soothing lullaby. The crickets in the grass began to chirp their gentle evening song: chirp, chirp, crickets sing, sleep well, little zebra king. A friendly owl hooted softly from a branch far above: hoo, hoo, time for dreams. Zack closed his heavy eyelids. He listened to the wind rustling softly through the tall grass. He hugged his favorite plush toy, a little cloth monkey, right against his chest. He felt safe, he felt loved, and he felt wonderfully warm in his starry pajamas. With one last happy sigh, Zack drifted off to dreamland, where all his stripes danced with the stars until the morning sun came up again.

stories.title: Zeke the Zebra's Stripes
stories.text: Once upon a time, on the wide and sunny African savanna, lived a little zebra named Zeke. Zeke had the most wonderful coat of black and white stripes. Every morning, the golden sun would peek over the tall acacia trees, and Zeke would wake up ready for a brand new day of fun with his animal friends. Today, Zeke had a very important mission. He wanted to play hide-and-seek with his best friend, Pip the bird. 'Ready or not, here I come!' chirped Pip, hiding his eyes behind his soft little wings. Zeke knew just what to do. He trotted over to the tall, swaying green grass at the edge of the watering hole. He stood very, very still right in the middle of the grass. Because his stripes looked just like the shadows of the tall blades dancing in the wind, Zeke disappeared! 'Where did Zeke go?' wondered Pip, looking up and down, left and right. 'I can see the grass, and I can see the water, but I cannot see my friend!' Zeke giggled softly. He could not help it, because the tickly grass was making his nose want to sneeze. *Achoo!* sneezed Zeke, bursting out from the tall grass with a big, happy smile. 'Found you!' cheered Pip, flapping his wings with delight. Next, Zeke wanted to play a game with Tess the tortoise. Tess moved very slowly, but she was the best listener in the whole wide world. Zeke trotted over to Tess and showed her his shiny black and white hooves. 'Tess, do you want to race to the big rock?' asked Zeke gently. Tess nodded her slow, wise head. 'Ready, set, go!' shouted Pip from above. Zeke did not want to run too fast because he wanted Tess to have fun, too. He took gentle, bouncy little steps, trotting *clip-clop, clip-clop* across the warm dirt. Tess walked *step, slow step* right behind him. Even though Zeke reached the big rock first, he waited patiently for Tess and gave her a warm nuzzle. 'Good job, Tess! We both did it!' purred Zeke. As the afternoon sun began to turn a lovely shade of orange and pink, all the animals gathered together to share a cool drink of water. Zeke looked down at his stripes and felt so proud. His stripes helped him hide in the grass, they kept him cool in the sunshine, and they made him look so special. Zeke let out a happy little whinny and cuddled close to his mother as the bright stars twinkled in the night sky. It had been a wonderful, magical day on the savanna, and Zeke was ready for sweet dreams.

stories.title: Zoe's Muddy Adventure
stories.text: Deep in the green and leafy jungle, where the big raindrops fall, lived a cheerful little zebra named Zoe. Zoe loved the color white, and she loved the color black. Most of all, Zoe loved splashing in puddles after a big rainstorm. One warm afternoon, heavy grey clouds rolled across the sky. *Rumble, rumble, rumble* went the thunder. *Flash!* went the bright lightning. Zoe squealed with pure joy and did a little happy dance with her hooves. *Tap, tap, tap* went the first raindrops on the big banana leaves. Soon, the rain stopped, and the sun came peeking back out, making the world sparkle. Zoe trotted over to her favorite spot by the river path, and there she found it: a huge, squishy, wonderfully muddy puddle! It bubbled and gurgled in the warm sunlight. Zoe walked right up to the edge and looked down at her reflection. She saw her bright white stripes and her shiny black stripes looking right back up at her. 'I wonder what I would look like with a little bit of mud,' whispered Zoe to a friendly butterfly fluttering nearby. Without another second of hesitation, Zoe stepped right into the puddle. *Squish, squelch, squirt!* went the mud between her hooves. It felt so squishy and tickly! Zoe could not help herself. She dipped her nose down and blew bubbles in the mud. *Plop, blop, blop!* Then, she gave a happy little kick of her back legs, sending brown mud flying everywhere. *Splish, splash, splatter!* Oh, what a mess she was making! Her white stripes were now brown stripes, and her black stripes were covered in gooey muck. Just then, her mama trotted over, blinking in surprise. 'Well, hello there, little mud monster!' laughed Mama Zebra, her voice as warm as the sunshine. Zoe giggled and shook her head, sending a spray of tiny mud drops into the air. 'Look at me, Mama! I am a mud zebra!' Mama Zebra smiled and nuzzled Zoe’s muddy cheek. 'You certainly are, my sweet girl. But now it is time to get clean before suppertime.' Together, they walked down to the sparkling river. Zoe stepped into the cool, clear water. *Swish, swash, swish* went the river water as Zoe washed her legs and danced in the current. All the mud floated away, washing down the stream to help the jungle flowers grow. When Zoe stepped out of the water, she was cleaner than ever. Her black stripes were shiny like jet, and her white stripes were bright like snow. Zoe shook her coat until she was completely dry, feeling fresh and happy. She nuzzled her mama and whispered, 'Mud is fun, but being clean is wonderful, too.' And with a happy skip, Zoe trotted off to find her dinner, ready for whatever adventure tomorrow might bring.

stories.title: Zack's Stripe-tastic Day
stories.text: Good morning, little readers! Today we are going to meet a very special friend named Zack. Zack is a young zebra with a shiny, bouncy mane and a coat of stripes that go all the way from his nose to the tip of his tail. Zack lived in a wonderful valley full of flowers that smelled like sweet honey. Every single morning, Zack liked to practice his numbers and his colors by looking at the world around him. 'Let us count my stripes!' Zack would say to himself every day when he woke up. He would look down at his front leg. One stripe, two stripes, three stripes, four! Then he would look at his tummy. Five stripes, six stripes, seven stripes, more! Zack’s stripes were truly magical. When he stood still in the morning fog, he looked like a fluffy cloud. When he stood near the river, he looked like the rippling water. But Zack’s favorite part of the day was always playtime with his woodland animal friends. Today, Zack was planning a big safari parade. He trotted over to the big oak tree where his friends were waiting. There was Sammy the squirrel, Bella the bunny, and Leo the lion cub. 'Who wants to join my stripe-tastic parade?' asked Zack, shaking his tail with excitement. 'Me! Me!' shouted all the friends together. Zack stood at the very front of the line because he was the tallest and had the best view of the path. 'March, march, march!' sang Zack, lifting his hooves high in the air. *Clop, clop, tap, tap, patter, patter* went all their feet as they marched through the valley. Sammy the squirrel held a little acorn like a baton, waving it up and down. Bella the bunny hopped along right behind Zack, counting his black and white stripes out loud. 'One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!' chanted Bella happily. Leo the lion cub tried his very best to march like a zebra, lifting his paws high and roaring a friendly little roar. *Roar-squeak!* went Leo, making everyone giggle. They marched past the tall sunflowers, they marched past the big blue pond, and they marched all the way up to the top of the grassy hill. When they reached the top, they all sat down together to eat a delicious snack of crunchy green leaves and sweet berries. Zack looked around at his wonderful friends and felt his heart fill up with warmth and joy. He loved being a zebra, and he loved sharing his happy days with the people—and animals—he cared about most. As the afternoon shadows grew long and cozy, Zack gave a gentle yawn and waved goodbye to his friends. He trotted back to his cozy sleeping spot, curled up his long legs, and closed his eyes. Sweet dreams, Zack, and sleep tight until the morning light brings another day of stripes and smiles.

stories.title: Zeke the Zebra Loses a Stripe
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, in the middle of the big green grassy plain, lived a very happy little zebra named Zeke. Zeke had the most wonderful coat in the whole wide world. It was covered in bright, bold black and white stripes from the tip of his little fuzzy ears all the way down to his bouncy tail. Every morning, Zeke would wake up, stretch his long legs, and trot over to the watering hole to say hello to his animal friends. One sunny Tuesday, Zeke woke up and felt a funny tickle on his left leg. He looked down and gasped. Oh no! One of his lovely black stripes was missing! Zeke blinked his big brown eyes. Where could it have gone? He shook his tail. He did a little wiggle. But the stripe was definitely not there. Zeke decided he needed to go on a grand adventure to find his lost stripe. First, he trotted over to tall giraffe munching on acacia leaves. 'Excuse me, tall giraffe, have you seen a stray black stripe?' asked Zeke politely. Giraffe chewed thoughtfully and said, 'No, little Zeke, I have not seen any stripes today. My spots are all right here on my neck.' Zeke thanked giraffe and kept on walking. Next, he bounced past a family of fluffy pink flamingos standing on one leg in the shallow water. 'Hello, flamingos, have you spotted a missing stripe?' asked Zeke. The flamingos flapped their wings and shook their heads. 'Pink is our favorite color, but we have no black stripes here!' Zeke began to feel just a little bit sad. Without all of his stripes, did he still look like a proper zebra? Just then, a clever little monkey swung down from a tree branch holding a funny, gooey yellow object. 'Zeke! Look what I found over by the banana tree! It was stuck to a branch!' shouted the monkey. Zeke looked closer. It wasn't a stripe at all! It was just a sticky patch of dark mud that had brushed against his leg when he was playing hide-and-seek earlier that morning. Zeke laughed out loud, a big happy sound that echoed across the plain. He trotted down to the cool river and splashed some water on his leg until the mud washed right away. All of his real stripes were safe and sound, shining brightly in the warm sun. Zeke did a happy little dance, gave his monkey friend a big hug, and scampered off to play the rest of the day away, feeling completely wonderful just the way he was.

stories.title: Zack's Big Red Boots
stories.text: Deep in the rolling green hills of the savanna, there lived a cheerful little zebra named Zack. Zack loved to run, jump, and skip through the tall grass with all of his animal friends. But more than anything in the world, Zack loved bright, shiny things. One bright morning, Zack woke up and found a very special package waiting right outside his sleeping spot. He used his nose to gently nudge the brown paper open. Inside were four of the most amazing things he had ever seen. They were boots! Not just any boots, mind you, but big, bright, cherry-red rain boots that squeaked when you pressed them. Zack's eyes went wide with pure joy. He quickly slipped his little hooves inside them. Squeak, squeak, squeak went the boots! Zack was so excited that he immediately trotted over to show his best friend, Leo the lion cub. 'Look at my new boots, Leo!' shouted Zack, doing a little tap-dance in the mud. Leo giggled and roared with delight. 'They are so red and shiny, Zack!' Zack felt like the fanciest zebra in the entire kingdom. He decided to take his new boots for a long walk. He trotted down the path, making a happy squeaking sound with every single step. Squeak, squeak, squeak. The cheeky monkeys pointed and giggled from the trees. The wise old tortoise smiled warmly as Zack trotted by. But soon, the bright blue sky began to fill with big, puffy gray clouds. Uh-oh! A little rain shower was coming. Big, cool raindrops began to fall splish, splash, splish right onto the dry earth. The other animals scampered away to find dry shelter under the leafy acacia trees. But not Zack! Zack loved the rain. And guess what? His boots were rain boots! Zack stood right in the middle of the path and began to stomp in the puddles. Splish, splash, squish, squelch! Water flew everywhere, glittering like tiny diamonds in the gray light. The squeaking of his red boots mixed with the happy splashing sounds. Zack laughed and spun around in circles, his black and white stripes looking extra sleek against the wet green grass. Soon, the rain stopped just as quickly as it had started, and a glorious rainbow stretched across the sky in brilliant colors of red, orange, yellow, green, and blue. Zack looked up at the rainbow and then down at his bright red boots. He decided that rainy days were officially the absolute best days of all. He trotted all the way home, his boots still squeaking a happy tune, ready for whatever fun adventure tomorrow might bring.

stories.title: Zoe's Bedtime Pajamas
stories.text: The sun was beginning to sink low behind the distant hills, painting the sky in soft shades of purple, pink, and orange. Down on the savanna, it was almost time for bed. Little Zoe the zebra let out a big, wide yawn. *Yaaawn!* Her eyelids felt as heavy as big round stones. But before she could go to sleep, Zoe had a very important job to do. It was time to put on her favorite bedtime pajamas! Zoe trotted over to her cozy sleeping spot where her mama had left a neat little folded pile of sleepwear. Zoe picked up the pajamas in her mouth and shook them out. They were bright yellow pajamas covered in funny little blue sleeping stars and purple moons. There was just one tiny problem. Zoe was a zebra, which meant she already had a coat full of black and white stripes. Would the star pajamas fit over her stripes? Zoe decided to find out. She lifted her right front leg and wiggled it into the pajama sleeve. Then she lifted her left front leg and did the same. With a little hop and a wiggle, she pulled the top all the way up. Next came the pants. Zoe stepped her back hooves into the soft fabric and pulled them up high, wiggling her little tail right out of the special tail hole in the back. She looked down at herself. She had black stripes, white stripes, yellow fabric, blue stars, and purple moons all at the very same time! Zoe giggled, thinking she looked like a walking, talking rainbow of bedtime fun. She trotted over to the tall mirror made of a shiny puddle of water to take a look. 'Mama, look at me! I am a star-zebra!' she called out happily. Her mama walked over, nuzzled Zoe's soft cheek, and smiled warmly. 'You look absolutely wonderful, my sweet little star-zebra,' said Mama softly. Zoe felt so warm and cozy inside her silly pajamas. Mama tucked Zoe in under a big blanket made of soft moss and whispered a gentle bedtime story. Zoe closed her big brown eyes, listening to the quiet night sounds of the savanna. The crickets chirped a soft lullaby, the gentle wind rustled the leaves, and Zoe drifted off into the most wonderful dreamland, hugging her favorite stuffed toy tight, completely ready for a peaceful night of sweet slumber.

stories.title: Zeke the Zebra Loses a Stripe
stories.text: Once upon a sunny Tuesday in the big green grassland, there lived a very happy little zebra named Zeke. Zeke had the most wonderful coat of black and white stripes in the whole wide world. His stripes were shiny, neat, and lined up just like a brand new box of crayons. Every morning, Zeke would wake up, stretch his long legs, and trot over to the watering hole to splash with his animal friends. One bright morning, Zeke woke up and felt something a little bit funny on his tummy. He looked down, and oh, oh, oh! One of his black stripes was missing! Zeke blinked his big brown eyes. He blinked again. Where, oh where, could his stripe have gone? He looked under his pillow. No stripe. He looked inside his favorite muddy puddle. No stripe there either. Zeke let out a little zebra sigh. 'How can I play hide and seek without all of my stripes?' he wondered aloud. Just then, his best friend Bella the butterfly fluttered down. 'Good morning, Zeke! Why the long face?' asked Bella. Zeke spun around in a circle. 'Look, Bella! One of my favorite black stripes has gone missing from my tummy! Have you seen it?' Bella buzzed closely and looked at Zeke's white tummy. 'Hmm, let us go look for it together!' So, off they went on a big stripe-hunting adventure. First, they trotted over to tall, tickly tall grass. Zeke wiggled this way and that. 'Swish, swish, swish,' went the grass against his tummy. 'Does it tickle your missing stripe, Zeke?' asked Bella. 'No, just my tummy!' giggled Zeke. Next, they visited Sammy the squirrel, who was busy gathering crunchy acorns by a big acacia tree. 'Hello, Sammy! Have you seen a stray black stripe rolling around?' asked Zeke politely. Sammy nibbled an acorn and shook his furry head. 'I have only seen round nuts, Zeke, no stripes today!' Zeke and Bella thanked Sammy and kept on searching. The sun was getting higher and warmer in the sky. Zeke stopped by a cool, shiny river to take a little sip of water. He leaned his head down, looking at his reflection in the water. He blinked, and suddenly, he gasped with joy! Right there on his tummy, reflecting in the sparkling water, was his missing stripe! It had not gone anywhere at all. It was just covered in a little bit of silly white dust from the puffy dandelions he had rolled in earlier that morning. Zeke laughed a big, happy zebra laugh, kicking his hooves in the air. 'I am all stripes again, Bella!' Bella clapped her tiny wings. Zeke felt so happy and relieved. From that day on, Zeke always remembered to wash his tummy before bedtime, keeping all of his wonderful stripes safe, shiny, and ready for tomorrow's grand adventures in the lovely green grassland.

stories.title: Zuzu's Zippy Zebra Zoom
stories.text: Down by the edge of the sparkling blue river, there lived a little baby zebra named Zuzu. Zuzu was small, spunky, and full of bouncing energy. While the big zebras liked to spend their afternoons dozing quietly in the warm, golden sun, Zuzu liked to zoom! He loved to zip, zap, and zoom all over the grassy plains. Today was a very special day because Zuzu had decided he was going to learn how to run faster than the wind itself. He stretched his front legs way out, and then he stretched his back legs. He shook his fluffy little mane and gave a loud, happy snort. 'Ready, set, go!' Zuzu shouted to himself, and off he dashed. He zoomed past a family of lazy hippos taking a muddy bath. 'Splash, splosh, splish!' went the mud as Zuzu zipped right by them. The baby hippo blinked sleepily and opened its mouth wide in a big yawn. Zuzu didn't stop. He couldn't stop! He was moving too fast. Next, he zoomed past a tall giraffe munching on yummy green leaves at the very top of a tall acacia tree. The giraffe looked down and blinked his long eyelashes. 'Slow down, little Zuzu, or you might turn into a blur of black and white!' called out the friendly giraffe with a gentle chuckle. Zuzu giggled, his little hooves going tap-tap-tap against the soft dirt path. He zipped around a big round boulder and zoomed up a tiny grassy hill. When he reached the very top of the hill, he stopped and looked out at the huge, beautiful world below him. He could see the whole river winding like a shiny silver ribbon. He could see his mama way down below, munching on sweet clover and watching him with loving eyes. Zuzu felt so proud of his zippy little legs. He took a deep breath of the fresh, sweet air and decided it was time to trot all the way back down to his mama for a big, cozy cuddle. He pranced down the hill, making funny little clicking noises with his tongue. When he reached his mama, she leaned down and gave his soft cheek a warm, loving nuzzle. 'Did you have a fun time zooming today, my little Zuzu?' she asked softly. Zuzu nodded his head up and down eagerly. 'Oh yes, Mama! I zoomed past the hippos, I zipped past the giraffe, and now I am ready for the biggest nap in the whole wide world!' With a contented sigh, Zuzu snuggled right up against his mama's warm side, closing his eyes as the gentle breeze sang a sweet lullaby across the grassy plains, dreaming of all the wonderful places he would zoom to tomorrow.

stories.title: Zack's Zany Zebra Pajamas
stories.text: The sun was beginning to sink low behind the big green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink, purple, and sleepy orange. It was almost bedtime in the animal kingdom, but little Zack the zebra was not quite ready to sleep. Not yet! Zack was having far too much fun playing with his favorite dress-up box. Today, Zack had found the most wonderful treasure at the bottom of the box: a pair of bright yellow pajamas with glowing green polka dots. Now, most zebras wear black and white stripes all day and all night. But Zack was a very creative little zebra. He looked at his reflection in the big puddle mirror and smiled a big, toothy grin. 'I think yellow polka dots will make me run extra fast in my dreams tonight!' he whispered to himself. With a wiggle and a waggle, Zack slipped his four little hooves into the cozy pajama pants and pulled the shirt right over his head. The pajamas were wonderfully soft and felt like a warm hug. Zack trotted over to his cozy bed made of sweet-smelling hay to show his mama. 'Look at me, Mama! I am a polka-dot zebra!' Mama zebra looked up from her resting spot and blinked in surprise. She giggled a warm, gentle giggle that sounded like chimes in the wind. 'Oh, my goodness, Zack! Those are the zaniest, most magnificent pajamas I have ever seen in my life!' she said, nuzzling his fuzzy nose. Zack did a happy little spin, showing off his bright yellow spots to the evening breeze. Just then, his friends came by to say goodnight. Pip the parrot landed softly on a nearby branch and squawked happily, 'Polka dots look fabulous on a zebra, Zack!' Even the sleepy little frogs sitting by the pond gave a polite little croak of approval. Zack felt so cozy and happy in his silly yellow pajamas. He climbed into his comfy hay bed and pulled his soft blanket right up to his chin. Mama zebra tucked him in tight and softly hummed a sweet, soothing nighttime song. Zack closed his heavy eyes, thinking about all the colorful adventures he would have in his dreams while wearing his wonderful polka-dot pajamas. The stars twinkled high above in the deep blue sky, watching over the little polka-dot zebra as he drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep, ready for tomorrow's brand new day of fun and games.

stories.title: Zeke's Stripey Day
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in the middle of the big, bright green grass, lived a little zebra named Zeke. Zeke had black stripes and white stripes all over his body. They went tick-tock, tick-tock, all the way from his nose to his fluffy tail! Every morning, the sun would peek over the hill and say, 'Good morning, Zeke!' And Zeke would say, 'Good morning, sun!' Today was a very special day because Zeke was going on a big adventure to find the sparkling watering hole.

Zeke trotted through the tall grass. Tap, tap, tap went his little hooves. 'Hello, tall giraffe!' said Zeke. The giraffe bent down and whispered, 'Have a wonderful day, little zebra.' Zeke kept on going. Soon, he met his best friend, a little monkey named Milo. Milo swung from a tree branch and giggled, 'Can I come too, Zeke?' 'Yes, let's go together!' cheered Zeke.

As they walked, they played a fun game. They counted all the buzzing bees. One, two, three bees! Then they hopped over a little brown log. Hop, hop, hooray! The sun felt warm and cozy on their backs. Zeke loved his stripes because they made him look just like a moving rainbow, but in black and white.

At last, they heard a happy sound. Splash, splash, splash! It was the sparkling watering hole. Other animal babies were already there playing in the cool, clear water. A little hippo splashed mud, and a baby elephant trumpeted a happy hello. 'We made it!' shouted Zeke and Milo.

Zeke dipped his hooves into the cool water. It felt so good! He drank a long, refreshing sip of water. 'Ahhh,' sighed Zeke happily. He looked at his reflection in the water and smiled at his wonderful stripes. Playing with his friends and exploring the big world was his absolute favorite thing to do. As the sun began to go down, painting the sky pink and orange, Zeke gave a little yawn. It was time to head home for bedtime stories and sweet dreams. He trotted all the way back, snuggled close to his mama, and whispered, 'Today was the best day ever.' And his mama kissed his fuzzy forehead and said, 'Sleep tight, my little striped star.' The end.

stories.title: Zelda's Lost Tooth
stories.text:
Deep in the sunny savanna, a little zebra named Zelda was munching on some crunchy green leaves. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Suddenly, Zelda stopped. She felt something funny right in the front of her mouth. Her tooth was wobbling! It went wiggle, wiggle, waggle. Zelda touched it with her soft nose. 'MAMA!' called Zelda, her eyes big and wide. 'My tooth is dancing in my mouth!'

Mama Zebra trotted right over and gave Zelda a gentle nuzzle. 'That means you are growing up big and strong, my sweet girl,' said Mama with a warm smile. Zelda giggled. She wiggled her tooth with her tongue. Wiggle, wiggle, pop! The tooth came right out. Zelda caught it in her hooves. It was tiny, white, and shiny like a little pearl.

'Look what I have!' Zelda showed her friend, a fluffy white rabbit who lived nearby. The rabbit hopped up and down and clapped his paws. 'That is a magic tooth!' the rabbit whispered. 'Tonight, the nighttime fairy will come and leave a special surprise for you.' Zelda’s ears perked up. A surprise? She loved surprises more than anything in the whole wide world.

Zelda decided to make a special bed for her tooth. She found a soft green leaf, laid her shiny tooth right in the middle, and placed it gently on a flat rock near her sleeping spot. Then, she practiced brushing her remaining teeth. Brush, brush, brush, up and down, side to side, until her teeth sparkled in the moonlight.

As the stars twinkled like tiny diamonds in the dark sky, Zelda tucked herself into the cozy grass. She closed her big brown eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of sweet carrots and green meadows. In the middle of the night, a gentle breeze rustled the trees, and something wonderful happened. When the sun woke up the next morning, Zelda jumped up and ran to the rock.

Her tooth was gone! But in its place was a sweet little shiny pebble and a tiny flower. Zelda squealed with delight and did a happy little dance. Her hooves went tap-tap-tap on the ground. She ran to show Mama, holding her treasure high. It was a wonderful morning, and Zelda felt like the happiest zebra in the whole world. The end.

stories.title: Zack's Big Red Balloon
stories.text:
Once upon a time, a little zebra named Zack received a magnificent gift from the wise old lion. It was a big, round, shiny red balloon! Zack’s eyes grew as wide as saucers. 'Oh, thank you!' he cheered. The balloon bobbed up and down in the air. Whoosh, whoosh, went the wind. Zack held the string very tightly in his hoof so it wouldn't float away into the blue sky.

Zack walked through the grassy field to show his friends his brand-new red balloon. First, he trotted past the friendly tortoises. Slow and steady, the tortoises poked their heads out. 'Look at my balloon!' said Zack proudly. The tortoises blinked their slow eyes and smiled. Next, Zack met a little monkey swinging from the trees. 'Can I touch it?' asked the monkey. Zack shared the string very carefully, and the monkey patted the red rubber gently.

Suddenly, a strong gust of wind blew across the savanna. Whoosh! The wind tugged at the string. 'Hold on tight!' whispered Zack to himself. But oh no! The string slipped right out of his hoof. Up, up, up went the big red balloon. It looked like a floating cherry in the sky. Zack felt a tear well up in his eye. He thought he was going to lose his special balloon forever.

Just then, his tall friend the giraffe stretched his long neck way up high into the clouds. With a gentle puff of breath, the giraffe blew the balloon back down toward the ground. Swoosh! The balloon drifted right back into Zack’s waiting hooves. Zack hugged the balloon tight and laughed with pure joy. 'Thank you, my tall friend!' shouted Zack happily.

Zack learned that holding onto things with care is very important, but having good friends is even better. He tied the string securely around his sturdy hoof and continued his walk across the sunny plains. The red balloon bobbed happily behind him, casting a cheerful red glow on his black and white stripes. When the sun began to set, painting the clouds pink and purple, Zack trotted home with a full heart. He hugged his mama, tied his balloon safely to a twig near his bed, and fell asleep with a big smile on his face. The end.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra in the sun,
Tell me how your day has begun.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the happy zebra go.

Running through the grassy plain,
Dancing in the summer rain.
Stomping hooves upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Stripey legs and shiny mane,
Playing games out in the rain.
Swish your tail and give a shout,
That is what you're all about.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleepy in this grassy town.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Wait for morning, start to play.

rhymes.title: Zack Goes Zoom
rhymes.text:
Zack the zebra likes to run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Zipping fast across the floor,
Always looking to explore.

Gallop, gallop, hear him beat,
With his tiny little feet.
Jumping high up in the air,
Showing off his fuzzy hair.

Stop and munch some yummy grass,
Watch the fluffy birdies pass.
Time to rest his little head,
Climbing into cozy bed.

Sleepy zebra, time for rest,
Snuggled warmly in his nest.
Dreaming of a sunny sky,
As the quiet night goes by.

rhymes.title: Counting Zebras
rhymes.text:
One sweet zebra by the tree,
Looking up at you and me.
Two cute zebras side by side,
Taking such a happy ride.

Three quick zebras start to play,
Chasing shadows all the day.
Four nice zebras in a row,
Watch them gallop as they go.

Five white stripes and five are black,
Carrying hugs upon their back.
Now they stop to take a drink,
Standing by the river's brink.

Counting zebras is so fun,
Till the day is nearly done.
Say goodnight and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Little Zebra
rhymes.text:
Little zebra in the grass,
Watch her as she trots right past.
Black and white upon her back,
Walking down the sandy track.
She has ears that wiggle round,
Listening to every sound.
Kicking up her tiny feet,
Looking very nice and neat.
Time to stop and time to play,
Chasing butterflies away.
 Munching on a leafy tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy little bed.

rhymes.title: Stripey Hooves
rhymes.text:
Stripey zebra, big and tall,
Standing by the garden wall.
Coat of black and coat of white,
Shining brightly in the light.
Prancing through the morning dew,
Looking for a friend or two.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Watch her zig and watch her zag.
Can you match her happy stride?
Running fast and running wide.
Stopping by the river deep,
Where the happy fishes leap.
Now the stars are in the sky,
Singing out a lullaby.
Zebra, zebra, go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Zebra's Day
rhymes.text:
Morning comes with yellow sun,
Zebra days have just begun.
Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Dancing in the morning light.
Jumping high and running fast,
Having lots of fun at last.
Eating clover on the hill,
Standing very, very still.
Time to rest your weary feet,
Tucked in grass so soft and sweet.
Moon is shining up above,
Filled with sleepy peace and love.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Dreaming of another day.
Goodnight stripes and happy dreams,
Sleeping by the gentle streams.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Kicking up your little hooves,
Showing all your happy moves.

Walking by the river side,
Where the shiny fishes hide.
Eating grass that grows so tall,
You are not too big or small.

Stripes upon your back and face,
Running in a gentle race.
Underneath the golden sun,
Having lots of daytime fun.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for zebra to fall asleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your grassy meadow bed.

rhymes.title: Little Zebra's Day
rhymes.text:
See the zebra standing near,
Without any doubt or fear.
He has stripes from head to toe,
Watch him happily trotting go.

Jumping over sticks and stones,
Listening to the animal tones.
Birds are singing in the tree,
Happy as a bird can be.

Now he takes a little drink,
At the waterhole, just think.
Splash the water with his hoof,
Underneath the sky's blue roof.

Evening time is drawing near,
Time to cuddle up, my dear.
Mama keeps him safe and warm,
Safe from any windy storm.

rhymes.title: Zeke's Big Adventure
rhymes.text:
Little Zeke is feeling bold,
In the grassy plains of gold.
Running fast across the land,
With his friends on either hand.

Monkey swings from tree to tree,
Calling out so loud and free.
Elephant is walking slow,
Watch the trunk go to and fro.

Zeke the zebra joins the game,
Every day is not the same.
Hide and seek is so much fun,
Playing underneath the sun.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying everybody goodnight.
Zebra dreams of sunny skies,
Closing up his sleepy eyes.

rhymes.title: Zippy the Zebra
rhymes.text:
Zippy is a zebra bold,
With stripes of black and white.
He gallops on the grassy plain,
And dances in the light.
He has a fluffy little tail,
And ears that twitch and play.
He runs around the watering hole,
To start his happy day.
He eats the yummy greenest grass,
Beneath the sunny sky.
He watches all the fluffy clouds,
Go sailing slowly by.
When nighttime comes and stars awake,
He goes to sleep so deep.
His mama sings a lullaby,
To help him fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Black and White
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Trotting in the morning light.
Click-clack goes your little hoof,
Underneath the jungle roof.
Shake your mane and swish your tail,
Running down the grassy trail.
Say hello to monkey friends,
Where the winding river bends.
Jump up high and spin around,
Landing softly on the ground.
Now it is a resting time,
Listening to the turtle's chime.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.
Dream of running far and wide,
With your mommy by your side.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
See the zebra in the sun,
Having lots of outdoor fun.
Counting stripes upon his back,
Counting every white and black.
One, two, three, and four and five,
Glad to be so much alive.
He can trot and he can prance,
Doing such a happy dance.
Giraffe is looking from above,
Sending down a gentle love.
Lion roars a friendly sound,
As they play upon the ground.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Zebra rests his sleepy head,
In his cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the golden light.
Stamping hooves upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Running till the morning light.
Chewing grass so fresh and green,
Best little zebra ever seen.

Jump up high and kick your feet,
Your little hooves go beat, beat, beat.
Hide behind the grassy tree,
Come and play a game with me.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in the grassy town.
Close your eyes and dream all night,
Little zebra, black and white.

rhymes.title: Zippy's Trot
rhymes.text:
Zippy trot across the floor,
Looking for a magic door.
Black and white from tail to nose,
Tickle, tickle, little toes.

Gallop fast and gallop slow,
Watch the little zebra go.
Eating carrots from the plate,
Standing by the garden gate.

Flapping ears of softest grey,
Ready for a brand new day.
Run across the meadow wide,
With your mommy by your side.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little birds are flying high.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy little bed.

rhymes.title: Zuzu's Savannah
rhymes.text:
Zuzu runs across the land,
Running on the golden sand.
Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Dancing in the morning light.

Elephant is splashing near,
Making water crystal clear.
Monkey swings from tree to tree,
Happy as a bird can be.

Zuzu jumps and kicks her heels,
Oh, what happy joy she feels!
Nibble, nibble on the hay,
Having fun the livelong day.

Moon is glowing up above,
Filled with sleepy peace and love.
Close your eyes and dream of play,
Until the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Stomping hooves upon the grass,
Watch the happy zebra pass.

Stripey tail and fuzzy mane,
Dancing on the open plain.
Eating leaves and chewing hay,
Having fun the livelong day.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

Dreaming of a sunny sky,
As the gentle breezes fly.

rhymes.title: Zelda's Jump
rhymes.text:
Zelda zebra wants to play,
Jumping high throughout the day.
Over rocks and hills she goes,
Where the water softly flows.

Happy zebra, strong and fast,
Blowing bubbles in the blast.
Prancing through the muddy pool,
Water splashes, fresh and cool.

Now she shakes her coat so dry,
Waving to a butterfly.
Trot along and skip a beat,
Happy hooves upon her feet.

Time to snuggle in her bed,
Resting now her sleepy head.

rhymes.title: Counting Zebras
rhymes.text:
One sweet zebra, standing tall,
Near the big and leafy wall.
Two sweet zebras, side by side,
Ready for a bumpy ride.

Three sweet zebras shake a mane,
Trotting down the grassy lane.
Four sweet zebras start to run,
Playing underneath the sun.

Five sweet zebras stop to drink,
By the river's muddy brink.
All the zebras count to ten,
Then they start to play again.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Whispering a sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra in the grass,
Watch him as he trot and pass.
Black and white from head to toe,
See him zigzag as he go.

Swish your tail and stomp your feet,
Zebra days are such a treat.
Running fast across the plain,
Dancing in the golden rain.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

Dream of stripes of black and white,
Sleeping safely through the night.

rhymes.title: Zippy the Zebra
rhymes.text:
Zippy has a fuzzy mane,
Running through the sunny plain.
Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Shining in the morning light.

Jump up high and give a cheer,
Glad that little Zippy's here.
Prancing softly in the breeze,
All around the tall green trees.

Time to stop and time to play,
Eating clover all the day.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for Zippy fast asleep.

Goodnight stripes and goodnight feet,
Zebra dreams are soft and sweet.

rhymes.title: Zebra's Song
rhymes.text:
Hooray, hooray for zebra stripes,
Eating juicy forest types.
Trotting gaily down the track,
With a rider on his back? No!

Just a little happy friend,
Playing till the very end.
Shake your tail and stamp the ground,
Make a happy trotting sound.

Sun is warm and sky is blue,
Zebra loves to play with you.
Now the shadows start to grow,
Moving very, very slow.

Time to snuggle, time to rest,
Sleeping with the ones you love best.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Stripey legs go tap, tap, tap,
Time to take a little nap.

Eating grass so fresh and green,
Prettiest you've ever seen.
Running fast across the plain,
Wiggle, wiggle, fuzzy mane.

Hide and seek behind a tree,
Can the big lion see me?
No, my stripes blend in so well,
Stories to my friends I tell.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to go right into bed.

rhymes.title: Zuzu's Hooves
rhymes.text:
Click, clack, go my hooves,
Watch the little zebra move.
Jumping high into the air,
With a swishy, swishy hair.

Touch your nose and touch your toes,
Follow where the river goes.
Splash the water, make it bright,
Playing in the golden light.

Say hello to monkey friends,
Where the jungle pathway ends.
Eat a leaf and chew it slow,
Now it's time to gently go.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Little birds are flying high.
Zebra sleeps the night away,
Waiting for another day.

rhymes.title: Zippy the Zebra
rhymes.text:
Zippy has two funny ears,
Waving at the little dears.
Trotting down the sandy lane,
Smiling in the pouring rain.

Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the happy zebra go.
Gallop fast and gallop slow,
Where he stops, we do not know.

Jump up high and give a cheer,
Glad to have our playtime here.
Shake your tail and stamp your feet,
Life is always nice and sweet.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving us a cozy light.
Cuddle close and sleep so tight,
Sweet dreams, zebra, through the night.

rhymes.title: Stripes So Bright
rhymes.text:
Little zebra in the sun,
Running races, having fun.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the happy zebra go!

Kicking up his little feet,
Trotting down the dusty street.
Stopping by a shady tree,
As happy as a bird is free.

Chewing on the grassy green,
Finest zebra ever seen.
Blinking with his big brown eyes,
Underneath the sunny skies.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy zebra bed.

rhymes.title: Zebra's Morning Walk
rhymes.text:
Morning comes and birds awake,
Walking by the shiny lake.
Zebra takes a little prance,
Doing quite a happy dance.

Stripey legs go clip and clop,
Little zebra will not stop.
Greeting every bug and bee,
Prancing by a tall palm tree.

Nodding to a friendly frog,
Leaping over a brown log.
Having fun along the way,
On this lovely, sunny day.

Now the walk is at an end,
Time to rest, my stripey friend.
Snuggle down and close your eyes,
Underneath the evening skies.

rhymes.title: Count the Stripes
rhymes.text:
Can you count the stripes so neat,
On the zebra's tiny feet?
One and two and three and four,
Let us try and count some more.

Black stripes shining in the light,
White stripes looking clean and bright.
Swishing is his little tail,
Walking down the grassy trail.

Eating leaves of yummy green,
Best jumper you've ever seen.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Now it's time for him to go.

Say goodnight to zebra dear,
Knowing that your bed is near.
Close your eyes and sleep so tight,
Until the morning brings the light.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Trotting fast and trotting slow,
Watch the happy zebra go.
Stripes upon his fuzzy back,
Painted white and painted black.
Kicking up his little feet,
Looking very proud and neat.
In the grass so green and tall,
Zebra dances, watch him fall!
Giggling as he rolls around,
Right upon the grassy ground.
Now it is time to rest his head,
In his cozy grassy bed.
Close your eyes and sleep all night,
Little zebra, black and white.

rhymes.title: Counting Zebras
rhymes.text:
One little zebra eating some hay,
Chasing the butterflies all through the day.
Two little zebras splash in the stream,
Floating along like a wonderful dream.
Three little zebras run very fast,
Hoping that playtime will always last.
Four little zebras jump up so high,
Reaching their hooves to the beautiful sky.
Five little zebras dance in a ring,
Hear all the happy little animals sing.
Six little zebras lie down to snooze,
Nothing to worry and nothing to lose.
Seven little zebras wake up and play,
Welcoming in a brand new day.
Eight little zebras are sleepy and slow,
Time for the little ones home to go.

rhymes.title: Zoe's Zippy Hooves
rhymes.text:
Zoe the zebra loves to run,
Playing underneath the sun.
Zippy, zappy, fast and free,
Running to the old oak tree.
She has stripes from head to toe,
Watch the playful zebra go!
Stopping for a drink of water,
Like a happy little daughter.
Shaking her soft furry mane,
Waiting for the gentle rain.
Jumping over sticks and stones,
Making happy animal tones.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Dreaming of the morning light,
Zebra sleeping through the night.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra in the sun,
Running fast and having fun.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the happy zebra go!

Stomping feet upon the ground,
Looking all around, around.
Eating grass that grows so sweet,
Treats are such a yummy treat!

Wiggling ears and swishing tail,
Sailing like a happy whale.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Climbing in your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Zoe's Morning Walk
rhymes.text:
Zoe zebra starts her day,
Trotting down the grassy way.
Morning dew upon the grass,
Watch her as she wanders past.

Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Looking shiny, looking bright.
Saying hello to the birds,
Singing sweet and happy words.

Jumping over little rocks,
Wearing fancy zebra socks.
Now she stops to take a drink,
By the river cool and pink.

Happy zebra, strong and tall,
Best animal of them all.
Now she gives a friendly neigh,
Have a super happy day!

rhymes.title: Time for Sleep, Little Zebra
rhymes.text:
Stars are shining in the sky,
Little clouds are floating by.
Zebra baby, time for rest,
Sleeping in your cozy nest.

Black stripes matching white stripes too,
Mommy zebra smiles at you.
Rubbing noses, warm and sweet,
Tired little hooves and feet.

Moon is glowing round and bright,
Guiding you throughout the night.
Dreaming of the grassy plain,
Dancing in the gentle rain.

Sleep until the morning light,
Everything is calm and bright.
Whisper soft and whisper low,
Sweet dreams, little zebra, go.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Kicking up your happy feet,
Trotting down the grassy street.

Lines of black and lines of white,
Shining softly in the night.
Can you count them? One, two, three,
Dancing by the apple tree.

Mane is soft and tail is long,
Singing out a happy song.
Now it is time to go to sleep,
Counting stars instead of sheep.

Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.
Dreaming of the meadow wide,
With your mama by your side.

rhymes.title: Zooming Zebra
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, running fast,
Look at you go zooming past!
Through the grass and past the tree,
Wild and happy, wild and free.

Stripey legs go tap, tap, tap,
Never stopping for a nap.
Stopping at the water hole,
Drinking from a little bowl.

Monkey swings up in the air,
Watching zebra standing there.
Birds are singing in the sky,
As the clouds go floating by.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that you've had me yet.
Zebra rests upon the ground,
While the stars spin all around.

rhymes.title: Tickly Stripes
rhymes.text:
Zebra has some tickly stripes,
Eating leaves and juicy pipes.
Shake your tail and shake your head,
Time to jump right out of bed.

Black and white from nose to toe,
Everywhere you like to go.
Jump up high and land below,
Watch the sleepy flowers grow.

Give a neigh and give a shout,
That is what the day's about!
Run around the grassy ring,
Hear the happy birdies sing.

Sun is sinking in the west,
Time for little ones to rest.
Snuggle close and close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: Little Zebra Trotting By
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Trotting in the morning light.
Swish your tail and shake your mane,
Dancing in the grassy lane.

Clip-clop goes your little hoof,
Underneath the sunny roof.
Eating leaves that taste so sweet,
You are such a lovely treat.

Now the sun is going low,
Time for little zebras to go.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars watch from the deep.

Dream of running wild and free,
By the great big shady tree.
Sleep until the morning sun,
Ready for a brand new run.

rhymes.title: Stripes and Spots
rhymes.text:
Zebra has some stripes so neat,
Walking down the dusty street.
Giraffe has spots of yellow-brown,
Tallest creature in the town.

Lion has a golden mane,
Roaring softly in the rain.
Elephant has ears so wide,
And a trunk to show with pride.

All the animals like to play,
In the grassy fields all day.
Jumping up and running round,
Making such a happy sound.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying everybody goodnight.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Safe inside your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Zoe's Counting Stripes
rhymes.text:
Can you count the stripes you see,
On the little zebra's knee?
One black stripe and one white too,
Walking right in front of you.

Two black stripes upon her back,
Standing in a tidy track.
Three black stripes upon her head,
Ready for her cozy bed.

Four black stripes upon her nose,
Tickling her little toes.
Five black stripes upon her tail,
Swishing like a little sail.

Now the counting time is done,
Played we have beneath the sun.
Zebra rests her sleepy head,
Tucked into her grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Zebra, Zebra
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, black and white,
You look lovely in the light.
Walking down the grassy lane,
With a fluffy, bouncing mane.

Stomping hooves go tap, tap, tap,
Ready for a little nap.
In the golden afternoon,
Sleeping 'neath the rising moon.

Running fast across the grass,
Watch the stripes go past, past, past!
Stopping by the water hole,
Happy body, happy soul.

Blinking with your big, dark eyes,
Underneath the big blue skies.
Zebra, zebra, time to rest,
In your home you love the best.

rhymes.title: Tickly Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, tell me true,
What is it you like to do?
Do you like to run and play,
All throughout the sunny day?

Black and white from nose to tail,
Walking down the muddy trail.
Eating leaves that taste so sweet,
Moving quickly on your feet.

Can I count your stripes today?
One, two, three, and then away!
Hide and seek in tall green grass,
Watching sunny moments pass.

Shake your tail and stamp your hoof,
Underneath the open roof.
Little zebra, you are sweet,
From your head down to your feet.

rhymes.title: The Savanna Dance
rhymes.text:
Hear the zebra dance and prance,
In a happy little trance.
Swishing tails and bobbing heads,
Jumping right out of their beds.

Stripes of black and stripes of white,
Shining brightly in the light.
Trotting to the river side,
With a smile so warm and wide.

Splash the water, hear it sound,
As your hooves hit on the ground.
Spinning round and round again,
With your very special friend.

Stars are coming out above,
Filled with happiness and love.
Time to sleep and close your eyes,
Zebra under starry skies.

rhymes.title: Zebra Stripes
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Show me all your stripes today,
While we skip and jump and play.

Running fast across the grass,
Watch the little zebra pass.
Stomping hooves go beat, beat, beat,
Down the grassy jungle street.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that we've had us yet.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy, quiet bed.

Good night, zebra, sleep so tight,
Dream of stars and morning light.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Little zebra, you're the best.

rhymes.title: Count the Stripes
rhymes.text:
One little stripe, two little stripes,
Eating sweet and juicy pipes.
Three little stripes, four little stripes,
Jumping over garden swipes.

Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the friendly zebra go.
Swishing tail and floppy ears,
Chasing all away your fears.

Trotting through the muddy lane,
Singing in the gentle rain.
Splish and splash and puddle fun,
Underneath the golden sun.

Now the day is almost done,
We have had so much good fun.
Zebra hugs and kisses sweet,
Rest your tired, happy feet.

rhymes.title: Zebra's Song
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, in the zoo,
I am saying hello to you!
With your coat of black and white,
You are such a lovely sight.

Gallop here and gallop there,
Kicking up your heels with care.
Eating leaves from tall green trees,
Dancing in the gentle breeze.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Giving off a silver light.
Time to tuck your nose in tight,
Saying to the world good night.

Sleep until the morning sun,
Brings another day of fun.
Zebra dreams are soft and deep,
Time for little you to sleep.

rhymes.title: Little Zebra
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Running in the morning light.
Prancing through the grassy plain,
With a fluffy, fuzzy mane.

Kicking up your little feet,
Looking very nice and neat.
Stopping by the water hole,
Happy little zebra soul.

Eating clover on the ground,
Looking all around, around.
Time to rest your weary head,
Trotting to your cozy bed.

Now the stars begin to glow,
Swishing tail is moving slow.
Sleepy zebra, time for sleep,
Counting little fluffy sheep.

rhymes.title: Stripes on Parade
rhymes.text:
Zebra, zebra, what do you see?
Stripes as pretty as can be.
Walking down the dusty track,
White and black and white and black.

Can you jump and can you play?
In the sunshine all the day.
Blinking with your big brown eyes,
Underneath the big blue skies.

Shake your tail and stamp your hoof,
Like a galloping little hoof.
Running fast across the land,
In the lovely grassy sand.

Now the day is almost done,
Saying goodbye to the sun.
Zebra, zebra, go to sleep,
While the little crickets peep.

rhymes.title: Zebra Zoom
rhymes.text:
Zoom, zoom, zebra zoom,
Running right across the room.
Well, not really in a room,
On the grassland starts to bloom.

Black stripes, white stripes, shining bright,
Dancing in the golden light.
Greeting every animal friend,
From the start and to the end.

Giraffe says hello from above,
Sending lots of gentle love.
Hippos splash and make a sound,
As you gallop all around.

Time to stop and time to rest,
Sleeping with your very best.
Goodnight zebra, sleep so tight,
Dreaming till the morning light.

rhymes.title: Stripes So Bright
rhymes.text:
Little zebra, black and white,
Trotting in the morning light.
With your hooves going tap, tap, tap,
Time to wake up from your nap.

Stripes upon your fuzzy head,
Time to jump right out of bed.
Running through the grassy plain,
Dancing in the golden rain.

Nose is soft and ears are long,
Singing out a happy song.
Jump up high and spin around,
Make a happy stomping sound.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy grassy bed.

rhymes.title: Count the Stripes
rhymes.text:
Can you count the stripes you see,
Underneath the big green tree?
One stripe black and one stripe white,
Shining in the morning light.

Zebra walks across the grass,
Watch him as he gently pass.
Wiggle ears and twitch a tail,
Blowing in a gentle gale.

Time to find a drink to play,
Splashing water all the day.
Cool and wet upon your toes,
Water dripping on your nose.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little zebra goes to sleep.
Dreaming of the grassy lane,
Till the sun wakes up again.

rhymes.title: Zebra Friend
rhymes.text:
Hello, zebra, how are you?
Tell me what you like to do.
Do you like to run and play,
Out here on a sunny day?

Black and white from tail to nose,
Tickles go between your toes.
Laughing as you skip along,
Humming out a happy song.

Birds are flying in the sky,
Watching as you gallop by.
Trees are green and skies are blue,
All the world is waiting too.

Time for hugs and time for rest,
Sleeping with the ones you best.
Close your eyes and dream so sweet,
Rest your little trotting feet.

stories.title: Pip's Hungry Tummy
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a big green bamboo forest, there lived a little panda named Pip. Pip had round black ears, a soft white tummy, and a very big appetite. Every morning, the sun would peek through the tall green stalks, saying good morning to the sleepy animals. Pip would stretch his paws way up high, give a big toddler yawn, and rub his fuzzy tummy. Rumble, rumble, went Pip's tummy. It was time for breakfast! Pip waddled over to his favorite bamboo bush. He sat right down on his furry bottom and reached out his paw. Snap! Pip broke off a nice, crunchy bamboo shoot. He gave it a big munch. Crunchy, crunchy, crunch! Bamboo was his absolute favorite food in the whole wide world. But wait! Pip wanted something sweet. He looked up and saw a shiny red apple hanging from a low tree branch. Pip stood up on his two short hind legs and stretched. He stretched and stretched, but the apple was just a little bit too high. Oh no! Pip let out a soft little squeak. Just then, his wise old mommy panda walked over. Mommy panda had a gentle smile and a warm, fuzzy hug. She plucked the bright red apple right off the branch and handed it to little Pip. Pip’s eyes lit up with joy. He gave his mommy a big hug and took a juicy bite. Munch, munch, munch! The sweet apple juice made his whiskers tickle. After breakfast, Pip felt so full and happy. He rolled down a grassy green hill, going round and round like a fuzzy ball. Whee! Pip giggled as he landed in a soft patch of yellow daisies. He tickled his toes and looked up at the fluffy white clouds floating in the blue sky. One cloud looked just like a panda! Pip waved his paw at the sky. As the warm afternoon sun began to dip low behind the green trees, Pip felt his heavy eyelids close. Playing all day is hard work for a little panda. Mommy panda scooped him up into her cozy arms and carried him back to their soft bed of leaves. Pip curled up tight, closed his eyes, and dreamed about crunchy bamboo and sweet red apples. Good night, little Pip.

stories.title: Pip's Lost Red Ball
stories.text: In the heart of the bamboo forest, the sun was shining brightly. Little panda Pip had a brand new toy. It was a bright red rubber ball that bounced up and down. Boing, boing, boing went the ball! Pip loved his ball more than anything. He would chase it through the tall green grass, laughing with glee. Today, Pip was playing with his best friend, a little brown monkey named Coco. Coco swung from branch to branch, chattering happily. Pip rolled the ball to Coco. Coco caught it with his little hands and tossed it right back. They played catch for a long, long time. Then, Pip rolled the ball a little too hard. Whoosh! The red ball rolled away from the grassy clearing and straight into a patch of big, leafy ferns. Pip stopped running. He looked around. Where did the ball go? Pip crawled on his hands and knees, pushing the big green leaves aside. He looked under a heavy log. No ball there! He looked inside a hollow wooden stump. No ball there either! Pip began to feel a little sad. His bottom lip quivered, and a tiny tear formed in his eye. Oh, where was his favorite toy? Coco swung down from a tree and patted Pip gently on the back. Do not worry, little friend! Coco chattered. We will find it together. Teamwork makes the dream work! So, Pip and Coco searched again. They looked behind a big grey rock. And guess what they saw? A little flash of bright red! Pip let out a happy cheer. Yay! He scurried over and scooped the bouncy ball up into his fuzzy paws. He hugged the ball tight against his chest. Pip was so happy to have his toy back. He looked at Coco and gave him a warm, friendly hug. Thank you for helping me, Coco, Pip said softly. From that day on, Pip and Coco played together every single afternoon, always making sure to keep their favorite red ball safe. They played catch until the stars came out, shining brightly in the night sky.

stories.title: Pip Goes Splash
stories.text: It was a very hot summer day in the bamboo forest. The air was warm, and the sun felt like a big golden hug in the sky. Little panda Pip was feeling very hot indeed. He panted softly, sticking out his little pink tongue. Phew! It is so warm today, Pip whispered to himself. He wanted to cool down. He waddled through the green trees until he heard a lovely sound. Splash, splash, gurgle, gurgle! Pip followed the happy sound all the way to a clear, sparkling blue stream. The cool water flowed gently over smooth round stones. Wow, look at that! Pip gasped with delight. He walked right to the edge of the water and dipped one fuzzy toe in. Ooh! It is nice and cool! Pip giggled. He dipped his other toe in, then his whole foot. The cool water felt amazing on his hot little paws. Pip decided to be brave. He took a big step right into the shallow water. Splash! Water droplets flew everywhere, sparkling like diamonds in the sun. Pip sat right down in the middle of the stream. Splash, splash, go my paws! he sang out loud. He splashed the water with his hands, making big waves that tickled his tummy. A little yellow duckling swam over to say hello. Quack, quack! said the duckling, dipping its head under the water and popping back up. Can I play too? Pip clapped his hands together. Yes, yes! Let us play together! Pip and the friendly duckling splashed each other gently, giggling and quacking all afternoon. The water washed away all the heat, leaving Pip feeling fresh, clean, and happy. Soon, his tummy began to rumble again, signaling that it was time for a yummy bamboo snack. Pip climbed out of the stream, shaking the sparkling water drops off his thick black and white fur like a fluffy puppy. Shake, shake, shake! He dried off in the warm, cozy sunshine. What a wonderful day for a little panda. Pip smiled a big, toothy smile and trotted happily back home to his mommy.

stories.title: Pao's Big Bamboo Search
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green bamboo forest, lived a little panda named Pao. Pao had soft black and white fur, and he loved to play hide and seek with his butterfly friends. One sunny morning, Pao woke up with a very big rumble in his tummy. Time for breakfast! Pao waddled over to his favorite green bush, but oh no! The bush was completely empty. 'Where is my yummy bamboo?' Pao whispered with a sad little frown. He decided to go on a big adventure to find some more. First, Pao tiptoed past a sleepy brown bear taking a nap under a shady tree. 'Shh,' whispered Pao, making sure not to wake him. Next, Pao hopped over a bubbling blue brook that went splash, splash, splash against his fuzzy toes. It felt so tickly and cool! He giggled out loud and shook his little round bottom. Then, Pao climbed up a gentle grassy hill, using his paws to pull himself right to the top. From up high, Pao looked all around. He saw red ladybugs, yellow flowers, and fluffy white clouds. But wait! What was that green thing moving in the distance? Pao squinted his big dark eyes. It was tall, green bamboo swaying gently in the warm breeze! Pao let out a happy cheer, 'Yay!' He rolled down the grassy hill, going round and round like a fuzzy black and white ball. Wheee! When he reached the bottom, he tumbled right into a patch of the freshest, crunchiest bamboo you ever did see. Crunch, crunch, munch, went Pao as he happily ate his treat. His tummy was full, and he felt so cozy. Pao curled up in the soft grass, closed his sleepy eyes, and took a wonderful morning nap.

stories.title: Pao's Rainy Day Splash
stories.text: Drip, drop, plip, plop! Big raindrops began to fall from the grey sky down into the bamboo forest. Little panda Pao poked his fuzzy head out of his cozy treehouse. He looked up at the sky and blinked. The rain was making puddles everywhere. Instead of staying inside, Pao smiled a big toothy smile. He loved rainy days! Pao put on his favorite red rain boots. They made a funny squish-squash sound with every single step he took. Squish, squash, squish, squash! He grabbed his bright yellow polka-dot umbrella and stepped right out into the wet world. The forest looked so shiny and clean washed by the sparkling water. Pao waddled down the winding dirt path looking for fun. He stopped right in front of a big, beautiful puddle of water. 'Time to splash!' shouted Pao happily. He jumped up high into the air and landed with a huge SPLASH! Water droplets flew up like little diamonds in the air. Pao giggled and stomped his feet again. Splash, splash, splash! A little frog hopped out from behind a green leaf and said, 'Ribbit, ribbit!' Pao waved his paw at his new slimy friend. 'Hello, little froggy!' he called out cheerfully. They played together in the rain, hopping and jumping until the dark clouds rolled away. Suddenly, the warm golden sun peeked out from behind the clouds. Look high up in the sky! A magnificent rainbow stretched from one side of the forest to the other, glowing with red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple colors. Pao pointed his paw up high and gasped. It was so pretty! His fur dried off in the warm sunshine, and Pao felt very happy. He walked home slowly, humming a sweet little song about rainbows and puddles.

stories.title: Pao's Sleepy Starry Night
stories.text: The sun was starting to go down behind the tall green mountains, painting the sky in soft shades of pink and orange. Little panda Pao knew it was almost time for bed, but he wanted to play one last game. He chased a glowing firefly as it zipped through the twilight. 'Wait for me, little light!' giggled Pao, stumbling playfully over his own furry paws. The firefly landed gently on a sleepy flower and went to sleep. Pao yawned a very big yawn. His eyelids felt as heavy as big stones. Mama Panda walked over and gave him a warm, gentle hug. 'Time to get ready for sleep, my sweet little bear,' she whispered softly. Pao nodded sleepily and rubbed his eyes with his paws. First, he put on his striped pajamas with little moon prints all over them. Then, Mama Panda wrapped him in his favorite soft blanket that felt like a warm cloud. They sat together on a cozy mossy rock and looked up at the night sky. One by one, twinkling stars popped out like tiny silver diamonds shining in the dark velvet blue. Pao pointed his paw at the big bright moon. 'Good night, moon,' he whispered softly. Mama Panda sang a sweet lullaby about bamboo leaves blowing in the night breeze. Pao rested his head on Mama's soft lap, feeling safe and cozy. His breathing grew slow and steady. In, out, in, out. Pao drifted off to dreamland, dreaming of rolling down grassy hills and munching on crunchy green bamboo. Mama Panda smiled down at her little sleeping angel and whispered, 'Sweet dreams, my precious Pao.' The forest grew quiet, and all the animals went to sleep under the gentle glowing moonlight.

stories.title: Pip the Panda's Morning Munch
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a big green bamboo forest, there lived a little panda named Pip. Pip had round black ears, a soft white tummy, and two big black patches around his eyes that made him look like he was always ready for a silly game. Good morning, sleepy sun! Pip gave a big, wide yawn and rubbed his fuzzy eyes. His tummy let out a loud rumble. Grumble, grumble, went Pip's tummy. It was time for breakfast! Pip loved breakfast more than anything in the whole wide world. What was for breakfast? Crunchy, munchy bamboo shoots! Pip waddled out of his cozy tree hollow, using his short little legs to step softly on the mossy ground. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went Pip. He came to a tall, swaying bamboo stalk. It was bright green and smelled fresh and sweet. Pip reached out his fuzzy paw and tugged. Snap! A fresh bamboo shoot broke right off. Oh boy, oh boy! Pip sat down on his plump bottom, held the crunchy treat in his paws, and took a big, noisy bite. Crunch, crunch, crunch! Bamboo was so delicious. It tasted like sunshine and rain and sweet green grass. But wait! Pip saw another bamboo stalk even higher up. How could he reach it? Pip stood up tall on his back toes and stretched his arms way, way up. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Almost there! With a little hop, Pip grabbed the leaf and giggled. He tumbled over onto his back, rolling right into a patch of soft clover. Roll, roll, roll! Pip laughed a happy panda laugh. Being a panda was the most fun thing ever. After eating his fill, Pip wiped his green-stained mouth with the back of his furry paw. He patted his nice, full tummy. It was round like a little basketball. Now that his tummy was happy, Pip was ready to play. He saw a fluttering yellow butterfly dancing through the bamboo leaves. Wait for me, little butterfly! Pip scampered after it, his black and white coat flashing in the dappled morning sunlight. He chased the butterfly left. He chased the butterfly right. He tried to give it a gentle, friendly hug, but the butterfly fluttered up high into the blue sky. Bye-bye, butterfly! Pip smiled. The morning was so bright, the bamboo was so tasty, and the forest was so cozy. Pip curled up right there in the soft green grass for a little morning snooze, dreaming of even more crunchy bamboo treats waiting for him when he woke up.

stories.title: Pan-Pan's Red Balloon
stories.text: High up in the misty bamboo mountains lived a cheerful little panda named Pan-Pan. Pan-Pan loved shiny things, bright colors, and most of all, making new friends. Today, something very special happened. A gentle breeze carried a big, bright red balloon all the way from the village down below, floating right into the bamboo forest. Whew! The wind blew it gently, and it landed right in front of Pan-Pan's favorite resting rock. Pan-Pan blinked his big dark eyes. What was this marvelous floating wonder? It was bright red, round like a ball, and danced in the air on the end of a long, thin string. Pop, pop, no, it didn't pop! It just bobbed up and down. Boing, boing, went the red balloon. Pan-Pan reached out a cautious paw and gently poked it. Boop! The balloon bounced away with a happy little wiggle. Pan-Pan giggled. That was fun! He gently grabbed the string with his soft paws. Now he had a wonderful new toy to play with. Pan-Pan decided to take his red balloon on a grand adventure through the forest. He waddled down the winding dirt path, holding tight to the string. Come along, red balloon! First, they visited Benny the brown bear, who was busy trying to catch buzzing bees. Pan-Pan showed Benny the balloon. Benny smiled and waved a big furry paw at the pretty red color. Next, they visited Sammy the squirrel, who was jumping from branch to branch. Sammy stopped and chattered happily at the sight of the floating red sphere. Red balloon, red balloon, dancing in the sky! Pan-Pan felt so proud to have such a wonderful friend for the day. But suddenly, a strong gust of wind blew through the trees. Whoosh! The wind tugged at the string. Oh no! The balloon pulled upward, stretching the string in Pan-Pan's paws. Up, up, up went the red balloon, higher than the bamboo stalks, higher than the tall pine trees, and up toward the fluffy white clouds. Pan-Pan looked up with wide eyes. He let out a little gasp. The balloon was floating away into the big blue sky! Pan-Pan watched it go, feeling a little bit sad, but then he smiled a big, toothy panda smile. He knew the balloon was off to see the rest of the world, just like he had seen the forest today. Pan-Pan waved his paw. Goodbye, red balloon! Have a wonderful trip! With a light heart, Pan-Pan turned back toward home, ready for a cozy nap in his bamboo bed, knowing today had been the best day ever.

stories.title: Panda's Puddle Splash
stories.text: Pitter-patter, pitter-patter! Raindrops began to fall in the bamboo forest. Big drops, little drops, splashing on the green leaves and making sweet music all around.
