Pip waddled along his favorite winding path until he heard a fun, bubbly sound. 'Splash, splash, gurgle, gurgle!' Pip tilted his head. What could that be? He hurried his fuzzy little paws and peeked through the bushes. It was a sparkling, cool blue stream of water, twisting and turning right through the forest! Pip loved water. A big smile spread across his cute black-and-white face. He waddled right down to the muddy edge of the stream and dipped one soft, black toe into the water. 'Ooh, it is so nice and cool!' whispered Pip happily. He stepped all the way in, letting the refreshing water tickle his furry ankles. Pip splashed his right paw. Splash! Water flew everywhere in shiny drops. Then he splashed his left paw. Splash, splash! A little green frog hopped away, croaking with delight. Pip wanted to play even more. He sat right down in the shallow part of the stream and gave a mighty kick with both back legs. Water sprayed up into the air like a fountain of diamonds in the sunlight. Pip laughed out loud, clapping his hands together. 'Yay! Fun water!' he cheered. A little wooden stick floated by on the gentle current. Pip reached out, grabbed the stick, and watched it sail past him like a tiny boat. He splashed and played until he was completely soaked from his fuzzy ears down to his short little tail. When he was all done playing, Pip climbed out onto the warm, grassy bank. The warm sun hugged him like a cozy blanket, drying his thick fur. Pip gave a big, happy panda shake, sent a shower of sparkling drops flying into the air, and waddled home with a huge smile on his face, excited to tell his friends all about his wonderful splashy adventure.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and white,
You are such a lovely sight.
Black and fuzzy on your ears,
You chase away all my fears.
Sitting in the bamboo tree,
Eating leaves for lunch and tea.
Munching, crunching, all day long,
Singing out a happy song.
Now the sun is going down,
 Sleeping softly on the ground.
Time to close your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
When you wake to laugh and play.
Hugs and kisses, rest your head,
In your cozy little bed.

rhymes.title: Panda Roll and Tumble
rhymes.text:
Round and round the panda goes,
Touching his black button nose.
Rolling down the grassy hill,
Now he stops and stays quite still.
Up he pops with muddy feet,
Looking round for something sweet.
Finds a shoot of bamboo green,
Best little snack you've ever seen.
Chewing slowly, lick his paws,
Showing off his little claws.
Stretching arms out wide and tall,
Catching then a bouncy ball.
Now he gives a toddler yawn,
Greeting birds upon the lawn.
Time to snuggle, time to rest,
With his mommy, he is best.

rhymes.title: Panda Paws and Play
rhymes.text:
Pat-a-cake, pat-a-cake, panda bear,
Throw your paws up in the air!
Stomp your feet upon the ground,
Turn around and spin right round.
Splash the water in the stream,
Like a happy, waking dream.
Chase a butterfly of blue,
Saying cheerful little moos---
Wait, no moos, just panda squeaks!
Rubbing paws against your cheeks.
Now you sit and take a rest,
Mommy's hugs are simply best.
Soft and gentle, warm and tight,
Sleeping safely through the night.
Morning comes with yellow sun,
Ready for another run.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Eating bamboo day and night.
Sitting softly on the ground,
Looking all around, around.

Big round tummy, furry feet,
Chewing up a tasty treat.
Climbing up a tall green tree,
Happy as a bear can be.

Waving paws to say hello,
Watch the fuzzy panda go.
Rolling in the morning dew,
Little panda, I love you.

Now it is a sleepy night,
Stars are shining big and bright.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Panda Roll and Play
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, panda bear, do you see,
All the leaves upon the tree?
Soft and fluffy, round and sweet,
With four little furry feet.

Roll around upon the grass,
Watch the sunny day go past.
Munching on a green bamboo,
Eating tasty snacks for two.

Jump up high and give a cheer,
Glad to have you sitting near.
Pat your tummy, pat your head,
Time to crawl into your bed.

Dreaming of a sunny day,
While the gentle breezes play.
Sleep until the morning light,
Panda bear, oh sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Panda's Forest Friends
rhymes.text:
In the forest green and tall,
Lives a panda, round and small.
Playing games throughout the day,
Chasing butterflies away.

Jumping in a puddle splash,
Making such a funny dash.
Saying hello to a bee,
Sitting underneath a tree.

Eating green leaves every noon,
Hoping for a balloon.
Waving bye to sunny skies,
Rubbing sleepy little eyes.

Mama hugs him nice and tight,
Kissing him a sweet goodnight.
Stars are shining up above,
Filled with cozy peace and love.

rhymes.title: Panda, Panda, Turn Around
rhymes.text:
Panda, panda, touch the ground.
Panda, panda, spin around.
Panda, panda, reach up high.
Panda, panda, wave goodbye.

Panda, panda, blink your eyes.
Panda, panda, look so wise.
Panda, panda, tap your knee.
Panda, panda, smile at me.

Panda, panda, stomp your feet.
Panda, panda, find a seat.
Panda, panda, chew your leaves.
Panda, panda, feel the breeze.

Panda, panda, time to rest.
Panda, panda, sleep is best.

rhymes.title: The Little Black and White Bear
rhymes.text:
See the panda in the tree,
 Munching green leaves happily.
 Black and white and very sweet,
 Sitting down to rest his feet.

 Big round ears and fuzzy nose,
 Wiggling his tiny toes.
 Rolling down the mossy hill,
 Now he stops and stays quite still.

 Paws are muddy, tummy's round,
 Sleeping softly on the ground.
 Dream of bamboo in the sun,
 Playing games and having fun.

 When you wake up, little bear,
 Munching snacks is waiting there.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Snack for Fuzzy Jack
rhymes.text:
Fuzzy Jack has black and white fur,
 Hear the happy baby purr.
 He is hungry, yes indeed,
 Bamboo shoots are all he need.

 Reach up high and pull a stem,
 Snap them off and eat all them.
 Crunch and munch and chew so loud,
 Making mama panda proud.

 Wipe your mouth with fuzzy paw,
 Best little panda you ever saw.
 Now let's play a game of tag,
 Running with a happy wag.

 Stars are peeking in the sky,
 Little panda, now bye-bye.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Walking in the morning light.
Softly steps upon the ground,
Making not a single sound.

Munching on a bamboo treat,
Sitting on his furry seat.
Chewing green leaves, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Eating such a yummy lunch.

Rolling down the grassy hill,
Stopping with a little thrill.
Rubbing his round fuzzy tummy,
Saying that the food was yummy.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for panda fast asleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
In your cozy little bed.

rhymes.title: Panda's Red Balloon
rhymes.text:
Panda holds a bright balloon,
Floating upward to the moon.
Red and shiny, round and grand,
Held inside his furry hand.

Wind begins to softly blow,
Making little panda go.
Up above the trees so tall,
He is having such a ball.

Monkey swings from tree to tree,
Waving happy and so free.
Birdies sing a cheerful song,
As the panda floats along.

Now the balloon begins to sink,
Quicker than a rapid blink.
Panda lands upon the floor,
Ready for a new adventure more.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Soft and sleepy panda bear,
Curled up in your cozy chair.
Nighttime shadows start to fall,
Peaceful quiet over all.

Weary paws are resting now,
Underneath the bamboo bough.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
And the games you love to play.

Moonlight shines a golden light,
Keeping every baby bright.
Stars are twinkling in the sky,
Singing sweet sweet lullaby.

Sleep until the morning sun,
Brings another day of fun.
Hug your blanket nice and tight,
Sleepy panda, long goodnight.

rhymes.title: Panda's Round Tummy
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and round,
Sitting happy on the ground.
Chewing bamboo, crunch and chew,
Eating snacks of crispy green and blue.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the funny panda go.
Climbing up a fuzzy tree,
Looking very bright and free.
Waving paws up in the air,
Showing off his cozy hair.
Rounder than a giant ball,
He is not so very tall.
Patting now his tummy sweet,
Such a yummy, lovely treat.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
Crawling to his leafy bed.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Forest Dance
rhymes.text:
In the forest tall and green,
Panda is the dancing queen.
Swinging left and swinging right,
Playing till the fading light.
Stomping feet upon the floor,
Always asking for some more.
Spinning round a fuzzy top,
Never wanting it to stop.
Clapping paws and shouting yay,
Having such a joyful day.
Chasing butterflies so fast,
Hope this lovely game can last.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Panda falls right fast asleep.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till the coming of the day.

rhymes.title: Goodnight Little Panda
rhymes.text:
Moon is shining in the sky,
Little clouds are floating by.
Panda wears a sleepy frown,
Laying his soft body down.
Hugging tight his favorite toy,
Such a happy little boy.
Whispering a quiet tune,
Underneath the silver moon.
Stars are blinking bright and clear,
Morning time will soon be here.
Blanket made of leaves so green,
Warmest bed you've ever seen.
Close your eyes and breathe so deep,
Panda falls into a sleep.
Dreaming of a bamboo tree,
As happy as a panda can be.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda soft and sweet,
Walking on two furry feet.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the happy panda go.

Sitting in a bamboo tree,
As happy as a bug can be.
Munching on a crispy shoot,
Eating up the yummy fruit.

Time to play and time to run,
Basking in the golden sun.
Rolling down the grassy hill,
Now the little bear is still.

Time to close your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Cuddle up and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Round and Round the Bamboo
rhymes.text:
Round and round the bamboo tree,
Little panda wants to play.
Wiggling ears for you and me,
Chasing butterflies away.

Pit-a-pat go furry paws,
Climbing up the forest wall.
Happy bear with gentle claws,
Careful so he does not fall.

Splash into the water stream,
Making bubbles big and round.
Living out a lovely dream,
Not a single scary sound.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Turn the sleepy daytime down.
Whisper to the stars goodnight,
Best little panda in town.

rhymes.title: Panda's Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Hush a bye, little bear,
Wind is blowing through your hair.
Softly purr and softly sigh,
As the clouds go floating by.

Tummy full of bamboo treats,
Softest moss beneath your feet.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
In your cozy forest bed.

Stars are blinking in the blue,
Watching every dream of you.
Black ears drooping, eyes so low,
Watch the sleepy panda slow.

Morning light will come around,
Birds will make a happy sound.
Until then, sleep tight and deep,
Little panda fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and white,
Black and furry, what a sight!
Waddling softly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.
Sitting in the bamboo tree,
As happy as a bear can be.
Munching leaves that taste so sweet,
Eating is his favorite treat.
Rubbing now his fuzzy tummy,
Finding shoots that look so yummy.
Time to play and time to run,
Basking in the golden sun.
Climbing up and sliding down,
Happiest bear in all the town.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Little panda goes to sleep.

rhymes.title: Black and White
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, touch your nose,
Panda bear, wiggle your toes.
Panda bear, clap your hands,
Dancing in the forest lands.
Black ears and a fuzzy head,
Time to crawl into your bed.
Soft white tummy, round and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Chewing on a green bamboo,
Always smiling back at you.
Roll around upon the floor,
Do you want to play some more?
Up you go into the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying to the world, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Snack
rhymes.text:
Little bear in black and white,
Wakes up with the morning light.
Hungry tummy starts to growl,
Making such a funny howl.
Reaches for a leafy treat,
Something very fresh to eat.
Munch and crunch and nibble too,
Eating lots of green bamboo.
Wipe your face and lick your paw,
Cutest panda you ever saw.
Time to take a little nap,
Resting on your furry lap.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
While the breezes softly play.
Close your eyes and slumber deep,
Little panda falls asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Sleeping softly through the night.
Wakes up with a happy yawn,
Playing softly on the lawn.

Chewing on a bamboo treat,
Sitting on his fuzzy seat.
Crunching leaves so crisp and green,
Freshest snack you've ever seen.

Rolling down the mossy hill,
Now he's sitting very still.
Chasing butterflies that fly,
Reaching up into the sky.

Waving paws to say goodbye,
Underneath the gentle sky.
Curled up in a cozy bed,
Sweet dreams in his furry head.

rhymes.title: Panda's Round Belly
rhymes.text:
Round and soft, a fuzzy ball,
Panda plays both big and tall.
Has two patches on his face,
Running all around the place.

Climbing up a cherry tree,
Looking happy as can be.
Eating shoots of yummy green,
Bestest bear you've ever seen.

Splashing in a muddy puddle,
Needing lots of love and cuddle.
Shaking water from his fur,
Like a little purring purr.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly on the ground.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Time to snuggle in your bed.

rhymes.title: Buzzy Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Buzzy panda wakes from sleep,
Hear his tummy start to beep.
Time to find a morning snack,
With a patch upon his back.

Waddling through the forest green,
Cutest bear you've ever seen.
Finding bamboo sweet and tall,
Happy panda, short and small.

Munching happily away,
Having fun throughout the day.
Now he gives a sleepy sigh,
Watching clouds go floating by.

Time to rest his tired feet,
In his cozy, leafy seat.
Closing up his sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Sleeping softly through the night.
Wakes up when the sun is high,
Looking at the morning sky.

Time to munch on bamboo green,
Chewing leaves fit for a queen.
Crunch and munch and bite it fast,
Make the yummy breakfast last.

Little panda takes a stroll,
Looking for a muddy bowl.
Splish and splash and wiggle toes,
Water drips right on his nose.

Now the sun is going down,
Weariest panda in the town.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
Rest your sleepy, furry head.

rhymes.title: Roll Around
rhymes.text:
Round and round the panda rolls,
Playing with his wooden bowls.
Tumble down the grassy hill,
Mom says, 'Panda, please keep still!'

But the panda wants to play,
Running, jumping all the day.
Climbing up a bamboo tree,
Looking down at you and me.

Black patches around his eyes,
Looking at the butterflies.
Catching leaves that flutter down,
Happiest bear in the town.

Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Sleeping in his cozy nest.
Hug your blanket, squeeze it tight,
Panda baby, sleep all night.

rhymes.title: Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Panda paws go patter-pat,
What do you think he is at?
Looking for a yummy snack,
Walking on the beaten track.

Finds a shoot of green bamboo,
Chews it up and swallows too.
Rubbing now his little tummy,
Tasting something sweet and yummy.

See him wave his furry hand,
Bestest bear in all the land.
Sitting on his fuzzy bottom,
Counting spots, oh yes, he's got 'em.

Stars are shining in the deep,
Panda yawning, going to sleep.
Dreaming of a sunny day,
When he wakes to go and play.

rhymes.title: Panda's Round Tummy
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and sweet,
Finds some bamboo grass to eat.
Chubby paws and furry toes,
Black spots sitting on his nose.

He rolls over in the sun,
Having lots of fuzzy fun.
Chewing on a tender shoot,
Eating every single fruit.

Round and happy little bear,
Sitting in his cozy chair.
Patting now his hungry tummy,
Saying bamboo tastes so yummy.

Time to rest his sleepy head,
Crumbling down upon his bed.

rhymes.title: Climb Up High
rhymes.text:
Little panda starts to climb,
Up the tree trunk every time.
Reaching for a leafy view,
In the sky of brightest blue.

Scratch and scurry, up he goes,
Balancing upon his toes.
Mama watches from above,
Sending down a look of love.

Now he rests upon a branch,
Watching monkeys do a dance.
Swinging softly in the breeze,
Happy high up in the trees.

Time to take a little nap,
Resting in his mama's lap.

rhymes.title: Splish Splash Panda
rhymes.text:
Panda walks into the rain,
Feeling happy, feeling sane.
Puddles waiting on the ground,
While he looks all around.

Splish and splash go furry feet,
Down upon the forest street.
Water drops upon his head,
Time to leave his cozy bed.

Big white cheeks and fuzzy ears,
Washing all away his fears.
Making bubbles in the mud,
Like a little furry bud.

Now he's wet from top to toe,
Time for little bears to go.

rhymes.title: Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and round,
Sitting happy on the ground.
Black and white from head to toe,
Watch the little panda go.
Climbing up a bamboo tree,
As happy as a bear can be.
Chewing on a tender shoot,
Eating every crunchy fruit.
Washing furry little paws,
Snuggling up with fuzzy claws.
Yawning in the afternoon,
Waiting for the silver moon.
Stars are shining in the sky,
Lullaby and lullaby.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Round and Round
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, panda bear, turn around,
Panda bear, panda bear, touch the ground.
Panda bear, panda bear, show your shoes,
Panda bear, panda bear, shake the blues.
Eating bamboo, crisp and green,
Freshest leaves you've ever seen.
Rolling down the grassy hill,
Now the little bear is still.
Waving bye to butterfly,
As it flutters up so high.
Hugging trunk of ancient tree,
Safe and cozy as can be.
Night is coming, soft and deep,
Panda bear is fast asleep.
Sweetest dreams until the light,
Panda bear, sleep tight, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Crunch
rhymes.text:
Munch, munch, munch goes the panda bear,
Chewing bamboo everywhere.
Black furry ears and a button nose,
Wiggling all his little toes.
Rolling over, what fun play,
Playing games throughout the day.
Sitting in the morning sun,
Having lots of fuzzy fun.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Making little pandas sleep.
Wrap him in a cozy sheet,
Resting every tired feet.
Moonlight shines upon his bed,
Resting softly on his head.
Dreaming of a leafy tree,
As happy as a bear can be.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, soft and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Black and white and round and small,
You are loved the most of all.

Sitting in the bamboo tree,
Eating green leaves happily.
Munching, crunching, day and night,
Fur so clean and black and white.

When the sun begins to set,
And the grass is cool and wet,
Time to sleep and rest your head,
In your cozy little bed.

Close your eyes and slumber deep,
Little panda falls asleep.
Dreaming of the trees so tall,
Good night, little panda, small.

rhymes.title: Panda Roll and Play
rhymes.text:
Round and round the panda rolls,
Playing games with little bowls.
Waddling down the grassy hill,
Stopping with a sudden thrill.

Panda paws pat on the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Wiggling ears so soft and black,
Scratching on his furry back.

Climbing up a bamboo stalk,
Taking time for such a walk.
Looking at the sky so blue,
Panda wants to play with you.

Jumping down into the hay,
Having fun the livelong day.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Panda softly goes to sleep.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Snack Time
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, oh panda bear,
Eating bamboo everywhere.
Green and crunchy, sweet and tall,
Favorite snack of great and small.

Holding shoots in fuzzy paws,
Following the forest laws.
Chewing slowly, bite by bite,
In the lovely morning light.

Rubbing now a tummy round,
Sitting happy on the ground.
Time to play a little game,
Calling out the panda's name.

Chasing butterflies around,
Not a single worried sound.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Panda says a sweet good night.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, round and sweet,
Walking on your furry feet.
Climbing up a bamboo tree,
Looking down to wave at me.

Black and white and very neat,
You are such a lovely treat.
Eating leaves that taste so green,
Cutest bear I've ever seen.

Time to rest your sleepy head,
Crawling in your cozy bed.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Until the coming of the day.

Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with peace and panda love.
Sleepy cub, now do not weep,
Time to fall asleep, sleep, sleep.

rhymes.title: Roll Around
rhymes.text:
Panda roll and panda slide,
With no worries deep inside.
Sitting in the grassy mound,
Tumbling softly to the ground.

Chewing on a tender shoot,
Eating every tasty fruit.
Black patches around each eye,
Watching clouds go floating by.

Pat your tummy, nice and round,
Make a happy tummy sound.
Shake your fuzzy little tail,
Sailing like a happy whale.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Panda dreams of bamboo trees,
Swaying in the gentle breeze.

rhymes.title: Misty Mountain Bear
rhymes.text:
Up upon the mountain high,
Where the fluffy white clouds fly,
Lives a happy panda bear,
With black patches everywhere.

Paws are soft and steps are slow,
Walking in the sparkling snow,
Or upon the summer green,
Calmest creature ever seen.

Catching raindrops on his nose,
Wiggling all his furry toes.
Making funny growly sounds,
As he happily goes rounds.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying to the world goodnight.
Little panda rests his head,
Snug inside his leafy bed.

rhymes.title: Panda's Round Belly
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Chews on bamboo day and night.
Sitting on the grassy floor,
Always wants a little more.

Climbing up the tall green tree,
Looking happy as can be.
 Munching shoots of crispy green,
Happiest bear you've ever seen.

Rubbing now his fuzzy head,
Waddling to his leafy bed.
Closing up his sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

Dreaming of a sunny day,
Chasing little bugs away.
Goodnight, panda, sleep till morn,
 Sweetest bear that has been born.

rhymes.title: Roll, Panda, Roll
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, panda bear, turning around,
Rolling right down to the soft grassy ground.
Two fuzzy ears and a button black nose,
Wiggling fingers and ticklish toes.

Eating sweet bamboo so yummy and bright,
Chewing it up with a loud crunchy bite.
Pinching a leaf with his little black paw,
Best little panda you ever saw.

Walking along by the sparkling blue stream,
Floating away in a afternoon dream.
Chasing a butterfly into the sky,
Watching the beautiful colors float by.

Now it is time for a sweet little nap,
Sleeping right here in my cozy lap.
Closing his eyes till the morning light,
Sleep well, little panda, sleep tight, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: The Bamboo Dance
rhymes.text:
Up in the forest the bamboo grows high,
Panda looks up at the big blue sky.
Swishing his tail and tapping his feet,
Finding a yummy and wonderful treat.

Crunching the stalks with a happy big grin,
Letting the afternoon games begin.
Rolling over and over again,
Down in the valley and up in the glen.

Patting his belly that's round as a ball,
Answering softly when sleepy birds call.
Curling up tight in a furry embrace,
Finding a quiet and comforting place.

Stars are awake and the moon is so bright,
Hugging his blankie through all of the night.
Soft little snores from the black and white bear,
Magic and wonder are everywhere.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Sleeping softly through the night.
Wakes up with a happy cheer,
Glad to see the morning here.
Reaches for a bamboo treat,
Chewing slowly, oh so sweet.
Crunches up the leaves all day,
Then it is time for some play.
Rolls around upon the grass,
Watching butterflies drift past.
Climbs a tree up high and tall,
Careful so he does not fall.
Sits and rests his fuzzy head,
Crawls into his cozy bed.
Closes up his sleepy eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Round and Round the Bamboo Tree
rhymes.text:
Round and round the bamboo tree,
Little panda smiles at me.
Clapping paws and tapping toes,
Wiggling cute and shiny nose.
Climbing up the woody stem,
Finding greenest leaves for them.
Munching on a yummy snack,
Scratching at an itchy back.
Sliding down the muddy hill,
Sitting very, very still.
Splashing in the river blue,
Saying cheerful words to you.
Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that he has had yet.
Yawning big with sleepy sighs,
Time to close those tired eyes.

rhymes.title: Panda Bear, Panda Bear
rhymes.text:
Panda bear, panda bear, fluffy and round,
Sitting right down on the soft grassy ground.
Eating sweet shoots in the bright morning sun,
Jumping right up for a moment of fun.
Black furry ears and a sweet little face,
Waddling along at a very slow pace.
Hugging a tree with your arms open wide,
Sliding right down to the river side.
Drinking the water so cool and so clear,
Knowing that nighttime is now drawing near.
Crawling back up to your nest in the tree,
As quiet and cozy as sleepy can be.
Snuggling close to your furry brown bed,
Resting your weary and sleepy round head.
Dreaming of bamboo that stretches up high,
While twinkling stars light the beautiful sky.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Wakes up in the morning light.
Soft fur like a fuzzy bear,
Sitting in his bamboo chair.

Munching green leaves, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Eating bamboo for his lunch.
Round tummy, big and sweet,
Falling down to go to sleep.

Blinking sleepy, heavy eyes,
Underneath the quiet skies.
Curled up in a cozy heap,
Panda falls right fast asleep.

Dreaming of the forest trees,
Rocking gently in the breeze.
Goodnight, panda, time to rest,
Sleeping in your fuzzy nest.

rhymes.title: Roll, Panda, Roll
rhymes.text:
See the panda roll around,
Tumblin' softly on the ground.
Black patches on his face,
Running in a happy race.

Climbing up a mossy tree,
As happy as a bear can be.
Reaching for a leafy snack,
Scratching on his furry back.

Waddles left and waddles right,
Showing coats of black and white.
Paws go pat and paws go clap,
Ready for a little nap.

Big round belly, soft and round,
Sitting heavy on the ground.
Time to yawn and close your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

rhymes.title: Bamboo Crunch
rhymes.text:
Bamboo shoots are green and tall,
Panda loves them best of all.
Pulling stalks down with his paw,
Widest smile you ever saw.

Crunchy, munchy, in his mouth,
Looking north and looking south.
Green leaves falling on the floor,
Panda always wants some more.

Tummy round and full of treat,
Sitting on his fuzzy seat.
Wiping green stuff from his chin,
Let the afternoon begin.

Now he rolls into the shade,
Playing games that they have played.
Say hello and wave goodbye,
While the fluffy clouds float by.

rhymes.title: Little Panda Paws
rhymes.text:
Little panda, black and white,
Sitting in the morning light.
Chewing bamboo, crunch, crunch, crunch,
Having such a yummy lunch.

Round black ears and fuzzy toes,
Freckles on a button nose.
Waddling softly through the trees,
Feeling such a gentle breeze.

Climbing up a stalk so tall,
Making sure he does not fall.
Rolling down the grassy hill,
Now the little bear is still.

Time to sleep and rest his head,
In his cozy leafy bed.
Dreaming through the starry night,
Till the morning sun shines bright.

rhymes.title: Panda Roll and Play
rhymes.text:
See the panda round and sweet,
With his furry little feet.
Playing in the forest green,
Cutest cub you've ever seen.

Clapping hands and smiling wide,
Looking for a place to hide.
Peeking out behind a tree,
Won't you come and play with me?

Chasing butterflies around,
Sitting softly on the ground.
Nibbling leaves of green and bright,
Eating till his tummy's tight.

Now he lets out sleepy sighs,
Rubbing tiny tired eyes.
Snuggling close to take a nap,
Sleeping on a warm green lap.

rhymes.title: Panda's Bamboo Tree
rhymes.text:
Up a tall and leafy tree,
Climbs a happy panda, see!
Holding tight with fuzzy paws,
Showing off his little claws.

Chewing on a tender shoot,
Happy from his head to foot.
 Munching greens the livelong day,
Dancing in a funny way.

Now he slides down to the floor,
Looking for a little more.
Waddling fast from left to right,
Underneath the golden light.

Curling up to rest his head,
In his grassy woodland bed.
Twinkle stars up in the sky,
Sing a gentle lullaby.

stories.title: Fuzzy Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of a bright green forest, lived a little orange fox named Felix. Felix had very soft fur, a big fluffy tail, and two big ears that loved to listen. Every day, Felix went on a fun adventure. Today, he trotted down the winding dirt path, sniffing the sweet flowers. Sniff, sniff, sniff! He smelled lovely yellow daisies and tall pink clovers. Felix wagged his bushy tail from side to side. Swish, swish, swish! He was looking for someone to play a game of hide-and-seek with. 'Who wants to play?' whispered Felix with a happy giggle. Just then, he heard a rustling sound in the bushes. Rustle, rustle, crunch! Felix crept very quietly on his soft paws. Tip-toe, tip-toe, stop. He peeked behind a big round pumpkin. And guess who was hiding there? It was Pip, a tiny brown bunny with floppy ears! Pip had a twitchy nose and a little cotton ball tail. 'Boo!' squeaked Pip with a joyful hop. Felix jumped up with a playful bark. 'Yip, yip! I found you!' laughed the happy fox. Pip giggled and did a happy dance in the clover. 'Now it is your turn to hide, Felix!' said the bunny. Felix covered his eyes with his paws. One, two, three, four, five! He counted slowly while Pip hopped away to find a good spot. Pip hid behind a mossy green log, peeking out with bright eyes. Felix opened his eyes wide and looked all around. Where could Pip be? He checked behind a tall green fern. Not there! He looked under a giant mushroom. Not there either! Then, Felix saw two long bunny ears sticking out from behind the log. 'Aha! I see you!' cheered Felix, running over with a happy bound. Pip and Felix laughed and rolled together in the soft grass. They chased butterflies that fluttered gently in the breeze. They jumped over tiny puddles of sparkling water. Splash, splash, go the little paws! When the warm sun started to go down behind the tall trees, painting the sky in pink and purple, Felix and Pip sat down together. They were tired, but they had the biggest smiles on their faces. 'Thank you for being my best friend, Pip,' said Felix softly, giving his friend a gentle nuzzle. 'Let's play again tomorrow,' replied Pip with a sleepy yawn. Felix trotted all the way home to his cozy den, feeling so happy inside. He curled his warm, fluffy tail around his nose, closed his heavy eyes, and dreamed about his wonderful day with his very best bunny friend.

stories.title: Felix Fox and the Lost Star
stories.text: Deep in the enchanted woods, as the sun began to tuck itself in for the night, a little orange fox named Felix woke up from his afternoon nap. Felix stretched his legs, gave a big yawn, and stepped outside his cozy den. The sky was turning a lovely shade of dark blue, and the very first evening star was twinkling high above the trees. Twinkle, twinkle, little star! Felix loved to look at the pretty night sky. But wait. Something very strange was happening tonight. One tiny, bright yellow star was not twinkling in the sky. Instead, it was wiggling right near the ground! Wiggle, wiggle, wiggle! Felix tilted his head in surprise. His big ears perked up to listen. He heard a tiny, gentle voice crying softly in the grass. Oh dear, oh dear, thought Felix, someone needs my help! Being a very kind little fox, Felix trotted quickly toward the sound. Patter, patter, patter went his soft paws. He pushed past some tall green ferns and looked down. Right there, sitting on a shiny toadstool, was a little fallen star! It looked just like a glowing yellow button with tiny arms and legs. 'Hello there,' whispered Felix in his softest, friendliest voice. 'Why are you sitting down here in the grass?' The little star sniffled and wiped a sparkly tear from its glowing eye. 'I tumbled right out of the big sky, and now I am too tired to fly back up to my friends!' whimpered the star. Felix felt bad for the tiny star. 'Do not worry,' said the brave little fox. 'I will help you get back home!' Felix gently nudged the glowing star with his soft nose. The star climbed right onto Felix's back, wrapping its warm, sparkly arms around his fluffy orange neck. It felt just like a warm hug on a chilly evening. Felix began to climb up the big hill at the edge of the forest. Step by step, he climbed higher and higher. The grass tickled his paws. The night breeze blew softly through his fur. Up, up, up they went until they reached the very top of the hill, right beneath the big, beautiful moon. Felix stood on his tiptoes and gave a gentle toss into the air. Whee! The little star floated up, up, up into the dark blue sky, right back to its twinkling friends. 'Thank you, kind fox!' called the star, flashing a brilliant, happy light. Felix smiled a big fox smile and sat down to watch the beautiful night sky sparkle. Then, he trotted happily back to his den, ready for sweet dreams.

stories.title: The Great Berry Hunt
stories.text: Good morning, little toddlers! Today we are going on a very special adventure with Barnaby, a bouncy little fox with bright orange fur and a tail that looked like a feathery cloud. Barnaby woke up with a very rumbling tummy. Rumbly-tumbly goes the tummy! 'I am so hungry,' whispered Barnaby with a wide grin. 'Today is the best day to go find some yummy red berries for breakfast.' Barnaby hopped out of his bed and stretched his paws way up high to the sky. Big stretch! Then he scampered out the door of his little wooden den and into the bright, sunlit forest. The air smelled like fresh green leaves and sweet morning dew. Barnaby started to trot down the twisty-turny path. Trot, trot, trot, go his little paws. He looked up at the tall trees and down at the green grass. Where would the yummy red berries be hiding today? He sniffed the air with his twitchy black nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff! Ah-ha! He smelled something sweet and delicious coming from behind a big, rocky hill. Barnaby scurried up the hill as fast as his little legs could carry him. When he reached the top, his eyes went round like big saucers. Right in front of him was a giant bush covered in the brightest, juiciest red berries you ever did see! They glistened like tiny rubies in the morning sun. 'Yippee!' cheered Barnaby, clapping his paws together with joy. But there was a little problem. The best berries were hiding right at the very top of the bush, way out of reach! Barnaby jumped up into the air. Boing! But he could not quite reach them. He jumped again even higher. Boing, boing! Still too high! Barnaby scratched his furry head and thought very hard. How could he get those tasty treats? Just then, his good friend Oliver the owl flew down from a high branch. 'Hoot, hoot! Do you need some help, little fox?' asked Oliver kindly. 'Yes, please!' said Barnaby with a polite nod. Oliver gently flapped his big wings, creating a soft breeze that shook the berry bush. Shake, shake, shake! Plop, plop, plop! The juicy red berries fell right down into the soft green grass. Barnaby’s eyes sparkled with delight. He gobbled up the sweet berries one by one. Yum, yum, yummy in his tummy! 'Thank you, Oliver,' said Barnaby, rubbing his full tummy with a happy sigh. He gave his friend a big, warm hug, knowing that sharing makes every sweet adventure twice as fun.

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the bright green woods, lived a little red fox named Felix. Felix had very soft orange fur, a big bushy tail that swished like a feather duster, and two big pointy ears that could hear the tiniest whispers in the grass. Today, Felix was on a very important mission. He wanted to find a new friend to play hide-and-seek with. 

Felix trotted down the wiggly path, his little paws going pad-pad-pad on the dirt. 'Hello, butterfly!' whispered Felix as a blue butterfly fluttered past his nose. The butterfly landed gently on a yellow daisy and stayed still. Felix giggled. Then, he saw a little grey squirrel high up in an oak tree. 'Chitter-chatter!' went the squirrel, dropping an acorn onto the soft moss below. Felix scampered over and gave the acorn a little boop with his wet black nose. 

As Felix walked a little further, he heard a funny sound coming from behind a big log. 'Hee-hee-hee! Snort-snort!' What could that be? Felix peeked around the mossy log. There sat Pip, a little hedgehog with prickly quills, trying to roll a round red apple through the grass. But the apple was too big, and Pip was too small! Every time Pip pushed it, the apple rolled away. 

Felix smiled a big fox smile. 'Do you need some help, little hedgehog?' asked Felix in his kindest voice. Pip looked up with big round eyes and nodded. 'Oh, yes please! This apple is being very stubborn.' Felix used his strong nose to help push the apple. Boop! Push! Roll! Together, the fox and the hedgehog rolled the big red apple all the way to Pip’s cozy burrow under the roots of a friendly pine tree. 

'Hooray!' cheered Pip. 'Thank you so much, Felix!' Felix wagged his big bushy tail from side to side. 'You are very welcome, Pip!' said Felix. 'Would you like to play hide-and-seek now?' Pip clapped his little paws together with joy. 'Yes! I am very good at hiding!' So, Felix closed his eyes and counted to three, while Pip scurried behind a big fern. They played games all afternoon long, giggling and running through the sunny woods, because Felix had finally found a wonderful new best friend.

stories.title: Felix Fox and the Shiny Star
stories.text:
It was nearly bedtime in the whispering forest, and the sky was turning a lovely shade of deep purple. Little Felix Fox was snuggled up in his cozy den, getting ready to close his eyes and dream sweet dreams. But just as he pulled his furry tail over his nose to keep warm, he saw something twinkle through the leaves of his doorway. It was a bright, sparkly star, shining just for him! 

'Good evening, little star,' whispered Felix softly. The star twinkled back as if to say hello. Felix stood up on his soft paws and stepped outside into the cool night air. The grass tickled his toes with morning-or rather, nighttime-dew. He wanted to get a closer look at that beautiful shiny star. Was it a high-up nightlight? Or maybe a glowing button in the sky? 

Felix began to walk through the peaceful woods. The owls were hooting softly in the branches above. 'Hoo-hoo, little fox, where are you going?' asked Wise Old Owl from his branch. 'I am going to say hello to the shiny star!' whispered Felix. The owl blinked his big yellow eyes and smiled. 'Keep walking straight ahead, little one.' 

Felix walked past the sleepy bluebells and tiptoed across the babbling brook. Splash went his tiny paw in the cool water. He looked up again, and the star seemed to be guiding him right to the edge of the glassy, quiet pond. Felix peered into the water. Oh, look! The star wasn't just in the sky anymore. It was dancing right on top of the ripples in the water, glowing in the reflection of the moon. 

Felix reached out a paw to touch the sparkly water. Ripples spread out in circles, and the little star seemed to giggle and dance away from his paw-pads. Felix laughed out loud. The water was like a giant magic mirror! He realized that the stars up in the big sky can light up the earth just by sharing their lovely glow. With a happy yawn, Felix rubbed his sleepy eyes. He knew it was time for bed now. He trotted back to his cozy den, curled up in a warm ball, and drifted off to sleep while the stars watched over him all through the night.

stories.title: Felix Fox's Busy Day
stories.text:
Good morning, sunshine! Today was going to be a very busy day for Felix Fox, and he woke up feeling extra bouncy. He stretched his front paws way out, gave a big yawn that showed all his tiny white teeth, and shook his orange fur. Shake-shake-shake! Now he was ready for whatever adventures waited outside his door. 

First, Felix needed to find his breakfast. He tiptoed through the meadow where the grass was sparkling with dew. He stopped and sniffed the air. Sniff-sniff, sniff-sniff! What did he smell? He smelled sweet strawberries growing near the old wooden fence. Felix trotted over and found three big, juicy red strawberries hiding under their green leaves. Yum! He gobbled them up with happy little crunches. 

Next, Felix had to practice his jumping skills. In the middle of the meadow lived his friend, bouncy bunny. 'Can you jump as high as me, Felix?' asked Bunny with a twitch of his long ears. 'I can try!' said Felix. Bend your knees, and... BOING! Felix jumped high up into the air, landing softly on all four paws in a patch of soft yellow dandelions. Poof! A cloud of white dandelion seeds floated up into the breeze, dancing like snow in the summertime. 

After jumping, Felix felt a little warm, so he trotted down to the cool, bubbling brook. He leaned down and lapped up some fresh, clear water with his pink tongue. Slurp, slurp, slurp! A little yellow duckling swam by and quacked a friendly hello. 'Quack-quack, Felix!' 'Hello, little duck!' replied the fox with a cheerful wag of his tail. 

By now, the sun was high up in the blue sky, and Felix was beginning to feel wonderfully tired. He had eaten sweet berries, jumped like a bunny, and splashed in the brook. It was time to go home. Felix trotted slowly back to his den, curled up in his favorite spot of warm sunlight, and closed his eyes. What a wonderfully busy and happy day it had been for a little red fox!

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, deep in the green and leafy woods, lived a little orange fox named Felix. Felix had very fluffy fur, a big white-tipped tail, and two big ears that could hear the softest whispers of the wind. Today, Felix woke up feeling very happy. He stretched his front paws, gave a big yawn, and scampered out of his cozy den. The sun was shining warm and bright, making the morning dew sparkle like tiny diamonds on the green grass. Felix wiggled his nose. Sniff, sniff, sniff! What was that delicious smell? It smelled sweet, just like ripe, juicy berries. Felix decided to go on an adventure to find the yummy treat. He trotted down the winding dirt path, his little paws going patter-pat, patter-pat. Along the way, he greeted his forest neighbors. 'Good morning, Mr. Owl!' hooted Felix in his happiest voice. Mr. Owl blinked his big round eyes and hooted back from high up in the oak tree. Felix kept walking, hopping merrily over a tiny mossy log. Soon, he reached the edge of the sunny meadow. And right there, growing near a big grey rock, was a wonderful bush full of shiny red berries. But wait! Someone was already there. It was Penny, a little brown bunny with floppy ears, looking very sad because she could not reach the high branches. Felix smiled a kind fox smile. He trotted over and said, 'Hello, Penny! Would you like some help?' Penny nodded her head up and down. 'Oh, yes please, Felix!' Together, they went to work. Felix used his strong paws to gently bend the leafy branch down low, just enough so Penny could nibble the sweet berries. Then, Penny helped dig up a lovely yellow dandelion flower for Felix. They shared the tasty snacks together in the warm sunshine, laughing and playing hide-and-seek in the tall meadow grass. Felix learned that sharing made his heart feel even warmer than the morning sun. When the afternoon shadows grew long, Felix gave Penny a friendly wave goodbye and trotted back down the path to his den. As he curled up into a cozy orange ball for his afternoon nap, he smiled. He had gone out looking for berries, but the best thing he found was a wonderful new friend. Goodnight, sweet little forest.

stories.title: Felix and the Shiny Star
stories.text: The sun was finally sinking low behind the tall green hills, painting the evening sky in pretty shades of pink, purple, and gold. Little Felix Fox sat right outside his cozy den door, wrapped in the cool evening breeze. He twitched his whiskers and watched the very first star blink on in the darkening blue sky. 'Twinkle, twinkle,' whispered Felix softly. It looked just like a bright, glowing yellow button stuck way up high in the clouds. Felix tilted his head and thought to himself, I wonder how high I can jump to touch that lovely star? So, Felix decided to play a fun little game. He stood up tall on his four paws, wiggled his fluffy bottom, and leaped up into the air. Boing! But the star was still way up high, twinkling down at him with a gentle wink. Felix giggled. He tried again. Boing! He leaped even higher this time, reaching out with his tiny black paws. But the star just danced playfully among the fluffy clouds. Just then, his mother walked out of the den, her soft orange coat brushing against his. 'What are you doing, my little Felix?' she asked with a warm, loving smile. Felix pointed his paw up at the sky. 'I want to catch the shiny star, Mama!' Mama Fox let out a gentle, rumbling laugh. She nuzzled his soft forehead with her nose. 'Oh, my sweet little fox, the stars belong high up in the sky where they can light the way for all the woodland creatures at night. But you carry your very own little star right inside your heart.' Felix blinked his big brown eyes, thinking about her words. He looked up at the vast, beautiful night sky. Millions of little stars were popping out now, glowing softly like a cozy blanket of lights. Felix realized Mama was right. He didn't need to hold the star in his paws. He yawned a huge, sleepy fox yawn, showing all his tiny white teeth. The day had been so long and fun, and now his eyelids felt very heavy and tired. He crept back inside his warm, snug den, curling his big fluffy tail right over his nose to keep cozy. Outside, the stars kept shining brightly, singing a quiet lullaby to the sleeping woods. Felix closed his eyes and drifted off to dreamland, smiling as he thought of his twinkling friends up in the sky.

stories.title: The Great Fox Puddle Jump
stories.text: Pitter-patter, pitter-patter! The rain had finally stopped falling from the grey clouds, leaving the whole forest cool, wet, and wonderfully fresh. Little Felix Fox poked his bright orange nose right out of his den. He looked down at the soft mud and saw big, beautiful, shiny puddles everywhere he looked. Felix loved puddles! They were big, round mirrors reflecting the bright blue sky. With a happy yip, Felix bounded right outside into the cool air. Splash, splash, splash went his little paws as he trotted through the wet grass. He stopped right at the edge of the biggest puddle in the whole path. It was huge! It stretched out wide like a little ocean in the middle of the woods. Felix backed up two steps, got a running start, and whispered to himself, 'Ready, set, jump!' He leaped high into the air with all his might. Splash! He landed right in the very middle of the puddle. Cool water sprayed up everywhere, sparkling like drops of liquid crystal in the returning sunlight. Felix giggled out loud, shaking the water off his fluffy tail so it went whish, whish, whish in the air. A little green frog sitting on a lily pad croaked happily, 'Ribbit, ribbit!' as if cheering him on. Felix splashed his right paw, making little ripples that grew bigger and bigger until they touched the muddy edges. Then he splashed his left paw, and then both back paws together. Oh, what a fun game! Soon, he was jumping from puddle to puddle, making wonderful splashing sounds that echoed through the quiet trees. Splish! Splash! Hop! By the time he was done, his paws were covered in happy mud, and his fur was a little bit damp, but his heart was full of pure joy. He trotted back to his den, leaving a trail of cute little muddy paw prints on the clean rock path. His mother met him at the door with a warm, soft leaf to help him dry off. She gave him a gentle lick on his forehead. 'You look like a very busy adventurer today,' she chuckled softly. Felix curled up in his warm bed, still hearing the happy sound of splashing water in his dreams. It had been the most wonderful, muddy, splashy day ever.

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning in the big green woods, a little orange fox named Felix woke up with a big stretch. Yawn! Felix had a fluffy tail that bounced like a spring when he walked. Today, Felix wanted to play a game. He trotted down the mossy path, his little paws going patter-pat, patter-pat on the soft ground. Along the way, he saw a shiny red apple hanging low on a branch. Felix jumped up. Boing! But the apple stayed on the tree. Oh, silly apple! Just then, a little brown bunny came hopping by with a twitchy nose. Hello, bunny! said Felix with a happy wag of his tail. The bunny stopped and wiggled its ears. Hello, little fox! said the bunny. Can you help me reach that yummy apple? asked Felix. The bunny smiled and said, Let us try together! Felix bent down low, and the bunny hopped right up onto Felix is soft back. Stretch, stretch, stretch went the bunny, and pop! The apple came right off the branch. Hooray! cheered Felix and the bunny. They shared the crunchy apple together, taking big, happy bites. Yum, yum, yum! Eating snacks with a friend is so much fun, thought Felix. The sun began to sink behind the tall trees, painting the sky in pink and orange. It was time for Felix to go home to his cozy den. Thank you for the wonderful playtime, said the bunny. You are very welcome, said Felix. They gave each other a gentle nose-bump goodbye. Felix trotted back home, his fluffy tail swaying side to side. He curled up in his warm bed, closed his eyes, and dreamed about his new bunny friend. Good night, forest. Good night, Felix.

stories.title: Felix and the Lost Star
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods, night time had come to stay. The moon was a bright silver banana in the sky, and the stars twinkled like tiny diamonds. Little Felix Fox peeked his head out of his cozy den. Look at all the lights! he whispered. Felix loved to look at the night sky. But wait. What was that little yellow glow down in the tall grass? Felix tilted his head. Tilt to the left, tilt to the right. He crept forward very quietly. Soft paws, soft paws, step, step, step. He pushed aside a big green fern, and there it was! A tiny, glowing star had tumbled right out of the sky and landed on a soft patch of clover. Oh, dear, said Felix gently. Did you fall down? The little star gave a tiny flicker, like a firefly waking up from a nap. It looked sad and cold. Do not worry, little star, said Felix. I will help you get back home. Felix used his soft nose to give the star a gentle nudge. Roll, roll, roll went the star across the moss. Felix led the star to the big oak tree, the tallest tree in the whole forest. Can you climb up on my fluffy tail? asked Felix. The star hopped right onto Felix is tail, which glowed with a warm, golden light. Wow! whispered Felix. Now you are super bright! Felix climbed up the grassy hill, higher and higher, until he reached the very top. Ready, set, jump! Felix gave a happy leap into the air. Whee! The little star flew up, up, up, right back into the dark blue sky, right next to the moon. Yay! You made it! cheered Felix, clapping his paws together. The star twinkled twice to say thank you. Felix smiled a big fox smile, feeling so proud and happy. He trotted back to his warm den, yawned a sleepy fox yawn, and drifted off to dreamland.

stories.title: Felix Counts His Colors
stories.text: Good morning, bright world! shouted little Felix Fox as he hopped out of bed. Today was a very special day because Felix was going on a color hunt all through the sunny meadow. Are you ready to hunt for colors with me? asked Felix, wiggling his nose at a busy bumblebee. Buzzz! went the bee. First, Felix looked down at his own coat. Look at me! I am bright orange! Just like a sweet, juicy carrot. Crunch, crunch! Next, Felix skipped over to a patch of green grass. He rolled around, tickle, tickle, tickle! Green grass feels so tickly on my tummy, giggled Felix. He stood up and shook off the blades of grass. Then, he spotted a bush full of bright red berries. Yum! Felix loved red berries. He ate one, two, three sweet berries. Red like a fire truck! said Felix, making a beep-beep sound with his nose. Oh, look over there! Felix trotted toward a big puddle left over from the morning rain. In the puddle, he saw the big blue sky looking right back up at him. Splash, splash went Felix is front paws in the cool water. Blue like the splashing ocean! he laughed, shaking water drops from his paws. Shake, shake, shake! Finally, Felix looked up at the warm, golden sun shining high above the trees. Yellow like a smiley face! Felix smiled his biggest, happiest smile. He had found orange, green, red, blue, and yellow all before lunch time. Felix skipped all the way home, his bright orange tail waving a happy goodbye to every color he had seen. What a wonderfully colorful day it had been in the forest.

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text:
Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the bright green woods, lived a little red fox named Felix. Felix had a shiny orange coat, two big pointy ears that could hear the softest whisper of the wind, and a big bushy tail that swished like a plume of feathers whenever he was happy. Today, Felix was very happy because it was a brand new day full of exciting adventures.

Felix trotted through the tall grass, his little paws going pitter-patter, pitter-patter on the soft dirt path. "Good morning, little ladybug!" he chirped happily as a tiny red bug flew past his wet black nose. The ladybug waved a tiny leg in reply. Felix loved the woods. Everywhere he looked, there was something wonderful to see, touch, or smell.

As he walked deeper into the forest, past the big oak tree and around the patch of sweet blue berries, Felix heard a strange sound. It went, "Hoo-hoo! Sniff-sniff! Oh dear, oh dear!" Felix stopped right in his tracks. He tilted his head to the left, then he tilted his head to the right. His big ears twitched. He peeked behind a large, mossy log and saw a little brown bunny sitting all by himself.

It was Barnaby Bunny, and he looked very sad. His long floppy ears were drooped down low, and a tiny teardrop rolled right down his twitchy pink nose. Felix gently stepped out from behind the log. "Hello there," Felix said in his softest, friendliest voice. "Why are you crying, little bunny?"

Barnaby sniffled and wiped his nose with his paw. "I lost my favorite shiny red marble, and now I cannot play my favorite rolling game. Have you seen it, Mr. Fox?"

Felix smiled warmly. "I haven't seen it yet, but two sets of eyes are always better than one! Let us look together." Felix and Barnaby started searching all around the big log. Barnaby looked under the clover leaves, while Felix used his strong nose to sniff around the roots of the trees.

Suddenly, Felix's tail gave a happy wag. "Aha!" he cried out. Right underneath a patch of yellow daisies, something shiny was blinking in the warm sunshine. It was the red marble! Barnaby clapped his paws together with joy. "You found it! You found my special marble! Thank you so much, Felix!"

From that day on, Felix the fox and Barnaby the bunny were the very best of friends. They played together every single day in the sunny woods, sharing games, jumping over logs, and having lots of fun until the sun went down and the sleepy stars came out to watch over them.

stories.title: Fiona Fox and the Lost Mitten
stories.text:
Winter had finally arrived in the quiet woods, and everything was covered in a thick, fluffy blanket of sparkly white snow. The trees wore white hats, the ground looked like a giant marshmallow, and the air was wonderfully crisp and cold. Little Fiona Fox popped her head right out of her cozy underground den. "Brrr!" she giggled, shaking a tiny snowflake off her bright red nose.

Fiona loved the snow more than anything else in the whole wide world. She loved how it crunched under her paws. She loved how she could leave little paw prints wherever she walked. Most of all, she loved wearing her brand new, extra-warm, bright yellow winter mittens. Her grandma had knitted them especially for her, and they kept her paws as toast-warm as a freshly baked muffin.

"Time for a snow adventure!" Fiona cheered, hopping out into the winter wonderland. She skipped down the snowy path, leaving a trail of cute little star-shaped paw prints behind her. She bounced through the drifts, making cute little snow puffs every time she landed. It was so much fun to explore the chilly morning air.

After walking for a little while, Fiona stopped to make a snow-fox. She laid down in the fluffy white snow and swept her arms and legs back and forth. When she stood up, she looked at her snowy masterpiece with a big smile. But suddenly, something didn't feel quite right. She looked down at her paws. Oh no! Her left paw was bare and cold!

"My mitten! My yellow mitten is gone!" Fiona gasped, her big brown eyes growing wide with worry. She looked all around her. She retraced her steps, walking backward very carefully. She checked behind a snowy bush. She looked under a frozen pine branch. But there was no yellow mitten to be seen anywhere.

Just then, a little gray squirrel poked his head out from a hole in a tree branch. He was wearing Fiona's bright yellow mitten right on his head like a silly winter hat! "Hello, Fiona!" chattered the squirrel. "I found this funny yellow thing in the snow. Is it a hat for my ears?"

Fiona burst into a fit of happy giggles. "No, silly squirrel! That is my warm winter mitten for my paw! It fell right off when I was playing."

The squirrel hopped down and handed the mitten back to Fiona with a polite little bow. Fiona put her warm mitten right back on her paw and gave the squirrel a sweet thank-you hug. With both paws warm and cozy once again, Fiona continued her joyful winter day, ready for whatever fun came next.

stories.title: Freddie Fox and the Starry Night
stories.text:
The sun was slowly going down behind the tall green hills, painting the evening sky in glorious shades of pink, purple, and deep orange. Down in the cozy meadow, a little fox named Freddie was getting ready for bed. Freddie wore his favorite blue pajamas with little yellow moon prints all over them, and he held his favorite stuffed owl tightly in his paws.

Freddie's mother tucked him gently into his bed made of soft moss and warm ferns. "Time to close your eyes, my sweet little fox," Mama Fox whispered, kissing his forehead softly. "The stars are coming out to watch over you as you sleep."

Freddie blinked his sleepy eyes and looked up at the sky. One by one, tiny white stars began to sparkle like tiny diamonds sprinkled across a giant velvet blanket. "Good evening, little stars," Freddie whispered in a soft, sleepy voice. He wanted to stay awake and count them all, but his eyelids felt heavier than big bags of heavy wool.

Suddenly, a gentle night breeze rustled the leaves outside. *Whoosh-whoosh* went the wind. A little firefly danced right past Freddie's window, blinking its bright yellow light on and off, on and off. "Look, Mama, a flying star!" Freddie pointed his paw toward the dancing bug with a sleepy grin.

Mama Fox chuckled softly and stroked his soft orange fur. "That is a friendly firefly, Freddie, coming to say goodnight to the sleepy woods. Everything in the forest is getting ready to rest now. The birds are sleeping in their nests, the bunnies are resting in their burrows, and the little foxes are snuggling in their beds."

Freddie let out a long, happy yawn. *Yaaawn!* It was the biggest yawn he had ever made all day long. He hugged his stuffed owl a little bit tighter and snuggled down deep into his warm bed. The cool night air felt so nice against his fuzzy cheeks, and the gentle sounds of the forest sang a quiet lullaby all around him.

"Goodnight, firefly," Freddie whispered softly. "Goodnight, trees. Goodnight, bright little stars."

Slowly, Freddie's breathing grew deep and steady. His little paws relaxed, and his eyes stayed closed as he drifted off into wonderful dreamland. Mama Fox smiled down at her sleeping baby, whispering one final goodnight as the bright moon shone down like a gentle nightlight, keeping him safe and warm until the morning light.

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of the bright green woods, lived a little red fox named Felix. Felix had very soft orange fur, a big bushy tail with a snowy white tip, and two big ears that could hear the tiniest sounds. Every day, Felix loved to play hide and seek with his woodland neighbors. Today, Felix woke up feeling extra bouncy. He stretched his front paws way out, gave a big yawn, and scampered out of his cozy den. The sun was shining through the tall pine trees, making sparkly golden puddles on the ground. Felix trotted down the bumpy path, sniffing the sweet flowers. Suddenly, he heard a soft rustling sound in the bushes. Swish, swish, went the green leaves. Felix stopped and pointed his twitchy black nose right at the bush. Who could it be? He took one tiptoe step, then another. With a playful little jump, Felix peeked behind the leaves. Pop! Out jumped Barnaby Bear cub, wearing a big smile and holding a shiny round berry. Hello, Felix, said Barnaby in his deep, happy voice. Do you want to share my yummy berry? Felix wagged his bushy tail from side to side. Oh yes, please, Barnaby! said Felix, his eyes sparkling with joy. The little red fox and the fuzzy brown bear sat down together on the soft moss. They shared the sweet red berry, chewing very carefully. Yum, yum, yum, it was so delicious! After their tasty snack, Felix and Barnaby decided to play tag. Felix was super-duper fast. He zipped past the tall ferns and dashed around the big oak tree. Barnaby ran as fast as his little bear legs could carry him, laughing a big belly laugh. Ready or not, here I come, shouted Felix, darting behind a mossy log. They ran and jumped all through the warm afternoon until the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange. Felix felt so happy and warm inside. Playing with a good friend was the best thing in the whole wide world. Felix gave Barnaby a friendly bump with his nose. See you tomorrow, my friend, whispered Felix. Then, the little red fox trotted back down the winding path to his cozy den, curling his big fluffy tail around his nose to keep warm as he drifted off to dreamland.

stories.title: Felix and the Lost Balloon
stories.text: The wind was blowing a gentle breeze through the forest, making the leaves dance a happy jig. Felix the little fox was skipping along the winding dirt path, looking for adventures. Suddenly, something bright red caught his eye up in the sky. Float, float, float went a big shiny red balloon! But oh dear, the balloon was tangled in the low branches of an apple tree. A little yellow string was dangling down, just out of reach. Felix stopped and tilted his head. He wanted to help that balloon get free! Felix backed up three big steps, bent his knees, and made a mighty spring. Boing! He leaped up into the air, but his paws only touched the cool breeze. He missed it by just a tiny inch! Felix landed softly on his feet in the green grass. He tried again. One, two, three, jump! Whoosh went the wind, blowing the balloon a little higher. Felix frowned for a second, but then he had a clever idea. Foxes are very smart, you know! He looked around the forest floor and found a long, wiggly stick. That stick would make a wonderful helper. Felix picked up the stick gently in his teeth. He walked right under the apple tree, stood up tall on his back paws, and reached up high with his special stick. Poke, tap, tap went the stick against the branch. Shake, shake went the tree. Pop went the string, sliding right off the twig! The bright red balloon floated down, down, down, right into Felix's waiting paws. Felix caught it safely and hugged it tight. He looked around to see who the balloon belonged to. Just then, Sammy Squirrel peeked out from behind a tree trunk, clapping his paws together with glee. Yay, my balloon! squeaked Sammy, running over with a happy bound. Felix smiled a big fox smile and handed the shiny string right to his little friend. Thank you so much, Felix, chattered Sammy happily. Felix gave his bushy tail a joyful wag. You are very welcome, Sammy! They watched the red balloon bob up and down in the blue sky, feeling so proud of their teamwork. It was truly a wonderful day in the woods.

stories.title: Felix Counts the Stars
stories.text: The sun had finally gone down to sleep, and the velvet night sky was sparkling with a million tiny lights. Felix the little fox stepped softly out of his den. The night air was cool and crisp, making his nose tickle. Felix loved nighttime in the forest because that was when the sky put on its brightest show. He walked to the edge of a quiet, glassy pond that reflected the moon like a giant silver coin. Felix sat down in the soft grass, curled his bushy tail neatly around his paws, and looked straight up. One star, two stars, three stars, whispered Felix softly to himself, pointing his paw at each bright speck. The stars twinkled and blinked like sleepy eyes saying hello. Felix gazed at the glowing moon, which looked just like a big yellow banana hanging in the dark sky. A little owl up in the oak tree hooted a gentle lullaby, hoo, hoo, hoo. Felix let out a long, happy yawn. All that star-gazing was making his eyelids feel very heavy and tired. He stretched his front legs out and gave his ears a little wiggle. The forest was so quiet and peaceful now. Every animal was tucked safely into bed, dreaming sweet dreams. Felix decided it was time for him to rest, too. He stood up, shook out his soft orange fur, and trotted back into his cozy den. He curled up into a warm, furry ball, tucking his cold nose right into his fluffy tail. As the gentle night wind whispered through the pine needles outside, Felix closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of chasing shooting stars across the velvet sky. Good night, stars, whispered Felix softly in his dreams. Good night, little fox, whispered the night right back.

stories.title: Felix Fox Goes to the Park
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright green forest, there lived a little red fox named Felix. Felix had very pointy ears, a tiny black nose, and a big, fluffy tail that swished side to side like a giant feather duster. Today was a very special day because Mommy Fox said they were going to visit the big park at the edge of the woods. Felix jumped up and down with excitement. Yip, yip, hooray! He put on his favorite red boots. Tap, tap, tap went his boots as he ran down the sunny trail. When they arrived at the park, Felix's eyes went wide. There were so many wonderful things to see and do! The first thing Felix saw was a bright yellow slide that went swoosh all the way down to the soft green grass. Felix climbed up the ladder, one step at a time. He sat right at the top, gave a little giggle, and went wheee! Down he slid, as fast as the wind. When he reached the bottom, his fluffy tail gave a happy wiggle. Next, Felix spotted a shiny red swing. He sat in the seat and held on tight with his paws. Mommy Fox gently pushed him, higher and higher. Up, up, up into the sky! Felix felt like he could touch the fluffy white clouds. The cool breeze tickled his nose. Then, Felix heard a funny sound. Giggles and laughs! He looked over and saw a group of bunny rabbits playing hide and seek behind a big oak tree. Can I play too? asked Felix kindly. Oh yes, said the little bunnies. Felix covered his eyes with his paws and counted to three. One, two, three! Ready or not, here I come! Felix sniffed the air and used his clever fox ears to listen. He heard a little wiggle behind a bush. I found you! laughed Felix, gently tapping the bunny on the shoulder. They all clapped their paws and played together until the sun began to turn a pretty shade of orange and pink. It was time to go home. Felix was very tired from all the fun. Mommy Fox gave him a big warm hug. As they walked back down the trail, Felix held Mommy's paw and yawned a big, sleepy fox yawn. What a wonderful day at the park. Felix snuggled into his cozy bed, closed his eyes, and dreamed about his happy red boots and his new bunny friends. Good night, little fox.

stories.title: The Lost Button
stories.text: Deep in the whispering woods, where the bluebells grow, lived a cheerful little fox named Rusty. Rusty wore a bright blue coat with four shiny yellow buttons. He loved his coat more than anything in the whole wide world. Every morning, he would button it all the way up and trot through the forest to see his animal friends. One sunny morning, Rusty woke up, jumped out of bed, and put on his favorite blue coat. He looked down and gasped. Oh no! One, two, three. Only three buttons! Where was the fourth yellow button? Rusty looked under his bed. It was not there. He looked inside his toy box. It was not there either. I must go on a button hunt! said Rusty bravely. He stepped outside into the cool morning air. The dew sparkled on the grass like tiny diamonds. First, Rusty trotted over to his friend Sammy Squirrel, who was busy collecting acorns beneath a tall pine tree. Good morning, Sammy! Have you seen a shiny round yellow button anywhere? Sammy stopped digging and scratched his head. I haven't seen a button, Rusty, but I did see something shiny near the big muddy puddle! Thank you, Sammy! said Rusty. He trotted over to the big muddy puddle. Splash, splash went his little paws. He looked carefully at the edges of the water. Bubbles popped up, but no button. Just then, a little green frog popped his head out of the water. Ribbit! Are you looking for this? asked the frog, holding something bright in his webbed foot. It was the shiny yellow button! Oh, thank you, kind frog! cried Rusty happily. Rusty skipped all the way home to his cozy den. He asked his mother for a needle and thread. Together, they carefully sewed the shiny yellow button back onto the blue coat. Rusty buttoned it up all the way to the top and gave a happy spin. His coat was complete once more. Rusty smiled a big, toothy fox smile and gave his mother a giant hug. He promised to take extra good care of his buttons from that day on.

stories.title: Pip's Big Red Ball
stories.text: Once upon a time, a curious little fox cub named Pip found a wondrous surprise resting right in the middle of the garden path. It was a big, round, shiny red ball! Pip had never seen anything so bright. He poked it gently with his wet black nose. Boop! The ball rolled a little bit to the left. Pip let out a happy little yip and gave the ball a gentle tap with his paw. Whee! The ball rolled across the soft green lawn, bouncing over a tiny pebble and stopping right near a patch of sweet strawberries. Pip chased after it as fast as his stubby legs could carry him. Patter, patter, patter went his little feet. When he caught up to the ball, he rested his chin right on top of it. Suddenly, a little brown bunny hopped out from behind the strawberry leaves. Hello there, little fox! said the bunny whose name was Barnaby. Is that a red apple? No, silly! giggled Pip. It's a big red bouncing ball. Do you want to play with me? Barnaby's long ears perked straight up with joy. Oh, I would love to play! So, the little fox and the little bunny began a wonderful game of catch. Pip rolled the ball across the grass to Barnaby. Barnaby stopped the ball with his fluffy paws and rolled it right back to Pip. Round and round the garden they played, laughing and chasing each other until they were both quite out of breath. The warm afternoon sun shone down like a big golden blanket. Soon, a sleepy feeling washed over Pip. The red ball sat quietly between his paws. Barnaby gave a little rabbit yawn and curled up in the soft grass. Pip curled his big fluffy tail around his nose to keep warm. They didn't need to chase the ball anymore. They just wanted to rest together in the quiet, peaceful garden. Pip closed his eyes with a happy smile, dreaming of bouncing high up into the sky with his shiny red toy.

stories.title: Felix Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, in the middle of a bright green forest, lived a little red fox named Felix. Felix had very soft orange fur, a big bushy tail with a snowy-white tip, and two big, floppy ears that loved to listen. Every day, Felix would bounce through the tall grass, practicing his tippy-toe steps. Soft pitter-patter went his little paws on the moss. Today, Felix was on a very important mission. He wanted to find a new friend to play hide-and-seek with. First, Felix trotted over to the big oak tree. He peeked behind the trunk and whispered, 'Hello, little squirrel!' But the squirrel was too busy munching on a crunchy acorn and scurried right up the tree. Felix giggled and kept on walking. Next, Felix skipped down to the muddy riverbank. He dipped one wet paw into the cool, splashing water. Splish, splash, went the water! He saw a little green frog sitting on a lily pad. 'Ribbit!' said the frog, and it jumped high into the air with a big KERPLUNK! Felix clapped his paws together with delight. But the frog was too fast for hide-and-seek. Felix began to feel a tiny bit lonely. He sat down on a warm rock and gave a soft sigh. Suddenly, he heard a rustling sound in the bushes behind him. Rustle, rustle, snap! Felix turned his head very fast. Out popped a little brown bunny with floppy ears and a twitchy nose. The bunny looked at Felix, and Felix looked at the bunny. The bunny did a little happy hop. Felix did a little happy spin. 'Do you want to play?' asked Felix in his softest voice. The bunny nodded its head up and down and wiggled its whiskers. Hooray! They played the best game of hide-and-seek ever. Felix hid behind a patch of yellow daisies, and the bunny counted to three. Then the bunny hid behind a big round pumpkin, and Felix found him right away. They giggled and played all afternoon until the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, just like Felix's fur. Felix gave his new friend a warm hug and whispered, 'Tomorrow, let's play again.' Then, with a happy heart and a wagging tail, Felix trotted all the way home to his cozy den for a good night's sleep.

stories.title: Felix Fox and the Lost Star
stories.text: It was bedtime in the quiet forest, and the moon was shining like a big silver coin in the dark blue sky. Little Felix Fox stepped outside his den to look at the twinkling stars. Twinkle, twinkle, little star, shining bright so far! But wait. Felix rubbed his sleepy eyes. Right down in the soft grass, something was glowing with a warm yellow light. Felix walked very slowly, tiptoe, tiptoe, tiptoe. He sniffed the air. Sniff, sniff. It smelled like warm honey and sweet flowers. Felix parted the tall blades of grass with his nose. Oh! Sitting right there on a clover leaf was a tiny, glowing creature. It looked just like a little star that had tumbled down from the sky. 'Hello up there,' whispered the star in a tiny, tinkling voice. 'I think I fell off my cloud.' Felix gasped. He wanted to help his new little friend get back home. But how do you help a star get back to the sky? Felix thought hard. He used his big fox ears to listen. He used his clever fox nose to smell. Then, Felix had a bright idea. He pointed to the highest hill in the forest. 'Up there!' said Felix happily. 'The sky is much closer from the top of the hill!' Felix gently scooped the tiny star onto his fluffy, soft tail, where it sat safely like a glowing lantern. Off they went, a brave little fox and his starry passenger, marching up the winding path. Tap-tap, tap-tap went Felix's paws. When they finally reached the very top of the windy hill, Felix stood up tall on his hind legs. He gave a gentle wiggle of his tail. Whoosh! The little star floated right up into the air, spinning with joy. It twirled around Felix's head once, twice, three times, as if to say a big thank you. Then, pop, it zoomed all the way back up to its cozy place in the velvet night sky, shining brighter than ever before. Felix smiled a big, toothy fox smile and gave a happy yawn. He curled his bushy tail around his nose, feeling warm and cozy. The forest was quiet, the stars were safe, and little Felix Fox was ready for the sweetest dreams.

stories.title: Felix Fox's Big Red Balloon
stories.text: Today was a very special day in the forest because it was Felix Fox's birthday! To celebrate, his mother gave him a wonderful surprise. It was a big, round, shiny red balloon tied to a long piece of yellow string. Felix's eyes went wide with pure joy. 'Oh, wow!' he cheered, jumping up into the air. He grabbed the yellow string gently in his little paws. The balloon bobbed up and down in the breeze, saying float, float, float! Felix decided to take his new red balloon for a walk to show all his woodland neighbors. First, he pranced past the old oak tree where wise old Oliver Owl was resting. 'Happy birthday, little fox,' hooted Oliver Owl, blinking his big round eyes. Felix beamed with pride and waved his balloon high in the air. Next, Felix skipped across the bubbling brook on stepping stones. Clop, clop, splash went the water around his toes. He held the string extra tight so the balloon wouldn't touch the water. But oh no! Suddenly, a gust of playful wind came swooping through the trees. Whoosh! The wind tugged at the string. It pulled and pulled, and before Felix could say stop, the red balloon slipped right out of his paws. 'Come back!' cried Felix, reaching up as high as he could. The balloon floated higher and higher into the blue sky, passing the treetops and drifting toward a fluffy white cloud. Felix felt a big sad tear tickle his cheek. But just then, a friendly bluebird flew down from the branches. 'Don't worry, Felix,' chirped the bluebird. 'Follow me!' The bluebird flew up, and Felix scampered along the ground below, running as fast as his little legs could carry him. Fast, fast, fast went Felix! They chased the balloon across the meadow until it gently bumped against the branches of a low apple tree and got stuck. Felix leaped up with a joyful YIP! He caught the string and pulled it down safely into his paws. He let out a big sigh of relief and hugged the round red balloon tight. He shared his birthday berries with the bluebird, and they danced in the grass together. It turned out to be the best birthday ever.

stories.title: Fuzzy Fox Finds a Friend
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, deep in the green and leafy woods, lived a little fox named Felix. Felix had bright orange fur that matched the falling autumn leaves, a white-tipped tail that swished like a fluffy cloud, and big, pointy ears that could hear the softest whisper of the wind. Today was a very special day because Felix was going on an adventure to find a brand-new friend. With a happy bounce in his step, Felix trotted down the winding dirt path.
