She bent down, picked it up with her paws, and tucked it safely inside her cozy pouch. That made a nice little weight against her tummy! Just a few hops further, Kora spotted a brilliant red feather floating gently down from the sky, carried by a soft breeze. She chased after it—flutter, flutter, hop, hop—until she caught it right out of the air. Kora giggled with glee and slid the soft red feather right next to her shiny pebble. Her pouch was starting to feel like a magical treasure chest. As Kora continued her bouncy journey, she heard a soft rustling sound in the bushes. Out popped her best friend, Pip the bilby, with his long pink nose twitching. 'What are you doing, Kora?' asked Pip with a curious twitch of his whiskers. 'I am collecting treasures for my pouch!' answered Kora proudly. She opened the top of her pouch just a tiny bit to show Pip her shiny pebble and her soft red feather. Pip's eyes grew wide with wonder. 'That is the best collection ever!' he cheered. Then, Pip reached down and handed Kora one last treasure: a crisp, sweet green leaf shaped like a tiny heart. Kora smiled her biggest smile and placed the leaf gently inside her pouch. With her tummy full of wonderful treasures and her heart full of joy, Kora hopped all the way back home to her mother, ready to share the story of her very special treasure hunt before bedtime.

stories.title: The Great Out-Jump Race
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the rolling green hills, and all the animal friends had gathered for the very first annual Out-Jump Race. There were fuzzy wombats, speedy lizards, and, of course, a little kangaroo named Barnaby who was famous for his wiggly, jiggly energy. Barnaby loved to run, but mostly he loved to jump high into the air where the birds flew. 'Are you ready, set, go!' chirped a little kookaburra from high up in a gum tree. With a mighty cheer, all the animals started moving, but Barnaby knew just what to do. He bent his strong back legs, took a deep breath, and launched himself forward with a tremendous BOING! He sailed through the air like a superhero, his long tail balancing him gracefully as the wind rushed past his fuzzy ears. Down he came with a soft thump, and then—boing again! Barnaby was flying over patches of bright wildflowers and small, babbling brooks. But wait! Ahead of him was Toby the Tortoise, who was moving very slowly and steadily. Barnaby wanted to win, but he was also a very kind kangaroo. As he bounced past Toby, he saw that Toby looked a little tired under the warm sun. Barnaby pulled back on his bouncing speed, landed softly right next to Toby, and asked, 'Are you doing okay, my friend?' Toby smiled and said, 'I am just taking my time to enjoy the lovely flowers.' Barnaby had a wonderful idea. 'Would you like to ride on my shoulders for the rest of the race?' he asked politely. Toby's eyes lit up, and he climbed carefully up onto Barnaby's back, holding on tight to his soft fur. With extra care and a very special cargo, Barnaby began to hop again. Boing, boing, hop, hop! He didn't jump quite as high, but he bounced with extra love and care. Together, Barnaby and Toby crossed the finish line side by side. All the animals cheered loudly, clapping their paws and wings. Even though Barnaby didn't win first place for speed, he won the big golden ribbon for being the kindest hopper in the whole wide world. They all celebrated with a big picnic of sweet berries and cool water as the stars began to twinkle in the evening sky.

stories.title: Kip's Big Jump
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day in the green, green grass, a little baby kangaroo named Kip woke up from a wonderful nap. Kip had very long ears, a very long tail, and very, very big feet. "Good morning, big world!" whispered Kip to a passing yellow butterfly. Kip wanted to do something very special today. He wanted to jump all the way over the sleeping log. His mama, whose pouch was cozy and warm, smiled and said, "You can do it, my little jumping bean!" Kip bent his fuzzy knees. He tucked his tiny front paws right up against his chest. He wiggled his nose—twitch, twitch, twitch—just like a happy little bunny. Then, with all his might, Kip went BOING! Up, up, up into the warm, bright sky went Kip. He felt the soft wind tickle his whiskers. He saw the green treetops waving hello. Down, down, down came Kip, landing with a soft thump right on the other side of the log. "Hooray!" cheered a friendly koala sitting in a nearby eucalyptus tree. Kip was so proud of his big, brave jump. He did a happy little wiggle dance with his feet. He jumped back over the log, and then he jumped over a little yellow flower, and then he jumped all the way back to his mama. Mama kangaroo opened her warm pouch wide. Kip hopped right inside, snug as a bug in a rug, feeling safe and sleepy. "You are the best jumper in the whole wide world," whispered Mama. Kip closed his big brown eyes and dreamed about floating on bouncy clouds. The sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and purple colors. All the forest animals whispered goodnight to little Kip. It had been a wonderful day of big jumps and sweet cuddles. Kip snuggled deeper into the pouch, ready for sleep.

stories.title: Pouch Full of Fun
stories.text: Deep in the sunny Australian outback, a cheerful young kangaroo named Joey had the most magnificent pocket in the whole wide world. It was his mama's cozy pouch, and inside it lived all of Joey's very favorite treasures. Every morning, after a big breakfast of crunchy green leaves, Joey would pop his head out to see what adventures awaited them. First came the bright red rubber ball that bounced with a silly squeak. "Squeak, squeak!" went the ball as Joey tossed it across the soft red dirt. A cheeky little kookaburra laughed from a branch above, making Joey giggle. Next, Joey reached deep into the magical pouch and pulled out his trusty wooden drum. Tap, tap, tap went his little paws against the wood, making a happy rhythm that matched the beating of his own happy heart. But wait, what was that wiggling at the bottom of the pouch? It was a shiny blue feather! Joey tucked the feather behind his floppy ear so he looked like a fancy jungle prince. "Look at me, Mama!" cried Joey with a joyful hop. Mama kangaroo hopped gently over the hills, keeping her little explorer safe and snug inside her warm embrace. They passed tall green eucalyptus trees and sparkling blue streams of water. Whenever Joey felt tired of walking, or rather, hopping on his own two feet, he would tuck his long legs together and slide right back down into his snug little pocket. It was the warmest, safest place in the whole wide world. The sun beamed down with golden rays, warming their furry backs. Joey yawned a big, wide, sleepy yawn. He hugged his squeaky ball tightly against his chest. With the gentle rocking motion of Mama's hops, Joey closed his eyes and drifted off to a peaceful sleep, safe and happy inside his pouch full of fun.

stories.title: Roo's Red Balloon
stories.text: Little Roo loved red things. He loved red strawberries, red ladybugs, and especially his big, shiny red balloon. It was round like a cherry and floated happily on a long yellow string. One breezy afternoon, Roo was hopping through the tall grass when a sudden gust of wind went WHOOSH! The wind tickled Roo's long ears and gently pulled at the yellow string. "Hold on tight!" giggled Roo, but the balloon wanted to dance in the sky. It lifted Roo's hand just a tiny bit. Roo had an idea. If he did a little bounce, the balloon would bounce too. Boing, went Roo! Float, went the balloon! They played the happy game together over the rolling green hills. A friendly wombat poked his head out of his burrow and waved. "Hello, red balloon! Hello, Roo!" called the wombat. Roo waved back with his fuzzy paw while his big feet kept a steady rhythm on the ground. Suddenly, the balloon floated a little too high, right toward the low branches of a leafy acacia tree. "Oh no!" gasped Roo. He knew the sharp leaves might pop his precious red friend. Without missing a beat, Roo bent his strong knees and prepared for the biggest jump of his life. He sprang upward like a coiled-up spring. Up, up, up he soared through the air, his arms stretched out wide. Just in the nick of time, Roo caught the trailing yellow string safely in his paw. He brought the balloon down with a gentle tug and hugged it tightly against his chest. "Phew!" sighed Roo with a big smile. He sat down in the soft clover and shared a quiet moment with his floating friend. The sun dipped low, turning the sky orange and gold. Roo held the string firmly as he hopped all the way home to tea time, happy and safe.

stories.title: Kip the Kangaroo's Big Bounce
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day in the green, green grass, a little kangaroo named Kip woke up with a giant wiggle in his toes. Kip had soft brown fur, big floppy ears, and feet that were made for hopping. "Good morning, sun!" Kip called out, giving a happy little hop. Today was a very special day because Kip was going to try and jump all the way to the big eucalyptus tree at the end of the meadow. His mama smiled and said, "Bend your knees, Kip, and push off with all your might!" Kip squatted down low, just like a spring being wound up tight. Ready, set, boing! Up, up, up he went into the blue sky. He felt the warm wind tickling his whiskers. He sailed over a patch of yellow daisies and landed softly on the grass with a gentle thud. "Whee! That was so much fun!" giggled Kip. But the big tree was still far away. Kip knew he needed more than one hop to get there. So, he got ready for his next big adventure. Boing, went Kip! Boing, boing, boing! Each jump took him a little bit higher and a little bit further. Along the way, he saw his friend Sammy the snail crawling slowly on a rock. "Hello, Sammy!" called Kip as he soared right over him. Sammy waved his little antennae and smiled. Kip kept on bouncing, feeling strong and happy. Soon, he reached the big eucalyptus tree. He looked up at the high branches and gave one super-duper mega-hop, landing right next to his mama. They cuddled close together in the shade of the leaves. Kip felt his tummy rumble, but he was so proud of his journey. "I did it, Mama! I bounced all the way!" he cheered. Mama nuzzled his soft head and said, "You are my super jumper, Kip." With a happy sigh, Kip closed his eyes, ready for sweet dreams of bouncing through the sky.

stories.title: Kiki's Cozy Pouch
stories.text: Little Kiki was a sweet baby kangaroo who lived in the Australian outback. The outback was a wonderful place with red dirt, bright yellow sun, and lots of friendly animals. Kiki loved exploring, but today she was feeling just a little bit tired. Her little legs felt heavy, and her eyelids were drooping low. "Mama, carry me?" whispered Kiki, rubbing her sleepy eyes. Mama kangaroo smiled warmly and opened up the warm, soft pouch right on her tummy. It was the coziest place in the whole wide world, lined with the softest fur and smelling like sweet sunshine. Kiki scurried right inside, tucking her long legs and her little arms snuggly against her mama. It was dark and peaceful, like a tiny secret cave made just for her. As Mama hopped along to gather fresh green leaves for dinner, Kiki felt a gentle, rocking motion. Up and down, up and down went the rhythm, like a lullaby sung by the wind. Inside the pouch, Kiki felt completely safe and loved. She poked her little head out just for a moment to watch the world go by. She saw a colorful parrot fly past and a lizard sunning himself on a warm rock. "Good afternoon, world," Kiki chirped softly. Then, she pulled her head back down into her cozy nest. The rocking motion continued, soothing her tired muscles. Mama gently patted the outside of the pouch, humming a soft tune. Kiki yawned a big, wide kangaroo yawn. Her eyes closed tight, and she drifted off into a deep, peaceful sleep. Safe inside the warm pouch, she dreamed of fluffy clouds and bouncing over rainbows. When she woke up much later, she was rested and ready for more fun, but for now, she just wanted to stay tucked in her favorite spot in the whole universe.

stories.title: The Joey Who Lost His Bounce
stories.text: Barnaby was usually the bounciest joey in the whole outback. Every morning, he would leap over bushes and skip across the dirt trails with a big grin on his face. But today, something strange had happened. Barnaby woke up, bent his knees, and tried to jump, but his feet stayed glued to the ground. Oh no! His bounce was completely gone! "Mama, my bounce is broken!" Barnaby cried, looking down at his feet in dismay. Mama kangaroo gently patted his shoulder and said, "Don't worry, little one. Sometimes bounces just need a little help to come back out." Barnaby tried again. He wiggled his toes, he shook his tail, and he even tried standing on his head, but still, no bounce! Just then, his best friend Pip the koala ambled over. "Why are you so still, Barnaby?" Pip asked, munching on a eucalyptus leaf. "I lost my bounce," Barnaby sighed sadly. Pip thought for a moment and said, "Well, maybe you need to laugh! Laughter makes everything lighter." Pip started to tickle Barnaby gently under his furry chin. Barnaby let out a loud giggle. Then he chuckled, and then he let out a great big belly laugh. Suddenly, Barnaby felt a funny tickle in his toes. A little bubble of energy popped inside his tummy. His knees started to bend all on their own. "Look!" shouted Pip, clapping his paws. Barnaby gave a little hop. Then he gave a bigger hop. And then, with a joyful shout, he bounced as high as the clouds! His bounce was back, brighter and better than ever before. Barnaby hugged his mama and thanked Pip for the wonderful giggles. From that day on, whenever his bounce felt a little slow, Barnaby knew just what to do: laugh out loud and let the joy lift him right off the ground.

stories.title: Kip the Kangaroo's Big Bounce
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day in the green and leafy outback, lived a little baby kangaroo named Kip. Kip had two big, strong feet, a long, heavy tail, and two very big ears that loved to wiggle. More than anything in the whole wide world, Kip loved to bounce. Boing! Boing! Boing! He bounced over tiny pebbles. Boing! Boing! He bounced past the sleepy koala in the eucalyptus tree. Kip’s mama always told him, 'Practice makes your legs super strong, little one!' Today was a very special day because Kip was going to try his very first big jump across the wide red creek. He stood at the edge of the water and looked across. It looked so far away! His tummy felt a little bit fluttery, like butterflies were dancing inside. But Kip remembered his mama's happy smile. He squatted down low, tucked his tail in just right, and squeezed his eyes tight. One, two, three, BOUNCE! Up, up, up into the sky went Kip. He felt like a fluffy cloud floating in the air. Whoosh! He flew right over the bubbling water and landed softly on the other side with a big thump. 'I did it! I did it!' Kip cheered, doing a happy little dance with his feet. Mama kangaroo hopped over and gave him the biggest, warmest cuddle in the whole world. 'We are so proud of you, Kip,' she whispered. Kip felt so happy and warm inside. He realized that trying new things was wonderful, especially when you had the courage to take that first big jump. As the golden sun began to sink low in the sky, Kip and his mama hopped all the way home, ready for sweet dreams and tomorrow's big adventures.

stories.title: Pockets for Everyone
stories.text: Deep in the sunny Australian bush, a little kangaroo named Rosie woke up with a big stretch and a wide yawn. Rosie had something very special. She had a cozy, warm pouch right on her tummy. It was her pocket! Rosie looked at her pocket and wondered what it was truly for. 'Is it for holding shiny smooth stones?' she asked herself. She hopped over to the creek and scooped up three sparkly pebbles, popping them right inside. Clink, clank, clink went the stones as she hopped. But soon, her friend Sammy the wombat came waddling by, looking very sad. 'Oh Rosie,' sniffled Sammy, 'my favorite little teddy bear is so tired, but my arms are too short to carry him all the way home.' Rosie smiled a big, bright smile. 'Put him in my pocket!' she cheered. Sammy gently placed the sleepy teddy bear inside Rosie's cozy pouch. Next came Penny the sugar glider, who had found a bunch of sweet, juicy berries and needed a safe place to carry them. 'In the pocket!' said Rosie happily. Soon, Rosie's pouch was full of teddy bears, sweet berries, and even a tiny, tired frog. Rosie felt wonderfully helpful. Even though her pouch felt a little heavy, her heart felt as light as a feather. She hopped gently all the way down the dusty path, making sure not to bump her precious cargo. When they reached the big shady gum tree, all her friends climbed out and shouted, 'Thank you, Rosie, for being our wonderful pocket friend!' Rosie gave a happy little hop and a giggle. She curled up in her cozy nest that night, knowing that sharing her special pocket made helping others the best adventure of all.

stories.title: The Starry Night Hop
stories.text: The sun was sinking behind the tall eucalyptus trees, painting the sky in gorgeous pink and purple swirls. Little Joey the kangaroo was snuggled up next to his mama, getting ready for sleep. But Joey's ears twitched. He heard a soft, magical sound coming from the tall grass. Swish, rustle, twinkle! It sounded like music. Joey popped his head out of the pouch. 'Mama, what is that sound?' he whispered with wide eyes. Mama smiled softly and said, 'That is the lullaby of the night stars, little one.' Joey hopped out onto the soft, cool grass. He looked up at the giant, dark blue sky, dotted with a million twinkling stars. They looked just like tiny glowing fireflies dancing in the heavens. 'I want to touch a star!' whispered Joey. He bent his knees, stretched his long legs, and bounced up into the air. Boing! He reached his little paws up as high as they could go. He didn't quite reach a star, but he felt a cool night breeze tickle his nose. He giggled and bounced again. Boing! Higher this time. The moon smiled down at him with a gentle, glowing face, as if to say, 'Keep trying, little jumper!' Joey bounced and spun in the cool night air, feeling like he was flying among the constellations. He imagined he was a soaring bird or a shooting star streak across the dark. After a few more happy jumps, his little legs began to feel wonderfully tired. His eyelids felt heavy like sleepy curtains. Mama opened her warm pouch wide and whispered, 'Time to rest, my sweet star-hopper.' Joey hopped right back inside, tucked himself into the soft, cozy lining, and closed his eyes. As the night sang its quiet song, Joey dreamed of bouncing across the Milky Way, touching every single star in the sky.

stories.title: Kip the Kangaroo's Big Bounce
stories.text: Once upon a sunny day, in the warm and grassy Australian outback, there lived a little kangaroo named Kip. Kip had two big, strong back legs, a long balancing tail, and very soft, floppy ears. Every morning, Kip would wake up and wiggle his little pink nose. 'Good morning, sun! Good morning, trees!' he would say in a happy voice. Today was a very special day because Kip wanted to learn how to do the Super-Duper Big Bounce. Kip's mama hopped over to him and gave him a gentle nudge. 'Are you ready to practice your bouncing today, my little joey?' she asked with a warm smile. 'Oh yes, Mama! I want to jump as high as the fluffy white clouds!' Kip squealed with delight. First, Kip bent his knees down low, just like a coiled-up spring. He tucked his little front paws right against his chest and wiggled his toes. Then, with all his might, he pushed off the warm dirt and went BOING! Up, up, up he went into the bright blue sky. 'Wheee!' shouted Kip as he sailed through the air. But he went a little too high and wobbled to the left. WHOOPS! Kip tumbled softly into a big, fluffy bush of yellow wattle flowers. 'Giggly-wiggly!' laughed Kip, shaking yellow petals off his head. His mama hopped over and helped him up. 'That was a wonderful try, Kip! Remember to use your long tail to help you balance when you land.' Kip nodded seriously. He tried again. Bend those knees, push with your strong feet, and keep that long tail steady. BOING! Kip leaped over a smooth brown rock. BOING! He jumped right past a sleepy koala resting in a eucalyptus tree. This time, when Kip came down, he landed right on his two feet with a soft thud. 'I did it! I did it, Mama!' cheered Kip, doing a little victory dance with his front paws. The sun began to set, painting the sky in gorgeous shades of pink and orange. Kip was tired, but he was the happiest little kangaroo in the whole wide world. He hopped safely back to his mama's warm pouch, tucked himself inside, and fell fast asleep under the twinkling stars.

stories.title: Rosie's Pouch Full of Treasures
stories.text: Deep in the green and leafy bush, a friendly mama kangaroo named Rosie hopped along the winding dirt path. Rosie had a wonderful, cozy pouch right on her tummy. It was soft like a velvet blanket and warm like a sunny afternoon. Today, Rosie was on a very important mission. She was collecting special treasures for her sleepy little joey, Barnaby, who was resting inside her pouch. Rosie hopped a few steps and stopped by a sparkling blue stream. 'Look, Barnaby, a shiny smooth river stone,' Rosie whispered softly. She picked up the grey, slippery stone with her paw and gently slid it into her pouch. Barnaby poked his tiny furry head out and blinked his big brown eyes. He gave the stone a little sniff and chattered happily. 'Hop, hop, hop,' went Rosie as she continued down the path. Next, she stopped beneath a tall gum tree where the afternoon breeze made the leaves dance. SWISH, SWISH, went the leaves. A bright green gum leaf fluttered down and landed right on Rosie's nose. Rosie crossed her eyes and giggled. She took the leaf and tucked it safely into her pouch beside the smooth river stone. Barnaby squeaked with joy and gave the leaf a gentle nibble. But Rosie was not finished yet. She hopped a little further until she reached a patch of golden wildflowers. The flowers smelled sweet like honey and sunshine. Rosie carefully plucked three yellow petals and added them to her growing collection. Now her pouch held a shiny stone, a green leaf, and sweet flowers. Barnaby felt all the wonderful things tickling his tummy, and he giggled a high-pitched baby kangaroo giggle. 'Are you having fun in there, my little sweetpea?' Rosie asked, looking down at her tummy. Barnaby nodded his head up and down and let out a sleepy yawn. The day was growing cool, and the golden sun dipped low behind the hills. Rosie gave a gentle, rocking hop with every step she took, creating a lovely rhythm like a lullaby. Barnaby closed his heavy eyes, feeling safe, warm, and loved inside his cozy pouch. Rosie smiled a gentle motherly smile and hopped softly all the way home.

stories.title: Joey's First Hop
stories.text: The Australian sun was just beginning to peek over the red dirt hills, painting the morning sky with pink and gold. Inside a cozy, warm pouch, a little baby kangaroo named Toby stretched his tiny arms and yawned a big, sleepy yawn. 'Yawn-yawn-yawn,' went Toby as he rubbed his sleepy eyes with his paws. His mama, Matilda, felt a gentle wiggle against her tummy. She stopped hopping and looked down with a loving smile. 'Good morning, my little sleepyhead,' Matilda whispered softly. 'Are you ready to see the big, beautiful world today?' Toby poked his fuzzy little head out of the pouch. The morning air felt cool and fresh on his nose. He sniffed the sweet smell of eucalyptus leaves and damp grass. 'Out? Me?' Toby asked, his big ears twitching with excitement and a tiny bit of shyness. 'Yes, you,' Matilda encouraged, gently nudging him with her soft nose. Toby wiggled his shoulders, squeezed his tummy, and slowly climbed out of the warm pouch. He put one tiny foot on the ground, then the other. The dirt felt bumpy and tickly under his toes. Toby looked down at his tiny feet and then up at his mama. 'My legs feel so wiggly!' Toby giggled. 'That is because they are strong growing legs,' Matilda said proudly. 'Now, let us try a little baby hop together.' Matilda showed him how to bend her knees and spring gently into the air. Toby copied her. He bent his little knees, scrunched up his face, and pushed off the ground. BOOP! He jumped just one inch into the air. It was the smallest hop in the whole wide world, but to Toby, it felt like flying. 'I hopped! Mama, did you see me? I flew like a bird!' Toby cheered, clapping his front paws together in pure delight. Matilda laughed a warm, rumbling laugh. 'You did a magnificent hop, Toby! You are going to be a great jumper.' Toby tried again. BOOP! This time he jumped two whole inches and landed with a happy little thump. He felt brave, strong, and full of joy. After practicing their jumping all morning long, Toby felt his little legs getting tired. He scampered back to his mama, climbed right back into his cozy pouch, and curled up tight. With a happy sigh, Toby closed his eyes, ready to dream of even bigger hops tomorrow.

rhymes.title: Little Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo, hop, hop, hop,
Jump so high and do not stop!
Touch the clouds up in the sky,
Wave to birds as they fly by.

Soft gray fur and twitchy nose,
Big strong feet and fuzzy toes.
In the pouch, you rest your head,
Safe and warm like cozy bed.

Time to bounce across the floor,
Let us hop and play some more.
Left and right and all around,
Barely touching grassy ground.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time for little joey, go!
Curl up tight and close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Jump, Joey, Jump
rhymes.text:
Jump, little joey, jump so high,
Reach your paws up to the sky.
Land so softly on the ground,
Make a happy bouncing sound.

Tail is long and helps you balance,
Hopping is your special talent.
Over bushes, past the trees,
Flying in the morning breeze.

Stop and munch a leaf or two,
That is what good joeys do.
Chew it slow and chew it sweet,
Then you stamp your fuzzy feet.

Time to hop back home to bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.
Snuggle in the pouch so deep,
Close your eyes and go to sleep.

rhymes.title: The Bouncy Outback
rhymes.text:
In the outback red and wide,
Little roo is full of pride.
Bouncing fast and bouncing slow,
Watch the happy creature go.

Big brown eyes and perky ears,
Chasing all away his fears.
With a boing and with a bound,
Joy is scattered all around.

Friends are watching from a tree,
Clapping for the jump they see.
Can you hop just like a roo?
Jump and play the whole day through.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little roo is fast asleep.
Mother holds him safe and tight,
Sleeping softly through the night.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Jumps
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Hops around and has such fun.
Big strong legs and furry feet,
Jumping down the grassy street.

Up into the sky so high,
Reaching for a passing fly.
Down he comes with gentle thump,
Making such a happy jump.

In his mummy's pocket deep,
He curls up and falls asleep.
Safe and warm all through the night,
Till the morning brings the light.

Wake up, joey, time to play,
Hopping through another day.
Boing and bounce across the floor,
Ready now to jump some more.

rhymes.title: Bouncy Pouch
rhymes.text:
See the kangaroo go hop,
Never stopping, never stop.
Long tail swinging in the air,
Leaping here and leaping there.

On the grass and in the green,
Best jumper you've ever seen.
Ears go floppy as he flies,
Looking at the sunny skies.

Tucked away inside his pouch,
Never makes a single ouch.
A tiny baby peeks her head,
Leaving her soft grassy bed.

Bounce and hop and skip along,
Singing out a happy song.
Kangaroo is full of cheer,
Best hopper of the year.

rhymes.title: Hop, Hop, Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Jump up high and touch the cloud,
Make a happy hopping sound.
Kangaroo is strong and fast,
Having such a gentle blast.

Over bushes, over stones,
Hear the happy meadow tones.
Big brown paws upon the ground,
Leaping with a joyful bound.

Baby rides inside the pouch,
Resting safe without a slouch.
Mummy hops to find a tree,
Happy as a bird is free.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that they'll not forget.
Time to rest the bouncy feet,
Sleeping in their cozy seat.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Bounces High
rhymes.text:
Little joey jumps around,
Barely touching grassy ground.
With his two big furry feet,
Hopping down the dusty street.

Up and over logs he goes,
With a button on his nose.
In his pouch, a toy is kept,
While the sleepy koala slept.

Round the tree and past the lake,
Watch the little ripples shake.
Now he stops to take a rest,
In the warm and cozy nest.

Twinkle stars begin to gleam,
Joey has a jumping dream.
Close your eyes and time for bed,
With a pillow for your head.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Little Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Bounce, bounce, kangaroo,
I can hop and so can you!
Up into the sunny sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.

Down below the flowers grow,
Making such a lovely show.
Little joey laughs with glee,
Jumping by the gum tree tree.

Now he bends his knees so low,
Ready for another go.
Faster, faster, off he flies,
Reaching for the happy skies.

Safe inside his mama's care,
Blowing kisses in the air.
Now the day is done and bright,
Say a happy, sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: The Pouch So Soft and Warm
rhymes.text:
Kangaroo has feet so big,
Dancing an Australian jig.
Hopping through the golden sand,
In the happy animal land.

Carries baby in her pouch,
Sitting on a mossy couch.
Baby looks out at the sun,
Thinking jumping is so fun.

Wind is blowing through his ears,
Chasing all the little fears.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.

Dreams of bouncing very high,
Touching all the starry sky.
Rest your paws and close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so sweet,
Jumping on your furry feet.
Hopping high and hopping low,
Watch the little baby go.
In the pouch you like to stay,
Resting through the sunny day.
Then you pop your furry head,
Leaping from your cozy bed.
Over bushes, through the grass,
See the happy creature pass.
With a wiggle of your nose,
Up and down the forest goes.
Big brown eyes and giant ears,
Cheering up your forest peers.
Time to sleep and time to rest,
Snuggle in your mama's chest.

rhymes.title: Bounce to the Moon
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop across the floor,
Kangaroo wants to explore.
Up into the sky so bright,
Bouncing in the morning light.
Long tail helps you stand up tall,
Never let yourself down fall.
Touch the clouds up in the blue,
Just like happy kangaroos.
Spin around and take a bow,
Time to stop and listen now.
Crickets sing a gentle tune,
Underneath the silver moon.
Time for little joey eyes,
Closing down beneath the skies.
Dreaming of a sunny hop,
Until morning bids you stop.

rhymes.title: The Joey's Song
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Jumping is so much fun.
Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as you can see.
Land upon your fuzzy feet,
On the grass so soft and sweet.
Mama smiles and watches you,
Bouncing all the morning through.
Wiggle ears and twitch your nose,
From your head down to your toes.
Laughing as you tumble down,
Best jumper in all the town.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little joey sleep.
Close your eyes and dream away,
Till the golden break of day.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Hopping Fast
rhymes.text:
Little joey, soft and sweet,
Jumping high on furry feet.
Through the grass you love to bound,
Making such a happy sound.

Up into the sunny air,
With the wind right in your hair.
Down you land upon the ground,
Looking all around, around.

Time to rest your little head,
In a cozy, sleepy bed.
Mama hugs you nice and tight,
Kissing you a sweet good-night.

Stars are shining in the sky,
While the gentle breezes sigh.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little kangaroo, sleep tight.

rhymes.title: Hop, Hop, Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
See the kangaroo go hop,
Never ready yet to stop.
Big long tail helps her to stay,
Balanced nicely all the day.

Through the yellow outback grass,
Watch her as she swiftly pass.
Big strong legs go bending low,
Where she leaps, she loves to go.

Baby joey in the pouch,
Looking from his cozy couch.
Peeking out to see the sun,
Thinking jumping looks so fun.

Now the day is almost done,
Say goodbye to golden sun.
Time to rest your sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.

rhymes.title: The Outback Dance
rhymes.text:
Hear the thump upon the floor,
Hopping near the cabin door.
It is Joey, full of grace,
Running through the sunny place.

Jump up high and touch the cloud,
Call out to your friends aloud.
Spin around and tap your toes,
Right up to your furry nose.

Kangaroo is jumping fast,
Having such a joyful blast.
Landing softly on the earth,
Filled with happiness and mirth.

Now the jumping time is through,
Time to sleep for little roo.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Till another sunny day.

rhymes.title: Little Joey
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Hop around and have some fun.
Bend your knees and jump so high,
Reach right up and touch the sky.
Soft brown fur and floppy ears,
Bouncing through the forest clears.
In the pouch you rest so sweet,
Rest your tired furry feet.
Mama watches from afar,
Shining like a little star.
Time to sleep and close your eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Dream of hopping far away,
Till the waking of the day.
Goodnight, joey, sleep till dawn,
While the quiet night goes on.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Kangaroo, Bounce
rhymes.text:
See the kangaroo go hop,
Jumping up and will not stop.
Over bushes, over stones,
With his big and sturdy bones.
Tail is long and helps him stand,
In this sunny outback land.
Up he goes into the air,
Wind is blowing through his hair.
Down he lands upon the floor,
Ready to jump even more.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
As he plays the day away.
Happy hopper, big and strong,
Singing out a happy song.
Now he rests upon the grass,
Watching all the shadows pass.

rhymes.title: Pouch of Gold
rhymes.text:
In the cozy pouch so deep,
Baby joey falls asleep.
Rocking gently, back and forth,
Going south and going north.
Mama hops with gentle grace,
Finding such a quiet place.
Leaves are green and sky is blue,
Kangaroo is saying boo!
Little nose and whiskers twitch,
Leaping over every ditch.
Safe and warm and tucked away,
Till the end of active play.
Close your eyes and take a rest,
Mommy's pouch is still the best.
Dream of jumping far and wide,
With your mother right beside.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Roo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so bright,
Jumping in the morning light.
Bouncing high and bouncing low,
Watch the happy baby go.

Big green grass and yellow sun,
Jumping is so much fun.
Over rocks and flowers too,
Way to go, sweet kangaroo!

Flopsy ears and fuzzy feet,
Making little friends to meet.
Twitch your nose and give a smile,
Rest and sit a little while.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Close your eyes and time to rest,
Little roo, you are the best.

rhymes.title: In Mama's Pouch
rhymes.text:
Warm and cozy, safe and deep,
Where the baby goes to sleep.
Mama holds her little one,
Now that playing time is done.

Hop along the dusty track,
Riding safely on her back.
Peeking out to see the day,
While the other animals play.

Soft fur hugging all around,
Not a single scary sound.
Rocking gently left and right,
Sleeping softly through the night.

Morning sun begins to glow,
Time to wake, sweet roo, hello!
Jump back out and start to play,
Have a happy, joyful day.

rhymes.title: The Boing Song
rhymes.text:
Hear the sound of big feet thump,
Watch the kangaroo jump, jump!
Up into the sky so blue,
He can jump as high as you.

Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as any tree!
Land with safety on the floor,
Then go jumping even more.

Wiggle ears and shake your tail,
Sailing like a furry whale.
Round the bush and past the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.

Now the jumping time is through,
Time to cuddle, roo, roo, roo.
Rest your legs and hug your mom,
Safe inside her loving arm.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Joey
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, little kangaroo,
Jumping high the whole day through.
Big strong feet and fuzzy toes,
Where you bounce, nobody knows.

Jump across the grassy land,
Landing softly on the sand.
Wiggle ears both pink and sweet,
Using nimble hopping feet.

Up into the sunny sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds go by.
Now it is time to rest your head,
In your cozy mommy bed.

Close your eyes and softly sleep,
While the stars begin to peep.
Dream of bouncing high and low,
Sleep well, little baby joey, so.

rhymes.title: Pocket Full of Joy
rhymes.text:
Kangaroo has a pocket deep,
Where a little friend can sleep.
Soft and warm and cozy too,
Bestest pouch for me and you.

Hop along the dusty track,
With a baby on your back.
Peeking out to see the sun,
Having lots of bouncing fun.

Round the tree and past the lake,
What a lovely trip to make.
Swinging tail to help you go,
Fast or very, very slow.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Time to say a sweet goodnight.
Pocket tucked away so tight,
Sleeping softly till the light.

rhymes.title: Bouncy Paws
rhymes.text:
Bouncy paws upon the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
One, two, three and up you spring,
Like a bird without a wing.

Over clover, past the stream,
Life is like a happy dream.
Big brown eyes and furry face,
Hopping all around the place.

Catch the breeze and touch the sky,
Let the feathered birds fly by.
Never stop the cheerful play,
Running through the sunny day.

Shadows lengthen on the floor,
We will jump and play no more.
Snuggle close and rest your paws,
Underneath the leafy shaws.

rhymes.title: Jump, Little Roo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo can hop,
Jumping high and will not stop.
Over bushes, through the trees,
Sailing on the gentle breeze.

Soft brown fur and whiskers long,
Singing out a happy song.
Big strong legs that bend so low,
Watch the happy kangaroo go!

In the pouch, a cozy space,
Safe and warm in every place.
Time to rest and time to play,
All throughout the sunny day.

Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Kangaroos are oh so sweet!
Jump around and shout out wee,
As happy as can ever be.

rhymes.title: The Bouncing Game
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop across the floor,
Kangaroo wants to explore.
Big fat tail helps him to stand,
In this sunny, lovely land.

Up and down and all around,
Barely even touching ground.
Friendly smile upon his face,
Running in a joyful race.

Little joey looks ahead,
Time to bounce to cozy bed.
Snuggly pouch is soft and deep,
Ready now for gentle sleep.

Close your eyes and dream of jumping,
While the happy heart is thumping.
Goodnight, joey, time to rest,
Sleeping in your mama's nest.

rhymes.title: Pouch of Gold
rhymes.text:
Look across the grassy plain,
Dancing in the golden rain.
There is furry kangaroo,
Jumping right in front of you.

One two three and four and five,
Glad to be so much alive!
Leaping over yellow flowers,
Playing games for many hours.

Touch his nose and pat his head,
Time to tuck him into bed.
Mama's pouch is warm and tight,
Keeping little roo just right.

Stars are shining in the sky,
As the sleepy clouds float by.
Quiet now and go to sleep,
While the little roos count sheep.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Little Joey
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so sweet,
Jumping on your furry feet.
Hopping high up in the air,
Showing all your joyful flair.
In the pouch you like to ride,
Snuggled safely warm inside.
Ears so big and nose so pink,
Winking with a little blink.
Land upon the grassy ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Leaping over rocks and trees,
Feeling like a gentle breeze.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Hopping right into your bed.
Dreaming of the sunny day,
When you wake to leap and play.

rhymes.title: The Out Back Jump
rhymes.text:
See the kangaroo go hop,
Never ready for a stop.
Big long legs and heavy tail,
Down the sunny sandy trail.
Through the grass and past the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as you can see!
Land with a soft thud and thump,
Taking such a funny jump.
Mama smiles and calls your name,
Joining in the leaping game.
Twitch your nose and shake your ears,
Waving to your forest cheers.
Now the stars begin to glow,
Time to rock back to and fro.

rhymes.title: Pouch Full of Sunshine
rhymes.text:
Kangaroo jumps up and down,
Best jumper in all the town.
Soft brown fur and eyes so bright,
Hopping in the golden light.
Carrying a treasure toy,
Bringing every heart much joy.
Bounce across the yellow plain,
Dancing in the gentle rain.
Hide inside a cozy pouch,
Resting softly on the couch.
Friends are waiting in the sun,
Time to play and have some fun.
Leap across the grassy floor,
Always wanting to do more.
Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying to the world goodnight.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
See the little kangaroo,
Hoping in the morning dew.
Big strong legs and furry feet,
Jumping down the sunny street.

Boing and bouncing all around,
Barely touching on the ground.
Soft warm pouch to rest your head,
Better than a cozy bed.

Twitch your nose and flap your ears,
Chasing all away your fears.
Jump up high into the air,
Showing everybody there.

Now it is a sleepy night,
Stars are shining big and bright.
Fold your paws and close your eyes,
Dreaming of the morning skies.

rhymes.title: The Joey's Big Jump
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Having lots of bouncing fun.
Pushing off the red dirt floor,
Jumping higher than before.

Through the grass and past the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Landing softly with a thump,
Making such a happy jump.

Mama watches from afar,
Shinning like a guiding star.
Calls the little one to rest,
In the pouch she loves the best.

Snuggled deep and cozy too,
Sleepy little kangaroo.
Rest your legs and quiet paws,
Dreaming of the woodland saws.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Bounce, Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Bounce, bounce, kangaroo,
Tell me what you like to do.
I like jumping up so high,
Reaching for the big blue sky.

With a wiggle of my nose,
And a tickle on my toes.
I can hop across the land,
Over every piece of sand.

Friends are watching as I go,
Moving fast and moving slow.
Clapping paws and shouting yay,
Playing games throughout the day.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in the town.
Joey curls up in the pouch,
Far away from any couch.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Hopping
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Time to jump and time for fun.
Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as you can see.

Big brown ears that wiggle round,
Big soft feet upon the ground.
Through the grass you leap and play,
Hopping all the sunny day.

In a pouch so warm and deep,
Time to rest and time to sleep.
Close your eyes and dream a dream,
Floating down a sleepy stream.

Mama watches from above,
Filled with gentle hugs and love.
Stars are shining bright and deep,
Little kangaroo, fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Bounce, Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Kangaroo, kangaroo, big and tall,
Do you want to play with a ball?
Bounce so high up in the air,
Show your fluffy tail right there.

Over the rocks and through the trees,
Feeling the soft and gentle breeze.
Land on the grass with a happy thud,
Right beside the golden mud.

Little paws and happy smiles,
Hopping many happy miles.
Twirl around and touch the sky,
Watch the little birds fly by.

Now it is time to rest your feet,
Find a cozy place so sweet.
Curl up tight and sleep till dawn,
While the stars keep shining on.

rhymes.title: The Jumping Game
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop goes the kangaroo,
Jumping high for me and you.
Down the dusty outback track,
With a baby in her pack.

Little joey peeks his head,
Ready for his cozy bed.
Waves a paw to say good day,
While the emus run and play.

Jump across the yellow sand,
In this happy animal land.
Feel the sunshine on your face,
Moving at a bouncy pace.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Saying everybody good night.
Close your eyes and slumber deep,
Kangaroo is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so sweet,
Jumping high upon your feet.
In the grass and in the sun,
Having lots of bouncy fun.

Long ears twitching in the breeze,
Hop around the green gum trees.
Soft pouch holding cozy things,
Happy joy each minute brings.

Big strong legs go up and down,
Best jumper in all the town.
Now the sun is going low,
Time for little roo to go.

Curl up tight and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.
Dream of bouncing in the light,
Little kangaroo, goodnight.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Bounce, Joey
rhymes.text:
See the little joey hop,
Never wanting it to stop.
Bouncing over every stone,
Making this green world his own.

Up into the air he flies,
Reaching for the sunny skies.
Land with such a gentle thud,
Playing softly in the mud.

Mother watches from afar,
Shining like a guiding star.
Calls him back to rest his head,
In his cozy grassy bed.

Time to close the sleepy eyes,
Underneath the twilight skies.
Dreaming of the morning dew,
Sleep well, little kangaroo.

rhymes.title: Hop, Hop, Hooray!
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop goes the kangaroo,
Jumping all around for you.
With a wiggle of his nose,
To the tallest hill he goes.

Look at how he leaps so high,
Almost touching up the sky.
Landing softly on the ground,
Making not a single sound.

Friends are cheering from the tree,
Happy as can ever be.
Dance and jump until it is night,
Bathed in silver moonlight light.

Time to cuddle in the pouch,
Far away from any slouch.
Rest your legs and sleep till dawn,
When another day comes on.

rhymes.title: Hop, Little Roo
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so sweet,
Jumping on your big back feet.
Up you go into the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds drift by.

Time to bounce across the floor,
Let us hop and play some more.
Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as you can see.

In your mama's pouch so warm,
Safe from wind and cozy storm.
Now you rest your sleepy head,
Tucked inside your furry bed.

Twinkle stars begin to peep,
Little Roo is fast asleep.
Dreams of bouncing in the sun,
Till tomorrow's day is done.

rhymes.title: Bounce to the Moon
rhymes.text:
Kangaroo, kangaroo, in the grass,
Watch the yellow ladybugs pass.
Kick your legs and give a bound,
Lift your toes right off the ground.

Spin around and touch your nose,
Wiggle all your fuzzy toes.
Take a leap and touch the sky,
Wave to birds that flutter by.

Land with thump upon the floor,
Do not stop, lets hop some more.
Big green tree and smiling sun,
Every day is filled with fun.

Now the moon is shining bright,
Say to kangaroo goodnight.
Close your eyes and softly rest,
Sleeping in your furry nest.

rhymes.title: The Happy Joey
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the pouch,
Never grumpy, never grouch.
Pop your head out, say hello,
To the flowers in a row.

Jump across the grassy lane,
Dancing in the gentle rain.
Big long tail helps you to stay,
Balanced nicely while you play.

Clap your paws and shout out loud,
Make your kangaroo mom proud.
Bounce from here to over there,
Jumping high into the air.

Now the twilight shadows fall,
Quiet whispers greet us all.
Snuggle deep and dream away,
Till the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Bouncing High
rhymes.text:
Little joey, hopping fast,
Springing past the green soft grass.
Up into the sky so blue,
Happy little kangaroo.

Bend your knees and give a push,
Jumping over every bush.
Landing softly with a thud,
Playing in the warm red mud.

Flppy ears and shiny eyes,
Looking at the sunny skies.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Hopping right back to your bed.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Little joey goes to sleep.
Goodnight moon and goodnight sun,
Hopping time is nearly done.

rhymes.title: In Mama's Pouch
rhymes.text:
Cozy pouch of furry wool,
Keeping little baby full
Of sweet dreams and feelings bright,
Safe and warm throughout the night.

Mama hops across the land,
Over rocks and yellow sand.
Rocking gently up and down,
Far away from any town.

Poke your nose out, see the day,
Watch the little birdies play.
Then tuck back inside to rest,
'Cause the pouch is simply best.

Sleepy eyes begin to close,
Right down to your little toes.
Dream of hopping through the sky,
Mama's pouch is safe and high.

rhymes.title: The Boing-Boing Song
rhymes.text:
Boing and jump and leap around,
Barely touching on the ground.
Kangaroo has feet so big,
Dancing with a little twig.

Left foot, right foot, off we go,
Moving fast and moving slow.
Over hills and valleys wide,
With a happy hop inside.

Friends are cheering all around,
As you leap above the ground.
Spinning in the sunny air,
With a smile so bright and fair.

Now the jumping day is done,
We have had so much good fun.
Sit down softly on the floor,
Ready for a slumber more.

rhymes.title: The Happy Little Roo
rhymes.text:
See the happy little roo,
Hopping down the avenue.
With his two big furry feet,
Looking for a tasty treat.

Up and down and all around,
Barely even touching ground.
Big long tail to help him stay,
Jumping all the live-long day.

In his mama's pocket deep,
Safe and cozy fast asleep.
Dreams of bouncing in the sun,
Having lots of jumping fun.

When the morning light is clear,
He will give a happy cheer.
Boing and jump and skip and play,
Have a super happy day!

rhymes.title: Bounce, Roo, Bounce
rhymes.text:
Little kangaroo so sweet,
Jumping on your heavy feet.
Up into the sky you go,
Watching all the world below.

Over bushes, over stones,
Hear the happy gentle tones.
Flapping ears of velvety brown,
Never want to tumble down.

Find a friend to share the game,
Call each other by their name.
Wombat runs and koala sleeps,
While the happy kangaroo leaps.

Now the stars begin to peep,
Time for little roos to sleep.
Close your eyes and rest your head,
Tucked inside your cozy bed.

rhymes.title: Hop, Hop, Hooray!
rhymes.text:
Hop, hop, hop goes the kangaroo,
Jumping through the morning dew.
Twirling round and turning fast,
Having such a joyful blast.

Strong back legs and tummy pocket,
Shooting upward like a rocket.
Looking at the trees so green,
Best jumper you've ever seen.

Stop to munch some tender grass,
Watch the fluffy clouds pass.
Then it's time to jump again,
Over hill and down the glen.

Sun is shining bright and high,
Birds are singing in the sky.
Kangaroo is full of cheer,
Best little friend right here.

rhymes.title: Little Joey Jumper
rhymes.text:
Little joey in the sun,
Time to jump and time for fun.
Bend your knees and count to three,
Jump as high as you can see!

Strong back legs go push and spring,
Hear the happy birdies sing.
Through the grass and past the tree,
Happy as a bug can be.

Long tail wagging left and right,
Landing softly, what a sight!
Now it is time to rest your head,
In your cozy mommy bed.

Twinkle stars are shining bright,
Kangaroo, sleep tight all night.
Dream of bouncing to the moon,
Morning sun will wake you soon.

rhymes.title: Bounce, Bounce, Kangaroo
rhymes.text:
Hopping down the dusty track,
Momma has a pouch of sack.
Little baby peeks his head,
Ready now to leave his bed.

Bounce and jump across the floor,
Looking for a world to explore.
Big brown ears begin to shake,
What a lovely day to make!

Jump across the yellow flower,
Playing games this happy hour.
Soft green leaves upon the tree,
Swaying gently wild and free.

Time to turn and turn around,
Make a happy little sound.
Hop back home where it is warm,
Safe away from wind and storm.

rhymes.title: The Happy Hopping Song
rhymes.text:
Up and down the red dirt hill,
Sometimes fast and sometimes still.
See the kangaroo go bound,
All across the grassy ground.

Fluffy ears and nose so pink,
Drinking water at the brink.
Splash the water with a paw,
Cutest baby you ever saw.

Springing high up in the air,
Jumping without any care.
Land on feet and wobble twice,
Bouncing is so very nice.

Sun is sinking in the west,
Time for joey now to rest.
Snuggle in the warm pouch tight,
Say a sleepy, sweet goodnight.

stories.title: Pip's Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the cold and snowy land of Antarctica, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black-and-white feathers, tiny orange feet, and a very big curiosity. Today was a very special day because Pip was going on his very first big walk across the sparkling ice. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle,' went Pip's little feet as he moved along. He looked at the big, white mountains of snow. He looked at the bright, blue sky. And then, right in front of him, he saw something amazing. It was a round, smooth, shiny gray pebble! It sparkled in the winter sun like a little star. Pip waddled up to the pebble and gave it a gentle tap with his beak. 'Clack!' said the pebble. Pip smiled. He decided right then and there that this pebble was his new best friend. He bent down, scooped the shiny pebble up with his beak, and held it safely. Now, how was he going to carry it home? Pip tried to balance it on his flipper, but it rolled right off. Oh no! 'Splat!' went the pebble into the soft snow. Pip blinked his big round eyes. He didn't give up. He bent his neck down low, rolled the pebble carefully with his beak, and waddled all the way back to his cozy nest. When he reached home, he tucked the shiny pebble right under his warm tummy. His mom and dad penguin smiled proudly at him. 'Good job, Pip!' they honked. Pip closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of all the fun adventures he and his shiny pebble would have tomorrow. The cold wind howled outside, but in his snug nest, little Pip was as warm and happy as could be. He gave one last little happy wiggle, hugged his pebble tight, and snuggled deep into the snowy dreamland.

stories.title: Pico's Slide
stories.text: Down by the great blue ocean, where the icebergs floated like giant marshmallow castles, lived a little penguin named Pico. Pico loved to play. But more than anything in the whole wide world, Pico loved to slide! Every morning, Pico would waddle as fast as his little flippers could carry him up the highest snow hill. 'Hooray!' he would peep, looking down at the long, slippery path of ice below. Today, Pico invited his fluffy friend Barnaby the seal to join the fun. 'Ready, set, go!' cried Pico. And with a joyful wiggle, Pico plopped right onto his tummy. Whoosh! Down the slippery ice hill he went, sliding faster and faster. 'Wheeeee!' shouted Pico, his flippers stretched out wide like airplane wings. The cold wind tickled his face and made his eyes water with happy tears. Whoosh! He zoomed past giant snowbanks and over little bumps, spinning around in a joyful circle. At the bottom of the hill, Pico did a funny little flip and landed right on his fuzzy bottom in a soft pile of powdery snow. 'Ta-da!' he giggled, shaking the white flakes off his head. Barnaby the seal clapped his flippers together. 'That looked so fun!' Barnaby cheered. Pico stood up, brushed himself off, and looked back up the big hill. His little tummy was warm, his heart was happy, and his feet were already itching to go again. 'Let's do it again!' Pico honked happily. Hand in flipper, the two little friends waddled back up the snowy slope for another thrilling ride. They slid and slid until the golden sun began to dip low in the sky, painting the clouds in shades of pink and orange. It was the best day ever.

stories.title: Little Penguin's Lost Feather
stories.text: Deep in the frosty snowfields, a baby penguin named Percy was getting ready for bed. He fluffed his feathers and gave a big yawn. But wait! Something felt a little bit breezy. Percy looked down at his soft tummy and let out a little gasp. One of his fluffiest, softest feathers was missing! 'Oh dear,' whispered Percy. 'Where did my feather go?' He turned around in a circle, but his feather was nowhere to be seen. Just then, a gentle breeze blew by, carrying a little gray fluff through the air. 'There it goes!' cried Percy. He began to waddle after the floating feather. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle!' went his little orange feet. The feather floated up, up, up over a little snow mound. Percy scrambled up the mound. The feather drifted down, down, down past an icy blue cave. Percy peeked inside the cave, but it wasn't in there. The little feather danced in the wind, playing a fun game of hide-and-seek. Percy giggled. It was almost like the feather wanted to play! Finally, the soft feather floated gently downward and landed right on top of a sleeping polar bear's fluffy white nose. 'Achoo!' sneezed the polar bear, waking up with a start. The sneeze sent Percy's feather flying back into the air, right toward waiting flippers. Snap! Percy caught his feather safely in his beak. He let out a sigh of relief. He hugged the soft little feather close to his chest and waddled happily back to his cozy nest. The polar bear waved goodnight, and Percy tucked himself into bed. His feather was safely home, and so was he. With a happy smile, little Percy closed his eyes, ready for sweet dreams under the twinkling polar stars.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in the sparkly white snow, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip loved to waddle. Waddle, waddle, waddle! His feet went patter-pat on the ice. One morning, the wind blew very hard. Wooosh! Pip shivered. Brrrr! 'I am cold,' said Pip. Mama Penguin smiled and gave him a soft, bright blue scarf. Pip wrapped the scarf around his neck. It was so cozy! Pip went outside to play with his best friend, Penny Polar Bear. Penny was building a big snow castle. 'Look at my scarf, Penny!' said Pip proudly. Penny clapped her paws. 'It is so blue, like the deep ocean!' Pip wanted to help build the castle. He waddled over to a pile of fluffy snow. He scooped up snow with his flippers. Pat, pat, pat! But oh no, the long blue scarf dipped into the snow. 'Uh-oh,' whispered Pip. He pulled the scarf up, but it had a big clump of white snow stuck to the end. Pip giggled. He shook his head, and the snow fell off with a soft plop. *Splat!* 'Let us slide!' shouted Penny. Up, up, up the snow hill they climbed. Whee! Pip slid down on his tummy. Swoosh! The blue scarf trailed behind him like a magical kite tail. It flew in the air. Flutter, flutter, flutter! Pip laughed all the way to the bottom. *Splash!* They landed right near the chilly blue water. A friendly seal popped his head up and barked, 'Hello, Pip! Nice scarf!' Pip waved his flipper. 'Thank you!' The sun began to set, painting the sky pink and orange. Pip felt warm and happy inside his tummy and all around his neck. He waddled back home to his cozy ice cave. Mama Penguin was waiting with a fish snack. *Yum, yum!* Pip unwrapped his scarf and folded it neatly. 'Goodnight, my little blue scarf,' whispered Pip as he closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of more snowy adventures.

stories.title: Pico Learns to Swim
stories.text: Deep in the frosty land of Antarctica, a little penguin named Pico lived on a big sheet of ice. Pico had shiny black and white feathers and two little webbed feet. Every day, Pico watched the big penguins dive into the deep, sparkling blue ocean. Splash! They would swim so fast, looking like flying torpedoes. Pico wanted to swim, too. But Pico was just a tiny bit scared. The water looked very big, and Pico was very small. 'Come on, Pico!' called Papa Penguin from the edge of the ice. Pico waddled to the edge. Waddle, waddle, waddle. He looked down. The water was cold and deep. He dipped one webbed foot into the water. Brrr! Pico quickly pulled his foot back. 'It is too cold!' squeaked Pico. Papa Penguin smiled gently. 'Your feathers are waterproof, Pico. They keep you safe and dry underneath.' Pico took a deep breath. He waddled a little closer. He looked at his friend, a little blue fish swimming by, waving its fin. *Glub, glub!* Pico bent his knees. He raised his little flippers high in the air. One, two, three, jump! Pico tumbled into the water. *Splash!* At first, everything was bubbly and blue. Pico opened his eyes. Wow! The underwater world was amazing. Tiny bubbles floated past his beak. Pico flapped his flippers. Up and down, left and right. Guess what? Pico was swimming! He did not sink. He zoomed through the water like a happy little rocket. *Zoom, zoom!* He looped around an underwater rock and popped his head back up into the air. 'Papa! Look at me! I am swimming!' cheered Pico. Papa Penguin clapped his flippers together. *Clap, clap, clap!* Pico swam in circles, feeling brave and strong. Swimming was the most fun thing in the whole wide world. When it was time to go back to the ice, Pico hopped out, shook his feathers until they were fluffy and dry, and gave Papa a big penguin hug.

stories.title: The Lost Fish
stories.text: Barnaby was a very helpful little penguin. He lived near a big iceberg where the snowy wind whispered softly. One sunny afternoon, Barnaby was looking for shiny pebbles to add to his special collection. Click, clack, went the pebbles in his flippers. Suddenly, he heard a funny sound coming from behind a snowbank. *Squeak!* Barnaby stopped waddling. He tilted his head to the side. *Squeak, squeak!* Barnaby peeked behind the fluffy white snow. There, lying on a patch of ice, was a tiny, sparkly silver fish. But this was no ordinary fish—it was a little balloon fish that had drifted away from its school! The little fish looked up with big, round, shiny eyes. 'Oh dear,' bubbled the fish, 'I am lost, and I cannot find my way back to the deep blue sea.' Barnaby felt a little wiggle of worry in his tummy. He wanted to help his new tiny friend. 'Do not worry,' said Barnaby in his deepest, bravest penguin voice. 'I will help you find your family!' Barnaby carefully scooped up the tiny fish in his webbed flippers. The fish felt cool and tickly against his feathers. Barnaby started to waddle toward the water. Waddle, waddle, waddle, go his little feet. He hopped down a small snow step. *Hop!* He slid across a patch of smooth, shiny ice. *Swoosh!* The tiny fish giggled. 'Whee! This is fun!' Soon, they reached the edge of the icy shore. The big ocean waves gently kissed the ice. *Swish, swish.* Not far away, a whole group of sparkly silver fish were swimming in a circle, looking for their missing friend. Barnaby gently lowered his flippers into the water. The little fish leaped out with a happy flip-flop! *Splash!* The fish joined its family and swam in a happy circle. The little fish poked its head out of the water and blew a bubble heart. *Pop!* 'Thank you, Barnaby!' it called out. Barnaby waved both of his flippers high in the air. 'You are very welcome!' he chirped happily, feeling like the proudest, kindest penguin in the whole snowy world.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a snowy land filled with sparkling ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had feathers as black as night on his back, a tummy as white as a marshmallow, and the happiest little beak in the whole wide world. Every single morning, the cold wind would go whoosh, and Pip would shiver. Brrr! One sunny morning, Mama Penguin gave Pip a surprise. It was a long, bright blue scarf! It was soft, fuzzy, and smelled like peppermint. Pip wrapped the blue scarf around his neck once, twice, and a third time. He waddled outside to show his best friend, Barnaby Bear. 'Look at my scarf, Barnaby!' Pip squawked happily. 'Waddle-waddle!' Barnaby smiled and said, 'It looks wonderful, Pip! It matches the sky.' Pip felt so warm and cozy. He waddled to the top of the snow hill. He wanted to slide down. 'Wheee!' shouted Pip as he zoomed down the slippery ice. Splash! Pip landed right in a soft snowbank. But wait! Where was his blue scarf? Pip looked around. Oh no! The blue scarf was stuck at the top of the hill, blowing in the wind like a little flag. 'Help, my scarf!' cried Pip. Barnaby Bear used his big paws to climb up the hill. He gently picked up the blue scarf. He brought it back down to Pip and wrapped it snugly around the little penguin's neck again. 'Thank you, Barnaby,' Pip chirped, giving his big friend a gentle hug. Together, they waddled across the snowy ice, playing hide-and-seek behind the big white glaciers. Pip was so happy. His tummy was full of yummy fish, his best friend was right by his side, and his neck was as warm as toast. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and orange, Pip yawned a big penguin yawn. He waddled back to his cozy nest, cuddled up close to Mama, and dreamed sweet, happy dreams about his wonderful blue scarf.

stories.title: Pippa's Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Deep down in the frosty south, where the snow sparkled like a million tiny diamonds, lived a little penguin named Pippa. Pippa loved to collect things. She collected fluffy white feathers, bits of green seaweed, and round, smooth pebbles. Today, Pippa was on a very important mission. She wanted to find the shiniest pebble in the whole icy kingdom to give to her papa as a special surprise. Pippa waddled down to the edge of the blue, blue ocean. Waddle-waddle-waddle went her little webbed feet. She looked to the left. She looked to the right. She peered under a big chunk of glittering blue ice. 'Peep-peep!' chirped Pippa. Suddenly, she saw a little glint of silver. Could it be? Pippa hurried over as fast as her little legs could carry her. Buried in the wet sand was a pebble unlike any other. It was round like a button, and it shone in the sunlight just like a star! Pippa reached out her beak and picked it up. It felt smooth and cool. 'I found it! I found the shiniest pebble!' Pippa squawked with joy. She held the precious pebble safely in her beak and waddled all the way home. Papa Penguin was resting on a warm rock, waiting for her. When he saw Pippa coming, he opened his wings wide. Pippa waddled right up to him and dropped the shiny silver pebble right at his webbed feet. Papa's eyes grew big and round. He picked up the pebble and rubbed it gently against his cheek. 'Oh, Pippa,' Papa said warmly, 'this is the most beautiful pebble I have ever seen in my whole life!' Pippa did a happy little dance, flapping her flippers and sliding on her tummy across the snow. 'Slide-wheee!' she giggled. Papa wrapped his warm wing around Pippa, and they sat together, watching the gentle waves roll onto the shore. Pippa felt so proud and loved. She knew that even though she was a very small penguin, she could do big, wonderful things to make the people she loved smile.

stories.title: Pablo's Big Splash
stories.text: Pablo was a baby penguin who lived on a big block of ice. Pablo loved to look at the deep blue ocean. The water looked so sparkly and fun. Other penguins were swimming all around, doing flips and twirls. Splash! Splash! Went their flippers. Pablo wanted to swim too, but he had a tiny problem. Pablo was scared of the water. What if the water was too cold? What if he sank like a heavy stone? Pablo sat on the edge of the ice, hugging his knees and watching. 'Come on, Pablo!' called his friend Penny. 'The water is lovely!' Pablo shook his head. He took a little step back. His flippers felt shaky. Just then, a little red ball bounced across the ice. Boing! Boing! The wind blew the ball, and it rolled right off the edge of the ice and landed plop! in the water. Oh no! That was Pablo's favorite ball. Pablo gasped. He loved that red ball. Without even thinking, Pablo waddled quickly to the very edge of the ice. He leaned down and stretched out his flippers. He reached and reached, but he couldn't quite touch the ball. He had to go into the water. Taking a deep breath, Pablo closed his eyes and jumped. Plop! Into the cold ocean went little Pablo. But wait! Pablo didn't sink. His little webbed feet started to paddle naturally. Kick, kick, kick! His flippers scooped the water. Swish, swish, swish! Pablo opened his eyes. Underwater, everything was bright blue and magical. Silver fish swam past his beak, tickling his feathers. Pablo felt so light, almost like he was flying! He swam right up to the red ball, scooped it up in his beak, and paddled back to the surface. 'I did it! I'm swimming!' Pablo cheered, tossing the ball into the air. Penny clapped her flippers together. 'Hooray, Pablo!' Pablo climbed back onto the ice, shaking the water droplets from his fluffy feathers. He wasn't scared anymore. He was a brave swimming penguin, ready for his next big watery adventure.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly day, in a land of sparkling white snow and deep blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black feathers, a bright yellow beak, and the warmest heart in the whole wide polar world. But even with a warm heart, Pip sometimes felt a little cold on his flippers. One morning, the chilly wind blew extra hard. Whoosh! Pip shivered. Brrr! Just then, his mother waddled over with a surprise. It was a long, bright blue scarf, knit from the softest wool. Pip squeaked with joy. He wrapped the blue scarf around his neck once, twice, and a third time. It felt so cozy! Pip waddled out of his icy nest to show all his friends his wonderful new scarf. First, he waddled over to Penny the polar bear cub. 'Look, Penny!' said Pip, doing a happy little penguin dance. Penny clapped her paws and smiled. 'That blue scarf matches the sky, Pip!' Next, Pip waddled down to the bright blue sea to see Sammy the seal. 'Splash!' went Sammy into the water. Pip wanted to play, but he knew his wool scarf might get wet. What should he do? Pip carefully unwrapped his scarf and gently folded it on a soft snowbank. 'Watch my scarf, please!' he called to Sammy. Then, Pip dove into the cold ocean water. Whee! Pip zoomed through the waves, doing flips and spins. He kicked his little flippers and played tag with the silver fish. Swimming was so much fun! After a little while, Pip felt nice and warm from his swim. He hopped back up onto the snowbank and shook the cold water right off his feathers, just like a furry umbrella. Shake, shake, shake! Pip picked up his blue scarf and wrapped it snugly around his neck again. The wool was dry and kept him snug as he waddled back home to his cozy nest. The sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and purple. Pip curled up tight, tucked his beak under his blue scarf, and closed his eyes. He had the happiest penguin dreams about swimming in the sea and wearing his favorite blue scarf.

stories.title: Pico's Red Boots
stories.text: Deep in the southern snow, where the ice sparkled like diamonds, lived a curious little penguin named Pico. Pico loved to explore. He waddled here, he waddled there, always looking for a new adventure. One afternoon, while peeking behind a big block of blue ice, Pico found something marvelous. It was a pair of bright red boots! They were small, shiny, and just the right size for penguin feet. Pico gasped. 'Oh, boy!' he chirped. He stepped his left foot into the first boot. Squish! Then he stepped his right foot into the second boot. Squish! Pico looked down at his feet. They looked so red and bright against the white snow. He tried to take a step, but—slip, slide, whoops! Pico tumbled right onto his fluffy tummy. Giggling, he pushed himself back up. Walking in boots was a little bit tricky! Pico decided to practice. He took one slow step, then another. Left boot, right boot. Tap, tap, tap! The boots made a funny clicking sound on the hard ice. Pico thought it sounded like music. He waddled over to his friend Oliver the owl, who was resting on an ice mound. 'Hoot hoot! What are those shiny red things on your feet, Pico?' asked Oliver, blinking his big round eyes. 'They are my magic walking boots!' said Pico proudly. Pico showed Oliver how he could march in a circle. Left, right, left, right! Oliver hooted with delight. Suddenly, a little snowflake drifted down, then another, and another. It started to snow softly. Pico loved the snow, but his feet were getting a little tired from all the marching. He decided it was time to head home for fish supper. Pico waddled all the way back to his cozy nest, his red boots going click-clack, click-clack every step of the way. When he got home, his mother helped him slide his flippers right out of the boots. Pico gave his boots a big hug. They had made his day so special. He curled up in his warm nest, leaving his bright red boots right by the entrance, ready for another fun adventure tomorrow.

stories.title: The Great Ice Slide
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the big snowy hill, making the ice sparkle like a million tiny stars. A little penguin named Barnaby waddled to the very top of the hill. Today was the day! Barnaby had built the biggest, shiniest ice slide in the whole neighborhood. It curved this way, it curved that way, and it ended in a soft snowbank. Barnaby looked down the slide and felt a tiny flutter in his tummy. It looked high! But Barnaby was a brave little penguin. He fluffed out his feathers, put his flippers straight out to the sides like airplane wings, and sat right down on his bottom. 'Here I go!' he cheered. Whoosh! Barnaby slid down the ice. The wind rushed past his face, making his black-and-white feathers tickle. Wheeeee! He zoomed around the curve, sliding faster and faster. With a gentle plop, Barnaby landed right in the middle of a fluffy white snowbank. Snow puffed up all around him like a little white cloud. Barnaby popped his head out of the snow, wearing a crown of white powder. He burst out laughing. That was the most fun he had ever had! Soon, all his penguin friends heard the laughter and waddled over to see what was happening. There was Bella, and Toby, and little Lily. 'Can we try?' asked Bella, her eyes shining with excitement. 'Of course!' said Barnaby, climbing right back up the hill. One by one, the little penguins took turns on the great ice slide. Toby went swoosh! Bella went zooming! Little Lily went giggling all the way down. They held flippers and made a long penguin train, sliding down together in a big happy group. Splash, zoom, whee! The snowy hill echoed with happy penguin squeaks and joyful chirps all afternoon long. When the sun began to sink low in the sky, turning the clouds orange and pink, the little penguins knew it was time to go home. They waddled back to their nests together, tired and happy, dreaming of the wonderful slides they would take tomorrow.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white snow and deep blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip was round like a roly-poly ball and had the softest black and white feathers. Every morning, Pip loved to slide on his tummy. Whoosh! Down the big snow hill he went, laughing all the way. Today was a extra special day because Mother Penguin had made Pip a brand new gift. It was a long, bright red scarf! The red scarf was as warm as a hug from the sun. Mother Penguin wrapped it gently around Pip's neck. 'Keep warm, my little chick,' she whispered. Pip waddled over to his best friend, Penny the polar bear cub. Penny had thick white fur, but she thought Pip's red scarf looked so jolly. 'Look at me, Penny!' quip Pip, doing a happy little penguin dance. Flap, flap, wiggle, wiggle! Pip waddled this way and that. But oh dear! The scarf was a tiny bit too long. As Pip spun around in a circle, the end of the scarf trailed behind him in the fresh white snow. Drag, drag, went the scarf. Suddenly, Pip tried to run to catch a sliding snowflake, and—oops-a-daisy!—he tripped right over his own scarf! Down he tumbled into a soft, fluffy snowdrift. Pip popped his head out of the snow, blinking his big round eyes. He wasn't hurt at all, but he giggled so hard that his tummy shook. Penny waddled over and gently helped her little friend up. 'Your scarf is very pretty, Pip, but maybe it needs a little tuck,' Penny said with a friendly growl. Together, Penny and Mother Penguin folded the long red scarf neatly so it wouldn't drag on the ground anymore. Now Pip could run, jump, and slide without tripping. He flapped his little flippers and hugged his dear friend Penny. The sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and gold. Pip looked down at his bright red scarf and smiled. It was the best day ever in the snowy wonderland.

stories.title: The Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Deep in the great southern ice sheet, where the wind blew a soft whoosh-whoosh sound, lived a little penguin named Pogo. Pogo was curious about everything. While the other penguins were busy swimming in the cold blue ocean, Pogo loved to go on treasure hunts. He waddled across the crunching snow, looking down at his webbed orange feet. Tap, tap, tap went his beak as he checked behind every block of blue ice. Today, Pogo was looking for the shiniest, smoothest pebble in the whole wide world. Why? Because he wanted to give it to his grand-penguin as a special thank-you gift for telling wonderful bedtime stories about the glowing stars. Pogo looked under a big slippery slope of ice. Nothing there except a sleepy little seal pup snoring softly. He looked behind a tall snow mound. Nothing there except a playful puffin flying by. Pogo let out a little sigh. He sat down on his fuzzy bottom and rested his chin on his flippers. Just then, a tiny sunbeam broke through the cloudy gray sky. It danced across the snow and landed right on something half-buried in the ice. It twinkled like a little diamond! Pogo scrambled up instantly. He waddled over as fast as his short little legs could carry him. He gave a gentle nudge with his beak. Roll, roll, click! Out popped a pebble that was as round as a marble and sparkled with silver specks. It was the most beautiful pebble Pogo had ever laid his eyes on. 'I found it! I found the magic treasure!' Pogo squeaked happily, doing a little hop of joy. He carefully picked up the pebble in his beak, holding it very tightly so it wouldn't roll away. Pogo waddled all the way back to the cozy nesting grounds where his grand-penguin was resting. With a proud little bow, Pogo dropped the shiny pebble right at his grand-penguin's webbed feet. Grand-penguin opened his sleepy eyes, looked at the sparkling stone, and gave Pogo a big, warm penguin cuddle. Pogo closed his eyes and purred like a little motor. He was the happiest little treasure hunter in the whole snowy world.

stories.title: Little Penguin's First Swim
stories.text: The ocean water was as blue as a sapphire, and tiny white waves lapped gently against the edge of the great ice shelf. Today was a very big day for Barnaby, a little penguin with a coat of fluffy gray baby down. Today, Barnaby was going to learn how to swim in the big, deep ocean! Barnaby stood right at the edge of the ice, looking down at the rolling water. His tummy felt full of fluttering butterflies. The water looked so big, and Barnaby was so small. 'Can I really do this?' Barnaby asked, looking up at his father with big, worried eyes. Father Penguin nudged Barnaby gently with his smooth black wing. 'You are a penguin, Barnaby. Swimming is in your heart and in your feathers,' Father said encouragingly. Barnaby took a deep breath. He waddled right to the very edge. One webbed foot stepped forward. Then the other. Splash! Down into the cool, refreshing water went little Barnaby. At first, Barnaby felt a little bit silly and bobbed around like a little cork. But then, he remembered what his father had taught him. He stretched out his little flippers. He kicked his webbed feet. And suddenly—whoosh! Barnaby wasn't sinking; he was flying right through the water!
