It felt just like flying in the sky, only much cooler and wetter. Barnaby did a joyful loop-de-loop under the water. He chased a tiny, darting silver fish that tickled his tummy. He blew a stream of happy bubbles that popped right on the surface. 'Look at me, Daddy! I am swimming!' Barnaby chirped loudly, his voice echoing over the waves. Father Penguin dove into the water right beside him, splashing happily. They swam side by side, making graceful circles in the sparkling sea. When they finally climbed back up onto the warm, safe ice, Barnaby shook his wet feathers until the water droplets flew everywhere like a shower of diamonds. He was tired, and his tummy was wonderfully full of yummy little fish. Barnaby snuggled close to his father, closing his eyes as the gentle sea breeze lulled him to sleep. He couldn't wait to wake up and swim all over again.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a snowy place where the wind went whoosh, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black-and-white feathers, tiny orange feet, and a very big problem. His neck felt cold! Every morning, the icy wind blew right past his beak. Brrr! One sunny afternoon, Pip waddled over to his friend Mama Bear. 'My neck is cold,' squeaked Pip in his tiny penguin voice. Mama Bear smiled a warm, cozy smile. She reached into her basket and pulled out something wonderful. It was a long, bright blue scarf, soft as a fluffy cloud. Pip gasped and clapped his flippers together. 'Ooh! Ahh!' he chirped happily. Mama Bear wrapped the blue scarf around Pip's neck once, twice, three times. It was so snug and warm! Pip waddled down to the slippery blue ice slide. Waddle, waddle, slide! Whee! He zoomed down the snowy hill, his blue scarf flying behind him like a superhero cape. Splash! Pip landed right in the cold ocean water. But wait, his neck stayed nice and toasty! Pip paddled in the water, doing happy little spins. He swam past Sammy Seal, who was balancing a shiny blue ball. 'Look at my scarf!' quacked Pip proudly. Sammy Seal clapped his flippers. 'So warm! So blue!' Then Pip saw his friend Penny Penguin shivering softly. Penny's beak was tapping together. Tap, tap, tap. Pip stopped. He looked at his long, beautiful blue scarf. He looked at Penny. Pip knew just what a good friend should do. He swam over to Penny and unwrapped the scarf from his own neck. He gently wrapped it around Penny's shivering shoulders. Penny's eyes grew wide. 'For me?' she asked. Pip nodded and smiled with his whole beak. 'For you!' Pip chirped. Penny hugged Pip tightly with her flippers. 'Thank you, Pip. Now my neck is warm too!' Even though Pip's scarf was now keeping Penny cozy, Pip realized something even better. Sharing made his heart feel warm, right down to his little orange toes. Hand in flipper, the two happy penguins waddled back home to cuddle with their families as the stars twinkled in the snowy sky.

stories.title: Pippa's Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Deep down in the land of snow and ice, there lived a little girl penguin named Pippa. Pippa loved to collect things. She collected fluffy snowflakes on her beak, slippery bits of ice, and most of all, she collected smooth, round pebbles. Her very favorite place to find pebbles was down by the sparkling blue sea. Every morning, Pippa would waddle down to the water's edge. Waddle, waddle, waddle! She would look left. She would look right. Then, she would look down. One bright morning, Pippa saw something very special. It was tucked right between two big chunks of white ice. It was a pebble, but not just any pebble. It was sparkling silver, shining bright like a little star fallen from the sky! Pippa gasped. She opened her beak wide. 'Squawk!' she cheered. She bent down and picked up the shiny silver pebble in her beak. It was smooth and cool. Pippa decided this pebble was too special to keep all to herself. She wanted to share it with her best friend, Barnaby. Pippa turned around and waddled as fast as her little orange feet could carry her. Waddle, waddle, waddle, fast, fast, fast! She found Barnaby sitting on a snowdrift, trying to catch snowflakes on his tongue. 'Mlem, mlem,' went Barnaby's tongue. Pippa tapped Barnaby gently on his fluffy wing. She opened her beak and dropped the sparkling silver pebble right at his webbed feet. Barnaby blinked his big black eyes. He looked down at the shiny pebble, and then up at Pippa. A big penguin smile spread across his beak. 'Ooh, Pippa! Is that for me?' he asked softly. Pippa nodded her head up and down and chirped a happy little song. Barnaby picked up the pebble with his beak and turned it around. It sparkled in the winter sun. 'It is the shiniest pebble in the whole wide world,' whispered Barnaby. Together, the two happy penguins built a tiny snow tower and placed the shiny silver pebble right on top. It shone like a beacon for all their friends to see. Pippa felt so happy inside. Giving a gift was even better than finding one. As the bright sun began to set, painting the snow pink and gold, Pippa waddled back to her cozy nest, ready for sweet penguin dreams.

stories.title: The Great Waddle Race
stories.text: It was a wonderful, snowy morning at the South Pole, and all the little penguins were buzzing with excitement. Today was the day of the Great Waddle Race! There were big penguins, medium penguins, and very tiny baby penguins. At the very front of the snowy track stood Barnaby, the fastest waddler in the colony. He stretched his flippers and shook his tail feathers. 'Ready, set, go!' honked wise old Grandpa Penguin, blowing a loud blast through a horn made of ice. Off they went! Waddle, waddle, waddle, slide! Barnaby zoomed ahead, his flippers moving super fast. But wait! Little Penny Penguin was trying her very best to keep up, but she tripped over a little snowball. Bump! She tumbled right onto her soft tummy. Oh no! Penny let out a little squeak of surprise. She looked like a furry bowling ball lying in the white snow. Up ahead, Barnaby heard the little squeak. He stopped running. He looked back at the finish line, and then he looked back at Penny. Barnaby turned himself around and waddled back to his friend. He didn't care about winning the race anymore. He cared about his friend. Barnaby reached out his flipper and helped Penny push herself back up onto her little orange feet. 'Are you okay, Penny?' asked Barnaby kindly. Penny shook the snow off her head and blinked her big eyes. 'I am okay, Barnaby, but my knee hurts a little bit.' Barnaby gently touched her flipper. 'We can finish together,' he said with a warm smile. Penny smiled back. So, instead of racing like lightning, the two little penguins linked flippers. Waddle, left, waddle, right! They walked side by side all the way down the snowy track. The other penguins cheered loudly, clapping their flippers together. 'Yay Barnaby! Yay Penny!' they squawked. When they crossed the finish line together, Grandpa Penguin cheered the loudest. 'A tie! The best kind of win!' Everyone shared yummy ice-fish snacks and celebrated. Barnaby and Penny sat side by side, watching the snowy stars come out. Barnaby learned that winning is fun, but helping a friend is the greatest victory of all.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white snow and bright blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip was not like the other penguins. While they loved to play rough games of slide-on-the-tummy, Pip loved to look at colors. His very favorite color was bright, sunny yellow. One chilly morning, Mama Penguin gave Pip a surprise. It was a long, cozy, blue scarf! Pip wrapped the scarf around his little neck once, twice, three times. It was so soft! 'Squeak!' said Pip happily. He waddled over to his best friend, a little seal named Sammy. Sammy had big whiskers and a shiny nose. 'Look at my new scarf, Sammy!' said Pip, doing a little happy dance. 'It keeps my neck as warm as toast!' Sammy clapped his flippers together. 'It is so pretty, Pip!' Together, they waddled down the snowy hill to the edge of the big, blue ocean. The water looked very cold, but Pip was ready. He took a deep breath. Splash! Into the water went Pip. He did a big loop. He did a little spin. The water was so much fun! But soon, Pip started to shiver. Brrr! Time to get out. He climbed back onto the slippery ice and shook off the cold water. Shake, shake, shake! But wait. Where was his scarf? Pip looked to the left. He looked to the right. Oh, no! The blue scarf was gone! Pip felt a little tear in his eye. He loved that scarf. Sammy looked around, too. 'Don't worry, Pip, we will find it!' They waddled back up the hill. And guess what they saw? Sitting right on top of a snow mound was a little snowbird. And the snowbird was wearing Pip's scarf! It looked like a tiny blue tent on the bird's head. 'Chirp, chirp!' sang the bird, looking very proud. Pip giggled. He walked up to the bird. 'Excuse me, little bird, that is my special scarf.' The bird tilted its head and gave the scarf back. Pip wrapped it around his neck again. Ahh, warm again! 'Thank you,' whispered Pip. He hugged his friend Sammy, and they waddled home to eat fish for dinner.

stories.title: Pip Learns to Slide
stories.text: Down in the great white south, where the wind blows the soft snow into little hills, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had two tiny feet, a black and white coat, and a big dream. He wanted to slide! All the big penguins could slide down the big ice hill with a whoosh! They went so fast, zooming past the glaciers like little black rockets. Pip wanted to zoom, too. But every time Pip tried to slide, something funny happened. He would wiggle his flippers, fall right on his tummy, and stop after one little inch. 'Plop!' went Pip. He sighed a little penguin sigh. His friend Barnaby, a fluffy white albatross with huge wings, flew down from the sky. 'What is the matter, little Pip?' asked Barnaby in a gentle voice. 'I cannot slide like the big penguins,' said Pip sadly. 'My tummy gets stuck on the snow.' Barnaby smiled and fluffed his feathers. 'Sliding is not about your tummy, Pip. It is about joy in your heart! Let us try together.' Barnaby showed Pip how to tuck his flippers in close and point his toes straight back. 'Ready, set, go!' cried Barnaby. Pip took a deep breath, wiggled his little bottom, and gave a tiny push. Whoosh! Pip started to move. He went faster than an inch. He went past a snowball. He went past a patch of blue ice. He was actually sliding! 'Look at me, Barnaby! I am flying without wings!' shouted Pip with glee. He slid all the way to the bottom of the hill, right into a soft snowbank. Poof! A cloud of white snow flew up into the air. Pip popped his head out, covered in sparkling snowflakes, and laughed a big, happy penguin laugh. He had done it! From that day on, Pip was the happiest slider in the whole snowy land. Whenever he felt a little unsure, he just remembered to tuck his flippers, point his toes, and let the snow guide his way home to his loving family.

stories.title: Pip and the Lost Star
stories.text: The sun was starting to set over the great icy sea, painting the sky in shades of pink, purple, and gold. Little penguin Pip loved this time of day. It was the hour when the first little star would twinkle in the deep blue sky. Pip called it his bedtime star. But tonight, when Pip looked up into the twilight, something was wrong. The little star was not there! Pip rubbed his round eyes with his flippers and looked again. Still nothing. 'Oh, no,' whispered Pip. 'Did my star fall asleep?' He could not go to sleep without saying goodnight to his sparkling friend. Determined to help, Pip set off on a gentle night adventure across the snow. The ice crunched softly under his webbed feet. *Crunch, crunch, crunch.* The moon was bright and round, shining like a big silver coin in the dark sky. Pip walked past an ice cave where the icicles hung down like crystal chandeliers. He walked past a family of sleeping seals who were snoring softly. *Snooze, honk, snooze.* Finally, Pip reached the very highest snow hill in the land. He climbed up to the top, huffing and puffing. *Hoo, hah, hoo, hah.* He stood on his tiptoes and stretched his neck up as high as it could go. 'Little star? Where are you?' he called out softly. Suddenly, a soft beam of light tickled Pip right on his beak. He blinked and looked down. Right beside his left flipper, resting in a soft hollow of snow, was a tiny, glowing golden feather. It was warm to the touch. And when Pip looked up again, there was his star, twinkling merrily right above his head! It had just been hiding behind a fluffy cloud. Pip picked up the glowing feather with his beak and tucked it safely under his wing. 'Goodnight, little star,' he whispered. Then, feeling cozy and happy, Pip waddled all the way back down the hill to his warm, safe nest, ready for sweet penguin dreams.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in the snowy, glowing white land of the South Pole, lived a tiny, fluffy penguin named Pip. Pip had the shiniest black feathers, the brightest orange beak, and two very cold feet. Brrr! The wind went whoosh, and the snowflakes danced all around. Pip loved to waddle in the snow. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went Pip's webbed feet. But today, the wind was extra chilly, and Pip's neck felt super cold. Oh, dear! Mama Penguin saw that Pip was shivering. She smiled a big, warm penguin smile and wrapped a long, soft, bright blue scarf around Pip's little neck. It was the softest scarf in the whole wide world! Pip flapped his flippers with joy. Yay! The blue scarf kept him so cozy and warm. Pip waddled over to his best friend, Barnaby, a bouncy little penguin who loved to slide on his tummy. 'Look at my scarf, Barnaby!' chirped Pip. Barnaby clapped his flippers. 'It is so pretty and blue, Pip! Let us go sliding together!' Together, the two little penguins waddled up the snowy hill. Ready, set, go! Whoosh! Down the slippery ice they slid, right on their fuzzy tummies. Whee! The wind rushed past them, but Pip did not feel cold at all because his special blue scarf kept him snug. After a very fun ride, they bumped softly into a fluffy snowbank. Giggling, Pip and Barnaby popped right back up. They shook the snow off their feathers and ate some crunchy, yummy ice cubes for a snack. The sun began to set, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and purple. It was time to go home for bedtime stories and cuddles. Pip waddled back to his cozy nest, feeling warm from his head all the way down to his toes. He curled up next to Mama, still wearing his wonderful blue scarf. As the gentle snow fell outside, Pip closed his eyes and dreamed sweet dreams of sliding down the icy hills. Goodnight, little Pip. Sleep tight in your blue scarf.

stories.title: The Shiny Purple Pebble
stories.text: Deep in the land of ice and snow lived a curious little penguin named Penny. Penny had big, round eyes and loved to collect treasures. Not shiny gold coins, because penguins do not know about those, but shiny, smooth pebbles! Every morning after breakfast, Penny would waddle down to the rocky shore to look for her favorite things. Today, Penny was on a very important mission. She wanted to find the most special pebble in the whole wide world to give to her papa as a special surprise. Penny waddled along the pebbly beach. Waddle, waddle, look, look! She turned over a gray stone. Nope, too dull. She peeked under a mound of white snow. Brrr, too cold and just ice! Then, something caught her eye near the edge of the blue-green water. It was a little mound of wet sand, and sticking right out of the top was a perfectly round, sparkling purple pebble! Penny gasped. Oh, it was so pretty! It shimmered in the bright sunlight just like magic. Penny carefully picked up the purple pebble with her beak. It was smooth and cool. She held it very tightly so she would not drop it in the snow. With a happy squeak, Penny turned around and waddled as fast as her little feet could carry her back to the nesting grounds. Waddle, waddle, waddle! There was Papa Penguin, standing tall and proud in the snow. Penny waddled right up to him and dropped the sparkly purple pebble softly at his webbed feet. Papa looked down, and his eyes grew wide with joy. He bent his neck and gave Penny a big, gentle nuzzle. 'Is this for me, little Penny?' he asked softly. Penny bobbed her head up and down and chirped happily. 'Yes, Papa! It is just for you because you are the best papa ever.' Papa picked up the shiny purple pebble and tucked it safely right beside his nest. He wrapped his warm wing around Penny, and they stood together in the gentle breeze, sharing a snuggle. Penny felt so proud and happy inside. Finding treasures was fun, but sharing them with someone you love was the very best thing of all.

stories.title: Penny's First Splash
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the great icy shelf. It was a beautiful day for swimming! All the big penguins were diving into the deep, dark blue ocean with a big splash. Splash, splash, splash! They swam like rockets, chasing little silver fish. But little Pablo was standing right at the very edge of the water, and he was feeling a little bit scared. The water looked so big, and Pablo was so small. He wiggled his toes in the freezing water. Brrr! It was very cold. 'Come on in, Pablo!' called his mommy from the water. She did a happy little spin and blew a bubble right out of her beak. Pablo wanted to swim, too. He flapped his little black and white flippers. But his webbed feet stayed firmly planted on the snowy shore. Just then, a friendly little seal popped its head out of the water. 'Hello, little penguin! Do not be afraid. The water is wonderful!' said the playful seal with a cheerful bark. Pablo took a deep breath. He looked at his mommy, and he looked at the fun seal. He decided he was brave enough to try. Pablo took one step forward, then another step forward. Waddle, waddle, slip! Oops! Pablo slid right down the snowy bank on his tummy and went straight into the water. Whee! Splash! Down, down, down he went, and then pop! Pablo bobbed right back up to the top like a little cork. He blinked the water out of his big eyes and looked around. Hey! He was floating! Pablo kicked his webbed feet. Kick, kick, kick! He moved forward through the water. It was not scary at all; it was pure magic! Pablo did a little happy squeak. He flapped his flippers and zoomed through the water just like a real fish. Mommy swam right beside him, clicking and whistling with pride. 'You did it, my brave little Pablo!' she cheered. Pablo smiled a big penguin smile. Swimming was the most fun thing he had ever done. He splashed and played all afternoon long in the cool, blue sea, knowing he was the bravest little penguin in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white snow and slippery blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black feathers on his back, a fluffy white tummy, and two big, bright eyes that loved to look at the world. Today was a very special day because the wind was blowing extra hard. WOOOSH! went the wind. 'Brrr!' shivered Pip, wrapping his flippers tight around his little body. Mama Penguin saw her little baby shivering and waddled over with a big smile. 'Do not worry, my little Pip,' Mama said, pulling a long, bright blue scarf from her pocket. 'This will keep you warm.' Mama wrapped the soft blue scarf once, twice, three times around Pip's neck. It was the prettiest blue Pip had ever seen, matching the bright icy sky above. Pip felt so warm and cozy right away. He waddled over to the edge of the shiny ice slide to show his best friend, Penny. 'Look, Penny!' squawked Pip happily, wiggling his flippers. 'My new scarf!' Penny clapped her flippers together. 'How wonderful, Pip! Let us go sliding!' Down the slippery ice slide they went, wheeeee! Pip zoomed down, his blue scarf trailing behind him like a colorful flag in the wind. Splash! They landed softly in the slushy snow at the bottom. Oh, playing in the snow was so much fun! But suddenly, Pip felt a little tug. Oh no! The wind gave one huge gust, WHOOSH, and blew the blue scarf right off Pip's neck! It fluttered up, up, up into the air like a flying bird. 'My scarf!' cried Pip, reaching out with his short little flippers. The scarf landed gently on the very top of a tall, pointy snow mound, just out of reach. Pip looked at the snow mound, and then he looked at Penny. 'We can work together,' said Penny with a cheerful chirp. Penny crouched down low, and Pip climbed carefully onto her back. He stretched and stretched, reaching up with his flippers. Tip-toe, tip-toe, almost there! With one final little stretch, his flippers grasped the soft blue fabric. 'Got it!' cheered Pip. He wrapped the scarf securely around his neck again, tying it with a snug little knot. Pip gave Penny a big penguin hug. They waddled all the way home together, hand in flipper, feeling as warm and happy as two little penguins could possibly be.

stories.title: The Shiny Red Ball
stories.text: Deep in the frosty southern lands, where the snow twinkled like thousands of tiny diamonds, lived a curious little penguin named Barnaby. Barnaby loved to explore. Every morning, he would waddle around looking for something new and interesting. Waddle, waddle, waddle went his webbed feet on the crunchy snow. One sunny afternoon, while peeking behind a big block of ice, Barnaby spotted something bright and round. It was a shiny red ball! It did not belong to the snow, and it did not belong to the ice. It was just sitting there, glowing like a little cherry in the white landscape. Barnaby tilted his head to the left, then to the right. 'Squawk?' he said in surprise. He gently poked the ball with his black beak. Boop! The ball rolled a little bit forward. Barnaby giggled, a sweet bubbling sound. He gave the ball a gentle nudge with his tummy. Whee! The ball rolled across the smooth ice, leaving a little track behind it. Barnaby waddled fast to catch up. Tap, tap, tap went his flippers as he dribbled the ball across the frozen playground. Soon, his friend Oliver the seal popped his head up from a round hole in the ice. 'Hello, Barnaby! What are you playing with?' asked Oliver, his whiskers twitching. 'Look what I found!' chirped Barnaby proudly. 'It is a bouncy, shiny red ball!' Oliver blinked his big brown eyes. 'Can I play too?' Of course, Barnaby was a sharing penguin. 'Yes, Oliver! Catch!' Barnaby kicked the shiny red ball with his webbed foot. It slid across the ice right toward Oliver. Oliver caught it gently on his wet nose, balancing it up and down. Boop, boop, went the ball on Oliver's nose! Barnaby clapped his flippers together in delight, cheering, 'Yay, Oliver! Good catch!' They played together for a long, happy time. They kicked it, rolled it, and bounced it until the golden sun began to dip low in the sky, painting the snow in shades of pink and orange. The stars started to twinkle overhead, blinking like sleepy eyes. Barnaby picked up the red ball in his beak and gave Oliver a warm hug. 'Time for bed, Oliver,' said Barnaby softly. 'Goodnight, red ball.' Barnaby waddled back to his cozy nest with Mama and Papa, holding his special treasure tight. He snuggled down into the warm feathers, dreaming of all the fun games they would play again tomorrow when the sun came up.

stories.title: Barnaby's Big Splash
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the icy beach, making the snow melt into little puddles. It was a gorgeous day for swimming! Little penguin Oliver stood at the very edge of the deep, blue-green ocean. Splash, splash, went the waves against the shore. Oliver’s big brother, Felix, was already swimming in the water, doing fast little loops and backflips. 'Come on in, Oliver! The water is wonderful!' called Felix, shaking droplets from his sleek black feathers. Oliver looked down at the cold, moving water. He gripped the edge of the ice with his little webbed toes. His tummy felt a little bit fluttery. What if the water was too cold? What if he forgot how to swim? Oliver took one step back. 'I am not sure, Felix,' Oliver squawked nervously. Just then, his wise old grandmother waddled over, her soft grey feathers looking like a cozy blanket. She nuzzled Oliver’s cheek with her warm beak. 'Do not be afraid, my little one,' Grandma whispered softly. 'You were born to swim. Your feathers are waterproof, and your flippers are strong like little oars. You can do hard things.' Oliver looked at Grandma’s kind, encouraging eyes. He looked back down at the inviting ocean. He took a deep breath, puffed out his little white chest, and decided to be brave. Waddle, waddle, waddle, he walked right to the very edge of the ice. He closed his eyes tight, held his breath, and jumped. WEEEE! Down, down, down he fell through the salty air until—SPLASH! Oliver plunged right into the cool, refreshing water. At first, everything was blue and bubbly. Then, Oliver opened his eyes. Wow! It was amazing down here. He did not sink at all; he floated right like a cork. He beat his flippers once, twice, and zoomed forward like a little underwater rocket. Whoosh, go left! Whoosh, go right! He did a happy little spin around a patch of green seaweed. Felix swam up beside him with a proud grin. 'Look at you, Oliver! You are a fast swimmer!' Oliver surfaced, popping his head out of the water with a joyful squawk. Water droplets sparkled on his beak. 'I did it, Grandma!' he called out to the shore. Grandma clapped her flippers proudly. Oliver paddled happily in the waves, realizing that trying new things was one of the greatest adventures in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had glossy black feathers, a bright orange beak, and the coziest blue scarf in the whole wide world. His mama knitted it for him with yarn as soft as a fluffy cloud. Every single morning, Pip would waddle out of his cozy ice cave, flap his little flippers, and go on grand adventures. Today was a very special day because the sun was shining, making the snow sparkle like a million tiny diamonds. Pip waddled over to his best friend, Barnaby the seal. 'Hello, Barnaby!' chirped Pip. Barnaby rolled over and barked a happy hello. 'I want to slide down the big snow hill today,' said Pip, adjusting his blue scarf. He waddled up, up, up to the very top of the highest snow mound. Pip looked down and giggled. It was a long way to go! He tucked his flippers tight against his sides, sat right down on his fluffy bottom, and shouted, 'Wheee!' Whoosh! Down, down, down went Pip, sliding as fast as a shooting star. Wind tickled his cheeks and snowflakes danced all around him. Splash! He landed right in a soft snowdrift at the bottom with a happy giggle. 'Again! Again!' cheered Barnaby, clapping his flippers together. But suddenly, Pip reached up to touch his neck. Oh no! His favorite blue scarf was gone! Pip looked up the snowy hill. There, fluttering in the breeze at the top, was a flash of bright blue. The wind had whisked it right off his neck during the ride! Pip’s lower lip quivered. Without his blue scarf, he felt a little chilly. 'Don't worry, Pip!' barked Barnaby kindly. 'I will help you find it!' Together, the little penguin and the friendly seal climbed back up the hill. Step by step, waddle by waddle, they marched through the cold white snow. When they reached the top, they saw a little snowbird playfully tugging on the blue yarn. 'Excuse me, little bird,' said Pip politely. 'That is my special scarf.' The bird chirped a sweet apology and let go. Pip wrapped the warm blue scarf tightly around his neck. It smelled like peppermint and sunshine. He hugged Barnaby and said, 'Thank you for helping me, friend.' With his heart as warm as his neck, Pip waddled all the way home for a nice fish snack and a long, happy nap.

stories.title: Pip Goes Splash
stories.text: Down by the edge of the great blue ocean, where the water was as cold as ice cream, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip loved looking at the ocean. He loved the way the tiny waves went back and forth, tickling the pebbles on the shore. But there was one big problem. Pip had never been swimming in the big blue sea! Every day, he watched his older brother and sister dive into the water with a joyful splash, twisting and turning like little black-and-white torpedoes. Pip would stand at the water's edge, wiggle his orange toes, and say, 'Brrr! It looks too cold!' He would back away and build a little snowman instead. But today, the sun was warm, and Pip felt very brave. He puffed out his little feathered chest and said, 'Today is the day I swim in the ocean!' His mama waddled over and gave him a gentle nudge with her beak. 'You can do it, my sweet little penguin,' she encouraged. Pip took a deep breath. He waddled right to the very edge of the slippery blue ice shelf. He looked down into the deep, clear water. He could see shiny little silver fish swimming past, waving hello. Pip dipped one foot into the water. 'Ooh! It is chilly!' he giggled. But it also felt very refreshing. He dipped his other foot in. Splash, splash went his webbed feet! Then, Pip held his breath, closed his eyes tight, and took one big step forward. Whoops-a-daisy! Pip tumbled right into the water. Splash! He popped right back up to the surface like a bobbing cork. Water droplets sparkled on his feathers, and the bright sun warmed his back. Guess what? Pip wasn't cold at all! His thick penguin coat kept him wonderfully cozy. 'Look at me!' cheered Pip. He kicked his webbed feet. One, two, three, kick! He flapped his little flippers. Up and down, just like a bird flying through the sky. Pip was swimming! He zoomed through the water, spinning in a happy circle. He even caught a wiggly silver fish right in his beak for a tasty snack. All his friends cheered from the shore. Pip felt like the happiest penguin in the whole wide world. Swimming in the ocean was the most fun thing ever. From that day on, Pip never missed a chance to make a big, happy splash.

stories.title: The Shiny Pebble
stories.text: Once upon a sparkling glacier, a little penguin named Pip woke up with a very important mission. Today was Friendship Day in the penguin colony, and Pip wanted to give his very best friend, Penny, a special surprise. But what do penguins give as presents? Why, a pebble, of course! Not just any pebble, but the most beautiful, shiniest pebble in the whole wide world. Pip set off on his search across the crunchy white snow. He waddled past a sleeping whale, who let out a big, bubbly snore. He waddled past a row of icicles that jingled like wind chimes in the breeze. 'Hello, icicles!' called Pip. He looked under big snowdrifts. He peeked behind glittering chunks of blue ice. But all he found were dull grey rocks covered in cold, boring dust. Pip let out a little penguin sigh. 'Oh dear,' he chirped softly. 'Where is the shiniest pebble?' Just then, a little snow-bunny hopped past, twitching its pink nose. 'Hop, hop, hop, look by the frozen waterfall, Pip!' whispered the bunny. Pip’s eyes lit up. He flapped his flippers and waddled as fast as his little legs could carry him toward the frozen waterfall. When he arrived, his jaw dropped open in amazement. The afternoon sun was shining through the ice, and right there, resting on a bed of powdery white snow, was a round, smooth pebble that sparkled like silver. It glittered with shades of purple, green, and gold. It was the most magical pebble Pip had ever seen! He carefully leaned down and picked it up with his bright orange beak. 'This is it!' he chirped happily. Pip hurried back across the snowy path as fast as a waddling penguin could go. He found Penny waiting by the big snow mound, wrapping her flippers around herself to stay warm. 'Happy Friendship Day, Penny!' chirped Pip proudly, dropping the sparkling pebble right at her webbed feet. Penny gasped and her eyes grew as big as saucers. 'Oh, Pip! It is the most beautiful pebble I have ever seen in my life!' she beamed. She gave Pip a warm, gentle penguin hug. Pip smiled from ear to ear, feeling even warmer than if he were standing next to a cozy fireplace. They spent the rest of the afternoon sliding down the snow hills together, sharing fish crackers, and watching the lovely silver pebble sparkle in the bright polar sun.

stories.title: Pip's Shiny Pebble
stories.text:
Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of glittering white snow and bright blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip was small, but his curiosity was as big as the icebergs. Today, Pip had a very important mission. He wanted to find the most special, shiny pebble in the whole wide world to give to his mama.

"Squawk!" said Pip, waddling as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him. Waddle, waddle, waddle! He looked to the left. He looked to the right. He peeked behind a snowy mound. There were lots of gray rocks, but none of them sparkled. None of them shined like the morning sun on the ocean waves.

Just then, Pip saw a tiny flash of light near the edge of the blue water. He hurried over, sliding down a snowy slope on his tummy. Wheeeee! That was fun! Pip popped up, shook the snow off his flippers, and blinked his big round eyes. Right there, nestled in the soft white snow, was a round, smooth pebble that sparkled with silver and gold.

"Ooooh!" cooed Pip. It was the prettiest pebble he had ever seen. He gently picked it up in his beak. It was nice and smooth. Pip turned around and waddled all the way back to his cozy nest. Waddle, waddle, waddle! Mama Penguin was waiting there, keeping the nest warm.

Pip dropped the shiny pebble right at her feet and did a happy little tap-dance with his flippers. Mama Penguin smiled her warmest penguin smile and scooped Pip up in a big, feathery hug. "Thank you, my sweet little Pip," she whispered. Pip snuggled close, feeling happier than a penguin on an ice floe. The snow fell softly all around them, and Pip closed his eyes, dreaming of more grand adventures for tomorrow.

stories.title: Pablo's Big Splash
stories.text:
Deep in the frosty southern lands, where the wind whispered a chilly song, lived a plump little penguin named Pablo. Pablo loved the snow. He loved making snow-angels with his wings. He loved sliding on his tummy down the big white hills. But there was one thing Pablo had never, ever done. He had never swum in the big, deep blue ocean.

Every day, Pablo would stand right at the very edge of the ice shelf and look down. The water looked so big. It looked so deep! "Brrr," Pablo would shiver, shaking his head. "It looks too cold!" His big penguin friends would dive right in with a joyful splash. Splash, splash, splash! They would spin and flip like feathered torpedoes. Pablo wanted to spin, too. He wanted to flip, too. But his webbed feet stayed glued to the ice.

One sunny afternoon, Pablo's favorite red ball rolled away. It bounced across the snow and bounced, boing-boing, right into the sparkling water! "Oh no!" cried Pablo. That was his very best ball. Without even thinking, Pablo waddled fast to the edge. Waddle, waddle, waddle! He leaned forward to grab it.

Whoops-a-daisy! Pablo tumbled right off the ice. Splash! Into the cool, blue water went Pablo.

At first, Pablo squeezed his eyes tight. But wait... he didn't sink! He felt light as a feather. Pablo opened his eyes. The water was magical! He kicked his webbed feet. He swoished his wings. Zoom! Pablo zipped through the water just like the big penguins. He caught his red ball in his beak and popped up to the surface, laughing out loud. "I did it!" shouted Pablo. He paddled back to the ice, ready for another swim.

stories.title: Pogo's Feathered Pajamas
stories.text:
The sun was beginning to dip low in the sky, painting the snowy hills in soft shades of pink and purple. Down by the frosty shore, a little penguin named Pogo was yawning a giant penguin yawn. Yaaawn! His eyes felt heavy. His flippers felt floppy. It was almost bedtime in the land of ice.

"Time to get ready for sleep, Pogo," called Papa Penguin softly. But Pogo wasn't wearing his pajamas yet. Penguins don't wear cotton pajamas with footies; they wear their very own built-in feathered tuxedos! Pogo looked down at his tummy. His black-and-white feathers were a little messy from playing in the snow all day.

"First, we need a snowy bath," said Papa. Pogo giggled as he scooped up a beakful of fluffy snow and tossed it over his head. Fluff, fluff, fluff! He shook his tail feathers until every speck of dirt was gone. His white chest gleamed like a bright star, and his black back was as sleek as a shiny pebble.

Next came the bedtime stretch. Pogo stretched his flippers out wide, wide, wide. He stretched his neck up high to the sky. Then he curled himself into a cozy little round ball. Waddle, waddle, hop! Pogo hopped right into the center of the snug family huddle. All the other penguins were snuggled close together, sharing their warm body heat.

Papa Penguin tucked Pogo right under his warm, soft wing. It was darker under there, and very, very cozy. Pogo could hear the gentle hum of the wind outside and the rhythmic heartbeat of his papa. He closed his eyes tight. "Good night, snow," whispered Pogo. "Good night, stars." And the sleepy little penguin drifted off to sweet, frosty dreams.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white ice, there lived a little baby penguin named Pip. Pip loved to waddle. Waddle, waddle, waddle! His little orange flippers flapped by his sides, and his black-and-white tummy was as soft as a marshmallow. Today was a very special day because the wind was blowing extra hard. Whoosh! The cold wind tickled Pip’s feathers. 'Brrr!' giggled Pip. Mama Penguin saw that Pip was shivering, so she gave him a bright, beautiful blue scarf. It was as blue as the summer sky and as cozy as a warm hug. Mama wrapped it around Pip’s neck once, twice, and a little bit more. 'Now you are ready for your big adventure, Pip,' she smiled. Pip waddled out of the cozy nest to show his friends. First, he waddled past a snowbank. 'Hello, snowbank!' he chirped. Then, he waddled over to his best friend, Penny the seal. Penny popped her shiny head out of the icy blue water. 'Splash!' she barked happily. 'Look at my blue scarf, Penny!' said Pip proudly. He spun around in a little circle. The long blue scarf danced in the air. Whee! Just then, Pip saw a big, slippery slope of ice. It looked like the best slide in the whole wide world. 'Time to slide!' shouted Pip. He sat right down on his fluffy little bottom. Zoom! Down the icy hill he went, faster and faster. The wind whipped past his cheeks, but his neck stayed wonderfully warm and snug inside his blue scarf. He zipped all the way to the bottom and bumped softly into a soft pile of snow. 'Whee! Let's do that again!' laughed Pip. He climbed right back up, waddling with a big smile on his face. When the golden sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange, Pip knew it was time to go home. He waddled back to the nest, his tummy full of happy memories and his blue scarf tucked safely around him. Mama Penguin was waiting with open flippers. 'Did you have fun today, my little penguin?' she asked softly. 'Oh, yes, Mama!' piped Pip, yawning a big, sleepy yawn. 'My scarf kept me warm all day long.' He curled up tight beside his mama, pulled his blue scarf close, and closed his eyes. Goodnight, Pip.

stories.title: Pippa's First Splash
stories.text: Deep in the frosty southern lands, where the snow sparkled like glitter under the bright sun, lived a little penguin named Pippa. Pippa had shiny black feathers on her back and the fluffiest white tummy you ever did see. Today, Pippa had a very big job to do. It was time for her very first swim in the big, deep blue ocean! Pippa waddled to the edge of the ice. Waddle, waddle, waddle went her little feet. She peeked over the edge. Down below, the water was dark and shiny, and little waves went swish, swosh, swish against the ice. Pippa took one tiny step closer. Then, she quickly stepped back. Her heart went thump, thump, thump inside her chest. 'Oh my,' whispered Pippa. 'It looks very big down there.' Papa Penguin waddled up beside her and gave her a gentle nudge with his warm flipper. 'You can do it, little one,' encouraged Papa. 'The water is wonderful, and your feathers are made for swimming.' Pippa took a deep breath. She waddled right to the very edge again. She closed her eyes tight and counted to three. 'One, two, three, splash!' she cheered. Down, down, down she went into the cool, refreshing water. For a second, everything was bubbly and bright. Then, something magical happened. Pippa didn't sink like a pebble; she floated right back up like a happy cork! She opened her eyes and flapped her flippers. Whoosh! Zoom! Pippa shot through the water like a tiny black-and-white rocket. 'Look at me, Papa!' she squealed with delight. Little bubbles danced all around her beak. She twisted to the left and zoomed to the right. She did a happy little loop-de-loop underwater. The ocean felt cool and silky against her feathers. Swimming was the most fun thing she had ever tried in her whole life. After swimming and playing tag with a friendly little fish, Pippa hopped back up onto the safe, warm ice. She shook her feathers hard. Shake, shake, shake! Water flew everywhere in sparkling drops. 'How was it, Pippa?' asked Papa Penguin with a proud smile. Pippa puffed out her little white chest and beamed from ear to ear. 'I am a super swimmer!' she declared. With a happy wiggle, she waddled off to share her great adventure with all her penguin friends.

stories.title: The Shiny Starfish
stories.text: The snow was falling in soft, quiet flakes over the great white ice sheet. Little Pablo the penguin was out exploring. Pablo loved to look for treasures. He had a keen eye and a very wiggly beak. Today, he was searching near the rock pools where the ocean met the shore. Tap, tap, tap went his little beak against the rocks as he looked under every shell and pebble. 'Where are you, little treasures?' whispered Pablo. Suddenly, something caught his eye. It was bright, sparkling, and glowing right at the edge of an icy pool. Pablo waddled over as fast as his little legs could carry him. Waddle, waddle, splash! He peered into the clear water. Resting right on a green sea sponge was a bright pink starfish. It looked just like a fallen star from the nighttime sky. 'Hello there, little star,' said Pablo softly. The starfish didn't move, but it shimmered in the pale sunlight. Pablo wanted to give the starfish a special gift. He looked around and found a smooth, round pebble that looked like a shiny moon. Carefully, using his beak, Pablo rolled the pebble gently into the pool until it rested right beside the pink starfish. The starfish and the pebble looked like best friends. Pablo clapped his flippers together in delight. 'Clap, clap, clap!' he cheered. Just then, his friend Maya the penguin waddled over, sliding on her belly all the way to the pool. 'What did you find, Pablo?' she asked, peeking into the water. 'Look!' said Pablo proudly. 'I found a sea star, and I gave it a moon stone.' Maya gasped. 'It is so pretty!' Together, the two little penguins sat by the edge of the pool, watching the pink starfish sparkle in the water. As the sun began to set, turning the sky a lovely shade of lavender, Pablo said goodbye to his new friend. He knew the starfish would keep the moon stone safe all night long. Pablo waddled back home to his cozy nest, feeling warm and happy inside, ready for sweet dreams of stars and snow.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in the sparkly white snow, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had shiny black feathers, a bright orange beak, and the softest, warmest, fluffiest blue scarf in the whole wide world. His mama knitted it just for him, and Pip wore it everywhere he went. One sunny morning, Pip waddled out of his cozy ice cave. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle,' went his little feet on the crisp white snow. 'Hello, fluffy snow!' chirped Pip. He wanted to play hide and seek with his best friend, Barnaby the polar bear cub. 'Ready or not, here I come!' roared Barnaby playfully. Pip giggled and scurried behind a big, glittering block of ice. He tucked himself in tight. But oh no! A playful gust of wind went 'WHOOSH!' and scooped Pip's blue scarf right off his neck. 'Oh dear!' gasped Pip. The scarf fluttered up into the air like a bright blue bird. It danced over a snowdrift, twirled past a sleepy seal, and landed right on top of a tall, pointy ice sculpture. Pip waddled over as fast as his flippers could carry him. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle!' But the ice sculpture was much too tall for a little penguin to reach. Pip looked up and blinked his big round eyes. Just then, Barnaby came lumbering up. 'Need some help, little buddy?' asked Barnaby with a friendly smile. Barnaby stretched out his big furry paw, reached up, and gently plucked the blue scarf off the ice sculpture. 'Yay!' cheered Pip, clapping his flippers together. Barnaby carefully wrapped the cozy blue scarf back around Pip's neck, tucking it in nice and snug. 'Thank you, Barnaby,' said Pip, giving his big friend a warm hug. 'You are the best.' Barnaby smiled and gave a gentle rumble. Pip felt so warm and happy inside. The sun began to set, painting the sky in pretty shades of pink and purple. It was time for little penguins to go to sleep. Pip waddled all the way home to his cozy ice cave, still wearing his favorite blue scarf. He curled up next to his mama, closed his sleepy eyes, and dreamed sweet dreams of floating blue scarves and friendly polar bears. Goodnight, Pip. Goodnight, little scarf.

stories.title: The Slippery Slide
stories.text: Down by the sparkling blue sea, where the giant icebergs float like magic castles, lived a little penguin named Penny. Penny loved adventures. More than anything else in the world, Penny loved sliding on her tummy. 'Wheee!' she would shout every single time. One afternoon, Penny found the most magnificent slide she had ever seen. It was a giant hill of smooth, shiny ice that went all the way down to the edge of the water. It sparkled in the afternoon sun like a million tiny diamonds. Penny waddled to the very top of the hill. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle, hop!' She looked down the long, steep slope. Her tummy gave a little flutter of excitement. 'Here I go!' squealed Penny. She plopped down right on her tummy, tucked her flippers in close to her sides, and gave a little push. WHOOSH! Penny zoomed down the ice like a shooting star. 'Wheeeee!' she laughed, the cold wind tickling her cheeks. The world blurred into a beautiful mix of white snow and blue sky. Faster and faster she went. But suddenly, Penny realized something. She was going super-duper fast! 'Uh-oh!' she giggled. At the very bottom of the slide, instead of stopping in the soft snow, her path curved right toward a fluffy snowbank. SPLAT! Penny slid right into the soft, powdery snow, making a funny penguin-shaped hole. Her orange feet popped straight up into the air. For a second, Penny just blinked. Then, she burst out laughing. Her little penguin tummy shook with giggles. From nearby, her papa waddled over, shaking his head with a fond smile. 'Are you okay down there, little slider?' asked Papa Penguin, gently pulling her out of the snowbank. Penny shook the sparkly snow off her feathers and grinned from ear to ear. 'That was so much fun, Papa! Can we do it again? Please, please, please?' Papa laughed and patted her head. 'Of course we can, my little adventurer.' And together, hand in flipper, they waddled all the way back up the hill for another amazing, slippery, slidey ride.

stories.title: Penny's Big Splash
stories.text: Deep in the land of endless ice and snow, there lived a little penguin named Pablo. Pablo loved the snow. He loved making snow angels, he loved catching snowflakes on his tongue, and he loved playing tag with his penguin pals. But there was one thing Pablo was just a tiny bit nervous about. Water. The ocean looked so big, and deep, and wiggly. All of his brothers and sisters loved to swim, diving into the waves like shiny silver torpedoes. 'Come on in, Pablo!' they would call out, splashing water with their webbed feet. Pablo would stand right at the very edge of the ice, wiggle his toes, and whisper, 'Maybe tomorrow.' One sunny afternoon, a bright shiny fish jumped right out of the waves and landed with a plop on the ice near Pablo's feet. It was his favorite kind of fish! The fish did a little flop and slid right back down into the sparkling blue water. 'Oh no!' cried Pablo. That was his lunch! Without even thinking, Pablo waddled as fast as his little legs could carry him. 'Waddle, waddle, waddle!' He reached the edge of the ice and looked down into the clear, beautiful sea. He could see his yummy fish swimming away, blowing little bubbles. Pablo didn't want to lose his lunch. So, taking a very deep breath, he closed his eyes tight, held his breath, and jumped. SPLASH! Into the cool, refreshing water went Pablo. At first, he felt a little chilly. But then, something amazing happened. Pablo's little wings weren't just for waddling anymore. They were flippers! He opened his eyes and realized he could glide through the water like a bird in the sky. He did a happy loop-de-loop and a funny wiggle. With a quick snap of his beak, he caught his fish. 'I'm swimming!' cheered Pablo, blowing a trail of happy bubbles. He swam up to the surface and peeked his head out of the water. His family cheered and clapped their flippers. 'Hooray for Pablo!' they shouted. Pablo climbed back onto the ice, shaking the water droplets off his feathers until they sparkled in the sun. He wasn't scared of the big blue ocean anymore. In fact, he couldn't wait to jump back in. 'Look at me!' laughed Pablo, diving right back down for another fun swim.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly time, in a land of sparkling white snow and slippery blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black-and-white feathers, tiny orange feet, and a very big problem. The wind in Antarctica blew super-duper fast, and it made Pip's little beak go brrr-choo! "Achoo!" sneezed Pip, shaking a little snowflake off his head. Pip's mama knew just what to do. She waddled over to their cozy ice cave and pulled out a long, bright blue, fuzzy scarf. It was as soft as a cloud and smelled like peppermint. "Here you go, my little explorer," Mama said, wrapping the warm blue scarf once, twice, three times around Pip's neck. Pip looked down at the bright blue wool. It trailed all the way down to his little webbed toes. He gave a happy little flipper-flap and waddled outside to show his friends. First, he saw Barnaby the polar bear cub. Barnaby was sliding down a snowbank on his tummy. "Wheee!" shouted Barnaby. Pip wanted to slide too, but he had to be careful not to get his new scarf wet. Waddle, waddle, slide! Pip zipped down the snowbank right behind Barnaby. The blue scarf fluttered behind him like a superhero cape. "Look at me! I'm Super Pip!" he giggled. Next, Pip met Sammy the snowy owl. Sammy blinked her big round yellow eyes. "Hoot, hoot! What a lovely blue scarf, Pip! It matches the sky!" Pip beamed with pride. He loved his blue scarf so much. But then, disaster struck! While trying to catch a bouncy snowflake with his beak, Pip tripped over a small mound of snow. Whoops-a-daisy! He tumbled head over flippers into a soft drift. When he popped back up, his beak was covered in fluffy white snow, and—oh no!—one end of his scarf was dragging in a puddle of slush. "Oh dear," squeaked Pip, his little heart doing a tiny flutter. But guess what? Barnaby and Sammy rushed over to help. Barnaby used his big paw to brush the snow away, and Sammy gently lifted the wet end of the scarf into the crisp air so it could dry. "Thank you, friends," Pip said warmly. He realized that even though the scarf kept him cozy, having kind friends made him feel even warmer inside. As the sun began to set, painting the sky in pink and purple swirls, Pip waddled home with his mama. He snuggled deep into his nest, still wearing his wonderful blue scarf, and dreamed of snowy adventures for tomorrow.

stories.title: The Shiny Red Pebble
stories.text: Down by the great icy shore, where the cold ocean waves splashed against the rocks, lived a little penguin named Penny. Penny loved to collect things. Her favorite things in the whole wide world were pebbles. Not just any pebbles, mind you—only the roundest, smoothest, most special pebbles she could find. One sunny morning, Penny decided it was time to find the ultimate treasure. She set off on a grand waddling expedition across the glacier. Waddle, waddle, waddle, went her little feet. Tap, tap, tap, went her little beak as she searched through the snow. She looked behind a sparkly blue icicle. No pebbles there, just a sleepy little seal pup yawning a big yawn. She looked under a big block of ice. Still nothing, just a patch of green moss. Penny let out a little sigh. "Sigh," went Penny, her breath puffing out in a tiny white cloud. Just as she was about to turn back and head home for a fish snack, she saw a tiny glimmer of color poking out from a snowbank. It was not black. It was not white. It was bright, brilliant red! Penny gasped. She hurried over as fast as her little webbed feet could carry her. She dug with her flippers, gently brushing away the powdery white snow. There, resting in the ice like a tiny glowing star, was a perfectly smooth, shiny red pebble. It was polished by the waves and sparkled in the winter sun. "Ooh!" whispered Penny, her eyes wide with wonder. She leaned down and picked it up gently in her beak. It felt warm and smooth. It was the prettiest pebble she had ever seen in her entire life. Penny decided this pebble was far too special to keep in just any old place. She wanted to give it to the most important penguin she knew—her papa, who was always building their nest. Waddle, waddle, waddle, hurried Penny all the way back home. Papa was standing by their nest, looking out at the sea. When he saw Penny waddling toward him with a big grin and something shining in her beak, he tilted his head curiously. Penny waddled right up to him, dropped the shiny red pebble gently at his webbed feet, and gave a happy chirp. Papa looked down, gasped, and scooped Penny up into a warm, feathery hug. "My goodness, Penny! This is the most magnificent pebble in the whole Antarctic!" Papa placed it right in the very center of their nest. Penny snuggled up right beside it, feeling very proud, very happy, and ready for a lovely nap.

stories.title: Penny's Big Splash
stories.text: The sun was high and bright over the icy shores of the Great South. It was a wonderful day for swimming, splashing, and fishing! All the big penguins were diving gracefully into the deep blue ocean, swooping and looping through the water like feathered torpedos. But little Pablo stood right at the edge of the ice shelf, peering down at the water. Gulp! Pablo was a little penguin, and today was the very first day he was supposed to try swimming in the big ocean all by himself. The water looked awfully deep. And awfully cold! Pablo waddled forward, peered over the edge, and then quickly stepped backward. "Uh-oh," muttered Pablo, shaking his head. His flippers felt heavy, and his tummy felt fluttery, like a swarm of curious snow-butterflies. Mama waddled up beside him and gave him a gentle nudge with her soft beak. "You can do it, my sweet Pablo," she encouraged with a warm chirp. "Just take it one little flubber-flap at a time." Pablo looked at his best friend, a little penguin named Lily, who was already splashing happily in the shallows. Lily kicked her webbed feet and sent a shower of sparkly water droplets flying into the air. "Come on, Pablo! The water is super fun! It feels like a big, cool hug!" Pablo took a deep breath. He puffed out his fluffy white chest. He looked at the water. Then he looked at Mama. Then he looked at Lily. Okay! He could do this. He was a brave little penguin! Pablo closed his eyes tight and waddled as fast as his little legs could go. One, two, three—jump! Wheeeee! SPLASH! Pablo went right into the water with a magnificent splash that sent ripples all around. He popped right back up to the surface, sputtering and shaking water off his little black beak. And guess what? He wasn't sinking! His fluffy feathers kept him afloat, and his strong little flippers knew just what to do. Pablo started to paddle. Flap, flap, go the flippers! Kick, kick, go the feet! He zoomed through the water like a tiny rocket. "Look at me! I'm swimming!" Pablo cheered, doing a happy spin underwater. Lily swam up beside him, and together they did loop-de-loops under the sparkling waves. Pablo realized that trying new things could be a little scary, but once you took the plunge, it was the most fun in the world. When it was time to climb back onto the ice, Pablo shook himself dry and gave Mama a big, happy hug.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a time, in the snowy, sparkly land of Antarctica, lived a very small penguin named Pip. Pip loved to slide down the big white hills. Whoosh! Down, down, down he went on his tummy, laughing all the way. But today, the wind was blowing a cold, chilly breeze. Brrr! Pip shivered. His little flippers felt icy cold. Mama Penguin smiled and wrapped a bright, soft, sky-blue scarf around his neck. 'There you go, my little sweet-pea,' Mama cooed, giving him a warm snuggle. Pip waddled over to his best friend, Barnaby, a fluffy seal pup. 'Look at my scarf!' Pip chirped proudly. The scarf was so long that it trailed behind him in the snow like a little river of blue. Pip and Barnaby played hide-and-seek behind the giant ice blocks. Ready or not, here I come, thought Pip. He waddled fast, but oh dear! He stepped right on the end of his long blue scarf. Oops-a-daisy! Pip tumbled forward into a fluffy drift of white snow, landing right on his bottom. Barnaby giggled, clapping his flippers together. 'Are you okay, Pip?' Barnaby asked. Pip popped his head out of the snow, shaking tiny ice crystals off his head. Instead of crying, Pip started to giggle, too. 'I am okay! That was a funny tumble!' Pip said. They decided to make snow-angels, spreading their arms and legs in the fluffy white powder. When they stood up, they saw two perfect penguin and seal shapes in the snow. As the sun began to sink low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and gold, Pip felt so warm and cozy in his lovely blue scarf. He waddled home hand-in-hand with Mama, his tummy full of yummy fish, and dreamed of snowy slides and happy times.

stories.title: Pip Learns to Swim
stories.text: Little Pip loved the icy shore. Every single day, he watched the big penguins dive into the deep blue ocean. Splash! Splash! They darted through the water like little torpedoes. Pip wanted to swim, too. But the water looked so big, and Pip was very small. 'Come on in, Pip!' called his papa from the sparkling waves. Pip took one little waddling step toward the water. Then he stopped. The tiny wave tickled his webbed feet and then trickled away. Pip let out a nervous little chirp. What if the water was too cold? What if he forgot how to float? Papa penguin waddled back up the slippery bank and gently nudged Pip's back. 'You can do it, my brave little explorer,' Papa whispered gently. 'Your flippers are made for flying right through the water.' Pip took a deep breath. He closed his eyes and took three fast waddles. One, two, three—and jump! Wheeee! Pip plunged right into the cool, refreshing sea. At first, he sputtered and blinked away the salty water. But then, something amazing happened. Pip stretched out his little wings. He didn't sink at all! He floated right up to the top like a cork. 'I am swimming!' Pip shouted with glee. He flapped his left wing, then his right wing. Zoom! Pip darted through the water, turning left and right. He chased a tiny, shimmering silver fish that tickled his tummy. The fish swam fast, and Pip swam faster, spinning in a happy circle. The ocean felt wonderful, bright, and full of magic. When it was time to climb back onto the ice, Pip shook the water droplets from his feathers until they sparkled in the sun. He waddled over to Mama, beaming with pride. 'I swam all by myself!' he cheered. Mama gave him a big, loving hug, proud of her brave little swimmer.

stories.title: The Shiny Pebble
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the great white snow-fields of the South Pole. Pip the penguin was on a very important mission. He wanted to find the most special, sparkly present in the whole wide world for his dear mama. Pip began his search near the big glacier. He looked under snowy hummocks and behind frosty rocks. He waddled this way, and he waddled that way, peering closely with his bright, curious eyes. Suddenly, something caught his attention. It twinkled like a little star resting right in the middle of the grey stones. Pip scurried over as fast as his little webbed feet could carry him. There, half-buried in the snow, was a smooth, round pebble. It was not just any ordinary pebble. It was polished to a bright, glossy sheen, and when the sunlight hit it just right, it sparkled with flecks of silver and gold. 'Oh, wow,' Pip whispered, his eyes wide with wonder. 'This is the most beautiful treasure ever.' Pip carefully picked up the pebble with his beak. It felt nice and heavy, just right for a special gift. He waddled back home as fast as he could, making sure not to trip on his own flippers. When he found Mama resting near the nursery, he waddled up to her, his little heart beating with excitement. With a gentle bow, Pip dropped the shiny pebble right at Mama's feet. Mama gasped softly. She looked down at the glittering treasure, and then she looked at her sweet, thoughtful little penguin. 'Oh, Pip,' she smiled warmly, scooping him up into a cozy cuddle. 'This is the most wonderful gift in the whole wide world. Thank you, my precious little one.' Pip snuggled close, feeling happier than a king on his throne, knowing his love had made Mama smile.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly day, in a land of sparkling white snow and deep blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip had soft black feathers, a bright orange beak, and the coziest red feet in all of Antarctica. But today, the wind was blowing super-duper hard. Whoosh! The cold wind tickled Pip’s tummy and made his little feathers puff right up. "Brrr!" said Pip. "I need something to keep my neck warm!" So, waddle, waddle, waddle, Pip went on a little search. He waddled past a sleeping seal. He waddled past three jumping fish. Splash! The fish jumped back into the deep blue ocean. Finally, Pip found what he was looking for: a sparkly, bright blue scarf resting on top of a snowdrift. It was soft like a cloud and smelled like peppermint. Pip picked up the scarf in his beak and wrapped it around his neck once. Then twice. Then three times! Oh, it was so warm and snuggly. Pip felt like a happy little king. He waddled back to his mama and showed off his new treasure. Mama penguin gave him a big hug with her flippers and kissed the top of his head. "You look so handsome, my little Pip," she said. The sun began to set, painting the sky in lovely pink and purple colors. Pip curled up in the snow right next to his mama. He tucked his beak under his soft blue scarf, closed his eyes, and drifted off to sleep, dreaming of fish and sunny days. Goodnight, Pip!

stories.title: Pippa's First Slide
stories.text: Down at the edge of the big, slippery glacier, a little baby penguin named Pippa was learning how to slide. Now, adult penguins could slide on their bellies super fast, like rocket ships on ice. But Pippa was very small, and her tummy was round like a little bowling ball. She looked down the big white hill and gulped. "Uh oh," she peeped. Her big brother, Pablo, smiled and said, "You can do it, Pippa! Just sit down, put your flippers out wide, and let gravity do the work!" Pippa took a deep breath. She wiggled her flippers. She sat right down on her fluffy feathers. Ready, set, go! Whoosh! Pippa started to slide down the snowy hill. At first, she went slow. Then, she went a little bit faster. "Weeeee!" giggled Pippa. The cold wind rushed past her cheeks. The sparkling snowflakes danced all around her. She zoomed past a patch of blue ice and a funny-looking rock. She was going so fast! But then, oh no, a little bump in the snow made her wobble. Uh oh, wobble, wobble, splash! Pippa landed right in a soft snowbank. Her feet were stuck up in the air like two little orange twigs. Pablo skidded over, laughing a happy penguin laugh. "Are you okay, little sister?" he asked. Pippa wiggled her feet and popped right back up. Snow was stuck to her nose. She shook it off with a big sneeze. "Achoo!" giggled Pippa. "That was so much fun! Let's do it again!" So hand in flipper, the two little penguins waddled back up the hill for another magical, snowy ride.

stories.title: The Shiny Purple Pebble
stories.text: Deep in the icy rookery, millions of penguins were chatting away. Squawk, squawk, honk, honk! Amidst all the noise was a little penguin named Penny. Penny loved to collect things. She collected smooth white stones, tiny feathers, and sometimes even frozen bits of sea glass. But today, Penny was looking for the most special treasure of all. She wanted to find a gift for her best friend, Barnaby, who was feeling a little bit sad because he dropped his favorite fish in the water. Penny waddled over to the rocky beach. She looked under the ice. She looked behind a big snow mound. Suddenly, something caught her eye. It sparkled in the pale sunshine like a little piece of magic. Penny hopped over and blinked her big round eyes. It was a pebble, but not just any pebble. It was bright purple, smooth as glass, and shone with all the colors of the rainbow. "Oh, wow," whispered Penny. She gently picked up the shiny purple pebble in her beak. It felt cool and wonderful. Penny turned around and waddled as fast as her little feet could carry her back to Barnaby. Barnaby was sitting on a block of ice, looking down at his flippers with a little frown. Penny tapped him gently on the shoulder. She dropped the shiny purple pebble right at his webbed feet. Barnaby looked down. His eyes grew wide with wonder. He picked up the purple stone and smiled a huge, beaming penguin smile. "For me?" he asked softly. Penny nodded happily and did a little tiptoe dance. Barnaby gave Penny a warm, feathery hug. The purple pebble sat between them, glowing brightly in the snow, reminding them both how wonderful it is to share.

stories.title: Pip's Blue Scarf
stories.text: Once upon a very chilly day, in a land of sparkling white snow and deep blue ice, lived a little penguin named Pip. Pip was not like the other penguins. While the big penguins zoomed through the icy water to catch shiny silver fish, Pip loved to explore the snowy hills. But today, the wind was blowing a strong, chilly breeze. Whoosh! Whoosh went the wind. Pip shivered. Brrr! He pulled his little flippers close to his plump tummy. Just then, his mama waddled over with a big surprise. It was a bright blue scarf, soft as a cloud and warm as the cozy sun. 'For you, my little Pip,' Mama said gently. Pip wrapped the scarf around his neck once, twice, and a third time. Oh, how cozy it felt! Pip waddled over to his best friend, a fluffy white seal pup named Sam. 'Look at my scarf, Sam!' Pip honked happily. Sam clapped his flippers together. 'It is so blue and bright, just like the sky!' Together, Pip and Sam played a fun game of slide and seek. Pip slid down the snowy hill on his tummy. Wheee! The bright blue scarf trailed behind him like a waving flag. Every time the wind blew, Pip felt warm and safe inside his cozy knit hug. When the golden sun began to sink low in the icy sky, painting the snow pink and orange, Pip felt a big yawn coming on. He waddled back to his snug little nest with Mama. He curled up tight, keeping his blue scarf wrapped safely around his neck. Pip closed his eyes and dreamed of sliding down rainbow mountains of snow. Goodnight, little Pip. Sleep tight in your warm blue scarf.

stories.title: The Shiny Red Pebble
stories.text: Deep in the land of ice and snow, a little penguin named Pogo was having a wonderful adventure. Pogo had bright, curious eyes and little webbed feet that went flap, flap, flap against the frozen ground. Today, Pogo was on a very important mission. He wanted to find the most special treasure in the whole wide world to give to his papa. Pogo waddled past a tall ice sculpture. He waddled past three resting sea lions who were snoring softly. Snore, honk, snore! Pogo peeked behind a big snowbank. He scratched his head with his little flipper. Where could a special treasure be hiding? Suddenly, something caught his eye near the edge of the blue ocean. It sparkled in the frosty sunlight like a tiny ruby. Pogo hurried over as fast as his little legs could carry him. Tap, tap, tap went his toes. He bent down and scooped it up in his beak. It was a pebble, but not just any pebble. It was bright red, perfectly round, and smoother than a polished stone. 'Oh, how wonderful!' Pogo chirped happily. He waddled proudly all the way back to where Papa was resting on the snowy shore. With a gentle nudge of his beak, Pogo rolled the shiny red pebble right up to Papa's webbed feet. Papa looked down, his eyes widening with surprise and delight. He scooped up the pebble and gave Pogo a big, warm penguin hug. 'Thank you, my sweet little Pogo. This is the most beautiful pebble I have ever seen!' Pogo beamed with joy. He snuggled close to Papa, feeling happy and loved as the gentle snow began to fall.

stories.title: The First Splash
stories.text: The ocean water looked deep, blue, and very cold. Little Penny stood right at the edge of the ice shelf, peering down into the swirling waves. Her little webbed toes curled at the very edge. All around her, her brothers and sisters were already splashing and diving, playing a fun game of tag in the water. Splash! Splish! They looked like happy little torpedoes zooming through the foam. Penny wanted to join the fun, but her tummy felt a little bit fluttery. What if the water was too cold? What if she forgot how to paddle? Her daddy waddled over and stood right beside her, giving her a reassuring nudge. 'You can do it, my brave little Penny,' Daddy said with a warm smile. 'Just take a tiny step.' Penny took a deep breath. She puffed out her chest, wiggled her tail feathers, and counted to three. One, two, three! She took a big leap off the edge of the snowy ice. Wheee! Down, down, down she went into the crisp, refreshing sea. Splash! The water rushed around her feathers, but guess what? It did not feel cold at all. In fact, it felt amazing! Penny flapped her little wings and zoomed straight up toward the surface. She popped her head out of the water and let out a joyful honk. 'Look at me, Daddy! I am swimming!' Her daddy cheered from the ice above. Penny joined her brothers and sisters, doing loop-de-loops and chasing bubbles in the bright blue deep. It was the best day ever, and Penny knew she would never be afraid of the water again.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
See the penguin walking by,
Underneath the winter sky.
Waddle left and waddle right,
Black and white and oh so bright.

Flapping flippers in the snow,
Watch the happy baby go.
Sliding down the icy hill,
Stopping with a little chill.

Now he swims into the sea,
Happy as a bird can be.
Splishing, splashing all around,
Making not a single sound.

Time to go back to his nest,
Time for little birds to rest.
Close your eyes and go to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Pebble for My Friend
rhymes.text:
I found a pebble on the ground,
The smoothest stone that can be found.
I'll pick it up with my small beak,
And bring it to the one I seek.

Across the ice I waddle fast,
To find my cozy home at last.
I give the stone to you with care,
Because I love you, oh so rare.

We touch our beaks and say hello,
Where you will go, I too will go.
We snuggle close against the cold,
As winter winds begin to scold.

The snow may fall, the ice may freeze,
We rest beneath the winter trees.
Goodnight, my friend, sleep safe and sound,
The happiest penguins all around.

rhymes.title: Ice Slide Fun
rhymes.text:
Up the snowy hill we climb,
Having such a jolly time.
Put your tummy on the ice,
Sliding down is very nice.

Whoosh we go from top to floor,
Let us do it three times more!
Spinning round and sliding fast,
Hope this winter day will last.

Catch a snowflake on your nose,
Warmly wrapped from head to toes.
Little flippers in the air,
Jumping without any care.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping softly in our town.
Waddle home to bed so sweet,
Resting all our tired feet.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin, black and white,
Steps into the morning light.
Waddle, waddle on the ice,
Snowy world is very nice.
Flapping flippers left and right,
Underneath the sky so bright.
Sees a fish swimming away,
Time to chase and time to play.
Into water with a splash,
Swimming in a speedy dash.
Up and down and all around,
Happy bubbles make no sound.
Time to climb back on the shore,
Ready now to waddle more.
Shake your feathers, dry and neat,
Rest your little webbed feet.

rhymes.title: Slide on the Ice
rhymes.text:
Down the snowy hill we go,
Sliding on the frosty snow.
Penguin tummy round and neat,
Pulling in your webbed feet.
Swoosh and slide all through the day,
Ice is such a fun-filled way.
Bump a little, giggle too,
Skies above are bright and blue.
Stop right at the ocean side,
Where the gentle whales abide.
Watch the water ripple slow,
Watch the sparkling icebergs glow.
Turn around and climb the hill,
Waiting for another thrill.
Happy penguin, full of glee,
Jumping right into the sea.

rhymes.title: Fish for Dinner
rhymes.text:
Hungry little penguin friend,
Walking to the water's end.
Looking for a silver fish,
Wanting dinner in a dish.
Plunge into the ocean deep,
While the little starfishes sleep.
Catch a wiggle with your beak,
That is what you came to seek!
Swim back up and shout hooray,
Evening skies of pink and gray.
Time to waddle to your nest,
Snuggle down and take a rest.
Close your eyes and softly dream,
Floating on a frozen stream.
Mama hugs you nice and tight,
Sleep well, penguin, through the night.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin dressed in black,
Carries snow upon his back.
Waddle-waddle goes his feet,
Looking for a fish to eat.
Standing on the icy floor,
Listening to ocean roar.
Softly falls the fluffy snow,
Where the freezing waters flow.
Flapping flippers left and right,
Underneath the starry night.
Sliding on his tummy down,
Bestest swimmer in the town.
Happy penguin, safe and warm,
Safe from every winter storm.
Now it is time for bed,
Rest your sleepy little head.

rhymes.title: Pebble for My Friend
rhymes.text:
Found a pebble in the sand,
In this cold and frozen land.
Round and shiny, smooth and gray,
To give my dearest friend today.
Waddle fast and waddle slow,
Walking through the crispy snow.
Here is a gift for you to keep,
While the little fishes sleep.
Penguin hugs are warm and sweet,
Standing on our webbed feet.
Bowing low and smiling bright,
In the lovely polar light.
Share a fish and share a song,
All the whole long winter long.
Now the sun begins to set,
Best day that we've had yet.

rhymes.title: Jump Into the Sea
rhymes.text:
Little penguin on the ice,
Thinks the water looks so nice.
Looking down into the blue,
Wondering what he should do.
Kick your feet and flap your wings,
Hear the happy ocean sings.
Take a breath and count to three,
Jump right into the deep sea!
Splish and splash and dive around,
Making every happy sound.
Chasing little silver fish,
That is all a penguin's wish.
Now it's time to climb back high,
Underneath the twilight sky.
Shake the water from your coat,
Like a happy little boat.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Walk
rhymes.text:
Little penguin, black and white,
Waddling in the morning light.
Flapping flippers left and right,
Walking in the snow so bright.

Down upon the ice he slides,
Where the silver water hides.
In the chilly sea he glides,
Happy where the whale abides.

Catching fish so shiny small,
Jumping up and having a ball.
He is never sad at all,
Answering the ocean call.

Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in his fuzzy gown.
Bestest bird in all the town,
Wearing nature's snowy crown.

rhymes.title: Five Little Penguins
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready to play in the fluffy white snow.
One little penguin takes a little slide,
Looking for a place where he can go to hide.

Two little penguins flap their little wings,
Listening to everything the cold wind sings.
Three little penguins dive into the bay,
Swimming with the fishes in the middle of the day.

Four little penguins shake off all the foam,
Getting very ready for a trip back home.
Five little penguins cuddle up so tight,
Sleeping all together through the quiet night.

rhymes.title: Penguin's Hat
rhymes.text:
A little yellow hat upon his head,
Sleeping in his cozy little ice bed.
He wakes up and gives a happy cheer,
Glad to see the winter time is here.

He waddles to the edge of the blue sea,
And calls out to his friends, 'Come play with me!'
They jump into the water with a splash,
And swim around the iceberg in a flash.

They catch a little fish for a sweet treat,
Using all their flippers and their feet.
Then they climb right back upon the land,
Leaving little footprints in the sand.

The stars begin to twinkle in the sky,
As all the sleepy birds start saying bye.
They tuck their little beaks in feathers deep,
And dream away the night while fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
See the little penguin walk,
On the ice and snowy block.
Waddle, waddle, left and right,
In his coat of black and white.

Now he stops to shake his tail,
Watching for a passing whale.
Down he slides upon his tummy,
Looking for a fish so yummy.

Into water deep and blue,
Swimming fast just like a fish do.
Up he pops and shakes his head,
Time to go to cozy bed.

Flap his flippers in the air,
Blinking with a sleepy stare.
Goodnight, penguin, sleep so tight,
Dreaming through the polar night.

rhymes.title: Five Little Feathers
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a line,
Looking at the snow so bright and fine.
One little penguin takes a little leap,
Down into the water blue and deep.

Four little penguins marching in a row,
Looking for their friends down below.
Two little penguins slide upon the ice,
Finding that the chilly day is nice.

Three little penguins flapping in the sun,
Having lots of winter playtime fun.
Three little penguins dive into the bay,
Swimming all the sunny hours away.

Now the stars are shining in the sky,
Little sleepy penguins wave goodbye.
Cuddled up together warm and deep,
All the little penguins fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Blue and White
rhymes.text:
