Little penguin, small and sweet,
Walking on your webbed feet.
Wear a jacket made of stone,
In the snowy world alone.

Catch a pebble in your beak,
That is what you came to seek.
Give it to a furry friend,
Happy moments without end.

Now the sun begins to hide,
Closer to your mum you glide.
Underneath a starry dome,
This cold place is cozy home.

Wake up when the morning gleams,
Wake up from your happy dreams.
Waddle through the frosty day,
Ready now to laugh and play.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin
rhymes.text:
Little penguin dressed in black,
Carries snow upon his back.
Waddling left and waddling right,
Shining feathers, soft and bright.
He has got a little beak,
When he opens it, he'll squeak.
Jumping in the icy sea,
Swimming fast as fast can be.
Splashing water all around,
Happy with a joyful sound.
On the ice he loves to slide,
With his flippers open wide.
Now the sun is going down,
Sleeping in his furry gown.
Dreaming of the frosty sea,
As happy as a penguin can be.

rhymes.title: Waddle Waddle
rhymes.text:
Waddle, waddle, on the ice,
Cold and snowy, very nice.
Little flippers flap and play,
Playing games all through the day.
See him dive into the blue,
Catching tiny fishes too.
Up he pops with happy cheer,
Glad to have his family near.
Snuggling close when night is cold,
Brave and fuzzy, bold and bold.
Counting snowflakes in the sky,
Watching fluffy clouds go by.
Time for little eyes to close,
Resting up his little toes.
Dreaming of a snowy hill,
Now the winter night is still.

rhymes.title: Penguin Friends
rhymes.text:
Two sweet penguins stand and play,
Greeting you this snowy day.
One has got a fuzzy hat,
One is very round and fat.
Sliding down a slippery slope,
Filled with joy and penguin hope.
Plop they go into the foam,
Ocean is their happy home.
Chasing fish of shiny blue,
Saying hello and how do you.
Clapping flippers in the air,
Showing love and joy to share.
Walking up the snowy land,
Footprints left upon the sand.
Now the stars begin to peep,
Little penguins fall asleep.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin dressed in white,
Waddles left and waddles right.
Flapping flippers in the snow,
See the little penguin go.
Jumping on the icy floor,
Wanting to play even more.
Sliding down the snowy hill,
Now he stops and stand quite still.
Looking for a shiny fish,
Eating from a silver dish.
Time to rest his little head,
Climbing into cozy bed.
Snuggle tight until the morn,
Happiest bird that has been born.
Good night, penguin, time to sleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: Ice Cube Fun
rhymes.text:
On an iceberg cold and tall,
Lives a penguin very small.
Tuxedo coat of black and white,
Shining softly in the night.
Down the slope he takes a slide,
With his happy friends beside.
Splash into the ocean blue,
Swimming fast the whole day through.
Catching fish that swim around,
Without making any sound.
Climbing back up to the land,
Leaving prints upon the sand.
Shaking water from his coat,
Floating like a little boat.
Now the sun begins to set,
Best day he has had just yet.

rhymes.title: Penguin Friends
rhymes.text:
Two small penguins in the snow,
Where they walk, they want to go.
Holding flippers, hand in hand,
Walking through the winter land.
Wind is blowing very cold,
Making little penguins bold.
Red scarf wrapped around a neck,
Pecking snow with tiny beak.
Happy voices in the air,
Showing love and joy to share.
Dancing softly on the ice,
Everything is neat and nice.
Moon is rising high and bright,
Kissing every speck of white.
Time to dream of fish and sea,
As happy as a bird can be.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin in the snow,
Where are you so glad to go?
Waddling left and waddling right,
Feathers black and feathers white.

Flap your flippers in the air,
Show your tummy, neat and fair.
Slip and slide upon the ice,
Cold and snowy, oh so nice!

Find a fish that swims around,
Make a happy little sound.
Squeak and squawk and jump so high,
Reaching up to touch the sky.

Now the sun begins to set,
Time to cuddle and forget.
Close your eyes and sleep so deep,
Little penguin, time to sleep.

rhymes.title: Five Little Flippers
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready for a journey in the frosty snow.
One little penguin takes a little slide,
Wiggling his flippers with a joyful pride.

Two little penguins jump into the sea,
Swimming all around so happy and so free.
Three little penguins catch a shiny fish,
Eating every bite upon a snowy dish.

Four little penguins waddle up the hill,
Standing on the glacier, very safe and still.
Five little penguins cuddle with their mom,
Feeling very cozy, safe, and warm and calm.

Now the stars are shining brightly in the night,
Bathing all the snow in a gentle light.
Whisper soft and low to the sleepy crew,
Little baby penguins, I am loving you.

rhymes.title: Tuxedo Bird
rhymes.text:
Little bird in a black tuxedo,
Swimming fast like a quick torpedo.
Hopping on the icy floor,
Waddling right up to the door.

Orange beak and happy smile,
Dancing on the frozen tile.
Catching snowflakes on your head,
Time to find your cozy bed.

Slide upon your belly down,
Bestest penguin in the town.
Splash into the ocean blue,
Water laughs and splashes too.

Time to dry your feathers dry,
While the stars shine in the sky.
Dreaming of the icy sea,
As happy as a bird can be.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin on the ice,
Everything looks very nice.
He has got a tummy white,
Stepping out into the light.

Flapping flippers left and right,
Underneath the starry night.
Waddling softly to and fro,
Walking in the sparkling snow.

Now he takes a little dive,
Glad to be so well and alive.
Splashing in the ocean blue,
Saying hello, friend, to you.

Swimming fast and swimming high,
Watching snowy clouds go by.
Time to rest his little head,
In his cozy snowy bed.

rhymes.title: Five Little Feathers
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready to play in the winter snow.
First little penguin goes for a slide,
With a happy little grin and a tummy ride.

Second little penguin flaps his wings,
Listen to the happy little songs he sings.
Third little penguin catches a fish,
Putting it right on his dinner dish.

Fourth little penguin takes a big leap,
Into the ocean so cold and deep.
Fifth little penguin says goodnight now,
Bowing his head with a little snow bow.

Snuggling close to his mama's chest,
Sleeping all night is the very best.
Stars are shining bright above,
Filled with peace and penguin love.

rhymes.title: The Slippery Slide
rhymes.text:
Up the snowy hill they go,
Walking very slow, slow, slow.
Little flippers black and neat,
With their cute webbed little feet.

At the top they stop and look,
Right out of a story book.
Down the icy slide they zoom,
Flying right across the room.

Wheeeee goes the penguin band,
Loudest creatures in the land.
Splash into the water cold,
Brave and happy, bright and bold.

Chasing fish and playing games,
Calling out each other's names.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time to leave the icy show.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin, black and white,
Waddling softly left and right.
Flapping flippers in the air,
Looking happy everywhere.

Down the snowy hill he slides,
On his tummy fast he glides.
Into water with a splash,
Swimming in a merry dash.

Catching fishes, small and bright,
Eating every single bite.
Now the sun is sinking low,
Time to sleep upon the snow.

Snuggle close and shut your eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Dreaming of the icy sea,
Happy as a bird can be.

rhymes.title: Five Little Penguins
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Wiggling their toes in the fluffy white snow.
The first one said, 'Let us slide on the ice!'
The second one said, 'Oh, sliding is nice!'

The third one said, 'Let us jump in the deep!'
The fourth one said, 'Before we go to sleep.'
The fifth one said, 'Look at fishes swim by!'
Then all of them gave a happy little cry.

They waddled around in a circle all day,
Laughing and shouting and ready to play.
They flapped their short flippers up to the sky,
As snowy white clouds went floating on by.

When evening arrived and the stars started bright,
They whispered together a sleepy goodnight.
Cuddled up close in the frost and the chill,
The five little penguins were quiet and still.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Ocean
rhymes.text:
Pebble in the beak, shiny and round,
The best little treasure that can be found.
Ping the penguin looks at the sea,
Wondering what his day is going to be.

Water is cold, but feathers are warm,
Safe from the wind and the winter storm.
He jumps right in with a joyful shout,
Watching the bubbles float all about.

Spinning around like a top on the floor,
Waving hello to the seal on the shore.
Climbing back up with a shake of his head,
Ready for fun in his cozy snow bed.

Mother is waiting to give him a hug,
Wrapped up tight in a feathery rug.
Twinkle, star, twinkle up in the blue,
Little sweet penguin, we're cheering for you.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin, black and white,
Waddling through the snow so bright.
Flapping flippers left and right,
Shining stars up in the night.

Little penguin, on the ice,
Cold and windy, but so nice.
Eating fish and swimming twice,
Not a single crumb of rice.

Little penguin, big round tummy,
Snowy hills look very yummy.
Sliding down, oh feeling chummy,
Hug me tight and call me mummy.

Time for bed and time to sleep,
While the cold winds softly sweep.
Close your eyes and do not peep,
Counting little woolly sheep.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Ocean
rhymes.text:
See the penguin by the sea,
Waiting for a swim with me.
Jumping up with joyful glee,
Happy as a bird can be.

Into water, cool and deep,
Watch the feathered torpedo leap.
Underneath the waves they sweep,
Down where little fishes sleep.

Bubble, bubble, in the blue,
Penguin friends are swimming, too.
Spinning fast for me and you,
Ocean water bright and new.

Now the swimming day is done,
Evening comes to hide the sun.
Waddling home, we had such fun,
Every little sleepy one.

rhymes.title: Pebble for My Love
rhymes.text:
Walking on the frozen floor,
Looking for a treasure more.
Finding pebbles by the shore,
Happy sounds of penguin roar.

Pick it up and hold it tight,
Shiny pebble, smooth and bright.
Carrying it through the white,
Walking in the fading light.

Give it to my dearest friend,
Love that has no time or end.
Around the snowy bend we wend,
Messages of joy we send.

Now the cozy nest is deep,
Penguin babies fall asleep.
Stars above begin to peep,
Silence all around is steep.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin on the ice,
Walking once and walking twice.
Waddle, waddle left and right,
Wearing black and feathers white.
Flappy flippers by his side,
Looking out so full of pride.
Sliding down the snowy hill,
Stopping with a little chill.
Jumping in the ocean blue,
Saying hello to a fish or two.
Swimming fast and diving deep,
Till the stars begin to peep.
Climbing back up to the shore,
Ready now to waddle more.
Time to rest his sleepy head,
In his cozy snowy bed.

rhymes.title: Penguin Shoes
rhymes.text:
Have you seen the penguin walk?
He does not use a knife or fork.
He wears a tuxedo, very neat,
With little flippers on his feet.
Waddling slowly through the snow,
Where does little penguin go?
To the water, cold and clear,
Splash! He dives and has no fear.
Chasing bubbles all around,
Making not a single sound.
Then he hops back on the land,
Standing on the icy sand.
Shaking water from his coat,
Floating like a little boat.
Now the sun begins to set,
He is happy, warm, and wet.

rhymes.title: Five Little Penguins
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready for a fun day in the white snow.
First little penguin slides on his tummy,
Second little penguin finds a fish yummy.
Third little penguin flaps his wings high,
Fourth little penguin looks at the sky.
Fifth little penguin says let us play,
We will have a happy and wonderful day.
Waddling together across the cold floor,
Opening up a frosty white door.
Jumping right into the deep blue sea,
Swimming together as happy as can be.
Splishing and splashing until the night,
Underneath the moon's lovely glowing light.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin in the snow,
Watch him waddle to and fro.
Flapping flippers black and white,
Underneath the starry night.

Happy feet upon the ice,
Cold and crisp and very nice.
He has got a tummy round,
Making not a single sound.

Jump into the ocean blue,
Swimming fast the whole day through.
Catching fish to eat for tea,
Happy as a bird can be.

Now the sun begins to set,
Best day penguin hasn't met.
Time to sleep and close his eyes,
Underneath the polar skies.

rhymes.title: Five Little Flippers
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready for a journey in the frosty snow.
First one waddled to a slide of ice,
Crying out, 'Oh boy, this is so nice!'

Second one is wearing a red woolen hat,
Looking very funny sitting like a cat.
Third one loves to dive into the sea,
Swimming all around with boundless glee.

Fourth one catches fish so shiny bright,
Eating up his dinner as it turns to night.
Fifth one is so sleepy, time to go to bed,
Tucking underneath his cozy feather head.

Now they dream of sliding all the winter day,
While the gentle breezes softly blow away.
Little penguin babies resting in the cold,
Cutest little creatures that the world has told.

rhymes.title: Tuxedo Bird
rhymes.text:
Wearing a tuxedo of black and white,
Penguin is a very happy little sight.
Walking on the glacier with a funny hop,
Penguin never wants to ever stop.

Sliding on his tummy down a snowy hill,
Going very fast with quite a sudden thrill.
Splashing in the water with a joyful cheer,
Knowing that his family and his friends are near.

Shaking off the water from his shiny coat,
Floating on the ocean like a little boat.
Chirping to his mama with a happy sound,
Best little penguin to be found.

Now the moon is shining bright up in the air,
Showing sleepy magic everywhere.
Close your little eyes and drift away to sleep,
While the quiet ocean makes a gentle beep.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin on the snow,
Watch him waddle to and fro.
Black and white from beak to toe,
Where is little penguin go?

Flapping flippers left and right,
Feathers shining clean and bright.
Underneath the winter light,
Standing as a tiny knight.

Now he slides upon his tummy,
Looking for a fish so yummy.
Ice is cold and very gummy,
Making every penguin summy.

Time to rest his little head,
In his cozy snowy bed.
Dreaming of the blue ahead,
Safe and warm in white and red.

rhymes.title: Five Little Flippers
rhymes.text:
Five little penguins standing in a row,
Ready for a journey in the frosty snow.
First one waddles where the cold winds blow,
Second one catches a dancing flake below.

Third one finds a pebble shiny, smooth, and round,
Fourth one spots a little fish beneath the ground.
Fifth one gives a happy and endearing sound,
Joyful little creatures dancing all around.

Jump into the water, splash and make a cheer,
Swimming with the fishes in the crystal mere.
Winter time is happy when your friends are near,
Cheering for each other through the happy year.

Now the sun is setting in the icy sky,
Little fuzzy penguins wave a sweet goodbye.
Stars are twinkling brightly as the night goes by,
Rocking gently softly like a lullaby.

rhymes.title: The Slippery Slide
rhymes.text:
On the top of icy hill,
Little penguin sitting still.
Waiting for a sudden thrill,
Frozen water very chill.

Down the slope he starts to glide,
Arms are open oh so wide.
Laughing softly deep inside,
With his happy penguin pride.

Swish and swosh and round they go,
Spinning in the powdery snow.
Fastest penguin you can know,
Watch him travel down below.

Splash into the ocean blue,
Saying to the friends hello.
Swimming is a thing they do,
Happy penguins through and through.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin dressed in black,
Carries feathers on his back.
Waddling left and waddling right,
Shining feathers in the light.

Down to the water he will go,
Walking on the shiny snow.
Splish and splash and in he springs,
Flying with his little wings.

Chasing fish that swim around,
Making not a single sound.
Up again to catch his breath,
Safe from any chilly death.

Now he climbs back on the shore,
Ready to go play some more.
Snuggling close against the cold,
Worth more than a pot of gold.

rhymes.title: Penguin Slide
rhymes.text:
See the penguin on the hill,
Sitting very, very still.
Ready, set, and off he goes,
Sliding on his tummy-toes!

Wheee, he shouts into the breeze,
Past the giant blocks of ice.
Stopping at the ocean's edge,
Standing safely on the ledge.

Time to dive and time to play,
Splashing all the blues away.
Bubbles floating all around,
Not a single human sound.

Sun is sinking in the sky,
Time to wave a sweet goodbye.
Little penguin goes to sleep,
Buried in a snowdrift deep.

rhymes.title: The Penguin Parade
rhymes.text:
Marching in a happy line,
When the winter sun doth shine.
Flippers out and noses high,
Watching snowy clouds go by.

One is short and one is tall,
One is just a baby small.
Step by step they walk along,
Humming out a happy song.

Stopping for a little game,
Playing tag and shouting names.
Jumping up and turning round,
Feet go patter on the ground.

Now the marching day is done,
They have had so much good fun.
Cuddled tightly in the nest,
Time for little birds to rest.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin dressed in black,
Carries snow upon his back.
He has flippers big and wide,
Ready for a snowy slide.

Waddling left and waddling right,
Standing in the morning light.
Bright orange beak and happy feet,
Walking down the icy street.

Now he stops to catch his breath,
Looking at the snow beneath.
Time to dive into the sea,
Swimming fast as he can be.

Splish and splash and underwater play,
Having such a happy day.
Now the stars begin to glow,
Time to sleep upon the snow.

rhymes.title: Ten Little Feathers
rhymes.text:
Ten little feathers soft and warm,
Safe from any winter storm.
A little penguin starts to play,
Chasing snowflakes far away.

Hop, hop, hop upon the ice,
Everything looks cold and nice.
Mother calls him from afar,
Shining like a little star.

He flaps his flippers in the air,
Throwing snowballs everywhere.
Giggling with a happy sound,
Jumping up and turning round.

Now the sun is sinking low,
Time to rest his sleepy toe.
Close your eyes and dream all night,
Little penguin, pure and white.

rhymes.title: Slide and Glide
rhymes.text:
Up the snowy hill he goes,
Freezing wind upon his toes.
Ready for a speedy ride,
Sitting right upon his side.

Whoosh he goes across the floor,
Wanting just to slide some more.
Spinning round and upside down,
Bestest jumper in the town.

Landing in a cozy heap,
Feeling ready now for sleep.
Cuddling close in penguin style,
Resting with a sleepy smile.

Dreaming of the ocean deep,
While the stars their watches keep.
Goodnight penguin, sleep till dawn,
When the snowy day is born.

rhymes.title: Little Penguin Waddle
rhymes.text:
Little penguin on the ice,
Walking once and walking twice.
Flap your flippers, big and small,
So you never, ever fall.

Black and white suit coat you wear,
Marching in the chilly air.
Point your beak up to the sky,
Watch the fluffy clouds float by.

Waddle left and waddle right,
Shining in the snowy light.
Now it is time to take a rest,
Curled up in your cozy nest.

Close your sleepy little eyes,
Underneath the polar skies.
Dream of fish and sunny days,
While the gentle snowflake plays.

rhymes.title: Splash in the Sea
rhymes.text:
Down to the water the little bird goes,
Tickling snow with his little webbed toes.
Ready, set, jump with a flip and a bound,
Making a splash with a wonderful sound.

Swimming along like a dart in the blue,
Catching some fish for a snack or two.
Bubbles are floating up high in the foam,
This chilly ocean is where he calls home.

Jumping back up on the slippery shore,
Ready to play and to waddle some more.
Shaking the water right off of his back,
Quack goes the... wait, that is not a duck quack!

Honk goes the penguin, so happy and gay,
Having a wonderful, sunshiny day.
Time to go cuddle with Mama and Dad,
Best little penguin that you ever had.

rhymes.title: Snowy Slide
rhymes.text:
Up the snowy hill he climbs,
Singing little penguin rhymes.
Tummy down and ready, go!
Sliding on the packed white snow.

Wheee goes the penguin all through the day,
Chasing his friends in a wonderful way.
Spinning around in a circle so neat,
Using his flippers and cute little feet.

Stopping right at the edge of the freeze,
Feeling the breeze in the cold winter trees.
Now it is time for a cuddle up tight,
Snuggling close through the long polar night.

Stars are awake in the velvet blue sky,
Singing a sweet little lullaby. 
Dream away, penguin, until the new sun,
Brings you another fine day full of fun.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo was a big boy now. He was three years old, which meant he was big enough to be Mommy’s special helper with baby sister Mia. Mia was very small and wore soft, crinkly diapers. Today, Mommy needed Leo’s help. 'Can you be my best helper, Leo?' Mommy asked with a warm smile. Leo puffed out his chest proudly. 'Yes, Mommy! I a big helper!' he cheered, clapping his hands. First, Leo gently walked to the basket and picked out a clean diaper with bouncing blue bears on it. He carried it very carefully, just like a waiter carrying a heavy tray. 'Good job, steady hands!' whispered Mommy. Next, it was time for Mia’s special wipe. Leo handed the cool wipe to Mommy one by one. Mia gurgled and kicked her tiny toes, reaching out to grab Leo’s finger with her little hand. Leo giggled. 'Look, Mommy, she holding me!' he said softly so he wouldn't scare her. Once Mia was fresh, clean, and dressed in her soft yellow pajamas, it was time for the final touch. 'Which toy should we give Mia for her happy time?' asked Mommy. Leo toddled over to the rug and picked up the crinkly purple star. He gently placed it right next to Mia’s tummy. Mia squealed with joy and patted the star. Mommy wrapped her arms around Leo and gave him a giant hug. 'Thank you, Leo. You are the kindest big brother in the whole wide world.' Leo beamed from ear to ear. Helping baby sister felt so warm and cozy inside. He loved being a big sibling, and he loved his sweet little sister, Mia, more and more every single day.

stories.title: Maya and the Gentle Toy Train
stories.text: The living room rug was a busy train station. Maya, who was four, sat cross-legged with her shiny red toy train. Choo-choo! Choo-choo! went the train as it rolled over the fuzzy green hills. But little brother Toby was crawling over, wobbling on his hands and knees. Toby loved Maya’s trains. He reached out a chubby hand to grab the red engine. Maya almost said, 'No, mine!' But then she remembered what Daddy told her about being a gentle big sister. Toby was still learning how to play softly. 'Hi, Toby!' Maya said in a sweet, happy voice. Instead of pulling the train away, Maya slid a big, safe wooden block right into Toby’s open hands. 'You can play with the big block, Toby! It has yellow stars!' Toby blinked, hugged the block, and let out a happy baby chatter sound. Maya felt a warm, proud bubble grow inside her tummy. She was being a wonderful big helper. 'Look, Toby, the train is coming to visit your block station!' Maya sang out, chugging the red engine slowly toward Toby’s block. Toby clapped his hands together, his eyes shining brightly. When Daddy walked into the room carrying a basket of laundry, he smiled a big, proud smile. 'Maya, you are showing such wonderful sharing and kindness to your little brother. You are a super big sibling!' Maya beamed with happiness. Sharing her space and her toys made playtime even more fun. She gave Toby a gentle pat on his fuzzy head, and Toby gave her a drooly, happy baby smile right back.

stories.title: Sam's Bedtime Story Symphony
stories.text: The moon was peeking through the bedroom window, painting soft silver stripes on the floor. It was bedtime for little baby Noah, but Noah was feeling a little bit restless. He was rubbing his sleepy eyes and whimpering softly. Big brother Sam, who was five years old, knew just what to do. Sam was Noah’s bedtime superhero! 'I can help get Noah ready for dreamland,' Sam whispered quietly to Mommy. Mommy nodded. 'That would be wonderful, Sam. You are a wonderful bedtime helper.' Sam tiptoed over to the bookshelf and picked out Noah’s absolute favorite book about a sleepy little bear. He carried it carefully with both hands, holding it up high so he wouldn't drop it. Sam climbed up onto the big rocking chair right next to Mommy and Noah. 'Ready for your story, little bro?' Sam asked in his softest, coziest voice. Noah curled up close, snuggling into Sam’s shoulder. Sam opened the book and pointed to the big moon on the cover. 'Look, Noah, the moon says goodnight,' Sam whispered, tracing his finger gently under the pictures. Noah listened to Sam’s calm, gentle voice and stopped whimpering. His heavy eyelids fluttered, closing slowly as Sam turned the pages with care. When the story was finished, Sam whispered, 'Time to sleep, little bear.' Noah let out a long, relaxed sigh, completely safe and cozy. Mommy kissed them both on the forehead. 'Thank you, Sam. You helped soothe your brother so peacefully.' Sam puffed out his chest with pride. Being a big brother was a big job, but hearing his baby brother breathe softly as he fell asleep made Sam feel like the happiest boy in the world.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, big boy Leo! Today is going to be such a wonderful day because Leo is a big brother helper. Little baby sister Mia is waking up from her crib. Can you hear her soft coos? "Good morning, Mia!" says Leo with a giant, happy smile. Mommy and Daddy are so proud of how helpful Leo is every single day. Mommy needs a tiny helper to fetch a fresh diaper for baby Mia. Can Leo find the softest diaper in the basket? Yes, he can! Tip-toe, tip-toe, go! Leo brings the diaper over with big, careful steps, holding it gently like a precious treasure. "Thank you, my wonderful helper," says Mommy, giving Leo a warm, cozy hug. Now, it is time to choose a baby wipe. Leo picks the yellow pack with the happy duck on the front. Mia kicks her tiny toes and giggles because her big brother is making funny faces to keep her happy. Being a big brother is such an important job, and Leo does it with so much love in his heart. When the diaper change is all done, Leo helps snap Mia's cute polka-dot pajamas. Snap, snap, snap! Every little button goes in the right place. Daddy claps his hands and says, "Look at our super helper!" Leo puffs out his chest and feels so proud. He is not a tiny baby anymore; he is a big boy who can do so many helpful things. Mia reaches out her tiny hand to gently pat Leo's cheek. She loves her big brother so much. Leo takes Mia's tiny hand and gives it a soft squeeze. What a wonderful way to start the morning together! Working as a team makes every single day brighter. Leo is ready for whatever helping adventure comes next in their cozy home.

stories.title: Maya's Toy Rescue Mission
stories.text: Ring, ring! It is time for playtime with baby brother Toby. Toby is sitting on the big soft play mat, shaking his favorite red rattle. Shake, shake, shake! But wait, Toby's green bouncy ball rolled far away under the big green armchair. Toby makes a sad little pouty face. Oh no! But do not worry, because Maya is here! Maya is a super-duper big sister helper, and she is always ready for a toy rescue mission. Maya puts her hands on her hips and says, "Don't worry, Toby, I will save the ball!" Down on her hands and knees goes Maya, crawling like a brave little puppy across the carpet. She reaches her arm far under the chair. Stretch, stretch, stretch! Her fingers touch something round and smooth. Got it! Maya pulls the green bouncy ball back out into the bright room. Toby claps his hands together and lets out a happy squeal of pure joy. "Yay, Maya!" coos Toby. Maya hands the ball back to her baby brother with a big, proud grin. "Good job sharing, Maya," says Daddy from the kitchen, smiling warmly at his kind little girl. Being a big sister means taking care of the people you love. Next, it is time to clean up the play area before lunchtime arrives. Maya sings her favorite tidy-up song while she gently puts the wooden blocks back into their special blue box. One block, two blocks, three blocks in! Toby tries to help by dropping a tiny yellow ring into the box, too. Maya gives Toby a high-five. "High-five, little buddy! You are a good helper, too!" Together, the brother and sister clean up every single toy until the floor is all tidy and clear. Mommy walks in and gives them both a big, cozy cuddle. Maya feels so happy inside her heart. Helping her family is the best feeling in the whole wide world. They are the best team ever.

stories.title: Sam's Bedtime Story Share
stories.text: The sun is slowly going down, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors. It is almost bedtime in the cozy house! Big brother Sam knows just what to do to help get baby sister Lily ready for sleep. Sam is the official bedtime helper tonight. First, Sam tiptoes to the bookshelf to pick out the very best bedtime story. He carefully chooses the book about the sleepy little bear who loves honey. Sam holds the book securely against his chest with both arms. Walking very slowly so he does not trip, Sam brings the book over to the rocking chair where Mommy and baby Lily are waiting. "Here is our book, Lily!" whispers Sam softly so he does not wake any sleeping fairies outside. Lily reaches out and touches the colorful cover of the book, smiling her sweet sleepy smile. Sam climbs up onto the big armchair right next to Mommy, settling in for a cozy moment. As Mommy begins to read the gentle story, Sam turns the pages one by one, very carefully so they do not tear. Turn, turn, turn! Sam watches closely to make sure Lily can see all the lovely pictures of the twinkling stars and the cozy cave. When the story is finished, Sam gives Lily her favorite soft bunny toy to hold for bedtime snuggles. Lily hugs the bunny tightly and rubs her sleepy eyes. Yawwwn! Lily is getting so tired. Sam whispers, "Sleep tight, baby sister, I love you to the moon and back." Mommy smiles lovingly at Sam and whispers, "You are such a caring and helpful big brother, Sam. Thank you for making bedtime so peaceful." Sam beams with pride, feeling so warm and happy inside. He whispers goodnight to Mommy and Lily, then climbs into his own comfy bed, ready to dream sweet dreams after another wonderful day of being a super big sibling helper.

stories.title: Leo's Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo was a big boy now. He had big boy shoes, big boy pants, and a very big job today. His baby sister, Mia, needed her diaper changed. Mom smiled and asked, "Leo, can you be my super helper?" Leo puffed out his chest and nodded. "Yes, Mom! I am a super helper!" First, Leo had to fetch a fresh diaper from the basket. He waddled over, tip-toe, tip-toe, holding the diaper high in the air like a big white flag. "Good job, Leo," whispered Mom. Next, Mia needed a clean wipe. Leo carefully pulled one single wipe out of the box. "One wipe for baby Mia," he said softly. Mia giggled and reached out to pat Leo’s hand. Leo felt so proud. He was gentle and kind, just like a big brother should be. When the new diaper was all snapped and secure, Mia gave a happy little squeal. Mom clapped her hands. "Look at that! Mia is clean and comfy, all thanks to her wonderful big brother, Leo!" Leo beamed from ear to ear. He gave Mia a gentle kiss on her tiny forehead. Being a big sibling helper was hard work, but it made his heart feel warm and full of happy sunshine. Time to play blocks together!

stories.title: Maya's Stroller Push
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly outside. It was time for a lovely family walk to the park. Maya stood by the front door, wearing her sparkly pink sneakers. Today, Maya had a very important mission. She was going to help push the stroller where baby Toby was sitting! "Are you ready, Big Helper Maya?" asked Dad, handing her the strap of the diaper bag. Maya nodded seriously. "Ready, Dad!" She walked over to the big stroller and placed both of her small hands right on the foam handle, right next to Dad’s big hands. Together, they pushed. Push, push, go the wheels! Whirrr, went the stroller down the sidewalk. Toby peered over the edge and made a happy gurgling sound. Maya looked down at her baby brother and smiled. "Don't worry, Toby, I am steering us safely!" she told him. They walked past a fuzzy brown dog, a big green tree, and a mailbox painted bright blue. Maya made sure to walk very slowly and carefully so the ride was smooth for Toby. When they reached the park, Dad knelt down. "Thank you, Maya. You kept Toby so happy on our walk. You are a super driver!" Maya felt like she could fly. She loved being a big sister and helping out every single day.

stories.title: Sam's Toy Rescue
stories.text: The living room was full of colorful toys. Blocks were on the rug, books were on the sofa, and rattle toys were scattered near the rocking chair. Sam’s baby brother, Eli, was sitting on his play mat, looking for his favorite red squeaky ball. Sam zoomed over like a speedy race car. "Vroom! I am on a toy rescue mission!" Sam announced with a giggly grin. Mom looked up and said, "Oh, Sam, can you help Eli find his ball?" Sam put his hands on his hips. "Leave it to me, Mom!" Sam searched under the couch. No ball. He searched behind the fluffy blue pillow. No ball. Then, peekaboo! There it was, hiding underneath a big wooden block. Sam scooped up the red squeaky ball in both hands. He carried it carefully, walking slowly so he wouldn't trip. "Here you go, Eli!" Sam said gently, kneeling down on the soft rug. Eli squealed with absolute delight and squeezed the ball. Squeak, squeak! Eli reached out and gave Sam’s leg a little hug. Sam giggled and hugged him right back. "You are welcome, baby Eli," Sam whispered. Mom smiled warmly. "You are such a caring big brother, Sam. Helping others makes our home so happy." Sam felt like the luckiest and best big brother in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo was a big boy now. He was three whole years old! Today, Leo had a very important job. His baby sister, Mia, needed a fresh diaper. Mommy smiled and asked, 'Leo, my big helper, can you get a clean diaper for Mia?' Leo puffed out his chest proudly. 'Yes, Mommy!' he cheered in his happy voice. Pat-pat-pat went his little feet as he scurried over to the basket. He looked inside and found the softest, fluffiest diaper with cute little bears on it. He grabbed it tightly with both hands, lifting it up high like a trophy. 'I got it!' Leo shouted softly so he would not startle the baby. Mommy clapped her hands together. 'Wonderful job, Leo! You are such a super helper.' Mia gurgled and kicked her tiny toes, blowing happy little bubbles. She loved her big brother so much. Leo walked carefully back to the changing table, making sure not to trip over his own shoes. He gently placed the diaper right next to Mommy, just where she needed it. 'Thank you, sweet boy,' Mommy whispered, giving Leo a warm hug and a kiss right on top of his head. Leo beamed with pride. Being a big brother felt so wonderful. He helped wipe Mia's toes and sang her a silly song about a bouncing bunny. Mia giggled her sweet baby laugh, her eyes sparkling with joy. Leo felt warm and cozy inside his heart. He knew that taking care of his baby sister was the best job in the whole wide world. When Mommy finished, Leo helped throw the old diaper into the bin, walking step-for-step like a proud little soldier. 'All done!' Leo cheered, raising his hands in victory. Mommy smiled big and gave him another tight cuddle. Leo was the best big helper ever, and he could not wait for the next fun adventure with his baby sister.

stories.title: Maya's Gentle Touch
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly through the window, waking up the cozy living room. Maya woke up and stretched her arms up high. 'Stretch, stretch, stretch!' she whispered to herself. Today was a very special day because her baby brother, Toby, was taking his morning nap in the big cradle. Mommy was busy in the kitchen making yummy oatmeal and needed a quiet helper. Maya tiptoed into the living room on her tip-toes, making her feet go *tip-toe, tip-toe, tip-toe*. She wanted to be as quiet as a little mouse. Toby stirred in his sleep and gave a tiny little whimper. Oh no! Toby was starting to wake up too soon. Maya knew just what to do. She remembered the gentle touch rule. Slowly, Maya reached out her hand and softly stroked Toby's tiny, warm blanket. She patted it gently, *tap-tap-tap*, just like the rain falling on the roof. She leaned in close and whispered in her softest, sweetest voice, 'Shh, shh, little Toby. Big sister Maya is right here. Sleep tight.' Toby heard her soothing voice and stopped crying. He scrunched up his tiny nose, let out a long sigh, and fell right back into a deep, peaceful sleep. Maya beamed with joy. She did it! She kept the baby sleeping all by herself. Just then, Mommy walked quietly into the room holding a warm cup of tea. She saw Maya standing guard like a brave little superhero. Mommy smiled the biggest, warmest smile and whispered, 'Maya, you are the most gentle and helpful big sister in the whole world.' Maya felt so proud and happy. She puffed out her chest and stood tall. Helping take care of her baby brother made her feel like a giant. She stayed right there by the cradle, humming a quiet lullaby until Toby woke up with a happy smile.

stories.title: Oliver's Toy Rescue Mission
stories.text: Oliver loved playtime. He had blocks of red, blue, and yellow scattered all across the soft playroom rug. But even more than playing alone, Oliver loved playing with his little sister, Lily. Lily was just learning how to crawl, and she loved to explore every single corner of the room. 'Beep beep! Here comes the toy train!' Oliver shouted happily, pushing his wooden engine across the tracks. Lily giggled and clapped her hands, crawling as fast as her little knees could carry her toward the blocks. But oh dear! A big red building block was right in the middle of Lily's crawling path. If she kept going, she might bump her knee and feel sad. Oliver jumped right into action. 'Stop, baby Lily! Big brother is on a rescue mission!' he said in his most heroic voice. Oliver quickly scooped up the red block and put it safely back into the toy box where it belonged. Then, he grabbed a soft, squishy yellow duck and placed it gently in front of Lily instead. Lily's eyes lit up with excitement. She squeezed the duck, and it went *squeak-squeak!* Lily laughed out loud, kicking her feet with pure delight. Oliver felt so warm and proud inside. He loved seeing his baby sister so happy. Daddy walked into the playroom and saw what a wonderful helper Oliver was being. He walked over and gave Oliver a high-five. 'Great job keeping your sister safe and happy, Oliver! You are a fantastic big brother,' Daddy praised. Oliver beamed from ear to ear. Helping Lily play safely was so much fun. He grabbed a blue block and built a tall tower together with her, sharing all his favorite toys like a truly big boy.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, little Leo! Today is a very special day because Leo is a big brother. Baby Maya wakes up from her crib and gives a big, happy yawn. 'Good morning, Maya!' whispers Leo. Mommy smiles warmly at her big boy. 'Leo, can you be my special helper today? Maya needs a fresh diaper.' Leo puffs out his chest proudly. 'I can help! I am a big boy!' Mommy sets out the soft diaper and the wipes. Leo toddles over and carefully hands Mommy a warm wipe. 'Thank you, helper,' says Mommy. Maya giggles and reaches out to touch Leo's fingers with her tiny hands. 'Look, Mommy, she likes my fingers!' says Leo, beaming from ear to ear. Next, it is time to pick out Maya's clothes for the day. 'Should Maya wear the yellow duck shirt or the green frog shirt?' asks Mommy. Leo points excitedly. 'The duck shirt! Quack, quack!' Mommy dresses baby Maya in the yellow duck shirt, and Leo makes funny duck noises that make Maya burst into giggles. 'You are such a wonderful big brother, Leo,' says Mommy, giving him a big squeeze. Being a helper makes Leo feel so tall and important. He gently pats Maya's soft hair. 'Good job, Maya. Good job, me!' he says happily. Together, they walk into the kitchen for breakfast, ready for more fun adventures as a team.

stories.title: Mia's Song for Baby Sam
stories.text: The afternoon sun is shining brightly through the window, but little baby Sam is feeling a little bit fussy. He rubs his sleepy eyes and lets out a tiny cry. 'Wah-wah!' cries Sam. Big sister Mia hears him from the playroom. She stops building her tall block tower and runs right over. 'Don't worry, Sam! Big sister is here to help!' says Mia in her sweetest, softest voice. Daddy looks up from the rocking chair and smiles. 'Mia, Sam needs his favorite blue rattle, and maybe you can sing him a gentle song to help him rest.' Mia nods seriously. 'I am the best helper!' She finds the bright blue rattle on the rug and gives it a soft shake. 'Jingle, jingle!' Sam stops crying for a second and blinks his big brown eyes at the shiny toy. Mia gently places the rattle near his little hand, and Sam grabs it with his tiny fingers. Now it is time for the song. Mia sits right next to the rocking chair and takes a deep breath. She sings her absolute favorite lullaby about a sleepy little star in the night sky. Her voice is soft and sweet, like a gentle breeze. Sam yawns a big, wide yawn and lets his eyelids flutter closed. The fussy tears are all gone now. Daddy whispers, 'Thank you, Mia. You sang so beautifully.' Mia feels warm and cozy inside. She strokes Sam's soft cheek very gently. 'Sleep tight, baby Sam,' she whispers. Being a big sister helper is the best job in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Noah's Toy Pickup Train
stories.text: The living room rug is covered in colorful toys. There are red blocks, yellow cars, and green dinosaurs everywhere! Mommy looks around and sighs gently. 'Oh my, look at all these toys taking a nap on the floor.' Big brother Noah marches right into the room with a big smile. 'Don't worry, Mommy! I am a big boy helper!' Noah announces, putting his hands on his hips like a superhero. 'Let us make a toy pickup train!' Mommy claps her hands. 'Choo-choo! What a fantastic idea, Noah!' Noah's job is super important. He has to drive the big red toy box, which is his chug-chug train engine. First, Noah zooms over to the blue blocks. He scoops them up one by one and drops them inside the box. 'Clatter, clatter, crash!' goes the box. 'One block, two blocks, three blocks!' counts Noah proudly. Next, he drives his train over to the green toy dinosaur. 'Roar! Hop into the train, Mr. Dinosaur!' Noah giggles as he puts the dinosaur inside. Baby Lily sits on the big rug nearby, watching her big brother with wide, curious eyes. Lily wants to help too! She picks up a soft yellow ball and holds it up high. 'Ba-ba!' says Lily. Noah stops his train and runs over. 'Good job, Lily! Put it in the train!' Lily drops the ball right into the box, and Noah cheers loudly. 'Yay, Lily! We did it together!' Mommy smiles and hugs them both. The floor is all clean, and the toys are tucked safely away. Noah feels so proud to be such a wonderful big brother and helper.

stories.title: Leo's Big Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo was a big boy now. He had big boy shoes, a big boy cup, and today, he was a big sibling helper! His baby sister, Mia, was sitting on her play mat, making happy little giggles. 'Buh-buh!' she said, kicking her tiny pink feet. Mommy walked over with a fresh diaper and a box of wipes. She looked down and smiled. 'Leo, my wonderful big helper, can you fetch a diaper for baby Mia?' Mommy asked. Leo puffed out his chest proudly. 'Yes, Mommy!' he cheered in his biggest boy voice. He trotted over to the basket and scooped up a fluffy, soft diaper, holding it carefully against his tummy like a precious treasure. He marched it right back to Mommy. 'Good job, superstar!' Mommy praised, giving Leo a warm hug. Mia clapped her little hands together, making a happy clapping sound. 'Yay, Leo!' she seemed to say. Mommy gently opened the diaper and needed a wipe. 'Can you hand me one wipe, please?' Mommy asked softly. Leo reached into the wipe box and pulled out one single, cool wipe, handing it over with great care. 'Thank you, sweet boy,' Mommy whispered. When the diaper change was all done, Mia was as fresh as a daisy and smiling from ear to ear. Leo felt so warm and cozy inside. Being a big brother was the best job in the whole wide world because helping mommy made him feel so tall, so smart, and so very loved. He gently patted Mia’s soft tummy and whispered, 'All clean, baby sister!' Mia let out a happy squeal, reaching up to gently touch Leo’s nose with her tiny finger. Leo giggled. Mommy beamed down at them both, her heart overflowing with so much love for her helpful boy and her sweet baby girl. Together, they made the happiest little team in the house.

stories.title: Maya's Gentle Lullaby
stories.text: The sun was starting to peek behind the big green hills, painting the sky in lovely shades of orange and pink. It was almost sleepy-time in the nursery. Baby brother Toby was rubbing his sleepy eyes. 'Yawn!' went Toby, snuggling deep into his cozy blanket. Maya, who was a wonderful big sister, knew exactly what to do. 'It is nap time, Toby,' Maya whispered softly, using her quietest, sweetest voice so she wouldn't scare the little birds outside. Daddy smiled warmly at Maya. 'Maya, my gentle helper, would you like to pick out a bedtime story for your brother?' he asked softly. Maya’s eyes lit up with joy. She tiptoed over to the bookshelf and scanned all the colorful spines. She gently pulled out her absolute favorite book about a sleepy little bear who loved honey. 'This one, Daddy!' she whispered proudly, holding the book up high. She climbed up onto the rocking chair right next to Daddy and Toby. Toby rested his sleepy head right in Maya’s lap. Maya felt so proud and important. She opened the cover and pointed her little finger at the big pictures. 'Look, Toby, the bear is sleeping,' she pointed out gently. Toby cooed, staring sleepily at the bright pages. Maya turned each page with slow, careful fingers, making sure not to rip the paper. When the story was all finished, Daddy began to softly hum a sweet lullaby. Maya joined in, whispering the gentle notes she knew by heart. Toby’s heavy eyelids fluttered, and soon, he was fast asleep, dreaming sweet little baby dreams. Maya gave her sleeping brother a tiny kiss on his soft forehead. 'Goodnight, baby brother,' she whispered ever so quietly. Daddy gave Maya a big, proud hug. 'You are the best big sister helper in the whole world,' Daddy whispered. Maya smiled happily in the dim light, feeling cozy, kind, and ready for her own sweet sleep.

stories.title: Sam and the Sharing Toy Basket
stories.text: It was a bright, sunny morning in the playroom, and the toy basket was overflowing with fun things to do. Sam stood right next to the basket, holding his favorite red bouncy ball. His little sister, Lily, toddled over on her wobbly legs, looking around with big, curious eyes. Lily spotted a shiny yellow duck and reached out her tiny hands, but the duck was tucked way at the bottom under a pile of blocks. Lily let out a little sad whine. 'Ah-bah!' she mumbled, looking like she might cry. Sam remembered he was a big sibling helper. He took a deep breath and smiled a big, friendly smile at Lily. 'Don't worry, Lily, I can help!' Sam said in a kind, encouraging voice. He knelt down on the soft playroom rug and carefully moved the blue blocks to the side, one by one, stacking them up neatly. Lily clapped her hands, watching her big brother work his magic. 'There it is!' Sam cheered happily. He reached deep into the basket and gently pulled out the shiny yellow duck. Instead of keeping it for himself, Sam held it out with both hands and offered it right to his little sister. 'Here you go, Lily!' he said cheerfully. Lily's face lit up with a huge, joyful grin. She grabbed the duck and squeezed it, making it squeak a happy 'Quack, quack!' sound. 'Quack!' Lily giggled, hugging the duck tight. Mommy walked into the playroom with a tray of apple slices and saw the whole sweet moment. She clapped her hands with delight. 'Sam, that was such a kind and helpful thing to do! Sharing makes our home so happy,' Mommy praised, giving Sam a warm, squeezy hug. Sam beamed with pride. Helping Lily find her favorite toy made his heart feel as bright as the morning sun. He sat down right next to her, ready for their next big adventure together as the best brother and sister team ever.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text:
Leo was a big boy now. He was three years old, which meant he was very, very tall. Today, his mommy needed help with baby sister Mia. Mia was sitting on her changing mat, giggling and kicking her tiny toes. 'Can big helper Leo get a fresh diaper for Mia?' asked Mommy with a warm, happy smile. Leo puffed out his chest proudly. 'Yes, Mommy! I am a super-big helper!' 

Leo walked over to the basket. He stood on his tiptoes to reach inside. He grabbed a fluffy, clean diaper with colorful stars on it. 'Look, Mia! Stars!' cooed Leo, holding it up high. Mia clapped her little hands together. 'Da-da!' she squealed happily. Leo carefully carried the diaper back, walking very slowly so he wouldn't trip. He placed it right next to Mommy just like a professional assistant. 

'Thank you, sweet boy,' Mommy said, giving Leo a gentle kiss right on his forehead. Leo felt warm and cozy inside, like a warm cup of cocoa. Next, Mommy asked for the baby wipes. Leo zoomed across the room like a fast train, making soft chugging sounds. 'Choo-choo! Wipes coming through!' He handed them over safely. 

When Mia was all clean and dressed in her soft yellow pajamas, she reached out her tiny arms for a hug. 'Do you want to give Mia her rattle, Leo?' Mommy asked. Leo gently placed the crinkly blue rattle in his little sister's hand. Mia shook it, making a cheerful rattling sound. Leo beamed from ear to ear. Being a big brother was the absolute best job in the whole wide world. He gave Mia a gentle pat on her soft curls and whispered, 'Good job being my sister, Mia.' Mommy smiled and wrapped her arms around both of them in a big, cozy cuddle.

stories.title: Maya's Storytime Surprise
stories.text:
The sun was peeking through the fluffy white curtains, and it was time for quiet afternoon reading. Maya, who was four years old, loved books with bright shiny pictures. Today, her baby brother Toby was feeling a little bit fussy. He rubbed his sleepy eyes and let out a tiny yawn. 'Toby needs help calming down for his nap,' whispered Daddy. 'Would big sister Maya like to pick a special book for him?' 

'Oh, yes, Daddy!' whispered Maya excitedly. She tiptoed over to the overflowing bookshelf. Her tiny fingers traced the spines of her favorite books. Should they read about the bouncy green frog? Or the sleepy brown bear? Maya decided on the bear book because it had shiny foil honey pots on the cover. She hugged the book tightly against her chest and marched over to the rocking chair where Daddy and Toby were sitting. 

'Sit right here, big helper,' Daddy said, patting the cozy cushion next to him. Maya climbed up carefully. Toby looked at the bright book and stopped fussing. His big blue eyes widened with curiosity. 'Can I hold it, Maya?' Daddy asked softly. Maya held the book open wide so both Toby and she could see every single picture. 

'Look, Toby! The bear is eating honey,' Maya pointed her finger at the glossy page. Toby reached out a tiny hand and patted the paper page, making a happy gurgling sound. Maya used her best storyteller voice, reading nice and slow just like her teacher at preschool did. Toby grew quieter and quieter. His heavy eyelids fluttered shut, and he snuggled deep into Daddy's warm shoulder, fast asleep. Maya whispered very quietly so she wouldn't wake him up. 'You did a wonderful job reading, Maya,' Daddy whispered back, squeezing her hand. Maya smiled proudly, feeling like the best big sister in the whole neighborhood.

stories.title: Noah's Cleanup Train
stories.text:
Living room playtime was so much fun, but now the giant box of colorful wooden blocks was spilled all across the soft blue carpet. There were red triangles, blue squares, and yellow rectangles everywhere you looked. Mommy looked at the messy floor and then smiled down at Noah, who was four and a half years old. 'Noah, buddy, it is time to tidy up. Do you think our big helper can drive the cleanup train?' 

Noah’s eyes sparkled with joy. 'Chug-chug-choo-choo! I am the cleanup train!' he shouted happily, pumping his arms back and forth like chugging wheels. 'All aboard the block train!' Mommy grabbed a big wicker basket and set it in the middle of the room. That was going to be the train station where all the blocks needed to go. 

Noah bent down and scooped up three red triangular blocks in his strong hands. 'Beep beep! Cargo coming through!' he chugged across the carpet, making loud train engine noises. *Chug, chug, chug, WHOOSH!* He dropped the blocks gently into the wicker basket. Mommy clapped her hands together. 'Wonderful job, engineer Noah! You are so fast!' 

Encouraged by the cheering, Noah went back for more. He found a big blue square block hiding underneath the fuzzy green sofa. He rescued it just in time. 'Gotcha!' he giggled. One by one, the colorful blocks found their way back into the basket. When the very last yellow rectangle was tucked safely inside, the carpet looked neat and tidy again. 

Mommy scooped Noah up into a giant bear hug and spun him around, making him laugh out loud. 'Thank you for being such an amazing helper, Noah. Our living room looks wonderful!' Noah beamed with pride, feeling like a true superhero. Keeping the playroom clean was hard work, but doing it together made it feel like a fun game.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, big boy Leo! Today is a very special day because Leo is a big brother. Little sister Mia wakes up from her cozy nap and gives a little squeak. "Ma-ma!" she says. Leo smiles a big, proud smile. He knows exactly what to do. "I can help, Mommy!" says Leo, walking over with his tippy-toes. Mommy beams down at him. "Thank you, helper Leo. Can you bring me a fresh diaper, please?" Leo runs to the basket as fast as a bunny. He finds the softest diaper with little yellow ducks on it. He carries it carefully with both hands, holding it high like a trophy. "Here is your diaper, Mia!" coos Leo. Mia claps her tiny hands together and giggles. She loves her big brother so much. Next, Mommy needs a baby wipe. Leo zooms back to the basket. "One wipe for Mia!" he says, handing it over gently. Mommy tickles Mia's toes while she cleans her up. Leo sings a silly monkey song to keep Mia happy and smiling. "Ooh-ooh, ah-ah!" sings Leo, scratching his tummy. Mia laughs a belly laugh that fills the whole room with sunshine. Now it is time for the clean diaper. Mommy puts it on, and Mia kicks her legs with joy. "All done!" cheers Leo, giving a high-five to Mommy. Mommy hugs Leo tight and kisses his forehead. "You are the best big brother in the whole wide world, Leo. Such a wonderful helper." Leo puffs out his chest with pride. Being a big brother is hard work, but it is also the best job ever. He gives baby Mia a gentle kiss on her soft cheek. Mia reaches out and boops Leo right on his nose. They both giggle together. Leo is ready for whatever adventure comes next today, knowing he is Mommy and Daddy’s super helper.

stories.title: Maya's Storytime Surprise
stories.text: The afternoon sun shines brightly through the living room window, making golden patches on the cozy rug. Maya, who is three whole years old, sits criss-cross applesauce with a stack of chunky board books in her lap. Next to her sits baby brother Toby, who is learning how to crawl. Toby wobbles on his hands and knees like a little turtle. "Time for stories!" announces Maya in her happiest voice. Toby crawls over as fast as he can, making happy baby noises. "Dada!" he babies, though he means book. Maya opens her favorite book about a sleepy brown bear. "Look, Toby! The bear is sleeping. Shh, shh," whispers Maya, putting her finger to her lips. Toby copies her, making a soft "shh" sound that is the cutest thing ever. Maya feels so proud to show him how things work. "Can you turn the page, Toby?" asks Maya gently, guiding his chubby little hand. Toby turns the cardboard page with a crinkling sound. He claps his hands when he sees a bright red apple on the page. "Apple!" says Maya, pointing to the picture. Toby babbles happily and tries to take a little nibble out of the corner of the book. Maya laughs and gently pulls the book away. "No eating books, silly goose! We only read them with our eyes and hands." Toby gives a gummy smile, understanding completely. They read about a happy green frog that jumps, and Maya demonstrates a big frog hop right on the carpet. "Ribbit! Ribbit!" she calls out. Toby giggles and tries to hop too, falling over softly onto his tummy. Mommy walks in with two cups of water and smiles warmly at the sweet scene. "Look at my wonderful big sister helping Toby read," Mommy praises softly. Maya glows with happiness from head to toe. She pats Toby’s head gently. "Good reading, Toby," she says. They finish the last book together, cuddled up side by side, sharing stories and lots of love.

stories.title: Noah's Cleanup Train
stories.text: The playroom is a sea of colorful toys. There are blocks stacked high, puzzle pieces scattered like autumn leaves, and little cars zooming everywhere. It is time to tidy up before dinner, but baby sister Lily is just waking from her nap. Daddy picks up Lily, and she reaches her arms out toward big brother Noah. "Noah!" she babbles happily. Noah looks at the messy floor and then at his baby sister. "Don't worry, Lily, Noah will save the day!" he declares bravely. Noah pretends his arms are the wheels of a big red train. "Choo-choo! All aboard the cleanup train!" he calls out happily. He chugs over to the green blocks box. "Time to load the cargo!" Noah picks up one red block, then a blue block, and drops them clitter-clatter into the bin. Lily watches from Daddy's arms, her big round eyes wide with wonder. She loves her big brother's magic train game. "Can you help, Lily?" asks Noah, driving his train over to the soft toy basket. Daddy carries Lily closer so she can drop a soft yellow duck inside. "Yay, Lily!" cheers Noah, clapping his hands. Lily beams and lets out a happy squeal. Working together makes the cleanup go super fast. Together, Noah and Lily put away the cars, the puzzle pieces, and the funny rubber ducks. Soon, the floor is totally clean, and the toys are resting snugly in their proper homes. "Look how wonderful our playroom looks!" says Daddy, setting Lily down to give Noah a giant bear hug. "You are such an amazing big brother and helper, Noah. You made cleanup time so much fun." Noah smiles ear to ear. He loves being big, he loves his baby sister, and he loves being the best helper in the whole house.

stories.title: Leo's Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo was a big boy now. He had big boy shoes, a big boy cup, and today, he had a very important job. His baby sister, Mia, needed her diaper changed! Mommy smiled and asked, "Leo, can you be my big helper?" Leo puffed out his chest and nodded. "Yes, Mommy! I am a super big helper!" First, Mommy needed a fresh diaper. "Can you fetch a diaper, please?" asked Mommy. Off went Leo, patter-patter-patter, as fast as his little legs could carry him. He zoomed to the basket and picked up the softest diaper with a picture of a happy little duck on it. "Found it, Mommy!" he cheered, handing it over carefully. Mia giggled and kicked her tiny toes. "Look, Mia is smiling at you! She loves her big brother," Mommy said softly. Next, Mommy needed a wet wipe. Leo knew just what to do. He gently pulled one wipe from the box. "One wipe, please!" he said, practicing his sharing voice. Mommy cleaned Mia up, and Leo helped toss the dirty wipe right into the tall diaper pail. Swish! Good job, Leo! Finally, it was time for the new diaper. Leo gently stroked Mia’s soft foot while Mommy worked her magic. "You are doing amazing, Leo. Such a gentle touch," praised Mommy. Leo felt warmth spread all through his tummy. Being a big brother felt so wonderful. When Mia was all fresh and dressed in her polka-dot pajamas, she reached out her little hands and made happy baby noises. Leo gently gave her a high-five with just one finger. "Good job, baby Mia!" Leo whispered proudly. Mommy hugged them both tight. "What a wonderful big brother you are, Leo." Leo beamed with joy, ready for the next big adventure of the day.

stories.title: Maya's Toy Rescue
stories.text: The living room rug was a sea of colorful blocks and fuzzy stuffed animals. Little brother Toby sat right in the middle, crying softly because his favorite squeaky red ball had rolled under the big green armchair. Oh no! Toby looked so sad. Maya, who was three whole years old, marched right over. She put her hands on her hips and said, "Don't worry, Toby! Big sister is on the case!" Maya knew just what to do. She got down on her hands and knees, ready to crawl like a brave little bear. Pitter-patter went her hands on the carpet as she crept closer to the big green armchair. She peeked underneath into the dark, dusty shadow. It was a little scary, but Maya was very brave. And there it was—the shiny red ball! Maya reached out her arm as far as it could go. Her fingers wiggled, stretch, stretch, stretch! Tap! She touched the ball. With a gentle pull, she rolled it right out into the bright living room light. Toby’s eyes went big and wide. He clapped his chubby hands together and giggled, "Ball! Ball!" Maya scooped up the red ball and handed it right to her little brother with a bright smile. "Here you go, Toby!" Toby squeezed the ball, and it made a happy little squeak. Squeak-squeak! Toby reached up and gave Maya a big, sticky toddler hug around her knees. Maya giggled and patted his curly hair. "Good sharing, Toby. We are a good team," she said, remembering the words Mommy always used. Mommy walked into the room holding a basket of clean laundry and smiled warmly. "Maya, look at you! You are such a helpful and kind big sister. You solved the problem all by yourself!" Maya felt like a superhero. Helping her little brother made her heart feel so warm and happy. She sat down right next to Toby and helped him build a tall tower with his blocks.

stories.title: Sam's Bedtime Story
stories.text: The moon was peeking up into the dark blue evening sky. It was almost bedtime for little sister Lily. Lily was rubbing her sleepy eyes, and her favorite brown bunny was resting in her lap. Daddy looked at Sam, who was wearing his cozy dinosaur pajamas. "Sam, would you like to help read Lily her bedtime story tonight?" Daddy asked gently. Sam’s eyes sparkled. "Oh, yes, Daddy! I can read to my baby sister!" Sam loved books, and he knew all the best ones by heart. Sam crawled onto the big rocking chair right next to Lily. Lily snuggled close, smelling like sweet baby lotion and fresh soap. Sam picked up the thick book about the sleepy little bear who lost his honey pot. He opened the cover very carefully, making sure not to rip the paper. "Can you point to the moon, Lily?" Sam asked softly, using his quiet indoor voice. Lily pointed her tiny finger right at the big yellow moon painted on the page. "Good job, Lily!" Sam cheered in a whisper. Sam turned the page slowly. Swish went the paper. He pointed to the pictures and made funny animal sounds that made Lily giggle behind her pacifier. "Hoot-hoot!" went the wise old owl. "Grrr!" went the sleepy bear. Lily laughed her sweet baby laugh, which was Sam's favorite sound in the whole wide world. Sam felt so important holding the book and sharing the story. He patted Lily's soft back just like Mommy did when she was tired. Soon, Lily’s heavy eyelids fluttered shut, and her breathing slowed down. She was fast asleep, cuddling her brown bunny. Daddy whispered, "You are the best big brother helper in the whole world, Sam. You helped Lily fall fast asleep." Sam smiled proudly in the dim room. He kissed Lily’s forehead gently and whispered, "Goodnight, sweet baby sister." Then he tiptoed off to his own bed, feeling like a very big, very helpful boy.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, big boy Leo! Today is a very sunny day, and Leo has a very important job. Baby sister Lily is crying in her crib. 'Uh-oh, is Lily's diaper wet?' asks Mama with a warm smile. Leo nods his head up and down. 'I can help, Mama! I am a big helper!' Leo walks over to the diaper basket with his little tippy-toes. He picks up a soft, fluffy diaper and hands it right to Mama. 'Thank you, my wonderful helper,' says Mama. Lily stops crying and gives a big, gummy smile to her big brother. Leo feels so proud inside. His chest puffs out like a brave little bird. Next, it is time for the wipes. Mama asks, 'Can you hold the wipes box, Leo?' Leo holds the box with both of his strong hands. He holds it very still, just like a statue. 'Good job holding!' cheers Mama. Lily kicks her happy little feet in the air, splashing the air with giggles. Leo gently pats Lily's tummy. 'All done, baby sister!' he sings in a sweet voice. When Mama picks Lily up, Leo walks beside them all the way to the rocking chair. He carries Lily's favorite rattle toy to keep her happy. 'You are the best big brother in the whole wide world,' whispers Mama, giving Leo a big, tight hug. Leo beams with joy. Being a big sibling helper is so much fun, and Leo's heart feels as warm as the morning sun.

stories.title: Mia's Gentle Rock-a-Bye
stories.text: The clock says it is naptime in the cozy yellow room. Baby brother Toby is rubbing his tired eyes. 'Yawn!' goes Toby. Mama has her hands full folding warm laundry on the big bed. She looks at Mia and asks, 'Mia, sweetie, can you help soothe Toby while I finish folding?' Mia claps her hands together softly. 'Yes, Mama! I am Toby's helper!' Mia tiptoes across the soft rug so she does not make a loud noise. She walks over to Toby's rocking chair. 'Shh, shh, little brother,' Mia whispers in her quietest, sweetest mouse voice. Toby looks up at Mia and starts to calm down. He likes his big sister's gentle face. Mia picks up Toby's favorite blue blanket with the fluffy stars. She drapes it carefully over his tiny legs. 'So cozy, Toby,' Mia says with a loving smile. Then, Mia starts to sing. She sings her favorite lullaby about a twinkling star. Her voice is soft and sweet like honey. Toby closes his heavy eyes and listens to the pretty music. He snuggles deeper into the soft cushions. Mama walks over quietly and gives Mia a gentle kiss on top of her head. 'You have magic helper hands, Mia,' Mama whispers. Mia feels so peaceful and happy standing beside her sleeping baby brother. She watches him breathe softly in and out. Being a gentle helper makes Mia feel like a true princess of kindness.

stories.title: Sam's Mighty Toy Cleanup
stories.text: The playroom floor is covered in colorful blocks, plastic dinosaurs, and rolling cars. It looks like a rainbow tornado came to visit! 'Time to tidy up!' sings Papa. Little sister Emma sits on the floor, trying to put a big round ball into a tiny basket. She tries and tries, but it rolls away. 'Uh-oh!' says Emma with a little pout. Sam, the big brother, runs right over to the rescue. 'Don't worry, Emma! Big brother Sam is here to help!' Sam picks up the bouncy ball and drops it right into the basket. 'Yay!' claps Emma, her sad frown turning into a bright sunshine smile. Sam feels so happy inside his tummy. 'Now let us clean up together, team!' says Sam. He grabs the big yellow toy box and pulls it to the middle of the room. Sam picks up a red block and tosses it in. Clatter-clatter-clash! Then he picks up a green dinosaur and tucks it in safely. Emma wants to help too! She picks up a soft yellow duck and hands it to Sam. 'Good job, Emma!' praises Sam, using a big-kid voice just like Papa. They work together like busy little worker bees. Block by block, toy by toy, the messy floor becomes clean and clear. Papa comes in and gasps in surprise. 'Look at this amazing cleanup! You two are the greatest helpers ever!' Sam wraps his arms around Emma in a joyful group hug. Helping together makes playtime and cleanup time twice as nice.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, big boy Leo! Today is a very special day because Leo has an extra-important job. His baby sister, Mia, just woke up from a nice long nap, and she needs a fresh diaper. Mommy looks at Leo and asks, 'Can my wonderful big helper bring me a clean diaper, please?' Leo puffs out his chest and says, 'Yes, Mommy! I am a big boy helper!' Off he goes, marching into the nursery with happy little steps. He walks right up to the basket and finds the softest, fluffiest diaper with cute little yellow ducks on it. He carries it back carefully with both hands, holding it tight just like a precious treasure. 'Here you go, Mommy!' Leo says proudly, handing it over with a big, bright grin. Mommy gives him a warm, cozy hug and says, 'Thank you so much, Leo. You are such a caring big brother.' Next, Mia needs a little wipe for her hands. Mommy asks, 'Leo, can you pick out a wipe too?' Leo nods eagerly and toddles back to the changing table. He grabs one gentle wipe and hands it to Mommy with care. While Mommy gently cleans Mia, Mia looks right at Leo and makes a happy little gurgle sound, like she is saying thank you in baby talk. Leo giggles and gently pats his baby sister's tiny foot. 'Good job, Mia,' he whispers sweetly. Being a big helper makes Leo feel so tall and proud inside. He loves his baby sister very much, and he loves being her special helper every single day.

stories.title: Maya's Storytime Song
stories.text: The sun is going down, and the house is getting nice and quiet. It is almost bedtime for baby Toby, but Toby is feeling a little bit fussy and wants to wiggle all around. Big sister Maya knows just what to do! Maya loves to use her wonderful big girl powers to help out. She walks over to the cozy rocking chair where Daddy is holding baby Toby. 'Daddy,' Maya whispers softly, 'can I help sing Toby to sleep?' Daddy smiles and whispers back, 'I think that would make Toby very happy, Maya.' Maya climbs gently onto the footstool and sits down right next to them. She thinks of her favorite song about a little star twinkling in the sky. She takes a big breath and starts to sing in her sweetest, softest voice. 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star...' she sings, swaying her head gently from side to side. Baby Toby stops squirming right away. He turns his sleepy head toward Maya and blinks his big round eyes, listening to her comforting voice. Maya smiles even bigger and keeps on singing, adding hand motions with her fingers just like little twinkling stars. Toby lets out a long, cozy yawn and rests his heavy head right on Daddy's shoulder. His little eyelids are getting heavier and heavier. 'Good job, superstar helper,' Daddy whispers softly to Maya. Maya feels a warm, cozy feeling spread all through her tummy. She leans over and gives Toby a tiny, gentle kiss on his soft forehead. 'Sleep tight, baby Toby,' she whispers. Helping her little brother get ready for bed makes Maya feel like the best big sister in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Sam's Toy Rescue Mission
stories.text: Ring-a-ling! The playpen is getting a little bit crowded because baby sister Lily wants to play with all of her colorful blocks at the same time. But oh no! One bright red block rolls far away across the soft rug, all the way under the big yellow rocking chair. Lily points her little finger at the red block and makes a sad little sound. 'Buh-buh!' she says. Big brother Sam is playing nearby with his choo-choo train, but he stops right away when he hears his sister. Sam is a brave toy-rescue hero! He puts his train down gently and says, 'Don't worry, Lily, Sam will save your block!' Sam gets down on his hands and knees. He crawls across the floor like a happy little puppy dog, moving quickly and carefully. He looks under the rocking chair and spots the shiny red block hiding in the shadows. Sam reaches out his strong arm, wiggles his fingers, and grabs the block safely. 'Got it!' Sam cheers happily. He crawls back to the playpen and gently places the red block right back into Lily's waiting hands. Lily claps her hands together and lets out a joyful squeal of delight. She hugs the block tight and gives Sam a big, gummy smile. Sam feels so proud and happy to be such a helpful big brother. 'Good rescue, Sam!' Mommy calls out from the kitchen, giving him a warm, proud thumbs-up. Sam stands up tall and smiles from ear to ear. Being a big helper is so much fun, especially when it makes his baby sister smile.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Good morning, big boy Leo! Today is a very sunny and bright day. Leo has a tiny baby sister named Mia. Mia is sleeping in her cozy crib. Yawn, stretch! Mia wakes up and makes a soft little squeak. 'Good morning, Mia!' whispers Leo. Leo is a big brother now, and big brothers are super helpers. Mommy smiles and says, 'Leo, can you be my special helper today?' Leo puffs out his chest proudly. 'Yes, Mommy! I am a big helper!' Mommy needs a clean diaper for baby Mia. She asks Leo to fetch a fresh diaper from the basket. Pitter-patter go Leo’s fast feet. He runs over to the colorful basket and picks out the softest, fluffiest diaper with little stars on it. 'Here you go, Mommy!' says Leo, handing it over with two hands. Mommy gives him a warm hug and says, 'Thank you, sweet boy!' Next, Mia needs to pick her outfit for the day. Mommy asks Leo to choose a onesie. Leo looks at the pile of clothes. He sees a yellow onesie with a happy little duck on it. 'Quack, quack!' says Leo. 'Let's wear the ducky one!' Mommy claps her hands. 'What a wonderful choice!' While Mommy fastens the snaps, Leo gently shakes a squeaky yellow rattle. Shake, shake, rattle, rattle! Mia looks up at the toy and giggles a happy baby giggle. Her eyes sparkle with joy. Leo beams with a big, proud smile. Being a big brother is so much fun, and he is very good at it. Mommy kisses the top of Leo's head. 'You are the best big helper in the whole wide world, Leo.' Leo feels warm and happy inside his heart. He gently pats Mia’s tiny hand. 'Good job waking up, Mia,' Leo whispers softly. Together, Leo and Mommy take care of baby sister, making a happy team. Time for breakfast, big helper Leo!

stories.title: Maya's Storytime Song
stories.text: The clock says it is almost nap time in the cozy pink house. Little brother Toby is rubbing his tired eyes. He is yawning big, wide yawns like a sleepy little bear. Toby wants his favorite bedtime story book, but it is sitting all the way across the soft rug. Mommy is busy rocking the sleepy baby, and her hands are full. Enter Maya! Maya is a wonderful big sister, and she loves to help out. 'I can get it, Mommy!' whispers Maya in her quiet, indoor voice. Maya tiptoes across the soft carpet like a sneaky little mouse. Tip-toe, tip-toe, tip-toe. She reaches the big blue basket and picks up the thick book about the sleepy green frog. She holds it carefully against her tummy with both arms. 'I got it!' Maya whispers happily. She walks back very carefully so she does not trip. Toby is sitting on the floor now, looking a little bit grumpy because he is tired. Maya kneels down right beside him on the rug. 'Look, Toby! It’s the frog book!' Toby’s grumpy frown turns right upside down into a sweet little smile. Maya opens the book to the very first page. She points her finger at the big green frog. 'Ribbit, ribbit,' says Maya in a silly, croaking voice. Toby giggles and tries to copy her. 'Rib-bit!' he says. Maya turns the paper page gently, be careful, not too fast. 'Turn the page, just like this,' Maya tells him softly. Toby watches his big sister with big, bright eyes. Mommy smiles a big, warm smile from the rocking chair. 'You are such a helpful and gentle big sister, Maya,' whispers Mommy. Maya feels so proud and happy. She loves sharing special moments with her little brother. Toby rests his heavy head right on Maya’s shoulder. They snuggle close together while they look at the pictures. Maya whispers a soft story to her sleepy baby brother until his eyes close tight. Goodnight, little Toby. Good job, big sister Maya!

stories.title: Sam and the Toy Rescue
stories.text: Ring, ring! The playpen is full of bright, colorful toys, but baby brother Noah cannot reach his favorite red ball. The red ball rolled all the way into the corner, behind the big blue plush teddy bear. Noah reaches out his tiny hands, but he is too short. He lets out a little whine. 'Oh no!' says Sam. Sam is a big boy, and big brothers are expert toy rescuers. Sam walks over to the playpen with a very important look on his face. 'Don't worry, Noah! Big brother Sam is on the case!' Sam declares in his strong, brave voice. He bends his knees down low and reaches his arm far, far out. Stretch, stretch! His fingers wiggle, trying to touch the bouncy red ball. Almost there... just a little bit more! Tap! Sam’s fingers brush against the shiny red surface. He scoops it up safely into his hands. Noah claps his little hands together and cheers, 'Yay! Ball!' Sam holds the red ball up high in the air like a trophy. 'Mission accomplished!' says Sam with a huge grin. Then, Sam remembers that sharing is caring. He gently rolls the red ball across the smooth wooden floor toward Noah. Roll, roll, roll! The ball goes right into Noah’s lap. Noah giggles and throws it right back to Sam. 'Catch!' says Noah in his sweet baby talk. Sam catches the ball against his tummy. 'Good catch, Noah!' praises Sam. Mommy walks into the room carrying a basket of clean laundry. She sees Sam playing nicely and sharing with his baby brother. 'What a wonderful big helper you are, Sam! You are so kind and thoughtful,' Mommy says, giving him a big squeeze. Sam beams with joy. He loves playing games with his little brother. Cleaning up and sharing makes the whole house happy. Sam gathers up the rest of the toys, putting them gently back into the toy box. One, two, three blocks go in! Noah helps by tossing in a soft yellow duck. Teamwork makes playtime so much fun for the two brothers.

stories.title: Leo's Special Diaper Duty
stories.text: Leo woke up with a big stretch. 'Good morning, sunshine!' whispered Mommy. Today was a very special day because Leo was a big brother.
