Washing his hands and brushing his teeth, Leo gets ready for his own bed. He cuddles under his blankets, feeling peaceful and proud, knowing his toys are tucked away safely until morning.

stories.title: The Starry Night Toy Shelf
stories.text: The moon is glowing high and bright outside, sending soft silver beams across the bedroom floor. Lily is wearing her favorite star-printed pajamas and holding her favorite bedtime storybook. But wait! The room is still a little bit messy. Plastic animals are standing on the rug, and colorful stacking rings are rolling near the bed. Lily wants to be a great helper. "Where do the toys sleep when the moon comes out?" Lily asks, looking up at her big sister, Sarah. Sarah smiles warmly and takes Lily by the hand. "Let's look at the toy shelf, Lily. That is where all the toys go to dream under the stars." Lily walks over to the wooden bookshelf. The shelves are empty right now, waiting for guests. Lily picks up the bright pink piggy bank first. "Time for sleep, little piggy," Lily sings softly. She places the piggy safely on the very top shelf where it can watch over the room. Next, Lily scoops up the little plastic farm animals: the cow, the horse, and the little pink pig. One by one, she walks them over to the middle shelf, lining them up neatly so they can talk about their fun day. "Goodnight, cow. Goodnight, horse," Lily whispers to each one. Then, she gathers the stacking rings and puts them back on their tall yellow pole, making a colorful tower that looks like a sleepy rainbow. The bedroom floor is all clean and tidy now! Lily steps back and looks at the shelf. Every toy has its own special, cozy spot to rest until the sun wakes up tomorrow. Sarah claps her hands gently. "You did a fantastic job, Lily! You are such a caring friend to all your toys." Lily feels a warm, happy glow in her heart. She loves helping out and making things neat. Climbing into her own cozy bed, Lily pulls her favorite blanket up to her chin. She smiles in the quiet room, closing her eyes as she drifts off to sleep, feeling safe and happy alongside her resting toys.

stories.title: Teddy Bear's Cozy Bedtime
stories.text: The sun was starting to go down, painting the sky in pretty pink and orange colors. Little Leo rubbed his sleepy eyes. 'Time to tidy up, Leo!' said Mommy with a warm, gentle smile. Leo looked all around the playroom. Blocks were scattered on the soft rug, and his favorite brown bear, Barnaby, was sitting all alone on the cold floor. 'Oh no, Barnaby,' Leo whispered softly. 'Are you tired?' Barnaby gave a little squeak in Leo's imagination, as if to say yes. 'Don't worry, little bear. It is time to find out where do the toys sleep!' Leo picked up Barnaby and gave him a big, squeezy hug. He carried him over to the big toy chest in the corner of the room. The toy chest was open wide, lined with a fluffy, soft blanket that felt just like a cloud. 'This is your special sleepy bed, Barnaby,' Leo said happily. He tucked the little bear right in, making sure his fuzzy head rested on a tiny pillow made of scrap fabric. Next, Leo went back for the colorful wooden blocks. One by one, he picked them up. 'Time for bed, block number one! Time for bed, block number two!' He gently placed them inside a neat little basket right next to the chest. 'Goodnight, blocks,' Leo said. Then came the squeaky toy duck. 'Quack quack says goodnight,' Leo giggled, placing the duck on a low shelf where he could watch the moon. Leo looked around the room. Everything was picked up, safe, and sound asleep in its own special spot. Mommy clapped her hands proudly. 'Look at you, Leo! You are such a big helper. You tucked all your toys in so nicely.' Leo felt so proud inside his heart. He knew that when toys have a cozy place to sleep, they wake up rested and ready for brand new adventures the very next morning. With a happy yawn, Leo washed his hands, brushed his teeth, and hopped into his own warm bed. He closed his eyes, knowing Barnaby and his friends were resting peacefully right down the hall. Goodnight, toys. Goodnight, sweet Leo.

stories.title: The Train's Journey to the Garage
stories.text: Choo-choo! Clickety-clack! The little blue toy train rolled right across the living room rug, stopping near the sofa. Mia giggled and clapped her hands. 'You are a very fast train, little engine!' she cheered. But outside the window, the big yellow sun was hiding behind the hills. The sky turned a sleepy, dark blue. It was getting close to bedtime. 'Do you know where do the toys sleep, little train?' Mia asked softly. The train sat quietly on the track, waiting for its driver. Mia knew just what to do. 'Every sleepy train needs a cozy garage to rest its wheels,' she said with a bright smile. She scooped up the train in her gentle hands. She walked over to the wooden cubby shelf by the bookshelf. The bottom cubby was empty, clean, and waiting. Mia had placed a soft washcloth inside to make it feel extra warm and snug. 'This is your roundhouse garage for the night,' Mia whispered. She gently parked the train inside the cubby. 'Puff, puff, rest your engine.' Next, Mia looked around for the train tracks. She picked up each curved wooden piece, stacking them neatly in a sturdy cardboard box just beneath the shelf. 'All the tracks go to sleep together so they can make new roads tomorrow!' Mia encouraged herself, feeling very helpful. She found the little plastic station house and placed it right beside the garage. Mia stepped back and looked at the tidy corner. Everything looked so peaceful and organized. Daddy walked in and gave Mia a gentle pat on the head. 'What a wonderful job you did cleaning up, Mia! You took such good care of your toys.' Mia beamed with pride. Putting toys to sleep was actually a lot of fun when you did it with love. She waved goodnight to the little train and whispered, 'Sweet dreams on the tracks.' Then, Mia skipped off to take her bath and snuggle into her own comfy bed, ready for a wonderful night of sleep.

stories.title: Dolly's Starry Night Pajama Party
stories.text: The stars were beginning to twinkle in the night sky like little diamonds. Inside the bedroom, Maya was playing with her favorite doll, Rosie, who wore a dress with pink polka dots. 'Can you hear that, Rosie? The stars are telling us it is almost time for bed,' Maya whispered. Rosie sat quietly in Maya's lap, looking very ready for a rest. Maya gently bopped Rosie on the nose and asked, 'Do you know where do the toys sleep when the moon comes out?' Maya knew Rosie loved to feel safe and warm. She stood up and walked over to the doll's special white wicker bed tucked neatly in the corner of the room. The doll bed had a tiny, flowered mattress and a folded-up quilt that smelled like lavender. 'Here is your cozy bed, Rosie,' Maya said with joy in her voice. She carefully laid Rosie down on the mattress. She pulled the little quilt all the way up to Rosie's chin. 'Close your eyes and dream of sweet things,' Maya hummed softly, brushing a stray piece of yarn hair from the doll's forehead. But wait! There were other toys that needed to sleep, too. Maya looked down at the floor where a fluffy stuffed bunny and a rubber dinosaur were resting. 'Come along, friends!' Maya said encouragingly. She picked up the bunny and tucked him right at the foot of Rosie's bed. Then, she placed the dinosaur in a soft basket filled with plush toys, making sure he had plenty of room to stretch his long tail. Maya looked around the room. All her favorite playthings were tucked into their proper, cozy beds. Mommy peeked through the doorway and smiled a huge, loving smile. 'You are such a caring and responsible big girl, Maya. Look how happy your toys look!' Maya felt a warm, glowing feeling inside. Taking care of her toys made her feel like a wonderful helper. She turned off the bright overhead light, leaving only the soft glow of her star nightlight. 'Goodnight, Rosie. Goodnight, bunny. Goodnight, little dinosaur,' Maya whispered. Then, she climbed into her own bed, ready to drift off to sleep right alongside her sleeping friends.

stories.title: The Big Toy Sleepy Train
stories.text: The sun is sinking low in the sky, painting the bedroom wall with soft pink and golden light. It is almost bedtime for Leo, but wait! What about all of Leo’s favorite toys? They have played so hard all day long, zooming cars, building blocks, and flying high in the air. Now, their little toy eyes are starting to blink. They look very, very tired. Leo’s mom smiles and whispers, 'Time to tuck the toys in, little one.' Leo claps his hands with joy. He loves taking care of his friends. First up is Teddy Bear. Teddy gives Leo a big, fuzzy hug before climbing into his special cardboard box bed. 'Goodnight, Teddy,' Leo whispers, pulling a tiny washcloth over him like a warm blanket. Next come the racing cars. Vroom, vroom, quiet now! They park themselves neatly in a row inside the low toy chest garage. No more zooming tonight, little cars. It is time to rest your wheels. Last of all is Dolly, who sits right on the soft reading chair, looking ready for sweet dreams. Leo walks around the room, making sure every single block is back in the big bin and every puzzle piece is tucked safely inside its box. Everything is so quiet and peaceful. Leo feels so proud of himself. He helped all his toys find their cozy resting places. 'Sleep tight, toys,' Leo says softly. Then, Leo walks to his own big bed, snuggles under his own soft blanket, and gets ready for sleep. Just like his toys, Leo has had a wonderful, busy day, and now it is time to rest. Goodnight, toys. Goodnight, Leo. Sweet dreams to you all.

stories.title: The Pajama Party for Blocks and Bears
stories.text: The moon is peeking through the bedroom window, smiling down at Maya. The day has been full of laughter, stacking blocks as high as the clouds and dressing up dolls for a tea party. But now, the room is getting quiet. The shadows are stretching long, and the stars are twinkling outside. It is time for everyone to go to sleep, even the toys! Maya looks around the floor. There are bright yellow, red, and blue blocks scattered everywhere. 'Time for bed, little blocks,' Maya says in her gentlest, sweetest voice. She picks up each block one by one and places them inside their cozy wooden house. Click, clack, snap! They all fit together perfectly, resting happily until tomorrow. Next, it is time for the fluffy stuffed bunny. Bunny has hopped all around the rug today and needs a good cuddle. Maya scoops Bunny up, gives her a gentle nose-rub, and places her right on the fluffy pillow at the head of the doll bed. 'Time to rest your floppy ears, Bunny,' Maya sings softly. The toy dinosaurs stomped their last stomp and now they are gently lying down on the soft bedroom rug, dreaming of green jungles. Maya looks around her room. Every single toy is tucked into its special bed or resting place. The room looks so neat and calm. Maya beams with a big, happy smile. She is such a wonderful helper! Tidying up feels so good. Now, Maya climbs up into her own warm, cozy bed. She pulls her blanket up to her chin and lets out a big, relaxed yawn. Her toys are sleeping peacefully, and soon, Maya is fast asleep too. Goodnight, little helper.

stories.title: The Sleepy Star’s Toy Lullaby
stories.text: Twinkle, twinkle, little star, time to rest both near and far. The day is done, and shadows fall over the playroom floor. Toby hears a big yawn. Was that a yawn? Yes! It came from the shelf where the wooden train engine sits. Toot-toot, whispers the little engine, I am ready for sleep. Toby smiles and runs over to help. 'Let’s get everyone ready for bed,' Toby says. The toy train rolls slowly onto the blue track rug and stops at the wooden station house. That is the train’s cozy bed. Next, the soft lamb plushie is looking for a snuggle. Toby picks up the lamb and places it gently inside the toy hammock hanging by the window. The lamb sways back and forth, gently rocking to sleep. Rock-a-bye, little lamb. Then, Toby finds three colorful balls rolling near the door. Up they go, back into the round basket where they can cuddle together and not roll away in the dark. Toby makes sure every doll, truck, and puzzle piece is resting in its proper home. The room is so tidy and peaceful. A warm feeling glows inside Toby’s tummy. Cleaning up is like giving the room a big, loving hug. Toby feels like a true superhero of tidiness. Now, the toys are all safe, tucked in, and resting quietly under the soft moonlight. Toby turns off the bright overhead light and leaves the soft nightlight glowing. It is time for Toby to rest, too. Toby crawls under the covers, snuggles the favorite blanket, and closes tired eyes. Sweet dreams, little toys. Sweet dreams, Toby.

stories.title: The Sleepy Bear's Cozy Cave
stories.text: The sun is sinking low in the sky, painting the living room walls in soft, golden light. It is time for little Leo to start getting ready for bed. But wait! What about all of Leo's friends who have been playing so hard all day long? Teddy Bear is sitting right in the middle of the soft rug, and Bright Yellow Car is parked near the sofa. 'Where do the toys sleep, Daddy?' Leo asks softly, rubbing his sleepy eyes. Daddy smiles and gives Leo a gentle hug. 'Every toy has a special, cozy bed just like you, Leo. Let us go tuck them in so they can dream sweet dreams.' Leo's face lights up with a big, happy smile. He picks up Teddy Bear first. Teddy is very heavy with sleep. Leo carries him carefully to the fluffy toy basket in the corner. 'Time for bed, Teddy,' Leo whispers, pulling a soft blanket right up to Teddy’s furry chin. Next, Leo finds Bright Yellow Car. 'Vroom, vroom, time to park for the night,' Leo says softly. He rolls the little car right into its special garage spot on the low wooden shelf. All the blocks go back into their big wooden box, hugging each other in a neat little stack. The bright blue ball rolls gently into the toy chest, saying a silent good-night. Leo looks around the room. Everything is so clean, tidy, and quiet. 'You did such a wonderful job helping your toys find sleep, Leo,' Daddy praises, giving him a high-five. Leo feels so proud of himself. Now that all the toys are tucked safely into their beds, Leo knows it is his turn, too. He walks hand-in-hand with Daddy to his own warm bed. He climbs under his favorite star-printed quilt and snuggles deep down. As Leo closes his eyes, he feels safe and happy, knowing his toys are resting peacefully, waiting to play again when the bright morning sun comes back to say hello. Good-night, toys. Good-night, little Leo. Sleep tight until tomorrow brings a whole new day of fun and happy adventures.

stories.title: The Toy Train's Journey Home
stories.text: Choo-choo! Clickety-clack! The little wooden train engine chugs across the bedroom floor, making soft chugging sounds. Little Maya is playing her favorite evening game. But look—the shadows are stretching long across the floorboards, and the stars are starting to twinkle outside the window. It is almost bedtime for Maya, which means it is also bedtime for all her busy toys. Maya sits cross-legged on the carpet and looks down at her colorful collection of playthings. 'Where do the toys sleep?' Maya wonders out loud. Mommy walks over, stepping softly, and sits right down beside her. 'Let us find out together, Maya,' Mommy says with a warm, encouraging smile. 'Toys love to rest after a wonderful day of play. Can you help them find their sleeping stations?' Maya nods eagerly, her eyes shining with excitement. She picks up the wooden train engine first. 'All aboard for Sleepy Town!' Maya whispers. She guides the train along the track and right into its wooden station box. Click-clack, stop! The little train is parked safely for the night. Next, Maya spots her favorite doll, Rosie, sitting on the armchair. Rosie looks a little bit tired. Maya gently picks her up, brushes her yarn hair, and places her carefully on the small doll bed with a pink pillow. 'Sleep tight, Rosie,' Maya says, kissing the doll's soft cheek. The colorful stacking rings slide back onto their pole one by one, like stacking up sweet little pillows. The crayons go back into their box, all lined up like soldiers ready for a long night's nap. Mommy claps her hands softly. 'Look at you, Maya! You are a super helper. You tucked every single toy into its cozy home.' Maya beams with joy and pride. Her room looks so peaceful and tidy. Knowing her toys are resting comfortably makes Maya feel ready for bed herself. She brushes her teeth, puts on her soft pajamas, and crawls into her own cozy bed. Mommy reads her a favorite bedtime story, and soon, Maya's eyelids grow heavy. She drifts off to sleep, dreaming of the happy trains and dolls resting quietly in the dark.

stories.title: Starlight Lullaby for the Toy Box
stories.text: The moon is shining bright and round like a silver coin in the deep blue night sky. Inside the warm and cozy nursery, little Toby is getting ready for his nightly slumber. But before Toby can close his eyes, he remembers his wonderful toys scattered across the colorful playroom rug. Dinosaur is resting near the reading chair, and Duck is floating in an imaginary pond on the carpet. 'Where do the toys sleep when the moon comes out?' Toby asks in a soft, whispery voice. Grandma walks over, her slippers making a gentle swishing sound on the floor. She kneels down beside Toby and strokes his soft hair. 'The toys get very tired after playing with you all day, Toby. They need a deep, restful sleep just like you do. Shall we tuck them into the Great Toy Box?' Toby nods with enthusiasm and crawls over to Dinosaur. He picks up the green dinosaur and gives it a gentle pat on the head. 'Time to sleep, Dini,' Toby whispers, placing the dinosaur gently inside the big, open toy box. Dinosaur rests right on top of a pile of soft stuffed animals who are already yawning. Next, Toby rescues Duck from the middle of the floor. 'Quack-quack, time for bed,' Toby giggles, guiding Duck to a special corner of the box next to a fluffy bunny. The building blocks slide together into a neat stack, making clicking noises as they settle down for the night. The picture books close their covers with a soft thud and slide back onto the low bookshelf, lined up neatly like a row of sleeping friends. Grandma smiles and wraps her arms around Toby in a warm, loving hug. 'You are such a kind and thoughtful boy, Toby. You made sure every single toy is warm and safe.' Toby feels a warm glow of pride in his tummy. His room is wonderfully quiet and tidy. With his toys resting happily in their beds, Toby feels completely ready for his own sleep. He climbs into his comfortable bed, pulls up his quilt, and listens to the quiet night. He closes his eyes, smiling softly, knowing that tomorrow, he and his well-rested toys will wake up ready for a brand-new day of fun and games.

stories.title: The Big Toy Sleepytime Train
stories.text: The sun is going down, painted in soft pinks and sleepy purples. Time for bed! But wait, what about the toys? The living room looks like a busy playroom, but the toys are yawning big, wide yawns. Big yawn, little teddy! Big yawn, shiny red car! Let us help them find their cozy beds, just like you find yours. First, we find the fuzzy brown bear. Bear has had a very busy day of climbing sofa mountains and giving the biggest hugs. Where does Bear sleep? Not on the hard floor! Bear sleeps right on the fluffy blue armchair, snuggled up with a soft striped pillow. Goodnight, Bear. Next comes the bouncy green frog. Frog loves to leap, but even happy little frogs need to rest their jumping legs. Where does Frog sleep? Right inside the toy basket, tucked beneath a cozy blanket made of soft felt. Goodnight, Frog! Look over there by the window. It is the shiny red toy train. Choo-choo! The train has puffed smoke all day long. Now the wheels are still. The train sleeps on its special wooden tracks right on the nursery rug, dreaming of happy tracks that go all the way to the moon. Finally, we look at all the colorful building blocks. They are scattered everywhere! Let us gather them up gently, one by one. Plop, plop, into the big toy chest. The chest is their cozy nighttime house where all the blocks snuggle together in the dark. Every single toy is tucked in tight and fast asleep. Now the room is quiet, neat, and peaceful. Just like the toys, you had a big day of playing, learning, and growing. You did such a wonderful job helping the toys find their sleepy spots! Now it is your turn to snuggle into your warm bed. Close your eyes, take a deep, gentle breath, and let sweet dreams wrap around you. Goodnight, sweet little one, and goodnight to all your wonderful toy friends.

stories.title: Starlight Bedtime for Dolly and Friends
stories.text: Twinkle, twinkle, little star! The evening sky is turning dark and velvety blue. The stars are blinking hello, which means it is time for the toys to settle down for the night. Come along, little helper, let us tuck our friends in for sweet dreams. First, we look for Dolly. Dolly has lovely yellow yarn hair and a pretty pink dress. She danced all afternoon and now her painted eyes are heavy. Where does Dolly sleep? She has a lovely wooden doll cradle right in the corner of the room. We lay Dolly down very softly. Pat, pat, go the little blankets over her shoulders. Goodnight, Dolly! Next, we find the spotted puppy dog with floppy ears. Puppy barked happy helloes all day and wagged his tail until it got tired. Where does Puppy sleep? Right at the foot of Dolly's bed, curled up in a snug little circle. Goodnight, Puppy! Oh, look behind the rocking chair. It is the yellow duck with bright orange webbed feet. Quack-quack, but very softly now, because the house is falling asleep. Duck sleeps on the bottom shelf of the bookshelf, right next to your favorite bedtime storybooks. That way, Duck can guard the stories all through the night. Every toy has a special home where it rests until morning time. You are so gentle and kind when you put the toys away. Tidying up is like giving your room a big, warm hug. When the toys are tucked in safe and sound, they feel so loved and happy. Now look around the room. Everything is tidy, quiet, and peaceful. The moon is shining softly through the window, smiling down at you and your sleeping toys. You did a fantastic job tonight. You are growing up so big and responsible! Now it is time for you to climb into your own cozy bed, pull up your blankets, and drift off to dreamland. Sleep tight, little star.

stories.title: The Pajama Party for Tiny Dinosaurs
stories.text: The lamps are glowing with a warm, soft light. Outside, the crickets are singing a sleepy nighttime song. The day is over, and playtime is done. But wait! The little plastic dinosaurs are still sitting right in the middle of the rug. Roar? No, no, little dinosaurs, it is time for shh-shh, not roar-roar! Let us help them find their nighttime sleeping nests. Dinosaurs are big and strong, but these tiny toy dinosaurs are ready for bed. Where do the dinosaurs sleep? They sleep in the green toy bin, which makes a wonderful, cozy cave! One by one, we pick them up. Here is the long-necked brontosaurus. Into the cave he goes, resting his long neck on a soft cotton washcloth. Goodnight, brontosaurus! Here is the mighty T-Rex with his little arms. Into the cave he goes, curling up so he can dream of green fern leaves. Goodnight, T-Rex! And here is the flying pterodactyl, folding his wings nice and flat. He sleeps right on top of the pile, watching over his dinosaur friends like a sleepy guard. Every single toy has a cozy place to rest until the sun wakes up tomorrow. Picking up your toys makes your room feel so calm and happy. You are such a helpful superstar! Putting things away is a wonderful way to take care of the things you love. Now the room is neat, tidy, and ready for a peaceful night. The little dinosaurs are sleeping soundly in their toy-bin cave. And you? You have worked so hard today, playing and learning and helping. It is time for you to snuggle under your own covers. Close your eyes and breathe in peace. Sweet dreams to the toys, and the sweetest dreams to you.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is sinking in the west,
It is time for toys to rest.
Teddy bear is feeling yawning,
He will sleep until the morning.

Put the blocks back in their box,
Fold the little baby socks.
Car is parked inside the lane,
Time to catch a sleepy train.

Dollie closes both her eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Puzzle pieces fit so tight,
Say to everyone goodnight.

Every toy is snug and deep,
Now the room is fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Tuck In Time
rhymes.text:
Time to tidy up the floor,
Open up the toy box door.
Rocker horse is standing still,
Resting by the painted hill.

Robot turns his switches down,
No more walking through the town.
Ball rolls softly to his nook,
Next to every picture book.

Dinosaurs lie in a row,
Softly whispering hello.
Train set stops upon the track,
No more chugging down and back.

Blankets wrap them nice and warm,
Safe from any windy storm.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Stars and Toys
rhymes.text:
Moon is shining bright and clear,
Bedtime for our playthings dear.
Puppy dog is on the rug,
Waiting for a sleepy hug.

Crayons rest inside their cup,
No one picks a yellow up.
Boat sails to the sleepy shore,
Sailing out and round the door.

Action figure bends his knee,
Sitting underneath the tree.
Building bricks are tucked away,
Till the coming of the day.

Dreaming dreams of happy fun,
Sleeping till the morning sun.

rhymes.title: Where Do Toys Go?
rhymes.text:
Where do all the toys go sleep?
Watch the little shadows creep.
Teddy sleeps upon the chair,
With a ribbon in his hair.

Kittens made of fuzzy wool,
Keep the toy chest nice and full.
Top stops spinning on the floor,
Rolling softly to the door.

Lego towers tumbled down,
Resting softly on the town.
Music box is quiet now,
Duck is bowing with a bow.

Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
Now the toys are fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Night-Night Playtime
rhymes.text:
Playtime hours are done and past,
Bedtime comes around at last.
Monkey climbs up to his shelf,
Curling up to rest himself.

Trucks are parked in tidy rows,
Stopping where the carpet goes.
Pegs are in their proper place,
Smiling with a happy face.

Fairies fold their shiny wings,
Listening what slumber sings.
Blanket covers up the bear,
Resting softly on the chair.

Stars are twinkling up above,
Filled with sleepy peace and love.

rhymes.title: Teddy's Cozy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is going down to sleep,
It's time to count our toys and leap!
Where does little teddy go?
In the basket, nice and low.

Blocks are stacking in the bin,
Let us put them safely in.
Cars are parking in a row,
Ready for the morning glow.

Dolly closes both her eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Puzzle pieces fit so tight,
Saying to the room, good-night.

Every toy is tucked away,
Resting for another day.
Now we turn the lights down low,
Time for bed, off we go!

rhymes.title: The Toy Train's Garage
rhymes.text:
Choo-choo train goes chugging by,
Time to tuck the toys nearby.
Where does the big train sleep tonight?
In the station, out of sight.

Rubber ducky takes a rest,
In the water, he likes best.
Action figures stand so tall,
By the bedroom's painted wall.

Crayons go inside their box,
Next to fuzzy woolly socks.
Teddy bear is on the chair,
Combing down his fuzzy hair.

Put them in their proper place,
With a happy, smiling face.
All the toys are fast asleep,
While the stars their watches keep.

rhymes.title: The Great Toy Sleepy Time
rhymes.text:
Listen to the sleepy sound,
As the toys curl on the ground.
Where does baby doll now lay?
On the pillow, far away.

Lego bricks are in their chest,
Every piece is taking rest.
Balls are rolling on the floor,
Near the bedroom's open door.

Puppy dog with floppy ears,
Wipes away our sleepy tears.
Monkey climbs up on the shelf,
Looking happy by himself.

Cleanup time is almost done,
We have had a lot of fun.
Sleep well, toys, until the morn,
When a brand new day is born.

rhymes.title: Night-Night, Playthings
rhymes.text:
Time to tuck the toys in tight,
Making sure they sleep just right.
Where do furry bunnies snooze?
In the basket with our shoes.

Robot stops his flashing light,
Saying everything is right.
Books are resting on the shelf,
Reading stories to themself.

Musical instruments are quiet,
Finished with their daytime riot.
Stuffy whale is in the tub,
Waiting for a morning scrub.

Hands can help to put them straight,
We do not have long to wait.
Sweet dreams, toys, until the sun,
Tells us that a day's begun.

rhymes.title: The Toy Box Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Stars are shining in the deep,
Time to put the toys to sleep.
Where does fuzzy kitty lie?
On the blanket, warm and dry.

Wooden horses stop their race,
Resting in a quiet place.
Kitchen set is locked and neat,
Resting every plastic seat.

Balloons are floating up above,
Filled with gentle hugs and love.
Little truck parks in the shed,
Just like children in their bed.

Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We cleaned up our toys today.
Now the room is calm and bright,
Peaceful slumber, sweet good-night.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is going down to rest,
It is time to do our best.
Pick up teddy, pick up bear,
Put them softly in the chair.

Where do all the green blocks go?
In the box, down very low.
Stack them neatly, one, two, three,
Happy as a bumblebee.

Little truck and racing car,
Did you drive too fast and far?
Park your wheels upon the mat,
Give a friendly little pat.

Now the room is shining bright,
Time to say a sweet goodnight.
Toys are sleeping safe and sound,
Not a single peep around.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Time for Bears
rhymes.text:
Little dolly, close your eyes,
Look up at the starry skies.
Time to tuck you in your bed,
With a pillow for your head.

Teddy bear is yawning wide,
He is ready to go inside.
Put him on the fluffy shelf,
He can hardly help himself.

Where do puzzles want to stay?
In their boxes, locked away.
All the pieces snug and neat,
Resting up their tiny feet.

Now the floor is clean and clear,
Morning time will soon be here.h
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Sleeping toys are doing best.

rhymes.title: The Toy Train's Garage
rhymes.text:
Choo-choo train upon the track,
Time to put your wagons back.
Into the tunnel, out of sight,
Sleeping through the quiet night.

Rubber ducky in the tub,
Time to finish every scrub.
Dry your feathers, jump on out,
Join the bedtime sleepy rout.

Ball is rolling on the floor,
Right beside the bedroom door.
In the basket you must go,
Rocking gently to and fro.

Every toy is in its place,
With a happy, smiling face.
Moon is shining from above,
Filled with cozy bedtime love.

rhymes.title: Time for Toy Dreams
rhymes.text:
Soft and gentle evening breeze,
Whispers through the sleepy trees.
Time to gather up our toys,
Little girls and little boys.

Where do furry bunnies sleep?
Where the shadows softly creep.
On the cushion, soft and white,
Holding very still all night.

Plastic bricks of yellow hue,
Red and green and shiny blue.
Into the bucket, splash and drop,
Keep on going till we stop.

Clap your hands and give a cheer,
Bedtime is finally here.
Toys are resting, snug and deep,
While the little children sleep.

rhymes.title: The Goodnight Toy Parade
rhymes.text:
Marching, marching, one, two, three,
Put the playthings where they be.
Dino roaring softly now,
Taking a polite little bow.

Where do action figures stay?
Done with running all the day.
On the shelf they stand so tall,
Not a single one will fall.

Crayons in their paper bed,
Blue and yellow, green and red.
Snap the cover nice and tight,
Everything is out of sight.

Now the room is dark and cool,
Just like floating in a pool.
Sweetest dreams to every toy,
Sleep in peace, my little boy.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bedtime
rhymes.text:
The sun goes down, the day is done,
Now bedtime comes for everyone!
Where do the toys sleep when it is night?
Tucked in so cozy, warm, and bright.
Teddy Bear yawns and rubs his eyes,
Beneath the covers big and nice.
Dollie rests her sleepy head,
Right inside her wooden bed.
The little cars put on the brakes,
No more zooming in the wakes.
Blocks stack up in a quiet row,
Ready for tomorrow's show.
Put them in the toy box deep,
Time for all the toys to sleep.
Shh, shh, close your eyes,
Dreaming underneath the skies.

rhymes.title: Teddy's Soft Pillow
rhymes.text:
Playtime's over, time to rest,
Sleeping in a cozy nest.
Where do the toys sleep, can you say?
After all the fun today.
Teddy needs a pillow soft,
Up upon the shelf aloft.
Ball rolls gently to the floor,
By the little bedroom door.
Puzzle pieces fit and stay,
Resting till the break of day.
Train engine turns off his light,
Saying to the tracks, goodnight.
Tidy up and put them right,
Dreaming happy dreams tonight.
Sleep, sweet toys, until the dawn,
When the happy day goes on.

rhymes.title: The Toy Box Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Clap your hands and give a cheer,
Bedtime for the toys is near.
Where do the toys sleep when stars appear?
Resting safe and very dear.
Robot bends his metal knee,
As sleepy as a child can be.
Dinosaur finds a cozy spot,
Cooling off his stomping trot.
Crayons go back in their box,
Next to fuzzy winter socks.
Books are resting on the shelf,
Reading stories to theirself.
Hug your toys and tuck them in,
Let the sleepy dreams begin.
Softly sing a gentle song,
While the night is calm and long.

rhymes.title: Time for Toy Dreams
rhymes.text:
Pack away the toys with care,
Give a hug to every bear.
Where do the toys sleep in their home?
Never more they have to roam.
Rocker horse stops going round,
Standing quiet on the ground.
Action figures take a break,
No more jungle paths to make.
Rubber ducky dries his wing,
Not a single song to sing.
Music box plays one last tune,
Underneath the sleepy moon.
Close the lid and turn out lights,
Wishing all the toys good nights.
Morning time will come around,
Safe and sound upon the ground.

rhymes.title: Goodnight, Little Toys
rhymes.text:
Gather up the toys you love,
While the stars shine bright above.
Where do the toys sleep when day is through?
Sleeping just the same as you.
Wooden blocks are in their bin,
Waiting for the fun begin.
Puff the dragon lays his head,
On the fluffy blanket bed.
Puppet rests his strings so still,
At the bottom of the hill.
Everything is neat and clean,
Best routine you've ever seen.
Time to tuck them all away,
For another happy day.
Sleep until the morning sun,
Playing games for everyone.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is sinking in the west,
It is time for toys to rest.
Teddy bear is feeling yawning,
He will sleep until the morning.

Put the blocks back in their box,
Fold the little baby socks.
Car and truck go in the bin,
Now let's push the cover in.

Doll is tucked beneath the sheet,
Cover up her tiny feet.
Trains are parking on the floor,
We can close the closet door.

Every toy is snug and deep,
Now the room is fast asleep.
Shh, shh, time for bed,
Rest your sleepy wooden head.

rhymes.title: Night-Night, Little Car
rhymes.text:
Red car, blue car, time to go,
Driving very soft and slow.
Park them in the toybox stall,
Say goodnight to one and all.

Rubber ducky leaves the tub,
Ready for a cozy rub.
Put the puzzle pieces down,
Quiet now in Toyland town.

Lego bricks are stacking tight,
Saying cheerful bugs goodnight.
Crayons rest inside their cup,
Nobody is waking up.

Moon is shining bright and clear,
Morning time will soon be here.
Sleepy toys upon the shelf,
Resting softly by themselves.

rhymes.title: Teddy's Slumber Time
rhymes.text:
Teddy needs a cozy nap,
Holding softly on your lap.
Put him in his little bed,
With a pillow for his head.

Puppy dog is tired too,
Right beside the worn-out shoe.
Monkey climbs up on the chair,
Resting with his fuzzy hair.

Sing a little sleepy tune,
Underneath the shining moon.
Close your eyes and breathe in deep,
All the toys are fast asleep.

Not a sound is in the room,
Swept away with magic broom.
Morning brings another day,
Time for happy games to play.

rhymes.title: Clean Up, Sleep Well
rhymes.text:
Gather up the tumbling ball,
Catch it softly as it fall.
Drop it in the green toy chest,
Now the ball can take a rest.

Robot friend has stopped to beep,
Robot baby falls asleep.
Dino lies upon the rug,
Waiting for a bedtime hug.

Stack the rings from big to small,
Put them neatly by the wall.
Tick-tock goes the bedroom clock,
Safe inside their wooden box.

Blankets wrap around so tight,
Stars are twinkling in the night.
Sleep until the light of day,
Ready for another play.

rhymes.title: The Pajama Party Box
rhymes.text:
Rabbits in a fuzzy row,
Where do tired dollies go?
In the basket, deep and wide,
Where the gentle shadows hide.

Spinning top is done and still,
Resting at the paper mill.
Books are back upon the shelf,
Reading stories to themself.

Pat the bunny on the ear,
Tell him that you love him dear.
Close the lid and turn the light,
Everything is tucked in tight.

Dreaming dreams of sky and sun,
Now the sleepy day is done.
Hush-a-bye and sweet repose,
Touching every little nose.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is sinking in the west,
It is time for toys to rest.
Teddy bear is feeling yawning,
He will sleep until the morning.

Put the blocks back in their box,
Fold the little baby socks.
Trains are stopping on the track,
Put the yellow engine back.

Dolly closes both her eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.
Puzzle pieces all in place,
With a happy smiling face.

Now the room is neat and sweet,
From the ceiling to the feet.
Time to tuck them in so tight,
Say a happy, sleepy night!

rhymes.title: Sleepy Time for Cars
rhymes.text:
Red car, blue car, time to go,
Driving very soft and slow.
Into the garage you creep,
While the babies fall asleep.

Teddy hugs his fuzzy rug,
Giving everyone a hug.
Put the crayons in their cup,
No more playing, time is up.

Robot bends his shiny knee,
As quiet as a mouse can be.
Lego bricks are stacking down,
Lying softly on the ground.

Now the floor is clean and neat,
Resting every little seat.
Close your eyes and count to ten,
Wake up for to-morrow then!

rhymes.title: Where Do the Toys Sleep?
rhymes.text:
Where do all the toys go now?
Let us put them down, and bow.
Puppy dog is in his bed,
Resting down his furry head.

Monkey swings up on the shelf,
He can tuck away himself.
Bouncing balls go in the net,
Do not lose a single pet.

Blankets warm and blankets nice,
Hiding all the little mice.
Books are resting on the wood,
Reading stories was so good.

Everything is in its place,
Showing such a gentle grace.
Time to dream and time to rest,
Sleepy toys are doing best.

rhymes.title: The Toy Box Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Hush-a-bye, my little bear,
Sitting on the wooden chair.
Time to put your toys away,
For another happy day.

Climb into the toy chest deep,
All the animals are asleep.
Giraffe is folding up his neck,
Checking on the final deck.

Rubber ducky dries his wing,
Not another song to sing.
Close the lid and give a pat,
Who could ever sleep like that?

Moonlight shines upon the floor,
Peeking softly through the door.
Sweetest dreams to every toy,
Every little girl and boy.

rhymes.title: Tidy Up and Sleep
rhymes.text:
Tick-tock, tick-tock goes the clock,
Time to store the building block.
Into baskets, big and round,
Not a single toy is found.

Lion goes into his den,
Ready for the morning when.
Dolls are tucked inside their bed,
Resting every sleepy head.

Music box has stopped its tune,
Underneath the shining moon.
Stars are twinkling in the sky,
Singing them a lullaby.

Room is tidy, room is bright,
Everything is put out right.
Time for sleeping through the dark,
Resting every little ark.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is going down so low,
It is time for toys to go.
Teddy Bear is feeling sleepy,
Looking rather soft and wee-py.

Time to tuck him in his place,
With a smile upon his face.
Put the blocks back in the box,
Next to fuzzy woolen socks.

Trains are resting on the track,
No more clicking, click-clack-clack.
Ball is quiet on the floor,
We don't bounce it anymore.

Now the room is neat and sweet,
Time for bed for sleepy feet.
Shh, goodnight to every toy,
Sleep until the morning, boy!

rhymes.title: Sleepy Time for Cars
rhymes.text:
Red car, blue car, time to rest,
Sleeping in the wooden chest.
Driving fast all through the day,
Now it is not time to play.

Park the truck and park the jeep,
All the wheels are fast asleep.
Bus is quiet on the shelf,
Resting all, yes, by itself.

Lift the lid and put them in,
Let the quiet night begin.
Close the box and shut the door,
Toys are resting on the floor.

Moon is shining bright and clear,
Morning time will soon be here.
Sleepy motors give a sigh,
Little racecars, wave goodbye!

rhymes.title: Dolly's Dreamland
rhymes.text:
Dolly blinks her painted eyes,
Looking at the starry skies.
She has danced the whole day through,
Now her sleepy time is due.

Lay her gently on her bed,
Softly pat her cotton head.
Pull the blanket to her chin,
Let the happy dreams begin.

Put the puzzle pieces right,
Say a gentle, sweet goodnight.
Crayons resting in their cup,
Nobody is staying up.

Teddy joins her for a nap,
Hugging tightly in her lap.
Room is tidy, room is bright,
Sleep tight, dollies, sleep till light!

rhymes.title: The Toy Box Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Where do all the birdies fly?
Up into the evening sky.
Where do all the toys retire?
Far away from wind and fire.

Into the chest they like to creep,
Ready now for soundly sleep.
Monkey hangs his tail so low,
Now he has no place to go.

Robot turns his switches down,
Bestest little toy in town.
Dinosaurs stop stomping round,
Not a single roaring sound.

Lock the latch and turn around,
Quiet peace is all we found.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
Just like toys tucked in their bed.

rhymes.title: Night-Night, Playtime
rhymes.text:
Building towers tall and grand,
Made of plastic blocks and sand.
Now we take them down again,
Just like little mice in pen.

Put them in the yellow tub,
Give the room a little rub.
Everything is neat and fine,
Shining like a little pine.

Puppy dog is on the rug,
Waiting for a sleepy hug.
Duckie floats no more in tub,
Just a cozy little rub.

Stars are twinkling in the deep,
Every little toy is asleep.
Morning brings a brand new day,
When we wake and start to play!

rhymes.title: Teddy Bear's Bedtime
rhymes.text:
The sun goes down and day is through,
It is time to put away your zoo.
Teddy Bear is yawning wide,
He needs a cozy place to hide.

Where do the little fluffy toys sleep?
Under the covers where they don't peep.
Where does the bouncy rubber ball rest?
Inside the toy box is its best.

Line them up in a happy row,
Time for bed, away they go!
Blocks go clack upon the floor,
Stack them nicely by the door.

Give a hug and turn out the light,
Say to your toys a sweet goodnight.
Tomorrow morning they will wake,
Ready for a game to make.

rhymes.title: The Toy Train's Station
rhymes.text:
Choo-choo train upon the track,
Time to bring your pieces back.
Where do the choo-choo engines sleep?
In the station, nice and deep.

Crayons in their little box,
Folded up your fuzzy socks.
Where does the dolly close her eyes?
Underneath the starry skies.

Put the puzzles in their frame,
Every toy has got a name.
Puzzles love to snuggle tight,
Sleeping safely through the night.

Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We cleaned up our toys today.
Now our room is neat and sweet,
From the ceiling to our feet.

rhymes.title: Where Do the Cars Rest?
rhymes.text:
Vroom and zoom across the floor,
Now we park behind the door.
Where do the little racing cars sleep?
In the garage where shadows creep.

Little truck and big red van,
Put them in the metal can.
Where does the robot rest his head?
Right beside your little bed.

Soft plush bunny hops away,
He is tired from the play.
Lay him on the pillow now,
Give a gentle little bow.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Sing a happy lullaby.
All the toys are tucked up fast,
Bedtime time has come at last.

rhymes.title: The Toy Box Lullaby
rhymes.text:
Time to tidy, time to pack,
Put the dinosaurs on the rack.
Where do the plastic blocks all go?
In the big green bucket below.

Where does the teddy snuggle down?
Right beside the golden crown.
Where does the rattle take a nap?
Resting on the velvet wrap.

Tick-tock clock begins to chime,
Cleaning up is such a fun time.
Find a home for every toy,
Bring a smile of gentle joy.

Close the lid and pat it twice,
Everything looks neat and nice.
Moon is glowing bright and clear,
Sleep well, little playmates here.

rhymes.title: Goodnight, Little Toys
rhymes.text:
The day is done and stars appear,
Bedtime magic is drawing near.
Where do the action figures sleep?
In the toy chest dark and deep.

Where does the little puppy plush?
Resting in the corner hush.
Where do the books go on the shelf?
Lined up neatly by themself.

Pick them up and hold them tight,
Kiss your dolly sweet goodnight.
Put the bucket on the mat,
Stroke the sleepy kitty cat.

Now the room is shining bright,
Everything is put out right.
Jump into your cozy bed,
Sweet dreams to your sleepy head.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is sinking in the west,
It is time for toys to rest.
Teddy bear is feeling yawning,
He will sleep until the morning.

Put the blocks back in their box,
Fold the little baby socks.
Car is parked inside the stall,
Ball goes rolling to the wall.

Robot blinks a sleepy eye,
Say a gentle, sweet goodbye.
Puppy dog is in his chair,
No more playing everywhere.

Now the room is neat and bright,
Toys are sleeping through the night.
Close your eyes and snuggle deep,
Time for little you to sleep.

rhymes.title: Tuck Them In Tight
rhymes.text:
Playtime hours are done and through,
What are little toys to do?
They are tired, yes indeed,
Rest is what the dollies need.

Softly tuck the blanket high,
Watch the sleepy birds fly by.
Dino lays his scaly head,
Right beside his cozy bed.

Train is stopped upon the track,
No more clicking on the back.
Puzzle pieces fit the floor,
We will play again tomorrow.

Stars are shining in the sky,
Let us sing a lullaby.
Toys are snoozing fast asleep,
While the gentle shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Time for Toy Land Dream
rhymes.text:
Listen to the sleepy sound,
Quiet takes the playroom round.
Where do all the toys retire?
By the glowing picture fire.

Monkey climbs into his tree,
As happy as a monkey can be.
Duck is floating in the tub,
Give his little wings a rub.

Crayons rest inside their cup,
Nobody is staying up.
Blocks are stacked in towers high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Moonlight beams a silver glow,
On the lovely toys below.
Dreaming sweet and dreaming low,
Off to slumber land they go.

rhymes.title: Goodnight, Little Toys
rhymes.text:
Pack away the fun and play,
We have had a busy day.
Put the bucket on the shelf,
Teddy helps me by himself.

Horse is trotting to his shed,
Lion crawls into his bed.
Doll is wearing silken lace,
Smile upon her little face.

Everything is in its place,
Clean and tidy is the space.
No more running on the floor,
Closed is every toy box door.

Time to rest your engine gears,
Wipe away the tired tears.
Sleep until the morning light,
Little toys, I say goodnight.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Toy Parade
rhymes.text:
Marching down the bedroom street,
Stomping with your tiny feet.
Time to end the games we played,
For the sleepy toy parade.

Soldier drops his plastic gun,
Evening time is almost done.
Boat sails into harbor port,
Ending every playful sport.

Rabbit snuggles up so near,
Whispering a word of cheer.
Kitten rests upon the rug,
Waiting for a sleepy hug.

Now the stars begin to peep,
All the toys are fast asleep.
Dreams are floating soft and sweet,
Peace is on the quiet street.

rhymes.title: The Big Toy Bed
rhymes.text:
The sun is going down so low,
It is time for toys to go.
Teddy Bear is feeling deep,
Time to put him down to sleep.

Blocks go in the wooden box,
Right beside the striped socks.
Little truck parks on the floor,
Right behind the bedroom door.

Put the puzzle on the shelf,
So it rests all by itself.
Dolly closes up her eyes,
Underneath the starry skies.

Say goodnight to every friend,
Now our playtime meets the end.
Shh, shh, time to rest,
Sleeping toys is what is best.

rhymes.title: Tuck In Time
rhymes.text:
Where do toys go when we rest?
Every toy is in its nest.
Robot bends his shiny knee,
Resting till we count to three.

Train engine stops its chug,
Resting on the furry rug.
Ball rolls softly to the wall,
Not a single bounce at all.

Dinosaurs lie in a row,
Where the gentle breezes blow.
Cradle holds the rattle tight,
Sleeping softly through the night.

Now the room is calm and still,
Moonlight shines upon the hill.
Time for toys to dream away,
Until comes another day.

rhymes.title: Sleepy Playhouse
rhymes.text:
Evening comes around the bend,
Time to tuck in every friend.
Where do toys sleep in their bed?
Pillow under fuzzy head.

Puppy dog is yawning wide,
Lying down on the side.
Kitty cat in velvet fur,
Softly starts to purr and blur.

Boat is docked upon the chair,
No more sailing anywhere.
Rocket ship is parked up high,
Watching comets in the sky.

Close your eyes and slumber deep,
While the little children sleep.
Morning brings a happy sun,
Then we play and have our fun.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Bear
rhymes.text:
Hush-a-bye and softly creep,
All the toys are falling asleep.
Where do the toys go to rest?
Right inside their cozy chest.

Action figure drops his shield,
In the carpet clover field.
Rubber ducky floats no more,
Sitting dry beside the door.

Crayons rest inside their cup,
No one picks a color up.
Book is closed upon the knee,
As quiet as can ever be.

Dream sweet dreams of yellow sun,
Playtime wait until it's done.
Snuggle down and catch some zees,
Blowing gently in the breeze.

rhymes.title: Goodnight, Toyland
rhymes.text:
Twinkle stars begin to peep,
Time to rock the toys to sleep.
Where do the toys tuck away?
Resting from a busy day.

Monkey hangs his tail so low,
Where the sleepy shadows go.
Pony lies upon the mat,
Right beside the sleeping cat.

Building bricks are safe and sound,
Not a single tumbling sound.
Music box has stopped its song,
All the sleepy night along.

Wrap them up in blankets tight,
Give them all a kiss goodnight.
Morning time is drawing near,
Sleep well, every toy so dear.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket
stories.text: Leo was growing up so fast! Today was a very special day because Leo was getting a brand-new big kid bed. It wasn't just any bed; it looked like a fluffy white cloud that lived right in the middle of his cozy bedroom. Mom and Dad carried in the softest blankets and Leo’s favorite stuffed bear, Barnaby. 'Is this really my rocket ship to dreamland?' asked Leo, his eyes wide with wonder. 'It sure is,' smiled Dad, tucking the corners in tight. At bedtime, Leo brushed his teeth and put on his star pajamas. He climbed up, up, up into his big kid bed. It felt so roomy and wonderful! There were no bars on the sides like his old baby crib. He could stretch his legs all the way out and wiggle his toes. 'Look how much space I have,' giggled Leo, hugging Barnaby close. Mom turned off the big light and turned on the friendly moon lamp that cast a warm, golden glow across the room. She leaned down and kissed his forehead. 'Goodnight, my sweet big boy. Have wonderful adventures on your cloud rocket.' Leo snuggled deep into the pillows. He felt safe, cozy, and oh-so-proud. He was sleeping in his big kid bed all by himself. As his eyelids grew heavy, Leo imagined floating gently through the night sky, ready for sweet dreams. Goodnight, Leo.

stories.title: Maya and the Starry Canopy
stories.text: Maya had a big girl job today. She was going to sleep in her big girl bed for the very first time! Her old crib was tucked away in the closet, and in its place stood a beautiful wooden bed with a headboard shaped like a smiling sun. Maya’s big sister, Lily, helped her pick out her favorite pink polka-dot sheets. 'You are going to love it, Maya,' Lily said cheerfully. 'It feels like a magical island.' Maya felt a tiny bit nervous, but mostly very excited. After her warm bath and storytime, it was time. Maya walked over and crawled between the crisp, sweet-smelling sheets. She brought her fuzzy bunny along to keep her company. 'Testing, one, two, three,' whispered Maya, rolling from side to side. 'Plenty of room for bunny too!' Mom sat on the edge of the mattress and brushed a stray curl from Maya’s cheek. 'You are growing into such a capable big girl,' Mom whispered proudly. 'Remember, we are right down the hall if you need us, but your big girl bed is your very own cozy castle.' Maya nodded, feeling brave and strong. She looked up at the ceiling where glow-in-the-dark stars twinkled softly in the dark. She counted one star, two stars, three stars, and then closed her eyes with a happy sigh. She was safe, she was loved, and she was resting in her wonderful big girl bed all night long.

stories.title: Sammy’s Dinosaur Sleepover
stories.text: Sammy stood proudly in the center of his bedroom, pointing at his brand-new toddler bed. It was painted bright dinosaur green, complete with a friendly T-Rex painted on the footboard. 'Roar!' whispered Sammy, making his hands like dinosaur claws. Today was a milestone day. Sammy was leaving his baby bed behind because he was a big boy now. Grandma helped him arrange all his stuffed dinosaurs in a neat row along the pillow. Rexy the T-Rex, Triceratops, and Stegosaurus were all invited to the very first sleepover in the big boy bed. When bedtime arrived, Sammy brushed his teeth until they sparkled and hopped right into his green bed. It felt so nice and breezy! He didn’t need to climb over any rails anymore; he could just hop right in and out whenever he wanted. 'Time for sleep, little dinosaurs,' Sammy whispered to his toys. Dad sat in the rocking chair nearby, reading one last story about a brave little explorer. When the book closed, Dad gave Sammy a big hug and a kiss. 'I am so proud of how well you sleep in your big boy bed, Sammy. You are growing up wonderfully.' Sammy smiled in the dark, hugging Rexy tightly. The room was quiet and peaceful. Sammy felt like the luckiest and bravest boy in the whole wide world as he drifted off to sleep in his awesome dinosaur bed.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket Bed
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo had a very exciting night ahead of him. Tonight was the very first night he was going to sleep in his brand-new big kid bed! Leo felt a little bit tiny, but he also felt very, very brave. His big kid bed was not just any bed; it looked just like a fluffy white rocket ship ready to soar into the sleepy sky. Mommy helped Leo tuck in his favorite star-patterned blanket. Daddy brought over Barnaby Bear, Leo’s cuddliest stuffed friend, and tucked him right under Leo's arm. 'Are you ready for your big adventure, Captain Leo?' Daddy whispered with a warm smile. Leo nodded his head and giggled. He climbed right in, wiggling his toes under the cozy sheets. It felt so roomy and nice! He didn't even need the sides of a crib anymore because he was growing bigger and stronger every single day. Leo closed his eyes and took a deep, slow breath. He imagined his bed lifting off the floor, gently floating past the moon, and sailing through a sea of twinkling stars. Barnaby Bear stayed right beside him, keeping watch over the rocket ship. Leo felt so proud and safe in his special big kid bed. He knew that morning would bring new games and bright sunshine, but for now, it was time to rest. With a soft sigh, Leo drifted off to dreamland, smiling all through the night. He was a true big kid now, and his bed was the best place in the whole wide world.

stories.title: Mia's Cozy Mountain Peak
stories.text: Mia loved mountains. She loved looking at pictures of them in her favorite books, tall and strong and reaching up high. Today, Mommy and Daddy told Mia something wonderful: her new big kid bed was just like a cozy mountain peak, waiting for her to climb up and rest. Mia clapped her hands with joy! The mattress was soft like a fluffy moss patch, and her quilt was as colorful as wildflowers in the spring. At bedtime, Mia brushed her teeth, put on her rabbit pajamas with the floppy ears, and hopped into her room. The bed was wide open, welcoming her with open arms. No bars, no gates, just freedom! Mia climbed up, snuggling deep into the center of her mountain peak. 'Look how tall you are, Mia! You are soaring high,' Mommy said, kissing her forehead. Mia felt like a brave explorer who had just reached the top of the world. She lined up her three favorite stuffed ducklings along the edge of the bed to keep her company. They looked ready for a cozy night under the starry sky too. Mia wrapped her arms around her plush pillow. It felt so grown-up to crawl into bed all by herself without any fuss. She felt warm, loved, and wonderfully secure. As the room grew quiet, Mia listened to the gentle night sounds outside. She closed her eyes, feeling like the happiest explorer on Earth, ready for sweet dreams on her mountain peak.

stories.title: Oliver's Starry Night Train
stories.text: All aboard the bedtime express! Oliver’s new big kid bed wasn't just a bed—it was a magnificent, chugging night train, and Oliver was the very important conductor. Tonight was his maiden voyage. Oliver wore his striped pajamas that made him look just like a real train engineer. Mommy walked him to his new bed, which had shiny wooden rails and a headboard shaped like a steam engine. 'Choo-choo!' whispered Oliver softly, making a tiny puffing sound with his lips. He climbed aboard the comfy mattress, pulling his blue-and-green striped duvet all the way up to his chin. It was so much bigger than his old bed, giving him plenty of room to stretch out his legs like train tracks. Daddy tucked him in tight and placed his favorite toy train right on the nightstand to watch over the engine. 'Have a wonderful journey, conductor Oliver,' Daddy said, giving him a gentle hug. Oliver felt a warm, happy glow inside his tummy. He wasn't a baby anymore; he was a big boy who could sleep all night in his very own train bed. He closed his eyes and listened to the imaginary rhythm of the wheels clicking along the tracks: clickety-clack, clickety-clack, off to dreamland we go. Oliver smiled as the sleepy train rolled smoothly through the dark, peaceful night, carrying him safely toward morning.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket
stories.text:
Leo was growing so big and tall! Today was a very special day because Leo was getting a brand new big kid bed. It wasn't just any bed; it looked just like a real rocket ship! Leo clapped his hands and giggled. 'Look, Mommy! My bed can fly to the stars!' Mommy smiled and gave Leo a big, warm hug. 'It sure can, little astronaut,' she said. 'And guess what? You are the captain.' 

Bedtime came soon, filled with soft pajama snuggles and a favorite bedtime story about the moon. Then, it was time to climb into the rocket ship. Leo crawled under the cozy, starry blankets. They felt so soft, just like a fluffy white cloud. He rested his head on his pillow, which felt like a marshmallow. 

'Time for blast off!' whispered Daddy, kissing Leo on the forehead. Leo closed his eyes and pretended he was floating gently through the sleepy night sky, past twinkling stars and smiling planets. He felt so safe and so proud. He stayed right in his big kid bed all through the night, dreaming sweet, wonderful dreams. When the morning sun peeked through the window, Leo sat right up and cheered. 'I did it! I slept in my big kid bed!' Daddy and Mommy came in with happy morning smiles and cheered right along with him. 'We are so proud of our big boy!' they said. Leo beamed with joy. Being a big kid was wonderful, and his rocket ship bed was the coziest place in the whole wide world. Every night after that, Leo climbed into his bed with a happy heart, ready for his next big space adventure.

stories.title: Mia and the Bear Hug
stories.text:
Mia had a very important job today. Her old crib was moving away to help a tiny baby, and in its place stood a gorgeous, wooden big kid bed, covered in a quilt made of pink and yellow flowers. Mia walked around the bed slowly, touching the smooth wooden post. 'Is this really mine?' she asked softly. 'All yours,' said Grandma, kneeling down beside her. 'You are growing up into such a wonderful big girl.' 

To make the bed feel extra friendly, Mia decided to invite her favorite stuffed animals to a sleepover. First came Barnaby Bear, then Penny Penguin, and finally, sleepy-eyed Bunny. Mia tucked them in a neat row right beside her. 'Now nobody will be lonely,' Mia told Grandma proudly. 

When the stars came out to twinkle in the dark blue sky, it was time for Mia to snuggle down too. She brushed her teeth, put on her soft bunny pajamas, and climbed under the floral quilt. It gave her a wonderful, warm feeling, just like a giant bear hug from Grandma. Mia rested her cheek against her pillow and hugged Barnaby Bear tight. 

Grandma softly sang a lullaby while the night light glowed a gentle, comforting yellow on the wall. Mia felt so relaxed and happy. She closed her eyes and drifted off to sleep, sleeping soundly all night long in her very own big girl bed. In the morning, the birds sang a happy song outside. Mia woke up stretching her arms up high to the ceiling. 'Good morning, Barnaby!' she chirped. Grandma walked in with a tray of sliced bananas and a big hug. 'Good morning, my big girl! How did you sleep?' Mia smiled proudly. 'Like a cozy bear!' she said.

stories.title: Pip's Treehouse Bed
stories.text:
Pip loved trees. He loved climbing them, looking at their green leaves, and listening to the wind rustling through their branches. So when it was time for Pip to sleep in a big kid bed, his parents surprised him with a wooden bed that had a headboard shaped like a leafy green tree! 

'Look, Pip! It's your very own indoor treehouse,' said Daddy. Pip's eyes grew as wide as saucers. He ran over and patted the painted green leaves. 'A treehouse just for me!' he shouted happily. He could not wait for bedtime to arrive. 

Evening came with the soft glowing of firefly lights. Pip took a warm bath with lots of bubbly soap, brushed his sparkly white teeth, and put on his striped pajamas. Mommy and Daddy walked him to his new treehouse bed. Pip climbed in eagerly. The sheets smelled like fresh springtime flowers, and his green blanket felt like soft moss. 

'Time to rest your branches, little tree,' whispered Mommy, kissing his cheek. Pip nestled down deeply into the mattress. He felt so snug and secure, like a little bird resting safely in a high-up nest. He listened to the quiet hum of the night and let out a long, happy sigh. 

Pip stayed tucked safely in his treehouse bed until the morning sun kissed his nose. When he opened his eyes, he felt rested and full of energy. He jumped up and did a happy morning dance right on his cozy mattress. Mommy and Daddy walked in, clapping their hands. 'Good morning, sleepyhead! How was your first night in the treehouse?' Pip smiled from ear to ear. 'It was the best, Mommy! I'm a big kid now!' They shared a giant group hug, celebrating Pip's wonderful big kid bed milestone together.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket Bed
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo had a very exciting night. Tonight was the night Leo got to sleep in a brand new Big Kid Bed! His old crib was cozy, but his new bed looked just like a big, fluffy white cloud waiting in the sky. Leo’s mom and dad helped him carry his favorite sleepy bear, Barnaby, right into the middle of the soft mattress. "Look, Leo!" whispered Mom, tucking a starry blue blanket all around his toes. "This is your very own rocket ship to dreamland." Leo climbed under the covers and let out a big, happy yawn. The bed felt so open and wonderful. He could roll this way, and he could roll that way, all by himself! Dad gave Leo a gentle kiss on his forehead. "Goodnight, sweet astronaut," Dad said softly. Leo hugged Barnaby tightly and looked up at the glow-in-the-dark stars on his bedroom ceiling. He felt so proud. He was growing up big and strong, just like a true explorer. With a soft sigh, Leo closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, floating happily on his cloud rocket bed.

stories.title: Maya and the Morning Sunshine
stories.text: Maya woke up before the sun was even fully awake. But wait—her room looked different today! There were no tall wooden bars around her bed anymore. Maya opened her big brown eyes and smiled a huge morning smile. She was in her Big Kid Bed! Last night, she had fallen asleep listening to a wonderful story about a little bunny, and she had stayed right in her big bed the whole night through. "Good morning, my big girl!" called Daddy softly as he peeked around the bedroom door. Maya sat right up and stretched her arms way up high toward the ceiling. "Daddy, look! I stayed in my big bed all night!" she cheered proudly. Daddy came over and gave her a giant hug. "We are so proud of you, Maya. Sleeping in your big bed makes you so independent." Maya hopped out of bed all by herself, her tiny fuzzy slippers going pit-pat on the wooden floor. She walked over to her window and pulled back the curtains to let the bright golden sunshine in. Today was going to be a wonderful day because she was a big kid now, ready for all sorts of fun new adventures!

stories.title: Oliver’s Cozy Nighttime Train
stories.text: All aboard the sleepy train! Chugga-chugga, choo-choo! Little Oliver loved trains more than anything in the whole wide world. Today, his mommy and daddy turned his bedroom into a special train station, because Oliver was sleeping in his Big Kid Bed for the very first time. His bed had shiny wooden headboards that looked just like the front of a powerful locomotive. Oliver lined up his three favorite pillow cars right beside him on the mattress. "All passengers please take your seats," Oliver whispered in his best conductor voice. He snuggled under his red-and-white striped quilt, which felt as warm and comforting as a warm cup of cocoa. Mommy sat in the rocking chair nearby and smiled. "Are you ready for the night express, conductor Oliver?" she asked gently. Oliver nodded, his eyelids growing heavy and sleepy. The room grew quiet and cozy, filled with the soft hum of the night. Oliver imagined his bed rolling gently down the tracks, past sleepy hills and dreaming forests, carrying him safely through the dark. He took a slow, deep breath, feeling so safe and loved in his wonderful new bed. Chugga-chugga, choo-choo, sweet dreams to you!

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket
stories.text: Leo had a little wooden bed with tiny teddy bear pillows. For a long, long time, it was his favorite cozy spot in the whole wide world. But lately, Leo was growing bigger. His toes peeked right out past the blankets! "Time for a big boy bed, Leo," said Mommy with a warm, proud smile. Leo felt a tiny bit of wiggly worry in his tummy. Changing things can feel a little bit strange sometimes. But Daddy held his hand. They went to the big furniture store and picked out a wonderful new bed. It was large and wide, covered in bright blue sheets with shining yellow stars all over them. It looked just like a spaceship ready to blast off into the night sky! That evening, Leo helped make his sleeping space super cozy. He lined up his favorite stuffed animals: Barnaby Bear, Hoppy Frog, and Sleepy Sheep. "Now my crew is all ready," whispered Leo. Mommy and Daddy tucked him in tight. The mattress felt soft like a fluffy cloud, and Leo had so much more room to stretch out his growing arms and legs. "You are such a big boy, Leo. We are so proud of you," said Daddy, kissing his forehead. Leo closed his eyes and imagined he was floating on a gentle white cloud, soaring up high past the moon and the twinkling stars. He didn't even think about his old bed once. When morning came, the warm yellow sunlight tickled his nose. Leo sat right up and stretched his arms way up high. He did it! He slept the whole night through in his big boy rocket ship bed. He hopped out of bed all by himself, feeling brave and strong. "Good morning, big boy!" cheered Mommy from the kitchen. Leo grinned a big, proud grin. Growing up was turning out to be quite an adventure, and he was ready for whatever came next.

stories.title: Mia's Magical Treehouse
stories.text: Mia loved her little white crib. It kept her safe and snug for many months. But Mia was a big girl now, almost three years old! Her legs were strong, and she could run very fast. "Mia, do you want to see your new big girl bed?" asked Daddy. Mia clapped her hands. "Yes, please!" Their living room was quiet as they walked into her bedroom. There it was—a wonderful wooden bed low to the floor, shaped just like a magical forest treehouse. Green leafy curtains hung around the sides, and a rainbow quilt was folded neatly on top. Mia gasped. It looked like a secret fairy fort! "This is your special resting place," said Mommy softly. Mia crawled inside and touched the soft pillows. They felt like moss in an enchanted forest. That night, the bedtime routine was extra special. They read three books about woodland animals instead of two. Then, Mia gave her baby doll a hug and tucked herself under the rainbow quilt. At first, the room looked a tiny bit different in the dark. Mia felt a little flutter in her chest. But then she remembered her magic treehouse was safe and strong. She whispered goodnight to the moon outside her window. The mattress was so wide and comfortable that Mia could roll this way and that way without bumping the sides. She hugged her fluffy bunny tightly and closed her eyes. Throughout the night, Mia slept deeply and soundly in her cozy wooden haven. When the morning birds began to chirp outside, Mia opened her eyes. She smiled from ear to ear. She had stayed in her big girl bed all night long! Mia jumped up, skipped into the kitchen, and shouted, "I sleep in my treehouse!" Mommy and Daddy hugged her tightly. Mia felt like the happiest, bravest explorer in the whole world.

stories.title: Sammy's Captain's Ship
stories.text: Sammy was growing taller every single day. His shirts were getting shorter, and his shoes were getting snugger. "Look at you, Captain Sammy!" said Mommy. "You are getting too big for your baby bed." Sammy scratched his curly hair. A big boy bed sounded very exciting, but also very new. Daddy noticed Sammy's thoughtful face. "Don't worry, buddy. We will make it the coolest ship on the ocean." Together, they built Sammy's brand-new big kid bed. It had a wooden headboard shaped like a steering wheel on a pirate ship, and the bedspread was deep blue like the sparkling sea. Sammy helped place his favorite red sailboat right on the nightstand to keep watch. When bedtime arrived, Sammy put on his favorite striped pajamas. He climbed aboard his captain's bed. It felt sturdy and grand, like he was ready to sail across the Atlantic Ocean. Mommy and Daddy sat on the edge of the mattress and tucked him in securely. "Set sail for dreamland, Captain Sammy," whispered Mommy, kissing his cheek. Sammy felt the comforting weight of the blankets. The room was quiet, and the moonlight danced on his blue sheets like shimmering waves. When he felt a little wiggle of bedtime nervousness, Sammy just squeezed his teddy bear and took a deep, slow breath. He was the captain of this ship, and captains are always brave! He closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, sailing smoothly through the starry night. The next morning, bright rays of sunshine woke up the captain. Sammy sat up, rubbed his eyes, and looked around his room with a proud smile. He had stayed in his big boy ship all night without getting up once! He marched into the kitchen like a proud sailor reporting for duty. "Good morning, Captain!" said Daddy with a laugh. Sammy puffed out his chest proudly. Being a big kid was wonderful, especially when your bed was a magnificent ship.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket
stories.text: Leo has been playing with his favorite blue truck all day long. Now, the sun is starting to go down, painting the sky with pretty pink and orange colors. It is time for Leo to get ready for bedtime. But tonight is a very special night! Leo gets to sleep in his brand new, big-kid bed. It is shaped just like a zooming rocket ship. Mommy helps Leo put on his soft star-patterned pajamas. They brush his little teeth until they sparkle. Then, Daddy brings in Leo's very best friend, Teddy Bear. Leo climbs up the sturdy wooden steps of his rocket bed. Oh, it feels so wonderful! The mattress is bouncy and cozy, wrapped in bright blue sheets. Leo snuggles deep under the blankets. Mommy and Daddy tuck him in securely, making sure Teddy is right beside him. 'Are you ready for your big mission, Captain Leo?' Daddy whispers with a warm smile. Leo nods happily. 'Ready!' he giggles. Mommy turns on the soft glowing star light on the nightstand, casting gentle lights across the ceiling. They lean down and give him a sweet goodnight kiss on his forehead. 'You are such a big boy now, Leo. Sweet dreams,' Mommy says softly. Leo looks around his wonderful new bed. He feels safe, proud, and oh-so-cozy. He hugs Teddy Bear tight, listens to the quiet hum of the night, and slowly closes his eyes. He is ready to float off to sleep in his very own big-kid bed.

stories.title: Maya's Forest Friends
stories.text: The moon is peeking out from behind the fluffy white clouds. Bath time is all done, and Maya is smelling wonderfully like sweet lavender soap. Tonight is a big night in Maya's bedroom. Her tiny toddler crib is gone, and in its place stands a magnificent big-kid bed made of light wood, covered in a quilt made of patchworks. Maya's big sister, Lily, helps her pick out her favorite pink bunny pajamas with little green polka dots. Maya brushes her curly hair and gives her toys a gentle goodnight wave. Now, it is time to try out the big-kid bed. Maya walks over and climbs right up, all by herself! 'Look at me!' Maya cheers proudly. The bed is wide and soft, surrounded by her favorite stuffed animals. There is Barnaby the Bear, Flopsy the Rabbit, and wise old Hoot the Owl. Maya arranges them in a nice cozy circle. Mommy sits on the edge of the mattress and opens up a magical fairy tale book about a friendly dragon. Maya listens closely, snuggling into her pillow. When the story finishes, Mommy gently pulls the patchwork quilt up to Maya's chin. 'You did such a wonderful job climbing into your big-kid bed tonight, Maya. We are so proud of you,' Mommy beams. Maya smiles a big, proud smile. She feels like a true big girl. She closes her eyes, surrounded by her forest friends, and drifts off to a deep, peaceful sleep.

stories.title: Sammy's Starry Canopy
stories.text: The stars are twinkling brightly outside Sammy's window. Inside his bedroom, a magical transformation has happened. Gone is the little baby bed. Today, Sammy got a wonderful big-kid bed with a beautiful canopy draped in glowing fairy lights that look just like real stars. Sammy's daddy helps him put on his comfy yellow dinosaur pajamas. Sammy roars softly, 'Roar! I am a sleepy dinosaur!' Daddy laughs and gives him a tickle. Then, they brush Sammy's teeth together until they are shiny and clean. Sammy walks over to his new bed. It is low to the floor, just right for his little legs. Sammy crawls in and pulls up the forest-green duvet. It feels like a warm hug. Daddy turns on the fairy lights above the canopy, filling the room with a gentle, comforting glow. Sammy's puppy plush toy, Buster, curls up right at his feet. Mommy comes in and sits beside him, stroking his soft hair. 'Are you cozy, my big boy?' Mommy asks tenderly. 'Very cozy,' Sammy sighs happily, looking up at his starry canopy. Mommy and Daddy sing his favorite lullaby in quiet, soothing voices. Sammy feels so safe and happy in his big-kid space. He gives his parents a big hug and a kiss, then snuggles down into his pillow. With a happy yawn, Sammy closes his eyes, ready to dream big dreams in his wonderful big-kid bed.

stories.title: Leo's Cloud Rocket
stories.text: Leo was growing up so fast. Today was a very special day because Leo was getting a brand-new big kid bed! His old crib was cozy, but his big kid bed looked like a real spaceship ready to launch to the stars. Mommy and Daddy brought in soft blue sheets that felt just like a fluffy cloud. Leo helped stretch the corners over the mattress. 'Look, Leo!' said Daddy. 'Your very own rocket ship.' Leo clapped his hands and giggled. 'Blast off!' he whispered. At bedtime, Leo brushed his teeth and put on his favorite star pajamas. He crawled into his big kid bed and snuggled deep under the covers. The mattress felt so roomy and nice. He could roll this way and that way without bumping the sides. Mommy tucked him in with extra care and gave him a warm kiss on his forehead. 'Sweet dreams, my little astronaut,' she said softly. Leo held his favorite stuffed bear tight. He looked up at the ceiling where glowing star stickers twinkled in the dark. It felt a little different than his old crib, but it also felt very brave and wonderful. He was not a tiny baby anymore; he was a big kid now. Leo took a deep breath, listening to the quiet sounds of the house. He felt safe, cozy, and so proud of himself. His big kid bed was the best place in the whole wide world for resting after a busy day of playing. With a happy sigh, Leo closed his eyes and drifted off to sleep, ready for wonderful adventures in the morning light.

stories.title: Mia's Cozy Castle
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a bright and sunny room, lived a little girl named Mia. Mia had outgrown her little crib, and today she received a magnificent big kid bed made of sturdy wood that looked just like a royal castle. Mia’s eyes sparkled with joy. 'A castle for me?' she asked. 'Yes!' said Grandma. 'A special place for a sweet princess.' Together, they piled the bed high with colorful pillows—pink ones, yellow ones, and fluffy white ones that looked like marshmallow fluff. Mia placed her sleepy bunny right in the middle of the pillows, guarding the castle walls. When the sun began to set and painted the sky in shades of purple and orange, it was time for sleep. Mia put on her crown pajamas and washed her hands and face. She walked over to her castle bed and climbed right up. It was so easy to climb in all by herself! No bars to look through, just an open, welcoming space. Grandma sat on the edge of the mattress and read a magical story about fairies and forests. Mia listened closely, feeling the soft breeze from the window. When the story ended, Grandma tucked the heavy quilt snugly around Mia. 'Sleep well, Princess Mia,' Grandma whispered. Mia smiled in the dark. Her big kid bed felt warm, friendly, and wonderfully safe. She hugged her bunny and closed her eyes, ready to dream royal dreams in her very own castle.

stories.title: Sammy's Train to Dreamland
stories.text: Choo choo! All aboard the Sleepy Train! Sammy was the happiest little boy on the block because his big boy bed was shaped just like a red railway car. It even had a painted engine on the headboard and wheels on the sides. Sammy loved cars and trains more than anything, so getting a big boy bed that looked like a locomotive was a dream come true.
