stories.text: Good morning, little sunshine! Today is a brand new day at preschool, and the big clock on the wall says it is almost time for Circle Time! Sammy the little bear hears the happy chime of the music box. Clang, ding, dong! That is the special song that tells all the children it is time to gather together on the big, soft rainbow rug. Sammy is so excited. He finishes putting away his colorful building blocks. 'Great job cleaning up, Sammy!' says Teacher Jen with a warm, gentle smile. Sammy beams with pride and scurries over to the rug. But wait, where should he sit? There are so many cozy spots. He sees a sparkly green circle right near his best friend, Lily. Sammy takes a slow, careful breath and sits right down on his bottom. Cross-patch, applesauce! He makes his legs into a little pretzel just like the big kids do. 'Look at Sammy sitting so nicely,' praises Teacher Jen. Sammy feels like a glowing ray of sunshine inside. He looks around the circle at all his friendly classmates. Everyone is getting ready. Today, the special helper is holding the bright yellow sun pointer. Sammy raises his hand up high, reaching for the sky, but he remembers to wait patiently until it is his turn to speak. That is what good listeners do! Teacher Jen starts singing the morning greeting song, and Sammy joins in with his sweet, happy voice. 'Good morning to you, good morning to you, we are all in our places, with sunshine on our faces!' Sammy wiggles his fingers and sways from side to side. He loves Circle Time so much. Sitting together on the rug makes him feel safe, happy, and ready to learn all kinds of wonderful new things. As the song finishes, Sammy takes a deep breath of fresh air and gets ready for the next fun activity of the bright, beautiful day.

stories.title: Pip's Listening Ears
stories.text: Ring-a-ling-ling! It is Circle Time time! Little Pip the bunny hops all the way across the playroom. Today, Pip has his big, floppy bunny ears wide open. Do you know why? Because today is story and sharing day on the big yellow rug! Pip loves sharing stories. But before he can share, he needs to practice his best listening skills. Pip hops right onto a soft blue square and sits down. He tucks his little paws neatly in his lap. Teacher Sarah holds up a beautiful picture book with a shiny red cover. 'Are your listening ears turned on, everyone?' asks Teacher Sarah playfully. Pip reaches up and touches his furry ears. 'Click, clack, my listening ears are on!' whispers Pip with a giggle. Around him, all the other little friends do the same. Click, clack! Now the room is very quiet and peaceful, just like a calm, sunny meadow. Pip looks right at Teacher Sarah. When someone else is talking, Pip keeps his mouth closed tight like a little zipper. Zip! He watches the pictures in the book as Teacher Sarah turns the big, paper pages. A fluffy white rabbit hops across the storybook page, just like Pip! Pip gets so excited, but instead of shouting out loud, he raises his hand softly in the air. He waits patiently until Teacher Sarah smiles at him and says, 'Yes, Pip?' Then Pip speaks in a kind, gentle voice. 'Look, teacher, that bunny looks just like me!' Teacher Sarah nods and says, 'You are so right, Pip. Thank you for raising your hand and waiting your turn.' Pip feels warm and happy all over. Being a good listener during Circle Time is so much fun, and it makes all his friends feel happy too.

stories.title: Maya's Sharing Star
stories.text: The sun is shining brightly outside the big classroom window, casting warm, golden rays right onto the cozy circle rug. It is time for Circle Time, and Maya is the special Sunshine Leader of the day! Maya wears a bright yellow ribbon headband with a sparkly silver star right in the middle. She feels like a true morning star. 'Time for our sharing circle, little friends!' sings Teacher Mark cheerfully. Maya helps carry the special sharing basket to the middle of the rug. Everyone sits in a lovely, big circle, knee-to-knee and heart-to-heart. Maya gets to go first because she is the leader. She reaches into the basket and pulls out a smooth, round wooden stone that is painted with a friendly smiley face. It is the talking stone! Whoever holds the stone gets to share one happy thing about their morning. Maya holds the stone gently in both of her hands. She thinks for a moment, looking at all her wonderful friends sitting around her. 'This morning, I ate yummy strawberries for breakfast, and they tasted like sunshine,' Maya says in a clear, happy voice. Teacher Mark smiles and claps his hands softly. 'Thank you for sharing, Maya!' Then, Maya gently passes the smiling stone to the little boy sitting right next to her, Leo. 'Your turn, Leo,' she whispers kindly. Leo takes the stone with a big grin and shares his happy thought. Maya listens with her whole heart, nodding and smiling. She loves being part of this wonderful circle. When everyone has had a turn, they all hold hands and sing a joyful song about friendship and sunshine. Maya squeezes her friends' hands gently. Circle Time is the happiest part of her whole day, filled with warmth, sharing, and love.

rhymes.title: The Morning Hello Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We start our day with pure delight.
Come sit down on the cozy floor,
And open up learning's big door.

We cross our legs and tap our toes,
We wiggle every little nose.
We clap our hands up in the air,
And show how much we love to share.

Look left and right to see a friend,
Our happy circle has no end.
We wave hello and start to sing,
We love the joy that songs can bring.

The clock ticks on, it is so sweet,
To sit together on our seat.
Now circle time is here today,
Let's shout hooray and gently play.

rhymes.title: Sitting Tall And Listening
rhymes.text:
It is time to make a ring,
Sit right down and start to sing.
Find your spot upon the rug,
Give yourself a cozy hug.

Backs are straight just like a tree,
Eyes are open wide to see.
Listening ears are turned up high,
Watching clouds float in the sky.

Our teacher speaks with gentle grace,
With happy smiles on every face.
We take a breath and count to three,
As quiet as a mouse can be.

No running feet or busy hands,
We listen to our leader's plans.
This circle time is warm and bright,
We feel so safe and feel so right.

rhymes.title: The Sharing Circle Song
rhymes.text:
Hold the yellow rolling ball,
Pass it gently to us all.
When it lands inside your hand,
You are part of our sweet band.

Tell a story if you choose,
There is nothing here to lose.
Or just smile and pass it on,
Until the sunny day is gone.

We take turns and wait our space,
With a shiny, happy face.
Everyone gets time to speak,
Every single day this week.

Kindness rules our circle floor,
We want to learn and share some more.
Pass the ball and watch it go,
To every little friend we know.

rhymes.title: Wiggle And Freeze Circle
rhymes.text:
Wiggle fingers, wiggle toes,
Touch the tip of tiny nose.
Shake your shoulders up and down,
Turn around and make a crown.

Now the music starts to play,
We are dancing through the day.
Spinning round upon the floor,
Ready for a little more.

When the sudden signal sounds,
Silence all around the grounds.
Freeze like statues in the sun,
Look at what we've just begun.

Not a finger out of place,
Frozen with a happy face.
Now relax and breathe so deep,
No one makes a single peep.

rhymes.title: Goodbye Circle Sunshine
rhymes.text:
Circle time is almost done,
We have had a lot of fun.
Pack away the sharing toys,
All the girls and all the boys.

Stand up slowly from the rug,
Give your special friend a hug.
Wave goodbye and count to four,
Walking gently to the door.

The sunshine stays inside our heart,
Even when we have to part.
We will rest and we will play,
And come right back another day.

Put your coats and jackets on,
Now our morning circle's gone.
Cheer up, toddlers, smile and sing,
Tomorrow brings another ring.

rhymes.title: Good Morning, Circle Ring
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We wake up with a happy light.
Come along and join our space,
Put a smile upon your face.

Sit down softly on the floor,
Leave our worries by the door.
Cross your legs and make them neat,
Rest your little rocking feet.

Look around and see your friends,
Where the happy feeling bends.
Wave hello to everyone,
Now our circle time has begun.

Hold your neighbor's gentle hand,
We're the kindest in the land.
Ready, steady, look and see,
How bright and sunny we can be!

rhymes.title: Sunshine on the Carpet
rhymes.text:
See the yellow sunshine gleam,
Shining like a happy dream.
Right across the circle rug,
Giving everyone a hug.

Clap your hands and count to three,
Look right here and look at me.
Fold your hands and tuck them tight,
Everything is feeling right.

Listen close and hear the sound,
As we sit upon the ground.
Sing a little morning tune,
Dancing with the sun and moon.

Now we share our favorite toys,
Happy girls and happy boys.
Circle time is shining bright,
Bathing in the golden light.

rhymes.title: The Happy Circle Song
rhymes.text:
Up above the sky is blue,
Sunshine comes to visit you.
Gather round the circle mat,
Where we sit and have a chat.

Reach your arms up to the sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.
Bring them down to touch your toes,
Wrinkle up your little nose.

Nod your head and blink your eyes,
Look at all the sweet surprise.
Share a smile so big and wide,
Sunshine glowing deep inside.

We are special, yes it's true,
I love me and I love you.
Circle time is so much fun,
We are warming in the sun.

rhymes.title: Sunshine and Story Wheels
rhymes.text:
Golden rays come peeping in,
Let the circle time begin.
Make a circle, big and round,
Sitting nicely on the ground.

Turn your listening ears on now,
Can you make a friendly cow?
Moo, moo, moo and hear the cheer,
Glad that everyone is here.

Pass the sunshine ball around,
Not a single angry sound.
Catch it safely, hold it tight,
Everything is feeling bright.

Now we get to read a book,
Take a happy little look.
Circle time is full of grace,
Such a warm and sunny place.

rhymes.title: Wiggle and Shine
rhymes.text:
Sunbeams dancing on the floor,
Let us sing and giggle more.
Wiggle fingers in the air,
Sunshine glowing everywhere.

Stomp your feet and make a beat,
Sitting down now, nice and neat.
Breathe in deeply, count to four,
Ready for a fun day more.

Point to something bright and yellow,
Say hello to every fellow.
Share our toys and share our love,
Thank the sunny sky above.

Circle time is nearly done,
We have had a lot of fun.
Stand up tall and feel so grand,
Best friends in a sunny band.

rhymes.title: The Morning Hello Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We start our day with pure delight.
Come sit down upon the floor,
We have fun behind this door.

Cross your legs and touch your toes,
Wiggle, wiggle, little nose.
Look around and see your friends,
Happy time that never ends.

Clap your hands up in the air,
Wave hello to every chair.
Smile a big and happy smile,
Rest and listen for a while.

Teacher has a book to read,
Listening is what we need.
Circle time is here today,
Time to sing and time to play.

rhymes.title: Roll the Rhythmic Ball
rhymes.text:
Sit in a circle big and round,
Not a single angry sound.
Roll the ball across the space,
Catch it with a happy face.

Push it gently to your friend,
Watch it rolling to the end.
My turn, your turn, take it slow,
See the shiny colors glow.

Bounce it lightly, one, two, three,
Laughing loud for all to see.
Hold it tight and give a squeeze,
Pass it downward if you please.

Circle games are fun to share,
Showing love and showing care.
Now we put the ball away,
Ready for our brand new day.

rhymes.title: The Wiggle and Freeze Song
rhymes.text:
Wiggle fingers up so high,
Reach to touch the sunny sky.
Wiggle toes down on the floor,
Then we wiggle even more.

Shake your shoulders left and right,
Twinkle like a little light.
Spin around and count to three,
Happy toddlers full of glee.

When the music starts to play,
We can dance the blues away.
When the music stops just so,
Freeze like statues in the snow.

Not a finger, not a toe,
Watch the happy children grow.
Now we sit and take a breath,
Calm and quiet as can be.

rhymes.title: Listening Ears and Quiet Hands
rhymes.text:
Put your listening ears on now,
Listen closely to the cow.
Put your quiet hands to rest,
Sitting here is truly best.

Eyes are watching, looking straight,
Circle time is feeling great.
Keep your bubbles in your mouth,
Flying north and flying south.

Nod your head if you agree,
You are as sweet as honey bee.
Everyone is in their place,
Smiles upon each little face.

Now the talking time is done,
Learning things is so much fun.
Ready for the next big task,
Whatever teacher has to ask.

rhymes.title: Goodbye Circle Song
rhymes.text:
Circle time is almost through,
We have had great fun with you.
Pack the toys and clear the space,
Move to our next happy place.

Wave goodbye to all our peers,
Cheering loud with happy cheers.
Stand up tall and stretch up high,
Blinking like a butterfly.

Line up ready at the door,
Walking softly on the floor.
Hold a friend's hand nice and tight,
Making everything feel right.

Sun is shining overhead,
Time for lunch or time for bed.
Tomorrow we will meet again,
Boys and girls and teacher Ben.

rhymes.title: The Morning Circle Song
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We start our day with pure delight.
Come sit right down upon the floor,
And we will sing a little more.

Cross your legs and show me grace,
Put a smile upon your face.
Look around and say hello,
To all the friends you come to know.

Clap your hands and tap your knees,
Listen very close, oh please.
Circle time is here at last,
Watching all the worries pass.

Reach up high and touch the sky,
Wave a happy hand goodbye.
Now we are all ready, see,
Learning as a family!

rhymes.title: Roll the Circle Ball
rhymes.text:
We sit together in a ring,
So many happy songs to sing.
Roll the ball across the floor,
Let us roll it more and more.

Catch it gently in your hand,
Best little circle in the land.
Pass it to your neighbor near,
Spread a lot of joy and cheer.

Look at who is sitting right,
Eyes are sparkling and bright.
Share a giggle, share a grin,
That is where the fun begins.

Now the ball is put away,
Ready for another day.
Circle time is such a treat,
Sitting here with hands and feet.

rhymes.title: Listen to the Story Wind
rhymes.text:
Quiet voices, soft and low,
Now it is time for books to go.
Open up the big brown book,
Take a very careful look.

Animals are playing games,
Can you call out all their names?
Point your finger at the page,
Actor on a little stage.

Turn the paper, one by one,
Reading stories is so fun.
Nod your head if you agree,
Happy as a bird, you see.

Close the cover, hold it tight,
Reading fills our hearts with light.
Circle time is great and grand,
Best routine in all the land.

rhymes.title: Wiggle Wiggle Stop
rhymes.text:
Wiggle fingers in the air,
Wiggle toes without a care.
Wiggle shoulders, shake your head,
Time to move just like I said.

Stomp your feet upon the ground,
Make a happy rhythm sound.
Spin around and count to three,
Then sit down as still as can be.

Freeze like statues in the sun,
Now our little race is run.
Breathe in deeply through your nose,
From your head down to your toes.

Stretch your arms out very wide,
Keep our happy glow inside.
Circle time is done for now,
Take a polite little bow!

rhymes.title: Sharing Our Big Feelings
rhymes.text:
Tell me how you feel today,
While we sit and softly play.
Are you happy, are you glad?
Are you feeling just a tad?

If you have a smile to share,
Show it bouncing in the air.
If you need a gentle hug,
Wrap up cozy like a bug.

Everyone is welcome here,
Speaking out so loud and clear.
Holding hands and feeling bold,
Best routine for young and old.

Now the circle is complete,
With our happy little feet.
Ready for the day ahead,
Just like every song we said.

rhymes.title: Good Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We clap our hands with pure delight.
It is time to sit upon the floor,
And learn a little bit and more.

Cross your legs and show your smile,
We will stay here for a while.
Look around and see your friends,
Where the fun so softly blends.

Hold your neighbor by the hand,
Best little kids in all the land.
Now we listen, now we share,
Showing everybody care.

Sing a happy little song,
Everybody sing along!
Circle time has just begun,
Basking in the golden sun.

rhymes.title: The Sunshine Ring
rhymes.text:
Circle up and make a ring,
Hear the happy birdies sing.
Sunshine warms us from above,
Fill our hearts with peace and love.

Touch your nose and touch your toes,
Watch how sweet the morning grows.
Point your finger to the sky,
Wave a little bird hello and bye.

Sit down softly on the mat,
Listen to the friendly chat.
We are ready, smart and bright,
Ready for the morning light.

Eyes are watching, ears are wide,
Happy feeling deep inside.
Circle time is shining through,
Made especially for you.

rhymes.title: Bright Morning Hello
rhymes.text:
Good morning, good morning, to you and to me,
As happy as birds sitting high in a tree.
The sunshine is dancing right down on the floor,
We open our minds and we open the door.

Put your hands up in the air,
Wave them gently here and there.
Now fold them gently in your lap,
And give your knees a little tap.

It is time to share our toys,
All the precious girls and boys.
We take turns and play so sweet,
Tapping rhythm with our feet.

Circle time is here at last,
Watching happy moments pass.
Sunshine smiling from above,
Surrounded by our circle love.

rhymes.title: The Happy Mat
rhymes.text:
Come along and find your spot,
Whether sitting high or not.
Circle time is calling you,
With a sky of brightest blue.

We sit cross-legged, nice and tall,
Biggest friends and children small.
Sunshine beams across the room,
 Chasing any cloud of gloom.

Clap one, two, and clap one, three,
Look how happy we can be.
Nod your head and smile around,
Softest voices make a sound.

Now we ready, now we wait,
Learning things is really great.
Circle time is warm and bright,
Bathing in the morning light.

rhymes.title: Sunshine Circle Song
rhymes.text:
Roll your hands and roll them fast,
Circle time is here at last!
Sunshine streams across the floor,
Welcoming us through the door.

Hold the sunshine in your hand,
Spread it softly through the land.
Touch your cheeks and touch your chin,
Let the circle time begin.

Breathe in deeply, breathe it out,
Listen to the gentle shout.
We are sharing what we know,
Watch our little friendships grow.

Now the circle is complete,
With our happy, busy feet.
Sunshine warms us all the day,
Guiding every word we say.

rhymes.title: Good Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We clap our hands with pure delight.
It is time to sit upon the floor,
And learn a little bit and more.

Cross your legs and show me toes,
Touch a happy little nose.
We wiggle fingers in the air,
And look at all the friends right there.

Teacher smiles and calls your name,
Circle time is such a game!
We pass the smiling sunshine ball,
And share a happy cheer for all.

Now listen close to what we say,
We are ready for a brand new day.
So sing along and join our song,
With all your friends, you loud belong.

rhymes.title: Sitting on the Rug
rhymes.text:
Soft and cozy is our rug,
Like a giant teddy hug.
Time to sit and time to share,
With every friend who gathered there.

Fold your hands right in your lap,
Get ready for a friendly clap.
We look up high and look down low,
Watching how the flowers grow.

The sunshine beams inside the room,
Chasing off the sleepy gloom.
We sway together left and right,
Bathed in golden morning light.

Our circle is a special place,
Filled with joy and every face.
We take a breath and count to three,
How happy as can be are we!

rhymes.title: The Sunshine Hello Song
rhymes.text:
Hello sun up in the sky,
Wave your little hands goodbye
To sleepy time and pillow dreams,
Wake up to the golden beams.

We form a circle round and round,
Sitting quietly on the ground.
Pat your knees and keep the beat,
Happy hands and happy feet.

Who is here today to play?
Let us shout a loud hooray!
We are learning every day,
In a fun and gentle way.

Circle time is shining bright,
Filling up our hearts with light.
Smile around to left and right,
Everything is feeling right.

rhymes.title: Clap and Sing Together
rhymes.text:
Can you clap your hands with me?
One, two, three and happily!
Circle time has just begun,
Basking in the morning sun.

Turn around and touch the floor,
We want sunshine even more.
Blink your eyes and wink your cheek,
Listen close to hear us speak.

We share a story, sweet and grand,
Holding tightly to a hand.
Nod your head and shake it slow,
That is how we say hello.

Bright and cheerful is our crew,
Smiling every day at you.
Now the circle is complete,
With our happy little feet.

rhymes.title: Golden Rays of Circle Time
rhymes.text:
Golden rays come shining through,
Saying cheerful words to you.
Gather on the magic rug,
Safe and warm like in a bug.

Stretch your arms up to the sky,
Watch the morning bird fly by.
Bring them down to touch your toes,
Wiggle every single pose.

We sing a little happy tune,
Underneath the morning moon?
No, the sun is out so high,
Painting blue across the sky!

Circle time is warm and sweet,
Making every moment neat.
Give a cheer and shout hooray,
We are ready for the day!

rhymes.title: Good Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We clap our hands with pure delight.
It is time to sit upon the floor,
And learn a little bit and more.

Cross your legs and show me toes,
Touch a happy little nose.
Look around and see a friend,
Our happy circle does begin.

We wiggle fingers in the air,
We brush and fix our morning hair.
We sing a happy little tune,
Beneath the shiny morning moon.

Now we listen, now we share,
Showing everybody care.
Circle time is here today,
Time to smile and time to play.

rhymes.title: The Sunshine Mat
rhymes.text:
Come along and gather round,
Hear the happy greeting sound.
Find your spot upon the rug,
Give yourself a gentle hug.

Sunshine streams across the floor,
Knocking softly at the door.
We sit down so nice and tall,
Ready for the fun for all.

Roll the ball across the ring,
Clap our hands and sweetly sing.
Nod your head and blink your eyes,
Look up at the golden skies.

Sharing stories side by side,
With our hearts so full of pride.
Circle time is warm and bright,
Filling up our day with light.

rhymes.title: Sitting Tall
rhymes.text:
Time to put the toys away,
Circle time is here today.
March your feet and stomp the ground,
Sit right down without a sound.

Spine is straight like tall green trees,
Hands are resting on our knees.
Look at teacher, big and bright,
Everything is feeling right.

We pass the smiling sun around,
Not a single whisper sound.
Then we cheer and shout out loud,
Making everyone so proud.

Breathe in deep and let it out,
That is what we're all about.
Circle time is cozy here,
Bringing joy and lots of cheer.

rhymes.title: Happy Hearts Together
rhymes.text:
Hold a hand and form a ring,
Let us dance and let us sing.
Sunlight peeping through the glass,
Shining softly on the grass.

Breathe the sunshine in and out,
Hear the happy children shout.
Turn around and touch the floor,
We are ready for much more.

Whisper names of friends so dear,
Glad that everyone is here.
Nod your head and shake your head,
Just like little ducks instead.

Circle time is sweet and kind,
Leaving worries far behind.
Smile at me and smile at you,
All the happy things we do.

rhymes.title: Bright Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
Golden sun begins to rise,
Opening our sleepy eyes.
Time for circle, big and round,
Sitting safely on the ground.

Pat your knees and keep the beat,
Stamping with your little feet.
Reach up high to touch the sun,
Circle time has just begun.

Pass the happy sunshine star,
Sending love both near and far.
Listen close to what we say,
Learning in a joyful way.

Now our circle time is through,
Look at all the things we do.
Stand up slowly, stretch up high,
Wave a happy, cheerful bye.

rhymes.title: Good Morning, Circle Ring
rhymes.text:
The morning sun begins to glow,
It's time to find our spots, let's go!
We sit cross-legged on the floor,
And ready up to learn some more.

The teacher smiles so bright and wide,
With all our happy friends inside.
We clap our hands and sing a song,
And hope that you will sing along.

Good morning to my special friend,
Our circle time is here again.
We look around and say hello,
To every little boy and beau.

Now stretch your arms up to the sky,
And watch the little birdies fly.
We breathe it in and breathe it out,
And give a happy little shout!

rhymes.title: The Sunshine Hello
rhymes.text:
Step into the circle bright,
Bathed in golden morning light.
Cross your legs and sit up tall,
Welcome, welcome, one and all!

Roll your shoulders, shake your head,
Time to wake up from your bed.
Reach up high to touch the sun,
Circle time has just begun.

Pass the sunshine all around,
Keep it safe and safe and sound.
Smile big at the friend next door,
Sitting nicely on the floor.

Now our hands are on our knees,
Listening as quiet as bees.
Ready for the day ahead,
By our loving teachers led.

rhymes.title: Twirling in the Circle Light
rhymes.text:
Ring around the circle now,
Take a bow and say hello.
Sunshine beams are peeking through,
Dancing right in front of you.

Hold a hand and make a ring,
Let us dance and let us sing.
Spin around and then sit down,
Best listeners in all the town.

Point your toes and tap your shoes,
Circle time is made to choose.
What we want to play and share,
Love is floating in the air.

Pat your knees and keep the beat,
Tapping with your little feet.
Sunshine warms us every day,
Ready now to learn and play.

rhymes.title: Sitting Tall in Sunshine
rhymes.text:
Golden rays upon the floor,
Open up a learning door.
Find your spot and sit right down,
Leave behind your sleepy frown.

Backs are straight like willow trees,
Hands are resting on our knees.
Eyes are watching, ears are wide,
Happy hearts are beating inside.

Sunshine whispers in the air,
Magic moments everywhere.
Now we share our news today,
In a kind and gentle way.

Clap your hands and shout hooray,
Circle time is here to stay.
We are smart and we are bright,
Shining like the morning light.

rhymes.title: Hello, My Golden Sun
rhymes.text:
Good morning sun, hello to you,
We have so much we want to do.
Sit together, knee to knee,
As happy as a chickadee.

Wave hello to left and right,
Make your smiling faces bright.
Circle time is warm and grand,
Holding tightly to a hand.

Listen close to what we say,
Learning something new today.
Count our fingers, count to ten,
Then we start it all again.

Now the sunshine fills the room,
 Chasing off the morning gloom.
We are ready, bold and brave,
Waving like a gentle wave.

rhymes.title: Good Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We clap our hands with pure delight.
It is time to sit upon the floor,
And open up a learning door.

Cross your legs and make them flat,
Wear a happy little hat.
Look around and see your friends,
Where the happy circle bends.

Reach up high and touch the sky,
Wave a little bird goodbye.
Bring your hands right to your knee,
Smile for everyone to see.

Now we listen, now we share,
Showing that we really care.
Circle time has just begun,
Learning here is so much fun.

rhymes.title: The Sunshine Mat
rhymes.text:
Golden rays upon the floor,
Come inside and close the door.
Find your spot upon the mat,
Time to chat and time to pat.

Sunshine yellow, bright and warm,
Keep us safe from any storm.
Twiddle thumbs and wiggle toes,
Watch how sweet the morning grows.

Pass the smiling sun around,
Not a single sleepy sound.
Hold it tight and let it glow,
See how fast our feelings grow.

Now the circle is complete,
Sitting down on little feet.
Ready for the day ahead,
Happier than books we read.

rhymes.title: Wiggle and Freeze
rhymes.text:
Wiggle fingers in the air,
Wave to people everywhere.
Now it is time to sit so still,
Just like shining on a hill.

Sunshine circle, big and round,
Sitting nicely on the ground.
Tap your shoulders, touch your nose,
Wiggle all your tiny toes.

Stomp your feet and beat the drum,
Look at all the friends who come.
Freeze like statues in the sun,
Look at us, we are so done!

Deep breath in and let it out,
That is what this time is about.
Ready now to sing and play,
Starting off our happy day.

rhymes.title: Hello Friends
rhymes.text:
Circle time is here again,
Calling all the little men.
Calling all the maidens too,
We have lots of things to do.

Say hello to neighbor Ned,
Nod your sleepy little head.
Catch a sunbeam in your hand,
Bestest kids in all the land.

Sing a song of morning light,
Everything is feeling right.
Clap a rhythm, soft and sweet,
Stomp our happy little feet.

Now the circle is so tight,
Glowing in the morning light.
We are ready, bold and bright,
Hugging sunshine very tight.

rhymes.title: The Happy Sunshine Ring
rhymes.text:
Make a ring that shines so gold,
 Stories waiting to be told.
Hold your neighbor by the hand,
Walking through a sunny land.

Sit right down upon the rug,
Give yourself a giant hug.
Sunshine beams are shining down,
Not a single little frown.

Blink your eyes and count to three,
Look at all your friends and me.
We are sharing space and time,
Like a happy nursery rhyme.

Now the circle time is sweet,
Resting every little feet.
Smile and cheer because we sing,
In our happy sunshine ring.

rhymes.title: Good Morning Circle
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
We clap our hands with pure delight.
It is time to sit upon the floor,
And learn a little bit and more.

Cross your legs and show me toes,
Touch a happy little nose.
Look around and see a friend,
Our happy circle does not end.

We sing a song so loud and clear,
To bring our preschool family near.
We wiggle fingers, count to ten,
And then we start to smile again.

So hold your neighbor by the hand,
The nicest circle in the land.
We take a breath and then we say,
Good morning to a brand new day!

rhymes.title: The Hello Song
rhymes.text:
Ring the bell and hear the sound,
Sit in a circle on the ground.
Look at me and look at you,
We have so many things to do.

Wave hello and say good day,
We are here to learn and play.
Nod your head and blink your eyes,
Look up at the sunny skies.

Share a toy and share a smile,
We will sit here for a while.
Pat your knees and keep the beat,
Sitting nice upon your seat.

Now our circle time is bright,
Bathed in morning golden light.
Everybody shout hurray,
We are ready for the day!

rhymes.title: Sunshine on the Rug
rhymes.text:
Sunshine streaming through the glass,
Shining on the greenest grass.
Find your spot upon the rug,
Give yourself a little hug.

Circle time is starting now,
Can you take a little bow?
Stretch your arms up to the sky,
Watch the happy day go by.

Breathe in deeply, smell the air,
Show that everybody cares.
Point to red and point to blue,
Colors shining bright for you.

Now our circle circle spins,
That is where the magic begins.
Clap your hands and stomp your feet,
Circle time is so complete.

rhymes.title: Twirl Around the Circle
rhymes.text:
Stand up tall and touch your toes,
Follow where the rhythm goes.
Now we sit down on the floor,
Ready for a fun explored.

Listen close and hear the chime,
It is special circle time.
Turn around and face the center,
Where the happy feelings enter.

Roll your hands and make a wheel,
Tell me how you want to feel.
Happy, sleepy, bright, or bold,
Stories waiting to be told.

Keep your hands upon your lap,
Take a gentle little tap.
Circle sunshine warms us through,
Ready for whatever is new.

rhymes.title: Our Happy Meeting Spot
rhymes.text:
Step by step we gather round,
Sitting quietly on the ground.
Sunshine warms us from above,
Filled with happiness and love.

Pass the smiling ball along,
Singing out our favorite song.
Look up high and look down low,
Watch our friendly circle grow.

 wiggle fingers up so high,
Wave them gently to the sky.
Now we fold them nice and neat,
Resting hands and resting feet.

Circle time is shining bright,
Filling up our hearts with light.
Time to learn and time to share,
Sunshine floating in the air.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Firetruck
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sammy had a bright red firetruck. It rolled very fast across the soft carpet. Vroom, vroom! Went the little firetruck. Soon, his friend Maya came over to play. Maya looked at the shiny red firetruck with big, happy eyes. She wanted to play too! Sammy held the truck a little bit tighter. He loved his firetruck very much. Mommy knelt down with a big, warm smile and a friendly little box with a ticking hand. 'This is our sharing timer, little ones,' Mommy said softly. 'When the bell goes ding-dong, it is time to switch and share the fun.' Sammy nodded. He knew how to share, but waiting can be tricky for little boys. Mommy set the friendly timer for two whole minutes. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the timer. Sammy gave the firetruck a gentle push across the floor to Maya. Maya giggled and rolled it right back. They played together, passing the truck back and forth. They counted the wheels and made funny siren noises together. Ding-dong! Sang the little timer. It was time for Sammy to hold his firetruck again. Sammy felt so proud. He smiled at Maya and said, 'Now it is my turn!' Maya clapped her hands and cheered. Sharing was so much easier with the friendly timer to help them take turns. They played happily all afternoon, sharing blocks, puzzles, and books. Mommy gave them both a big hug and said, 'You are such wonderful sharers.' Sammy went to sleep that night dreaming of all the fun games he could share with his friends tomorrow.

stories.title: Leo and the Purple Crayon
stories.text: Leo loved to draw pictures. Today, he had a giant piece of paper and one very special purple crayon. Scribble, scribble, went the crayon, making lovely purple circles on the page. Leo was drawing a big bouncy balloon. Suddenly, his little sister Lily waddled over. She pointed her tiny finger at the crayon and said, 'P-up-ple!' Lily wanted to make a purple picture too. Leo took a gentle breath. He liked his purple crayon, but he loved his little sister. Daddy walked over holding a cute yellow kitchen timer shaped like a happy lemon. 'Let us use the sharing timer to help us play nice,' Daddy said in a cheerful voice. Leo placed the purple crayon on the table. 'You can use it first, Lily,' Leo whispered kindly. Daddy twisted the lemon timer. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the lemon. Lily made a happy squiggly line on the paper. Leo waited patiently, watching the little hand move around the clock face. He clapped his hands to encourage his sister. Ding-dong! Went the happy lemon timer. Lily handed the crayon back to Leo with a gummy smile. 'My turn now!' Leo said happily. He drew the string on his bouncy balloon. Then, it was Lily's turn again. Taking turns was so much fun because they did it together. Daddy smiled and gave them high-fives. 'You both showed such great patience,' Daddy said. Leo felt warm inside. Sharing made playing twice as nice, especially when the friendly lemon timer helped them remember to share.

stories.title: Zoe and the Dinosaur Puzzles
stories.text: Zoe had a wonderful puzzle with big, chunky wooden dinosaurs. There was a green T-Rex, a blue Triceratops, and a long-necked Brachiosaurus. Zoe loved fitting the pieces into their special spots. Snap, went the pieces into place. Her cousin Toby came over to play in the sunshine. Toby loved dinosaurs just as much as Zoe did. He reached for the green T-Rex piece. Zoe gently pulled her hand back. 'That is mine!' she said. Grandma walked over with a cute blue owl timer that had big, blinking eyes. 'Let us make the owl our sharing helper,' Grandma said sweetly. 'The owl helps us take turns so everyone gets a chance to play.' Zoe looked at the cute owl and nodded. She wanted Toby to have fun, too. Grandma set the owl timer for a few minutes. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the owl. Zoe placed the green T-Rex into Toby's open hands. Toby roared like a happy dinosaur. Grrr! Zoe giggled and fitted the blue Triceratops into her own board. They worked together as a team, building a wonderful dinosaur park on the rug. Ding-dong! Sang the cute owl timer. It was time to switch pieces. Toby carefully handed the T-Rex back to Zoe, and Zoe shared her yellow pterodactyl. They smiled big, happy smiles at each other. Grandma clapped her hands and said, 'Look at you two sharing like big kids!' Zoe felt so proud of her kind heart. Playing together was the best part of the whole day, and the sharing timer made taking turns feel like a magical game.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Firetruck
stories.text: Little Sammy loved the shiny red firetruck. It had big black wheels that rolled so smoothly across the living room rug. Wee-ooo, wee-ooo! Sammy pushed it back and forth, making happy engine noises. Just then, his little sister, Mia, toddled over with big, hopeful eyes. She pointed at the firetruck and made happy grabby hands. Sammy hugged the firetruck a little tighter. He did not want to let go. Sharing could be so tricky sometimes! Mommy walked over with a soft, warm smile and kneeled down beside them. She held up a small, colorful kitchen timer shaped like a happy yellow duck. 'Look, Sammy,' Mommy said gently. 'This is our special sharing timer. When we turn the dial, it counts down your special turn. When it goes ding-dong, it is Mia's turn to play. That way, everyone gets a turn with the fun firetruck!' Sammy thought about this. He loved the firetruck, but he also loved his little sister. Mommy helped him twist the duck timer until it clicked. 'Ready, set, tick-tock!' said Mommy. Sammy zoomed the firetruck two more times. He pushed it to the couch and made a loud siren sound. Then, *ding-dong!* went the happy duck timer. Sammy looked at Mommy and smiled. He proudly picked up the shiny red firetruck and handed it right to Mia. 'Your turn, Mia!' he said softly. Mia clapped her little hands with glee and grabbed the wheels. Sammy felt a warm, cozy feeling in his tummy. Sharing was a big-kid thing to do, and he was a big boy now. Mommy gave him a giant hug and whispered, 'Such wonderful sharing, Sammy! You are so kind.' Sammy waited patiently for the next tick-tock, feeling very proud of his kind heart.

stories.title: Leo and the Purple Paintbrush
stories.text: Leo sat at the little blue art table with a giant piece of white paper. Dipping his brush into the bright purple paint, he made big sweeping swirls all over the page. Swish, swash, swish! The purple paint looked just like a friendly giant octopus swimming in the ocean. Across the table sat his best friend, Maya. Maya looked at her paper, then looked at Leo's purple paint, and let out a little sigh. She wanted to paint her octopus purple too! Leo noticed Maya looking at his paint pot. His eyebrows scrunched together for a tiny second. He liked having the purple paint all to himself. But then, Teacher Sarah walked over with a bright green timer shaped like a friendly frog. 'Hello, artists,' Teacher Sarah said in a sweet, singsong voice. 'Are we having trouble sharing our special purple paint today? Let us use our froggy timer to make it fair and fun.' Teacher Sarah set the frog timer and pushed its nose. *Tick-tock, tick-tock,* went the friendly frog. Leo took a deep breath and painted three more purple bubbles on his paper. *Ribbit! Ding-dong!* went the frog timer. It was time for Maya to use the purple paint. Leo carefully slid the paint pot across the table toward his friend. 'Here you go, Maya,' Leo said with a brave, kind smile. Maya's face lit up like sunshine. 'Thank you, Leo!' she cheered, dipping her brush into the lovely purple paint. Leo watched her paint a happy purple star and realized that sharing made art time even more fun because they were doing it together. When the timer went *ribbit* again, it was Leo's turn once more. He smiled brightly, knowing that sharing was easy when you took turns with a friend.

stories.title: Daisy and the Bouncing Ball
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly in the backyard, and Daisy had the most wonderful yellow bouncing ball. Boing, boing, bounce! The ball flew up into the air and came right back down into Daisy's waiting hands. She giggled with pure joy as she chased it across the green grass. Her cousin, Toby, ran over, laughing and reaching out his hands. 'My ball!' Toby said happily. Daisy clutched the yellow ball against her chest. She wanted to bounce it forever and ever. Sharing felt hard when a toy was so much fun. Daddy walked over, holding a bright blue kitchen timer shaped like a smiling whale. 'Hey there, little ones,' Daddy said cheerfully. 'Who wants to play a game with the sharing whale?' Daisy nodded slowly. She trusted the smiling whale. Daddy turned the whale's tail, and the timer began to tick softly. *Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock.* 'Daisy gets to bounce the ball until the whale sings its song,' Daddy explained. Daisy bounced the ball one, two, three times as high as she could reach! She caught it against her tummy just as the whale timer let out a cheerful *splash-ding!* Daddy smiled and looked at Daisy. 'Time to share with Toby!' Daisy looked at the yellow ball, took a deep breath, and rolled it across the grass to her cousin. 'Catch, Toby!' she called out. Toby laughed loudly and caught the ball, rolling it right back to her when his turn was finished. Daisy caught the ball and cheered. She realized that sharing didn't mean losing her toy; it meant doubling the fun because playing together was the best game of all.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Truck
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy yellow room, little Sammy had a favorite toy. It was a shiny red truck with big black wheels that went vroom-vroom across the soft green rug. Sammy loved his truck very much. Soon, his good friend Maya came over to play. Maya looked at the shiny red truck and smiled a big, happy smile. She wanted to play vroom-vroom too! Sammy felt a little tiny bubble of worry in his tummy. He loved his truck and did not want to share it right away. Mommy knelt down beside them with a bright green timer. She said, 'Sammy, sharing can be tricky, but this special timer helps us take turns. When the little hand stops, it is your turn again!' Mommy set the timer for three happy minutes. Tick-tock, tick-tock went the friendly timer. Sammy gently handed the shiny red truck to Maya. Maya cheered, 'Yay! Thank you, Sammy!' Sammy watched the truck roll across the rug. He took a deep breath and felt a warm, proud feeling in his heart. Sharing was safe! He waited patiently while the little hand moved round and round. Suddenly, the timer made a happy little chime: ding-dong! Maya smiled and gently pushed the truck right back into Sammy's lap. 'Your turn, Sammy!' she said kindly. Sammy hugged his truck. He felt so happy that he shared. He gave Maya a big high-five. Taking turns was so much fun when you had a special sharing timer to help! The rest of the afternoon was filled with laughter, vroom-vroom sounds, and lots of happy sharing.

stories.title: Leo and the Magical Dinosaur
stories.text: Deep in the land of the living room, Leo held a roaring green dinosaur. The dinosaur had big white teeth and made fierce rawr sounds. Leo loved making his dinosaur stomp over the cushions. Just then, his little sister Lily walked over. She reached out her tiny hand and said, 'Dinosaur, please!' Leo pulled the dinosaur close to his chest. He wanted to play with it all by himself. Daddy saw Leo's tight grip and smiled softly. 'It is hard to let go of a favorite toy, Leo. Would you like to use our magical sharing timer?' Daddy showed Leo a cute yellow bear timer. 'When the bear says it is time, we switch!' Daddy twisted the bear's tummy, and it began to tick gently. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock. Leo looked at Lily, who was waiting so patiently. With a brave little smile, Leo handed the green dinosaur to his sister. 'Here you go, Lily,' he whispered. Lily giggled and made the dinosaur do a little happy dance. Leo watched her and felt a wonderful flutter of pride in his chest. He was being a super-duper big brother! He waited and watched the cute bear timer. Time flew by quickly. Ring-ring! went the little timer. Lily handed the dinosaur right back to Leo with a sweet hug. 'My turn now!' Leo cheered. He took his dinosaur back and gave Lily a gentle pat on the head. Sharing made everyone smile, and the magical timer made taking turns feel like an exciting adventure. They played together happily until the sun went down.

stories.title: Emma and the Glittery Art Box
stories.text: Bright colors filled the little white table where Emma sat with her cousin Noah. Emma had a brand new box of sparkly, glittery markers. They shone pink, gold, and purple under the warm room light. Noah gasped, 'Ooh, Emma! Those markers are so sparkly!' He wanted to draw a magical rainbow with the gold marker. Emma liked holding all the markers in her hands, but she also loved Noah very much. Grandma walked over with a cute blue apple timer. 'Let us use the sharing timer, my sweet little artists,' Grandma said with a warm hug. 'This helps us share the sparkly fun fairly.' Grandma turned the apple stem, and it began to tick softly. Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock. Emma opened her hands and passed the gold marker to Noah. Noah beamed with joy. 'Thank you for sharing, Emma!' he said. Emma picked up a pink marker to draw her own fluffy pink clouds while Noah drew his golden rainbow. Emma felt so happy inside. She was sharing her special art supplies like a kind friend. They both colored busily while the apple timer ticked away. Suddenly, the timer chimed a sweet little song: beep-beep! Noah smiled warmly and handed the gold marker back across the table. 'Your turn for the gold, Emma!' he said. Emma took the marker and added a golden sun to her picture. She felt proud, kind, and wonderfully happy. Taking turns was easy and fun, especially when shared with someone you love.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Fire Truck
stories.text:
Once upon a time, little Sammy had a shiny red fire truck. It was his most favorite toy in the whole wide world! He loved to zoom it across the living room rug. Neeee-naw! Neeee-naw! went Sammy, pushing his truck with a big smile.

Soon, his friend Lily walked over. Lily looked at the shiny red fire truck with big, curious eyes. She wanted to play too! Sammy held the truck a little bit tighter. He wasn't quite sure he wanted to share his special toy. Sharing can feel tricky sometimes, and that is okay.

Mommy smiled gently and knelt down beside them. 'Would you like to use the Sharing Timer, Sammy?' she asked in a warm, cozy voice. Sammy nodded slowly. He liked the timer because it helped him know just what to expect.

Mommy set the little yellow timer shaped like a friendly duck. *Tick-tock, tick-tock*, went the timer. 'When the timer sings beep-beep, it is time for Lily to zoom the fire truck,' Mommy explained. 'Until then, Sammy gets to play!'

Sammy felt a happy bubble pop in his tummy. He zoomed the truck one more time. Then, the little duck timer went *BEEP-BEEP*! Sammy took a gentle breath, just like Mommy taught him, and handed the fire truck to Lily. 'Your turn, Lily!' he said proudly.

Lily giggled and rolled the truck back and forth. Sammy watched, feeling so proud of himself for being a great sharer. While Lily played, Sammy cuddled a soft teddy bear. He knew his turn would come back very soon.

*Tick-tock, tick-tock* went the duck timer again. *BEEP-BEEP*! 'My turn!' cheered Sammy, taking back his fire truck with a huge grin. Sharing together made playtime twice as fun. Sammy gave Mommy a big hug. 'I did it, Mommy! I shared!' Mommy kissed his forehead. 'You did it, Sammy. You are a super sharer!'

stories.title: Bella and the Soft Purple Bear
stories.text:
Deep in the sunny playroom, little Bella hugged her soft purple bear named Barnaby. Barnaby was extra fluffy and smelled just like lavender. Bella loved to brush his fuzzy ears and give him gentle hugs. *Squeeeez!* whispered Bella.

Her cousin Leo came over to play. Leo reached out a little hand to touch Barnaby's soft paw. 'Bear!' said Leo happily. Bella pulled Barnaby back just a tiny bit. She loved her bear so much and wanted to keep him all to herself. Sharing felt a little scary in her heart.

Grandma walked over with a kind, loving smile. She sat down on the soft rug with Bella and Leo. 'It is wonderful to love your bear, Bella. Would our magical pink bunny timer help us share Barnaby?' Grandma asked softly.

Bella looked at the cute bunny timer. She liked the floppy pink ears. 'Okay, Grandma,' Bella whispered.

Grandma wound up the bunny timer. *Tick-tock, tick-tock*. Grandma explained, 'Bella gets to hold Barnaby while the timer ticks. When it sings, it is Leo's turn to hold the soft bear.' Bella felt reassured. She knew her bear would come right back to her.

Bella held Barnaby close, singing a little quiet song to him. She stroked his soft purple fur. The timer went *TICK-TOCK, TICK-TOCK*. Then, it made a happy little chime: *DING-DONG*!

Bella took a deep breath and gently passed Barnaby to Leo. 'Here you go, Leo. You can hold Barnaby now,' she said sweetly. Leo's face lit up with joy as he cuddled the soft bear.

While Leo hugged the bear, Bella played with some colorful stacking blocks. She built a tall, wonderful tower. Before she knew it, the bunny timer chimed *DING-DONG* again! 'My turn with Barnaby!' Bella cheered, taking her beloved bear back into her arms. Grandma clapped her hands. 'Look at you two! Sharing makes our hearts so full and happy. You are wonderful friends!'

stories.title: Max and the Magic Dinosaur
stories.text:
Max had a big, green toy dinosaur that stomped around the rug. *Stomp, stomp, roar!* roared Max, making his dinosaur walk over the pillows. The dinosaur was so much fun because its tail could wiggle back and forth!

His friend Maya came over to play blocks. Maya heard the roaring and walked over. She reached for the green dinosaur with a hopeful smile. 'Roar!' said Maya, joining in the fun. Max hugged the dinosaur close to his chest. He wanted to play with it all afternoon. Sharing could be hard when you love a toy so much.

Daddy walked over and sat down cross-legged on the floor with them. 'Hey there, little dinosaur tamers. Would our special blue rocket timer help us share today?' Daddy asked with an encouraging wink.

Max looked at the rocket timer. It looked like it was ready to blast off into space! Max nodded. 'Yes, Daddy, let's use the rocket.'

Daddy turned the top of the rocket. *Tick-tock, tick-tock* went the little timer. 'Max is the rocket pilot first,' Daddy said. 'When the timer makes a rocket-launch sound, it is Maya's turn to make the dinosaur roar!'

Max felt safe and happy. He made his dinosaur do a funny little dance. *Tick-tock, tick-tock* went the timer, counting down the fun seconds. Suddenly, the timer made a happy sound: *WHOOSH-BEEP*!

Max smiled proudly. He remembered to use his gentle hands. He handed the green dinosaur to Maya. 'Your turn to roar, Maya!' Max said nicely. Maya took the dinosaur and made it stomp on a pillow. 'Roar! Thank you, Max!' she said.

While Maya played with the dinosaur, Max zoomed a little race car across the floor. He loved watching Maya smile. Soon enough, the rocket timer went *WHOOSH-BEEP* again! 'Blast off, my turn!' Max laughed, taking the dinosaur back. Daddy smiled big. 'You are both such wonderful sharers. Sharing brings so much joy to everyone!'

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Firetruck
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy yellow room, little Sammy had a big red firetruck. It was his absolute favorite toy in the whole wide world. It had shiny silver wheels that went round and round, and a tiny ladder that went up and up. Sammy loved making beep-beep sounds as he pushed it across the soft blue rug. Soon, his best friend Maya toddled over. Maya looked at the bright red firetruck and gently asked, 'Sammy, can I play too?' Sammy hugged the firetruck a little tighter. It is hard to share your most special toys, and Sammy felt a little flutter in his tummy. Mama knelt down beside them with a big, warm smile. 'I know it is hard to share, Sammy,' Mama said softly. 'How about we use our magic Sharing Timer? You play for a little bit, and when the beep sounds, it is Maya's turn to drive!' Mama set a cute little timer shaped like a smiling yellow duck. Tic-toc, tic-toc went the duck. Sammy pushed the firetruck across the rug one more time. He made the loudest siren sound he could! 'Weee-ooo, weee-ooo!' Then, suddenly, the little duck timer went, 'Quack-quack-beep!' It was time! Sammy took a big breath. He looked at Maya and gently handed her the shiny red firetruck. 'Your turn, Maya,' he said proudly. Maya's face lit up with the biggest smile. 'Thank you, Sammy!' she cheered. Maya drove the firetruck all around the rug, and Sammy clapped his hands. Waiting was not so scary after all, and Sammy felt so proud of his kind and sharing heart. When the duck timer beeped again, it was Sammy's turn once more. Sharing made playtime twice as fun for everyone in the cozy yellow room.

stories.title: Leo and the Purple Paint
stories.text: In a sunny green house, little Leo sat at a low wooden table with a big jar of bright purple finger paint. Oh, how Leo loved that purple paint! He dipped his chubby little finger right into the jar and made a swirl on his paper. It looked just like a squiggly octopus! Just then, his little sister Lily walked up. Lily pointed her finger at the purple jar and said, 'Purple! My turn?' Leo shook his head and pulled the jar closer to his tummy. Sharing can feel tricky when you are having so much fun creating your masterpiece. Papa walked over and gave Leo a gentle hug. 'You are doing such wonderful painting, Leo,' Papa whispered. 'Do you want to use the friendly turtle timer to help us share the paint?' Leo nodded his head. Papa set the green turtle timer on the table and twisted its shell. The turtle smiled a happy painted smile. Tic-toc, tic-toc went the little turtle. Leo used his purple paint to make polka dots all over his paper. He pressed hard and made wonderful purple circles. Then, with a soft little ding, the turtle timer told them the time was up! Leo looked at the turtle, then looked at Lily. He took a deep breath, slid the paint jar across the table, and said, 'Your turn, Lily.' Lily giggled and dipped her finger into the purple paint, making a lovely flower on her own paper. Leo watched her and felt a warm, fuzzy feeling grow right inside his chest. Sharing felt really good! When the turtle timer dinged again, the purple jar came sliding back to Leo. They painted together, sharing happily until the very last drop.

stories.title: Mia and the Starry Puzzle
stories.text: In a bright pink bedroom, little Mia was putting together a glowing puzzle of the night sky. She had already found the big yellow moon and three twinkly star pieces. She was searching for the last piece, a shiny blue star, when her cousin Toby skipped into the room. Toby pointed at the puzzle and said, 'Star! Me help?' Mia covered the puzzle with her hands. She loved this puzzle so much, and she wanted to finish it all by herself. It is totally okay to feel that way, but Grandma was right there to help. Grandma knelt down on the fluffy rug and gave Mia a gentle pat on the back. 'You are doing a fantastic job with those puzzle pieces, Mia,' Grandma said in a sweet voice. 'Would you like to use our magic sharing star to take turns?' Grandma held up a little star timer that lit up with soft rainbow colors. Mia thought about it for a moment. She loved rainbows and she loved her cousin Toby. 'Okay, Grandma,' Mia said softly. Grandma turned on the rainbow star timer. It began to glow and softly tick. Mia picked up the blue star piece and carefully fitted it right into the puzzle. Click! It was a perfect fit! Everyone cheered. Then, the rainbow star timer flashed a happy green light. Beep-beep! Time to share! Mia smiled and gently picked up the next puzzle piece to hand to Toby. Toby took the piece with wide, happy eyes and placed it carefully on the board. Mia clapped her hands and cheered for Toby. Taking turns made playtime so joyful, and the rainbow star twinkled happily as they finished the glowing puzzle together.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Firetruck
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy sat right on the soft blue rug in the living room. He was playing with his absolute favorite toy in the whole wide world: a shiny, bright red firetruck. It went 'Nee-nah, nee-nah!' as it zoomed across the floor. Just then, his sweet friend Maya walked over with her big, curious brown eyes. She pointed at the little wheels and whispered, 'Can I please play with the firetruck too, Sammy?' Sammy hugged the truck a tiny bit closer. It was hard to let go of something so fun! But then, Mommy walked over with a big, warm smile and a magical yellow kitchen timer shaped like a happy lemon. 'Let's use the sharing timer!' Mommy said gently. 'When we share, everyone gets a turn to play.' Sammy pressed the top button and twisted it until it clicked. 'Ding!' went the timer. 'When it rings,' Mommy explained, 'it is time to switch.' Sammy handed the firetruck to Maya. At first, Sammy felt a little tiny wiggle of worry in his tummy. But Mommy gave him a big hug and said, 'You are being such a wonderful sharer!' Maya was so gentle with the firetruck. She rolled it back and forth, right to Sammy. Sammy giggled and rolled it back. They took turns making loud siren noises together. Then, tick-tock, tick-tock went the timer. Suddenly, *RING-RING-RING!* went the happy lemon timer! It was time to switch. Maya smiled warmly and handed the red firetruck right back to Sammy. Sammy held his shiny toy again and felt so proud. Sharing made playing together twice as fun! Sammy gave Maya a high-five and said, 'Yay for sharing!' The rest of the morning was filled with happy giggles, zooming firetrucks, and wonderful teamwork.

stories.title: Leo and the Magical Dinosaur
stories.text: Deep in the jungle of the playroom, little Leo discovered a magnificent creature. It was a green, stomp-stomping dinosaur with soft squishy spikes on its back. Leo loved his dinosaur so much that he named him Barnaby. Barnaby could roar softly and give the best hugs. Suddenly, Leo's little sister, Lily, toddled over. She clapped her hands and reached out, saying, 'Dinosaur! Roar!' Leo pulled Barnaby away for a second. He wanted to play with Barnaby all by himself forever and ever. But Daddy knelt down beside them with a special green timer that looked like a friendly frog. 'Hey there, little helpers,' Daddy said in a cozy, gentle voice. 'Do you want to try the sharing timer today? It helps us share our special toys.' Leo blinked and nodded. He knew sharing was a kind choice. Daddy twisted the frog's tummy, and the tiny gears started to purr. *Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock.* 'While the frog is counting down,' Daddy said, 'Leo gets to make Barnaby stomp across the pillows.' Lily watched with big, excited eyes and clapped every time Barnaby did a big stomp. Leo felt very proud to show his sister how cool the dinosaur was. Then, *RIB-BIT!* went the frog timer, chiming a sweet little bell sound. 'Time to switch!' said Daddy. Leo gently handed Barnaby to Lily. Lily hugged the green dinosaur and made happy little gurgling noises. Leo waited patiently, watching his sister play so nicely. He felt a warm, fuzzy feeling in his heart because he was being a great big brother. When the timer rang again, it was Leo's turn once more. Sharing with the magic frog timer made playtime peaceful, happy, and full of love.

stories.title: Mia and the Sparkly Puzzle Pieces
stories.text: At the little yellow table by the window, Mia was putting together a wonderful puzzle with big, sparkly pink and purple unicorn pieces. Each piece clicked into place with a satisfying little snap. Her cousin Toby stood nearby, watching the glittery unicorn come to life. Toby softly asked, 'Can I put a piece in, Mia?' Mia paused. She loved her unicorn puzzle very much, and she wanted to finish it all by herself. But she also loved playing with Toby. Grandma walked over, carrying a cute little blue timer shaped like a singing bird. 'Would you like to use the sharing timer, my little loves?' Grandma asked softly. Mia nodded and smiled. Grandma explained, 'When we share our puzzle, we take turns making the magic happen.' Grandma turned the bird's head, and it began to tick softly like a tiny heartbeat. *Tick-tock, tick-tock.* Mia picked up a sparkly purple piece and fitted it right into the unicorn's flowing mane. Toby cheered, 'Yay, Mia!' Mia felt so happy and encouraged. She loved making her cousin smile. They worked together for a few minutes, passing the puzzle pieces back and forth. Then, *CHIRP-CHIRP!* went the sweet little bird timer. It was time for Toby to take a turn placing a piece. Mia handed the shiny pink unicorn horn to Toby. Toby carefully guided it into the empty space. *Click!* It fit perfectly! Toby clapped his hands in delight, and Mia clapped right along with him. They took turns back and forth, sharing the puzzle until the sparkly unicorn was completely finished. Grandma clapped her hands and said, 'Look what wonderful teamwork can do when you share!' Mia and Toby high-fived each other, feeling proud, kind, and ready for their next fun adventure together.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Firetruck
stories.text: Little Sammy loved the shiny red firetruck. It had big black wheels that rolled so smoothly across the living room rug. Every time Sammy pushed it, he made a fun siren sound. WOO-WOO! Just then, his little sister Lily walked over with bright, hopeful eyes. She pointed at the firetruck and said, "My turn, please?" Sammy hugged the firetruck a little tighter. It was his absolute favorite toy in the whole wide world! Mommy knelt down on the soft rug next to them. She smiled a warm, gentle smile and gave Sammy a reassuring hug. "It is hard to share our very favorite things, isn't it, Sammy? But remember our special friend, the Sharing Timer! When the timer goes ding, it is Lily's turn to play. Then we wait for the next ding, and it is right back to you." Sammy thought about this for a moment. He looked at Lily's sweet face and then at the friendly little yellow timer sitting on the shelf. Mommy turned the timer's dial all the way to five minutes. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the timer, singing its quiet little song. Sammy pushed the firetruck to Lily. "Here you go, Lily! You can drive it until the timer goes ding!" Lily giggled with pure joy and zoomed the truck around. Sammy watched her, feeling a warm, proud bubble grow inside his chest. Sharing felt so good! Tick-tock went the clock, counting down the minutes. Suddenly, the timer made a happy little sound. DING-DONG! Lily looked up and smiled. "All done! Your turn, big brother!" she said, gently rolling the firetruck right back to Sammy. Sammy clapped his hands with absolute delight. He took the firetruck back, feeling so proud of himself and his sister. Mommy cheered, giving them both big, loving squeezes. "Look at you two sharing so wonderfully! What a fantastic job!" Sammy grinned from ear to ear as he zoomed his firetruck again, knowing that taking turns was easy when you had a helpful timer by your side.

stories.title: Bella Builds a Rainbow Tower
stories.text: Bella was a master builder. Today, she was using all her colorful wooden blocks to build the tallest tower in the whole playroom. Red block, orange block, yellow block, green block! It stretched all the way up to her nose. Her friend Toby walked over, holding a special sparkly blue block. "Can I put this on top, Bella?" Toby asked softly. Bella shook her head. "No, Toby, it's my tower! I want to build it all by myself." Toby looked a little sad and sat down quietly on the floor. Daddy saw what was happening and walked over with a gentle step. He sat down between the two friends and gave Bella a loving pat on the back. "Bella, sweetie, building together is so much fun, but waiting can be tricky. Would you like to use the magic Sharing Timer to take turns placing the top blocks?" Bella thought about it. She loved her tower, but she also liked playing with Toby. "Okay, Daddy," she whispered. Daddy smiled and set the cute little green timer right next to the wooden blocks. He twisted the top, and it started to tick. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the friendly timer. Bella placed two more blocks on her tower while Toby cheered her on. Then, tick-tock, the timer whispered softly. Bella handed the sparkly blue block to Toby. "Your turn, Toby!" she said with a bright, encouraging smile. Toby carefully placed the blue block right on the very top of the tower without knocking it down. Bella clapped her hands and cheered loudly. "Yay, Toby! Great job!" Toby beamed with happiness. They took turns back and forth, building higher and higher, watching the timer tick happily along. When the final chime rang out, the tower was taller than ever, built by two cooperative friends. Daddy wrapped his arms around both of them. "I am so proud of how nicely you shared and took turns. You are such wonderful friends!" Bella hugged Toby, feeling so happy that she shared her special blocks.

stories.title: Leo's Cozy Dinosaur Safari
stories.text: Leo was going on a big dinosaur safari across the bedroom floor. His favorite green T-Rex stomped through the jungle of pillows, letting out a loud ROAR! Leo loved his dinosaur so much that he squeezed it close to his chest. Soon, his cousin Maya wandered over, holding a fuzzy stuffed monkey. Maya looked at the green T-Rex and made a happy monkey sound. OOK-OOK! "Can I play with the dinosaur too, Leo?" she asked nicely. Leo hesitated. He wanted the T-Rex to go on every single adventure today. Grandma walked over with a calm, loving smile and knelt down on the rug. "It is wonderful to play with our favorite toys, Leo. But sharing makes playtime twice as fun! Let's use our special helper, the Sharing Timer, so everyone gets a turn to go on a safari." Leo liked the sound of that. Grandma showed him the little blue timer with a smiling star on the front. She turned the dial, and it began its gentle ticking sound. Tick-tock, tick-tock, went the timer. Leo let the T-Rex stomp across one more pillow mountain. Then, the timer gave a cheerful little chime. RING-RING! "Okay, Maya, it's your turn to take the T-Rex on safari!" Leo said, passing the green dinosaur to her with a kind smile. Maya's eyes lit up with excitement. She took the T-Rex and made it stomp on a pillow island, roaring gently. Leo waited patiently, watching the timer tick away the minutes with his monkey friend. When the timer chimed again, Maya handed the T-Rex right back to Leo, just like they practiced. "Thank you for sharing, Maya!" Leo said happily, taking his dinosaur back for another journey. Grandma clapped her hands. "Look at you two! You share so patiently and kindly. You are superstar sharers!" Leo gave Maya a big high-five, feeling warm and proud inside as they continued their fun safari together.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Fire Truck
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy sat on the warm playroom rug. In his hands, he held the most magnificent toy in the whole wide world: a bright red fire truck. It had shiny silver wheels that spun so fast and a little yellow ladder that went up and down. Vroom, vroom went Sammy, pushing it across the fluffy carpet. Just then, his sweet friend Maya toddled over. Her big brown eyes looked right at the fire truck, and she said softly, 'My turn, Sammy?' Sammy hugged the truck a little closer. His tummy felt tight, like a little knot. Sharing is sometimes very hard for a little boy. Mommy walked over and kneeled down softly. She gave Sammy a gentle hug. 'It is hard to wait, isn't it, Sammy? But remember our magical friend, the Sharing Timer?' Sammy nodded. He loved the Sharing Timer. It was bright yellow and looked like a happy little duck. Mommy set the timer for two minutes and pressed the big button. 'Beep-boop!' said the timer. 'When the bell rings, it is Maya's turn to drive the fire truck.' Sammy watched the little red hand tick away. Tick-tock, tick-tock. While he waited, he counted the buttons on his shirt. One, two, three, four! Before he knew it, the timer sang out, 'Ding-dong!' Sammy smiled a big, proud smile. He gently passed the red fire truck to Maya. 'Here you go, Maya!' Maya clapped her hands with glee and zoomed the truck around. Sammy felt a warm, happy glow in his heart. Waiting was tricky, but sharing made playtime twice as fun. When Maya's turn was done, the bell rang again, and the fire truck rolled right back into Sammy's happy hands.

stories.title: Leo and the Magical Purple Crayon
stories.text: At the little yellow table in the sunny kitchen, Leo was having the best time making art. He held a thick, chunky purple crayon and drew a giant, wiggly dinosaur on a big piece of paper. Roar! went Leo, coloring the dinosaur's tummy with lovely purple swirls. His baby sister, Lily, walked by wobbling on her little feet. She pointed a chubby finger at the crayon and let out a happy giggle. 'Pewple!' she said. Leo loved his purple crayon. It was his absolute favorite color for drawing grapes and octopus tentacles. He did not want to let go. But Daddy knelt down beside him with a warm, loving smile. 'Leo, sharing means everyone gets a turn to make beautiful art. Shall we ask our friendly Sharing Timer to help?' Leo thought for a moment and then nodded bravely. Daddy brought over the little blue timer shaped like a friendly whale. Click! Daddy set it for a special turn. 'Let's watch the timer together, Leo,' Daddy said softly. Leo took a deep breath in and blew it out slowly, just like cooling down hot soup. He watched the whale's eye blink. One minute, two minutes. To pass the time, Leo pretended his fingers were dancing spiders on the table. Tap, tap, tap! Suddenly, the whale timer let out a cheerful 'Trum-peta!' sound. Leo beamed with pride. He opened his hand and handed the purple crayon to Lily. 'Your turn, Lily,' he said gently. Lily squealed with joy and drew a little purple squiggle on her paper. Leo felt so proud inside. Sharing was an adventure, and he was getting better at it every single day. Soon, the timer chimed again, and the crayon came back to Leo for more fun drawing.

stories.title: Zoe and the Bouncing Ball
stories.text: Out in the green backyard, the grass was tickly and the sky was as blue as robin's eggs. Zoe was holding a big, bouncy rubber ball with colorful polka dots. Boing, boing, boing went the ball as Zoe threw it down and caught it in her small hands. She laughed a bubbly laugh. Her cousin Toby came running over, his cheeks pink and rosy. 'Can I bounce the ball, Zoe?' he asked eagerly. Zoe squeezed the ball tight against her floral shirt. She liked playing with her ball all by herself. A tiny frown touched her forehead. Grandma walked over, spreading a cozy picnic blanket on the grass. She sat down and patted the soft spot next to her. 'It is okay to love your toys, Zoe,' Grandma said in her sweetest voice. 'And it is also wonderful to share. Let's use our little green apple Sharing Timer to make it fair and fun for everyone.' Grandma wound up the apple timer, and it made a happy clicking sound. 'Tick-tick-tick goes the apple,' Grandma whispered. 'When it rings, Toby gets to bounce, and you get to rest your hands.' Zoe watched the green stem of the apple timer. She pretended she was a sleeping kittycat resting in the sun. Meow. One, two, three moments passed. Then, the apple timer gave a sweet little 'Ding!' chime. Zoe opened her arms and rolled the polka-dot ball across the grass to Toby. 'Go get it, Toby!' she called out happily. Toby chased the ball and bounced it high into the air, shouting, 'Wheee!' Zoe smiled from ear to ear. Waiting was a breeze when you knew your turn was coming right back. When the timer sang again, the ball rolled back to Zoe, and they both clapped with joy.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Firetruck
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy yellow room, lived a little boy named Sammy. Sammy loved cars, but his absolute favorite was a big, shiny red firetruck. It had a long ladder that went up and down and wheels that spun so fast. One sunny morning, his good friend Maya came over to play. Maya looked at the firetruck and her eyes grew very big and bright. 'Can I play with the firetruck too, Sammy?' she asked softly. Sammy held the firetruck a little tighter. He loved his firetruck very much and wasn't sure he wanted to let go just yet. His mommy came over with a warm, gentle smile and a bright blue timer that went tick-tock. 'Let's use the sharing timer,' Mommy said kindly. 'When we hear the friendly beep, it is time for the next friend to have a turn.' Mommy set the timer for a few minutes and handed the shiny firetruck to Maya. Sammy felt a little flutter in his tummy, but Mommy held his hand and whispered, 'Waiting is just a little pause before your next turn.' Sammy watched Maya roll the firetruck across the soft carpet. Vroom, vroom went Maya. She made happy engine noises that made Sammy giggle. He practiced taking big, deep breaths in like smelling a flower and blowing out like blowing out a birthday candle. Suddenly, the timer went off with a cheerful beep-beep-beep! Maya smiled sweetly and handed the firetruck right back to Sammy. 'Thank you for sharing, Maya!' said Sammy happily. Sammy discovered that sharing wasn't losing his favorite toy at all; it was making playtime so much more fun with a friend. He felt so proud of his patient heart.

stories.title: Leo and the Magical Paintbrushes
stories.text: High up on a little stool in the bright blue kitchen, little Leo was painting a picture. He had a big brush and lots of gorgeous, colorful paints: yellow like the sun, blue like the sky, and green like the grass. His sister Lily sat right beside him, looking at the sparkly paints with wonder. 'Can I use the blue paint now, Leo?' Lily asked, holding up her own clean paper. Leo frowned just a little bit. He was right in the middle of painting a giant ocean and needed the blue paint for the waves. Daddy knelt down beside them with a kind, reassuring hug and a cheerful kitchen timer shaped like a smiling green frog. 'Sharing can feel tricky sometimes, Leo, but our little frog friend is here to help,' Daddy said gently. 'Let’s use the sharing timer so everyone gets a turn with the blue paint.' Daddy wound up the frog timer, and it started to tick softly. Leo handed the blue paint to Lily. While Lily painted a wonderful blue whale on her paper, Leo worked on painting a bright yellow sun in the sky. He counted the clouds and practiced waiting patiently, breathing in and out. Ring-ring went the friendly frog timer! It was time to switch. Lily smiled and passed the blue paint right back to her big brother. 'My turn!' said Leo with a joyful grin. He used the blue paint to finish the sparkly ocean waves. Leo learned that sharing helped both him and his sister create a wonderful masterpiece together. He gave himself a big pat on the back for being such a wonderful, sharing brother.

stories.title: Mia and the Dinosaur Parade
stories.text: Down in the soft play corner of the sunny playroom, little Mia was building a magnificent dinosaur park. She had a green stegosaurus, a tall brachiosaurus, and her very best friend, a roaring T-Rex. Her friend Noah walked over, looking at the mighty T-Rex with enormous excitement. 'Roar! Can I play with the T-Rex, please, Mia?' asked Noah. Mia loved her T-Rex because it could stomp the loudest. She hugged the toy close for a second, wondering what to do. Grandma walked over with a basket of toys and a bright yellow egg timer that looked just like a duck. 'Let’s share our dinosaur friends using the duck timer,' Grandma suggested with a loving pat on Mia's head. 'When the duck quacks with a beep, we trade our toys so everyone plays.' Grandma turned the duck timer, and it made a gentle tick-tock sound. Mia handed the roaring T-Rex to Noah. Noah made the T-Rex stomp softly over the pillows. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Mia watched and giggled at the funny dinosaur dance. While she waited for her turn, she played with the green stegosaurus, making it munch on imaginary leaves. She took calm breaths and felt very proud of how well she was waiting. Suddenly, the duck timer gave a happy little beep! Noah turned around with a big, bright smile and handed the T-Rex right back to Mia. 'Your turn, Mia!' said Noah. 'Thank you, Noah!' Mia beamed, taking her dinosaur back. Mia felt so warm and happy inside, knowing that sharing made playtime twice as fun and filled the room with giggles and joy.

stories.title: Sammy and the Shiny Red Car
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy sat on the warm living room rug. In his hands, he held the shiniest, fastest red toy car in the whole wide world. Vroom, vroom! It zoomed across the green carpet hills. Just then, his sweet friend Maya walked over. Her big brown eyes looked right at the red car. She used her gentle voice and asked, 'Can I have a turn with the fast car, please, Sammy?' Sammy felt a little tiny bubble of worry in his tummy. He loved his red car so much! But Mommy was right there with a bright yellow smile. She held up a special helper called the Sharing Timer. 'Let us make magic,' Mommy whispered. 'We can set the timer for a fun turn, and everyone gets a happy playtime.' Sammy nodded and gently handed the car to Maya. Beep, beep! The little timer started to tick, tick, tick. Sammy took deep breaths in like smelling a flower, and out like blowing a birthday candle. One, two, three! While Maya played, Sammy looked around and found a bouncy blue ball. Bounce, bounce, catch! He had so much fun with the ball. Suddenly, the timer made a happy little sound. Ring-ding-ding! It was time for Sammy to hold the red car again. Maya smiled and passed the car back with care. Sammy felt so proud and happy inside. Sharing made playtime twice as fun! Mommy gave Sammy and Maya the biggest, warmest hugs. They giggled together and kept on playing happily.

stories.title: Leo and the Purple Paintbrush
stories.text: The art table was all set up with big white papers and bright, wonderful colors. Leo dipped his brush into the jar of sparkly purple paint. Swish, swish, swish! He painted a giant purple star right in the middle of his paper. Right next to him, his little sister Lily pointed at the purple brush. 'Purple, please!' she cheered. Leo liked having the brush all to himself. He hugged his paper a little closer. Daddy knelt down beside them and spoke in a soft, soothing voice. 'Leo, sharing can feel tricky, but you are so big and kind. Let us use our friendly Sharing Timer.' Daddy set the cute little green frog timer on the table. Ribbit, ribbit! The timer started its gentle countdown. Leo shared the purple paintbrush with Lily. Together, they painted purple polka dots all over. Leo counted the dots out loud. 'One, two, three dots!'
