Take a breath and blow it out,
Give a tiny happy shout.
Watch the smoke dance in the air,
Floating gently up the stair.

Candle is asleep and done,
Waiting for the morning sun.
Pull the blankets up so tight,
Sleep well, baby, sleep all night.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Star
rhymes.text:
The day is done and night is near,
Time to rest, my toddler dear.
We brush our teeth and wash our face,
Ready for a cozy place.

On the table stands so tall,
A little candle, red and small.
Watch it flicker, watch it glow,
Dancing softly to and fro.

Now take a breath, deep and wide,
With your family by your side.
Puff your cheeks out, nice and big,
Like a happy little pig.

Blow it out, hip, hip, hooray!
Darkness takes the light away.
Sweet dreams now until the morn,
Sleep tight, little unicorn.

rhymes.title: Make a Wish and Blow
rhymes.text:
Birthday party, cake is here,
Singing loud and full of cheer.
One more year you've grown so sweet,
Time to taste this yummy treat.

See the candle burning bright,
Shining with a golden light.
Make a wish inside your head,
Sitting cozy on the bed.

Take a breath and count to three,
One, two, three, as bold as can be!
Blow the flame right out of sight,
Make the room go dark and night.

Clap your hands and shout aloud,
Make your family very proud.
Eat the cake and lick the plate,
Growing up is truly great.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Flame
rhymes.text:
Evening time is coming fast,
Playing games is done at last.
Time to cuddle, time to rest,
Snuggling is the very best.

Light a candle on the shelf,
Little flame, you cute little elf.
Glow so yellow, glow so red,
As we get prepared for bed.

Are you ready? Take a cue,
Here is what you have to do.
Pout your lips and blow a breeze,
Off to dreamland, if you please.

Whoosh! The smoke goes up so high,
Reaching all the velvet sky.
Now the room is dark and deep,
Time for babies fast asleep.

rhymes.title: Puff, Puff, Puff!
rhymes.text:
Wash your hands and change your clothes,
Wiggle fingers, touch your nose.
Quiet moments now are here,
Whispering so soft and near.

There's a candle in a cup,
Let us all go looking up.
Orange wick is burning high,
Like a little star nearby.

Blow it gently, do not shout,
Help the flame to sputter out.
Take some air into your chest,
Giving those big lungs a test.

One big puff and it is done,
Wasn't that so much fun?
Nighty-night, sleep safe and sound,
While the quiet world goes round.

rhymes.title: Goodnight, Little Candle
rhymes.text:
Shadows dance upon the wall,
Some are big and some are small.
Jumping up to say goodnight,
To the cozy candle light.

It has burned the whole day through,
Working hard for me and you.
Now it's time to dim the glow,
Ready, steady, here we go.

Wrap your arms around your bear,
Climb up on the rocking chair.
Blow a kiss and blow a breeze,
Make that candle freeze, oh please!

Smoke is dancing in the air,
Peace is resting everywhere.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Waiting for another day.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Star
rhymes.text:
The day is done and night is near,
Time to rest, my toddler dear.
We brush our teeth and wash our face,
Ready for a cozy place.

On the cake there is a light,
Glowing soft and shining bright.
Time to blow the flame away,
And say goodnight to all the play.

Take a breath and puff real wide,
See the spark go down and hide.
Blow it out, one, two, and three,
Now you're snuggled safe and free.

Sweet little dreams for you and me,
As happy as a sleepy bee.
The room is dark, the stars are high,
Whispering a lullaby.

rhymes.title: The Magic Flame
rhymes.text:
Look at the candle, tall and red,
Right beside the cozy bed.
It flickers high, it dances low,
Watch the pretty orange glow.

Now the bath is clean and warm,
Safe and snug from any storm.
Pajamas on, we're ready now,
To take a bow and say chow-ciao.

Gather close and count to four,
We don't need the light no more.
Puff your cheeks out round and fat,
Blow it out, just like that!

Smoke goes drifting up so high,
Off to wander in the sky.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Until the dawning of the day.

rhymes.title: Puff, Puff, Little Spark
rhymes.text:
The house is quiet, day is through,
There is a little task to do.
A tiny candle starts to burn,
Let us take our sleepy turn.

Softly blow so gently now,
Make a little gentle bow.
Watch the flame go dancing round,
Without making any sound.

Take some air inside your chest,
Time for bed and time for rest.
Puff it out with all your might,
And kiss the tiny flame goodnight.

Darkness falls upon the floor,
We do not need the candle more.
Sleepy head upon the bed,
Rest your little tired head.

rhymes.title: Blow It Out, My Sweet
rhymes.text:
Evening shadows start to creep,
Time for little ones to sleep.
We had fun the whole day through,
Now there is one thing to do.

See the candle burning bright,
Bringing us a lovely light.
Time to make the bedroom dark,
And say goodbye to every spark.

Make your mouth an oval O,
Make the little breezes blow.
Puff again and watch it die,
Wave a happy sweet goodbye.

Blankets pulled up to your chin,
Let the quiet dreams begin.
Sleep until the morning sun,
Because your sleepy day is done.

rhymes.title: The Birthday Bedtime
rhymes.text:
Every day is special too,
With so many things to do.
Now we turn the lights down low,
Watch the final candle glow.

It is time to clear the mind,
Leaving all the toys behind.
Take a breath and hold it in,
Let the slumber time begin.

One big puff and off it goes,
Right beneath your little nose.
Poof! The shiny fire is out,
No more need to run about.

Snuggle down and hug your bear,
Love is waiting everywhere.
Rest your eyes and go to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Star
rhymes.text:
The stars are shining in the sky,
The sleepy moon is floating high.
It is time to go to sleep,
Do not make a single peep.

We wash our face and brush our hair,
We put away each little bear.
We turn off every glowing light,
And softly say a sweet goodnight.

Look upon the glowing wick,
Little flame is dancing quick.
Take a breath and count to three,
Blow it out so bright and free!

Whoosh goes the wind, away it goes,
Right down to your little toes.
The room is dark, the room is still,
Sleepy dreams your eyes will fill.

rhymes.title: Make a Wish
rhymes.text:
Happy birthday, time for cake!
Look at all the friends we make.
Yellow candles in a row,
Watch them flicker, watch them glow.

Take a breath and puff your chest,
Blow them hard and do your best.
Make a wish for something fun,
Smile at everyone you've won.

First you clap your little hands,
Dancing through the party lands.
Take a deep and steady breath,
Blow it out and cause no death.

Smoke goes curling up so high,
Reaching for the cotton sky.
Everybody shout hooray!
That was quite a happy day.

rhymes.title: The Sweet Nightlight
rhymes.text:
When the sun goes down to rest,
And birds are sleeping in their nest,
We light a candle big and bright,
To chase away the spooky night.

It flickers red, it flickers gold,
A cozy story to be told.
We watch it dance upon the wall,
So very pretty, short and tall.

Now the story time is done,
We had so much quiet fun.
Time to rest your sleepy head,
And snuggle nicely in your bed.

Puff your cheeks and blow it out,
No more need to run about.
Darkness comes with quiet grace,
Sleep is on your happy face.

rhymes.title: Spooky Ghostly Glow
rhymes.text:
On a cozy autumn night,
Pumpkin faces glowing bright.
Carved with smiles and spooky eyes,
Looking like a sweet surprise.

Inside sits a candle tall,
Casting shadows on the wall.
We can wave and we can shout,
See the little flame pop out.

Pucker up and take your breath,
Blowing hard to wake up Seth.
Blow it out with all your might,
Say goodbye to candlelight.

Now the pumpkin goes to sleep,
No more noises left to keep.
Dreams are waiting in the dark,
Like a happy little spark.

rhymes.title: The Magic Spark
rhymes.text:
Little wick of yellow wax,
No more playtime, time to relax.
Strike a match with mom and dad,
See the happy glow we had.

Flame is dancing left and right,
Making everything feel right.
Warm and gentle, soft and sweet,
Sitting nicely on our seat.

Soon the wax begins to melt,
Bestest feeling ever felt.
Time to end our little game,
Say goodbye to little flame.

Blow a gentle breeze so grand,
Blowing magic through the land.
Smoke is rising to the air,
Peace and quiet everywhere.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed
rhymes.text:
The day is done and night is here,
We rest our heads, my little dear.
The tiny flame glows bright and tall,
It casts soft shadows on the wall.
Now pucker up and take a breath,
And blow it out, there is no death.
We count to three and then we blow,
To watch the little fire go.
One, two, three, let's give a puff,
The room is dark and cool enough.
The smoke goes dancing in the air,
Without a single hue of care.
The candle sleeps upon the tray,
Until the dawning of the day.
Goodnight to stars so high above,
We drift to sleep wrapped up in love.

rhymes.title: Make a Wish
rhymes.text:
A yellow flame upon the wick,
We light it fast and make it quick.
It dances up, it dances down,
The happiest light in all the town.
Now close your eyes and wish a dream,
As sweet as any ice cream stream.
Take a breath so deep and grand,
The biggest breath in all the land.
Blow hard and strong with all your might,
And put away the glowing light.
The wobbly smoke goes up so high,
Way up into the starry sky.
The party's done, the room is still,
The quiet night comes down the hill.
Goodnight sweet flame, sleep tight and deep,
While little babies go to sleep.

rhymes.title: The Little Flame
rhymes.text:
See the little orange tongue,
Singing out a bedtime song.
Waving gently left and right,
Keeping all the dark the night.
Now it is time to say goodbye,
While sleepy owls go flying by.
Bring your mouth up close and sweet,
To make the bedtime routine complete.
Take a breath and puff it out,
With a happy little shout.
Puff, puff, puff, the flame is gone,
Now the stars are shining on.
Feel the quiet in the room,
Chasing off the nighttime gloom.
Snuggle down into your bed,
With a pillow for your head.

rhymes.title: Puff and Sleep
rhymes.text:
The red wax candle stands so tall,
Its lovely light can reach us all.
It flickers in the evening breeze,
As soft as leaves upon the trees.
Now fold your hands and rest your head,
It's time to snuggle in your bed.
We have to put the fire to sleep,
Before the shadows start to creep.
Take a breath and blow it out,
There is no need to cry or pout.
Watch the smoke curl round and round,
Falling softly to the ground.
The little wick is black and cool,
Like a quiet woodland pool.
Now close your eyes and dream away,
Until the morning brings the day.

rhymes.title: Sweet Dreams
rhymes.text:
A glowing spark upon the stand,
The coziest light in all the land.
It burns so bright, it burns so clear,
To show that bedtime now is here.
Let's count together, you and I,
As time goes drifting softly by.
One and two and three and four,
We do not need the candle more.
Take a breath and blow so strong,
To finish up our sleepy song.
Puff it out and make it dark,
No more glowing little spark.
The room is safe, the room is warm,
Protected from any little storm.
Now sleep until the morning sun,
Because your sleepy day is done.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Star
rhymes.text:
The day is done, the stars are bright,
We get ready for the night.
Wash your hands and brush your teeth,
Time to sleep and find sweet peace.

Look up high, a little spark,
Burning softly in the dark.
A cozy glow of yellow light,
Everything is calm and bright.

Now we take a breath so deep,
Before we cuddle up to sleep.
Ready, steady, count to three,
Blowing wind is blowing free!

Puff, puff, puff, go on and blow!
Watch the little fire go.
Now the room is dark and still,
Sleepy dreams upon the hill.

rhymes.title: Happy Birthday Wish
rhymes.text:
A yummy cake with frosting sweet,
Such a special, tasty treat!
Candles standing in a row,
Ready now for us to blow.

One bright flame for growing tall,
We love you so much, big and small.
Clap your hands and sing the song,
Everybody sing along!

Take a breath and fill your chest,
Time to put your might to test.
Pucker up and make it grand,
Bestest birthday in the land!

Whoosh! The smoke goes up so high,
Reaching all the way to sky.
Make a wish and clap your hands,
Happiest in all the lands.

rhymes.title: The Sleepy Little Flame
rhymes.text:
Evening time is coming fast,
Busy playtime days have passed.
Snuggle in your cozy chair,
Softly brush your tangled hair.

On the table sits a light,
Glowing warmly in the night.
Red and orange, flickering bright,
Giving us a lovely sight.

Little finger, touch your nose,
From your head down to your toes.
Take a breath, a mighty breeze,
Blow it out now, if you please!

Puff goes wind and out it goes,
Now the sleepy night wind blows.h
Blanket hugs and pillow rest,
Sleeping is what babies do best.

rhymes.title: Make a Wish and Blow
rhymes.text:
Twinkle, twinkle, little wick,
Burning down so nice and quick.
Golden wax and yellow flame,
Everybody knows its name.

Time to finish up our play,
Say goodbye to active day.
Close your eyes and make a wish,
Sweet as honey in a dish.

Lips out round just like a O,
Now it is your turn to blow!
Take a breath and let it out,
Hear the happy cheering shout.

Poof! The light has gone away,
Saved until another day.
Moonbeams dancing on the floor,
Sleepy time is here once more.

rhymes.title: Puff, Puff, Puff!
rhymes.text:
Dinner's eaten, toys put down,
No more running all around.
Pajamas on, so soft and neat,
Resting every little feet.

There's a candle burning low,
Watch the little shadows grow.
Dancing wildly on the wall,
Big and short and very tall.

Time to send it off to sleep,
While the quiet shadows creep.
Ready hands upon your knee,
Blow as hard as you can see!

Whoosh! The smoke begins to curl,
Every happy boy and girl.
Into bed and tucked up tight,
Saying everybody goodnight.

rhymes.title: Time for Bed, Little Star
rhymes.text:
The day is done and night is near,
Time to rest your little ear.
We had so much fun today,
Now we put away our play.

Look up at the glowing light,
Shining softly in the night.
Time to say goodnight, sweet dear,
Is the sleepy time right here?

Take a breath so deep and grand,
Breathe it out across the land.
Blow the flame and watch it go,
Make the little flicker low.

Puff and puff with all your might,
Blow it out and dim the light.
Now the room is dark and deep,
Time to fall right fast asleep.

rhymes.title: The Birthday Glow
rhymes.text:
Happy birthday, look and see,
One more year for joyful glee!
Cake is frosted, sweet and bright,
Glowing with a yellow light.

See the candle standing tall,
Waiting for a breath and call.
Are you ready? Count to three,
Then you blow it wild and free.

Take a breath into your chest,
Blow it out and do your best.
Puff and blow the flame away,
Clapping hands for happy day!

Smoke is floating in the air,
Smiles are shining everywhere.
Make a wish up to the blue,
All your dreams are coming true.

rhymes.title: Soft and Cozy Night
rhymes.text:
Bath is done and pajamas on,
Waiting for the early dawn.
Candle flickers in the room,
Chasing off the sleepy gloom.

Sit right down upon my knee,
Quiet as a honeybee.
Watch the flame dance up and down,
Wearing such a pretty crown.

Can you make a windy breeze,
 Blowing gently through the trees?
Round your lips and push the air,
Send it floating through the hair.

Puff! The flame begins to drop,
Now it's gone and made a stop.
Peaceful night and cozy bed,
Resting now your sleepy head.

rhymes.title: The Magic Puff
rhymes.text:
Magic candle, burning bright,
Give us just a little light.
Dancing on the table top,
When will it begin to stop?

Time to put the fire to bed,
Rest the weary little head.
Magic breath is waiting here,
Blow it out, my tiny dear.

Deep breath in and hold it tight,
Make the wind blow with your might.
One big puff and watch it fly,
Up into the evening sky.

There it goes, the smoke so gray,
Blowing all the dark away.
Now we whisper soft and low,
Sweet dreams in the candle glow.

rhymes.title: Goodnight Little Flame
rhymes.text:
Sun is hiding, moon is out,
No more running all about.
Candle burns a steady flame,
Calling out our sleepy name.

Come and gather close and near,
Sing a song of cozy cheer.
Watch the yellow fire swing,
Like a happy little king.

Lips are ready for the test,
Blowing air will work the best.
Puff your cheeks out round and wide,
Push the wind from deep inside.

Whoosh! It vanishes from sight,
Leaving only starry night.
Snuggle down and close your eyes,
Till the morning sun arise.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Once upon a time, there was a little lion named Leo. Leo loved to roar. He roared when he woke up in the morning. Good morning, sun! He roared when he ate his breakfast. Crunch, crunch, yum! But sometimes, Leo forgot how to use his gentle talking voice inside the cozy house. When Leo wanted his favorite red truck, he would let out a huge, loud lion roar. ROAR! His mama gently covered her furry ears and smiled a soft, loving smile. Mama said, 'Leo, my sweet cub, your roar is big and strong. But inside our house, we use our gentle talking voice so our ears feel happy and calm. Can you try your talking voice to ask for the truck?' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He took a tiny breath and made a soft, happy sound. 'Truck, please, Mama,' he whispered. Mama clapped her paws together with joy. 'Yes! That is your wonderful talking voice! Such sweet music to my ears.' Leo felt so proud inside. He used his talking voice to ask for his banana. He used his talking voice to ask for his blue blanket. Using his talking voice made Leo feel like a big, clever boy. When it was time to play with his blocks, Leo kept his voice soft and nice. His block tower grew tall and high, reaching all the way up to the clouds. 'Look at my tower!' he said with his gentle voice. Mama hugged him tight and whispered, 'I love hearing your talking voice, Leo.' Leo smiled and hugged her back. He knew that big roars were fun outside in the bright sunshine, but inside the house, his talking voice was the best way to share his happy thoughts with the people he loved.

stories.title: Mia Asks for Help
stories.text: Little Mia was having a wonderful morning playing with her shiny yellow puzzle. Piece by piece, the puzzle came together. A duck here, a cow there. But oh no! The very last piece, a fluffy little sheep, was stuck underneath the heavy wooden table. Mia wanted her sheep right now. Her little tummy felt tight, and she started to squeeze her eyes shut. She felt a big, loud scream bubbling up inside her throat. A scream was ready to pop right out! Just then, her teacher, Miss Sarah, knelt down beside her on the soft playroom rug. Miss Sarah had a warm, gentle smile. She softly touched Mia’s hand and said, 'Mia, I see you are feeling frustrated. Take a deep, slow breath with me.' Mia breathed in the sweet air and breathed it out. 'Ahhh.' Miss Sarah continued, 'When we need help, we don't need to scream. We can use our lovely talking voice. Let’s try it together.' Mia nodded her head. She opened her mouth and used her sweet, clear talking voice. 'Help, please, Miss Sarah,' she said. Miss Sarah's face lit up like the morning sun. 'What a beautiful talking voice! I would love to help you.' Miss Sarah reached under the table and gently pulled out the fluffy sheep piece. She handed it right to Mia. Mia giggled with delight and pushed the sheep into its special spot. The puzzle was all done! Mia clapped her hands together. She felt so happy that she used her words. Using her talking voice made everything so much easier and friendlier. She looked at Miss Sarah and said, 'Thank you!' Miss Sarah beamed and gave her a gentle pat on the head. Mia smiled brightly, knowing her talking voice was a powerful magic key that opened every door.

stories.title: Pip's Playground Words
stories.text: Pip the bunny loved the playground more than anything in the whole wide world. The bright red slide was his favorite. Today, Pip scampered up the ladder, his little paws going patter-patter-patter. He wanted to go down the slide right away. But wait! His friend Toby the turtle was sitting right at the top, tying his colorful shoelace. Pip stood behind Toby and wanted to shout, 'Move out of my way!' But Pip remembered the special rule. We use our talking voice! Instead of yelling a loud, bossy bunny sound, Pip took a gentle step closer. He tapped Toby softly on his green shell. Toby turned around with a friendly blink. Pip used his sweetest, clearest talking voice and said, 'Excuse me, Toby. Can I please go down the slide when you are all done?' Toby looked down at his shoes, finished the last little loop, and gave a happy nod. 'All done, Pip! You can go now!' Toby said with a sunny smile. Pip's long ears wiggle-waggled with happiness. 'Thank you, Toby!' Pip said in his friendly talking voice. Pip slid all the way down the slide. Wheee! He landed on the soft wood chips with a joyful giggle. He jumped right up and ran back to his friends. Whenever Pip wanted to play with a shiny red ball, or ask for a turn on the big green swing, he always used his wonderful talking voice. All the animals on the playground smiled whenever Pip spoke, because his voice sounded like a happy bird singing in the trees. Pip felt so cozy and warm inside, knowing that using his talking voice made playing with his friends so much fun.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo woke up ready for a big day of play. He jumped out of bed and shouted, 'Good morning, sun!' His voice bounced off the walls and made a loud BOOM sound. Mommy covered her ears with a giggly smile and said, 'Good morning, Leo! But remember, inside we use our gentle talking voice so we don't hurt our ears.' Leo nodded and tried again. 'Good morning, sun,' he whispered softly, like a little mouse. 'That is a wonderful talking voice!' cheered Mommy. After breakfast, Leo wanted to play with his favorite toy dinosaur, Rex. Rex was green with big, sharp-looking teeth, but he was very friendly. Leo wanted Rex to roar, so Leo roared super loud, 'ROAR! I am a big T-Rex!' The room felt very noisy. Daddy walked over and gently knelt down. 'Leo, when we play inside, a big roar can be a bit too loud for our cozy living room. Can you use your talking voice to make Rex talk?' Leo thought for a moment. He hugged Rex close and made a soft, rumbling sound. 'Hello, I am Rex,' Leo said in his normal, happy voice. Rex nodded happily in Leo's hands. Next, it was time to go to the park. Outside under the big blue sky, Daddy said, 'Guess what, Leo? Outside is a wonderful place for big voices!' Leo took a deep breath and shouted, 'Yay, the park!' as loud as he could. It was so much fun to let his voice fly up to the clouds. When it was time to go home, Leo practiced lowering his volume again. He knew just when to use his quiet talking voice inside, and when to use his big voice outside. Mommy and Daddy gave him a huge hug and said, 'We are so proud of you for using your wonderful talking voice everywhere you go!'

stories.title: Mia Asks for Help
stories.text: Mia was building a tall, wobbly tower out of bright red and yellow blocks. She stacked one block, then two, then three! The tower was getting taller than her knees. Mia wanted to put the very last blue block right on the top, but her hand was just a little too short to reach. Oh no! Mia felt a tiny bubble of frustration in her tummy. She wanted to let out a big grumpy grunt and squeeze her eyes shut. Instead, Mia took a nice, deep breath, just like her teacher taught her at preschool. She turned around to see Grandma sitting nearby in the comfy armchair, knitting a soft pink scarf. Grandma looked up with a kind, loving smile. Mia opened her mouth and used her sweet talking voice. 'Grandma, please help me?' she asked clearly. Grandma put down her knitting needles right away and walked over. 'I would love to help you, Mia,' Grandma said warmly. Together, they gently placed the blue block right on top of the tower. It did not fall down at all! It stayed balanced and looked just like a castle turret. Mia clapped her hands together with joy and shouted a happy yay, remembering to use her outdoor voice for just a second of excitement, before giggling softly. Grandma patted Mia's soft curls and said, 'Using your clear talking voice is such a wonderful way to ask for help, sweetheart. I heard you right away because you spoke so nicely.' Mia felt so proud and happy inside her heart. She knew that whenever she needed a hand, her talking voice was a magical key that opened up help from the people who loved her. She gave Grandma a big, warm hug, ready for her next fun block adventure.

stories.title: Sam's Snack Time Choice
stories.text: It was snack time in the bright yellow kitchen. Sam sat in his little wooden chair, waiting very patiently. On the counter sat a plate of yummy apple slices and a shiny banana. Sam was very hungry, and his tummy let out a little rumble: rumbly-rumble-rum! Sam wanted his snack right this very second. Sometimes, when Sam was excited and hungry, he would make squeaky noises or point and whine. But today, Sam remembered a special trick. He sat up tall, put his hands in his lap, and cleared his throat gently. He looked right at his big brother, Toby, who was helping pour the cups of water. Sam used his best, clearest talking voice. 'Toby, may I please have some apple slices?' he asked politely. Toby turned around with a big, surprised smile. 'Wow, Sam! I heard you loud and clear because you used your nice talking voice,' Toby said happily. Toby picked up a crisp, sweet apple slice and handed it over on a little blue plate. 'Thank you, Toby,' Sam said, keeping his voice gentle and sweet. Sam took a big, crunchy bite of his apple. Crunch, crunch, crunch! It tasted so delicious and sweet. When he finished, he wanted a sip of water. Instead of just grabbing the cup, Sam remembered again. 'Water, please,' he said in his friendly talking voice. Mommy walked into the kitchen and winked at him. 'I love hearing you use your wonderful talking words, Sam,' she praised. Sam beamed with a big smile. Using his talking voice made everyone happy, and getting his favorite snack was the best reward of all. He finished his snack with a happy hum, ready to play with his blocks.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Leo loved the library. It was a big room filled with towering shelves of books with shiny covers and colorful pictures. Today, Leo found a book about big blue whales. He was so excited that he wanted to tell his dad all about it right now! Leo opened his mouth and took a deep breath, ready to shout, "Dad, look at the giant whale!" But then, Leo stopped. He remembered the special library rule. The library was a quiet place where people liked to read peaceful stories. If Leo used his loud outside voice, it might scare the quiet reading time away. Dad knelt down next to Leo and gave him a warm, gentle smile. "Remember our library game, Leo?" Dad whispered softly. "Let's use our special talking voice. It is soft like a gentle breeze rustling the leaves." Leo nodded. He closed his mouth, took another breath, and tried again. This time, he made his voice smooth and quiet. "Dad, look at the giant whale," Leo whispered into the air, keeping his voice just right for the cozy room. Dad beamed with pride and gave Leo a gentle high-five. "Wonderful job using your soft talking voice, Leo! You are a superstar helper." Leo felt a warm, happy bubble pop up inside his tummy. Speaking softly felt very nice indeed. He gently turned the page of the big whale book, whispering all the wonderful ocean facts to his dad. When they checked out their books, the librarian smiled warmly and gave Leo a colorful star sticker for being such a polite reader. Leo stuck the sticker proudly on his shirt, feeling so proud of his calm, quiet talking voice.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Request
stories.text: The playground was bustling with happy energy on a bright Tuesday morning. Maya stood at the bottom of the twisty red slide, watching her big friend Sam climb all the way to the very top. Maya wanted a turn on the slide more than anything in the whole wide world. At first, Maya felt a tiny rumble of frustration in her tummy. She squeezed her eyes shut and started to stomp her foot, opening her mouth to let out a loud, frustrated whine. But wait! Maya remembered what Mommy always told her at home. Whining and yelling do not help our friends understand what we need. Maya took a big, deep breath, smelling the imaginary flowers and blowing out the imaginary birthday candles. She relaxed her shoulders and looked right at Sam. Instead of using a grumpy whine, Maya used her strong, clear talking voice. "Excuse me, Sam! May I have a turn on the slide next, please?" Maya said with a bright, happy smile. Sam heard her loud and clear from the top of the slide. He waved his hand and called down, "Yes, Maya! You can go next!" Maya did a happy little dance with her feet. Using her talking voice made everything so much easier and faster. She waited patiently as Sam slid down with a happy whoosh. Then, it was Maya's turn! She climbed up the ladder, feeling so proud that she used her words instead of getting upset. When she zoomed down the slide, she laughed all the way to the bottom. Playing together was so much fun when everyone used their kind, clear talking voices.

stories.title: Oliver's Breakfast Choice
stories.text: The morning sun was shining brightly through the kitchen window, warming the cozy yellow kitchen table. Oliver sat in his booster seat, waiting for his yummy breakfast. Grandma was busy by the stove, flipping warm, fluffy pancakes on a hot griddle. Oliver was very hungry, and his tummy let out a little rumble that sounded like a happy kitten. He wanted his banana slices right now! At first, Oliver started to make grunting noises and pointed his finger angrily at the fruit bowl, crossing his arms over his chest. Grandma turned around and gently smiled. "I see a little grumpy face, Oliver, but I don't know what you need when you make grumpy sounds," Grandma said kindly. Oliver took a deep breath and unfolded his arms. He remembered to use his helpful talking voice to share his thoughts. "Grandma, please may I have some bananas on my plate?" Oliver asked, using his sweet, clear voice. Grandma’s face lit up with a big, happy grin. "Of course, my sweet boy! Thank you for using your wonderful talking voice to tell me what you need." Grandma carefully placed three bright yellow banana slices right on top of Oliver's warm pancakes. Oliver clapped his hands together with joy. Using his words felt like magic! He picked up his fork and happily ate his breakfast, knowing that talking clearly is the best way to ask for things. Grandma sat down with her own cup of tea and gave Oliver a loving forehead kiss, praising him for being such a big boy.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Leo loved the library. It was a big, quiet room filled with towering shelves of magical books with shiny covers. Today, Leo wanted to find the biggest book about dinosaurs with sharp teeth and long tails. He spotted a sparkly blue book high up on a wooden shelf. 'Look at that!' Leo shouted in his biggest, happiest outside voice. His voice bounced off the walls and echoed all the way to the ceiling. Zoom! The librarian smiled kindly and put a finger gently to her lips. 'Shh, Leo,' she whispered softly. 'In the library, we use our quiet talking voice so everyone can enjoy their reading time.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He wanted to be a good listener. He took a deep breath and practiced his gentle whisper. 'Can I have the dinosaur book, please?' he whispered to his mom. His voice sounded like a soft rustling leaf. His mom smiled and gave him a warm, cozy hug. 'What a wonderful talking voice, Leo!' she whispered back. Together, they pulled the heavy book down and sat on a soft blue rug. Leo turned the pages very carefully, pointing to the T-Rex with his tiny finger. He whispered roar sounds to himself, making sure not to disturb the other readers around them. When it was time to go home, Leo felt so proud. He learned that inside spaces like the library are special places where gentle whispers keep the peace and make reading extra cozy. As they walked out the sliding glass doors into the bright afternoon sunshine, Leo let out a happy cheer in his normal voice. But he always remembered how nice it felt to use his quiet talking voice when he wanted to share a secret or keep things peaceful indoors. The library was wonderful, and Leo was a very polite little dinosaur explorer.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Request
stories.text: The playground was bright, sunny, and full of fun. Maya stood near the big red slide, waiting her turn to zoom down. Bobby, a little boy with curly hair, was playing at the very top. He had the yellow bucket that Maya wanted to use to build a giant sandcastle in the sandbox. Maya wanted the bucket right now! Her chest felt tight, and she opened her mouth to let out a loud, frustrated whine. But then, she remembered what her teacher always said about using her words. Maya closed her mouth, took a big breath, and let her shoulders relax. Instead of grabbing or whining, she decided to use her strong, clear talking voice. She walked over to the bottom of the slide and looked right up at Bobby. 'Excuse me, Bobby,' Maya said clearly and politely. 'May I please use the yellow bucket when you are finished?' Bobby stopped and looked down. Because Maya used her nice talking voice instead of crying, Bobby understood her right away! A big, friendly smile spread across his face. 'Sure, Maya!' Bobby called back happily. He slid down the slide and handed the shiny yellow bucket right to her. Maya beamed with joy. 'Thank you, Bobby!' she said in her sweet, encouraging tone. She grabbed the bucket and ran over to the sandbox, ready to build the biggest, tallest castle ever. She felt so proud of herself for solving her problem like a big kid. Using her talking voice made everything so much easier and kept playtime fun for everyone. She even shared her red shovel with Bobby when he came over to help decorate the castle walls. It was a wonderful day at the park, full of sharing, smiling, and happy talking voices.

stories.title: Sam's Snack Time Choice
stories.text: The afternoon sun was streaming into the cozy kitchen, making little golden squares on the shiny wooden floor. Sam was sitting at his little blue table, feeling very hungry after playing blocks all morning. On the high counter, just out of reach, sat a bright red bowl filled with crunchy apple slices and sweet yellow banana chunks. Sam wanted that snack right away! Instead of pointing and making grumpy growling noises in his throat, Sam decided it was time to use his wonderful talking voice. He sat up straight in his little chair and looked right at his dad, who was washing dishes near the sink. Sam took a deep breath and spoke up clearly. 'Dad, I want a snack, please,' he said in his best growing-up voice. Dad turned around, wiped his hands on a blue towel, and smiled a big, proud smile. 'I love hearing you use your clear talking voice, Sam!' Dad said warmly. 'It helps me know exactly what you need.' Dad walked over to the counter, picked up the bright red bowl of fruit, and carefully placed it right in front of Sam on the table. Sam clapped his hands together with delight. 'Thank you, Daddy!' he said happily, his voice bubbling with excitement. He picked up his chunky red fork and happily munched on a sweet apple slice. Eating snack time was always fun, but today it felt extra special because Sam knew that using his words was the best way to communicate. Dad sat down across from him and ate a banana slice too, telling Sam a funny story about a silly monkey. Sam giggled and used his talking voice to ask questions about the monkey. It was a happy, peaceful snack time filled with love, giggles, and clear, beautiful talking words.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo went to the big, quiet library with Mommy. The library was full of tall shelves and colorful books. Leo was so excited! He found a shiny book all about zooming rockets, and he wanted to share. He took a big breath and opened his mouth to shout, 'Look, Mommy, a rocket ship!' But Mommy gently touched her lips and smiled. 'Shh, sweetie. In the library, we use our quiet talking voice so everyone can read peacefully,' Mommy whispered. Leo blinked. He wanted to respect the quiet room. 'Can I use my special whisper voice?' Leo asked softly. 'Yes, that is wonderful,' Mommy replied. Leo leaned in close to Mommy's ear. He made his voice soft and breathy, like the wind rustling through the trees. 'Look, Mommy, a rocket ship,' he whispered. Mommy beamed a big, proud smile and gave him a gentle squeeze. 'Such a good listener! You used your lovely talking voice.' Leo felt so proud inside his tummy. They sat together in a cozy yellow chair, whispering about moonbeams, stars, and brave astronauts. Using his quiet talking voice made Leo feel like a very big boy. When it was time to check out the books, the friendly librarian smiled at Leo and said, 'Thank you for keeping your voice so nice and soft today.' Leo smiled back, holding his rocket book tightly. He learned that different places have different kinds of voices, and his whisper voice was just right for magical libraries. The end.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Word
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly, and Maya was playing in the sandbox at the park. She was building a gigantic sandcastle with a very tall tower. Suddenly, her friend Sam walked over and accidentally bumped the edge of the bucket, making the tower wobble. Maya felt a hot, frustrated feeling bubble up inside her throat. She wanted to let out a loud, angry screech. But she remembered what Daddy always taught her. Instead of yelling or crying, Maya took a deep, calming breath. She puffed out her cheeks and let it out slow. Then, she used her strong, clear talking voice. 'Sam, please be careful. My castle is fragile,' Maya said calmly, looking right at him. Sam stopped and looked down. 'Oh, I am sorry, Maya!' he said kindly. 'Can I help you fix it?' Maya's face relaxed into a happy smile. 'Yes, please!' she replied in her cheerful talking voice. They worked together, packing wet sand and smoothing out the walls until the castle looked even better than before. Daddy walked over and clapped his hands gently. 'I am so proud of you, Maya. You used your talking voice to share your feelings instead of screaming. That is a wonderful way to solve a problem.' Maya felt like a sunshine beam was warming her heart. She gave Daddy a big hug and went right back to playing happily with her friend. Using her talking voice made everything so much better. The end.

stories.title: Pip the Penguin's Inside Voice
stories.text: Pip the little penguin lived in a cozy igloo with his family. Outside, the wind howled and the snow danced, but inside, it was warm and snug. Pip wanted to play with his favorite red bouncing ball. He rolled it across the floor, but it bounced right under the big green sofa. 'Oh no!' thought Pip. He wanted to throw a little tantrum and cry out loud to get his big brother's attention. But Pip paused. He shook his flippers and remembered to use his helpful talking voice. Instead of whining, Pip walked right over to his brother, tapped his arm gently, and spoke in a clear, friendly voice. 'Big Brother, my ball is stuck under the couch. Can you help me reach it, please?' Big Brother turned around with a warm, loving smile. 'Of course I can, Pip!' he chirped happily. Big Brother reached his long penguin fliptail under the sofa and scooped out the red ball, handing it right back to Pip. 'Thank you so much!' Pip said brightly, using his sweet manners. Mommy penguin waddled over and wrapped her soft wings around both of them. 'I love hearing you use your clear talking voice, Pip. It makes it so easy for us to understand what you need,' Mommy praised gently. Pip hugged his red ball close to his chest and did a happy little waddle dance. He felt so understood and so loved. Speaking up with his kind talking voice always made his day brighter. The end.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Leo the little lion loved to roar. He roared when he woke up. He roared when he ate his breakfast bananas. ROAR! ROAR! went Leo, loud and big. Today was a very special day because Leo and Mommy were going to the library. Mommy knelt down and gave Leo a gentle hug. 'Leo,' Mommy said softly, 'the library is a quiet place full of wonderful books. When we are inside, we use our talking voice. That means we speak softly, like a gentle breeze.' Leo nodded his fuzzy head. He wanted to read all the shiny picture books about spaceships and dinosaurs. When they pushed open the big wooden door of the library, Leo took a deep breath. A friendly librarian smiled at them from behind a tall desk. Instead of letting out a big lion roar, Leo whispered, 'Hello!' His voice sounded like rustling leaves. Mommy beamed with pride and gave his paw a happy squeeze. 'Good job using your talking voice, Leo!' she whispered back. Leo tiptoed over to a cozy corner with a big blue rug. He found a wonderful book about a little rocket ship. Instead of shouting across the room, Leo gently tapped Mommy on the arm and pointed to a picture. 'Look, Mommy, up in the sky,' he whispered, keeping his voice nice and soft. Mommy leaned in close and read the words on the page together with him. It was so nice and peaceful. Leo realized that whispering could be fun, too. It felt like sharing a secret between best friends. When it was time to leave, the librarian waved goodbye, and Leo whispered, 'Thank you, bye-bye!' All the way home, Leo practiced his gentle voice, feeling like a very big, very polite lion.

stories.title: Mia's Playground Choices
stories.text: Mia loved the playground. The yellow slide was shiny and fast, and the red swings could go way up high into the fluffy white clouds. But today, the playground was very busy with lots of happy children running around. Mia wanted the red bucket in the sandbox, but another little boy was holding it. Mia opened her mouth to let out a loud, frustrated squeal. But then, she stopped. She remembered what Daddy always told her about using her talking voice. Daddy knelt down beside her in the warm sand and said, 'Mia, when you want something, or when you feel upset, take a big breath and use your talking voice. Your words are strong and clear.' Mia took a big, deep breath in through her nose and blew it out through her mouth like a sleeping dragon. She walked over to the little boy. Instead of grabbing or crying, Mia used her calm, clear talking voice. 'Excuse me,' Mia said nicely. 'May I please use the red bucket when you are finished?' The little boy looked up, smiled, and handed the bucket right to her. 'Yes, you can!' he said cheerfully. Mia felt a warm glow of happiness spread all through her tummy. She didn't need to shout or cry to be heard. Her talking voice worked like magic! She built a tall sandcastle with the red bucket and decorated it with shiny green leaves. Later, when she wanted to go down the big slide, she turned to Daddy and used her happy talking voice to tell him all about her amazing sandcastle. Daddy smiled and clapped his hands. 'I love hearing your wonderful talking voice, Mia,' he cheered. Mia felt so proud of herself for using her words.

stories.title: Sam's Snack Time Words
stories.text: It was snack time at the little red table, and Sam was very, very hungry. On the bright green plate sat three round apple slices and a yummy cup of apple juice. Sam wanted the juice right now! Because he was in such a hurry, Sam started to make a grumpy whining sound in the back of his throat. 'Mmm-nnnn-gah!' Sam whined, pointing a finger at the cup and kicking his little sneakers against the chair legs. Teacher Sarah walked over with gentle steps. She knelt down so her eyes were right at Sam's level. She gave him a sweet, understanding smile. 'Sam,' Teacher Sarah said softly, 'I see your yummy juice, but I cannot understand your whining sounds. Can you use your big-boy talking voice to tell me what you need?' Sam stopped kicking his sneakers. He looked at Teacher Sarah and took a nice, slow breath. He remembered that his voice was a tool for sharing his thoughts. Sam opened his mouth and tried again, this time using his clear, polite talking voice. 'Juice, please, Teacher Sarah,' Sam said clearly. Teacher Sarah’s face lit up with a big, bright smile. 'What a fantastic talking voice!' she praised warmly, sliding the cup closer to him. 'Thank you for using your words.' Sam took a happy sip of his juice, feeling so proud and accomplished. Speaking nicely made everyone feel happy, especially him. A few minutes later, when he wanted more apple slices, he didn't need to whine at all. He just smiled and used his sweet talking voice once more. Sharing his thoughts with words was so much better than making grumpy noises. Sam finished his snack with a happy tummy and a very happy heart.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Leo was a very happy little dinosaur. He had big green scales, a long bumpy tail, and a super-duper loud dinosaur roar! ROAR! went Leo, bouncing up and down in the living room. It was fun to roar when he played outside in the big open yard, but today Leo was inside, and he wanted to talk to Mommy. Mommy was resting on the cozy sofa because she had a tiny headache. Leo trotted over, taking big stompy steps. 'MOMMY! PLAY WITH ME!' Leo boomed at the top of his lungs. Mommy winced just a little bit and put her hands gently over her ears. 'Ouch, my ears, sweet Leo,' Mommy said softly. 'That is your big outdoor dinosaur roar. Inside the house, we use our gentle talking voice so our friends and family feel nice and cozy.' Leo blinked his big round eyes. He did not want to hurt Mommy's ears! He wanted to make her feel happy. 'Can you try your soft talking voice?' Mommy asked with a warm, loving smile. Leo took a tiny breath in. He squeezed his tummy just a little bit. Instead of a loud BOOM, he let out a sweet, gentle whisper-sound. 'Play with me, Mommy?' he asked, using his softest, nicest words. Mommy smiled a big, proud smile and pulled Leo into a giant, warm hug. 'Oh, what a wonderful talking voice! That sounds so lovely to my ears,' Mommy whispered back. Leo felt so proud inside. He practiced his talking voice all afternoon, telling his teddy bear stories and asking for juice with his polite, sweet words. Using his talking voice made Leo feel like a big, helpful boy. And best of all, Mommy's head stopped hurting because the house was so peaceful and quiet. Leo gave his teddy bear another gentle cuddle, whispering, 'Good job using your talking voice, bear.' It felt so good to speak softly and kindly.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Words
stories.text: Maya loved the playground. The slide was shiny and slippery, the swings went high up into the clouds, and the sandbox was full of sparkly brown sand just waiting to be dug into. Today, Maya was building a huge, magnificent sandcastle with her very best friend, Sam. Maya wanted to put a bright red bucket on top of the castle tower, but Sam was holding the bucket to make a round sand-ball. Maya opened her mouth and shouted, 'MINE! GIVE IT!' Her voice was loud and sharp like a squeaky siren. Sam jumped, looking very startled and a little bit sad. He pulled the bucket close to his tummy. Maya felt her tummy feel tight, too. She wanted the bucket, but she did not like seeing Sam look sad. Just then, Teacher Sarah walked over, kneeling down beside the sandbox with a kind, gentle look in her eyes. 'Maya,' Teacher Sarah said softly, 'when we want something from a friend, shouting can make them feel scared. Let us try using our calm talking voice.' Maya took a deep breath, smelling the warm sunshine. She looked right at Sam and softened her shoulders. 'Sam, may I please use the red bucket when you are finished?' Maya asked using her best, sweetest talking voice. Sam's worried frown melted away into a bright, happy grin. 'Okay, Maya! Here you go!' Sam said, handing her the red bucket right away. Maya clapped her hands together with glee. 'Thank you, Sam!' she said happily. Sharing and talking nicely made playing together so much more fun. Maya and Sam built the tallest castle in the whole wide sandbox, taking turns and using their kind talking voices all afternoon long. It was the best day ever at the park.

stories.title: Pip's Library Adventure
stories.text: Pip the bunny loved books. Big books, small books, books with fluffy bunny tails on the cover, and books about flying rockets. Today was a very special day because Pip and Daddy were visiting the magical children's library. The library was filled with shelves and shelves of colorful stories waiting to be read. Pip hopped up to a big shiny red book about a clever little fox. He was so excited that he wanted to tell Daddy right away! Pip took a deep breath, puffed out his furry cheeks, and started to squeal at the top of his lungs, 'DADDY! LOOK AT THIS BOOK! IT HAS A FOX!' His voice bounced off the walls and echoed all around the quiet room. Shhh! went the kind librarian, putting a finger gently to her lips with a friendly smile. Pip stopped and looked around. Everyone else in the room was reading very quietly, turning pages with soft rustling sounds like autumn leaves. Pip felt his cheeks turn a little bit pink. He whispered, 'Oops.' Daddy knelt down beside Pip, his soft fur brushing against Pip's shoulder. 'Remember, Pip-pip,' Daddy whispered right into Pip's fuzzy ear, 'the library is a special, quiet place. When we are here, we use our soft talking voice so everyone can enjoy their reading time.' Pip nodded his little head up and down. He wanted to be a respectful reader. He leaned in very close to Daddy, right near his long floppy ear, and whispered in his sweetest, softest voice, 'Daddy, can we please read this fox book together?' Daddy's eyes crinkled with happiness. 'I would love that very much,' Daddy whispered back. They found a cozy beanbag chair in the corner of the room. Pip snuggled right up next to Daddy, keeping his voice gentle and low as they turned the pages together, looking at all the wonderful pictures. Pip loved using his quiet talking voice because it felt like a secret between just the two of them.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text:
Little Leo loved to play at the community library. It was a magical place filled with tall shelves and colorful picture books about roaring dinosaurs and zoomy rocket ships. Today, Leo found a wonderful book about a very happy monkey who swung through the leafy green jungle. 

Leo was so excited that he wanted to share the fun with his big sister, Maya. He opened his mouth wide and took a big breath. 'ROAR!' he shouted, sounding just like a fierce jungle lion. His loud voice bounced off the shiny windows and tickled the ceiling. 

Oh, my! A friendly librarian named Mr. Sam gently smiled and put a finger to his lips. 'Shh, sweet Leo,' Mr. Sam whispered softly. 'In the library, we use our quiet talking voice so everyone can enjoy their reading time.' 

Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He did not want to disturb the other readers. He looked down at his shoes and then up at Maya. How could he talk without being loud? 

Maya knelt down right beside him. She gave him a warm, reassuring hug. 'Let us practice together, Leo. Put your hand right here on your tummy. When we use our talking voice, we keep it gentle and low, just like a purring kitty cat.' 

Leo placed his tiny hand on his tummy. He took a soft, slow breath. Instead of roaring, he let the words float out like a gentle breeze. 'Look, Maya. The monkey has a banana,' he whispered with a huge grin. 

Maya clapped her hands with joy. 'Yes! That is your wonderful talking voice, Leo! Soft, clear, and kind.' 

Leo felt so proud inside. He whispered to Mr. Sam, 'Thank you for helping me.' Mr. Sam beamed and nodded. For the rest of the afternoon, Leo turned the pages of his jungle book, using his sweet talking voice to tell Maya all about the silly monkey. He learned that sharing stories is even better when you use a voice that makes everyone feel peaceful and happy.

stories.title: Mia's Morning Choices
stories.text:
Good morning, sunshine! Little Mia woke up with a big stretch and a happy wiggle. The sun was peeking through her bedroom window, painting bright yellow stripes on her cozy yellow rug. Today was a very special day because Mia was going to the park with her daddy to feed the fluffy ducks at the pond. 

Mia hopped right out of bed and ran toward the kitchen. She was so hungry for breakfast, and she could smell delicious oatmeal warming on the stove. Daddy was standing by the counter, pouring milk into a glass. 

'Daddy! Daddy! I want the blue bowl! The blue bowl right now!' Mia yelled at the top of her lungs. Her voice was sharp and loud like a squeaky siren. She stomped her foot on the floor just to show how serious she was. 

Daddy turned around and gently knelt down to Mia's eye level. He placed a kind hand on her shoulder. 'Good morning, my little star,' Daddy said softly. 'I hear that you want the blue bowl. But when you use a loud, shouting voice, it hurts my ears. Let us try using our kind, calm talking voice instead.' 

Mia looked at Daddy's gentle face. She took a deep breath and let her shoulders relax. She wanted Daddy to feel happy, too. She tried again, making her voice smooth like a gentle river. 'Daddy, please may I have the blue bowl for my oatmeal?' 

Daddy's face lit up with a brilliant smile. 'What a beautiful talking voice! I would love to get the blue bowl for you.' He reached up to the high shelf and carefully handed the shiny blue bowl to Mia. 

Mia scooped her warm oatmeal with her spoon, feeling so cozy inside. She loved knowing that she could use her words in such a nice way. Later, at the park, when she wanted to point out a swimming duck, she remembered her talking voice. 'Look, Daddy, a swimming duck!' she said softly. Daddy smiled and held her hand, proud of his growing girl.

stories.title: Sam's Block Tower
stories.text:
The afternoon play space was buzzing with energy. Golden sunlight streamed across the carpet, where little Sam was building the most amazing tower in the whole wide world. He stacked red blocks, yellow blocks, and tall blue triangles. Higher and higher it went, reaching all the way up to his nose! 

Just as Sam was placing a wiggly green cylinder right on the very top, his little puppy plush toy tumbled over and knocked the whole tower down. Crash! Boom! The blocks scattered everywhere like colorful autumn leaves. 

Oh no! Sam felt a hot, frustrated feeling bubble up inside his tummy. He wanted to scream and cry. He opened his mouth and let out a loud, high-pitched screech that made his friend Noah look up from the puzzle table with wide eyes. 

Sam's teacher, Ms. Clara, walked over slowly with soft, gentle steps. She sat down beside the pile of scattered blocks. 'I see your tower fell down, Sam,' she said in a soothing voice. 'That is very frustrating when you worked so hard. But when we screech, it startles our friends. Let us take a breath and use our talking voice to ask for help.' 

Sam took a shaky breath. He closed his eyes for a moment, then opened them. He looked at Ms. Clara and pointed to the blocks. 'My tower fell down,' Sam said in a small, polite talking voice. 'Can you help me build it again?' 

Ms. Clara smiled warmly. 'I would love to help you rebuild, Sam. Thank you for using your wonderful talking voice.' 

Noah hurried over with a red block. 'I can help, too!' Noah said happily. 

Together, the friends stacked the blocks even higher than before. Sam felt so glad he used his talking voice. It made problem-solving easy and playing with friends so much fun.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo went to the big, quiet library with his mommy. The library was filled with tall shelves of books with bright, colorful covers. Leo loved books! He saw a big red fire truck book and wanted to show his mommy right away. In his loudest voice, Leo shouted, "Look, Mommy! A truck!" Oh my! The librarian put her finger to her lips and made a soft shushing sound. The room was so quiet, and Leo's loud voice made a few people jump. Mommy knelt down right beside Leo and gave him a gentle hug. She said, "Leo, sweetie, the library is a place for quiet reading. Let's use our talking voice. You can use a soft, gentle indoor voice to tell me about the truck." Leo nodded his head. He took a deep breath and practiced. He whispered softly, "Look, Mommy. A red truck." Mommy smiled a huge, proud smile and patted his head. "That is such a wonderful talking voice, Leo!" she whispered back. Together, they sat on a soft blue rug. Leo opened the big red fire truck book. He pointed to the shiny wheels and whispered about the firefighters all by himself. He felt so proud of his calm, quiet talking voice. When it was time to check out the books, Leo used his sweet talking voice to say thank you to the nice librarian. The librarian smiled and handed him a colorful sticker. Leo put the sticker proudly on his shirt. As they walked out into the warm sunshine, Leo realized that using his indoor talking voice was a super special way to share his thoughts without startling anyone. Mommy held his hand tightly and said, "You did such a fantastic job using your talking voice today, Leo. You are growing up so much!" Leo giggled and skipped all the way to the car, feeling happy, calm, and ready for his next quiet adventure.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Words
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly in the sky, and Maya was playing in the sandbox at the park. She had a bright yellow bucket and a shiny blue shovel. Maya was busy building a giant, magnificent sandcastle with a tall tower. Suddenly, her friend Sam came running over. Sam wanted to use the blue shovel to dig a moat around the castle. But Sam did not ask; he just reached down and snatched the shovel right out of Maya's hand! Maya felt a big rumble of frustration deep inside her tummy. Her lips pressed together, and she felt a big, noisy growl building up in her throat. She wanted to scream or snatch the shovel back as hard as she could. But then, Maya remembered what her teacher said at school. She took a big, deep breath in through her nose and let it out slowly through her mouth. Instead of yelling, Maya used her strong, clear talking voice. She looked right at Sam and said, "Sam, please do not grab. I am using the blue shovel right now. You can ask for a turn." Sam stopped and looked at Maya, a little surprised. He heard her kind, clear words. Sam nodded and said, "Maya, can I please have a turn when you are done?" Maya beamed with happiness. She felt so proud because she used her talking voice instead of getting mad. She handed the shovel to Sam and said, "Yes, you can have it in two minutes, Sam!" They shared the sandbox together, digging and building side by side. Mommy walked over and clapped her hands. "Maya, I am so proud of you. You used your big-girl talking voice to solve a problem!" Maya smiled from ear to ear, knowing that her words were powerful, helpful, and kind.

stories.title: Oliver's Breakfast Choices
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! Little Oliver woke up in his cozy bed and stretched his arms way up high. Today was a brand new day full of fun. Oliver hopped out of bed and scampered into the kitchen for breakfast. Daddy was standing by the stove making yummy food. Oliver was so hungry that his tummy let out a little rumble. Oliver wanted his favorite yellow banana right now, but instead of using his words, Oliver just pointed at the counter and made a funny whining sound. "Hhhnnnn!" he grunted, crossing his little arms over his dinosaur pajamas. Daddy turned around and smiled gently. He knelt down so he was eye-to-eye with Oliver. Daddy gave him a warm, comforting hug and said, "Oliver, my big boy, I want to help you, but I cannot understand your grumbles. Let's use our lovely talking voice so we can chat." Oliver took a breath and relaxed his shoulders. He looked at the counter and remembered how to use his words. In a clear, happy voice, Oliver said, "Daddy, please may I have a yellow banana for breakfast?" Daddy's face lit up like the morning sun. "What a polite request! I would love to give you a banana, Oliver." Daddy peeled the sweet, yellow banana and placed it on a bright blue plate for his happy little boy. Oliver sat at the table and munched happily on his treat. He felt so proud of himself for remembering to use his clear talking voice instead of whining. When he finished, he wiped his mouth with a napkin and said, "Thank you, Daddy, that was yummy!" Daddy kissed the top of Oliver's head and said, "Using your talking voice makes our mornings so wonderful, Oliver. You are doing such a brilliant job growing up every single day!"

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Little Leo loved going to the big library with Mommy. It was a magical place filled with giant towers of colorful books. Leo felt so excited that he wanted to shout out loud. 'Look at all the trucks, Mommy!' he yelled in his big, booming outside voice. Heads turned, and the friendly librarian smiled gently, putting a finger softly to her lips. Mommy knelt down to Leo's eye level and gave him a warm, reassuring hug. 'Leo, sweetie,' Mommy whispered softly, 'we are inside now. This is a special place where we use our indoor talking voice. Can you try it with me?' Leo blinked his big brown eyes and nodded. He thought about how a little mouse talks. So, he took a tiny, gentle breath and whispered back, 'Like this, Mommy?' Mommy beamed with the biggest, proudest smile. 'Yes, my little star! That is your wonderful talking voice.' Feeling very proud, Leo tiptoed over to the picture book shelf. He found a shiny book all about a friendly red fire engine. Instead of shouting, Leo tapped Mommy on the arm and used his smooth, gentle talking voice. 'Mommy, please read this red truck story with me.' Mommy clapped her hands softly and whispered, 'I would love to, Leo!' They cuddled up in the big, cozy armchair together. As Mommy read the story aloud in a soft, soothing tone, Leo practiced keeping his voice calm and sweet. He loved how nice and peaceful it felt to talk softly. When they checked out the book, the librarian even gave Leo a shiny star sticker for being such a good listener. Leo looked at his star and whispered a happy thank you. Using his talking voice made him feel like a big, clever boy. It was wonderful to know that he could share his big excitement using a sweet, quiet tone that made everyone around him feel happy and calm.

stories.title: Mia at the Playground
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly, and Mia was having the absolute best time zooming down the orange slide at the park. Wheee! She landed in the soft woodchips with a happy giggle. Across the playground, her friend Sam was playing in the sandbox, building a tall, sparkly castle. Mia wanted Sam to see her sliding, but she was too far away. Her chest felt full of excited energy, and she opened her mouth to let out a huge, roaring dinosaur screech. 'Raaaawrrr!' Before the sound came out, Daddy gently touched Mia's shoulder. He knelt down beside her in the warm sunshine and spoke in a kind, encouraging tone. 'Mia, I know you are so excited, sweet pea. But when we want our friends to hear us across the playground, we don't need a dinosaur roar. Let’s use our clear talking voice instead.' Mia looked at Daddy and took a deep breath. She practiced saying 'Hello' in her normal, friendly speaking voice. Daddy nodded proudly. 'That is it! Your clear talking voice is strong and wonderful. Let's try calling Sam together.' Mia cupped her hands gently around her mouth and spoke clearly. 'Hi, Sam! Look at me!' Sam looked up, his face lighting up with a big, joyful grin. He waved his little plastic shovel in the air and shouted back, 'Hi, Mia! Nice sliding!' Mia felt a warm glow of happiness inside her heart. She didn't need to roar to be heard. Her clear talking voice traveled all the way across the park, just like magic. She walked over to the sandbox to help Sam build the tallest castle towers. They took turns talking and sharing their toys, using their happy talking voices the whole afternoon. Daddy watched them play and gave Mia a gentle thumbs-up. Mia smiled, knowing that using her talking voice was the best way to make friends smile.

stories.title: Oliver's Toy Time Trouble
stories.text: Oliver sat on the soft playroom rug, surrounded by his favorite blue blocks. He was building a magnificent rocket ship that stretched all the way up to the sofa cushions. It was going to fly to the moon! Just as Oliver placed the very last red block on the very top of his tower, his big yellow block rolled away and bumped against the couch. Oliver squeezed his eyes tight. He felt a frustrated growl rumbling deep down in his tummy. He wanted to scream and toss his blocks because things didn't go his way. Instead of letting the growl out, Oliver remembered what Grandma always taught him. He took a big, deep breath, smelling the imaginary flowers, and blew out the birthday candles. Slowly, the frustration melted away. Grandma walked over with a gentle, loving smile and sat right down on the rug next to him. 'Oh, Oliver, my sweet boy, you built such a tall rocket ship!' Grandma said softly. 'It looks like you hit a little bump. When we feel upset, do we use a grumpy growl, or do we use our helpful talking voice?' Oliver thought about it, running his small fingers over the smooth wooden blocks. He shook his head and gave a tiny smile. 'Use my talking voice, Grandma,' he whispered. 'That is right,' Grandma cheered softly, stroking his hair with affection. 'Let's use your strong, calm talking voice to ask for help.' Oliver looked at Grandma and used his polite, even tone. 'Grandma, please can you help me reach my yellow block?' Grandma's face lit up with joy. 'I would love to help you, Oliver.' Together, they reached under the couch, retrieved the yellow block, and placed it safely back onto the rocket. Oliver felt so proud of himself. He used his talking voice to solve his problem without any fuss. He gave Grandma a big, happy hug, ready to fly his rocket all the way to the stars.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper and Roar
stories.text: Little Leo loved to play games with his big toy dinosaur, Rex. Rex had a very loud, booming voice. 'ROAR!' shouted Leo, making his voice as big and loud as the real dinosaur. But oh dear, today Leo and Mommy were visiting the quiet neighborhood library. It was a special place filled with tall shelves of books, cozy reading chairs, and lots of thinking friends. Mommy gently knelt down to Leo's eye level and smiled. 'Leo, sweetie, we are inside the library now. This is a place for quiet concentration. Can we use our talking voice, please?' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He wanted to look at the pop-up animal books, but he knew he needed to adjust his volume. He took a deep, calming breath and tried again. 'Roar,' he whispered softly, almost like a mouse. Mommy clapped her hands together gently. 'Wonderful job, Leo! That is your wonderful talking voice. It is calm, polite, and very easy to hear right up close.' Leo beamed with pride. He felt so grown-up using his inside voice. Together, they walked over to the colorful rug and picked out three bright books about fuzzy puppies and zooming rocket ships. Leo held each book carefully in his lap. When he wanted to show Mommy a picture of a puppy wearing a red hat, he remembered his special skill. He did not yell across the room. Instead, he gently touched Mommy's arm and used his smooth, happy talking voice. 'Look, Mommy, a puppy hat!' Mommy smiled warmly and gave him a gentle squeeze. 'I love hearing your sweet talking voice, Leo. It makes sharing stories together so peaceful and happy.' Leo turned the pages slowly, feeling safe, cozy, and very proud of himself for knowing just how to use his voice at the right time in the right place.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Message
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly over the neighborhood playground, and Maya was having the most wonderful time zooming down the slippery green slide. Whee! Down she went, laughing and giggling. Next to her, her friend Sam was busy building a magnificent castle out of sparkly yellow sand. Maya really, really wanted to use the red bucket that Sam was holding. Her first feeling was a big urge to snatch the bucket right out of his hand, and maybe even let out a frustrated growl. But Maya remembered her daily practice at home with Daddy. She took a big breath, let her shoulders drop, and walked right over to Sam. Instead of grabbing or whining, Maya remembered to use her strong, clear talking voice. 'Sam, please may I have a turn with the red bucket when you are finished?' she asked, keeping her tone kind and friendly. Sam looked up from his sandy moat and smiled. He liked it when Maya used her nice words instead of being grumpy. 'Sure, Maya! Here you go!' Sam said happily, handing her the shiny red bucket. Maya's face lit up with a huge, glowing smile. She felt so proud inside her tummy. She had used her talking voice to solve a problem all by herself! 'Thank you, Sam,' she said warmly. They spent the rest of the morning working together as a team, building the tallest sandcastle with gates and towers. Later, when it was time to go home, Maya ran over to Daddy and gave him a big hug. 'Daddy, I used my talking voice on the playground today!' she cheered. Daddy picked her up and spun her around in a gentle circle. 'That is fantastic, my superstar! Using your talking voice makes playing with friends so much fun for everyone.'

stories.title: Oliver's Morning Choices
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! The cheerful morning light was peeking through the window of Oliver's bedroom. Oliver rubbed his sleepy eyes and stretched his arms up high like a tall giraffe. It was time to get dressed for preschool, which was always an exciting adventure. But today, Oliver felt a little bit tired and grumpy. When Daddy asked if he wanted the blue shirt or the green shirt, Oliver just crossed his arms, stomped his foot softly on the soft rug, and let out a loud, high-pitched whiny squeal. 'Mmm-grrr!' he made a fuss. Daddy did not get upset. He knelt down beside Oliver, gave him a gentle, loving tickle on his tummy, and waited patiently. 'Oliver, buddy, I know you are still waking up, but I cannot understand what you need when you use a whiny sound. Let's try using our nice, clear talking voice, okay?' Oliver took a deep breath and let all the grumpy feelings float right out of his mouth like a big puffy cloud. He thought about what he really wanted. He cleared his throat and tried again, using his regular, happy volume. 'Daddy, please can I wear the blue shirt with the happy star on it?' he asked politely. Daddy's face lit up with joy. 'I love hearing that wonderful talking voice, Oliver! That is so helpful and clear.' Daddy helped him slide his arms through the soft sleeves of the bright blue shirt. Oliver looked down at his star and felt all his morning grumpies completely disappear. He felt energized and ready for the day. At breakfast, Oliver used his talking voice to ask for more yummy crunchy toast, and again when he said thank you for his cup of sweet apple juice. He felt like such a big, capable boy. As they walked out the front door hand-in-hand, Oliver smiled, knowing that his talking voice was his very own superpower for a happy day.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Leo was a very happy little dinosaur. He had big green scales, a long bumpy tail, and a super-duper loud ROAR! ROAR, went Leo in the morning when he woke up. ROAR, went Leo when he found his favorite blue sock. ROAR, went Leo when he wanted a banana for breakfast. His mama smiled and gave him a gentle hug. 'Good morning, my sweet dinosaur,' Mama said softly. 'You have such strong lungs. But remember, inside the house, we use our gentle talking voice so our ears stay happy.' Leo blinked his big round eyes. He wanted to practice. He took a deep breath in through his nose, just like smelling a flower, and let it out through his mouth. 'Can I have a banana, please?' Leo whispered. His voice was soft like a fluffy cloud. Mama clapped her hands together with joy. 'Yes, you can, Leo! What a wonderful talking voice. That sounds so sweet.' Leo felt very proud of his gentle sound. Later, it was time to play with his colorful wooden blocks. He built a tall, tall tower that reached all the way up to the couch cushions. Oh no! The tower wobbled. The tower shook. Crash, boom, bang! All the blocks tumbled down onto the soft carpet. Leo opened his mouth wide to let out a giant dinosaur ROAR. But then he remembered his special helper breath. He closed his mouth, took a tiny breath, and used his talking voice instead. 'Uh oh, my blocks fell down!' he said to his teddy bear. Teddy bear looked very pleased. Mama came walking into the living room and smiled. 'I heard you use your talking voice when your blocks fell. That was so helpful, Leo.' Leo giggled and gave his blocks another try. Building was so much fun, especially when he used his inside voice to share his happy thoughts. He whispered to his toys, 'Let us build a castle together.' The day was quiet, calm, and full of sweet little words. Leo learned that his voice could be strong, but it could also be gentle as a whisper. And that made everyone in the cozy house smile from ear to ear.

stories.title: Maya's Playground Words
stories.text: Maya loved going to the big sunny park down the street. The grass was green, the sky was bright blue, and the swings went swoosh through the warm breeze. Maya ran as fast as her little legs could carry her toward the shiny red slide. She wanted a turn right now! She opened her mouth to shout across the playground, 'MINE!' But then Maya remembered something very important. She stopped running, planted her little sneakers firmly in the woodchips, and took a deep, calming breath. She looked for her friend, the park helper. Maya walked right up to the slide where her friend Sam was climbing. Instead of yelling, Maya used her kind talking voice. 'Excuse me, Sam. Can I have a turn on the slide after you, please?' Sam turned around and beamed a big, happy smile. 'Yes, Maya! You can go right after me!' Sam said. Maya did a little happy dance. Using her talking voice worked like magic! She waited patiently at the bottom, counting the seconds. One, two, three. Sam zoomed down the slide and giggled. 'Your turn, Maya!' Now it was Maya's turn to climb up the ladder. Step by step, she climbed to the top, feeling the warm sun on her back. When she sat down at the very top of the slide, she looked out over the whole park. She wanted to tell her dad how high up she was. Dad was sitting on the green bench reading a book. Maya didn't need to scream. She took a breath and used her clear talking voice. 'Daddy, look at me! I am way up high!' Dad looked up from his book and waved his hand high in the air. 'I see you, Maya! You are doing great!' Dad called back with a warm, encouraging smile. Maya pushed off with her hands and went wheeeee all the way down to the bottom. She landed softly in the woodchips and giggled. Playing at the park was the best thing ever, and using her talking voice made sharing the fun so easy for everyone.

stories.title: Pip's Library Adventure
stories.text: Pip the bunny loved story time at the big community library. The library was a magical place filled with thousands of colorful books about puppies, stars, trucks, and sleepy little kittens. Pip hopped along behind his big brother Toby, clutching his favorite stuffed rabbit very tightly. Everywhere Pip looked, there were shelves and shelves of wonderful stories waiting to be read. He was so excited that he wanted to squeal at the top of his lungs. 'Look at all the books!' Pip started to shout in a loud, booming voice. Toby gently placed a furry paw on Pip's shoulder and whispered, 'Shh, Pip. The library is a quiet place where people are reading. We use our quiet library voice here.' Pip blinked his bright pink eyes and nodded. He knew about quiet voices. A quiet voice was like a soft murmur, just loud enough for the person right next to you to hear, but quiet enough not to disturb the sleeping books. Pip took a soft little breath and tried again. He leaned close to Toby's long ear and whispered, 'Look at the books, Toby.' Toby smiled warmly and rubbed his nose against Pip's. 'Yes, Pip. There are so many stories. Let us find one about carrots.' Hand in paw, the two bunnies tiptoed softly over to the animal section. Pip scanned the bottom shelf with his clever eyes. There it was! A bright orange book with a picture of a very happy bunny eating a crunchy carrot snack. Pip reached out his paw and gently pulled the book from the shelf. He held it close to his chest and looked at the friendly librarian behind the big wooden desk. The librarian was wearing sparkly glasses and smiling at them. Pip walked right up to the desk and used his very best polite talking voice. 'Please, can we borrow this book today?' The librarian nodded happily. 'Of course you can, little bunny. Enjoy your reading.' Pip beamed with pride all the way home, knowing that his talking voice was just the right volume for a wonderful day of adventures.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo went to the big library with Mommy. The library was a wonderful place filled with tall shelves of books. There were shiny books with sparkly covers, big books with pictures of dinosaurs, and tiny books about sleepy kittens. Leo was so excited! He grabbed a bright red book about a friendly firetruck and wanted to share it with Mommy right away. 'Mommy, look at the big red wheels!' Leo shouted in his loud, booming playground voice. A friendly librarian with round glasses gently put her finger to her lips. 'Shh, sweetie,' she whispered with a warm smile. 'Inside the library, we use our quiet talking voices.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He wanted to respect the quiet library, but he still wanted to talk about his firetruck. Mommy knelt down to Leo's eye level and gave him a gentle hug. 'Remember, Leo, you have a big voice for the park and a soft talking voice for indoors. Let's practice your soft talking voice together.' Leo nodded. He took a big, deep breath in through his nose, pretending to smell a sweet flower, and let it out through his mouth. Then, he tried again, leaning close to Mommy's ear. 'Mommy, look at the big red wheels,' he whispered softly, with a huge grin on his face. Mommy clapped her hands softly. 'Wonderful job, Leo! That is such a nice talking voice.' Leo felt so proud inside. He whispered about the firetruck's ladder, the shiny bell, and the brave firefighter dogs on every single page. Using his special indoor talking voice made him feel like a big boy.
