When they checked out the book and walked back outside into the bright sunshine, Leo shouted, 'Yay for books!' using his big outdoor voice again, because every voice has its very own special time and place.

stories.title: Maya at the Playground
stories.text: The sun was shining brightly, and Maya was having the most wonderful time at the neighborhood playground. She zoomed down the yellow slide, swung high on the green swings, and dug deep holes in the soft, warm sandbox. It was time for her turn on the tall climbing wall. Maya looked up, but another little boy named Sam was standing right in front of the handholds. Maya wanted to go up so badly that she stomped her foot and let out a loud, frustrated whine. 'Mmm-nnnh! Move!' she cried, using her grumpy whine voice. Sam looked confused and didn't know what Maya wanted. Maya's big brother, Toby, walked over and knelt beside her in the woodchips. 'Maya,' Toby said gently, taking her little hands in his. 'When you use your whine voice, it is hard to understand what you need. Let's take a breath and use your strong talking voice instead.' Maya took a deep breath and let out a little puff of air. She looked right at Sam and tried again, using her clear, friendly talking voice. 'Excuse me, Sam, may I have a turn on the climbing wall, please?' Sam smiled brightly and stepped aside. 'Sure, Maya! You can go right up!' Maya beamed with happiness. 'Thank you, Sam!' she said in her lovely talking voice. She scrambled up the handholds easily, feeling so proud of herself. She realized that using her clear talking voice helped her friends understand her right away, and that made playing together much more fun for everyone.

stories.title: Oliver's Toy Dinosaur
stories.text: Oliver loved his green toy dinosaur named Rex. Rex had big white teeth, a long squishy tail, and he could make a mighty roar. Rex was Oliver's very favorite toy in the whole wide world. One sunny afternoon, Oliver was building a gigantic block tower in the living room. He placed a yellow block on top, then a blue block, and finally a red block right at the very peak. Suddenly, Rex the dinosaur fell over and knocked the tower right down! Crash, bang, went the blocks. Oliver wanted Daddy to help him rebuild the tower, but instead of asking, he crossed his arms, squeezed his eyes shut, and began to make loud, grumpy dinosaur growls. 'Grrr! Rarrr!' he yelled loudly, stomping his feet on the rug. Daddy walked over from the kitchen with a gentle, loving smile. He scooped Oliver up into a big, warm bear hug. 'Oh, Oliver,' Daddy chuckled softly. 'Are you using your dinosaur roar or your talking voice right now?' Oliver giggled a little bit and opened his eyes. 'My dinosaur roar,' he whispered. 'Rex knocked my blocks down.' Daddy nodded. 'Dinosaur roars are super fun for playing, but when you need help, your talking voice works much faster. Can you ask me with your words?' Oliver nodded and cleared his throat. 'Daddy, please help me build my block tower again?' he asked in his sweetest, clearest talking voice. Daddy smiled proudly and gave Oliver a high-five. 'I would love to help you build an even bigger tower, buddy!' Together, they stacked the blocks high into the sky, and Oliver learned that his talking voice was the best way to get help from the people who loved him.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Leo was a very happy little dinosaur. He had big green scales, a long bumpy tail, and a super-duper loud ROAR! When Leo played outside in the big backyard, his roar could travel all the way over the tall oak tree. 'ROAR! I am the king of the sandbox!' Leo would shout to the clouds. His mommy would smile and clap because outside was a wonderful place for big roars. But one sunny morning, Leo and his mommy went inside the cozy library to find a brand new storybook. The library was very quiet, like a sleeping kitten. Shhh, went the wind outside the window. Leo wanted to tell his mommy about a blue book with shiny stars on the cover. He opened his big mouth and took a deep breath to let out a happy dinosaur ROAR! Mommy gently put her soft hand on Leo's scaly shoulder. 'Wait a minute, my sweet little dinosaur,' Mommy whispered with a warm, loving smile. 'Inside the library, we use our gentle talking voices. That way, everyone can read their books in peace.' Leo blinked his big round eyes. He wanted to try. Instead of a loud boom, Leo squeezed his tummy and let out a soft, sweet sound. 'Mommy, look at the star book,' he whispered, just like a gentle breeze rustling through the leaves. Mommy beamed with joy and gave Leo a big, warm hug. 'Such a wonderful talking voice, Leo!' she praised him. Leo felt so proud inside. He carried the shiny book to the cozy reading rug. Whenever he wanted to share a secret or ask a question, he remembered to use his sweet talking voice. The librarian smiled at Leo, and Leo smiled right back. Using his talking voice made him feel like a big, clever boy. When it was finally time to go back outside to the sunny yard, Leo knew just what to do. He took a deep breath, grinned from ear to ear, and let out a gigantic, happy ROAR! Inside was for talking softly, and outside was for big fun. Leo was learning how to do both, and it felt just right.

stories.title: Mia's Morning Song
stories.text: Ring-a-ding-dong! The little yellow alarm clock sang its happy morning song, waking up the whole house. Mia opened her sleepy eyes and stretched her arms up high toward the ceiling, as tall as a giraffe. Good morning, sunshine! Today was a very special day because Mia was going to the park with her daddy to feed the fluffy ducks at the big pond. Mia hopped right out of her warm, cozy bed and rushed over to the toy box. She wanted to play with her bright red firetruck before breakfast. But oh no! The firetruck was stuck way at the bottom under a big mountain of stuffed animals. Mia really, really wanted her truck right now. She opened her mouth wide and let out a loud, high-pitched screech that made the windows rattle. Eeeeeee! Daddy came walking into the bedroom, looking very gentle and kind. He knelt down right beside Mia on the soft rug. 'Good morning, my little star,' Daddy said softly. 'I hear a very loud noise, but I cannot understand what you need when you use a screech. Can you use your lovely talking voice?' Mia took a little breath and stopped the loud noise. She looked at Daddy's kind eyes. She took another breath and tried again, using her clear, everyday speaking voice. 'Daddy, please help me find my red firetruck,' she said, keeping her voice calm and sweet. Daddy's face lit up like the morning sun. 'Of course I can help you, Mia! Thank you so much for using your clear talking voice.' Together, Daddy and Mia gently moved the fuzzy teddy bears and the soft bunnies out of the way. And there was the shiny red firetruck, ready for action! Mia gave Daddy a huge hug. Using her talking voice made everything so much easier and happier. They went downstairs together to eat yummy pancakes with sticky maple syrup, chatting happily the whole time. Mia felt like a big helper as she told Daddy all about the games she wanted to play at the park today. Her talking voice was like music, and it made the whole morning bright.

stories.title: Sammy's Snack Time
stories.text: The kitchen clock ticked softly as the bright afternoon sunlight streamed through the clean glass window. Sammy the bunny rabbit sat at his little yellow table, waiting patiently for his afternoon snack. He was getting very hungry, and his tummy let out a little rumble. Rumble, rumble, went Sammy's tummy! Mommy was busy by the stove, stirring a warm pot of delicious apple cinnamon oatmeal. Sammy wanted his snack right this very second. Instead of waiting, Sammy started to bang his spoon on the wooden table. Bang, bang, bang! He made a big clatter and whined in a loud, grumpy tone. 'I want it now! Now, now, now!' Sammy cried loudly, crossing his furry little arms over his chest. Mommy stopped stirring the pot and turned around. She didn't look mad; she just looked gently into Sammy's eyes. She knelt down beside his little chair so they were eye-to-eye. 'Sammy,' Mommy said in a soft, soothing voice, 'banging the spoon and whining doesn't tell me what you need. Let's take a deep breath together.' Sammy took a slow, deep breath in through his nose, smelling the sweet cinnamon. Then he blew it out gently through his mouth, like blowing out a birthday candle. Ahhh. 'Now,' Mommy prompted gently, 'use your polite talking voice.' Sammy uncrossed his arms and put his hands nicely in his lap. He looked right at Mommy and tried again. 'Mommy, please may I have my apple snack?' he asked, using his sweet, clear talking voice. Mommy's face broke into a huge, proud smile. 'Yes, you may, my polite little bunny!' she cheered. Mommy scooped up a warm, delicious bowl of oatmeal and placed it gently on the table right in front of Sammy. Sammy felt so happy inside. Using his talking voice was much better than making a loud mess. He ate every single bite of his yummy snack, thanking Mommy nicely when he was all done. Being polite and using his words made snack time the best part of the whole afternoon.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo the lion woke up with a big, bubbly, roaring energy inside his tummy. "ROAR!" shouted Leo. "Good morning, sunshine!" Leo’s roar was super duper loud because he was a strong lion. But wait! Leo was inside his cozy house. His baby sister, Lily, was still taking a little nap in her crib. "Rumble-roar!" Leo tried to say hello to his mommy, but it sounded like thunder. Mommy smiled a gentle, loving smile and knelt down so her eyes were right next to Leo’s sparkling eyes. "Good morning, my sweet lion cub," Mommy whispered softly. "Your roar is wonderful and strong. But inside our house, we use our gentle talking voice so we keep our friends and family feeling cozy and calm." Leo touched his throat. He wanted to feel how his voice worked. "Can I use my talking voice?" he asked. Mommy nodded. "Let's try it together." Leo took a big, deep breath in. He let it out slowly. "Good morning, Mommy," he said in a smooth, sweet voice that sounded like a purring kitten. Mommy clapped her hands with joy. "Yay, Leo! That is your wonderful talking voice! It is so clear and lovely." Just then, baby Lily woke up from her nap. She did not cry because there was no loud thunder roar. Instead, Lily opened her big blue eyes and giggled happily at her big brother. Leo felt so proud. He used his talking voice to tell Lily a story about a friendly sunbeam. Using his talking voice made everyone feel happy and safe. Leo gave Mommy a big hug. He knew that when he was inside, his talking voice was his superpower for kindness.

stories.title: Maya at the Playground
stories.text: Maya the little monkey loved the park more than anything in the whole wide world. Today, the park was buzzing with bouncing balls, whirring swings, and happy laughing children. Maya wanted to go down the shiny green slide right this very second. She zoomed over to the ladder, but her friend Sam was already climbing up to the top. Maya wanted to yell, "MOVE OUT OF MY WAY!" at the top of her lungs. But she remembered something very important. She put her hands on her tummy and took a big, deep breath. Then, she opened her mouth to use her talking voice. "Excuse me, Sam," Maya said clearly, right in the middle of the noisy park. "Can I have a turn on the slide after you, please?" Sam turned around on the ladder and beamed a giant, sunny smile. Because Maya used her kind talking voice, Sam heard her loud and clear over all the playground sounds. "Yes, Maya! You can go right after me!" Sam called back. Maya waited patiently, swinging her arms and humming a happy little tune. When Sam finished sliding down with a joyful "Whee!", it was Maya’s turn. She climbed up the ladder, sat right at the top, and zoomed down the green slide with her hair blowing in the wind. "Wheeeee!" she giggled. When she landed safely on the soft rubber floor, she looked at Sam and said, "Thank you for sharing, Sam!" Using her talking voice made playing together so much fun. Maya felt like a superstar because she knew how to use her words to be a wonderful friend to everyone at the park.

stories.title: Pip's Toy Trouble
stories.text: Pip the penguin was building the tallest block tower in the whole igloo. He stacked a red block, a blue block, and a sparkly yellow star block right on the very top. It was magnificent! Just then, his best friend Penny waddled into the room. Penny wanted to help, so she reached out her flipper to add a green block. Oh no! Bump! The tall block tower wobbled. It swayed to the left. It swayed to the right. Crash! All the blocks tumbled down onto the soft carpet in a big, colorful heap. Pip felt a hot, frustrated feeling bubble up inside his feathers. His beak opened wide, and he felt a big grumpy squeak ready to burst out. But Pip remembered his daily routine magic trick. He stopped, closed his eyes, and took a slow, deep penguin breath. In and out. He opened his eyes and looked right at Penny. Instead of crying or using a grumpy squeak, Pip used his clear, strong talking voice. "Penny, my tower fell down," Pip said gently. "That makes me feel a little bit sad." Penny looked down at the scattered blocks and her flippers drooped. "I am sorry, Pip. I just wanted to help you build." Pip saw that Penny was sorry, and his kind heart felt warm again. He used his talking voice to say, "That is okay, Penny. Let's build a bigger tower together!" Penny cheered and clapped her flippers. Together, the two little penguins stacked the red blocks, the blue blocks, and the yellow star blocks even higher than before. Using their talking voices solved the problem and made playtime twice as fun for everyone.

stories.title: Leo's Library Whisper
stories.text: Leo loved the library. It was a big, quiet room filled with towering shelves of magical picture books with shiny covers and bumpy pages. Today, Leo found a book all about zooming rockets that blasted into the starry night sky. He was so excited that he wanted to share it with his big sister, Maya, right away. Leo opened his mouth wide and took a giant breath to yell across the room, "Maya! Look at the big rocket!" But wait, said the gentle voice in Leo's head. Inside the library, we use a different kind of voice. It is called our talking voice, or sometimes, our cozy whisper voice. Leo put his little hand on his tummy and felt it go soft and slow. He closed his mouth just a little bit and walked on tiptoes over to where Maya was sitting by the big window. Instead of shouting, Leo used his special talking voice. He leaned in close and whispered happily, "Maya, look at the big rocket zooming up to the moon." Maya smiled a warm, sunny smile and gave Leo a gentle high-five. "That is a very cool rocket, Leo," she whispered back. Using his talking voice felt so calm and nice. It did not hurt anyone's ears, and it let him share his wonderful secret without startling the sleepy library cat curled up on the rug. Leo felt very proud of himself for remembering. When they checked out their books, the librarian smiled and gave Leo a star sticker for being such a good listener and speaker. Later, as they walked home under the leafy trees, Leo practiced his talking voice again, telling a passing ladybug all about his new rocket book. His voice was soft, clear, and just right for sharing happy moments with the world around him.

stories.title: Mia at the Playground Slide
stories.text: The playground was bustling with bright colors, joyful laughter, and the happy squeaks of swinging children. Mia stood at the very top of the twisty yellow slide, clutching her fluffy toy bunny tightly. She was ready for a super-fast slide down to the soft rubber ground below. But right in front of her sat Toby, who was still tying his bright red shoelace and getting ready to move. Mia wanted him to hurry up so she could go. Her first instinct was to squeeze her eyes shut and scream at the top of her lungs, "Move, Toby! I want to go!" But Mia remembered the important game she and her daddy played at home. She took a big, deep breath, puffing out her cheeks like a happy red balloon, and let it out slowly. She remembered to use her talking voice. Mia tapped Toby gently on his jacket sleeve and spoke in a clear, friendly tone. "Excuse me, Toby, can I go down the slide next when you are finished?" Toby turned around, blinking his big brown eyes, and gave a bright, friendly nod. "Sure thing, Mia! All done!" he chirped, scampering off to the sandbox. Mia felt a wonderful flutter of happiness in her tummy. Using her talking voice worked so much better than yelling or crying. It helped her solve the puzzle without making anyone feel sad. She slid down the twisty slide with a gleeful giggle, wind blowing through her curls. When she reached the bottom, she gave Toby a cheerful wave and thanked him. It was wonderful to know that her kind words were like little magic keys that opened doors to playing nicely together in the big, sunny park.

stories.title: Sammy's Snack Time Choice
stories.text: The kitchen smelled deliciously of warm cinnamon and sweet, ripe bananas. It was afternoon snack time at Sammy's house, and his tummy was rumbling a hungry little tune. Rumble, rumble, went his tummy. Sammy sat in his blue booster chair at the small wooden table, watching his mother slice up a juicy red apple. He wanted a piece right this very second. Sammy felt a tiny grumble starting in his throat, and he opened his mouth to let out a loud, frustrated whine. But Sammy paused. He remembered what he practiced with his teacher at preschool today. When he wants something, he can use his big-boy talking voice instead of grumbling or whining. Sammy took a deep breath, letting his shoulders drop down comfortably. He looked right at his mother and used his bright, clear talking voice. "Mommy, please may I have a slice of apple?" he asked politely, pointing his little finger toward the cutting board. Mommy stopped slicing and turned around with a radiant, proud smile that lit up her whole face. "Of course you may, my sweet boy! You used such a wonderful talking voice to ask," she said lovingly, placing two crisp, sweet apple slices on his favorite dinosaur plate. Sammy beamed with pride. Using his talking voice made Mommy happy, made him feel grown-up, and got him his yummy snack much faster than whining ever could. He munched happily on his apples, chewing slowly and listening to the birds chirp outside the kitchen window. It felt so good to communicate clearly, knowing that his words mattered and that his voice was a powerful, positive tool for getting what he needed every single day.

stories.title: Leo's Inside Voice
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo woke up with a big, bright sunshine smile. Today was a very special day because Leo was going to the park with his big sister, Mia. Leo was so excited that he jumped right out of bed and shouted, "Yay! Park!" His voice was loud, like a roaring lion. ROAR! Mia covered her ears with a giggly smile and said, "Good morning, Leo! But remember, inside the house, we use our gentle talking voice so we do not wake the sleepy sleeping cat." Leo blinked and looked at Whiskers, who was curled up on the rug, snoring softly. Leo wanted to be a good friend to Whiskers. He took a big breath in, smelling a pretend flower, and let it out slowly like blowing out a candle. "Let's try again," Leo whispered softly. "Good morning, kitty." His voice was quiet and sweet, just like a soft breeze rustling through the leaves. Mia clapped her hands happily. "Wonderful job, Leo! You used your special talking voice!" At breakfast, Leo wanted some yummy banana slices. Instead of yelling across the kitchen, Leo walked right up to Mommy, gently tapped her arm, and used his clear talking voice. "May I please have a banana, Mommy?" Mommy beamed with pride and gave him a big hug. "Of course, my sweet boy. I love hearing your lovely talking voice." When they finally arrived at the park, Leo saw the big blue slide. He waited patiently for his turn, said "Excuse me" to a little friend, and used his happy talking voice to ask Mia to push him gently on the swings. Leo learned that using his talking voice made everyone feel happy, calm, and ready for fun adventures together. From that day on, Leo felt like a superhero of sounds, knowing just when to use his quiet indoor voice and his happy outdoor voice. The end.

stories.title: Maya asks for Help
stories.text: Deep in the playroom, Maya was building the tallest block tower in the whole wide world. She stacked a red square, a yellow triangle, and a big blue rectangle right on top. It was getting higher and higher, almost touching the ceiling! Maya was so focused. Suddenly, wobbled, wobble, CRASH! All the blocks tumbled down onto the soft carpet in a big colorful pile. Maya felt a hot, frustrated feeling in her tummy. She squeezed her eyes shut and wanted to let out a giant, loud squeal of frustration. But instead, Maya remembered the magic trick her teacher taught her at preschool. She opened her eyes, took a deep, calming breath, and let it out through her mouth. Then, Maya reached out for her favorite stuffed teddy bear and hugged him tight. Instead of crying or screaming, Maya decided to use her wonderful talking voice. She looked right at her daddy, who was sitting nearby reading a book, and spoke clearly. "Daddy, my tower fell down. Can you please help me build it again?" Daddy smiled a warm, loving smile and set his book down on the floor. "I would love to help you, Maya. Thank you so much for using your clear talking voice to ask me." Daddy and Maya sat down side by side on the soft rug. Together, they built an even bigger, stronger block tower with a bridge and a castle tower on top. Maya cheered softly, feeling so proud of herself. She realized that using her talking voice instead of yelling or grumbling was the best way to solve any problem. Daddy high-fived her tiny hand, and they both giggled as they knocked it down just to start all over again. The end.

stories.title: Oliver at the Library
stories.text: Oliver the little bunny rabbit loved storytime at the cozy neighborhood library. Today, the friendly librarian, Mrs. Gable, was reading a magical book about flying dragons and shiny stars. Oliver sat criss-cross-applesauce on the colorful rug, listening very closely. He saw a picture of a sparkly green dragon blowing bubbles instead of fire. Oliver was so thrilled that he wanted to tell his friend Lily all about it right that very second. He opened his mouth wide to shout across the room, "Look at the dragon!" But then he remembered where he was. The library was a quiet place where everyone used their gentle, quiet talking voices so that other friends could read peacefully. Oliver gently closed his mouth, tapped his chin, and leaned in close to Lily. He cupped his hand near her furry ear and whispered in his softest, kindest talking voice, "Look at the green dragon, Lily." Lily smiled brightly and whispered back, "He is so silly!" Mrs. Gable looked over at the two little bunnies and gave them a warm, approving nod for being so respectful. When storytime was all finished, it was time to pick out a brand new book to take home. Oliver wanted to find the book about dinosaurs. Instead of running around the shelves and yelling, Oliver walked slowly with his little paws holding onto Mommy's hand. He used his polite talking voice to ask, "Mommy, can we look for the dinosaur book on this shelf, please?" Mommy smiled down at her clever bunny and gently squeezed his hand. "Yes, Oliver, let's find it together." They found the big green dinosaur book, and Oliver whispered a happy thank you. He felt so proud of his wonderful talking voice. The end.

When I want to talk to you.
Use your words and tell me why,
We can wave the tears goodbye.

Now you speak so nice and sweet,
Making every moment neat.
Talking voices sound so grand,
Best invention in the land!

rhymes.title: Let Your Words Come Out
rhymes.text:
Are you mad or feeling sad?
That is totally not bad.
Just remember what to do,
Use your talking voice for you.

Stomping feet and making noise,
Doesn't help us share our toys.
Take a breath and count to three,
Say the words for you and me.

Tell me what is on your mind,
In a way so nice and kind.
Talking words can fix it all,
Even when you feel so small.

Now I hear you loud and plain,
Sun is shining through the rain.
Use your voice and share a smile,
We can chat a little while.

rhymes.title: The Talking Train
rhymes.text:
Chugga chugga, hear the sound,
Talking trains go all around.
Use your voice to say hello,
Watch the happy engine go.

Whisper low or speak right out,
There is never need to shout.
Just use words we understand,
Bestest speakers in the land.

Tell your teddy time for bed,
With the happy things you said.
Talking voices work so fast,
Making good times come and last.

Clap your hands and give a cheer,
For the voices we love near.
Use your words and sing along,
Now you know the talking song!

rhymes.title: Speak Up Sweetly
rhymes.text:
When you have a story grand,
Share it through the smiling land.
Use your talking voice to say,
Everything you think today.

Makes no sense to yell and scream,
Wake you from your sleepy dream.
Soft and gentle is the way,
We will talk throughout the day.

Ask for help when blocks fall down,
No need for a grumpy frown.
Say I need a little hand,
Building castles in the sand.

Words are magic, words are sweet,
Making every playtime neat.
Use your talking voice with pride,
With your helpers by your side.

rhymes.title: The Inside Voice Song
rhymes.text:
When we play inside the room,
We can sweep just like a broom.
Keep your voice so sweet and low,
Just like whispers soft and slow.

Shouting loud is for outside,
Where the big green hill is wide.
Inside here we talk so neat,
Making gentle words so sweet.

Use your talking voice with me,
Happy as a buzzing bee.
Say hello and say please too,
I am so proud now of you.

Soft and kind is how we speak,
Playing games throughout the week.
Clap your hands and sing along,
Now you know our gentle song.

rhymes.title: Inside and Outside Voices
rhymes.text:
Are you ready, girls and boys?
Let us use our quiet joys.
When we play upon the street,
We can stomp our little feet.

When we step into the door,
Walking softly on the floor,
Then we use our talking voice,
Making such a gentle choice.

No need to yell across the room,
Or make a loud and scary boom.
Just speak up so I can hear,
Words of kindness crystal clear.

Talking voice is best to share,
Showing friends you love and care.
Nod your head and smile today,
Listen to the words we say.

rhymes.title: The Gentle Talking Time
rhymes.text:
Little bird up in the tree,
Sing a gentle song to me.
We can talk and we can share,
Happy voices everywhere.

When you want a yellow toy,
Ask me nicely, little boy.
Use your talking voice to say,
Can we share and can we play?

Crying loud or making noise,
Does not help us share our toys.
Take a breath and count to three,
Speak so softly next to me.

Now your words are clear and bright,
Making everything feel right.
Talking voice is such a treat,
Keeping all our playtime sweet.

rhymes.title: Use Your Words Today
rhymes.text:
Stomp your feet and wiggle toes,
Touch the tip of tiny nose.
When you have a thing to say,
Use your talking voice today.

If you whine or if you scream,
Like a monster in a dream,
No one knows what you desire,
Stoking up a little fire.

Take a breath and use your tongue,
Every toddler, old and young.
Tell me what you want to do,
I am here to list to you.

Talking voice is strong and clear,
Music to a mommy's ear.
Say it kindly, nice and plain,
Sun comes shining through the rain.

rhymes.title: The Happy Talker
rhymes.text:
Happy faces all around,
Making such a lovely sound.
Talking voices shine so bright,
Morning, noon, and starry night.

When you speak so calm and clear,
Everybody wants to hear.
No more shouting in your play,
That is not the friendly way.

Use the voice that sounds so sweet,
Walking down the sunny street.
Ask for juice or ask for bread,
Right before you go to bed.

Good job using words so grand,
Best talker in all the land.
Give a cheer and give a hug,
Snuggle like a little bug.

stories.title: Sam's Sunny Yellow Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sam sat at the bright yellow table with a big piece of paper. He loved to draw big, happy suns. Today, he picked up his very favorite yellow crayon. It was long, smooth, and smelled just like paper. Sam pressed down hard to make the sun shine super bright. *SNAP!* Oh no! The yellow crayon broke into two pieces. One piece went this way, and the other piece went that way. Sam's bottom lip quivered, and he looked ready to cry. Big tears welled up in his eyes. Just then, gentle Mommy walked over and knelt down beside his chair. She gave Sam a warm, cozy hug and smiled a sweet smile. 'It is okay, my sweet Sam,' Mommy said softly. 'A broken crayon is not ruined at all. Look, now you have magic powers!' Sam sniffled and wiped his eyes. 'Magic?' he asked with a little wonder in his voice. 'Yes!' nodded Mommy. 'Now you have two crayons instead of one. You can share one with your friend, or use both hands to color twice as fast.' Sam looked at the two pieces of yellow crayon. A little smile crept onto his face. He picked up the short piece in his tiny fingers. It actually fit his hand so nicely! He pressed it gently onto the paper, and a beautiful, golden sunbeam appeared right away. Then he picked up the other piece and drew fluffy clouds. Sam giggled and clapped his hands together with joy. He did not need a long crayon to make wonderful art. His broken crayon made his drawing even more special because he made it all by himself. Mommy kissed the top of his head and told him how proud she was of his clever problem-solving. Sam felt so brave and happy as he colored his masterpiece all afternoon long.

stories.title: Maya and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Maya loved drawing colorful bridges that connected magical lands of unicorns and fluffy bunnies. Her crayon box was full of reds, blues, greens, and purples. Today, Maya reached for her bright blue crayon to make a sparkling river under her rainbow bridge. She gripped the crayon tightly in her fist and pressed down with all her might. *SNAP!* The blue crayon broke right in the middle. Maya gasped and looked down at the two halves resting on her paper. For a second, she felt a little sad because her favorite blue stick was shorter now. But Maya was a very smart toddler. She remembered what her big brother taught her about little accidents. Instead of getting upset, Maya took a deep breath and let out a little puff of air. 'Uh-oh,' Maya whispered to herself with a tiny giggle. Papa walked by and noticed the broken crayon. He crouched down to her eye level and gave her a gentle high-five. 'Oh, look at that, Maya!' Papa cheered. 'Your crayon multiplied! It has babies now.' Maya thought that was the funniest thing she had ever heard. She laughed out loud and picked up both pieces. 'One for the river, and one for the sky!' Maya declared proudly. She used the shorter piece to gently shade in the deep blue water, and the longer piece to color the bright blue sky above the bridge. Her picture looked more wonderful than ever. Maya felt so proud of her lovely artwork. She learned that a little break does not mean things are broken forever; sometimes, breaking things just means you get double the fun. She put the two blue pieces safely back into her crayon box, ready for her next big art adventure tomorrow.

stories.title: Leo's Little Green Helper
stories.text: Leo was sitting on his cozy blue rug, coloring a big picture of a jungle filled with roaring lions and tall, leafy trees. He needed a bright green crayon to make the tall grass where the friendly zebras play. He grabbed his green crayon and started coloring as fast as his little hand could go. *SNAP!* The green crayon snapped into two pieces with a tiny sound. Leo stopped coloring and stared at the pieces. The crayon was broken! Leo's shoulders slumped, and he felt a little frown forming on his face. He loved his long green crayon so much. Grandma heard the little snap from the kitchen and walked into the room with warm, loving eyes. She sat right down on the rug next to Leo and gave him a gentle squeeze. 'Did your crayon decide to turn into twins, Leo?' Grandma asked with a cheerful twinkle in her eye. Leo looked at the crayon, then looked up at Grandma, and his frown turned into a little grin. 'Twins!' Leo repeated happily. 'Yes, twins!' Grandma said. 'And you know what is wonderful about a shorter crayon? It is much easier for your growing fingers to hold control of it.' Leo picked up one piece of the green crayon. He wrapped his little fingers around it and made wavy lines for the grass. It felt so comfortable in his hand! Then he took the second piece and drew little green leaves on the trees. Leo was amazed at how well he could draw with his newly sized crayons. He didn't feel sad anymore at all. He felt like a big boy who could fix anything with a little imagination and a happy heart. Grandma kissed his cheek and told him what a fantastic artist he was. Leo beamed with pride and finished his wonderful jungle picture, adding extra green grass just for fun.

stories.title: Leo's Magic Blue Bridge
stories.text: Leo loved the color blue. Every single day, he used his favorite blue crayon to draw big, happy skies and zooming airplanes. But today, something surprising happened. Snap! Leo pressed just a little bit too hard on the paper, and his lovely blue crayon broke right in half. Oh no! Leo looked at the two little pieces on the table, and his lower lip started to wobble. A tiny tear peeked out from the corner of his eye. He felt so sad because his favorite crayon wasn't whole anymore. Just then, gentle footsteps walked into the room. It was Mommy. She sat down right beside Leo on the cozy little chair and gave him a warm, comforting hug. 'It is okay to feel sad when something we love gets broken, Leo,' Mommy whispered softly, wiping away his tiny tear with her gentle thumb. 'But look closely. You didn't lose your crayon. You actually found something wonderful. Now you have two blue crayons!' Leo blinked and looked down at the table. Mommy was right! He picked up the first piece in his little fingers and drew a fluffy cloud. Then, he picked up the second piece and drew a sparkling river right underneath it. 'Look, Mommy!' Leo giggled, his sad feelings turning completely into happy smiles. 'I made a magic blue bridge!' Leo discovered that accidents can lead to brand new adventures. He used both pieces of his broken crayon to finish his beautiful picture, pressing softly this time. From that day on, Leo knew that even when things broke, they could still be useful and make wonderful art. He clapped his hands together with joy, feeling so proud of his clever problem-solving. Being gentle with his crayons made drawing even more fun, and Leo's heart felt warm, bright, and completely happy for the rest of the sunny afternoon.

stories.title: Mia and the Sunshine Sunflowers
stories.text: Mia had a very important job to do today. She was going to draw a giant, bright yellow sunflower for Grandma's special birthday card. Mia picked up her big yellow crayon, her absolute favorite tool in the whole wide world, and began to scribble joyful circles on the paper. Swish, swish, went the crayon! She pressed down firmly to make the petals look extra bright and sunny. Suddenly, with a little click sound, the yellow crayon snapped into two pieces. Mia gasped and stopped drawing. Her eyes went wide, and she looked up at Daddy with a worried expression. 'Oh, Daddy, my crayon broke! Can we fix it?' Daddy smiled a big, reassuring smile and scooped Mia up onto his strong lap. 'We cannot glue it back together instantly, sweet girl, but guess what? Broken crayons still color just as beautifully,' Daddy explained in a warm, encouraging voice. Mia looked down at the two smaller pieces resting in her tiny hand. She decided to give it a try. She laid the long side of the broken yellow crayon flat against the paper and rubbed it gently. Wow! It made a wide, soft patch of sunshine yellow that looked just like a fluffy cloud of pollen. 'Look, Daddy! It makes a different kind of magic!' Mia cheered, her worries melting away like ice cream on a warm day. She used the second piece to draw tiny little dots for the sunflower's seeds right in the middle. The birthday card looked even more creative and special than Mia had originally planned. Grandma was going to love it so much! Mia learned that day that making a mistake or breaking a toy isn't the end of the world. With a little imagination and a positive attitude, any little hiccup can turn into something wonderful and fun.

stories.title: Sam's Rainbow Train
stories.text: Sam was sitting on the colorful playroom rug, busy as a little bee. He was drawing a long, chugging train that traveled all across the paper tracks. Sam loved his green crayon because it made the grassy hills where the train would travel. He pressed hard to make the grass super green. Crack! Uh oh. The green crayon broke right in the middle. Sam looked at the pieces and felt a little flutter of frustration in his tummy. He wanted his crayon to be whole. Teacher Anna walked over, knelt down on the soft rug, and shared a gentle, loving smile. 'Accidents happen to everyone, Sam, even grown-ups,' Teacher Anna said kindly. 'When a crayon breaks, it just means it is ready for a new job.' Sam took a deep breath and let his frustration float away. He picked up the broken pieces and looked at them with curious eyes. 'A new job?' Sam asked softly. 'Yes!' Teacher Anna nodded. 'Now you have two crayons to share with a friend, or you can use the flat edge to color big spaces super fast.' Sam thought that sounded like a brilliant idea. He used one piece to draw green bushes by the train tracks, and he handed the other piece to his friend Lily so she could color the leaves on the trees. Lily smiled big and said, 'Thank you, Sam!' Working together was so much fun, and the green crayon worked harder than ever before. Sam felt so proud of himself for staying calm and finding a creative way to keep playing. He hugged his friend, finished his wonderful train picture, and decided that broken crayons weren't bad at all—they were just little helpers in disguise.

stories.title: Leo's Magic Blue Crayon
stories.text: Leo loved drawing big blue oceans. Splash, splash, went his favorite blue crayon across the big white paper. He pressed down hard to make a happy whale swimming in the sea. Suddenly, there was a little snap! Oh no! The blue crayon broke into two separate pieces. Leo looked down, and his bottom lip started to quiver. Two big tears welled up in his eyes. His favorite crayon was broken. Mommy walked over softly and sat right down beside him on the warm rug. She gave him a gentle, loving hug and smiled. 'It is okay, sweet Leo,' Mommy whispered in a kind voice. 'Nothing is ruined. Look closely at what we have now. You do not have just one crayon anymore. You have two magic pieces!' Leo wiped his tears away with his soft sleeve and looked down at his hands. Mommy showed him how to hold the smaller piece gently between his thumb and fingers. 'Try coloring with the side of the paper wrapper,' she suggested brightly. Leo pressed the broken blue piece sideways onto the paper. Wow! It made a wide, beautiful, wavy ocean current that looked just like real ocean water moving in the breeze. Leo giggled with pure delight. He picked up the second piece and used it to draw tiny blue bubbles floating all around his happy whale. 'Two crayons!' Leo cheered proudly, clapping his hands together. He learned that sometimes, when things break, they can actually become twice as fun to use. Mommy kissed the top of his head as Leo kept on coloring his wonderful, bright blue sea with his two special crayon pieces.

stories.title: Mia and the Rainbow Collage
stories.text: Mia was sitting at her little yellow table, working very hard on a masterpiece. She was drawing a bright yellow sun high up in the sky. She pressed the yellow crayon down and round and round it went. But Mia was growing so strong, and she pressed just a little too hard. Snap! The yellow crayon broke right in the middle. Mia gasped and stared at the two pieces resting on her paper. She felt a little frustrated inside. Daddy walked by and noticed her frowning face. He knelt down beside her chair and gave her a warm, reassuring pat on the back. 'Oh look, Mia,' Daddy said with a big, cheerful smile. 'Your crayon went on an adventure! Sometimes things break when we are using all of our big-kid strength.' Mia looked at Daddy, and her frown slowly turned into a tiny smile. 'Can we still use them?' she asked softly. 'We sure can,' Daddy answered enthusiastically. 'In fact, we can make something extra special.' Daddy brought out a bottle of safe, sticky glue. He helped Mia squeeze a tiny dot of glue onto a brand new piece of paper. Then, Mia carefully pressed both broken pieces of the yellow sun right onto the page. But that was not all! Because she had two pieces now, she used them to color extra rays stretching all the way across the paper. 'Look, Daddy! My sun has double sunshine!' Mia shouted happily. She added pink and green crayons to the picture too. Mia felt so proud of her clever idea. Even though her crayon had broken, her artwork turned out even more creative and beautiful than before.

stories.title: Sam's Two-Handed Dinosaur
stories.text: Sam loved green crayons more than anything in the whole wide world. Today, he was drawing a giant, stomping green dinosaur with big sharp teeth. He pushed the crayon forward, making loud stomping noises with his mouth. Stomp, stomp, stomp! Crack went the green crayon. It snapped into two uneven pieces right on the table. Sam stopped coloring and looked at his hands. He felt a tiny bit sad because his favorite tool was broken. Grandma heard the little snap from the kitchen and walked over with warm, freshly baked cookies. She knelt down and smiled gently at Sam. 'Don't worry, little buddy,' Grandma said lovingly. 'Accidents happen to everyone, even grown-ups. And guess what? You are a great problem solver.' Sam blinked and looked down at the two pieces of green wax. 'How can I draw with two?' Sam asked curiously. Grandma gently took one piece in her right hand and the other piece in her left hand. 'You can share the fun with both hands!' Grandma explained happily. 'Hold one piece in this hand for the tail, and one piece in this hand for the head!' Sam’s eyes lit up with excitement. He grabbed a piece in each hand. With his left hand, he drew a long, bumpy green tail. With his right hand, he drew a big, friendly green head with a big smile. 'Look, Grandma! A two-handed dinosaur!' Sam laughed joyfully. He colored faster and faster, using both hands at the same time. Sam was so happy that his crayon had broken, because now he could make double the art in half the time!

stories.title: Leo's Magic Half-Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Leo sat at his low wooden table. A big box of bright crayons stood right in front of him. Leo pulled out his very favorite color. It was sunny yellow, bright like a smiley face. Leo loved the yellow crayon so much. He pressed down hard to draw a big, beautiful sun in the corner of his blue paper. Suddenly, there was a little snap sound. Oh no! The yellow crayon was not one long piece anymore. It was two little pieces! Leo looked down at his hands. His lower lip started to quiver just a tiny bit. Two big tears welled up in his big brown eyes because his favorite crayon was broken. Mommy walked over softly and gave Leo a warm, gentle hug. She smiled a big, happy smile and wiped away his tiny tear. Mommy said, 'Oh Leo, look! Your one crayon just turned into two magic crayons! Now you have double the fun.' Leo blinked and looked at his hands again. He picked up the first piece of yellow. Then he picked up the second piece of yellow. He pressed them both to the paper. Guess what? They still made the exact same bright, sunny yellow color! Leo giggled a happy giggle. He drew two suns instead of one in the corner of his paper. He gave Mommy a big high-five. Learning how to share your colors with two little pieces is so much fun. Leo felt so proud of his special magic half-crayons. He kept drawing all morning long, making sunny pictures for everyone in his family. The broken crayon was not broken at all; it was just extra special now. Leo smiled wide, feeling brave, smart, and so very happy with his colorful day.

stories.title: Maya and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: It was a cozy afternoon in the playroom. Maya was sitting on her fluffy green rug, coloring a long, winding rainbow. Red, orange, green, blue, and purple stripes danced across her large white paper. Maya reached deep into her box and pulled out her bright red crayon. She wanted to color a big red heart right in the middle of her rainbow. Maya pushed down with all her might. Crack! The red crayon broke right down the middle, splitting into two uneven pieces. Maya gasped and stared at the pieces lying on the rug. Her little shoulders slumped down. She felt sad because her favorite red tool was in pieces. Daddy sat down right next to her on the rug. He put his arm around her and whispered, 'It is okay to feel sad when something breaks, Maya, but let us look at what we can do now.' Daddy showed her how to hold the short piece sideways. Maya tried it. Wow! The side of the short red crayon made a wonderfully thick, wide stripe of red. Then she used the other piece to make pointy tips. 'Look, Daddy! I can color with both ends now!' Maya cheered. She realized that having two pieces meant she could color twice as fast. She used one piece for the top of the heart and the other piece for the bottom. Her heart turned out bigger and brighter than ever before. Maya clapped her hands together with joy. She gave Daddy a giant cuddle. Mistakes and little breaks happen to everyone, but Maya knew just how to fix them with a little bit of imagination. Her rainbow bridge looked magnificent, sparkling with red love hearts all along the way. Maya was a super-duper coloring champion today.

stories.title: Sam's Two-Handed Masterpiece
stories.text: The kitchen table was covered in big sheets of paper. Sam was busy making a drawing for his grandma. He loved Grandma very much. Sam picked up a lovely green crayon to draw tall, swaying grass for a friendly dinosaur. He pressed down with all his might to make the grass strong and tall. Snap! The green crayon snapped into two pieces. One piece rolled to the left, and the other piece rolled to the right. Sam looked at his hands. He felt a little bit frustrated because the crayon did not stay one long stick. Grandpa was sitting right across the table, sipping his warm tea. Grandpa chuckled a warm, kind chuckle and said, 'Sammy, my boy, you are so strong! You broke that crayon with your mighty dinosaur muscles.' Sam giggled. That made him feel very strong indeed. Grandpa said, 'Now you have two crayons. You can draw with both hands at the exact same time.' Sam opened his eyes wide. Could he really? He picked up the left piece with his left hand. He picked up the right piece with his right hand. Ready, set, go! Sam scribbled with his left hand, making swishy green grass. Then he scribbled with his right hand, making even more swishy green grass. Green zig-zags flew across the paper like magic. The dinosaur picture looked alive and amazing. Sam grinned from ear to ear. He held up both hands to show Grandpa his super-cool trick. Breaking a crayon was not a sad thing at all; it was an invitation to try something new and wonderful. Sam finished his masterpiece with a happy heart, ready to give the best dinosaur drawing ever to his grandma.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo sat at his bright yellow table. He had a big piece of paper and a box of chunky, wonderful crayons. Leo loved the color blue the most. He picked up the bright blue crayon to draw a giant, happy sky. He pressed down hard, because he wanted the sky to be very bright and cheerful. Suddenly, with a little *snap*, the blue crayon broke right in the middle! Oh no! Leo looked down at the two pieces in his hands. His lower lip started to tremble just a tiny bit. He felt a little sad because his favorite crayon was broken. But then, Mama walked over and kneeled down beside his chair. She gave him a warm, cozy hug. 'It is okay, my sweet Leo,' Mama whispered softly with a big smile. 'A broken crayon is not ruined at all. Look, now you have two little blue helpers instead of one!' Leo blinked away his little frown and looked closely at the pieces. Mama showed him how he could use the long side of the crayon to color a wide, soft cloudless sky, and the short piece to make little blue birds flying way up high. Leo giggled. He tried it out. Scribble, scribble, went the long piece. Tap, tap, went the short piece. His drawing was turning out even better than before! Leo felt so proud. He did not need a whole crayon to make something magical happen. He had two pieces, and that meant double the fun. He finished his beautiful picture, adding green grass and a smiling yellow sun. When Daddy came home, Leo pointed right to the sky and said, 'Look! My blue crayon broke, but I made two helpers!' Daddy clapped his hands and cheered. Leo learned that little mistakes are just new ways to play and create. He put both blue pieces gently back into his crayon box, ready for his next big art adventure tomorrow. The end.

stories.title: Maya's Sunny Sunflower
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! Little Maya was sitting on her cozy rug, coloring a picture of a giant flower for Grandma. She chose a brilliant yellow crayon to make the big petals shine like the morning sun. Maya drew a big circle and started coloring fast, fast, fast. *Snap!* The yellow crayon broke into two pieces right on the paper. Maya stopped coloring and looked at the pieces. Her eyes got wide. She felt a little flutter of worry in her tummy. 'Oh, oh,' Maya said softly. She held up the broken pieces. Papa walked by and saw Maya looking down. He sat down right next to her on the rug and smiled. 'Did your crayon turn into twins, Maya?' Papa asked gently. Maya giggled a little bit at that funny word. 'Twins!' she said. Papa nodded. 'Yes! Now you have one piece for your left hand and one piece for your right hand, or you can share with your paper.' Maya loved that idea. She took the long piece of yellow and used the flat side to shade the big, round center of the flower. Then, she took the shorter piece and used the pointy tip to draw little sunshine rays shooting out all around the edges. It was so easy and so much fun! Maya worked very hard, making her flower bright and yellow and full of love. When she finished, it was the prettiest sunflower in the whole wide world. She hugged Papa and thanked him for helping her see the magic in her broken crayon. Maya learned that when something breaks, it is not the end of the world. Sometimes, it just means you get to do things in a brand new way. She proudly signed her name with a wiggle and a squiggle, excited to give her masterpiece to Grandma later that afternoon. The end.

stories.title: Sam's Red Firetruck
stories.text: Vroom, vroom! Little Sam was zooming a pretend firetruck across the living room floor before sitting down at his little red desk to draw a real one. He grabbed his favorite red crayon, ready to make the biggest, fastest firetruck ever seen. Sam pressed down with all his might to make the red super bright. *Crack!* The red crayon snapped into two pieces. Sam let out a little gasp. He looked at the long piece, and then at the short piece rolling on the desk. He felt a little grumpy. Why did it have to break? Grandma was sitting nearby, knitting a warm scarf. She looked up and saw Sam's furrowed brow. She put her knitting down and came over with gentle, loving eyes. 'Ah, look at that, Sam,' Grandma said cheerfully. 'Your red crayon just decided to grow a friend!' Sam looked up and smiled a tiny bit. 'A friend?' he asked. 'Yes,' Grandma nodded. 'And now you can color twice as fast.' Sam thought about that. He picked up the short piece in his little fingers and used it to color in the wheels of the firetruck. Then, he picked up the long piece and used it to color the big, shiny body of the truck. Back and forth, back and forth went the red crayon pieces. Sam felt so clever. He didn't need to be upset at all. The broken crayon worked just as well, and drawing with two pieces felt like a special secret game. He added a big red ladder and a flashing red light on top. When he was all done, Sam held up his picture and roared like a loud firetruck siren. 'Wee-woo, wee-woo! Look at my truck, Grandma!' Grandma cheered loudly and clapped her hands. Sam felt so happy and proud of himself. He learned that even when things break, a positive attitude and a little imagination can fix everything right up. He carefully put both red pieces to bed in their crayon box, knowing they were still his best coloring buddies. The end.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo sat at the bright yellow table with a big piece of paper. He loved coloring. Today, Leo wanted to draw a giant sky, so he picked up his favorite blue crayon. He pressed down hard because he wanted the sky to be very, very blue. SNAP! Oh no! The blue crayon broke right in the middle into two smaller pieces. Leo looked at the two little pieces, and his lower lip started to wobble. A little tear popped into his eye. But then, Mommy walked over with a warm, gentle smile and gave him a big, soft hug. 'It is okay, sweet Leo,' Mommy said softly. 'Things break sometimes, and that is not your fault.' Leo wiped his eye and looked down at his crayon pieces. Mommy showed him a magical trick. She took one piece of the blue crayon and laid it flat on its side. When Leo pushed it gently, it made a wide, beautiful patch of blue! It looked just like a fluffy cloud floating in the sky. Then, Leo took the other small piece and used the pointy tip to draw zooming airplanes flying way up high. Leo giggled. Having two pieces meant he could share one with his baby sister, Mia, who was sitting right next to him. Mia clapped her little hands and picked up the other blue piece to draw some squiggly rain. Leo smiled big and bright. His crayon was broken, but it did not ruin his drawing at all. In fact, it made drawing even more fun because now they had two crayons to play with together. Leo felt so proud of his clever brain for figuring out a new way to use his broken crayon. He finished his whole picture, filling the paper with happy blue skies and zooming airplanes. When it was time to clean up, Leo carefully put both little blue pieces back into his special crayon box, ready for another fun drawing adventure tomorrow.

stories.title: Maya's Sunny Sunflower
stories.text: Maya was sitting on her cozy bedroom rug, working on a very special picture for Grandma. She was drawing a big, happy sunflower with bright yellow petals. Maya loved yellow. It was the color of sunshine and warm buttered toast. She picked up her long yellow crayon and began to color in the center of the flower. She pushed and pushed with all her might. Suddenly, there was a little sound: snap! The yellow crayon was broken into two uneven pieces. Maya gasped. She looked at the crayon, and then she looked at her drawing. She felt a little frustrated inside. Her crayon was not long anymore! Just then, Daddy walked into the room, smelling like fresh soap. He knelt down beside her on the rug and scooped her up into his lap. 'Did your crayon take a little rest, Maya?' Daddy asked with a kind, silly voice. Maya giggled and nodded. Daddy explained that even when crayons break, they still have lots of magic left inside them. 'Look,' Daddy said, showing her how to hold the shorter piece of the crayon. 'Because it is shorter, it is much easier for your little fingers to hold tightly.' Maya tried it out. She took the small piece and used the flat side to make a wonderful, textured sunbeam. It looked even cooler than a regular line! Then, she used the other piece to color the rest of the flower petals. The sunflower looked bright, warm, and full of life. Maya felt so happy and proud. She learned that a broken crayon is not broken forever; it just changes shape to help you create something different. She added a big green stem and some green leaves with her other crayons. When Grandma came over later that afternoon, Maya proudly handed her the sunflower picture. Grandma smiled a huge smile and gave Maya a big kiss on the cheek, saying it was the most beautiful sunflower she had ever seen in her whole life.

stories.title: Sam's Red Firetruck
stories.text: Sam lovedfiretrucks. He loved the big red trucks that went wee-ooo, wee-ooo down the street. Today, Sam was drawing his very own firetruck on a large sheet of white paper. He had his bright red crayon ready in his hand. He was coloring the big wheels and the long ladder, and then he started coloring the heavy truck body. He pressed very hard, going fast and slow, fast and slow. SNAP! The red crayon broke right in two. Sam stopped coloring and looked at his hands. One piece was in his left hand, and one piece was in his right hand. Sam let out a little sigh because he thought his firetruck was ruined. But Grandma was sitting right across the table, ready with a cheerful smile. 'Oh, look, Sam! Your firetruck has two pieces now, just like a train with an engine and a caboose!' Grandma said cheerfully. Sam smiled at that silly idea. Grandma gently reminded him that making mistakes or having things break is just a normal part of making art. She showed him how to use the side of the broken red crayon to fill in the big spaces of the truck quickly and smoothly. Sam tried it, and swish, swish went the red crayon across the paper. The color filled in the white spaces like magic. Then, Sam used the pointy tip of the other red piece to draw flashing red lights on top of the truck. The picture looked amazing! Sam felt a wave of happy confidence wash over him. He did not need a long crayon to make a wonderful picture; his own imagination was all he needed. When the picture was all done, Sam held it up high and made a loud firetruck sound: 'Wee-ooo, wee-ooo!' Grandma clapped and cheered for his hard work. Sam carefully put his two red crayon pieces to bed in their box, feeling happy, clever, and ready for his next creative project.

stories.title: Sam's Sunny Yellow Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a time, in a cozy little yellow house, lived a happy little boy named Sam. Sam loved to draw more than anything in the whole wide world. Every single afternoon, he would sit at his little blue table with his big box of colorful crayons and make wonderful masterpieces for Mommy and Daddy. Today, Sam reached for his absolute favorite crayon. It was the bright, sunny yellow crayon. It was his favorite because it looked just like the warm morning sun and made the happiest smiley faces on the paper. Sam held the yellow crayon tightly in his small hand and pressed it down hard to draw a giant, glowing sun in the corner of his picture. Suddenly, with a little *snap*, the crayon broke right in half. Oh no! Sam looked down at the two little pieces lying on the table. His bottom lip quivered just a tiny bit, and he felt a little sad. Mommy walked over quietly, sat down right beside him, and gave him a big, warm hug. She whispered, 'Oh, Sam, it is okay to feel sad when something breaks. But look! Now we have two sunshine pieces instead of one.' Sam blinked away his tears and looked closely. Mommy showed him how he could use the long side to color big spaces, and the short piece to color special corners. Sam smiled a big, proud smile. He picked up both pieces of his yellow crayon and went right back to drawing. He drew extra sunshine rays all over his paper, and they looked even brighter than before. Sam learned that sometimes, a broken thing can turn into two wonderful new adventures. He clapped his hands and gave Mommy another big hug, feeling so proud of his clever problem-solving self.

stories.title: Mia's Magic Blue Sky
stories.text: Every morning after breakfast, a cheerful little girl named Mia loved to color pictures of the big blue sky. She had a favorite blue crayon that she used every single day to make puffy clouds and flying birds. Her blue crayon was getting smaller and smaller, but Mia loved it just the same. One sunny Tuesday, Mia was pressing her blue crayon down on the paper to make a deep blue ocean for a little paper whale. She pressed a little too hard, and—*snap*—the blue crayon broke right in the middle. Mia gasped and stared at the two pieces. For a second, she felt a little rumble of frustration in her tummy. Her big brother, Leo, walked by and smiled gently. 'Don't worry, Mia!' Leo said with a kind voice. 'Broken crayons still work just as well, and now you can share with a friend!' Mia thought about this for a moment. Her frustration melted away, replaced by a warm, happy feeling. She picked up the larger piece of the blue crayon and used it to shade the big, beautiful ocean waves. Then, she picked up the smaller piece and handed it to Leo. 'You can use this piece to draw a little blue fish in the water!' Mia said happily. Leo took the small piece, and together, they worked side by side, coloring the most wonderful ocean picture anyone had ever seen. Mia realized that a broken crayon wasn't ruined at all. In fact, it made art time even more fun because she got to share her favorite color with her big brother. They hung their special picture right on the refrigerator, where it made everyone smile all day long.

stories.title: Leo's Red Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Leo was a busy little boy who loved building tall towers with blocks and coloring bright, bold pictures. Today, Leo was working on a magnificent, colorful rainbow. He had red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple crayons lined up neatly like little soldiers on his table. When it was time to add the bright red arch to the very top of his rainbow, Leo picked up his red crayon. He reached up high and pressed down with all his might. *Crack!* The red crayon snapped into two pieces, and one piece rolled right off the table and hid under the couch! Leo looked at the half-crayon in his hand and sighed. He felt a little bit discouraged because his red arch was only half-finished. Grandma heard the little sigh and walked over with a gentle, loving smile. 'Oh, my sweet Leo,' Grandma said softly, 'let us find the other piece and see what we can do!' Grandma knelt down and peeked under the couch, safely retrieving the missing red piece. Then, she brought both pieces back to the table. 'See, Leo? Now you have a Mommy red crayon and a baby red crayon.' Leo giggled at Grandma's funny idea. He decided to use the Mommy piece to finish the big red rainbow arch, and he used the baby piece to color tiny red strawberries in the grass at the bottom of his drawing. Leo felt so proud of his clever artwork. He gave Grandma a huge squeeze and whispered, 'Thank you for helping me fix my red crayon, Grandma.' From that day on, whenever Leo used his crayons, he knew that a little snap was never the end of the story—it was just the beginning of something new and creative.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo sat at the bright yellow table with his favorite blue crayon. He was coloring a big, fluffy sky for his happy paper turtle. Leo pushed down hard. *Snap!* Oh no! The blue crayon broke into two pieces. Leo looked down. His lower lip started to quiver, and his big brown eyes filled with surprise. Mommy walked over softly and gave him a gentle hug. She smiled a warm, cozy smile and said, 'It is okay, Leo! Accidents happen when we are busy making art.' Leo wiped his nose and looked at the two pieces. Mommy gently took one piece and showed him a secret trick. 'Look! Now you have two blue crayons instead of one!' Leo clapped his hands with glee. He used the flat side of the first piece to color the wide clouds softly. Then, he used the second, smaller piece to draw little blue raindrops near the turtle's feet. *Tap, tap, tap,* went the crayon. Leo giggled. His picture looked even more magical and special than before. He learned that a broken crayon was not ruined at all. It just meant he could color in brand new ways. Leo beamed with pride and gave Mommy another big hug. 'I did it!' he cheered. Mommy nodded proudly. They finished the wonderful blue sky together, side by side, feeling happy, calm, and ready for their next cozy craft time adventure.

stories.title: Maya's Sunny Sunflower
stories.text: Sunny morning sunlight streamed through the window where Maya sat with her bright yellow crayon. She was drawing a giant sunflower for Grandma. Maya pressed down with all her might to make the petals super bright. *Snap!* The yellow crayon broke right in the middle! Maya gasped. Her shoulders slumped down. She felt a little sad because her favorite crayon was in two pieces. Daddy knelt down beside her chair. He patted her soft curls and whispered, 'Let's take a deep breath together, Maya.' They both breathed in deep like smelling a flower, and breathed out slow like blowing out a candle. Maya felt much better. Daddy picked up the broken pieces. 'You know what? Breaking means we have double the fun!' Maya tilted her head. Daddy handed her both pieces. Maya tried holding the short piece in her tiny fingers. It felt funny, but it worked! She colored the left side of the petal with the top piece, and the right side with the bottom piece. *Scribble, scribble, scratch.* The sunflower looked so bright and cheerful, just like the real sun outside. Maya smiled a big, proud smile. She showed Daddy her lovely artwork. 'Look, Daddy! Two crayons make double yellow!' Daddy cheered and high-fived her little hand. Maya felt so smart and happy. She knew that even if things break sometimes, she can always find a clever way to keep on creating her wonderful masterpieces.

stories.title: Sam's Red Apple
stories.text: Little Sam sat on his green rug, coloring a big red apple in his shiny new coloring book. He loved the color red so much. He pushed the red crayon down on the paper, rocking it back and forth. *Snap!* The red crayon broke into two pieces with a little soft sound. Sam blinked. He looked at the long piece and the short piece lying on the rug. For a second, Sam felt a little frustrated. Grandma walked over with a gentle, loving smile. She sat down right beside him on the green rug. 'Oh, Sam, look at that! Your crayon worked so hard it split into twins!' Grandma said cheerfully. Sam giggled at that funny idea. Grandma showed him how to hold the short piece sideways to color big spaces super fast. *Whoosh, whoosh!* The apple's big round tummy turned bright red in no time. Then, Sam used the longer piece to draw the little stem and outline the edges carefully. *Tap, tap, trace.* Sam worked with such focus and care. When he finished, the apple looked sweet, juicy, and delicious. Sam held up the picture to show Grandma. 'I made a red apple with my twin crayons!' he shouted happily. Grandma kissed his forehead. Sam felt so proud of his clever problem-solving. He hugged his broken red crayons, knowing they were still his very best friends for making art.

stories.title: Leo's Magic Little Blue
stories.text: Leo loved the color blue. Every single day, he used his favorite blue crayon to draw big, happy skies and zooming airplanes. One sunny morning, Leo pressed down just a little bit too hard on his paper. Crack went the crayon! Oh no. Leo looked down, and his big blue crayon was now two little blue crayons. His lower lip started to wobble, and he felt a tiny tear pop into his eye. Mommy came over and kneeled down beside him. She gave him a warm, gentle hug and smiled. 'It is okay, Leo,' Mommy said softly. 'Broken does not mean it is all done. It just means we have twice as much magic to share!' Leo blinked his big brown eyes and looked at the two pieces. Mommy showed him how to hold one piece in his tiny fingers and press gently. Guess what? It still made a bright, beautiful blue line! Leo giggled. He picked up the second piece and gave it to his stuffed bear, Barnaby. 'Look, Barnaby, now you have a crayon, too!' Leo cheered. Together, Leo and Barnaby drew a huge ocean full of splashing whales. Leo realized that having two small crayons was actually twice as fun as having one big one. He clapped his hands and smiled a big, proud smile. He learned that when things break, we can find a new way to play. The rest of the morning was filled with colorful joy, and Leo felt so happy and proud of his clever problem-solving fingers. From that day on, whenever a crayon snapped, Leo never cried. He just smiled, shared the piece, and kept right on creating his wonderful masterpieces.

stories.title: Maya and the Sunshine Sun
stories.text: Maya was sitting at her little wooden table, working very hard on a picture for her grandma. She was drawing a giant, glorious sun with her favorite yellow crayon. She colored in circles, round and round, making the paper glow like a warm summer day. But then, snap! The yellow crayon broke right in the middle. Maya stopped. She looked at the two pieces sitting on her paper. For a second, Maya felt a little bit frustrated because her tool looked different now. Daddy walked by, carrying a basket of laundry, and stopped to see what was wrong. He knelt down to her eye level and gave her a reassuring pat on the back. 'Maya, look at that,' Daddy said cheerfully. 'Your crayon turned into a helper duo!' Maya tilted her head, wondering what Daddy meant. 'Try holding both pieces together, side by side,' Daddy suggested. Maya picked up both little yellow pieces and pressed them against the paper at the same time. Swish, swish went the yellow! The sun looked even bigger and brighter than before because she could cover more space with two hands. Maya's eyes lit up with pure delight. 'Look, Daddy! I have double sun power!' she exclaimed, bouncing up and down in her chair. Daddy laughed and kissed the top of her head. 'You sure do, my clever girl.' Maya finished her sunshine picture, adding lots of sparkly glitter stickers to celebrate her victory. She felt so proud of herself for not giving up when the crayon broke. When Grandma received the picture in the mail a few days later, she called to say it was the brightest sun she had ever seen. Maya smiled proudly, remembering how her broken crayon helped her make the best art ever.

stories.title: Sam's Mighty Green Tree
stories.text: Sam loved trees. He loved tall trees, short trees, and green, leafy trees. Today, Sam had a big mission. He was going to draw a giant forest on a giant piece of paper using his bright green crayon. He colored fast and furiously, making swoosh-swoosh sounds with his wrist. Snap! The green crayon broke into two pieces right on the sidewalk. Sam stopped his swooshing. He looked at the broken crayon and let out a little sigh. Big brother Toby walked over with a snack. 'Hey, Sam-Sam, did your green crayon take a little nap?' Toby asked with a kind grin. Sam nodded slowly. 'It broke, Toby. Now it is ruined.' Toby shook his head gently. 'Not ruined at all, buddy. In the big art world, we call that a happy accident!' Toby showed Sam how to use the flat side of the broken crayon to make wide, fuzzy leaf stamps instead of thin lines. Sam tried it out. Press, lift, press, lift! Wow! The crayon made the most amazing fluffy green bushes and tree tops he had ever seen. Sam giggled and clapped his hands together. 'Look, Toby! I made a bumpy bush!' Sam shouted happily. Toby high-fived him. 'You are an amazing artist, Sam.' Sam spent the rest of the afternoon making the most magnificent forest filled with bumpy bushes, tall trunks, and green grass. He realized that a broken crayon was not a bad thing at all; it just showed him a brand new, super-cool way to draw. Sam packed up his crayons at cleanup time, feeling so happy, confident, and ready for his next big art adventure.

stories.title: Leo's Magic Half-Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Leo sat at his low wooden table. A big box of bright crayons was open right in front of him. 'I am going to draw a giant blue sky,' Leo whispered with a big happy smile. He reached down and picked up his absolute favorite bright blue crayon. He pressed it hard onto the paper to make a big, bold cloud. *SNAP!* Oh no! The blue crayon broke right in half. Two little pieces rolled on the table. Leo looked down and his bottom lip started to tremble. A little tear popped into his eye. 'Oh dear,' said Mommy, walking over with a warm and gentle hug. 'Is everything okay, Leo?' Leo pointed a tiny finger at the broken crayon. 'It's broken. It's ruined.' Mommy smiled softly and wiped away the tear. 'It is not ruined at all, sweet boy. Look what just happened. Now, instead of having one crayon, you have two magic half-crayons! One for each hand.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. He picked up the first piece in his left hand and the second piece in his right hand. He pressed them both to the paper at the same time. *Swoosh, swoosh!* Two blue lines danced across the page like happy little train tracks. Leo giggled. 'Look, Mommy! Two trains!' 'You did it, Leo,' Mommy cheered. 'You solved the puzzle all by yourself.' Leo felt so proud inside his chest. He colored the rest of the morning away, making a wonderful picture with his wonderful little halves. When snack time came, he carefully put both pieces back into the box, ready for more fun tomorrow.

stories.title: Maya and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Maya loved coloring more than anything in the whole wide world. Today, she was drawing a magical castle for her favorite teddy bear. She picked up her sunny yellow crayon to color the big castle towers. She pressed down firmly because she wanted the yellow to be super bright. *CRACK!* The yellow crayon snapped right in the middle. Maya stopped coloring and stared at the two pieces. Her shoulders slumped down. 'My yellow is broken,' she said in a tiny, sad voice. Her big brother Sam came running over to see what was wrong. 'Did something happen?' he asked kindly. Maya held up the two pieces. 'I broke it.' Sam gave her a gentle pat on the head. 'That is okay, Maya-bear. Crayons break sometimes because they work so hard making our pictures pretty. But guess what? Broken crayons are actually super-duper special.' Maya tilted her head. 'They are?' 'Yes!' Sam said with an encouraging grin. 'Now you can share. You can use the top piece, and I can use the bottom piece.' Maya looked at the short piece in her hand. A smile began to spread across her rosy cheeks. 'Can we make a rainbow bridge?' she asked. 'We sure can,' Sam answered. Maya took her piece and started coloring the left side of the bridge. Sam took his piece and colored the right side. Their hands met right in the middle of the paper, making a giant, beautiful yellow arch. Maya clapped her hands together with joy. 'We made a bridge together!' She felt so happy and warm inside. Breaking a crayon wasn't bad at all; it was just a new way to share a wonderful adventure with her big brother.

stories.title: Toby's Two-Handed Tree
stories.text: Toby was having a wonderful time drawing a big green tree in his special notebook. He had big green leaves, brown branches, and even a friendly little bird sitting on top. 'Time for the trunk!' Toby said happily. He reached into his crayon box and pulled out a long, sturdy brown crayon. He pushed down hard to make the tree trunk strong and thick. *SNAP!* The brown crayon broke into two uneven pieces with a little soft sound. Toby looked down at the pieces. For a second, he felt a little frustrated. He took a deep breath, just like his teacher taught him at preschool. In and out. In and out. Daddy walked over and kneeled down beside Toby's chair. 'How is the big tree coming along, buddy?' Daddy asked in a soothing, happy voice. Toby held up the broken brown pieces. 'I pushed too hard, Daddy. The crayon broke.' Daddy nodded and gave Toby a reassuring squeeze on his shoulder. 'That happens when we put our strong muscles to work, Toby. You are getting so big and strong! But do you know a secret? A broken crayon still colors just as beautifully as a whole one.' Toby looked at the pieces, then looked back at his picture. 'Really?' 'Really and truly,' Daddy smiled. 'Why don't you try holding one piece in your fist? It makes coloring big spaces super easy.' Toby tried it. He grabbed the shorter piece and used his whole hand to shade in the tree trunk. It was so fast and so much fun! *Scratch, scratch, scratch!* The trunk filled up with rich, warm brown color. Toby grinned from ear to ear. 'Look, Daddy! I used my strong muscles!' 'You sure did, superstar,' Daddy cheered. Toby proudly finished his tree, feeling so clever for turning a little oops into a wonderful masterpiece.

stories.title: Sammy's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy sat at the little red table with his favorite blue crayon. 'Squeak, squeak, scribble,' went the blue crayon as Sammy drew a big, happy sky for his paper. He pressed down just a little bit too hard because he was so excited, and with a soft little *snap*, the blue crayon broke right in half. Oh no! Sammy looked down at the two pieces. His bottom lip quivered, and he felt a big bubble of frustration in his tummy. But then, big sister Maya walked by and smiled a warm, gentle smile. 'It is okay, Sammy,' she said softly. 'Broken does not mean it is broken forever. Now you have two magic pieces instead of one.' Sammy wiped his eyes and looked closely at the two pieces. Maya showed him how to hold the top piece in his fingers and the bottom piece in his other hand. Suddenly, Sammy gasped with delight! He could color with the pointy tip, and then he could turn the other piece sideways to color big, wide fluffy clouds. 'Look, Maya! Two crayons!' Sammy giggled, feeling very proud of his clever hands. He finished his picture with a bright blue sky and fluffy white clouds made by two happy crayon pieces. When cleanup time came, Sammy carefully put both pieces back into his special green crayon box, ready for a brand new adventure tomorrow. Taking a deep breath helped him solve his problem, and he knew he could try again whenever something unexpected happened. Great job, Sammy, for being such a flexible thinker and keeping your positive attitude all morning long. Every little mistake is just a new way to learn something wonderful and bright.

stories.title: Leo and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Leo loved drawing colorful bridges. Today, he chose his brightest yellow crayon to make a golden bridge for a tiny toy car to drive across. He colored fast and furiously, making zooming sounds with his mouth. *Zzzzoom!* Suddenly, the yellow crayon made a funny little click sound and snapped right down the middle. Leo stopped zooming.
