He stared at the two pieces sitting quietly on his paper. For a second, he felt a little sad because his longest crayon was now two short ones. But Leo remembered what his teacher whispered at preschool: when things change, we can find a new way to play. Taking a deep breath, Leo picked up the shorter piece. He noticed how easy it fit right inside his tiny toddler fist. 'Two crayons are better than one!' Leo cheered softly to himself. He used the first piece to draw the golden bridge, and then he used the second piece to draw little golden stars shining down from above the bridge. The picture looked even more magical than he had planned. Mommy walked over and gave him a big hug. 'Look at how creative you are, Leo! You turned a little hiccup into a masterpiece.' Leo beamed with pride. He learned that mistakes are not bad at all; they just give us a chance to try something totally different and fun. As he put his crayons away in their tidy little row, he felt so happy and capable. Good for you, Leo, for turning a broken crayon into a sky full of shining stars with your wonderful, helpful imagination.

stories.title: Mia's Two-Tone Flower
stories.text: Mia was sitting on her cozy rug, coloring a big red flower for her grandmother. She loved the bright red color so much. She pressed the red crayon down, moving it in big circles. *Press, press, swirl.* All of a sudden, *snap!* The red crayon broke into two pieces right under her fingers. Mia blinked in surprise. She looked at the pieces, and for a tiny moment, she felt like she might pout. But Mia was a great problem solver. Daddy sat down beside her on the rug and gave her a reassuring pat on the back. 'Oh look, Mia,' Daddy said gently. 'Now you have a short piece and a long piece.' Mia looked closer and smiled. An idea popped into her head like a bright lightbulb. She took the short piece of red and used it to color the petals nice and dark. Then, she picked up the other piece of red and used the flat side to make a lovely, soft pinkish-red background all around the flower petals. It looked like a sunset! 'Daddy, look! I made a two-tone flower!' Mia clapped her hands together happily. She felt so proud that she did not give up when her crayon broke. Instead, she used her bright ideas to make her drawing even more special and unique than before. When she gave the picture to Grandma later that afternoon, Grandma said it was the most beautiful flower she had ever seen. Mia smiled a big, proud smile, knowing that little bumps in the road just lead to wonderful new adventures. You did a fantastic job staying positive and creative, Mia, showing everyone how to turn a broken moment into a beautiful masterpiece.

stories.title: Leo's Magic Half-Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Leo sat at his low wooden table. He had a big piece of paper and a box of bright, shiny crayons. 'Time to color a happy sun!' Leo whispered to himself. He reached into the box and pulled out his very favorite color. It was sunny yellow, bright like a real morning. Leo held the crayon tight in his little fist and pressed down hard on the paper. *Snap!* Oh no. The yellow crayon broke into two pieces. One big piece stayed in his hand, and a little piece rolled away onto the floor. Leo’s bottom lip began to tremble. A little tear popped into his eye because his favorite crayon was broken. Mommy walked over softly and sat right down beside him on the small chair. She gave him a warm, gentle hug. 'It is okay, Leo,' Mommy said softly with a big, loving smile. 'A broken crayon is not ruined at all. Look, now you have two magic pieces instead of one!' Leo wiped his tear away and looked down at his hands. Mommy showed him how to hold the short piece on its side to color big, fluffy yellow clouds, and the other piece to make pointy sun rays. Leo giggled. Coloring with two pieces was actually super fun! He pressed both crayons down and made the brightest, happiest sun in the whole wide world. He was so proud of his clever fix. Mommy clapped her hands, and Leo beamed with joy. He learned that accidents are just a chance to try something new. With a happy heart, Leo colored all morning long, using his special two-part magic crayon to make a whole galaxy of bright yellow stars.

stories.title: Maya and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Little Maya loved to draw pictures of her kitty cat. Every afternoon after her nap, she would take out her big red crayon and draw long, sweeping tails and wiggly whiskers. Today, Maya wanted to draw a magnificent rainbow arching over her kitty. She picked up her sparkling purple crayon. She pressed it down to make the top stripe of her rainbow. *Snap!* The purple crayon broke right in the middle. Maya gasped. She looked at the two little sticks resting on her paper. Her shoulders slumped down, and she felt a little sad because her favorite purple line was interrupted. Daddy walked by and noticed the tiny frown on her face. He knelt down to her eye level and smiled warmly. 'Oh, look at that, Maya!' Daddy said in an encouraging voice. 'You have two purple crayons now. That means double the fun!' Maya tilted her head and thought about it. She picked up the first piece and drew a fluffy purple cloud. Then, she picked up the second piece and drew tiny purple raindrops falling down. 'Look, Daddy! It is raining purple sparkles!' Maya cheered, her sadness completely melting away. Daddy praised her for having such a wonderful imagination. Maya felt so brave and smart. She realized that even when things break, she can still make something wonderful and beautiful. She finished her entire picture, adding green, blue, and orange, too. Her fridge was soon decorated with her masterpiece, and every time she looked at the broken purple crayon marks, she smiled, knowing that she turned a little hiccup into a colorful work of art. She was a true little artist!

stories.title: Sam's Two-Handed Masterpiece
stories.text: Sam was having the best time drawing dinosaurs on his big blue rug. He had green crayons, orange crayons, and a big strong blue crayon. He was drawing a giant T-Rex with huge, stomping feet. Sam pressed down with his green crayon to make the dinosaur's bumpy back. *Crack!* The green crayon snapped into two uneven pieces. Sam stopped and blinked. He looked at the broken pieces and let out a little sigh. He felt a bit frustrated because his dinosaur was only halfway done. Big sister Lily was sitting nearby reading a book, and she looked over with a kind smile. 'Hey Sam, do you want to play the two-hand game?' Lily asked gently. Sam looked up, curious. 'What is the two-hand game?' he asked. Lily explained that he could take one piece of the green crayon in his left hand and the other piece in his right hand. Then, he could color super fast with both hands at the same time! Sam’s eyes lit up with excitement. He grabbed a piece in each fist. Left hand, right hand, scribble, scribble, stomp! He made funny green polka dots all over his dinosaur. It looked silliest and coolest dinosaur ever. Sam laughed out loud and clapped his hands together. He hugged Lily and thanked her for the fun idea. Sam felt so happy and proud of his extra-special dinosaur. He learned that a broken crayon is never the end of the world—sometimes, it is just the beginning of a brand new adventure. He put both green pieces back into his box, ready for his next big drawing adventure.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Leo loved the big blue crayon. It was his absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world. Every single morning, Leo would sit right down at his little wooden table and draw huge, fluffy blue skies. He would draw happy blue clouds, soaring blue birds, and swooping blue airplanes flying high. He held that crayon tightly in his small hand because it made him feel so wonderful. One sunny afternoon, Leo was pressing extra hard to make a very special blue ocean. Suddenly, there was a tiny little snap! Oh no. Leo looked down at his hand, and his favorite blue crayon was broken right in half. Two pieces! Leo's lower lip started to quiver, and his big brown eyes filled with big shiny tears. He looked at Mommy and whispered, 'Oh no, Mommy. My blue crayon is broken. It is all ruined.' Mommy walked over with the softest, warmest smile on her face. She gently knelt down right beside his little chair and gave him a big, comforting hug. 'It is okay, sweet boy,' Mommy said in her most soothing voice. 'Nothing is ruined at all. Look closely, Leo. Now, instead of just one crayon, you have two special pieces. Magic pieces!' Leo wiped his little cheek with the back of his sleeve and blinked. 'Two pieces?' he asked softly. 'Yes!' Mommy cheered gently. 'And you know what that means? Now you can share one piece with me, and we can color the sky together side by side.' Leo thought about this for a moment. He looked at the two blue pieces sitting right there on the bright yellow paper. A little smile crept onto his face. He picked up one piece and handed it to Mommy with so much excitement. 'Here you go, Mommy!' he giggled happily. Together, Leo and Mommy colored the biggest, most beautiful blue ocean the world had ever seen. They colored and laughed all afternoon long. Leo learned that sometimes, when things break, it just means there is twice as much room for fun and sharing with the people you love the most.

stories.title: Maya's Sunny Sunflower
stories.text: Maya was an artist. She loved bright colors more than anything else in her whole house. Today, Maya was drawing a giant yellow sunflower for her grandma. She picked up her bright yellow crayon and began to draw big, beautiful petals stretching all the way across the paper. She pressed down with all her might to make the yellow super bright and cheery. Crunch! Oh dear! The yellow crayon snapped right in the middle, rolling across the table and stopping near her little red shoes. Maya gasped. Her happy face turned into a little frown. 'My yellow is broken!' she said, looking very sad indeed. Daddy walked by and saw the two pieces on the table. He scooped Maya up into his strong arms and gave her a gentle tickle on her tummy, making her giggle softly. 'Do not worry, my little sunshine,' Daddy said with a warm, encouraging grin. 'A broken crayon is just a clever crayon in disguise.' Maya tilted her head, her brown curls bouncing. 'A clever crayon?' she asked. 'That is right,' Daddy explained softly. 'When a crayon breaks, it is actually much easier for little fingers to hold. Let me show you a wonderful trick.' Daddy set Maya back down in her chair and helped her pick up both pieces of the sunny yellow crayon. 'Look,' Daddy said, showing her how to hold one short piece in her fingertips. 'Now you have double the coloring power.' Maya looked at her yellow paper and pressed the short piece down. It made a wonderful, bold mark! 'Look at that!' Maya cheered, her sad feelings completely melting away like ice cream on a warm day. She used one short piece to color the left side of the sunflower and the other short piece to color the right side. It was the fastest she had ever colored anything in her life. When Grandma came over later that afternoon, Maya proudly handed her the bright yellow sunflower picture. 'I broke my crayon, Grandma!' Maya beamed proudly. 'And then we made magic!' Grandma clapped her hands with joy and gave Maya the biggest hug in the whole world.

stories.title: Sam's Green Dinosaur
stories.text: Sam was on a very important mission. He was drawing a stomping, chomping green dinosaur in the middle of a prehistoric jungle. Sam loved green. He loved green grass, green leaves, and especially green dinosaurs with big pointy teeth. He was coloring the dinosaur's big tail when suddenly—snap! The green crayon broke into two uneven pieces. Sam stopped coloring immediately. He looked at the broken pieces and let out a little sigh. His big brother, Toby, sat right across the table. Toby looked up and said, 'Hey, Sam, do not be sad. Broken crayons are awesome!' Sam looked skeptical. 'Awesome? How can a broken crayon be awesome?' Toby smiled kindly and slid a piece of paper over. 'Watch this,' Toby said. He took one of the broken green pieces and turned it flat on its side. He rubbed it gently across the paper, creating a wonderful, textured patch of green leaves that looked just like a real jungle bush. Sam's eyes went wide with wonder. 'Whoa!' Sam whispered. 'You can do that?' 'Sure can!' Toby nodded enthusiastically. 'When crayons break, you can color with the pointy tip, or you can use the flat side to make cool secret textures.' Sam felt a burst of excitement. He picked up his own broken green pieces. He used the pointy tip of the first piece to draw sharp dinosaur scales on the back. Then, he used the flat side of the second piece to color a whole field of grass under the dinosaur's big feet. It was so much fun! Sam laughed out loud as the green paper filled up with his fantastic dinosaur artwork. He realized that a broken crayon was not a broken toy at all—it was a new way to create art. Sam looked at Toby and smiled a big, proud smile. 'Look what I made, Toby! My dinosaur has a jungle now!' Toby high-fived his little brother and cheered. Sam felt so happy, proud, and ready to color the whole world green.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Leo loved the color blue. Every single day, he used his favorite blue crayon to draw big, beautiful skies, deep splashing oceans, and flying bluebirds. He pressed hard because he loved the bright color so much. One sunny morning, while drawing a very happy whale, *SNAP!* The blue crayon broke right in the middle into two smaller pieces. Leo’s lower lip started to tremble. Big tears welled up in his eyes. He looked at his broken crayon and felt so sad. His mom walked over, knelt down beside his little wooden table, and gave him a warm, gentle hug. 'Oh, Leo,' she whispered softly, 'it is okay to feel sad when something we love breaks. But look closely! Now you have two blue crayons instead of just one.' Leo wiped away a tear and sniffled. He picked up the two smaller pieces. He tried holding one in each hand. 'Two blue crayons!' he gasped with a tiny smile. 'Yes!' said Mom encouragingly. 'Now you can color twice as fast, or share one with your teddy bear.' Leo beamed. He used the top piece to finish the splashing ocean waves, and the bottom piece to color a fluffy blue hat for his teddy. He realized that a broken crayon was not ruined at all; it was just changed. And changing could be lots of fun. He felt so proud of his clever problem-solving. From that day on, whenever a crayon snapped, Leo did not cry. He just smiled, knowing he had created a brand new drawing tool. He hugged his mom and went right back to coloring his wonderful, bright world with happy little hands. The sun shone warmly through the window, making his blue masterpiece sparkle with joy and creativity. Leo was a big boy who could handle tiny bumps in the road with grace and a positive heart.

stories.title: Maya's Sunny Sunflower
stories.text: Maya was sitting on her cozy pink rug, holding a bright yellow crayon. She was drawing a gigantic sunflower for her grandma. She wanted the petals to be extra sunny and warm. Maya pressed down with all her might, making little grunting noises because she was working so hard. Suddenly, with a little *pop* sound, the yellow crayon snapped into two pieces. Maya gasped. She dropped the pieces and looked at her mom with wide, worried eyes. 'Oh no, Mommy! I broke it! I broke my best yellow crayon!' Her mom smiled gently, reached out, and stroked Maya’s soft curls. 'Accidents happen, sweet girl,' Mom said in a soothing voice. 'That just means you were drawing with lots of enthusiasm and strong muscles!' Maya blinked. She looked down at her strong little hands. She did have strong muscles! Mom showed Maya how to peel a little bit of the paper wrapper off both pieces of the broken crayon. 'See? Now you can use the flat side of the crayon to color big spaces super fast.' Maya tried it. She laid the piece sideways and rubbed it gently across the paper. *Swish, swish!* A huge, bright yellow circle appeared instantly. Maya giggled out loud. 'Look, Mommy! It makes a giant sunshine spot!' Her face lit up like the sun itself. She used the other piece to carefully draw the pointy flower petals. By the time she finished, the sunflower was the brightest, happiest flower in the whole wide world. Maya felt so proud of herself for trying a new way to color. She learned that even when things break, you can find a wonderful new way to use them. She packed up her crayons, gave her mom a big squeeze, and carefully carried her special sunflower drawing to the kitchen to surprise her grandma with a heart full of joy.

stories.title: Sam's Red Firetruck
stories.text: Sam lovedfiretrucks more than anything in the whole world. Today, he was using his favorite bright red crayon to draw a giant firetruck with a very long ladder. *Nee-naw, nee-naw!* he made siren noises as he colored the big wheels and the shiny body. He pushed down hard to make the red super bright. *SNAP!* Oh dear. The red crayon broke right in half. Sam stopped his siren noises. He looked at the two little pieces rolling across the table. His shoulders slumped down. He felt a little frustrated. His big brother, Toby, came over to see what was wrong. Toby gave Sam a gentle pat on the back. 'Hey buddy, don't worry,' Toby said encouragingly. 'A broken crayon is just a helper in disguise.' Sam tilted his head. 'A helper?' he asked softly. 'Yes!' Toby smiled. 'Look, now we can play a game. You have a short red crayon and a medium red crayon.' Sam picked them up. They felt funny in his hands, but he could still hold them just fine. 'Can I still finish my firetruck?' Sam asked hopefully. 'Of course you can,' Toby cheered. 'You can use one piece for the front and one piece for the back!' Sam’s face lit up with a big, happy grin. He picked up the short piece and colored the cab. Then he picked up the other piece and colored the water tank. He even used the broken edges to make little red buttons on the side of the truck. It looked even cooler than before! Sam clapped his hands together. 'I did it! I fixed my picture!' He felt so brave and capable. He gave Toby a high-five. From that day on, Sam knew that breaking something by accident wasn't the end of the world. It was just an invitation to try something new, be creative, and keep on having fun.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo sat at the bright yellow table with his favorite blue crayon. He was coloring a big, fluffy sky for his happy paper rabbit. Leo pressed down hard. *Crack!* Oh no! The blue crayon broke into two little pieces. Leo's bottom lip quivered, and a tiny tear peeked out of the corner of his eye. He looked at his mom and whispered, 'It's broken.' Mom walked over with a warm, cozy smile and gave him a gentle hug. 'It is okay, sweetie,' Mom whispered softly. 'Things break sometimes, but that just means we get to try something new.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. 'Something new?' he asked. 'Yes!' Mom said cheerfully. 'Look, now you have two blue crayons instead of one!' Leo picked up the pieces. He looked at the long piece and the short piece. A little smile tickled the corners of his mouth. He tried coloring with the short piece, and guess what? It worked just as well! In fact, it was easier for him to hold with his little fingers. Leo colored the top of the sky with the long piece and the bottom with the short piece. His rabbit looked happier than ever floating in the bright blue sky. Leo clapped his hands together with joy. He learned that a broken crayon is not a ruined day, but a brand-new way to play. He proudly showed his masterpiece to Mom, who cheered loudly. Leo felt so proud of himself for not giving up. He carefully put both pieces of his special blue crayon back into his green crayon box, ready for tomorrow's big art adventure. The sun shone warmly through the window, wrapping the room in a happy, cozy glow as Leo cleaned up his art supplies all by himself.

stories.title: Mia's Sunny Sunflowers
stories.text: Mia loved the color yellow more than anything in the whole wide world. Today, she was drawing a tall, bright sunflower on her large drawing pad. She swirled her yellow crayon round and round to make the big petals shine. Suddenly, with a little *snap*, the crayon broke right in the middle! Mia gasped and looked down at the two halves sitting on her paper. For a second, Mia felt sad because her favorite crayon wasn't whole anymore. But then, big brother Sam walked by and peeked at her picture. 'Wow, look at those petals!' Sam said with a big grin. 'You have double the sunshine now!' Mia giggled. Double the sunshine sounded like a magical idea. Mia picked up the first piece of her yellow crayon and colored the left side of her flower. Then, she picked up the second piece and colored the right side. It was like teamwork, right in her own hands! When she was all done, the sunflower looked brighter and happier than it ever had before. Mia felt so proud and gave herself a little pat on the back. 'I fixed it!' she cheered softly. Mom walked in and gasped, 'That is the most beautiful sunflower I have ever seen!' Mia beamed from ear to ear. She learned that when something breaks, you can still make wonderful things happen with a little bit of imagination and a happy heart. She carefully tucked her two yellow pieces back into her box, feeling like a real artist who could solve any little problem that came her way today.

stories.title: Zoe's Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Zoe was making a wonderful picture of a rainbow for her sleepy kitty cat. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple! She held her purple crayon tightly to draw the very last stripe across the top of the sky. *Snap!* The purple crayon broke into two pieces right on top of the paper. Zoe let out a little gasp and stared at the broken pieces. Her tummy felt a little bit fluttery and sad. Dad sat down right beside her on the little red chair and wrapped his big, warm arm around her shoulders. 'Is your crayon broken, Zoe-bear?' Dad asked gently. Zoe nodded slowly. 'That is okay,' Dad said with a reassuring smile. 'Sometimes things break, but we can fix them together.' Dad showed Zoe how they could use both pieces. 'Look, now you can share with your other hand, or make double purple dots!' Zoe's eyes lit up with excitement. She took a piece in her left hand and a piece in her right hand. She tapped them on the paper to make polka-dot raindrops falling from her purple rainbow. *Tap, tap, tap!* It made a funny little sound that made Zoe giggle out loud. The picture looked so unique and special with all those lovely purple dots. Zoe felt so happy and brave. She didn't let a broken crayon stop her fun at all. She gave Dad a big hug and said, 'Look, Dad, magic dots!' Dad smiled proudly and kissed the top of her head. Zoe finished her drawing and proudly hung it on the refrigerator, where it sparkled with love and happy memories every single day.

stories.title: Leo's Blue Sky
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo was sitting at his bright yellow table, coloring a big picture of the sky. He was using his favorite blue crayon, pressing down with all his might to make the clouds look extra fluffy. Suddenly, *snap* went the blue crayon! Leo stopped and looked down. The crayon was broken right in the middle into two smaller pieces. Leo's lower lip began to quiver, and he felt a little tear in his eye because his favorite crayon was broken. Mommy walked over softly, knelt down, and gave Leo a warm, gentle hug. She smiled and said, 'Oh, look, Leo! Now you have two magic pieces instead of just one! We didn't lose a crayon; we actually made a friend for it.' Leo wiped his tear away and looked closely at the two pieces. Mommy showed him how to hold one piece in his little fingers to color the left side of the sky, and the other piece for the right side. Leo giggled. It was actually much easier to hold the short pieces now! He colored furiously, making the most beautiful blue sky he had ever seen. He used both hands at the same time, stamping blue dots for little birds flying high. When the picture was all finished, Leo held it up proudly and showed Mommy. 'Look, Mommy! Two crayons are better than one!' Mommy cheered and clapped her hands, telling Leo how clever he was for turning a little oops into a happy art adventure. Leo felt so proud and happy inside. He learned that when something breaks, it is not the end of the world—sometimes, it just means you get to play in a brand new, wonderful way. And from that day on, Leo loved his short little crayons just as much as he loved the big ones, coloring happy pictures all afternoon long.

stories.title: Mia's Sunny Sun
stories.text: Little Mia loved the color yellow more than anything else in the whole wide world. Today, she was drawing a giant, happy sun right in the middle of a big white paper. She pressed hard, making big yellow circles round and round. *Snap!* The yellow crayon snapped right in half. Mia gasped and looked at her hands. One piece was in her left hand, and one was in her right hand. Her shoulders slumped, and she felt a little sad bubble in her tummy. Daddy saw what happened and walked over with a gentle smile. 'Ah, Mia! Your crayon worked so hard making that bright sun that it just needed a little rest in two pieces!' Daddy said cheerfully. Mia smiled through her tiny frown. Daddy showed her a fun trick. He took one piece of the yellow crayon and showed her how to color with the flat side of the paper wrapper peeled back. The sun looked textured and even brighter! Mia clapped her hands in delight. She took the second piece and gave it to her teddy bear so he could help color the sunshine rays too. 'Teddy wants to help!' Mia whispered happily. Together, Mia and her teddy bear colored the rest of the paper with the two yellow pieces. They made the sun shine down on green grass, yellow flowers, and a smiling yellow cat. Mia realized that having a broken crayon wasn't bad at all. In fact, it meant sharing was super easy now because she had double the tools. Daddy kissed the top of Mia's head and told her she was a very creative problem solver. Mia beamed with joy, feeling so proud of her lovely yellow sun and her wonderful broken crayon magic.

stories.title: Sam's Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Sam was making a colorful rainbow for Grandma. Red, orange, green, and purple were all dancing across the paper. When it was time for the green stripe, Sam picked up his bright green crayon. He pushed down hard to make the grass at the bottom of the rainbow. *Snap!* The green crayon broke into two uneven pieces. Sam looked at the broken crayon on the table and let out a little sigh. He felt a bit frustrated because he wanted his crayon to stay long and perfect. Grandma walked over, knelt right beside him, and kissed his cheek. 'Oh, Sam, look at that! Your green crayon is like a little bridge now,' Grandma whispered softly. Sam tilted his head and smiled. 'A bridge?' he asked. 'Yes,' said Grandma. 'One piece can color the grass on the left, and the other piece can color the grass on the right.' Sam picked up the pieces with his little fingers. He noticed how nice they fit right inside his palm. He colored carefully, making green grass patches all over the bottom of his picture. Then, he decided to use the two pieces to make green polka-dots bouncing over the rainbow like happy little frogs. 'Ribbit, ribbit!' Sam giggled, making his crayon hop across the page. Grandma laughed and told him what a fantastic artist he was. Sam felt a warm, cozy feeling in his heart. He learned that even when things break, he can still make wonderful things happen with his own two hands. He finished his picture, wrote his name at the top, and hugged Grandma tight, ready for his next big art project with his favorite broken crayon.

stories.title: Sam's Sunny Blue Crayon
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sam sat at the bright yellow kitchen table. It was drawing time! Sam loved his big box of crayons. He reached in and pulled out his very favorite crayon. It was a bright, happy blue, just like the summer sky. Sam smiled from ear to ear. He pressed the blue crayon down onto the big white paper to draw a big ocean wave. But wait! Oh no! With a little sound that went snap, the blue crayon broke right in half! Sam looked down at the two pieces. His bottom lip started to quiver just a tiny bit. He felt a little sad because his crayon was broken. Mommy walked over softly and knelt down right beside his chair. She gave Sam a warm, gentle hug and said, 'It is okay to feel sad, Sam. But look closely. Now you don't just have one crayon. You have two magic drawing pieces!' Sam blinked his big brown eyes and looked at his mommy. 'Two pieces?' he asked softly. Mommy smiled and nodded. 'Yes! One for each hand, or to share with a friend.' Sam looked down at the two blue pieces. A tiny smile popped back onto his face. He picked up one piece in his left hand and one in his right hand. He drew two happy waves at the very same time! Swish, swish went the crayons across the paper. Sam giggled and clapped his hands together. A broken crayon did not mean drawing time was over. In fact, it made drawing time even more fun and extra special. Sam kept on coloring his beautiful ocean, happy as a little bird, knowing that even when things break, wonderful new ways to play are always waiting right around the corner. Great job, Sam!

stories.title: Mia's Magic Red Apple
stories.text: Little Mia was sitting on her cozy little rug, coloring a picture of a crunchy red apple. She picked up her favorite red crayon and began to color in big, sweeping circles. Red, red, red went the crayon! But Mia pushed just a little bit too hard because she was so excited. Snap! The red crayon broke into two pieces right in the middle. Mia stopped coloring and looked at her hands. She let out a little sigh. She wanted her apple to be colored with one long, smooth crayon. Daddy heard the little sigh and walked over with a gentle smile. He sat down on the rug right next to her and said, 'Do not worry, sweet girl. Breaking a crayon happens to everyone, even grown-ups!' Mia looked at Daddy and tilted her head. 'Can we still fix it?' she asked. Daddy shook his head gently and said, 'We do not even need to glue it. Watch this!' Daddy took the short piece of the red crayon and turned it sideways on the paper. Rub, rub, rub, went the side of the crayon. It made a wonderful, wide red patch! Mia's eyes grew big and round with wonder. 'Ooh!' she gasped. Then she took the other piece and colored the rest of the apple. 'Look, Daddy! I have a top piece and a bottom piece!' Mia said proudly. She used both pieces to finish her beautiful red apple. She even used the flat side to make a pretty red shadow underneath. Daddy gave her a high-five and told her what a clever artist she was. Mia felt so proud and happy. Her broken crayon had just taught her a brand new trick. Drawing was just as wonderful as ever, and Mia kept on creating her masterpiece with a big happy grin on her face.

stories.title: Leo and the Rainbow Bridge
stories.text: Leo loved making colorful pictures for his grandma. Today, he decided to draw a big, beautiful rainbow arching high across his paper. He grabbed his bright yellow crayon to make a shiny sun and yellow stripes. He colored fast and happy. Suddenly, snap! The yellow crayon broke right in two. Leo looked at the broken pieces and frowned. He felt a little frustrated because his crayon was no longer long and pointy. Grandma walked over, wiping her hands on a towel, and looked down with a loving smile. She gently patted Leo's soft curls and said, 'Oh, my little sunshine, look what happened! Your crayon just multiplied.' Leo giggled a little bit. 'Multiplied, Grandma?' he asked. 'Yes,' Grandma whispered kindly. 'Now you have a short piece and a medium piece. That means double the fun!' Leo picked up the short piece. He realized it was actually much easier for his little fingers to hold tightly without dropping it. He colored the sun with the short piece, and it worked like absolute magic! Then, he used the other piece to add bright yellow stars all around the sky. 'Grandma, look! I made sunshine and stars!' Leo shouted happily. Grandma clapped her hands together and cheered for him. 'You did it, Leo! You are a super-duper artist.' Leo felt so proud of his wonderful drawing. He learned that a broken crayon was never a mistake, just a new way to make art. He hugged his grandma tightly, ready to draw even more wonderful pictures with all his special, broken, beautiful crayons.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we going to do?
It snapped right in the middle space,
With sadness on its little face.

Don't cry, don't fuss, let's take a look,
And check inside our paper book.
Two little pieces side by side,
Are ready for a joyful ride.

We grab some tape that's nice and clear,
And wrap it tight right over here.
Press it down and give a squeeze,
We fixed our favorite color, please!

Now blue is back and feeling strong,
To sing our happy coloring song.
Draw a circle, draw a square,
Happy crayons everywhere!

rhymes.title: Two Happy Colors
rhymes.text:
Red is tall and red is bright,
Drawing sunshine warm and light.
Oops it cracked and tumbled down,
Let's not wear a grumpy frown.

Now we have a piece that's small,
And a piece that's not at all.
Wait, we have two friends instead,
Two happy little pieces of red!

Use the short one for the top,
Use the long one till you drop.
Draw a heart and draw a rose,
Right upon the paper toes.

Broken crayons still can play,
Brightening up our special day.
Color here and color there,
Creating art beyond compare.

rhymes.title: The Magic Paper Patch
rhymes.text:
Yellow sunshine on the page,
Dancing on the wooden stage.
Snap! It broke into the air,
Landing on the big brown chair.

Pick it up and do not sigh,
We can make the yellow fly.
Wrap a tissue round the break,
For our drawing project's sake.

Hold it gently in your hand,
Bestest artist in the land.
Make a star and make a bee,
Buzzing happily and free.

See the trick we just have done,
Coloring is so much fun.
Broken bits are brand new toys,
Made for little girls and boys.

rhymes.title: Double Drawing Time
rhymes.text:
Green goes round the jungle tree,
As happy as a honeybee.
Uh-oh, crack! It came apart,
Breaking up a work of art.

Is it ruined? No, oh no!
Watch the magic double show.
Now we hold one in each hand,
Finishing the leafy land.

Left hand colors up so high,
Right hand reaches for the sky.
Tap them both upon the sheet,
Making forest pictures sweet.

Two is better far than one,
Look at all the work we've done.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
Crayons saved another day!

rhymes.title: The Brave Little Crayon
rhymes.text:
Purple crayon, bold and grand,
Coloring our wonderland.
Snap it went upon the floor,
Rolling right toward the door.

Pick it up and brush it clean,
Bestest purple we have seen.
Even though it took a break,
Look at pictures we can make.

Press it down with all your might,
Making magic shiny bright.
Draw a castle, draw a crown,
In our happy little town.

Broken pieces, do not fear,
We are glad that you are here.
Sing a song and smile and play,
Coloring the hours away.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we going to do?
It snapped right down in half today,
But we can still find time to play!

We grab some tape that's nice and wide,
And stick the pieces deep inside.
We wrap it up both neat and strong,
So we can sing our art-time song!

Look at that, it's fixed so fast,
This little crayon's going to last!
We draw a whale, we draw a sea,
Just you and little happy me.

So do not frown when things will break,
Look at the pictures we can make!
Up and down and all around,
The happiest crayon we have found.

rhymes.title: Two Little Crayons
rhymes.text:
Red is short and red is sweet,
Drawing pictures on the sheet.
It broke right off with quite a snap,
Right upon my little lap!

Now I have one, and now I have two,
Tell me, what is red to do?
One for the top and one below,
Watch the pretty colors grow!

We press them down upon the page,
We are the artists of the age.
Two little pieces side by side,
Filling up the paper wide.

We love our crayon, short and tall,
We love our drawing best of all.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
Art is fun for us today!

rhymes.title: Magic Paper Glue
rhymes.text:
Yellow crayon went ker-splash,
Broken in a little dash!
Do not cry and do not pout,
We can figure this thing out.

Get the paper, get the glue,
I will share my paste with you.
Rub it here and stick it there,
Show our yellow friend some care.

Hold it tight and count to three,
One, two, three, now look and see!
The pieces join and hold so fast,
We made our yellow crayon last.

Now it's time to draw the sun,
Look at how we get it done!-
Bright and golden in the sky,
Wave our little hands on high.

rhymes.title: The Double Rainbow
rhymes.text:
Green is strong and green is bright,
Drawing leaves with all its might.
Oops it cracked into a twin,
Let the double fun begin!

Now I hold a pair of green,
Cutest things you've ever seen.
One will draw a clover patch,
Both of them are quite a match.

Tap them softly on the floor,
We don't need to feel no more.
Every break is something new,
A double crayon made for two!

Coloring high and coloring low,
See the pretty garden grow.
Smile and dance and sing along,
This is our happy crayon song.

rhymes.title: Little Artist Hands
rhymes.text:
Purple crayon took a fall,
Right against the playroom wall.
It broke in two upon the floor,
Ready for some painting more.

Pick it up with gentle care,
Place it safely right in there.
Two small crayons ready to go,
Making magic make a show.

We draw a grape, we draw a plum,
Tap it with our little thumb.
Nothing stops our creative play,
We are smiling all the day.

Fix it up and make it gleam,
We are in a painting dream!
Cheer aloud and give a shout,
That is what our art is about.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we ever going to do?
It snapped right down, it snapped in two,
I know a trick for me and you!

We grab some tape so nice and neat,
To make our crayon look complete.
We wrap it round and give a squeeze,
And draw a happy little breeze!

No tears at all, we fix it fast,
So all our colors long will last.
We draw a bird up in the sky,
And watch our little jet plane fly!

Two pieces now can draw as one,
And making art is so much fun!

rhymes.title: Double the Drawing Fun
rhymes.text:
My purple crayon went ker-snap,
Right on top of my drawing lap!
I felt a frown upon my face,
Inside this cozy toddler place.

Then teacher smiled and gently said,
'Lift up your little sleepy head!'
Now you have one, and now you have two,
To draw a shiny silver shoe.

We press them down upon the page,
And color on the wooden stage.
The short one draws, the long one too,
We have such happy work to do!

So do not worry, do not cry,
We wave our broken parts goodbye.
We make a smile, we sing a song,
And color all the whole day long!

rhymes.title: The Little Red Band-Aid
rhymes.text:
Red is my very favorite hue,
Today it broke right through and through.
A little snap, a little break,
Oh what a picture we can make!

Let's wrap a band-aid round its toe,
And watch the lovely color glow.
It looks so brave, it looks so grand,
The finest crayon in the land.

We press it down and scribble round,
The happiest sound upon the ground.
It draws an apple bright and sweet,
A special treat for little feet.

We clap our hands and shout hooray,
Our crayon is okay today!
We sing a little morning tune,
And draw a smiling paper moon.

rhymes.title: Mended with Glue
rhymes.text:
Yellow sunshine on the floor,
We want to draw a little more.
Alas, alack, the yellow broke,
Just like a funny little joke!

Bring the glue and bring the brush,
There is never any rush.
We dab a spot upon the side,
And watch our clever skill applied.

We press them close and count to ten,
To make it strong and whole again.
One, two, three and four and five,
See our yellow come alive!

Now we draw a bumblebee,
Buzzing by the big green tree.
We sing along with happy cheer,
The best routine of all the year!

rhymes.title: Two Tiny Wands
rhymes.text:
Green grass is growing in the spring,
And happy little birdies sing.
My green broke off into my hand,
The finest crayon in the land.

They look like magic wizard wands,
To draw the frogs down by the ponds.
I hold a piece in every fist,
And twist and turn my little wrist.

Up and down and all around,
Making such a joyful sound.
Two little wands to trace a line,
Everything is looking fine!

We put them safely in the cup,
And pick our happy faces up.
A broken crayon is okay,
We love to draw another day!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Squad
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we ever going to do?
It snapped right down, it snapped in two,
I know just what we have to do!

We will not cry, we will not frown,
We'll pick the little pieces up from down.
With glue so sticky, thick and neat,
We'll make our blue crayon complete!

Press it gently, count to three,
Look how happy it can be!
Now we have two colors to share,
Drawing pictures everywhere.

Draw a star and draw a tree,
Drawing is so fun for me!
Fix it up and play all day,
Hooray, hooray, hip, hip, hooray!

rhymes.title: Two Little Crayons
rhymes.text:
My sunny yellow broke apart,
It made a sad face in my heart.
But wait a minute, look and see,
Now yellow has a twin for me!

One for you and one for me,
Sharing art is full of glee.
Draw a sun so big and bright,
Shining down with yellow light.

Side by side they love to go,
Making lovely lines just so.
We can draw a happy duck,
Oh boy, oh boy, what good luck!

No more tears, just happy cheer,
Drawing time is the best time here.
Up and down and all around,
Best yellow crayons ever found!

rhymes.title: Magic Tape Fix
rhymes.text:
Red crayon fell upon the floor,
And snapped right by the playroom door.
Is it ruined? Oh, not quite!
We can fix it, make it right.

Bring the tape, the shiny roll,
Wrap it round to reach the goal.
Wrap it tight and wrap it round,
Best fixed crayon to be found!

Coloring books are waiting near,
Spread the joy and spread the cheer.
Make a heart and make a rose,
Right beneath your button nose.

Look how strong our red is now,
We fixed it up, just take a bow!
Sing a song and clap your hands,
Best artist in all the lands.

rhymes.title: The Double Draw
rhymes.text:
Green crayon broke in half today,
While we were in the middle of play.
Instead of one, now I have two,
And I know just what to do!

Put them both inside my hand,
Draw the best grass in the land.
One goes left and one goes right,
Making pictures looking bright.

Double lines and double fun,
We are not sad, no, not one.
Color bushes, color trees,
Swaying softly in the breeze.

Two little crayons doing their best,
Passing every single test.
Give a cheer for the color green,
Prettiest art you've ever seen!

rhymes.title: Purple's New Job
rhymes.text:
My purple crayon took a tumble,
Which made my little tummy rumble.
But accidents will always hap,
When crayons take a little nap.

We can use the little piece,
To draw grapes and yummy cheese.
Hold it sideways, shade it wide,
See the purple colors glide!

Short and sweet is so much fun,
Look at all the work we've done.
Color fast and color slow,
Watch the lovely purple glow.

Problem solved with happy smiles,
Drawing pictures for miles and miles.
Clap your hands and shout aloud,
We are feeling very proud!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a crack in two,
My red crayon is feeling blue!
But do not cry and do not frown,
This is not the end of the town.

We grab the tape and wrap it tight,
To make the broken piece feel right.
We press it down and count to three,
As happy as a bumblebee!

Now draw a sun so big and round,
The happiest red crayon found.
It colors fast, it colors slow,
And makes our lovely picture glow.

So give a cheer and clap your hands,
The best crayon in all the lands!

rhymes.title: Two Little Wands
rhymes.text:
My purple friend snapped right in half,
Let's turn the sad face to a laugh!
We didn't break just one, you see,
We made two magic wands for me.

One wand is short, one wand is tall,
We use them both to paint a ball.
We wave them high up in the air,
And sprinkle glitter everywhere.

Draw a flower, draw a tree,
Two little wands for you and me.
They fit so nicely in our grip,
Ready for a drawing trip.

Good job, helper, dry your tear,
We love our little crayons here!

rhymes.title: The Side-by-Side Song
rhymes.text:
SNAP went the green upon the floor,
We need not worry anymore.
We pick it up, we wipe it clean,
The finest green you've ever seen.

We lay them down side by side,
With lots of room and lots of pride.
Press down gently, nice and slow,
Watch the pretty colors grow.

Green grass blowing in the breeze,
Green leaves dancing on the trees.
A broken stick is just okay,
We find a brand new way to play.

Sing a happy toddler song,
Painting all the whole day long!

rhymes.title: Crayon Hugs and Kisses
rhymes.text:
Oh dear, oh dear, my yellow friend,
Is broken right here at the end.
Let's give the pieces such a hug,
Snug as bugs inside a rug.

We hold them close and make them strong,
With this little bedtime song.
Now press the paper, make a streak,
A happy sunshine on your cheek.

Yellow duckies swimming by,
Yellow stars up in the sky.
A broken tip is nothing new,
We know just what we can do.

Smile and wiggle, shout hooray,
We fixed our crayon for the day!

rhymes.title: The Magic Double Draw
rhymes.text:
Blue is broken, snap, snap, snap,
Let it rest upon your lap.
Now you have a double treat,
Two blue crayons, oh so sweet!

Hold one in your left hand, too,
Now you have a double view.
Draw a river, draw the sea,
As happy as can ever be.

Tap them softly on the desk,
Drawing shapes that are grotesque.
Wait, let's draw a puppy dog,
Sitting on a happy log.

Good job fixing things today,
Time to put the books away!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Split
rhymes.text:
Oh no look at the blue,
Tell me what shall we do?
It went snap right in two,
Now there are pieces new!

Do not cry do not frown,
It is still a fun town.
Draw a smile on your face,
Put the halves in their place.

Big piece and little piece,
Drawing fun does not cease.
Make a dot make a line,
Everything will be fine.

Coloring is so bright,
Holding it just a mite.
Happy art all day long,
Singing our happy song.

rhymes.title: Two Little Crayons
rhymes.text:
Red crayon snapped apart,
Right here at the very start.
Is it broken? Oh dear no,
Now we have an extra show!

One for left and right hand,
Drawing all through the land.
Make a house make a tree,
Happy as we can be.

Press it down nice and light,
Colors shining so bright.
Use your fingers just so,
Watch the pretty pictures grow.

No tears on your sweet face,
Art is such a happy place.
Snap goes the crayon fun,
Look what our hands have done!

rhymes.title: The Magic Snap
rhymes.text:
Yellow crayon took a bow,
Snapped in half right up now!
Is it broken? Let us see,
Now there are two for me!

Share one with teddy bear,
Coloring everywhere.
Draw a sun in the sky,
Watch the happy birds fly.

Tap tap tap on the page,
Best artist of our age.
Keep your smile nice and wide,
Joy is waiting inside.

Put it in the box neat,
Stamping with both your feet.
Even broken it is grand,
Best crayon in the land.

rhymes.title: Green Crayon Magic
rhymes.text:
Green crayon went ker-splat,
What do we think of that?
It broke right in the middle,
Making us do a wiggle!

Pick up piece number one,
Now the drawing is fun.
Pick up piece number two,
Painting the world anew.

Draw a leaf draw a vine,
Everything looks so fine.
Cheer up now little friend,
Joy is here to attend.

Use the side make a block,
Tick tock goes the clock.
Broken crayons still draw,
Best picture that I saw.

rhymes.title: Crayon Hugs
rhymes.text:
Purple crayon took a nap,
And it made a little snap.
Do not worry or pout,
That is what art is about!

Give the pieces big hugs,
Draw some ladybug bugs.
One piece goes here to play,
One piece stays right away.

Magic fingers so strong,
Singing our drawing song.
Make a dot make a ring,
Hear the little birds sing.

Art time is always sweet,
From our head to our feet.
Broken crayons are neat,
Making our world complete.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Hug
rhymes.text:
Oh no look at the crayon break,
A little fix is ours to make.
It snapped right down right in two,
Now what are you and I to do?
We are not sad we are not mad,
It is the best day we have had!
We take a hug and twist it round,
The happy colors can be found.
Stick it up and stick it down,
No more turning to a frown.
Draw a tree and draw a sun,
Making art is so much fun.
Two small pieces work like one,
Look at all the things we've done!
Color high and color low,
Watch our pretty picture grow.

rhymes.title: The Magic Glue
rhymes.text:
My blue crayon went a snap,
Falling right into my lap.
Do not worry do not cry,
We can give a little try.
Grab the tape and grab the glue,
I can fix it yes I do.
Wrap it tight and wrap it round,
Best new crayon to be found.
Draw the ocean draw the sea,
Drawing makes me glad and free.
Press it softly on the page,
At this very tender age.
Now it's strong and now it's neat,
Painting pictures is a treat.
Happy colors all around,
Happiest art in all the town.

rhymes.title: Double the Fun
rhymes.text:
Red went pop and red went crack,
Let us put it right back track.
Wait a minute let us look,
Open up our picture book.
Now we have got two reds to play,
We can use them through the day.
Give one to my little bear,
Sharing colors is so fair.
Draw a heart and draw a rose,
Right down to your tiny toes.
One for me and one for you,
That is what we daily do.
Double colors double fun,
Smiling brightly at the sun.
Break a crayon do not fear,
Painting with my friends so dear.

rhymes.title: The Tiny Pieces
rhymes.text:
Yellow crayon split in half,
Let us share a happy laugh.
Small is special small is neat,
Using fingers on our sheet.
Hold it close and hold it tight,
Making everything so bright.
Draw a star up in the sky,
Watch the little plane fly by.
Little bits can draw a sun,
Look at how we get it done.
No mistakes just happy art,
Coming straight from every heart.
Press it gently on the pad,
Making mommy very glad.
Yellow sparkles yellow gleam,
Living out a happy dream.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Band
rhymes.text:
Green got broken in the race,
Put a smile upon your face.
We can build a crayon band,
Holding pieces in our hand.
Tap them softly on the floor,
We can always draw some more.
Roll them left and roll them right,
Making colors shine so bright.
Draw the grass and draw the trees,    
Dancing in the morning breeze.
Every piece has got a job,
Even little broken blob.
Color happy color free,
Just like little birds and bee.
Crayon friends are here to stay,
We will draw another day.

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Squad
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we going toddlers to do?
It snapped in half upon the floor,
We do not need to cry no more!

We grab some tape and hold it tight,
We roll it up and make it right.
Two little pieces now are one,
And making art is twice the fun!

Draw a circle, draw a star,
Look how clever that we are!
One blue crayon in the cup,
Never ever give it up.

Sing a happy toddler song,
Making art is right where we belong!
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We fixed our crayon for the day!

rhymes.title: Two Happy Crayons
rhymes.text:
Red and yellow, green and bright,
Drawing pictures with delight.
Wait a minute, what is that?
A broken crayon on the mat!

Do not worry, wipe your tear,
We have got two helpers here.
Now you have got a piece of red,
Right beside your cozy bed.

And I have got the other part,
Ready for a brand new heart!
Draw a puppy, draw a tree,
One for you and one for me.

Sharing colors is so sweet,
Making every picture neat.
Tap your toes and sing along,
Nothing here is going wrong!

rhymes.title: The Magic Crayon Hug
rhymes.text:
Purple crayon takes a fall,
Right against the playroom wall.
Snap and crackle, oh oh oh,
Where did the purple piece go?

Give a hug and give a squeeze,
Put them back together please.
Twirl it round and give a spin,
Let the drawing now begin!

Make a dot and make a line,
Everything is looking fine.
Broken pieces can be strong,
If you help the whole day long.

Wiggle fingers, wiggle toes,
Watch how fast the picture grows.
Smile big and shout hurrah,
Best little artists near and far!

rhymes.title: Sunny Yellow Fix
rhymes.text:
Yellow sunshine on the page,
Drawing in the toddler age.
Oops a daisy, snap it breaks,
Look at all the art it makes!

Split in two, a little short,
Just the proper toddler sort.
Hold it gently in your hand,
Bestest crayon in the land.

Color duckies in the pond,
Of this game we are so fond.
Short crayons still can draw,
Biggest smiles you ever saw.

Wave goodbye to any frown,
Best little artist in the town.
Sing a song of yellow sun,
Coloring is so much fun!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Parade
rhymes.text:
Green is marching down the street,
Moving with its little feet.
Oh dear me, it broke in twain,
Falling like a drop of rain!

Pick it up and count to four,
We are safe upon the floor.
Make a tall tower up high,
Reaching for the sunny sky.

Draw a frog upon a log,
Draw a happy little dog.
Short and sweet is okay too,
We can make a art anew.

March around the table now,
Take a little toddler bow.
Sing a happy marching tune,
We will draw again real soon!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we going to do?
It snapped right down in half today,
But we can still find time to play!

Pick up the pieces, big and small,
We love our crayon best of all.
Let's press them down upon the sheet,
To make our picture look so neat.

Draw a circle, draw a star,
Look how clever that you are!
Two little blues can color wide,
With happy feelings deep inside.

When things break, we do not cry,
We give a clever fix a try!
Good job, helper, hooray, hooray,
We colored all our blues today!

rhymes.title: Red Red Rainbow
rhymes.text:
My favorite red is in two parts,
Just right for drawing little hearts.
Snap and crack, it took a fall,
But it is not the end at all!

Take the first piece in your hand,
Draw the finest in the land.
Take the second piece right there,
Color up into the air.

Double crayons, twice the fun,
Coloring circles like the sun.
Red on paper, bright and bold,
Look at stories to be told.

We don't need a brand new pack,
When our red is coming back.
Tap your fingers, give a cheer,
Drawing time is joyful here!

rhymes.title: Sunny Yellow Smile
rhymes.text:
Yellow sunshine on the page,
Best invention of our age!
Wait a second, what is that?
Yellow broke and went ker-splat.

Do not worry, wipe that tear,
We can fix it right down here.
Push the pieces side by side,
Watch the yellow wiggle wide.

Draw a duckling in the pond,
Of this broken friend we're fond.
Color fast and color slow,
Watch the pretty yellow glow.

Two sweet pieces doing tricks,
That is how a toddler fixes!
Clap your hands and sing a song,
Coloring all the whole day long.

rhymes.title: Green Grass Magic
rhymes.text:
Green crayon went snap today,
While we danced and went to play.
Is it ruined? No, oh no!
Watch the happy colors grow.

Take piece one to draw a tree,
Happy as a bumblebee.
Take piece two to draw the grass,
Watching all the hours pass.

Two little crayons doing a dance,
Giving our art a second chance.
Green and leafy, bright and tall,
Crayon magic for us all.

Let us smile and let us sing,
Crayons are our favorite thing.
Broken pieces work just fine,
Look at this nice drawing of mine!

rhymes.title: Purple Power Patch
rhymes.text:
Purple royal, purple grand,
Bestest crayon in the land.
Oopsie daisy, it just cracked,
Right upon the carpet tract.

Pick it up and do not frown,
Turn that little upside down!
We can use both bits with pride,
Coloring far and coloring wide.

Draw a grape and draw a plum,
Tap your finger and your thumb.
One part here and one part there,
Purple magic everywhere.

Broken things can still be sweet,
Making tidy toddler art complete.
Sing along and shout hooray,
We fixed our crayon for the day!

rhymes.title: The Crayon Rescue Team
rhymes.text:
Oh no, oh look, a broken blue,
What are we going toddlers to do?
It snapped right down, it snapped in two,
But we will know what we must do!

We grab some tape and hold it tight,
We wrap it up and make it right.
We count one, two, and count to three,
A brand new crayon, happy and free!

Now draw a star and draw a tree,
How very happy we can be!
The blue is back to play and say,
We saved the art-time day today!

So do not cry when things divide,
We'll put them right back side by side.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We fixed the broken blue today!

rhymes.title: Two Little Crayons
rhymes.text:
Red and yellow, green and bright,
Drawing circles, left and right.
Wait a minute, what is that?
Splittsy-splats and broken flat!

Instead of one, now we have two,
Tell me, friends, what can we do?
We share a piece with brother Bear,
Sharing toys is so much flair!

Now we color side by side,
With a happy, joyful stride.
Double sunshine, double red,
Jumping softly on the bed.

A broken crayon is no sin,
That is where the fun begins!
Two short sticks go tap, tap, tap,
Taking up a happy nap.

rhymes.title: The Magic Glue Hug
rhymes.text:
Purple is my favorite hue,
Drawing grapes and skies of blue.
Pressing hard to make a mound,
Snap! It tumbled to the ground.

Don't be sad and don't feel bad,
It is not a reason sad.
We will give a magic hug,
Snugger than a little bug.

Glue it here and glue it there,
Show the crayon tender care.
Let it rest and count to ten,
Ready for the page again!

Purple magic, strong and sweet,
Making every picture neat.
Now we draw a purple bear,
Dancing lightly in the air.

rhymes.title: Short and Stout
rhymes.text:
Green is growing on the vine,
Drawing leaves that look so fine.
Oopsie daisy, snap and pop,
Green went rolling with a stop!

Is it ruined? Oh, oh, no!
Short and stout can still say hello.
Hold it low and hold it near,
Draw a happy little deer.

Short crayons are easy to hold,
Like a secret piece of gold.
Coloring fast and coloring slow,
Watch the little garden grow.

Every piece is useful still,
Painting every little hill.
Cheer for green, so short and stout,
That is what our art is about!

rhymes.title: The Happy Mender
rhymes.text:
Orange sun up in the sky,
Watch the paper flutter by.
Pressed too hard and split it through,
Now what are we going to do?

Time to mend it, nice and neat,
Keep the art-time rhythm beat.
Band-aid wrap it round and round,
Bestest fix that can be found.

Orange pieces side by side,
Filled with giggles, full of pride.
Draw a pumpkin, round and sweet,
Look at our completed sheet!

Broken things can start anew,
I can fix it, so can you!
Sing a song of work and play,
Fixing crayons every day.

stories.title: Pip's Sticky Block Tower
stories.text: Little Pip the bear was having a super-duper fun morning building a tall tower out of bright wooden blocks. Red block, yellow block, blue block, reach up high! Pip was so proud of his wonderful tower. Just then, his little friend Daisy duck waddled by, flapping her soft yellow wings. Whoops-a-daisy! Daisy’s wing bumped the blue block. Crash, bang, thud! All the blocks tumbled down onto the soft playroom rug. Pip’s face scrunched up. He felt a hot, grumpy bubble of anger pop inside his tummy. He wanted to stomp his paws. But Mama Bear sat down next to Pip and gave him a gentle cuddle. She whispered softly, 'Oh sweet Pip, accidents happen, but how do we make our friends feel better?' Pip took a big, deep breath in, smelling the sweet strawberry air, and let it out slowly. He looked at Daisy, whose eyes were big and sad because she did not mean to knock the blocks over. Pip remembered his favorite daily habit: the warm apology hug! Pip opened his furry arms wide, just like the big wings of a butterfly, and stepped forward. Daisy waddled right into his embrace, and they squeezed each other gently for three whole seconds. One, two, three! Suddenly, the grumpy bubble in Pip’s tummy popped away, replaced by a warm, fuzzy feeling. Daisy smiled a big, happy duck smile. 'I am sorry I bumped your tower, Pip,' Daisy quacked softly. 'That is okay, Daisy,' Pip said in his sweetest voice. Together, they knelt down on the cozy rug and started building a brand new tower, working as a team. Red block, yellow block, blue block, higher than before! Pip learned that even when things go splat, a warm apology hug can fix a sad moment and make friendship shine brighter than ever.

stories.title: Leo's Loud Voice
stories.text: Little Leo the lion cub loved playing outside in the sunny backyard. Today, Leo had his favorite shiny red firetruck. Wee-oo, wee-oo! He zoomed it across the green grass, making loud siren noises. His little sister, Lily lion cub, was sitting nearby with her puzzle pieces. She was trying so hard to fit the little green frog piece into the puzzle board. Leo got so excited that he roared a loud, booming lion roar right in Lily’s furry ear! Roar-roar! Lily jumped, startled by the big noise, and dropped her puzzle. Her lower lip began to quiver, and big, shiny tears welled up in her golden eyes. Oh dear, Leo realized he had used much too big of a voice and hurt his sister’s feelings. Leo’s Mama smiled gently from the porch and nodded. She reminded him of the magic way to show love after a mistake. Leo felt a little flutter of worry in his chest, but he knew what to do. He crawled over on his hands and knees, keeping his voice very quiet and soft. 'I am so sorry I roared so loudly, Lily. It scared you, didn't it?' Lily sniffled and wiped a tiny tear away with her paw. Leo opened his arms wide for a big, cozy cuddle. Lily leaned in, wrapping her little paws around Leo’s neck. They shared a long, warm apology hug. It felt like standing in a patch of warm sunshine on a breezy afternoon. Lily’s frown turned upside down into a bright, happy smile. 'Apology accepted, big brother,' she whispered into his fuzzy mane. Leo felt so glad inside his heart. Sharing a warm apology hug made both of them feel safe, loved, and ready to play nicely together again, sharing the sunny yard in sweet, peaceful harmony.

stories.title: Maya's Missing Crayon
stories.text: Little Maya the bunny loved coloring bright rainbow pictures at the little wooden art table. She had pink, purple, green, and orange crayons scattered everywhere. Maya was coloring a very happy sun when her friend Sam the puppy scampered up to the table. Sam saw the bright yellow crayon sitting right on the edge and grabbed it with his paws to draw a bouncy yellow ball. 'Hey! That is my yellow crayon!' Maya squeaked, feeling a grumpy frown pull down the corners of her mouth. She snatched the crayon right back from Sam’s paws, pulling it a little too hard. Sam looked surprised and blinked his big brown eyes, looking very sad. He dropped his head down low. Maya’s teacher, kindly Miss Bunny, walked over with gentle steps. She knelt down beside them and spoke in a soothing, kind voice. 'Maya, sharing is caring, but how can we use our kindest manners when we snatch?' Maya looked at her yellow crayon, then looked at Sam’s sad puppy face. She knew her hands had acted too fast. Maya took a sweet, slow breath through her nose, smelling the fresh paper. She opened her arms wide like blooming flower petals. Sam looked up, his tail giving a little happy wag. Maya stepped closer and wrapped her arms around Sam in a cozy, sincere apology hug. They squeezed gently, sharing a warm moment of pure kindness. 'I am sorry I snatched the crayon from you, Sam,' Maya whispered gently. 'You can use it right after me.' Sam hugged her back, his furry coat soft and warm. 'That is okay, Maya,' Sam barked softly with a happy grin. They sat side by side, coloring beautiful pictures together, proving that a warm apology hug turns any clumsy moment into a wonderful time of sharing and love.

stories.title: Benny Bear's Bumpy Blocks
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Benny Bear was building a big, beautiful tower out of wooden blocks. He stacked a red block, a blue block, and a shiny yellow block right on top. It was the tallest tower in the whole playroom! Just then, his little sister, Baby Bella, came toddling by. She was so excited to see the pretty colors that she waved her little paws in the air. Oh no! WHOOSH! Bella bumped right into the table, and the tower went CRASH! All the blocks tumbled down onto the soft rug. Benny Bear felt a hot, grumpy feeling in his tummy. He wanted to stomp his feet and roar like a big grizzly. He opened his mouth to say, 'Hey!' But then, Benny looked at Baby Bella. Her bottom lip was starting to quiver, and big tears welled up in her shiny brown eyes. She didn't mean to knock it over; she just wanted to play. Mommy Bear knelt down beside them and gave Benny a gentle nudge. 'Benny,' Mommy whispered softly, 'accidents happen. Sometimes, a warm apology hug helps mends a broken heart and a tumbled tower.' Benny took a deep breath. The grumpy feeling in his tummy started to float away like a puffy white cloud. He crawled over to his little sister and opened his furry arms wide. 'It's okay, Bella,' Benny said in his sweetest voice. 'Do you want a warm apology hug?' Bella sniffled and leaned right into Benny's soft chest. They squeezed each other tight, one, two, three seconds. Benny patted her back gently. Bella giggled, and Benny smiled too. Together, they picked up the blocks and built an even bigger tower. Benny learned that saying sorry and sharing a big cuddle makes everyone feel safe, loved, and happy inside.

stories.title: Pip Penguin Shares the Swing
stories.text: Down by the sparkly blue ice pond, little Pip Penguin was having the best day ever. He was swinging back and forth on the stretchy vine swing. *Whee!* Up to the fluffy clouds! *Whoosh!* Down to the snowy grass! Pip loved the swing so much that he hugged the ropes tightly and whispered, 'Mine, mine, all mine!' Soon, Penny Penguin waddled over. She looked at the swing and then down at her flippers, her little face looking very sad. She had walked all the way from the igloo just to have a turn. Pip saw Penny standing there, but he turned his head away and kept swinging. He did not want to share. Suddenly, Pip felt a little flutter of worry in his chest. It didn't feel very nice to leave his friend out in the cold. Daddy Penguin skated over and gently touched Pip's shoulder. 'Pip,' Daddy said with a warm smile, 'swings are much more fun when everyone gets a turn. When we make a mistake and keep toys to ourselves, a warm apology hug makes things right again.' Pip stopped the swing with his webbed feet. He hopped down onto the soft snow and waddled over to Penny. He felt a little shy, but he knew what to do. 'Penny,' Pip said bravely, 'I am sorry I wouldn't share the swing. Would you like a warm apology hug?' Penny's face lit up with a big, bright smile. She stepped forward, and the two little penguins wrapped their flippers around each other for a cozy cuddle. 'Apology accepted!' Penny chirped happily. Then, Pip kindly pushed Penny on the swing, cheering her on. Pip's heart felt warm and fuzzy. Sharing and hugging truly was the best magic in the snowy land.

stories.title: Daisy Duck's Loud Quack
stories.text: Out by the sparkling duck pond, little Daisy Duck was playing with her favorite shiny pebble. It was smooth and grey, just like a little moon rock. Her best friend, Oliver Owl, landed softly on the grassy bank. 'Good morning, Daisy!' Oliver hooted happily. Oliver leaned in close to look at the pretty pebble. Daisy suddenly felt a bit protective of her treasure. Without thinking, Daisy let out a loud, grumpy quack! 'NO! Go away, Oliver! It's mine!' Her voice sounded harsh and sharp in the quiet morning air. Oliver blinked his big, round yellow eyes in surprise. He stepped backward, looking very hurt, and tucked his wings into his fluffy feathers. He hadn't meant to bother her; he just wanted to be friendly. Daisy saw Oliver's drooping feathers, and her own tummy did a little flip-flop of regret. She knew her loud quack had hurt her friend's feelings. Granny Duck waddled over and gently preened Daisy's head feathers. 'My sweet duckling,' Granny said softly, 'our words can sometimes splash like cold water. But a warm apology hug is like a cozy blanket that makes everything warm again.' Daisy nodded. She waddled over to the little owl, her webbed feet making soft pattering sounds on the grass. 'Oliver,' Daisy said softly, 'I am so sorry I shouted at you. Will you accept a warm apology hug?' Oliver perked right up. He opened his velvety wings and wrapped them gently around Daisy in a soft, feathery embrace. They held each other close for a long moment. 'I forgive you, Daisy,' Oliver hooted gently. Daisy felt so relieved and happy. She even let Oliver hold the shiny pebble for a little while, knowing that kind friends and warm hugs are far more precious than any rock.

stories.title: Benny Bear's Bouncy Ball
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, Benny Bear was playing with his very favorite bouncy ball in the cozy living room. Bounce, bounce, went the bright red ball! Benny giggled and leaped into the air. But oh no! Benny bounced the ball just a little too hard. Zoom! It flew right past the sofa and bumped softly into his little sister Bella's block tower. Crash! All the wooden blocks tumbled down to the rug. Bella blinked her big round eyes. Her mouth made a little pout, and tears began to well up in her eyes. Benny felt a heavy, squishy feeling right in his tummy. He knew he had made a mistake. His mommy walked over, knelt down gently, and gave Benny a warm, loving hug. Mommy whispered in his ear, 'It was an accident, Benny, but it made Bella sad. Do you know what makes things better?' Benny nodded softly. He walked over to Bella on his tiptoes. 'I am so sorry I knocked your blocks down, Bella,' Benny said in his softest, kindest voice. Then, Benny opened his arms wide. 'Can I give you a warm apology hug?' Bella sniffled, wiped a tear away, and smiled. She leaned in, and the two little bears wrapped their fuzzy arms around each other in a big, cozy squeeze. It felt so warm and safe. Benny helped Bella pick up every single block, stacking them even higher than before. Bella giggled again, and Benny felt happy inside. Saying sorry and giving a hug is a wonderful way to mend a broken moment. The rest of the afternoon was filled with gentle sharing and lots of happy cuddles.

stories.title: Pip the Penguin's Blue Paint
stories.text: Down by the chilly blue sea, little Pip the penguin was painting a picture on a big piece of paper. He dipped his brush into bright blue paint and swished it back and forth. Swipe, swish, swoosh! Pip was having so much fun. His friend Penny Penguin waddled up to see his masterpiece. 'Look at my painting, Penny!' cheered Pip, waving his flippers. But oops! A tiny blob of blue paint flew off the brush and landed right on Penny’s fluffy white tummy. Oh dear! Penny looked down at the blue spot on her tummy and gasped. Pip’s heart went thump-thump. He didn’t mean to paint Penny, but he felt very silly and sad that he made a mess on his friend. Pip’s papa knelt down beside them on the ice. Papa gave Pip a reassuring pat and a gentle hug to help him feel brave. 'Mistakes happen, little one,' Papa whispered. 'Let's make it right.' Pip took a deep breath. He waddled over to Penny and looked right into her eyes. 'I am so sorry I got paint on your tummy, Penny,' Pip said sincerely. 'Will you accept my warm apology hug?' Penny smiled her brightest, warmest penguin smile. She opened her flippers wide, and the two friends squeezed each other tight. The hug felt so comforting against the chilly wind. Afterwards, Pip gently used a warm, damp cloth to wash the little blue spot right off Penny’s tummy until it was fluffy and white again. Penny giggled as it tickled. They decided to paint together, sharing the brushes with extra care. Pip learned that a warm hug has the magic power to turn an oops into a happy smile.

stories.title: Maya Mouse's Quiet Time
stories.text: High up in the green meadow, Maya Mouse was building a wonderful bridge out of colorful autumn leaves. It was almost finished, reaching all the way across the soft moss path. Just then, her friend Toby Mouse came scampering past in a big hurry. Squeak, rush, zoom! Toby didn't see the leaf bridge. Crunch! His little paws stepped right on top of it, scattering the leaves everywhere. Maya’s ears drooped down. She had worked so hard on her bridge, and now it was ruined. Maya stomped her little foot and let out a tiny squeak of frustration. Toby stopped running and looked at the scattered leaves. He saw Maya’s sad face and felt a little flutter of worry in his chest. Toby’s big sister, Minnie Mouse, trotted over. She gently wrapped her paws around Toby and gave him a warm, supportive squeeze. 'We need to use our gentle words when we make a mistake, Toby,' Minnie reminded him softly. Toby nodded and took a few steps toward Maya. He looked so sorry. 'I am so, so sorry I rushed and ruined your bridge, Maya,' Toby said gently. 'Can I give you a warm apology hug?' Maya looked at Toby's kind, remorseful face. The frustration melted right out of her heart. She opened her arms, and the two little mice gave each other a big, comforting hug. 'Thank you for apologizing, Toby,' Maya said softly. Together, they knelt down in the soft grass and collected the leaves. This time, they built an even bigger, stronger leaf bridge side by side. They cheered happily as they placed the very last leaf on top, knowing that friendship and hugs can fix almost anything.

stories.title: Benny Bear Shares the Blocks
stories.text:
Once upon a time, in a cozy little den in the big green woods, lived a sweet little bear named Benny. Benny was two and a half years old, and his absolute favorite thing in the whole wide world was playing with bright red wooden blocks. He loved to stack them up, up, up until they reached his fuzzy nose, and then—CRASH!—he loved to watch them tumble down.

One sunny morning, Benny was busy building a giant tower on the soft yellow rug in his playroom. Just then, his dear friend Lily Bunny hopped by. Lily had long, soft ears and a very kind heart. She looked at the blocks and smiled her biggest smile. 'Can I help build, Benny?' she asked in a soft, gentle voice.

Now, Benny was having so much fun that his paws moved a little too fast. Instead of sharing, he gave a quick little shove, and—oh no!—he knocked over Lily's favorite blue block right out of her paws. Lily's ears drooped down, and a tiny tear popped out of her eye. She felt very sad.

Benny looked at Lily's sad face. His tummy felt a little bit heavy and squiggly, like he had swallowed a bumpy rock. His mama bear, who was sitting nearby knitting a bright yellow scarf, looked over with kind, understanding eyes. 'Benny,' Mama whispered softly, 'sometimes our paws move too fast. When we make a mistake, what helps make our friend's heart feel better?'

Benny remembered! He took a big, deep breath. He crawled over to Lily on his hands and knees. 'I'm sorry, Lily,' Benny said in his sweet little bear voice. Then, he opened his arms wide, wide, wide. Lily opened her arms, too. They wrapped themselves around each other in a warm, cozy apology hug. Squeeeeze! 

Instantly, the heavy rock in Benny's tummy disappeared. Lily's ears popped right back up, and she smiled a big, happy bunny smile. 'Apology accepted, Benny!' she cheered. Together, they built the biggest block castle the woods had ever seen, side by side, as happy as could be.

stories.title: Pip's Broken Crayon
stories.text:
High up in the leafy branches of the great oak tree lived Pip the little squirrel. Pip loved art time more than anything. He loved bright yellow crayons, sparkly green crayons, and especially the big red crayon that looked just like a sweet, juicy strawberry. 

Today, Pip was sitting at his little acorn-cap table, coloring a picture of a smiling sun for his papa. Just as Pip was pressing down hard to make the sunbeams extra bright, his friend Sam Squirrel zoomed by, chasing a bouncy little bug. Zoom! Swish! Sam's furry tail bumped right into Pip's table. SNAP! 

Oh, dear! The big red crayon broke right in half. Pip gasped, and his little whiskers twitched. He felt a hot, prickly feeling inside his cheeks. He wanted to stomp his foot and shout, 'Hey! That was my favorite crayon!' He opened his mouth to be grumpy.

But then, Pip looked at Sam. Sam's eyes were wide and round. Sam looked so sorry, and his ears were pressed flat against his head. Sam didn't mean to bump the table; he was just having too much fun playing.

Pip's papa walked over, carrying a cup of warm blackberry tea. He knelt down beside the tiny wooden table. 'Pip,' Papa said gently, rubbing Pip's furry back, 'accidents happen when we play fast. But we can always fix our friendships with love.'

Pip took a slow, deep sniff, smelling the sweet berries. The prickly feeling in his cheeks started to melt away. He looked at Sam and spoke in a kind voice. 'It was an accident, Sam. But my crayon is broken.' Sam nodded sadly. 'I'm sorry I bumped your table, Pip,' Sam whispered.

Pip knew just what to do. He opened his arms as wide as they could stretch. Sam leaned in, and the two little squirrels gave each other a wonderful, warm apology hug. It was so soft and snuggly! 

'All better!' Pip chirped happily. Papa helped them tape the red crayon together, and guess what? They found out that a taped crayon makes double the squiggles. They colored together all afternoon, sharing giggles and hugs.

stories.title: Mia's Gentle Tumble
stories.text:
Down by the sparkling blue pond lived Mia the little duckling. Mia had bright orange webbed feet that loved to splash in the puddles. Today was a wonderful day for running through the soft green grass and chasing fluffy white dandelions as they floated in the breeze.

Mia was running super-duper fast, flapping her little yellow wings. 'Look at me fly!' she quacked. But her webbed feet got a little tangled in a patch of clover, and—whoops-a-daisy!—she tumbled right into her friend Oliver Duckling, knocking him down into the soft moss.

Oliver let out a surprised little 'Quack!' and landed right on his tail feathers. He looked down at his tummy, and his little beak turned down into a tiny frown. He scraped his knee just a tiny bit, and it stung.

Mia scrambled right up to her feet. She saw Oliver's frown and felt a funny, heavy wiggle in her chest. She didn't mean to knock him over, but she felt bad that her friend was sitting in the moss with a frown.

Mia's grandma, who was resting by the reeds, quacked softly. 'Mia, sweet duckling, when we bump into our friends, a warm hug makes everything bright again.'

Mia nodded her yellow head. She waddled right over to Oliver. 'I'm so sorry I bumped you, Oliver,' she said, her voice as gentle as a floating feather. Then, Mia opened her wings wide and leaned in close. Oliver opened his wings too, and they gave each other a long, warm, feathery apology hug.
