He puts on his bright yellow t-shirt and his favorite sneakers with the Velcro straps. Then, he remembers his very best helper. It is time for the helmet! Sam runs inside and grabs his helmet with the dinosaur pictures on it. There is a green T-Rex and a blue Triceratops right on the side. Sam loves his dinosaur helmet. He carefully puts the helmet on his head, making sure the dinosaurs are looking straight ahead. Mummy helps him adjust the straps so they fit comfortably under his little chin. Click! Goes the buckle, snapping securely into place. Sam gives a big roar like a dinosaur to test out his voice. Roar! Mummy laughs and roars back. Sam is fully geared up and looking super cool. He trots outside to the driveway where his balance bike sits patiently. He straddles the frame, holding onto the handlebars with both hands. His feet touch the ground, ready to push. Push, push, glide! Sam lifts his feet up into the air for one whole second. Look at him balance! He is gliding along like a bird on the wind. The wheels rumble softly over the sidewalk cracks. Sam feels so proud and strong wearing his helmet. He knows that taking care of his head means he can keep having fun adventures tomorrow, and the day after that, too. He pushes off again, a huge grin spreading across his face. The world is big, his bike is fast, and his helmet keeps him safe. Keep on rolling, little Sam!

stories.title: Leo's Shiny Blue Helmet
stories.text: Ring, ring! Good morning, sweet Leo! Today is a very exciting day because the sun is shining, and it is a wonderful day for a ride on the big blue tricycle. But before the wheels can start to roll, Leo needs to get ready. Do you know what helps keep Leo safe and smart? His very own shiny blue helmet! Leo walks over to the shelf where his special helmet is waiting. It is the color of the big sky, and it has a shiny star right on the front. Leo picks it up with both hands. It feels smooth and cool. 'Time for your helmet, Leo!' says Mama with a big, happy smile. Leo sits right down on the little wooden chair and places the helmet gently on his head. Pop goes the little cushion inside! Now, it is time for the best part—the click. Leo pulls the two straps together under his chin. Snap! They make a happy little click sound. Mama gives the helmet a gentle wiggle to make sure it is wearing its cozy seatbelt. It stays right in place, snug as a bug. Leo gives a big, proud stomp with his sneakers. 'All safe!' cheers Leo. Mama claps her hands. 'You look like a super rider!' Now that the shiny blue helmet is snug and secure, it is time for the wheels to roll. Leo runs outside to the driveway. His little feet pedal round and round. Zoom, zoom, go the tricycle wheels! The breeze tickles Leo's nose as he pedals down the sidewalk. He feels so strong, so brave, and so happy. Wearing his helmet makes him feel like he can go on any adventure in the whole wide world. When it is time to park the tricycle, Leo gently takes off his helmet and puts it back on its special shelf, ready for the next fun day. Great job, safe rider Leo!

stories.title: Maya and the Scooter Sparkle
stories.text: The morning sun is peeking through the fluffy white curtains in Maya's room. Good morning, Maya! Today, the pink scooter is waiting by the front door, ready for a grand adventure. But wait! Before the little rubber wheels can spin down the path, Maya has a very important superhero job to do. She needs to put on her sparkly pink helmet! Maya skips over to the hallway hook where her helmet hangs like a little dome of magic. It is covered in bright silver sparkles that catch the light and twinkle like stars. Maya reaches up high on her tiptoes and grabs it. 'My sparkly helmet!' she whispers happily. She brings it down and sets it right on top of her curly hair. It feels like a crown fit for a fast little princess. Now, let us check the safety hug under the chin. Maya finds the two soft straps. She brings them together and—click!—they give a friendly little hug right under her chin. Not too tight, and not too loose, but just right. Maya gives her head a little shake. The helmet stays snug, protecting her happy thoughts inside. 'Ready for takeoff!' calls Papa from the porch. Maya does a happy little dance, her sparkly helmet bobbing up and down. She steps outside, places one sneaker on the pink scooter, and pushes off with the other foot. Whoosh! The scooter glides smoothly over the pavement. The wheels make a soft whirring sound as they roll. Maya smiles from ear to ear, feeling like she is flying through the air. Wearing her helmet keeps her safe while she explores the big, beautiful neighborhood. When the ride is all done, Maya parks her scooter and carefully hangs up her sparkly helmet. What a wonderful, safe ride!

stories.title: Sammy's Balanced Bicycle
stories.text: Knock, knock! Who is ready to ride today? It is Sammy, the energetic little explorer! Sammy has a brand-new red balance bike with handlebars that shine in the morning light. He cannot wait to feel the wind in his hair and practice his super balancing skills. But first, every smart rider knows the golden rule: helmet on, wheels roll! Sammy runs into the living room where Daddy is holding Sammy's favorite green helmet. It has funny little dinosaur spikes running right down the middle, just like a friendly little stegosaurus! Sammy giggles. 'Roar!' says Sammy to his helmet. Daddy laughs too. 'Time to put on your dinosaur protector, Sammy.' Sammy sits down on the fluffy carpet and lowers the green helmet onto his head. It feels warm and comfortable. Next comes the most important safety step of all—the click! Sammy holds one strap in his left hand and one in his right. He brings them together under his chin. Click! The buckle fastens securely, giving a gentle pat to his chin. Daddy checks it with one finger. 'One finger space, nice and snug. Perfect!' Sammy stands up tall and beats his chest like a little dinosaur. He feels ready for anything. Out to the park they go, where the path is smooth and green. Sammy straddles his red balance bike. He pushes off with his strong legs, lifting his feet up as he glides along. Whee! The little wheels roll fast and smooth over the pavement. Sammy keeps his eyes looking straight ahead, feeling so proud and secure with his dinosaur helmet guarding his head. When it is time to go inside for lunch, Sammy gives his bike a big hug and proudly carries his helmet inside. Riding safely is so much fun!

stories.title: Leo's Shiny Red Helmet
stories.text: Good morning, little Leo! Today is a very sunny day, and Leo's shiny red balance bike is waiting right by the front door. It has two big wheels and soft rubber handles, ready for a fun outdoor adventure. But wait! Before Leo can ride down the driveway, he needs something very special to keep his head safe and happy. Do you know what it is? It is his bright red helmet! Leo sits right on the soft living room rug and picks up his helmet. He looks at it in the mirror and gives a big, proud smile. He places the helmet right on top of his head, just like a crown for a brave little rider. Click! Goes the buckle under his gentle chin. Leo wiggles his head left and right. The helmet stays snug and secure, hugging his head with love. 'All safe!' cheers Mama, clapping her hands together. Leo stands up tall and walks to the front door. He grabs the rubber handles of his balance bike and pushes off with his little shoes. Push, glide, and roll! The red wheels spin round and round on the smooth pavement, making a happy whirring sound. The warm morning breeze tickles Leo's cheeks as he zooms down the path. Because he wore his helmet, he feels like a soaring superhero ready to conquer the whole wide world. Stopping gently with his shoes, Leo looks at Mama and giggles with pure joy. Wearing a helmet is so much fun when you are cruising on wheels. When it is time to go back inside, Leo takes off his helmet and gives it a gentle pat, saying thank you to his trusty head protector. What a wonderful ride! He hangs his helmet up on its special peg, ready for the next sunny day of zooming around.

stories.title: Maya's Scooter Adventure
stories.text: Time to wake up, little scooter stars! Maya looks outside her bedroom window and sees the sparkling sidewalk calling her name. Her pink scooter with the shiny purple wheels is parked right on the porch, waiting for a morning journey. Maya loves her scooter so much, but she loves her safety even more. She knows the golden rule of wheels: helmet on before the scooter rolls! Maya skips over to the basket where her sparkly purple helmet lives. She picks it up with both hands, feeling how light and sturdy it is. With a little help from Papa, she places the helmet right on her head. It fits like a cozy hat designed just for her. Papa holds the strap under Maya's chin and makes a funny little clicking sound with his tongue. Click! The buckle fastens securely, resting softly against her skin. Papa gives Maya a gentle nose-beep. 'Ready for takeoff, Captain Maya?' he asks with a warm, loving smile. Maya nods enthusiastically. 'Ready!' she shouts. She steps out onto the sidewalk, places one sneakered foot on the scooter deck, and pushes off with the other foot. Zoom! The purple wheels spin smoothly over the sidewalk cracks, humming a cheerful little song. Maya feels like she is flying over the ground, her arms steady on the handlebars. She steers gently around a friendly chalk drawing of a star. Because her helmet is buckled snugly, she feels brave, safe, and completely unstoppable. Riding her scooter makes her heart feel light and bubbly. After a few wonderful turns up and down the path, Maya brings her scooter to a gentle stop. She hops off, unbuckles her helmet, and gives Papa a big hug. Putting on her helmet is the best way to start a rolling adventure.

stories.title: Sam's Tricycle Journey
stories.text: Ring, ring! Good morning, little Sam! The birds are singing outside, and Sam's big yellow tricycle is waiting in the yard. It has three sturdy wheels, shiny yellow pedals, and a little basket in the back for his favorite teddy bear. Sam is so excited to pedal around the yard, but first, it is time for a very important helmet ritual. Sam marches right over to the hallway shelf where his green dinosaur helmet rests. It even has cute little soft spikes on top, just like a friendly stegosaurus! Sam picks up his dinosaur helmet and giggles. He places it carefully on his head, making sure the dinosaur spikes are pointing straight up toward the sky. 'Roar!' whispers Sam with a happy grin. Grandma helps him adjust the straps so it fits just right, hugging his head in a warm, protective embrace. Click goes the buckle, secure and cozy. Sam touches his green helmet and feels like a speedy, safe little dinosaur ready to explore the big green grass. He walks outside, climbs onto the comfortable seat of his yellow tricycle, and places his sneakers right on the pedals. One, two, three—push! The yellow wheels roll forward, turning in smooth, steady circles across the lawn. Sam pedals past the bright yellow sunflowers and waves to the buzzing bees. The wind dances through his clothes while his dinosaur helmet keeps his head safe and snug. Riding his tricycle is the happiest part of the whole morning. When his legs get just a little bit tired, Sam uses his feet to brake gently to a stop. He climbs off his tricycle, gives his dinosaur helmet a loving pat, and runs inside for a yummy snack. Helmet on, wheels roll, and safety makes every ride a happy adventure!

stories.title: Leo's Shiny Blue Helmet
stories.text: Ring-ring! Goes the little bicycle bell. Good morning, Leo! Today is a very sunny and bright day, and Leo’s blue balance bike is waiting by the front door. But wait! Before the little wheels can roll, something very important must happen. Can you guess what it is? Yes! It is time for Leo's shiny blue helmet. Leo sits right on the cozy living room rug. Mommy brings the helmet over. It is blue like the summer sky and has shiny silver stars painted all the sides. Leo reaches out with his little hands and touches it. 'Beep beep!' says Leo with a happy giggle. Mommy gently places the helmet right on top of Leo's fluffy hair. Click! Goes the buckle under Leo's chin. Mommy checks it with a gentle wiggle finger. 'Is it comfy, sweetie?' asks Mommy. Leo smiles a big, warm smile and nods his head. 'Comfy like a hug!' says Leo. A helmet is a cozy little hug for your head that keeps you safe while you play. Now Leo is ready for adventure! He stands up tall, walks outside to the sidewalk, and hops onto his blue balance bike. Push with the left foot, push with the right foot. Zoom! The wheels go round and round. The breeze tickles Leo's cheeks. He rides past the big green tree and waves hello to a fuzzy brown squirrel. 'Look at me, wheels!' cheers Leo. He feels so brave and strong. When it is time to go back inside for a snack, Leo stops his bike all by himself. He gives his blue helmet a gentle pat. 'Good job keeping me safe,' he whispers. What a wonderful bicycle ride today!

stories.title: Mia's Scooter Adventure
stories.text: Clitter-clatter, goes Mia's pink scooter on the porch. Mia loves her scooter more than almost anything in the whole wide world. It has two sparkly pink wheels and handles that are just the right size for her little hands. But before Mia zooms down the driveway, she knows just what to do. Safety first, fun second! Mia runs inside to grab her special pink helmet with the polka dots. It looks just like a giant strawberry! Mia sits on the bottom step of the porch. She holds her strawberry helmet carefully in her lap. Daddy sits down right next to her to help. Together, they slide the helmet over Mia's pigtails. Click! Goes the little buckle. Daddy gives a gentle tickle to Mia's tummy. 'Buckle snug, just like a hug!' sings Daddy. Mia wiggles her head from side to side. The helmet stays right in place, protecting her head like a crown. 'I am a safety princess!' declares Mia proudly. She stands up and skips over to her pink scooter. One little foot goes right on the deck, and the other foot pushes off the ground. Push, push, glide! The wheels spin fast, making a happy whirring sound against the pavement. Mia rides in big circles around the driveway chalk flowers she drew earlier. The sun feels warm on her back, and she is having so much fun. Riding with her helmet on makes her feel like she can fly. When her tummy starts to rumble for lunchtime, Mia parks her scooter neatly by the door. She unbuckles her helmet all by herself. Click! 'All done!' says Mia, clapping her hands. What a happy morning on wheels!

stories.title: Sam's Tricycle Journey
stories.text: One, two, three big red wheels! Sam's tricycle is parked right on the back patio. It is shiny, bright red, and ready for a big journey around the backyard track. Sam races over to his trike, but Grandma holds up a yellow stop sign with a smile. 'Hold on, little driver! First things first,' says Grandma. Sam stops and giggles. He knows the rule! No wheels roll without a helmet on the head. Grandma brings out Sam's favorite yellow helmet. It even has little dinosaur spikes on the top, just like a friendly green stegosaurus! Sam loves his dinosaur helmet. He sits on the patio chair and holds his arms up high. Grandma places the yellow helmet gently onto Sam's head. Click! The little black buckle fastens snugly under his chin. Grandma gives the helmet a gentle tap. 'Is your dinosaur ready to roar?' asks Grandma. Sam lets out a loud, silly 'Roar!' that makes Grandma laugh out loud. The helmet is snug, safe, and super cool. Sam hops off the chair and runs over to his big red tricycle. He climbs up onto the comfortable seat. His feet find the pedaling spots easily. Left foot, right foot, push and go! The three red wheels rumble softly over the patio stones. Sam steers his trike past the yellow daisies, past the garden hose, and all the way to the big oak tree. He feels like a brave dinosaur explorer discovering new lands. Every time he pedals, he smiles bigger and bigger. When Grandma calls out that it is time for lunch, Sam gently slows his tricycle to a stop. He climbs off and carefully takes off his yellow helmet. He gives the dinosaur spikes a little high-five. 'Good riding today!' says Sam happily.

stories.title: Leo's Shiny Red Helmet
stories.text: Good morning, little Leo! Today is a very sunny day, and the sidewalk is calling your name. Zoom, zoom! Are you ready to ride your shiny red balance bike? But wait! Before our wheels can roll, we have a very important friend to meet. Can you guess who it is? It is your super-duper, superhero helmet! Let us go find it resting on the shelf. Look how shiny and bright red it is, just like a fire truck. When we put on our helmet, we are keeping our smart, happy head safe and sound while we have fun. Let us practice together. You hold it with your two little hands. Great job! Now, place it right on top of your head. Wow, you look like a real racing champion! Now, let us check the straps. Underneath your chin, we do a gentle little click. Click! Did you hear that happy sound? Let us give your head a little wiggle. Does it wiggle? No, it stays snug and comfy like a warm hug for your noggin. Perfect! Now that your helmet is securely on, your head is ready for a fantastic adventure. Are you ready? Let us grab your favorite balance bike. You push off with your strong little feet. One, two, three, glide! Look at you go down the pathway, zooming past the green grass and the dancing flowers. You are balancing so well, keeping your eyes straight ahead. Your little feet are kicking the ground, making happy pattering sounds. Pat-pat-pat, zoom-zoom-zoom! Your helmet stays right where it belongs, protecting you every single inch of the way. When you ride safely, you can play longer and have even more fun. You did such a wonderful job remembering your safety gear today, Leo. Riding bikes is so much better when we take care of ourselves first. Let us take a little break on the bench and give ourselves a high five. Thump! High five! You are a superstar rider, and your shiny red helmet is your trusty sidekick. Let us take it off gently, undoing the click, and set it down for next time. What a wonderful morning of outdoor fun!

stories.title: Maya's Scooter Adventure
stories.text: Ring, ring! Good morning, sweet Maya! The birds are singing outside, and the pavement is waiting for your sparkly pink scooter. Are your feet ready to scoot, scoot, scoot? Before we fly down the sidewalk like a butterfly, we need to do our special safety check. Do you know what the most important rule is? Helmet on, wheels roll! Let us waddle over to the gear box and pick out your favorite teal helmet with the silver stars. This helmet is magical. When you wear it, you are protected and ready for anything. Let us place it right on your head. Make sure it sits nice and flat, covering your forehead just like a crown. Now comes the trickiest, most important part: the chin buckle. Can you make a pincher with your fingers? Pinch! We bring the two straps together underneath your chin and press them until we hear a magical click. Yay! Let us do a quick wiggle test. Shake your head yes! Shake your head no! Does the helmet stay snug and secure? Yes, it does! It hugs your head like a soft, cozy pillow. Now your head is safe, and you are ready to roll. You pick up your teal scooter with the sparkly handlebar streamers. You step on with your strong left foot, and you push with your right. Push, glides, scoot! Look at you go! The wind is gently blowing through your hair, and the scooter wheels are humming a happy song. Whirrrr, whirrrr! You steer gently around a big fluffy leaf on the sidewalk. You are doing such an amazing job watching where you are going. Your teal helmet sparkles brightly in the warm sunshine, showing everyone that you are a smart and safe driver. Scouting outside is such a joyful way to move your body and feel the fresh air. Whenever you stop to look at a bug or wave to a neighbor, your helmet stays comfortably in place. You are showing so much responsibility today, Maya. When it is time to head back inside for a yummy snack, you gently unbuckle your chin strap with a soft snap. You put your helmet right back in its special spot. You are a true scooter pro!

stories.title: Sammy's Tricycle Journey
stories.text: Beep, beep! Good morning, little Sammy! The sun is peeking through your bedroom window, and your yellow tricycle is parked right by the front door. Those three big wheels are spinning with excitement, waiting for you to climb aboard. But wait just a second! Before those wheels can start to roll, we have an important job to do. Helmet on, wheels roll! Let us find your awesome blue helmet with the cool dinosaur stickers on the side. Can you roar like a dinosaur? Roar! Your helmet is ready to keep your brain safe and cozy while you pedal around the driveway. Let us lift the helmet up high and place it gently onto your head. Tilt it just a little bit so it sits right above your eyebrows. You look so handsome and ready for action! Now, let us look down at the chin strap. We need to be very careful and gentle here. We bring the straps together and snap them into place. Click! There is that wonderful sound. Let us check together. Can you open your mouth wide like a happy dinosaur? Ahhh! Good, the strap has just enough room for a gentle smile. Now, let us test it. Shake, shake, shake your head! Wonderful, it is snug and secure. Your head is fully protected by your dinosaur friends. Time to ride! You march over to your yellow tricycle, climb up onto the comfortable seat, and place your feet firmly on the pedals. Ready, set, pedal! One foot pushes down, then the other foot pushes down. Round and round go the pedals, making a happy clicking rhythm. Click-clack, click-clack! You steer your tricycle in a big circle around the chalk drawings on the driveway. You are pedaling so smoothly and using your strong leg muscles. Your blue dinosaur helmet bops up and down as you ride, cheering you on every step of the way. Riding your tricycle makes you feel so strong and free. When your ride is all done, you park your trike neatly by the porch. You unbuckle your chin strap and take off your helmet, giving it a gentle pat. You played so safely today, Sammy. What a fantastic adventurer you are!

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Put your helmet on and play.
Snug and safe upon your head,
Better than a sleepy bed.

Buckle fast and buckle tight,
Now you fit just right, just right.
Click goes the buckle on your chin,
Let the happy ride begin!

Wheels go rolling down the street,
Moving fast your little feet.
Pedal round and pedal high,
Reaching up into the sky.

Stop and look and smile and grin,
Safe and happy, you can win!
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Best adventure of the past.

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Grab your bike and grab your gear,
No more waiting, time is here.
Lift the helmet, big and round,
Set it nicely, safe and sound.

Fingers ready, snap the click,
Make the little buckle quick.
Pull it gently, check it twice,
Look at you, you look so nice!

Push away and off you go,
Fast and steady, not too slow.
Wheels go spinning round and round,
Touching lightly on the ground.

Sing a happy riding song,
As you safely roll along.
Helmet on and wheels roll free,
Happiest kid for all to see!

rhymes.title: Ready for the Ride
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Wave to every bird on high.
Time to ride the sidewalk track,
With a shiny backpack back.

First a helmet for your head,
Keep it safe just like I said.
Strap it under, gentle squeeze,
Now you look like buzzing bees.

Push the pedals with your toes,
Feel the wind upon your nose.
Wheels go humming down the lane,
Happy as a choo-choo train.

Turn the corners, beep the horn,
Best young rider ever born.
Helmet on and wheels roll grand,
Safest cyclist in the land.

rhymes.title: The Big Red Helmet
rhymes.text:
Red and shiny, round and bright,
Puts our safety first tonight.
Wait, it's daytime, time to play,
We will ride the day away.

Place it gently on your brow,
We are ready, starting now.
Snap the button underneath,
Show me all your pearly teeth!

Out the door and down the street,
Moving fast your tiny feet.
Wheels go whirring, shiny things,
Making you feel like you've wings.

Laughing as you breeze along,
Singing out a happy song.
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Make this joyful moment last.

rhymes.title: Helmet Hero
rhymes.text:
You're a hero, brave and bold,
Wearing armor made of gold.
Well, it's plastic, blue and cool,
Ready for the riding school.

Put it on and lock it tight,
Making sure it fits just right.
No more waiting, doors are wide,
Time to take a little ride.

Wheels roll over bumpy stones,
Listen to the happy tones.
Cling and clang and ring the bell,
Everything is going well.

Home again before the night,
Helmet off and feeling bright.
Helmet on and wheels roll true,
What a fun day it was for you!

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Get your gear and shout hooray!
First thing first, let's find our treat,
To keep us safe from head to feet.

Bring the helmet, shiny red,
Place it gently on your head.
Buckle fast under your chin,
Now the zooming fun can begin!

Strap goes click and feels so snug,
Giving your sweet head a hug.
Is it comfy? Yes, it's grand!
Best protection in the land.

Now grab the handlebars so bold,
Watch the wheels roll, strong and old.
Pedal fast and feel the breeze,
Riding happy through the trees!

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Time to watch the world go by.
Before we ride our scooter fast,
Let's make sure this safety's last? No, first!

Hold the helmet, round and bright,
Set it on your forehead right.
Pull the strap and make it neat,
Ready down upon the street.

Hear the little buckle click,
Doing up the strap so quick.
Tap the top to test it well,
Safe inside our shiny shell.

Push away and off we go,
Watch the wheels roll to and fro.
Spinning round and shining bright,
Riding safely in the light!

rhymes.title: Ready, Set, Helmet
rhymes.text:
Bicycle is waiting near,
Time to get our proper gear.
Every rider knows the rule,
Keeping safe is really cool.

Pick the helmet off the shelf,
Put it on all by yourself.
Snap the buckle underneath,
Show me all your happy teeth!

Snug and cozy, fits just right,
Holding on with all its might.
Now our head is safe and sound,
Best protection to be found.

Push the pedals with your toes,
Where we're going, no one knows.
Watch the wheels roll down the street,
Moving fast on happy feet!

rhymes.title: Helmet Hug
rhymes.text:
Time to ride upon our bike,
Going any place we like.
Wait a minute, stop the clock,
Need to lock up and unlock?

Need our helmet for the ride,
Keeping safety by our side.
Put it on the curly hair,
Sitting nicely way up there.

Underneath the little chin,
Buckle up and let's begin.
Give the strap a gentle pull,
Now our joy is feeling full.

Wheels are spinning on the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Watch the wheels roll round and round,
Happiest kid in the town!

rhymes.title: The Zooming Hat
rhymes.text:
Little trike is waiting low,
Begging us to start and go.
First we need our special hat,
We are very sure of that.

It's a helmet, hard and strong,
Nothing here can get it wrong.
Rest it on your crown so high,
Reaching upward to the sky.

Snap the clicker, hear it sound,
Feet are planted on the ground.
Is it comfy? Give a nod,
Ready for the parking quad.

Grab the grips and start to stroll,
Watch the wheels roll to the goal.
Zooming fast and zooming high,
Wave as all the trees go by!

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Get your gear and shout hooray!
First thing first before we run,
Let us get our helmet on.

Snap the buckle underneath,
Show your happy little teeth.
Is it snug and is it tight?
Now we know that it is right!

Grab the scooter, hold the bar,
We can travel very far.
Push your foot and off you go,
Watch the pretty wheels roll slow.

Round and round the driveway track,
Smiling front and smiling back.
Helmet safe upon your head,
Time to ride until we're fed!

rhymes.title: Wheels Roll Fast
rhymes.text:
Red and shiny, bright and neat,
Ready for the rider's feet.
Take your helmet off the shelf,
Put it gently on yourself.

Click the clip below your chin,
Let the bicycle fun begin!
Push the pedals round and round,
Lift your toes up off the ground.

Wheels roll fast and wheels roll slow,
That is how we love to go.
Down the sidewalk, past the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.

Keep your balance, look ahead,
Wear your safety shield instead.
Helmet snug and wheels roll free,
Come and ride along with me!

rhymes.title: Little Biker
rhymes.text:
Little biker, time to play,
We are going out today.
Bring your helmet, shiny blue,
Waiting right in front of you.

Put it gently on your crown,
Covering the bumps right down.
Click the strap to keep it near,
Now you have no cause to fear.

Wheels are rolling on the street,
Moving fast with tiny feet.
Spinning fast and spinning bright,
Catching all the morning light.

Safe and happy, off you steer,
Having lots of fun, my dear.
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Make this joyful ride last!

rhymes.title: The Roll and Ride
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Let us wave the house goodbye.
Time to ride our tricycle fast,
Winter days are in the past.

Strap the helmet on your dome,
Farther than we stay at home.
Buckle clicks with such a snap,
Ready for a rolling lap.

Wheels roll round upon the floor,
Rolling right outside the door.
Listen to the rubber sound,
As we circle all around.

Guard your head and keep it tight,
Everything is feeling right.
Helmet on and wheels roll high,
Underneath the big blue sky!

rhymes.title: Happy Helmet
rhymes.text:
Happy helmet, cozy head,
Better than a cozy bed.
Time to grab your rolling gear,
Adventure time is finally here.

Lift it up and place it square,
Right upon your curly hair.
Snap the button underneath,
While you flash a happy teeth.

Push the tricycle along,
Singing out a happy song.
Watch the shiny wheels roll past,
Moving steady, moving fast.

Safe and sound from side to side,
Enjoying every single ride.
Helmet on and wheels roll away,
What a truly joyful day!

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Put your helmet on and play!
Snug and safe upon your head,
Better than a cozy bed.

First we find the shiny shell,
Does it fit you nice and well?
Bring it down upon your brow,
You are looking ready now!

Find the straps that hang below,
Are we ready? Here we go!
Click the buckle, hear it snap,
Now you have a helmet cap.

Push the wheels and feel the breeze,
Moving fast with such great ease!
Round and round the pedals go,
Helmet on, wheels roll, ho ho!

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Scooter waiting by the door,
Time to explore more and more!
Fetch your helmet off the chair,
Put it gently in your hair.

Pull it down to guard your nose,
Right above where thinking goes.
Look for straps of black and blue,
Let me loop them under you.

Underneath your little chin,
Time to push the buckle in!
Click! It tells us we are right,
Snug and comfy, not too tight.

Give a high five, start to stroll,
Helmet on, and wheels will roll!
Pushing off with happy feet,
Riding down the sunny street.

rhymes.title: My Shiny Helmet
rhymes.text:
Big red tricycle is here,
Let us give a happy cheer!
First we grab the brightest hat,
Let us buckle up with that.

It protects your noggin well,
Like a little turtle shell.
Slide it on and tap the top,
Ready now, we will not stop.

Find the chin strap, soft and sweet,
Make the loop look nice and neat.
Click the buckle into place,
With a smile upon your face.

Toes are pushing on the ground,
Wheels are spinning all around!
Helmet on, wheels roll away,
What a super fun-filled day!

rhymes.title: Strap It Tight
rhymes.text:
Roller skates begin to shine,
Everything is looking fine!
Time to get your armor on,
We will skate until the dawn.

Grab your helmet, hold it tight,
Place it on your head just right.
Level on your forehead grand,
Finest helmet in the land!

Fingers busy, find the clip,
Just a little zip and slip.
Click it fast and hear the sound,
Off we go to skim the ground!

Legs are bending, arms are wide,
What a joyful, bumpy ride!
Helmet on, wheels roll so fast,
Making happy moments last.

rhymes.title: Ready for the Ride
rhymes.text:
Bicycle with shiny bell,
We love riding it so well!
First rule of the riding game,
Put your helmet on the same.

Lift it high and guide it down,
Crown you like a safety king or queen,
Let your happy eyes be seen.

Now the buckle needs a snap,
Underneath your chin a tap.
Snug and comfy, give a nod,
Ready for the travel pod.

Push the pedals with your toes,
Watch how fast the driveway goes!
Helmet on, wheels roll along,
Singing out our riding song!

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Get your gear and shout hooray!
First thing first before we run,
Time to have some rolling fun.

Pick your helmet off the floor,
Right beside the garden door.
Put it gently on your head,
Just like Mommy always said.

Is it comfy? Is it tight?
Let us check and get it right.
Snap the buckle underneath,
While you show your happy teeth!

Helmet on and ready now,
Make a deep and happy bow.
Wheels roll fast and wheels roll slow,
Jump upon your bike and go!

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Wave to birdies flying high!
Scooter waiting in the street,
Tap your little happy feet.

Grab your helmet, shiny red,
Place it softly on your head.
Look into the looking glass,
Watch the happy toddler pass.

Find the straps and pull them through,
Click the buckle, yes you do!
Snug and safe and feeling grand,
Best protector in the land.

Helmet on and wheels roll out,
Give a happy little shout.
Scoot around the block with glee,
Safe as safe as safe can be!

rhymes.title: The Tricycle Train
rhymes.text:
Ring the bell and ding-a-ling,
Let us dance and let us sing.
Time to ride our trikes around,
Listen to the happy sound.

Every rider needs a hat,
Not a woolly winter cat.
A shiny helmet strong and round,
Best protection to be found.

Lift it up and press it down,
Fit it like a golden crown.
Underneath the little chin,
Buckle up and let us spin!

Helmet on and wheels roll free,
Pedal fast for you and me.
Round and round the yard we go,
Fast and steady, fast and slow!

rhymes.title: Strap It Snug
rhymes.text:
Pups are barking, birds are near,
Time to get our riding gear.
Safety first is what we say,
Every single happy day.

Bring the helmet, don't forget,
Best accessory just yet.
Sit it right upon your brow,
We are almost ready now.

Fingers busy, click the snap,
Like a little turtle trap.
Not too loose and not too tight,
Just so comfy and just right.

Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Look at how our shadows cast!
Smiling faces in the sun,
Rolling is so much fun!

rhymes.title: Ready Set Roll
rhymes.text:
Wheels are spinning on the ground,
Making such a happy sound.
Grab your helmet off the chair,
Give your curly hair a care.

Slide it on your busy head,
Blue or yellow, green or red.
Pull it forward, nice and low,
So you are ready for the show.

Find the buckle, click it in,
Right beneath your little chin.
Give a nod and give a shake,
For safety's sweet and gentle sake.

Helmet on and wheels roll by,
Wave hello up to the sky.
Off we go to wheel and play,
Having such a lovely day!

rhymes.title: The Shiny Red Shield
rhymes.text:
Time to go outside and play,
We will have a happy day.
First we find our helmet bright,
Buckle up and hold it tight.

Round and safe upon your head,
Shining bright like strawberry red.
Click the strap and give a cheer,
Now the bicycle is near!

Wheels go rolling down the street,
Moving with our happy feet.
Pedal fast and pedal slow,
Watch the shiny bicycle go.

Time to ride and time to smile,
We will travel many a mile.
Safety first is what we say,
All along the sunny way.

rhymes.title: Click! Snap! Let's Roll!
rhymes.text:
Sun is up and skies are blue,
I have got a job for you.
Bring your helmet, big and round,
Off we go to look around.

Put it gently on your brow,
We are getting ready now.
Underneath your little chin,
Push the buckle, let it spin.

Click and snap, it fits so neat,
Ready for the neighborhood street.
Wheels go round and wheels go fast,
Having lots of fun at last.

Glide along the grassy park,
Playing safely till it's dark.
Helmet on and wheels roll too,
Happy little rider, you!

rhymes.title: The Scooter Super Star
rhymes.text:
Scooter waiting by the door,
Time to explore and so much more.
Grab your helmet off the chair,
Put it snugly in your hair.

Keep it level, keep it square,
Safety hugs you everywhere.
Snapping fast beneath your ear,
Now there is no need to fear.

Pushing off with little toes,
Off the speedy scooter goes.
Wheels are spinning on the ground,
Making such a happy sound.

Watch us zoom and watch us race,
Smiling happy little face.
Helmet on and wheels roll free,
Best explorer you can be!

rhymes.title: My Magic Safety Hat
rhymes.text:
Magic hat to keep us safe,
Riding down the driveway wave.
Put the helmet on your head,
Just like your big brother said.

Strap it down so it is snug,
Like a cozy ladybug.
Now your noggin is protected,
Just the way we all expected.

Push the pedals, hear the squeak,
Having fun throughout the week.
Wheels are rolling left and right,
Underneath the golden light.

Keep on moving, keep on steering,
All the neighborhood is cheering.
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Making joyful moments last.

rhymes.title: Tricycle Adventure Time
rhymes.text:
Tricycle with three big wheels,
Look at how it spins and squeals!
First we need our helmet gear,
So we ride without a fear.

Lift it up and drop it down,
Best protector in the town.
Click the buckle underneath,
Big smile showing all your teeth!

Ready now to take a trip,
Time to take a little zip.
Wheels roll round and wheels roll high,
Underneath the big blue sky.

Pedal forward, turn around,
Having fun upon the ground.
Helmet on and wheels roll great,
Cruising through the garden gate.

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Put your helmet on and play.
Snug and safe upon your head,
Better than a sleepy bed.
Click the buckle, nice and tight,
Now your gear is feeling right.
Wheels go round upon the street,
Moving fast with happy feet.
Pedal fast and pedal slow,
Watch the pretty flowers grow.
Turn the corners with a smile,
Riding safely for a while.
Ring the bell, oh hear the sound,
Happiest kid in all the town.
Sun is shining bright and clear,
Riding bikes is what we cheer.

rhymes.title: Ready to Roll
rhymes.text:
Scooter waiting by the door,
Time to explore the kitchen floor.
First things first, what do we need?
A special hat to take the lead!
Pop it on and chin strap down,
Best protector in the town.
Wheels are spinning round and round,
Off we go across the ground.
Push with one foot in the breeze,
Moving right beneath the trees.
Safety first is what we say,
Every single sunny day.
Faster, faster, hear us cheer,
Glad to have our helmet here.
Park the scooter, time to rest,
Wearing safety is the best.

rhymes.title: Strap It Snug
rhymes.text:
Little bike is painted red,
Place the helmet on your head.
Colors bright for all to see,
As happy as a honeybee.
Underneath your little chin,
Buckle up and let us spin.
Wheels roll smoothly on the path,
Splishing in a puddle bath.
Keep your balance, hold on tight,
Everything is feeling right.
Wave to puppy passing by,
Reaching up to touch the sky.
Pedal forward, do not stop,
Going straight up to the top.
Safe and sound and full of fun,
Till our daily ride is done.

rhymes.title: The Helmet Dance
rhymes.text:
Wiggle, giggle, do the dance,
Put your helmet on, advance!
Shiny plastic, comfy foam,
 Safe when we are far from home.
Under chin we click it fast,
Now the safety test is passed.
Wheels roll over bumpy ground,
Making such a joyful sound.
Steering left and steering right,
Underneath the morning light.
Smiling big for all to view,
My bicycle and little blue.
Push the pedals with your toes,
On the sidewalk where it goes.
Stop and smile and look around,
Best adventure to be found.

rhymes.title: Roll Away Today
rhymes.text:
Morning sun is shining bright,
Hesitate and lose the light.
Get your helmet off the shelf,
Put it on all by yourself.
Snap the buckle underneath,
Show me all your pearly teeth!
Wheels are rolling down the lane,
Happy as a passing train.
Keep your eyes upon the street,
Moving right along our feet.
Safety makes us feel so bold,
Bravest kids of young and old.
Ring the bell to say hello,
Watch us as we go, go, go.
Time to head back home to play,
Safe and happy all the day.

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Put your helmet on and play!
Snug and tight upon your head,
Bright and shiny blue or red.

Now we buckle up the chin,
Let the happy day begin!
Click and lock it, nice and neat,
Ready for the quiet street.

Scooter, scooter, big and small,
We are careful when we fall.
Wheels go rolling down the lane,
Happy as a choo-choo train.

Pedal fast and pedal slow,
That is how we safely go!
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Having fun from first to last.

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Get your helmet off the shelf,
You can put it on yourself!
Rest it gently on your brow,
Time to be a rider now.

Find the strap beneath your chin,
Push the little buckle in.
Click! It holds you safe and tight,
Everything is feeling right.

Now your tricycle is near,
Time to shout a happy cheer!
Push your pedals with your feet,
Down the sunny little street.

Wheels are spinning round and round,
Making such a happy sound.
Helmet on and wheels roll high,
Wave as all the trees go by.

rhymes.title: Super Rider Ready
rhymes.text:
Little rider, look around,
Time to leave the grassy ground.
First a helmet on your head,
Safe and sound just like we said.

Buckle under, make it snug,
Hug your helmet like a bug!
Now you look so brave and tall,
Ready for a rolling ball.

To your wagon or your bike,
Go the way you mostly like.
Push away and feel the breeze,
Sailing past the leafy trees.

Wheels go rolling on their way,
Playing games throughout the day.
Helmet on and wheels roll free,
Come and ride along with me.

rhymes.title: Round and Round We Go
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Little bird is flying high.
Time to ride your favorite toy,
Fill your heart with so much joy.

Grab your helmet, don't forget,
It's the safest friend you've met.
Slide it down upon your hair,
Safety is our proper care.

Underneath your little chin,
Buckle up and lock it in.
Now your rolling wheels are free,
As can happy children be.

Pushing off with happy feet,
Rolling down the little street.
Helmet on and wheels roll low,
Round and round and round we go.

rhymes.title: The Happy Helmet Song
rhymes.text:
Bicycle and wagon too,
Waiting right outside for you.
First we need a special hat,
We are very sure of that.

It is shining bright and strong,
Helps us safely sing our song.
Place it right upon your dome,
Far away and close to home.

Snap the buckle, click it tight,
Now you're ready for the light.
Green means go and off you race,
Big smiles on your little face.

Wheels are spinning, shiny bright,
Making everything just right.
Helmet on and wheels roll sweet,
Happy footsteps on the street.

rhymes.title: The Shiny Helmet Song
rhymes.text:
Time to ride our bikes today,
Let us go outside and play.
First we need our safety gear,
Nothing in the world to fear.

Pick the helmet off the shelf,
Put it on all by yourself.
Snap the buckle underneath,
Cheesy smile with all your teeth!

Is it comfy? Yes indeed!
Ready now for joyful speed.
Helmet sits up big and tall,
Protecting heads both great and small.

Push the pedals with your feet,
Riding down the sunny street.
Helmet on and wheels roll fast,
Having fun from first to last.

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Scooter waiting at the door,
Time to explore the neighborhood floor.
Grab the helmet, shiny red,
Place it gently on your head.

Bring the straps down nice and low,
Buckle clicks and off we go!
Pull it left and pull it right,
Make it snug and make it tight.

Toes are tapping on the ground,
Ready for a happy sound.
Wheels go round and wheels go fast,
Look at us go zooming past!

Safety first is what we say,
Every single riding day.
Helmet on and wheels roll true,
Happy little friend are you.

rhymes.title: The Tricycle Parade
rhymes.text:
Trike is parked and looking neat,
Waiting for my active feet.
But before we start to race,
Put the helmet into place.

Round my crown it fits so sweet,
From my forehead to my seat.
Click the buckle, hear the snap,
Tap it gently, tap-tap-tap.

Now my head is safe and sound,
Best protection to be found.
Hop on up and grab the bars,
We can ride up to the stars!

Pushing pedals round and round,
Making such a happy sound.
Helmet on and wheels roll free,
Come along and ride with me!

rhymes.title: Ready, Set, Roll!
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Little birds go flying by.
We have places we must go,
Watch the bicycle wheels go.

Stop right there and take a look,
Grab our gear just like a book.
Helmet goes upon the head,
Pink or yellow, blue or red.

Underneath the chin we lock,
Steady as a ticking clock.
Now we look so big and grand,
Best riders in all the land.

Two big wheels begin to spin,
Let the joyful game begin.
Helmet on and wheels roll bright,
Cycling in the morning light.

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Every hero wears a crown,
Best protector in the town.
It is strong and it is neat,
Walking down the driveway street.

Lift it up and set it down,
Right on top your little crown.
Buckle fast and check it twice,
Following the safety advice.

Now the wheels begin to hum,
Playing like a kettle drum.
Rolling fast and rolling slow,
Everywhere we want to go.

Wave goodbye to mom and dad,
Having fun and feeling glad.
Helmet on and wheels roll sweet,
Happy cruising down the street.

rhymes.title: The Safety Crown
rhymes.text:
Time to play outside today,
Put your helmet on and play.
Snap the buckle underneath,
Show your big and happy teeth.

Now your head is safe and sound,
Ready for the playground ground.
Colors bright like shiny gold,
Watch the little wheels unfold.

Push with one foot on the floor,
Rolling right outside the door.
Spinning fast and spinning slow,
This is how we learn to go.

Round and round the pavement bends,
Riding with our happy friends.
Helmet stays right on your head,
Safe and happy, go ahead!

rhymes.title: Click and Roll
rhymes.text:
Look at what is in my hand,
Bestest hat in all the land.
Put it gently on your dome,
Far away from stay-at-home.

Find the strap beneath your chin,
Make a happy little grin.
Click it fast and hear the sound,
Feet are lifting off the ground.

Wheels are spinning, shiny blue,
Made for little kids like you.
Pushing hard to make them speed,
This is all the fun we need.

Safety first is what we say,
Every single time we play.
Helmet snug upon your brow,
Time to start the rolling now!

rhymes.title: The Happy Bike Ride
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Watch the little birdies fly.
Time to ride our bikes today,
Hip hooray and hip hooray!

First the helmet, big and round,
Lifting up above the ground.
Strap it gently, nice and tight,
Making sure it fits just right.

Rubber tires on the street,
Moving fast with little feet.
Pedal forward, pedal slow,
Look at how the wheels can go!

Wind is blowing in your face,
Moving at a happy pace.
Helmet on and wheels will roll,
Happy body, happy soul!

rhymes.title: Strap It Tight
rhymes.text:
Scooter waiting by the wall,
Ready for the toddler roll.
Grab your helmet off the chair,
Put it on your fuzzy hair.

Buckle click and pull it near,
Nothing left to cause a fear.
Snug and cozy on your head,
Better than a sleepy bed.

Foot goes down to push and glide,
Taking such a happy ride.
Wheels go clickety-clack-clack,
Never want to turning back.

Up the sidewalk, down the street,
Moving with your little feet.
Helmet stays right in its place,
Biggest smile upon your face!

rhymes.title: Wheels Go Round
rhymes.text:
Time to gear up for the drive,
Glad to be so much alive!
Helmet shining in the sun,
Now the day has just begun.

Snap the buckle, click so neat,
Ready for the busy street.
Now your head is guarded well,
Safe inside your little shell.

Wheels are rolling on the floor,
Right outside the garden door.
Gliding smoothly, fast and sweet,
Using tiny hands and feet.

Keep it safe and keep it bright,
Everything is feeling right.
Helmet on and wheels will roll,
Happy times for heart and soul!

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text: Leo loved building towers. High, high up to the sky went the shiny red and blue blocks. Clack, tap, go the blocks! Leo was making a very special castle for his fuzzy bear friend. Suddenly, Mom walked into the living room with a big, warm smile on her face. 'Leo, my sweet helper,' Mom said gently, kneeling down beside the tall blocks. 'It is almost time to clean up our toys and wash our hands for a yummy, tummy-filling dinner. We have five more minutes of playtime.' Leo blinked. Five more minutes? He looked at his tall tower. That meant he had just enough time to add one more yellow triangle on the very top! Mom gave a little nod and sat right beside him. 'I will help you watch the special time go by,' she whispered, patting his soft curls. Leo carefully picked up the bright yellow triangle. His little fingers were so steady and strong. He placed it right on top of the highest tower. Ta-da! The castle was complete. Bear looked very happy sitting next to the door. Leo clapped his hands together with a happy giggle. 'Good job, Leo! You used your five minutes so wonderfully,' cheered Mom, giving him a big, cozy squeeze. Then, Mom made a tick-tock motion with her hand. 'Beep, beep! Five minutes are all done.' Leo did not feel sad at all. He felt so proud of his castle and ready for the next fun thing. Together, they sang a happy cleanup song as they put the blocks back into their big brown box. Cleaning up was a game when you had a great helper like Leo. Washing hands with warm, bubbly soap was next, and Leo splashed his fingers with a big smile. What a wonderful day of playing and growing up big and strong!

stories.title: The Backyard Mud Pie Bakery
stories.text: Squish, squash, squish! Maya loved the cool, wet mud in the backyard garden. She was the master chef of the Mud Pie Bakery, baking delicious pretend cookies for the wiggly earthworms. Pat-a-cake, pat-a-cake, bake a mud cake! A lovely yellow butterfly fluttered gently past her shiny red boots. Just then, Dad stepped out onto the back porch with a clean, fluffy green towel draped over his shoulder. 'Hello there, Chef Maya,' Dad said in his warm, singing voice. 'The sun is getting ready to go to sleep, and it will be time for our warm bath soon. But guess what? You have five more minutes to bake your wonderful mud pies.' Maya looked down at her muddy little hands and then up at Dad. Five more minutes! That meant she had time to make one extra-special mud pie decorated with shiny green leaves and purple flower petals. 'Okay, Daddy!' Maya called out happily. Dad smiled and sat on the wooden garden bench, cheering her on. Maya scooped up a big handful of rich, soft earth. She pressed it firmly into her favorite plastic pie tin. Press, press, pat, pat! Then, she found three lovely yellow daisies and pushed them gently into the middle of the pie. It looked like a masterpiece. 'Look, Daddy! A flower pie!' she shouted proudly. Dad clapped his hands together. 'That is the most magnificent mud pie I have ever seen, Maya. And look, the timer in our hearts says your five minutes are up!' Maya felt so happy. She gently rinsed her muddy hands under the warm garden hose, watching the brown water swirl away into the grass. She took Dad's big hand in her clean little one, and they walked inside together, ready for storytime.

stories.title: The Dinosaur's Final Roar
stories.text: Stomp, stomp, roar! Toby was a fierce green dinosaur running through the soft living room jungle. He had big green spikes made of cardboard taped to his shirt, and he stomped his feet very loudly. Grr-rawr! Grandma sat in the comfy armchair, smiling warmly as the little dinosaur stomped past her knee. 'Good afternoon, little dinosaur,' Grandma said with a soft chuckle. 'The big yellow sun is hiding behind the trees now, and our fun park adventure is coming to a close. We have five more minutes before we put on our cozy pajamas.' Toby stopped stomping and tilted his head. Five more minutes? That was plenty of time for one final, gigantic dinosaur journey across the rug mountain! 'I need to save my dinosaur family, Grandma,' Toby announced in his best deep dinosaur voice. Grandma nodded encouragingly. 'Go ahead, brave dinosaur. I will keep watch right here.' Toby took a deep breath. Stomp, stomp, stomp! He marched over to the couch, rescued the tiny plastic triceratops from beneath a sofa cushion, and carried it safely to the green blanket nest. Roar! He let out one last, happy, friendly dinosaur roar. Grandma cheered and clapped loudly. 'Wonderful job, little dinosaur! You used your five extra minutes like a true champion.' Toby smiled a big, toothy grin. The five minutes were up, but he felt so accomplished. Grandma helped him gently take off his cardboard spikes, folding them neatly for tomorrow. Toby washed his face and put on his soft star-printed pajamas. He snuggled into bed, feeling safe, loved, and ready for sweet dreams after a wonderful day of play.

stories.title: Leo's Last Train Track
stories.text: Leo loved building train tracks. He had red tracks, blue tracks, and curvy yellow tracks that went all around the living room rug. Choo-choo! The little wooden train zoomed past the sofa mountain and through the tunnel made of pillows. Leo was busy making a very tall bridge when Mom walked into the room. She smiled softly and knelt down beside him. 'Leo, my sweet builder,' Mom said in her most gentle voice, 'it is almost time to clean up our toys and wash our hands for yummy dinner. You have five more minutes to play with your train.' Leo looked at his big bridge. Five more minutes? That was a whole lot of time! 'Five more minutes?' Leo asked happily. 'Yes, five more minutes,' Mom nodded. 'I will set the timer on the microwave so you can hear when it goes beep-beep.' Leo went right back to work. He carefully placed one more curvy track to make the loop complete. Then he drove the train all the way around the track one, two, three times! Choo-choo, clickety-clack! He even loaded a tiny wooden block into the train car. Just then, the kitchen timer went off. Beep, beep, beep! Leo smiled because he was ready. He knew the beep meant his time was up, but he had felt so happy getting that extra warning. 'All done!' Leo said proudly. He gently picked up the red engine and placed it inside the big toy box. Mom clapped her hands and gave him a warm hug. 'You did such a wonderful job finishing your track and listening to the timer. Thank you for being such a big helper, Leo! Now let's go wash our hands together.'

stories.title: Mia's Magical Sandbox
stories.text: The afternoon sun was warm and golden in the backyard. Mia was digging a deep, deep moat around her wet sandcastle. She had a sparkly pink shovel and a blue bucket filled with shiny smooth pebbles. Scooping and patting, patting and scooping, Mia was having the most wonderful time. Suddenly, Dad stepped out onto the back porch with a warm towel draped over his shoulder. He walked over to the sandbox and squatted down next to Mia. 'Mia, my little explorer,' Dad said with a kind smile, 'the sun is getting ready to go to sleep, and it is almost time to head inside for our warm bath and bedtime stories. You have five more minutes to dig in your sandbox.' Mia paused and looked at her castle. Five more minutes! That meant she had just enough time to finish her very special road. 'Five minutes?' Mia asked, blinking her big brown eyes. 'Yes, sweetheart, five minutes,' Dad said, pointing to his wristwatch. 'When the little hand points straight up, we will pack up our tools together.' Mia felt so glad to have a warning. She didn't have to stop right this second! She quickly scooped up three more buckets of sand to make the tallest tower yet and decorated the top with her favorite shiny pebble. 'Look, Daddy, I finished it!' she cheered. Dad beamed with pride. 'That is a magnificent castle, Mia! And look, our time is up.' Mia proudly handed her pink shovel to Dad and helped place the bucket on the shelf. 'Good job transitioning, my big girl,' Dad whispered, giving her a cozy piggyback ride all the way inside to the bathroom.

stories.title: Pip's Final Playground Swing
stories.text: The neighborhood park was Pip's absolute favorite place in the whole wide world. Up and down, up and down went the blue swing! Pip pumped his little legs as hard as he could, trying to touch the fluffy white clouds floating in the sky. Higher and higher he flew, giggling with pure joy as the breeze tickled his nose. Grandma sat on the green park bench nearby, watching him with loving eyes. She checked her watch and gently stood up, walking closer to the swings. She waited until Pip safely slowed down to a gentle glide before she spoke. 'My soaring little bird,' Grandma said in a sweet, encouraging sing-song voice, 'we are going to pack up our water bottles and head home soon for our cozy evening routine. But don't worry, you have five more minutes to swing as high as you like.' Pip smiled a big, toothy grin. Five more minutes meant he could do his ultimate countdown swings! 'Five more minutes?' Pip asked. 'That's right, my love,' Grandma replied softly. 'I will count down with you.' Pip gripped the chains tightly and took off again. One, two, three, four, five big pushes! He soared up like a superhero. When Grandma called out, 'Two minutes left, Pip!' Pip knew he was getting close to home time, which made him feel calm and prepared instead of surprised. Finally, Grandma said, 'Time's up, my sweet pilot.' Pip gently dragged his sneakers in the rubber mulch to help himself stop. He hopped off the swing all by himself. 'I used my brakes!' Pip announced proudly. Grandma wrapped him in a big, cozy bear hug. 'You are getting so big and responsible, Pip. Thank you for listening so nicely to our five-minute warning! Now let's hold hands and skip all the way home.'

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text: Leo loved building towers in the living room. He had red blocks, blue blocks, and yellow blocks stacked all the way up to his tummy. "BEEP! BEEP!" went his toy train, chugging right past the tall, beautiful building. Leo giggled and reached for a green triangle roof. Suddenly, Mom walked into the room with his favorite green coat and little red boots. "Time to get ready for the park, my sweet builder," Mom said with a warm, loving smile. Leo let out a little sigh. He was not quite ready to stop building. He wanted to make his tower even taller! Mom knelt down right beside him on the soft carpet. She gave him a gentle squeeze and whispered, "I know you are having so much fun, Leo. Let us give you a five-more-minutes warning. That means you have time to finish putting your very highest roof on the tower, and then we will put your blocks to sleep in their big box." Leo’s face lit up. Five more minutes! That was plenty of time. He carefully placed the green triangle right on top. Balance, balance, balance... and it stayed! "Look, Mom! I did it!" Leo cheered, clapping his hands together. Mom clapped too. "You are an amazing builder, Leo." When the timer on the microwave beeped five minutes later, Leo felt ready. He gently took down the roof and put the blocks away one by one, feeling so proud of his wonderful tower and so happy for his fun trip to the park.

stories.title: The Sandbox Grand Finale
stories.text: Maya was knee-deep in the warm sandbox at the backyard playground. She was busy digging a deep, secret tunnel for her plastic dinosaur. "Roar!" Maya whispered, making the little green dinosaur crawl through the soft, golden sand. The sun was shining gently, and the birds were singing sweet songs in the big oak tree. Dad walked over with a gentle breeze, holding Maya’s fuzzy blue sweater. "Maya, my little explorer, it is almost time to pack up our toys and head inside for yummy veggie straws and story time," Dad said softly. Maya frowned just a tiny bit. She loved her dinosaur tunnel so much. She was not finished digging yet! Dad smiled his kind, understanding smile and knelt down in the grass beside her. "Let us do a five-more-minutes warning, Maya-bear," Dad suggested warmly. "That means you have five whole minutes to make the grand finale for your dinosaur before we head indoors." Maya’s eyes sparkled. A grand finale! She scooped up big handfuls of sand, building a huge mountain right over the tunnel. "The dinosaur is hiding in a volcano!" Maya announced proudly. Dad cheered, "Oh, what a magnificent mountain! You are such a creative builder, Maya." When five minutes gently came to an end, Maya felt happy and satisfied. She gave her dinosaur a little goodbye pat, helped Dad shake the sand from her shoes, and walked inside, ready for her cozy afternoon snack.

stories.title: The Pajama Party Train
stories.text: Sam was zooming around the bedroom floor. "Vroom! Vroom!" went his favorite race car, driving over the fluffy rug and under the big rocking chair. Bedtime was coming soon, but Sam was still full of zooming energy. Mom stepped into the doorway, holding his cozy striped pajamas and his favorite bedtime book about sleepy bears. "Time to park the race car in the garage, sweet Sam, and get our pajamas on," Mom said in a soft, soothing voice. Sam shook his head and drove the car under the bed. "Not yet, car is still driving!" he giggled. Mom walked over and sat right on the rug next to him, giving him a big, loving hug. "I know, zooming is so much fun," Mom whispered kindly. "How about a five-more-minutes warning? That means your race car gets to take five more fast laps around the room, and then it is time for the car to rest in the parking lot while we put on our cozy pajamas." Sam thought about this and smiled a big, happy smile. Five more laps! He zoomed the car super fast. One! Two! Three! Four! Five! With a happy "Beep beep!", Sam parked the car neatly right beside his pillow. "Great driving, champion," Mom praised warmly. Sam felt so proud of following the plan, and he climbed into his cozy bed, ready for a wonderful night's sleep.

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text: Leo loved building towers. He stacked red blocks, blue blocks, and green blocks high up to the sky. His tower was the tallest tower in the whole living room! Just then, Mommy walked into the playroom with a big warm smile. 'Leo, my sweet helper,' Mommy said softly, 'it is almost time to put on our shoes and go outside to the park.' Leo looked at his big tower and felt a little sad. He wanted to play longer! Mommy gave him a gentle hug and said, 'Let us use a five more minutes warning. That means you have five more minutes to play right here.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. 'Five minutes?' he asked. Mommy nodded. 'Yes! You can finish your tower and add one more special block.' Leo felt happy again. He reached into the box and carefully placed a yellow triangle right on the very top. Balance, balance, steady... hooray! The tower was complete. Leo clapped his hands together with joy. Mommy smiled and gently touched his shoulder. 'Five minutes are up, my big builder. Look at what a wonderful job you did! Now, let us gently take down the tower together and put the blocks back in their happy home box.' Leo helped put the red blocks away. Then he put the blue blocks away. 'Good job, Leo!' cheered Mommy with lots of praise. Transitioning to shoes was so much easier when he knew what was coming. Leo hopped over to the rug and sat down to put on his shiny red sneakers. 'Ready for the park!' said Leo proudly. Mommy kissed the top of his head. 'I am so proud of how you listened and finished your play time nicely.' Together, hand in hand, they walked out the door, ready for a brand new adventure in the sunshine.

stories.title: Mia's Magical Mud Pies
stories.text: Splash, squish, squelch! Mia was having the best time in the backyard sandbox. She had a little yellow bucket filled with wet brown dirt. 'Behold!' giggled Mia. 'A chocolate mud pie with a leaf on top!' Daddy walked out onto the green grass carrying a soft green towel over his shoulder. 'Mia, my little sunshine,' Daddy said in a sweet voice, 'dinner time is getting closer. In five more minutes, we need to wash our hands and go inside for yummy macaroni.' Mia pouted just a little bit. Her mud pie was not quite baked yet! She wanted to stir it more with her stick. Daddy knelt down beside her in the grass and gave her a gentle, loving pat. 'I know it is hard to stop playing when you are having fun,' Daddy said kindly. 'That is why we use a five more minutes warning. You have five minutes to finish baking your special pie and say goodbye to the sandbox.' Mia nodded slowly. Five minutes was just enough time! She stirred the mud one, two, three times. Then she carefully placed a pretty yellow daisy right in the middle of her mud pie masterpiece. 'All done!' announced Mia with a big grin. Daddy clapped his hands. 'What a magnificent mud pie, Chef Mia! Now, our five minutes are all done. Time to wash our hands so they are nice and clean for dinner.' Mia stood up and shook the tiny bits of sand off her knees. She proudly walked to the garden hose with Daddy. Together, they splashed warm water and bubbly soap on their hands, washing all the dirt away. 'Look at those clean fingers!' praised Daddy. Mia felt so proud of herself for listening and transitioning smoothly. They walked inside the warm kitchen, smelling the delicious food waiting on the table, happy and ready for their next cozy family moment.

stories.title: The Final Train Ride
stories.text: Choo-choo! All aboard the living room express! Toby pushed his shiny wooden train along the winding track. The track went over the blue rug couch-mountain and under the dining room chair tunnel. Toby made happy train noises. 'Chug-chug, toot-toot!' Then, Grandma walked into the room carrying Toby's cozy blue pajamas and fluffy slippers. 'My wonderful little engineer,' Grandma said gently, 'bedtime is peeking around the corner. We have a five more minutes warning before we clean up our train tracks.' Toby frowned slightly and slowed down his train. He wanted the train to make one more trip to the toy box station! Grandma sat down on the floor next to him and rubbed his back lovingly. 'It is so hard to stop playing with your favorite toys, I understand,' Grandma whispered. 'A five more minutes warning gives your brain time to get ready. You can drive your train around the track one last time.' Toby's face lit up with happiness. 'One last big trip!' he cheered. He pushed the engine full speed ahead. Chug-chug-chug! The train zoomed over the mountain and through the tunnel, making a happy whistle sound as it pulled into the final station right by the toy box. 'Ding-dong! End of the line!' said Toby. Grandma smiled warmly and kissed his cheek. 'You did such a fantastic job driving, Toby. And look, our five minutes are finished. Are you ready to park the train for the night?' Toby nodded happily. He gently lifted the engine and placed it in the wooden bin. Then he put the track pieces away one by one. Grandma praised him with a big hug. 'I love how helpful and responsible you are, sweet boy.' With his cozy pajamas waiting, Toby felt safe, loved, and ready to snuggle up for sweet dreams.

stories.title: The Big Yellow Tower
stories.text: Leo sat on the soft playroom rug, surrounded by dozens of colorful wooden blocks. He was building the tallest tower in the whole wide world! It had red squares on the bottom, green triangles in the middle, and a shiny blue arch right on top. It looked magnificent. Just then, Mama walked into the room with a gentle smile and a soft hum. She knelt down beside Leo and gave his shoulder a warm, loving squeeze. 'It is almost time to wash our hands for yummy lunch, my sweet builder,' Mama whispered softly. 'So, you have five more minutes of block time.' Leo looked at his tall tower. Five minutes sounded like just enough time to add one more special yellow block to the very top. 'Five minutes!' Leo repeated happily. Mama set a cheerful little timer right beside him so they could watch together. Tick-tock went the friendly timer, counting down the moments. Leo carefully placed the yellow block on the top arch. Balance, balance, balance! It stayed up! He clapped his hands with joy. He had plenty of time to admire his wonderful creation and feel so proud of his building skills. When the timer let out a sweet little beep-beep sound, Leo didn't feel sad at all. He knew it was coming! He gently tapped the tower to let it rest, standing up tall and strong. 'Great job using your warning time to finish up your masterpiece, Leo,' Mama praised, giving him a big hug. Leo felt warm and happy inside. Putting the blocks away in their big toy basket felt like a fun game because he was ready. Hand in hand, Leo and Mama walked proudly to the kitchen to wash their hands, ready for their next big adventure of the day together.

stories.title: Luna’s Last Flight
stories.text: Zoom! Whoosh! Little Luna was flying her favorite purple toy spaceship all around the living room couch. The couch was a bumpy moon crater, and the big green armchair was a faraway planet made of stardust. Luna made zooming noises with her lips, her eyes wide with excitement. Papa sat nearby reading a cozy book, looking up just in time to catch Luna's happy gaze. He smiled a gentle, loving smile and walked over to sit on the edge of the cushions. 'Captain Luna, you are doing a fantastic job exploring the galaxy,' Papa said in a warm, encouraging voice. 'In five more minutes, our spaceship needs to land in the toy box so we can get ready for our cozy bath.' Luna paused her spaceship mid-air. Five minutes! She had just enough time for one final, super-duper fast flight around the green armchair planet. 'One more fast flight!' Luna declared. Papa nodded and smiled. 'You got it, Captain. Five minutes to finish your mission.' Papa gently counted down the minutes with her, cheering her on. Luna zoomed the purple spaceship around the armchair one, two, three times! It was the best flight of the whole day. When Papa softly said, 'Time’s up, Captain Luna,' Luna knew exactly what to do. She landed the spaceship gently right inside the big toy box, parking it safely for the night. 'Mission accomplished!' Luna cheered, feeling so proud of her teamwork. Papa scooped her up into a giant bear hug, kissing her forehead. Luna smiled from ear to ear, knowing that little warnings made stopping playtime feel safe, easy, and full of love.

stories.title: Pippa’s Splashy Sea
stories.text: Pippa was swimming her bright orange toy duck through a sea of bubbly blue bathwater. Squeak, squeak! The little duck hopped over soap mountains and dived under warm, soothing waves. Pippa giggled, splashing her little toes and making happy ripples in the tub. Grandma sat on the wooden bathroom stool, keeping Pippa company with a soft, cozy towel resting right on her lap. Grandma leaned in close and smiled a sweet, reassuring smile. 'Pippa, my little water pixie, you are having such a wonderful time in your sea,' Grandma said gently. 'In five more minutes, it will be time to wrap up in this fluffy towel for bedtime stories.' Pippa loved her bubbly sea, but she also loved cozy bedtime stories. Five minutes meant she had just enough time to swim her duck through one last magical waterfall. 'One last waterfall, Grandma!' Pippa called out cheerfully. Grandma nodded and smiled warmly. 'Five more minutes of splashy fun, then we will hop out together.' Grandma set a gentle timer on the counter. Pippa made her duck swim in big circles, creating a grand finale splash. The bubbles tickled her toes, and she felt so cozy and happy. When the timer chimed its friendly little song, Pippa was completely ready. She made her duck do a final bow. 'All done swimming!' Pippa announced proudly. Grandma wrapped the big, fluffy, warm towel around Pippa like a superhero cape, rubbing her back to keep her cozy. 'Look how wonderfully you finished your bath time, Pippa,' Grandma whispered lovingly. Pippa beamed with pride, feeling safe, happy, and so very loved as they headed to bed.

stories.title: The Magic Block Tower
stories.text: Leo sat right in the middle of the soft green living room rug. All around him were big red blocks, little yellow blocks, and tall blue triangles. He was building the most amazing castle in the whole wide world! It had a very high tower for his toy dragon to live in, and a long bridge made of flat green blocks. Leo smiled a big, happy smile. He pushed a little yellow block right on the very top. Crash! Oh no, the very top fell down! But Leo did not give up. He giggled and picked up the yellow block to try again. Just then, Mama walked over softly and sat down on the rug right next to him. She gave him a gentle, loving squeeze on his shoulder and said, 'Leo, my sweet helper, in five more minutes it will be time to clean up our toys and wash our hands for yummy lunch.' Leo looked at Mama with big, curious eyes. 'Five more minutes?' he asked softly. Mama nodded with a warm, bright smile. 'Yes, my love. That means you have just enough time to finish building your castle tower and make sure your dragon is safe inside.' Leo felt so happy and smart. He looked back at his blocks and knew exactly what to do. One, two, three more blocks went up, up, up! He placed the little yellow block right on the very top, and this time, it stayed up high and proud. 'Look, Mama! I did it!' cheered Leo, clapping his little hands together. Mama clapped right along with him, her eyes sparkling with pride. 'You did it, Leo! You made a wonderful castle!' Then, Mama gently sang the special clean-up song. Because Leo had his five-minute warning, his tummy was ready for lunch, and his heart felt so peaceful and proud of his wonderful block tower.

stories.title: Splashy Time at the Tub
stories.text: Maya was having the absolute best time in the warm, bubbly bathtub. She had a bright yellow rubber ducky that squeaked happily whenever she gave it a gentle squeeze. Squeak, squeak! went the duck. Maya also had a shiny red cup that she used to scoop up the warm bathwater and pour it right back down like a splashing waterfall. Splash, splash, went the water! Her brown hair was piled high in a funny, fluffy bubble crown that looked just like a queen's hat. Maya laughed a bright, bubbly laugh and splashed her toes. Papa knelt beside the tub, dipping his hand into the warm water to feel the bubbles. He smiled at his clever little girl and said, 'Maya, my little water princess, in five more minutes it will be time to wrap up in your cozy, warm towel and get ready for bedtime stories.' Maya stopped splashing for a tiny second and thought about what Papa said. 'Five more minutes?' she asked, tilting her head. Papa nodded kindly. 'Yes, sweet girl. Five more minutes to play with your ducky and make one last giant waterfall.' Maya felt so glad to have time to finish her fun game. She grabbed her red cup, scooped up a whole bunch of water, and poured it over her rubber ducky so it could take a fun bath too. 'Goodnight, ducky!' Maya whispered with a big, sweet grin. Papa handed her the soft, fluffy white towel with the cute little bear ears on the hood. When the timer chimed gently, Maya was completely ready. She stepped out of the tub all by herself, feeling warm, clean, and so proud of her wonderful bath time.

stories.title: The Playground Sunset
stories.text: Sammy zoomed down the curvy green slide with a joyful shout. Wheee! He landed softly on the squishy wood chips and immediately ran as fast as his little legs could carry him toward the bright red swings. He loved how the cool afternoon breeze felt whooshing past his cheeks as he swung high up into the air, reaching all the way up to touch the fluffy white clouds. Higher and higher went Sammy! Grandpa sat on the park bench nearby, watching his energetic little boy with so much love in his eyes. The golden sun was beginning to peek behind the tall green trees, painting the sky in lovely shades of pink and orange. Grandpa stood up slowly and walked over to the swings, gently catching Sammy's toes to help him slow down safely. 'Sammy, my brave little explorer,' Grandpa said in his warm, gentle voice, 'in five more minutes it will be time for us to say goodbye to the park and walk home for our warm dinner.' Sammy pouted just a little bit because he was having so much fun. Grandpa gave him a comforting hug and said, 'That means you have five more minutes for one last super-duper high swing ride!' Sammy's face lit up with excitement. He gripped the swing chains tight and pumped his legs with all his might. One, two, three, four, five big pushes! 'Look how high I am, Grandpa!' called out Sammy happily. When the five minutes were finished, Sammy felt ready. He hopped down from the swing, held Grandpa's warm hand tightly, and waved a cheerful goodbye to the slide and the swings as they walked happily home together.

stories.title: The Last Tower of Blocks
stories.text:
Leo loved building towers. His blocks were red, blue, green, and yellow, reaching all the way up to his tummy. Sometimes they touched the sky, or at least the edge of the living room rug. Today, Leo was building a special castle for his toy dinosaur, Barnaby. Barnaby had a long green tail and loved stomping around the colorful towers.

"Time to tidy up soon, Leo," said Mama, walking over with a gentle smile. She kneeled down beside the blue rug. "We need to wash our hands for lunch in five more minutes." 

Leo made a little squeaky sound. He was not finished! He still had three blocks left in the bucket. "Five more minutes?" asked Leo, holding up his little fingers to count.

"Yes, sweetie. Five more minutes," Mama said, giving his shoulder a soft, warm pat. "That means you have just enough time to place your last few blocks and make sure Barnaby is safe inside his castle. When the big timer chimes, we will put the blocks to bed together."

Leo felt happy. Five minutes was a whole lot of time! He quickly picked up the yellow block and balanced it right on the very top. Tap, tap, tap went his little fingers. Then he placed the red block as a grand doorway for Barnaby. 

"Roar!" said Barnaby. The castle looked wonderful. Leo beamed with pride. He knew he didn't have to stop playing right this second, which made him feel calm and in control. 

Soon, a gentle little beep-beep sound came from Mama's phone. "Ding-dong! Five minutes are up, my little builder," Mama sang softly. 

Leo stood up tall, feeling very proud of his work. "All done building!" he cheered. Together, Leo and Mama sang a fun cleanup song as they dropped the red, blue, green, and yellow blocks back into their big round bucket. Washing hands for lunch was going to be wonderful, too.

stories.title: The Swing Set Sky
stories.text:
