The park was Maya's favorite place in the whole wide world. Today, the afternoon breeze was warm and tickled her cheeks. Maya was swinging high on the red swing, flying up, up, up toward the fluffy white clouds. Every time she went forward, she tried to touch the oak tree leaves with her toes. "Look at me, Daddy! I'm a bird!" she laughed, her pigtails bouncing in the wind.

Daddy sat on the green park bench nearby, smiling brightly at her joyful face. He looked at his watch, then called out in a soft, musical voice, "Maya, my little bird! We need to head home for dinner soon. You have five more minutes on the swings."

Maya pouted just a tiny bit. Five minutes? She wanted to stay and swing forever! But she loved hearing Daddy's gentle voice, and she remembered what five minutes meant. It meant she had time for five more big swooshes into the sky.

"Okay, Daddy!" Maya called back. She gripped the silver chains tight and counted out loud. "One! Higher and higher! Two! Almost touching the clouds! Three! Feel the wind! Four! Look how fast I go! Five! The very biggest swing of all!"

By the time she finished her fifth big swoop, her tummy felt tickly and happy. She didn't feel rushed at all because Daddy gave her a warning to get ready. 

Daddy walked over with open arms as Maya dragged her sneakers softly on the woodchips to slow down. "You were the flyingest bird in the whole park," Daddy said, lifting her down with a gentle hug.

"I swung five times," Maya reported proudly. 

"You did, superstar. Now let's hold hands and skip all the way to the car for our yummy pasta dinner." Maya took Daddy's big warm hand, ready for the next fun part of her day, feeling happy, heard, and loved.

stories.title: The Pajama Train
stories.text:
The living room was full of soft pillows and glowing lights. Toby was driving his favorite toy train across the carpet tracks. Choo-choo! Chug-a-lug! The train was carrying a sleepy teddy bear and a tiny plastic duck to the mountain station under the sofa.

Grandma walked into the room carrying a pair of cozy blue pajamas covered in little white stars. "All aboard, little engineer," Grandma said with a twinkling smile. "It is almost time to change into our jammies and brush our teeth. You have five more minutes to play with your train."

Toby looked at Grandma, then down at his train tracks. Five minutes was great! It meant the train could make one last big journey across the room before bedtime.

"Five more minutes, Grandma," Toby repeated happily. "The train has to go over the mountain!"

"That sounds like a wonderful plan," Grandma said, sitting on the armchair and gently rubbing her hands together. "I will wait right here while your train finishes its trip."

Toby felt so peaceful. Grandma didn't snatch his toys away; she gave him a chance to finish what he was doing. He chugged the train up the sofa cushion mountain, made a loud whistle sound—*Woo-woo!*—and safely parked the train inside the toy box garage.

Right as he closed the garage door, Grandma hummed a sweet little tune. "BEEP BEEP! Five minutes are up, engineer Toby! Time to transform into a cozy star."

Toby giggled. He loved being a cozy star. He walked over to Grandma, ready and excited to put on his star pajamas. Transitioning from play to bedtime was smooth and easy because he had the time he needed to wrap up his adventures.

stories.title: The Last Great Castle
stories.text: Leo sat on the warm playroom rug, surrounded by a mountain of bright wooden blocks. He was building the tallest castle the world had ever seen, complete with a tall tower for his favorite brave knight. The castle reached nearly as high as Leo’s tummy, and he was just about to add a pointy roof made of a shiny blue triangle. Suddenly, Mommy walked over with a gentle smile. She knelt down beside the colorful blocks and said, 'Leo, my sweet helper, in five more minutes, it will be time to put our toys away and wash our hands for yummy lunch.' Leo frowned just a tiny bit because he loved his castle so much. But then he remembered what five minutes meant. It meant he had just enough time to finish his special project! Mommy set the friendly timer on the shelf so they could watch the little hand move together. Leo nodded and went right back to work with a happy focus. He carefully balanced the blue triangle on the very top of the tower. Tap, tap, tap went his little fingers. 'Done!' cheered Leo. He placed his brave knight safely inside the front gate to guard the walls. He had plenty of time to finish his creation without feeling rushed. When the friendly timer let out a soft little chime, Leo didn't feel sad at all. He felt proud. He looked at Mommy and said, 'Look, Mommy! My castle is all finished.' Mommy clapped her hands and gave him a warm, cozy hug. 'You did such an amazing job building that, Leo, and you listened so wonderfully to the five-minute warning. Now, let's fly our blocks back into the toy box together like airplanes.' Leo giggled, scooped up a red block, and zoomed it through the air right into the bin. Transitioning from play to lunchtime was smooth, happy, and filled with a sense of wonderful accomplishment.

stories.title: The Sandbox Symphony
stories.text: The afternoon sun was golden and warm in the backyard. Maya was deep in the sensory sandbox, digging a giant tunnel that connected her toy turtle's house to the red plastic bucket. She scooped up the soft, sparkling sand with her yellow shovel, humming a little tune to herself. Papa walked across the grass, his footsteps making a soft crunching sound. He crouched down beside the sandbox and gently touched Maya’s shoulder. 'Maya, my little builder,' Papa said in his kindest voice, 'you have five more minutes to finish your wonderful digging before we need to head inside to put on our shoes for the park.' Maya looked down at her tunnel. Five minutes sounded like a lot of time, but she wanted to make the tunnel extra deep. Papa smiled and said, 'I will set a timer on my watch so we can hear it beep when time is up.' Maya nodded, feeling very grown-up. She used her hands to smooth the sides of the tunnel, making sure the toy turtle would have a very smooth road. Dig, scoop, pat, pat, pat! Maya worked with happy concentration. She even added a tiny pile of sand on top to look like a mountain. The time flew by, but because she knew it was coming, she didn't feel surprised when Papa’s watch let out a cheerful beep-beep. Maya stood up, brushed the stray sand grains off her knees, and smiled. 'Papa, I made a mountain and a tunnel!' she announced proudly. Papa smiled back and high-fived her sandy hand. 'You used your five minutes so well, Maya! You are a super planner.' Maya felt so proud of her tunnel and happy to transition to the next fun part of their day. She took Papa's hand, ready for their next adventure.

stories.title: The Final Splash
stories.text: The bathtub was full of warm, bubbly water that smelled like gentle lavender. Sam was the captain of a yellow rubber duck fleet, sailing his brave ships through big mounds of soapy foam mountains. Splash, splash went his hands as he made giant ocean waves for the ducks to ride. Grandma sat on the little wooden stool beside the tub, holding a big, fluffy blue towel that she had just warmed up in the dryer. She smiled down at Sam’s happy, wet face. 'Captain Sam,' Grandma said softly, 'you have five more minutes of bath time fun before we wrap up in this cozy towel and get ready for our bedtime story.' Sam pouted his lower lip for just a second because the bubbles were so much fun. But Grandma gently stroked his wet hair and said, 'Five minutes is just enough time for one final, giant splash race with your ducks!' Sam’s face lit up with a big, bright grin. A splash race was his absolute favorite game! He lined up all three yellow ducks on the edge of the tub. 'Ready, set, go!' whispered Sam. He splashed the water with both hands, sending the ducks zooming across the bubbly waves. One, two, three ducks reached the other side of the tub. Sam laughed out loud, clapping his hands together as the warm water rippled all around him. When Grandma gently said, 'Time is up, Captain,' Sam was ready. He unplugged the drain and watched the water swirl down with a funny gurgling sound. Grandma wrapped the warm, fluffy towel all around him, turning him into a snuggly little burrito. Sam cuddled close, feeling warm, clean, and happy that he had enjoyed every single second of his warning time.

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text: Leo loved building blocks. Every afternoon, his living room rug turned into a busy construction site. Today, he was building a tall, wobbly tower that touched the big sofa cushions. He carefully placed a red triangle on the very top. 'Look, Daddy! I made a castle for my toy dinosaur!' Leo cheered, clapping his hands together. Daddy smiled and sat down beside him on the soft carpet. 'That is a magnificent castle, Leo,' Daddy said softly. 'You worked so hard to balance those blocks. In five more minutes, it will be time to pack our blocks away and get ready for a warm bath.' Leo frowned just a little bit. He did not want to stop playing yet. But he knew what five more minutes meant. It meant he had just enough time to add one tiny yellow bridge to the side of his castle. 'Five more minutes?' Leo asked to be sure. 'Yes, little one,' Daddy answered with a kind smile, setting a gentle timer that beeped with a happy chime. Leo nodded and got back to work. He carefully slid the yellow bridge into place, making sure the dinosaur could walk right across it. He drove his toy truck under the archway one, two, three times. The chime rang out with a cheerful little song. Beep-beep! Time was up! Daddy reached out and gave Leo a warm hug. 'All done, buddy,' Daddy whispered. Leo did not feel sad at all. He felt proud of his castle. Together, they sang a happy cleanup song as they dropped each block back into the big blue toy box. One by one, the blocks went night-night. Leo even got to choose his favorite bedtime storybook. By the time they walked to the bathroom, Leo was smiling from ear to ear, ready for his cozy evening.

stories.title: The Backyard Swing
stories.text: The afternoon sun was warm and golden, casting long shadows across the green grass in the backyard. Maya was swinging higher and higher on the wooden swing set. 'Wheee!' she shouted, feeling the cool breeze tickle her nose and flutter her bright pink jacket. Every time she kicked her legs up toward the fluffy white clouds, she felt like she was flying. Mommy sat on the garden bench nearby, reading a book of poetry and watching Maya's happy face. When the breeze slowed down a little bit, Mommy closed her book gently and walked over to the swings. She caught the ropes to slow Maya down to a gentle sway. 'You are such a wonderful flyer, Maya,' Mommy said with a loving smile. 'You have five more minutes left on the swings before we go inside for snack time.' Maya hugged the rough ropes tightly. Five more minutes? That sounded like just enough time for three more big, soaring flights into the sky. 'Okay, Mommy! Three more big ones!' Maya agreed, her eyes sparkling with excitement. Mommy nodded and checked her watch. 'Ready, set, go!' Maya pumped her legs with all her might. One! She reached the highest branch of the big oak tree. Two! She touched the sky with her toes. Three! The final swoop brought her gently back down to earth as her feet touched the grass. The timer on Mommy's phone chimed with a gentle bird chirping sound. Chirp-chirp! 'Time's up, my sweet flyer,' Mommy said, holding out her hands. Maya hopped off the swing and grabbed Mommy's hand. She wasn't upset because she knew the rule, and Mommy had given her a fair warning. As they walked inside to wash their sticky hands, Maya chattered happily about the birds she had seen from way up high in the sky.

stories.title: The Magic Sandbox
stories.text: Max was sitting in the community sandbox, knee-deep in shimmering white sand. He was using a bright green shovel to dig a deep, winding moat for his plastic pirate ship. The ship was loaded with colorful glass marbles that sparkled like real treasure in the sunlight. Max loved the feeling of the cool, soft sand running right through his tiny fingers. Across the park, Grandma was packing up the picnic basket and folding the red blanket. She walked over to the edge of the sandbox, her shoes making soft crunching sounds on the gravel path. She kneeled down beside Max and wiped a speck of dust from his forehead. 'Max, my little explorer, your pirate adventure looks so much fun,' Grandma said in her sweetest, most comforting voice. 'We need to head home soon for dinner, so you have five more minutes of digging time left.' Max looked down at his unfinished moat. He wanted the pirate ship to sail all the way around the sandbox corner. Five more minutes meant he could finish digging the channel and bury his treasure chest safely. 'Can I finish my secret tunnel, Grandma?' Max asked hopefully. Grandma nodded gently and patted his soft curls. 'Yes, sweetheart. Five minutes is plenty of time for one last secret tunnel.' Max got right back to work, scooping sand with super-fast shovel movements. Scoop, dump, scoop, dump! He buried the marble treasure chest deep under a bridge of sand and parked his pirate ship right on top. The kitchen timer in Grandma's pocket beeped softly, sounding just like a happy little cricket. Chirp! Max smiled proudly. He stood up, shook the loose sand from his little red shorts, and gave Grandma a big hand-holding squeeze. They walked home together, talking all about the pirate treasures they would find again tomorrow.

stories.title: The Last Two Blocks
stories.text: Leo loved building tall towers. He had red blocks, blue blocks, and yellow blocks stacked all the way up to his nose! They looked just like a magical castle where a happy little dragon lived. CRASH! The dragon flew away as Leo gently knocked the blocks down to start all over again. Suddenly, a gentle hand tapped Leo's shoulder. It was Mommy, smiling softly. 'Leo, my sweet builder,' she whispered, 'in five more minutes, it will be time to clean up our blocks and wash our hands for yummy lunch.' Leo looked at his blocks. Five minutes? What does five minutes mean? Mommy explained with a warm cuddle, 'Five minutes means you have just enough time to build one more extra-tall tower and say goodbye to your dragon.' Leo nodded, feeling happy that he had time to finish his fun. He grabbed two more yellow blocks and placed them very carefully on top. One. Two. There! His tower was complete, reaching high into the afternoon sunshine. Just then, Mommy came back with a soft chime on her phone. 'Beep-boop! Five minutes are up, superstar.' Leo didn't feel sad at all. He felt proud of his tower and ready for the next adventure. 'Bye-bye, dragon!' he cheered. Together, Leo and Mommy sang a happy cleanup song as they put every single block back into its cozy red box. Mommy gave him a big high-five. 'You did such a wonderful job listening and finishing your play, Leo!' Leo beamed with pride, washing his hands with bubbly soap. He learned that hearing a five-minute warning wasn't scary; it was just a helpful little helper that gave him time to finish his creations and get ready for yummy food. Lunchtime tasted extra delicious today because he felt so accomplished. The kitchen was warm and bright, and Leo was ready for his next fun part of the day.

stories.title: The Final Slide
stories.text: The park was buzzing with golden afternoon light. Maya was zipping down the yellow slide, wheeee! Her curls bounced in the breeze, and her giggles sounded like little silver bells. She ran back up the ladder as fast as her little legs could carry her. 'Look at me, Daddy! I am a rocket ship flying to the moon!' she shouted happily. Daddy sat on the nearby bench, smiling. He loved watching Maya play so much. He checked his watch and walked over with gentle footsteps. 'Maya, my little astronaut,' Daddy said softly, crouching down to her eye level. 'In five more minutes, we need to pack our bags and head home for our cozy bath.' Maya pouted for just a second. Stopping playtime was always a bit hard. But Daddy gave her a reassuring hug. 'Five minutes means you have time for two more rocket ship flights down the slide. Ready for countdown?' Maya's eyes lit up. Two more rides! That sounded like plenty of time. 'Yes! Countdown!' she cheered. 'Five, four, three, two, one, blast off!' She zoomed down the slide with a giant grin, faster than before. Then she climbed back up for the very last time. 'This is my moon landing!' she declared, sliding down and landing safely on the soft woodchips. Just then, Daddy's watch beeped with a cheerful bird chirp. 'Time's up, astronaut! Mission accomplished!' Maya stood up proudly and grabbed her pink backpack. She didn't throw a tantrum because she had felt completely ready. 'We had a great flight, Daddy,' she said, holding his hand tightly as they walked to the car. Daddy praised her wonderfully. 'You are such a fantastic listener, Maya. You finished your space mission like a true pro.' Maya smiled all the way home, proud of how well she handled her transition.

stories.title: The Pajama Parade
stories.text: The living room floor was covered in cozy blankets and soft stuffed animals. Toby was deep in the jungle, roaring like a friendly lion. Roar! Roar! His stuffed bear, Barnaby, roared right along with him. It was their favorite game before the stars came out to twinkle in the night sky. Mommy walked into the living room holding the softest, warmest pajamas with little green dinosaurs on them. She sat on the big blue rug next to Toby. 'Toby, my brave little lion,' Mommy said in a sweet, sleepy voice. 'In five more minutes, our jungle game needs to take a little pause so we can put on our dinosaur pajamas and read our bedtime story.' Toby hugged Barnaby tight. Five minutes? Toby didn't want the jungle to end just yet. Mommy stroked his hair gently. 'Five minutes is just enough time for your lion to protect his blanket cave one last time, and then we will march like dinosaurs to the bedroom.' Toby thought about that. Protecting the cave was very important work! 'Okay, Mommy,' he whispered. He arranged his blankets into a super-strong fort, tucking every corner in. 'Roar! The cave is safe!' Toby announced proudly. Just then, a soft musical chime played from the kitchen. 'Ding-dong! Five minutes are up, little lion,' Mommy smiled. Toby stood up and stretched his arms high into the air. He was actually starting to feel a little bit sleepy in his tummy. 'Time for the dinosaur march!' Toby giggled, stomping his feet slowly. *Stomp, stomp, roar! Stomp, stomp, roar!* They marched all the way to the bedroom together. Mommy clapped her hands. 'Look at how well you transitioned, Toby! You are a superstar at listening.' Toby snuggled into his bed with Barnaby, feeling safe, happy, and so very loved as the moon watched over them.

stories.title: Leo's Last Blocks
stories.text: Leo loved building tall towers in the sunny living room. His blocks were red, blue, green, and yellow, reaching almost as high as his nose. He carefully balanced a tiny yellow triangle right on the very top. 'Look, Mommy, a castle!' Leo giggled, clapping his hands together. Mommy smiled warmly and knelt down on the soft rug beside him. 'That is a magnificent castle, Leo,' she said in her most gentle voice. 'In five more minutes, it will be time to tidy up our toys and wash our hands for yummy lunch.' Leo scrunched his little nose. Five more minutes? He wanted to play forever! But Mommy gave him a reassuring hug. 'That means you have plenty of time to add a special garage for your toy truck.' Leo’s eyes lit up. A garage! He zoomed his blue truck across the floor and parked it right beneath the tall tower. One minute passed as he added a soft green rug made of felt. Two minutes passed as he counted the blocks out loud. Three minutes passed as he straightened the walls. Four minutes passed as he gave his castle a happy little pat. Then, Mommy gently sang the cleanup song. 'Time is up, my sweet builder!' Leo didn't feel sad at all. He felt proud because he used his five minutes so well. Together, he and Mommy sang as they put every single block back into the big red box. 'Great job transitioning, big boy!' Mommy cheered, giving him a high-five. Leo washed his hands with bubbly soap, feeling very happy and ready for his lunch.

stories.title: Maya Goes to the Park
stories.text: The afternoon breeze was warm, and the playground swings were swaying gently back and forth. Maya was having the absolute best time zooming through the air, shouting 'Higher, higher, up to the clouds!' Her bright yellow sneakers kicked happily toward the blue sky. Daddy walked over to the swings, holding her favorite blue jacket. 'Maya, my love,' Daddy said softly, crouching down to her eye level. 'We are having so much fun, but in five more minutes, we need to pack up our buckets and head home for dinner.' Maya pouted just a little bit and squeezed the swing chains. Five more minutes felt short, but Daddy nodded understandingly. 'That is plenty of time for five more big, wonderful swings!' Maya thought about this. Five more big swings? That sounded wonderful! She counted out loud as she soared through the air. 'One! Two! Three! Four! Five!' On the fifth swing, she stretched her legs out super far and made a soft landing in the woodchips. Daddy clapped for her. 'Look how well you listened and finished your swinging adventure, Maya!' Maya beamed with pride. She grabbed her bright red bucket and helped Daddy collect the stray sidewalk chalk. Transitioning from the park was easy because she knew what to expect. Holding Daddy's warm hand, Maya skipped all the way home, talking excitedly about the yummy pasta waiting for them at the kitchen table.

stories.title: Sam's Splashy Bathtime
stories.text: The bathtub was a magical ocean filled with floating plastic ducks, bubbly foam mountains, and a shiny red toy boat. Sam was a brave sea captain sailing his boat across the warm, soapy waves. 'Snoot, snoot! Make way for the captain!' Sam laughed, making zooming sounds as the boat sailed past a yellow rubber duck. Grandma sat on the little stool beside the tub, holding a fluffy white towel shaped like a puppy. 'Captain Sam,' Grandma said in a sweet, gentle tone, 'your sea voyage has been wonderful. But in five more minutes, it will be time to drain the water and wrap up in your cozy towel.' Sam splashed the water playfully. Five more minutes? He wanted to navigate the foam seas all night! But Grandma smiled and rubbed his back gently. 'Five minutes means you have just enough time to rescue your duckies and steer your ship back to the harbor.' Sam loved rescuing things! He quickly gathered the red boat, the yellow duck, and the green frog, lining them up neatly on the edge of the tub. One minute, two minutes, three minutes, four minutes, five minutes ticked by while Sam played happily. When Grandma pulled the silver plug, Sam didn't cry. Instead, he watched the whirlpool swirl around and helped say goodbye to the bathwater. Grandma wrapped him in the warm puppy towel and gave him a giant bear hug. 'You are such a cooperative big boy,' Grandma whispered. Sam smiled, feeling cozy, clean, and ready for his bedtime stories.

stories.title: The Tower of Ten Blocks
stories.text: Leo sat right in the middle of the soft green living room rug. Around him were all of his favorite wooden blocks. Red blocks, blue blocks, yellow triangles, and long green rectangles. He was building the biggest, tallest tower in the whole wide world! 'Look, Mama!' Leo giggled, carefully balancing a tiny yellow square right at the very top. 'My tower is touching the clouds!' Mama smiled a warm, gentle smile and sat down beside him. She gave him a soft, loving hug. 'That is a magnificent tower, Leo,' Mama said softly. 'You are a wonderful builder. But playtime is zooming toward bedtime, and soon it will be time to brush our teeth and get our pajamas on. So, I am going to give you a special helper. Five more minutes warning!' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. 'Five more minutes?' he asked. 'Yes,' Mama explained kindly. 'That means you have just enough time to build the very highest top and put the flag on your tower. When the timer makes a gentle beep, we will pack our blocks away together.' Leo felt so happy to have a little bit more time. He carefully placed one, two, more blocks on his tower. It was getting super duper tall! He added a green triangle for the roof. 'Done!' he cheered proudly. Just then, the kitchen timer went ding-dong! Leo smiled. He didn't feel sad at all, because he knew the warning was coming. 'Time to tidy up!' Leo said cheerfully. He helped Mama put every single block back into its cozy red box. Mama clapped her hands and cheered for him. 'Great job listening, my big boy!' Leo felt so proud inside. He was ready for a cozy bedtime story.

stories.title: The Final Splash in the Tub
stories.text: Splash, splash, splish! Maya’s little pink rubber duckie was swimming all around the warm, bubbly bathtub. Maya loved bath time so much. She had a bucket for pouring water and a special sponge that felt tickly on her toes. 'Quack, quack, Mr. Duck!' Maya laughed as she made her duck dive under the foamy waves. Papa sat on the little wooden stool right next to the tub, holding a big, fluffy white towel that smelled like sunshine and lavender. Papa looked at Maya with so much love in his eyes. 'Maya, my sweet little fish,' Papa said in his softest, kindest voice. 'You have been having so much fun. But soon it will be time to dry off and get ready for sleep. I am giving you a five more minutes warning.' Maya looked at her rubber duckie. 'Five more minutes?' she asked. Papa nodded gently. 'That means you have five more minutes to make big waves, sail your duck, and wash your tummy. When the five minutes are done, we will pull the plug and watch the water go down the drain together.' Maya loved having a warning because it meant she could finish her important duck-swimming mission. 'Okay, Papa!' she said. She gave Mr. Duck one final, super-duper big splash that made water droplets sparkle in the bathroom light. 'Last swim, Mr. Duck!' she whispered. When Papa told her the five minutes were up, Maya was ready. She handed her duck to Papa and reached up with a big smile. 'All done!' she announced. Papa wrapped her up in the warm towel like a snuggly burrito. 'You are such a great listener, Maya,' Papa praised her, giving her a kiss on her forehead. Maya felt cozy, clean, and happy as they walked to her bedroom.

stories.title: The Last Swing in the Park
stories.text: Wheeeee! Toby flew through the golden afternoon air on the bright red park swing. The cool breeze tickled his nose, and the fluffy white clouds seemed to race right along with him. 'Look how high I can fly, Grandma!' Toby called out happily. Grandma sat on the park bench underneath the big green oak tree, smiling as she watched her energetic little boy play. The sun was starting to dip low in the sky, painting the clouds pink and orange. Grandma knew it was almost time to pack up their buckets and go home for a yummy dinner. She walked over gently as the swing slowed down. 'Toby, sweetheart,' Grandma said in her sweetest, most encouraging voice. 'You are doing such a wonderful job on the swing today. The park is closing soon, so I am giving you a five more minutes warning.' Toby stopped with his toes touching the soft woodchips. 'Five more minutes?' he asked. Grandma nodded and stroked his soft hair. 'Yes, darling. That means you have enough time to take three more giant flights to the sky, and then we have to say goodbye to the swings until next time.' Toby thought about it and smiled. 'Okay! Three more giant flights!' he counted out loud. One! He swung way up high. Two! He stretched his legs toward the oak tree. Three! The highest and best flight of all! When he gently landed on his feet, Toby felt completely satisfied. He didn't even feel sad to leave. 'I did all three!' Toby told Grandma proudly. Grandma hugged him tight. 'You are growing up to be such a wonderful listener, Toby. Let's walk to the car together.' Toby held Grandma’s hand, feeling proud, happy, and ready for his evening adventure.

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text: Leo loved building block towers. His red blocks went on the bottom, yellow blocks in the middle, and a shiny blue triangle went right on the very top. It was the tallest tower in the whole living room! Just then, Mommy walked over with a big, warm smile. 'Leo, my sweet builder,' Mommy said softly, 'in five more minutes, it will be time to put our toys away and wash our hands for yummy dinner.' Leo looked at his tall tower. Five more minutes? That sounded like just enough time for a tiny garage at the bottom! 'Five more minutes, Mommy?' Leo asked happily. 'Yes, my love. Five more minutes to play, and then we tidy up together,' Mommy answered, giving him a gentle hug. Leo went right back to work. He carefully placed two little green blocks side by side to make a door for his toy car to drive inside. One minute passed, then two, then three. Leo zoomed his little red car vroom-vroom through the block door. He felt so proud of his clever garage! 'Ding-dong!' whispered Mommy gently. 'That is our friendly chime. Five minutes are all done, Leo!' Leo did not feel sad at all. He knew what to expect, and he felt like a big boy. 'Time to clean up!' said Leo brightly. Together, he and Mommy sang a happy cleanup song as they placed every single block back into its cozy toy box. Leo carefully put the shiny blue triangle on top of the pile all by himself. 'High five!' said Mommy. Leo slapped her hand with a loud smack and giggled. Cleaning up was actually pretty fun when you had a nice warning. Hand in hand, Leo and Mommy walked to the kitchen to wash their hands, ready for a wonderful evening.

stories.title: The Sandbox Symphony
stories.text: Maya was digging a giant moat in the sandbox. Scoop, dig, dump! The sparkling brown sand made a wonderful mountain. The sun was shining warmly on her shoulders, and her pink bucket was overflowing with shiny pebbles. Daddy walked over to the edge of the sandbox, crouching down so he was right at Maya’s eye level. 'Maya, my little explorer,' Daddy said in a cozy, gentle voice, 'we are going to head inside for our bath soon. You have five more minutes to finish your wonderful sandbox creation.' Maya stopped digging for a second and blinked. Five more minutes? That was plenty of time to build a secret tunnel through her sand mountain! 'Five more minutes, Daddy?' Maya asked with a hopeful grin. 'That's right, sweetheart. Five more minutes to dig and play,' Daddy replied, gently brushing a speck of sand off her knee. Maya turned back to her project with a happy heart. She used her little blue shovel to carve a tunnel right through the middle of the mountain. She pushed her toy dinosaur through the dark tunnel. Roar! The dinosaur made it safely to the other side. One minute, two minutes, three minutes went by in a flash. Maya loved knowing how much time she had left. Then, Daddy held up his hand and said, 'Beep-beep! Five minutes are up, my wonderful builder.' Maya smiled. She wasn't surprised at all because Daddy had given her a helpful warning. 'Time to brush the sand off our toes,' said Maya. She gently shook out her shoes, emptied her bucket, and gave her toy dinosaur a big hug goodbye. 'Great job finishing up when it was time, Maya,' Daddy cheered, taking her hand. They walked happily inside together, ready for bubbly bath time.

stories.title: The Last Swing to the Sky
stories.text: Sammy loved the playground swing. When he pumped his little legs, he could fly all the way up to the fluffy white clouds! Whoosh, went the wind past his ears. Sammy giggled as the swing went higher and higher. Grandma walked over and held the chains of the swing gently to slow it down just a little bit. 'Sammy, my brave little bird,' Grandma said in her sweetest voice, 'in five more minutes, we need to leave the park and walk home for our afternoon snack.' Sammy pouted for just a split second, but then he remembered what five minutes meant. It meant he had enough time for three more big, soaring swings! 'Grandma, can I do three big swings?' Sammy asked. 'You certainly can, my love. Five minutes gives you time for a few more wonderful flights,' Grandma answered warmly, patting his little striped jacket. Sammy gripped the swing handles tight. One! He soared up high, touching the imaginary sky. Two! He went even higher, feeling the breeze tickle his nose. Three! He gave one final, giant kick and yelled, 'Wheee!' His tummy felt all fluttery and happy. Just as he coasted to a gentle stop, Grandma smiled and said, 'Time is up, my sweet flyer. Five minutes flew by like magic!' Sammy nodded happily. Because Grandma gave him a warning, he didn't feel surprised or upset. He hopped off the swing all by himself. 'Good job, swing,' Sammy whispered to the seat. Grandma held out her hand, and Sammy grabbed it tightly. They strolled down the sidewalk together, chatting happily about the delicious apple slices waiting for them at home.

stories.title: The Magic Block Tower
stories.text: Leo sat right in the middle of the soft green rug. Clack, clack, went the red and blue wooden blocks. He was building the tallest castle in the whole wide world! It had a very high tower for his little toy dragon to sleep in. The room was quiet and cozy, filled with the happy sound of playing. Suddenly, Mama walked into the playroom with a gentle smile. 'Leo, my sweet builder,' Mama said softly, kneeling down beside him. 'In five more minutes, it will be time to clean up our toys and wash our hands for yummy lunch.' Leo frowned just a tiny bit. He loved his blocks so much! But then he remembered what five more minutes meant. It was special bonus time! 'Five more minutes?' Leo asked. 'Yes, love,' Mama nodded warmly. 'Just enough time to put the very last magical flag on top of your tower.' Leo's face lit up with a big, bright grin. He carefully picked up the pointy yellow triangle block. Tap, tap, tap, he placed it right on the tippy-top of the highest tower. 'All done!' Leo cheered proudly. Mama clapped her hands together. 'Look at that magnificent castle! You are such a wonderful builder.' When the timer on the stove gave a soft little beep, Leo didn't feel sad at all. He felt ready. Because he had his five extra minutes, his tower was totally complete. 'Time to pack away!' Leo sang out happily, gathering the red blocks in his strong little hands. Mama gave him a big, proud hug. Cleaning up felt just as fun as building when you knew what was coming next. Together, they put every single block back into the big brown wooden box, ready for lots more fun tomorrow.

stories.title: The Sandbox Symphony
stories.text: The afternoon sun was warm and golden over the backyard sandbox. Maya was knee-deep in sparkly brown sand, holding a bright yellow shovel. Dig, dig, dig! She was digging a deep, wonderful moat for her royal shell kingdom. A little bumblebee buzzed happily by, and a gentle breeze tickled Maya's curly hair. It was such a lovely day for playing outside. Papa walked across the grass, holding Maya's soft blue sun hat. He knelt down right beside the sandbox edge. 'Maya, my little explorer,' Papa said in a warm, singing voice. 'We are having so much fun out here, but in five more minutes, it will be time to head inside for our nice warm bath.' Maya pouted her lower lip for a second. She didn't want to stop digging her moat just yet! Papa gently touched her shoulder. 'That means we have five more minutes right now. What is the very last thing you want to do in the sand?' Maya thought very hard. Her eyes sparkled. 'I want to make one giant sand volcano!' she squeled. 'Oh, a volcano sounds amazing!' Papa cheered, grabbing his shovel to help. For the next five minutes, the sandbox was a busy, happy construction site. Pat, pat, pat went the sand, shaping a huge mountain right in the middle. 'Three, two, one, volcano eruption!' Maya giggled, making happy sound effects. Papa laughed along with her. When Papa gently reminded her that the five minutes were all done, Maya felt happy and satisfied. Her volcano was finished and her moat was grand. 'Bye-bye, sandbox,' Maya waved cheerfully as Papa scooped her up for a piggyback ride inside. Transitions were easy peasy when you had time to finish your big ideas.

stories.title: The Last Chapter Journey
stories.text: The living room was wonderfully cozy and quiet. Mia was curled up on the big squashy sofa, wrapped in her favorite strawberry-print blanket. Grandma sat right beside her, holding a wonderful book all about sleepy woodland animals. Turn the page, flutter, went the paper. They were reading about a little fox getting ready for bed. Mia loved this story so much she could almost taste the sweet bedtime berries. Grandma stroked Mia's soft hair gently. 'My darling little reader,' Grandma whispered. 'This book is so wonderful, but in five more minutes, it will be time to turn off the reading lamp and tuck ourselves into our beds.' Mia snuggled even closer to Grandma's warm shoulder. 'Just five more minutes?' Mia asked softly, her heavy eyelids blinking slowly. 'Just five more minutes,' Grandma confirmed with a sweet, loving smile. 'That gives us just enough time to read about the sleepy little owl.' Mia's face relaxed into a peaceful expression. Five more minutes meant she didn't have to rush. She could listen to every single word about the fluffy white owl stretching its wings in the moonlight. Hoot, hoot, went the friendly owl in the picture. Mia listened carefully, feeling safe and warm. When Grandma closed the book with a soft thud, Mia smiled in the dim, cozy light. She felt completely ready for sleep. 'The owl went to sleep, and now I am ready too,' Mia murmured, giving Grandma a sleepy cuddle. Grandma carried her down the hall to her warm bed, singing a gentle lullaby. The five-minute warning was like a bridge, helping her walk peacefully from playtime all the way to dreamland.

stories.title: The Magic Sandbox Castle
stories.text: Leo loved playing in the backyard sandbox. He was building the tallest castle in the whole wide world. He had a big moat, a shiny green leaf for a bridge, and a very brave little toy dinosaur standing right on top of the highest sandy tower. Leo patted the walls to make them super strong. 'Roar!' said the dinosaur. 'We are having so much fun!' Just then, Mommy walked softly across the grass. She sat down right next to Leo in the warm sunshine and gave him a gentle, loving hug. 'Leo, my sweet builder,' Mommy said in her softest, happiest voice, 'it is almost time to go inside and wash our hands for a yummy, yummy lunch. You have five more minutes to play right here in your sandbox.' Leo looked down at his castle. Five more minutes! That was a wonderful amount of time. 'Five more minutes!' Leo repeated with a happy smile. Mommy gently set a little kitchen timer shaped like a happy yellow duck right beside them. 'When the duck goes beep-beep, we will pack up our toys together. Sound like a plan?' Leo nodded. He knew just what to do with his five extra minutes. He carefully placed one more tiny shell on top of his highest tower and made sure the moat had a smooth corner. He gave his dinosaur a happy goodbye pat. 'See you later, castle!' he whispered. The little duck timer went beep-beep with a cheerful sound. Leo did not feel sad at all. He stood up tall, brushed the warm sand right off his knees, and grabbed Mommy's hand. 'All done!' Leo cheered proudly. Mommy smiled bigger than the sun. 'You are such a great listener, Leo! High five!' They walked inside together, ready for a fun, happy lunch time.

stories.title: Building Blocks to Bedtime
stories.text: Maya was in the middle of building a gigantic rainbow tower in her cozy living room. Red block, orange block, yellow block, green block, blue block! It was taller than her knees already. She was just about to pop the shiny purple block right on the very top when Daddy walked into the room. Daddy stepped softly so he wouldn't knock over the rainbow. He crouched down beside Maya and gave her a warm, cozy squeeze. 'Maya, my wonderful builder,' Daddy whispered gently, 'it is almost time to put on our soft pajamas and read our favorite sleepy-time stories. But guess what? You have five more minutes to play with your blocks!' Maya looked at her beautiful rainbow tower. Five more minutes! That meant she had enough time to finish her tall creation. 'Five more minutes!' Maya said happily. Daddy smiled. 'That's right, sweetheart. I am going to set this little red clock right here. When it chimes, we will work together to tuck our blocks back into their special box.' Maya turned right back to her game. She carefully, super carefully, placed the purple block on top. Then she added a tiny toy bear right on the peak to stand guard. She clapped her little hands together because her tower looked so magnificent. Just then, the little red clock chimed a sweet, friendly ding-dong! Maya took a big, happy breath. She knew it was time to transition. 'Time to clean up!' Maya announced bravely. She gently laid the toy bear down and began placing the blocks back into their box, one by one, counting as she went. 'One, two, three!' Daddy helped her snap the lid on tight. 'You did such a super-duper job listening, Maya!' Daddy praised, giving her a big nose-scratch kiss. Maya felt so proud as they walked down the hallway to get her cozy pajamas.

stories.title: The Splashy Tub Adventure
stories.text: Oliver was the captain of a speedy red boat in the big blue bathtub ocean. Swish, swash, splish, splash! The red boat sailed over giant bubble mountains and past a floating yellow rubber duck. Oliver was having the absolute best time making big waves. 'Ahoy, captain!' whispered Grandma as she walked into the warm, steamy bathroom. She knelt by the side of the tub and gently stroked Oliver's wet curls. 'Oliver, my sweet little sailor, it is almost time to dry off and get all cozy for bedtime. But you have five more minutes of high-seas adventure!' Oliver smiled a big, toothy grin. Five more minutes of bath time! That was plenty of time to steer his red boat to the other side of the tub. 'Five more minutes!' Oliver chanted happily. Grandma smiled warmly. 'You got it, captain. I am going to set this cute little turtle timer right here on the counter. When the turtle sings its little song, we will let the water go down the drain together.' Oliver turned back to his captain duties. 'Full speed ahead!' he giggled, sailing his red boat through a sea of fluffy bubbles. He scooped up water with a green cup and poured it down like a waterfall. He was being such a focused, happy sailor. Suddenly, the turtle timer sang a sweet little melody: trill-trill-trill! Oliver listened closely. He knew the song meant his five minutes were done. He didn't fuss at all. Instead, he scooped up his red boat and his yellow duck, placing them right on their dry shelf. 'Bye-bye, boat!' Oliver said cheerfully. Grandma held out a big, fluffy, warm towel like a pair of giant butterfly wings. 'You are such a wonderful listener, Oliver! High five for being a great helper!' Oliver wrapped himself up in the warm towel, feeling so happy and proud of himself as he got ready for bed.

stories.title: The Last Block Tower
stories.text:
Leo loved building blocks. Every afternoon, his living room rug turned into a magical city with tall towers, zooming cars, and bustling train tracks. Leo was in the middle of balancing a very tricky red triangle right on top of his highest tower when Mama walked over with a big, warm smile.

"Leo, my sweet builder," Mama said softly, crouching down to his eye level. "In five more minutes, it will be time to put our toys away and wash our hands for a yummy dinner."

Leo frowned a little bit. Five minutes? What was five minutes? He wanted to keep playing forever! Mama gently touched his shoulder. "That means we have just enough time to finish this wonderful tower and zoom one last race car. I will set the timer so we can hear it beep together."

Mama set the little kitchen timer shaped like a smiling yellow duck. *Tick-tock, tick-tock*, went the clock. Leo looked at his red triangle. He knew what he had to do! Carefully, with his very steadiest fingers, he placed the triangle right on the peak. Balance! It stayed!

"Look, Mama! I did it!" Leo cheered, his face lighting up with pride.

"You did it, Leo! What a magnificent tower," Mama praised, clapping gently. Just then, the little yellow duck timer went *BEEP-BEEP-BEEP!*

Leo giggled. The timer was singing its song. Because Mama gave him five more minutes warning, Leo didn't feel rushed or upset. He felt like a successful architect who had completed his daily mission. 

"Time to tidy up!" Leo announced happily, gently taking apart his tower and placing the blocks back into their cozy wooden bin. Mama helped him, and together they sang a clean-up song as they walked to the sink to wash their hands. Transitions were easy and fun when you had time to get ready!

stories.title: The Sandbox Splash
stories.text:
The sunshine was golden and warm, and Maya was having the absolute best time in the backyard sandbox. She was a master baker, stirring dry sand and autumn leaves together in a blue bucket to make a giant chocolate-chip mud cake. Her hands were dusty, her knees were smudged, and she was completely happy.

Papa stepped out onto the back porch, holding a fluffy green towel. He walked over to the sandbox and sat down on the grass, smiling gently at Maya's wonderful creation.

"Maya, my little chef," Papa said in a soft, musical voice. "We are having so much fun, but in five more minutes, it will be time to pack up our buckets and head inside for a warm bath."

Maya pouted her bottom lip. Five more minutes sounded short. She wanted to bake a hundred more cakes! Papa reached out and gave her a gentle high-five. 

"I know, sweet girl. It is hard to stop playing when you are in the middle of a great game. That is why I am giving you a five-minute warning. That means you have time to bake one final, super-duper special cake and give it a big wave goodbye."

Maya thought about this. One super-duper special cake? She could do that! She scooped sand as fast as she could, packed it tight into the bucket, and flipped it over with a big *thump*. She decorated the top with three smooth round pebbles for cherries.

"My masterpiece!" Maya declared proudly.

"A true work of art," Papa agreed. Just then, a little bird chirped loudly from the tree overhead, sounding just like a gentle reminder. *Chirp-chirp!* 

"Time is up!" Maya said, feeling brave and prepared. She helped Papa stack the blue bucket and the yellow shovel. Because Papa told her five minutes early, Maya felt ready for the next adventure. She skipped inside holding Papa's hand, ready for splashy tub time.

stories.title: The Pajama Parade
stories.text:
The living room was full of cozy pillows, and Oliver was driving his favorite purple dinosaur all over the sofa cushions. Roar! The dinosaur stomped across a mountain of soft blankets. Oliver giggled, making silly dinosaur noises. Bedtime was coming soon, but Oliver was still full of zooming energy.

Grandma walked into the room carrying a pair of striped pajamas with little rocket ships on them. She sat down on the rug next to Oliver and smiled.

"Captain Oliver," Grandma said in a cozy, gentle whisper. "In five more minutes, our dinosaur friend needs to go to sleep, and it will be time to put on our rocket ship pajamas for storytime."

Oliver stopped his dinosaur for a second. Five minutes? He wanted to do one more giant dinosaur jump! Grandma stroked his soft hair. 

"The five-minute warning gives our brains time to get ready, Oliver. It means we have just enough time for the dinosaur to make one big final jump onto the big pillow mountain, and then we park our toys in the toy box."

Oliver's eyes widened. A final big jump? That sounded fantastic! He backed his purple dinosaur up, counted to three, and *WHOOSH*! The dinosaur soared through the air and landed safely right in the middle of the softest pillow.

"Safe landing!" Oliver cheered, feeling very accomplished.

"What a fantastic flight, Captain!" Grandma smiled warmly. She looked at the wall clock. The big hand had moved just enough. "And look, our five minutes have flown by just like a rocket ship."

Because Grandma gave him a loving warning ahead of time, Oliver didn't feel surprised or cranky. He felt proud and ready. He tucked his dinosaur into its spot on the shelf, picked up his rocket ship pajamas, and took Grandma's hand for a wonderful night of bedtime stories.

stories.title: The Magic Block Tower
stories.text: Little Leo sat right in the middle of the soft blue rug. All around him were big red blocks, yellow triangles, and long green rectangles. He was building the most amazing castle in the whole wide world! It had tall pointy towers and a wide bouncy bridge made of blocks. Leo smiled a big, proud smile. Just then, Mama walked into the cozy living room. She gave Leo a warm, gentle hug and whispered softly right into his ear, 'Leo, my sweet builder, in five more minutes it will be time to tidy up our toys and wash our hands for a yummy lunchtime.' Leo blinked his big brown eyes. Five minutes? He did not want to stop building his castle right this very second! Mama smiled back so warmly and said, 'That means you have just enough time to add one more tall tower and place your little toy dragon right at the very top!' Leo felt a happy flutter in his tummy. Five whole minutes was a wonderful amount of time! He quickly reached for a bright yellow triangle and carefully balanced it on the highest peak. Then, he gently placed his green dragon right beside the flag. 'Roar!' Leo whispered happily. He loved his dragon. Mama sat down right beside him on the rug to watch. 'Look at that magnificent castle, Leo. You are such a careful builder,' she cheered softly. As they counted down the last few seconds together, Leo felt so proud of his wonderful creation. When the timer made a happy little beep, Leo did not feel sad at all. He knew he had played wonderfully, and now it was time for a new fun adventure. He gave his castle one last happy wave and helped Mama put the red blocks back into their big wooden box, singing a silly song together all the way to the sink.

stories.title: The Last Swing in the Park
stories.text: The afternoon sun was shining down like a giant warm yellow button in the sky. Maya was at the park, and her favorite thing in the whole world was the blue swing. Up and up she went, reaching all the way up to touch the fluffy white clouds! Whoosh! The cool breeze tickled her nose, and Maya giggled a happy, bubbling giggle. Daddy stood near the sandbox, waving up at her. He walked over gently, knelt down right beside the swings, and said in a sweet, kind voice, 'Maya, my sunshine, we have five more minutes left on the swings before we pack up our bucket and head home for dinner.' Maya slowed her swinging down just a little bit. Five minutes? She loved the swings so much! She wanted to swing forever and ever. Daddy understood her big feelings completely. He gave her boots a gentle touch and said, 'That means you have time to touch the sky five more times! Let us count them together, okay?' Maya's eyes lit up. Five more big, wonderful swings! That sounded like the best game ever. 'One!' she shouted, pumping her legs. 'Two!' higher and higher she flew. 'Three!' the wind rushed past her ears. 'Four!' she could see all the tall green trees. And then came the very best one, 'Five!' With a happy little hop, Maya safely landed on the soft rubber chips below. She felt so proud of her strong legs and her wonderful swinging. Daddy clapped his hands and cheered, 'You are a super-duper swinger, Maya!' Holding Daddy's warm hand tightly, Maya happily skipped all the way to the car, ready and excited for a cozy evening at home with her family.

stories.title: The Final Splash in the Tub
stories.text: Splash, splash, splish! Tiny bubbles were flying everywhere in the warm, cozy bathtub. Toby was a brave pirate captain sailing his yellow rubber ducky across a sea of bubbly soap suds. He wore a washcloth like a pirate hat and laughed as the water swirled around his tummy. Bath time was simply the best! Grandma stepped into the bathroom with a big, fluffy, warm towel shaped like a little bear with cute round ears. She smiled down at her happy little sailor and said in her softest, coziest voice, 'Captain Toby, we have five more minutes of sailing time before our bath adventure comes to an end and it is time for our warm pajamas.' Toby looked down at his rubber ducky. Five minutes? He was having way too much fun making giant bubble mountains on his knees! Grandma leaned down and gently splashed some water. 'That means you have just enough time to make one gigantic volcano of bubbles and wash your happy little toes,' she suggested with a wink. Toby loved making bubble volcanoes! He scooped up handfuls of soft, soapy foam and piled them high on his ducky's back. 'Look, Grandma, a snowy mountain!' he cheered. Grandma clapped her hands together in delight. 'Oh, what a brilliant captain you are!' Toby quickly and happily washed his ten little piggies, making sure they were super squeaky clean. When Grandma wrapped him up in the warm bear towel, Toby felt like the coziest little cub in the whole wide forest. He gave Grandma a big, wet hug, feeling so happy about the fun game they played, ready for sweet dreams and sleepy bedtime stories.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Clock
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and tock,
Time to finish with your block.
Put the blocks back in the bin,
Let a brand new game begin!

Five more minutes, time to play,
Making up a fun new day.
Build a tower very high,
Reaching all the way to sky.

Tick-tock, tick-tock, hear the chime,
Playing is a happy time.
Soon we will be walking through,
Got a special job to do.

Five more minutes, make it count,
Climb upon your pony mount.
Tick-tock, tick-tock, time is near,
Time to give a happy cheer!

rhymes.title: The Playground Song
rhymes.text:
Down the yellow slide you go,
Swinging high and swinging low.
Sand castles upon the ground,
Running circles all around.

Five more minutes left to play,
Best part of a sunny day.
Slide again and count to ten,
Then we pack it up again.

Swinging high into the breeze,
Touching all the leafy trees.
Five more minutes, fast and sweet,
Dancing with your happy feet.

Now the timer starts to ring,
Hear the little sparrow sing.
Time to pack the toys away,
We will save some for another day.

rhymes.title: The Puzzle Piece Parade
rhymes.text:
Find the puppy, find the cat,
Where is little fluffy rat?
Fit the pieces in their place,
Put a smile upon your face.

Five more minutes, find one more,
Right beside the closet door.
Link the edges, snap them tight,
Everything is looking bright.

Almost finished with the game,
Call each little puzzle name.
Five more minutes, snug and neat,
Making sure the work is complete.

Put the box up on the shelf,
You can do it by yourself.
Time is up, we had such fun,
Look at what you went and done!

rhymes.title: The Train Track Express
rhymes.text:
Chugga-chugga, hear the train,
Driving through the tracks again.
Red caboose and engine blue,
Chugging right along with you.

Five more minutes down the track,
No one turning safely back.
Drive it fast or drive it slow,
Watch the little engine go.

Toot-toot, listen to the horn,
Best conductor ever born.
Five more minutes, make a stop,
Right beside the spinning top.

Now the engine comes to rest,
Playing trains is simply best.
Time to park the cars away,
Till we have another day.

rhymes.title: The Bubble Bath countdown
rhymes.text:
Floating bubbles in the air,
Floating right above your chair.
Pop a big one, pop a small,
Watch them gently rise and fall.

Five more minutes in the blue,
Splash a little water, too.
Catch a bubble on your nose,
Tickle down to tiny toes.

Five more minutes, make a splash,
In a speedy little dash.
Sail your little yellow boat,
Watch the funny captain float.

Time is going by so fast,
Make these final splashes last.
Dry you off and give a hug,
Snuggled in your cozy rug.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and chime,
It is almost bedtime time.
Toys are having so much fun,
Soon our playing day is done.

Time to listen, look and see,
Sitting softly on my knee.
Just a tiny bit to play,
Before we put our toys away.

Five more minutes, tick and tack,
Soon we won't be looking back.
Build a tower very high,
Wave the blocks a happy bye.

Now the timer starts to beep,
Time to brush and go to sleep.

rhymes.title: The Playground Pause
rhymes.text:
Swinging high up in the air,
Breezy wind is in my hair.
Slide down fast and laugh and shout,
That is what the park's about.

Listen closely, what's that sound?
Mommy's walking all around.
Five more minutes left to run,
So let's have some extra fun.

Slide one time and climb the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Now the seconds start to go,
Walking nicely, nice and slow.

Time to grab my little bag,
Off we go with not a lag.

rhymes.title: The Puzzle Piece
rhymes.text:
Puzzle pieces on the floor,
Let us do a couple more.
Find the puppy, find the cat,
Put them right upon the mat.

Clock says time is ticking fast,
Make this little minute last.
Five more minutes, can we try
To watch the little birdies fly?

Snap the corners, make it fit,
Sit and work a little bit.
Now the timer rings ding-dong,
Sing a happy little song.

Box is closed and put away,
Time to end our puzzle play.

rhymes.title: The Splashy Tub
rhymes.text:
Water splashing in the tub,
Rubber ducky needs a scrub.
Sailing boats of green and blue,
Swimming in the water too.

Evening stars begin to peep,
Soon the duckies go to sleep.
Five more minutes in the spray,
Splishing all our cares away.

Catch the bubbles in your hand,
Floating in a soapy land.
Time to dry off nice and warm,
Safe away from rain and storm.

Wrap me in a towel so sweet,
From my head down to my feet.

rhymes.title: The Leaving Song
rhymes.text:
Put your little shoes right here,
We are going out, my dear.
Get your jacket, zip it tight,
Making sure it fits just right.

Wait a second, pause and look,
Grab my favorite picture book.
Five more minutes by the door,
Looking out across the floor.

Wave goodbye to all our friends,
Where the hallway carpet ends.
Now it's time to step outside,
Ready for a happy ride.

Open up the big front gate,
Never have a cause to wait.

rhymes.title: The Big Clock Chimes
rhymes.text:
The kitchen clock begins to tick,
We have to pack up very quick.
Five more minutes left to play,
Before we put our toys away.

Blocks are tall and towers high,
Reaching up into the sky.
Build them up and watch them fall,
Have the best time of it all!

Listen close and hear the sound,
Toys are heading to the ground.
Into bins and boxes deep,
Till tomorrow they will sleep.

Now the timer starts to ring,
Time to dance and time to sing!
Great big hugs for sharing fun,
Look at everything we've done!

rhymes.title: Slide Down the Stairs
rhymes.text:
The golden sun is shining bright,
We will finish up just right.
Five more minutes on the slide,
Take a happy, speedy ride!

Climb the ladder, one, two, three,
Laughing loud and feeling free.
Whoosh and down you go again,
Playing with your favorite friend.

Now the warning bell is near,
Time to put away the gear.
Shoes are waiting by the door,
We won't play upon the floor.

Give the slide a little wave,
Acting brave and super brave.
Off to wash our hands so clean,
Best routine you've ever seen!

rhymes.title: Puddle Jumping Fun
rhymes.text:
Splish and splash in muddy shoes,
There is never time to lose.
Five more minutes in the rain,
Playing on the garden lane.

Jump up high and land so low,
Watch the muddy water go.
Big balloons of water pop,
Oh, we never want to stop!

Time is ticking, look and see,
Mom is calling out for tea.
Take your boots off by the mat,
Give a pat to our old cat.

Dry your toes and put on socks,
Safe inside away from rocks.
Warm and cozy by the fire,
Growing bigger, reaching higher.

rhymes.title: Bubble Bath Countdown
rhymes.text:
Bubbles floating in the air,
Wash the shampoo in your hair.
Five more minutes in the tub,
Give your tiny toes a rub!

Make a beard of soapy white,
Shining in the bathroom light.
Sail your plastic boats around,
Make a happy squishy sound.

Kitchen timer gives a beep,
Soon it's time to go to sleep.
Drain the water down the spout,
Time for everyone get out.

Wrap you in a towel so grand,
Softest bunny in the land.
Pajamas on, so snug and sweet,
From your head down to your feet.

rhymes.title: Park Swing Adventure
rhymes.text:
Swing so high up in the blue,
I am flying next to you!
Five more minutes at the park,
Before we have to beat the dark.

Kick your feet up to the trees,
Catch the lovely little breeze.
Touch the clouds and swoop back down,
Bestest playground in the town.

Buzzy bee is flying past,
Saying time is going fast.
Grab the chains and slow down low,
Ready for it time to go.

Jump right off and touch the ground,
Look at all the friends around.
Hold my hand and skip along,
Singing out our happy song.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and chime,
It is almost bedtime.
Pack your toys upon the floor,
We will close the playroom door.

Five more minutes, time to play,
Building blocks and cars away.
Time is flying fast and sweet,
Dancing on our happy feet.

Tick-tock, tick-tock, hear it ring,
Let us dance and let us sing.
Wrap your puzzle in a box,
Put away your colored blocks.

Now the timer makes a beep,
Time to brush and go to sleep.

rhymes.title: The Park is Calling
rhymes.text:
Swing and slide and run around,
Happy footsteps on the ground.
See the yellow morning sun,
We are having so much fun.

Five more minutes in the breeze,
Whispering to all the trees.
Slide one time and climb the wall,
Catch the bouncing rubber ball.

Time is ticking, hear it go,
Moving fast and not too slow.
Say goodbye to field and slide,
One last happy joyful ride.

Shoes are tied and coats are on,
Now our park adventure's gone.

rhymes.title: The Dinner Bell
rhymes.text:
Wash your hands and rub them clean,
Best little helpers ever seen.
Smell the carrots in the pot,
Dinner time is smoking hot.

Five more minutes at the chair,
Blowing bubbles in the air.
Stir the soup and set the spoon,
We will eat and sparkle soon.

Plates are waiting in a row,
Watch the hungry tummy grow.
Drink a sip of water cool,
Follow every table rule.

Now the timer rings its song,
Dinner time is right along.

rhymes.title: Morning Wake Up Song
rhymes.text:
Wake up sunshine, stretch up high,
Touching all the morning sky.
Rub your sleepy eyes so wide,
Joy is waiting right outside.

Five more minutes in the bed,
Pillow resting on your head.
Snuggle close and giggle low,
Ready for the day to go.

Throw the blanket off your toes,
Wiggle every single nose.
Put your fluffy slippers on,
Now the sleepy time is gone.

Bippity-boppity, time to rise,
Happy smiles and open eyes.

rhymes.title: Clean Up Symphony
rhymes.text:
Toys are scattered everywhere,
On the floor and on the chair.
Pick them up and sing a song,
Helping makes the feeling strong.

Five more minutes of our game,
Calling every dolly's name.
Stack the books upon the shelf,
Doing wonders by yourself.

Tick-tock goes the kitchen clock,
Put away the building block.
Tidy room is neat and bright,
 Shining like a lovely light.

Now the final bell has rung,
Every tidy song is sung.

rhymes.title: The Big Clock Chimes
rhymes.text:
The little hand moves round the clock,
It is time to pack our block.
Five more minutes left to play,
Before we put our toys away.

Build a tower very high,
Reach it up into the sky.
Five more minutes to run around,
Dancing softly on the ground.

Soon the music has to stop,
Like a spinning happy top.
Five more minutes, time is sweet,
Moving fast upon your feet.

Now the timer makes a beep,
Time to pack and not to weep.
Five more minutes done and bright,
Everything is feeling right.

rhymes.title: The Train is Leaving Soon
rhymes.text:
Choo-choo train is on the track,
Put your little blankie back.
Five more minutes on the floor,
Then we walk right through the door.

Drive the engine loud and wide,
Take a final little ride.
Five more minutes, toot-toot-toot,
Put on every shiny boot.

Wave goodbye to blocks and bears,
Walking nicely down the stairs.
Five more minutes having fun,
Now our playtime ride is done.

Station master rings the bell,
We can do it very well.
Five more minutes in the station,
Time to start our new creation.

rhymes.title: The Magic Timer Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the timer ring its song,
Singing right along, ding-dong.
Five more minutes to create,
Drawing pictures on a slate.

Paint a circle, paint a tree,
Happy as a bumblebee.
Five more minutes, make it bright,
In the lovely morning light.

Wrap it up with one more stroke,
Like a happy fairy folk.
Five more minutes, count them down,
Wear your shiny helper crown.

When the magic bell goes ring,
We can clap our hands and sing.
Five more minutes gently fade,
Look at what your hands have made.

rhymes.title: The Sunset Song
rhymes.text:
Sun is shining in the sky,
Time is quickly gliding by.
Five more minutes, play your game,
Call your favorite puppy's name.

Roll the ball across the floor,
Catch it right beside the door.
Five more minutes, jump up high,
Wave a happy wave goodbye.

Cozy blankets start to call,
Softly resting on the wall.
Five more minutes, snug and sweet,
Resting every tired feet.

Evening stars begin to peep,
Time to wind down from our leap.
Five more minutes softly close,
Tickle on your little nose.

rhymes.title: The Ready-Set-Go
rhymes.text:
Ready, set, the minutes fly,
Clouds are sailing in the sky.
Five more minutes of delight,
Playing in the morning light.

Puzzle pieces fit in place,
With a smiling happy face.
Five more minutes, find the spot,
Whether you have two or not.

Pack the puzzles on the shelf,
Doing such a job yourself.
Five more minutes to explore,
Walking to the kitchen door.

Now the little warning's through,
Ready for what we will do.
Five more minutes went so fast,
Such a happy time we passed.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and chime,
It is almost story time.
Toys are having so much fun,
Soon the daytime race is done.

Five more minutes left to play,
Build your tower far away!
Stack the blocks up very high,
Reach them up to touch the sky.

Time is ticking on the clock,
Just one more big yellow block.
Now the pointer moves around,
Hear the gentle ticking sound.

Five more minutes, time is neat,
Quickly tap your happy feet.
When the timer makes its ring,
We will put away each thing.

rhymes.title: The Train Station Stop
rhymes.text:
Chugga-chugga, choo-choo train,
Driving through the windy lane.
Drive your engine round the floor,
Right up to the bedroom door.

Five more minutes on the track,
Bring your passengers right back.
Drive the red car, zoom it fast,
Make this final journey last!

Round the rug and past the chair,
Driving cars is oh so fair.
Now the station comes in view,
Time to park the choo-choo, too.

Five more minutes to explore,
Then we close the playroom door.
Engine rests upon the mat,
Time to put away the hat.

rhymes.title: The Puzzle Piece Parade
rhymes.text:
Find a piece and fit it in,
Let the puzzle game begin.
Bear is hiding in the tree,
Put him where he ought to be.

Five more minutes, look around,
See what colors can be found.
Fit the puppy in his place,
Look upon his happy face.

Shapes and colors all align,
Working together is so fine.
Just a little bit of space,
Put the star in proper place.

Five more minutes, count to five,
Keep the puzzle fun alive.
When the little timer rings,
We will pack up little things.

rhymes.title: The Block Tower Sky
rhymes.text:
Build a castle tall and grand,
Finest castle in the land.
Add a window, add a door,
Spreading pieces on the floor.

Five more minutes, build it high,
Almost up into the sky.
Add a flag of yellow gold,
Best creation to behold.

Step back now and take a look,
Like a picture in a book.
Tower stands so strong and tall,
Careful that it doesn't fall.

Five more minutes, give a cheer,
Bedtime hour is drawing near.
When the melody is done,
We had lots and lots of fun.

rhymes.title: The Teddy Bear Parade
rhymes.text:
Teddy bears are marching round,
Making not a single sound.
Marching softly on the rug,
Giving everyone a hug.

Five more minutes to pretend,
Playing with your furry friend.
Dance around and skip and hop,
Soon it's time for us to stop.

Wave goodbye to fuzzy bear,
Put him resting in the chair.
He is sleepy, yes indeed,
Just like little ones in need.

Five more minutes, sway and bend,
Now our playtime nears the end.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We will rest until the day.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and chime,
It is almost story time.
Toys are having so much fun,
Soon the quiet time's begun.

Five more minutes, tick-tock-tick,
Pick up blocks and do it quick.
Build a tower very high,
Almost reaching to the sky.

Four more minutes left to play,
Smile and laugh the time away.
Drive the little truck around,
Making every happy sound.

Three more minutes, beep and toot,
Put the puzzle in the chute.
Now the final bell is near,
Time to cheer, hip-hip, hooray!

rhymes.title: The Sunset Slide
rhymes.text:
Sun is sinking in the west,
Time to do what you love best.
Just a little while to play,
Before we end this happy day.

Five more minutes on the slide,
Take a gentle, swooshing ride.
Climb the ladder, up and go,
Watch the happy faces glow.

Four more minutes, ready, set,
Best time that you haven't met.
Catch a bubble in the air,
Spin around and show your care.

Three more minutes, counting down,
No one's wearing any frown.
Pack the toys upon the shelf,
Help out mom or do it self.

rhymes.title: The Magic Minute Timer
rhymes.text:
Little hands are busy now,
Making every horse say moo.
Playing games is so much fun,
Till the golden day is done.

Five more minutes on the clock,
Spin the pointer round the block.
Paint a picture with your blue,
Make it bright and shiny too.

Four more minutes, dance and sway,
Jumping like a frog today.
Leap across the playroom floor,
Reach right for the bedroom door.

Three more minutes, sing a song,
Everybody sing along.
Now the warning time is through,
Ready for what we must do!

rhymes.title: The Train to Dreamland
rhymes.text:
Choo-choo train is on the track,
Going forward, coming back.
Playing with your trains is grand,
Best boy in the wonderland.

Five more minutes, chug along,
Humming out a happy song.
Bridge is built of blocks so tall,
Careful that it doesn't fall.

Four more minutes, whistle blows,
Where the engine chugs, it goes.
Park the train inside the shed,
Before we tuck you into bed.

Three more minutes, clickety-clack,
Put the pieces in the sack.
All aboard to rest your head,
Time to leave the toys instead.

rhymes.title: The Bubble Burst
rhymes.text:
Bubbles floating in the breeze,
Dancing through the leafy trees.
Catch them gently in your hand,
Floating in a magic land.

Five more minutes, pop them all,
Watch them tumble, watch them fall.
Chase a big one down the hall,
Biggest bubble of them all.

Four more minutes, ready, go,
Make the soap suds higher grow.
Blow a cluster of your own,
Flying up toward the throne.

Three more minutes, pop and play,
Savoring the happy day.
Wipe your hands and give a cheer,
Bedtime magic now is here.

rhymes.title: The Big Clock Chimes
rhymes.text:
The little hand moves round the clock,
It is almost time to stop.
Put away your blocks and toys,
Pack away the heavy noise.

Five more minutes, time to play,
Before we put the toys away.
Stack the boxes high and tall,
Catch the bouncing rubber ball.

Four more minutes left to go,
Make your engine chug quite slow.
Choo-choo train is pulling in,
Let the cleaning up begin.

Three more minutes, have some fun,
Now the counting has begun.
Two more minutes, big high five!
Glad we're happy and alive.

rhymes.title: The Golden Sun Song
rhymes.text:
The golden sun begins to sink,
Time to get a cup of drink.
Five more minutes left outside,
On the yellow rocking slide.

Run around the big oak tree,
Buzz around just like a bee.
Four more minutes, skip and hop,
See how high that ball can pop.

Three more minutes, take a breath,
Walk around without a step.
Two more minutes, find your shoe,
Tell me what you want to do.

One last minute, hold my hand,
Say goodbye to castle land.
Time to step inside the door,
We won't play outside no more.

rhymes.title: The Magic Timer Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the timer ring its bell,
Listen to the story spell.
Five more minutes in your chair,
Blowing bubbles in the air.

Four more minutes, draw a cat,
With a very funny hat.
Color yellow, color blue,
Draw a pretty picture too.

Three more minutes, close the book,
At the pretty pictures look.
Two more minutes, fold it flat,
Give a pat-a-cake-a-pat.

One more minute, stand up tall,
Wiggle fingers, touch the wall.
Now the time is up, my dear,
Time for lunch is finally here.

rhymes.title: The Teddy Bear Parade
rhymes.text:
Teddy bears are marching round,
Making such a happy sound.
Five more minutes in the room,
Sweeping with a little broom.

Four more minutes, dance and sway,
Happy little kids today.
Three more minutes, spin around,
Gently sit down on the ground.

Two more minutes, time to pack,
Teddy is going in his sack.
One more minute, cuddle tight,
Everything is feeling right.

Now the warning time is through,
I am so proud of you.
Time to wash your hands and face,
Moving to a brand new place.

rhymes.title: The Shoes and Socks Waltz
rhymes.text:
Put your shoes upon your feet,
Walking down the little street.
Five more minutes by the gate,
So we do not have to wait.

Four more minutes, wiggle toes,
Touch your funny button nose.
Three more minutes, clap your hands,
Dancing in the magic lands.

Two more minutes, reach so high,
Catch a star up in the sky.
One more minute, give a smile,
Rest your little legs a while.

Now the warning bell has rung,
And our little song is sung.
Grab your coat and grab your hat,
Time to go and do that.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Bell
rhymes.text:
Hear the clock go tick and chime,
It is almost bedtime.
Pack your toys upon the floor,
We will close the play-room door.

Five more minutes, time to play,
While the sun goes far away.
Build your tower very high,
Wave a happy, quick goodbye.

Blocks are dropping in the box,
Put on cozy polka socks.
Just a moment left to run,
Then we finish all our fun.

Big hand turning round and round,
Not a single extra sound.
Time is up, let's turn the light,
Say a cheerful, sweet goodnight.

rhymes.title: Park Bench Blues
rhymes.text:
Swinging high up in the breeze,
Touching all the leafy trees.
Slide down fast and laugh and shout,
What a lovely day about.

Five more minutes left out here,
To my little toddler dear.
Catch a butterfly and run,
Soaking up the golden sun.

Push the swing one final time,
Listen to the birdies chime.
Collect your bucket and your spade,
In the lovely parkland shade.

Shoes are dusty, cheeks are pink,
Time to get a yummy drink.
Homeward bound we start to go,
Walking in a happy row.

rhymes.title: Splashy Tub Time
rhymes.text:
Water splashing in the tub,
Rubber ducky needs a scrub.
Sailing boats of red and blue,
Having fun the whole day through.

Five more minutes in the spray,
Before we wash the dirt away.
Make big bubbles in the air,
Wash the shampoo in your hair.

Pouring water from the cup,
Drinking all the bubbles up.
Just a little time to float,
In your little plastic boat.

Plug is pulling, water drains,
Say goodbye to paper planes.
Wrap you in a towel so warm,
Safe and cozy from the storm.

rhymes.title: Clean Up Choo-Choo
rhymes.text:
Crayons scattered on the floor,
Puzzles stacked beside the door.
Teddy bear is on the chair,
Dolls are sitting everywhere.

Five more minutes for your train,
Driving through the windowpane.
Chug along the carpet track,
Never looking very back.

Now the whistle starts to blow,
Time to pack the toys up slow.
Put the crayons in the cup,
Zip the little backpack up.

Driver smiles and claps his hands,
Helping out as mummy stands.
Room is tidy, floor is neat,
Time to rest your little feet.

rhymes.title: Morning Sunrise Song
rhymes.text:
Morning sun is shining bright,
Chasing off the sleepy night.
Birds are singing in the tree,
Calling out to you and me.

Five more minutes in your bed,
Resting up your sleepy head.
Stretch your arms up to the sky,
Blink your sparkling little eye.

Snuggle blankets nice and warm,
Safe from every chilly storm.
Just a minute left to yawn,
Welcoming the happy dawn.

Throw the covers to the floor,
Open up your bedroom door.
Jump and wiggle, skip and shout,
Ready for the day about.

rhymes.title: The Big Ben Chime
rhymes.text:
The clock is ticking on the wall,
It is not time to end it all.
We hear the chime go ding and dong,
To sing our final little song.

Five more minutes, time to play,
Before we pack our toys away.
Build your tower nice and high,
Wave a happy block goodbye.

Push the swing up to the tree,
Happy as a bird is free.
Run around the yard so fast,
These sweet moments are our last.

Now the timer starts to beep,
Time to finish up our sweep.
Put the blocks back in the bin,
Ready for the next routine!

rhymes.title: The Sunset Countdown
rhymes.text:
The golden sun is getting low,
It is almost time to go.
Finish up your puzzle art,
Play your very final part.

Five more minutes left to share,
Teddy sitting in his chair.
Read your favorite picture page,
Actors on our playroom stage.

Make the choo-choo train go round,
Making such a happy sound.
Drive the truck across the floor,
Right up to the bedroom door.

See the numbers count right down,
Best routine in all the town.
Hand in hand we walk away,
Ready for a brand new day.

rhymes.title: The Magic Bell Song
rhymes.text:
Hear the gentle magic bell,
Listen to the story tell.
Five more minutes of our fun,
Playing underneath the sun.

Paint a rainbow in the air,
Brush your dollies golden hair.
Color with a purple hue,
Draw a happy picture too.

Slide down fast and climb right up,
Pour some water in the cup.
Stir the soup and bake the pie,
Wave the wooden spoon goodbye.

Ding goes bell and time is through,
Look at all the things we do.
Transition time is here at last,
Moving right along so fast.

rhymes.title: The Happy Pause
rhymes.text:
Take a breath and stop and pause,
Smiling just because, because.
Five more minutes on the rug,
Give your little bear a hug.

Roll the ball across the space,
Put a smile upon your face.
Stack the rings from big to small,
Catch the bouncing rubber ball.

Whisper softly to your friend,
Before this playtime has an end.
Dance around the carpet square,
Spinning lightly in the air.

Now the warning song is done,
We have had so much good fun.
Pack it up and skip along,
Singing out our daily song.

rhymes.title: The Train to Sleepy Town
rhymes.text:
All aboard the sleepy train,
Driving through the window pane.
Five more minutes in the station,
Time for final celebration.

Drive the engine round the track,
Forward, backward, and right back.
Blow the whistle loud and clear,
