What a wonderful morning in the kitchen with Mommy! Sammy smiled a big, toothy smile, ready for a day full of fun adventures, knowing he always made great choices.

stories.title: Bella and the Baking Day
stories.text: Today was baking day at Grandma’s house! The kitchen was filled with flour that looked like fluffy white clouds. Grandma was getting ready to bake a batch of chocolate chip cookies. The oven was turned on, getting nice and cozy. Bella loved baking day more than anything in the whole wide world. She put on her polka-dot apron and washed her hands with bubbly soap. Squish, wash, scrub! 'Grandma, can I help stir the bowl?' asked Bella eagerly. 'Of course, my sweet star,' said Grandma, pointing to the counter. But right near the warm oven was the big stove. Grandma gently placed her hand on Bella's shoulder. 'Remember our golden rule, Bella-bear: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Bella nodded her head up and down. She knew just what to do! She planted her little pink shoes right on the polka-dot floor mat. One, two, freeze! She stood as still as a shiny silver robot. 'Beep, boop, robot feet are frozen!' whispered Bella with a giggle. Grandma gave her a warm hug. 'You are doing such an amazing job keeping yourself safe.' Grandma brought the mixing bowl over to the safe kitchen table. There, Bella could stir the thick, sweet dough with a big wooden spoon. Stir to the left, stir to the right! They scooped the dough onto the baking sheet together. Soon, sweet smells filled the cozy kitchen. Bella sat safely at the little toddler table, watching the oven light glow. When the warm, yummy cookies finally came out, Bella clapped her hands with joy. She enjoyed every single bite of her cookie, feeling so happy and safe with Grandma.

stories.title: Leo's Safety Dance
stories.text: Leo was a busy little dinosaur today. Rarrr! He stomped around the living room looking for his favorite red ball. He stomped into the hallway, and then he stomped right into the kitchen where Daddy was making steaming hot vegetable soup. Bubble, bubble, went the soup in the big metal pot on the stove. The red orange flame was flickering underneath. Leo loved the bright colors, and he wanted to get a closer look at the bubbling bubbles. 'Stop right there, little dinosaur,' said Daddy in a gentle, singing voice. 'It is time for the Hot Stove, Freeze Feet dance!' Leo loved dancing! He stopped his dinosaur stomping instantly. He lifted his arms up high like pterodactyl wings. He kept his feet completely still on the kitchen tile. 'Freeze!' shouted Leo playfully. 'My feet are stuck in a block of ice!' Daddy smiled big and walked over to give Leo a gentle high-five. 'Wonderful freezing, Leo! You are a safety superstar.' Daddy explained how the stove was super hot, just like the sun, and needed space to do its important soup-making job. Leo understood completely. He stayed right in his safe dancing spot, wiggling his arms while keeping his feet planted like tree roots. When the soup was finished and safely cooled in bowls, Daddy scooped some out for Leo. They ate at the kitchen counter together, slurping up the yummy carrots and peas. Leo felt so proud of his freeze-dance skills. He knew that freezing his feet was the coolest trick in the world because it kept him safe every single day. He finished his soup and gave Daddy a big hug.

stories.title: Sammy and the Singing Soup
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sammy loved to help in the kitchen. Today, Mommy was making yummy vegetable soup for lunch. The big pot on the stove was bubbling and making happy little plip-plop sounds. Sammy tiptoed into the kitchen, carrying his favorite blue spoon, ready to stir. Just as he reached out his hand, Mommy gently touched his shoulder and smiled a warm, sunny smile. 'Wait a minute, my helper,' Mommy said softly. 'Remember our special kitchen game? Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy blinked his big brown eyes and looked at the stove. He knew right away what that meant. He stopped moving his feet just like a statue! One, two, three, his little red sneakers were glued right to the sparkly kitchen floor. He did not take one single step closer. 'Good job freezing your feet, Sammy!' Mommy cheered, giving him a gentle high-five. 'The stove is very hot right now to cook our yummy soup. Hot things stay on the stove, and our safe little feet stay right here on the floor.' Sammy felt so proud of his strong frozen feet. He stayed right where he was, safe and sound, watching the soup bubble from a happy distance. When the soup cooled down and it was time to eat, Mommy scooped a big bowl into his favorite green dish. Sammy used his big spoon and ate every single bite. He even told the soup thank you for being so tasty. Later that afternoon, when Grandma called him for snack time, Sammy remembered his special game. Whenever he walked near the stove, he checked his feet to make sure he was being super safe. He was growing up to be such a smart kitchen helper. Mommy hugged him tight and told him how wonderful he was at playing the safety game. Sammy smiled and hugged her back, happy, safe, and ready for his next big adventure in the wonderful world of growing up big and strong every single day.

stories.title: Mia's Magic Kitchen Dance
stories.text: Mia loved baking on sunny Saturday mornings. Daddy was making fluffy pancakes on the warm stove. The pan was sizzling with happy little popping sounds that sounded like tiny firecrackers. Mia skipped into the kitchen, humming her favorite tune, holding her toy spatula high in the air. She wanted to flip a pancake all by herself! As she skipped closer to the counter, Daddy suddenly called out in a playful, musical voice, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Mia giggled and instantly stopped right in her tracks. She froze just like a shiny silver statue in a museum. One foot was up in the air, ready for a step, and the other was planted firmly on the floor. She did not wobble, and she did not wiggle! 'Brrr, I am frozen like an ice cube!' Mia laughed, holding her pose. Daddy walked over and gently patted her head. 'You are the best statue in the whole wide world, Mia. The stove is super hot today to make our breakfast delicious. We always keep our safe distance and freeze our feet when we are getting close.' Mia smiled brightly because she knew how important kitchen safety was. Daddy let her stand safely on her sturdy step-stool a little bit later, far away from the hot burner, to pour in the blueberries with her own two hands. Together, they watched the pancakes turn golden brown. Mia felt like a master chef. When the pancakes were ready, they sat at the table and ate every crumb with maple syrup. Mia told Daddy all about her freezing skills. Daddy was so proud of how well she listened and kept herself safe. Mia knew that whenever she heard those special words, she would stop, freeze her feet, and keep herself out of harm's way. It was the best kitchen rule ever, and Mia was a pro at following it.

stories.title: Leo Learns the Safety Freeze
stories.text: Little Leo was a very curious explorer. Today, his mission was to help Grandpa bake warm apple muffins. Grandpa was taking a baking tray out of the oven, and the big stove was glowing with warmth. Leo marched into the kitchen with his firefighter hat on, ready for action. He saw the big dials on the stove and reached his little hand out to touch them. Grandpa gently caught his hand, knelt down to Leo's eye level, and said in a kind, reassuring voice, 'Hold on, little buddy. Hot stove, freeze feet!' Leo remembered this was the ultimate safety rule. Instantly, Leo planted his boots firmly on the kitchen tiles. He turned into a statue made of stone. He did not lean forward, and he did not take another step. He just stood super tall and straight. 'Look at me, Grandpa! I am a frozen firefighter!' Leo announced proudly. Grandpa smiled a big, proud grandpa smile and gave him a gentle squeeze. 'You are amazing, Leo. Stoves get very hot to bake yummy treats, and hot things are for looking at from far away. Your feet are safe right there.' Leo beamed with joy. He loved being safe, and he loved learning new rules. After Grandpa finished baking and the kitchen was cool and cozy, Leo was allowed to help put the paper liners into the muffin tin, standing safely on the floor. The muffins smelled like cinnamon and apples. When they finally got to taste them, they were the most delicious muffins ever. Leo chewed happily, thinking about his big adventure. He knew he was growing up big, strong, and very smart. Whenever he was near the kitchen, he kept his feet safe and ready to freeze whenever he needed to. Grandpa told him he was the best safety helper in the whole family, and Leo gave him a huge hug of agreement.

stories.title: Brave Bear Cooks Breakfast
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Barnaby Bear woke up with a big, rumble-tumble tummy. 'Time for yummy honey porridge!' said Mama Bear. Barnaby hopped out of bed with a happy bounce and scampered into the warm kitchen. On the big shiny stove, a little pot was starting to go bubble-bubble, pop! Barnaby reached out his furry paw to touch the side. 'Ooh, wait!' whispered Mama Bear gently. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Barnaby stopped right in his tracks, freezing just like a cool little snowman. He pulled his paws back safely to his tummy. 'Good job freezing your feet, Barnaby!' smiled Mama Bear. 'The stove is hot, which means it cooks our food to make it yummy, but we keep our hands and paws back so we stay safe and cozy.' Barnaby nodded his round head. He knew just what to do. He stood back on his tippy-toes and waited patiently while Mama Bear stirred the sweet oats. When the porridge was all done and cooled down just right, Barnaby blew on it gently—whoosh, whoosh—and ate every single spoonful. 'Yum, yum!' giggled Barnaby, patting his full, happy tummy. He felt so proud of his safe, smart bear steps. Whenever he walked near the cooking area, he remembered the special rule. Hot stove, freeze feet! And Barnaby knew he was growing up to be a very careful, clever little bear. The kitchen was such a safe and happy place for yummy treats and cozy morning cuddles.

stories.title: Pip's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Pip the rabbit had long, twitchy ears and a very busy day ahead. Today, Daddy Rabbit was making bright orange carrot soup for lunch. 'Sizzle, sizzle, pop!' went the big pot on the stove. Pip hopped into the kitchen, his little pink nose sniffing the delicious, sweet air. 'Mmm, soup!' cheered Pip, bouncing forward on his fuzzy bunny feet. He reached out a long paw to touch the shiny metal edge of the pot to see how it worked. 'Stop, little bunny!' said Daddy Rabbit softly. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Pip froze instantly, his ears standing straight up in the air like two tall tent poles. He didn't take another step forward. He kept his paws tucked safely against his soft chest. 'Thank you for freezing your feet, Pip!' praised Daddy Rabbit with a warm, proud smile. 'Stoves get very, very hot to cook our yummy meals. We stay a safe hop away so our paws stay safe.' Pip understood completely. He gave a happy little nod and sat safely on his blue booster chair at the table. He watched safely from afar as Daddy stirred the orange soup with a big wooden spoon. 'Look at the steam go up, up, up!' pointed Pip. When the soup was finally ready and cooled down to a nice, warm sip, Daddy brought it over. Pip used his spoon to slurp up every single drop, feeling so glad that he listened and kept his feet frozen when the stove was hot. What a wonderful, safe cooking day!

stories.title: Mia's Magic Freeze Dance
stories.text: Mia the kitten loved to explore. Today, the kitchen smelled like warm cinnamon apples. Grandma was baking a wonderful afternoon treat in the oven and on the stove top. Mia scampered into the room on her soft, quiet kitty paws, tail swishing happily behind her. 'Smells so sweet!' purred Mia. She trotted right up toward the warm counter where a teapot was whistling a happy tune. She reached her little hand out to touch the side of the hot burner. 'Hold on, little kitten!' sang Grandma gently. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Right away, Mia stopped moving. She stood completely still, just like a little statue, balancing on one foot with her hand frozen in the air. 'Such a wonderful freeze!' cheered Grandma, giving Mia a gentle, loving hug. 'Stoves are helpers for making warm food, but they are much too hot for little kitty fingers. We freeze our feet and stay back to keep safe.' Mia giggled at her funny statue pose. She loved playing the freeze game! She backed up safely to the rug and watched the steam dance in the air. When Grandma placed the yummy, cooled apple slice on a little yellow plate, Mia clapped her hands together. 'All done safe!' cheered Mia. She gobbled up her snack with a happy purr. Every time she walked into the kitchen, she remembered the fun freeze game. Hot stove, freeze feet! Mia felt safe, happy, and ready for her next big adventure.

stories.title: Sammy's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy skipped into the warm kitchen. Yummy smells tickled his little nose! The big stove was busy making yummy oatmeal for breakfast. Sammy stepped closer, reaching out his tiny hand to feel the air. 'Stop right there, little buddy!' whispered Mom with a loving smile. 'Remember our special rule: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Sammy giggled and stopped his feet right in their tracks, pretending to be a frozen penguin made of ice. 'Brrr!' he laughed, wiggling just his toes. Mom walked over and gave him a big, warm hug. 'That is right! When the stove is on, we keep our feet frozen safe on the floor. We never touch the big hot stove, because we are smart and careful!' Sammy felt so proud of his frozen penguin feet. He stayed right where he was, safe and sound, watching Mom stir the bubbling pot. 'Good job freezing your feet, Sammy!' said Mom. Sammy beamed with joy. He knew that listening to safety rules meant he was growing up big and strong. Soon, the oatmeal was ready, and they sat down to eat together. Sammy patted his tummy happily. Kitchen safety was easy when you were a clever penguin! Later that day, Sammy played kitchen with his toy blocks, pretending to cook yummy meals for his teddy bear. Whenever he imagined the imaginary stove, he practiced his freeze dance. 'Freeze feet!' he whispered to his teddy bear, making sure everyone was safe. Mom walked by and smiled, giving him another gentle high-five. It was a wonderful day full of learning, giggles, and safe kitchen adventures. Sammy learned that keeping safe could even be a fun game. He drifted off to sleep that night dreaming of penguin wiggles and warm, safe kitchens, ready for another happy day tomorrow.

stories.title: Maya and the Magic Kitchen Rule
stories.text: Maya loved helping in the kitchen. Today, Dad was making delicious vegetable soup for lunch. The pot on the stove was bubbling and making happy glub-glub sounds. Steam was dancing up toward the ceiling like a little white cloud. Maya walked toward the counter, her little shoes going pat-pat-pat. Dad turned around and said in a gentle voice, 'Hold on, my little star. What do we say when the stove is working?' Maya paused, put her hands on her hips, and remembered her favorite rhyme. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' she called out happily. Instantly, Maya stopped moving. She stood as still as a shiny silver statue in the park. Not a single finger wiggled! Dad clapped his hands. 'Wonderful job, Maya! You froze your feet just like a pro.' Maya smiled proudly, holding her statue pose for three whole seconds before taking a safe step backward. Dad explained how the stove gets very, very hot to cook our food, which means we must always give it plenty of space to do its important job. Maya nodded wisely. She felt like a very responsible helper. Together, they waited safely on the colorful kitchen rug until the soup was done and cooled down. Eating the warm soup felt extra special because Maya knew she had followed the kitchen safety rules brilliantly. Before nap time, Maya told her favorite doll all about the magic rule. 'You have to freeze your feet,' Maya whispered wisely to the doll. Dad heard her and smiled, proud of how well his little girl understood safety. It was another safe, cozy day in the warm family kitchen.

stories.title: Leo's Safe Kitchen Dance
stories.text: Leo was wearing his favorite yellow superhero cape. He zoomed into the kitchen where Grandma was baking yummy apple muffins. The oven light was glowing, and the kitchen felt cozy and warm. Leo flew toward the big stove like a super-pilot landing his airplane. Grandma gently held up her hand. 'Halt, superhero! Time for our safety superpower!' Leo instantly stopped his airplane zoom. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' shouted Leo with a big grin. He froze right in the middle of the kitchen floor, balancing on one foot like a brave flamingo. Grandma laughed and gave him a gentle cheer. 'You are the best freeze-dancer in the whole wide world, Leo!' Leo kept his feet totally frozen while Grandma carefully took the warm tray out of the oven. The sweet smell of apples and cinnamon filled the air, making Leo's tummy rumble with excitement. Grandma explained that the stove and oven are like sleeping dragons—they get very hot inside, so we must always keep a safe distance and never touch them with our fingers. Leo nodded seriously, keeping his superhero posture strong. 'Only grown-ups touch the hot dragon,' Leo repeated proudly. Grandma rewarded his great listening skills by letting him sprinkle a tiny bit of sugar on the cooled muffins later. Leo felt so happy and grown-up. He knew that being a real superhero meant keeping yourself and others safe. When evening came, Leo took off his yellow cape and hung it neatly by the door, ready for more safe and fun adventures tomorrow. He closed his eyes knowing he was smart, careful, and loved very much.

stories.title: Sammy and the Singing Soup
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sammy hopped into the warm and cozy kitchen. The sun was shining, and a big pot of soup was bubbling on the stove. Glug, glug, bubble, bubble! It sounded like the soup was singing a happy song. Sammy’s tummy rumbled. 'Yum, soup!' he said, reaching out his little hand. Suddenly, his big brother Leo called out, 'Stop, Sammy! Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy stopped right in his tracks, freezing his feet just like a statue. He looked up with big, curious eyes. 'What does hot mean, Leo?' Leo smiled gently and knelt down beside him. 'Hot means something is very, very warm, Sammy. It can hurt our gentle fingers if we touch it. So whenever we see the stove, we use our magic words: Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy nodded and practiced his statue pose. 'Like a penguin!' he giggled, keeping his hands safely behind his back. Mama walked over with big yellow oven mitts on her hands. She scooped up the yummy soup and blew on it to cool it down. 'Thank you for stopping, my smart helper,' Mama cheered, giving Sammy a gentle high-five. Sammy felt so proud. He learned that freezing his feet keeps him safe and sound. When the soup was finally nice and cool, Sammy got to eat every single spoonful. It was the best lunch ever. Whenever Sammy walks near the kitchen now, he remembers the song and keeps his feet happy and safe. He is a super listener and a very smart boy. Good job, Sammy! Every day is a new adventure in growing up big and strong.

stories.title: Mia's Magical Kitchen Dance
stories.text: Ring, ring! The kitchen timer went off, and Mia knew that Daddy was baking something delicious. The oven door glowed a warm orange color, and sweet smells filled the air. Mia skipped into the kitchen, wearing her favorite polka-dot dress. 'Is it ready? Is it ready?' she asked happily, walking right up to the hot oven door. Daddy scooped her up into a big hug and set her down on a safe, cozy step-stool a little bit away. 'Almost, my sweet Mia,' Daddy said warmly. 'Remember our special kitchen rule? Hot stove, freeze feet!' Mia blinked and looked at the glowing oven. 'Freeze feet!' she repeated cheerfully. She froze her little red shoes to the floor, standing as still as a shiny silver robot. 'Beep, boop, robot mode activated!' Mia giggled. Daddy clapped his hands. 'Wonderful listening, Mia! Because ovens and stoves get super-duper hot to bake our yummy treats, we always stop and freeze our feet before we get too close. That way, our skin stays safe and happy.' Mia understood completely. She waited patiently while Daddy used thick cloth mitts to take out a tray of warm, golden star-shaped cookies. They smelled like cinnamon and sugar! Daddy let the cookies cool down on the counter until they were just right. Mia sat at the table and enjoyed her warm treat, feeling so proud of her robot freeze-dance. Staying safe in the kitchen was easy when you remembered the magic rhyme. Daddy smiled and whispered, 'You are growing up so wise, Mia.' Mia beamed with joy, ready for her next big daily adventure.

stories.title: Oliver's Kettle Adventure
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! Little Oliver woke up ready for a wonderful day. He tiptoed into the kitchen where Grandma was making her morning tea. A silver kettle was resting on the stove, and a little white cloud of steam was puffing out of the top. Wheee! went the kettle. Oliver loved watching the steam puff up like a fluffy cloud in the sky. He took a big step forward to get a closer look. 'Whoa there, sweet boy,' Grandma said in her soft, loving voice. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Oliver stopped instantly. He looked down at his yellow duckie slippers and pretended they were glued to the floor. 'I'm a frozen duckie, Grandma! Quack!' Grandma chuckled warmly. 'That’s right, my clever duckie. That kettle and the stove are very, very hot. If little fingers touch them, it ouchies. So whenever we see cooking things on the stove, we freeze our feet just like you did.' Oliver wiggled his toes inside his slippers while keeping his feet right where they were. 'Good job keeping yourself safe, Oliver,' Grandma praised, pouring the hot water into her teapot far away from the edge. Oliver waited safely until Grandma was all done. 'Thank you for being so careful,' Grandma said, giving him a big warm hug and handing him a cup of warm apple juice. Oliver felt so happy inside. He knew that stopping and freezing his feet was a super important superpower. He practiced his freeze pose one more time just for fun. Grandma cheered for him, and Oliver smiled from ear to ear. Keeping safe made him feel like a big, responsible boy ready to take on the whole wide world.

stories.title: Brave Bear Cooks Breakfast
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Barnaby Bear woke up with a very big tummy rumble. 'Time for yummy honey porridge!' whispered Mama Bear from the cozy kitchen. Barnaby hopped right out of bed, pattered across the wooden floor with his fuzzy bare paws, and scampered into the bright kitchen. Oh boy, the big metal stove was warm and glowing. Mama Bear was busy getting the wooden spoon ready. Barnaby wanted to help stir the pot, but wait! What is our special rule when we see the big stove? Let's say it together: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Barnaby stopped his little paws right in their tracks. He planted them firmly on the floor. Freeze! One, two, three, four, five seconds. He did not jump, and he did not lean in. He stayed safely back at the magic safety line on the kitchen rug. 'Good job freezing your feet, my smart little bear,' Mama praised with a warm, gentle smile. Barnaby clapped his paws together proudly. He knew that keeping his distance kept him safe and sound. Mama gently lifted him up onto his sturdy helper tower so he was high above the stove level. From there, safely up high, Barnaby used his long wooden spoon to give the bubbly porridge a big, happy stir. Bubble, bubble, stir, stir! The porridge smelled like sweet cinnamon and warm honey. When the yummy breakfast was all done, Mama turned off the hot stove and let it rest until it was completely cool. Barnaby learned a super important lesson today. Whenever the stove is on and working hard to make delicious food, Barnaby's feet know exactly what to do. They freeze right where they are like friendly little statues. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Barnaby giggled, hugging his stuffed rabbit tight. Mama Bear gave him a big, proud hug right back. Eating warm porridge feels extra wonderful when you know you practiced safe kitchen habits all by yourself!

stories.title: Pip's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Pip the rabbit loved helping in the kitchen. Today, Daddy Rabbit was making vegetable soup for lunch. The kitchen smelled like yummy carrots and fresh parsley. Pip bounced into the kitchen, his long floppy ears swinging back and forth with excitement. He wanted to smell the delicious soup right away! But wait! The big red stove was turned on, and a little wisp of steam was dancing out of the silver pot. Daddy looked down and smiled his biggest, kindest smile. 'Remember our rule, Pip-squeak! Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' In a flash, Pip remembered just what to do. He stopped hopping immediately. He glued his fluffy bunny feet right to the kitchen tiles. Freeze! Not one hop, not one wiggle. He stood as still as a little statue. 'Great job freezing, Pip!' Daddy cheered. 'You are doing such a wonderful job keeping your paws safe.' Pip felt so proud standing there like a brave guard bunny. Daddy explained that the stove gets extra, extra hot to cook the carrots nice and soft. If little paws got too close, they could ouch! By freezing his feet, Pip kept himself safe while still getting to be part of the cooking fun. Daddy brought a special stool over to the counter, far away from the warm burners. He helped Pip climb up safely. From his safe spot, Pip washed some leafy green spinach in a little yellow bowl. Splash, splash, swish! He dropped the clean spinach leaves into a small dish for Daddy to add to the pot later. Pip felt like a real chef assistant. When the soup was all finished and the stove was turned completely off, Pip gave his feet a happy wiggle. 'Melt, feet, melt!' he giggled. Daddy and Pip sat down at the table to enjoy their warm, comforting soup together, feeling safe, happy, and so very proud of those smart, freezing feet.

stories.title: Leo Learns the Kitchen Magic
stories.text: Little Leo loved macaroni and cheese more than anything in the whole wide world. Today was mac and cheese day, and water was boiling on the big silver stove. Bubba, Leo's big brother, was standing by the stove getting ready to drop in the curly pasta. Leo scampered into the kitchen, his little yellow slippers going slip, slap, slip on the floor. He wanted to see! But wait! The stove had glowing orange rings. What is our special kitchen magic word? Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Leo stopped his little slippers instantly. Squeak! They gripped the floor tightly. He planted his heels down and made his feet turn into frozen ice cubes. One, two, three! He didn't take another step forward. Bubba turned around and gave Leo a high-five. 'Awesome job freezing your feet, Leo! You are a super safety star!' Leo beamed with joy. He knew that the stove was a helper that made our food hot, but it needed plenty of space so everybody stayed safe and happy. Bubba showed Leo where he could stand safely. It was right by the pantry door, far away from the heat. From his safe spot, Leo cheered Bubba on. 'Go, pasta, go!' Leo called out happily. They watched together as the water bubbled and churned. Once the pasta was cooked and the warm burner was safely turned off and cooling down, Bubba let Leo help stir in the creamy yellow cheese sauce with a big red spatula. Swish, swish, stir! The kitchen smelled like warm butter and yummy cheddar. Leo sat down at his little blue table to eat his delicious lunch. He felt so grown-up and smart knowing he could follow the important kitchen rule all by himself. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Leo whispered to his macaroni noodle before taking a big, happy bite. What a wonderful, safe day in the kitchen!

stories.title: Sammy and the Singing Soup
stories.text: Once upon a sunny Tuesday, little Sammy hopped into the big kitchen. Clang, bang, went a spoon! Mommy was making yummy vegetable soup on the warm stove. Sammy loved the yummy smell, but Mommy said the magic words, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy stopped right in his tracks. He froze like a happy little penguin, right where he stood. He planted his toes on the bright yellow floor mat and looked up with a big smile. 'Good job freezing your feet, Sammy!' cheered Mommy. Sammy learned that stopping keeps him safe and happy. The stove was for cooking yummy food, but his feet were for safe dancing far away. When Mommy said it was okay to move again, Sammy did a silly little wiggle-dance. He marched his feet over to the low table to draw a picture with his crayons instead. He drew a big red circle and a happy smiley face. Every time he heard the gentle buzz of the kitchen timer, he remembered to pause and check his spot. It felt so good to listen to his body and follow the safety rules. Mommy gave him a warm hug and a gentle high-five for being such a wonderful listener. Sammy felt proud and tall. He knew that stopping when told was a super-power. The kitchen was a place for family fun, cozy snuggles, and delicious meals, as long as everyone remembered the golden rule. Sammy took a deep breath, smelled the carrots and peas bubbling away, and happily played with his blocks on the safe kitchen rug. It was a wonderful, safe, and happy afternoon for everyone in the bright, cozy home.

stories.title: Leo's Safety Dance
stories.text: Leo loved to help bake! Today, Grandma was making delicious blueberry muffins in the big kitchen. The oven was warm and cozy, and the whole room smelled like sweet vanilla and juicy berries. Leo wanted to help stir the blue bowl, so he skipped across the shiny kitchen tiles. Just as he got close to the counter, Grandma held up her hand and sang out, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Leo knew that game! He immediately stopped hopping and planted his feet firmly on the floor. He squeezed his eyes shut and froze just like a frosty snowman in winter. One, two, three seconds went by. Grandma smiled warmly and said, 'Wonderful freezing, Leo! You are a super safety star.' Leo opened his eyes and giggled. He loved playing the freeze game because it kept him safe from things that were too hot to touch. Grandma explained that the oven and the stove were helpers for cooking, but they needed to stay nice and hot. Leo's feet were helpers for walking safely on the floor where it was cool. Together, they waited patiently while the sweet muffins baked to a golden brown. When the timer went ding-dong, Leo stayed right in his safe spot until Grandma brought the yummy treats to the low table. They sat down together to enjoy their snack. Leo felt so proud of his listening ears and his strong freezing feet. He knew that being careful meant he could have fun baking with Grandma every single day. He gave Grandma a big, sticky blueberry hug and whispered that he loved her safe kitchen rules.

stories.title: Maya and the Magic Pause
stories.text: Maya was a busy little bee buzzing around the house. Today, Daddy was making warm, cheesy toast in the kitchen toaster. The kitchen was bustling with wonderful morning energy. Maya zoomed toward the counter to see the yummy bread pop up. Suddenly, Daddy gave a gentle reminder song, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Maya knew exactly what to do. She hit her invisible brakes and stopped right on the colorful rug. She froze like a statue, standing as still as a tall tree in the forest. 'Freeze feet activated!' giggled Maya, holding her arms out wide for balance. Daddy clapped his hands and smiled. 'What a fantastic freeze, Maya! You kept your feet safe and sound.' Maya beamed with pride. She loved how her body could listen so quickly. Daddy explained that appliances like toasters and stoves get super-duper hot to help make our food, which means little hands and feet need to give them a friendly, safe distance. Maya nodded her understanding. She practiced taking three big steps backward to her designated helper spot. From there, she could safely watch Daddy butter the golden toast without getting too close to the warmth. When the tasty breakfast was ready, they carried the plates safely to the kitchen table. Maya munched happily on her crunchy toast, feeling like a very smart and capable big kid. She knew that listening to safety rules was just another way to take great care of herself. With a happy tummy and steady feet, Maya was ready for her next big toddler adventure, knowing safety always came first.

stories.title: Sammy's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy bounced into the bright, cozy kitchen. "Yum, yum, time for breakfast!" whispered Sammy, rubbing his tummy. Daddy was standing by the big stove, cooking up a warm, bubbly pot of yummy oatmeal. The air smelled like sweet cinnamon and apples. Sammy walked over, but wait! Daddy turned around and gave a big, friendly smile. "Stop, Sammy-bear! Hot stove, freeze feet!" Daddy called out gently. Right away, Sammy stopped his little toes. One, two, three, freeze! Like a statue of a happy puppy! Sammy giggled. He knew just what that special safety game meant. The stove was hot like a summer sunbeam, so Sammy's feet stayed safe and still on the kitchen floor. Daddy scooped a big scoop of warm oatmeal into a blue bowl. "Thank you for listening, my clever helper," Daddy cheered, giving Sammy a gentle high-five. Sammy sat right down at his little wooden table. He waited patiently while Daddy brought the bowl over. The oatmeal was warm and cozy in his tummy. Sammy learned that stopping right away keeps his fingers and toes safe and happy all day long. After breakfast, Sammy practiced his freeze-game again, pretending to be a frozen snowman in the living room. "Hot stove, freeze feet!" he chanted to his teddy bear, making sure teddy stayed safe too. What a wonderful, safe morning in the kitchen with Daddy! Sammy felt so proud of his listening ears and his strong, steady feet. Every time he heard about the stove, he remembered to pause, think, and freeze. Safety was easy when you played fun games together. Mommy walked in and clapped her hands for Sammy's great listening skills. Sammy beamed with joy, ready for his next big toddler adventure, knowing he was growing bigger and smarter every single day.

stories.title: Mia and the Magic Safety Rule
stories.text: Splish, splash, went Mia's little yellow duck in the bathtub later that afternoon. But now, it was dinnertime! Mia skipped into the kitchen, her red shoes going tap-tap-tap on the shiny tiles. Mommy was making delicious vegetable soup on the stove. The pot was making a happy little bubbling sound, like it was singing a song. Mia loved the kitchen, but she remembered the magic safety rule. Mommy turned around and said in a sweet, singing voice, "Hot stove, freeze feet, my darling Mia!" Mia stopped tap-tapping her shoes right away. Her feet froze to the floor like they were stuck with super-duper-duper-friendly glue. She stood very still, keeping a safe distance from the warm stove. "Good job freezing, superstar!" Mommy praised with a warm hug. Mia smiled from ear to ear. She felt so safe and clever. Mommy explained that stoves are wonderful for cooking yummy food, but they are very, very hot. That is why we play the freeze game! Mia nodded her little head. "Hot stove, freeze feet!" she repeated in her own sweet voice to show she understood. Mommy finished stirring the sparkly green broccoli and bright orange carrots in the pot. Then, Mommy and Mia washed their hands together with bubbly soap. At the dinner table, Mia gobbled up all her soup, feeling like a brave safety explorer. She told her stuffed rabbit all about how her feet magically froze just in time. Mommy smiled and told Mia how proud she was of her wonderful listening skills. Mia learned that staying safe can be a fun game that you play with the people who love you most. With a happy tummy and safe little toes, Mia was ready for bedtime stories and sweet dreams.

stories.title: Leo's Safety Dance
stories.text: Leo loved to dance. He danced when he woke up, and he danced when he played with his blocks. Today, Leo was dancing into the kitchen to show Grandma his brand-new robot wiggle. "Beep-boop-bop!" Leo sang, spinning around in his striped pajamas. Grandma was standing by the stove, baking yummy, sweet blueberry muffins for an afternoon snack. The whole kitchen smelled like warm berries and sugar. As Leo spun closer to the counter, Grandma held up her hands and said kindly, "Hold on, little robot! Hot stove, freeze feet!" Leo stopped spinning instantly. He planted his fuzzy slippers firmly on the floor. One foot here, one foot there, frozen just like a statue! Grandma beamed a big, proud smile. "Wonderful freeze, Leo! You listened so fast." Leo giggled and did a little wiggle with just his shoulders instead. Grandma explained that the stove gets super hot to bake the muffins, so our toes need to stay in the safe zone. Leo nodded seriously. "Hot stove, freeze feet," he chanted, making up a little rhythm to remember. Grandma finished putting the tray of muffins on the counter to cool down. She gave Leo a big, warm hug and a gentle nose-boop. "Thank you for keeping yourself safe, my sweet dancer." Leo felt so happy inside. He sat at the counter and waited patiently until the muffins were cool enough to eat. They tasted extra delicious because Leo knew he followed the safety rules. Later, Leo practiced his freeze-dance with his toy trucks, making sure all his cars knew how to stop when things got busy. Grandma and Leo clapped together, celebrating another safe, happy day filled with love, giggles, and smart choices.

stories.title: Sammy's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy skipped into the warm kitchen. Yummy smells filled the air! Mommy was making tasty oatmeal on the big stove. Sammy walked closer and closer, humming a happy little song. Suddenly, Mommy smiled big and sang out a magic rhyme: 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy stopped right in his tracks. He froze just like a frosty little snowman. Brrr! Sammy looked at the stove and remembered the safety rule. The stove gets very, very warm, and little fingers stay safe far away. 'Good job freezing your feet, Sammy!' cheered Mommy, giving him a gentle high-five. Sammy felt so proud and smart. He knew that stopping right away keeps his body safe and sound. Together, they stayed back a safe little step and watched the bubbles pop in the pot. Later, when the oatmeal cooled down into a yummy warm bowl, Sammy gobbled it all up. He loved his morning kitchen adventure. Whenever Sammy plays near the cooking area, he remembers to listen for the magic words. Hot stove, freeze feet! It is such a fun game that keeps him safe every single day. Sammy is growing up big and strong, and he always remembers his safety rules. The kitchen is a happy place for cooking and learning together.

stories.title: Bella and the Baking Day
stories.text: The kitchen was buzzing with excitement on baking day! Bella stood on her little helper stool, ready to help Daddy make blueberry muffins. The oven glowed warmly, baking delicious treats inside. Bella reached out her little hand to touch the shiny oven door. Just in time, Daddy scooped her up in a gentle hug and whispered, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Bella giggled and froze like a statue, not moving a single toe. 'That is right, my clever girl,' Daddy said with a warm smile. 'We look with our eyes, not with our hands, when things are hot.' Bella nodded and kept her hands tucked safely behind her back. She practiced being a safety star. Daddy explained how hot things need space to stay safe. Bella felt so happy to learn something new. They waited patiently until the delicious muffins were cooled down and ready to eat. Eating a warm blueberry muffin with Daddy was the best reward ever. Bella practiced her freeze pose a few more times just for fun. She felt like a superhero who mastered a very important power. Whenever she sees anything warm or cooking, she remembers to stop and think. Hot stove, freeze feet! Bella is always safe, happy, and ready for her next big adventure.

stories.title: Leo's Safety Dance
stories.text: Leo loved to dance around the house. Tap, tap, tap went his little red shoes as he explored every room. Today, Grandma was cooking yummy vegetable soup on the stove. A little steam was floating up into the air like a fluffy white cloud. Leo danced closer to the counter, ready to peek inside the big pot. Grandma gently placed her hand on his shoulder and sang, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Leo froze instantly, balancing on one foot like a silly flamingo. Grandma clapped her hands and laughed with delight. 'Wonderful freezing, Leo! You are a superstar safety dancer!' Leo beamed from ear to ear. He loved his special freeze dance. Grandma explained that the stove makes things super hot, so we must always keep a safe distance. Leo practiced stepping back and giving the stove plenty of room. He felt very responsible and grown-up. Grandma rewarded his great listening ears with a yummy slice of apple. Leo sat safely at the table, munching happily and swinging his legs. He knew that stopping when Grandma says the magic words keeps him safe from ouchies. Hot stove, freeze feet is Leo's favorite safety rule in the whole wide world. With a happy tummy and safe little steps, Leo was ready to play again.

stories.title: Sammy's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sammy hopped into the warm kitchen. Yummy smells filled the air! Mommy was making delicious vegetable soup on the big stove. Bubbles were popping, pop, pop, pop! Sammy reached out his tiny hand to touch the shiny metal pot. 'Wait, Sammy!' Mommy said softly with a loving smile. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Sammy stopped right away. He froze like a statue, just like a frozen penguin in the snow! 'Brrr!' Sammy giggled, keeping his little feet stuck right to the kitchen floor. Mommy walked over and knelt down to give him a big, warm hug. 'Thank you for stopping, my smart helper,' Mommy whispered. 'The stove is very hot, and we want to keep your fingers safe.' Sammy nodded. He knew that when the stove is on, his hands stay down and his feet stay frozen safe. Mommy showed him how they could stand on their little yellow step stool instead, high and safe, to watch the silly bubbles dance in the soup pot. Sammy felt so proud of his frozen feet! He learned that listening to safety rules helps everyone have a happy day. When the soup was finally done and cooled down in a blue bowl, Sammy clapped his hands. He ate every single bite, feeling safe and happy in his cozy kitchen.

stories.title: Leo and the Baking Day
stories.text: The kitchen was buzzing with excitement because today was baking day! Leo stood on his polka-dot rug, waiting for fresh banana bread to come out of the oven. Beep, beep, beep went the oven timer. 'It is ready!' cheered Daddy. Daddy opened the big glass door, and a cloud of warm, sweet air drifted out. Leo took a big step forward because the banana bread looked so yummy and brown. 'Hold on, Leo bear,' said Daddy gently. 'Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Leo immediately stopped. He planted his shoes firmly on the floor and pretended to be a sturdy green tree. His roots went deep into the rug, and he did not move a single inch! 'Wonderful freezing, Leo!' Daddy praised, giving him a gentle high-five. 'The oven and the stove are super-duper hot helpers, but they can hurt our skin if we touch them. That is why we freeze our feet and let the grown-ups do the moving.' Leo smiled brightly. He loved being Daddy's big helper. Together, they waited patiently until Daddy sliced a piece of banana bread and let it cool completely on the wooden counter. When it was warm and safe to eat, Leo took a delicious bite. He chewed slowly, feeling so proud of his wonderful listening ears and his super strong frozen feet!

stories.title: Mia's Tea Party Rule
stories.text: Mia was setting up her little wooden table for a grand afternoon tea party. Her teddy bear and bunny sat neatly on their chairs, waiting for make-believe tea. In the real kitchen, Grandma was heating up water in a shiny silver kettle on the stove. The kettle started to whistle a happy tune: 'Ssssss!' Mia loved the whistling sound and skipped toward the stove to see how it worked. She wanted to pat the kettle's shiny tummy. Grandma turned around quickly. 'Stop right there, my sweet butterfly! Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!' Mia froze instantly. She lifted one foot in the air, balancing like a fluffy pink flamingo. She stayed very still and giggled at her funny pose. 'Good job freezing, my clever girl,' Grandma said warmly. 'The stove and the kettle get extremely hot to make our tea, so we must always keep a safe distance.' Mia lowered her foot gently and nodded. She understood that Grandma only wanted to protect her little fingers. Grandma showed Mia how they could sit safely at the small table while Grandma poured the warm water into the teapot from far away. Mia clapped her hands with joy as they poured pretend tea into tiny cups. She felt so safe and loved, knowing that her frozen feet trick kept her out of harm's way every single time.

stories.title: Sammy and the Singing Soup
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Sammy hopped into the warm kitchen. Yummy smells tickled his nose! Plip, plop, bubble, bubble went the big silver pot on the big stove. Sammy’s big sister, Mia, was making yummy vegetable soup for lunch. Sammy wanted a closer look. He reached out his tiny hand, ready to peek inside the pot. Suddenly, Mom smiled a big, gentle smile and called out, 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy knew that special game right away. He stopped his little toes right where they were. He froze just like a frosty snow sculpture! Brrr! Not a single toe could wiggle. Sammy looked up at Mom with a big grin. Mom walked over and gave him a cozy hug. 'Thank you for freezing your feet, Sammy!' she said. 'That big stove is very, very hot. It is full of magic warmth to cook our soup, but it is much too hot for little fingers to touch.' Sammy nodded, keeping his feet frozen like happy statues. 'Hot stove means no touching!' Sammy repeated proudly. 'That's right, buddy,' said Mom. 'We look with our eyes and smell with our noses.' Together, they waited safely on the colorful rug. Sammy pretended to be a mighty mountain that couldn't move. When the soup was finally cool, they sat down at the table together. Slurp, slurp, went the delicious soup! Sammy was so proud of his super-duper listening ears and his frozen feet. He helped keep his body safe all by himself. Mom gave him a high-five, and Sammy giggled with joy. Kitchen safety was a big-kid superpower, and Sammy was learning how to use it every single day. The kitchen was warm, safe, and full of love, especially when everyone played the freeze game together!

stories.title: Leo's Leap Away
stories.text: BEEP! BEEP! went the kitchen timer. Leo scurried into the kitchen like a busy little bunny rabbit. Dad was baking yummy banana muffins in the hot oven. The kitchen smelled like sweet sugar and warm hugs. Leo loved baking day more than anything! He wanted to help pull the tray out. He reached his little hand toward the shiny glass door. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' sang Dad in a fun, musical voice. Freeze! Leo stopped right in his tracks. One foot was up in the air, just like a dancing flamingo! He stayed completely still, balancing on his tiptoes. 'Good job freezing, Leo!' cheered Dad. 'The oven is working hard to make our muffins nice and brown. It is super hot inside, just like a summer sun.' Leo lowered his foot slowly and stepped back to the safety line on the floor. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Leo said happily, remembering the important rule. He knew that big helpers keep themselves safe so they can enjoy the yummy treats later. Dad smiled warmly and knelt down to Leo's level. 'You did such a wonderful job listening, Leo. You are growing up so fast!' Dad used big, thick oven mitts that looked like monster paws to take the yummy muffins out. Roar! went Dad playfully, making Leo laugh out loud. They let the muffins rest on the counter until they were cool enough to touch. When it was time to eat, Leo took a big bite of his warm banana muffin. It tasted like sweet sunshine and success! Leo smiled around his yummy snack, feeling so proud of his listening feet. Keeping safe in the kitchen was easy when you played the fun freeze game with someone you loved.

stories.title: Maya and the Magic Safety Step
stories.text: Good morning, sunshine! Maya woke up ready for a brand-new day of adventures. Today, she was helping Grandpa make oatmeal for breakfast. Grandpa turned on the burner, and a little blue flame danced under the kettle. Whistle! went the kettle. Maya skipped toward the stove to see the steam puffing out. Her little fingers reached out toward the warm metal. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' called Grandpa softly. Maya knew what to do. She planted her little yellow sneakers firmly on the floor and turned into a heavy, sleepy stone. Not a finger twitched! Not a hair moved! Grandpa walked over and gently held her hand, guiding her back to the little red rug a safe distance away. 'Thank you for freezing your feet so quickly, my sweet Maya,' Grandpa said with a proud grin. 'The stove makes things very hot so our water can boil. We always keep a safe bubble of space around it.' Maya nodded seriously. 'Safe bubble!' she repeated. 'That's right, little helper,' Grandpa replied. 'We use our eyes to watch the pretty steam from far away.' Maya felt so clever. She pretended to be a brave guard protecting the kitchen. Grandpa poured the warm oatmeal into little bowls and added sweet blue berries on top. They sat together at the wooden table, eating breakfast and talking about all the fun things they would do that day. Maya looked down at her feet and smiled. Those same little feet knew how to freeze just at the right time to keep her safe. She was a kitchen safety champion, ready for any adventure that came her way!

stories.title: Brave Bunny's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a time, little Leo Bunny hopped into the warm, cozy kitchen. Sunbeams danced on the shiny floor, and yummy smells floated through the air. 'Sniff, sniff! Mmm, what is that?' asked Leo, wiggling his soft, furry nose. Mommy Bunny was making a special pot of yummy vegetable soup on the big stove. Bubbles were popping with happy little sounds. Pop! Pop! Pop! Leo wanted to see the pretty red light glowing on the stove. He took one happy hop forward. But wait! Mommy Bunny smiled a big, gentle smile and sang her special safety song: 'Hot stove, freeze feet! Keep our fingers safe and sweet!' Right away, Leo remembered what to do. He stopped his hopping feet right in their tracks. One, two, three, freeze! Like a happy little statue, Leo stood completely still. He did not wiggle. He did not wobble. He kept a safe, happy distance from the warm stove. 'Good job freezing your feet, my clever bunny!' praised Mommy. Leo felt so proud all the way down to his wiggly toes. He learned that freezing his feet keeps him safe while he explores his world. Instead of touching the hot stove, Leo stood on his tiptoes and clapped his hands happily. 'Yay for safe hands!' cheered Leo. He watched the soup bubble from far away, feeling very smart and very safe. When Mommy said it was time, they washed their hands together and ate a delicious, warm bowl of soup. Leo gave Mommy a big hug, so glad he knew the magic rule. Hot stove, freeze feet! It was his favorite way to stay safe and sound in his cozy home.

stories.title: Pip's Pause in the Playroom Kitchen
stories.text: Pip the puppy loved to help. Every morning, the kitchen was the busiest place in the whole house. Daddy was making fluffy, warm pancakes for breakfast. Sizzle, sizzle, went the pan! The butter was melting into golden pools of deliciousness. Pip trotted over on his four little paws, his tail wagging a happy rhythm. Thump, thump, thump! He wanted to get a closer look at the yummy pancakes. He reached out a little paw toward the big black stove. But Daddy looked down with kind eyes and gave a gentle reminder: 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Pip knew that rule by heart. Instantly, Pip stopped his wagging tail. He planted all four paws firmly on the kitchen rug. Freeze! He stayed as still as a sleepy puppy taking a nap. 'Good pause, little Pip,' Daddy said, giving him a gentle pat on the head. Pip felt a warm, happy feeling in his tummy. Freezing his feet was easy when he remembered how much he loved his safe paws. Daddy explained that the stove was a helper for cooking, but it stayed very, very hot. To keep safe, Pip always stayed behind the colorful taped line on the floor. Pip sat down nicely and waited for his breakfast, sniffing the sweet maple syrup smell in the air. When the pancakes were ready, Daddy put a special little piece on a cool blue plate just for Pip. 'Thank you, Daddy!' barked Pip happily. He munched his yummy treat, knowing that stopping and freezing his feet made him a very smart puppy. Every time he heard the word hot, his little feet knew exactly what to do. Freeze!

stories.title: Mia's Magic Kitchen Freeze
stories.text: Mia was a big girl now. She loved helping her big brother and her Grandma bake sweet apple muffins. The kitchen was filled with the wonderful smell of cinnamon and sugar. Grandma was taking a heavy metal pan out of the big, warm oven. The stove top was warm, too, ready for a pot of sweet tea. Mia walked across the shiny kitchen tiles, humming her favorite tune. Tap, tap, tap went her little shoes. She was so excited to see the baking magic happen! She took a big step closer to the stove to peek inside. Grandma held up a hand and said in a sweet, musical voice: 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Mia blinked her bright eyes. She knew this game! She planted her shoes right on the floor and made her body super still. One, two, freeze like a statue! Mia giggled because she was so good at stopping. Grandma smiled warmly and said, 'Thank you for keeping your safe distance, Mia. You are so smart!' Mia beamed with pride. She loved hearing how well she listened. Grandma showed her how they could stand safely by the counter instead, where they could mix the sweet batter together without getting too close to the heat. Mia stirred the bowl with a big wooden spoon, round and round, feeling like a real master chef. She learned that staying safe meant knowing when to stop and freeze. When the yummy muffins finally came out, they sat together at the table. Mia took a big bite of her warm muffin and smiled. She knew that freezing her feet was her own special superpower for staying safe in the kitchen every single day.

stories.title: Sammy's Kitchen Adventure
stories.text: Once upon a sunny morning, little Sammy hopped into the warm kitchen. Yummy smells tickled his nose! Pancakes were cooking on the big stove, and Mommy was humming a happy song. Sammy wanted to see the yummy pancakes up close, so he took a big step forward. But wait! Mommy turned around and said a very important safety word: 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Sammy knew what that magic game meant. Right away, his happy feet stopped dancing. One, two, three, they froze like little penguin statues on the kitchen floor! 'Brrrr!' giggled Sammy, staying safely back where he was standing. Mommy smiled a big, proud smile and gave him a high-five. 'Thank you for freezing your feet, Sammy-bear,' she cheered. Sammy felt so proud and strong. He knew that the stove makes things warm and yummy, but it is also very hot and not for little fingers to touch. Instead, he stayed behind the red safety line on the floor and clapped his hands while he waited. Soon, a fluffy, warm pancake landed right on his special blue plate. Sammy ate every single bite, feeling like a very smart big boy who knew how to keep himself safe in the kitchen. When the cooking was all done, Sammy helped wipe the table with a sponge. 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' he whispered to himself with a giggle, remembering the game that kept him safe. Mommy and Sammy shared a warm hug, happy for another wonderful, safe morning together in their cozy home.

stories.title: Leo and the Glowing Red Burner
stories.text: Ring-a-ding-ding! It was lunchtime at Leo's house. Leo washed his hands with bubbly soap and zoomed into the kitchen like a fast race car. Vroom! Vroom! Grandpa was making delicious tomato soup on the stove for Leo and his teddy bear. The stove was working hard, making the pot go bubble, bubble, pop! Leo zoomed a little too close to the counter. His little red shoes were rolling right toward the stove. Grandpa's eyes went wide, and he called out the special safety cheer: 'Hot stove, freeze feet!' Leo slammed on his imaginary brakes. Squeeeak! His feet stopped moving instantly. He planted his shoes firmly on the bright yellow floor tile and froze just like a frozen popsicle in the freezer. 'Good job freezing, super-driver Leo!' said Grandpa warmly. Leo beamed with joy because he listened so well. He knew that when the stove is on, it is like a little piece of the sun—way too hot to touch! Grandpa explained that we can look at the yummy soup bubbling away, but we must always keep a safe distance. Leo practiced his statue pose for three whole seconds before taking a safe step backward. When the soup cooled down just right, Grandpa poured it into a bowl with a happy spoon. Leo sat safely in his big chair and enjoyed every warm, slurpy spoonful. He even let his teddy bear have a pretend bite. What a safe and happy lunchtime!

stories.title: Mia's Magic Safety Game
stories.text: The kitchen was buzzing with the sounds of dinner time. Mia was playing with her wooden blocks on the rug, but the delicious smell of baked macaroni made her tummy rumble. She stood up and toddled toward the kitchen to check on the yummy food. The big oven was warm, and a pot was gently hissing on the stove top. Mia took a step, and then another, getting a little too close to the edge of the counter. Daddy looked down just in time and gave a friendly, cheerful reminder: 'Hot stove, freeze feet, Mia!' Mia stopped right in her tracks. Her feet froze like cement! She giggled, staying completely still like a painted picture on the wall. 'You did it! You froze your feet like a pro!' Daddy cheered, clapping his hands together. Mia felt like a safety superhero. She knew that freezing her feet is the best way to stay safe when grown-ups are cooking hot meals. Daddy bent down to her eye level and said, 'The stove is a helper for cooking, but it is much too hot for little hands. Thank you for listening so well!' Mia nodded her curly head. She stayed safely outside the cooking zone, playing a fun game of shadow-tag with her own shadow on the floor. Soon, the timer went ding-dong, and dinner was ready. Daddy served the macaroni in a bright pink bowl. Mia sat down at the table, feeling so happy and clever. She had played the safety game and won a wonderful, cozy family dinner.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Morning Warm-Up
rhymes.text:
Sun is up and shining bright,
Wake up little toes with light.
Stretch your arms up to the sky,
Wave a sleepy hand goodbye.

Time to cook a yummy treat,
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stand right still and count to two,
Now I see the dancing shoe.

Steping softly on the floor,
Walking right outside the door.
Brush your teeth and wash your face,
Moving at a happy pace.

Morning time is here to play,
We will have a super day!
Jump up high and give a cheer,
Glad to have you with us here.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Kitchen Helper
rhymes.text:
Little hands are washed and clean,
Best helpers you've ever seen.
We are cooking in the pan,
Helping mommy if we can.

Smells so good and tastes so sweet,
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Watch the bubbles pop and blur,
Let a grown-up take the stir.

Keep your toes upon the floor,
Do not touch that oven door.
Safety first is what we say,
Keeping all our fingers okay.

Dinner time is almost nigh,
Watching steam go floating by.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
Food is on the tray today.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Cleaning Up
rhymes.text:
Toys are scattered all around,
Time to pick them off the ground.
Blocks and bears and little cars,
Put them in their proper jars.

Walking fast upon the street,
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stop right there and look around,
Not a single toy is found.

Put the puzzle on the shelf,
Little builder by yourself.
Sweep the dust up in a heap,
While the tiny kittens sleep.

Room is tidy, look and see,
As happy as a honeybee.
Give a hug and take a seat,
Cleaning up is quite a treat.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Water splashing in the tub,
Time to give a little scrub.
Rubber ducky floats so high,
Looking at the bathroom sky.

Watch out for the soapy seat,
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Do not slip upon the floor,
Keep a towel by the door.

Wash the bubbles from your toes,
Wash your little button nose.
Splish and splash and have some fun,
Till the bath is nearly done.

Wrap you in a cozy wrap,
Ready for a little nap.
Dry and warm and feeling sweet,
From your head down to your feet.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Bedtime Stroll
rhymes.text:
Stars are peeking through the night,
Moon is shining round and bright.
Put your cozy pajamas on,
Till the setting of the sun.

Tiptoe down the hallway sweet,
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stop and listen to the clock,
Tick-tock, tick-tock, tick-tock.

Climb into your little bed,
Lay your sleepy, heavy head.
Pull the blankets up so tight,
Saying everybody goodnight.

Dreaming of a sunny day,
When we wake and start to play.
Close your eyes and drift away,
Safe and happy till the day.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Step into the kitchen bright,
Morning sun is shining light.
Smell the pancakes on the pan,
Help your mommy if you can.

Ah-ah-ah, now watch your beat!
Hot stove, freeze your little feet!
Stop right there and count to two,
Let the grown-ups work for you.

Now the danger time is past,
Walking safely here at last.
Wash your hands and sit down low,
Ready for a yummy show!

Eat your breakfast with a smile,
Sit and wiggle for a while.
Chew your food and take a sip,
Time for our big morning trip!

rhymes.title: The Safety Freeze
rhymes.text:
Time to cook, let's look around,
Keep your feet upon the ground.
Oven doors are getting warm,
Keep away from every storm.

Listen close and hear the beat,
Hot stove, freeze your little feet!
Freeze like statues in the snow,
Nowhere else for you to go.

One, two, three and now we play,
Safely in our kitchen way.
Dance around the table top,
Wait a minute, time to stop.

Good job following the rule,
You are looking very cool!
Wash your fingers, pat your head,
Time for lunch and butter bread.

rhymes.title: Red Light Kitchen
rhymes.text:
Cooking dinner, pots are hot,
Bubbling soup in every pot.
Smells so yummy in the air,
Pull your little helper chair.

When you hear the cooking beat,
Hot stove, freeze your little feet!
Like a statue, do not sway,
Keep yourself so safe today.

Now the stove is resting low,
Mommy says we're good to go.
Stir the bowl and count to four,
Tap your shoes upon the floor.

Hands washed clean and sitting neat,
Such a happy little treat.
Dinner time is here at last,
Hug your family very fast.

rhymes.title: Freeze Like Ice
rhymes.text:
Kitchen floors are shiny bright,
Helping out until the night.
Baking cookies sweet and round,
Best sweet treats that can be found.

Quickly listen to this treat,
Hot stove, freeze your little feet!
Turn to ice and count to three,
As safe as safe as safe can be.

Thaw out now and clap your hands,
Marching like a little band.
Keep your distance, way back here,
No hot danger coming near.

We are smart and we are wise,
Looking up with happy eyes.
Baking time is such great fun,
Cheer because the work is done!

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Dance
rhymes.text:
Wiggle fingers, shake your toes,
Follow everywhere it goes.
Smell the noodles boiling high,
Watching clouds up in the sky.

Sudden stop and hear the beat,
Hot stove, freeze your little feet!
Freeze so still and hold your breath,
Keeping safe from every scuff.

Now you're moving, up and down,
Best dancers in all the town.
Keep away from burning fire,
Reach your little hands up higher.

Safe and happy every day,
Learning how to work and play.
Kitchen rules are easy too,
Proud of little lovely you!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Walking to the kitchen floor,
Opening the pantry door.
Smelling yummy soup so sweet,
Hot stove, freeze your feet!

Stop right there and count to four,
Do not touch that iron door.
Keep your little fingers back,
Watch out for the yellow track.

Now we wiggle all our toes,
Touch our belly and our nose.
Mommy cooks the yummy meal,
Look how safe and sound we feel!

Sit down softly in your chair,
Wave your happy hands in air.
Time to eat our yummy treat,
Safe and happy, happy feet!

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Safety Freeze
rhymes.text:
Marching to the cooking zone,
Leave behind the ringing phone.
Watch the fire burning bright,
Keep our little fingers light.

Hot stove, freeze your feet right down,
Wear a happy toddler frown.
Not a step and not a sound,
Anchored tightly to the ground.

Now the cooking time is done,
Safety first is such great fun!
Walk around the shiny space,
With a smile upon your face.

Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We are growing every day.
Listen when the grown-ups speak,
Safe and sound all through the week!

rhymes.title: Red Hot and Frosty Freeze
rhymes.text:
Pots are boiling on the stove,
Through the kitchen now we rove.
See the steam go way up high,
Floating softly in the sky.

Hot stove, freeze your feet right now!
Make a little toddler bow.
Statues don't move here or there,
Standing frozen by the chair.

One, two, three and now we go,
Walking very soft and slow.
Keep your hands behind your back,
Staying on the yellow track.

Good job following the rule,
Toddlers are so very cool!
Now it's time to wash our hands,
Bestest kids in all the lands!

rhymes.title: The Hot Pot Hop
rhymes.text:
Time to make the mac and cheese,
Listen to the safety please.
Fire makes the water hot,
Bubbling in the big red pot.

Hot stove, freeze your feet up high!
Wave hello as we go by.
Freeze like ice and count to three,
As safe as safe as can be.

Now we melt just like the snow,
Moving where we want to go.
Step away and give some space,
In this happy cooking place.

Dinner time is almost here,
Give a happy toddler cheer.
Safe steps make us feel so bright,
Everything is doing right!

rhymes.title: Stand Still Like a Tree
rhymes.text:
Kitchen is a busy place,
With a smiling toddler face.
Smells are floating in the air,
Mommy standing by the chair.

Hot stove, freeze your little toes!
Touch your chin and touch your nose.
Like a statue on the floor,
Near the open pantry door.

Now we thaw and start to creep,
Quietly like little sheep.
Giving mommy lots of room,
Sweeping with a little broom.

Safety rules are great to know,
Helping little toddlers grow.
Clap your hands and sing along,
We love safety all day long!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Walking to the kitchen floor,
Coming through the swinging door.
Daddy cooks a yummy treat,
Listen to the warning beat!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stop right there upon the street.
Do not touch and do not reach,
That is what the helpers teach.
Eyes can look and that is fine,
Standing safely right in line.
Warm and cozy, smell the soup,
Spin around and loop-de-loop.
Safety first is what we say,
All through all our happy day!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Now we go and find our seat.

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Dance
rhymes.text:
Time to cook, let's dance and sing,
Happy rhythm in the spring.
Mummy stirs the pot around,
Making such a yummy sound.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Drop right down and take a seat.
Little fingers stay way back,
Watching every single snack.
Red and glowing, very hot,
Cooking in the metal pot.
Keep a distance, play it safe,
Smiling with a happy face.
Now the cooking time is done,
Eating is so much fun!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
That is our best safety feat.

rhymes.title: Red Light Danger
rhymes.text:
Baking cookies in the pan,
Helping mommy if we can.
Smell the sugar in the air,
Standing by the wooden chair.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Like a statue on the street.
Do not touch the metal ring,
While the happy birdies sing.
Keep your hands down by your side,
Taking joy in every stride.
Safety rules are good and bright,
Guiding us with all their might.
Soon we share a tasty bite,
Everything is feeling right.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Now our safety song is sweet.

rhymes.title: Freeze Like Ice
rhymes.text:
Step away, the burner's on,
Singing out our kitchen song.
Steam is rising, white and tall,
Happy toddlers one and all.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Freeze like ice upon the street.
Not a finger goes too near,
Growing up without a fear.
Brain is smart and eyes are wide,
Staying safely by my side.
Clap your hands and count to four,
Then we walk towards the door.
Living safely everyday,
In the best and brightest way.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Such a clever thing to repeat.

rhymes.title: The Brave Little Chef
rhymes.text:
Chef's hat on my little head,
Walking softly by the bed.
Into kitchen we will go,
Moving very, very slow.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Listen to the steady beat.
It is very hot to touch,
So we do not reach too much.
Keep our distance, watch the steam,
Floating like a happy dream.
Smart and careful all day long,
Humming out a little song.
Now we wash our hands so clean,
Bestest helpers ever seen!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Safe and happy, what a treat.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Morning Warm-Up
rhymes.text:
The morning sun is shining bright,
It is time to start the light.
Little toes get out of bed,
Put a hat upon your head.

Now we walk into the hall,
Big and happy, watch us all.
Stop right there and look around,
Don't make any shaking sound.

Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stand up tall and take a seat.
Wait a minute, count to three,
Look how safe you are with me!

Now we wiggle, wiggle toes,
Touch the tip of tiny nose.
Smile big and start to play,
We will have a happy day!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Kitchen Steps
rhymes.text:
Mummy cooks a yummy treat,
Walking on our little feet.
Smells are floating in the air,
Pulling up a little chair.

Cooking pot is very hot,
Do not touch it, ready, not!
Kitchen is a busy zone,
Listen to the safety tone.

Hot stove, freeze feet!
Keep away and look so neat.
Safety rules are good to know,
Watch our little bodies grow.

Now the cooking time is done,
Eating yummy food is fun.
Wash our hands and clap our hands,
Bestest helper in all lands!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Outdoor Adventure
rhymes.text:
Put on shoes and put on coats,
Sailing on our pretend boats.
Opening the big front door,
Ready for a walk explore.

Running down the garden path,
Splishing in a puddle bath.
Wait, a bicycle is near!
Better stop and listen here.

Hot stove, freeze feet!
Pause before we cross the street.
Hold my hand and look both ways,
Happy walking sunny days.

Now the coast is totally clear,
Nothing in the world to fear.
Marching onward, one, two, three,
Happy as a bird is free!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Bath Time Splash
rhymes.text:
Evening time is drawing near,
Time to wash behind the ear.
Bubbles floating in the tub,
Time to give a little scrub.

Water splashes on the floor,
Making puddles more and more.
Slippery tiles can be a trick,
Better move right super quick.

Hot stove, freeze feet!
Sit right down and take your seat.
No more running on the floor,
Till we dry outside the door.

Wrapped up in a fluffy towel,
Dry as any happy owl.
Now we brush our teeth up high,
Time to wave the day goodbye!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet! Toy Tidy Up
rhymes.text:
Blocks are scattered on the rug,
Teddy bear needs one more hug.
Time to put the toys away,
For another happy day.

Walking fast to fetch a box,
Picking up the woolen socks.
Wait, a puzzle piece is there,
Right beside the rocking chair.

Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stop and make the pathway neat.
Do not trip and do not fall,
We can tidy up it all.

Every toy is in its place,
With a smile upon your face.
Give a cheer and give a shout,
That is what we're all about!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Walking to the kitchen floor,
We are ready to explore.
See the big stove glowing bright,
Let us stop and do it right!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Time to pause our marching beat.
Keep your little hands away,
We are safe and we can play.
Now we turn around and walk,
Listen to the grown-up talk.
Cooking yummy food for you,
That is what the stove will do.
So we stay a step behind,
Being careful and so kind.
Hot stove, freeze feet, stand so still,
Yes, we know you always will!

rhymes.title: The Red Burner Song
rhymes.text:
Baking yummy treats today,
Listen to what we must say.
When the stove is turned on high,
Reach for it? Oh, my, oh, my!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Stop right in the middle of the street.
Not a finger, not a toe,
Near the hot red fire can go.
We can clap our hands instead,
Nod our happy little head.
Step back slowly, one, two, three,
Safe as safe can ever be.
Happy cooking, time to cheer,
Keeping all our helpers near.
Hot stove, freeze feet, good job, friend,
That is how our safety rules end!

rhymes.title: Freeze Like A Statue
rhymes.text:
Smell the soup upon the stove,
Through the kitchen now we rove.
It is bubbling, it is hot,
Do not touch it, leave the spot!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Like a statue on the street.
Freeze your fingers, freeze your toes,
Nobody near the burner goes.
Count to five and count it slow,
That is how the helpers go.
One and two and three and four,
Standing far away from the door.
Now we dance and wiggle round,
Happy feet upon the ground.
Hot stove, freeze feet, hold your pose,
Safety everywhere it goes!

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Safety Dance
rhymes.text:
Marching down the hallway wide,
Staying right by mommy's side.
Look ahead and what do we see?
A hot red stove for you and me!
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Listen to the safety beat.
Anchor down and do not slide,
Safety is our greatest guide.
We can wave and we can shout,
What is cooking all about?
Smells so yummy, soup and bread,
Pat the tummy, rub the head.
Keep our distance, nice and neat,
Dancing with our happy feet.
Hot stove, freeze feet, pause and glow,
That is all we need to know!

rhymes.title: Stop, Look, and Freeze
rhymes.text:
Pot of water on the top,
When we get too close, we STOP!
Keep our little hands right here,
Standing where it is safe and clear.
Hot stove, freeze feet!
Pause your little marching beat.
Big red burner, hot and high,
We just wave and say goodbye!
Backing up is so much fun,
Safe and happy every one.
Now we wiggle, now we sway,
Moving to a different way.
Helper rules are easy too,
Mom and dad are proud of you.
Hot stove, freeze feet, look at me,
As safe as safe can ever be!

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Walking to the kitchen bright,
Morning sun is shining light.
Smelling yummy breakfast treats,
Stop right now and freeze your feet!

Stove is hot and very red,
Keep your hands right by your head.
Do not touch the shiny ring,
Listen to the safety sing!

Walk around the magic line,
Everything is safe and fine.
Mommy makes a yummy cup,
Eat your happy oatmeal up.

Now the cooking time is done,
Safety first is such great fun!

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Safety Dance
rhymes.text:
Time to cook a happy meal,
Let us see how helpers feel.
Marching softly down the street,
When I yell out, freeze your feet!

Hot stove glows with orange light,
Keep our fingers out of sight.
Step away and count to three,
Safe as safe as safe can be!

Daddy flips a pancake high,
Watching clouds go in the sky.
We stay back and wave hello,
Watching how the yummy things grow.

Great big hugs for staying back,
Healthy snacks are in the sack!

rhymes.title: Freeze Feet Freeze!
rhymes.text:
Pitter patter go my toes,
Following my little nose.
Toward the stove we love to meet,
Suddenly we freeze our feet!

Red hot burner starts to glow,
What is the rule that we all know?
Never touch a thing that is hot,
Standing safely in our spot!

Clap our hands and sing a song,
Helping out the whole day long.
Smart little kids do what is right,
Keeping all our fingers white.

Kitchen is a happy place,
Big bright smiles upon each face.

rhymes.title: Stop and Look Song
rhymes.text:
Walking fast or walking slow,
To the kitchen we will go.
Hear the music, hear the beat,
Suddenly we freeze our feet!

Hot stove magic in the air,
Standing safely on our chair.
Never reach up high so tall,
Or our little cups might fall.

Smart and steady, watch and see,
As safe as safe can ever be.
Now the soup is in the bowl,
Happy tummy, happy soul!

Sing a little morning rhyme,
Cooking is a joyful time.

rhymes.title: Red Hot Burner
rhymes.text:
Time to bake a birthday cake,
Look at all the rules we make.
Stamping boots upon the street,
Time to stop and freeze our feet!

Hot stove warns us with a glow,
Caution is the way to go.
Step back twice and take a look,
Watching grown-up helpers cook.

Safe and sound is how we play,
Learning better every day.
Clap your hands and shout hooray,
We are safe in every way!

Now the cooking time is through,
Proud of little friends like you.

rhymes.title: Hot Stove, Freeze Feet!
rhymes.text:
Time to cook a yummy treat,
Listen now, my little sweet.
When the kitchen starts to heat,
Hot stove, freeze your feet!

Stop right there and count to four,
Do not step one inch up more.
Keep your fingers off the plate,
Standing still is simply great!

Mummy works so fast and bright,
Making dinner feel just right.
When the yummy meal is done,
Moving round again is fun.

Good job following the rule,
You are acting brave and cool.
Now we clap and give a cheer,
Safety time is better here!

rhymes.title: The Kitchen Safety Dance
rhymes.text:
Walking softly on the floor,
Approaching by the pantry door.
Smells are floating in the air,
We must use the greatest care.

Suddenly we hear the cue,
What is it we ought to do?
Hot stove, freeze your feet right down,
Wear a happy little frown.

Not a wiggle, not a hop,
Like a statue we will stop.
Counting slowly in our head,
While the soup is turning red.

Now the warning sign is past,
We can march around at last.
Safety first is what we say,
Every single time we play!

rhymes.title: Red Hot Burner
rhymes.text:
Pots and pans are bubbling high,
Reaching upward to the sky.
Grandma cooks a pie so sweet,
Hot stove, freeze your feet!

Plant your toes upon the floor,
Do not wander near the door.
Keep your hands behind your back,
On this safety happy track.

Red hot burner, glowing bright,
Keeping all the shadows light.
We can watch from far away,
While we sing a little lay.

Now the danger time is through,
We can find our favorite shoe.
Pat your tummy, time to eat,
What a clever toddler feat!

rhymes.title: Stop and Look
rhymes.text:
Bippity bop and in we look,
At the yummy things they cook.
Hear the kettle start to whistle,
Bouncing lightly like a thistle.

Wait a minute, take a look,
Reading from our safety book.
Hot stove, freeze your feet right now,
Take a gentle toddler bow.

Frozen solid like a tree,
No more dancing, no more glee.
